_childDocuments_.review: Having played every SW title and every DW since DW6, I can say SW5 is a great experience. However there are some differences. Most notably, you won't get 1,000 KOs just by blasting hyper attacks across the map like you can in say Warriors Orochi 4. The hyper attacks are more part of your standard move set than an absurd way to clear the entire map in moments. Also, SW5 is slow to build. The first two maps will seem slow, but by the 5th stage, much will feel familiar. At this point most if not all gameplay and character enhancement features will be unlocked. Your movement will be more DW speed, it will feel more deliberate. Your attacks need to be more purposeful, especially against officers as they're rather capable compared to their traditional toughness. Moves are the traditional 6 attack chain style where normal attacks can be supplemented by power attacks at any time.Characters develop proficiency in their starting weapon, but can develop proficiency in other weapons as well. Proficiency can be naturally acquired or boosted with a generic pool of weapon points. The same is true for character growth. You gain individual experience in battle as well as "Stock EXP", the latter of which can be applied to any character in your roster to level them up. Each character has their own supplemental skill tree to enhance their abilities. Skill points run across all characters so can be used as desired.Weapons have attributes tied to them (attack power up, range up, elemental enhancements, etc). Skills can be added to weapons at the Blacksmith via gems which are acquired in battle or purchasable at the shops. The same format follows for creating ever-better mounts at the Stables. This is not new. Additionally, each character has 4 abilities, or "Ultimate Skills", which perpetually recharge during battle. They consist of traditional temporary buffs (attack up, defense up, speed up) plus additional special abilities, some unique. You can assign these based on your preferences.Outside of the main storyline, or Musou Mode, you have Citadel Mode, where you complete scenarios with the highest score possible to obtain items to upgrade your facilities, and the Vault, which lets you read character backstories, see overall objective progress, watch cutscenes and listen to music. The art style is quite pretty and unique and that's about all there is to say on visuals. Only Japanese voice acting is available; fortunately it is quite good. English subtitles are present.So far, just a little ways in, I'm quite pleased with this installment. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Samurai Warriors 5 offers an exhilarating as well as refreshing experience of a newly designed musou game, which is demonstrated by the cell-shaded graphics used in the game, vastly different compared to its predecessors. Beware that since Samurai Warriors 5 focuses on the story of the Oda clan and the retainers of Nobunaga, a great number of characters are absent. Such fact becomes the main and the most frustrating flaw, which usually in the past, players got to experience a handful selection of characters that can be used throughout the game. In addition, despite having to cut down the rosters and unlike its previous predecessors in the past, there are some disturbing clones, which are gradually destructive to the game-play. I comprehend the direction taken by the developer as well as the publisher by focusing on one of the most influential clans during the warring states period of Japan, but the game should have come out better had there been no clones. Compared to Dynasty Warriors 9 with all of its performance issues, Samurai Warriors 5 proves to be extremely better, since the average FPS is comforting. Nonetheless, Samurai Warriors 5 is such a breakthrough, which is aimed to bring and create a freshly new direction, but in doing so, there are several fatal mistakes. In my personal opinion, Koei should have made and released the spin off, particularly focusing on the life of Nobunaga, rather than using the name of Samurai Warriors 5, which should have been used to indicate that this series will focus on numerous influential clans and conflicts rather than just on one clan only.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: If you've never played a Warriors title before, this review probably won't make much sense. tl;ldr It's a competent musou title but if you've played a lot of these games it might be overfamiliar in all the wrong ways and it doesn't really do anything spectacularly well so much as it refuses to do anything spectacularly wrong. This positive recommend is a 'meh', if you have a Switch you should be playing Three Hopes instead.When this game was in its pre-release state, everyone was declaring it as either the saviour of the genre or over the top anime garbage that would doom musou to the abyss forever. Ignoring the inherent hilarity of condemning a musou game for being 'anime', the game has been out for a year now and the question I've been pondering is simply:Which is it?And honestly? After thinking on it for a year and playing/replaying some other titles, the answer is just... It's neither.Samurai Warriors 5 is just a competent musou title.If you ask someone what they think of SW5, and they say 'It sucks', there's a good chance they'll point to two things: A cut-down roster compared to its immediate predecessor Spirit of Sanada, and characters having clone movesets. I'll concede, there ARE things that bring down this experience.But they aren't a part of it. No, I think a lot of SW5's most eyerolling moments come from how safe it is. Much of the marketing played the story up as a darker and grittier adventure than SW4 or SoS, and while I certainly bought into it, it's not exactly accurate. Nor would I say it's even 'dark'. Whereas SoS and even 4 to an extent told their story as a war drama with lots of pro-Japan angles (Do NOT ask Koei what Kato Kiyomasa was doing in Korea), SW5 is more... shonen. Very, VERY shonen in fact.If you've ever played MGSV, you might be getting deja vu. Much like that game, the marketing played up Nobunaga's 'fall to demonhood' or somesuch nonsense, and the main problem with the story is that he simply... doesn't make the fall? I'm not one to accuse games of being rushed, but the game's last act kinda speedruns the latter parts of his life and omits a lot of things. He doesn't really become a Demon King so much as he becomes a very naughty boy, and even then the story tries to pull the 'I had a noble goal all along!' thing.The perception of this game's story as 'dark' might come from all the character deaths, which isn't an unfair assessment inherently. My issue with that is that a lot of those deaths lack weight - even Dynasty Warriors, SW's more stone-faced cousin, handled some deaths better in 9. Not all, but certainly more than SW's. Couple this with some eyebrow-raising but ultimately inconsequential historical deviations by the franchise's standards, and it makes the tone of the story muddied and awkward.There is markedly less to discuss on the gameplay front.SW5 is the 4th game but with DW8's weapon system (sans the swap mechanic) and the special attack system from PW4. It never really evolves beyond this and runs out of new things to dangle in front of you really, REALLY fast. By the time I had every moveset in the game, the story was still pretending Nobunaga's ambitions were heroic.But oh, lord, we do need to talk about those movesets. Koei's philosophy for SW5 was "less is more" and while it sucks for the content, it really benefited the movesets. Much like DW8, the only unique thing that each character has for their preferred moveset is two EX attacks and a unique special skill to use with it. Regardless, all of these movesets are tons of fun and very effective at actually fulfilling their purpose. Having ran through the story thrice and Citadel Mode twice, I can tell you with confidence that you can slot together any weapon/character combination and win with relative impunity.However, that 'relative impunity' is the problem. This is no Dynasty Warriors Gundam 3 or Three Hopes, mooks pose even less of a threat than you'd expect and officers are a joke. There are 'special' peons that haunt the battlemap which might possibly stop your endless hyper attack string, but a single special skill will deal with them. Much like Three Hopes or WO4, officers sometimes stand still for a minute to charge a long, telegraphed attack with an AoE marker. I like to call these 'free damage'.Ah, right, content. Silly me, almost forgot about that.The story mode and Citadel Mode are actually all that exists in the game. While incredibly fun, this IS the shortest musou I've ever played - even Pirate Warriors 4 and Warriors Orochi 4 had a longer shelf life. Story mode's stages aren't particularly engaging, though the DLC chapters and postgame "What if?" stages were far more enjoyable, if only for offering you a more interesting variety of characters to choose from. As for Citadel Mode...It's bad. There's not really a diplomatic way to say it. The foundations are there for an interesting tower defense mode, but Koei did not commit to the idea and it essentially becomes a game of "chase the hydra" as you plop down your own mooks to stall conga lines of enemy mooks while you and your partner character go off killing. It has some good ideas but I'm just not into it. I hope it never returns and, if it does, it has a massive rework.Finally, let's talk about the visuals: They're good. End discussion. You've seen the screenshots; the game looks like that at all times. It's phenomenal.All in all, this game's major flaw is that it's an uncreative game from a developer who've consistently been putting out quality content with Pirate Warriors 4, Warriors Orochi 4, Age of Calamity and recently Fire Emblem: Three Hopes.If you enjoy Musous at a foundational level, you'll be able to squeeze some fun out of this. I sure did! But it's ultimately a giant standing at the kneecaps of titans, and standing on its tiptoes does nothing to bridge the gap. Here's hoping SW5-II or SW6 can add a few feet.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool Musou gameplay for any player, new or fan. Game works smoothly, has a new style of soundtrack (oriental music and some hints of ?power metal?). Despite the limited characters and the clone weapons, all of them have enough distinction to make up for it. As it is a reboot, Nobunaga Oda and Mitsuhide Akechi are the main characters, a departure from the usual Yukimura Sanada. The new characters are really cool, especially Shikanosuke, Yasuke, Kazuuji, Sandayu, while the reworked characters are mostly better than their former versions. Everyone also speaks Japanese, which some players might find irritating due to being unable to read through the fast-moving dialogue boxes. For me it was fine, just crush your enemies the Musou way.SW5 Musou mode has a shorter story than the other SW games, but it feels more humane and is less than a caricature compared to the previous games. Citadel mode is fun and exciting but can get boring really quickly. It's just to build Bonds between your characters, which unfortunately might be the downside of this game because it felt like a chore despite my hope to see something cool out of two characters working closely together. Also on another note, I don't understand why Nobunaga and Akechi are the only ones with a "mature" look, because Hideyoshi and Ieyasu stick around long enough to grow a beard or wrinkles.All and all Hisahide Matsunaga is probably the best of the reworks. Don't touch his Hiragumo, or you'll regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: In a word, fantastic! This game delivers in practically every respect. It's a wonderful sequal/ remake that puts a fresh spin on the series. The gameplay is classic musou ,and attacks feel very smooth and precise (horse-riding feels amazing too). The story is highly compelling and features a cast of colorful, dramatic characters. There is a total of 37 playable characters. The story mode is split into two paths that let you experience the events from both Nobunaga's and Mitsuhide's perspectives ,which makes for an extensive campaign. Most importantly, the game's new cell-shaded anime style looks great and fits the series well. What's more, the game runs very smoothly on modest specs. Overall, SW5 does a great job of reinventing the series, and I hope they continue using this style in future installments.

_childDocuments_.review: Samurai Warriors 5 provides all of the good stuff for fans of a Koei Warriors game. Plenty of individual systems (from weapon mastery, to individual passive skill trees, and beyond) for players to fiddle with between sessions of cutting down hoards of enemies. From my brief time with it (so far) I've found that the controls are responsive and the visuals are easy on the eye.The only point where it's lacking, in my view, would be the selection of characters and limited range of weaponry - as Koei seems to have opted for a shared arsenal rather than more individualised kit for each character.The story, while never the primary focus of these games, gives insight into the backstory of two of the series' mainstays. So far, it has proven to be easy enough to follow and gives an interesting change up to the previously identical formula that the games seemed to have followed (reworking many of the series' prominent figures).All in all, if you're a fan of Koei Warriors games - particularly Samurai Warriors - you'd be silly not to pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've really wanted to get back into the warriors games for a while now. I used to play one of the older Dynasty Warriors games when I was younger with a friend and we had a blast! However, after trying two warriors games since then and hardly playing them (both are in my library, Dynasty warriors 8 I think? and Warriors orochi 4) I was ready to give up because while the former was fun, it had a really bad tutorial and I was a bit confused, and Orochi put me off after the first mission because of it's overly simplistic combat (which is saying a lot for a warriors game lol).Anyway, I decided to give Samurai warriors a try because I figured this would be my one last try, and I thought it might help that I liked the idea of Feudal japan more anyway. I also read this game addressed a lot of my concerns about the previous games.Let me tell you, if you had a experience like mine with previous games, this game is for you! The tutorial is much better, and there's plenty to do. The story actually makes sense and is somewhat interesting. The graphics are actually pretty neat, not good, but visually appealing. The music is okay, pretty hit or miss withe me, but I like more than the previous games I mentioned.Also like I mentioned there's plenty to do as far as upgrading stuff, which is really important in these games because the combat can get pretty repetitive, so basically what keeps you coming back is improving or beating previous scores and unlocking things. Sounds kinda lame I know, but they do a good job of making it fun. If you are at all hesitant about getting into the series, and don't know where to start, this is definitely a good place as it's much more newb friendly. I might even go back and play some of the others in my library now that i understand stuff!I will say that it is kind of a niche interest, as it is it's own genre basically, so I would suggest if this is your first musou game, you should pick it up on sale. This is a new game so it's pretty expensive still!

_childDocuments_.review: Musou games have a long and varied history. I remember my first experience of playing Dynasty Warriors 3 back on the PS2 and I have really enjoyed the genre ever since. From Dynasty Warriors to Gundam Warriors, the formula hasn’t changed drastically over the years, but for those that enjoy the mindless slaying of thousands of enemy troops, it really doesn’t get old. Samurai Warriors 5 is the newest entry, which focuses on the Sengoku period in Japan, and there have been some minor changes to the formula that sets this entry apart from the rest.In the past, Samurai Warriors has typically focused on telling a story from the perspective of many different characters while never delving too deeply into anyone’s story in particular. You would see a few battles from many different characters such as Nobunaga, Hideyoshi, Yukimura, and countless others. Looking back at Samurai Warriors 4, the campaign was split between at least ten different faction story-lines, which can lead to a bit of confusion on what exactly is going on in the grand scheme of things. The entry before Samurai Warriors 5, Spirit of Sanada, took the opposite approach and focused mainly on the Sanada for its campaign mode. Samurai Warriors 5 takes a similar approach by retelling the Oda history.In Samurai Warriors 5, there is one major campaign story told from the perspective of two of the most influential figures: Nobunaga Oda and Mitsuhide Akechi. Each branch of the story has many overlapping points where the perspective of each character provides a deeper look at the motivations and feelings behind each character. While each branch is either focused on Nobunaga or Mitsuhide, there are plenty of other characters that are introduced and playable throughout the campaign. This is a welcome change of pace for players that perhaps want to learn more details about this time period. However, some fan favorite characters will not make an appearance in Samurai Warriors 5 due to them not being involved with this particular point in history.The overall gameplay of SW5 is the same as the past. You are given a roster of characters to choose two officers from for each battle – some rosters are more limited than others depending on the fight. As you play those characters, they gain experience and mastery of their equipped weapons and horses. During the battles, you will collect new weapons and skill points and gems to use to customize your characters even further. Each character has a skill tree which allows you to unlock better stats or new moves to use as the character grows in strength. For instance, you can unlock the passive ability to have a “second wind” when your character’s health reaches zero – they are automatically revived one time during the fight. Another example of upgrades are unlocking multiple special attack gauges that allow you to use the ability multiple times in a row. These aspects are pretty familiar to fans of the genre.In combat, you are able to select four abilities to call upon in battle. These can be buffs which allow you to deal more damage or bolster your defense. They can also be attacking abilities such as sprinting full speed into a group of enemies or performing huge attacks that sweep across the screen. These abilities are usable multiple times but have a short cooldown between uses. This separates older entries that may have relied purely on pressing combinations of light attacks and heavy attacks to perform a variation or special attack. Weapons are still customizable as in previous Samurai Warriors games. Weapons are given ranks, attack stats, and modifiers that are dictated by the gems you add to a weapon. For instance, you may find a weapon that has eight gem slots and you can pick and choose which modifiers you want to add to a weapon. You may find yourself wanting your katana to have a longer range of attack, with a wind element, and when you kill an officer you gain a buff to your speed for 30 seconds. This is completely achievable and up to the player to choose how they want to customize their weapons. These gems can also be upgraded to produce greater effects.Outside of the campaign, you can play an alternative mode called Citadel, which allows you to select two characters to fight waves of enemies to protect your castle. This mode allows characters to grow stronger relationships and provides you with materials to upgrade your buildings. As you upgrade the different aspects of your castle, such as the Dojo or Blacksmith, you are able to increase your gems’ level or upgrade your characters and their mastery with scrolls that provide experience. This gives motivations to play the alternative modes, but aren’t completely necessary to enjoy the base game. I was able to complete both campaigns without worrying about upgrading my castle on the normal difficulty, but I assume it would be very valuable as you increase the difficulty to Hard or Nightmare.The biggest update in Samurai Warriors 5 is the visuals. The characters are beautifully rendered with a cell shading ink that gives new life to the officers that we have seen for many entries. The attack animations combined with the sheer number of enemies on the screen at one time are quite a sight. There were times that I had to see at least 100 enemies on the field at a given time, mostly flying through the air as I performed huge attacks to knock them off their feet.There are a few downsides to Samurai Warriors, mostly being based on perspective – a lot of people do not like the monotonous killing of a thousand soldiers. The gameplay never really varies from battle to battle. Head to section, kill 200 soldiers, kill an officer, escort a support troop, retreat to another section. This is the bread and butter of Musou games so it should be expected. Also, I have no problem reading subtitles, and since this game is fully voiced in Japanese, you will definitely have to read. The issue with this is in mid-battle, characters will provide information that you will have to read on the fly, while trying to maintain combos and pay attention to the battlefield. It can be a bit much! I also miss modes that have been in past entries like Dynasty Warriors 7’s Conquest Mode or Dynasty Warriors 8’s Ambition Mode. Citadel just seems lacking comparatively but still not bad. Overall, I think there is a lot to like here with Samurai Warriors 5. Fans of the genre will enjoy the updated visuals and maybe enjoy how focused the story is compared to past entries, but may miss fan favorite characters. The abilities are fun to use to break up the typical mashing of attack buttons. It took about 30 hours to go through both the Nobunaga and Mitsuhide campaigns and there is third unlockable timeline which requires completing stages with S ranks to unlock additional stages. I would say there is a good 40-50 hours worth of content here, with quite a few more hours for completionists.

_childDocuments_.review: Samurai Warriors 5 is a new entry in the series with some new mechanics to change up the pace of its gameplay. It implements new character designs and a reimagining of the Sengoku period with Oda Nobunaga and Akechi Mitsuhide as main characters.=======================================================================Story:The story focuses more on the early days of the two main characters, exploring how they gain power and becoming who they are, their relationships with other characters, and their own reasons to fight. This game tells the story with two main storylines, each viewed using two main characters perspectives. Personally, I think the story is well written. You feel for the characters after you understand more about them. This game is heavily story orientated so I can't talk about details without spoiling it.=======================================================================Gameplay:There are two new game-changing mechanics.Hyper Attack: Pressing Y (I played with a controller) makes your character traverse great distance while attacking enemies, plus helping players to chain combos.Ultimate Skill: Skills that...I. Enhance your character's ability for a short period of time.II. Interrupt enemies' combo while dealing damage to them/dashing forward.III. Regenerates your Musou Gauge.These skills can be activated when doing a combo too. Speeds up the pace of combat by a lot.Also the locking system. I'm not sure if the previous games had it or not, but you can lock onto any enemy characters who are in the character roster or special enemies. It helps a lot when there are a bunch of enemies on screen.=======================================================================Graphics:This game uses an anime-like style, in which characters look like anime characters. It combines with the traditional Japanese painting and the result is pretty unique. The downside of the new design is that the environment design can be boring at times.=======================================================================Music:The music is a mix of traditional Japanese instruments and modern instruments (like electric guitar and bass). They all sound fitting and some of them sounds amazing.=======================================================================Pros:1. This game is a hack and slash game at its best, feels exhilarating every time I play it.2. The story, it is very good.3. Cool visuals!4. Some may not like it, but the new character design is refreshing IMO.5. Music sounds very fitting.=======================================================================Cons: 1. The way this game tells the story can be a bit confusing to some.2. The Citadel Mode is not that interesting, and also a bit grindy.3. The price is slightly higher than the average AAA game price.=======================================================================Verdict: This is a must-buy if:1. You are a long time Warriors series fan and you don't mind the new character design or the new narrative direction.2. You don't dislike the Warriors formula or the hack and slash genre, and you are looking for new games to play.Mechanically, this is the best in the whole Warriors franchise. I personally liked the new art direction and I enjoyed this game a lot. I would very much recommend it, especially to those who are interested in the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: <contains spoilers> in my opinion this is the second greatest samurai warriors of all time. 4 is still the best for me.Story wise, its superior to SW 4. Yes it only covers mainly nobunagas and mistuhides sides of the story.  But they did it really well. We always hear how Nobunaga is evil in previous SW games. But here you get to see why people think  he's a terrible brutal guy. You witness how Nobunaga evolves from this optimistic  and caring young daimyo to  become mass murdering cold blooded tyrant. And they did a good job at showing us why  and how he became a "demon king",  so to speak. You get to hate nobunaga <while loving his OP nodachi moveset>.  Mitsuhide's side of the story is better than Nobunaga. You get to symphatize with the guy. He is not just preaching "righteousness" for no reason like ma chao always does in dynasty warriors.Gameplay is solid. Combat is ultra satisfying.  Its unfortunate that many characters share the same weapons. But some power attack moves are uniquely different depending on which character you choose, so i guess that makes up for the lack of variety somewhat.   There are active combal abilities that you can activate by pressing R1 and corresponding keys  just like in one piece pirate warriors.Honda Tadakatsu is much slower and weaker in the game.  So if he's your favorite character, you maybe disappointed.Oda Nobunaga with Nodachi is definitely the most powerful character in the entire game. Kuroda Kanbei and Akechi Mitsuhide are also incredibly destructive and lethal.Yamanaka Shikanosuke <RIP> and hashiba hideyoshi are very fun to use, but they are so weak.  These guys along with Tokugawa Ieyasu and Sena have extremely fast attacks.Hattori hanzo is okay.  The rest of the characters are just alright, in my opinion. Its also cool that normal spear gives you additional attack moves while mounted on a horse. Horse musou is ridiculously overpowered. Its basically a mini tsunami, you can kill every living thing standing in your path with it.Citadel mode is too grindy. You spend foever just to upgrade one facility to the maximum level. It needs to be fixed.I like the skill progression system. Every character has a skill tree. In this game you need to upgrade your characters weapon proficiency  level if you want them to be able to use better weapons.There are hypothetical stages that allow you to play various "what if" scenarios. Extra hostorical stages can also be unlocked. These are  stages that dont directly involve either Nobunaga or Mitsuhide, like the Battle of Mikatagahara for example. Overall its a great game. Its very good. I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: First lemme clarify Ive been following this series since birth and have played every numbered title and most spinoffs. That being said I will say this has to be my favorite numbered entry yet. Emphasis on numbered cause Spirit of Sanada remains the best Samurai Warriors experience out there. But let me focus on what makes SW5 the best mainline entry so far for me.Story has taken a few notes from Spirit of Sanada and focuses alot on characters rather than just events. Problem is direction isnt always great and alot of characters can fall flat. Exremely obvious is the care the duo Nobunaga and Mitsuhide enjoy, with their story arcs and voice directions being pretty spot on. Overall I enjoyed the drama and the few historical tweaks Koei made to make it more compelling and dramatic were pretty neat. Both characters were kinda immortalized, Nobunaga the Fool who would become a demon and Mitsuhide the forever hesitant follower.Gameplay wise this is a step up from 4 with Hyper attacks still maintaining their form and movesets being mostly overhauled and sadly cloned. On the upside this has made every moveset fun to use and very versatile so Id say it was worth the sacrifice. No longer will you have characters with weird movesets sitting in the sidelines because their moveset is trash. That along with citadel mode and a mostly well thought out musou mode makes the breadth of the experience and it works pefectly. The loop /play musou stage/unlock characters/level up in characters in citadel mode and watch bonding cutscenes/ was addicting and gave options to cool off from the main plot.A downside is this is the first entry in years not to feature the rest of the story. For those knowledgable this game spans all the way from Nobunagas first campaigns in Mino all the way to the battle of Yamazaki, in painsticking detail. So Mitsunari fanboys I feel you, Im in pain too. Heres hoping this is a stepping stone and successful formula to hopefully see a Samurai Warriors 5-II one day.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as reboots go, this is a good one. A smaller cast and less weapons, more it feels like it has more substance than prior games.The redesigns of the characters also made it that I can't really 'dislike' any character's design. Compared to older titles where I definitely had a few I didn't enjoy playing purely by design.There's not much incentive in terms of replayability once you've gone through the story, but it's a musou game. And the combat is definitely the good bit. The new active skills, passive skills and combat system is very much to my liking and hopefully something they'll refine in future titles.Sadly, a few systems feel like an after thought and detract from the whole.Rather than crafting a sword, for example, you can reforge a bow into a sword, keeping its slotted upgrades.This seems needed as the majority of weapon drops is just fodder for disassembly. Nothing says "junk" like a melee weapon giving ranged bonusses.You can also buy weapons with empty slots from a vendor, but good luck finding one with more than 3 or 4 slots.The citadel mode may be fun for 2 players, but playing it solo is a drag.Your AI-teammate has as much worth as a sack of potatoes that can take a beating, but is otherwise not much use.I'd still recommend this game, but at a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay in general is decent, but just doesnt seem to really be a big improvement over SW4. The "brush" art style I think is very cool.My primary complaint about recent warriors games is the huge amount of distracting 'objectives', combined with a requirement to complete maps in under a certain time, with a certain combo/kill/whatever count. It makes every map seem frantic when it doesnt need to be. Now if this was just for completionist sake I wouldn't care, but additional post campaign maps are locked behind S ranking storyline maps.As other people have commented, i'm not a huge fan of movesets being tied to weapons, which means there are 15 movesets. Why would you play as Nobunagas bland younger brother who uses the same weapon as him? Especially since you are forced to use Nobunaga through much of the storyline so he is going to be WAY more powerful. Now I haven't maxed out nobuyukis level & weapon mastery so maybe he gets some cool unique attack, but I somehow doubt it. The same goes for many of the other characters who share weapons. _childDocuments_.review: An all around amazing game and a fantastic reboot of the series! I will provide details of the pros and cons below. Please note that my perspective is that of a veteran of the Samurai Warriors Franchise, having followed it from the first entry (I only buy the regular games though, no XL or Empires for me).Pros:- Reboot: Yeah, the very fact that it's a reboot is a pro in my book. I know others might view it as a con, due to the cutting of the roster, but to me, there are less characters, but those characters that remain are much more fleshed out. Moreover, the story mode is greatly improved due to this. Almost all characters have an established role or persona, instead of just having a couple of one-liners and a very caricatural one-dimensional personality.- Aesthetics: Now I know this is more of a subjective thing, but I find that the aesthetics are really amazing this time around - combining both some manga aspects to the artwork, but more importantly, a lot more emphasis on traditional japanese armors and weaponry! No longer do you have characters looking like Knights or some weird fantasy thing - in this game, it's all very "authenticly japanese" but they still manage to make it look diverse and interesting enough! Oh and yeah, the colors are much more visibly cool with this visual style.- Gameplay: The bread and butter of the series! Good ol Hack'n'Slash! It's essentially an improvement over Samurai Warriors 4, in the sense that the Hyper Attacks in this game are not Overpowered. The rest of the button-mashing remains the same, but there's a new thing that they added that adds more power and variety to your characters, and those are Skills. Skills are basically a cooldown based ability that will unleash a special attack or effect. If you are familiar with MMOs or some RPG games, then this is basically an ability that is subjected to cooldown - so yeah, add that to the regular hack'n'slash that we all know and love, and you have a recipe for some real serious firepower to deliver large amounts of whoop'ass.- Story: The story, while nothing extraordinary and relatively simple enough - the storytelling is what makes it great! What I mean by that is, although the story in itself is rather straightforward, the journey that you take to get through it is well done! You got two paths: Nobunaga's and Mitsuhide's, with a lot of overlap between the two, but also enough differences that justify the separation.As mentioned above, there's also more character development all across the board.Cons:- No English/Your Language Sub: I know, a lot of people prefer japanese VO. I like it too! However, there's so much going on during the game, and even outside of it, that, to me, a well done translation can really do wonders for the game. For example, when I'm busy fighting soldiers, I don't want to have to read everything just to get a grip of the story and what's going on in the game, if I speak the language, I can simply listen to things like "That garrison looks suspicious, we better investigate the area" or even when a character conveys emotions, simply reading the text is not the same as you savoring the emotions they're going through with a line in a language you understand.- Citadel Mode is bad: So, Citadel Mode is like a super short battle, which works the same way for every stage (with just very minor differences each). It's really not that good. I think even if you just want to beat some soldiers up without caring for story, you are better off going into Free Mode rather than this. The only thing that I like, that I actually would have liked in the Free Mode/Story Mode are the ability to summon different kinds of troops! They're not super strong or anything, but deploying them to your side makes you feel like a real commander!- Co-op Mode Online is restrictive: So I haven't experienced this myself, but a couple of people have noted that you have to have already completed the stage in order to play it with your friend - which means that, you basically cannot progress through the story for the first time with a friend. This is kind of a baffling decision to me, since, the whole point of going through the story mode via coop is to enjoy it together, not to simply "relive it" after having already done it yourself. So that's a DEFINITE downside and a rather disappointing one, if you were looking to play with someone online.Overall:In conclusion, this game is a huge upgrade from the previous installments and is a very successful reboot! I cannot speak for people coming into the series, as I've experienced it as a veteran - but if you're a Samurai Warriors or are familiar with any other Warriors title, then this is definitely a game that you shouldn't miss! As it is, it's definitely worth it, as not only the story, but the gameplay itself is very entertaining, which means that you aren't going to get tired of it anytime soon!I hope that the future of this game (DLC or expansions) go in good directions - as I've never been too fond of how they do them in the past honestly (just my personal take, but having played the OG games, I was never compelled enough by the XLs and Empires to ever buy them - I know some people like them! That's why they keep getting made lol).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lavish beat-em-up game, a really down-to-earth and solid entry into a pretty well-refined formula. For me, this is my first Samurai Warriors game, I got into Musou titles through Hyrule Warriors, but this is quickly becoming maybe my second favorite behind Hyrule -- the character designs are LAVISH, the level of artistry and detail put into each playable character and even a lot of the generic NPCs is really impressive to see. This game bursts with energy and visually just looks stellar -- the environments are pretty simple, but they get boosted by some cool details, lighting effects and small pieces of flair that make them enjoyable in the ten seconds or so you'll ever spend paying them the least mind. This game isn't about paying attention to its skyboxes, it's about murdering hundreds of men.In this regard, the one thing I will say against this game is that the enemies seem a bit meatier than usual. Hyrule Warriors it's pretty easy to rack up 2000 kills per fight, but here you're going to be hitting guys a lot, building up combos a lot...it does make battles drag out if you end up bringing in an underleveled character, adn since you have to complete battles to get exp to level up your underlevelled characters, you're going to be pushed to do some degree of grinding, even if you do regular trips into the Citadel Mode.Still, if you have never tried a "Warriors" game and if you like Japanese history (or history in general) this game is worth your time and money. There's a load of love put into it, a lot of attention to detail, it's bursting with content -- I haven't even beaten the game yet, I'm maybe 2/3s through one of the main storylines, so believe me, you'll be getting a lot for your money with this one.

Definitely recommend for musou fan's and new comers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Small note before you read. These are pros and cons YOU might be looking to know about and are not exactly my opinions.Pros:-The game uses a mix SW4 gameplay with some parts from DW8 and 9. Here me out here, yes 9 was bad but let me explain.--AOE circles when enemies use abilities similar to one of the later updates 9 had for archers telegraphing attacks.--Ultimate Skills are a light mix of DW8's Man/Heaven/Earth (RPS) + ideas from 9's State Combo system except the main focus is on enemy units. A specific attack might be designed for taking out shielded enemies.-Generic officers have a wider variety of weapons this time around. They will even use abilities.-Certain NPCs are playable in Free Mode with generic movesets. You'll unlock that person when they exit the Story Mode.-Anyone can equip any weapon, but weapons are level locked to that characters proficiency.-Mouse + Keyboard support-Citadel mode which is a score mode similar to ambition mode from 8.--In Citadel mode you can assign yourself 3 different units (Like archers, cannons, warrior monks, etc) to summon near you.Neutrals:-This game is a soft reboot. To have the most fun, your expectations should be based on the fact it is a reboot and not that it is "5". Obviously I can't force that on you, it's a recommendation. -While the music is great, a lot of it is music remixed mostly from 4 in the new style.-Boss enemies can have an extra health bar and go into a rage mode when the first is taken out.-A lot of characters have new personalities.--Some characters have new VAs. Some characters retain their VA but fit it to their new design/personality.Cons:-Roster has been cut. The game focuses on characters related to Nobunaga & Akechi. Your waifu/husbando is probably gone.-Most characters are cloned and use the same weapons. Their musou and unique attacks will differ.--Most characters have new weapons. Hisahide for example has a cannon instead of his sickle.--Playable generic characters share generic musous between each other.--Some weapon's movesets feel stale.-NO ENGLISH DUB.Notes:-Akechi campign is a small slog at the start since it reuses a lot of Nobunaga's maps and objectives and starts later. Akechi is generally overleveled at that point.-Citadel mode is basically like a base defense with objectives.-Sometimes you will do a stage with JUST Nobunaga  (or Akechi based on whose story you are playing). Sometimes a second character becomes playable in the middle of the stage. Sometimes not.-Anyone that isn't those two gets more EXP to make up for the fact you play as both the entire game.This is a fantastic Warriors game, maybe one of the better ones I have ever played. I love mindless hack and slash games.

_childDocuments_.review:
Experience exhilarating action set in a dramatic historical setting in SAMURAI WARRIORS 5. As the latest numbered entry in the SAMURAI WARRIORS franchise, the story, characters, and visuals have been re-imagined to set the stage for a thrilling new series. The story takes place after the Ōnin War during the golden age of the Sengoku period, and features a story that centers on the lives of two of the most representative military commanders of this era: Nobunaga Oda and Mitsuhide Akechi. Choose from a number of new and returning characters while utilizing new abilities to take on evolving enemy forces. Experience electrifying Musou action like never before in SAMURAI WARRIORS 5.
                               

・Experience an intense historical drama set during Japan's Sengoku period, told from the perspective of this era's foremost military commanders: Nobunaga Oda and Mitsuhide Akechi.

・Both returning heroes and brand new characters have received re-imagined designs in order to showcase the captivating world of the Sengoku period.

・Enjoy exhilarating strategic action on an evolved battlefield.

・Enemy forces continue to evolve as time passes in the story, making full use of a number of different military tactics to take on the player.

name: Loretta
detailed_description: Loretta is a psychological thriller that makes the player an accessory to the heroine’s crimes, leading her through a self-crafted nightmare. Loretta’s story revolves around a woman handling betrayal, her husband’s infidelity, and reclaiming her agency during the socially tumultuous 1940s. Choose dialogue, interact with objects and decide the depths to which Loretta's depravity spirals while navigating a nightmare of her own creation. Story Loretta is a housewife. Her husband Walter is a writer. Dragged from the glitz and glamour of New York City and thrust into a dilapidated farmhouse in the rural south, both are unsuccessful, struggling with their finances and their relationship. But when Loretta learns of her husband’s infidelity and a remarkably lucrative life insurance policy filed in his name, a grisly plan begins to take root. It is up to the player to decide how far she will follow it. Features Decide whether Loretta's story remains a web of deceit or crescendos into bloody murder through dialogue and discovery. Conceptually inspired by film noir, the art of Andrew Wyeth and Edward Hopper, as well as the works of Alfred Hitchcock, Philip Ridley, Stephen King and Vladimir Nabokov. Solve cryptic puzzles to dive deeper into Loretta's imperfect past and discover the levels of desperation she feels to reclaim control of her life. Whose side will you take in this story without heroes? Branching paths and multiple endings allow for a custom experience or opportunity for replay. Choose Loretta’s fate and explore the multiple opportunities as they present themselves to her.

_childDocuments_.review:
The year is 1947. Lora and Walter Harris move to a farm, which used to belong to his parents. Walter is a writer and Lora is a housewife. Both are quite unsuccessful.

The family is going through financial difficulties. The situation is also complicated by the fact that Walter owes money to people from New York. And although the husband keeps it a secret from his wife, Lora has a suspicion. Moreover, she suspects him of cheating.

As she struggles to make loan payments, she finds out that Walter's publishing house has insured his life. In the event of his death, the insurance sum would be 30.000$. A plan is born in Lora's mind.

Loretta is a story-driven adventure game in which gameplay focuses on choosing phrases in dialogue, interacting with objects, and making decisions: planning the murder and getting rid of the evidence. Killing a husband, trying to cover a crime, Loretta makes a player an accomplice.
_childDocuments_.name: Loretta

name: Terra Nil
detailed_description: Terra Nil: Vita Nova Update Vita Nova expands on Terra Nil’s deeply satisfying nature restoration with new missions, buildings, an updated wildlife system, and a brand new world map—which is now fully 3D and can be freely rotated—giving you a more accurate and personalized overview of your efforts to bring life back to this dead world. New levels include Polluted Bay, a barren landscape carved in half by a badly polluted river, and Scorched Caldera, a vast volcanic crater that you must transform into a life-filled freshwater lake. These, and all the new maps in the Vita Nova update, will put your reclamation skills to the test in interesting and unusual ways. A completely overhauled wildlife system makes Terra Nil’s transformed landscapes more alive than ever. Animals emerge more naturally and have a deeper set of needs you need to fulfill if you want to keep them happy and abundant. This adds a new dimension of strategy to the game and gives you more animals to admire—including a brand new species, the jaguar—as nature is steadily restored. About the Game Terra Nil is a game about transforming a barren, lifeless landscape into a thriving, vibrant ecosystem. Turn dead soil into fertile grassland, clean polluted oceans, plant sprawling forests, and create the ideal habitat for animals to call home. Then recycle your buildings and leave no trace that you were there. Reclaim the wasteland. A reverse city builder Use advanced eco-technology to purify the soil, creating plains, wetlands, beaches, rainforests, wildflowers, and more—then efficiently recycle everything you've built, leaving the environment pristine for its new animal inhabitants. Different maps every time Procedurally generated landscapes mean no two playthroughs of Terra Nil will ever be the same. Plan your build around randomized, challenging, and unpredictable terrain, including snaking rivers, mountains, lowlands, and oceans. A natural ebb and flow Each region of Terra Nil progresses through phases, with the ultimate goal being leaving pristine wilderness behind. Levels are not about infinite growth, but rather balancing and nurturing the environment before leaving it in peace. Experience tranquility Lush hand-painted environments, relaxing music, and an atmospheric ambient soundscape make Terra Nil a peaceful, meditative experience. When you're done, use Appreciate mode to bask in the natural beauty of the ecosystem you have restored.

short_description: Terra Nil is an intricate environmental strategy game about transforming a barren wasteland into a thriving, balanced ecosystem. Bring life back to a lifeless world by purifying soil, cleaning oceans, planting trees, and reintroducing wildlife, then leave without a trace.

_childDocuments_.review: The idea behind this game is different than other 'city builder' or management games and that was my appeal to wanting to try out the game.After the basic environmental conditions are met, you have to incorporate separate ecosystems in the same area and then make all the animals happy with where they are. Then after that is done, you have to recycle all the hardware so the animals can live peacefully. Sounds like a lot and some of the maps, I took my time on. Some maps, I ended up having to redo 1-2 times because I didn't plan correctly ahead.One thing is for certain - ALWAYS build the animal relocator building and pay close attention to what makes them happy. You can move an animal as many times as you want but you can't move them within certain amount of space from the same animals, it seems. Basically, different packs of the same animals don't seem to mix in that well together.Also, the music is amazing in the game, very peaceful and destressing.Only issues with the game are:1) I wish you could rotate the map.2) Larger hardware in the way of smaller things (like the monorail pillars) are not selectable because the larger item overlaps it.3) When things like  the sound is choppy Overall, I really loved this game and would recommend it (actually already have) to people.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one I have a strange opinion on. I really really enjoyed it. The graphics are absolutely beautiful, the game is engaging and interesting and it's really satisfying bringing worlds back to life in the way you do in this game, but it just feels like something is missing. For a game that's over £20 there was only 8 levels, 4 of which are alternate versions of the original 4, so I was just left really wishing there was more content for the game.It's an amazing idea, and it's been amazingly executed too but I just think the idea could have been taken so much further, it hasn't reached it's full potential.I recommend playing this game because it's amazing but wow do I just wish there was more of it. Maybe another planet or two to save after you save the first one would work really well in a future update.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is a very clever puzzle game in which you need to bring back nature from desolated environments. In order to do that, you have different machines/buildings that will interact with parts of the ecosystem (change temperature, clean the soil, get energy...). Each map has 4 different phases: 1. You need to clean the pollution and bring nature back2. You restore the different plants and ecosystems3. With point 2 done, it is time to get the animals back where they belong4. Finally, with everything done, you need to clean up your mess and remove all your buildings in a clean way before leaving.All this is done within a very nice chill mood. Graphics are good (even if I miss the old pixelated ones from the first demo) and the music makes a lot for the ambient. It is the kind of game for you to relax after a long day or just to spend a few hours in something very good. At the time of this review, I have completed 100% of all the areas in the standard difficulty, but I can see myself doing it all again in max difficulty or even play a map from time to time (they are randomized within the selected ecosystem so that helps replayability).
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is a ecological restoration game where you are tasked with helping animals and wildlife move into the land. When you begin, you will get a guide to show you what work needs to be done in that area. Every level you go through three phases:                    - Restoring the land                  - Increasing diversity of plants and bushes. Animals will potentially move in at this point,                    - Collecting all your technology before leaving the site. it is a very relaxing and slow game, so it is not the type to be rushed. There is a challenging achievement where ALL groups of animals need to be satisfied in one area, so really it is about patient and balancing what you add to the land. Also very educational about nature and wildlife. I throughly enjoyed as a someone who really connects to animals and nature.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I really do like this game. I find it genuinely fun and relaxing. I'm taking it slow and playing a little at a time and I find it so relaxing playing the first game mode and then will go back to try the other 2, just find it nice to played the demo a lot and I love the changes to things from it and the added elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun game. For people that want their time respected, there's a lot of options to play it your way and for the price tag, I don't think 7 hours is too little for what you get out of it. People will spend more on delivery fees alone with one door dash meal but will blink with this value? Seems a little odd.But it's pretty, relaxing, and like that it's not feeling like anything is dragged out just to pad the time to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a beautiful and relaxing strategy game / "anti-city-builder" game. A decent amount of complexity yet not overwhelming. Solarpunk vibes. Cute graphics. Beautiful melodies.Like, at the end of restoring a region on a planet you actually have to recycle all of the buildings you used to build yourself a spaceship and get out, leaving basically no trace you were ever there in the first place. How cute is that!?I loved the concepts here.brb, going to hug a tree
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: extremely bad, do not buy for any reason, massive waste of time and money, very pretty art.the game is worse than the "grow" series of flash games made like 10 years ago that are available for free. this game lures you in and then stabs you with brutally unforgiving difficulty even on the easiest difficulty.avoid this game like the plague. 0/10, these devs have literally no idea how to make a good game in this genre they should do something else with their lives.there are 4x strategy games on the hardest difficulty that are easier and more forgiving than this. this game is massively frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful concept, poorly put together.I loved the part where you get to reclaim a world, but the game is incredible short. The "recycling" and "finding animals" is made like tedious puzzle elements. They were not fun. The seed collection felt like a joke, just spamming buttons and then the game was over.This game would have done much better as an endless map expanding as you complete your current area.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A fun puzzle game where you frequently find yourself forced to make up for your previous bad choices, which is a pretty good distillation of the whole 'ruining the planet' problem as a whole. Resets are easy, though, so it's not masochistic in driving the point home. The game has nearly quadrupled in size since my initial purchase near release, which speaks well of the defvs.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting and fun to play puzzle/strategy game with the aims of juggling machines to rejuvenate the planet. Not a very long game but has replay value.The animals can be spotted if you follow the prompts and recreate the environment it will spawn in. I think the game has followed reality quite well. All in all highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing, no stress puzzle builder where the idea is to turn a wasteland into a thriving wilderness. Once you revive the land, collect your buildings, and finish the level, take some time to just watch the beautiful land live its life. Each level is random and can be replayed over and over with different layouts, so no worries about leaving something half done.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing puzzle game with a good graphical representation and immersion through sound and visuals.However, the gameplay leaves somewhat to be desired. It's too limited in scope when it comes to "terraforming" and the subsequent phases of setting animal life and the cleanup.The basics are here, but it needs quite a bit more expansion on all areas of gameplay to make this really compelling, I can't recommend it for now.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the "main" Terra Nil mission (so, not 100%, but  ) in normal difficulty.I loved the moment of reaching the ecological tipping point and seeing nature be restored. The game combines puzzle and resource management without becoming overtly complex. Some of the levels require certain knowledge that is only revealed after the fact, but given that the levels are somewhat short, it doesn't become a whole thing (although it did bother me a little). It is very satisfying to bring life back to the locations, and I would've loved more . Something that makes you think more of the risk/reward , or that shakes things up.My only complaint is that recycling by monorail was a bit tedious. Recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very relaxing game.  The concept of the anti city builder is strong, and amazing.  The better you do, the better the map looks.  There is a strong puzzle aspect as well, as you need to figure out how to best restore your environment to find all the animals, and get the perfect balance between the micro biomes.  Love it, can't wait to see what else they have planned for this game.  Seriously, you like city builders, give it a go! It's worth it. And it deserve being one of the more innovative titles of the year!  Just saying.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I've played likely 40+ hours of the prototype of Terra Nil and while I miss the beautiful pixel style of that version, Terra Nil's full release captures everything else I love about that original. As a puzzle game it's fun to optimize your point return per building while minimizing your ecological impact and ensure you have an ecosystem to support every species, but the soundtrack and zen mode will keep Terra Nil in my chill list.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A nice, light 'builder' game. You should know going in that it's not deep on tactics, and while it can be somewhat fun to just go zen-mode it's also not quite a landscape painting game either. But that said, the winning premise of being an 'unbuilding' game alone, along with pretty good execution goes a long way in my book, enough to make this a recommend, especially if it's on sale.EDIT: almost forgot. if you do like the premise, but are looking for a grander scale/somewhat more involved strategy, I'd highly recommend giving Plan B: Terraform a look. It may not be your cup of tea if you don't like factory-like games, but it's one of my little faves. A wonderful game from a 1 man developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is an absolute delight! It can be as laid back as you want it to be. Requires some critical thinking skills, as well as the ability to plan ahead. i.e.: if I terraform like this, will I have enough space for the jungle in the next stage?Highly recommend it if you enjoy casual simulation games!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game, having completed on the easiest mode I am halfway through the second difficulty. I can easily play this for hours and cant wait to see the game expand. More maps would be amazing and new animals to find would be fun too. Even more difficulty ratings would be fun, but as i've only done the first two, I may change that if I struggle on the harder levels hahaFiguring out how to do things on the more complex levels was hard at first but now i've got the hang of things its great. 20 hours over one weekend says it all really
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I have been looking forward to this game since I played the first free concept demo years ago, and boy, was the wait worth it. It's just as relaxing, detailed and lovingly made as I remember it and hoped it would be. Personally it's a bit of a pity that they dropped the pixel style, but that's just personal taste. The core concept itself is definitely unchanged.The only thing that I found slightly disappointing was the total playtime. As you can see, I'm at 100% after 6 hours, after not being in a particular rush. Personally it's still worth the 20€ for me, I got more entertainment out of it than I'd get out of 6 hours of cinema. Would I recommend it? Yes, if you love to just chill, enjoy watching stuff develop and have no pressure. But don't expect a 100 hour campaign mode to keep you busy for weeks. The one thing I would dearly wish for in this game: a replay-mode similar to Power Wash Simulator, allowing you to watch the desolate landscape turn lush and fertile in fast forward mode after you've completed the level. But that's just a small aside.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept, great game, but needs more levels and/or content. I know everyone wants more content from a game they enjoyed, but in this case I feel like completing all of the main scenarios was far too. I'm notorious for how slow I tend to take games, and I've got all of 14 hours on record from when I first started to when I 100% cleared the scenarios. Even if adding more mechanics was out of the question, adding more of the alternate levels that exist for each level would have added much more to the game. They actually did a great job with the existing alternate levels, using the existing content rearranged to add new challenges, but I feel the game needed more levels.Still, highly recommend this game. Great visual style, great mechanics, and lots of potential if the devs decide to expand further on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't really a city builder, it's more like a puzzle game where you have to reach certain conditions to progress.It has a very satisfying loop, as you proceed through each "phase" and there's a great sense of satisfaction as you clean up this shabby world you find yourself in.It has a lot of replayability, looks & sounds lovely and is very chill. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A reverse city builder for those looking for a chilling experience.Pros:- Each map is generated before playing, so no two maps will be the same even if you go back to the same mission- Relatively easy, good for relaxation- Some maps require some forward thinking and knowledge about the tools you need- This game isnt just about growing grass but adjusting the climate and luring in fauna- 4 different continents with 2 alternate map styles for each- Devs are looking into expanding the game after a short breakCons:- Game is quite short but at least we got a promise of future expansion- As of writing this review, the continents' alternate mission gives you the same first instruction as the first map, which is inaccurate, since the same tools and environmental properties are not present. This means you are getting instructions you cannot follow. It is not gamebreaking but it might confuse some first-time players.Cannot think of anything else...My personal gameplay was bug-free and I experienced no issues with impossible missions due to unlucky map generation.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game a lot, as it has a very interesting and different type of vibe to it. Each different area has different strategies and different techniques that make each one of them unique. Overall the graphics are good, and some of the visuals between the notebook and the landscapes are quite nice on the eyes. My only issue with this game would have to be the shortness of it. Of course it has replay-ability, giving you the chance to go back and redo each area over and over again, re-imagining the overall layout of the area. But nowadays, if I finish a game in less than two days I am quite disappointed in the length. I would say catch this game at a solid $15 or less price point for it to be really worth it. I see the vision, but there isn't really that much to this game. But really the length is the only issue for me. Everything else is quite fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend, with hesitance. I love the premise and hope the game receives continuing support. Right now it's very easy to get softlocked and have to reset, either due to bugs or a second, more fundamental design issue.You learn what to do in 4 phases for each biome. Each phase unlocks new tools. The biggest issue I ran into was *really* wishing I had known the future objectives earlier. In most maps I played, I would feel like I was doing great, detoxifying land and regreening the earth. Then the next phase would unlock, and if I had known the next goals I'd have gone about things totally differently. I'd find myself boxed into a corner without the tools to adjust. Can't destroy my buildings, can't terraform, it's just stuck as I did it in the last phase and I can't advance. Reset, try again.Apparently this cycle of getting softlocked and resetting is just the normal gameplay loop for strategy games. I don't buy that. You should know your objectives before you go into the field. The rigidity of your toolkit I kept encountering really didn't match the otherwise relaxing vibe. I've played other simulation/builder games before and you can usually backtrack to a significant degree if you find out your approach was wrong, not just wipe the whole level and reset. The way you recycle buildings in this game is very awkward - you can undo exactly one step backward, and otherwise can't get rid of buildings at all until the final phase, except in some cases by intentionally starting a wildfire near buildings you want gone. This game does let you reset phases, but it's often the first phase that really determines whether the rest will go well. That's enough complaining. I do like this game and think it deserves attention. It's pretty. The sound effects are lovely. I've never played another game like it. Reintroducing flora and fauna to newly-healed landscapes is deeply satisfying. I give this positive review in acknowledgement that the devs have made something new and special here, and the hope that they'll keep improving it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: For the rather short amount of game time of 4 different maps and 4 variants, this game shouldn't cost 25 bucks. Yes the replayability is there through random gen, but it's not enough to justify the price. However I have high hopes for the game and the devs as the game is only a weekish old, there are so many more biomes out there that they can put into this game to stretch the game time out even further. Honestly I'd say wait for a bit more for them to polish the game and adding more contents (hopefully not through paid DLCs).
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very satisfying! Restoring life to a barren wasteland step by step is both, fun & challenging. I finished everything, including the (very cool & interesting) alternate maps in 10 hours, which makes me agree that I would have liked a bit more content. Coming up with new maps with new twists can't be that hard, so I hope for a (free) DLC or some user created content to bring a bit more depth to this little gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was an option for 'mixed' rather than just yes or no.  I really do like this game.  I find it genuinely fun and relaxing.  I love that it breaks away from the typical city-builder and lets you repair an ecosystem instead of exploiting it.  If this game was $5 or even $10 this would be a positive review.I can't recommend it at a price point of $25.  I beat it in 3 hours.  It seems to last just long enough to make it so you can't refund it via Steam and then it ends.  Definitely buy it when it goes on sale, but definitely wait until then.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Hesitantly recommending this game.My main problem is it's quite short and there isn't a huge amount of replayability. It took me about 6.5 hours to completely restore the whole world, after which there's just achievement hunting to do. Additionally, the UI can be a bit clunky and the game as a whole is a little buggy.Still, it's a relaxing and fun game, with some great sound and game design. Kinda reminds me of the Spore space stage terraforming, in that you've got to balance the heat and humidity, along with introducing different plants and animals to create a stable environment. That was my favourite part of that game, so this one definitely appeals too.Is it worth £20? Probably not, but get it on sale and you should have a fun 6-10 hours with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay loop of Terra Nil takes as its first assumption that no matter how wrecked, ruined, and polluted something is, it can with the right tools be restored to thriving.  Strategic caretaking and restoration is what this game is about.  I wish it were bigger, I wish it were deeper, I wish it was less buggy, and I wish it was well-marketed enough that a generation of gamers all had to contend with its assertions.  But I am very glad the game exists, and I will be waiting for the next one like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A fascinating gameplay concept that has a potential to create a lot of different puzzle situations interesting to figure out, but sadly the game lacks for content and does no job of explaining its fundamental mechanics to the player at all. I am a big fan of games that await wit from the player and reward him for his clever solutions and unique findings (), however even these games must be designed in a way that promotes such way of thinking by hinting this kind of gameplay by different means. Even for me this process in Terra Nil was frustrating as I've spent almost 80% of total playtime just to find out things in this game which cannot be found by just thinking about possible solutions, which basically is the same problem of explaining the toolkit, so the only viable strategy that you can come up with is just to spam everything you have, if the displayed number is colored green... most of the time, at least. Unfortunately, the game has not only poor metagame, but also poor puzzle design: whenever you stuck in Terra Nil, you'll run out of possible parallel tasks very fast, so you'll be just looking at your screen and begging for help. The game does not give you any hints when they are trully needed and leave you alone fighting with uncertainty. This destroys all the joy of solving puzzles
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game as a demo on Itch io. It was just a cute little pixle game back then, then I played the demo. I was pleased to get the full release and pleasantly surprised by the added mechanics.Its easy enough to complete and honestly best for a little bit of cosy gaming. I did encounter a couple of weird placement bugs, where I was able to place things I shouldn't and then wasn't able to dismantle them, but nothing a reload couldn't fix.I hope future updates of this game, add more biomes and worlds.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with an interesting idea. The visuals are nice, really enjoyed transforming the wasteland back to a livable state. It was very relaxing. The puzzles are good. Once you solve everything, seeing the vegetation coming to live and the animals enjoying themselves was worth it. Wish they had this for the ocean in real life as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hard in a not-so-fun way.  That might have been more palatable to me (or I might have taken more time to learn it and found it less hard with more playtime), but I ran into a game-breaking bug: the handbook they tell you to consult when you get stuck doesn't load correctly for me, and none of the fixes I tried (including a complete reinstall) could make it appear.  I could see page-flipping animations, but not read the pages.  I took it as a sign and asked for a refund.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game is short and sweet. Very satisfying and relaxing.It's not a hardcore city/nature builder if that's what you're looking for. I don't agree with some of the negative reviews about the game progression, I think the game wants you to experience the different challenges that would come up from trying to restore our planet.I appreciate every little detail in the mechanics that make you reflect, like how you can recycle all your building except anything controlling radiation in the end.It's really satisfying to tweak the weather and slowly get each continent "back on its feet" when you don't have to decontaminate anymore and just let rain and nature take it from there.

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing game with a gameplay loop, which once figured out is repeatable with a few variations thrown in per level. I've been watching this game for a while, but I'm glad/lucked out that I waited until the major Vita Nova update. I can definitely see why the reviews that came in before this update labeled it as feeling incomplete. The game, even though enjoyable, still needs some polish. For example, it doesn't keep my 4k resolution choice once I shut the game down and level objectives do not get updated in the handbook when the handbook is shown at each phase completion notice during a level (you have to manually open the handbook to see if you've completed them or not). Two final things of note, the levels do not have more passive resource generators like other games - if you run out you have to restart the level. You do gain resources based on your actions, but it's not like you can just wait for workers to mine more ore or cut more trees etc. There also isn't a straight forward way to delete buildings you've created (you can go back one action as a built in function of the game and you can reset back to the last phase that you completed). There are some potential ways around this but they are not guaranteed methods. Both of these elements add a little more puzzle feel to the levels, but once you get used to it it just becomes part of figuring out each level and not a big deal.EDIT - end of game comment for the devs, might be a spoiler:>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>I still had a few levels to complete, but there is a certain level (bottom left on the continental land mass) which is technically the end of the game. I wish this was locked off until the others were completed or at least a warning in the title that it is the "last level". I can still go back and complete the levels that I didn't do yet, but sort of makes it anticlimactic now that I've seen the end.

_childDocuments_.review: A peaceful, uplifting atmosphere, wonderful aesthetics, yet strategically-demanding (unless you choose the more-forgiving Ecologist game mode and just wish to enjoy the greenery grow)., it's about performing the right sequence of turns in the correct order - prepare an area of the earth, cover it with grass, turn some of it into flora using a tree&beehive, and then start a controlled burn in that area (while making sure it's separated via cliffs, riverbeds, or wasteland) to finally sow trees in the ashes. You have limited resources that you gain by performing some of these actions, so plan your steps carefully - however, starting over with your new knowledge is encouraged, if needed. The game's strategy evolves gradually throughout the introductory tutorial, and then gets expanded upon over the three other main story levels. (There are four extra alternate levels, which I haven't gotten to yet). I won't spoil the other parts of the main gameplay, as I believe I had a better experience discovering them alone, at the pace the game presents them. are what really made the game for me though. Don't get me wrong, I'm a Factorio & Paradox player and I'll play by spreadsheets and find it fun, but the aesthetics of this game were a wonderful contrast to those games. This game celebrates ecology and presents it in a respectful and positive way that made it a joy for me to restore the wastelands to greenery. The music is reactive and enhances the peaceful atmosphere even more., this game was a relaxing departure from the usual subset of games I play. , I only spent an afternoon and evening doing the main story (I did all levels first try, though one time I came very close to running out of resources), . It's why I'm writing this review, I loved the atmosphere and design, and I want to support the game.

_childDocuments_.review: [x] core gameplay loop is fairly straightforward - terraform stuff, put green stuff on it, put green stuff on the green stuff and repeat[x] scenarios only last an hour at most if you're struggling----------[x] whole game is over in 10 hours[]  game over in 10 hours - wait for a sale[] it gets much more puzzley with the b-sides, with nerd loops to farm money----------straightforward ecology puzzle game.  largely chill so you can take scenarios at your own pace.  there are extra region rewards for developing your map in a certain way, like the snow maps encouraging boosting temperature before dropping it later.
