_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxing. feel-good resource management/building game. Very nice structure to the gameplay which gets more complex on the alternative maps. It is a bit short, I 100% completed the game's 8 levels in 10 hours, so expect roughly an hour and a bit per level. There's a few extra achievements that add a little bit of replay value and the maps are randomly generated too. There's a nice in-game art book that showcases the various species, biomes, and buildings but this could do with more text! The science behind the ecological restoration feels very fantastical, I wish they included some more detailed descriptions rather than just an idealised "this machines cleans soil" and "this building makes beaches". The diagrams in the book are very minimalist and pretty but also ridiculously vague, I only recognised what a few of them were trying to convey.tl;dr - cute and relaxing, if short, strategy game that has great ideals but lacks depth and explanation.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Well, waited quite a while for this game and in principle it is now just what it was in the preview version, only it is 4(+4) levels now.There is not a lot of content in this puzzle game (that's what it is) for 25Euros tbh, I do hope there will be more maps or an editor coming.I do like it even though I am not sure about the replayability. If you compare it to a simple game like Tetris, then Tetris had at least some high score to beat and benchmark yourself against. This one is just over and all you can thrive for is 100% in all levels.Then again, it let's you drift off into some satisfying and relaxing hours of a smooth game.If there is not more coming and keeping the relatively high price in mind, my thumb is down.If they add some stuff to improve longterm motivation, my thumb is up.Will keep it up for now and see where it will end.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to have to agree with a lot of people here. It's just not worth the price.Do I like this game? Yes. I think the game is really fun. The mechanics are neat (though not groundbreaking). It has a very satisfying feel as you fill out the map and then tinker with it to get all the animals.Graphics? They are decent but are pretty enough to get the job done.Replay-ability? None basically. I can't imagine the game has much to do a second time.Length? This is the killer. Basically 4 levels with 4 variants of those same levels. Then  you're done. I estimate by the time I 100% this game, maybe 6-8 hours depending on how fast you are? Not worth $24.99. If you can pick it up on sale for about $10.00 or they add more content then its a fun, neat little game. But don't waste your money right now if you're concerned about bang for your buck.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil is a very original and well done game. About 10-20 hours of gameplay, a little more probably with the new free Vita Nova update (I've not had time to try it, but I'll). There's some small bugs in scenario sometime, but still, it's an amazing experience. The visual are great, the music is relaxing and the game is interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: It's very pleasurable to see these lifeless environments gradually turn into little edens, the recycling stage is a brilliant idea from the devs which feels highly rewarding. Music is spot on. The second round of levels provide more challenging puzzle which will require you to efficiently manage ressources. Highly recommended to citybuilder noobs (which I am) looking for a fun and relaxing experience. Hoping to see a DLC coming out with more environments and mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: For the short time that it lasts, Terra Nil is a fun, addictive and relaxing city-sim. It’s a little hard to recommend at its current price of $37 AUD (on Steam) but is certainly worth checking out whenever it goes on sale. The breadth of content brings the overall experience down quite a bit, as once you’ve given the four biomes a go there isn’t a whole lot left to do. That said, if you like the sound of creating beautiful environments, without having to use your brain too much, then you’re likely to have fun with Terra Nil.Full review here:
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Terra Nil picked an unusual yet attractive angle to environment / terraforming, in reviving life in waste land. The game play mechanism is not hard to understand yet with sufficient depth to think about. It's game length is relatively short (I'm confident people can fully revive the planet and get game refunded), however not rushed. Perfect for passing afternoon time, with tea. However the game price is a over tagged IMO, a 20% to 40% discount will make player feel their money better spent than current price. Game play is indeed short, with passable re-playability, further regions would be very welcome.I shall note this still, preserving the eco-system is much easier and cheaper that rebuilding it after total devastation. It is not yet too late.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A great way to relax and make beautiful things. You can play this as an optimisation game if you want to, or you can just make the prettiest biome you can think of, it's all there. And when you're done, there's an Appreciate button that just lets you enjoy what you made without having to poke your computer, it's great! Oh, and I recommend checking out the artwork on every page of your restoration book (TAB), it's gorgeous.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this when it was just a demo; now that its live, i feel like its only improved and offered and even wider range of options and scenarios to mess around with. It has been very fun playing this game and I am looking forward to the many hours I will dump into this when I am looking to just sit back, have a drink, and relax while rebuilding a planet to sustain life once more.Truly a beautiful and relaxing experience that is hard to find these days. Definitely a game worth the sticker price.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute, fun and uplifting game. It's a strategy and puzzle game, with a little bit of resource management and forward planning a few moves ahead when you are working to bring life to a desolate wasteland.Each map is randomly generated and has challenges to overcome with each region offering a variety of goals and milestones.I think some people expected this game to be a city builder, or a simulator with long term construction and expansion. This is really a puzzle game, that presents you a scenario and asks you to figure out the best way to beautify a barren landscape.Terra Nil is great at what it goes, an endearing puzzle game with a fantastic premise and beautiful presentation and musical score, that makes for a relaxing and optimistic way to unwind after a hard day.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone who's feeling a little lost and hopeless, and for some reason you also just finished reading Braiding Sweetgrass, this one is for you. Excellent variety of difficulty (can be super casual or actually play the darn thing), great minimal piano soundtrack, and makes you feel like you can be part of ecosystem revitalization. Humans aren't just a cancer on the planet; we can also be good stewards for other lifeforms.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I have been desperate for a game with this concept for like a decade. Finally genuine relief from the extraction/combat model that 99.9% of other sim and god games use. Brilliant. I wish there were more detailed mechanisms for some things--like having fungi interact with plants, incorporating the right species, etc., but it's still wonderful. So gratifying and makes you smile. A few glitches--can't see the book/guide and idk why it's vertical format, which doesn't utilize my screen well, but frankly in return for finally getting a real restoration game I don't care.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This game quickly becomes unplayable because it will not save progress (common problem people post about online, also happened to me). In my version it crashed on the profile page every time it was opened--even after deleting all profiles, still showed as 38% progress on each. Uninstalling and reinstalling did nothing to help, and tech support never got back to me.Amazing concept. I hope someone either makes this game playable or makes one with fewer bugs and a similar concept.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Really disappointing. The whole campaign feels like a tutorial, and I was really expecting to go to another planet after done with missions. No such luck! The whole game is 8 missions, in 4 different biomes, takes around 10h to finish. Not a very good value for 20GBP.The game also feels rather shallow, there's very few interactions or complexities. First 2 phases of cleanup and terraforming are quire fun, and so is finding habitat for animals. Cleaning up the buildings however is not challenging, or difficult, it's just a terrible chore, especially in missions where you have to do it by river. Very annoying game design, that no fun part was easily 2h of the whole campaing time.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Good relaxing game about rebuilding an ecosystem. There are some open questions, but the spirit is good here. The game can lead to frustration, but fear not, if you try to revert/exit, you can just revert the Last chapter you were in, so you don't have to restart the whole thing.Played Beta, loved it. Played the first level again here, the same game from the time I got to the beta.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, for somebody who deeply cares for this earth and the environment, I play too many games about destroying it. That is why I love this game, it is a great game about restoring it. It not only balances the feeling of helping the earth no matter how much you get done, but also spices it up with many puzzles and enough challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I love everything about this game. i'm a huge fan of Terra-forming end Eco restoration games, the almost pixel art is beautiful and adorable, i love the addition of wildlife and the recycling system, i love the the fact that its also a puzzle game, especially on harder levels, you really have to consider things. My only complaint it that there's only 8 levels, I want MORE!!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: At its core this is a fresh wind and its just a very relaxing puzzle game with a cute artstyle. The idea of going from a wasteland to greens lush land has always drawn and I wish more games in this genre would be made and released.Also I applaud any developer for actually releasing a full game in this day and age.However, for the amount of current content and the time it takes to complete it, its release price of 25 Euro is way over the top. I can name multiple titles that will provide 10x the amount of time needed and have a ton of more content for the same price and a few even way that are cheaper.  The game does feel and look polished but again so do several other games in its price range.So I really, really hope more content will be made over time, until then please take note that the game is short so unless you don't mind spending that amount of money for 10+ hours max of gameplay. I would wait for the price to come down or on a sale.But since its a Full release, works and in general a fun game to play I will still recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: In this game, you place units to provide power, change the nature of soil then irrigate it. This part is boringly easy.Once a unit is placed, you cannot move it anymore. At most you can do one undo.I find this annoying.You have limitations about where you can place the units too and it's another little frustration because you can't reach everywhere.Then you need to cater for animals, except that most of your interaction with them will be to see them unhappy and you'll not be able to do anything for them. As stated above you can only add units.In the end I decided to ignore the critters and do my thing.Then, I'm being asked to pack everything and leave.  This is consistent in placing "trash cans" to gather your units, then send a boat to gather everything.I've spent about one hour in this game and I the amount of fun I had is way into in the negative.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a really nice game, but the game-breaking bugs have driven me absolutely crazy (ex. Maps that are unsolvable (due to randomness causing issues, and a bug on the last map that made it impossible to recycle everything). I also understand the idea behind the recycling at the end of each map, but it is NOT fun, and I wouldn't even consider it a challenge, it just just needless button clicking and it too has driving me crazy. It usually leaves me not wanting to play at the end of the map, since my sense of accomplishment was 20 minutes ago before i had to essentially build a rail network just to delete far away buildings. I DO NOT like that part of the game. The rest of it, however, extremely nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only saying "not recommended" due to the price--I got it on sale for $18, but I think $5-7 is a more reasonable price point. I've played for about 8 and a half hours and I feel like I've gotten all I need to out of the game. I also feel like it's simple enough of a game that it would be just as playable on a tablet.It's a fun puzzle game overall, and I do think it's worth playing. I like that once you get going, you have multiple ways to solve a problem--for example, do you waste resources melting the patches of snow you need to remove, or do you just raise the temperature and let it all melt for you? If you just raise temperatures, do you need the snow again to find some of the animals in the biome?It is pretty satisfying watching the empty wasteland come alive. The mechanics are explained very well, but you're not handheld into the objective. The overall balance is very good.There are 8 procedurally generated levels. I think I'd feel better about the price if there were about twice as many.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A very original, chill puzzle game that disguises itself as a "city builder" but really isn't, which I find is the reason for half the negative reviews here.It's NOT Cities Skyline or Sim City "in reverse". It's not "like other city-builders [you]'ve played before but not as good", because it's not the same genre. Don't expect hundreds of hours of infinite replayability. It's a puzzle game, about 10h long.That being said, If that's what you're looking for, I very much recommend it, the art style is gorgeous, the music chill and unintrusive, the gameplay varied - even though the cleanup phase can get a little tedious - and I greatly enjoyed the overall message of trying to "unfµck the world" then remove ourselves from it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game on a deal months ago, finally opened it today and don't know why i slept on this—it's so calming and satsifying, and after completing my first biome i can see there's quite a lot more game here left to enjoy. I picked the Gardener mode to start, but it also looks like there are more cmoplicated modes for people who are wanting mroe of a challenge. Recommend!!
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: It's highly alright. I've seen it compared to solitaire, the card game, which does feel accurate to some degree. The tags say "strategy", but in terms of gameplay it doesn't  that way, even if some of the usual challenges of working within a limited resource budget and route planning are there.I think part of that is the fact that it can take a playthrough or two of each biome to figure out what even needs to be done to "complete" it, as in, 100% of all optional objectives. As an example, you don't find out what you need to do to unlock all the animals in each biome ahead of time. You don't even know what tools are going to be available as the game moves through its 3 stages; getting stuck in stage 2 is probably the most common occurrence I had, and more than once I realized in retrospect that the random terrain generation had made for an unusually challenging map, since I would restart and immediately the problem had been simplified significantly.There's a lot of chatter in these comments about the slow pace and frustrating gameplay. For people who like more traditional strategy games, I can certainly see how this would be an incredibly dull, even tedious experience. It's very reactive. Often the best solutions are to simply poke things in the correct direction rather than trying to stamp a grand plan over the map, which I'm pretty sure was the explicit intention; whether you like that or not is another question. I think you'll know whether or not you'll enjoy finishing Terra Nil by the end of the second map, probably about 90 minutes in.Overall, I liked it as a little digital terrarium I could mess around with for an hour or two at a time, without any huge time crunch. I do think some additional content would be welcome, which the devs have already indicated they'll be working on, having recovered from the burnout they experienced in the rush to full release. I might also suggest reworking the terrain generation to result in fewer scenarios where 1 or 2 very minor mistakes can sink the entire playthrough (prepare to be frustrated by shade clothes if all your cliffs are far apart).But hey, I liked what I've seen, and I'll be excited to see what comes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A comfy atmosphere only gets you so far. Sorry, but quite frankly, for a strategy game like this, I expected more content. A short, focused game is fine, but Terra Nil doesn't even offer levels that feel hand crafted for interesting or challenging gameplay.At $25 for 6 hours, the experience needs to be more memorable than "decent, I guess". There are better options on steam. Get those instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game, I think the concept is great, and I appreciate the environmental goals behind it. The issue is that there just isn't $25 worth of content here. I have 7 hours played, but realistically that's only ~4, since I got distracted by work for a few hours. Considering the first level was the Demo, that only really leaves 3 new levels, and then 4 variations on the original levels. I don't expect to be paying $3 an hour for a game, considering the great value proposition that other games offer. Unfortunately, it's just long enough to get you past the 2 hour refund window, or I think I would have refunded this and picked it up on sale down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I don't have the proper words for the things this game makes me feel. Yes, there are only four biomes, and yes, I technically beat it in about eight hours but, everyone, listen to me. It was 8 hours I would gladly pay $25 to experience again, and the value is all in knowing that I can in fact experience it again, in a slightly different way, limitlessly. If you like puzzles, or nature, or beautiful art, or soothing music, or perhaps all four, get this game. On the central difficulty I felt it was perfectly compelling, relaxing while still making me remember I was playing a game. Just wonderful, overall. Make yourself a cup of tea, sit down, and restore a wasteland.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I see others complaining about the high cost for a short game, but I didn't get that far. I played the first level and gave up in frustration about halfway through the second level.The game is janky and frustrating and tedious. It couldn't have been thirty minutes in when the game gave me an unachievable goal: Click on the lake, in a map that had no lakes, that had never had any lakes.And the game does this extremely irritating thing where it only gradually reveals the rules you're playing by, allowing you to make mistakes early in a level that turn out to cause problems later. Mistakes that might have been avoided, or at least that might have felt more like my own fault, if the game hadn't withheld the parameters of the puzzle for no good reason.I suspect that many of the frustrations I encountered were due to the levels in this game being procedurally generated, and getting very unlucky with the maps that the RNG inflicted on my unwitting self. I am very good at puzzles and strategy games. I expected this to be a breeze. Yet struggling to make sense of this game on the normal difficulty was emphatically not a calming experience for me, as others seem to be having.Maybe pick this up on sale when it inevitably gets discounted down to 5 bucks. It's a neat idea, but the implementation sucks. It's really not worth more than that.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful and relaxing puzzle game that's sadly going to be overtaken by "it's short, so i don't recommend" as is the case with most games on steam nowadays.I definitely wish there were more biomes/levels - The game currently has 4 biomes to reclaim, being a river valley, a tropical island, a tundra, and a temperate forest . There could have been more variety here such as a desert, the ocean, rainforests etc. However, given what is there I will not hesitate in recommending it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The game is exactly what I expected. A small game where you have to restore ecosystems in barren regions of a world based on real natural environments using methods likely to be used in our current world to achieve your goal and then leave after erasing every trace of your presence. The visuals are charming, every step of the game is clear, the environments are well chosen. Also, it's a very soothing game, you won't be stressed with deadlines, mandatory timed objectives or recurring catastrophes. However, the game is very short. It took me a few hours to complete it 100%. I would really love to see a bigger game with more environments and possibilities based on same principle. Overall a really nice little game, I really enjoyed playing it.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The metaphor I would use is plumbing. The game feels like turning things off/on according to plumbing pipes, which is to say it doesn't really feel like city building or environment tuning. All things considered, not that interesting nor beautiful nor relaxing. The rapid creation/destruction of environments does not make me feel particularly tender or sensitive toward what I'm doing, either.The game is chill but for what it does, it feels more like a mobile game. I could imagine listening to several podcasts while playing this, but it felt low value to me and would need to be heavily on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow I lost 2 hrs playing this game today. It would have been more but work, ya know? But as for the game itself the soundtrack is amazing and relaxing. You don't feel stressed out while building out your ecosystem. The game play is intuitive and instructional, the developer did a great job of adding just enough tool tips without holding your hand completely. Even with the first map when it offered me to restart (due to a few mistakes of my own) I pressed on and managed to complete it with full marks on my first try.If you like sandbox games, "city" builders (and I use that term loosely) and strategy games then this is worth every penny you spend. Even as a content creator I didn't want to wait to receive a key and bought this game straight up when it was listed on steam for purchase. That's how awesome I think this game is.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I played this on gardener mode, and it's honestly one of the most peaceful games I've played in a while, and actually made me appreciate the greenery around where I live just that little bit more. Fully reccomend to anyone who liked games like farmville, sims cities, animal crossing, or minecraft. It can be a little buggy, but the satisfaction of reclaiming a wasteland to make lush beautiful greenery more than makes up for it
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: An adorable, and unique little puzzle game where you attempt to turn wastelands into thriving habitats by balancing different types of environments in unique regions. With three phases to work through; including, cleansing pollution, rebuilding habitats, and recycling your machines to let nature take over. Its fun to balance a region to fit and complete little optional goals and reestablish animals. It's a unique game that deserves to be experienced.All is not without flaws, and the most glaring is the severe lack of content. With only four regions (each with a post game challenge variant.) It's a very short lived experience, and an expensive one at that. On top of that, the only truly interesting and dynamic stuff happens in the final continental stage. I won't spoil it for players but some stuff actually happens that throws you some curve balls and was really cool, but it sadly only happens in that stage. It would be cool to see more stages and dynamic challenges added to the game, but I can easily imagine these ideas better grown expanded upon in a sequel too. All that said I thoroughly enjoyed my time with the game and would highly recommenced for the unique puzzle lite experience alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The game is visually beautiful and can be very relaxing just to see the world being alive. But for the price I would not recommend it, the game has no replayability after you cleared it for the first time. The gameplay is very shallow and doesn't offer much variety. I was really excited for the game but after playing it for a while it becomes very boring. You might have more fun watching others play than playing it yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo for a total of 18 hours. The demo. And this game is exactly what I was hoping for. It's beautiful, peaceful, and juuuuust difficult to have me mess up now and again, but not enough to annoy me (on medium difficulty anyway). I actually found myself smiling and giggling randomly cause it was just so satisfying to watch the grass and trees pop up. Not many games make me feel like a kid again, but damn, this one did.It's not a long game, I'm making my way through the second half (you get to replay regions, but with trickier maps) and taking my time to admire it too. So probably a 8-12 hour game if you take it slow. However the maps are randomized and I expect to replay this constantly.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Review based on finishing the game at 14 hours: Great relaxing game with some strategy elements added in. One thing I wish I knew before hand was that you really can't mess up a map to the point where you can't get all the biomes or animal discoveries. I also encountered a weird glitch with the monorail system where I'd put down a monorail, but it would be invisible, but when I restarted the save, they showed up. Other than than that, a very nice looking game with peaceful visuals and nice music.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A great, chill game that takes the opposite approach to city builders - rehabilitating and reseeding a world destroyed by industry.My only criticism is the length. 5-10 hours for the asking price is a little steep. I would wait until this is on offer for it to be truly worth the price.EDIT: I've gone back to play this, and looking at my playtime I got 13 hours out of the first playthrough. Admittedly I 100%ed the game, but 13 hours is more than I've got out of more expensive games :)
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: The game has 4 maps, 8 with the alternatives, but every play through is generated differently!I've loved it since the demo.  It's even better now that it's polished.I will say I miss the original recycling process - where you could recycle recyclers and inch them closer to the river.  Now you have to plan ahead a bit more.  Which...is probably the point.It's peaceful and addicting, and I've played the same level 4 times in 4 different ways and with different approaches.  It's soothing and wonderful.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A fun, pleasant, and short puzzle/light strategy game. The art design is lovely, the theme is quite appealing, and the gameplay has some unique elements I haven't seen elsewhere.It's definitely more puzzle-like than city sim/builder-like. The main constraint is that you have a single resource, and each action you take consumes and adds a certain amount of that resources. Each mission has a sequence of different terraforming stages, and your goal is to place buildings in a way that maximizes their impact for the current stage (as well as the next one). The challenge is in planning ahead a bit to avoid running out of resources or blocking your progress in future stages, and I think it works out quite well.I was a bit surprised how short it is, though: there are 4 main missions that can be finished in around 4-6 hours total. Procedural generation and one variation for each mission adds a bit of replay value, but it seems like there's a lot of potential for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and challenging puzzle game with the objective of restoring nature via using technology in the first place that need to be re-collected at the end. Only nature shall remain.The artstyle is minimalistic but lovely and create beautiful and colorful environments. The music is calm and peaceful.The only negative thing in my opinion is the currently limited content. I hope we get more maps and tasks in the future.Overall a challenging but relaxing game which feels just lovely to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: This is another game that needs a "eh" option. It seems more like a better mobile zen garden without the ads. Distracting for a bus ride or something, also nice not to have a waiting mechanic. Thinking that way Im not sure about the price, I try not to put to much into mobile games but I'm sure a few of them have gotten $10 or so out of me. So probably should wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Very meditative, can be a simple ecological puzzle or a thorough challenge.Edit: I've had to amend my review to include that this game is strangely addicting. I play 2-3 times a day and it's just so relaxing... seeing a desolate wasteland transformed into a thriving biome is a wonderful way to relieve tension.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR:Like the vibes? - Get it.Like pure gameplay? - Wait for saleLike a mix? - Read below.~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~People keep saying that it's short, but that's not full story. This game falls in to 2 genres: chill and management game. Chill games usually have wild price points, because people who play them seek reeeally unique experiences. These unique experiences are not efficient to develop for the general audience - hard work for a small group of people, that's why prices are sometimes disproportionally big with small play time.On the other hand, management games are complete oposite, they have superb replay value and a lot of content for relatively low price, but when it comes to visual stuff and vibes, they can underdeliver.This game is primarily a chill game priced accordingly, so if eou really enjoy the vibes of this game - get it. If you are interested in pure gameplay - wait for a sale, if you have a mix decide which side of the game you prefer more and if you are like me and love the vibes and management side of this Terra Nil - it is an excellent time.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so in love with this game so far. I have a career in environmental science, so I really wanted to try out this game. Not ONLY are the visuals and soft music SO CHARMING, but it's also extremely educational. Learning how to strategize and develop the land into the most optimized biomes is SUPER satisfying. I love how much thought was put into this game to make the play style flow so smoothly without feeling like there's too much hand holding or completely leaving you hanging. You will LOVE this game if you like: nature, science, strategy, and relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent gameplay, beautiful art, great themes, Terra Nil nails what it's going for from top to bottom. Ignore the gamers complaining about 'replayability' and 'length' it's the cost of a movie ticket for 10-15 hours of one of the best games this year.  It's nuanced ebb and flow of managing climate is a brilliant concept I'd love to see more in strategy/city management games, it really makes some of the goals and concepts challenging while allowing for a lot of manipulation. Very hard to to complete on harder difficulties, still requiring planning and thought but very completable on easy, featuring hard versions of each level that are a lot of fun. Once the mechanics sank in and I had a better grasp of the gameplay I was totally hooked. It's an excellent strategy game with impeccable vibes and great themes. Would love to see more devs risking such unique choices in the city/resource management genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

_childDocuments_.review:
Terra Nil, from eco-warriors Free Lives (Broforce) and recycled publisher Devolver Digital, presents players with the task of environmental rejuvenation. Begin with the water system, slowly purify the soil, and cultivate pioneer greenery. Embark on more ambitious tasks, restore biodiversity, fix the climate, introduce wildlife, and finally recycle all the structures you used to get there, leaving the environment pristine.

Each region of the game has its own flavour and procedural generation palette. Yet even within a region, no two playthroughs will be the same.

Navigate sprawling, verdant, hand-painted environments where everything but the rocks move and breathe. A meditative soundtrack and stunning audio palette will accompany your efforts.
_childDocuments_.name: Terra Nil

name: God of War
detailed_description: Enter the Norse realm His vengeance against the Gods of Olympus years behind him, Kratos now lives as a man in the realm of Norse Gods and monsters. It is in this harsh, unforgiving world that he must fight to survive… and teach his son to do the same. Grasp a second chance Kratos is a father again. As mentor and protector to Atreus, a son determined to earn his respect, he is forced to deal with and control the rage that has long defined him while out in a very dangerous world with his son. Journey to a dark, elemental world of fearsome creatures From the marble and columns of ornate Olympus to the gritty forests, mountains and caves of pre-Viking Norse lore, this is a distinctly new realm with its own pantheon of creatures, monsters and gods. Engage in visceral, physical combat With an over the shoulder camera that brings the player closer to the action than ever before, fights in God of War™ mirror the pantheon of Norse creatures Kratos will face: grand, gritty and grueling. A new main weapon and new abilities retain the defining spirit of the God of War series while presenting a vision of conflict that forges new ground in the genre. PC FEATURES High Fidelity Graphics Striking visuals enhanced on PC. Enjoy true 4K resolution, on supported devices, [MU1] with unlocked framerates for peak performance. Dial in your settings via a wide range of graphical presets and options including higher resolution shadows, improved screen space reflections, the addition of GTAO and SSDO, and much more. NVIDIA® DLSS and Reflex Support Quality meets performance. Harness the AI power of NVIDIA Deep Learning Super Sampling (DLSS) to boost frame rates and generate beautiful, sharp images on select Nvidia GPUs. Utilize NVIDIA Reflex low latency technology allowing you to react quicker and hit harder combos with the responsive gameplay you crave on GeForce GPUs. Controls Customization Play your way. With support for the DUALSHOCK®4 and DUALSENSE® wireless controllers, a wide range of other gamepads, and fully customizable bindings for mouse and keyboard, you have the power to fine-tune every action to match your playstyle. Ultra-wide Support Immerse yourself like never before. Journey through the Norse realms taking in breathtaking vistas in panoramic widescreen. With 21:9 ultra-widescreen support, God of War™ presents a cinema quality experience that further expands the original seamless theatrical vision.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic! I got it at a discounted price of 20 euros during the weekend, which is a steal considering how good it turned out to be.The game ran really well, even on my old GTX 1080Ti (High settings at 3440 x 1440). Frame rate was mostly close to 60 fps, with some occasional dips to 50-55 fps. I had no issues (not even a single crash) playing this on my PC with Nvidia driver version 560.81 in August, 2024. The only thing to keep in mind is that AMD FSR is enabled by default, which makes the visuals appear really bad. Do remember to turn it off.The story is very engaging and the visuals are quite breathtaking. I managed to complete it in about 43 hours. A lot more time can still be spent completing the side quests.

_childDocuments_.review: I approached this game from the standpoint of a father, expecting it to depict the typical struggles of a child growing up with a harsh, distant and unresponsive father. I thought God of War would teach me about realtionship between a father and son. Instead, it made me look deep into myself.	The main story focues on a journey of father and son through beautiful, spectacular yet sometimes harsh lands based on Norse mythology. However, the journey is just the background to the realtionship developing between the two. 	God of War immerses players in it's world thanks to it's camera, which stays close to main characters and seamlessly transitions to scripted cinematic events. The sound work and music further enhance this immersive experience. The graphics are spectacular.	The gameplay mechanics – combat, exploration, collectible hunts - rely on modern design principles, refined and polished to an incerdibely high level. However, the game fails to introduce any meaningful, innovative gameplay elements. This leads to simplified puzzles that almost solve themselves, as a means of avoiding player frustration. At the same time, the game offers depth and challenges through additional bossfights and light build-making options. The suprisingly wide roster of active skills, further increases player agency during combat.	In the end, the main strength of God of War, it's defining element, is it's writing. The story is incredible, with a narrow pool of well defined characters, each with distinct personalities, goals and interactions that enrich the narrative, creating an unforgettable experience. 	God of War proves that videogames can become artistic masterpieces, telling mature, emotional stories. Most of all, it proves that this medium can successfuly convey a message.	I strongly recommend this game.If you are interested in an overly analytic video version of this review then check out my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: This game is stunning! Is breath taking graphics and unbeatable gameplay are only a page in a massive book on things why this game is amazing. The story is a magnificent compelling attribute to an already perfect game, the story draws you in by constantly keeping you on a train of cliff hangers and systems where it make you want to unlock other plots advancing the story, all the while making each and every advancement into the plot as fresh as the previous one. The gritty nature of the story at heart is just a small layer shadowing the deeper lesson of understanding and acceptance of past actions. The game play is utterly brilliant, the fighting mechanics and the abilities are unseen is a franchise about hack and slash, while still retaining the incredibly addictive playability of not only it’s own series but of any game genre of us kind. The blocking in this game doesn’t just defend you from an enemy’s attacks is allowed you to counter damaging them stunning them allowing you to follow up with a barrage of strikes from your weapon of choice. The accessibility of progression in this title is irresistible the rewards that are given for complete side missions and main are more than fair, allowing you to upgrade and progress though a bewitching skill system. You also have your son as a side companion assisting you in battle as well as being a key character in the story having a major effect on the narrative. Your son Atreus can be used to attack enemies from a distance and be used to advance to new room and progress though levels and assists is tricky but fun puzzles. The graphics are unbelievably beautiful, unseen  I’m a game of this type. The miraculous terrain you travel is extremely realistic and vibrant, the surroundings are just down right prepossessing and gorgeous. The Nordic style of the environment is perfect for both combat and appealing to the eye. The water simulation in this game is a almost perfect example on how games have evolved from 2D side scroller to game that are unrecognizable from real life.  The attention to detail is unmatched, it’s clear nothing from graphics, gameplay to the story weren’t rushed. The musical score is also an absolute must when is come to setting the mood. The cinematography is on points making the game one continuous shot not cutting from one scene to the next, it creates a cinematic feeling putting in the actual perspective of the character. All around this game is extremely important in the advancements of game quality, and detail.P.S. I have to also say that this PC port is stellar! We have great options and optimizations is fantastic!

_childDocuments_.review: God of War(2018) is one of the last PS exclusives I ever expected to make the PC jump and boy, this stellar port steadily reminds me why I enjoyed it so much in the first place while subtly improving player experience in many areas. Somehow the developers at Santa Monica managed to nail keyboard and mouse controls, it feels pretty natural. This is a pleasant surprise as many games in this genre don't always work well playing on KB+M.This game's story is a sequel to God of War 3 but the gameplay has been redesigned making it a soft reboot of sorts. The voice acting and character designs remain top notch and the slow burn type story lends really well with Kratos learning about the lands he chose as his new home. Truly an amazing comeback for a series. I am definitely a fan of Norse Mythology, this game will satisfy those interests for anyone like me! _childDocuments_.review: When God of War won GOTY I was furious because at the time I had exclusively played RDR2 for many hours and had not even considered God of War as a game to play, so as you can probably tell I was incredibly biased towards RDR2 because to me it felt as if no game could come close to the masterpiece that it was. I was baffled by the idea that a game as large and detailed as RDR2 had been beaten by some Playstation exclusive God of War game that, at the time, looked like it was just riding off of the hype-train that was a God of War comeback for the fans set in a world that was nothing to do with the Kratos we knew from previous games. However, with RDR2 being out for quite some time now and me feeling like I had milked the game dry of content, I decided to give God of War a go seeing as it was released for PC and test for myself if it was worthy of the GOTY title it was given. Let me tell you, I have never been so wrong in my life...God of War does not only deserve the GOTY award it won, but in my opinion, it will also go down as one of the best games to EVER be released, and trust me, I do not make that claim lightly. The story of Kratos in a Norse mythology setting was an incredibly risky dice roll for the developers but I feel it not only worked, but launched the God of War series leagues above 99% of the gaming industry. I found myself captivated from the very start until the very end, constantly on the edge of my seat as Kratos and his son went on this grand adventure that I felt as if I was with them on the entire way. I would happily sit here and type out another 5 paragraphs worth of why this game is worth your money, but honestly, I think most people already know. I have spent time collecting every achievement and going to 100% completion in this game because of how passionate this game has made me feel towards it, and for a game in 2022 to do that to me is very rare let me tell you. My excitement for the next installment (Ragnarok I believe it is called?) is beyond measure.Anyway... that was my God of War review, not really a deep dive into the technicality's of the game, more like a note of admiration for the experience that this game has been. Now you will have to excuse me, it seems a second playthrough is calling my name!

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, the first God Of War completed not on youtube.Despite that fact that the game is mostly different against Greece games, this one is a masterpiece too.I'm fed up with all the so-called "open worlds"  that get shoved into any AAA project. And when I saw firstly tons of crates, enemy levels and RPG like progression I was upset.I almost forgot that such games can be enjoyable. This game keeps "magic" balance in all doubtful aspects. I've never though that Scandinavian mythology can be the same interesting as Greek .It was interesting how Ghost Of Sparta will get along in the new setting and the BOY . Anyway, story evolves smoothly, immersing you in a new world. You grow and evolve with Kratos and his BOY. Magnificent soundtrack and epic moments. Not much epic , but well done cut-scenes. The story only begins. Sometimes a bit slowly, but enough to dive into and not tired in the process. And I am very glad that I was finally able to catch and feel this moment not on video hosting. Much lore moments, especially if you decide to complete all side requests. Even collectibles are not junkie as It always were, I completed them all to fill gaps .Combat system feels more tactical, but dynamical and entertaining as was. Bunch of skills and variety of combinations offer you to create your own style and play with beating poor creatures. Challenging enough at the beginning, but then you realize how the world works.The levels are mostly corridor, but not tight. In general, richly made for the biome. Some of them will have to return several times. Not sure if I like this stuff, but that was okay. Someone complained about puzzles, but as far as I remember they always were. And these puzzles are mine level - for kids.Nearly ~40 hours of enjoyment. Although the fly in the ointment is the fact that you have to grind to fully improve weapons. Some craft items can be obtained in repetitive activities. However, first few runs are interesting and challenging enough. As a result, I found myself heavily pumped for the last hours of gameplay.+ 1 more high quality game with excellent story.For sure, I will wait for the next part.

_childDocuments_.review: *Minor Spoilers*Time played after I wrote this review is when I started my NG+, so you'll definitely get your money's worth. The soft reboot really makes you feel for Kratos and his extremely dark past. Relationship between the Boy is realistic and the voice acting is great. At times you literally feel like you're dealing with a kid growing up, which usually tends to be cringe in other titles, but this - it just hits the mark. The Dwarf-duo is a little on the dad-joke side, but it serves the humor purpose. I love how they still throw in Greek related references so you don't feel too detached from the previous game's theme, which most came to love.The combat eventually gets a little repetitive but here's the crazy part, the combat is so heavily in-depth, even 60 hours in, you'll find a neat little trick you didn't realize or master at it's fullest length as you continue to upgrade your weapons. Being so story heavy, it kinda slows down the speedrunning aspect once you completed your 100% playthrough and have seen everything quite a few times already. The gearing up system is rather close to basic in theory, but the stats, power gain system, and skills is extremely satisfying as you upgrade and craft better items, you really get hooked on the number increases.I was impressed with the size of the game for such a heavily polished cinematic single player. Difficulty wise, it's a perfect balance for all. From the easiest of Give Me a Story, to the hardest of Give Me God of War against the "Queen" Valkyrie, who will keep you company for a hot minute. NG+ or in my case GMGOW+, was so much fun seeking out the Zeus set and fighting Sigrun again in all the new NG+ gear while feeling super powerful. Consistency of same monsters/mini-bosses is present, but it's spaced enough where it isn't a major problem, but it's a thing. The final fight was probably personally the most annoying due to constant interruptions, stuns, ect., where it should be the finale fight - unleash everything you've learned and gained, only to get disturbed constantly by a character who doesn't exactly belong at that time or place, which brings me to the last negative. You can't play creatively on the hardest difficulty combo-chaining ability wise unless you're ready to man handle some monsters. You'll constantly get punished if you go for style points which is a shame.Overall it's visually pretty and the colors used are wonderful. Game noticeably falls flat in a big middle section of the game, the action and cinematic thrill is still there, but just a slight notice. Cinematic wise there's a few top tier moments here, mainly the ending with the line of, "Snow". This moment is by far the most well designed in the entire game by miles.GG

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, after I 100% the game I have a clearer view on it, I am now sure that I would never recommend it as soon as it's that expensive, simply because it doesn't offer anything to the slightest for the asking price. I expected for it to get better after the story, since you'd simply roam, exploring regions and realms... Sadly, that's not the case, the game gets even more tedious due to terrible design choices. (most of them, are your typical modern gaming BS)The bad ones:-Gameplay:The best thing about GoW was always its fast paced, hack n slash nature gameplay, the ultimate feeling of ripping your enemies apart.Unfortunately, GoW 2018 takes another route, your typical story rich modern game route, so that by itself is a downgrade already. I could see past that and simply adapt and enjoy on the new gameplay, however the terrible camera design and enemy design completely ruin the enjoyment. The cherry at the top is your starting weapon, Leviathan Axe. It's bad...just bad.. Combos are limited, slow, and you don't deal any damage, enemies are chunky to justify the lack of action and there are only a few types of them. You will end up fighting the same enemy over and over again, there isn't much variety neither on typical enemies nor on mini bosses.Mini bosses are the same giant troll 90% of times, with a different color and element applied to it.The ultimate problem with the gameplay  however, isn't the encounters, but what happens between them. You see my 40 hours on record? 20 of them were me climbing walls, doing quicktime events, talking to characters and watching cutscenes. So for every 5 minutes you spend in a fight, you'll spend 5 minutes to proceed to the next area.. And I mean this could be tolerable if everything wasn't THAT SLOW, I mean legit Kratos killed every god of olympus and a bunch of other titans, yet he cannot jump from a 5 meter distance? He really needs to climb down a wall manually? REALLY? There are a lot of modern gaming limitations that completely ruins a potentially okish game. -Story:Story is a mess, I really am surprised everyone saying this game's story is a masterpiece. It is full of plot holes, lazy writting and childish characters.Spoiler alert, you do everything because apparently Krato's wife didn't tell him she is a giant before she died, she wanted him and Atreus to risk their lives to scatter her ashes from the highest spot of Midgard. What she wanted in reality was for them to discover she was a giant..Wow, top notch, totally not retarded.There is nothing to inform you in detail about the gap between the last GoW title and this one, so you barely care about anyone at all. Like, who cares about Atreus really?Characters will start explaining a story in the most basic way of explaining a story, and they will end up saying "well, that's how it is, no one knows why for sure".. I mean even developers didn't care about the story lol-Characters:A complete spit on GoW's face, everyone is trying to be a comedian with their childish jokes and behavior, the game isn't serious or deep at all, Gods are acting like spoiled little brats, they don't have any goal or purpose doing what they are doing, except from Baldur, Atreus is irrelevant and pathetic, apart from Freya Baldur and Kratos, the rest is a disgrace and unmemorable.-BossesThis is the last complaint I have about the game, there are only 3 main story boss encounters, that says a lot about the game, 2 of them featuring you fighting gods in the most simplistic way possible, by simply hitting them, you just need to hit them till their HP bar is down to 0, no god turning into a giant attacking you with different abilities, no different phases, nothing. The only good boss battle is the first one where you fight a dragon..Now that's a decent boss battle that reminded me the older titles, multiple phases, different attacks, creative design overall. Sad it was only 1 in the entire game.The good ones:-Gameplay after Blades of Chaos:Thank Lord you pick up Blades of Chaos later (like, really late) in the game, they completely change the pace of the game and make the combat sufferable, even enjoyable sometimes. Everything becomes faster, they are more effective, more satisfying to play with.-Voice acting:Great voice acting, not much to say here.-Sound/Audio design:Top notch, they actually did care to this part of the game.-Customization:Even though nothing will top Krato's original design in my opinion, it's always a plus when you can customize one of your favorite characters, it really adds to the variety.All in all GoW 2018 is just another overrated modern PS exclusive title, anyone who has played more than 10 games in their life will probably notice that. The game suffer from tedious sequences and boring combat, and the lazy story cannot justify any of that.I am really shocked this game has overwhelmingly positive reviews, I mean, it sure isn't hot garbage, but it definitely isn't the masterpiece they are telling you it is.Overall: 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. I played on Give me God of War difficulty, and just completing the story quest without 100% of the rest took me 53 hours. I would recommend God of War to someone in a heartbeat, however I felt at times that the combat's controls were quite frustrating. As someone who loves Souls-like games, I believe that challenging games are fun if they are fair - the combat should be skilled based, and poor controls can be quite contradictory to the game's experience being fun. God of War has incredible graphics (if your computer can manage it), a wonderful story, great score, and the combat encounters typically feel well balanced. However, there is the occasional battle that I had to replay numerous times because I was being screwed over by an attack animation I was stuck in (that was supposed to grant me invulnerability) and I get blasted to death by some large attack by another character. Despite the fact that my gamer rage could far outclass Kratos's Spartan Rage at times, this game was a 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this at launch on the PS4 so I knew a lot about the game going in. However this time, went for all the achievements and did all the optional content which I did not do before. God of War is definitely a must play if you are on the fence. I'd say one of the GOATs of gaming. Its pretty crazy to think that Kratos went from a killing machine with no personality in the original trilogy to a father figure to Atreus and has some real character depth to him in this game. I vastly prefer the direction of this game (but I do have a soft spot for the original trilogy's Greek mythos, combat and epic setpieces). Story and characters are all great, very memorable and some of them have some pretty good humor to them. Combat seems very shallow but it actually is very deep if you want it to be. You can create different types of builds that suits your needs. SSM nails the norse mythos in the game; its somewhere you want to explore and learn more about its inhabitants, the land and its Gods. Tons of awesome lore to read up on and all the realms look gorgeous. Very curious to see where the sequel will go next, they have done a lot of setting up for future plot points and some MIA Gods.Regarding the port itself, I ran into zero performance related issues. Its one of the better PC ports I have played first hand. Tons of good features like DLSS and ultra widescreen support. I know its missing some stuff like a FOV slider, but seems that the developers are looking to implement fan requested features like that. Kudos to Santa Monica Studio and Jetpack Interactive for taking the time and effort for making such a stellar port. It's definitely paying off. Hope the wait to see God of War Ragnarok on Steam won't be that long!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been surprising.  I mainly got it for the graphics, on sale, to see what the fuss was about.  I didn't like GoW3, couldn't play more than 2 minutes of it, and in my 40s the whole 'me god, me kill all' kind of fell in the same bucket of boring as the film 300.  with trepidation I started this game, testing out graphics drivers and proton and a PS5 controller.  I can say, it wasn't at all what i was expecting.  or to be clear, it is definitely that same 'me god, must kill all' aspect if that's all you want, but it's mostly a feeling of a game that has matured with us.  the son is hilarious, parodying the absurdity of kratos.  it is a very intriguing story, not a lust for power or a silly revenge arc (at least not so far).  I can say it work magnificently with a rtx3090 on a 7 year old PC, running debian 11 testing, using proton-GE-7-33, on nvidia driver version 515.76 (you can find an easy install guide on a non-nvidia blog [seriously nvidia, why ur website sucks so much?]), just remember to turn on v-sync, it smoothes out vulkan loads which really only happen rarely in the game.  gorgeous, freaking gorgeous graphics in scenes.  I showed the witches house to the gf and she was blown away with how pretty the garden was.  games have sure come a long way since golden axe, that's all i'll say. i thought i wouldn't play games anymore as i grew older, even though i knew games are becoming the next stage of story-telling vehicle, i just thought it wouldnt keep pace.  but boy, the visuals here feel so much better than any marvel film.. and the story is really really nice.  it made me actually enjoy taking down trolls again.  it made me remember why i used to love computer games so much, and to be honest, reminded me why i loved research in quantum information for my phd.  silicon valley kind of was a huge bummer because it's very non-fun in its tech, silicon valley made me want to quit tech altogether.  but slowly, stuff like this is reminding me of what the real potential of tech is.  i know, it's silly to have a game make me reflect on my life.  but, this game did that.  it has a lot of self-reflection in it.  wholy recommend it, it is a complete game, where killing monsters with cool moves, while still a large part of the game, actually takes the back seat to a great story where gorgeous graphics really make the story pop.

Weapons and skills are fun to play around with and combat never gets boring thanks to the fluidity and weight of the weapons you wield.The story was compelling, very emotional and felt like a complete package - even though there's a sequel out. The environments (realms) you visit are vibrant and all distinctive from one another (although bigger enemy variety would've been better) and the main + side quests allow you to see all the realms have to offer. The puzzles are clever due to the fact you have to utilise your weapons' powers to solve them most of the time, and they help to break up the pace a bit.Performance was good (no bugs!), but I had to run it with the upscaler to get smooth 60 fps on a 1070 + Ultrawide.One of my favourite games I've played this year- would definitely recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan coming from the older games in the series and you're looking for more of what you love, just be warned that this isn't the same God of War anymore. Almost everything is different - the combat, atmosphere, perspective, gameplay, and even Kratos have all changed dramatically. I'm not saying change is a bad thing, I just didn't care for it.For example, the camera is huge pain in the ass. The previous camera perspective has been replaced by a much more limiting Resident Evil 4 style of camera. Get used to having like half of your screen constantly blocked by Kratos and all his damn equipment. Combat feels claustrophobic and visually impaired now. Lots of dodging blindly because I can't actually see the attacks coming.Open-world exploration is something I'm usually a big fan of in games, but not this time. There's more mindless canoeing around in circles looking for tiny, worthless bits of treasure than I ever could have anticipated. Same with the puzzle solving - it's basic, repetitive, and tedious. Oh and so much backtracking.. only made worse by the rubbish fast travel system. All of this filler garbage does very little to add to the quality of the experience, and it just murders the pacing of the game over and over again. Seriously, I never thought in a thousand years that God of War would be so bloody boring that I would actually fall asleep multiple times while playing. And how about the story? Story is lame at best. It presents itself like it's going to be an epic tale involving an awesome clash between gods. Really though, it's just a boring delivery quest that is stretched out to the extremes. Epic moments seem to take place once every blue moon or so.And what about the characters? I liked the dwarven blacksmiths and the talking head (sometimes), they could be entertaining. Kratos, however, used to be a lot more interesting, believe it or not. Now he's bordering on being a frigging vegetable that can't do much other than grunt and say "boy" over and over. Christ, this isn't even really his quest ffs! He's basically just a brain-damaged bodyguard that got manipulated (again) into running errands for people while you constantly have to listen to pointless drivel about how mean Odin and Thor are to the valkyries, giants, etc. It's a shallow and tacky story that does no justice to Kratos' character.But hey, the difficulty is pretty balanced for the most part and the soundtrack is enjoyable to listen to. Also, the graphics are quite nice and the game has maintained solid framerates on ultra settings with no crashing. See? It's not all bad.. Just really ******* boring, that's all.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War is hands down easily one of the best single player story games i have played ever. The lore is actually cool and interesting and plentiful. There is not a single flaw with the game that i can point out (seriously I tried to think of some) so I will point out my personal pros i noticed as I played. The difficulty, (played on the setting above normal) it is scaled so unbelievably well that in the beginning that you will be struggling and almost think you need to turn the difficulty down, but as soon as you hit that point, the difficulty becomes perfectly gauged to where you are barely beating hard enemies and fights and usually needing more than one to many attempts at boss fights. I consider myself good at the game, but it is definitely one that had me pacing around the house between attempts on certain boss fights.. When you complete the story, you are left with trials in the arena (still havent beaten them to unlock the valkyrie fight), triels in a fog realm, and valkyrie fights across the realms. Think of these as boss fights that you unlock and have to complete to 100% the game after fully levelling up and finishing the story, you still have playability and still will find yourself barely making it through the fights, long story short the difficulty is scaled amazingly well. I stil have not beaten all of the boss fights in muselheim, or the fog realm, or finished all the valkyrie fights and I have 37 hours on the game and am decent at it. Another pro is simply the story, its amazing and well done and entertaining yet serious yet funny yet action packed and at certain times is super immersive. I did not encounter a single glitch, don't think i ever had a crash, or ever really had a problem other than getting clapped in the muselheim trials, a humbling experience. If you have great taste you will love this game. The graphics are insanely good as well. the combat is challenging, rewarding, and visually pleasing. the puzzles in-game are the exact same. All in All, I would say this game deserves a spot on anyones top 10 list and personally for me maybe top 5-7. I would say that once you beat the story that you get depressed that it's over, but I know theres no way you will have beaten all of the arena trials and valkyries even at that point its a game that really requires you to try, sometimes over and over again, and eventually you will do everything right in the fight and progress. I cannot recommend this game enough, and i STRONGLY recommend playing on the difficulty ONE ABOVE NORMAL. it may seem hard at first but once you learn the movements and controls you will realize why I recommend it as it makes the game super immersive.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this God of War absolutely blind. I've never owned a console so I haven't played the previous games and though this game came out in 2018, I never really paid any attention to it since I never thought I'd end up playing this franchise. So I watched a recap video for the GOW franchise for the past games before jumping in here.. And let me tell you, that helps so much in adding context to character actions, reactions, dialogue. It also helps in understanding how Kratos is suddenly in Norse mythology when the past games were set in Greek mythos. While this is not necessary, I feel knowing Kratos's past adds so much more depth to this game.This game is something special. You take a cookie cutter character from a hack and slash franchise and you ground that character by giving him depth. And there is so much nuance and character development here for both Kratos and his son. It is a wonderful tale about family and adventure. And there is just so much to explore in this game. A lot of it hidden away cleverly and a lot are blocked off by metroidvania mechanics where you have to revisit some areas with some skills to explore further.  I finally understand how this game beat out Red Dead Redemption. The production quality, visuals, lore, music, voice acting are all magnificent. Every truly great game has moments which inspire chills. This game has plenty of them.And the final reveal at the end was magnificent. Pros:-Story, Visuals, Music, Performance(Runs brilliantly on ultra+high on an old gtx 1070), Art, Lore, Animation, Character Development, Exploration.Cons:-Lack of boss variety/special boss encounters, some minor old game design elements(archaic armor and rune system, environment interactions etc). Honestly don't even read this section. There are no significant cons that will ruin/hamper the experience.Rating - 9.5/10  ~ A Work of Art.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War remains one of the best most enjoyable, participating, and influential and effective games to come out of Santa Monica Studio. There is a lot of depth and passion in the plot, the mechanics are clever and interesting, and the presentation on the PC is just unmatched. Even after almost four years, this is still a pleasant surprise.Graphics and controls in the God of War PC edition are excellent, and the game is designed specifically for the PC platform. If you have always been intrigued in the God of War series but have been unable to play it owing to the brand's exclusivity to video game consoles, here is your opportunity to finally experience the brilliance of God of War. Experience the next-generation God of War before the release of God of War: Ragnarök will be an excellent option for God of War fans who are die-hard followers of the series.It is said that good things come to those who wait, and in this situation, this is especially true for PC gamers who are patient. This PC edition of God of War is unquestionably the greatest way to play the game, thanks to better graphics and added features like as ultra-wide support and NVIDIA Reflex for decreased latency, among others. Last but not least, this is a fantastic version of a terrific game, making it an immediate must-have for any PC player looking for an engrossing journey filled with furious fighting and thought-provoking puzzles.God of War for PC is, to put it bluntly, a fantastic version of one of the greatest games to ever grace the PlayStation machine.

_childDocuments_.review: Looking back to 2018 when the game first launched on PS4, God of War was an excellent take on the action-adventure genre and in many ways a much needed change of direction for the series. Fun combat, entertaining characters and a story with a lot of heart - in many ways one of the highlights of that year despite its shortcomings such as lack of enemy/boss variety, tacked on RPG mechanics resulting in much of the equipment suffering from redundancy and even more so it was clearly held back by technical limitations of PS4.That being said PC port obviously isn't drastically different, while it contains the changes that came as post launch patches on console (such as new game+) the main attraction are the technical improvements on PC. There are visual improvements across the board that ultimately make for a much better IQ: Better texture quality, higher resolution shadows, improved AO and SSR alongside with some options such as DLSS, FSR and Nvidia Reflex. But the main difference comes from unlocked framerates, running the game at 120 fps with Reflex enabled for example makes the combat feel considerably more responsive and enjoyable - what also caught me by surprise is that I ended up preferring mouse and keyboard over controller, although it took some amount of rebinding keys as the default keybinds are slightly poorly thought out.In overall GoW is an example of a well made PC port, even though things aren't perfect as there is no FOV slider or exclusive fullscreen mode and there are instances where some areas seem to have been missed on the visual improvements (such as noticeably worse reflections) which create an unfortunate contrast visually. Regardless it is clear that there was an effort made to make this port the definitive version of the game in addition to offering options that target PC enthusiast audience in particular.

_childDocuments_.review: Been gaming since Pong. This is #4 in my GGOAT list.-------------------------------------------------------- How do I keep this short?Presentation is a masterclass, the art direction is jaw dropping, the set pieces redefine the word Epic, etc etc. Nothing new under the sun, this was always the strength of this franchise. However, no one was ready for just how much this new instalment goes beyond merely being "God of War 4". I mean, a mere #4 per-se would probably have been a good game, but here, the formula evolves significantly, and is improved in every respect. We have a great balance between linearity and open world, a more visceral combat system, a greatly improved character progression & build system, superb pacing of the campaign, and even a plot that manages the impossible feat of making Kratos somewhat likeable. One thing that truly blew me away was the pitch perfect tuning of the maximum, "Give me God of War" difficulty setting. This setting manages something so rare I can not even think of any other examples right now: it is balanced for people who are both very skilled AND obsessive completionists. It requires you not only to "get good" - and oh Lord does it require you to get good - but also to hunt every nook & cranny for every bit of XP / loot you can find. Enemies are too deadly to tackle on pure skill, you need every little boost you can get. And no amount of god tier loot will let you cheese / win without also bringing skill to the table. That's like 80-100h of pure beauty + pure challenge for your initial 100% run. But on top of that, the NG+ mode is also great fun. Every enemy is max level, every piece of loot is available to be farmed again in an improved version, and the rock hard toughest bosses you were so proud to finally beat in NG all have new, even harder patterns to master! Bliss.---------------------------------------------------- 10/10 S tier. Perfect for newcomers to the series, and even more perfect for GoW veterans. Thank you Santa Monica.-------------------------------------------------- One item drop is bugged / does not occur in NG+. Do not upgrade the "Grip of Tanngiost" to max in NG. You must bring one "Leiptr Alloy" with you to NG+ if you wish to max the new variant. For every other item in the game, no worries, spend everything in NG, you can find it all again in NG+. Also, note that GmGoW difficulty cannot be downgraded mid-run. By all means try it, it is scrumptious, but be aware it's not for everyone. If the early game drives you crazy, restart.
