_childDocuments_.review: My story with God of War goes WAY back. The year is 2008. I'm staying in class waiting for the 1st lesson to start. Because I lived quite far from school I'd always leave earlier from home and have about 30 minutes or so left before the 1st course would begin. In walks my friend, Vlad with his PSP and a new game in hand. He goes:"Yo bro, guess what I got!"- being all hyped up, I'm like:"Bro I got no clue but do tell u seem ecstatic :D." He just shows me the cd and goes:"I got THE NEW GOD OF WAR: CHAINS OF OLYMPUS!!"- now, I knew of the series cause the first game was released on console was in 2005 and my gaming life started early, having my 1st computer at the age of 3, but not having a console I wasn't able to play it(and probably wouldn't have for at least a few more years, I don't think my parents would've bought me GoW even if we had a console back then xD). Now I'm even happier than he is and and he says:"You wanna give it a try?", and I'm like:"♥♥♥♥ yeah I do :D". I didn't even feel the rest of 25 minutes or so left to our class pass. I was HOOKED. In every break or any second I got left I would just get the PSP out and play. Near the end of the school day he says:"My family and I are taking a 2 day trip over the weekend and I really want you to play the game cuz u look like u love it." - no way, LET'S GO! Over the weekend I finished the game 2 times and come Monday we meet again in class and I give him the psp and now he goes bananas on the game. Around the end of 2010 came GoW: Ghost of Sparta and ofc we played that one too :D. Years go by and I get to play the other games that were on PS, and after that, silence. No news about the franchise. A few more years pass, 2016 comes around and I hear something about a new GoW game, with Cory as the director, and a new direction for the game so I have my hopes sky-high. Then E3 comes around. BOY. OH. BOY. Those 10 minutes of gameplay will always have a special place in my heart. I replayed that clip and the moment when Kratos uses the Spartan Rage countless times waiting for the game to be released. April 2018 comes around and the game is now released, but life gets busy when you are older, so I can't play it, but I watch some gameplay on Youtube and my hype gets increased 10 times which makes me not being able to play the game hurt even more. Almost 3 years later I have to make a choice. I had got a decent budget and I'm stuck between buying a good pc or a PS4. Even tho I really wanted to get a Playstation to play the game and some other exclusive titles for console, after almost a week of thought I decide to get a pc, cuz it will also help me in my IT Department journey. Not long after that, I'm talking with a friend from high school and as we are telling each other what has happened lately, I tell him about my recent purchase and what other option I had and I say something along the lines:"I just wish they would bring God of War to pc as well, that would be really amazing." Not even a week later, I'm in a game of solo ranked in League that I'm losing. As I'm trying to do something, I see 1 of my teammates go afk and another just stops communicating and goes around the map so I give up as well waiting for the enemy team to just finish, since they wouldn't even surrender. Meanwhile, I get a message - guess from who: my friend that from high school and he goes:"Bro u ain't gonna guess what I just saw." - I just go:"No clue bro, but please surpise me. I'm in a League game that feels like hell." - And after this I just see THE MOST UNEXPECTED YET WELCOME MESSAGE SOMEONE COULD'VE SENT ME THAT DAY:"BRO, GOD OF WAR IS COMING TO PC! IT'S ON STEAM RIGHT NOW!!! GO CHECK IT OUT!" - I'm like:"NO. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. WAY.", so I alt/tab out of League and go to Steam. Lo and behold, the news box pops up and the 1st game I see is indeed GOD OF WAR. I sat in awe with enough ecstasy coursing through my veins that could power up 10 rockets for the next hour just looking at the Steam page of the game. My decision to buy the pc suddenly felt like "a sign". It was meant to be <3. For another week I waited to make sure I am not dreaming or anything, and on the 27th of Octomber I pre-ordered the game. On the 14th of January I loaded up the game as soon as I could and I played as much as I could, stacking 70+ hours in just 7 days post-release, and after completing the game 100%(being the first game I ever did) and starting NG+, I feel like I can give a proper review to this masterpiece of a game.Now on the "actual review" of the game:- I loved the story and the reason that made Kratos and Atreus embark on this journey. And when Atreus responds to Freya saying:"It's everything." when she says:"What does this goal mean to you?" made me love the reasoning behind them even more. MASIVE PROPS to Cory Barlog, Christopher Judge(the voice of Kratos), Sunny Suljic(the voice of Atreus), Danielle Bisutti(the voice of Freya), Alastair Duncan(the voice of Mimir) and the rest of the crew for making this story come to life. The way the story unfolds in front of you when Mimir is telling you his tales makes this game feel like a movie at times. Just sit back and enjoy the ride.- The combat is marvelous. With all the skills and and build available you can never run out of thing to try, combos to learn and enemies to slay :D.- Graphics are gorgeous and the scenery is absolutely stunning.- I had no issues regarding performance, played with all settings: Original, High and Ultra, but keep in mind that I this all of this with a NVIDIA 30 series graphics card and an AMD Ryzen 5 processor.- Amazing port, good controls from the get goAll this being said, THANK YOU Cory and Santa Monica for giving us this masterpiece, and blessing my gaming life with this series, Godspeed to you beautiful people. Bring forth Ragnarok :D. And thank you, whoever you are, if u actually gave this whole review a read. You are amazing, have a wonderful life :D

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)God of War, the 2018 reboot of the iconic series, is a transcendent gaming experience that spent 21.5 hours unearthing the depths of Norse mythology. This reinvention of Kratos and his journey is a tour de force in storytelling, gameplay, and emotional depth.One of the most striking aspects of the game is its narrative. Kratos, the former Greek god of war, now embarks on a new adventure in the realm of Norse mythology, alongside his son, Atreus. The story is a masterfully woven tapestry of parenthood, redemption, and grappling with one's violent past. It's a journey that is as much about self-discovery as it is about gods and monsters.The relationship between Kratos and Atreus is at the core of the narrative. It's a portrayal of fatherhood that is both poignant and deeply moving. The way the game explores the complexities of their bond, as well as the secrets of Kratos' past, makes it a storytelling triumph in the world of gaming.Gameplay in God of War is a revelation. The game transitions from the traditional fixed camera and hack-and-slash combat of the original series to a more cinematic, over-the-shoulder perspective. The combat system is visceral and strategic, with a Leviathan Axe that can be thrown and recalled, as well as Atreus' ranged support, adding depth to the battles.The world of God of War is a breathtaking and expansive rendition of Norse mythology. From the towering mountain of Midgard to the realms of Alfheim and Helheim, the game's environments are not just visually stunning but also integral to the narrative. The interconnectedness of the world creates a sense of immersion and adventure rarely seen in video games.The attention to detail in God of War is staggering, both in the environment and the characters. The game's art and character design are a visual feast, and the voice acting is nothing short of exceptional. Christopher Judge's portrayal of Kratos and Sunny Suljic's performance as Atreus are particularly outstanding.Throughout your 21.5-hour journey, you'll encounter challenging enemies and epic boss battles. The sense of accomplishment when overcoming these obstacles is immensely satisfying. God of War strikes a balance between accessibility for newcomers and depth for series veterans.In conclusion, God of War is a monumental achievement in the world of gaming. The reboot takes a beloved character and reinvents him in a way that deepens the narrative and emotional resonance. With 21.5 hours of playtime, you've experienced the full breadth of the game's storytelling, gameplay, and breathtaking world. It stands as a testament to the potential of storytelling in video games, proving that they can be both emotionally gripping and artistically stunning. God of War is a journey that transcends its medium and is a must-play for anyone who appreciates the power of a well-crafted narrative in gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War is an amazing game that is let down by a few things. To start with the positives, the graphics are amazing, some of the best I've seen in any game and it runs really well. I barely noticed any frame drops while playing with the original ps4 graphics. Not only are the graphics really good, the art direction is also amazing, certain scenes framed perfectly with suitable lighting etc... The effort to make the game look like one continuous shot is also admirable, with cutscenes transitioning into gameplay  seamlessly and there are no loading screens unless you die. Although the spots where the game was loading were usually noticeable, playing on an SSD meant they were short.The gameplay is good, but could have been much more engaging. The enemy variety was pretty disappointing and the combat could get pretty repetitive, although without wishing to spoil, it does get better towards the end of the game.The story was really good, even if there were some things that just seemed a bit too convenient but overall it was very enjoyable with enough twists and changes to keep it interesting. God of War does call back to the original 3 games, but doesn't rely too heavily on the players knowledge of them so you don't need to play them beforehand, just a basic knowledge of them should be enough to avoid confusion. The overall story does seem like an excuse to go on a big sightseeing tour, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, although there is a lot of backtracking which can feel like filler as there are some areas that you return to a few too many times in my opinion. There are some light puzzling elements which slow the pace down a bit, but they help to add a bit of downtime between fights. The boss fights were frequent, although some of them could have been better, feeling overly scripted or just underwhelming. The first boss fight was really amazing thoughThe characters were really well written, and felt very believable.I was not a fan of the Rpg elements or the "open world" in God of War. The Rpg elements seemed so unnecessary and the entire levelling system could have been absent and I think the game would be no worse off as it just slowed down the game, it would have probably been better with just a simple upgrade system instead of the other stuff that is there. The open world didn't do much but add time between objectives and other than the few side quests, I never felt the need to explore the areas around me as I wanted to see what happened next in the story.Issues aside, God of War is an undeniably great game that has something for everyone, maybe at the expense of not being very unique. People looking for a good story will find one, people looking for engaging game play will find something, and the people who want to play for the graphics will find plenty to look at. God of War is definitely worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favourite game of all time. This is not just a game, but a work of art. The story is also crafted perfectly and its a very simple one, vis, you are trying to spread the ashes of your wife whose wish was that you (kratos) take your son to the highest peak if all of the realms and spread her ashes, and they have done an amazing job with how the story unfolds and the way other characters weave in to your journey. _childDocuments_.review: The gruff bearded god goes for a ride with his progeny in the worlds of Norse mythology. The duo Kratos/Atreus is the keystone of this software, both from a scenaristic and gameplay point of view. The narration is mastered, the journey is pleasant. We can always quibble about 2 or 3 writing pitfalls, but nothing prohibitive. The only problem is that there are no real stakes and no real antagonist, and the side quests are useless.A demanding and enjoyable combat system: the complementarity between Kratos and his apprentice works like a charm. A big magic axe for the daddy, for the cocoa or that you can throw from far away and get back when you want (great!), you can also throw some good stunning potatoes at the enemy and finish him off with a finish, an equally magic bow for the son. These weapons are also useful for exploration, very clever.This is the only thing that makes the game stand out, the rest of the game is just like the AAA adventure games released in the last years. The formula works, is applied with talent, but remains of an absolute classicism. Except for the central hub (the lake) which gives an illusion of openness, we actually explore a world of corridors, coupled with the impossibility of jumping where we want, it's linear!Fortunately, the good level design mitigates this feeling of compartmentalization, the game encourages a lot of exploration, but the big problem is that all too often the mobs you meet are too strong to be defeated (until a late stage of the story Kratos does too little damage, making any victory impossible), forcing you to postpone it for later: what's the point? There is too much imbalance in difficulty between main quest and side content.The PC port is clean, with beautiful scenery and an unassailable DA, even if we've seen too much of the Vikings universe in the last 10 years, since Skyrim. Incredible performance, the game is entirely in one shot, with loading times cleverly hidden. Supposed to be beautiful, the OST is inaudible as for all current AAA (except at the end where it wakes up)... so I'm sick of it, it's a bad point.Under its prestigious AAA exterior, the game is surprisingly lacking in ambition in what it offers. Few NPCs, only one real world to visit (the others are ridiculously small), a limited bestiary, half the mobs are ugly. The inventory menu lacks ergonomics (too many sub-menus), the map, not very clear, is of no use. Too many chests, too much loot and paradoxically there is always a material missing to make the armor of one's dreams, one gains too many runic attacks, talismans, painful to manage.But in the end, God of War remains a real pleasure to play and despite the few flaws that I mention while remaining as objective as possible, God of War remains a real masterclass with a consequent lifespan (between 40 and 50 hours), but here the qualities erase the flaws. The plot, bitterly resembling a big intro, seems to end where it should start.

I heard that the story is good so I ll manage the gameplay, I said to myself...Not only the story is terrific, but the gameplay is AWESOME. You ll be switching between various weapons and BOYs abbilities on the move, hacking and slashing your way through the realms, but this time not as a madman Kratos, but a calm (comparing to old self at least) and wise Father Kratos.Only thing I dont like about this game, which isnt that big of a problem, is a lack of unique types of bosses. You only have a few unique bosses in the game and later on they become a little repetative and rather easy to handle.All in all, this game is great, but for a 4 year old game (yes its rather new on PC, I know) you shouldnt be paying the full price. Objectively speaking this game should be 30 Euros. Buy it on sale or wait for a price to drop. But if you have money to throw, you wont be disappointed if you invest in this game. Its ton of fun, gameplay is good, story is out of this world (quite literally) and dialogues among characters while you are travelling are quite interesting and well acted. Voice actors did a tremendous job in this game, even the young guy that is voicing the BOY.This is what a true singleplayer expirience should look like. You get a complete game, no paywalls, and most importantly a well written story that leaves place for a sequel and yet it is good as a standalone too. It is not about the destination, its about the journey. Let me tell you, this is by far the most amazing journey i have ever been on.Wholeheartedly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games of all time. After platinuming it on PlayStation, it's still pretty fun to do on PC. Story is amazing. It's the best thing Santa Monica could've done after God of War 3. Kratos and Atreus are both fantastic characters and at their best writing wise in this game. Their character development throughout the game is great. I honestly think this game has a better story and writing than Ragnarok. Gameplay is amazing. It's some of the best gameplay I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing. There's a ton of moves you can pull off, and not only are most, if not all of them useful, but they're so flashy and fun to use. Midgard and the other 5 realms that are available are all very fun to explore. Alfhiem can be annoying gameplay wise, but it still has some incredible story moments that I think make up for the gameplay side. Side missions are great too. A lot of them kind of feel connected to the story with the messages that they convey, and a lot of them end up being mentioned in Ragnarok. The Valkyrie side missions are one of the best side missions of all time, and Sigrun is one of, if not THE best boss fight of all time.Taking both the story and gameplay into consideration, I think this is the best game of all time when it comes to balancing/mixing story and gameplay together. Although I love them, games like The Last of Us and Red Dead Redemption focus too much on their story, leading to (in my opinion) lackluster gameplay. This game puts an equal amount of focus on both the story and gameplay, so you get an amazing, well written story alongside some of the best gameplay of all time. Neither takes up too much time from the game or overshadows the other.Only gripes that I have are that Niflhiem can get a bit grindy and repetitive, and if you're looking to upgrade certain pieces of armor, Musplhiem can get grindy and repetitive as well, but those are both optional side missions. Aside from that the game is pretty much perfect.10/10Can't wait to see more PlayStation exclusives get ported over to PC. It'll be an excuse for me to replay them, and it'll allow PC players to experience some of the best games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War 4 had my attention ever since it was released 4 years ago, but due to it being a PlayStation exclusive at the time, I didn’t get to play it right away. Yet, I was still eager to play it. To be honest I missed the exact point when the port to pc came, so the game lost my focus for a bit. But when the winter sale came around and the sale was presented to me in the prime spot on the front page, I just couldn’t say no.Don’t be scared off by the 4 in the title, it’s no necessity to have played the previous entries of this franchise for you to understand the story. Even without the backstory of Kratos, the story of him and his son is just as touching not knowing what happened to Kratos in Greece. But I do have to admit that some points just hit you way harder when you know the background of some things.In short: I loved the story.You really notice the ammount of effort that Sony Santa Monica put into the characters and dialogue.In the following I will talk about the opening sequence of the game, so if you want to go in completely blind, just skip to the next topicIt is the way the game protrays it's characters and tells it's story, what sets this game apart from others. The best example for this is Faye, Kratos's passed wife and Atreus's mother. You never get to meet her in the game. Neither through a prologe or any flashbacks, yet you get to know her through other people in the world who knew her or when our protagonists talk about her. The further you get in your journey, the better you get to know her. By the end you might even have a picture of her just by the impression she left on the world.Combined with the character development of the whole cast, which doesn't just include the two protagonists, makes this world feel alive. It is seeing brothers grow closer or parents finding lost connections again, that make it feel like this world does not just exist for you to interact with, but it already existed before you and will continue to after your adventure.I think the main story took me about 30 hours to complete if you subtract the time of exploring and doing side-quests in the meanwhile. The side-quests offer an additioal 10 to 15 hours.Since I don't want to spoil any of it, because it is a completely different experience when you go into it blind.On the same notice you have to appreaciate the wonderfully designed world of Midgard and 4 other realms of norse mythology.For those not familiar: Midgard is basically the equivalent to our earth. This is where the main part of the game takes place. Because of that they probably also spent a lot of time on the design of this place. Everywhere you go and every new or hidden area you discover offers stunning visuals and level design. This of course if even more the case in sotry relevant areas since the focus naturally falls on those.Yet, the other realms available to you don't fall far behind in this category. Since I don't want to take too much of the wonder away when setting foot into a new realm, I'll just discuss two of the realms here.The first additional realm you visit is Alfheim. Mianly being lived in by both light and dark elves, it doesn't pose such a great look when you first visit it, but when you leave you get to see a lightfilled world full of life. Even though later on there is little reason to return here except for the valkyries(we'll get to that later), I did a couple times just to take in the magnificent visuals of this place.While you could say that the fighting-system has a bit of a souls-like flare, it yet differs greatly from it. You don't have acces to as many options to defeat your enemies as you might see in other games in terms of weapon variety. After all you just have 3 ways to kill your enemies really. You have the leviathan axe, your fists and another element I will not discuss because of spoiler reasons. Additionally, you can choose between runic attacks, which are more powerful attacks using magic with a cooldown and other skills you can unlock though the skill tree. You also have a rage meter that fills up over time. When activated, you change to your fists and start hammering away at your opponents. This fills up your health and deals significant ammounts of damage. But Kratos himself is no the only one on the battlefield.Atreus poses another big facotr in the combat of God of War. He helps defeat Enemies by stunning them or summoning powerfull spirits. He is even able to interrupt some of the attacks stronger foes throw at you later in the game. This becomes particularly important in the fight against some of the optional end-game bosses.While the game is not as hard as some other titles it is especially crucial on the higher difficulties to master all the aspects of God of wars combat to defeat your foes.While the enemies start off as challenging and varying, they become more and more repetetive later one, since they stop introducing new enemy types at about the mid point of the game.Since we're already on the topic of repetitive enemies, I have to mention the trolls. The first boss type enemy you fight in the tutorial area is one of these trolls. If you have seen the gameplay trailer, you probably know which I mean. While this first encounter is fun and also challenging at times, this fight repeats itself throughout the game over and over again. Even though the appearance of the trolls get varied slightly over the different encounters, the moveset stays mostly the same. This appears all the more disappointing when you take into account that the previous titles of the series was all the more remarkable.Yet, there is a perfect example that you can also handle this incredibly better in the same game.The Valkyries are a set of bosses seperate from the main story line. They are spread over the realms with different levels each. So there are some you can fight early on but for some you should wait until later on in the game. Although in this case they are all of the same enemy type as well, they all pose a unique boss fight, since every Valkyrie holds another exclusive attack, which brings a challenging change into these boss fights. This can also be said about the final of these challenging bosses, because she not only deals incredible ammounts of damage and is the highest level enemy you will encounter in the game, but combines all the moves mastered by the others.This poses a very challenging boss fight and combines all that you have learned in the previous fights.I had a blast with the game. At the time of writing this, I have spent about 50 hours with the game and have aquired all achievements. Yet, I plan on completing the game on "give me god of war" next. This is the game's highest difficutly in which it kinda breaks it's own rules just to mess with the player and provide one of the most challenging expirences I have played yet.The movie worthy story is masterfully written, with seeing this father and son duo growing together, being worthy of the Game of the year award it won back when it came out.I can only recommend to play it if you are at the slightest interested in story games or just wants a challenging combat experience or just to explore this wonderful world.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War is a beautifully crafted third person action game that continues Kratos’ story among a new pantheon. If you have ANY inclination to buy it, then do it. You will not be disappointed.  Goodness where to begin. This game is  God of War see's a more grizzled Kratos in a new land, years after the events of God of War 3. Here he has settled among the Norse mythology, hiding his past and daring to start a new life, and even starting a family and having a son named Atreus. Alas, The opening is a somber one as your first actions as Kratos are to cut down the necessary trees to build a pyre for your deceased wife. It was her final wish that her ashes be spread from the highest mountain in the realm, and this is the vehicle for the whole story.Whereas previous God of War games were tales of a bloody path of rage fueled vengeance, this story is an adventure between a father and his son (who are barely antiquated thanks to Kratos’s preference for seclusion) working to fulfill the last request of a woman they both loved. In that way the story focuses on similar subjects as older games (the relationship between parents and their children, vengeance, and the cruelty of the gods) but from a completely different perspective, both literally, and metaphorically. The game now takes an over the shoulder third person camera, not dissimilar to a Gears of War game, tightening the focus on enemies in your line of sight. Kratos no longer fights with his iconic Blades of Chaos but instead wields the Leviathan Axe which is not just brutal weapon of slaughter, but the primary tool for solving puzzles. Much like Thor’s Mjolner, the Leviathan Axe can be thrown and “summoned” which causes it to come spinning back to Kratos’s hand, allowing to to strike enemies both ways.This functionally changes much of the games principle encounters over older games where the Chains of Chaos offered brutal AOE damage, the Leviathan Axe is a thinking man’s tool. Enemies can be tripped by flinging the axe with a light attack at their feet, knocking them to the ground and causing a great deal of stun. Kratos can use a heavy throw on an enemies head to freeze them in place, effectively removing them from the fight, and all the while the axe is out Kratos’s hands he can use a series of brutal punches and kicks to bludgeon enemies.The aforementioned stun mechanic is also built up much quicker with punches and once the stun meter fills Kratos can execute in an often gory cinematic take down. Atreus can fire his bow at whatever enemy Kratos is facing multiple times, dealing increased stun damage and making these takedowns that much easier to execute. Atreus himself is largely invisible as a combatant. Enemies may go after him but for the most part Kratos will be the focus of their ire, allowing Atreus to dart around taking pot shots until his arrow attacks are called, for and calling out attacks that are coming towards Kratos from off camera.  As the game progresses, so do both Kratos and Atreus’s abilities, including combo’s that happen impromptu in the middle of the battles. One such combo that will occur will cause Atreus to leap off of Kratos’s back and reign a barrage of arrows down on enemies if you tell him to fire. Other times Atreus might sneak up and start choking out an enemy with his bow, giving Kratos an opening for a charged heavy hit to split them wide open. Learning how to do these combos, and executing them at the right times are all part of a system that is immediately accessible to players new to the franchise, and impressively deep for those DMC SSS combo practitioners. Runic Attacks are special attacks Kratos can execute which sit on a cooldown. There are several types of these (20 or more perhaps) and each has it’s own little utility that makes it usable in a given situation. Some will cause massive stun while another might freeze enemies immediately around Kratos, where a third might deal giant chunks of damage to a single target. When combat isn’t happening the other half the game focuses on exploration and puzzle solving and does it as well, if not better, than the combat half. It’s more difficult to talk about these parts of the game without spoiling much, but I have never played a game who’s puzzle design is so brilliantly interwoven with it’s level design.Again, I wish to spoil next to nothing with details but the layout and pathing of each level is a joy to experience. Branching halls and hidden chests abound, there is not an ounce of wasted space when navigating the beautifully rendered environments. Dozen’s of “ah-ha!” puzzles and secrets and sights await. Oh yes, the game has a story too. A long one, which I reckon would clock in around 20 hours if I skipped a good chunk of side content. Would you believe me if I said it was also as good as the combat and level design? It is, but the less said there the better. This is an adventure game, and the fun comes from experiencing it, not reading about it. I will say, I was surprised at how genuinely funny the game could be for  one who’s predecessors mostly focused on lots of shouting and dismemberment, and virtually nothing else.If God of War has any faults it is these. 1. There’s to much game here. 2. It ends to soon. If you made it through this whole review, the former will not be an issue for your.If it isn't my 2022 PC GOTY, then I'm in for an excellent year.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War (2018), also known as God of War 4, is a game that has the potential to revolutionize the gaming industry and set it apart from the rest of the field.God of War features breathtaking visuals which push the PlayStation 4 console to its boundaries. The game is set in Norse mythology, and the surroundings are stunningly produced, ranging from lush woods and towering mountains to labyrinthine caves and fantastical worlds. With rich textures, realistic lighting effects, and magnificent landscapes that immerse players in the game's environment, the attention to detail is excellent. Character models are very detailed, with lifelike emotions, fluent actions, and elaborate armour and weaponry. The graphic quality and art design of the game work together to provide a visually stunning and engaging experience.God of War 4's gameplay departs significantly from its predecessors while preserving the spirit of the franchise. The battle mechanics are rich and engaging, allowing players to chain strong strikes, combos, and magical powers together. The game also includes RPG aspects like as character growth, weapon upgrades, and a skill tree, allowing players to tailor Kratos' powers to their preferences. Furthermore, God of War features puzzle-solving and exploration components, rewarding players with hidden treasures, knowledge, and mysteries as they travel the gorgeously constructed universe.Overall, God of War 4 is an outstanding game that excels in aesthetics, gameplay, and plot, it comes highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, first off, the game looks great, and is pretty well optimized. It runs pretty well for a Playstation port. I run almost everything on "Original" (basically Normal) and get around an average of 80fps on my meager 1070ti. Also has no micro-transactions (as of the time of writing this), so that's also a plus. The story-telling is pretty good as well. You actually see progress in Kratos and Atreus and they don't stay the same throughout the game. The visuals, despite me only playing at "Original" look fantastic and are a shining example of how every console port should be done. I do have some gripes about the game though. This game is BLISTERINGLY HARD. Like, I've only played the first 5 minutes or so of Dark Souls and I've never played Bloodborne, but this game kind of reminds me of what it must feel like to play those games. It feels like you do next-to-no damage to hit-sponge enemies, meanwhile, you take ♥♥♥♥-TONS of damage, no matter the amount of armor or upgrades you invest in (I'm only playing on "Give Me a Balanced Experience" (Basically Normal) but I'm routinely getting my ass kicked by even fodder enemies. I've tried using all the tools the game has given me, but none seem to keep me alive long enough to progress without immense frustration. The control scheme also makes Kratos feel weighty and hard to maneuver, making an already difficult game even harder. This game runs beautifully and is well optimized, but if you're looking for a game with a similar difficulty to Normal on the original God of War trilogy with better story-telling, this game will only fufill the later of those too.To summerize:Positives:-Well Optimized-Looks Great on Any Graphical Setting-Story-Telling and Character Development is GreatNegatives:-Too Difficult, Even at Lower Difficulties-Combat System Feels Sluggish and Makes Combat HarderConclusion: If you're looking for a God of War that is harder than the original with better story-telling and actual character development, then this game is great for you. If you'd rather just be told a story and not have to worry about trying to get good at the combat, I can't recommend this game. Maybe I'm just too old, but this game has no right to be this difficult.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is an interesting well written story.  I'm over 25 hours into play.  My main dislike with the game is that at least 5 hours of that is half play/half cutscenes where you have to sit and hold the controller forward and watch your character walk very slowly.  There is very little dialog to keep you interested and they drag on way too long.  Then there are actual cutscenes like riding very slowly in a boat for 20 minutes or watching the characters talk and having to press a button every 5 minutes to keep the scene moving.  Of course there are also cutscenes travelling in elevators that go on for way too long.  These things completely take me out of the game and can be extremely frustrating because the amount of time I have to play is limited.Update:  Finished the game.  The story was incredibly well written, but the game is just not well designed.  The combat is clunky and over-complicated.  The map is useless for navigation.  The fast travel even forces you to run long distances instead of just taking you from one point to the next.  There are multiple open door/chest mechanics that require you to get a certain item before you can open them, but these chests and doors are in even the very first area forcing backtracking for no real reason.  Of the 9 realms, 4 don't unlock until after you beat the game.  Two of those don't unlock unless you start a new game plus.  There is nothing interesting in them.  Just areas to grind for more armor after you've already finished the game.  A+ for the writers.  F- for the developers.

_childDocuments_.review: Boy! Read this!God of war is amazing! I played the original trilogy and was excited to finally play this game now that it's on PC. There is something about this game that the creators did so right, it brings out an anger in me while playing it, the good kind of anger and it manifests at the same time that Kratos rages and then beats the snot out of the enemy during a provoking cut scene. The puzzles are unique and sometimes had me stumped sometimes a little longer than I would like to admit, but it was never too hard or easy of a puzzle. The designs of the puzzles feel fun to complete especially when the two brain cells finally get it and everything falls into place.The graphics look great, and the environment is fun to explore. I was always happy to come back and revisit old areas when I earned new weapons that opened previously locked chests and paths. The story is compelling and it always felt like I had a good reason for what I was doing next, but also giving plenty of chances to go side questing without seeming like it didn't make sense.The weapons are fun to use and satisfying when you get a kill animation or a perfect parry. The game also allows you to build for straight damage, stun, or runic attacks which is nice to have the custom ability that wasn't seen in the original trilogy.I think the best part of God of War are the characters, especially the relationship between Kratos and Atreus. The conversations between the two feel like real people with real problems and not a poorly written script. We also see great character development not only in both Kratos and Atreus, but also smaller side characters such as the Dwarven brothers that makes the progress throughout the story all the more satisfying.A couple of minor downsides I feel that are worth mentioning is that first, if you're not using a controller and are rebinding controls for mouse and keyboard, there are certain buttons such as 2 that aren't initially bound to anything because it's for something later in the game, but if you rebind something to one of these buttons it resets all of your bindings without telling you what isn't working or why. This isn't game breaking but it was a little frustrating when I was adjusting bindings in the beginning. Another minor problem I had is that the field of view is not adjustable, it's pretty close and you can mostly only see over Kratos' right shoulder, limiting your view a bit. A friend says it's to add to the challenge, but to me if that's the case why isn't it at least an option to adjust it just like the difficulty setting? Again these are just minor complaints I think were at least worth a mention and do not break or ruin the game.The game is overall amazing and I Highly recommend this game especially for people that enjoy story driven games with compelling characters and also wish they could drop a skyscraper onto their enemies when things don't go their way. Can't wait to play Ragnarok!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a short review based mostly on the console version, but also having made sure that it seems to be running decently on my PC. And according to most outlets and groups that have delved a lot deeper into the performance side of things it seems to be a pretty great port overall. In terms of the game itself, in short it's a pretty great reboot to the God of War series. I never really liked the original God of War games since I found them pretty button-mashy action games. More often than not the game turned very mindless in how much you have to spam attacks. That's the thing this reboot adjusts, making the action more mindful and less button-mashy. Animations, both yours and the enemies', have a longer windup which means you have to take greater care with the timing of it all.In terms of gameplay systems the game plays very much like a metroidvania game where you explore a hub-based "open-world", with a little itemization and abilities/skills to unlock. And you use various abilities which you unlock across the story to be able to access newer and newer areas. It's all very satisfying and enjoyable. The story is decent enough, but where it shines is the acting of most of the characters. The acting, the animation and the photorealistic character models really gets you hooked. Some of them are really impressive, especially later on. And I hear there are plenty of emotional hooks for people that played there original games. Suffice to say, most of those have gone over my head, I think.Other things left to mention, I guess are the various set pieces you encounter. Most of them are pretty incredible in terms of scale and location. Most of the locations are also especially beautiful, with gorgeous scenery. The whole game is a real treat for the eyes. And shockingly, it has native support for ultra-wide resolutions. So no needing to browse the internet for fan hacks that enable it.It's also a pretty chunky game from what I remember, taking around 60-80h if I remember correctly, but I enjoyed it most of the time. If you're a completionist and want to unlock and collect everything (plus I seem to remember it also has an end-game item grind system which I never bothered much with) it can surely take you a lot more. But I think I didn't want to drag out the ending more than it was needed. Maybe on a second playthrough if I ever get the chance. To conclude, I'd score it at a 8.5/10. It's a very competent AAA game with plenty to offer. And hopefully a sign of other great games that Sony might want to bring over. I'm still waiting for The Last of Us and Bloodborne on PC! It's been 6 years years already Sony! :(

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really fun and fast paced third person action game with a lot of depth (maybe a bit too much, Kratos has a move list deeper than some fighting game characters) to the controls, weapons, abilities and ways you can fight. That allows for a ton of variety in how you approach fights and allows for a range of enemies to always keep you on your toes. I couldn't handle the finger gymnastics to play with a controller so I switched to a keyboard and mouse it worked perfectly.The exploration parts are my favorite part of the game. It's like a Zelda-lite with a hub overworld that's done in a really cool way and lots of secret passages to explore and non-story related areas to wander around.The story is pretty good but not the twistiest or best compared to some other games. It's all presented extremely well though, with awesome set piece battles and normal fights that feel like set piece battles. If you like fast action games this one is a great one!A few nitpicks:- You can’t sprint while locked on.- The target lock doesn’t automatically go to next enemy. Although once I switched to keyboard + mouse I stopped using the lock on and it was less of an issue then.- The camera is in really tight and the “they’re right behind you” arrows don’t always account for attacks from the sides.- You never get to see Baldur's Gate 😉

_childDocuments_.review: This game is extremely fun, but please do not set it to the hardest difficulty unless you're extremely sweaty or you have the patience of a monk. I'm already 51.4 hours in and I'm just now at the fight with Modi and Magni. Overall though the game is insanely fun and the weapons, abilities, and whatnot are really cool. The combat is kind of annoying sometimes, especially while playing on the hardest difficulty. Each enemy requires a certain strategy for defeating them however, more often than not, you'll have to constantly fight more than one type of enemy. Each one requiring a different strategy than the other. While you're focusing on an Ogre, for example, 7 Reavers just destroy you in 1 hit. It's annoying, on the hardest difficulty at least, but the game overall is very enjoyable and easy to get lost in.Edit: I've put in right at almost 86 hours of playtime and I'm at, what I assume to be, the final boss fight with Baldur. The game has been very fun, however this final fight represents my gripes with the combat in this game a lot. If I attack Baldur with a certain move, such as the move where Kratos slams his axe down three times for the heavy runic attack, I'll get locked into that animation. This is problematic because Baldur loves to switch tactics in the blink of an eye. One moment he'll be right in front of me, then I'll use the axe slam attack, and then he'll quickly jump in the air and slam down on me while I'm still locked into the axe slam animation. I've also noticed that when he does that jump attack, if you're close enough to it, when you try to roll away for some reason the game pulls you towards the area where Baldur slams down. The constant stun locking is annoying in other ways too because you might be fast enough to react to his attacks, but that doesn't matter when you keep getting stun locked every 5 seconds. It's easy to say "hurr durr skill issue." but I've played on only Give Me God of War difficulty and this is my first playthrough, so I must be semi-decent at it. I can't be the only one who's felt annoyed about that part of the combat. But overall the game has been really fun and it's been cool trying to get through each combat challenge.

Set aside to cool slightly for 15 mins.STEP 3Using an electric hand whisk, mix in 150g light brown soft sugar, then 3 large eggs, one at a time, followed by ½ tsp vanilla extract and finally 50g plain flour. Can be cooked straight from frozen for 16 mins, or bake now for 10-12 mins until the tops are firm to the touch but the middles still feel squidgy.STEP 5Carefully run a knife around the edge of each pudding, then turn out onto serving plates and serve with single cream.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall pretty good game, but story-wise your character is actually a god of STUPIDSome criticism on gameplay (from 1st playthrough Give me God of War Difficulty):- The third-person right-shoulder shooter camera doesn't really fit a hack-n-slash game. The game would be more fair and fun to the player if the camera was at least more wide in FOV.- The shield basic enemy is actually busted af just because if you are attacking someone and you accidently happen to hit them, your attacks just bounce back and you briefly flinch from that reflect. The amount of zoning they have (especially later on) is just way too much. I'm almost sure this was not intended and they wanted you to get pass the shield in a 1v1, not zone you constantly.- Enemy Devil Trigger is insanely fast, I like challenge but it would just be more fun if it was tuned downed slightly (like limiting how many enemies can do it or giving you more time to stop it).- The boss fights are overall just good enough. Nothing too interesting, nothing too boring- With the exception of Dark Elf which is badly designed imo. You are punished for parrying.- Atreus can get annoying in fight call-outs- The game may or not be so balanced early-game on Give me God of War difficulty

They really know what they're doing when it comes to optimization. I consistently got ~90fps with my 2080 super, using ultra settings. Truly gripping story, amazing graphics, satisfying and just challenging enough combat. That feeling when you get a new upgrade for your axe and  and go "Oh, I can go back here and unlock this area and do these things now!" is so pleasing. There's no open world just for the sake of an open world, but the open-ish zones are fun (and gorgeous) enough to go explore and solve puzzles for a bit. I used to be a slave to Ubisoft's overstuffed open-world games, but God of War set me free. I don't want to play another Far Cry, Ghost Recon, or post-Syndicate AC game ever again.Honestly, this game made me enjoy games again. I had been feeling like I've just been going through the motions with gaming lately, but I was excited to finish work and play this game because I WANTED to, not because I needed to occupy my free time with something. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough review to write because reading all the glowing reviews from consumers and in media, I feel like something must be wrong with me, but I did not enjoy most of my time with this game. It's beautfiully presented with some of the best graphics I've ever seen and all the actors do a very good job with their characters, but I'm here to play a game, not watch a movie and as a game this just falls painfully short. First, this game loves long repetitive animations and it's going to make you sit through every single one everytime you do anything. At around the 15 hour mark I just wanted to stop opening chests all together. Combat is clunky and difficulty is all over the place. There's a side quest with a series of 9 boss fights that will challenge you, but the rest of the game is surprisingly easy. Then there's the grind. There are two fully optional realms that are designed as challenges. They're silly, they're out of place, they waste the potential of these realms and the grind is so slow in one realm that it probably represented 5 or more hours of my final play time and it was not fun. The world is full of repetitive puzzles and lots of backtracking as certain events happen. Even the main story itself doesn't get going until the end and WOW, that end. It felt like the game was just getting started, there's an interesting reveal and then roll credits. It was so abrupt and the game teases a handful of realms and characters that you never even get to see. If this game didn't have the optional grind realms, if it didn't slow everything to a crawl with it's sluggish movement and combat, and if it didn't have the damage spunge enemies, there really isn't a whole lot to the main experience. This is my first God of War game being a PC only gamer and I'm just not getting what the fuss is all about. It was an excellent looking brawler with mediocre combat and all I see are 5/5 and 10/10 reviews. And the interface, ugh. Don't get me started on the interface. It's one of the slowest, most unintuitive and ugly interfaces I've seen in a while. It has none of the character of the setting of the game and it looks like some cheap mobile design. Maybe at some point I'll have a change of heart, maybe I'll appreciate it more when and if I get to play the sequel, but this game just didn't do much for me. To be fair I seem to be in a small minority here, so your mileage may vary, but I'm here to give you my honest opinion and when it was all said and done, this wasn't the experience I'd been waiting for all these years.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War is a masterpiece of storytelling, action and exploration. The game follows the journey of Kratos, a former Greek god of war, and his son Atreus, as they venture into the realm of Norse mythology. The game is set years after Kratos’ vengeance against the gods of Olympus, and he now lives as a man in a harsh and unforgiving world. He must teach his son to survive and fight, while also dealing with his own rage and past.The game is visually stunning, with high fidelity graphics that enhance the beauty and brutality of the Norse world. The game supports true 4K resolution, on supported devices, with unlocked framerates for peak performance. The game also offers a wide range of graphical options to customize your experience, such as higher resolution shadows, improved screen space reflections, GTAO and SSDO, and more.The game is also a joy to play, with visceral and physical combat that challenges you to use your skills and strategy. You can use Kratos’ new main weapon, the Leviathan Axe, which can be thrown and recalled at will, as well as his fists and shield. You can also command Atreus to assist you in combat with his bow and arrows, or use his abilities to stun or distract enemies. The game features a variety of enemies, from draugrs and trolls to dragons and valkyries, each with their own strengths and weaknesses. The game also has epic boss battles that test your limits.The game is not just about combat, though. It is also about exploration and discovery. You can travel across nine realms of Norse mythology, each with their own secrets and surprises. You can find hidden chests, collectibles, lore markers, side quests, puzzles and more. You can also upgrade your gear, skills and abilities by using resources and currency found in the world. The game has a lot of content and replay value, as you can unlock new areas and challenges after completing the main story.The game is also a powerful emotional journey, with a compelling story and characters. The game explores the themes of fatherhood, family, identity, redemption and fate. The game has excellent voice acting, motion capture and facial animation that bring the characters to life. The game also has a dynamic and immersive soundtrack that matches the mood and tone of the game.God of War is a game that deserves all the praise and awards it has received. It is a game that will stay with you long after you finish it. It is a game that you should not miss. It is a game that I highly recommend to anyone who loves action, adventure and storytelling.**If you're a 3070 user, lower your Target Power and Temperature to enjoy the game without any noise from the fans.**

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.I mean it: *wow*This is one of those rare games that transcends its medium, and just is an amazing story and experience no matter what. That it's also a fun and exciting game with great combat mechanics, amazing environments and fun challenges and puzzles, that's just the cherry on top. This game is *good*, full-stop.It manages to avoid so many popular gaming tropes, while delivering a deeper and more emotional story than the 10 next-best games put together. You can genuinely relate to this simple story of a dad and his son coming to terms with tho they are, even while they are demi-gods fighting monsters and flying through the air on gigantic snakes. I honestly have a hard time finding the words to really describe the experience, it is one you have to have yourself to know what it really is like.Suffice to say, even without all of that, this is a truly top-tier, solid game that never stops being fun and exciting, and that even beyond the 20-30 hour main story offers a surprisingly large amount of separate stories, challenges, quests, adventures and experiences. Get this if you have any interest whatsoever in fantastic single-player games, no matter what you think of this type of fighting game.Yes, it really is that good.

_childDocuments_.review: Story: 10/10 - fantastic story with lovable characters, side plots, and fun lore.Gameplay: 10/10 - every attack makes you feel like the god of war, complemented with fluid combat movement and unlockable skillsUI/UX: 5/10 - The majority of the UI/UX is fine, and most players may not take issue with it. Read below for more.The UI/UX gets a harsh rating from me for the 2 (personal/preference-based) reasons below. 1. The Map (7/10) - Works well for the most part, and I don't think most players will take issue with it. However, I HATE it when maps refuse to let you zoom in further into the map. When exploring, I found myself disoriented (direction wise) quite often. If I could've zoomed in further, I think I would not have been as frustrated when exploring. Again, most players will find the map fine, just my 2 cents. Other than that, the map is pretty informative2. Picking up Items (3/10) - This is my biggest issue with the UX. When you pick up rare resources (i.e. Asgardian steel) or equippable items, the game displays a small prompt on the screen telling you what item you picked up and a short description of it. The absolute worst part about this is that it's a prompt that takes 2-4s to animate completely (when it opens to when it closes) PER ITEM. While that's a short amount of time, these kinds of interface decisions absolutely ruin the looting aspect for me and it will ALWAYS frustrate me. To be dramatic and exaggerative, I can't understand how a group of people decided this was even acceptable UX. In GoW Ragnarok, this has been removed (or at least significantly shortened to the point where I don't even realize the prompt was even there). It would be great if they could this (and any other QoL updates) to GoW 4 as well.

Kratos is still at confict with his former self though, until the end of the game. God Of War is game that is one of a kind, and the likes of which I have never experienced before. The game has  and also many different realms for you to explore.You can upgrade your gear this time around and you have a new weapon, . It's an axe that can freeze enemies or objects in place. You can explore more this time around, in hopes of finding , or better items and character upgrades.  are resources that are spent on character upgrades for both Kratos and Atreus. _childDocuments_.review: This was an interesting experience for me, it is definitely a fantastic game yet it is overrated IMO.- First of all, they say the story is amazing, yet I did not find it that much, especially after the first cheap plot twist on the top of the mountain.  C'mon, that is like the cheapest trick in the book. If you do not know the Norse Gods and that world, the story is missing a lot of points for you, they are talking about some other ones, who they are where they are, what happened, etc, you have no idea. Yet, it is not that crucial for this game, because it is mostly focused on Kratos and Atreus, and their relationship. Btw, the story is pretty good, but it is not God-like as how everybody talks about it. Probably one of the reasons why people feel like that is not being able to skip, you have to see all. And the storytelling, camera angles, and everything sells this pretty well. But I think the most important aspect is having a single camera, no cutscenes, no waiting for loading, etc. It increases the immersion, and you feel like you are in the action all the time. That is revolutionary for me, this is the thing that mesmerized me. Maybe it is because I am also a developer, and thinking about the technical side of it made me feel so good. Of course, it comes with some side effects like you have to travel a lot by foot or boat, fast travel cannot work as we used to in other games, and going from one realm to another takes a lot of time. But still, they tried to fill those times with some conversation and some details with the story, etc. So it is alright.- I like grinding and treasure hunts, scavenging to find the best possible combo for gears, selling the weaker ones, and making more money to get better things, etc. In this game, it is not that important and I did not feel like I should do it at all. It is not something bad or good, it is just my preference. I would love to have a lot of options so I would go after those favors, treasure maps, etc. But just following the main story is enough to get the necessary level of gear to finish the game.- The feeling of combat is pretty good, I really enjoyed it although there are a lot of repetitive animations when it comes to bosses. I do not like having way many different ways of fighting, like press this while doing that, and then do this... It is not my thing so I like to find the ones that are easy to use and effective enough, and keep using these till the end. Yet I enjoyed the battle, I cannot imagine the joy someone who likes to learn them all and use them all gets. I died a lot while having balanced gameplay, I do not even think I would try anything more difficult than this. I simply would not be able to survive. - Puzzles are enough, not that hard but sometimes not easy to detect the objects around. I like how they hide things above tho, I think it is a nice way of reminding players to look up, not just front. - I think the overall menu and especially the map are terrible.Would I play it again, I do not think so. Would I try to finish the side quests etc, I do not think so. In the end, I am happy for playing and finishing the game. It is an amazing game, yet I think it is overrated.

I also found a couple of armor pieces about half way through that carried me almost to the very end.Combat system is... meh for me.  Fun, but not engaging enough to make me want to do NG+.  I found the camera frustrating, because Kratos's giant body covers 25% of the screen. Really wish I could pull that camera back a little.Beat 3 Valkyries, but didn't feel compelled to fight the others for a challenge.  Yes, these fights are tough, but they didn't encourage me to try new things.  I ended up just learning the patterns, figuring out positioning, punishing openings, and avoiding mistakes... and then I realized this was a Souls battle at heart, and that's just not what I wanted from this game.

_childDocuments_.review: To start with a recollection, I grew up playing the first couple God of War's on PS2 years back and thoroughly enjoying them especially since I've always had a liking to Greek/Norse mythology etc. even though the combat in those old ones could be pretty unforgiving to me(hate Souls-like games sorry...). So when I finally got the opportunity to play Santa Monica's new rendition of another God of War, with an over-the-shoulder viewpoint, I was even more excited. Back to present; after having played THIS one for a pretty hefty 60 some hours as of this review I can confidently say 2018's God of War is one of the greatest achievements video games will ever offer. The game plays out like a movie(everyone knows about the one-take throughout) but it's more in the story and characters that the game may shine the most and make most sense. Whether it's Kratos/Atreus family dynamic as they venture from one land to another, the bantering of dwarves Brok and Sindri, or the psychotic meltdowns of the cursed and villainous Baldur. And don't even get me started on the more polished combat/gameplay. The game is just more fun this way. Less ferocious, less demanding, and much more story-driven. The way Kratos glides and sways with his Leviathan Axe and Blades of Chaos is more artlike rather then button-smashy.To be honest there is still a good amount of content left for me to finish but I can easily say this game hit me in every way a video game. Just a great piece of art. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: My name is Walter Hartwell White. I live at 308 Negra Arroyo Lane, Albuquerque, New Mexico, 87104. This is my confession. If you're watching this tape, I'm probably dead– murdered by my brother-in-law, Hank Schrader. Hank has been building a meth empire for over a year now, and using me as his chemist. Shortly after my 50th birthday, he asked that I use my chemistry knowledge to cook methamphetamine, which he would then sell using connections that he made through his career with the DEA. I was... astounded. I... I always thought Hank was a very moral man, and I was particularly vulnerable at the time – something he knew and took advantage of. I was reeling from a cancer diagnosis that was poised to bankrupt my family. Hank took me in on a ride-along and showed me just how much money even a small meth operation could make. And I was weak. I didn't want my family to go into financial ruin, so I agreed. Hank had a partner, a businessman named Gustavo Fring. Hank sold me into servitude to this man. And when I tried to quit, Fring threatened my family. I didn't know where to turn. Eventually, Hank and Fring had a falling-out. Things escalated. Fring was able to arrange – uh, I guess... I guess you call it a "hit" – on Hank, and failed, but Hank was seriously injured. And I wound up paying his medical bills, which amounted to a little over $177,000. Upon recovery, Hank was bent on revenge. Working with a man named Hector Salamanca, he plotted to kill Fring.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War takes God of War, mixes it with Norse Mythology and adds a new perspective to it, as well as changing the lore behind the Aesir, and other Norse creatures a little bit (read in the spoiler section).While it's known that Thor, Odin and most other Aesir are arrogant bastards, here you will experience a brand new view from the other side. Combat is smooth, sound design is S+, the characters have depth. Overall, without giving any spoilers I will absolutely recommend this game, if you enjoy Norse Mythology in the slightest!Baldur in Norse Mythology embraces his new gift of invulnerability - here he wants to kill Freya for it. Loki is absent from the lore entirely, until the very end. Jörmungandr definitely does not approve of others, regardless of who they are.Mimir was beheaded by the Vanir, and remained a loyal friend to Odin until Ragnarök.And a lot moreNow - if you're a fan of Norse Mythology, like me, reading this might make you shiver, but don't worry - it's executed really well. Mimir still serves his purpose, Baldur is made extremely interesting, the big Loki moment will get you jumpy, etc., etc.Personally I have two issues with the game however:1. Alfheim took way too long. It was so much mindless fighting into the same one or two enemies over and over again that it became very stale. 2. Atreus after learning that he was a god, became a power hungry, arrogant ass. So far so good - however it ended way too abruptly. You arrive in Helheim, Kratos tells him off once, and that's that. He's just made a huge leap in character development and became wise. Still, that's 2 things out of probably 30 I really enjoyed. Combat is very smooth, the sound design is great, the characters (albeit lore inaccurate) are very charming in their own ways, and after beating Baldur for the last time you don't feel hate - you understand that he is a broken god that lived through torment. He was very compassionate towards Freya at first, as you can see in Helheim. He was no monster. My absolute favorite bit though was Jörmungandr.The sound design was astonishingly well done - the first time shocked me, the second time I thought I remember how unsettling his voice was until I felt uneasy again, the third time I just accepted that I would fall back into my chair slightly. 8.5/10 Alfheim really annoyed me, and there could have been more characters. Though I 100% understand that that was saved for Ragnarök :')

_childDocuments_.review: A great successor to the original God of War trilogy. Although still a hack and slash, combat is certainly different. Captures the father/son adventure very well. As much as I enjoyed this game, I did have a few issues with it. Dialogue would sometimes be a bit buggy, xp gains snowballed and I didn't have much to spend it on -- this could've been remedied with 1-2 more optional weapons I think. Enemy variety at the beginning is pitiful. Boss variety is pretty bad, most bosses are repeats of the same moveset you'll have seen earlier in the game just with different quirks like different models or elements. The map could be a bit more informative.Not many protagonists have the luxury of getting sequels in the future after their saga already ends. This was a fantastic continuation of the series that felt like a genuine continuation of Kratos. The swap from greek to norse mythology fit way more than I would think. The leviathan axe and shield will slowly grow on you as being fitting for this new setting, and an older Kratos. A good bit of optional content, and even a couple optional endgame grinds you can do. Very pretty, with decent combat, and the best story the series has seen thus far. Emotional, cinematic, and rewarding -- this was a great pleasure to see to the end. It started off as a slow burn and I wasn't too hooked for a while, but I'm glad I gave this a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a best-in-class entry for sure. For context, I loved the original GoW trilogy and it was hugely technically impressive, but tonally it kind of left things to be desired from my perspective. Kratos was a bit one-dimensional, the game used brutality and gore as a spectacle without any real meaning, women were utilized almost exclusively for "bedroom" minigames or as dead bodies for solving puzzles, stuff like that. Not things that were a huge deal for me, but they did leave a bit of a sour taste in my mouth.This title somehow manages to shed these weaknesses and strike a much more mature and emotional tone, while still feeling faithful to the heart of the original three. it pays constant homage to Kratos's journey, but is completely narratively accessible to someone who never played the original trilogy. It brings new depth to Kratos's personality, and tackles his failures without trying to walk back anything from the past installments. Kratos has grown old, his life has deeply affected him, and everyone around him - especially the people he grows to love - is impacted by the baggage he has carried over from Greece.If I had been granted absolute creative freedom in writing a new Kratos who both felt like the same person but could also be a wise and sympathetic protagonist, I wouldn't even know where to start; somehow Santa Monica Studio has accomplished that task with grace and raw talent that beggars belief. You often hear about lame sequels degrading the quality of their predecessors, but this game is somehow so well-made and brilliantly written that it actually elevates the original trilogy. It's nearly unheard of in this kind of franchise, a miraculous feat of storytelling.The game is amazingly well-optimized for PC, and I had zero issues during my playthrough. No framerate drops, no performance problems, I just set the graphics to high, turned on DLSS, and had a rock-solid 120fps the whole way through. The game has graphics that still hold up nearly 5 years after release, great art direction, awesome mocap and facial animation, just brilliant from front to back. And of course the music is great, Bear McCreary is really in his element. Chris Judge deserves special mention for his unbelievable voice and mocap work; I deeply felt every single one of his lines. Kratos is so expressive and thoughtful in this game, but he still feels like an absolute a force of nature, just exuding restrained anger and raw power.The combat rocks; it's top-tier 3rd person melee combat with mid-depth RPG elements. There are plenty of collectibles that each feel significant and strongly grounded in the world, and every side quest is worth doing...none of the content in this game feels low-effort, honestly. It's open world, but great discipline has been exercised in restricting the scope of the game. As a result, something interesting is waiting for you around every corner, and in every cutscene.GoW 2018 is truly a masterpiece of a game, and a standard to which other AAA games ought to aspire. I can't recommend it highly enough.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War on PC is a true masterpiece that captivates at every turn. Its engaging storyline, well-developed relationships between characters, and the emotional journey of Kratos and Atreus make it hard to step away from the screen. The game offers stunning graphics, which look even better thanks to the capabilities of the PC, showcasing every detail of the Norse mythology-inspired world. The combat is dynamic and satisfying, while the puzzles make you feel like a true explorer. It's an absolute must-play for any fan of action and adventure games!

_childDocuments_.review: So, picture this: you've got a jacked dude with more muscles than a butcher's dog, wielding a couple of swords, and stomping around in ancient Greece... no wait, Scandinavia... no, sorry, it's both. Welcome to "God of War" - a game where mythologies collide and daddy issues are as common as treasure chests.First off, we have our protagonist, Kratos, who's traded in his Blades of Chaos for a big ol' axe and a gruff demeanor. Gone are the days of indiscriminate rage against Greek gods; now he's a single dad trying to raise his son, Atreus. It's like someone decided, "Hey, let's take the angriest character in gaming and give him parental responsibilities. What could possibly go wrong?"But fear not, dear players, because Kratos isn't just slaying monsters; he's also slaying those dad jokes with the finesse of a master punsmith. You'll find yourself chuckling (or groaning) at his quips as you journey through the Nordic wilderness. "Atreus, why did the cyclops bring a flashlight? Because he wanted to see things from a different perspective!"Speaking of Atreus, he's like a combo of Robin to Kratos' Batman and that know-it-all kid from your high school physics class. He's there to shoot arrows, translate runes, and remind Kratos to moisturize because, let's face it, the dude's skin is drier than the Sahara.The gameplay? Oh, it's solid. You'll be hacking, slashing, and dodging your way through waves of enemies like a hot knife through Skadi's butter. And let's not forget the boss fights - they're bigger, badder, and more epic than trying to explain Norse mythology to your grandma.But what really sets "God of War" apart is its attention to detail. From the breathtaking landscapes to the intricate lore, every corner of this game feels meticulously crafted. And let's not forget about the hidden collectibles; finding them all is like trying to find the meaning of life in a bag of potato chips - frustrating yet oddly satisfying.In conclusion, "God of War" is a masterpiece of gaming. It's got action, humor, heart, and enough dad jokes to last you a lifetime. So grab your axe, polish your quiver, and get ready for an adventure that's truly godly... or should I say, dadly?

_childDocuments_.review: God of War for PC is a must-play game that tells a surprisingly heartfelt story with witty and memorable characters. The dynamic between Kratos and his son is done really well, and you can tell Kratos really loves his son but is having a hard time coming to terms with allowing himself to be soft and loving in times where it would be appropriate. The game’s audiovisual direction is incredible, and the combat is relentlessly satisfying. However, the RPG/level up mechanics and grinding for gear can be tedious at times. My favorite part of the game was seeing the end scene of all of the giants and the build-up to the top of the mountain in Jotunheim. Overall, God of War for PC has hours of entertainment value and is more than worth the money even at the original launch price of $40 on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the greatest storylines I've seen in a video game. The journey has a lot of depth and the actors had such great charisma with one another. Gameplay may seem repetitive at times, but there is a lot of customizability in regards to the gamer's playstyle (using blocking to your advantage vs becoming more of a hack & slash brute vs going with a more range based tactic to keep distance between you and your foes). There are lots of different enemies to face, each with their own strengths and weaknesses, which forces the gamer to adapt with each encounter. This allows for combat to not feel entirely repetitive to the point of monotony. If that's not enough, the world is vast and there are so many side quests to go on and places to explore that I recommend not just rushing through the storyline, but taking your time and looking around everywhere you go.

_childDocuments_.review: God of War is a good game but I personally feel it is overrated. It surely has some good moments and wonderful production value, but everything else is just kinda of mediocre for an AAA title. The main story for me is not really memorable and the combat gets boring fairly quickly-even as you continue to get new skills and a new weapon later in the game. The game proves that open world is not always superior. I think the game would be much better to be more linear and focus on the main journey. It is not fun to always have to solve puzzles to just traverse the regions and I hate how many chests this game has and it just makes sick seeing the same chest-opening animations over and over. The variety of enemies is laughable for a game of this caliber and god there was even less variety when it comes to boss fights. Again I respect that many people love the game and I can understand that, but personally I would not recommend the game to my friends. It is not the God of War sequel/reboot I personally wanted. And no KRATOS does not need armor.
