_childDocuments_.review: Oh my! I would lie if I'd say that this game took me by surprise as I played the demo before release but still, oh my! I haven't even been much into "Collect-a-thon" games at all but this one. I can't stop smiling while playing. Moving around the cute/beautiful lvl on a kickass "soapboard" just feels too good. It's a welcome break of all those skill based games. Just have a nice, chilled time while you "GOTTA CATCH EM ALL!" (nope, I never played Pokemon) nor Pikmin.Cute artwork, cute characters, fluid gameplay. I really hope there will be more content (or a sequel) for this little gem. I am not done yet (half through the game I think) but I am already sad thinking about the end. Can't remember I've ever had such a chilled yet fun gaming experience. Being an 41yo old fart I feel like a kid again while playing this game. No worries, no pressure, just fun cruising around. Game runs well on a rather old rig (GTX 970, Xeon 1231v3), no bugs so far (tho I've read about some other players encountered some of).If I would have to mention a little downside it would probly be the fact that it CAN be somewhat frustrating at times if you can't find the last 10-50 pollen but - at least for me - that's not a big deal. 10/10 would hug those explosive cute tinykins again ♥

_childDocuments_.review: Wrote a long review but it got destroyed, so to tldr myself:6/10 The game is carried by its music, level design, and charm. The game is held back by its shallow gameplay, puzzles, and references (and the bugged achievements). Play it if you like collectathons, don't play it if you're looking for something to tide you over until Pikmin 4, as they're about as similar as Super Mario is to Super Meat Boy. Pikmin is all about micromanaging your minions to solve your puzzles, Tinykin's puzzles are a question of "do I have enough of X tinykin?" and the answer is almost always yes.If there were a Tinykin 2 that released as is, I'd only check out the OST. If they released with better/harder/more in-depth puzzles, I'd definitely give it a look and might even buy. Couldn't hurt to also have a collectible tracker when you have <100 pollen left, as that was probably how I spent the most amount of time on each level.

_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for 3D platformers, and when I discovered that Tinykin has some elements in common with Pikmin, I was very happy.Here's what I like:- An excellent mash-up of Pikmin and 3D platformer collectathons- Tinykin is a more relaxing experience than Pikmin. There aren't enemies to beat up, you can only get hurt by falling from high places or by staying in the water for a long period of time- If you intend to 100% the game, it may be quite challenging: collecting all the pollens and artifacts, and gathering every Tinikyn on the map are quite the task; moreover, Wasp Races are especially difficult (and fun) to beat the best times in order to get all the platinum medals- Funny easter eggs (spoiler)But, there are two issues about Tinykin:- All NPCs have 30 fps, while Milodane (the main character) has 60 fps. They probably did it to improve performance, but sometimes I find it a little unpleasant for my eyes- Some achievements related to collecting everything may not unlock; in case it happens, just visit every room in the game and then they must pop upIt took me about 8 hours to complete the main story, and 2 more to 100% the game.The best "Pikmin" game on Steam so far, I wish they were more games like this.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinkyin is an adorable 3D platforming game where you go through a house of bug-like creatures and help them help you go home. This game is so filled with charm, from the bouncy art style to the weird characters (many of whom were nerdy references) to the bouncy Tinykin themselves. It's very similar to Pikmin but with more of a focus on exploration than any management or combat. There's so much to explore, and the environments feel so immersive and fleshed out. There are a ton of different challenges, but nothing is missable, so this game is a great pick for completionists like me. I loved my time with this game, and I'd recommend it to anyone who enjoys running around creative worlds and solving puzzles with cute little Pikmin-like guys.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Great little game. I was surprised how fleshed out and great the environments felt. There was lots to do and I loved the sense of scale with all the household objects and stuff, made it so much fun to explore. Game isn't overly challenging other than the races, which I ended up not engaging with in the end as it was just bonus content. You need some really precise inputs to do well on them from what I noticed and it's an insane difficulty jump. However, it isn't essential in any way to beating the game and has no impact on 100% achievements, it is there for those who like speedrunning and an extra challenge. But yeah, other than the races, the rest of the game has some simple platforming that shouldn't be too challenging for most people. But at the end of the day, it doesn't need to be challenging to be fun because I still had loads of fun with this game, as exploring and getting around the environments was a really enjoyable experience. There are a lot of collectables and bonus quests and things to do in each environment which is a lot of fun to do as well if you enjoy that kind of thing. You'll have to try and explore every little area to find them all which can be quite satisfying finding little hidden spots where they're hiding something. However, it can be a mild source of frustration if you are missing just one little thing as the game doesn't provide you with any way of finding them. I think this is probably the biggest and only flaw of the game in my opinion, since it can be incredibly tedious to find one tiny little collectable in such a huge environment. But I really do think the rest of the game makes up for that, and if you explore thoroughly and really take in each place you go to, you shouldn't have to do any backtracking to find anything.Overall, very cute and simple game that can bring a lot of joy and relaxation. The story is also very cute and interesting along with all the dialogues from the characters you can speak to. Just a great world to immerse yourself in. I shall give it a solid 9.5/10 easily

_childDocuments_.review: The game was enjoyable enough for me to roll credits. The art style is gorgeous and movement is fluid. Every stage introduces a new mechanic that keeps things fresh. This keeps exploration and platforming interesting all game long. There are also hidden Easter eggs and references littered throughout the game that are nice to stumble upon.While you don't play games like these for their story, I will still mention that the story felt a bit underwhelming to me. The premise of tiny creatures living and thriving in a giant house is really intriguing, but unfortunately was never utilized to its full potential. The developers did highlight various problems a civilization can run into in every stage, but the resolution of these problems were laughably bad. It felt like watching a history piece on the French Revolution that ends up with everyone actually eating cake.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this during a short period of time where I wasn't enjoying playing any video games, and found this refreshing. It's a casual "walking sim" and "collectathon" platformer, like a Banjo Kazooie or Spyro game if you remove the enemies. _childDocuments_.review: I tried Tinykin at PAX East a few years ago, intrigued by a giant sign advertising the "World's Tiniest Man". What I found was an incredibly cute, charming, and creative 3D platformer that has all the best aspects of collect-a-thons and none of the tedium. The levels are all incredibly well-thought out and designed with a fantastic art style, the characters are funny and charming (I love bugs, so all the inhabitants of the game's world being bugs was great), and the light puzzles and challenges were fun, but not overly difficult. The story of the game was also fantastic, the plot was engaging and entertaining, and the mysteries unfolded at a perfect pace- not too slow that you forget things, but not too fast that you figure out the ending before you get there. The game isn't a long one, I beat it in 8 hours, and that's including collecting all the major items and upgrades per level, but not 100%ing them. But in those 8 hours, I had a blast! If you love 3D platformers or comfy games, this game is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I had never heard of Tinykin before, but I received it as a gift from a friend. This one definitely flew under the radar for me because it ended up being a surprise hit for me!The closest game to Tinykin for comparison sake might be Pikmin, but even then they're very different in execution. The game does have you gathering different colors of the titular Tinykin to use their unique abilities to solve problems and overcome obstacles, but unlike Pikmin, you don't really have to protect take care of them. By this I mean the game has no combat and no hazards that will affect your Tinykin, so once you have them, you don't have to worry about losing them, save for a few types that are consumed upon achieving their function. This creates a very low stress environment which places the emphasis on exploration and puzzles.The exploration is easily the game's strongest aspect. Controls are precise and responsive, with the ability to jump, skate on soap (don't ask), or float with bubbles, in addition to using your Tinykin. Levels are large with plenty to see, and you progress by completing core objectives in each level to obtain a Thing. You also collect Nectar in the levels, which can be found lying around in the levels and also be rewarded for completing side quests and objectives. I actually enjoyed that Nectar had an incentive beyond simply collecting them for the sake of collection, for each level has a Nectar benchmark that once reached rewards you with the ability to lengthen how long you can glide. The levels are all appropriately varied, although some definitely flow better than others as a few of them could be a bit of a slog, especially the 2nd and 4th. Even so, the levels are charming and exploration and collection are rewarding.If there's anything holding the game back though, it's that it's a tad too easy when utilizing Tinykin. That is to say, when you target any object that can be interacted with by Tinykin, it will glow in the same color as the correct Tinykin, and automatically select that Tinykin for you. It makes it so the puzzles feel like they're effectively solving themselves for you; by the end I was just blowing through the levels gathering all the Tinykin I could first and foremost so I could just haphazardly toss them at any obstacle in my path without stopping. This doesn't make the game bad per se, but I didn't find myself as engaged as I could have been if I'd had to use a modicum of thought when solving them. This is especially significant considering the length of the game, as it only takes about 10 hours if you want to 100% the game. The visuals are charming with 3D environments contrasting with 2D Paper-like Characters. The character designs are nice and were fairly expressive, although I admit I can't say I was particularly attached to any of the characters given their role was rather small and only a few had unique models.  Likewise, the music is upbeat and charming as well, perfectly complementing the low-stress vibe of the game and matching the feel of each level appropriately. Overall, the game is a lot of fun, but don't expect to be challenged or need to put a whole lot of effort into succeeding. But if you want a short, low-stress game where you can explore and vibe, then this may very well be the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Really beautiful and really fun, I couldn't put it down and finished it in one day.  It's less like pikmin than it seems, more of a collectathon puzzle platformer.  The puzzles are really simple, and won't give you any friction, but sometimes that's what you want.  Great visuals, I love the shrunk down bug civilization in a suburban house setting, great music.  A+! A breezy and incredibly pleasant time!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a 3D platformer with a gorgeous visual style, extremely fun and fluid controls, and is very comfy. It seems like it'd be similar to Pikmin, but there's no combat or time management or risk of losing your guys, so it's much more about exploration, and the little guys just help with that. You start each level with no Tinykin, and as you find more in the level, that opens up more paths and objectives to do.The levels are larger than life, and in particular, if you're a big fan of Chibi-Robo like I am, you will definitely love playing this game. The characters you meet in each level and the objectives you have to do for them are pretty entertaining. There's also optional challenge races that are a ton of fun to go for Platinum Medals in. The movement has a ton of depth, and I bet this will be a fun game for speedrunners to optimize.

_childDocuments_.review: is perhaps the best word to describe latest offering, , and not just because of the cute little critters that follow you around. The gameplay is reminiscent of that of Pikmin, which effectively blends together a puzzle-based real-time strategy to produce a unique and captivating experience. Although it is not the first game to feature a mixture of different genres, it does take the concept to new heights of complexity and design.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   The story takes place in an unfamiliar world of characters with balloon heads, saucer eyes, and pretzel limbs. You take on the role of Milo, tasked with finding parts to a ship that will eventually take him home. But Milo’s not alone in this endeavor as little critters called Tinykins are scattered about ready to help him accomplish the task.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   Giving orders to your little companions is straightforward as you only need to throw them at corresponding objects to do their thing. When you witness the Tinykins heave-hoing as they lift up heavy objects and faithfully rally back to you with a blow of a whistle will make you fall quickly in love with your little friends.Some of the puzzle elements early on are pretty simple but do get more complex the deeper into the game you get. Tinykins also have unique abilities and talents based on their character types so make sure to grab as many different ones as you can.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   Watching your babies grab onto each other to form ladders and bridges or act as electrical conduits to connect two circuits together will make you feel like proud parents, and unlike Pikmin, there are no fighting sequences which makes the game ideal for any age group.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   Aesthetically, struts down the PC catwalk as a perfect example of visual extravagance. The whimsical artistic style chosen by the developers has blossomed into a fully 3D world where everyday household items are all realized in stunningly realistic forms. The developers show us the world of Tinykin as a perturbing place where the inhabitants exist to be peculiar, obnoxious, but always funny.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   Each level reflects the changing scenery with lush beauty: a bedroom, a kitchen with an overflowing sink, and a playroom just to name a few. On the mountaintop of cabinets, for example, shiny bits of pollen are perched high above waiting to be discovered as the camera uses effective lateral movements to sweep across the opulent landscape. ⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   The graphics are bright and vibrant and each level is littered with all things cute and friendly. The Tinykins themselves are so wonderfully modeled that you actually feel a sense of sadness when you aren’t able to collect and free them all. And despite having literally dozens and dozens of Tinykins on screen, the graphics engine holds up very well without any noticeable slowdown whatsoever.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀   The only real disappointment I had with the title is that like any good game, it ends pretty quickly right as it’s hitting its stride. A few more diverse levels to explore would have made this much better. Even with this minor gripe, however, is so well developed that it will stand out against many of the bigger AAA titles out there. Its refreshing gameplay and innovative design will make it go down as one of the best games of the year.⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀⠀

_childDocuments_.review: Felt like a mix of an N64 collectathon and a more relaxed Pikmin, which for me means the game is fantastic. It looked amazing and ran great on my old potato of a machine. I also preferred mouse & keyboard in this game which was odd to me.Some negatives:I wouldn't have minded a few more abilities unlocked throughout the adventure and they're wasn't any reward besides achievements for collecting everything, which was disappointing considering how hunting down the last few pollen in a level was always a tedious challenge. Also, a few of the types of Tinykin were only useful as they were required for solving a few puzzles (yellow and blue) and they felt underwhelming. Green was definitely the most useful for exploring and sequence-breaking.Overall though, for a short romp, I loved this game. Definitely interested in looking into the speedrun. I would not recommend collecting everything, however; just get enough pollen to unlock the bubble upgrades.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I'm such a sucker for games with a unique art style and a good OST... And this game delivers that in spades. Sure, the game is heavily inspired by the Pikmin series but it still has its own unique charm that allows it to stand on its own merit. I really enjoyed how much attention to detail the developers put into the game (i.e the OST changes dynamically to match whatever section of the level you are on... If you are inside a guitar, the level's theme song would change into an acoustic rendition of the song which made traversing each level really fun to do).  I thought the many references to pop culture was a nice touch to modernize the feel of the game and the controls felt so fluid and natural. My only gripe with the game is that the path to acquiring all the achievements was heavily focused on collectibles which can be a bit tedious given how daunting the scale of the levels can be. Overall, the game is packed with fantastic third-person platforming, creative mechanics, and levels that are a joy to explore... I definitely recommend checking this game out if the genre interests you at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun platformer + collectathon + a bit of Pikmin thrown in. The controls are fun, responsive, and never frustrating. The music and sound design is great on every level. _childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: The Pikmin comparisons are hard to avoid, but the game does enough to differentiate itself through its artstyle and charm. It's a low stress, lighthearted game, that wins you over through its joyful world that is fun to explore. Filled with details, that makes you feel the passion and love that the devs put into creating the environments. Importantly, aside from the great visuals, the game plays very well. The controls are noticably smooth and snappy, and I rarely had any moments, where I felt like it wasn't doing what I was intending to do. It's also the perfect length for a game like this. Not that I wouldn't have enjoyed to play more of it, but I believe the duration allows the game to end on a very high note, and feels like its not overstaying its welcome. The music is fun and adds to the charming presentation of the game. Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: While Tinykin has a refreshing sense of style and brings unique Pikmin-like gamepaly to the PC for the first time, the gameplay elements - the environments, dialogue, puzzles and platforming - are simplistic and lose their novelty too quickly. _childDocuments_.review: What a cute, inoffensive, little game. I played through the entire thing in one sitting and 100% it with very little difficulty. There's no enemies and the only thing you really do is use your movement and tinykins to explore, collect various items and currency, and solve simple environmental puzzles. That may sound negative, but it made for a fun time that hooked me with its gameplay loop. The controls feel great on a controller, though there can be a few times you miss a longer jump due to the slightly odd hover mechanic. You get used to it, but that and the soap-board grind mechanic tripped me up every now and then. A tiny nitpick in an otherwise solid game. I enjoyed my time playing and was pleased that it was only around 6 hours long. Didn't have enough time to outstay its welcome, so it left me wanting just a bit more (which is a good thing). I'd recommend this if you like 3D platformers, mixed with a little pikmin, all tied together with a cute story. Thanks for the fun game, developers!

Pay attention to how the music and audio changes, all the little stories as you pass by, and small details like walking into the dust. Here is a 100% pollen run of Sanctar for a good sample: I look forward to continuing my adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I need to set your expectations of what this game is:This is a 3D platformer / collectathon. It does not play like Pikmin.Now that you expect a 3D collectathon, let me reset those expectations too: 1. Each large level is played one at a time, in order. You don't generally revisit a previous level except for optional speedrun challenges or for pursuing 100% completion.2. There is virtually no danger of dying or taking damage. You explore, jump, climb, and collect everything in a safe and stress-free treasure hunt. The few things that can kill you, such as fall damage or the occasional hazard, cost you nothing and set you back to your last safe standing spot. Instead of enemies, the world is populated by NPCs, most of which serve no purpose except to drop some cute dialogue. (Once I realized that most NPCs were pointless, I almost entirely stopped talking to them. Many had an attempt at humor, but most of the humor boiled down to a pun in their name or a pop culture reference.)Every level in this game is both visually impressive and structurally fun to climb around on. Every bit of space is made use of, and little hidden areas are everywhere. The gameplay essentially is a matter of collecting Tinykin of various colors which in turn allow you to access key objectives and more Tinykin, until you're able to explore the entire level. New Tinykin types are introduced throughout the game; most don't add a whole lot to the gameplay, but one of the earlier ones (green) is an especially clever idea for an ability for a 3D platformer. (No spoilers ;) )The music is great, the graphics feature crisp 2D character sprites and awe-inspiring environments. Interactive objects are clearly noted by colored outlines and designs, such as green climbable shoelaces or objects that need a particular type of Tinykin. The only interactive objects that sometimes betray your trust are grindable ledges - using a bar of soap for faster speed, you can get even more speed by grinding along ledges, but more than a few times I didn't enter the expected grind and instead fell the cliff. Bummer.Overall, Tinykin is like the bubble-wrap-popping version of a 3D platformer/collectathon. There's no danger and very little difficulty at all. It's just satisfying to explore and find everything. The only exceptions to the easy difficulty are the speedrun challenges: These are pure platforming challenges that route you all over the level with target times for bronze, silver, gold, and platinum. As an experienced speedrunner, I was usually able to get gold on my first or second try, but that certainly won't be the case for most players. For platinum medals, I was pleasantly blown away by how tough the times to beat were! It is seriously rare for a game to expect so much of a player (albeit for completely optional awards). These are like staff ghost times in racing games, and I love it.Anyway, Tinykin is fantastic, but you need to set your expectations accordingly. Also it's only around 5 1/2 to 7 hours long, depending on how thorough you are.

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is an extremely enjoyable platformer collectathon that doesn't overstay and is fun from beginning to end. The controls are tight, the music is fantastic, and there are tons of small things that make the game feel very polished. An hour goes by quickly while playing and there's a great feeling of "I'll just go explore over there real quick" which is always rewarding. It's a great time.

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Steam Deck.Game was fun, controls felt great on SD and it made you feel good to explore the entire level. However, the game felt shallow at times, but it’s shallowness lends itself well to playing this while listening to music in the background. Story was okay, neat, but missing that big hook for me. Dialogue was meh, felt like a chore to read all the citizens dialogue at times. Overall I’d recommend it, but only on sale.

I was scared of it being like Pikmin but it is so much better and I like that its lacking strategy and is more real time and arcade based. _childDocuments_.review: Read this review and others Imagine the problems associated with being shrunk down to the size of a tiny insect! Spiders bigger than us! Scary… Fortunately, Tinykin takes this idea very lightly and unfolds an imaginative adventure in a mix between Pikmin and a 3D adventure platformer, with a hint of collectathon, which will surely leave a smile on players’ faces.This title puts the player in the shoes of Milo, an archeologist from a planet called Aegis, who has a dream of finding the origins of the human race. After an accidental teleportation event, Milo finds himself transported to planet Earth in the year 1991. The main objective is to recover elements for the reconstruction of the machine that will take this peculiar character back to his planet. For this, he will have the help of Ridmi, who will serve as a guide, and the little Tinykin, who serve as support to cross the various obstacles presented and that gives the name to this title.Tinykins are extremely useful and the main point in the adventure story throughout the house that opens up while searching for the necessary elements. In each level, there are several types of eggs, which, when you pass over them, give life to Tinykins that closely follow Milo. Each Tinikyn has a color that is associated with a different skill. For example, the pink one has a strength like Hulk, so they are associated with heavier tasks, such as pushing objects or even transporting them from one place to another, while the blue ones, for example, allow you to position a conductive line of energy between two points, giving energy to electrical equipment. All tasks associated with Tinykins are associated with a number of elements, so if you find an obstacle but don’t have enough of them, the best is to explore the level a little more.Exploration is key and part of the fun. Using a soap instead of a skateboard or a flying platform serves the purpose of faster traveling and is somewhat reminiscent of the adventures of Ratchet and Clank. In fact, this title pays homage to different worlds and genres of pop culture. It is possible to see the moon and the bicycle from the movie E.T, Gary, the Spongebob snail, the symbol of Sly Cooper, among others. Explore and discover these delicious details.During the 7 hours of gameplay that I had, until I reached the end of his main story, divided between the main story and side missions, Tinykin presented 5 different rooms in the house, which are naturally associated with 5 different levels. Each division has a different insect civilization with its own ideas and where there is a need to help them to recover the captive object, which is necessary for the reconstruction of the machine. The mix between 3D levels with the paper craft aspect of the main character applies a very vibrant and different look than usual. Imagine a bathroom full of small castles made entirely of toilet paper, or a playroom with an intergalactic story where you can even destroy meteorites.Tinykin is certainly one of this year’s highlights. There’s no great depth, but what it does, it does it in a fun way. Of note are the small cutscenes that are fantastic. Will we be able to have a small Tinykin series in the near future?

_childDocuments_.review: (psst, if you like this game, play A Hat In Time)A charming collectathon platformer, that captures the 'tiny' theme and runs with it all the way to the end.The minute by minute collecting of tinykins and nectar is crunchy and satisfying. The tasks you are sent out to do are cute, and with just enough variance to stay enjoyable, though it is still a collectathon, so there is certainly a degree of repetition. The artstyle's 2D cartoons in a 3d world works really well (even though once i thought about how Milodane is technically always running backwards, I couldn't unsee it!) and the character designs are great, using qualities of the bugs to build this house world is really inventive! Each 'level' has a distinct vibe to it, and I'd enjoy discovering what the next theme would be each time.In all, this is a good game that is easy to snuggle into an enjoyable couple hours at a time. In the same way it consistently stays a pleasant experience, I wouldn't say it ever really hits incredible highs. But I don't begrudge that of it, I'd say if you're looking for a good collectathon to relax and smile with, this is a great choice!

The art style ties it all together perfectly, and makes it a fun experience. I'd easily give this game a 10/10, with my one gripe being I wish it was longer! I really hope a sequel pops up one day.

_childDocuments_.review: While on the surface this game might seem like a Pikmin clone - what this game does, it does very well.  This game is all meat no filler.  It combines light puzzle solving with fun platforming and wraps it in a really polished presentation.  Put simply - I enjoyed everything minute I spent in this game's world.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A joy from start to finish! In the middle of playing Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom, I needed something mindless, easy, and relaxing, and this game did all that and more! It's a simple platformer, with no puzzles or skill trees, or alternate routes to take. Just progress through the five areas talking to characters and finding the collectibles. Simple but tight mechanics and a well-implemented concept with the tinykins left me wanting more, but it was definitely short and sweet! Glad I picked this up
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Quality: It feels fun, snappy and quick to play. Even though the floating bubble you use can sometimes be somewhat slow, its still really fun to generally move around. Style: The animations are great! The levels are well decorated, each with their own distinct theme. It makes great use of the "smol" theme throughout the game, such as using a sink leaking to make a waterfall and clips clipped together to make walls. It has a ton of small details like these that really bring its worlds to life.Story: The story feels a bit thrown in, but its core is pretty thought provoking, despite how little it is used throughout the game.The closest thing I could compare this to is a mix of Pikmin and either Astros Playroom or Mario Odyssey. The biggest gripe i have is that there is no pollen (the in game collectable) detector, making 100%ing a bit of a pain, with you having 2 left in a level, making you have to go through every nook and cranny to find it. All n all, I really recommend! It has a charm and life to it that is rare and hard to find, and my entire experience was really positive! Well worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: Really great casual experience; perfect if you were ever a fan of Banjo-Kazooie (Honestly got BK vibes throughout my playtime). _childDocuments_.review: Bajillion times better than I expected. If you are not an APM player, don't worry, controlling the "tinykin" is ZERO hassle, because you don't. I wasn't too sure about it from the screenshots & trailers, had this feeling it would be hassle to control, boy oh boy, couldn't be more wrong. A real joy to play. Buy the game, GLHF.

_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game literally feels like it was made by Nintendo, enough said, buy this game ! But I will slightly elaborate further, from marketing and heresay this game is supposed to be a Pikmin style game, whilst true, that isn't the entire narrative of the gameplay feel. Tinykin feels more like a mishmash of Pikmin, with a paper Mario/Bug Fables aesthetic built around a collectathon puzzle-platformer in pretty decently large interconnected hub levels with numerous different things to collect and interact with. It took me about 2 hours to get everything in the first main level and there is supposed to be another 5 after that. In terms of the Pikmin side of this game, you collect different types of Tinykin in each level, with a new type getting introduced in each subsequent level. These Tinykin have abilities that will help you solve environmental puzzles, from the standard pink Tinykin which you use to interact with the environment, to transportation of items, then there are the red Tinykin which you hurl at objects in a kamikazi attack to blow up obstacles to create new paths, or the green ones where they build a step ladder, growing higher and higher the more you obtain to gain new heights! All of these numerous mechanics culminate to create something visually and mechanically delightful, playing this game at 60+ fps just feels incredibly smooth, which goes to why this game feels so much like a Nintendo game, coupled with the fact that I haven't ecperienced any bugs at all, the overall polish for this game shows the developers truly put in the care for this sleeper hit of a title they've created. This game is said to be around 10 hours to 100% and for this price i really do encourage anyone reading this review to purchase and dive into this game, you won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so Good!Gameplay is basically "walk around and find Tinykins, Objects or stuff to interact with" and its not boring, instead, its very Entertaining! you can flush the toilet, open the cash register by pressing a button, slide down the couch.This game also have ULTIMATE, SUPER, MIND BLOWING storyline with many funny characters that have their own personality, some dialogues between characters made me laugh very much :Dmusic is just....AMAZING, its that type of music which makes you relax, whoever created this music did great job!my rating to this game: 10/10great musicgreat charactersgreat game.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I've yet to finish the game, it seems short but sweet.Usually I don't like this kind of modern 2D cartoon style; bean mouths, flat, no detail. But it carries a nice charm here. The game itself feels very tight and responsive to play. Big, open level design that naturally encourages you to find collectibles and objectives, rather than marking it all down for you. Great sound design and dynamic music make the whole world burst with life. Lots of (optional) amusing dialogue. The main reason I wanted to write this review, before even finishing the game, is to point out a design choice that the developers could've done without. Whenever you unlock a rope or silk-rail to let you quickly navigate to and from various spots throughout the levels, the camera pulls back and strips control away from you. This might be fine if there were only a small number of ropes/rails. With so many of them, however, it's an unnecessary momentum-killer.  Even dumb players don't need the game to explicitly show them that a rope or rail was just created.

_childDocuments_.review: Pikmin who? No but seriously Tinykin wears its inspiration on its sleeves half, Pikmin half Banjo Kazooie. To explain how "Tinykin" work they are like little worker bees you can command at objectives to solve puzzles, For example making bridges, lifting heavy objects, and destroying scaffolding. and you collect said Tinykin in egg pods that are non-renewable which works in making Tinykin a resource for locking off areas of the map and progression but as a result lacks at combat in the game. but the game makes up for in map design. I do feel that the ways the Tinykin are used gets a little too samey later on if they used more puzzles requiring multiple types being used in tandem, or more puzzles it would fix the problem. but i'd say its made up for in the level design and boy oh boy it's amazing and why I compared it to Banjo Kazooie before, the maps for the most part have no restrictions and multiply ways of being traversed it just feels like a blast to navigate, with you clearing a small chunk of a area at a time and each "mini area" feeling stitched together in the best way possible. but with the unsolvable problem of missing one collectable and not being able to find it for 20 minutes, Although I can't hold that against the game only myself. Still, blasting through a map and knocking out all of the objectives just feels satisfying and you don't have to backtrack to previous areas, if that's a good or bad thing is up to personally preference. That's why i said it's similar, a mix of Pikmin and Banjo Kazooie for resource management and free moving level design. sadly no time management its only to save you time but no real reason not that it needed it to be fair. And now for the menial stuff, First the music is nice and sets the tone nice and I do like the "dynamic music" (It changes depending on what part of the area you're in on a subtle level). The graphics all look nice and fit in despite being 3D with flat (Physical) characters they fit in. Akin to Paper Mario in that sense. I do also like the world building they establish with a religion worshiping Salvior Ardwin (I can't for the life of me tell if it's some joke I'm not getting) and other aspects of the world like how the dung beetles are shunned from the people. granted they're played for Jokes, and the game is humorous with witty writing and all. and the world feels "alive" and you're just a nobody stranded here experiencing it but it never gets brought up after the first 5 minutes oh well. I won't spoil the ending but it does fall victim to the age old "end of game exposition dump" would had been a bit better if there was a bit of build up, but its not to big of a deal you're playing the game for the game play not Shakespeare.  The game is a short but a quality title worth the price of admission and not too hard to 100 percent but be careful if you did everything and some achievements don't show up just enter the areas again and check the menus. I think this game is quite the hidden gem and I think there is a lot of potential for a sequel maybe not in the same setting but either way this team proved they know how to make a great game. for every minor downside it has a major upside. if you like "Collectathons" this will be right up your alley. My final rating is 8.6-8.8. Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed it, definitely up there with "A Hat in Time" for best Steam Platformers/Collectathons. There are also so many references/cameos/puns in this game that you might find amusing as you play. The only gripe I have about this game is when using the soapboard it doesn't always snap to edges/ledges as easily as I'd like it to, especially noticeable when doing the races. Took me many tries to platinum every race just because of that. Speaking of races, this game would be a fantastic speed running game, since I've noticed a few small skips every now and then. I would love to see more levels in the future and more types of tech (such as a triple jump, but that may require reworking some levels).Achievements: I got 100% in about 8-10 hours, it's largely dependent on if you find all the pollen (coins) the first time.

_childDocuments_.review: Pikmin  meets Super Mario Odyssey in a perfect fusion.I love this game, it might even be a 10 out of 10. It just feels so wonderful to control, and everything feels so player friendly. I can’t remember the last time I wanted to 100% every level in a platformer/collectaphon.It gives you the most important movement options close to the beginning, so movement around the levels feels fantastic. And the levels? INCREDIBLE. They feel like interconnected sandboxes, where you can go wherever you want and eventually it will link up with other parts of the level in unexpected yet natural ways. Really struggling not to make the overdone Dark Souls level design comparison but…This game really hooked me. Usually how I gauge how much I enjoy a platformer is how easily I can sequence break. Or how often I think “I wonder if I can _______” then try it and it turns out to be possible. This game satisfies that itch far more than both A Hat in Time and Psychonauts 2 - which days a lot about the game’s mechanics and level design.I really wasn’t expecting to love this. I thought it would be too focused on puzzles and the platforming would be an afterthought. But they both work hand-in-hand perfectly.This game will be a sleeper hit, I guarantee it. I can’t wait for it to get the attention it deserves. Oh and for it’s worth: it’s PERFECT for the Steam Deck. Especially if you bind the back buttons to jump and slide.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best indies I have played in years. It is not quite up there with say Kena but this is a truly special indy!Think Pikmin mixed in with platforming and a hint of chibi robo (given you are a tiny person exploring a house). There are no time limits however which is a big differential from chibi and pikmin, but I see this as a good thing. The gameplay loop is solid, you explore room by room solving various puzzles and finding new tinykin companions along the way as you jump and solve your way to fixing a ship to go home. The platforming is solid, and feels pretty good, It could be slightly tighter but overall it feels great. The levels are very well designed and an absolute joy to explore. The art style is solid, the tinykin are great and there is a decent enough variety. After disabling SMT the game ran very well on deck there were dips down to 50 and very rarely into the 40s but majority of the time it was 60fps. The only problem with this game is a problem all good games have it ended". To complete all side quests and collect everything I would say you will likely be in the 6.5-7.5 hours range. Keys can be bought for a bit less from GMG. For the price I paid the game was absolutely worth it, it was a truly fun and memorable experience, it is very rare I see a game through to the end these days, with tinykin that was an easy choice.Try the demo, if you like it BUY THE GAME IT IS GENUINELY GREAT.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very visually pleasing and is a collectathon fan's paradise.A delightfully fun platforming experience and a nice casual game that will have enough playtime to easily warrant the price - if you go for 100%. + The mix of 2D and 3D graphics is aesthetically pleasing and the style lends itself well to the whimsical feeling the game provides+ TONS of things to collect in each area. Really scratches that collectathon itch+ Catchy, fun music that fits well within the game+ Fun, interesting mechanics with the different types of Tinykin you get throughout the game+ Navigating the world is fun and fluid. Controls really smoothly (at least with a gamepad, I did not test keyboard + mouse)+ TONS of Easter Egg/references. A lot of fun cultural references, many of which I was delighted to see. Some are less obvious than others, but there seems to be something in there for everyone. I'm sure I missed a few, but that just goes to show the massive variety of them. ~ WAITING. So much . A lot of the side quests and some of the  quests require you to wait for your little buddies to carry a "large" object from one area to another. The saving grace here is that you are able to go off and complete other tasks while your lil dudes are making their delivery. ~ Repetition. This almost went into  category. Each area has nearly identical side quests. While the old saying goes "if it ain't broke don't fix it" usually applies, this is not one of those times. It's an indie game with a smaller team though, so it gets a pass on that. I just wish some of the different mechanics were mixed up within these side quests to make them a  more interesting at least.- The main thing I can really put here is the story. While somewhat unique it is not incredibly engaging. There are bits that are told well by the environment but the majority of the story is exposition at the beginning and end of the game. What could have been a deeply moving story loses its punch by not showing enough of the story throughout, and putting it on the back-end.- At the time of this review I should also mention that the game has issues with a few of the achievements. Specifically the collection ones. Click the spoiler to see how I was able to fix the issue
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Sid Meier when asked to define a game answered it was a series of interesting decisions. I am afraid that based on that definition, Tinykin is not a game at all. Never at any point does the game ask you any question more engaging that "do you have X tinykin of Y colour". This game has no combat at all, and no puzzles in any meaningful sense, leaving pure exploration and collectibles as the only form of engagement.The story is similarly shallow. Almost the entire game you are mostly strung along with a simple premise about building a machine that is simply assumed to be a way for Milo to return home, with mostly trivial conflicts along the way. Normally this wouldn't be worthy of much criticism, but what makes this disappointing is how the story ends and the themes it attempts to incorporate. Almost the entire story is simply dumped on the player at once in the last few minutes, resulting in a story that is as shallow and underwhelming as the gameplay, to the point it is hard to tell what is actually supposed to be substantial and what's just there for the sake of having a conflict. What makes this frustrating is Tinykin seems to want to incorporate certain themes but presents them so shallowly that it almost comes off as a parody of the views it seems to want to present seriously.In conclusion, Tinykin is a facade of a game, not in the sense of being fraudulent mind you, but simply that there is no substance to it. Tinykin is like the set of a sitcom, aesthetically pleasing when viewed from the correct angle, but the appearance is all it has.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a 3rd person puzzle platformer collectathon game, where you explore a big house as a tiny person from the future. You'll find little Tinykin helpers along the way, that all have a specific talent. Some can lift heavy objects, some can transfer electrical currents, some can make ladders for you to reach new heights... Think Banjo-Kazooie meets Pikmin.There's no combat of any kind, no pressure to complete optional objectives, and quite frankly, this is just the most delightful game I've played in a long time. It's charming, top to bottom. It's hand drawn characters and great music really immerse you into it's cute world, and I can't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to rate this as "Not recommended" because this isn't a bad game, it just isn't a game that has enough good qualities in my opinion. The main rundown on the game is you're tiny and need to get around doing tasks in a regular sized household environment. You get the tasks done with tinykin that you need to collect while also collecting nectar and a couple small other things.I got this game since it came from the team that brought us "Splasher" but they couldn't be more different. Splasher is a punishing platformer but this game is an absolute breeze. There are no failure states which is fine but there also is no challenge in any of the platforming. The gameplay boils down to turning off your brain and just making sure you walk around thoroughly and interact with objects by throwing your tinykin when you have the requisite amount that the game pops up and tells you on every interaction. You walk over the main collectible, pollen, which there are probably 1000 littered per level and tinykin, probably 300 per level, by just walking over it. There's nothing interesting in it.I do like the environment as there does seem to be quite a bit of detail that goes into it. I will say though that the environment lacks connectivity and realism. Levels are "connected" in the sense that you can travel from one to the other via tunnels but it basically acts like fast travel. You can't spatially map out how they connect physically nor do they impact each other. I also say it lacks realism in the way that you can't picture the levels as a real place someone would actually live in. There's 18 salt and pepper shakers above the vent hood or something in the kitchen level for example. A game can't just be a "collect-a-thon", there needs to be something on top of it to drive you to do so. As far as I see, the two things going for the game and that is gameplay and NPC interaction. The gameplay I already went over. The NPC interaction also aren't too interesting since there is no overarching plot for me to care about with the characters. There's the main storyline but that's barely anything. All of the NPC characters are almost all just small isolated quips that you talk to once and then walk away and forget. There's nothing insulting about the gameplay or NPCs. Getting around isn't bad, just not fun. Talking to NPCs isn't bad, it's just "junk food" quips. Maybe chalk it up to me not being the intended audience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: It is quite fun the first hours, but the more you go forward the more it becomes slow and insufferable, even not counting the gliding starting mechanic, that is one of the worst and most fluidity killer I've ever seen, that does make the races not difficult, just bleh. And what I mean about the game being more insufferable the more you go forward, it's not because it adds difficulty, it's just that the new mechanics added every time makes it forcefully slower than before and not in a fun way. And I'm saying this as someone who loves collectathon, but if a games that has collecting stuff as the main point becomes both less fun and/or doesn't become more challenging the more you go forward well...And also if the fall damage was nullified by using the soap board it would make the races both more fluid and with the need of a better sliding precision than before.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very happy to get to change this review to a yes!The devs implemented a fix and I was able to unstuck my character.It is rare for me to finish a game, and even rarer to 100% it, but that I did with Tinykin. A very relaxed game, with just the right mix of puzzles, collect-a-thon and, of course, Pikmin. Unlike Pikmin, there's no time limit or need for moving quickly or you'll run out of food, nor is there combat, which makes for a very chill, pleasant game that's nice to wind down with. Plus, it's just long enough without overstaying it's welcome and a lovely experience throughout.Side note: I played through on Xbox Game Pass, as to why I have no playtime here.Original Review for Posterity:This is an incredibly sad no to have to give.The game is wonderful, and I absolutely adored it up until it broke. My character fell through a wall while climbing up the boxes at the top of the stairs in Transidor Crossing and is now stuck. After poking around looking for a solution, it would seem this is not an uncommon game breaking bug where the player will clip through a wall, ceiling or floor and be forever stuck. I even went as far as requesting help on their Discord and got no response, nor does Googling find any help on how to "unstuck" a character.So, until they implement some way to unstuck the character, unfortunately the game is broken for me. I do not want to start over after spending so much time 100%ing every level up to this point and especially with the fear that this might just happen again.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like a rip-off of Pikmin in the worst ways, the story itself is bare-bone and exposition is shallow (Why is there a museum with nobody there?? Just lazy and lacks immersion), graphics are amateur, and  to some degree I don't think anything was meant to be polished. Hate to be a critic, but for people who haven't played the entirety of what Pikmin has to offer, this game just lacks... soul.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 Pikmin, but less stressfulnone of your little guys can die and the game has no enemies other than leaf shaped 3D platforming where you clip the edges of them and fall off.only about 7 hours of gameplay, on the short side so i would grab it on sale.left the game open to farm the steam cards. refused to drop the last 2
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This was a truly delightful experience. It's kind of like a mix between Mario Odyssey and Pikmin with its own little charm to it. It took me about 14 hours to collect everything in the game, including getting the platinum badges for the time trial challenges. If you like platformer collectathons, then you'll like this game. The story isn't anything to write home about, but it has its charm and parts of it could tug on your heartstrings a little. Overall, I would definitely recommend checking this game out if you're even remotely interested. I saw this game around when it came out, and frankly, I'm a little upset I waited as long as I did to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a charming collectathon-platformer that will really hook the player into completing each level. The mechanics of this game are pretty simple but the game does it so well with the charming art style and atmosphere. It is a very chill game that can be finished in under 10 hours. The plot was not super captivating or memorable but overall the game does what its supposed do. Tinykin is a highly fun and innocent game that can also be relaxing.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a fun platformer + puzzler + collect-em-all. You may become proficient at move-tech for all the map crawling (if 100%ers) that awaits you. Also some "yeah, I can climb that!" type of platforming.Map races are optional and challenging to Platinum. Requires smashing inputs on oft-clippy terrain. I had fun with it. I'd prefer a Plat-every-race achievement for fellow monitor-moaners shaving 0.44s and rage-restarting from red +time deltas.Some achievements are buggy. Tinykin can be 100% by revisiting every room again (including attic) if you have met the requirements. There are no helpers for 100%. You will crawl (with a glideboard) all over each level for a missed corner.Art was fun, humor is clean (I hopped on a toilet-flushing button), levels are interesting and unique. I ignored most of the story and immediately got to collecting and grinding the races. Thanks for the game, Splashteam.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun utilizing the variety of tinykin, a mechanic which shines better in late game, and is missed when/if backtracking. Unfortunately, I've never played Pikmin, but this scratched that itch for me. Going for 100% can be a bit laborious, but at least the time-trials weren't included in achievements, only for cosmetics.If you don't get the Gotta Catch 'em All achievement after collecting all the tinykin, walk into each of the levels after finishing the game and it should unlock for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a joyful excursion through a giant house that was mysteriously abandoned by it's owner and then taken over by tribes of (mostly friend) bugs. All the bugs worship the previous inhabitant like a god and creator. Everything in the house is humorously to scale, including a bath tub that's a giant pool party and elitist bugs that live up in the high shelves. The gameplay is a puzzle based collect-a-thon platformer mixed with a little Pikmin. There's no combat or bosses though. I picked this game up on a whim and it's been nothing but pure joy. It's not that long over all, but it has that simple yet effective charming quality where it knows it's a game that's meant to be enjoyed and it never takes itself too seriously. It's polished, colorful and fun from start to finish. I highly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A short and sweet 3D collectathon that's frankly an extremely pleasant experience all around. This is one of those games that just feels great to play, the controls are super responsive and it runs shockingly well for how big some of the environments are. Speaking of those environments, if you're one of those people who enjoys the giant house level trope in platformers, this is made for you. The entire game is based around exploring different rooms in a giant house while trying to find your ship parts and escape, and it's done in a really imaginative way that definitely sells what it would be like for a small creature trying to navigate these spaces. I can tell this is a game I would've fallen in love with as a kid for that aspect. Despite how big the levels are, they never feel empty. There's always a ton of stuff to do along the way from short but satisfying sidequests to collectables littered everywhere. It really lights up the Spyro fan within me that really just wants to run around and collect shiny objects sometimes. There's also the Tinykin themselves, these Pikmin-like dudes you use to interact with the world and transport items. There's a pretty good variety of them, ones that can conduct electricity, build bridges, explode, it's always kept pretty fresh with how they give you a new variation to mess around with each level. Now while this is probably sounding like "we have Pikmin at home" so far, that's pretty much where the similarities begin and end. There's no time limit in this game, and actually no combat to speak of. It's a lot less about tactics and survival, and more about just being a super chilled out experience. While it doesn't end up requiring that much player thought at the end of the day, I could definitely see this appealing to younger players or people who were interested in Pikmin but were put off by some of the more stressful elements. It's a simple game that doesn't push the envelope too far with its ideas, but is still a really good time and honestly just nice to zone out and relax with for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: To put it short, this game is a masterpeice. To put it long? While some cutscenes are a tiny bit dissapointing, and some concepts, carrying, pushing, etc. can be a bit overdone, they are still used in creative ways, and the characters, plot, pikminlike gimmick, are all really interesting and well done. This game is a 8-10 in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe i haven't posted a review for this game yet, shame on me!I've 100% this game (other than the platinum racing medals, i'm not good enough for those yet) and i have to say this is by far one of my favorite games ever. It has so much charm in both the visuals and characters. I'll try my best to go over each thing i love about this game without spoiling anything.The story:I won't go into too much detail with this. All i'll say is that the story is charming and has a GREAT ending. A good tip is to talk to every NPC, i know that sounds like a chore, but trust me when i say that nearly EVERY NPC in this game has their own charm to them and adds so much to the story. The gameplay:The gameplay is extremely fun. It's not TOO hard, but still gives you a challenge at moments still. The best way i can describe it is platformer Pikmin. The Tinykin are adorable and add a lot to the gameplay. You'll encounter multiple types that specialize in different tasks.My favorite thing about the gameplay though is how open each area is. You pretty much get free reign to explore as much as you want the moment you get there. The game doesn't force you to do the main mission first. It'll tell you what you need to do, but you can do it whenever you want to. The game encourages you to play at your own pace. You can either do the story mission immediately, or explore around the area. You'll find some NPCs have little side missions that expand on the quirky little world you're in. There's so many secrets in each area too, so make sure you're on the lookout for them.The Visuals:Man does this game look really pretty, everything is so vibrant! Each NPC's design is really charming too. Each area has it's own theme with it's own species of NPC with their own quirks and lifestyles. I know i've already said this, but everything just OOZES charm.I highly recommend this game to anyone that wants a fantastic platformer collectathon. I know i'm not the best at writing reviews, but i hope i've sold you if you're reading this! Trust me, it's well worth the price!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: What an utterly brilliant and charming game this is. I downloaded it when it came on Xbox game pass, never played it before it left. Then got in a Humble Choice bundle. Forgot about it then months later had a go. Instantly hooked. Everything from the controls to the level design are just perfect and the gameplay is pure fun. And it runs like a dream on Steam Deck. I simply can’t praise this high enough, most real proper fun I’ve had with a game in years and I’ve still got half of it to play. An easy 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A cozy, nostalgic collect-a-thon with surprisingly fun, interesting writing. Tinykin reminded me of Gamecube-era games like Chibi-Robo. Mechanically, it just feels good to move around in the game; something a lot of games don't seem to prioritize, everything else exploration wise just falls into place when the actual act of exploring the world is enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say THANK YOU! For a long time, I had been waiting for this kind of game on PC. This game gave me everything I've ever wanted, with this concept: "Mouse World." Basically, everything around you is larger, and you see the world from a mouse's perspective in a vast, expansive world.This game was amazing because it captured that vibe perfectly. It was cozy, the art direction was stunning, and the level design was incredible. Thank you for this! ❤️
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Playtime: 12.2 hrsIt kinda surprised me that I have only used like 12 hours to complete the game but felt like this game was way longer than that. Maybe because the content felt quite compacted in the sense that they have put many bits and pieces in the game. The graphics looked nice and the gameplay was fun. The challenges were a bit hard for me but thankfully they were not in the achievement list. Overall, it was a good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: It's very much like Pikmin. The graphics aren't as good. It's kinda papercraft-y and two dimensional. But the levels are much more fun. Climb around a house, a bathroom, a greenhouse. Solve people's side quests, explore, find little creatures to follow you. The art is nice, and the story unfolds naturally as you explore.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Really smooth and vibrant Pikmin-lite game. I dare say I had more fun with Tinykin than I did with OG Pikmin when it came out. Here you play as Milo who is crashed and shrunken down to insect size and you need to find and negotiate all your spaceship parts to repair your craft.Each part you need to find is contained within a level of sorts, which is one room/area of a two story house. You'll speak with a variety of common household insects (who are adorably modeled) to collectathon everything along with the tinykin (pikmin) who help you traverse the environment.Each area is very cleverly designed and the platforming is not very difficult. I had a lot of fun just scooting around finding every little thing I could. There is a kind of ASMR quality to it between the textures and SFX. The little animation sequences when you discover new tinykin are also ridiculously adorable. The dialogue and plot are not very serious and nothing really overstays is welcome. The main story can be finished in around 5-6 hours but there are some extra features if you want to stick around longer. Length also depends on how distracted you get completing side objectives and collecting everything in each level.It's difficult to not like this one. I played entirely on Steam Deck OLED and it looked great and had zero issues. I was playing some heavier games before this and I was happy to lighten the mood.I sat on this for a long time and wish I hadn't- if a sequel released I wouldn't make the same mistake.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed playing this game 10/10. I thought it was going to be easy, but it seems I just found out I'm not cut out for playing platformer games. Haha!  But I fell in love with the gameplay even though I was struggling. I managed to finish the main storyline and tbh, I wish there is a sequel. I wanna know what happens after!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cute, charming, and overall just good vibes. The inspiration from Pikmin and Chibi-Robo is seen, but it doesn't seem like it's trying to be a boring or generic copy of those games. If anything, it stands on it's own, right next to these other phenomenal games. Don't expect the same gameplay as Pikmin, as they change it up the gameplay enough to be it's own unique experience. Pleasantly surprised how much I love this game, and how addicting it is. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: One thing to keep in mind is that this game is not a platformer, despite looking like one.  There is no challenge in the jumping because you can float in the air (Though there are optional difficult races to unlock outfits, so I guess it does have that if you want it.)  I really enjoyed this game, thought it didn't overstay it's welcome, but it also didn't reach it's full potential.  The later Tinykin powers are very boring and a little annoying to use, but the devs seem to think it's fun as heck.  In addition, when you do questlines to unlock new potions of the map they are often just 2-3 rooms that take a few minutes to explore.  You will never have your mind blown.So I hope they make a second one and really knock it out of the park then.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people make the Pikmin comparison, and undeniably there are some shared mechanics, but Tinykin has its own identity and it's a lot of fun (also surprisingly deep in places). The main focus is on exploration with an underpinning of story - there is no combat and no time limits, you can scour every corner of the sprawling levels at your own pace. The art style is a blend of 2D and 3D which you get used to quickly, and the animated cutscenes add extra charm. Character movement has platform elements which are sharp and responsive, and checkpoints were generous. The menus helped you keep track of what quests you had completed and which were currently active. Overall, I loved discovering new areas in each room, and hearing what all the insect inhabitants had to say. Gathering all the nectar around the level to trade for extra hover ability time definitely scratched a collectathon itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A super fun platformer that I think people who are completionists will really enjoy. The environments are quite huge and it takes some time to do quests, collect items, and navigate the spaces. Also, the ending of this game has a very nice resolve. If I have one complaint, it is that sometimes the camera can be a pain, but it's not a constant thing. Mostly when you are in close spaces.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: If you grew up playing Pikmin and wanna try something SLIGHTLY similar, this game is so much fun and I recommend it 100%!The controls, movement and everything is super smooth and it's so much fun going around collecting everything. The enviroments are beautiful and interesting and the characters are cute. Love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Neat and simple little Pikmin-like exploration game with puzzle-solving/collectathon, similar aesthetic of a tiny space explorer in a human-scale worldNo combat at all, just fall damageFew mobility options based on soap for some reason, with a "soapboard" skateboard for speed and a glider bubble that can be upgraded for longer floats5 different types of Tinykin that you hatch out of eggs found around the environment, used for different puzzle-solving aspectsStory is... there, I guess - seems purely to be an A-to-B-to-C in order to get you to go through the various stages
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin
