_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Pikmin, you'll love this!I've only finished the first full room of the house so far, but I can already tell it's going to be a favorite. Feels so great to run around in - the controls are fun, the soapboard is fun, race mode is fun, the dialogue is fun... I could go on! So much to do and see every way you turn, but not so unfocused that it's hard to keep track of objects. Much less micro management/pressure than Pikmin titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: The game was a joy from beginning to end. The game is a lot like Pikmin with its exploration and puzzles, just minus the time limit and combat. You explore a house from a small view which reminded me of games such as Chibi Robo (and Pikmin haha), and I love how the bugs reworked each area to fit in their world. While there isn't much of a major overarching story, there is little environmental hints and secrets that well let you make some guesses. I won't say more on that regard as not to spoil anything. I really enjoyed my time with this game and heavily recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely game of the year for me.  Perfect casual, exploration experience, with great soundtrack, beautiful visuals and witty writing.  The world building feels a little like Supraland, style of humour and locations (the gameplay is very different), I think if you enjoy those types of games, you'll find a place in your heart for this.  Can't remember the last time a game has actually made me impatient to get back to it between breaks.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good chill and relax type game. The movement and traversing is very satisfying some of the best I've ever experienced. Very responsive and consistent. Collecting pollen felt similar to collecting Power Moons in Mario Odyssey. Each environment felt grand filled with hidden treasure will very little hand holding. Everything in this game is just perfect 10/10. Hope they make a sequel and look forward to anything this developer makes in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great 3d platformer/collectathon. Now halfway through the game and having a ball. The movement feels really good and the puzzles are pleasing. The one downside (if you even want to call it that) is getting the platinum medals in the races is really tough. Luckily you only need the gold medals to get the unlocks.9.5/10 - gets a little stale at points and the races might be frustrating for a beginner but if you like Mario Odyssey or Hat in Time this is for you
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A funny lil' puzzle-platformer with funny dialogue, memorable characters, an appealing presentation and great controls. Every Tinykin has its own purpose, meaning that the gameplay never feels stale, and every single world not only has its own subplot, but also a lot of depth and attention to detail, as every single area in the game is made out of various household objects that make sense from not only a gameplay perspective, but an aesthetic perspective as well. For example, at one point you come across a building that is literally just a guitar, allowing you to bounce and surf on the strings of the instrument, but also enter it and talk to the various NPCs that inhabit it. The game also has a subtle, slowly unfolding narrative about some sort of deity worshipped by some NPCs that leaves you speculating throughout your entire playthrough, with it all culminating in the ending. Overall, this game is a high recommend, but let me make something very clear: Despite having pretty much the exact same gameplay premise, the game plays very differently from Pikmin, so it's more of a recommend to fans of collectathons like Super Mario 64 or Banjo Kazooie than fans of Pikmin.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a very cute and creative platformer, with an interesting storyline and fun challenges. Game has a similar idea to Pikmin, but with its own vibe and themes around it. A great, chill game to play and relax with (except when attempting timed challenges). My total playtime for completing the game 100% was about 12 hours (I did get stuck at some points), and the achievements are well-integrated into the game which make them great to earn. Excellent game to get :3
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: One of the very best collect-a-thon game ever made. Level design is top notch, controls are perfect, visually it's beautiful and cute, it's funny, it's not too long, not too difficult... It's just perfect. I finished it two times on Xbox through GamePass, and I bought it again on Steam to play it on my ROG Ally. It's that good.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is just great!It's a game where you can lay back, relax and enjoy some simple platforming and collecting.The little details like the grunts from the Tinykin synchronizing with the soundtrack (which is also great btw) really make this game feel polished.The game and it's levels doesn't overstay their welcome, every level is timed just right to stay interesting from beginning to end.I hope the developers provide some new levels or add paid DLC for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most fun games I've played in a long time. It's everything I liked about Pikmin, with a few creative twists that make it a totally unique experience. I also appreciate that all the achievements completely doable without sinking too much time or following guides; I hit 100% after around 15 hours. Thumbs up all around.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Had seen recommended, and picked it up on sale. I would have 100% paid full price for it. In incredible package in a short, fun romp. Feels as if Pikmin meets Mario Odyssey. Around ever corner is something new to take your attention away from the current objective, in a good way. I always saw something off in the distance I wanted to explore next, and never once did I feel the game drag or slow, rather only pickup as you unlock new zones, and learn how to better utilize the tinykin.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I did not rush through this game, nor am I one to go out of my way to platinum anything. That said, I finished the game in one go, got a decent amount of achievements just by playing/exploring, and I feel like it went by too fast. I'll get some hate for this next bit - I recently played the first Pikmin sometime within the last 2 years. I strongly feel that this game is what Pikmin could have, nay, SHOULD have been. Tinykin was a joy, and I haven't felt that with a game for an extraordinary amount of time; since maybe PS2/Gamecube? It was short, sweet, and to the point as they say, but being able to enjoy (literally) every nook and cranny was simply a delight. I'm aware not every game is for everyone, but if you think you will like it, go for it when you next get paid - Treat Yo Self! P.S. I enjoyed all the punny references I recognized.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Adorable game with great world design and writing. base mechanics are rather simple with most puzzles being solved by aim at thing and throw tinykin, but theres enough variety in what you are throwing at and the function of the tinykin that it stays interesting enough for the 7 hours I played it. Was reccommended to me because of Pikmin appreciation, and while on the surface does seem very pikminy, in mechanics it is much more a collectathon than a creature management. I tend to enjoy collectathons so it wasn't a turn off, but sadly left my itch for combat and challenging strategy unscratched. its a very easy game with the most difficulty just coming form the new time trials and even they can be beaten without too much time.As a collectathon its a pretty fun game but suffers from 2 collectathon sins. overcrowding worlds with collectables and not including in game ways to track down the final ones. its near impossible to find missing tinykin or pollen without watching 10-20 minute guides and retracing whole rooms again in what is just a major slog. They really needed some unlockable pollen/tinykin compass or some other method to locate them in a room.Writing and world design are easily where tinykin does its best. all the races and characters have entertaining and cute personalities that makes you want to learn more of them and help them solve their rather petty issues. The way the world is broken into real house rooms is done amazingly with each one getting very different astetics and really making you feel like its a different stage proper. I was a little surprised to find no modding community at all exists for this game. but after playing I think I see why, the mechanics of the game wear out quickly. and without that fresh writing and world design theres no reason to play or replay the game new content or no. Was just really hoping someone had modded in a compass for finding those last collectables.Tinykin is worth the time and price to play, but definitely could've done with some small changes to make the endgame completion actually manageable, and more gameplay variety and difficulty would go a long way.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a charming and engaging game that I really enjoyed playing. The unique blend of 2D and 3D platforming elements, combined with the adorable Tinykin creatures, made for a delightful experience. The mechanics are simple, yet the game keeps you hooked from start to finish. My only wish is that it was longer, as I found myself wanting more after completing it. Overall, Tinykin is a cool game that I highly recommend to anyone looking for a fun and refreshing platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really well-made 3D collect-a-thon. It's supposedly a Pikmin clone, but having not played any of the Pikmin games I didn't care at all.The graphics are easily some of the best of any indie game, blending realistic and cartoony graphics with ridiculously high attention to detail. It's incredibly how such finely crafted and somewhat large levels are loaded in full and the game still runs super well.Controls are crisp and responsive. It feels ridiculously good to jump around, throw your little buddies around, and dash through spider string. This goes hand-in-hand with the amazing sound design that makes everything feel that much more punchy and satisfying. It's a dangerously addicting game in a very natural way.I really only have three issues with the game. The first being that I wish there was some sort of compass that tracks missing collectibles. The game doesn't even need to give it to you right away, maybe it can give it you only when you already have 95% of the collectibles on a level, for example. Similar games like A Hat in Time and Sludge Life have something like this already, and it's great with these types of games when you're cleaning up your collectibles list. My second issue is that the story of each level is kinda bland, which isn't a major issue by any stretch.My last issue is that the game is really short. You can complete it in 9 hours, which is a shame because I really did want to play more. There's a lot that can be done with the concept, and I really wish a sequel is in the works.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and very well made!  is yet more proof that smaller teams can make great games by combining a strong grasp of what makes a genre so satisfying with a dedication to getting the basics right.The levels are big and enticing, just begging to be explored. They're packed with the usual collectibles and environmental puzzles, as well as a lot of charming background detail. There's the design itself, cute and evocative, as well as many NPCs providing dialog, fleshing out the world-building, and just being silly and funny. The world of  doesn't take itself seriously, but the writing is decent and internally consistent. It's nice to spend some time with these folk.It's a relatively easy game. You can get 100% of everything by just exploring, paying attention, and patiently trying things out. Puzzles are simple and there's no combat. The only real challenge might come from some 3D platforming, but controls are tight and forgiving and shouldn't cause much frustration. There are optional race challenges that do push your skills much more, but they are actually quite fun if you're into that, and do well to demonstrate that the basic control scheme is solid. You're not going to be thinking too much about angles and camera positions, which is exactly as it should be in 3D platforming games.My only critique, really, is that it's just too easy for my tastes. My favorite game of this type is , which has challenging puzzles, lots of secrets, combat, and is just far bigger and more complex than . It's OK and nice to keep things simple!  scratches a more casual itch, but delivers fully on its promise. Still, I'm confident that Splashteam can go much bigger, too, and hope they will in the future.Two thumbs up from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: (ignore my play time, I played it on another account through family sharing)Great game! Originally I thought this was a Pikmin clone, but it's actually a pure collectathon platformer without any combat, or puzzles really. Art and music are amazing, and the controls are top-notch, even on mouse and keyboard. Here's hoping they make a sequel!Lastly, on the subject of length, this does not have much of it. It's a 6 hour game, take it or leave it or buy on a sale. Either way, this is a unique experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun collectathon with a purpose. What purpose you may ask? Explore and enjoy the cool atmosphere! How can you not love "Honey I Shrank the Pikmin"? It's old school platforming (think Banjo-Kazooie that uses collectibles as a focal point) with modern sensibilities (lots of shortcuts within the levels and no game overs).
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A mix of Psychonauts and Pikmin, but probably closer to Psychonauts in gameplay and Pikmin in setting. Cute art style accompanying very fun level design that does a great job encouraging exploration. Took me about 7ish hours to complete 100%, so the length really hits that sweet spot for me where it doesn't feel too short for the money spent but not too long where you begin to get bored. Kinda like those movies that are a very tight, well paced 90-100 min runtime.However, I think with a collectathon like this there could be a better way to keep track of what you collect (primarily the Tinykin). Psychonauts 1 and 2 have that figment book which makes it easier to go search up the location of a missing collectable as opposed to carefully combing through the level again. Overall, very fun. One of those games you can play when you want something relaxing but also want to change it up from playing another farming simulator cozy game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I truly can't put into words how much I loved this game. I've always loved tiny things. The Borrowers, Littlest Pet Shop and Polly Pocket (the OG designs) and Kelly dolls. I just loved the idea of being tiny in a huge world. This game was perfect for that.I see this game compared a lot to Pikmin but I honestly might like it better. With Pikmin I think we get like a few levels inside but mostly we're in a garden. In Tinykins we're crawling up and down and all over so many rooms in a whole house. It's perfect. Scratched an itch I didn't know i had. The design of this game was perfect. All the little details in the house that made up the world of Tinykins were just so clever and continually brought a smile to my face. I've been having a hard go of it lately and I just needed a change of pace from my switch. I had bought this game in a humble bundle awhile back and decided to give it go on my PC and I'm so glad I did. I just spent hours having such a great time. I was playing and suddenly thinking "oh my gosh is that serotonin? Wow I forgot what that felt like." I just loved crawling over every inch of this adorable little world. I loved it all. I even teared up at the end. Such a sweet story. Will definitely be replaying. This game was a gift and so needed. You can feel the love that went into it. Wonderful little game that now has a big place in my heart. If I could hug the Dev team, I would. You guys brought me so much joy playing this game. Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been extremely happy with the game! The humour, gameplay, the world and the performance on steam deck were all top notch.I am very pleasantly surprised by the high quality of this game. It seems like a nice palette cleanser between heavier games, with its cuteness, humour and nostalgic aesthetics. It is pretty short like most of these games are. However the challengers update expands on the content a bit and I haven’t even played that fully yet! The game doesn’t feel drawn out or too rushed as a benefit. Every world is different, beautifully hand crafted, with secrets and nice character dialogue all throughout the maps. The different quests and types of Tinykin keep the gameplay fresh and dynamic.The exploration is amazing, moving with the soap board is so neat and quick, and the amazing soundtrack and beautiful but simple art style come together to create a true gem of an experience. It honestly transported me back to my childhood at some moments. The characters were a pleasant surprise, every level is full of different bugs; silverfish, ants, dung beetles (my favourite), dragonflies and other types I don’t know of. Some memorable bugs were Jack and Rose who you need to bring together, Guevara that is trying to start a revolution, Marx that talks about religion being the opium for the people, Tesla and Edison that argue about the microwave. The bugs all follow a religion and every bug species has a different personality and role in the house. It’s all so fun! A definite recommendation and a very pleasant surprise!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Went into this game expecting something like Pikmin, instead got something closer to a 3D Mario but with nearly no challenge. Approachable, charming and well executed in nearly every way, but too simple and easy for what my blind expectations were, which left me a bit disappointed. Still, for what it is, it is very good. Dung beetles best bois.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I came to this game looking for something like pikmin. While it shares a few elements I wouldn't quite say it met those expectations. However this game is so gosh darn good as the collectathon that it is. All of the mechanics have a good and reasonable purpose even if I didn't initially understand why they were the way they were. The collectables aren't bonkers hard to find and are fun to look for. It's fun to piece together things from context clues. Basically this game is fun and totally worth the $25 it costs at full price. If it ever goes on sale and you think you might be interested I would not hesitate on the purchase. Also not hard to 100% and fun to do so.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Takes inspiration from Pikmin and platformers on the N64. While a short game and so not as complete as a full release Nintendo game, it has a lot of charm and is a relaxing and low-pressure experience set in a house which evokes feelings of warmth and cosiness.Platforming skill level required is around Lego game level with a little more needed to 100% all achievements.A worthwhile purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone's initial thought is going to be this is just more Pikmin, but it's really not. The game is more-so a collectathon, with the main thing you're going to be collecting is more Tinykin to collect more collectables. Pikmin is a survival/strategy/puzzle game where this is an exploration game. If I do have any negatives, it's that the puzzles are very easy, you don't even have to know what puzzle you're solving just throw resource at glowing object and it'll work out. Most of the time I wouldn't talk to the NPC's and just start exploring till I noticed something to pick up, not knowing why. That's not totally bad, the game is centered more on a casual experience where you walk around and take on the environment, no enemies, simple puzzles, just explore. The game excels at that, it's beautiful and I couldn't put it down because I wanted to see more. If you're looking for a new Cozy game where you just explore as a lil guy then this is the game for you.TLDR: Game simple and cute  :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I stumbled upon this game on accident, and gave it a shot while it was on sale. And wow. Definitely worth full price! Such a fun addictive game! I'm so sad there isn't a sequel yet. I want more levels! If you like simple, addictive gameplay, this is it. Adorable characters, cute story line. LOTS of collectables and challenges. I would say the two biggest cons are that it's pretty short, and that there isn't any DLC or sequel yet :/
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I've had an eye on this game. Since it was on sale, I decided to finally pick it up and give it a whirl.Holy crap, this game is awesome!If you like 3D Platformers and collecting things, I highly recommend that you play this game. I love Super Mario 64, Banjo-Kazooie and other 3D platformers along those lines, and this game fits perfectly in with them. I also really love the "rats" feel with being tiny. It reminds me of those rats maps that people made for Counter-Strike. I'd say this game is the child if Psychonauts and Pikmin had a baby.If you can't enjoy a game if it is not difficult, this may not be for you as the game doesn't pose much of a challenge. It is purely about platforming, exploration, collecting and solving puzzles. There really isn't any combat to speak of.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great.If you want a fun little adventure game, puzzle game and exploration game with no enemies highly recommend this one.The art style and canvas is adorable and works well, the backdrop and the world are very creative and fun. So much nostalgia of platformer games came through while i was playing this. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible.Everything is amazing, characters (take a look at every characer's name), camera, movement, jumping, menus, dialogs, world/environment... It's been so long since I didn't find any game as engaging as this one, I want to play it at every time of the day, it's soooo pleasant to play to find everything on the map and continuing the small story it has.It's like Pikmin but faster, without time restrictions and super dynamic to play.By the way, this game looks made specially for Steam Deck, everything at max works flawlessly, just be sure to use ProtonGE last version to be able to play the cutscenes and other fixed stuff. The performance is almost perfect at 60 and maxed out (only minor hiccups in some situations).
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Nice bitesized 3d platformer bursting with charm. The visuals and world design are easily the highlights. Mostly quick, engaging platforming with reasonable control. Exploring/discovering the zones is rather fun, though some of the puzzles near the latter half of the game become tedious/time consuming. Rather short story though, so I'd recommend it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: is a delightful little collectathon 3D platformer, and well worth a look if you're a fan of the genre or just want a chill game to vibe with.  It's got a lovely visual style, with 2D characters contrasted wonderfully against 3D environments, and working through its numerous worlds collecting items and solving puzzles with the Pikmin-like Tinykin is consistently engaging.  For those that want something a bit more fast-paced and challenging, an update even added time trial races that get surprisingly difficult!  The game can be a bit fiddly about what counts as a rail to grind on during these races, though, which can lead to occasional frustration.  Also, the option for some sort of direction when finding the last few collectibles in a level would be nice, as there's a lot of little nooks and crannies they can hide in that aren't immediately obvious.  These issues are minor when taking the game as a whole, though, and I had a great time 100%ing  and definitely recommend giving it a look if it piques your interest.Full review
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Solid collect-athon platformer.  I can see the immediate resemblance to Pikmin, but the similarities really stop at "using the abilities of tiny little guys".  There is far more in common with something like Banjo-Kazooie with its collection and hovering jump, where the abilities are just unlocked by collecting little guys (the tinykin). Level design is nice, with a focus on verticality.  Shortcuts are plentiful, and levels are generally good at not overstaying their welcome.  Might have been nice to have some levels that follow a different formula.  Maybe some kind of more linear level, instead of each one essentially being a big box?Art design, music, and sound design is fantastic.  World felt very cohesive.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game was available as part of a bundle containing a bunch of tinyBuild games for only 15 bucks. I'd highly recommend checking out Humble Bundle for great bundles like this, the proceeds from your purchases are also donated to charity!This was a really good and fun game. It took a long time to 100% all achievements but it was worth it. Some of the achievements like "Gotta Catch 'em All" and "Master Brewer" were extremely tedious, as you have to search every corner of each map to find every last tinykin or pollen, and that can prove to be a real challenge.I may have spent more time hunting for those items than I did actually playing the game, but it was still a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Steam achievements are broken and haven't been fixed in over 2 years!Beside that I had fun with the game. The building bridges and carrying around objects gets tedious later on but the visuals are great and exploring is still satisfying. Building your army of Tinykin and getting stronger with them over time is a cool game loop. There isn't much story except for the end scene.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly charming way to while away ten hours.  Completely child friendly without being exclusive to them, Tinykin tickles the innocent collect-em-up urge as well as compulsion to explore and interact with the secrets of a massively scaled-up house room with a miniaturized hero.  And as soon as exploration's done, you're off to another, new, untouched room.  Expertly pitched to not outlast its welcome in any aspect, Tinykin is a holiday-romance of a game.  You'll love it utterly for two days, spend every moment with it.  And when it's time to say goodbye, it leaves with a fond farewell.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: It's obvious why people compare this to Pikmin, what with being the size of a bug and being followed by loyal minions, but it plays entirely different.  The Tinykin really aren't the star of the show, being more like tools than anything else.  Instead, this is a relaxing, low stress, but more importantly an enjoyable collectothon.  The maps are well designed with lots of verticality and nooks everywhere, providing for plenty of exploration and some light puzzle solving.  The variety of objectives with sufficient rewards without outright requiring you to find every last speck of pollen means there is still a satisfying end to the game without aiming for 100%.  It's not usually my type of game, but it was a great time nonetheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun and charming 3D collectathon, with pretty good traversal mechanics.Tinykin offers a few hours of pure enjoyment, exploring its cute levels and unlocking new abilities.It has a pretty intersting artstyle, offering a 3D world mixed with 2D characters - all in a colorful and joyful palette.Level design is top notch.The small missions sprinkled through the levels were varied enough and funny to solve. Everything feels pretty polished, but what surprised me the most were the controls: they just felt right. It's not hard by any means, and I didn't connect at all with the story (but the writing is okay). Yet I'm glad I played it: it shows 3D platformers can still be fun even with simple mechanics.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I have now played this game three times. If Tinykin has no fans I apparently wasn't asked. This game is just SO darn cute. I have cried at the end, every. single. time. I love the way the outside characters were able to be built just through photos and the way the home is decorated. I am in love with all the dialogue from all the bugs and love their names. Whenever I get my next pet in life I plan on naming them Dovycan after one of the ants in the City of Sanctar. This game has a special place in my heart. If you like cute games, a little bit of challenge, and a great story I would definitely recommend Tinykin. I am the kind of gamer that likes to collect everything I can in games and this one is perfect for it. The first play I was definitely frustrated finding some of the pollen, I'm talking I searched high and low and just wanted to find that ONE I was missing but as soon as its in your grubby paws, pure bliss. I would love to see more games like this one in the future. I'd love to see them figure out an interesting way to make a sequel but am totally fine just having my baby Tinykin to replay whenever I please. Great job to everyone who worked on this game. All of your hard work is very much appreciated by me. Buy it if you like cute collection story games.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin captures on of the things I miss a lot from 3D platformers and that is just the ability to go wherever you'd like within a level. Want to go up those cupboards over there instead of following the main mission path? Sure, go for it. Throw in the incredibly unique look of the game and the charm that all the little Tinykin bring, you've got yourself a pretty great way to spend a couple evenings as the game isn't any longer than it needs to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Pikmin, this game is for you. If you don't like Pikmin, this game might still be for you. Another take on visiting the potential original Earth, you use specialized creatures called Tinykin to navigate the different bug-governed sectors of a giant house.The bugs are quite cute (besides the cockroaches, ew) and have great stories. A few of them even follow you around the house, which makes a nice side story whenever you find a familiar character. I never thought I'd care about a shield bug, but this game surprised me. The ending was kind of rushed I think, but for such a short game I suppose that's merited.Gameplay-wise, I started to get bored in the last level, but at that point I was only chasing some more achievements and could easily finish the game when the search became too much. This game is pretty purely a collectathon, but it does a great job designing levels to lead you naturally to most things you'd want to find. It's much less stressful than Pikmin, opting for more of a platformer genre rather than a combat strategy. The most punishment you receive is wasting time by falling off the top of a cabinet.Overall it was a lot of fun, and short enough it didn't overstay its welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: A great collectathon for all ages. There is no penalty for death and no real threats around the house. Just explore the colorful levels and collect all the stuff you can find. The level-design is also pretty clever on how it gets easier to traverse to parts where you've already been before. The controls feel great and responsive.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an adorable charming pikmin-like game. I'm having lots of fun playing it and traversing the environment. I decided I would stream it and today is a non-streaming day and I wanna PLAY! Not many games make me wanna play them without a break.I love the 2D characters in a 3D world. The insect characters are adorable. Some of the names make me groan (and laugh), but everyone groans at puns. It's nice that I can start doing quests without even realizing it's a quest just because I came upon something that felt out of place and decided to go after it. It's rather intuitive. You can start a quest and not even realize you were doing one until it finishes the the quest giver is all, "Yo thanks Milo!" It's just good fun. Chill, cozy, low stress, perfect for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: This game plays a little bit like Pikmin, but it's a collectathon through and through. The levels are giant house rooms, like in Chibi-Robo, demanding vertical exploration as well as horizontal. Also, there's zero combat.There's so many things I loved about this game!Exploring every level, searching, finding, collecting!Meeting every bug NPC and reading their fun dialog! Taking on their quests fed back into that exploring and collecting gameplay.The level design is a delight! Every level is a massive room in a human-sized house, and everyday objects have been assembled into structures that make for platforming setups or for living quarters for the bugs. It's so charming and I was continuously delighted to stop and appreciate which giant household objects were used to make up the things I was walking around.Using the Tinykin's abilities is a massive upgrade from Pikmin 4 in terms of QoL features and ease of use. (Minor spoiler what green Tinykin do) For example, if you want to construct a , you just hold down right trigger. The Tinykin rapidly form a  on the spot and Milodane rapidly . No need to swap to a specific type of Tinykin! Example 2: Hold left trigger to aim a throw, then tap or hold right trigger to throw Tinykin. Again, no need to swap types! They automatically know which specialized type to toss when aimed at whatever kind of thing you're aiming at. Tinykin use is streamlined so I never felt inconvenience, and that really helped my flow while exploring and traversing.My one and only gripe are the Tinykin's visual design themselves. These little cyclops don't have an endearing design IMO, and they don't have much personality as a result. I didn't feel any bond or fondness toward them. Completely inferior to their counterpart, Pikmin, in this respect, who are charming, adorable, and full of personality.Luckily this was only a problem with the Tinykin themselves. Every insect NPC has an awesome design, charm, and personality. And to be clear my critique is only aesthetic: I vastly prefer the Tinykin's utility and interactions over Pikmin's.

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun 3D platformer I just finished. I highly recommend this if you are looking for some old school 3D platforming\collectathon. Set in a whimsical world, players embark on a journey with the adorable Tinykin to save their stranded spaceship. _childDocuments_.review: pikmin if it was good /j i love pikmin smok but this was so delightful to just burn through. the level design makes traversal/looping back so fluid. it absolutely scratches the Pikmin itch and with the added platforming elements, it feels like an evolution of the formula in some cases. although, it's more in line with Pikmin 2 or 4 in that the speed running/focus on dandori is left up to you rather than it being ingrained into the story. there is no combat as well, but i don't think there needs to be. despite my heavy mentioning of its inspiration, it's a wonderful game that stands on its own and my biggest critique is there isn't more of it for me to play now.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite scratching the Pikmin itch and obviously inspired by Pikmin, Tinykin stands as it's own unique game. You want to explore everything and the best part is that it's *reasonable* to explore it all, AKA It doesn't feel pointless or overwhelming, it feels just right. Exploration is even more fun with how great it felt moving the character around. It's a super polished, cute game and satisfying to play. My only wish is that it had a slightly higher difficulty and more to do/explore. Overall, it's a comfort game that is fun to play and makes you feel accomplished with each session.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A funny game worth playing.A small tip for who wants to get all achievements: just go and search every corner of each place  to find all tinykin and pollen, talk with every character, and you can unlock the few most difficult achievements. For the remaining achievements, it is easy to know the method to unlock just by understanding the name of those achievements.If you have already collected everything but no achievements pop out, go back to each place you have completed, then all achievements will unlock.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin, like the name and visuals may suggest, is a Pikmin-like game, but how does it hold up?You take on the role of Milodin, a human who finds a distress signal and is teleported to a strange, seemingly giant world. Upon doing so you meet Tinykin, strange little creatures that follow you and that you can use to engage with the environment in a variety of ways. Your goal is to collect pieces of a machine in order to get back home. To do so you must use a variety of Tinykin to help out the bug denizens of the household. All in all there are five Tinykin types. They all have a purpose and they vary in their utility. The game is rather casual, opting for more of a collectathon platformer as opposed to Pikmin's tactical RTS roots. It fits well and plays well overall but I do wish the Tinykin had a bit more to them overall. Having a singular purpose is a tad underwhelming.  Movement in the game is fantastic however, it's again not complicated but it feels really good to float around and surf on the soap board. I think for some the gameplay could get quite repetetive, I think that the world's design itself is interesting and really cool, there's a great sense of scale and a lot of things to interact with. I just wish that the interactions could be a bit more nuanced or the tinykin could be used in more ways as a lot of it is aim at thing, the game switches to the correct tinykin and you throw it. I think maybe having more room for player error could help to make the gameplay less static as you can't really screw up anything. Despite the free roam of each level, you are on rails in how you approach the solutions to everything. On the aesthetic and audio side of things, the game is phenomenal. The visuals are gorgeous, everything looks great, the 2D characters all look well drawn and have a lot of great detail and the environments are incredible. Sound wise, the soundtrack is quite strong. It's quite dynamic and changes as you explore areas but is overall quite light but all fits together well. The sound effect and visual effects are also really well put together and make the whole thing satisfying and engaging. All in all, it's a fantastic game that just could do with a little more going on, a little more player control and a little more variety. I would like to see a sequel and given how it concludes, the opportunity would be there. I hope that there's just more to engage with and a little more nuance if the devs choose to build from a game with some great bones.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game fairly blind; all I knew was it was inspired by Pikmin, a game I had heard of but never played myself. Now, having finished a playthrough, let me say: Wow, this is a really great game. This absolutely deserves the high rating it has on Steam right now. For an indie game, this has an incredible amount of polish and charm. If you like collectathons with light puzzle mechanics, you will love this. It stays fresh from start to finish, and runs awesome on Steam Deck, too. Play this one, you wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I always appreciate games that are somewhat challenging, but have a lot of QOL features so that when you mess up a handful of times, you're not paying for it with hours of your life. Some people like that... I think they're masochists. But anyway. Controls are super responsive, fun platformer. Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so much fun. The art style is super cute and the gameplay is similar to that of Pikmin where you command different kinds of Tinykin to complete tasks and explore. Like Pikmin, the goal is to collect "ship parts" to return to your home planet. The writing is quite fun and there are a TON of references to other media like Spongebob and Avatar the Last Airbender which I enjoyed spotting.Be warned however, some of the trophies are slightly bugged. If you exit playing the game and then log back in to continue collecting items afterwards, some of the related trophies do not pop when you finish collecting everything. I was missing 4-5 trophies until . After doing that, all of them popped at once for some reason.Overall, it feels good to play and collecting all of the items felt rewarding. In terms of difficulty, personally I'm not good at platformer games but I was able to navigate the world just fine. For those who are experienced in platformer exploration games, this probably won't be challenging for you. The main game can be completed in about 6 hours or less.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was awesome and reminded me a lot of my favorite platformers from the N64 and Gamecube days. Its a wonderful, chill collectathon with a surprisingly bizarre story. While not very challenging, its engaging, silly and fun. Its a great game to just zone out and play through in one Saturday or something.
