_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: You start an adventure as Milo discovering the sweet Tinykins and then you surf on a bar of soap which I like to call a biscuitand send orders to the little guys who will do anything for you in order to progress further!Love how the name of the game and the publisher both has ''tiny'' in their names.This is an 11/10 platformer with unique gameplay, art and whatnot which is worth to have in your collection if you love creative and chill 3D platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, cute platformer/collectathon game. Engages you just enough and doesn't overstay it's gameplay. Finding the last few things on any level can be a slog, but at about 6 hours for a 100% completion, it's not that bad. (Only didn't complete races and therefore outfits.)I found the controls smooth and fluid. The overall was a complete experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Fun, the "puzzles" have just been 'how do i get to that place?" Does a great job of making you feel very small in the world. The rooms are put together really nicely and look pretty. The tinykins are cute and the new tinykin videos are informative and funny. If you like simple exploring, with some traversal puzzles, and gathering all the things, this is a nice simple game to play. So far no stress, except when falling from heights, curious what happens next in the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is one of the most polished and fun 3d platformers I've played. This is right up there with series like Spyro or Mario. In fact, if I were to compare it to anything, it'd be some weird hybrid of Mario Odyssey and Pikmin. This is the most Nintendo game not made by Nintendo, and I mean that as praise. But really, it's very much got it's own identity and spin on things.The first thing you might notice aside from how beautiful and bright and cheery everything is, is that the game has you collecting little creatures. These guys can be used to perform several different tasks from climbing to carrying. The main flow of the game is you exploring and collecting these little dudes. The more you find, the more you can explore, and the more you can solve the problems of the denizens of this giant house. It's a very satisfying loop.And the loop feels great in part to the excellent controls. You zip about the place, and have this amazing soap surfing move to go faster or fly across wires that act as unlockable shortcuts, and a bubble floating ability that can be upgraded. The environments seem huge but it's a breeze to get back to anywhere you've been. And it's not without fun platforming bits either, those are important in a platformer after all. It's just so dopamine inducing to climb the worlds tallest potted plant and then zoom along a string back to the center of the current room you're exploring.And the rooms are the real star of the show to me, even more so than the tinykin. Each one is just so jam packed with details and little nooks and crannies. It's so cool to get high up and be like, yep this is a living room, but then you get down close and there's an apartment of bugs in the bookshelf and a secret platforming challenge inside a piano or a church under the big cardboard box. Who knows what you'll find under the couch?This has so much heart and polish, and is just such fun to play, that you owe it to yourself to not miss out. If you even halfway like platformers, PLEASE give this one a chance.Curator page:
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is nothing new, just a solid 3D platformer/collectathon but the level/environment design in this just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ shines, it's amazing. Somehow the story is also ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ great, has a real strong moment towards the end that was just unexpected—which is undermined by some extra dialogue right afterwards, which I wish was left more vague, but whatever, a moment is a moment— The side dialogues are riddled with references which can get annoying but they're side ♥♥♥♥ so who cares, the core narrative is pretty tight. Buy the game and support the devs this really was something, just go exploring and skating around the house, try not to get involved with the religious and political failures of the bugs (or ).
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a glorious achievement in skeletal game design. Splashteam has done a phenomenal job with the Pikmin-like formula, and has in some ways surpassed Nintendo's age-old franchise. The level of polish on display mixed with its perfect art design and mechanical precision is one which will stay with any player who gives it a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is an absolutely phenomenal little adventure game absolutely burtsing at the seams with charm. I adored every minute of my time with it. I've never actually played a Pikmin game myself, only having seen streams of it, but from what I know Tinykin really captures the same atmosphere of experiencing the world from a miniscule point of view. I loved the art direction, the environments all felt larger than life with plenty of detail to get lost in, telling a story without words. The contrast between the slight realism in the environmental design and the much more cartoonish character design works really well, the bright colours standing out and grabbing your attention. The writing and worldbuilding really brought a smile to my face. I found it incredible how such a light-hearted game was able to capture the issues that occur in societies more genuinely than some other games that take themselves more seriously. I loved how each species of insect had distinct personality types, the shy and anxious dung beetles, the stoner silverfish, the paranoid mantises and so on. There's was so much superb dialogue, dozens of references to different media, I highly recommend taking the time to talk to every NPC possible. Gameplay wise the platforming and general movement all feels tight and fun to do, sliding and floating around quickly becomes intuitive. There's a good sense of depth so I never feel like I don't know where my character is going to land. And I found the tinykin abilities had good variety and implemented into the environment well.Collectathon style gameplay isnt for everyone, but it plays well into my completionist nature, the one big downside of Tinykins collectables is there's no form of hint system for them and often I found myself going back and forth in a level desperately looking for the last 10 or so pollen. Implementing some form of hint/radar to the AR goggle mechanic for the smaller and more numerous collectables would have been a nice addition but not a deal breaker. The only other negative I encountered was the animated cut scenes didn't play properly for me, I only saw a no signal visual, I'm not sure if this was due to playing on the Steam Deck or not but it was a bummer I didn't see the animations throughout the game. Overall I think Tinykin is well worth the time to play, there's something here for most people to enjoy, wether it be the visuals, writing or gameplay, it exceeds on all fronts.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a wholesome little 3d platformer where you play a tiny astronaut exploring a giant house. There's no combat at all - the game is entirely focused on platforming, collectables and puzzles. It's well worth giving this game a whirl if that sounds like your sort of thing. For me it was the perfect low stress, high fun game I've been looking for.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Got it on sale and really enjoyed my time with it. There are no timers which is fantastic as I can explore without worrying about losing out or getting any kind of anxiety while playing. You can fall from a huge height and die but there's no consequences - you just start back where you jumped off at. The controls are intuitive (Steam Deck, controller) in that the little pikmin guys will dynamically build or attach as needed rather than you having to remember who does what and selecting them individually. Highly recommended for a chill collecting and puzzle type of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome Collectathon!- movement in this game is great, its fast enough to not get bored and has a lot of potential to get better at it- the whole tinykin mechanic is awesome aswell and makes the game really fun- the races are really challenging but still fun enough to not give up- the level are beautiful- it has about 9-12 hrs of playtime (till 100%), which is a good amount imo. didnt get boring but im still satisfied with the time i got from thisso all in all a great game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is an air-tight, absolute joy of a platformer. This game is pure platforming fun, and rides that line of “challenging enough to be stimulating but simple and easy enough to never get frustrated while playing.” Definitely a “sit back and relax” type of game. -> Exceptional movement system-> Creative environments-> Adorable art style-> Well-optimized -> Great environmental & adaptive musicMy only real con is that I didn’t find the characters particularly interesting? And I had a hard time telling some of them apart except for the residents of Chrysal. But this didn’t bother me much.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A charming and chill 3D platformer you can finish in <10 hours. The music is excellent, the characters are cute, and the controls are responsive. It has some elements of Pikmin, but overall its more like halfway between Banjo-Kazooie and Pikmin. Unlike Pikmin, it doesn't have any time limits; that will make it less stressful for some people, but also means you lose the element of having to plan your days and multitask efficiently.I got maybe 95% of all the collectables in about 9 hours, which was a perfect length for how complex the gameplay is. My only complaint is I like to 100% games like this, but finding the last 2 or 3 collectables out of >1000 on each level is a big pain. I wish there was a post-game item that gives you an optional radar or something for people who want to get everything without spending hours re-checking every nook and cranny.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this platformer! It's such a fun and simple game that's perfect for chilling out after a long day. The levels are super creative and rewarding, and you really have to explore every nook and cranny to find all the collectibles. The story is interesting and the dialogue is hilarious, so don't be afraid to chat with some of the random strangers you encounter along the way. The visuals are absolutely stunning and cartoony, making it a joy to look at. The controls are spot on and the introduction to them is done in a way that's easy to understand. I especially loved the casual level of puzzles and challenges, and the fun movement abilities that the game offers. And bonus points for no deaths! It's clear that the developers put a lot of attention to detail into this project. The audio is just right, and even though there's no voice acting, it's still atmospheric and enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so charming, and a joy to play. The controls were great and the platforming/puzzles were light and fun. The craziest thing is I really like Pikmin but this game puts nintendo completely to shame. All in all it took me about 10.5 hours to 100% the game, and my only real complaint is I didn't want it to end and a few achievements were finicky about popping. As of the time of this writing the fix is to load up the game and visit every area (don't forget transidor and also the final attic area). Once you do this it will force 4 achievements to pop. If they put out any DLC or sequels I'll buy them no questions asked on release day. Also, I played the entire game on steam deck without any issues or crashes and did no tweaking at all to the graphics or performance settings. Kudos to the devs for great work!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: 9.1/10Pros: +Fun and engaging platforming (major selling point for me)+Cool world building and atmosphere+Great sound track+Unique 2d and 3d art style+Decently easy achievementsCons:-No way to skip cut-scenes-Not much replayability (other than maybe speed running but also the cut-scenes are brutal)Conclusion:I got this game on sale for 10$ and I think it was well worth it. The enjoyable world building mixed with stellar platforming had me locked in. Definitely one of my favorite games of this year. me/me would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this a thumbs up, but it's VERY borderline as, although the game is quite charming, it feels very unadventurous in its design (they basically took the easiest parts to code from Pikmin and ignored anything challenging), and a wholesale rip-off in some of its other aspects (a more charitable person might call the way they name the artefacts a homage to Pikmin, to me it's simply a stolen idea).Also, it's unappealingly frictionless, with no enemies and nary a challenge in the main game, other than a few brief optional sections. They've bolted on some extra race stuff, but it's the sort of fluff they cram into similar games just to pad out them out. I blitzed through the entire thing in about 7 hours with only a few missing side-objectives. It's ironic that I played this game over the Christmas period, as like much of the food I consumed, it's empty calories.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is a relaxing, low-stress puzzle platformer where you zip around a normal house as a bug-sized little guy named Milo. You collect even smaller friends called Tinykin that you throw at things. Things explode a lot. Everything's extremely cute.While there are a few things about this game that are a bit frustrating - there's no radar to help you find those really hidden collectibles, and a few of the achievements are a bit glitchy on steam - overall this game is very smooth and fun. The level design is both clever and charming, and I recommend this game to players of all ages and skill levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: a lot i could say about this game from its frictionless exploration to its cute n cozy aesthetic to its tight controls to its boppy music to its expansive, vertically focused level design but MAINLY tinykin understands two important things that make it an outstanding game:1- its inherently fun to have a bunch of lil fellas following you around2- its inherently fun to be a lil fella yourself exploring a big house
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 game. Everything works great: the platforming feels good, the level design is interesting. The aesthetics are appealing and the narration is solid. There's no annoying objectives or levels in the game. The only thing I didn't notice much was the music, but it's still quite good. A short platformer with wide appeal and relaxed pacing. Easy recommend for anyone who like platforming and exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible 3D Collectahon Platformer. Very tight controls, beautiful graphics mixing 2D sprites and 3D worlds. Reminds me a lot of Banjo Kazooie with isolated worlds that you get to explore freely. Game has 6 worlds to explore which was the perfect length. The game did not over stay it's welcome (I 100% the game) and hope to see a sequel in the future. Great job SplashTeam!! My only recommendation for future DLC or a sequel is some type of optional hint/gadget to help find collectibles when you are down to a single pollen or TinyKin. Was a bit challenging finding stragglers.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This was such a blast of a game! It reminded me of Pikmin quite a bit, and I loved seeing another game take on their concept! The tinykin are all adorable, the bugs are all so full of personality (make sure to read their names, there's so many pop culture references, I love it!), collecting everything never felt too tedious thanks to their helpful counters, and each level was amazingly creative! I seriously cannot recommend this game enough! Buy it now and start exploring and collecting!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun collectathon game with light Pikmin elements. It's so much fun just sliding and gliding around the gigantic rooms being the size of an ant. Each of the tinykin have unique abilities that make you want to collect them so you can explore more of each room and get around the rooms easier. Same with collecting the pollen for more bubbles. It's also fun to talk with all the inhabitants of the house and see their stories and their names which are usually references to something or relate to their story in the game. I really love this game but it felt like it ended way too fast. Several characters mention different parts of the house like the capitol or the backyard and you never end up going there. A few more types of tinykin would have been nice too. Other than that, Tinykin is definitely worth a playthrough and I can't wait for them to add some dlc or even just make a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favorite platformers in a long time. Buttery smooth controls and a delightfully colorful cast are just some of the highlights of this gem of a game. It isn't terribly long, but all the time it took to beat was certainly well-spent. Each area is brimming with character, and it was a joy to fully explore the world in search of all the Tinykin, pollen, and achievements. Also the soundtrack is a BANGER.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is more of a 3d platformer collectathon similar to Mario despite it's obvious inspiration from Pikmin. And it nails the addicting and satisfying gameplay and fun, creative style that you'd expect from such a game. The levels are huge and unique, with fun little platforming sections and light puzzles scattered throughout the areas. The movement is also really tight and makes traversing each area feel great.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I loved this game- anyone with a craving for Pikmin should play this.  Great mechanics, fun characters, cool level design.  Very relaxing to play- the challenge is to explore every corner of the level to find collectibles, tinykin, & hidden areas.  No consequences for death- no way to really land yourself in a "dead man walking" situation.That said, the story/narrative is somewhat lacking.  No spoilers, but it is somehow both overly complicated and too simplistic.  It feels like at some point they were doing for an ambiguous "show don't tell" approach but then someone decided they'd rather just spell it all out.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Greetings traveler, come sit and hear of a game unlike anything you could imagine! A lost human marooned in a tiny world surrounded by countless of bugs and perhaps a way to get home? Listen in and we'll run it over with you!GRAPHICS :Something that truly is a match made in heaven! The blending of both cartoonish styles and the realism of the world is perfectly in sync here. There's a level of blending that makes everything work so well. Not once did I feel anything felt out of place or looked too awkward in any level. Characters, animations or even the videos are all BUTTER smooth and then some! From start to end it never faltered on its graphical quality. Also, LOVE and adore how the carpets look and move. ^O^MUSIC:A true rarity to find in any game the level of quality of music. And in Tinykin, everything feels so well tuned an genuinely beautiful to listen to. The immense variety, calmness and even peace of mind is something to witness. Even the little changes of the music where it speeds up or changes in different aspects of the level itself. I never felt once bored or anyway bothered by it. Heck, I even want to buy the Soundtrack to be honest!DIFFICULTY:Even for someone who isn't much of a platformer player, this game is very much safe for everyone. It WILL lightly test you here and there, but I found even the jumping and mechanics EXCEPTIONALLY forgiving. Even if you make fault of a bad jump, you'll be insta-brought-back to your last point. PLUS, there's even tiny ropes to be dropped about each level to help you come back to a lost jump or so. Again, NO issues with difficulty.BUGS:Besides the ones that fill the world, I didn't come across a SINGLE glitch/hiccup/etc in my game that could even have removed the fun. Despite a tiny, tiny, tiny issue with some platforms, I think it may have been myself being too speedy to take a platform or two into account.LEVEL DESIGN:Feel this earns its own amount of praise. No joke! The levels are TRULY so vast, open, gorgeous and so lavishing in its details. Each room/level feels like something in a real house and even more how MASSIVE every part of it feels. The auto-save the game does is needed as you might spend an hour or MORE in just one level itself. And furthermore I really have to hand it to the remarkably talented people behind this game for crafting such diversity, fun and even hidden nooks and crannies I never would have thought up of. You'll be in awe when you step into some of these rooms and just how wonderful it feels to be like a bug in the human world. <3CHARACTER DESIGN:This is another cheat, perhaps. However, much like the level mentions from before I really have to stop and marvel at the work here. The bugs are so vastly different and yet amazingly detailed, I really couldn't stop BUT notice them. Even in terms of their audio cues being so different whether its adults/kids/seniors or even if they're a different insect species sounding entirely different from another insect species. I love and adore the Dung Beetles and how sweet/cute/shy they all are. By the end of the game you'll be in love with way each species of bug looks, acts and sounds. Small touch or not, I thank so much to stuff like this with Milo, the Tinykin and SOOOOOOOOOOOO much more. *tips hat*GAMEPLAY:Don't think anybody wouldn't mention the hints of Pikmin here and I entirely agree. A good solid chunk of the game relies on the main objectives to complete and get the item you seek. BUT, there's a twist! There are mini objective to completes, both for additional fun and others that need to be done to accomplish part of your main task. They get bigger and more elaborate as the game goes on and I love the way exploring, collecting Tinykin, talking to bugs always kept the game so varied and vast. Its simple in its execution and effective in everywhere else. *nods*CONTROLS:SO BUTTERY SMOOTH AND CLEAN ITS TRUE PERFECTION. And this is coming from the most awkward person ever to play games with a keyboard and mouse. ^O^PRICE:WORTH EVERY PENNY, nuff said!!!!STORY:So there is a main story and then there's...............a little something else. What could it all be? Who knows?!?! But I'm more than assured if you keep a close eye on things, explore a bit and talk to some crazy bugs......you might find out what that little something is. *winks*EXTRAS:Each level has its own little extra objectives to achieve and even just some fun ones that you can discover solely by exploring more here and there. You'll get a good amount of extra playtime out of it and even more amusement from the banter of the bugs or amazing jaw drop to how well a piece of pollen was so well hidden. ^o^FINAL THOUGHTS:I went into Tinykin NOT as a fan of Pikmin, but a fan of what looked to be a truly astounding looking game designed with charm and beauty behind it. From its wonderful music, insanely charming character design, to even the levels being worthy of their mention, what an enjoyable wonderful ride. I proudly put this game high upon my favorite list as a beautiful little project that managed to surprise even me (and get me with a few laughs on the way). Didn't mention there was some EXTRA touches they added in with some of the dialogue. If you spot it, you'll be chuckling just as much as myself. But do yourself the greatest of favors. Strap on your Bubble Device, hug your nearest (hopefully non-exploding) Tinykin and get ready for one of the most charming adventures you'll find in this bug-sized world. Hope you get home safe and sound! *cheers and tips hat*TLDR:10000000/10 - Even if you are slightly curious about Tinykin and the world and even the visuals interest you, GET....THIS...GAME. Its a labor of love and so very noteworthy of notice and so much more. ^-^GHASPER:BOO! <3

_childDocuments_.review: Pikman this is not. No, this is more of an adventure platformer, similar to the likes of Banjo-Kazooie or Yooka-Laylee.  However, unlike these games, Tinykins doesn’t have enemies… at least so far and five hours into my game.  The challenge comes in the form of discovery, collection, and quest completion mainly.  Your tools are the tinykins that help you traverse and perform special functions as you find and collect them. Generally every new level introduces you to at least one new game mechanic and a tinykin that will be used as your tool for that mechanic.  You also have the ability to float within a bubble that you can create and can be upgraded based on how much pollen you can find.  …and you will find a lot of it.  If you want to find all of it, you really have to put your best explorer hat on and find the nooks and crannies you may have missed.The game is extremely charming and works perfectly on a SteamDeck.  Controls are great and very snappy.The level designs are fun and well laid out. It’s worth a play.  As of now, I see myself playing the entire game and as a completionist. Overall, a good and surprising game.. Maybe a little more on the casual side, but completing everything might be harder for some.

_childDocuments_.review: My impressions video: When I first played the dmeo for this during a prior Next Fest, I already knew it was something special. Having now finished it, this is among my top games of the year so far.Tinykin is essentially the core concepts of Pikmin, but with no combat and in a "Honey, I Shrunk the Kids" type of world. It's not particularly hard, nor really a grind, unless you want to 100% it and even that's not super hard to do. The different rooms of the house you'll explore are well crafted, amazing to look at and intelligently designed, with lots of collectibles and side missions that are cleverly hidden, but also not a chore to find. You can return to prior levels and you'll want to as you unlock more powers for your suite and more and different types of Tinykin.There is a story in Tinykin, though it's fairly light. While obviously inspired by Pikmin, it's also not nearly as complicated as that. Truthfully, this is a fairly casual experience that's obviously meant to be enjoyed by players of all skills. However, that's not to say it's boring. It's a more chill experience where the fun of exploration and collecting is more the goal than combat or difficult puzzles. I like more challenging games too, but this is a title where you don't have to work super hard, but will still feel satisfied at the end.It looks and sounds great and also runs like a dream. There are very few load screens and they're quick. Friends who have much lower spec machines than mine have said it runs well for them too, so it seems to scale well.If you like relaxing platformers and especially if you like Pikmin, don't skip Tinykin. This game hasn't gotten nearly the amount of attention it deserves and I absolutely adore it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes modern day movement and blends it well with classic old school platforming.It's cute, it's got family friendliness, it's simple, it's fun, it's a total win.(I haven't beaten the game as of the making of this review so that is doing you guys a bit of a disservice, meaning I can't give my entire start to finish opinion. But, here's what more I can say about it.I picked this game up to play specifically on the steam deck, and boy does it do GREAT!60fps, the colors pop nicely, the controls are very easy and intuitive to a console's game controller setup, and the idea of playing this game on the go just works. Commuting? Boot up Tinykin.Lunch break? Tinykin.Again, it just works.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the most purely joyful game of this year.You're going to enjoy Tinykin if you enjoy exploring simply for the sake of exploring. Also, if you just love when a game has snappy movement that just makes it feel super satisfying only to navigate around. Because, yeah, the levels are wonderfully designed and rendered. They feel real, and lived in. There's just enough balance between a typical, normal home, and fantastical elements to make it feel grounded, but not boring. And you can zip around these huge levels very quickly, without losing the feeling that you're incredibly small. The verticality of the levels is also super impressive. If you loved games like Toy Story 2 or A Bug's Life growing up, this nicely brought a lot of those vibes back for me.I also love all the character designs and art, they're very cute and well drawn. And the music is well made and fits the game nicely, even if it's not the kinda style of game soundtrack that I'm gonna be listening to outside of the game.That said, there's a negative review of the game here that I find myself agreeing with on a lot of points. There's no real challenge, no real puzzles. There's a hint of unique mechanics that change up HOW you can explore in the stackable green Tinykin (that are essentially a mobile ladder), and I genuinely wish there had been more elements in the game like that. There's also no easy way to track down whatever collectibles you still might be missing after completing the game. All of these aren't necessarily bad things - I still enjoyed my time with the game. But it does feel like it keeps the game from greatness.The more negative factor is the writing. It feels like 70% of NPCs you come across are just less-than-subtle references to pop culture, 20% give you quests, and 10% contribute to actual interesting themes of misplaced faith, which, while interesting, felt rather heady for a cutesy, chill platformer about exploring a house as a tiny creature. There's also some sci-fi worldbuilding going on, but that's mostly relegated to the opening and ending cutscenes, and it just feels messy. Ideas that are interesting, but fall flat. It's a shame. I feel like if the game hadn't tried at all, and had just gone for a much less ambitious plot and had you explore the place as one of the bugs inhabiting the house, it might have felt more successful.So yeah. TL;DR: It's a good game, but far from a perfect game. Get it if you enjoy chill platformers focusing on vertical exploration, don't expect a memorable story or a challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and cute game, not very challenging, but sweet and charming.Don't be fooled, this game really isn't very similar to Pikmin at all. There's not fighting, no survival, no time limits. It's more akin to something like Banjo Kazooie or other 3D platformers where you are mostly tasked with collecting all the things. And a pretty easy one at that. It's worth pointing out I'm a fully grown person, gaming for decades so maybe I'm not the intended audience, and kids will find it a great and appropriate challenge. The platforming isn't difficult, the puzzles are pretty light. Your tinykin will pick up an object and automatically take it where it needs to go, even if you don't know where that is. There was one stage I managed to collect all the items and finish all the tasks without even talking to the people I was supposed to talk to. I just grabbed every item with an interactive glow and occasionally moved or blew up an obstacle on the path.If there is a challenge to Tinykin, it is in spotting all of the places you can go. Sometimes you will see a bunch of collectibles glowing in the distance and you won't know how to get there. Even then it's not usually all that hard. You just have to be persistent and keep looking, and eventually you will find the path. There definitely are some hidden spots and optional challenges for the seasoned gamer to find and beat, but these are the exception, not the rule, and I have pretty much been breezing through the main quest and most of the side activities (but not all) without difficulty.But the game is still fun. It's quirky and charming, and it's simply fun to wander around the stages, talking to NPCs and piecing together the story. It's  well written and nice enough, with a couple fun references hidden away in there. Art, music, and sound effects are all a delight. My partner and I enjoy the sounds the little bugs make when they shoot a web over the level, or when the pink tinykin grunt in time with the music as they carry something to its destination. It's the little details like that that make the game enjoyable. If you like the art style and charm of the game and aren't looking for a challenge to your reflexes or real head scratching puzzles, then pick this one up.

_childDocuments_.review: Without a doubt, the best platformer collect-a-thon to date. Forget "oh it's like Pikimin." This is Pikimin, Chibi-Robo, Banjo Kazooie, and Psychonauts for goodness sake! While Pikimin is more fixated on very slow gameplay and a lot of tactical thinking, Tinykin has a great sense of speed, verticality, and control. Every level is has one main quest that varies between locations, but between that is collecting pollen for hover upgrades and getting higher and higher up. While Pikmin destroys most of your guys with each task, Tinykin grows you little army of kin until you have a nice parade following you through each specific level. The most fun parts are unlocking every section of the room to discover greater heights. I half expected us to crawl into the attic which... maybe you do >,>The game has a skateboard (or soapboard) which makes moving around a fun test of how much speed you can build up going down slope. I was astounded to see it even has a grind. It's not Tony Hawk levels of control, but it's enough to help you get around which is the point. There's also a hover mechanic which I'd say is required in all platform games so you can adjust you landing every time. Both the soapboard and hover bubble work together to make platforming a breeze.While it seems like that's exactly what they were going for, I'd say it's a disservice to simply call this 'like Pikmin," because it's so much more. I almost wish they put more development into making it like a collect-a-thon. You'll only be collecting three things, main quest items, side quest items (which range from 1 to 2 per level), and a [butt] load of pollen for upgrades. There are also secret challenges you can do once you have upgraded hover bubbles, which encourage you to go back to other levels. While all of that is very fun and makes for a solid gameplay loop it's a shame how it makes me wish they could allow more things to collect or obstacles to overcome.Really my only complaint is it's a lot of great stuff in about a 10 hour experience. You might even finish it faster if you're a speedrunnygunny type. I'd say support these guys. Encourage them to make more. Throw this game everywhere, because they have a great eye for this. And whether they want to or not, I dunno but... I'm really hoping if they get enough support they'll just do a collect-a-thon one of these days. GOD MAN, that'd be sick...

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an amazing blend of Pikmin and Chibi Robo with a bit of Bug Fables aesthetic thrown in there.But that's just a surface-level comparison. To delve a bit under the surface of this game, I gotta talk about the flow of gameplay and the design that comes with it and how well it works.First: the gameplay has you wandering around a large open level (not to be confused with open world) where you explore for pollen and tinykin to help you along the way. Your starting equipment: the soapboard and the bubble glider allow Milo to maneuver some basic platforming pretty well, but his maneuvering is enhanced when you find some Tinykin that can help you unblock pathways, climb up higher, and cross large gaps. Starting in a new zone will require you to find a group of Tinykin first before you can get to work on opening up paths, shortcuts, and objectives.Second: the world design and character writing is wonderfully charming, funny, and mysterious. It has a bit of everything for everyone (adults included, for those who know a lot of media references) I love the original world-building that the game has to offer, and the lore will not disappoint you either. Of course, everything else is left up to the imagination but play through to the end to find out for yourself! You may find a few secrets and other interesting tidbits along the way as you view each room and talk to characters. Speaking of rooms, I love how the levels are laid out in terms of progression and accessibility. You find a lot of Tinykin near the floor level and you can gain more along the ways you open up so you don't end up hitting a dead end anywhere. The only gripes I have are that the second counter for total Pollen in the room is never filled up all the way, but you still get enough to earn your next Bubble Glider from the pollen brewer. Just don't worry too much about finding any more than that.Finally: the mission objectives are clear enough so that you can go immediately for them and coherently find your way to the items you need, however I find that exploring at my own pace and just collecting everything as I go works perfectly well too. The open level dynamic allows for this kind of structure so that you can tackle anything within your reach at any time and order as long as you can climb up to it (so make sure to open up some shortcuts as you explore so you can return to these places if need be).
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A very charming, enjoyable 3D platformer that's more than worth checking out for any fans of the genre. The art design for the game is gorgeous, and the puzzle design is wonderful, being relatively straight-forward if you just want to beat the game, but definitely having some tricky or more hidden collectables that really test how much you're paying attention if you're going for 100%. Just an all around pleasant experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This is hands down the best platformer I have ever played, before it came out I replayed the demo 6 times just so I could feel how smooth it is to control again. It feels SO smooth and fun to control, and the collectibles and secrets are fun to nab, with the exception of the pollen, which can be annoying when you're missing like 3 of em lol. Still it's just like, I love this game I adore it to pieces, it's so easily my game of the year, absolutely. I only wish there were multiple save files so I could replay this game over and over and over without deleting my save.PLAY TINYKIN IT'S THE BEST GAME **EVER**
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A great game overall that brings back those feelings you had when exploring through N64 platformer games but with a modern aesthetic and touch. It looks like it may play like Pikman but it doesnt. Its on its own and the tinykins are used mostly differenty with them being used for traversal and opening up secret pathways. the gameplay is satifying and the sound design is great. Well worth the price! and the ending left the door WIDE OPEN for a sequel that I am very much looking forward too. If a sequel comes out, i'll just say "shut up and take my money!"Edit 12/21/2022: They added several QoL improvements and some new content in the form of Time Trials that can earn you cosmetic rewards and some small extra dialog. The time trials were challenging but fun and satisfying as it makes full use of the soapboard(Its like a skateboard/hoverboard type thing but it helps you move faster and grinding on edges makes you move faster and gain momentum a bit). The soapboard handles well and traversal is very satisfying when you get the flow of it. This game seems to leave everyone wanting more, and thats a good thing!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Exceeded my expectations. Levels are absolutely beautiful and I never got bored exploring every inch. Constant action, fluid controls, and plenty of nostalgia for kids of the 90s. Puzzles are simple but satisfying. If you're looking for a game that lets you turn your brain off (mostly) and just have fun, Tinykin is it.Some reviewers complain that the game is too short at only 6-8 hours, but I think if you're speeding through it that quickly, you're doing yourself a disservice. Take your time, complete the side quests, and immerse yourself in the world. Having said that, I hope there's a sequel or DLC in the future because I was sad to see it end.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: If you ever wanted Pikmin on the PC, this is basically it. Tinykin does a great job of emulating the theory of gathering dozens of little minions to help you solve puzzles and progress through the story. Unlike Pikmin, however, there are no monsters, combat, or time limit; instead the game takes the form of a more traditional 3D platformer. There is a lot to see and collect, the environments and soundtrack are pretty good, and the game is a solid platformer/collectathon all around. If you like Pikmin or are a fan of 3D platformers in general, this one is worth getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, not complicated, I got a really good time playing it. But even with doing some lvl again to fulfill max achievement, the completion took me only 10 hours (everything recolted).There is the real problem of the game, 20 euros is too much for a 10 hours gameplay game. The game is great, but at 20 it's too much in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but great fun. Reminds me of the good times I had with Supraland. Fun environments, funny dialogues, and fun gameplay. I have only two complaints. First, I wish it was longer. 10 hours to 100% is pretty short. Second, they need to implement a way to more easily search for missing Tinykin after you complete the story. The headache it was to 100% this was unnecessarily frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review just after completing the game, so the hours listed are roughly the playtime if you aren't trying to be insanely thorough.Tinykin is a great game, but it might not be exactly what you expect judging from the trailer. While the aesthetic resembles the Pikmin franchise, or maybe Overlord, the game DOES NOT play like either of those games. You are not directing around your Tinykin to do battle, and in fact there is no combat in the game whatsoever. Instead, the Tinykin serve a dual purpose - they help you traverse the environment in different ways, and also serve as the main collectible in each level that allows you to progress.It's a pretty ingenious idea, and the game does just enough with it so as not to overstay its welcome. Each level is clearly lovingly designed, and a joy to explore in miniature form. There is an underlying story but nothing spectacular, just there to give some context to your actions.What could improve? As mentioned, there is no combat in the game, and also only a few levels in total. The first isn't necessary, but it wouldn't have hurt to have seen a final boss or two to really drive the story home (those that finish the game will understand what I mean). The second will likely come with time if Splashteam decides to create DLC or another game entirely.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is such a fantastical game and one I would love to see get a sequel to.     - The game is very much a fusion of the pikmin exploring and puzzle solving       with the help of the tinykins.     - With each Tinykin having there own unique ability from carrying items, helping         clear passage ways of debris, to helping you explore the map.     - On top of that you also get a fun gliding mechanic and a soap board that helps        you traverse around the level faster and also allows you to access new areas     - The whole time the movement felt solid and well thought out and the ability to         combo movement abilities together felt amazing and fun.     - The story is sort of easily missable while nearly every NPC in the game has some        sort of dialogue a lot of it doesn't push the story as a whole but instead builds        out the world and the area's your exploring. There is a over arching story however        and has a nice pay off to it if you keep up with it.     - Ill add that this game is also very funny with a lot of great dialogue and references       spread throughout that get a nice chuckle through out.     - now the main reason i wanted to write this review is the detail to the world.        each level is thremed of a room of a house from a kitchen that has become a massive farmland to bathrooms where the cities skylines are made from toilet paper skyscrapers this game just has such amazing attention to detail and love poured in nearly every part of the game. even small things like the sound of your foot steps on what flooring you are on is just so perfectly designed and just immerses you into this beautiful world the devs crafted.    - Now i slightly touched upon it before but the sound design in this game is phenomenal all the sounds just bring you deeper into the world.    - The music for the levels, oh my another favourite for me, it has this amazing focus on accommodating throughout the level. an example of this is  This motif and just everywhere in the game and truly make the world just feel so much more alive.     - While i love this game there is a few ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ I've had that made me just the littlest bit upset. I am a completionist I love 100% games i enjoy or at least trying to get as much as i can and this game is perfect for that kind of gamer however I don't know if it is the steam version or maybe just a small bug but I have found some achievements just aren't completed even tho i know I've done what they need. some like the collect all brews has been completed but yet is not appearing on my achievements in game or on steam with the number of complete brews changing every time I open the game.     - Not really a negative but more a nice quality of life id love to see is at the end of the game an ability to help guide in the right direction where any last collectables are missing. they show the major collectables but im talking the pollen and any hiding tinykins. Oh and a tracker for how many of each tinykins would be awesome for one of the achievements also.      - This game is a fantastic time it is on the shorter side but very much worth it I bought it on a whim and it immediately became one of my favourite games of this year.      - While I would love to see a sequel its mostly for the game play it was just so addictive to me that I want more but understand likely wont be happening any time soon.      - To the devs thank you for all your hard work into this just honestly amazing game its so fun and blast to get through      - To potential buyers if you ever enjoyed the platformer puzzle genre and needed more of it in your life this game is definitely for you. If you are on the fence then try the demo.TLDRLike puzzle platformers with great world design and amazing art buy game if not sure play demo.

_childDocuments_.review: Harkorn Back to the Good days of hearing the PS2 START UP.Hit me with childhood Wimsey.It's not left me at all.Exploration of a colourful home feels like a dream of colour and Crisp 2D on 3D art style that makes it Different on all other's in the 3d Platform Space.It's not Pikmen 3 in terms of management and Careful planning with it's creatures, but that's good because it flows as smooth a soap down a strand on nylon with it's platforming even when making harsh falls.Explore,Feel Joy,Collect.If you like 3D platformers then it's a Must.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Cool little game which squeezes an enormous sense of scale (almost vertigo inducing) out of very ordinary spaces. Nice, soft fetch-quest style puzzle solving and quick respawn if you fall too far. The only thing I would say against it is that it can take you a while to track down every last collectible and side-quest object, as the special view mostly only indicate where to go to complete a side-quest, it does little to help you find the objects you need. Other than that though, this is great fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: To get it out of the way, the game is short, like really short (as of writing this I 100% the game on the current version).  Despite that, the game is still a blast to play; mixing both a Pikmin style and classic collectathon 3D platformer game play with  a Paper Mario-like art style.  If I had to bring up any complaints, the game is very short (6-10 hours), can be rather easy/repetitive at times, and doesn't give any real way to easily locate the pollen that's scattered throughout the levels which can lead to mindless searching (could have reduced the game play time by at least 20 minutes if it had a way to more easily find the more hidden collectibles).
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: As a preface I played this on the Steam deck and steam seems to have a hard time counting time played.Game took about 7 hours and 20 min to finish but said I had played it for 74 hours. (My guess is that steam still counts time even when the steamdeck is off if you didn't quit game to desktop). And when I tried to give a review it didn't let me until I installed it on pc and it reset time played.Tinykin runs great on steam deck, Even better than a regular controller because the back buttons feel really natural for actions in this game.The game itself is really fun. It's chill and cozy. Music is fantastic, art style is charming. The controls are very responsive. The bugs are endearing. Totally recommend for anyone looking for a 3D platformer.Cons:-Game really needs a pollen tracker and tiny kin tracker (Maybe unlock for the goggles after you finished the main objective in the level?) I would love to 100% the game but I do not want to spend 20 minutes searching every nook and cranny to find that 3 missing pollen.-Milo is as bland as a white sheet of paper, he could use some personality.Top shelf game!
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A delightful short-but-sweet puzzle platformer where you're given a bunch of tasks and objectives in big expansive feeling levels and allowed to just take your time combing through it all. Absolutely lovely stuff, cannot recommend enough. Awesome music, wonderful sound design, adorable character design. Don't pass this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game that was enjoyable through almost all of my ten hours. Reminds me of Pikmin (obviously) with a mix of more classic 00's platformers. The puzzles and platforming is relatively simple and forgiving, but it provides just enough of a unique spin and game loop to make it all feel special. I also played most of this on my Steam Deck, which ran flawlessly.My only minor complaint is for achievement hunting. One of the collectibles (the pollen) can be hard to finish on each level simply because there are so many. On several levels I was missing just 6 out of 1200 pollen, and I spent a fair amount time trying to find that last bit. I ended up looking up some YouTube videos to finish out two of the levels after I got tired of it. If there was a small additional feature that pointed you in the general direction of the remaining pollen (like after you hit the first benchmark to make the brew for Sikaru) that could cut down on the frustration.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Really cute and cozy 3D collectathon with minor pikmin elements - it's definitely the former first with the latter more being tools and -occasionally- carrying stuff around, but it does the 3D platforming side so well that the relatively downplayed mechanics aren't a problem and honestly overemphasizing them too much may have dragged the game down anyways.The game looks gorgeous, the individual levels are all -huge- and full of stuff to collect, each took at least an hour or more to fully clear - plus the designs are all so creative, repurposing rooms of the house for different environments and giving each a unique feel along the way. Add in the escalation of tinykin types that enhance your ability to explore or solve puzzles and the game never gets stale or tedious - it's not super long in the end with only five and a half levels, but what's there is really good.And Milo feels great to control, plus the soapboard and glide bubble mechanics open up a lot of platforming possibilities - and especially the green tinykin as well, they also significantly change the game when you start getting them. Not every mechanic is perfect - the "tracker" goggles are virtually useless and the yellow tinykin can get a bit annoying to go back and forth between building different bridges but it's like, tiny nuisances at most.I dunno, I don't think this game is gonna blow your mind, but for what it is, it's really charming and really damn fun, just an all-around pleasant experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game that took me just a little over 10 hours to 100%. Well worth the price for a fun and silly adventure with tiny little bugs for companions.If you grew up with Pikmin 1 and 2 this WILL scratch your itch for a pikmin game. While there is no combat there are plenty of dialogue, puzzles, and collecting to give you plenty of things to do in this wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A real charming collect-a-thon with an excellent take on the whole, “a bug’s perspective of a human’s home”.Each level delivers a great sense of scale that’s satisfactorily populated with things to do and places to visit. Completionism comes naturally with how tempting it is to investigate any intriguing landmarks or uncover the next secret nook. The layout of each room does a fantastic job of letting the levels be very open-ended without being too complicated or disorienting. Time flies when you’re sucked into the cycle of seeing an interesting new side area, making your way over to it in style, and then rummaging through that area for trinkets until yet another path catches your eye. The music is quite catchy as well, and I’m always a sucker for clever use of "audio middleware” where elements of a musical theme seamlessly change to better match your local context.Tinykin is just generally a blast to play. It’s got good, wholesome platformer energy that’s never more demanding than it needs to be. It’s got a clever blend of intrinsic “Ooh, what’s over here?” and extrinsic “Give me all the gold orbs” motivations. I might not recommend trying to 100% complete the game, but I do 100% recommend Tinykin for a few relaxing sessions of methodical clean-up and spatial reasoning gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I played a portion of the demo at Pax East and really enjoyed the concept and game play. I finished the demo at home and was really excited to play the game when it came out. I am almost done with the game and I really enjoy looking around and trying to gather everything and speaking with the bugs along the way. I do really wish there were more side quests and games while looking for keys because I feel like getting through the levels go by fairly quickly. I really hope that there is a second game because I have enjoyed this one so much <3
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty fun Pikmin-like puzzle game. You're a space explorer that teleported into a 90s house. The twist is you are the size of a bug and the other bugs have developed a society across many rooms, complete with a religion worshipping a previous tenant of the house that has gone missing some time ago. So uncover what is going on and get back to your ship by solving a number of rather simple exploration puzzles aided by cute and eager to help Tinykin critters.The game will take you about 7 hours to beat, and a few more to 100%. It's pretty fun and leisurely, but lacks that sense of accomplishment you'd get from Pikmin where unlocking shortcuts and planning what you were going to do next was an actual challenge.Plus surprisingly enough the game makes you be a scab during one of its levels (the one where ants are protesting because they don't want to bake a cake for a religious ceremony so it falls on you to do it). Kind of jarring for there not to be an option not to be a strikebreaker. At least everyone is happy in the end, but still...
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: A total triumph of a game.  Combines some of the best collect-a-thon elements of Banjo Kazooie/DK64, combines them with the Pikmin'esque followers, takes out all the annoying/irritating fun-blocking elements from those games - and leaves a true polished gem.  Really tight controls so you always feel in control, charming graphics, and great NPC dialogue filled with winkwink references to lots of pop culture games/tv/film. The only negative is that it will leave you wanting more because its so good and easy to play through in a few sittings.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is actually a really good 3D platformer that kinda came out of nowhere for me. While I haven't finished the game yet what I've played so far has made it a favorite of the year.It really captures that simplistic exploration/reward gameplay loop in a semi-big level that I think a lot of modern 3D platformers miss. They didn't even need any form of combat, that I've seen yet anyway, to accomplish this.Anyone that's comparing this game to Pikmin in any way is doing the game and potential buyers a disservice. While the game does feature some surface-levels similarities, they are simply superficial and shouldn't be taken as "this game is just indie Pikmin" like one could say for Bug Fables is for the Paper Mario franchise.Buy this game if you're looking for a light-hearted 3D Platformer based around exploration. I'd say don't buy it if you're looking for that high-intensity army and time management of the Pikmin series. Because you're simply not going to get it with this game.Bonus Points for the game working right out of the box for Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most charming games I've played in ages. Fun and cute art style combined with relaxing gameplay. It's not anything too hard or challenging, but it is genuinely fun to explore the world looking for every last collectible to get that 100%. Tinykin satisfies an itch for someone like me who likes to explore every nook and cranny of a level, and brings me back to the days when 3d platformers were more common.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game. Rarely do I ever just play a game from start to finish within a day or two but this game is something special. While it's true it has some similarities with PIKMIN, they are only slight. Certain tinykins have specific abilities and you use them in a very specific manner to solve some environmental puzzles or other tasks. What the game does different however is take away the more tedious micromanagement of the PIKMIN titles. The little guys just do what they do and a task requires x amount of them and often you have to use several in tandem to complete tasks but there's no stressful combat or timer involved.Tinykins is also a fairly competent 3D platformer. The controls are tight and responsive. The levels are incredibly designed, honestly they impressed me with their density and size despite the fact that I am a bit of an old school platforming fan dating back to the 1980s when Mario first debuted. The game is a near perfect sandbox collectathon with only some minor issues.Problems tend to come from the sheer size of the levels and trying to remember or find where objectives are. At one point, the little guys had carried an object for me but I didn't see where they went. The game showed me where they ended up but I hadn't been there yet.  Eventually I found where the item was but a QOL fix to make that item show up with the visor would have helped. That's basically all the game needs, some QOL fixes. Amazing game, I truly loved this experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: From start to finish, this game has charm and the thrill of finding everything in every little nook and cranny. Some day one achievement bugs, but if you think you have everything, try just entering every room again and it should pop up with the achievements. Also if you think you have all the tinykin, go to the ending sequence in the attic and it should pop the achievement once end cutscene plays. Wonderful game, would love a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this game.  I finished it in probably 9 or so hours, since it doesn't seem like the time I spent on the demo (the entire tutorial and first level) is added to the Steam Game Time calculation.  Luckily, all of my progress transferred over without any problems when I bought the full game.  I loved the puzzle solving, and I felt like the game was long enough that I felt like I was able to feel like I really understood my options for interacting with the world, without becoming frustratingly padded out.  If you're not into collect-a-thon platformers, you probably won't enjoy this, but this game was engaging and compelling to an extent that genuinely surprised me.  The story was decent, and I'm normally a very story-driven player, but I just couldn't wait to explore each area and see all the different ways I could use the Tinykin to get to new places.  I found the controls fluid and responsive using a controller, and almost all of my deaths felt like my error and not the game's fault.  I really hope this becomes a series.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: Been waiting for this game quite some time now and even played the demo every single time it was available because it was super fun! Now we have the full game and it's even better with some of the best visuals out there and great gameplay. If you like collecting stuff this game is for you that's for sure and it's super cheap as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Tinykin

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the best of Super Mario Odyssey, Pikmin and Overlord combined. I haven't been able to stop playing it since I launched the demo and quickly bought the game, which carried my progress over from the demo.This game just wants you to have FUN. There are so many tiny aspects to this game that are so rare but much appreciated: unlimited sprint immediately, platform mechanics that aren't picky, constant unlocked shortcuts to make exploring levels easier as you move on, etc. They all add up to just letting you focus on the fun aspects of the game: puzzle solving and exploration.

Go and try it out, I swear to you you're going to have such a blast. 10/10I'm editing this because I want to give a huge shout out for you guys to pick this game for the best 2022 game nominee.

_childDocuments_.review: Tinykin is what I like to call a "Well rounded game", yeah you might find a few little details that could have been more polished but overall the game is just PERFECT.Before I get into those few little detail I would like to list every aspect that makes the game really good:-I got to play a demo of it a few months back and at first it gaved me the "Pickmin vibes" with it's own flavour.Now after completing it I can confirm my thoughts on that matter, yeah you get those vibes but Tinykin it's completly it's own thing and offers it's own dynamics especially when you take in count the level design of the game.-The duration of the game is on point, exactly what the gameplay mechanics could give is what you get since there's no "extra" tastless content in this game. But in case you want to play around with it's mechanics just for fun you can always comeback to it and go for a 100% in each level or just explore new ways to aproach the levels. Having that nice duration for the main story and offering that replay value feels awesome (I completed it in gamepass first and then got a key that I might use to exploit that replay value through steam)-The controls are smooth AF and once you master the soapboard you can find yourself running around the levels at an awesome pace despite of how huge they are.-The story is interesting and know where to put it's efforts to catch the attention of the player to keep it engaged.-Visually the game looks amazing, the art directtion it's outstanding. I really dig the combination of the few art artstyles used (2D-ish character design, with cartton elements in a 3D world that's filled with little details).-Well optimized, run correctly as I expected taking in count my PC config, but the important thing here is how SMOOTH it felt during my gameplay experience.-Many more positive little details.Just a few negative details:-The electricity gameplay mechanics sometimes it's a little bit "meh", the concept is good, interesting and works great when it come to "how it is implemented in the world", BUT sometimes it can feel bad when you find yourself having to completly stop the rhythm of the game and start making a row to carry electricity just to end up seeing that you've arrenged you "bois" incorrectly and they can't reach the cable they are supposed to connect to.-A few times the gamera got crazy when getting into tiny spaces instead of taking a good angle (not a big deal tbh, but I wanted to include this)Conclusion: DUDE, buy it. Awesome game.Here you have some footage of my walkthrough:

name: Lost Ark
detailed_description: Embark on an odyssey for the Lost Ark in a vast, vibrant world: explore new lands, seek out lost treasures, and test yourself in thrilling action combat. Define your fighting style with your class and advanced class, and customize your skills, weapons, and gear to bring your might to bear as you fight against hordes of enemies, colossal bosses, and dark forces seeking the power of the Ark in this action-packed free-to-play RPG. Discover a World Brimming with Adventure Explore seven vast, varied continents and the seas between them to find vibrant cultures, strange and fantastical beasts, and all the unexpected marvels waiting to be discovered. Delve into the secrets of Arkesia, prove your might in battles and raids, compete against other players in PvP, travel to distant islands in search of hidden riches, face packs of enemies and colossal bosses in the open world, and more. Your Odyssey Awaits Splash into massively satisfying ARPG-style combat and progression as you quest, raid, and fight on the scope of an MMO. Whether you want to play solo, in groups with friends, or matched up with other adventurers in the world, there’s an epic adventure waiting for you. Fight in the open world or delve into chaos dungeons, go head-to-head in expert PvP duels, test your mettle on epic quests, raid against bosses big and small, and hold your own in the fight against the Demon Legion to reclaim the power and light of the Lost Ark. Define Your Fight Lost Ark offers easy-to-learn features with unexpected depth and room for customization. Hit the ground running with pick-up-and-play action then take control of your combat with the unique Tripod system. Unlock three tiers of customization for each of your abilities, giving you powerful control of exactly how you fight. Lost Ark’s ever-expanding roster of iconic classes—each with their own distinct advanced classes—offers plenty of room to explore until you find the combat style that’s just right for you. The same goes for other features: as you continue your journey, you’ll find non-combat skills, crafting, guilds and social systems, and other rich features that bring the world alive. Whether you want to skim along the surface or dive deep into the details is up to you. ACCESSIBILITY FEATURES: Personalize your adventure with accessibility settings before game play. Define your fighting style with your class and advanced class, and customize your skills, weapons, and gear to bring your might to bear as you fight against hordes of enemies, colossal bosses, and dark forces seeking the power of the Ark in this action-packed free-to-play RPG. _childDocuments_.review: EDIT:TL;DR: fun classes fun raids but be aware that it is extremely time consuming, not only to play the game, but to sit around and get into party to start playing. I recommend it if you have a lot of time to play and looking for a game to grind. There is a lot to work towards and because it is an alt heavy game. I also recommend you get a static to raid with so you don't have to wait in party finder but good luck getting 8 people to get on at the same time to raid and none of them be bad vibes or total goobers. I DON'T RECOMMEND THIS GAME  AT ALL FOR CASUALS.7 months later and double my hours there's enough worthwhile content in this game that I can recommend it. BUT, it requires more time than ever before. Whether you're whaling or not, you will need time. Time to prog raids, which is understandable, but time to apply for a raid and wait for a support, and then time to do the raid and potentially fail over and over again with the wrong people, then back again into the party finder.  In the following weeks of Vykas release, my friends and I waited for 1 hour and 30 minutes to get 4 more people, we couldn't even get DPS's to join for a full dps party. I no longer have the patience or enough will to play this game to wait a fraction of that time. When I open the party finder for brelshaza and every single real party is "LF sup" I just log off b/c I know that if I get in I'll have to wait for god knows how long for 1-2 supports to join the party that I'm in that's also competing with 7 other parties. Full DPS parties take just as long to recruit a competent DPS and have a higher chance of ending in disaster. NOBODY wants to raid with no supps, they only do it out desperation. Content is beatable without a support but the game is designed around supports. Many of the meta builds in the game crutch the yearning set that supports provide. If you're a casual player wanting to play this game for 1-2 hours everyday or every other day, I can't see how you can raid anytime soon without being very lucky or spending money. Not only do you have to reach the required ilvl to attend a raid, if you are a dps, you have to compete with the other dps for a spot in that party. If you started now and planned on spending no money and you had average luck you wouldn't be able to compete with one of my over ilvl dps ALTS that is 5x3 lvl 7 gems Lost wind Cliff 12 card set for a spot in the party. What about somebody's alt w/ even better gems? LoS 18, LoS 30? On top of that your roster level is low which is a big red flag to most people. Basically, nobody wants to play with you. I don't want to play with you. Nobody wants to waste even more time getting jailed by an inexperienced player or teaching something to someone with no guarantee that the will understand and the raid will be finished, all for 5K gold and some more crap. We all have 15 more legion raids, 12 chaos dungeons, and 12 guardian raids we want to do to make the most gold we can in a week. But hey, you can always pick up mokokos or some ♥♥♥♥.I could sit here for hours explaining everything thats good and bad about this game. However, its a free to play game with fun legion raid and fun classes that's worth a try. (If you're willing to spend 20+ hours to go through the main story and who knows how long to get to the actually end game and see your first real player.)ORIGINAL REVIEW:current stage of the game is pretty bad. 1 fun content per week, queues on NAW (good luck trying to organize raids or play the game if u have priorities), rampant rmt and bots, nearly zero drip available, level 1-50 grind was so bad I reached a point where I could only do 2 levels a day, t1-t2 content is dead and unnecessarily difficult compared to t3. Also, AGS has no idea when they will ship out a big content update and neither does smilegate, so you won't ever know if you should prepare for a big update until the last minute.However, the characters are fun and the 1 raid we can do rn, valtan, is fun. But its already getting to the point where a competent group can run over valtan in 30 min. Which means, if u die early, your group will kill valtan without you and there goes your weekly fun. honing isn't as bad as some people make it out to be (for most of us), but if you start this game with a couple friends expect to be doing different content at some point b/c some of you will get unlucky with honing. Its baffling that smilegate knows that all content prior to legion raids are Monster Hunter wannabe garbage and still shipped out the inferior version of lost ark to the west. You might hear from streamers that right now is the best time to play lost ark. But if you started now you won't reach the legion raids for at least 1-2 months. I'm still going to play the game, but if you haven't started then don't bother, maybe in 6 months when there are more legion raids and theres an express event to send you to the legion raids.tl;dr game has very little content that you can only do once a week, AGS and smilegate are ass, characters and legion raids are fun, and our version of the game is inferior to KR, play in 6 months.

_childDocuments_.review: Copying directly from my discussion entry of this game:Look, I ain't looking for a lot here alright?I'm not looking for long time engagement or not even end-game stuff. P2W doesn't bother me as much, just here to waste time until Dragon's Dogma 2 comes out or something.However, I found love in this game. Love I never thought I'd see ever again after WoW turned into a daycare version of what an MMO is. There are actual adults in this game. Not the boring ones no, the ones that are grown on the outside but actual children on the inside. Man-children if you will.Man-children who form a community. In a beautiful garden of Eden called Mokoko.The chat...is glorious. Simple yet elegant, casual yet hardcore, aggressive yet peaceful. It provides something more than just a way of communicating with other people. It provides a safe haven for those who knows what "Barrens chat" means. It's a proof that the server Mokoko is specifically designed and named for people who are familiar with the best and the worst of the internet. Mokoko is for people from all over the internet: 4chan, Reddit, hell maybe even 9gag.No Tumblr though. Tumblr can go f*ck itself.And the gameplay. Things...go boom. Lights everwhere, skill chains all around, health bars draining faster than my will to live whenever I read an article on Kotaku.I roleplay as a Paladin with a massive handlebar mustache who DEFINITELY spends Sundays engaging with the youth group.I roleplay as a hell-spawned assassin who is literally a ***** demon. (I manually put the stars to not get banned but imagine a word that rhymes with a secondary word used for sailors)I roleplay (and my favorite character by the way) as LITERALLY Megumin. You know how? There are macro text options in this game. You can type in text in those fields and once you press the shortcut keys, it says whatever's there. You can find the incantations on the front page of the internet .The game's fun. It's not amazing maybe, and it DEFINITELY feels like an Eastern Asian MMO. But you can just enjoy simple things in life.TL&DR: Game's ok, I'd say great time killer since it's free but it is a free asian mmo so do be aware about paywalls. Still, you can get at least a 20-30 hours of fun time killing stuff. Also, there are a lot of server queues so if that still goes on and if you're in the EU, try to opt in any other server than Mokoko. Unless you're fun, in which case come in and do feel at home.

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is amazingly fun, and lots of activities to do, things to collect, base to decorate. Game is gorgeous.However, gear progression is ugly and so is the culture participating in it. Gear progression fractures the player base instead of unites. Your item level dictates what content you can do, and not do, and there are many tiers of content. It is impossible to keep people aligned as a result, and with such a small player base combined with so many tiers, finding groups is hard; even if everyone plays the same amount, RNG can put them in different places.End game is really hard, and gatekept by veterans who have no incentive to help new players but the exact opposite. They are incentivized (due to design of end game gear progression) to keep players out of the content so they can charge them (so they can advance their character) to have access to it. There is nobody in public queues, and if you do get lucky to get one to pop, be prepared to be called names if you make a mistake.Gear progression is RNG based where you farm materials, and have a chance to upgrade gear. And by chance, I mean...no chance until you go broke, and so you need an army of alts to do 8 hours of grinding in hopes of maybe getting 1 upgrade. The game has never done a reset of any sort, and the power difference between players is immense. There is no hope for new players to catch up. Which means new players won't have access to end game content where they don't have to pay to get carried.
