_childDocuments_.review: Know what you are in for.This is a Korean MMO with all that includes. Pay to progress faster mechanics, grinding and more.But there is a reason this game is so hyped. The gameplay can be amazing, the Endgame Bosses are very fun to fight, the classes and characters are varied and unique, and if the aesthetics are your cup of tea the game looks great.Some call the story "press g to skip simulator", I personally enjoyed it somewhat. Yes the characters are forgettable, the voice acting (english) can be sub par, and the plot is generic. Despite all that it had some great moments, cool Dungeons, and was a decent introduction to the mechanics and the game.The endgame is standard MMO fare: Do your dayly and weekly Quests and Dungeons to slowly grind better and better equipment. What carries this game is the gameplay. Therefore if you enjoy that you will enjoy the game.As far as monetization goes, I payed for the "Gold Founder Pack" and so far, after 200+ hours, have not felt the need to spend more money. It is important to mention, that the PvP is divorced from the pay to progress mechanics. So in that regard it is not directly p2w. It honestly depends on your definition of p2w if this game falls under that definition. There is no way to pay for something that is objectively better than anything you can obtain in the game. On the other hand there are some features, especially those linked to your pet, that are incredibly convenient. I recommend you give Lost Ark a try. You won't even feel the need to invest money the first 30 to 50 hours and after that you can probably make up your own mind if paying for convenience or progress is worth it for you.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are someone who wants to play a game in the evening after a long day of work and just enjoy yourself then this is the wrong game for you. There is extreme and needless time gating that heavily restricts the activities you can do. As an example i am trying to do a quest at the moment that requires the completion of a co op event that is up for 2 min once per day. i have spent that last 5 days trying to do this quest and every time it gets remotely near the events start time something comes up and i miss itAnd it is the same for most of the content in the game. they are either on a daily lockout, such as guardian raids, and chaos dungeons, weekly lock outs such as abyssal dungeons, entry ticket lock outs such a the cube and boss rush or on this frankly insane timer lockout where the objective in question is only active for a handful of minutes every day. There is also the tower which is a single run per character. I have the following additional grievance with the end game Chaos dungeons, You can do these twice a day, before the rewards fall through the floor. they are an utterly mindless mob grind that take longer to queue for than to complete. they are dull to the point of being tedious. There are no mechanics and nothing to think about just explode monsters. They take about 5 min each. Honestly I don’t even know why this type of content exists. It barely fills any time and is about as fun as doing the dishes or ironing. Guardian raids. Advertised as 1-4 players this content actually has quite a good foundation. Aside from 2 main issues. The first being the fight lengths. The content sits on a hard time of 20 min. you either kill the boss in that time or you fail. My issue is that 20 min for a wipe on a boss is extremely tedious. It restricts the maker’s ability to design good fights and really dose just lead to an experience where you either look the boss up before hand or waste an ungodly amount of time learning the fights. The fights themselves are very dull and rely heavily on mechanics that stun lock a character in order to reduce the amount of time they can spend dpsing. What this leads to in practice is boss fights that are either so easy that you get bored and wonder why its taking so long to die. Or a boss fighting experience where you spend 40 or more seconds in a stun chain because the mob hit you with an unavoidable attack. My second issue is that for something that is advertised as 1-4 players it is very solo unfriendly, mainly due to the stun lock issue above. Finally the content is just boring. It isn’t hard it just wastes your time until you run out of it with big hp pools and long stuns. I outline these two together because The rewards for chaos dungeons and guardian raids are almost identical. But the difference in their time cost is very very different. It is utterly ridiculous that they would even have remotely similar rewards. Abyssal dungeons these are wonderful. The closet thing ive found to traditional mmorpg dungeon. They have great challenges and boss fights that are not too long and have much more fast paced and interesting mechanics. My only issue is the weekly lockout. I play with a group of about 11 people. And it sucks that because I did an abyssal dungeon on Friday with 3 of them I cant even enter to assist another group with the same content. I would prefer to be able to enter again and just get no loot to being completely locked out of it. Also 1 entry a week to the only content that is remotely amusing is very harsh The Cube The cube is great. Its an rogue like esc mini dungeon where you clear floors of enemies. Made much easier in a group but fun to do alone. I don’t really have anything bad to say about the cube. Other than I wish chaos dungeons were more like the cube. The fact that there are events that pop up and zone wide buffs / debuffs make it much more interesting than just mindlessly killing 8000 monsters on 3 identical maps. My complaint here is the same as the abyssal dungeon I would like to be able to do this more and less of the boring content. Sea activitiesThere are actually a lot of different sea activities available. Ide love to go into more detail but sadly each one is only active for a handful of seconds each day and if you so much as go to the toilet at the wrong time well sorry you have missed it and need to wait for the next one. This is by far the most irritating thing in the game. And frankly is the reason im so sick of this game. To conclude. Lost arks endgame has a lot of content but its either time games to the point of being out of reach to the normal player or so mind-numbingly boring that it is just not worth the time and effort to play. I really regret starting this game and I regret getting my friends to play it. It is honestly not worth the pixels it take up on the screen and frankly ide rather be playing new world

_childDocuments_.review: After over 3k hours of playing Lost Ark (RU, KR, and now NA) I cannot recommend this game to anyone. The game has gone downhill in a multitude of ways. Let's jump in.1) The CONSTANT disconnect/ping issues that have been plaguing the player base for MONTHS just never get fixed. Have you ever tried to run a raid with 7 other people and have people disconnecting randomly throughout the fight and you need those people alive for certain mechanics? WELL SUCKS TO SUCK, YOU GOTTA RESTART.2) Bots. holy bots. Any new player will come across only bots in the beginning of the game, for a good WHILE until they hit the current main hub of the game. Those bots are all farming gold in order to sell to players through RMT. Its just straight up a disaster and they cant fix the issue because of how the game market operates sadly. It isnt like BDO where you can limit everything and it works, LA has too many variables when it comes to the market for it to be viable. the market will always be doomed for NA EU.3) Inconsistent judgement from the AGS support team. Going off of the RMT problem the game faces, AGS wont perma ban people who do RMT. Instead they slap their write, firmly say "no", and ban them for maybe 1-2 weeks. It depends on the amount of gold, but its never really long. They allow for up to 3 strikes before a perma ban, and there has been evidence of them not even banning people after 3 strikes. PLUS there are methods of getting around the possibility of getting a ban entirely. It's disgusting and will most likely never get fixed4) The community. Dear GOD this community is toxic when it comes to pve. Due to the fact we have to play 6 characters in order to min max our accounts, people want only THE best players in their raids even if it means overgearing by over 100 item level (which is a lot as your damage will skyrocket). The first raid in the game is hard for newer players to complete because everyone wants to recruit people who are 1460 ilvl, when the raid is only 1370...and they gatekeep the hell out of new players trying to learn and complete content. They cant complete it. I was 1550 upon quitting lost ark and i would run with lower level people to help them just get through their weekly grind without stressing too much. I can essentially solo raids in terms of damage, but so many people gatekeep and are just straight up toxic in a PVE game...i understand wanting the best for pvp, but that game mode is dead as hell.Don't get this game. Youll waste your time

_childDocuments_.review: My experience after 8 hours of having played Lost Ark (also sprach Steam) and way more on New World is Amazon Games' servers handling is so bad they should let you go through the queue with the main client closed. _childDocuments_.review: Game starts out fun.  The first continent is well-done overall.  The game crashes and burns immediately afterwards though.  The point where the game loses all sense of fun is the tournament ark.  Now, you might be thinking hey, beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of a dozen guys in a tournament sounds like fun - and you'd be right, the boss battles are quite a lot of fun.  Unfortunately, there's dozens of side quests that you have to do for half the fights to learn about your opponents to try to exploit their weaknesses or some ♥♥♥♥, idunno, I didn't care.  The game also assumed that I'd played dirty to win rather than just beating the ♥♥♥♥ out of them (which is what I did) which broke immersion pretty hard.There's a lot of daily events you can supposedly do once you get to 250 ilvl, except, you can't.  I tried two of them.  One of them was a pvp bloodbath and the other required you to know a song to get any rewards.  The game doesn't give you any hints about requirements or anything other than ilvl, so you'll waste time going to events that don't tell you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ about what they are.Another major issue is that the game introduces (or rather, fails to introduce you to) ways to enhance your gear - engravings.  It does this real early.  Unfortunately, even after hitting the soft cap for player level, I haven't been able to use a single one - because the game has zero useful instructions on how to use the system.To top it all off, the game has like 30 million currencies and doesn't give you any indication of what they're for or how to get them.Update: Stuck with it and played for a bit longer to reach 'endgame' content.  It's just a huge-ass grind-fest.Chaos dungeons are easy, but boring as ♥♥♥♥.  You just mindlessly kill hordes of mobs over and over again.Guardian Raids have bosses with several times the HP that they need to and take ages to do.Abyssal Dungeons are the real cancer though.  Most/all bosses have a badly explained 1-shot mechanic.  A tooltip will pop up in the middle of the fight for a few seconds.  If you fail to read it because you're watching what you're doing, or running from a mechanic, it goes by to fast, or you just can't understand it (because it's incomprehensible), you wipe.  Hell, the second boss of the second dungeon has a mechanic that heals him to full over and over and over and over again if you don't figure out the completely unexplained mechanic.  It doesn't get better from their either.  In the 3rd dungeon, the very first boss has multiple insta-kill mechanics without any explanation about how they work.  I get mechanics, but insta-kill mechanics are just completely stupid and suck all the fun out of a game.  Doubly so if they punish you for not following instructions that were never given.

_childDocuments_.review: Have been playing LA since February and have mostly enjoyed it up until the last month and a half.  I joined friends playing it not knowing anything about the server other than it was West Coast North America.  Seems that it was a high pop server but never had any trouble with ques up until about a month and a half ago, with ques consistently anywhere from 9000 to 19000. For someone who is more a casual gamer after work its pretty disheartening to never be able to log on because of these ungodly ques.  Games graphics have become choppy, with micro stutters all the time and fps drops down into the teens from 140 fps for no apparent reason.  I don't have a top of the line rig, but I am able to play Cyberpunk with very high settings and have no problems.  Again, this was not happening the first three months of playing, and the forums are riddled with people experiencing the same problems video-wise (with rigs vastly superior to mine) to the point that it is getting unplayable. The list of potential causes have little to nothing to do with actual game settings and more with random causes like having Zone chat turned on. Customer service is a joke because it is Amazon's CS, and while great with getting me a refund for broken merchandise, they know sweet f**kall about video games. If i get told to update my drivers one more time (wow thanks never once thought to do that, maybe I should turn it off and on again too?) I am going to reach through my screen and ♥♥♥♥♥ slap someone. And the botting, wow, I haven't seen botting like this since the days of the Yahoo chat rooms of the early 2000's.  Trains of Bezerkers going through zones, toons glitching on terrain, toons doing the funky chicken, to quote Ronnie James Dio, It goes on and on and on.  Easy Anti Cheat is obviously not working at all.  I like this game, I really do, but the compounding issues are really making me consider just walking away from it, and that is too bad because it is a fun game.  They have made it so you don't have to grind to level alts, so it seems they want to make it easy for people to enjoy this game, but with the ♥♥♥♥ show it is becoming, without some serious changes, the bots will be the only ones playing this game in a year.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so im doing a review for lost ark where i will try to explain what this game is(there are already a lot of reviews but i dont care), so Lost ark is a mmo about the power of darkness fighting against the light, your classic hero vs villain drama, demons come bla bla bla kill somebody etc etc.. now lets talk about the good, the bad and the ugly of lost ark.The Good:It's a very beautiful visual mmorpg, it has a lot of diversity and each continent makes me feel like im in a new game, sure the first area feels basic and meh, but after that you start to feel the love of the developers and how much they wanted to make this game shine, note that im just about 50~%-ish done with the story  so i didn't ge to experience all the locations this game has to offer but so far it made me think of other games and reminded me of some memories i made back in the day.. so i really liked that..,there is also a Roaster option which basically lets you romance the main characters and some side characters you meet throughout the story, they are done pretty well and you can also give them gifts or dance/chat with them to increase your friendship lvl so to say, Lost ark also has a create your island type of thing where you can invite your Roaster into it and let them live besides you, and you can craft a bunch of stuff which is cool, i bet in some months there will be some dedicated people who will create some really nice art., there is also hunting/fishing/lumbering/mining and discovering lost artifacts.. and a ton of collectibles like the great "mokoko", a lot of hidden quests and some special enemies that you need to kill to complete your adventurer journey which is a great way to make you revisit the map and look for hidden stuff or things that you've missed., there is also a sea which is nice., there are also a ton of cards to collect which makes me happy cause i love collecting cards, wish they did a card battle system tho, the raids are also very challenging and require team work and some timing which makes the game harder and more enjoyable unless you.. ya'know.. meet bots as your teammates. :)The Bad:Lost ark is very repetitive like most mmos, and that is not a bad thing unless you had your usual quests where you just go and hunt some enemies come back, deliver some stuff, come back again and deliver some more stuff and in the end you enter a dungeon and kill the boss and that's about it., the dungeons as well are very mediocre and easy, they give you a normal/hard difficulty but you will always be overleveled and won't even use the gear they give you in those dungeons, besides coming back to get your mokokos there will be no reason to ever come back to those dungeons which is a shame,pvp seems very weird and unbalanced but take this with a grain of salt i only played 2 matches as a sorceress and it felt very dull, there is no server transfer, and we also have a Crystalline Aura benefits which is basically your way to get some bonuses regular players don't have, think of it as the 30 day premium packages from Riders of Icarus if you ever played that mmo., the game is also incomplete and by that i mean there are classes that the western version does not have yet i think there are 20 classes in the korean version vs our 15 atm, which sucks for some people but they said in the near future they will also introduce those said classes still a bummer.The Ugly:The game tries to slow you down with meticulous ways such as fishing or mining takes energy or action points and you start with  10k action points and you get 10 energy back every 30m, and an action costs between 30~90(or more) depending on what you do, even your island has an action point meter which limits your playability by a little, also there are research blueprints that you gotta craft which also take time between 20m~1day, another way the game tries to make you spend more time in it is by having time scheduled events which this tbh isnt such a bad thing but its still scummy, you basically have to wait another cycle for the event if you missed it because you went to the bathroom or went to dinner, raids in this game and other contents such as guardian fights(which basically is fighting bosses 4v1) are also on a daily limit, and this is the main part where you can get loot and gear and improve your character level, now imagine that you maybe want to play more in a day than others and want to farm some raids or what not, but the game says you cant enter anymore until next week after you entered once in a raid.. yeah a 1 week chill pill,imagine steam having a 1 game buy/play per week policy but you want and can pay/play more.. that is the raid in lost ark.. also there is character lvl restriction such as reach item lvl x to progress the story which forces you to do other content even if you dont want to and locks you out of other places on the map/sea, even if you would go there the game would just push you back because you don't meet the requirements., and lastly.. the QUEUE... if you played lost ark or heard about it you will understand that atm the game is a queue simulator, i have 110 hours but i think 35~h are just waiting in a queue to enter the game.., the devs said they cannot improve the queue or transfer characters for the new europe region so basically you will have to wait around 3~5 hours if you have a life and a job and come back around 3~6 pm home., if you enter in the morning it's okay no queue tho which is.. good ig., there is also a 15m afk timer which basically means if you go and eat for more than 15m and you are in game well.. say goodbye to your 5 hours of queue time you waited.Now would i recommend lost ark to people if they asked me if its a good game to play?Mixed feelings about it, on one part its a great visual game which looks good and feels smooth(most of the time) there are a bunch of stuff to do in this game and that's pretty neat but on the other hand you are forced to wait for resets and have a daily/weekly/energy limit and cannot do anything about it unless you pay to reset a part of it which for me this kinda ruins the mood. so for now i would so no wait some months or so and see what the devs are planning to do about the game and check some other forums to see what they improved or what not, unless they improve the queue i would say pass on this game unless you wish to wait 3~4 hours daily to play for some hours.

As a female gamer, I love the outfits available to wear for both male and female characters (except the female gunslinger because those shorts look silly to me but that's just an opinion). _childDocuments_.review: TLDR; fun-ish for awhile but grinding becomes a boring chore after level 50. I picked this game up for the first time and made it to level 51 and have played 114.6 hours at the time of this writing. This game is like the most expensive phone game ever made. The resources you need are limited by day/week. You cannot move to the next zone until you hit a certain item level. While you are working towards the next item level, everything you do is EASY and becomes very boring really quickly. When you do reach the item level to go to the next area, everything is still EASY and it's just a mindless boring slog. Nothing seems challenging combat wise except for occasional opponents that just have HUGE hit points. The Chaos dungeons and some combat is fun and feels satisfying until you realize you can only do it once or twice a day before you stop getting the resources you need to progress. Then you gotta sink time into daily quests that are again limited. Building you base is limited by energy. What makes this worse imo is every piece of gear per tier looks the exact same. Common, rare, epic, legendary of each items per item tier looks EXACTLY the same. I was working towards getting a legendary tier 1 armor piece but by the time I got there I was able to do the next chaos dungeon that I can easily solo in under 10 minutes and the rare drop is 100x better than a legendary tier one piece of gear. This game has potential but it just feels like a super expensive phone game that looks nice but feels hollow. I do not enjoy trying to grind for that next piece of gear or to upgrade what I have at all. I don't want to make multiple alts to replay thru the same story over and over just so I can funnel mats to my main so I feel like I'm making progress. They really should remove the item level requirements to progress so that combat is challenging while you work towards the end game. This game may be fun to play thru maybe one time but that's it. lvl 1-50 are basically solo. I had reported over 300 bots by the time I was level 40. It's just thousands of bots playing this game getting in your way and killing mobs you need. I've only met a handful of real players and only one of them wasn't thru matchmaking and talked to me and was cool. The others have obviously been playing for a long time. During my "challenge" dungeons, the other players are so powerful they one shot everything, including the boss with a 20x health bar. I literally don't even get one hit on the boss before it's dead which takes the only potential fun out of what you have to do a lot of to get your gear score up.I'll play this game a little because I have a friend who is new to gaming and enjoying it because it's free and I can only recommend you check it out because it's F2P but if they charged me even $1 for this game it's an hard pass imo.

_childDocuments_.review: After pouring a fair amount of time into this game (323 hours) I can say it's not healthy for me to continue playing it. Visually it's a beauty but beyond the flash and sparkle the systems and mechanics are like any other MMO/ARPG live service. Designed to lure you in and indoctrinate you towards the grind. Without extensively researching how you want to interact with this game it's easy to become overwhelmed by the many RNG systems or %chance failure rates re: levelling up your equipment. It is designed to be time consuming and confusing and played with friends. DO NOT SOLO! This game is geared towards end game group content for the best rewards. Without support you will find yourself disadvantaged if not completely lost. I suppose this is all pretty standard affair with F2P games this generation. It's average to good fun if not excellent in places at the beginning but the story - that I can access - loses it's initial appeal. It's a theme park of adventure games that decided to keep the waiting in lines as a feature. Do not step into this uninformed. Certain currencies are locked to character when opened so opening every chest will leave you with an abundance of materials you can neither use nor sell.Anybody that suffers with OCD should run as far as they can from this product.Shockingly though as far as F2P games go it's probably a 7/10 As a solo experience it wanes to a 4/10 I'm a little older and I wasn't looking to join a guild or min-max every statistic. I certainly wasn't looking to wait for islands to mystically appear at 11AM on a Monday then boot me after 20 minutes when I'm trying to explore a new area and what it offers. I'm disappointed and I can't recommend investing the time I have into this unless you want the whole community, guild, teamwork experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't believe the hype around this game. Like most Korean games, it LOOKS flashy, it LOOKS high budget, and it LOOKS like there's a lot to do. In fact, there is very little of any substance beneath the sparkle. Most of your playtime from levels 1-50 will be spent clicking through horribly written dialogue read by voice actors hired off of Fiverr. Each quest will have you, at most, kill three to five enemies that die in a single hit before moving on to the next NPC, who will flap his gums at you with no passion and then tell you to kill five more rats. The story is downright awful. It's just about the most intensely generic, soulless Korean MMO story I have ever experienced, and I've played TERA, Black Desert, Maplestory, Aion and both Lineage games. It's actually insulting how little effort and originality Korean game studios put into writing their stories and doing their worldbuilding, and Lost Ark STILL managed to shock me with how bad its story and writing were. On top of that, the localization is PAINFULLY bad. There are CONSTANT typos and awful transliterations everywhere. I mentioned the abysmal quality of the voice acting, but some of that credit surely needs to go to how AWFUL the localization was: no human being could fathom how to naturally deliver these awkward Engrish sentences.Once you reach level 50, you will be doing one of 3 things on an average day, all with the end goal of pressing a button on an upgrade screen that will make some arbitrary numbers on your gear (extremely unreadable and hyperinflated numbers, I should add: it is a Korean game after all) go up, or fail to go up once you start to reach higher gearscores. These 3 things are as follows: a less interesting version of Nephalem rifts from Diablo II, isometric Monster Hunter, and a few actually engaging heroic dungeon ripoffs (these have since been nerfed into the ground). Said Nephalem rifts only reward worthwile payouts twice a day per character, the same goes for each monster you carve. The only arguably redeemable and engaging content the game has to offer currently, the Abyss dungeons, have FULL WEEK LONG COOLDOWNS PER CHARACTER. That's right, you will be waiting a full week per character before you get to do content that requires an activated neuron. This has the admittedly hilarious side effect of causing literally 99% of the community to be incapable of performing the most basic of mechanics, because they only get to practice them once a week.Why not just make alts to replay the fun time gated content, you may ask. Well, it's worth mentioning that all of that content is gated based on item score. This isn't the sort of gating you'd see in, say, a worthwhile MMO like FFXIV, where you can bypass gear score requirements by queuing with a full premade. No, you are physically incapable of entering content that you do not meet the minimum ilevel requirement for. I would say that, for the average player, the act of upgrading a SINGLE CHARACTER'S ilevel to mid-endgame is going to take a month and a half without spending money on the game. Now imagine you wanted to do dungeons twice a week, and you've already spent that astronomical amount of upgrade materials getting your first character's gear up to snuff. Yeah, your alts will be stuck well behind for quite a while, only capable of running the few tutorial dungeons that have been nerfed into snoozefests.Skip this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. It baffles me how anyone can leave a positive review here. If you like the grind, that's one thing, but I can give you at least seven other grindy Korean MMOs that have better stories, better gameplay loops, better visuals, better graphics, better PvP. It might be that a ton of people just have ♥♥♥♥♥♥ taste. Don't be one of them: don't play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game used to be fun to me; I started about a month after it launched. I am a very casual player who does not enjoy end content in ANY game; I enjoy the journey. But even just questing and getting to new zones to progress through the story is gatekept via gear level requirements. I used to use the story events which gave higher (current at the time) level gear, but haven't seen one of those events in a while. The gold got nerfed, too, thus my ability to acquire it really slowed down to almost nothing. So, after ~2k hours, I just more or less quit playing, other than logging in to slowly level my guild to level 10 (a goal i had set way back in the day - I have OCD and completionist issues, lol).If you enjoy games which include lots of gatekeeping and harsh punishments for end content failures, the excessive Pay-to-Win structure, and painfully slow gear grinds, then this game is for you. If you don't care about that and just enjoy logging in and doing whatever you can, progression be thrown to the wind, this game is also for you. If you enjoy end content but don't enjoy the prior-mentioned issues, or if you're a very casual quest-leveler like me yet can't progress due to gear requirements, this game is very likely NOT for you. I'd advise to seek fun in another game unless you just really enjoy masochism.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★☆☆Lost Ark is a visually stunning action role-playing game that promises an immersive and epic adventure in a beautifully crafted world. While the game boasts impressive graphics, engaging combat, and a rich storyline, it falls short in its endgame experience due to its pay-to-win mechanics that hinder the overall enjoyment and fairness for players.One of the standout features of Lost Ark is its breathtaking visuals and art design. The game world is meticulously crafted, with stunning landscapes, intricate details, and vibrant environments that immerse players in its fantastical setting. The character designs are diverse and visually appealing, adding depth to the game's immersive experience.The combat system in Lost Ark is fluid and enjoyable, offering a wide range of abilities and playstyles to choose from. The fast-paced action and responsive controls make battles exhilarating, and the variety of classes allows for diverse gameplay strategies. Whether you prefer close-quarters brawling or long-range spellcasting, there is a class to suit every playstyle.The story in Lost Ark is compelling, taking players on a grand quest filled with twists, turns, and memorable characters. The narrative is well-paced and unfolds through engaging cutscenes and dialogue, immersing players in the lore-rich world and driving their motivation to progress further.However, Lost Ark's endgame experience is marred by pay-to-win mechanics, particularly in the acquisition of powerful items. The game heavily relies on a randomized loot system, where players have a chance to obtain rare and valuable items. Unfortunately, the presence of loot boxes and a real-money marketplace creates an imbalance in the game's economy and progression. Those willing to spend real money have a significant advantage over players who choose to rely solely on their in-game efforts, undermining the sense of achievement and fairness.Moreover, the grind required to progress in Lost Ark's endgame content can be daunting and repetitive. The reliance on repeating dungeons and grinding for specific drops can become monotonous, dampening the overall enjoyment and sense of progression. While some players may find satisfaction in the grind, it may deter others who prefer a more balanced and rewarding gameplay loop.Additionally, the game's localization and translation can be inconsistent and occasionally awkward. While the overarching story is intriguing, the dialogue and text can sometimes feel stilted or poorly translated, leading to moments of confusion or disconnect from the narrative.In conclusion, Lost Ark delivers a visually stunning and engaging ARPG experience with its captivating visuals, immersive combat, and compelling storyline. However, its endgame progression is hindered by pay-to-win mechanics that disrupt the fairness and enjoyment for players. While the game offers an enjoyable journey through its early and mid-game content, the presence of these pay-to-win elements in the endgame may discourage those seeking a more balanced and competitive experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I kept waiting for the catch in "free" with this game but it never happened. Clearly lost ark has been designed with such confidence in it's ability to win your heart that you will eventually be inclined to buy the novelty glamour packs that come with it. None of these gives an advantage over someone in the game who hasn't spent a dime. The battles feel epic, the game is huge, and there is humour woven in. I have played some of the biggest MMO's. Warcraft, Elder Scrolls. FF14. All are fantastic, But this does something wonderful. The quests are broken up into bitesize quests so you don't get exhausted but it is monumental at the end. Each area you go to brings you a completely different scenario. In one its an epic battle for a castle. In other,d you are shrunk and running around with little people on their little island riding a ladybird. Then you find yourself in some sort of Mortal Combat homage leaderboard. Next thing you know you have landed in mechanoland. This game is absolutely excellent, and did I mention it is free? Only a company like amazon could have pulled this off as its clearly a loss leader.If I have a complaint it is that despite the feeling of the world being huge and diverse it's a bit perplexing, nay perhaps narcissistic or just plain lazy that everyone has an American accent. Also why oh why do the female characters in these games always look like prostitutes, really there is no way anyone could lep around in those heels. Can we please address that tedious trope? There is a lot of sameness about the gear and it takes away from all the great things about the game.4 out of 5 stats from me.

_childDocuments_.review: Are you wanting to try Lost Ark because of the hype and because everyone you know is playing it? Are you more of a casual gamer not wanting to min-max and just wants to play the content the game has to offer? This game will probably not for you. Many things, including the main story, will be gated behind item level. Your main goal is basically to upgrade your gear and reach certain requirements to play what the game has to offer. The fights are fun and challenging, but to even reach them is a pain. So get to grinding and more grinding on alts to funnel to your main. Your progression will be halted for some time, even if p2w or f2p player. The game is brutal and punishing with materials if you fail to enhance/hone your gear. Compared to other games that will push you to level up or get better gear to continuing playing the game, you're playing the game here to upgrade your equip. Or well, that's what it feels like. No longer fun but a chore. Game is pretty and other stuff like sailing is fun. But, again, you get to the point of grinding out those other content for the same goal of leveling up your gear.When your progression is halted by the game unless you slowly grind or bust out your wallet for your convenience and time, it's not a game for everyone. It's fun for grinders and old-skool MMO gamers though, so be prepared to waste your time if you are used to this.Edit: I've come back after playing double my previous hours, and I stand by everything I've said. Failing honing will make you go nowhere for days or maybe even weeks. Alts seem to almost be a must for quicker progression. You WILL have to invest in your time in various ways, unless you get ready to swipe your VISA or whatever card. Fun game, as I'm still playing, but be warned. _childDocuments_.review: There seems to be a consensus that Lost Ark  isn't really an ARPG but an isometric MMORPG in the Tera or Black Desert style. It's definitely both. The moment to moment gameplay is mechanically an ARPG, the combat is meaty, fast-paced and addictive. But the mechanisms that govern the overall progress of a character is almost painfully derivative of those aforementioned games, with a baffling number of currencies acting as gates to progress in almost every aspect of your character's development. Little of this really matters before level cap however, and one can safely pass through the levelling journey in cruise control. But while it's overall a very derivative and linear path to endgame everything it does is to an uncommonly high level of flair and polish. There's a great deal of creative energy been put into how the world, it's characters and plots are presented. So yes, it's hackneyed, you've definitely experienced it's story beats many times over before, but you'll seldom have seen them this well presented. And as filler quests whizz by you might even occasionally find yourself being drawn into the odd bit of drama and find the odd nugget of gold among the packed out "go here and get those" and "speak to that guy 10 yards away" stuff. It's a weird prospect overall, there are all sorts of reasons for it not to appeal to me, but the net experience is that it really is a lot of fun. . I like it's combat more than any other ARPG I've played,  it's extremely satisfying. The explosion of loot has been replaced with a bunch of stackable collectibles, there are loads of mechanics involved in building a viable endgame character, and a ton of grinding to be done. It's an ARPG and it's a South Korean MMORPG, and an even split of both. If the best and worst aspects of those genres balance out for you then this will probably click.

_childDocuments_.review: As a game, there is a lot to say about Lost Ark.The graphics are amazing, as is the combat. It's a lot of fun with genuine skill expression. While the game can be full of gatekeeping and toxicity, learning runs are a thing, as is the mokoko mentor program in the unofficial lost ark discord. I would recommend this game to anybody who wants to spend the time learning it, because it can be relatively time consuming and unintuitive to learn the game. A fair warning though, this is NOT a game meant to play your favorite character and that's it. Into endgame, having 5-6 characters to run raids on is almost essential to farm enough mats.However, it is possible to enjoy the game without pushing to the very newest content, as there is still relative "early" game content such as valtan and vykas, the beginnings of the endgame.All in all the community isn't as bad as its rep, and the game is worth a try if you're looking for something to grind and do in your spare time, but it will take you time to reach the endgame, to learn all the fine details, and you need to be open, honest. In my experience, saying "Hey fair warning I am kinda new so kick me if you want, but I studied the raids and I feel confident" has gotten me a lot of forgiveness and patience. Just give people that honesty, that chance to kick you to another party if they don't have the patience. "How Will I get into runs if they all kick-" Shut up, they won't, and those parties would stop everything to kick you out after you messed up twice anyway.Be patient, and the game isn't so painful to learn.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks pretty and the combat is pretty awesome. The rest of it is just... ugh.The story could have been copy pasted from any of a million cheap fantasy novels. It's dull and has nothing of any note in it. There are demons, and a prince who doesn't think he is worthy of being king and blah blah blah "insert tired and repetitive fantasy trope here". The characters are cringeworthy and their voice acting is bland.The currencies and crafting and extra curricular activities are beyond ridiculous. Every day for the several weeks I played I was finding a new currency or a new crafting mechanic or a new daily activity or a new collectible or something else that I forgot almost immediately because I couldn't even remember the shopping list of other things that had already thrown in my face. Sure this is a big part of MMOs, but you can reach a point where there is just too much, and this game goes way beyond that point.The questing is absolutely atrocious. 90% of your time is spent going from person A to person B then back to person A again. Often these people would literally be standing a few metres apart but for some reason needed a third party to play Chinese whispers with. The quests themselves are constantly being recycled, and aren't even remotely interesting to begin with. The maps are precise, cleverly constructed funnels that allow you zero freedom to do anything but move from point A to point B because that's what you are supposed to do. The challenge is nonexistent. I had one character death in 17 hours of play, and that was as much because I wasn't paying attention as because the fight was difficult.This is a game that believes being easy + cramming every possible idea every MMO has ever had in there = good. It doesn't.It's free, so you may as well give it a try. But I found it profoundly disappointing and mind numbingly boring, particularly considering the massive hype train preceding it.

_childDocuments_.review: I had typed out a long drawn out discussion on this game but you know what I'm just going to make it semi short and sweet. Here we goThis game isn't dumbed down. If your a gamer and your tired of everything being made for an xbox controller with 3 or 4 skills then you will like this game. It takes a bit of thinking at the start and the keyboard combat feels weird at first but stick with it practice in a noob area learn your first few skills you start out with get use to figuring out some cool combat combos and just have some fun.Don't panic with all the pages of things in the UI telling you to collect cards, to make decks, to do engravings and all the other 900 things you can do in this game. Just play the game do some quest and take your time. Have fun. Don't give up you will get pretty good and things will start clicking for you.The dungeons are great you can find scrolls with lost dungeons, there are also quest dungeons. You can play on normal difficulty or Hard. You have a chance for some better loot if you play on hard. The dungeons take 10 to 15 min so its great if you don't have a ton of time to do things and they have enough action and things going on in them to keep it exciting.As you are exploring around zone boss mobs can spawn and people will all start fighting along side of you its pretty exciting. Also smaller mini bosses will spawn that can drop loot as you explore these are random.  If you like to explore there are secret areas that are honestly pretty well hidden you have to really look around seriously look around hidden things are all over.Give this game a chance till after lvl 20ish when you do the Mori Ruins. It's a dungeon where you complete the first big part of the main quest line.  It's a bit longer and has traps, ambushes hidden rooms a series of mini booses leading up to a main boss. That dungeon blew my mind. It was harder than the others and I had to work for it but dang it was fun. Real quick Id like to mention that you can find all sorts of neat things in your inventory campfires you can make for your group, all sorts of gernaeds and bombs. Shielding potions and a ton of other James Bond type things to help you out in combat / exploring (pets to pick up loot for you which is nice) If you like loot this game has tons of it. At lower levels you will burn through it.Im going to cut this short but let me wrap this up by saying. This games FREE get it. Don't worry about how crazy hard it looks. Just get out there and fight till you get comfortable. Its going to feel weird at first. Getting use to the combat really turned me off at first. Getting use to using the mouse to move and basic attack then using wasd / keyboard attacks was odd. After an hour or two messing around in the noob area fighting trash mobs I got the hang of it and I actually like it now. Don't quit if you don't like a class try one of the other ones. Play till at least the Mori Ruins! Remember you don't have to learn everything about this game just play it and take baby steps. Learn the combat then start dipping your feet into other things as you go.

_childDocuments_.review: Core of the title.Lost Ark, at its core, is an upgrade simulator. You basically do daily activities like Una's Tasks, island quests, Chaos dungeons, Abyssal, Cube and/ or Boss Rushes to acquire upgrade materials. You then use the materials for a chance at upgrading.I made it to 1370, straight up quit because it's just more upgrading after that. Lost Ark's endgame is just upgrading with no end.You also have a daily limit on how many activities you can get rewards for. The game encourages users to make alternate accounts because of this. No rewards, no way to upgrade = free to play, player stuck or you need to use money.Lost Ark does have a bunch of collectibles, but the majority are interconnected to each other, so basically you need to invest time with all of them to complete any of them.ClassesThe actual gameplay of using in-game characters is like a solid 5/10, but nothing extraordinary. Classes are mostly different from one another and are fun to play for the most part.Some say Lost Ark is an open-world, I don't.When I think of open-world I picture Skyrim, GTA, Rust, Dayz. Not a bunch of loading screens to move you to a new area. Also the camera is in a fixed position, you see the world the same exact way as everyone else.Title feels old, dated.With the game being old, I never felt like I was doing anything new. All of the playstyles and/ or gear sets have already been achieved. It was almost like I was using a strategy guide to play.Bots, Bots and Bots...The game is riddled with hundreds of thousands of them. The majority of the starting areas are just full of them. People do this to collect gold to sell on websites. Also the open chat in most areas is just bots marketing websites for gold.My Honest OpinionLost Ark feels like a simi-linear mobile title and/ or upgrading simulator while people using bots trying to exploit ingame rewards for easy profits. The people that might get stuck in this game, might have gambling addictions.If you have gambling issues, please don't play this game.I say that as the game is designed to be as flashy as possible in hopes it attracts users to stay engaged longer. It uses the practice of making things always seem shiny and/ or moving to entice people they're doing great things.CommunityThe community of Lost Ark is a mixed bag for me. If someone has spent a ton of resources and/ or time on upgrading just to fail doing so, they tend to be rude and/ or toxic to anyone they come in contact with.It's very common for new users in Abyssal dungeons to be bullied, attacked in chat if they're not familiar with the activity. Because the title is so old, people are expected to watch the mechanics online like YouTube before trying such activities.It's like the same toxicity levels as DOTA 2 and/ or LOL at times, but it was just my experience.I don't recommend this title.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ark is everything it promises to be and more. The MMORPG genre is something that has not seen innovation in decades, and Lost Ark is here to shake that up. As a WoW and ESO player, I'd consider myself well versed in the MMORPG genre and have an everlasting love for it, but the genre has had a very consistent format over the years only truly varying in interface and story. Lost Ark, however, takes a whole new approach to this by taking a unique approach to classes and character creation, gameplay style and feel, and world interface as a whole. A particular strength of this game is the responsiveness and incredible feel of combat, as it is extremely visually pleasing and truly makes your character feel like a god among men on a quest to slay great enemies of formidable strength across an incredible environment.

_childDocuments_.review: Best MMO I've played in years. 10/10. Bad: Very few actual ingame glitches despite the instability in the servers at launch. Small lag spikes here and there, but nothing that significantly detracted from the experience. Story is KPop silliness, voice acting is borderline High School Musical and there are a LOT of activities, currencies and such at endgame to try and keep track of.Good: Most of those things above, plus impactful combat and a deep skill and mod system that lets you customize your character to a good extent. Wonderful visuals, better than a lot of AAA MMOs on the market. The dungeon design and experiences are out-of-this-world, best I've experienced in an MMO full-stop with zero doubt in my mind. I cannot remember EVER being this blown away by dungeon puzzles and boss mechanics. The closest I can think of would be the mechanics of GuildWars2 bosses with puzzle work from Skyrim, all in an isometric view that cuts to in-engine cinematics frequently enough to wow you but not so often that it's annoying. Just brilliant work.

_childDocuments_.review: The game offers a large variety of tasks to do, from raids to dungeons, and the more chill tasks, like sailing the open seas, looking for all kinds of treasures on islands, and resource gathering that contributes to your Stronghold, your own private island. The story and voice acting is pretty mediocre, there's no sugar coating that, but I find the world design very intriguing, and a lot of characters have pretty dope designs. The combat is fluid, and the animations are lovely, and you really feel involved in every encounter. As I'm writing this review, it's sitting at a mixed rating on Steam, a far cry from it's "overwhelmingly positive"before official launch, but the vast majority of people who've given a negative review aren't actually critiquing the game itself, but the horrible launch and server queues. Amazon really f'ed up in this regard, New World should have prepared them for this reality, that is certainly true, but most reviews are disingenuous and don't reflect the quality of the game, simply the connectivity issues and hellish queues. Don't let the recent reviews fool you, in my opinion, Lost Ark has a lot to offer you, but that's only if you're willing to give it an honest try. And hey, it's free, so the only thing you'll be losing is time... or your money, but that’s your own business.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, it's unfair to rate this between Yes and No. I don't play many to be fair, but this seems like a run-of-the-mill MMORPG, one of the benefits is the game is free, so you can check it out and see what you think. I will say, and I think most of these games are like this, the quests are INCREDIBLY tedious. Most of your quests are simple fetch quests, like go over to that area five feet away and kill X amount of monsters, then return and turn in the quest, seriously I'm not exaggerating. There's also several instances where you'll be talking to an NPC giving you a quest and for no reason at all you have to talk to them or someone right next to them several times. The leveling system is kinda interesting, though it's not for me. You upgrade equipment to level, there isn't a number system or something. I can see people liking this because it adds to different potential builds and experiences, (more so with different classes) however i'm just not super into it.The game is Pay-to-win, but it's still pretty generous for players who don't wanna cough-up all their money for gold or a costume or something. _childDocuments_.review: Great ARPG, even better MMO, this game is must play if you are into both genres. It has the endless grindiness of Path of Exile/Diablo 3 mixed with a super interconnected and interactive social environment, and plenty of things to do with guildies or friends. The only complaint I have thus far is that the leveling experience is designed for one to do solo, as there are many many solo instances and dungeons that you cannot do with your party, but do not base the co-op experience off of the leveling. The co-op PvE starting at level 50 is awesome, with something for every kind of player, whether you want to do chaos dungeons (like greater rifts from Diablo 3), guardian raids (like isometric monster hunter), abyssal dungeons (4 person raids with mechanically difficult bosses), island exploration, and tons of world events to hop into depending on your item level. This list only goes on the further you progress into the endgame. I have spent almost as long in the first part of endgame content as I have leveling three characters to 50, and I am not even close to true endgame content. This game has a LONG progression curve if you do not spend a ton of money on honing materials, and even though there are plenty of people that have spent hundreds even thousands of dollars on this game, I have not spent a penny and I have no plan to open my wallet at any point. Free to Play progression does get very slow once you hit item level 600, and continues to slow down after that, but there is much more to progress other than item level. You can focus on collectibles and side quests and get 100% area completion for every quest zone, or you can focus on life skills like foraging, hunting, mining, woodcutting, etc.. The materials you gather from life skills can be used at your stronghold for crafting or upgrading, or you can sell the materials you gather for gold on the market place, which allows you to have all of the benefits of spending money on the game without ever doing so. There are many ways to play this game, and every way I have tried so far has felt fun, addicting, and worthwhile. On top of the fact that this is a great game, even if it were single player, it also has a massive player base, and a large portion of the people actively playing are either too deep to stop or enjoying the game too much to play anything else. One of the only games I've ever played where I am excited that it takes around 2 years to get to max item level as a Free to Play.

_childDocuments_.review: The art and graphics are nice, the content is abundant, and the combat is satisfying (feels very close to Diablo 3). However, the game refuses to let you fight anything. The gameplay is an endless barrages of dull quests built on uninteresting dialogue and inane chores. The game is so intensely infatuated with its own NPCs that in the rare occasions where you encounter a boss fight, it always gets interrupted by a cutscene where some quest NPC swoops in to finish off the boss while your character lies helpless in the dirt.The translation/writing is uninteresting, and it seems a lot of the story has been mangled and censored from its original Korean version. The English voice direction is uninspiring.The character progression systems are cluttered and complicated, but do not offer any added depth. There is an excessive variety of currency tokens. The time investment for endgame progression seems overly inflated (and also relies on gambling mechanics) in order to puff up the appeal of the cash shop.But the most crucial issue is Amazon being the pinnacle of incompetence, taking no lessons from their failures with their previous MMO, New World. The launch of Lost Ark in America and Europe was a trainwreck. It's been about a week since the servers went online and standard login queue time is still around 5-7 hours. The playerbase is severely fractured due to terrible infrastructure and the lack of a character transfer option. Character names are unique to the entire region so it's impossible to name your avatar anything remotely pronounceable.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't make many posts/reviews but i felt like an informative one was needed for this. First off, after playing for an extended amount of time, I can't recommend this game because it is essentially a time-gated time-sink.Graphically it's beautiful, the combat works well, the raids/abyssal dungeons are fun, and the certain charm whilst levelling is nice. Those are the PROS.The cons far outweigh the pros in it's current state, examples being the gear time-gate is ridiculous! You can do 2 chaos dungeons (boring as f) per day which give you upgrade materials, 2 monster hunter style raids per day (but get very little) and various timed events that give you very little in the way of actual progress.Unless you do all of the above things on 3/4 alts, of the same ilvl, you can only expect to progress 3-6 ilvl's per week. Don't mind a grind, hell i've played over a thousand hours of Runescape but this grind feels more like a chore and is not fun.On top of the gear grind, you have limited daily rapport (reputation) emotes/songs that you can perform to gain rewards (some of which reward Skill points, collectables, emotes and non-combat stat pots that again gate future progress with other rapport npcs).Lastly there is the dailies which reset on Thursday, these are a necessity, as they're your main source of free gold (non brought) in the game. These again are gated to keep you coming back.. 3 weeklies and 3 daily quests (repeatable).Final note as a con is the RnG, which is an acceptable evil in most games, but nearly all the collectables in this game (which give very valuable / profitable / necessary items) are gated behind tedious repeatable timed dailies that have very little chance of dropping the collectables.TLDR : Good game with good PvE but the progression (all aspects) feels more like 90% chore and 10% fun.Unless you're willing play the same content over and over again on 4+ character or spend a lot or RL money don't expect to keep up  with current content.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is playable at best.  And I mean "playable" as in the "being able to play", not as in something one would enjoy playing.In terms of the UI, the click controls and overuse of the keyboard to do simple things is really weird (keyboard shortcuts and UI layout is, apart from a few options, largely non-intuitive).  The move (left-click) and attack (right-click) being on separate mouse clicks feels super clunky, especially:  - the talk to (or rescue) NPCs is the same as the command for movement, making it super hard to actually interact with the NPC.  NPCs are harder to click on if another player or an object is standing nearby.   - combat where you're repositioning during fighting. Also, having to jump between interact button ("G" for some reason), point and click with the mouse, and other commands during conversation interactions makes it super messy and overcomplicated, especially when you're providing dialogue options for us to choose but there is only one option.  If this game had adopted a simpler movement control from D3, it might be much more playable.Menu layouts is about as bad as when Pokemon Unite was first released, and that's something.  Some of the menu labels aren't obvious about what is encapsulated within the menu, which is a no-no in UX design.In terms of quests, the fact where quest objectives are simply you having to bounce conversation between NPCs that are literally beside each other is really annoying.  All the quests are either "slay X monsters" or "pick up X items" or "talk to X", and this repetition of quest style gets super monotonous really quickly.  BGM is really nice, but dialogue and voice acting is almost as bad as House of the Dead 2.  The high pitched priest during the Prologue is like listening to scratches on a chalkboard.  Further, hearing the NPCs say the one line over and over as you have to run around the town to do the constant supply of "quest errands" is super annoying.  Change it up.  The back story and lore is weak and non-compelling.  It feels like it was a story created by a toddler.Terrain movement is slow and deliberately drags on: although you get a horse, you have to dismount to fight, pick up items, move between terrain, and interact with most things.  Every use action has a cast timer, and using Wayport teleporting or summoning your horse drags on so much it's a deliberate time suck.  This is absolutely unnecessary for an MMO.Questing as a party with friends is painful.  There are many parts of quests that can only be completed solo, and that feels like such a let down which defeats the purpose of partying.  There also doesn't happen to be a way to get to a party member easily, so it's a long and painful trek to get to party members.  From the hours I've played, the dungeons have been super short, and dungeons can only be initiated by a party leader.  This too, was painful.If you're going to do stuff to suck time, make it meaningful.  Doing it with repetitive and super annoying animations (it's not even gameplay at this point) is super painful.  This gameplay may have been acceptable in the early 2000's, but in 2022, it feels extremely dated.Seriously, what your dev team lacks is an interaction designer.  Hire one plz.  It feels like you're trying to use D3's gameplay with MMO style questing and map layouts, and some implementation of dialogue mechanics like Witcher or Fallout.  However, your don't excel in any of those, and this results in a lacklustre game.****EDIT:  After encouragement from my friends and partner, I went and forced myself to play an additional 36 hours to really try to get myself to experience and maybe like the game.  TLDR: I still don't enjoy this game. From what I've experienced and is consistent with what mates have told me, the game's early game drags on painfully (they claim this continues until you hit lvl 50, when everything gets unlocked and partying actually shines.  To give a reference for time, I've been playing for over 36 hours and am only lvl 38.  Not great for casual players.).  In terms of the issue with the left and right clicks for move and attack, I am slowly getting used to it, but am finding that there are times where the attack commands stop and the character awkwardly sits there taking free hits. In terms of the menu and layout, I'm getting used to the layout of where everything is.  I'd argue there are way too many game mechanics, and that overloads new players (which makes up most people as it's a new game).   - The mechanics for engraving and faceting ability stones and why I should use them is still pretty oblivious to me.  Had to go to Youtube to actually figure out what on earth these are for.   - The card mechanics would have been useful, but I'm finding it weird because I may have unlocked a card from my Inventory, but I don't see it in a deck.   - I don't fully understand how stats work here; there seems to be different sets of stats for questing and combat, but they're also influenced by consumables, rewards, level bonuses, card combos, etc (leaving an etc because I don't know if I've missed anything.  That's how many stat influencing mechanics there are.) - Daily rewards are claimed and then added to your mail box first, which you then have to claim from your mail box to then end up in your inventory (if you have several mail rewards, you have to open them manually one at a time), where they can be used.  This is convoluted. - Currency (including spare lives, but excluding Silver coin drops) are put in your inventory first, and then you have to consume them in order for the currency to be added.  These as quest rewards are typically not tradeable. - There are multiple levelling systems in place - combat levels, roster levels, item levels.  I don't see why these are all necessary. - Usage of the GUI isn't so clear.  Had to google search to find out how to leave party, and if I have to do that for something that should be intuitively basic, something is wrong.It just feels a lot of the systems are redundant or convoluted, and could have been optimised or cut and then added later on when the game needs something to revamp it.   - The horse doesn't need a dismount to talk to NPCs or going between maps now, but you do need to dismount if you do any form of interaction, combat (this you have to manually push the dismount button, from my experience you don't dismount automatically), use quest items (again, manual dismount), or cross terrain.There are also useful mechanics but are applied inconsistently, such as the Wayporting.  Alt clicking on the preview map to Wayport is useful, but don't recall it being described.  Really annoying to use the Wayport to reach a location for a quest when the location is on a totally different map that you accessed several maps prior (which happens frequently later on in the story). This is mainly because you can't preview the map to see which location on the map to Wayport to so I'm closest to the objective, so I'm either stuck having to click on portals on the map to go between each map until I find where the objective is, or having to fiddle with really cumbersome dropdown combinations (trying to remember which map is in which area/continent) to find what I'm looking for.  Really wish trade skills were picked up way sooner.  I feel a lot of the potential sites for fishing and hunting were removed.  It would have helped break down the monotony of travelling through the world dramatically.  But most of the previous points still stand.  I'd still suggest you get a UX and interaction designer on your team.  They would've picked up on a lot of these issues early on.  The gameplay feels draining, repetitive and unenjoyable to me.  This game feels surprisingly alienating for an MMO, when the whole point of an MMO is to have friends and a community that you get to play with together, and you don't get to experience this until you go past level 50.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I started playing solely because my friends were interested in this title. Then, I got curious and I jumped into it. And finally, I had to get out of it as soon as possible. Why, you may ask? Don't get me wrong, the game itself has a potential, but I think it got wasted in the end game.First, what I liked about this game the most - the graphics. For a title that uses isometric POV and doesn't necessarily need this kind of polish, the game looks gorgeous and extremely detailed, down to your character's hair or your mount's mane. They didn't need to add physics to most of the clothing, hair, tree's branches, etc... but they did! And that's awesome.Next up: the way your skills and your character are animated and the common feel of those skills. You can actually feel an impact when you use a hard hitting skill. You can see that you leave a trail of destruction while using said skill, not to mention the amount of flying your enemies do when they get hit by you. It's purely satisfying and I can feel my brain doing all those happy hormones stuff that makes me want to play some more.And finally, the amount of customization you have while playing. Well, this part is a double edged sword, really. On one hand, you have a control over your character - you can set up your skill and their passives the way you want to play. That goes to almost all other systems that directly impact your playstyle and stats. However, on the other hand, giving that much freedom almost at the beginning of the game to the player isn't necessarily a good idea. Sure, the game tries to guide you through those systems as you go, but most of those can be skipped during the leveling up process and introduced near max level.Now, to the negatives. Despite being an MMO, this game has almost linear progression, where you are carefully guided by hand from one location to another, If you want to explore the map, you can do it, but there is not much to explore since Lost Ark's zones are tailored to be run through, not explored in the true meaning of the word. Players can drop items that can show you some hidden zones, but those are a joke - small caverns or bridges with almost no ground on either side and couple mobs to kill and a potential upgrade for your character. And that's it. Another thing - character creation. I have nothing against women being bulky warriors or men taking up a job as a sneaky thief. What I don't like is gender locking. I love the female character design, I love womanly curves, but in contrast to my friends, I like to play as a guy. Just because I am a guy myself. In MMOs such as World Of Warcraft, Guild Wars 2, etc, where you can see your character up close it is kind of understandable that you may want to look at your char's butt most of the time, but I don't care about that. And I want to have an option to choose not to have my Shadow Hunter character forced upon me as a female (even if she ends up being somewhat gorgeous). Options, people! Do not take them away.Speaking of options - the ingame settings is quite good, I give it that. But - developers don't give you an option to change the aspect ratio to completely mach your screen's resolution. Right now it is locked to 16:9, whereas my monitor's aspect ratio is 16:10. The resolution is the right one (1920x1200), but it would be more enjoyable to play without having two black bars at the bottom and top of my screen.Going back to the game itself. It is not very fun experience after a while and it becomes monotonous. After a prologue, you are sent into the world and you jump from one quest hub to another further into the zones available. And almost all of the quests I've experienced have the same collective pattern: talk to X number of NPCs, go kill Y number of mobs, gather Z number of resources, go talk some more. Are you done here? Then move along. You SOMETIMES get an additional quest to go into a dungeon or a training quest to learn about yet another system introduced to the game. But besides those two, quests are basically the same.Finally, the endgame. If I were to sum it up using one word, it would: grindfest. If you want to achieve anything meaningful, you have to prepare yourself for what is basically another job. I stopped playing WoW for the same reason - it didn't feel as a game I an enjoy after a stressfull day at work. It's another couple hours of a grinding job after I come home from my regular work. It is fun to do some activities in this game once. But on a daily basis, without any real alternatives? No, thank you.You can skip a grinding process, of course. But it will cost you. This game is not a Pay 2 Win. It's Pay 2 Progress. If you are into this kind of games - by all means, enjoy it. Because there is content to enjoy. It will just get repetitive really fast, really soon. And those of you who want to have their minds intact - avoid.So, to end my review, I won't give this title a 0/10. Because it deserves more. I give it a "Press G to continue" / 10.

_childDocuments_.review: Update November 2023: Definitely do not get it. The Quality of Life changes are drawing out the playtime, but make no improvements to terrible issues like the honing system bring a timesink, the pay-to-win honing system allowing end-game access only to whales and the abysmal treatment of old content. If you missed it the first time it was "current content", you often cannot complete it (example: old islands require a minimum amount of players to finish. There are no players interested in old content any more, so you can spend weeks or months trying to complete. The drop chance for content has not been adjusted, so you're still stuck on a 1% chance to gain what you went there for). New classes are added regularily, combined with quick advance events. This means that existing players progress to the current endgame with stored materials, new players are stuck without others in former endgame raids. Exactly the grind you'd expect from a Korean MMO, but exceptionally badly maintained. Stay away. Far, far away. Don't get it yet (February 2022). At the moment, the "new"ness of the game lead to overpopulated servers. As always, this means that it's impossible to log in after work - queues that take hours at best or a straight kick from the login menu. This experience is garnished with a rather resource hogging "Easy Anti-Cheat" and load times that are abysmal. On the upside, the game does play like a weird MMO version of Diablo. The enemies respawn quickly and are spaced out (like an MMO). The playstyle depends on pressing the right buttons at the right time. Unlike most MMOs there are no healer classes, more typical for a eastern MMO you get to use super-armour and staggers to beat groups. Some classes are more tricky than others - my experience is limited to the 6 character slots, and from those it doesn't appear that there are massive power imbalances in PvE (again: February 2022). The story is probably okay, the side quests are filler fluff to make sure you get to kill at least three groups in one direction, there is a stupid amount of running around. I didn't get far enough to experience the crafting and stronghold and boat system - guildies tell me those are interesting, but the evening primetime hours are unaccessible. Overall: Diablo fans might like it, it's not a typical MMO (I did _not_ enjoy the weird quest system), the masses of enemies you occasionally get to AoE are right fun and it's a massive disappointment due to lack of playability.

_childDocuments_.review: Negatives:If you're a solo player then don't be fooled, this is not a game for you outside of the story.  No matter how generous the devs are with freebie materials (and they are generous) the RNG for upgrading gear honing system farming will burn you out if you want to enter raids. The reason being the only way to get into groups which don't have bots are in the lobby and they will be asking you for a ridiculously over the top item level requirement unless you are a support class.The only other way to get in would be to join a guild but then you wouldn't really be a solo player then.What is this 0.5 to 2 second delay on clicking everything from "Accept" to simply loading up achievements. I have never encountered a game with such a weird loading issue (and no it's not my comp because i can play Cyberpunk 2077 just fine). Almost every click makes another hair on my face go grey.Maintenance Days:Why oh WHY do they have to touch inventory items and put them into Universal Storage for you to collect? This is nonsensical and again I have never seen this in any other game I have played.Recent server mergers retroactively reduced my Card Cap for some reason. When looting it hit cap at 260/260 from the Universal Storage but 28 more cards are sitting in limbo being unable to be retrieved which were saved in the card roster, NOT in my bags or personal storage.Stronghold: Although it can provide you with buffs it just feels like unnecessary fluff they could've just given your character in other ways. If you're not into stickers or posing you won't want this...but it's required for reducing your material costs which I find a bit of a slight of hand cheap trick.It's a terrible shame that what felt like a REALLY fun game to start with at launch now feels like a second job to pay off a second mortgage. Una's Dailies, Shipping and Island Co-op, Chaos dungeons, Abyss dungeons, Guardian Raids all get stale very quick. I seriously doubt these recent server mergers will help anything much apart from more lag.Positives: Artistry, animation, special effects, environmental set-pieces, music, move sets, sub-classes, being able to mass save preset set-ups of abilities, gear and cards, ALL GREAT!

_childDocuments_.review: While Lost Ark can be said to have some of the most frustrating endgame paywalls I've ever seen, I personally don't believe it detracts too heavily from the experience of the game. Over three weeks I've consistently come back every night to play because its just that damn good. Mechanics, gameplay loops, boss fight progression, story, collectables, dailies, weeklies, islands, graphic and animation fluidity. Each of these as a separate element within the game are honestly amazing, up until end game content it genuinely feels like it adds something to your character and to your experience, improving your dps or gaining access to significant rewards. Together, they create an activity rich game where I sometimes get lost as to what I need to do next to improve my stats or abilities etc. End game is a different matter, the rewards feel weaker, very suddenly, T3 resources become less impactful forcing you into two options;            make an alt and grind upto T3 again             pay thousands of dollars to progress minimallyI'm picking the alt route, alot of other people quit at that choice, but I feel like there's alot more to the game I've yet to experience and I'm happy to plug in another 100 hours to get to that point. I will say, the game is built so that the highest tier content will almost always only be available to the people who put in ridiculous amounts of grinding or to those who can spend thousands on the game, I don't think that will change, however there is enough already there to do that missing out on that top-end content for a couple patches until catchup mechanics are introduced doesn't phase me, im happy to take it slow. Lost Ark will be one of your favourite games until T3, I recommend playing it until then and make a choice at that point for if you want to grind up to end game content or wait until those catch-up mechanics are introduced. Even though I feel left behind to some extent, i've really enjoyed this game and i'm excited to get to that content one day.
