_childDocuments_.review: While this game isn't terrible, an overwhelming hype train and huge wave of initial positive reviews has tainted its' appeal to me. For every time I try to defend its' mechanics and story, I lose confidence in my own argument. Lost Ark is a watered down MMO which mainly appeals to new players of the genre. For anyone familiar with MMOs, unlike a game like FFXIV, Lost Ark's story is incredibly shallow. The characters are forgettable and the side content is a distraction from the poor writing and direction. It executes the ideas it takes from other MMOs badly; I have found myself skipping most of the dialogue having failed trying to invest into the story. Any reviewer that supports the direction of the main arc has not played a good MMO. The gameplay so far feels brainless. Squishy, uninteresting targets run across your screen and a combination of 1 or 2 buttons is usually enough to wipe an entire wave of these minions. Its' appeal comes from free-to-play Andy's who are unfamiliar with other games and find comfort in mindlessly mashing their keyboards. The lack of a level-scaling system means that playing with friends is obsolete, essentially transforming Lost Ark into a solo experience. The dungeons have all lacked any innovation and feel like copies of each other. I have quickly lost all interest in the story and the gameplay. So what does Lost Ark offer? For its' shortcomings in other areas, it sure looks pretty. The graphics are beautiful and coupled with mediocre at best music, makes for good eye candy. The graphics can't be faulted; The performance on the other hand needs polishing. Playing this game on a RTX 3070, Ryzen 5 3600 and 16GB 3000MHz Memory, I am encountering stuttering issues. Note that this issue isn't apparent in any of my friends' games who I have asked. Whether this is a specific issue with my combination of components, or backend issues with their engine, I am unsatisfied with this performance from a game heralded as a game changer. Although it won't solely deter me from playing, alongside all the other faults, the performance is a big fudge you for the consumer.I will continue to give this game another opportunity and will update this review if appropriate. For now though, unless you are completely new to the genre and ignorant of other MMOs, I would advise you lower your expectations and follow reason rather than the torrential train of hype that has followed this game from pre-release.

_childDocuments_.review: Personally for me, these are just intial thoughts of my brief playthrough. I found these issues that I just couldn't ignore. I just couldn't get past some issues which made me not want to even start the game up again to play more.I found the initial story to be so shallow. I found the intro to the game just felt so rushed, that it didn't really take the time to explain how you got there in the first place. Then throws you into the world on a ship, with no knowledge of why you are there, or even who these people are in the first place. The questing and dialogue structure to the game feels extremely outdated. I know that the game is 3 years old now at this point, but I felt like these issues were very much more outdated by at least 7+ years. It's very bare-bones in this regard.Combat is the shining star here for sure. It's fast paced, style of Diablo gameplay. I think the game would be a massive flop without it. Very flashy and unique style of animations.Gender locked classes are here also. It was frustrating that I couldn't make a male assassin. So went with Male deadeye instead. Character customization was serviceable. Nothing great. Struggled to make a character that I really loved.Everyone's tastes are different and their enjoyment of different parts of games, but MMO's have been all about "my character" and being immersed in the world and characters around me. Without it, I would just be playing a grind fest on autopilot. I just didn't care about anyone I met in the game. Which killed any excitement I had for the launch. Maybe my feelings would change with progressing more, but that initial impression was a very flat and uninspiring one.The game is worth at least trying out. It's free to play. So you have nothing to lose.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a very expensive Tax in the form of Pheons (One of the dozens of currencies). You need Pheon to buy every single item in the Auction House. The only way to get Pheon is to buy it from people that spend money on the game, and its not cheap. For every transaction that occurs on the AH, someone has to have spend money in the game. A single relic accessory is more than $5 worth of Pheons. You need 5 for each character.I'm not gonna even talk about Ability Stones, a pure RNG item that costs Pheon and is mandatory for an endgame build, with the potential of costing hundreds of dollars worth of Pheons to get what you need.All of this for a single character. In this game, you NEED alts, its not an option. The only way of making consistent gold is to do the weekly raids, which you can do only 3 times max per character, if your character is high level enough.This creates an infinity loop that only benefits the greedy devs/publisher:Need gold to play > Need alts to farm gold > Need to build alt to be able to do raids > Dont have pheon to build alt > Need gold to buy pheon. Repeat. Unless you buy Pheons with money.The only fun part of this game was the early and mid game back when it launched when everyone was progressing through the game together, not knowing what waited everyone down the road. This part of the game is now dead. And the endgame only exists to bleed you dry.And all of this is only the worst of the worst. Theres plenty more. Dont waste you time like I did.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Salad of easter mmo cool features with no cohesion. Nonsensical , stock bland lore. Throws rewards at you for basically breathing. I am a fan of Diablo, PoE , Last Epoch , etc. First thing I don't like about the game is the zones feel like rails, barely any open space. Maps feel really small.Also there are too many currencies and system that work in parallel instead of building on top of each other. Too much noise everywhere. you get FOMO from hell as soon as you are out of what they call tutorial. All sorts of collections, that give stats. So many directions to progress in but no clear way on how to progress there. It just feels like a salad of features from eastern games.Story is so generic and lacking, might as well have been written by AI. I have no idea why this game was so acclaimed. And here I am not talking about PVE campaign , an MMO does not need that to be good. But there needs to be a story , lore that "explains" in fiction the mechanics of the game. But then what fiction can you explain when most of the time it clearly states that the mechanic is to collect stuff for the sake of collecting stuff , and get stats for it. 0 cohesion between features , and 0 relationship to lore , game setting or anything else.I was expecting the world to be more alive , with NPC's having more AI behind them. There is a disconnect between lore and graphics, character models, mobs. you could take the same story and put it in Scifi setting.Where the game excels is combat. It is awesome for this type of game. I will give it that , best out of all games mentioned above. And the verticality of the world is at times impressive.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most shallow ARPGs I've ever played. The combat completely misses out on the point of ARPG-style skills, opting instead for an excessive number of generic attack skills all set up with arbitrary cooldowns to juggle for no added benefit. There's a mana bar, but I can't fathom what it would ever be used for as you regen faster than your skill cooldowns. I'll admit it might work different for another class, or perhaps become relevant after leveling up some more and skills might get more expensive... but I can't see how that would make it any better.It's clearly designed to waste your time like the most grindy of MMOs, where every quest to slay X monster is interspersed with talking to several different NPCs at separate locations, every map-traversal animation is long for no reason, and cutscenes/dialogs/menu animations have a lot of padding.Beyond the feel of the gameplay, it's really upsetting to see two different instances of Class selections using the same name, just being split by gender. When "Martial Artist (Male)" and "Martial Artist (Female)" are two separate classes entirely for no reason, it's pretty annoying. Even discounting the gender politics of it, why are they even the same name if they're entirely different classes?I will say I did enjoy the Character creation screen. They clearly put a decent amount of effort into it. The voice acting is a decent display of talent, too (although I question some of the decisions the Director made on certain lines' tone and pacing).Overall, I am immensely unimpressed, and do not recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I will preface this by saying I have a lot of fun in Lost Ark, as indicated by 1,000+ hours played on Steam. I am a Day 1 F2P player with 6 characters in various progressions from mid to endgame. But I just honestly cannot recommend this game to any new players at the game’s current state. I am a generally patient gamer when it comes to gaming, as I enjoy game activities such as exploration and collectibles. Lost Ark has both, and even more to offer through its rich contents (not counting the obvious raids and PVP). Extreme steep vertical progression aside, the game offers a lot of horizontal progression that can boost playing experience of your subsequent characters’ progression. So what went wrong?The problem is the myriads of potential game breaking issues since the launch day are still present, and have gotten worse. To summarize: -Bot armies are still running rampant and out of control-Gold selling ads are still spamming in zone chat, or even through in-game mail system-RMT’ers (Real money trading) are not punished and in Forum Community Manager’s own words, they are either “temporarily or permanently banned”-In-game currency exchange rate for gold to in-game shop currency ratio is staggeringly absurd (Gold to Blue Crystals)-Game’s economy is in shambles -The insane-ridiculous queues of up to 15K and queue time of up to 2 hours to get through -Queue is no longer exclusive to early mornings and late evenings (NA West servers), queues of up to 4K are seen from noon to 5-6PM; basically queue for the entire day…and that’s just the major issues without accounting for other minor ones.What really broke the camel's back is the login queues. It doesn't matter what time you play, whether it's early morning, noon, afternoon, late evening or nighttime, you are greeted with a queue, and it ranges from 1k to 15k. Once you get through the queue of 1-2 hours, your motivation or urge to play are all but vanished. This is just another sad case of a promising KMMORPG that gets derailed by the same problems that have always plagued other KMMORPG games in NA/EU regions. Can’t help but think Lost Ark is doomed to repeat the cycle. A real shame.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED REVIEW BELOW - 11/2/22Overrated copium. Game is fun and extremely polished, but gear progression is typical of K-MMOs. If you value your time, go play something else. The fanboys will scream "sunk cost fallacy" for LA, while other games like FFXIV or even WoW reward you for your time spent, over your money. Went into this game expecting a loot-grind, mob slaughtering addiction, instead you get boring story, boring fetch quest and RNG gates to do raids. No mob killing (best part of the game is mobbing.) It's a shame, but this is not the MMO that people have been waiting years to sink their life into. Also, goodluck past Tier 2-3, all you visa warriors :)----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Updating my review after giving it another chance. I hit iLevel 1410 so I can say I've done most things. Completed all the continents and even finished the story. Lost ark is really fun in categories it shines, like Raids and Dungeons. It's very fun trying to learn the boss mechanics and the limitations/damage windows of your class. The combat is top tier and very addicting, but in order to have fun and play the content that is worth your time, you have to dedicate a lot of it to boring and mindless timesinks. Anyone who tells you that Makoko hunting or Island completion is fun, is seriously huffing their own farts through a latex bodysuit. This ♥♥♥♥ is so mundane and boring. Half the islands require you to have some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ completed through some random side quest you forgot about 5 continents ago to access the loot/seeds that you need to progress your iLevel to see the cool end-game content. Una's Dailies and Weeklies are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ terrible. They involve you running around the entire world, completing useless side quest that take like 2 minutes to finish. but 15mins to get to. Wouldn't be so bad if you could track them and teleport to the Triports nearby, but you either need Bifrost slots (credit card) or a really fast ship to get to the areas. You are going to spend a lot of your freetime traveling to pickup boring side quest with little to no reward. They seriously need to rework Una's quest and create a proper Daily/Weekly timesink that doesn't suck your amount of ♥♥♥♥♥ out you. Luckily they buffed the rates at which gear hits to +15 so it's not that bad reaching 1350+ but onwards it's very typical of Korean "♥♥♥♥ you give us money to keep playing" trope that plagues the Korean MMO industry. Even when you DO spend an absorbent amount of money on the game, you aren't rewarded. This game is designed to make you feel like 250$ is nothing in the grand scheme of things. If you want to stay current or ahead of the curve, you will need to fork out hundreds of $$$ a month. You're better off subscribing to a subscription based MMORPG that actually values it's playerbase over exploiting them and their FOMO attitudes. TL;DR - Lost ark gameplay is fun if you can stomach spending $$$ top dollars to skip the meticulously designed soul sucking side content. _childDocuments_.review: In essence, this is wholeheartedly a mobile game in disguise as an MMO, it lacks any real depth, and seems to be in the middle of ARPG, and MMO, but realistically with the gameplay of neither.  The combat seems to play similar to that of Tera, at least, the many years ago I played it, its very much aoe farming with some bosses thrown in, the bulk of your skills are aoe, and give you a sheer feeling of unearned power from the get-go, you do not start as a waif with little ability, you can one hit aoe kill entire groups from the start, including trained, armed and armoured soldiers very shortly after.  It doesnt have the general stat and precision of most ARPGs, for instance Grim Dawn, PoE or Diablo, and feels very much that you just throw out skills, wait for cooldown, move on (the waiting being colloquial most of the time).The game also feels plagued with cut content, areas of zones that dont need to be visited, more enemies and highly populated enemy areas than ever needed, the respawn rate is *fast*, with named mini boss mobs that are never required to kill, or in some cases, entire sections of the map avoided before moving on, if there was content here, its gone, and we're being pushed to get to the "endgame" as quickly as possible via few quests and story per zone at times, some of which just require back and forth talking, picking up objects, getting an overdose of XP doing so, mobs themselves fundamentally don't give any exp at all.There are also a lot of currencies, premium items, caps per day, and such, all mobile game stuff in MMO format, not that daily quests aernt a thing in other places, but the side games, resource gathering, NPC rapport gain, is either capped per day, or in some cases, paywall'd easier methods, gathering tools, for instance, will slowly break, and their max durability will lower permanently until repaired via cash shop items, similarly, teleporting to zones is an expensive ordeal, especially backtracking to very old areas, without special items that reduce that to zero, from endgame farming or cash shop.There are also many currencies, mixed with RNG late game minor boost stones and other nick nacks, that have a chance to permanently fail, giving further busywork, not much of it explained all that well ingame, which is tiresome and off-putting.Some of the translation and localisation is a little off, and good number of the voice actors used are fairly poor quality, showing little to no emotion, or quite frankly sounding like young californians that havent had any adversity in their life (and just sound very out of place), soldiers dont sound grizzled or professional, a lot of them sound like wimps, with one instance being a gate guard that sounded like he'd never spoken to a real human being in their life, there's also the frankly overly common issue of characters grunting and moaning, gasping and spluttering, which is prominent in Asian media, but sounds very off in localisation... more so when combat hasnt even started yet and they sound like they've run a mile in lead armour, and are still running while talking.  Voice acting should never be this weak and emotionless, even the original Resident Evil did it better and that was pure unadulterated cheese.Negatives aside the game does have a lot to *do* but its all generally busywork to keep you in the game, and to give you an eventual time and sunk cost feeling, the quality of the zone designs, assets created/used are fairly high quality, character models aernt bad, while not always an art style I personally enjoy, I can see the merits.I've up til now poked my head into a fair bit of the content, none of which really drags me in, if anything its making me want to go play an *actual* RPG, or an *actual* ARPG, not a mobile game masquerading as a MMO-ARPG.  If you want either of these, I suggest playing something entirely different.  While this game has some good set pieces, and if you want to feel overpowered, you will, I wouldnt play this enough for time or the sunk cost fallacy to kick in.Avoid this, there are better things to do.

_childDocuments_.review: 👎 Lost Ark, in which your character carries out a series of  whose sole purpose is to move you from map to map,  the repetitiveness causing a loss of interest and inability to follow what you're doing any longer.  And this is the main storyline, it's like 90% "go and get me a pumpkin", you get the pumpkin, "OK now I will tell you the secrets you need to know."  Two minutes later, "Go and talk to this person standing next to me and ask him a question." So you go and talk to the person standing next to the quest giver, ask the question, get the answer, and go back.  That's it, that's what the quests feel like, mostly filler, punctuated by occasional ones related to "Lost Ark".  👎 And it's not even like there's any motivation to go through the quests for its rewards.  The .  I don't even mean in an entitled, choosing beggars sense.  I mean just objectively, stats wise, the rewards are barely there. The game is really stingy with giving better drops than current gear.  There's no point in trying to grind either, the mob kills give just a few XP, as compared to quests.  So you're pretty much forced to quest and still get nothing worthwhile out of it. 👍 In contrast the abysmal progression and storyline, the  is actually a joy, it's really fun.  All the classes feel powerful and the battle effects are elaborate.  👍 And what's more, the  are also quite beautiful.  It's richly detailed while being easy on the eyes, it's fun to run around.  👎 Sadly it's the quest progression that brings it down and makes the beautiful lands feel dull, lifeless and empty. Even worse is the overwhelming number of  for different purposes.  It's all introduced early on, when you have none of it, and is of no real use.  👍 The  is decent too, there's a good variety of configurations and you can spend a decent amount of time in the character creator.  The male-classes are decently designed, though the female-classes, who are wearing Traditional Female Armor™️, look awkward running around in high heels on rough terrain. 👎 I went into the in-game shop to see what they had to purchase... and it's just awful.  The  are out of touch with the rest of the in-game world and feel totally out of place.  I can understand the occasional swimwear or jokey skewer-sword, but even their serious stuff looks designed for dolls, just odd.  It's like they're made for collectors but not people interested in the role playing aspect of the game.  And not only that, they're really expensive too.  And they bind to a single character only!  Not just costumes but many rewards bind to just one character.  Which kills any motivation.  👎 The  are pretty dead, there's nobody queuing for it, so you have to solo it.  It's doable, just not that fun especially long dungeons.  I believe everyone is at the end game.  👎 The game is sorely lacking in .  At some point it starts getting more and more crowded, and the only option is to use Alt+X to hide certain UI elements. It's possible to go fully immersive if you press Alt+X 3 times I believe, but the moment you interact with something, you get all the screen clutter again, it resets. I'm convinced that there were two separate teams at work on this project.  The one that did the combat, the artwork, and character designs.  And the one that did the story, quests, costumes, cosmetics shop.  The second team's work felt out of touch with the first team's work.  I found myself actually nodding off while playing or going through some of the tedious dialogue.  I might give it another shot anyway to be fair to it and revisit the gorgeous locales, but after 30 hours on my first try, I found myself bored with no motivation to continue or recommend this to anyone.2022-09-17: Just tried again and I actually, involuntarily, fell asleep at my desk.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played as a casual since it's NA launch and never before and I've enjoyed the game. My only complaint is the gender locked classes. And thats just personal preference cuz I like to put myself into the game and pretend its me in some alternate universe lol. Heres a small list of things others may or may not like about the game.1. For those new to it, the first continent you start out on is rather generic, the game gets much better as you explore it and opens up to a massive world you can sail around and explore to your hearts content.2. Only the 1st line of quest dialogue is spoken for some reason, which can be off putting and make you just mash G through typical quests. This doesn't bug me as much cuz I just mash G through them anyways unless its a main story quest. And typically have always mashed through the side quests of any MMO anyways.3. Housing has timers on things you build, which means slow progress on building a home for yourself. This annoys me, but it's not a deal breaker, it's akin to Warframe if you've ever played that.4. Endgame is heavily RNG based, as in you need luck on your side at times to progress your character to the next tier in order to unlock more content. I don't mind this since I just enjoy the journey, but for those focusing solely on endgame and rushing to it and min maxers you are very likely ganna just get annoyed. 5. PvP is standardized and fair, everyone has equal footing and it is not P2W at all. PvE has P2W features in that a player with $$$ can get to endgame faster than you but in no way does a player who pays ever have more power than a character just casually played who has obtained the same level of power through playing the game. So in essence, paying only for convenience sake to get something faster. To me it makes no sense to pay to do this anyways.6. Make sure friends are ON your server IN your region, else your ganna have a bad time. Friends need to be on the same server to play together, there are no megaservers here like ESO or some other games.7. The story is semi generic, I would say its your typical light vs dark story. What makes it cool is the feeling of exploration and how each zone has its own mini stories to follow that typically unfold into really cool climactic dungeons and scenarios. This helps the main story not feel so cut and dry since they usually all involve finding Lost Arks which tie back into the main story.8. As far as I am aware, Groups are 4 player max, with Raids being 8 player max...Unsure if that gets higher or not after some point. All basic dungeons can be done solo or with friends or through matchmaking, they scale accordingly.The launch of this game was a tad wonky, most of these negative reviews are cuz of launch, or just people who really don't have a clue how MMO's work and expected this to be straight up Diablo or something. Give the game a chance if you are unsure, I went into it thinking I wouldn't enjoy it anywhere near as much as I actually have, give it time to pick up the pace, the game has a slow burn sort of start to it. But most of all, just focus on having fun and enjoying the journey imho, games are meant to be fun anyways! <3

_childDocuments_.review: Technical problems and an awful leveling process. Disappointing compared to advertising.The game is forcefully zoomed in to an uncomfortable degree. When using range attacks your targets often are past the monitor's edge and when traveling or just trying to get the hang of the surrounding you're forced to rely on the minimaps. There is an option to force 21:9 resolution but it looks pixelated and creates big black bars.The leveling process lacks most of the features the game is praised for and lasts too much. Boring process of moving from one NPC to another sometimes slaying a few enemies on the way. So what if you change territories, talk to different people, etc, if everything is identical anyway? This feels like the beginning of the century, not a relatively fresh game.The combat lacks any weight to it. All quests are slow, focused on slowly walking or just slightly faster riding from one mark on the map to another and clicking G. The combat lacks momentum, skills mostly differ from each other by animations and hitboxes, and the dodging ability has a long cooldown. Early game is so painfully easy, the combat is just clicking buttons till everything dies to your boring simple-minded DPS skills. Running hard mode dungeons though, can be described as boring dance when you walk between enemies releasing simple-minded DPS skills when they can't hit or surround you. There are many better isometric action MMORPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: Devs constantly mess things up. Most recently they just gave placers a highly sought after currency by mistake and then removed it from them.If you're new to the game or any  content that's released for that matter, you're effed. Your play options are Raids with super intense mechanics that require practice to learn and outside the first week of release of new content no one is going to have the patience to let you learn. So your only option is to pay other players for buses. The game didn't release all available classes. So the class I wanted to play isn't getting released until next month - a year after the game started. I'll then have to play catch up and spend a few hundred thousand gold to get caught up if I want to play the class I wanted.Speaking of gold...inflation way out paces the capacity to obtain gold. Your options are to either buy it with real money or spend an unhealthy amount of time on alts doing raids. But this second point might not even be an option for you if you're new to the content (refer to paragraph above). Each raid can give you anywhere from 2-4k gold per character. On top of that you can do crafting that might net you about 10k a week. Accessories run $50k -$100k each, engraving books cost about $15k x 20 books x 2 engraving slots. Ability stones that you have to keep purchasing again and again due to horrible success chances cost 500-1000 gold each x about an additional 1000 gold in pheons (see next paragraph about that terrible system).The game has this pheon system that is a currency you have to spend on top of gold for gear you want to buy out of the AH. You obtain pheons by either spending real life money or spending an extra 3,000 gold to purchase the necessary amount of pheons on top of the insane price of what's posted on the AH. The chances of getting the right gear with the right stats is well below less than 1%. I have been playing this game every day for a year and I think ONCE out of 6 character running dungeons every day have I gotten a piece of gear with the right stats.To level your gear, there is a honing system that drops down to 3% success starting out. Each attempt gives you a little over 2% towards a pity hone so you have to go through about 50 attempts to get a pity upgrade. Each attempt 300 gold, costs silver, costs shards, costs leapstones, cost stones, and costs infusion stones. Five currencies to do one function...all come with gold costs except for the silver. Refer to paragraph above about how it sucks getting gold and the game's inflation.They don't accurately translate tooltips or important information like...expiration dates on power passes. So you might be saving a power pass for an upcoming class only to find out it expires shortly before your class is released. But it was your fault for not finding the information buried somewhere in a bulletin they had posted months prior.

_childDocuments_.review: Latest update: Well the shine has worn off and I can conclude with certainty that the game is a total missed opportunity. Great mechanics and it's fun to play. But everything is time gated and gate kept. The billion different currencies ruin the rest of the fun.  It's so unfortunate.  I'd pull so much from this game to make a great one, that's the bittersweet aspect of it all. But I have no desire to play it because of time gating and P2W plus all the currencies to hide that P2W.  Pointless to play without paying way more than you should for a game. But even if you're rich, it's time gated, which ruins fun for a day off you have where you want to binge play. Can't do it. Well you can, but it's so diminished returns it's pointless. So the game basically forces the schedule it wants you to keep with it. Screw that.  Unplayable.=======================================================================Older updater: changed to recommended because I keep playing it. Also, while I don't like the pay structure, I decided it is not pay to win because if you do not have the skill to escape raid killing instant abilities, it doesn't matter how much gear you have paid for. You will instantly die and not be able to see endgame content.A LOT of bad to this game, but good in gameplay.Lost Ark proves that the MMO community is alive and well -- it's just companies that have been failing them. Huge player numbers on day one here.  A bit of bloat in millions of different kinds of currencies and inventory management being a lost cause.  The combat is the best feeling combat I've ever experienced in not only an ARPG, but any game. However, there are a lot of problems. One of my biggest gripes is the constant dialogue windows for every quest. Not just one NPC, you normally will be clicking through pages upon pages of meaningless drivel to only be directed to another NPC where you do the same. You repeat this for like 7 NPCs at which point you are told to "kill 10 boars" or whatever. The boars are always going to be about 10 feet away, and grouped together in 5 packs. You are done with the quest in about 45 seconds. At which point you repeat the process of NPC dialogue spam. You literally spend more time trying to click dialogue spam away than you do playing the game while leveling, imo.You can't insta-click the dialogue windows to move to the next either. It takes like a second for each window.  Thousands upon thousands of these. Unskippable animations between them. I just want it to end. Then there is the P2W aspects.  Any game that is a shared online experience has a level of status/competition. No one pays someone to level their character in a single player game, for instance. Anyone denying that there is competition in MMO pve games is either and idiot or lying to protect their P2W preferred model.  Everything is locked behind daily caps. So if you are a player that only has time to play ALOT during a weekend or something, this can't be done by you. Skip it. You are capped in a day.  You can't catch up in bursts.  So it's more like a phone game than a regular PC MMO.  It reaks of phone game.Paying for all this, however, is what the company wants.  It's P2W.  Not the worst I've seen but far from the least P2W.  If you are not opening up your wallet big time, there is no way to truly be competitive. Companies like this need to start introducing systems where you pay for one license per month and get everything offered on their cash shop. And if you don't want to pay for that per month, then you can buy things al a carte.  They need to start capping what you can achieve with spending hundreds of dollars a month, and make that price about $15. Anything more than that is greed, and these companies need to be called out on it. They are ruining what could be great games because of their greed. It just sucks that there are all these negatives because without them, this would be one of the best games I've ever played.  It's so bittersweet.  The game "plays" very well, especially when you can get past the leveling up process and the blasted quest dialogue spam.Then there are the menus. What a cluttered mess. Not one menu UI looks like another.  It's all different. No uniformity. It's like a maze trying to navigate them, which you are doing ALL the time.  The initial load time is like 5 minutes because of its anti cheat engine. Very frustrating if you're just logging in to send your sailors on a mission. Speaking of that, loading anything takes a few extra seconds than it should, even on low settings (my computer handles ultra high just fine after loading) Load times are aggravating, to say the least.updated 2/17: I like to do gathering professions in games, just roam around and gather things. Well it's gated here. Only so much you can do until you need to buy more "energy" to gather plants, and chop down trees. _childDocuments_.review: My original review was naive. In fact, don't believe anyone's opinion on this game unless they've at least made it to Tier 2 or have approx.150-200 hours in-game. Otherwise, they don't know the game at all. Anyhow, this is a mess, but it's likely the most informative review you'll currently find on  (NA/EU).Now, as other reviewers have said before me, this game is fun and addictive. It looks great, plays great, boy... It's great, huh? However, since pre-release, it's been annoyingly frustrating. I play on Galatur and the server was shut down for four hours because of Asmongold announcing the server on his live stream. That costed me -- a founder (silver) -- game time. I proceeded to make an alt on Regulus while the server was down. I created a bard. I bought the bard skins and I also bought a pet and mount for the character. I figured I could transfer the character to Galatur or use my Royal Crystals left over for my character on Galatur, etc. You know, as if that  currency was account wide, not server or character bound.  Secondly, there was a poor launch. On top of that, I purchased a Vanquisher pack for the cosmetic items. This was after I learned guild mates had purchased multiple Founder's packs. **** me, huh? I figured the extra blue crystals would help me along.  To further add to the frustration, when they released free Explorer packs to those affected by Main Story Progression Loss on Galatur, I never received one. It was released on 02/17/2022, mind you. As for the additional Founder's pack I was granted... It's continued to sit in my inventory. What good does it do me to use it? Wow... A duplicate title and different colored cat. That'll juice me up, huh? Now, for my real complaints... The game has had gold farmers/spammers since shortly after launch. They have ruined the currency conversion, the market, and they're even getting accounts banned by refunding items sold on the auction house, etc. There are several time-gated events and everything has an invisible paywall/grind that you don't notice until post-Tier 1. It becomes worse in Tier 2 and Tier 3. Part of this is to stall players because they don't have any actual endgame content. Currently (and this is subject to change soon) there's no ranked pvp, gvg/gve, etc. There are only a handful of ways to acquire honing materials and believe me, you'll spend all your time doing it each day. Moreover, there are hardly any cosmetics for the game right now. As for pvp, what's the point? Former RU/Korean players dominate and the matchmaking is terrible... Three Deathblades? Come on. No, seriously, COME. THE. HYUCK. ON. M8.If you've ever played Black Desert Online (BDO), you'll find this game more forgiving, only because it doesn't roll back your gear or permanently break it. That's it. Everything else feels like a cheap mobile P2W MMO. So, have fun. That's what gamers like these days, right? Right. Why? Because you (like me) continue to be buy them... To buy from their in-game shops, their dlcs, their this and that and that and this... I know... I know, believe me.Lastly, The game also suffers from stabilization, optimization, and general performance issues, either affecting the hardware or server connection. That's with medium graphical settings and performance preferred over quality.  If you know, you know... In pre-release, I never disconnected or had stuttering issues... Fast forward one month later and 240 hours of game time, and this is no longer the case. This is what your time will look like:-- Level 1-50: EZ mode. Seriously, I miss these days. PS: You can use two powerpasses to skip this for alts or transfer knowledge and spend gold to create alts at higher gear score levels. Js.Everything after Level 50:For most of this, you'll do the story quests. You'll do side quests. You'll then do all the islands for honing materials. Then... You'll do Steps 1-10 for each Tier (3) ad infinitum. Remember, skip all dialogue and cutscenes. Don't waste your time. It's all contrived.1. Login rewards. Address any stronghold updates. Start new missions/research. Then support any guild research. Donate to your guild as well. Manage the guild if you're a guild owner/deputy/officer and set weekly tasks, etc.. 2. Do your daily Una Tasks (3) and weekly Una Tasks (3). If you have enough Una Tokens, redeem them. Use them to buy gold. 3. Grind Chaos Dungeons. Spend currency from Chaos Dungeons to buy more honing materials. Buy the jewelry too, break it all for the honing materials. Then go to guild shop and buy all honing materials with Bloodstones. Buy all honing materials from Trade Merchants with pirate coins while you're at it.4. Do Guardian Raids, Abyssal Dungeons, Tower, Cube, and Boss Rush. The last two only if you have tickets. 5. Do Events. From Events, sell items on the market for gold. Perhaps bid on the maps with gold. Make gold back by doing the maps with others (who also have maps), then sell items you gained for gold.6. Work on rapport, server level, and combat level. Also, farm anything else you can for gold or materials.7. Play PVP to reach "Tier 1" which is useless btw. You do this to complete certain weekly challenges for leapstones. This is what the average player does. 8. Work on collectibles so you can get more gold. Therefore, collect Mokoko seeds, Island Souls, Masterpieces, etc. Turn them in for their rewards. 9. Work on Trade Skills. Enhance gems, enhance ability stones, enhance enhancements, enhance cards, enhance everything.10. Now take everything you've collected, spent currencies on, etc. to hone your gear. Use the books you bought with crystals or gold, likewise with the Breath bs and other "chance enhancers". Congratulations, all the materials you've accumulated for the day, just went down the drain. Now wait for tomorrow to do all the boring crap again. Also, wait until the next reset to buy from vendors again (because you can only buy a select amount for a specific duration) and until then, repeat Steps 1-10 with alts. After doing all the above, you'll have spent every day for a month wasting your life in the hopes of EVENTUALLY reaching the next Tier list only to find that there's nothing waiting for you. Lastly, and this is only if you pvp, you'll want to flesh out your Book of Coordination and assign skill points and skills based on a Meta (which is absolute bs btw) and get stomped. Revise the Book of Coordination to fit your own playstyle. Finally, you've succeeded at winning pvp matches. Congratulations, you've learned that streamers are   pvp islands are worthless. If you're reported for pvping there too frequently, you'll likely be banned. Yeah... Makes sense, right? I mean, they're PVP ISLANDS. Now, keep working on your PVE build which is also taken from the same website as the PVP build. It sucks too. Do as you did before. Wow... Now keep getting skill points to fully Min-Max something . Btw, I've won almost 200 duels and lost about 30... No reward, nothing. Only useful for practicing with a new skillset.In sum, this game is better if you and friends (if they exist) treat it like a marathon, rather than a race. Mostly, try to have fun... Good luck. I've been playing MMOs since Ultima Online, Everquest, Runescape and Ragnarok Online. I've spent the most time playing World of Warcraft and various other mid-to-late 2000's MMOs. However, the 2010's have been boring. That said, I can tell you now: if there's a toss up between Black Desert Online, Elder Scrolls Online, New World, FF14, Guild Wars 2, or Lost Ark... Choose Lost Ark. There's no need for an in-depth discussion. It's free-to-play... Once you're level 30, decide if it's for you. Most likely, it is...

_childDocuments_.review: Tl:dr. This game wasn't for me, but it may be for you. So while the following are what I deem pros / cons, you might feel differently.This is arguably the most important thing anyway. The combat feels silky smooth and the animations make you feel powerful. The gameplay made me keep playing even though I disliked most of the game.The dungeons that I have access have been fun so far. These are typical MMO raids that require throwing yourself at the encounter until you figure out some mechanic to not wipe. There is a huge caveat to this one which I outline below but overall, I had fun.(Sort of. Depends on whether or not these things are important to you).It's generic and not really compelling. Not much else to say about it.It's bad. Even the people who enjoy this game will say the grind from Lvl. 1-50 is just no fun at all. Since the game has no story, this part of the game is really about getting yourself to end-game where the progression system shifts from levels to gear score. The game starts at level 50.The game's gear-score system is infuriating. The best content is locked behind gear-score so high, that very few people will be able to reach it. It requires players to create many alts in order to funnel resources into their main, but because each subsequent upgrade has a lower chance of succeeding the grind becomes longer between each step. The activities to get these resources are brainless and time-gated. There will be days where you dump hours into the game only to fail your upgrades and receive no progression at all. I'm at 100+ hours and I'm at the point of needing to grind probably another 20 hours to just unlock the next 30-min dungeon. I'd rather play Elden Ring for 20 more hours. Some people really love this hamster wheel grind but I find it pointlessly difficult for the sake of adding "game time". There is a difference between mechanically difficult and difficulty in order to defend poor design choices.There are actually a ton of collectible categories within the game. Some of them are pretty fun to do. However, most of the rewards are pointless. Some give you special toys which are fun until you realize you can't use them in most places for some odd reason. Almost no skins can be earned through collectibles except for the infamous gold mount which because of the reputation system, probably takes over a year of time-gated waiting to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: Lost Ark offers a great MMO Experience, with some changes to the usual formula.Even in this updated format, you will see the bones of a rather terrible design that has improved and matured into the game it is now. This isn't something akin to FFXIV:ARR, Developer Smilegate continuously chips away at issues while also releasing new content. Content it has! Lost Ark allows for plenty of horizontal progression, but unlike other games you are not only rewarded in cosmetic items or bragging rights but tangible player power. This can be frustrating, but it certainly isn't necessary to complete your collectibles tab to enjoy Raid content. The game is very much built around rewarding the player for playing the game. You CAN grind endlessly, by making more alts and repeating the usual daily Gameplay loop, in fact you are heavily incentivized to do so. Unless of course you spend money on the games cash shop. Pay to Win is part of the game, though you might argue that any money spent doesn't save you from getting 1-shot by failing a mechanic in a raid, it certainly is beneficial. The power crave also plays into one of the main issue plagueing the game. Botting, Scripting, RMTing and co. take their place as in every other F2P MMO thought the struggle here seems different as AGS has seemingly not learned their lesson from the New World release, even if they only take the Publisher role. Meanwhile Smilegate enjoys the benefit of extra security measures in their domestic region and hence seemed unprepared for this global release in this regard.As many others have mentioned the game is not released on the full scale of what the current Korean Server has to offer. It is planned to release content patch after content patch until the Global version reaches parity. Clearly many struggles are coming along this way. Players dive in, experience the classic Asian MMO grind and burn out before the first "true" raid tier. Others are hungry for more and bang at AGS gates to release the content that already is in the game files. Ultimately, what is available is enjoyable and while the game design and communication (road maps for 1 month instead of a year) doesn't promote a healthy relationship here. Lost Ark IS a game you can put aside and come back to. That is if you don't derive your enjoyment from being the biggest fish in the pond. The Community in the Global release is very young and Lost Ark doesn't have the most robust social systems. It is a great game to hang out with friends in, but don't expect to find a better experience than your usual MMO here. The isometric perspective also seldom leaves you face to face with others, unless you make use of the games photo-mode. Your Name, Title and Guild as well as your weapon glow, will be the recognizable features not your characters appearance, despite the vast clothing and character customization options. Combat and gameplay is enjoyable, the core that allowed this game to survive in the first place. You have a wide range of classes (some to be released as mentioned above) with two build options each, which are viable for a surprisingly large amount of classes. Balance is fine, yes some classes are "better", but these things are temporary when you invest into characters for months and the next balance patch or update is around the corner. All classes can complete all content, even in the highest tier. Just opt out of trying to be a support that only does damage and you will be rewarded. Lost Ark as an ARPG means fights aren't always scripted performances or mindless button mashing for big DPS. It's a more reactive style that rewards you for reading the enemies behaviour. Especially the guardian raid content is very much inspired by Monster Hunter rather than games like WoW. Of course experience will have you slay everything blindfolded, but finding the "uptime" instead of spamming 123 might just be the combat experience you are looking for. Overall, Lost Ark is a great game, especially in the context of other MMORPGs that are available on the market. My recommendation is to take it easy as content releases Publisher AGS is simply forced to lift up newcomers and returning players, so enjoy the catch up systema and decide if the Gameplay and side-content truly is for you. Lost Ark is worth playing, how much is up to you and AGS/Smilegates grip on Cheating as well as managing the release as a whole.

_childDocuments_.review: Sailing: utterly pointless, just let us teleport directly to each mini island, sailing adds nothing to the games experience, there's no enemies in the sea, nothing to dodge, you can auto-sail, it's essentially just one more way for the devs to waste your time and keep you on longer.Gear progression: Just do your 2 dungeons a day to get a bunch of materials and then pray to the RNG honing jesus that it works, otherwise you wait another day and try again until you pity enhance, you don't even need to do bosses or proper dungeons like other MMOs to progress, just do your weekly dungeons for a once RNG drop of rarer gear with the same stats but it has a bonus gear set stat on it, troll through boring effortless to kill trash mobs, then do some lack-luster bosses, some that have terrible un-fun mechanics behind them.Mokoko seeds: Website simulator to find where they are because you will not be doing this without a site guide, made more annoying later due to things like charisma restrictions or needing to consume a drink to get to it, or wait till you've got the song from the zone rewards.Insignia token grind: The thing that you're trying to get in every zone if you grind it out, the problem with it? it's the same ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing every map and more website simulator gameplay, you won't find the hidden quests without the site or anything for that matter so you're stuck checking a site all the time, the gameplay of this is basically Dragon Age Inquisition or Mass Effect: Andromeda where every single new map you go to has the exact same side objectives all the time, absolute snooze-fest.Combat: This follows on from gear progression, but the combat is the only redeeming factor on this game, it's just a damn shame it's let down by lack-luster bosses, again some that have terribly designed mechanics while others just feel like you walk through them like nothing unless your team is terrible or havn't bothered to check a guide and get killed on repeat, while the killing of general mobs on this game requires the least amount of effort possible, so the satisfaction I feel in combat is minimal at best.Story: OMEGALUL is all I'll say, I've never seen a plot or story telling at bad as this in my entire life, it's basically a G spamming simulator for many even though I've forced my self to read it all hoping it will get better.Time gated event simulator: "Events" that happen at set times of the day, why is this a thing? it basically keeps you on the game a lot longer than you'd like if you want to get that extra bit of progression, or god forbidc you're a collector and trying to get things like Island souls etc, having to wait till set times it's an absolute garbage system made worse with sailing.I give this game a 2/10, the combat barely redeems it.

name: Not Tonight 2
detailed_description: Immigration Enforcement Case #112: You are under arrest. Unless your friends can cross a broken America, retrieve your identifying documents and stay out of trouble... this is the end of the American dream for you. In an alternative broken America, where capitalism and political greed have taken center stage, your friend has gone missing. Snatched during a protest, Eduardo Suarez has been seized by the authorities, and now sits ready for processing in the Miami gulag. Not Tonight 2 is an American document-checking road trip, fusing a time-pressure RPG with a politically charged, dark comedy where every decision matters. Will Eduardo's friends Malik, Kevin and Mari manage to locate and deliver his documents to Miami in time, or is this the end of the American dream? Three compelling stories, written by a team of diverse authors Make your way across America, making terrifying decisions along the way Work the doors of clubs, churches, race tracks, casinos, and cults Check IDS, while completing a variety of silly, poignant minigames Rhythm games, wizard shooting, serving poutine, assessing religion, checking chickens, and more

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first full playthrough, with some re-loading but accepting imperfect plays. A straight playthrough without any reloading or deaths would probably take about 5 hours. Overall, a true sequel to Not Tonight (and Papers, Please). There is more variation in the mini games compared to the original, which got a bit aggravating as they continued adding more things to check etc. This time, each location has different mini-games/requirements, so even if you hate one of them (looking at you, Montana), it's only for a couple rounds. The save style allows for easy re-loadability, and it was fun enough to consider replaying from the beginning at hard difficulty. I missed the keyboard function additions from Not Tonight 1. Dunno about the good ending, still seems like a dystopia to me... makes me wonder if there's a hidden ending.And what self-respecting Canadian would eat poutine with green gravy?

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, writing a review for this game feels weird. I very much enjoyed "Not Tonight 1" and was hoping to see big improvements and expansions of game mechanics. The promotional material with the US map and branching roads especially made me think there would be some kind of choices in jobs and places to visit, maybe even re-playability through different paths in which you could stitch together the story after reaching all of them. Alas the game is painfully linear, but it was made from the same recipe than the first game, so i can still somewhat recommend it when taking it out of the context of being a sequel.The good: Gorgeous pixel art like always as well as fitting music. I encountered no bugs and the game ran smooth. Solid core gameplay à la "Papers Please".The bad: No innovation really. The travel map serves more as a tool to facilitate the plot than any meaningful addition to gameplay. There is way less customization and many of the gameplay additions feel gimmick-y, although they kept me entertained enough. You don't really manage much anymore and I am very sad that they dropped the player agency and time management from the first game. Where in the first game you tried to amass money to get cool upgrades and progress the story, money here is relegated to being something you simply need to get on with the linear levels. I get that they wanted to double-down on storytelling and I also get that the absurd politcal landscape of the US lends itself well to that, but this somehow ended up feeling disjointed and weird. The political message is obvious, as is expected if you played the first game, but feels a lot less poignant and stylish. Having this multiple POV story also takes away the very personnal story that was being told in the first game. I have to comment on the big final judgement as well: It is way too easy and there is no way to ♥♥♥♥ it up. In the first game you had to actually somewhat think and work towards getting the good ending Getting some ressources and making good choices is relegated to knowing pop culture trivia and sometimes choices are just opaque and I felt like I had no idea what I was supposed to do. Instead of clever management of time and ressources you now have to remember names, USA trivia and little visual quirks on character and I do not appreciate that as much. But I do understand the devs are trying to do some things different. It is important to note that this sequel is also somehow a lot shorter than the first game, this is compounded by the fact that a quarter or more of your time in this game will be spent reading text boxes. I just listed a lot of negatives, but I still recommend this game. My personal dissapointment stems mostly from a lack of innovation and a departure of many more complex aspects of the first game, as well as US politics as the story backdrop, something I am just so incredibly tired of as it is just everywhere. The gameplay still makes it a fun ride, but I truely hope they try to actually expand things for the next game and make things more complex and engaging. TL;DR: As a fun little game? I think it's okay. As a sequel? I don't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is inferior to the original in every aspect.Unlike the first game, it is completely linear, and there is no choice about where you are going to work, or if you should skip work. Being unable to skip work implies that your health drops everyday and there is no way to stop it. The only way to recover health is completing MapO quests. However, if you fail these specific tasks, in which it's not always clear what you must do, you won't be able to heal, and you will end up dying because the health drops to zero. In this case, you essentially soft locked and forced to restart from the previous chapter, since the MapO rewards are only received in the end of the chapter and health drops 10 points everyday before that.While health is very difficult to recover, you make money from work everyday and there is no real use for it. In the original game, there was an urgency to make enough money and pay the debt until a deadline as reached. You could also buy useful upgrades for your job as a bouncer. In the sequel, money is only used to buy cosmetics and doesn't help you at all. There is no way to use it to buy items that improve your health, like the heating and the bed from the original game.Most of the plot is inexplicably told through text, so it's up to you to imagine what is happening in the story. Unlike the original game, there are no cutscenes. They have been replaced by a map interface that always shows up when you are not working as a bouncer. This is a really poor choice by the developers, because, while the map looks nice, it has no practical use. You can't choose your destination, because the story is completely linear. I would rather have the visual storytelling of the original game rather than this map and narrative through text that just feels lazy. As a matter of fact, the lack of so many features from the first game in this sequel make the entire experience feel rushed and unfinished.If you are a fan of the first game, I don't recommend buying this one. You would be better off playing something like .

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game an above-lukewarm thumbs up. Regardless of one's political leanings, I believe most people can agree that everything across the board has been exaggerated to the point of farce. And that's okay! Farce in itself is not bad, I found it enjoyable and amusing enough, save for the odd moments where the game tries to take itself too seriously. At one point you have a character grappling with having killed a man/seen a man murdered in front of him, then almost immediately after you're checking the IDs of chickens for nugget processing. There was a lot of hype regarding the diverse cast, but like most everything in the game, the experiences portrayed were all very, very surface-level. None of the protagonists' unique circumstances manifest themselves in a narratively or mechanically meaningful way. The astonishingly uncritical, pretty much all positive portrayal of the "hip" tech CEO manipulating politics and monopolizing everything was particularly baffling, though I suppose they know their market and publisher. (a character toothlessly, vaguely griping every so often about how it's kinda creepy is not substantive)The gameplay's simple: approve or rebuke a given number of folks in a time limit based on the level's criteria, usually with a tacked on minigame. I played on hard mode and only had to redo a few levels, mostly because a few of the minigames were primarily reliant on chance. Engaging enough, if not particularly challenging. These segments are broken up by text segments with the occasional blatantly obvious choice or blatantly obvious inventory decision. The characters in the text portions are mostly broad-strokes; no one's very deep here, not even the protagonists. There's the pretense of having to manage stats and money, but even on hard mode I'll admit I didn't even really have to think about those at any point. You do the easy "action" segments well, pick the obviously correct choices in dialogue, and that aspect of the game will literally never give you any challenge.There are some technical things that could use improvement: Audio settings are not saved between sessions, which is a pain. The delay for text boxes and texts in the in-game phone are a touch long, and needless inventory items linger throughout the whole character's playthrough, perhaps to add some artificial difficulty. Overall, I'd say the game has an identity crisis, I want to like it more because I find the core gameplay loop of the action segments enjoyable, and find farce an underutilized genre. There's a lotta fun ideas and aesthetic designs here! But the work itself and the marketing cannot decide whether it's an all-out farce or a darkly comedic political look at the logical conclusions of real world issues. It cannot decide if it wants to be an adventure game, it cannot decide what it wants its story to be and say, and it cannot decide on what level it wants to engage the player.

_childDocuments_.review: This recommendation is really two-sided, because on one hand I recommend this game, but on the other not really.As from a person, who really loved the original Not Tonight and the DLC, this game was kind off a let-down. It is a good bouncer simulator, but less charming and likeable as the first one. First of all, the positives why I would still recommend the game. The gameplay is still the same, fantastic, ID checking madness. The new location quests give a good challenge to the game, figuring them out is sometimes quite fun (even though some of them are a bit nonsensical). I liked the location designs, they were unique and quite authentic (besides some). The OST is great as usual, great electronic and house music mixes all around, with multiple other genres making an appearance. The gameplay loop is solid as always, some of the new mechanics are really creative and fun (and some of them are an annoying pain). The roadtrip core idea is really interesting and quite cosy, you could immerse yourself into it (for the first roadtrip).Now, the negatives. The story is completely devoid of charm, likeable characters or interesting plot points. Not to mention, that even though the first NT felt somewhere a bit overexaggerated, this whole game feels like that. I don't like when stories reflect the developers' political views and they distort reality to fit their views. The first NT was depressing and overlooming, really immersive in feeling like an outcast in oppressed society. But this story, is just shocking for the sake of being shocking and mocking one certain side, huge dislike. (Also why was club rock music playing in the border, where you literally stopped people from emigrating. The Wall in 1 was authentic, depressing, you could feel the people's pain and this is just ???) Second, some gameplay mechanics are simply annoying or outright broken (looking at you musical tickets). They are not fun at all and just make it hard and tedious of A-ing some of the stages. Also some of the dialogue choosing mechanics don't make any sense and sometimes if you choose the wrong one you have to replay the whole night just for the A mark quest. Also, the absence of the custom character mechanic is just bad. I understand that they wanted to make the game focus around other characters as a normal story, but when the characters are not fledged out or interesting enough, you can feel the sting of it's disappearance. Also also, why were the hotkeys removed? They just made the game 10x more annoying, because of misclicks and whatnot.In conclusion, Not Tonight 2 is a good successor to 1 on gameplay front but stumbles in everything else. I would recommend it as a one-play game if it's on sale.
