The game is easyI know this sounds contradictory, but despite the bugs and the unfairness, the rules never get difficult. The only real difficulty is the time management, as sometimes you have enough time to get 1.5 times more than bonus2, while others you just let the last people in without checking their stuff, hoping that they're legit, because there's simply no time.4. The game is by far not a bad game.I'll be honest, the game has many great ideas, the story is very good, the main characters are enjoyable. It's just that from a gameplay perspective, it doesn't stand a chance against Papers Please for example, where the difficulty is very high, it's fair and the only waste of time is the scanner, and it isnìt even too bad. In papers please, they throw in completely new stuff to throw you off while I have the feeling that Not Tonight 2 throws in new gameplay elements to try to add difficulty, but fails doing so, as the changes are minor and get reset at each new area.If the game updates and improves on at least the unfairness and the difficulty, then I'm very willing to make the thumb go up.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: I've 100% both the first and the second game and personally liked the original Not Tonight way more. The second game appears to be more... superficial? casual? sometimes boring? Not really sure how to describe it.Plenty of challenging "paperwork" stuff got substituted by no-brain mini-games, the ones you could probably encounter in hypercasual mobile products. There are three protagonists, each doing the very same thing but in different cities. Almost each city is strictly 2 identically structured levels (the first one is normal, the second one is with VIP / guest list) and you move through those cities relatively quickly and do somewhat the same stuff all over again (check IDs for the very same issues mostly), but now with a different mini-game to "play". Like hold the button pressed for a couple of seconds to fill the Oxygen container or hold the button pressed for a couple of seconds to fill the car with gas, Or give a person one of the three items depending on their "level". On top of that, two of the mini-games have random mechanics in them, as in you have very little control over the results and have to wait the long animation while the card or the dice plays out. Definitely not something I enjoyed.The story seemed alright, although not as engaging as the one from the first game, in my opinion. I also encountered a recurring bug with the Oxygen refilling mini-game in all of my three Mari playthroughs: after you place the Oxygen Container into the corresponding place to fill it from one of the three Oxygen Tanks, the container might start flowing around and therefore you can't really measure the filling rate properly, because the measuring limit flows stays in the place, while the container filling meter flows around with the container itself.Nonetheless, the game is still OK, but if you were to play both the first and the second games, I think I'd rather recommend to play Not Tonight 2 first for a more casual and mediocre experience and then play Not Tonight 1 for a more deep and meaningful experience (and then enjoy Papers, Please for a really hardcore dessert, hehe).
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: While I won't say this game is terrible, but coming from the first game this one just...isn't it. the progression system lost something. I'm almost through one section of potentially 3 of the game and there have been no upgrades. The timed choices leave something to be desired for many reasons: A. There are multiple screens to click through so you may end up progressing the text and land on a timed choice without knowing. B. Not everyone reads as fast or can process things as fast when they read them. While I didn't have that problem, I know some who might... C. not very friendly for those who their first language might not be the ones that are provided. D. Just WHY? Like I get you might be forcing people to commit but never have or never will like timed choices.I loved the charm of getting to see the inside of the pubs, bars, etc that I visited in the first game as well as getting to talk to the boss and earn double the cash and a prize if I achieved head doorman. I hate that most of this game is done via a beige box full of text and character portraits.  I do understand that the map being the "homebase" sort of place is understandable because of the setting and the story but I feel so very disconnected from everything...and okay I guess in a round about way that does very much describe my experience living in America but idkDo not come in expecting to have more of the charm you got in the first game and usually I try NOT to come at things expecting the exact same thing but unfortunately I'm not a fan of the progression system, how the story is told, the environments, the addition of character portraits, the music or even the bouncer tasks. Beware the wannabe rhythm game section as it comes with 0 forgiveness and laggy timing. It's been too long to request a refund so I will attempt to see this game through and may come with more thoughts as I go along. This game is mostly positive so it obviously was a hit with some but it was definitely a miss for me.Edit: So In fantastic style I'm almost through the second part of the game and I continue not caring much for the bouncer tasks. You have to play hi-lo at a casino to let people in and I was thrown back to my dad playing an ad-ridden game on his cellphone. Also I think another thing that gets me is the tone in this one is much more serious and less satire. Like the subject matter was a serious sort of subject matter in the first one but there was a lot more weirdness and satire going on in that one. I will say that it wouldn't specifically fit with the story they have painted to do that here but IDK. The jobs are teethgrinding, there's no real progression and the story is pretty depressing honestly. This is something I might be more into if I was looking for a game like Not Tonight but...yknow wasn't actually Not Tonight. I wanted more quirky satire but honestly I'm wishing I could go back to before I had more than two hours in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: it's not as good as the first imo. it's more like a visual novel compared to 1, and there are no upgrades to make bouncering easier like unlocking hotkeys or something new like to make people wait in line longer without getting angry. instead i suppose it keeps things fresh by introducing a new gimmick with every bouncer location you get a job at, however these gimmicks are not always good; the rhythm minigame in new york/that other city was annoying, but not as crap as the hi-lo minigame in vegas, or the dice roll ♥♥♥♥ in the vr section and the robots in the 3rd roadtrip story. at least the rhythm tickets relied on skill, i'm not down for minigames based on pure rng and luck.anyway with that said, if you can get it during one of the big sales and you've already played 1, i'd say it's worth getting, just keep in mind it is very short so don't go expecting to get more than 15-20 hours out of before 100%-ing it. however, if all you want is a game like papers please and you haven't played not tonight, buy that instead
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not Tonight 2 unfortunately pales in comparison to the previous title. I didn't really care for the mini games that replaced the multiple forms of documentation — it felt a bit too gimmicky for my liking.Challenge Mode isn't available like in the original title so if you want to continue playing after the story is complete, your only option is to restart the story.On the upshot, the music is still pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Retro pixel feel combined with modern dystopian political and social themes, and unique gameplay that doesn't involve shooting or battling or harvesting or crafting, or any of the other boring things that almost every other modern game relies on.  The story is clever and a bit frightening, and the humour is sharp and on-point.  A very good follow-up to the original game, and I do hope that there is a third game coming in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: I can't really recommend this game. The original Not Tonight is so much better in every aspect it's not an exaggeration.-The characters were better.-The gameplay was better.-The story was better.You don't spend enough time with anyone to really get to know them, and the core gameplay loop makes it impossible to come to know any of them.Each location has a gameplay gimick that is unique to the area and nowhere else. Except for two mechanics that pop up one additional time. Gone are the mass of papers you need to quickly sift through to get enough people in before times up, welcome Dance Dance revolution.The story is split into three chunks, three acts like the original, each act is it's own story and is almost entirely disjointed from the rest of the acts. Acts 1 and 2 take place simultaniously and you can see the progress the other is making in your current act through the text messages. Act 3 is easily the worst the game has to offer. It's the only act that actually uses the map for some gameplay in avoiding Martyr agents wandering the map that you have to avoid or else get an instant game over. The story was passable, but slowly became absolutely forgettable. I don't like this game, I don't think it's very fun, I'd rather play Not Tonight 1 than play this again
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is the sequel to Not Tonight. Many differences from the original, but those differences are what make this game unique and interesting. Similar concept to Papers, Please, but you play as three different bouncers, unlike the first game. This, already, is a new concept. At first, I thought that this might make the storytelling confusing, as this game is much more story-oriented than the first game, but no, it was well-delivered and easy to follow. You play as one bouncer (Kevin) until their journey ends, then you play out the other (Malik), and lastly the third one (Mari). Each stopping spot/location has its own unique task on top of the regular ID checking part. For example, you would be providing poutine sauce to customers at one stop, then you would be doing dice battle against bots, and at some point you would be filling gas for people. Overall, it is not too difficult to understand, and there are two guides (English) there to help you complete the game without too much sweat. If you wonder whether this is a confusing concept, I would rather say it makes the game less of a bore, and it is not that hard to understand at all.In terms of difficulty, I played on the regular mode, which is not supposed to be too difficult, and it was actually very easy in my opinion. I personally would recommend this gamemode because anything easier than this might just be way too easy, but it could well be just me for being familiar with the gameplay already. For your reference, I managed to complete every shift but only one without a problem. Customers push over way less often than the last game, which is great as it saves you a few seconds for the next person in line. In the original Not Tonight we had people pushing over almost all the time you deny them, which makes it annoying if you wish to achieve the highest grade for the shift.To conclude whether this game is worth trying if you have already played through the first game, it is a definite yes from me. The gameplay is refreshing thanks to all the new features, and the story definitely plays a huge part as well. Kudos to the developers, you have made one fun game.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is AMAZING I just finished my first complete playthrough of Not Tonight 2, and I am in love. The story is amazing, the game isn't too long or too short. Just overall amazing.Here's my basic rundown of how I think the game is.STORY { 10/10 }OH BOY. The story for this game is absolutely top tier. It's well thought out, the different stages of the game flow together really nicely, it's just an amazing story. I found myself being lost in the story, not being able to just stop playing. I was captivated by the story-line, wondering what's gonna happen next. And frankly, it was super nice being able to see exactly how my decisions affected the story, at least a little bit.GAME MECHANICS { 8/10 } The game mechanics to Not Tonight 2 aren't bad ! You use your mouse the entire game, which isn't bad at all, especially if you're just trying to relax and game. It would be really easy for someone who has never played a pc game in their life to play. The only issue I had, was I could use shortcuts on my keyboard, such as setting a key on my keyboard to pass people quickly. Other than that though, I had no complaints.CHARACTERS { 10/10 }Every single character I met (good, bad, neutral) were all well designed. They all had so much character to them, all had amazing dialogue, and even the lore to the characters was beautiful and neatly made. I have no complaints whatsoever to any of the characters and their designs.WORTH THE MONEY? ABSOLUTELY. I think if you're looking for a new game to play by yourself, go for it. And, as a small streamer, I recommend it to stream. They even have a streamer friendly option for the music, so you don't have to worry about copyright !! It's a small game that could run easily on any pc/laptop (unless you're still using an ancient computer).OVERALL, I think this game is wonderful. I can definitely see myself coming back to play it anytime. Plus, as of this review, I have 8 hours on the game. And that was enough to complete the game completely. So, although it is a short game, and you can probably speed run it much faster than me, I believe it would make for an amazing stream ! Or just a nice short game for you to play if you're trying to relax. And of course, at the end, well all I've got to say is.... Glory to Arstotzka!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: And we're back, ladies and gentlemen! This time, our favourite Arstotzkan immigration officer takes over three young fellas from the (remains of the) US of A. I really like some of the levels and ideas, but I feel like the pace of the storytelling doesn't feel right. In the previous game, you have like a month to achieve certain things. Here, you've only got two days and most of them are in the character conversations. I might have to say the previous game's story mechanics are a bit better.That being said, I quite enjoyed the story being told from three different perspectives. It's really a nice addition. I also recognized a few familiar faces from the previous game.I really liked the gameplay and the music I hear in this series of games. It's the main appeal for me, and I'm glad they kept this style. I hope they would make more improvements for the third game (if any).9/10 MapO A Grades.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Bought a trucker hat in Act 3 and couldn't equip it on the character. 0/10, unplayableIn seriousness: the game is all right. Not terribly difficult, but I did find myself playing just to get through sections rather than out of enjoyment. The location mini-games are hit-or-miss in terms of actually breaking up the repetition of checking docs (stop invading air wizards? winner. musical tickets? not even close). The loss of keyboard actions is a huge downgrade from the first game.It's easy to see a lot of work went into the art and development, and it deserves support and praise for that. Happy to have supported the creators' work, but not itching to replay any time soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game has the same simple fun as the first. Although I spent five years doing this sort of thing for a convenience store in the 1990's, I'm not getting any PTSD flashbacks... ;) The story is more interesting, situations change, and it's not just one guy trying to keep himself from being deported. Maybe I should renew my food-handling cert in case I find myself checking IDs for a living again......and I'm still jonesing for poutine. (sigh)
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, this game is odd. if I an an option for "meh" - I would choose that.I would've spent much less time in the game if I hadn't reloaded a bunch trying to get the "right" things - but it turned out for the most part, not messing up didn't impact anything. A really big thing is that this game has pretty much nothing in terms of accessibility options outside of colorblind mode. If you have any motor disabilities, this game will be incredibly difficult - it almost entirely involves using the mouse and being able to move it quickly, even for tasks that could EASILY allow button presses like the counter, or the drum machine, or the arrows (or similar things in different areas). The story is pretty decent - I never played the first one, but this felt like a watered down Papers, Please - traveling around felt sort of unnecessary, and the traveling in the third roadtrip just got annoying when you had to look at the map and attempt to see all of the lines when people were in the way of them. It would've been better if it had stuck to text and said "Oh, he went north, then southwest, then east" instead of the arrow system. If you're looking for another Papers, Please and really want a similarish game to play, get this.I got the game for $14.99 on the Steam Summer Sale and I feel like I sort of got my money's worth, but it feels sort of... hollow now that I finished the game.If I were to give this a true number ranking (and not the gamer rankings where if it isn't a 9 or a 10, it sucks), I would give it a 6/10, as it was mediocre. It wasn't bad, but it wasn't great.The pixel art was cool and the voices were distinct, so I could differentiate between the characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: 3/5 Get it if you want or if you’re thinking, the game is honestly carried by the gameplay and art which are pretty important all things considered. A decent sequel to the first Not tonight, takes place in the USA as it essentially crumbles. Which is ew the USA sucks. If you haven't played the first not tonight you don't need to play it to play this game, but you probably should just play it to get the references and to get a better hang of gameplay. Both games are very reminiscent of 'Papers, please' which I loved they even had a thank you to 'papers, please' and Lucas Pope for the inspiration. Get the game if you really liked the first Not Tonight and Papers, please. If your on the edge just try papers, please first. The story is fine, but lackluster. There is a lot going on for it, all to amount to what I felt like wasn't much. Also way too much dialogue, so much dialogue, it was honestly the biggest thing that turned me off the game. The dialogue was getting a bit repetitive and boring. I do appreciate all the satire surrounding american politics and the current climate of many areas. So many subtle things that were great which were then ruined by the dialogue explaining/pointing out the satire. The loop of checking for different things as a bouncer is fun, they usually cycle in new gimmicks per area which are a gamble whether their good or not. Some of the gimmicks were pretty fun and some were making me suffer like the one where you had to hit according to a beat and it didn't help that it was also somewhat bugged. The game doesn't give you much time to really enjoy any of the fun gimmicks though.  Backgrounds and pixel art are really good, but the profiles are ugly. The backgrounds are all really cool and are one of the things I most anticipated when arriving in a new area. Every area had a new song which was cool and a lot of them complimented the area, but most of the songs were pretty annoying and I ended up muting a lot of them. No voice acting but the characters did make sounds which were super annoying especially Kevin who had a squeaky voice. Somewhat fun, made me want to play the original Not tonight again. Relatively bugless, but there is one issue with the IDs. Since the pixel art isnt very detailed (which would have been fine) some characters will have a slight difference between their ID and it will be very difficult to tell the difference (if the ID is fake or not). I've also gotten plenty of IDs with the only difference being a hat or earrings and they were somehow fake. They also didn't learn from the first game on the denying issue. Kicking someone out for having fake paperwork takes way too long which sucks when you are trying to beat the clock. I remember seeing a review saying that it would be faster to just let someone in and take the penalty than it is to kick someone out which is completely true. You also don't get paid for people you kick out so if you get three fake IDs back to back you could be screwed on some levels which sucks. Either make kicking out people faster or pay us for kicking people out with fake papers.Overall, decent game and a great addition to the paperslike genre. I've named it that and you can't stop me.Theres also no infinite mode? I 100% the game and there is no infinite mode given at the end. Super dissapointed.Also what's with the lighter?? Its the desktop logo and its being thrown by Kevin on the banner, but there is no lighter that plays any important part? Sometimes you can catch people with lighters, but they play no role in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Quite different from the first one but I'm still really enjoying it! I LOVE the different scenery and locations, every location killed it. The different minigames are a lot of fun so far, really loving that added mix up. I think maybe the character interaction doesn't feel as witty or sharp as before, but I do enjoy all the characters a lot! The map across America is also really awesome, both as a concept and in execution. Looks great! Definitely loving it so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Coregame remains, but is more varied due to new, different minigames. This time, the action takes place in the United States. Not Tonight 2 addresses a number of political issues in its usual sarcastic manner. Examples include deportations, religious fanaticism and land grabbing. In contrast to the first part, the developers now indirectly force the player to actually follow the story: If you don't pay attention to the conversations that tell the story, you'll miss the solutions that are required at certain points to be able to complete an area with "A" - the best rating. Of course, as before, you can load an older save point and try again. Reading helps though ^^
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is worth playing if you like games like Papers Please and the first Not Tonight. I wasn't ecstatic about it from start to finish but some of the gimmicks were amusing (minus the music one!) The story is bland and not as engaging. I couldn't bring myself to care much about the characters. Although, not as interesting as its predecessor it's still worth grabbing if there's a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: The music is fun and the game is entertaining. I do, however, prefer the original because I felt more invested in the characters and I didn't quite like the switching of perspectives this game offers. One strength Not Tonight 2 has in comparison is that the pace is steadier and you don't spend too much time at the same locations. I liked that they experimented with different game mechanics and I appreciate the other themes they incorporated.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not Tonight 2 is the same as the first game, but fixes a bunch of issues that the first game had, and is a more "clean" experience.If you played the first game, but want more, buy this instead of the overpriced dlc the first game had.The game now has you work only 2 nights per location instead of 5.This small change fixes the pacing issues the first game had, but at the same time it makes the game feel like an arcade adventure experience rather than a "bouncer"-"papers, please" sim, and honestly i prefer this change, HOWEVER, i do wish that they would add a "endless mode" of some sort.The story is fun, it's nice, is it as good or better than the first game's story? well, that's debatable, but a sequel does not have to be "better", however i did ultimately have a better time with this story because of the fixed pacing.The gameplay has more variety, but is somehow easier?? Hard mode is not that hard, and that's sad, because half of the reason why people play "stress-games" is because of the challenge. BUTThe soundtrack slaps, again.very, very, very good soundtrack.Overall, not a very innovative sequel, but still enjoyable.Is it worth 17€?...nah, id value it at 12€.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: I've only just completed the first arc of  the story, and I can already say that this game is so much better than the first. Even though I'm a few hours in at the time of the review, Not Tonight 2 is already better than the first game, and that's saying a lot.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the first game, but this seems more like a mobile game. The best thing about the original game was eventually you map things to the keyboard, but as far as I can see you never get the option and frankly I hate having to use the mouse for everything. The different minigames are interesting, I guess, but the only one I liked was the puzzle one. The music ones are the absolute worst, especially without being able to use the keyboard. _childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just as, if not more, ridiculous than the first instalment, and it's bloody excellent. It expertly balances the serious and the absurd, giving a satirical and yet heart-wrenching portrayal of one of many possible futures. It's also great if you like checking IDs in a video game for hours. 10/10 recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game! There are so many hidden gems that show the developers put in a massive amount of hard work. This is a huge step up from the first installment in this series. Hats off to the developers are PanicBarn! They have really outdone themselves with a great game. There are a few things I would change, but overall great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say that I will ever finish this game. From the moment I opened it up I knew I was in for a different animal then the OG, but i wasn't expecting this.The story isn't engaging in the slightest, and the bad design choices make that aspect even worse. The characters are bland, the story is filled with real politics mixed in with grand amounts of satire that in all honesty isn't funny at all. The negative reviews about this game are true. If you respect the OG, don't play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: if youre one of the losers who think this game is crt woke brainwashing or...other buzz words...i am happy to say youll be sorely disappointed. this game really pulls its punches with the political commentary and i felt pretty unchallenged and underwhelmed. there is one scene where a black man is treated unfairly by the police, and another where a latina woman is cat called. and, really, thats about it. theres comments made here and there about how dumb republicans have gotten, but theyre played mostly for laughs and those points arent very profound. like, yeah. they basically want to spread a deadly disease and perpetuate a pandemic indefinitely for the sake of their corporate masters. this isnt news. aspects of american society that are particularly egregious and gross, like ethnic disenfranchisement and, i dunno, the fact that we happen to dump all of our toxic waste in black communities, would have made for much more biting political commentary. things that, even to americans, go under the radar. i can tell this game was written by a team of brits because their knowledge of americas racial issues really only go as far as "black people are treated differently by the police". i will say though, that it was a particularly well done depiction of it. malik saying to himself "just remember what mom and dad taught you" was pretty upsetting, as well as an accurate portrayal of how police brutality has, in a sense, permeated into black culture.i also felt that the music wasnt as good as in the original. "you got nothing on me," "dont love me," and "racing hearts" are just some of the songs from the first game that really stick out in my mind even a few years after playing it. there arent really any songs in not tonight 2 that i can remember. the pixel art has taken a dramatic turn in quality, becoming probably the second best pixel art in a game, behind only katana zero.like in the original, the ending is super underwhelming. its better, but not by that much. the writing in general is about as good, which is to say nothing special. except for maliks chapter. that one made me feel super uncomfortable and sad, but in a good way. this is going to sound like a joke, but trust me, it isnt: i was absolutely FURIOUS at the end when i didnt get an epilogue from shannon. she is your best character, and you have completely shafted her by giving epilogues to the soup guy and the occult lady, but not shannon. i want a spin-off with shannon. seriously. do it, cowards. make shannon the protagonist of not tonight 3.anyway, its alright. i cant say whether or not its better than the original because i feel like the difference in quality is so minuscule that it doesnt matter to identify one or the other as better. i recommend it, but no more or less than i do the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. Much better than the first. Love the story and how relatable it is. Choices do matter if you let them but the game gives you the option to bypass it by just letting the prompt expire which is also nice if you don't want to mess it up. Only thing I want differently is for the side bonuses to be better summarized so I know how to better complete them to get the bonus. It's pretty vague, although, not sure if that was their intent.EDIT: THAT ENDING!!!!! WHAT?!?!?!?! OMG! Y'all.... play this game. Not kidding.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of the first game and this one adds all the elements that I enjoyed from the original plus an increased level of difficulty whilst being able to retain the same humour throughout. I very much enjoyed the additional mechanics of the rhythm based mini-games, different environments plus the recurring characters from the original game. I disliked the random luck based elements (the card hi-low game and the robot battle system) as I felt it cheapened the point of the game a little bit and it made certain goals much harder to succeed, even when choosing the most likely option.This is also a fantastic social commentary (as was the original) on the state of the world in the modern age. Whilst not everyone may agree with the stances being made the satire is evident throughout and they are a group who will happily make fun of themselves to some degree at the same time as talking about a serious topic.I hope to see more games in this style from the developers and it is a great example of how well a small team can put together such a fantastic game, certainly they have gained a fan for life.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: This will be a hard one. The review I mean, not the game. Game is easy, even on medium difficulty; will try hard on my second play through. :)First of all, let me tell you why I recommend this game. There are a few reasons but mainly 2; I enjoyed playing both games and I think it has very high potential as an IP. If I just had to tell about this specific one, the second in the series, the review would still be a recommending one but to be honest, not be by far.If you played the first one you won't need any explanation or tutorial, it is pretty much the same mechanics with the same setup and the same choice of graphics style. Yes there are some new "mini-games" (using "" because the original game mechanic itself can almost be called a mini game), but it won't take you to repeat a level to learn them, maybe you'll get in 1 or 2 people less.If you never played the first one, the game mechanics can be explained as simple as; document check. Check the name, dob, this number, that hologram etc. the game is basically this plus the new mini games.Graphics are OK, not the best pixel art around but is enough for this game as it was for the first one.Story is good. Not as good as the first one in my opinion, but still good. Choices in the story seems pretty meaningless though, except when you take 100 damages from them and die, but it is OK. I have also read the reviews you just read before or will read after this one. I do not agree that the game is woke and that it pushes you to take the decisions that the writers/producers want you to take. Actually, I agree with the part of them pushing you to take some decisions that are right for them. But it is not so weird, most of the adventure or RPG games does it, didn't see many RPGs that you can befriend the dragon instead of killing it. There are some games that player choices matter, this one, like many others, is not a game like that. If you think it pushes leftist agenda I invite you also reviewing any militaristic combat game, historical game etc. with the same glasses on, you will be surprised of the level of ideology pushing in many games. Almost every fiction is on a side if look deep enough, this one uses that as a fun creating element. I would say, deal with it or do not play anything that has an actual subject.Music is great. Nothing to say there. Effects and fake speech sounds though; those makes one wonder if that was really the best they could do. It becomes pretty boring after a while.Is it bug free? Almost but not fully, as no complex software can be. Very acceptable.I bought the game for around 15€ at the launch sale. Does it worth it? Well, honestly, no. I think the price point should have been a little lower, maybe around 10€ or something. It took me 10h to finish the game and I read that for some it took only 5. Yes I know the 2$ per hour "rule" but I think it is a bit unfair to gamers, we consume a lot, and in general the games are consumed a lot, they should be cheaper. This could have been avoided by a simple design trick, of course I am not the game designer of this game but I will give my personal opinion about how it should have been in the coming paragraph.If you had the patience to read until here you are probably questioning how is this going to turn into a recommended review? Well I can tell right now; it is the gameplay. It is repetitive, it is same same, but it is brilliant. I can say that it very quickly captures you and brings you to that immersion level which only happens while playing good games. The immersion that makes you easily get out of the negative mood you were in just before you clicked the shortcut of the game. This game requires a high level of focus or you will fail. Yes, there are similar titles around, but believe me, as fan of genre, this one is good. Is it the best one? No, the best is the original one, Papers Please, but this series is close second. Although the flow of the first game was better this one is also very captivating and fun. I would never understand the choice of making us play mini games max 4 times from a design perspective, but it still works, you don't get bombarded with new tricks to learn as it is short. I think if they would have made every city 4 or 5 games instead of 2 they would have built a game that takes longer to finish, would have time to award the player for learning the mini games, would have a more balanced story/game ratio and then maybe a 16€ price point would also be more reasonable. There are some other game design choices I have difficulties to understand but I think it would be going in too much detail for a Steam review.In short the game is good, it has it's shortcomings but it is fun to play. I won't go and tell you to play the first one instead of this one; NT and NT2 both deserves your time and money. Maybe wait for a sale on this one, but get it and play it, I am almost certain you will enjoy it if you are already checking these reviews to decide.

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to the original "Not Tonight".  We're not dealing drugs to make money, though there's definitely some shady stuff in which to get involved in the former USA.  If you're left-of-center politically, I think you'll appreciate this game's story.  It's definitely not shy about who its audience is in that sense, and I find that comforting.If you found the first game too hard to enjoy, fear not, because the sequel has a range of difficulties from "CASUAL" to "HARD", where CASUAL is not even really made to be a challenge at all.  You can just go through the motions and see the story stress-free.  Easy adds a little bit of pressure, but certainly not tough for anyone experienced with the first game or with "Papers, Please".One thing I'll warn you about, though.  You cannot take a day off and rest to recover health, and working always drains some of your health.  The main way to recover health is to complete Map-O quests, so don't think of them as optional things to do for a branching choice.  Think of them more as things you REALLY need to complete in order to complete the game, unless you're on casual difficulty.The game has occasional stark and disturbing themes, as well as occasionally absurd and humorous scenes, not to mention an enjoyable reference once or twice to those who enjoyed the original game.  There are times where the game clearly doesn't mean for you to take it too seriously, and there are times where you cannot help but see the seriousness in it as it hits home on something sadly all too real.Replay value isn't super great, as the game follows the same general progression regardless of your choices.  However, there definitely is some replay value when it comes to trying to complete the game on higher difficulties, trying to collect all the achievements, and trying to purchase all of the outfits.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot to say about this game, so much that it's difficult to organize my thoughts, so I'll begin with the more basic stuff and move into the more complicated critiques I have. This review will contain spoilers for the game, as I'm analyzing the themes of the game; TL;DR I really do recommend this game but I have notes for the developers and writers!Gameplay: A simple deviation from the Papers, Please formula that emphasizes speed over multi-factor testing with linear "travel" segments between them. As one of the three of our Millennial main characters (Kevin, Malik, and Mari) you're meant to take bouncing gigs through a gig economy-style app to make enough money to travel across the fractured states of America to collect documents to rescue your friend and comrade, Eduardo. It's impressive how well the developers managed to shoehorn the Papers, Please formula of gameplay into a wide suite of different locales: throwing in chickens depending on their age and hormone requirements, doing stat-based RNG battles with robots between letting in actual customers, playing a hi-lo card game with potential entrants to a casino, it's all genuinely inspired. My biggest criticism is the lack of space on the document-processing screen at the bottom, which can lead to some annoying clutter, and the RNG components of some of the gigs mean you're not entirely in control of how well you'll do, but overall, this stuff is great. Meanwhile, the interspersed driving/conversation segments lack some variety in how to approach a problem, but ultimately it's solid enough to reinforce the themes of the game that I don't mind.Aesthetics/Music: I *LOVE* the look and feel of this game. It uses the same pixel art style of Papers, Please, while adding a fun, colorful, and vibrant twist to it, even if the locations the characters are placed in are dour (turning the brainwashing facility into a literal theme park is a great idea). The music uses a variety of modern EDM, reggaeton, hip-hop, and R&B, which is probably more suitable for a game literally taking place in alternate-universe 2022. When the soundtrack comes out, I'm definitely checking it out on Spotify or YouTube Music.Story/Themes: Okay, this game gets a lot of things correct and a few minor things incorrect. America is divided between two factions along the North and South (pretty much the Mason-Dixon line of the Civil War) with two factions: the Alliance (proper liberals, inclusivity without justice) and the Martyrs (authoritarian conservatives, nationalistic and dogmatic). The game critiques both factions, with the Alliance being too focused on compromise and civility politics to focus on the threat of insurrection via liberal democracy, and the Martyrs wielding their power to silence dissent and induce complacency. As a critique of American politics in 2022, I think this particular dividing line is highly effective. However, (and this is where my criticism comes in), the CEO of MapO, a tech company that gives you reward drops for completing missions along the way, rises up in the good ending to help reunite America in a technocratic facts-and-logic unity. The game is tongue-in-cheek about this being a "good" ending, but I would think given the other progressive messaging in the game that you would be able to sidestep this conclusion with the hopes of sparking a more progressive, leftist movement. How this is a part of the good ending is difficult for me to grasp and wound up leaving a bitter taste in my mouth, but I'm assuming it's for the sake of appealing to the broadest audience possible, your Twitter leftist gamers and your Elon Musk stan gamers.Ultimately, I'd give this game a 7/10. If you liked Papers, Please, political commentary included, then you're gonna have a good time bouncing people in Not Tonight 2.

_childDocuments_.review: An all around inferior sequel to Not Tonight that still manages to be engaging enough to be worth playingA nice fresh cast of well-written characters with some contrived usage of old favourites from Not Tonight. The way the story is told works well, with the three story-arcs for each character each being interesting and unique. The ending gives you that warm fuzzy feeling from saving all your friends, but ultimately doesn't feel dramatic or impactful to meThe wide variety of mini-games kept the game feeling fresh all the way through, and made the game feel more varied than it was challenging (compared to say, Papers Please, where there's little variety but the level of challenge just keeps going up). I don't consider myself particularly good at this genre of game, but on the default medium difficulty I got bonus 2 every single night, and only got fined for mistakes once.The main let-down of some of these mini-games was that they were entirely luck-based and counted against your performance for the night, and the side quests, which is a monumentally stupid design decision that fortunately doesn't matter unless you're trying to go for all achievementsSpeaking of the side quests, they were a welcome addition, though to me it feels stupid that you're not told explicitly what you have to do for a given quest, then either have to redo a given area if you didn't accidentally get everything, or just try and luck out enough times to get the A grades necessary for the good ending of the game. Personally, I just used a guide to tell me what I needed to do to pass the quests, as I found it frustrating to be given low grades for making ambiguous dialogue choices or outfit decisions incorrectlyFollowing a guide also had the added benefit that I wouldn't mess up dialogue choices that could lead to a game over and repeating a night. As far as I can tell, the only way to work out the right choices is through trial and error in a couple of sections (e.g. )I miss the money pressure of Not Tonight and the drug selling & bribing mechanics that you could opt into to get more money for the higher riskSo yeah, overall, an interesting twist on Not Tonight that I don't think worked out that well in the end, but I was still happy to support the devs and put in the relatively short number of hours required to beat this game

_childDocuments_.review: Not Tonight 2 is pretty good, but overall I think the first game is better.NT2 tries to do a similar story to the first game concerning nationalism and facism, but it's also a lot sillier and the constant tone shifts are much more jarring. There's a few parts that are genuinely disturbing but like, also sometimes you have to play a rhythm minigame to accept tickets or shoot wizards out of the air. Even putting that aside, the narrative feels much weaker. It's really unfocused in what it's trying to say. In general it's presenting a capitalist dystopia run by corrupt governments, but also your primary ally is... a megacorp. Who the characters seem to think runs the nicest city in the country. Huh??? There's more, but I won't spoil it.But going back to the minigames: if you found that NT1 was too repetitive, this game fixes that. You only work at a location for 2 nights before moving on, and each place has a different gimmick. The gameplay is overall tuned better than the first game. I never felt like I was facing a huge difficulty spike out of nowhere like I did on some levels in NT1. But moving around so much also means you don't get to know characters for as long as you do in NT1, which is a bummer.If you've never played a NT game, get the first. If you played the first and want more of the same gameplay, give this a shot, but maybe on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: The sequel that I didn't know existed, but glad it does. The game play is similar to the other game, but has a lot more added gimmicks that increase difficulty to an extent. I will say I am annoyed that their isn't any sort of free play or endless mode yet because replaying specific story chapters could get a bit tedious, but I can forgive it for that. While all the recent political references may date the game going forward I think it can still serve as a time capsule for the time period. I can see the political references turning some people off, but personally I don't think the game takes itself too seriously in the way it uses them. At specific points I will say that it becomes very clear that the game expects you to disagree with a majority of the old fashion boomer beliefs of the Martyrs, but like I said I don't think its that serious. It's a committed dark comedy that is supposed to make you think about what it would be like if the USA fell because of recent events and I can honestly say it is definitely one of the more unique stories I have seen in a while. _childDocuments_.review: Not Tonight 2 is a solid B+. I enjoyed it more than the original. The general gameplay loop is the same, clearly inspired by Papers Please, where you simply compare documents under ever-increasing rulesets.I felt that the original Not Tonight was too grindy. The gameplay loop rooted you to the same venue generally for five shifts straight. Rather than making me feel like it was perfecting my playstyle, I just got bored. I meant to go back and give it another go, but instead gambled on Not Tonight 2, and I'm glad I did. Any given "job" in NT2 is only repeated once before you're off to another location to learn a new mechanic. Even better, the mechanics don't always stack, so I never felt overwhelmed. The pacing was perfect, and I was hooked for the gameplay start to finish.The story is against the backdrop of the United States being split into warring factions, and it's heavy on political themes. It's also heavy on tropes and stereotypes in all directions, with even the main characters relegated to having a couple characteristics each and that's it. I didn't expect top-tier writing from Not Tonight 2, but I also didn't expect it to be that trope-heavy and cringy. It's fine as satire, but lacks any semblance of subtlety. If you're not the type to use the word "woke" unironically while blathering about who's ruining the country this week, I don't think you'll be upset at what you read here. I just don't think it'll provoke anything close to a thought during its entire playtime.Luckily, the gameplay, music, and graphics more than make up for the story's heavy-handedness. If you're on the fence about Not Tonight 2, I say it's worthy of a buy.

Also, added QuickTime events within dialog, testing memory and information collected along the way in your inventory. It has a board game feel to it, mixed with great characters from the original game and new ones too! The multiple perspectives of each of the main characters along the way really tie up the story beautifully. Almost as Beautiful as Sean Shawn Shaun's Singing.

_childDocuments_.review: What a strange game.I'm glad they tried to fix the problem the first game had with it being too repetitive by adding gimmicks but they went WAY overboard with the gimmicks. Most of them are decent but some of them are absolutely dreadful like the cult names or musical tickets. Also, having stats like morale and health for this type of game seems pointless.As for the story, it's just... bizarre. Stuff just randomly happens with little rhyme or reason. I like that there is dialogue choices but sometimes it just feels random as to whether or not it was the right decision. Playing as different characters between different roadtrips makes the story feel incoherent and a mess to put together especially since the game itself is linear.Overall, as someone who didn't enjoy the first game, I enjoyed this one more although that's mostly because this game frequently adds new gimmicks to prevent staleness. I wouldn't recommend this as a 'sequel' and more as a standalone experience. If you really want to play it, wait for it on sale as a small recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely do recommend NT2 to anyone that has played the original, but I think NT1 is a better game overall. NT2 both improved and regressed in certain areas - I did enjoy just how many locations you get to visit in NT2, with new mechanics for almost every job that you must complete. it kept it from feeling as grindy as the original, and all the pixel art was so beautiful! it also has great humor, just like the first. however, two of my favorite things about the original was the shop & the music, and I was disappointed by those things in NT2. I at first was intrigued by the concept of the quests and their purposeful vagueness, but it got really frustrating to not entirely control replenishing your health or morale(i liked the decision making of having to work or not in NT1). i missed having a house to decorate! it would have been cool if you could have bought stuff for your car(s). also, all of the music in NT2 felt rather same-y to me? in NT1 i really enjoyed the massive variance depending on the theme of the place you were in, even if i didn't enjoy the songs themselves, but in NT2 there were several moments in which i was confused by the song choice matching the location. yes, NT1 is more laborious to get through, but you feel more connected to the journey and more in control. i sense that it was perhaps the point to make NT2 feel more out of your hands, but after a certain point it goes past enjoyable for me and just feels unfair/tedious. I ended up doing ok with my first blind playthrough, but wouldn't say I enjoyed this game enough to return to (all of the dialogue quizzes/meh music/route taking just built up a lot) but I would definitely replay NT1. they're very different, and i'm still glad i played it, but not stoked with some of the changes they chose to make. regardless, you can see the love that went into this game! i loved the ending bit :)

_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Not Tonight 2 is such a stark improvement on the first game. There wasn't a single time that I felt disinterested in what was happening.The story was fantastic! It was a lot less despairing than the first game. It really leaned into a style that was a great mix of fun and disturbing, rather than downright depressing, and it really worked for it! I found it way more engaging to play as friends who were trying to help their friend escape rather than being entirely alone. The way all three roadtrips interweave with each other was perfect; the choice to make it a roadtrip rather than staying in one city was definitely an excellent choice. As a non-American, I found it was also nice to see different facets of America written into the story; each city was so unique and yet at the same time completely American. It really set it apart from the first game.Words can't describe how happy I am with how the gameplay was implemented in this game. In the first game, the mechanic was tedious and it felt like it was dragging of for the sake of longer content. Not Tonight 2 had a perfect balance of introducing new mechanics while also keeping the game fresh. I love that you only had to do 2 nights minimum per city because it felt like the perfect amount of time to learn a new mechanic and master it without wearing the player's patience thin. The pacing of the game was just sublime; I'm buzzing with how much I geniunely enjoyed it.The art style and music were more or less the same than the first same. Completely sticks to the overall theme, style and feel of the game, but nothing too standout. I really enjoyed the addition of the polaroid portraits though, as it gave the characters a face and made me feel more attached to them.Honestly, Not Tonight 2 is so damn good I would just skip the first game altogether (unless you really want to see the easter eggs). The devs really leaned into their own style with this game; anyone who loves this genre would not regret picking this one up!
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my first actually review of a game lol.***spoilers below***Overall 8/10The story is great, it's refreshing how they used separate characters but stayed within the same universe/style of Not Tonight.  I had a lot of fun playing this game and it was an amazing sequel to the first. Also, the soundtrack is way better than the first. The music goes along great with the venues you work in. Very minimal bugs, which is nice. I love playing games that are made by small developers and are done well. This game was extremely fun, with new and interesting challenges. Btw Dave is starting to grow on me.However, there are a few reasons that it's not a 10/10. I am not a fan how they took away customization. There is minimal customization to your character. Being that this is more of story driven game, I understand which is not a huge issue. I did miss not having an apartment to upgrade to take care of and so on. The one thing that really turned me off was when you hit the last road trip portion of the game. I understand the political satire of the Not Tonight universe (which is hilarious) which led me to buy this game. The first two road trips had a clear mission, and came along some awkward and funny situations that involved political satire. The last road trip, seemed to try harder on getting a political point across rather than being satire. It was over-the-top, to the point where it was not funny and straight bashing. The writer of that road trip makes it clear that they are extremely "left wing" and feminist. In the future I would like to see the political satire continue but staying within satire format. I play video games to have fun and to escape reality, not to live in it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the first game, then this is more of the same good quality entertainment. Fantastic music, great pixel art, fun characters and interactions, and a fairly addictive play loop that manages to change just enough every few nights so as not to out stay it's welcome. The game is simple but effective, where it chooses to throw new concepts individually at you rather than consistently add more and more onto the pile like Papers Please does. This makes it a lot more chill and 'easier' without too much of the Brain Hurty, but still fun.There are some cons, however. Some that are personal opinion, and some that are able to be fixed. The main few negative bits of feedback are:- Many Bugs. While my first playthrough was relatively painless, I've found on replays that I'm encountering multiple game breaking bugs. They're usually solved by quiting to desktop and restarting the night, but it gets frustrating when you need to keep restarting every 30mins to an hour and then having to replay the night because the game saves BEFORE the night, not AFTER it finishes. In the space of just under 3hrs of gaming while achievement hunting, I had to restart the game 4 times due to the same few bugs.- The night doesn't start until you press the clicker, which is great for prepping, except there's not a queue already waiting for you. This means you'll often find yourself standing around wasting 30 in game minutes waiting for your first customer to wander past, which is punishing on hard difficulty. Would be far better imo to have a people waiting from the start. Plus some processes are just unnecessarily slow and feel sluggish, such as when you defeat a robot, the system wastes several seconds on the animation before you can turn the away.- Speaking of slow animations, while I love the map and travel aspect of this game, the walking/driving between each point can be unnecessarily slow at times. You'll be travelling between states sometimes with nothing to do, just watching a small icon take 20-30 seconds to walk from one point to the next. This is more noticeable on 2nd playthroughs when you've already read all the texts and news.- While the different mechanics can be fun, the ones based solely on RNG (aka casino and robot fighting) can be unfair to the point of frustrating at points. The joys of this game for me are successfully managing and sorting through IDs, and the failures coming from your own mistakes, so to get the ID check right and then still get a warning for an RNG card pull or dice roll isn't rewarding, you're being punished for something beyond your power. On normal difficulty none of these are a huge issue, but on hard they become annoying. I also HATE the dance beat mechanic but that's personal opinion.Overall an amazing little game that I'd recommend to others, especially when it's on sale, just weighed down by a few minor issues that prevent it from being a full on favourite.
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent successor to the first game! The stories were well written and the characters were memorable with nice nods to the first game. I played through the game on hard, but still found the game mechanically very easy and never had a problem reaching the second bonus each night. My only complaint about this game is the inclusion of two RNG based minigames. While they have some way to mitigate the RNG, these were the only times I routinely had to restart a level (because I wanted perfect runs which are NOT necessary). I would prefer all mini games be skill based around our observation as a bouncer rather than observing correctly and having fate decide if I pass or not.Overall a solid game that I enjoyed exploring fully! Looking forward to any future entries to the series and loved the nod to the game's inspiration. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Not Tonight 2

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and as someone who finished NT, I enjoyed playing through NT2. Not Tonight 2 has a new different stuff but still keeping the same look and feel from the first one. One of the main elements, the various mini games makes each location feel distinct and challenging on their own instead of having more and more stuff to process. The road trip part fits in with the story and looks interesting having to move from one place to another while passing through some events and perhaps listening to some tunes. NT2 also has a bunch of characters both new and returning with the portrait look gives them a little bit of personality and uniqueness to each of them.Like the first one, Not Tonight 2 has that pixel art goodness from each location you work at and the character portraits. Each place has its mini game that makes it unique from each other and gives new challenges. However, as much as I like some of its soundtrack, they don’t feel as stand out as the soundtrack from the first one (which I often listen to at times). Some of the minigames can feel daunting and hard, especially the ones with RNG to them but after two times playing I learn to hang around.There are some things I missed from the first one, like the keyboard shortcuts and each place inside view both I like from the first game but seeing the game, I can see why they didn’t include them in which I’m okay with it. One thing that I love from the game that can be used in NT, is how you can wait before starting your day. It helps the player to review the rules of the gameplay and as a time to prepare.TL;DRNot Tonight 2 has lots of new features while maintaining its charm from the first one. Charming pixel art graphics and various mini games make playthrough enjoyable with different challenges. There might be things that are not as good, but I learn to enjoy them nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review:
In an alternative broken America, where capitalism and political greed have taken center stage, your friend has gone missing. Snatched during a protest, Eduardo Suarez has been seized by the authorities, and now sits ready for processing in the Miami gulag.

Not Tonight 2 is an American document-checking road trip, fusing a time-pressure RPG with a politically charged, dark comedy where every decision matters. Will Eduardo's friends Malik, Kevin and Mari manage to locate and deliver his documents to Miami in time, or is this the end of the American dream?

name: Demon's Mirror
detailed_description: Demon’s Mirror combines roguelike deckbuilding and a grid manipulation battle system to create a unique experience where Slay the Spire meets Puzzle Quest. Play as one of three trapped souls and embark on a treacherous journey where your worst nightmares lie in ambush! Collect new cards and gain power as you navigate an ever-changing labyrinth of increasing challenges to solve the mystery of the demonic mirror that trapped you here. Discover over 200 cards to create the ultimate deck! Select cards that grant special powers to deal heavy damage to your enemies or set up clever synergies and punishing combos. Get creative and experiment! Combining deckbuilding and chain-3 mechanics puts you in control of the battle! Collect and wield powerful cards to manipulate the grid and unleash devastating combos upon your foes while chaining tiles to attack, defend, gather resources or decrease your enemy’s power. The added complexity brings depth to traditional deck-building, providing a fresh and engaging experience. Encounter formidable enemies and unpredictable scenarios designed to test your wits. Hasty decision-making will lead to certain death. Only by mastering the strategic balance between playing cards and chaining tiles can you hope to survive! No two playthroughs are ever the same! Unique enemy encounters, items, and randomly dropped cards are generated with each run. Discover chance events where you’ll make interesting choices, meet strange creatures, and uncover hidden secrets about the world, ensuring near-endless replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: It's... alright.It combines two of my favorite genres into a competent, delightful package, but it just lacks that  factor that beckons "just one more round!"  The biggest issue I have is the ; fights can take , with some enemies buffing every round or making copies of themselves while you wait for  RNGs to line up: both your card draw and the board draw.  It's like a see-saw where you have the perfect board but none of the cards, or all your OP cards but a board of weak chains.  Eventually you have to start spending your resources instead of wasting turns and taking damage, and most rounds end up with you nickel-and-diming your way through battles instead of those rare occasions where it all lines up.The best feeling about match-3 games is getting killer chains, but they usually only amount to single-turn advantages in this game.  There's very little in the way of snowballing OP combos, and they usually take several turns just to set up because you're too busy dinking and diving just to stay afloat.There's some cool concepts and synergies to be found, but the three characters feel like one or two-trick ponies, making replay value scarce.  It feels a little barren content-wise, and I'd be surprised to see anyone but masochists with more than 20 hours.The game cribs from existing genres and combines them into something unique, but it's just not enough to sustain long-term interest.  It's definitely worth a shot if you're into this mash-up, but I'd wait until there's a sale.  I just found myself wanting to play other games instead of thirsting to jump right back in.

_childDocuments_.review: I already had a lot of fun with the demo and the full game doesn't disappoint. This is not just another slay the spire clone. It combines known elements from Puzzle Quest/Ironcast and Slay the Spire into something special. And most importantly - something fun! Your have to juggle between traditional card play and match 3 puzzles and many cards can manipulate the puzzle grid in interesting ways. It definitely deserves more attention than what it is currently getting.

_childDocuments_.review: I spent a few hours on the demo because I'm a huge sucker for roguelikes and Puzzle Quest/match 3. I *really* wanted to like this but I'm giving up on it.Cards don't feel interesting. Do X damage, or do X + 3 damage or turn these tiles into that tile. There are not many different kinds of tile manipulating cards.There's no mechanism for a board reset like what Puzzle Quest does. Sometimes you'll exhaust your supply of shield and then the enemy throws down a 1 turn hit you for 30 which means you're just gonna get sucker punched for a bunch.Speaking of enemy tiles, enemies love -- and I mean LOVE -- increasing enemy tile damage. Battles are frustrating because strong enemy tiles mean you're pretty much forced to either take a hit from an enemy, or take a hit from a tile. You don't have enough shield to do anything.The green tile is, imo, mostly useless. Some cards do extra damage if you have enough, but it decays off. In most cases they're junk tiles unless you have the card to make them into crystals.Crystals (willpower) are frustrating because enemies are constantly buffing themselves. Meanwhile your main non-card buff has a sharply increasing cost. So while enemies are free to constantly buff their damage tiles, you hit a point where you have to grab, like, 25 or so crystals for your next buff.Crystal buffs aren't that great. I chain together, what, 20 crystals and I get 3 peace (enemy tiles take 3 damage at the start of a turn). Cool. It took like 7 turns to put that together, and in the meantime the enemy buffed their tiles so now I have a 30 damage in 1 turn coming up. Cool.The game seems designed around the lizard because many enemies have counters if you attack them, but the lizard's attack (influence) doesn't count as damage. A good example is The Shell. Absolutely brutal if you're the wolf who only gets raw damage, but trival for the poisoner. Many enemies are like that.I think my biggest issue is that nothing comes close to that Good Build feeling in late StS. That feeling when It's All Coming Together, and you have your synergies. This game it's like, alright, Charged Fireball gains 3 damage every turn it's retained, and...oh hi there, three different damage tiles over 30. Hey game, you realize the board isn't growing, right? ...right?The art and sound effects are nice though.
_childDocuments_.name: Demon's Mirror

_childDocuments_.review: It's easy to mistake Demon's Mirror for just another Slay the Spire clone. It's not afraid to wear it's inspiration on its sleeve, for sure, but the interaction between cards and the match-3 board make for something special and unique. You can get really strategic in setting up combos, and you need to because each encounter is tough. I was a big fan of the original Puzzle Quest, using spells and abilities to manipulate the board, and this has some of that feel. Definitely not for everyone, but once you wrap your head around the mechanics, Demon's Mirror is super satisfying.
