_childDocuments_.review: Much more abstract than the first game by necessity, given the scale is much broader. A lot of reviews are thumbing down because of this, but what else could they have done? For a sequel they either would have needed to go much more micro in scale, or macro. Macro was the most natural evolution for the series.So far it's a bit easier as a result. It's completely possible that some wrench will get thrown into the campaign later on that upends everything, as often happens in FP1. But I'm kinda enjoying the fact that trial and error isn't so necessary here. In FP1, you absolutely had to know how and when certain disasters are triggered, not so much to ensure a win but rather to simply avoid losing. In FP2 intuitive planning is rewarded, and I'm enjoying this approach rather than simply failing a run and memorizing event triggers for the next attempt.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Great new take on the frostpunk series. Was hesitant at first as this one moves away from the smaller scope of the original. However, I've come to truly enjoy the new gameplay and larger scope of the sequel. I really enjoy the politicking required between many more factions in this one as well. I wish the story was longer and am hopeful they will release DLC as they did with the first installment. The utopia builder mode is great fun too despite not being a part of the story. Story sets you up to succeed in the end-gameplay of the utopia builder.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: This sequel serves as a modest evolution of the ideas and gameplay of the original. I do recommend the game. It fails to capture the emotional swells and tension of its predecessor, but it does create a very addicting loop of city-management.I have beaten the story mode on Officer, and I have 'beaten' endless on Steward difficulty. I have yet to tackle Captain difficulty, but I suspect after a couple tries - I'll conquer that too. This review will be a mixture of terrible opinions, bad advice, and feedback for the devs that they probably won't read. You've been warned.The original Frostpunk was like trying to steadily build a dam as a tsunami approached. This iteration is more like trying to protect a field of flowers, but a dozen children are running around with scissors trying to kill them all. If you are nice to the children, then sometimes they will support your proposals and not riot in the city. At the beginning of the game, you won't be 'stable' - and you'll race to the necessary technologies and exploration tools. You never have enough of anything, and raising funds makes you really unpopular. If you're playing story mode, then you 'should' get a stable economy by the first whiteout. By stable, I mean you are producing every resource in excess of what you consume. At this point, population growth just becomes a liability. Further, faction warfare will be your main threat. It will be compounded by events in the story, too. Assuming it's your first couple runs, you probably didn't push back on the radical factions steadily gaining popular support and council seats. Enjoy your punishment. Once that is resolved, story mode is finished. I'm oversimplifying, but that's the gist.If you're playing endless, then you spread as far as you can go. You can establish outposts and settlements to further your ambitions like story mode, but it's emphasized by the lack of alternative objectives. It usually takes me around 100 weeks to really stabilize. Faction control becomes much more important, as you need to keep the politics calm indefinitely. Radical factions steadily grow in population size throughout the course of a game - you need to beat them down (condemn / deradicalize) over and over. The most dangerous radicals in your city aren't the ones constantly protesting the direction the city is taking - it's the one growing to become a third of your population. When you import refugees from the frostlands, they have a dominant ethos - which can restore the moderates of your factions to healthier proportions of your city. The resource management, factions, and exploration are each simple mechanics, but taken together - can be quite complex.Factions can be cool, but I don't feel like I'm having any problems passing legislation in the council - even in the face of stern opposition. The AI doesn't know how to weigh policies appropriately - like Lords will vote for communal parenthood if I promise to build a patrol watchtower. As a result, with one or two promises - you can enact any legislation you like. And as a bonus, you get a trust bonus for satisfying those commitments. I've never felt like guided voting / propoganda were even useful tools to have. Balancing resources for multiple colonies, the main city, and settlements is tedious. The game really needs a resource overview, where I can quickly check that everything is positive in each of my communities without having to check each manually. However, once you have multiple balanced colonies sending each other complementary resources - it makes all that pain and suffering worth it. Very satisfying.My first playthrough in story mode was Progress focused, which is perfectly fine. But having played Endless on harder difficulties, Adaptation is clearly superior. Counter-intuitively, the bulk of your economy should come from the Frostlands - through settlements and colonies. An optimal central city is basically a bunch of housing districts and logistics. You want to minimize heat as much as possible, explore the Frostland rapidly, and all of that benefits from Adaptation significantly. Progress costs more heat, and produces more heat - but they're way harder to balance effectively. I'm not sure how to fix the disparity, but right now Adaptation just reaches a balanced economy with so much less work. Apex Workers, the cornerstone, everything - converges towards the late-game efficiency monster with Adaptation. In my endless run, I'm trying to see if I can turn off the generator and survive a white-out without any casualties. That's how busted it gets.Like the original Frostpunk, you'll need a failed run or two to get your bearings. Both games reward foresight and planning, so it's not unexpected. Game is fun, and I've enjoyed the process of trial and error.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Hits different from the original one. Can be difficult to learn even for a person who played the first one so much, but once you understand the dynamics and gameplay, the possibilities are huge. The nostalgia from the first one may affect your judgement on this one, but with time, it will become even greater than it's predecessor.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic and worthy sequel to Frostpunk 1, this game is everything i expected from the sequel and more, instead of making the same game and just slapping the number 2 on it 11 Bit Studios made a totaly new city builder that no other can compare to, with every update the game gets better and better, i truly can't wait to see what new DLCs will bring to the game. A 9/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: I love Frostpunk (1). I tried very hard to love 2. This is the only game I paid full price for on steam. I was waiting for this to be released and have no desire to play it as it is not the same as FP1. I went back and played FP1 after buying this and had way more enjoyment than I have with this release.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: I think Frostpunk 1 is one of the best games I have played, so I've tried very hard to like FP2. But I don't.It looks beautiful, but there are so many annoying parts in the game. Worst of all is the constant politics. This "feature" alone is enough for me to really not recommend this game to anyone.It's so sad. I had hoped to spend as many hours playing this as I did FP1. But I'm uninstalling it again now.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Should have been named something else other than "Frostpunk 2" as the expectation would have been a game similar to the original, such as the unique radial city builder of the original. The few things kept from the original is the frozen wasteland setting and story continuation after the fall of Winterhome. The story aspect which 11 bit studios laud themselves as their best aspect fell flat as a "society builder" is less intimate; there are names found in the council, but they are just names, they do not reflect the society being built. It simply does not have the staying power as the original Frostpunk does.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I was learning morse code to get a chance to play frost punk 2, so I can see for myself if the game is worth the 45 dollars. So, I obviously didn't learn morse code fast enough in time but I did get the steam code. Game performance is poorly optimized for the genre, which is a civilization city building game with moral and ethnic decisions. I can not recommend this game in its current state. I do like the laws and ethnic decisions, however, it's a shame that there isn't more laws or research for the game. Also, I do not like the fact that deluxe edition allow you to gain access to the game 3 days earlier. It seem like a cheap money trick just to get you to pay more for the game when in reality the content is not much even including utopia mode and future dlc. The game cannot handle your civilization surviving to the thousand week at all. After the patch, the game performance seem to gotten worse. Maybe, the dlc or patch can fix or change the game even more. Even then, this is a disappointing sequel compared to the first game.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: I've enjoyed it, though I was hoping for a little more from the story and more story play time. I will say it has some DirectX 12 shader issue that causes it to crash literally every time I play it, and losing time between an auto-save can be pretty frustrating. I really felt like this game company was going to be super impressive and put out a well-done, complete, seamless game - but yet again it feels like something that's half finished and still full of bugs. If you're interested in playing this game, I would wait until the price drop so its more worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: I've really enjoyed playing through FP2 and generally think that it evolves from FP1 in a positive way. Sure, its not as focused on individual people and the scale is much larger, but that makes sense within the world. You still get the feeling of powering through the whiteout and the experience of managing different factions and their needs is difficult but rewarding when done right. If you enjoyed the first, I recommend you try this one out with an open mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: What I love about Frostpunk 2 is that it doesn't cancel first installment, it actually is a natural expansion of that universe. If I want to play on micro scale - I can go with FP1, on the other hand if I want to play macro - FP2 is perfect for that. Top of my wishlist for FP2 was more involvement with frostland and that's what I got. I rushed little bit through story mode but that was still over 14hrs of gameplay and with how the game is designed I can honestly say I can get to 50hr on the story mode alone with different choices and outcomes.Being able to work on macro scale, explore frostland, deal with political issues - is very involving, so I don't assume I will get bore with FP2 anytime soon (I didn't get bored with FP1 at all tbh). As a cherry on top - building proper mood with an amazing sound design and recordings of live orchestra - THANK YOU!
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Good game but...A solid game that features many nods to the original, however fans of the first game might end up a little disappointed. I'll add a small caveat, that parts of the game are locked off, intended for additional playthroughs. The game is missing that gritty element that made Frostpunk what it was. Gone are the tough decisions that forced you to choose how your city moves forward (with the exception of one chapter). For those that played the first game picture this scenario: You have a stockpile of coal but it is about to get colder, you haven't yet researched suitable tech to help keep your workers healthy away from the generator. What do you do? Persevere, knowing some may not survive or see if you can outlast the weather before your stockpile runs out?Decisions like that are no longer a part of the game, or at least play such a minor part that they are barely noticeable.The artwork and lore remain fantastic. 11 Bit Studio's have done a phenomenal job expanding the landscape and the various points of interest you will encounter.Frostpunk built a reputation for being a grim and challenging game, it's your city vs the elements, with a strong emphasis on resource management and decision making, but it just isn't there any more. If you love the game and want to support the dev's buy it, otherwise wait until a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the first game, it was a gem, something unique, something intimate. Struggling to save your small group of people against all the odds. I didn't want FP2 to be exactly the same, that would be dull, but expected the sequel to evolve and keep the essence which made the first game a success, as most developers do, but...11 Bit thought it would be a great idea to strip away pretty much everything that made the first game so special and turn Frostpunk 2 into some sort of numbers game, a visual spreadsheet if you will. I don't care about the people any more, why should I, they are just a number in the top left of the screen.Politics takes a front seat and so now the citizens are just cannon fodder while factions fight for power. Most of your time is spent fulfilling objectives and then just waiting for something to happen, some text will pop up, you read it and you don't care. Nothing really seems to have any impact.Disappointed is an understatement.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: A Masterpiece of Strategy and SurvivalAt first, I found myself a bit confused by the tutorial and was missing some of the older animations from the original game, but now, after completing the game, I fully understand the scale and depth this game offers. It’s an absolute 15/10 experience.The game is a fantastic continuation of the first, with a gripping tone that expertly blends emotions, stress, and careful planning, especially on the maximum difficulty level. The management and micro-management systems are nothing short of brilliant—every decision feels meaningful, and the level of control you have over your city’s fate is both exhilarating and terrifying.The graphics and atmosphere are stunning, pulling you into the cold, desolate world in a way that few games can. There’s also plenty of lore from the first game, which enriches the story and makes it even more engaging for returning players. The seamless integration of lore ties Frostpunk 2 to its predecessor beautifully.With around 11 hours of gameplay (at least for me), it offers a deep, satisfying experience that's well worth the money. If you loved the first game, or if you're new to the series but enjoy challenging strategy and survival games, Frostpunk 2 is a must-play. It’s a shining example of how a sequel can build upon and elevate an already incredible game.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute gem, all the events, the writing, the intricate systems that work so well with each other, I'm on Chapter 4 and it's been amazing so far, only negative thing I would have to say is that performance goes down by a lot (and mind you I have an RTX4090 & i7-13700k) when your base starts to get bigger.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: With each passing minute spent in the game, it becomes more and more engaging. Of course, it's not the same type of game as Frostpunk 1, but because of that, we get the chance to experience something new. For me FP2 is incredible and highly addictive. I have great respect for the developers for not taking the easy route by simply tweaking the original game, but instead choosing the risky path and following their vision for the sequel. I haven’t finished the entire campaign yet, but I can’t wait for the Utopia Builder and the mods. The only thing I really don’t like is the not-so-useful tutorial, also known as the prologue. I understand that many people might get confused or lost playing it. Give it a try. I truly believe that 11 bit has delivered another extraordinary game.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: As a masochist I'd call it a very enjoyable successor.------------------------------------------------------------------------------------After playing a while longer I did notice some drawbacks hence the edit. First off I do agree with the existing critique of the game not feeling as personal or "up close" as the first one did. But in my opinion that's not necessarily a bad thing since Frostpunk 2 is a different game with focus on other aspects. We're beyond the times where the survival of each and single one mattered, we're now in a time where the only thing that matters is the survival of city itself. It's about politics, about power. It's about who shapes this city in their image. So it's more a continuation of the lore and of the story, not just a plain successor that tries only to refresh the gameplay loop with newer graphics and one or two new game mechanics.The game does try to explain this (could be better tho) and like I said I get that it can be disappointing if that's the aspect you enjoyed most in the first part.I do agree with the devs could have focussed more on how the impact of laws and technical development of the city is portrayed other than just placing buildings with different names or a text pop-up once in a while tho. I'd love to see more consequences to different laws and decissions.I read a review of someone saying the music isn't as good as in the first one and that it just doesn't hit as hard anymore and at first I agreed but then I did give the soundtrack a listen and it does still has character and impact. So what I think causes this effect is that the music has moved much further into the background than in the first part and therefore loses a lot of it's effect.Lastly lots of people complaining about the UI. Well.. I guess it's a matter of taste. Surely there's room for improvement but imho it's not that horribly bad. Yes it takes a second to fully understand but then it works totally fine for me - nothing special there.All in all I think it's a good game. There's still room for improvements but as of right now I'm enjoying it a lot. So yeah besides all still a thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Frostpunk 2 brilliantly expands upon the hauntingly beautiful world established in the original game. As a sequel, it elevates the survival city-building experience to new heights, seamlessly blending moral dilemmas with strategic depth.From the moment you step into this frozen post-apocalyptic landscape, you're greeted with stunning visuals and a gripping narrative that pulls you into the struggle for survival. The art direction is nothing short of breathtaking, capturing the bleak yet awe-inspiring environment that defines Frostpunk. Each decision feels weighty, impacting not only your city but also the lives of its inhabitants.The gameplay mechanics have seen significant improvements. The new systems for resource management and technological advancement offer fresh strategies to explore, making each playthrough feel unique. The introduction of new factions adds layers of complexity, forcing you to navigate intricate political dynamics while keeping your citizens hopeful amidst despair.What truly sets Frostpunk 2 apart is its ability to challenge players emotionally. The tough choices you face—balancing hope and despair, survival and sacrifice—are thought-provoking and linger long after you’ve put the game down. The narrative depth, coupled with the atmospheric soundtrack, creates an immersive experience that is both engaging and reflective.Overall, Frostpunk 2 is a remarkable continuation of a beloved franchise, blending rich storytelling with compelling gameplay. Whether you're a returning player or new to the series, this sequel is a must-play for anyone who appreciates a well-crafted challenge in a beautifully grim setting. It’s not just a game; it’s an experience that will stick with you. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything that I wanted! It has the same vibe as the last one but everything is turned up to 100 and more about the different types of humans that now live in your city. Only just finished the long yet amazing story and can't wait to go back and see how making different choices change things. 10 out of 10 and played it all on the Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: I am so disappointed. I cannot even bring myself to play it much more than an hour. Oh no a macguffin ran out, get a new macguffin.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Very different game from Frostpunk - but give this a chance. Absolutely tense/suspenseful experience trying to keep your city and outposts together, tensions down, political factions from rioting, all while fighting a doomed battle against the cold while an incredible soundtrack plays to it all.Just finished my first play through - the city survived but at what cost?
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, but feels little bit unfinished. I would like some better access to menus, for example, I would like building options of structures by clicking on an empty spot. Story wise, the game is also fine, but it feels like it could be expanded, there is a lot of artificial conflict, and I would expect the issues to rise when something doesn't work, not that people will complain when everything is running smoothly. I hope they will be some continuation of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: I fell in love with Frostpunk, like trudging across a barren wasteland warmed solely by hope only to suddenly crash thru thin ice. Waking up dazed in the bottom of a cavern, snow stinging my face as it fell down, whether to wake me or taunt me, the nightmare never ended. With Frostpunk 2 I didn't feel any of that. I worried about balancing resources and putting out fires, but there was never that heart wrenching, trauma bonding alike the first. Whether this is due to sequels always in the shadow of their progenitor, the macroscopic view this game sits in versus the micro view of the first (effectively districts vs buildings, factions vs citizens), my heart having withered in the time between, or any other reasons I am unsure, but I find myself wholly underwhelmed.FP2 is a beautiful yet under-optimized game - after 2 hours I had to crank my settings down from high to low and even then saving was a painstaking 30 seconds of wondering if the game was about to crash, though it never did. It is feature rich yet mechanics become repetitive. It has an infinite world of story telling yet easily ignored characters.I was expecting to spend time with a stiff drink or five while playing the story, which turned out to be all of ten hours, but seltzer sufficed. I was expecting to love this game as I did the first, but now it sits on my virtual shelf as just another city builder and I mourn that. It is good and well executed and I do recommend picking it up, but venture into the wastelands to scratch an itch, not to find a new home.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic follow up to Frostpunk, but keep in mind this is not a traditional city builder. It's much more of a strategy/4X/grand strategy style of game. There's a deep layer of politics, and the scale is way bigger than the original game. Expect a constantly shifting power dynamic while you struggle to expand New London and thrive!
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: I gave it a 2nd try after getting a refund for the pre-order early access. After 11 hours this game is still not enjoyable. Maybe some will find the less micro, more decision based game play entertaining. But I don't, the city building is wonky and almost just should be removed, imo. I understand what the intention was to make things more focused on bigger city management scale. Again, hopefully others will find it enjoyable. But the experience is nothing like the 1st one. I am really sad to have to write this as the first one, is one of my favorite games of all time.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Short summaryFinished the "tutorial" and storymode after 6 hours. Game ctd two times, UI is hard to understand in the beginning (and even at the end you're searching and don't know how to do some things), because you have to find all on your own, almost nothing is explained. But you can press "T" and read a tutorial, most of the time.The differences to the first part are so significant that it can no longer be called Frostpunk 2. It's a different game in the same universe. The whole setting, UI and the handling of the population and problems have changed a lot and have become very indifferent to the individual fates. It hardly bothers you anymore if 100-200 inhabitants die here and there. You still have a few tens of thousands left. With Frostpunk 1 in mind, my expectations of the game were largely disappointed. Hope they will add(/fix) some content, otherwise it is a bit meh for that price. For now it's okish but not worth it tbh. First Frostpunk was more fun.Recommended, but not for the full price. Wait for a discount or get it cheaper elsewhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Fundamentally this is a good game, perhaps not the same genre as the first title but still very enjoyable.However the UI/UX is a steaming pile of dog s**t. switching between settlements is buggy as hell, "abandon city" button has no confirmation and easily can be clicked on by accident; good luck finding a specific building add on; turniing on/off districts is a such hassle and a regression from the one button click in the first game; the new pathway system is counter intuitive, not visibly clear which segments can be reused; also dismantling a building add-on during construction will just put it in limbo forever you wont get those resources back(pretty sure its a bug) the list goes on...General performance can be improved as well but not a huge issue atm.I'm hopeful the devs will address those issues in due time, until then this review will stay negative.*edit*latest 1.1 patch resolved a lot of these issues and improved performance, massive step forward in the right direction, its looking good!
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the story in regular and captain mode and had a lot of fun while being extremely frustrated at points. Forstpunk 2 is not going to make you solve the problems you already did in the first one and comes up with new very challenging(specially in captain mode) and smart problems for the player to solve. I recommend this game for the fans of the first one with the caveat of knowing this is a completely different game with different challenges but somehow scratches the same itch in my brain.My biggest criticism is that the game runs really poorly. Major performance issues from chapter 5 on with almost 5 second hitching between your clicks(I have a 4070 and the hitching never stopped). The captain mode is supposed to be a challenge but in chapter 4 and 5  turns into a bit of nonsense due to many bugs and must happen events and requires many tries that feels completely unfair. I hope the game will be worked on and the performance issues are ironed out as I only endured it because I really enjoy the game and could imagine many players being turned off by these issues completely.There are many Utopia scenarios as well as the main story which are many more hours of play and fun. It is worth the money in my opinion but this game needs more work. Anyways I hope this helps.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: While the setting is cool, the game feels a bit underbaked. While the scale is cool and all, I feel more disconnected from the inhabitants of the town than something unimmersive like civ6. Camera controls are also a bit weird. You cannot zoom neither close in nor far out. Some gameplay mechanics seems buggy. Perhaps after a few patches it will be worth a revisit.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: It's not meant to be a Frostpunk 1 with improvements, I got it. But it feels an overwhelming experience because nothing is intuitive. You don't know what are your buildings unless you click them. The voting system is ok, but I'm feeling like I'm always there to please those who don't agree with something, and if I'm going agains it, I feel like there's no downside at all!The researching system is a mess. People seek to some research, but the game don't show that the f*** is the research, and you just agree with going with it without even knowing what that is, even if it is against the kind of ruler you're trying to be. You're just rolling a dice and if it's not what you want for your run, you can't restart de scenario. You have to accept it and the downsides of "your decision" or restart THE WHOLE CAMPAIGN!!! It sucks the fact that you have to play that many times just to memorize every research name just to make a promise that fits into your way of ruling.Frostpunk 1 still miles away from this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: I think my experience of Frostpunk 1 has lead to a disappointing playthrough of the 2nd. The game feels underwhelming & a few steps back in a few ways, especially when considering it took 3 years for them to design an entirely new game & mechanics that lack the soul the first game had.Bigger doesn't always mean better unfortunately, I miss being able to see your citizens actually trudging through the snow, slowly making a permanent path, the automatians from the first game seem to have vanished, buildings are all generic and all look the same only being identifiable by the 1 of 4 colours they will be, the new buildings hex system is a step backwards, it also seems that now ai operates the generator in the frost punk future as it's very limited in it's management settings & heating districts/ areas hardly even feels like a part of the game now with how the new heat & generator system work. I do not however hate the game, I did enjoy some aspects of it that made it feel more complex & fleshed out, like the council system, building new settlements & trade routes through the frost land however my biggest gripe with the game is that the last expansions of Fp1 introduced new mechanics & ideas that made the game feel more personal, complex & enjoyable & I think myself and a large part of the community wanted those aspects of the game to me further explored & expanded on but this was not the case.I think you'll enjoy Fp2 if you  haven't played the first however with that being said currently the first game is more fun so go buy and play that instead while it's on sale for dirt cheap and maybe one day after a lot of updates this game will meet expectations fans have for what the game should / could have been.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: i don't know how i feel about this game, its definitely not like FP1. everything is more simplified and more complicated at the same time.  everything that mattered in FP1 doesnt matter in FP2. everything that made FP1 amazing isnt in FP2. this is more of a city management and politics game.  dont need roads, dont need hunting huts, ect. need space to build stuff no problem!  FP1 is my all time favorite city builder survival game. this game isnt terrible but i wanted a FP2 not a civilization game. so if your anything me and really liked Frostpunk 1 you'll probably be decipointed  in this one.

Sometimes I want to just clear a few and leave spots snowy to mark as reserved for future tech/expansion.Transferring people between locations uses a slider; no manual input nor +X buttons.Graphics look fuzzy and almost 2-D, regardless of zoom level.Story leaves me cold so far, but in a bad way.Not recommended at this time

_childDocuments_.review: The first run through is very fun but the game is too repetitive to be fun after that. Once you have learnt the mechanics, there is very little to be excited about. I am hoping the DLCs add more mechanics. At the moment, this game combines an economy game and political sim, while not implementing either well. I imagine the devs did this to try and appeal to the largest player base possible, but all this has done has made a game that is fun for everyone for a few hours, and boring afterwards.On a separate note, the OST is very good, and the way the UI changes as the tension in the city changes is very cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: A little rough around the edges (random autosaves pausing the game, one crash that lost me a half hour of progress) and definitely different than the first game (less micromanaging, focus away from heat/survival onto politics) but had the same effect on me as Frostpunk 1 ha ha. Once I started story mode, I basically played non-stop and got super invested in the outcome of my population. I think having played the first one made my experience better.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend. This is a worthy sequel to FP1. The first 30 mins were the hardest - to adapt to the gameplay changes from FP1. Then got to enjoy the player choices, narratives, and city and regional build and networking more more.Likes: 1. I really liked the musical and soundscape. 2. The continuation of the FP1 story, linking to locations and narratives.3. Laws have more variety and multiple settings with costs and benefits. Can get a law passed, then change your mind and repeal it or do the opposite of it later to please a faction.4. Balancing the different factions was actually an enjoyable challenge. I liked the roleplaying of this.5, City building was more macro - quite different to FP1, but could experiment with different set ups of district adjacency bonuses, hubs and minimising squalor.6. Game pacing was quite good - challenges made sense to advance story line.7. The six competing philisophy/ideologies was quite thoughtful. It was a fun to pick a faction to champion, while liking some of their ideology but not others, and sometimes take the direction of a different faction for key decisions and swing back. I liked the simulated interactions dilemmas.8. Can't please everyone all the time. Choose your battles, choose what problems to solve and what costs to accept.9. I liked there were more resources/metrics like squalor, consumer goods. These added more interesting dilemmas. I liked that there can be a deficit but not nil, and over time the problems this causes.10. Visuals were quite good. Liked the art design of the people, story, still images, animations, views of the city. Moving around, looking at the models. Not that bothered with the zoom in of a district, doesn't reveal much.Dislikes:1. This game was released quite recently. There are still some UI fixes to do.2. Linking Frostland back to New London was not explained well. After I figured it out I was OK, but wasted resources learning on failed play throughs.3. Having to pre-frostbreak terrain. I found this a bit tedious. Could at least remove the need for this if expanding a district.4. It wasn't clear how to do some actions required of the challenges. For example I only discovered by clicking on the central district how to use some authority measures, and other buttons were not obvious or intuitively located. For example, the use of guards.5. When exploring Frostland, wasn't always obvious where the new discoveries were, no pointers off screen to the direction needed.6. need more sound and visual cues when something happens or is changed - ie research idle, idle Frostland teams, resource exhausted, squalor debuff, or why something happened. In FP1 when people pass, can find out how and try to prevent it. Not so clear here. I guess it will get better.7. The game pauses when there is an autosave. This is quite disruptive, but at least the music continues.8. the intensity of a buff or debuff wasn't always well explained, or made sense. Something a debuff would make sense to add but was absent and only buffs.9. Saw in another review that the larger scales has less connection to simulated individuals. I guess the game devs tried to add indivuality to council member but I didnt think much of whether a character has some secret hobby, but if they are going to vote for my proposal or not.Other Thoughts:This game reminded me of a bit of a choose your own adventure. There is a guided sandpit where how you solve the problems are up to you. There are usually costs and benefits to decisions and there is more sub decisions and variety than FP1.I assume many quality of life fixes will patch in, and this game will get better, with more replayability and expansion of content. There are hints of possible expansions in main story.Overall 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of in-game bugs and issues, like adaptive generator not being able to priortise which resources to use 1st to last. Some issues here and there with long wait times while the game is being saved. Being a lover of Frostpunk and wanting to support the company, I pre-ordered the deluxe edition for this Frostpunk 2 which comes with DLCs that is to be released... but this game is disappointing in its current state, and I cannot with good heart recommend it at this time. I believe lots of resources that could have been used to expand the game with DLCs, may have to be dedicated to fixing the base game, and that would means a delay of DLCs being released too. Overall, not recommended at this time. =(
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: I seriously cannot understand all positive reviews for this game. Frostpunk 2 is even without comparing it to the 1st game very... Flat and plain unfair. Somehow in F2 during the whole campaign no matter what I did I was always lacking something. Almost no endless resources and even if they are they are literally like single tile. Which is completely useless. I only beat the campaign because after I completely failed 1st attempt

_childDocuments_.review: The game is solid, its currently at time of review got a instability issue, I've had the game crash more often than I've closed it.Secondly the UI could have important things jump out at you better, too often will you miss that you can pass a law or start a research becasue all you get is a tiny little diamond that pops up, if your focused on something else you can easily overlook even the banner that pops up to inform you a research is complete, I think going the way FP1 went with a large satisfying CRUNCHY ice sound when law o clock as arrived. Demand my attention becasue so many other things in the game already do i know my researchers deserve more attention than the Lords do.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: They did it again!No, this is not Frostpunk 1. I, too, found myself missing Frostpunk 1 while playing this game. It wasn't until I completely finished the story campaign and started playing Utopia mode that I got the same stressed, how do I make my people happy, every-second-matters feeling that I loved so much in the first game. Which to me, is SO fun! This sequel is magic on its own and I recommend if you loved the first one, to really give this one a chance and not be sad that its not more of the original. They somehow managed to make an entirely new game but hold onto the elements that made the first one so addicting.I'm certain I'll be putting many more hours into both games for years to come, and now I have two great ways to explore the Frostpunk universe!My only negatives are there are some audio bugs, minor performance issues, and minor UI issues, but they've already been releasing updates to fix them, and I'm sure everything will be addressed soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was torn.When I launched the game and started playing, it felt very different from the first one and much more complex. I almost gave up. Then, with some free time, I decided to give it another shot. After playing for 2 hours... wow! What a surprise! The game is absolutely brilliant. Engaging, challenging, and I have no regrets! The developers deserve a lot of praise for having the boldness and courage to make a sequel with such a different approach. It’s fantastic! This isn’t like most sequels where they just add a few improvements. This is a completely new game, with new mechanics. The developers should be congratulated. This game is a must-play! Try it, you’ll LOVE it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a veteran of FP1 i ll just leave an early review here with some first thoughts.So far the game left me with a bit of a cold heart.I feel that my decisions dont matter at all.I dont care of what i ll press and which factions to please anymore.Population is just a number on the screen to send out of the city into the new collonies.Your city is playing now a secondary role, since its dependant solely on the colonies for most of the resources.The game cannot convince me at this state, to really care about it. About my city, nor its people.I might change my thought as i am progressing through the game. I m now on the 4th chapter and i didnt drop it because i payed 70 euros for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the mechanics in the first Frostpunk. the mechanics in Frostpunk 2 feels like a cheap knock off of civilizations with snow with the districts and tile based format. _childDocuments_.review: That is much less as city builder game like Frostpunk 1. You do not build roads between buildings anymore, just are supposed to place them on hexagonal fields after destroying the ice on the ground to do so. Also do not need to worry about heat or sickness that much. But there are new things that you need to take an eye on like goods, materials or degradation. Gameplay feels much different with similar design, but I am glad, that they've decided to take on experience and create something new instead of making everything the same as in Frostpunk 1 with some additions. 20 hours of adventure which i've enjoyed, now waiting for dlc.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished my first playthrough. This game is brilliant and waaay better than first one unless you are Sims player. What I love about Frostpunk is making hard decision and managing resources. All this was way way better in FP2.Moreover:1. First playthrough took me 10 hours. I guess I did way too much exploration and expansion than needed but I didn't have to reload or start over. No ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ way people finished story in 5 hours on first try. They had to be playing on baby difficulty which is completely against what this game is about.2. I see many people writing that they didn;t care about their people as much as in 1. How the ♥♥♥♥? I guess they had to really zoom in annd read names and remember names of their cute little citizens. Not me. City must not fall. _childDocuments_.review: I had so much hope for this game. Keep in mind, I am writing this review after one hour of play time. Unfortunately it is a distant shadow of the original and it feels like it's just not what it could be. I don't know exactly what I was expecting, but the city building feels unsatisfying because it's not a hub anymore. You just build districts on pre-determined spots and the rest is for houses... I guess? The law system has either been removed or changed to the point that I don't recognize it. (What fun is it if you can't put the kiddos to work on day one? lol) I couldn't find how to research, but maybe that comes later in the game. Some people might really love this game, so give it a shot if you like, but just don't expect the magic that was FP1. It's much more like a generic city builder where sometimes people freeze to death. I'll watch the reviews as time passes and maybe give it another shot when the DLCs come out.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite underwhelming. Meaningless emo videos which try very hard to make you feel something without building characters or telling a story. Over-engineered graphics which focus on spectacle instead of communicate game mechanics. Speaking of game mechanics - they are extremely basic to non-existent: shove snow, build resource thingy and some house stuff. Then some overly dramatized "decision" cards with pre-created events you basically have no influence over. The sounds of breaking is are quite nice, but become repetitive quickly as they, too focus on spectacle instead of game. This is a mobile game in UE5 engine which fails to create the illusion you are doing anything important.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Just finished story mode, and I really enjoyed it. If you played the first one in my opinion its basically Frostpunk one but Simcities. Bigger scale, districts with adjacency buffs like Simcities and Civilization 6. But the world, decision making, darker tone, and story is still there from the first game. A lot more of a focus on the people you are guiding and trading too like one of the shorter stories from the first game. The decision making and groups I think is the best part of the game.For the most part I like the changes, some changes to resources, ui, and especially performance late game. But I wouldn't say it's a MUST have like the first game.

_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, let me just say I'm an absolutely fanatical worshiper of Frostpunk 1. As a fellow Pole, I'm proud that the members of the development team are locals. I love the amount of work you put into the first game, the style and the post-apocalyptic setting is something that captured me for the most part. But when it comes to the sequel, there are some cons I find are needed to be shed light on.1. The blurFrostpunk 1 is absolutely crisp, well-optimized and has a coherent color and atmosphere theme which is present throughout. The issue I want to raise is the fact that FP2 seems to have a permanent blur filter, which basically makes the individual buildings and environment look like a blob. I thought at first that the DLSS could have something to do with it, or other graphical settings, but having spent a while tinkering around with the settings, the graphics still look subpar, not to my expectations.2. Individuals and automatonsWhat I adored about the prequel is the ability to trail a citizen walking around the city. They would huddle up at the generator, march on to work, or go to the mess hall. It just made sense. In FP2 implementing such a feature would require way more processing power since we're talking about tens of thousands of people, and not merely a couple hundred. Still, I'm not a fan of the frostbreakers disappearing randomly, or automatons just 'poof'-ing into thin air when the camera is positioned a certain way (it would happen when the camera was positioned in the most horizontal angle and would be moved over the models). I believe it could be made better, for example, with models disappearing when they're not in view.3. The musicFP1 had, in my opinion, the most beautiful, suiting, dark orchestral arrangement than any other game, that would essentially play endlessly. It could get boring after a while if you played the same scenario hours on end (extreme difficulty). BUT, with the expansions and new pieces, my ears were very happy and I felt a part of the game. I find it lacking in FP2. There is, of course, music that plays at times, just not enough. Or, it may just be not as noticable. You could add a frequency setting to how often the symbolic violin soloist (if you know, you know) plays. Still, the above-mentioned don't make the game unplayable, though there is room for improvement. I'm sure you will take as much feedback from the reviews as possible.I believe in you guys

_childDocuments_.review: Frostpunk 2's user interface feels overly complicated and cluttered compared to the streamlined design of the first game. The shift away from the neatness of the original makes it difficult to understand what’s happening at times, with too much filler content. Some research options appear across multiple tabs, causing confusion, and there’s a noticeable lack of quality-of-life features like the ability to cancel construction. Additionally, heat continues to be consumed even when a district is turned off, which feels counterintuitive. The six-slot district system seems like a questionable design choice, though it’s not my main issue. While I love the direction the game has taken, the execution feels lacking, with clutter and disorganisation detracting from the experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews, but this game just does everything right for me. I'm a big fan of Frostpunk 1 but I found the amount of systems you had to keep in check a bit complicated.This game takes everything from the prequel which was amazing:- Great Story- Good Narratives- Amazing Design- WOW feelingtakes away the finnicky systems and replaces them which a much simpler set of systems. I just finished my first playthrough and am definitely going to start a second where I take a totally different route. Am curious as to how different that will feel.I recommend this game to all who loved the first and everyone who wants a citybuilder-survivor with an amazing narrative and setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fantastic. It sounds like people complaining that it's not Frostpunk should maybe just load Frostpunk. We complain that companies like EA provide $70 data updates every year with Madden and FIFA, yet when 11 Bit Studios take a hugely ambitious risk -- because let's be honest they could have just "evolved" the first game -- many of you b*itch and complain. Frostpunk II is a sprawling macro-based upgrade to the beautiful micro-based first game that too was a masterpiece of innovation. This is the logical next step and fair play to them for not lazily banking on a sure thing and by giving us something different.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Set 30 years after Frostpunk 1, I feel it's a worthy successor to the original, it loses some of the intimacy but does what I think a sequel needs to and expands the scale of everything. You build whole districts instead of single buildings, you make multiple colonies and share resources between them. Laws require a little scheming with factions to pass. The main story took me 10 hours on a single successful first run. I played slow and overbuilt, overpopulated, by the time I got to the end I barely escaped mass starvation but had a good ending. The game achieved the same sense of urgency as the original, after almost 10 hours I believe I was down to about 10 minutes before I would lose, I was extremely close to trust (hope as it was in 1) hitting zero. I did everything I could to stay in power long enough to finish the final objective and win.Eager to see what the future brings in terms of DLC, though If I had to pick a game to replay between 1 and 2, it would be 1.Something about the smaller scale of the original and the general story just pulls me more. Those early days of seeing your people physically push through the deep snow, and that sense of "humanity is gone, your few dozen people are almost all that's left" just adds a more immersive experience.In Frostpunk 2 you don't physically see any people, everything is built up and warm and grand scale. Heat is not a problem unless you completely run out of fuel, your districts are snow free and have their own generators like it's nothing. The heat challenge and the pressure of the original is lost in this one. But this is a  minor gripe and is understandable as New London has survived 30 years at this point.Overall though...Frostpunk 1, 9.8/10Frostpunk 2, 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately as a long-time fan of the original Frostpunk game who had jumped on the pre-order early, I was disappointed on trying Frostpunk 2 that they had dropped the original gameplay style to go for something less directed and personal and more bland. I ended up refunding the game due to it not matching my expectations.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: A vast improvement in many ways to the first game. I've been a huge fan of Frost punk for a long time. Ill be the first to admit I went into this game thinking I would'nt enjoy it because I was expecting Frost punk 2 as in the same as the first game but expanded. I however was pleasantly surprised, after multiple failed attempts I managed to finish the story and what a ride it was. The scale compared to the first game is what hooked me, having a population of over 60K and fighting to keep the city alive near the end was super immersive and I was invested. The music building tension as the city crumbles over warring factions, you as the steward or in my case the Captain battling desperately to hold on just a bit more. But once all the warring is over you can achieve serenity and watch you society function. It is truly an amazing game and I seriously enjoyed this next entry. I am hoping to see some DLC content to add new maps and districts or hub buildings. I am already playing the end game utopia mode and having a blast. I highly reccomend the game to anyone new or returning to Frost Punk but I would also say play the first game before this to see how they both play and see what I mean.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Where the original frostpunk was an 11/10, this game is a solid 7.5/10, which is still good, but not great or amazing anymore. The orginial frostpunk excelled at everything. They got it all right, the building mechanics, the story, the little details of the story you discover the frostland, the music, the vibe, the feel of your city, just barely scraping by, seeing your atomatons at work. This frostland does it all, too, but less good. There are no more mysteries to uncover on the frostland map, its all just resources, how lame!!! In the original game there was wonder and mystery everywhere, here the map sucks! In the original frostpunk you could see how your city expanded and changed, industrialized; here, although the scale is larger, you dont feel your city anymore. The story, in the original frostpunk you felt the cold, here you dont feel much.The only thing that FP 2 does better, is the political voting system. Thats cool, but even faction conflicts and dilemmas are things FP 1 did waaay better. Maybe wanting to feel what you felt the first time is always an illusion. Maybe sequels can never surpass their original versions. I dont know. But Frostpunk didnt live up to Frostpunk 1, its just okay.In Summary:While Frostpunk 1 was a shocking story full of awe, wonder and horrer, a story that fully immersed you and made you invested in it; Frostpunk 2 feels more like a techdemo, clearly, the talented writing team was fired, because it lacks substance, story - soul.
_childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: I played the first game, loved it, and am loving this one too.A lot of negative reviews are worried about the game loosing its personal touch and constant feeling of doom, I feel like while yes, the game is on a much grander scale, it is still scary and personal. The sound design is great, voice lines very immersive, and it looks amazing. I think the game is a natural successor to the first one. I feel the economy and building system is not very intuitive nor explained well, but once you understand it it is very satisfying. Love the way politics has been added in, feels very in tune with the rest of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not the frost punk i was looking forward to. _childDocuments_.name: Frostpunk 2

_childDocuments_.review: Frostpunk 2 is a great pretender. A pretender of depth where there is none. The game is shallow, perhaps even shallower than frostpunk 1 was. The art:10/10Music and graphics and effects are all top-tier, nothing to complain about. I did notice a lack of diveristy in the music not seen in 1. Weird.The story: 1/10 Worst part IMO - Sometimes feels nonsensical. I could be a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ steward making ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ decisions, or literally build a utopia - The outcome is the same - always two radically opposing factions form, that never support you. Along the way one of those parties tries to gain power, which you of course grant, because a democracy in a survival situation makes no sense, and then you watch as the other party becomes straight up terrorists that bomb your buildings, protest all the time, etc.The story is completely unconclusive and doesn't feel as good as frostpunk 1's ending did - ESPECIALLY the storm. The storm in 1 was that "one-final-effort" push and after, a promised redemption.Here? You just press some buttons the game tells you to press, it gives you a title screen and essentially tells you the game is over. Nothing after. No environmental danger, just societal collapse as the danger, which of course doesn't happen because you can just kill/jail the opposing guys.  The story rewrites the ending of FP1 (still turbo winter, even after the storm) as well - which is cringe.Difficulty design: 3/10 There is no point in Trying to feed, heal, heat your people. You ALWAYS have a surplus of workers (and you're always looking for a way to kill them off), you ALWAYS have enough of everything (played on the second hardest difficulty for my first playthrough, was surprised at how easy and autopilot it was).Worst part about this is how they designed the coal/oil resource - At the beginning it's good - you're scrambling for scraps of coal - But later on they switch 100% to Oil you essentially ship in back to your main city, from an outpost city-like you build. That "city" is always the same oil dreadnaught, with 3 nodes of oil containing 4 million oil that never runs out. Compare this to FP1's system of coal nodes, as well as having to use thumpers and gathering stations, and you have something that is literally a downgrade in depth.Dumbed down the gameplay for no reason.All the research and civics are mostly just stat boosts - Enormous ones at that - Which means no real "improvement" you see with your own two eyes - You just have to "pretend" that something happened and suspend your disbelief a little.The gameplay: 4/10Like I said i difficulty, the gameplay is severely dumbed down compared to Fp1. Not being able to build buildings yourself, but districts in hextiles really "disconnects" you from your infrastructure. You cannot build roads, the buildings are all random, and looking very similar. Buildings are essentially "district plug-ins" that serve as stat boosts or abilities for the district, which IMO is a strict downgrade to what was before.Example:In frostpunk1, I could build a propaganda center. That propaganda center had a nice mesh, it had flags, it had speakers, it had a dedicated ability on it's building click, it had a strong effect and was quite expensive.In frostpunk 2, you "research" the propaganda center, and then your city just kinda "has it". People start talking about it, but you cannot see it, you cannot see any of it's abilities, you cannot really know what it does.I also despise not using numbers - Who came up with "Severely affects" and "Minor addition" instead of a simple +50 / -12 to something? You know this is what people want to see, right? So many times I saw "Severely reduces crime" only to see it basically do nothing because my population was 30k+.The district system is a boring borefest that disconnects you from your citybuilder hard enough that you start to disassociate with it - not a good thing.Exploration took a hit too - Most of the options seem completely... pointless? I don't think I used a single outpost the entire game except for the starter coal node, and they dedicated like an entire tree of research and civics for this. Why? Did they not play their own game?The balance: 6/10Balance was good on steward difficulty - none of the things felt too punishing, but some things felt way too good. This is what made the game really easy for me, and way easier than frostpunk 1. The game also retains the problem from 1 - IF you know how to beat it once, you will never have another problem ever again. It's a memory puzzle instead of a colony builder game.The biggest problem is the currency system - Everything in the game is bound to "Heatstamps" (gold) which essentially means that if you don't prioritize gold income early, you lose because you cannot outpace the cold.The cold is also basically not a problem - in the campaign, there is only one "proto-storm" that goes down to -110 celsius, but of course this doesn't mean anything - They made heat only relevant to the consumption of fuel for some reason - No more upgrades for the generator, no more area upgrades, just "every building uses X amount of heat per level of cold".Remember how in Frostpunk 1 you had to balance taking in refugees with how much heat you could output, so they wouldn't all die? Yeah. Not a thing here, everybody just strolling around when it's -110 deg outside if you have fuel in abundance (and you will).The feel: 3/10Overall the game is quite buggy, choppy framerate even with DLSS and frame gen: ON, on an RTX4080.It seems unpolished in many places and gives off a kinda "early access" feel.Additionally, please god make the "STEWARD, STEWARD WE CALL YOU" voices stop for god's sake - After 5h of constant STEWARD screaming i was exhausted.Overall: 4/10.Very sad to say this because I was a big enjoyer of FP1, despite it's flaws. Frostpunk 2 ultimately dumbs down the core gameplay while pretending it's deep - especially around the council mechanic.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who loved Frostpunk 1, I went into this with an open mind, not expecting the same game, but something fresh. Unfortunately, this isn’t just a new take—it’s a garbage one. Districts are utterly meaningless and confusing, and frankly, I can sum up the whole game that way: meaningless and confusing. Resources have been given strange new names that make no sense, and the mechanics? Many of them feel pointless, leaving me constantly asking, "Why?" _childDocuments_.review: My initial impressions with the game, having played the original Frostpunk for 130+ hours, has not been great. The game itself is... fine. Not great. But it's not some buggy mess, it just struggles to be fun. There is some part of me that wonders if we're going to see a mobile release follow shortly, because a lot of the structure of the gameplay could be akin to a mobile game. But outside of the setting, the vast majority of core mechanics have changed. It seems as if the team wanted to fix how late game Frostpunk 1 required quite a bit of building micro-management at times, but they've responded by throwing the entire gameplay style of the original out the window. Not only is there upsettingly little control over the actual resource harvesting itself, but furthermore there really isn't the opportunity to do much truly of value town customization wise. There is essentially zero opportunity to create your wasteland town as there was in the original game, all you truly do is pick which tiles are used for a very generic production pattern. Everything is tile locked, and it feels more like some sort of modded version of Civ V than it does the original Frostpunk game. If this wasn't being published by the original studio, I'd have sworn the Frostpunk IP had been sold off to another developer, because there is really nothing in common with the original gameplay loop. To make the changes easier to grasp, here's a list of what I've noted so far:- Time flows has been changed, with there no longer being a day/night cycle. Weeks fly by rather meaninglessly, rather than spending the day optimizing your town for what resources you need next.- Resources are stockpiled now. To what end, outside of occasional gameplay objectives, is pretty valueless. All it does is prevent debuffs from things like starving, or lack of goods, or lack of housing - and those debuffs generally aren't noticeable. Starving as a whole is pretty meaningless, as is your citizens dying, as they'll generally repopulate at a faster rate than whatever they're dying at. It's a minor inconvenience.- Research is entirely unclear as to what needs to be focused, as research generally doesn't unlock buildings, but rather bonuses. Personally, I think that lacks the punch of being able to then place the newly researched building afterwards, so it feels lackluster.- Heat is just this abstract thing that you have to make by getting fuel, but there's really no need to research to upgrade the generator in this gameplay loop. You just feed it more oil/coal, and you get more heat. No need for heat zones anymore. It feels pretty unrewarding generally, and while there's some small bonuses for planning your town to optimize heat, the bonuses are lackluster and almost not worth pursuing.- Breaking through the frostpack to build more buildings is pretty much just a bloat function to slow down the gameplay. It costs you resources, and I believe it's there to make you have to plan your settlement. But it fails at that, because you break through the frostpack in whatever section you choose pretty quickly. So it essentially just ends up being a credit drain, which isn't a fun or challenging dynamic, it just means you frequently find yourself unable to do anything as you wait for resources to build up.- The colony system, while somewhat novel, really just makes this game a resource balancing game between settlements. It does not seem to be intended to be a resource balancing game, so it's a pretty poor resource balancing game.- When you create a colony, it takes workforce equally from all your buildings. While it's nice that it doesn't do it randomly, thus ruining your economy, it does mean now every building you have is understaffed, and you will have to manually fix that for each and every one.- Frostland exploration feels like a checklist. There has yet to be any big decisions, or excitement from finding steam cores, or excitement from finding anything. Outposts you establish can give you a trickle of resources, but not a meaningful amount that does any more than replace one building in your city, and you already have to make one building to get the frost scouts to establish the outposts. I'm not excited when my frost scouts are going somewhere new. It's just another task that apparently has to be done.- Crime ends up being a factor, but it's just another debuff, rather than something where you're worried about your precious citizens being killed in the night. (Although again, night doesn't exist anymore) You might get a heartbreaking message about a missing child, but that child will be replaced within the next day by ordinary population growth.- The "roads" are just flavor on the screen, and appear to generate almost randomly. Zero regard is made for "would you actually make a road this way", and I want to compare it to slime mold paths, but slime mold paths actually try to be efficient.- You can't even zoom in far enough to truly enjoy the hustle and bustle of your city you're making. Gone are the days of seeing church processions in the night, your citizens are just gold streaks on a path.- Automatons, in all ways but flavor text and non-interactive objects on your road, appear to have been completely removed from the game.- Temperature changes happen. They're generally meaningless outside of suddenly you require more coal/oil. They're also far less frequent, so they tend to sneak up on you, at which point you are met with a generally uncompelling alert telling you things got colder. You tend to forget that occurred within about 15 seconds, because you really don't have to do anything.At time of writing, I've gone through the prologue and part of chapter 1. There has yet to be any compelling story, just "you're running out of coal, establish an outpost to get oil!" There's still plenty of content to follow, and I won't be refunding the game. Thus I'm hopeful I'll change this review down the line. But so far, I've been horrendously disappointed considering I was hoping this would be the original game, with expanded content and mechanics. Instead, this has been a kneecapped homage to the original. The changes that have been made to the original gameplay loop have been at best, different, and more frequently just downright worse. I want to give the game a chance to get fun, but so far it just hasn't been.One positive has been the town council meetings. It's a cool dynamic to add so far, and having the need to sway votes with other political votes has been interesting to have to factor into the gameplay. But even this aspect requires some criticism, as interactions with factions generally has felt like interacting with monoliths of different names. Each faction is really only being distinguished by what they may ask for, or how much they have to offer voting support wise.I could see how some people could find the game to be a 6/10. Maybe even a 7/10 if you like mobile games. But the insane amount of 9/10 reviews Frostpunk 2 is touting in it's advertising is just baffling to me. The vast majority of Metacritic reviews all seem to have one thing in common - very few of them mention any actual gameplay, and rather focus on the setting itself. Which would be fine if this was a visual novel, but it's a game being sold at AAA prices. On top of that, the setting is notably far less compelling than the first iteration of the franchise. Somehow, the studio that made This War of Mine, one of the most emotionally compelling games I have ever played in my life, has managed to make the emotional attachment you have to your citizens colder than the frostland itself.In conclusion, if you're looking at buying this because you loved the original, I do not think you'll enjoy how the gameplay loop has changed. If you're looking at buying this because you loved the setting, you may be able to trick yourself into enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has many negative reviews that it does not deserve, simply for the reason of being totally different from Frostpunk 1. This was announced far before the launch already though in each and every trailer - so it should not come at a surprise. Now let me explain why this is a good thing and in which way the game is different.11 Bit Studios could have taken the easy path: Simply a copy of FP1 with better graphics and new, harder missions. As the first game was a success, more of that would have been easy to re-sell. Instead of a copy, they delivered a true successor.  We build New London in part one and saved the city afterwards against the big storm. We provided food, shelter and heat to the people, hence they could survive.Now 30 years have passed and obviously the city and the people have changed / grown. This poses new challenges while old ones are a thing of the past. At the same time these new issues change the gameplay:1. Instead of a few hundred people we now have thousands or even tens of thousands. Obviously the city needs housing capacity for these masses and hence we do not simply create single houses anymore but housing districts. Similar we proceed with construction sites - we have plenty of workers and instead of creating a single saw mill into which we send 10 people, we build construction or industry districts which hire hundreds of employees at once.Yes - this makes Frostpunk 2 more into a city builder such as Cities Skylines than a clone of Frostpunk 1. It is a logical consequence of the new story line though and in my opinion nothing bad. On the contrary, it feels refreshing to not simply protect the city against a new, even harder, even colder super storm, but to expand it instead and make it move outside of the crater we once were trapped in.2. As the city stood already 30 years ago and it has now many more years of development behind it, obviously most of the basic needs are taken off. While we were fighting to barely survive in Frostpunk 1, we start with a working city in Frostpunk 2. People have food, people have houses and unless we take more people in, we are fine. Similar to real life, people get new desires though once their basic ones (sleep, food, shelter) are taken care of. In Frostpunk 2 the people have different ideas about the future of the city and they want to influence the decisions. Different factions build and each one has different interestes and dislikes the other factions. Furthermore, we life in a democracy now and politicians need to be convinced to vote for laws instead of us just passing them. This mechanism is completely new and poses many challenges we did not even have in Frostpunk 1. Yes - this is very difficult and it is potentially even impossible to make everyone equally happy. Is this a reason for negative reviews ? In my opinion not as 1. I do not play Frostpunk to have an easy game and 2. It is once again perfectly justified and explained by the story.3. Not really a new challenge based on the story but likely just taken from Anno is the fact that we can now control multiple cities. While New London stays our home, we can build housing districts and infrastrucure in Outposts to collect resources there and create trade routes between the different locations. I think this is a very nice feature as it makes the game much more complex and opens more possibilities for different strategies.I cannot believe at all that some negative reviews really claim that this is "intelectually too challenging" and hence use it as a negative argument, but this seems to be the reality. If you like easy games, this might scare you off, if you like a bit more in-depth strategy games you very likely like this change as well.Besides the 3 major changes above, the game kept many things from the old Frostpunk. We have to make hard decisions - often times there is just a lesser evil but no justice. Especially with the different factions we cannot make everyone happy. Often times it seems everyone is just getting more angry at us, no matter what we do. Probably how politicians feel in real life as well. :DIt is part of this game series though and in the end, when we passed the story and made people survive and unite (or not ?) we have the same feeling of satisfaction that we saved lifes. No matter what we lost, what we needed to sacrifice or how hard it has been.

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as the first. And instead you are forced to over and over just make hard decisions.Compared to the first game this game is a disaster. _childDocuments_.review: The sequel is quite a different experience from the first one. Whereas the first game required you to build around the generator for efficient heating, this one does not. Instead, the city layout is based on the location of your resources and careful planning of your districts adjacency bonuses. Overall, I like the gameplay and I don't mind the attempt to innovate the core gameplay of the first game, but the game is lacking a couple of things: some QOL changes for city management, the main story feels very short and some problems in the city become too easy to solve, mainly by having way too much fuel and the ability to stockpile it makes the heating problem trivial by the midpoint of the story. More importantly, the story is missing a key ingredient; the first game from the start sets a very harsh tone; it throws a lot of curveballs at you and just when you thought you had one problem under control, you'd get another (or multiple) pressing emergency on your hand which made a lot of impact on the overall tone of bleakness and hopelessness of the game. That tone made your success all the more satisfying which I think the sequel lacks. Still a decent sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: There may be other games like it, but in my opinion this is a pretty original take on city builders. Rather than a continuation of the original, I would say that Frostpunk 2 continues the story while completely revamping the gameplay mechanics. This is exactly the sort of thing players are asking for when it comes to sequels that we never seem to get.Pros:- Compelling story that connects to the original game and expands on it- New political system adds challenge to something that was guaranteed in the previous game- New social dynamics will make you question your beliefs- Actions appear to have deeper consequences- An apocalypse story that focuses on rebuilding and not just surviving- New scouting system is nice- The difficultly level builds slowly as you progress rather than punishing players from the onsetCons:- The world feels empty without the ability to see your citizens- You spend a good bit of time just waiting for timers to tick down, which wouldn't be so bad if there was something to look at- The prologue is weak, they attempted to introduce the new mechanics through an environment similar to that of Frostpunk 1, but the result is something confusing and unintuitive- Even after making improvements, the UI isn't perfect. Especially when it comes to making choices. There is text on each choice button, which on hover, changes to tell you more about the option. I clicked at least four options without realizing the text was changing. There should be a 'hover for more info' text in the dialogue box- When agreeing to a new law or technology, there is no indication of whether or not you have already chosen something for that category and that choosing something new will override the existing choice- There are a handful of bugs which cause not just crashing issues, but full PC shutdowns. However, I've played 10 hours and only encountered this twice. It shouldn't happen at all, but that's not too bad for a recent release
