_childDocuments_.review: Truly the definition of "easy to learn, hard to master". P4AU is a game that allows you to jump in relatively easily, but rewards players for taking the time to master its systems. Combine that with a cast of interesting and unique characters and one of the best soundtracks you'll ever find in a fighting game, and there's very little not to love. _childDocuments_.review: This is definitely my favorite fighting game (not that i play that many of them to begin with) it's so much fun to play with friends and alone. I find the campaign interesting but its not my main focus. I personally love the golden arena attack mode. If you don't know it's very similar to the normal game, however you go through "dungeons" (just a bunch of fights in a row, nothing fancy) and level up by defeating your opponents. you diverge said levels into your normal stats (attack, defence and whatnot) which increase your performance. It's a really small and silly thing but i adore it.Now to address the quality of this port. Having read the other reviews i realise a lot of people have had issues with various things. online not really working and borderless mode ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dying apparently or something idk didn't read that deep into it. Anyway i personally did not have these issues so i will nit pick instead. When playing with a controller the mouse never disappears of the screen. not a big deal but its quite annoying and i can imagine its not that big of a fix. I'm sure they are busy with more important stuff so i won't linger on it too much. There is one thing however i cannot stand. the control scheme alters between keyboard and controller controls when in the menus which bothers the hell out of me. I thought it was an issue with my janky setup, that the game sometimes registers keyboard or mouse input and switches to that control scheme but no. That is not the case, it just flickers between them every few seconds which when reading the dialouge in the story mode gets really annoying with a constant light flickering at the bottom of the screen.Anyway this game slaps but you should probably get it on console since those versions seem to have less problems and a bit more content (for some reason). However this version is also a banger and i would reccomend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely ADORE this game. In fact, it was the first real fighting game I ever played in my life, and it's what first got me interested in the fighting game genre in the first place all those years ago. Which is exactly why I just CAN'T, in good faith, recommend this port of the game. Don't get me wrong, it's nothing to do with the balance, or the presentation, or the music, or really anything related to the game itself - I love the game, and I love the balance in this version even if it's wack at times lol The reason why I can't recommend this version is because it's buggy as hell, has performance issues (Denuvo, seriously?), the game crashes at random times, the volume is all over the place (cutscenes are loud as ♥♥♥♥, while the rest of the game is extremely quiet), you can't alt+tab (or even click outside the game window) while in online mode or else you'll get disconnected, and it doesn't even have lobbies. Sure, it'll eventually get rollback later down the line, but at this point that's one step forward, three steps back.I got this version out of convenience, because I don't have a PS4 lol but all of this is just inexcusable. Atlus, do better.

_childDocuments_.review: --Edited on Apr 12 2022--As a mostly 4X/RTS gamer, Persona 4 Arena was the first 2D fighting game that I seriously got into back during my early 20s, and I'm still loving it! Initially I have left a negative review on Steam due to several technical issues that I have experienced, but after 2 patches most of these issues have been resolved (at least for me personally); as such, I have changed my review to that of a positive one. Although I got the original version of this game because I was a Persona 3/4 fan, what ultimately got me hooked to continue playing this game was due to the gameplay, tutorials/challenges, and all the available game modes; and I will say that it is still great and fun! Although the story mode does have long section of narratives, and I didn't feel engaged 100% of the time, I didn't mind it as I grew accustomed to playing the Blazblue series. Despite P4AU being a great game, there are still some minor issues at hand: -Certain parts of the art and the UI has not been properly up-scaled, leaving some visuals really unappealing to the eyes-Online lobby rooms still don't work for me at times (maybe others are having better luck)-No rollback netcode (planned for later this year though)Anyway, for the time being based on my personal experience, I will give this port a rating of 8/10. I undoubtly recommend this game fully if you are a fan of Persona 3 and/or 4, and will recommend it as a fighting game too once the Rollback netcode is introduced later this year.

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is so freaking good! Every character feels very fun to play and there is so much combo freedom. I cannot wait for rollback but the netcode as it is now is decent enough. The music is bumpin' and the UI is so clean! I love how this game embraces the feel and pizzazz of the mainline rpg persona games while also translating into a fighting game. It's great it now finally is on modern platforms and western players can finally enjoy the 2.5 edition of the patch. There are a few issues with the online functionality of the game, such as crashing when trying to find player rooms and the lack of a rematch button in online matches, that wasn't in the original console releases but it's not as if Atlus couldn't have added this. There are some people who have reported issues with the games start-up but I haven't experienced any so far and hopefully you won't either. The issues with the game will hopefully be patched fairly soon and there is of course rollback to be exited for. This game has very active discord channels, even before the release of this game people were finding matches through other means so hopefully there is no worry about a dwindling player base anytime soon. With all that said and done, this is a must buy for any fan of anime fighting games. The question now is:      are you ready to step up to the plate?

_childDocuments_.review: As far as Anime Fighting Games go, this is undoubtedly one of the most accessible ones. Like a good amount of games, it features an auto combo system, but learning its systems and how you can link different moves to one another is what makes a good fighting game. _childDocuments_.review: Persona 4 Arena Ultimax vastly improves on the gameplay from the original - which was already rather fantastic. That being said, there are a few unbalanced moves and the shadow characters tend to be overpowered.I spent most of my time playing the Switch port, as this PC port has audio issues; fails to start up for some; etc.The lack of rollback netcode at launch is also something that I cannot support, especially when it was in the original. However, I have had a rather fun time playing this game with friends.For the most part, the ranked online was extremely entertaining: being able to combat skilled players from all over the world was rather invigorating. Although, this does not come without its flaws: there are a vast number of "troll players". Troll players constantly spam moves merely to rank themselves up, it truly makes the experience irritating for most - and almost made me give up entirely before I learned how to overcome them. Regrettably, no fighting game comes without these, but Persona 4 Arena Ultimax's lack of cooldowns, ability to spam, etc makes it far more annoying.The story drags on quite a bit, and the lack of a Persona 3 port/remaster on any console is rather bizarre - considering that this is a spiritual successor to both that and Persona 4, but ATLUS will be ATLUS. Overall, though, having all of the DLC stories and mainline ones included is a fairly nice surprise - and the writing is what you'd expect from a Persona game. Seeing the SEES crew grown-up was a lovely shock as well, to be sure.The AI in Ultimax, in comparison to the original, is vastly improved upon. You can alter the difficulty of these AIs for a nice challenge, and the single-player modes will keep you entertained.I love having the DLC characters like: Adachi, Marie and Margaret - the only thing missing is the Persona Q music, plus some other DLC songs, but I suppose those aren't necessary.In conclusion, I would highly recommend this game - but only once the patches for the PC release have been put out. If you do not wish to wait, then the Switch or PS4 version is an excellent substitute.

_childDocuments_.review: My short time with Persona 4 Arena has left me with one primary takeaway: A plausible Persona 5 Arena can't possibly be worse.Looking at this from the perspective of someone who enjoyed a good amount of the writing in Persona 4 (save some characters I think were handled poorly), and has had a good time with Guilty Gear Strive and Xrd (newer fighting games from Arc System Works), I couldn't be more disappointed. I'm not really certain what people enjoy about this from a fighting game perspective or a story perspective, at least from where I'm standing.As a fighting game, I popped it open on a Saturday night to play with my buddy, as I have with many fighting games in the past year. We generally get a good time out of some of them, playing them for a couple night or sometimes much longer.  Injustice/Mortal Kombat weren't really our style, but it's clear there's something there that just doesn't gel with us. Tekken 7 and Guilty Gear Strive/Xrd have stuck around much longer. P4AU took maybe two or three matches before we were absolutely confounded at the thought that this game was developed by the same company that made several games we've been actively enjoying for several months. Most combos are either mashing the same button over and over again, or insanely varied and frame-perfect inputs, there's no in-between. The entire experience feels like it's stuck in some weird mode that focuses on making the game "accessible" and, in turn, makes learning and executing moves extremely difficult to compensate. I know I'm relatively new to the genre, but it seems like this lack of control goes solidly against why folks would play it. Either way, we tried it a couple times and could only bring ourselves to play maybe 30-40 total matches before we decided it just wasn't fun.So gameplay is out, but this is a Persona game. Even the weird spin-offs tend to still bring back our cast of memorable characters and still deliver an engaging story, even if the main gameplay loop of day-to-day life is no longer the focus. Strikers was a beautiful example of how they can shift into a different genre and bring our old pals from the main game along for an enjoyable adventure. The question is: Does P4AU do this well? I'd say, unfortunately, no. From the onset, there were a couple things that were a bit off-putting but not dealbreakers. For instance, the main character from Persona 4 is now fully voiced, rather than just having a few callouts in the game. An improvement if I'm being honest, just a little weird from someone who's spent hours playing as the guy, only to finally hear him have emotions and a personality. Another addition is voices are "lip-synced" to characters, meaning as they speak, it toggles between a "mouth open" and "mouth closed" portrait. This...was not a good change. More work for a lesser outcome unfortunately. But hey, it's a little goofy, but that's not all. It wasn't for a bit that we realized the main downfall of this game: narration. Whoever wrote for this game had dreams of writing novels and expressed that overwhelmingly here. For most scenes in this game, there are maybe a couple of voiced lines of dialogue interspersed with absolutely massive paragraphs of silent narration that absolutely obliterate the flow of the story. The story itself is already pretty mediocre (from what we've played of it) and this aspect drops it down to the floor. You'll hear a character say something to another, and you'll hear the worry in their voice about what's going on. This will be immediately followed by three paragraphs of "I was worried for her, I really did attack her with all I had, but I had no choice! It's like she wasn't hearing the words I was saying and beating the crap out of her was the only way to get my point across! I really wish there was another way. Seriously, what is going on right now?". It's like it's written for people to casually leave it play while they walk in and out of the room washing dishes, doing laundry, etc.I would love nothing more than to recommend you buy this game and prove to Atlus that these fighting games are a profitable avenue to keep going down, as the concept of getting a Persona 5 Arena is a dream. Unfortunately, I can't endorse this game as being worth your money, either for fans of these characters and series, or as a fighting game. I was genuinely excited for announcement of this coming to steam and, despite my mediocre expectations given its age, I can't help but be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite fighting game series of all time is finally on PC! I wish they had included the original P4A and not just Ultimax, or at least have ability to play as the original characters (like how you can pic GG and GGX mode in Guilty Gear Accent Core + R) or have the original yellow UI (health bars and meters) as a customization option. The lack of rollback netcode on release was a completely ignorant decision, and after a huge backlash the devs announced they will be providing rollback netcode in a later patch. Aside from that, the game does not currently function well as a PC game because if you alt+tab, it freezes the game for both players, and this can disconnect you from matches. So far, I have not seen players abusing this to cheat (aka lagswitching) but it should be patched out immediately as no other fighting game has this issue. Connecting to matches often fails, and sometimes the same player names appear on the ranked list twice. As people have mentioned, remote play has been disabled, which is a shame because that probably provides a better online multiplayer experience than the delay-based netcode the game currently has. There is almost nothing to spend the points you earn by playing matches on. You can buy a profile icon, and that's it. Other games let you buy colors for characters, but this game comes with every color unlocked. I enjoy unlocking colors in Under Night In-Birth and outfit pieces in Soul Calibur, so I wish it was the same here. Once you're in a match, the gameplay is a lot of fun, but I hope the devs improve the other aspects of the game to be the same level of quality.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 4 Arena Ultimax is a great fighting game. I haven't had any issues with audio or online play like some people are reporting. It plays perfectly other than missing rollback, which is coming later this summer. If you like Persona 4, and are passingly familiar with Persona 3, this game will be perfect for you. The original P4A story is still terribly slow and repetitive, but they're keeping it true to the original.People new to fighting games can still enjoy P4AU, as the game comes with a pretty basic but adequate lesson mode to teach the player. So Persona fans that just want the story won't find themselves limited by the gameplay if they put in a bit of effort. People new to the Persona franchise will get heavy spoilers for both Persona 3 and Persona 4, however; so if you're looking for an entry into the Persona franchise, I'd recommend at least playing Persona 4 Golden (or watching the Persona 4 anime) before playing P4AU. But if you're just looking at P4AU as a fighting game, you can easily ignore the story mode and other series entries entirely.The gameplay is a direct copy of the 2.5 version of Persona 4 Arena Ultimax originally released for Xbox 360 and PS3, so anybody looking to research frame data should make sure to look at the 2.5 version. It's a relatively typical anime fighter, with a large focus on combos, giving an auto combo option to each character for beginners, but offering much better combos for advanced players. Each character has a unique gimmick associated with them, offering a large variety of playstyles. These gimmicks change things up a lot, but are never broken in how they're implemented. Full button remapping is available, even for attacks that typically require inputting multiple buttons at the same time.Character palette selections are wide (~30 per character) and mostly unique. Some are references to other characters or personas from the franchise, which is fun to see. Most characters also have a shadow version, which plays a bit differently from the normal version.The one change I would ask for is to give the option to turn off the button HUD at the bottom of the screen in menus and story mode. It constantly blinks back and forth between displaying controller buttons and keyboard buttons and is incredibly distracting. Even if it was static for a single control scheme it would be perfectly fine. I'm using a controller, and not using any keyboard inputs, so why are you trying to show me both? It's a small thing, but it's already annoying me a lot.I sincerely hope that P4AU gets a long life as a relevant fighting game with this new port. I certainly think it deserves it.

Second, this audio, while functional, is way too quiet throughout the entire game (which is baffling considering how loud the opening video's audio is).  I turned every slider up to 100%, which helped, but it's still unnecessarily quiet compared to everything else on my computer.  Third, there's a bug that just crashes the game everytime you try to join your friends' online lobby or when you change your display resolution (though these will likely be patched)It's a shame because the game really is fantastic still all these years later. But for those of us that were impressed with the upscaling and remastering of Persona 4 Golden's PC port, this is a massive disappointment to say the least.  I'll be refunding until higher resolutions are added, and who knows, maybe the PS4 version will turn out better.

_childDocuments_.review: A very stale game not worth playing if you're into persona 3 and 4.It's impossible to tell from the videos and screenshots, but the story mode for this game is the most atrocious presentation I've ever paid to experience. It's long drawn out scenes of the characters saying maybe 1-4 lines of voiced dialogue and then 2-3 paragraphs worth of internal monologue you have to read that describes the scene, the character's thoughts, and the direction of the story. It is very frustrating every time it cuts between these two because the internal monologue will be half way summed up the next time the characters speak. The writing also very fan-fictiony. It felt like I was playing a flash visual novel off of new grounds.The gameplay, when you can actually play the game (only 4 fights in 2 hours of Yu's story in P4A's story mode), is very hectic. I don't play fighters, but I'm not a stranger to them. The first fight of the story mode was not a tutorial fight, nor were there any tutorial fights. It just dropped you right in with a very hyper AI and wanted you to fight. Needless to say, I almost died. The way the combat flowed in this game was just not for me. I'm more used to fighters that are heavier since it gives me time to react or decide what to do. Since all fights played like this, I didn't bother to progress after completing's Yu's story as far as the game would let me. Definitely not worth the price for the quality of gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm honestly really shocked with how good a fighting game based on a series with turn based combat is. They manage to incorporate elements of typical Persona gameplay like SP and element attacks like Ziodyne in such a smooth way that blends seamlessly with the fighting. The story was also entertaining but suffered a bit from the way it presents itself, especially in the P4A campaign. Events usually get repeated a lot with only miniscule differences in between each character's story which makes it very confusing as to what's actually canon and what isn't. This was fixed in the Ultimax campaign though by just having a semi-straight path you progress through instead of individual character stories. Other than that, the campaigns were cool and it was fun seeing the P3 and P4 cast interact with each other. Makes me excited to see them talk with each other more when I play Persona Q.

Also, I am reviewing this game solely on it's single player aspects.Pros:- The Music is amazing, as always from the Persona series- The Gameplay is pretty good- The Characters are pretty good, even though the story doesn't really focus on them that much- The story does a pretty good job at catching the people who haven't played Persona 3 and 4 up to speed while not spoiling 3 and 4 (with that being said, I recommend that you play Persona 3 and 4 before you play this game)- The crossover between Persona 3 FES and Persona 4 Golden is done very wellCons:- The plot is honestly just okay- The story is also a drag to play through, because of the cliffhangers that force you to go from one character to another- The developers didn't bother to update the cutscenes like they did for the PC port of Persona 4 Golden, and, to me at least, it's pretty noticeable- It's overpriced, especially since Persona 4 Golden (which is a game that is way better than this game, and is a game that I highly recommend playing) is only $19.99 while this game is $27.99Conclusion: Although this game does have good aspects, I wouldn't recommend purchasing this, due to the price, unless it's either on sale, or you're a fan of the Persona series and/or fighting games in general. _childDocuments_.review: As a fighting game it's pretty solid but that's not the real reason I wanted to play this. I'm mainly here for the story.The story itself is pretty alright but I enjoy these characters so I'm happy to go through it for that alone. Nice to see the Persona 3 crew again and their interactions with the P4 team.The way the story is told can be quite wordy. The dialogue is all voiced but there's a lot of internal monologuing that can become tedious to get through.The game is essentially a combo of Persona 4 Arena and Persona 4 Ultimax:Arena for the most part is a 3-ish part story told through various, conflicting perspectives. It's pretty short and as characters tread the same ground can be repetitive (I say it's short but it's probably the same length as Ultimax if you insist on seeing all perspectives). It's also hard to truly gauge what the canonical timeline even is due to no one's story being consistent.Ultimax thankfully sorts this by having a consistent linear story through through both the P4 team (Episode P4) and the P3 team (Episode P3) and while they do follow the same series of events, unlike in Arena, they vary enough so that they're both worth doing IMO.TL;DRIt's not Persona's finest story telling and a bit on the wordy side but the character interactions are fun and the gameplay is solid.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, the game itself is really fun, and if you enjoy the Persona series as a whole you can at least find some value in the Story mode (the presentation makes it somewhat tedious but it's interesting enough). However, the multiplayer aspect pretty much destroys this release as a fighting game; not launching this port with rollback netcode was a major mistake, and both the matchmaking and lobby system work poorly in general, especially the latter.Rollback was indeed promised later down the line but it came by the time this port's hype and relevance died down, and it did not even come as an automatic update for this version, only on the PS4 release. You need to go type some commands into the Steam settings of this game to get rollback here, which just shows Atlus kind of gave up with this halfway through (quite reflective of the Persona 25th Anniversary as a whole for that matter). There's a reason barely anyone's playing it anymore.If you're interested in this game as a Persona story, sure, go for it. If you're looking for a multiplayer fighting game experience, you might as well look for another ArcSys game; this one is by no means bad at a core gameplay level but everything else just drags the experience down.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're eyeing this game, it probably means you loved Persona 4. Maybe you're thinking of buying this game even though you don't care about 2D Fighters, because you're interested in the story mode.Pro-tip: Don't. The writing is bad.It's not merely bad compared to the original Persona 4 and it's incredibly high bar, that's a slightly unreasonable comparison for almost any game. It's bad all on it's own. It's bad compared to almost any decent Visual Novel (in case you didn't know, the entire story is told Visual Novel style with some fights in-between). I love Visual Novels, but I do not care about 2D Fighters (I don't hate them, they just aren't my jam). Despite this, I found myself SKIPPING swaths of text in the story mode to get to the fights. It doesn't just feel like fan service, it feels like fan fiction.There's some good art, good voice acting, great music... but it's not enough to redeem the game if you're here for the story.On the other hand, if you're here because you love 2D Fighters or BlazBlue, even a neophyte like me can tell the game itself is excellent, this review and subsequent down-vote isn't really for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Port's pretty good!I read lots of reviews complaining about technical issues, but I haven't really had any, so YMMV. I've also seen complaints about the graphics not being upscaled, but this isn't a 3D game, the graphics are all matte paintings and 2D animated characters that are intentionally pixel-y, so that doesn't really matter. I like the animation style of the characters. They have a lot of personality.The story is good and fun if you're a Persona fan, although going through the different character perspectives is kinda repetitive and the visual novel style isn't as immersive as the main series (atlus pls port royal it's been 84 yrs #portbegging). But getting to see things from the POVs of all your favorite characters is a fun experience that you don't get in the main games. Also, as a fan of the P4 anime series, I welcome any adaptation where Yu is not a silent protagonist, so having him be basically a normal character here is a treat.I'm new to fighting games, so I can't speak for how it stacks up in the genre, but it's enjoyable even if you're not competitive. The preset combos are really helpful, and you can do fancier stuff if you want, although if you're like me and bad at skill games that require reflexes, sticking with the basics is perfectly OK. (I still don't know how to do combos and animation cancels, but I also don't really play against other people, so that's fine with me for now.) There's a good variety of characters, all with different playstyles, some of which are more beginner-friendly than others. (Some of my initial impressions, as a beginner myself: Margaret is fluid and graceful, Yosuke is acrobatic and fun, Yukiko is very straightforward, Labrys is techy and kinda confusing, Mitsuru's moves are very annoying to pull off, Chie just has really cute animations.)I play on PC with a keyboard, since I don't have a controller, and this was my initial complaint when I first got the game--the controls are really hard to figure out for keyboard users. The tutorials will only tell you the buttons intended for controller users, so you have to go digging in the settings to find out which controls are mapped to which keys. What's especially helpful for keyboard users is that there are different keys mapped for some of the button combos, so you don't have to worry about pressing three keys at once, which on my keyboard just totally negates the output. When I first started playing, I was starting to worry that I just straight up wouldn't be able to use some functions due to the nature of the keyboard. Thankfully they accounted for that, but it shouldn't have been as hard to figure that out as it was! It does make keyboard gameplay much smoother. One thing that is not especially smooth is any move where you have to move the "joystick" at a diagonal, which on PC just means pushing two movement keys in quick succession, which is clunky and not always accurate. But I imagine it wouldn't be especially easy to do reliably on a controller, either, so again, YMMV.

_childDocuments_.review: Before anything, I mostly put Not Recommended because Steam doesn't have a neutral option of sorts, and I kinda leaned more towards a no than a yes. With that said...It pains me a bit to not recommend a game that belongs in the Persona franchise, but honestly, I feel it's at least a bit justified. Persona is my favorite RPG franchise and I've played all the recent mainline games since 3. I felt like this game was marketed as mostly a sequel to P4 and at the same time a kind of crossover with the P3 cast, and I was all for it. I like both games' casts, so it seemed cool to have those characters interact with one another and participate in a new plotline together. Of course I know it's a spin-off, so it wasn't going to have the story quality of the mainline games, and I didn't expect anything as good. I mostly expected interactions between characters from both games which had never met before and a serviceable story. And we kinda get that, but I left very disappointed nonetheless.First, the character interactions are there, and there are some good ones, but there aren't many. So you'll mostly have to slog through a forced and weak main story to get to those moments. The main plot for the previous game, P4A is okay but incomplete, so you'll have to play the Ultimax story to get to the conclusion. P4AU's story though is very weak in my opinion. What mostly forces the story to be like that is the fact that this is after all, a fighting game. Balancing and PvP takes priority over the story, that's what most if not all games in the genre do, so the story has to force situations in which characters from the roster, which are all for the most part good people, to fight each other or at least "Evil versions" of each other. I feel like that kind of helped in making the story mode even more bland in addition to the scarcity of good interactions and weak main plot. I obviously won't spoil anything here, so I won't talk about story details.There are two characters featured in promotional material which are introduced in this game, and they are pretty much hit and miss respectively. One of them, Labrys, is good and while her story doesn't feel too natural, it's believable and she's a pretty cool character for the most part. The other, Sho Minazuki, has a pretty one-note personality and a very generic motivation, as a result I didn't like him in the slightest.But I mean, this is a game that seems marketed more towards the Persona diehard fans, right? It joins together two games' casts, references past events and such, has a few good interactions and kinda expects you to know those characters and lore. So would I recommend this if you really love Persona? I don't think so.If you want to know the story you could just watch it on youtube or something, mostly because the gameplay sections are so quick and unimportant, also it isn't a self-insert story as the mainline games and there aren't meaningful branching choices, so for the most part that you won't be missing much. So who do I think this game is for? It seems to be for fighting game fans, I suppose. While it fails in the story department, I believe it's actually a competent fighting game. I wouldn't know the details though, mostly because I'm not a fighting game nut, so I didn't go too deep into the specific mechanics and such.Before we finish, just a quick overview of the PC port: It works for the most part, but borderless fullscreen was broken last time I played, so I had to use exclusive, and for some reason choosing 144hz in the options menu as the game's refresh rate would work fine, but after I closed the game it would crash instantly upon trying to start it again, so I had to open the config files and revert it to 60hz. It doesn't even make sense, since the 144hz option doesn't change the fact that the game is locked at 60FPS anyway, so why have that option and why does it break the game?Just an observation: I do have more than 60 hours in the game, but a lot of that time was me taking a break from it and leaving it running in the background while I did something else, so I don't personally feel I got much time out of it. I didn't finish the P3 perspective of things too, because honestly, by the time I've finished the P4 one I was too tired of it. Maybe I'll try that out in the future, I don't know.Knowing what it is and who it is for, why do I still not recommend it? Well, for one, it's because I personally didn't enjoy it much and this is a personal recommendation. And second, they did market this game as one with a story, and it does have one, it just isn't very good. I believe if you want to make a fighting game for mostly gameplay alone, there are many franchises you could do that, but it kinda stings when you do it to a story-focused franchise such as Persona and then throw in a half-baked story just because it needs one.If I had to rate this game it would be a 5/10. I know some people will blame me for expecting a decent story out of a genre in which that isn't the focus, but honestly, they tried to pass it off as having a story and it's a franchise that's well-known for that aspect, so I don't feel like I'm in the wrong here.I really hope Atlus decides to port the other mainline games outside of P4G for PC, or that the next spin-offs do a little better.

_childDocuments_.review: I was originally pretty enthusiastic about this game. It is stylish, has a banger soundtrack, a lovable cast of characters and is, at times, kusoge AF. The story mode is also quite extensive and a true sequel to P4's story. The Persona formula sure translates pretty well into a fighting game when passing through the expert hands of Arc System works.But this PC port came with its fair load of issues at launch, a still unresolved scaling problem for higher screen resolutions and, ultimately, the rollback-netcode implementation of summer 2022 is lacking, with no ability for players to choose their own frame delay settings.I could bear with all of this but, what breaks the camel's back, is that this game includes a very aggressive DRM that'll prevent you to play offline or will lock you out of your purchase for the next 24-hours if you're switching too much between Proton versions. Once again paying customers having a worst experience than pirates, it sure won't do much to deter people from sailing the high seas. Stay away from this stinker until the malware that is Denuvo is removed (if ever), especially if you're gaming on Linux OS.

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who finished the story mode for both P4A, P4AU and the Adachi route (true endings and all). And sunk at least 60 hours into the game both on PS3 and an emulator- I can proudly not recommend this port at all. Story, while not being worse than P4D's, might be only fit for those who want to see P3 characters in action as they are the most entertaining to follow except for maybe Naoto and Adachi. And like in Persona 4 Dancing, the story is mainly experienced in Visual Novel-like text boxes and long dialogues, occasionally with fights sprinkled in an episode or two.  Which don't even last long with low level AI-opponents they throw at you. It also splits into multiple paths which you have to complete to progress from one to the other branch- staggering your pace by pulling you into the boring part of the game which you don't want even see.Gameplay by itself is fine- issues mainly go for the paid characters and some unbalanced ones (not sure if they are unlocked in this version or not.) Times I got trapped to the side of the border by Yukiko's fan throw spam is laughable, and how people get demolished by simple combos. Which are often hard to input by the strange way how the game registers button presses. I've struggled putting in combos with a lot of characters, which makes it pointless to try and actually play the game unless you play characters like Shadow Naoto which relies on combos. But, generally, it's a really float-y feeling game and certainly not for everyone- although, it can be fun with mates or friends when not taken seriously by the party. It can be enjoyed despite it flaws because the game is actually fun. Just the concept of playing as Persona characters and kicking the ♥♥♥♥ out of each other.Unlockable artwork and renders of the characters are worthless by themselves with the quality worse than what I can find on the Megami Tensei Wiki. I got the game on launch, so I'm not sure if they have fixed the issues with that. Online? Haven't tried with this version- although other's have complained about the servers and problems with crossplay. Music and animation are nice and nothing to complain about.Honestly? Only get this game if you're a giant Persona historic and fan of P3 and P4, or want a simple game you and your Persona loving buddies want to play something locally- as lobbies are annoying to deal with.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start this by saying, this is the only fighting game I have ever loved and I love this game to death. I was so excited to hear this was coming out on steam, and it's easily one of my most anticipated games in like the last 5 years. Persona 4 Arena Ultimax is an amazing fighting game and is loads of fun.But there are problems. And they probably won't be the problems others have with the game.First off, some context about me. I only want to play online with close friends, and I obsessively hate the english voices. They grate on me like nothing else, and I legit just never want to hear them ever.Despite these two things, they enforce a character selection timer on all versus, online competitive or no, and mix the voices based on each players selection. What this means is, if my friend is set to english and I'm on japanese, they hear japanese for me and I hear english for their character..... which for some characters, literally makes me want to tear my ears off of my head.Then the forced timer on character selection. Why even have so many cosmetic options if that's a thing? Why enforce that in a personal lobby? I want to take my time selecting characters. Picking colors. Joking about the matchup with my friend on VC. In the original, my friend and I had a series of inside jokes centered around us counter picking each other in real time and.... that whole aspect of the game and our enjoyment is locked now. I don't even get to really consider who I feel like playing, and for me at least that's not possible to consider until I'm looking at the character screen.It's just impossible to even enjoy the game when it's set up like this. I don't want to be annoyed constantly when I'm trying to have a fun time with my friends. The last thing I want to do is refund literally one of my favorite games of all time but....Honestly, if they don't fix this, I might. It makes the game unplayable to me. Step it up ATLUS.

_childDocuments_.review: The P4AU Part - Awesome game, a nice balance of content with really fun side modes like Golden Arena, and all the DLC is a really nice bonus, although really, I think there'd been a lot of backlash if we had to rebuy the DLC, so I guess bonus is an understatement, I'm glad it's here. The actual game play when fighting against other people holds up really well, albiet I think balance is kind of wack for a few characters. Now I'm not familiar with the old online structure, but one thing I do have against this game as of now is the lack of Quick Rematch in Ranked, as well as matches having a tendency not to connect very frequently. Other than that, the online netcode is surprisingly decent for delay-based standards, and I can't wait for it to get better with the rollback update. Also has Adachi in it, 10/10The PC Port Job Part - Man you guys dropped the ball on that front. First off, volume. It's ♥♥♥♥. I think the best way to describe it is "normal in cutscenes, near-nonexistent in everywhere else," and thus causes an opposite effect when the gameplay volume is normalized, that being "fine in most places, my eardrums got blown out thanks to the cutscenes." I haven't had graphical issues with using a resolution higher than 1080p 60hz borderless, but I am hearing others report it, so I figured I'd mention it. I think part of the reason connecting to lobbies is unnecessarily hard as I outlined earlier is because unlike PS4, the PC and Switch versions lack a Player Lobby for some reason, like that just makes no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sense to not include. I think the last gripe I have with the port thus far is that tabbing out completely stops the game as opposed to keeps the process running, and therefore if I decide to tab out of a player match at any point in time, I get DC'd from the game. I'm also hearing crashing issues for some people, although I haven't dealt with that myself, I'm perfect on that front, but it really shouldn't be a problem others bring up in the first place, so that needs to be fixed. I'll give this a positive rating for the Persona part, cause in the end, it's Persona, and I don't feel the in-match gameplay has been hampered by the port. That said, fix the port, please it is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying to adjust my volume constantly. Add Player Lobbies and Ranked Quick Rematch while you're at it.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a ton of fighters out there, and I have played a lot of them. My journey with this game started lightly on PS3. I got into it, and then got out of gaming on my PS3 very shortly after. So I didn't get much time into it.But now...now I have the time. And that becomes a big problem. Because I have the time for this....but also for King of Fighters XV, or Guilty Gear, or Phantom Breaker, or Melty Blood, or Samurai Shodown, or a multitude of others on my list. So why do you need this with so many other fighters out there?That is a good question...and I think the best way to answer this is if you are a huge Persona fan. or let me be a little more specific: a Persona 3+ fan (i.e. Persona 3, Persona 4, and/or Persona 5). I mention that it is P3+ because I am a huge Persona fan...sorta. The first Persona is my favorite game of all time. I fell in love with it when I first played it on PSX back in like 1998. Persona 2, both parts, are not bad...but Persona 3 ruined the series. Social links destroyed the experience, to where I can't even play Persona 4. This means i have very little connection to the characters in it.So it comes down to: how is it as a fighter? Well, I am impressed how Arc was able to take the Persona feel and characters and transition them in to the fighting genre. However, Arc has become a cookie cutter fighting maker company. Guilty Gear, Blazblue, Granblue Fantasy....a lot of these games feel and play too similar when Arc is involved. Persona 4 Ultimax feels the same but worse: the fighting feels sloppy. A game like Guilty gear (be it AC, Xrd, or Strive) can feel chaotic, but I don't feel like I have limited control of my character.  P4U leans more to what could end up being just button pressing. Wee.....Also for steam deck user...be warned: you will need a little tinkering to get it to run properly. Even after switching protons, it just ignored any sort of device input...so I had to map out the keyboard to my joystick to get it to work. Fun.So to be honest, with all the other fighting games out there: why do you need this one?Well you don't.....unless you are a Persona 3+ freak. That is the only reason I can see for needing this game over all the others that do this style so much better.

_childDocuments_.review: edit : looking at the comments, i've seen people are having issues with the port. personally i haven't had any problems, nor have any of my friends who bought it. hopefully it's sorted out, I know P4G had a FMV issue at launch and they were pretty quick to fix it, so hopefully it doesn't get the nocturne treatment of being forgotten about lol.a fighting game that isn't Mortal Kombat that actually has single player content instead of just training mode and online! what a deal.fun game though. if you're a fan of P4G, and want another side story, i'd recommend it. it's accessible enough that if you want to just do the story, the beginner combos are pretty simple to learn, and the music is great, they have almost every track from P4 and P3 as well as some new stuff. Also, they added the story of the original, P4A, in order to give you some more value. There's a arcade mode, as well as a tower mode, where you level your character. For $30, it's definitely a better value than most Japanese fighters since there's way more to do.It's not perfect though, rollback isn't in the game at launch, and the story retreads over the events of P4 a little too much. Persona 4 arena was created before P4G, while the P4AU story was created afterwards, so it can get a little confusing bouncing between the two and just suddenly having Marie appear. If you've already played a P4 spinoff, you kinda know what to expect. They're never as good as the original, but they're never bad either, and most interesting of all, they're always canon, and it's pretty entertaining to see how they bend the lore of the original and kinda make this a persona 3 follow-up.Overall, if you like persona, i'd grab it, especially if you want to see more from Atlus here. Maybe they'll add an installment everyone wants, next. A big game that people really like, and have been begging for, for years. Dancing all night, of course!Joking aside, we'll get persona 5 soon enough. personally I enjoyed P4G more but I get the feeling most of Atlus' library will see steam eventually, especially with Sega being their publisher, and Sega has been pretty pro-PC this last decade.

_childDocuments_.review: This is actually the 1th entry in the Persona 4 Arena games, the 4 isn't there to display it's number in the franchise, its there as a stand in for the word "For" you see, In internet slang, "4" can replace the word "for" (as "four" and "for" are pronounced similarly). For example, typing "4u" instead of "for you". In Leetspeak, "4" may be used to replace the letter "A"So knowing this we can actually deduce that the title is really "Persona For Arena" and i just think that is a brave message to send, good job SEGA and ATLUS!!

_childDocuments_.review: This is perhaps my first anime fighter and everything is so fast. There's also stuff like cancels, skill boosts, ult boost, awakening, evade, hop evade, all out attack, persona abilities and other things. I'm just saying if you're into anime fighters like guilty gear or blazblue, you'd probably have some fun with this one too. Just don't expect insane stuff like melty.However, this game was a sideline for a series of RPGs, so it has to appeal to that audience (i.e. me). A lot of the single player content is visual novel storytelling. Hell, there's even a mode you can turn on to make story mode fights automatic. So, fans of the persona games will also have lots of fun here as well. The story isn't on par with the mainline games (you're not getting 100 hours of persona story) but you can get a semblance of the Persona 4 story. It's just that it's short, like one-character-arc short.Also, it features all of the persona 3 characters except for the MC. If you have played P3, you would know why. IMO P3 didn't have a lot of character background development, so I guess this game makes up for it in another way by telling the story of what happens after the story of P3.And that segways into spoilers. _childDocuments_.review: On the surface this game comes across as a diamond. You pick it up for the first time and everything feels right. The soundtrack is fantastic, gameplay feels responsive and well done, visuals are great with some neat effects, and comboing rolls off as satisfying and a tad bit challenging. Then you enter a match and realize just how absolutely screwed up this game is. Full invuln DP on every character that beats out most options. All out attacks just straight up are abused for someone pressing a button. Top it off you also have trashy anime fighter super beats super system. Also all finishers leave your character invuln and your attack is unblockable. The only other mechanic I consider worth mentioning is the status effects which add a little bit of variety and unpredictability to the match. Overall the game kinda just becomes an exploit match of non stop abuse leaving a gross sort of taste in the mouth. However despite its flaws it offers a unique experience. Every character is unique and has a different playstyle creating plenty of variety. The personas actually make the options fun and interesting as well as give a great look to each combo. The rollback netcode is great and makes online matches fantastic. At the end of the day it's 1 part addictive fun and 2 parts raw cheese. I definitely think it's worth the experience and who knows maybe this will be the fighting game you stick to.

_childDocuments_.review: this game's definitely unique. it's got stuff like shadow characters, status effects, OMB; a ton of stuff that helps strengthen the individuality and depth for a game that wasn't really lacking either. decent amount of single-player content here. you've got a pretty long story mode and the standard fg fare with survival and arcade and stuff. most interesting is the golden arena mode, where you progress through floors of AI opponents with RPG progression and skill allocation. it's pretty neat.kind of a low entry barrier? none of the motion inputs are more complicated than double quarter circles or charges, and it has a universal DP function that only takes 2 buttons, but then there's all the statuses, the move attributes, guard point, persona displacement, the persona system itself... it's kind of a lot.i also find the defense pretty lacking. a lot of the game's unique options are too specific and committal. like, roll only really beats your opponent's big moves with long recovery, sweep only beats chest moves, and hops only beat lows and grabs. so, even with these extra choices, you end up relying on the same tools you would any game. and this is one where you'd need viable alternatives, characters can at any point spend 50 meter for really brutal mix and some can get it for free!other than that, there's, like, the online? it's fine. i wish you had more options with this but it's not that big of a deal, it works. and it does have rollback! the game runs fine, too. not as good as it should by any means, but it's not too egregious a resource hog or that unstable.in total, it's a good game. though it's worth noting the playerbase is pretty really small as of now, so finding good matches is hard. still worth it, though, especially if you're into the persona series.

_childDocuments_.review: A very complex entry to the Persona franchise. All in all, this is a game for those who want more Persona lore content and also for the ones who desire pleasing fighting game experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not quite sure where to start with this game as there is history here, old memories from the PS3 era into now steam and endless hours playing P4AU while waiting for it to go live. Instead of waffling on about things that don't matter or rather most won't care about, I'll address personal pros and cons. Pros: -Its great for returning players whom just want to play offline or do local battles with family or friends who visit. -Audio balancing has been adjusted slightly to hear certain lines a little better. Combos feel responsive at times if you don't mind a little button mashing at times. -DLC has been made free-Adachi's balancing tweaks are welcomed-Sho Minazuki -The music selection and stages are great. Cons: -The story is a little weak. (Though you can skip text.)-The netcode killed a lot of the online players-The P3 cast at times feels underused or otherwise unnecessary. (Admittedly this was a thing in the original to.)-The port has stability issues at times, sometimes you could start a combo and it drops without fault-Certain textures are stretched or otherwise grainy. I love arcsys and atlus but to say they dropped the ball is certainly no understatement, its overpriced at current value for money. Do I recommend it? Yes but with a big asterisk in that the online needs some work and if you don't mind a little bit of cheesy dialogue here and there. TDLR; Old game got little to no changes and still manages to sell at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very reluctant "Yes" to recommend. First time I launched the game, it immediately crashed to desktop and I wasn't able to open up the game since - only fix was opting into Beta 1, else I presume I would have just had to refund it (yeah I tried reinstalling, installing drivers, restarting computer, the whole shabang.) As a note, I never played the non-port versions, so this is strictly from a Steam version standpoint.The gameplay is fast and fun - characters feel unique while retaining personality from their games, along with iconic moves - based Chie God Hand.The regular vs. shadow versions is a super cool mechanic, making characters play very different in one or the other, while maintaining most of their base moveset.The music being remixes of already amazing songs is honestly kinda cheating - they couldn't really mess up in that department.The implementation of Personas as a mechanic is pretty neat, along with the Persona Break card system - adds a super unique mechanic that you won't really find in any other gameStatuses are a cool nod to the series - makes attacks have unique effects like inability to move or reversing controls which adds variety to otherwise normal laser beams and suchThere seems to be a bug where some noises are just absolutely  It makes it hard to try and enjoy the music whenever Yosuke's kunai shatter my eardrums.As is, if you like Persona and fighting games, it's a good pickup. Otherwise, probably wait for a sale. (Or some bugfixes to make it playable >:/ )---------------------------------------1.0.3 UPDATE------------------------------------------------Game launches now. Fun game.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 4 Arena Ultimax is a 2d anime fighting game with the P3 and P4 gangs. There's is a story mode where it's mostly a visual novel with a occasional fighting sections. You play as everyone in their own story sections which branches out into a chapter for the Persona 4 gang and after that, a chapter for the Persona 3 team. The first half of the story is about about Persona 4 was all about facing yourself, and even if you already accepted your weakness their always going to be there, just don't forget. Also it introduces a new character, Labrys who it a living machine like Aigis but with a really messed up past and PTSD. The second half gives it's take on Persona 3's Dark Hour and subject matter. It's actually nice seeing what happened to the Persona 3 team after...... The Answer. There not so much to the gameplay, it's a fighting game. I feel like you ether like fighting games in general, or be a big fan of the Persona story to really enjoy this. And I give this a 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun fighting game with a surprising amount of solo content.I think one thing that defines this game is that it's rather easy to pick up. While it is not on the same level of simplicity as, say, Guilty Gear Strive, the fundamentals of the game are easy to understand and the existence of autocombos allows you to learn basics such as neutral and defending. Despite this easy to pick up status, it also has a high ceiling, so it's a win-win: beginners can learn the game really easily while veterans to fighting games can master the mechanics of the game. The story modes in this game are a direct sequel to that of Persona 4. However, it also includes Persona 3 characters and thus will spoil parts of that game as well.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a Persona 3 or Persona 4 fan, this game is worth playing for the story modes alone even if you're not into fighting games (there's an Auto mode that you can turn on or off if you struggle with the gameplay). If you haven't, though, be warned that the character roster alone contains both direct and indirect spoilers for both games;  I'd recommend being familiar with both games' stories at the very least before jumping in (the animated adaptations are a good way to do so should you not want to play through two 70+ hour RPGs). Regardless, there's a very solid fighting game here though if you're only interested in multiplayer I'd wait for the rollback netcode update coming in the summer before buying. I'd also advise waiting because the port's also not in the best state right now, but hopefully a lot of the issues will be ironed out by the time the rollback update comes out.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an awesome game, but the port really isn't great. (I only have 3 hours but I played the original PS3 version.) I still think it's worth it, but only at a sale price of around 20/25 dollars. The port has issues with frequent crashing when searching for an online battle, and the audio mixing is horrible. The intro is horribly loud, and the rest of the game is quiet, with some character dialogue randomly being loud.Also, the cutscenes and UI weren't upscaled or anything, so the cutscenes and UI look very low resolution, especially when playing at 1440p or 4K. All in all the game is still super fun and it's a great fighting game, especially if you like arcade style older fighting games. The characters look nice, the fighting is fun, and there's some cool modes to keep you entertained. Sadly, it does have issues although I think there's a good chance the issues will be fixed (they are already working on the crashing issue), and the game is getting rollback netcode soon.If you have an extra $30 and need the game right now, or you are buying it to play with a friend, go for it- it's a great game. Personally I'd wait for a sale or for the issues to be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the Persona series, this game was one that greatly deserved a port on modern consoles, including PC. The Story can be considered quite slow and repetitive, especially the story of the original Persona 4 Arena, however, if you played Persona 4 and/or persona 3, you may easily find this story to be quite interesting, regardless of the long intervals between gameplay segments.Speaking of Gameplay, the fighting system is very well curated, and very satisfying. When it comes to difficulty, it is simple to learn, but very, VERY hard to master. It can get frustrating at times, but with enough practice, it's not impossible to become a decent player, and the game's tutorial and challenge modes are very good at providing assistance.Now, it is important to mention that a lot of people have been having issues with the pc version of this game, mentioning Audio issues and Crashes. It is important to say that I have personally never experienced any of these issues, aside from the audio being too loud in cutscenes. I have played in every mode the game has to offer, but I never experienced crashes or other issues, so it may be different from person to person. It is worth noting that ATLUS has been pushing out beta updates to fix these issues, so if you are worried about getting this game because of them, you can ease your worries a little bit, as it seems that this game will be patched with time.Overall, a great game that I recommend to fans of fighting games, but most of all, fans of the persona series. Personally, this is my favorite fighting game of all time.

There is nothing stopping you from just tabbing out during your opponent's combos online to screw up their timing other than your own conscience, as far as I can tell. It's hard for me to imagine this isn't going to have to be fixed to make rollback work but based on their recent opt-in beta, I'm hoping the developers plan to iron this and many other issues out.

_childDocuments_.review: Persona 4 Ultimax is one of the best fighting games of all time, and in my personal top 3. It's the confluence of the work of many talented individuals. The music, UI, and art direction all manage the clear the high bar of expectation that Persona Team have set for themselves (and arguably, this game was the one to set it). Meanwhile, on the gameplay side, P4U features some of the most labyrinthine, engaging, and fun characters and systems ArcSys has ever designed. If you're on the fence at all, or if you're a Persona fan who got into the series with 5 and are looking to experience a bit of what came before, absolutely pick this game up. Especially if you don't typically like fighting games. This game will teach you to love them.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a port of the original PS3 game along side extra features such as the story from the first Arena game and balance changes made in the latest arcade version of the game. Purchasing this game will allow you to access all former DLC content which is a pretty good deal. The game's combat still remains one of the best in the industry and each character offers a variety of different play styles. This game has hours of content and bonus features to explore. With the promise of rollback netcode this summer, I highly recommend to any fighting game fan and also any Persona fan in general.However, this is a port and not a remaster, so if you're expecting HD textures and audio that works properly, then maybe this game isn't for you (yet). This looks like a PS3 game. I'm not talking about how the actual in-game characters look during fights (the sprites look amazing), I'm mostly talking about the menu textures, cutscenes, and any image that pops up looking muddy and pixelated. The SFX volume is louder than the rest of the game so it's something you need to adjust otherwise the opening cutscene and any SFX will be so loud compared to the actual game. On another side note, the game has severe lag issues (at least for me). Occasionally during training mode or doing challenges the game will slow down a lot for a few seconds. I don't think its my PC and has something to do with the game itself, but just be warned that it does severely affect gameplay since you will be playing at like 15 FPS. There are also major issues outside of it being a port, the game crashes when finding a public match online. This is normally inexcusable but this is something they are aware of and are planning on fixing very soon.The reason I added the (yet) part is because I feel like in the future people will make HD texture mods and other features. There is also a good chances Atlus themselves will continuously update bugs and sound errors before or when they add rollback this summer. This game is overall extremely fun to play with friends and offers fun single player content in the story mode for those who don't even enjoy fighting games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favourite fighting game of all time. I love the incredible mobility afforded to most characters and how they feel powerful to play as but also manageable to fight against, and really appreciate how well the personalities of the characters were captured. This PC version has been updated since my initial review and the most egregious issues have been resolved. However, as a port, this version still leaves some things to be desired compared to the PS4 version that launched at the same time.Pros- No problems with alt tabbing- Option to disable audio when the game is not in focus- Can plug in a controller after the game has started and it will be recognized- Supports modding custom palettes through palmodCons- Lacks the lobby system of the PS4 version where you can walk around a public room and play other players- The sprite scaling is messed up. The sprites in this game were intended for 720p, and appear smudged at high resolutions. As a result the game will never look fully 'right'. This is not the case in the PC version Blazblue CF, where at 1440p the sprites appear perfectly as this is just double 720p- Has more input delay than PS4 when not run at higher refresh rates (such as 144hz)- Some inconsistent issues with online play. One issue is that spectators will occasionally be desynced from the game they are watching

_childDocuments_.review: In P4AU, the characters from Persona 4 and Persona 3 once again find themselves teaming up to face off in the P-1 Climax, a series of battles which must be won before the world ends. The original cast of characters from Persona 3 and 4 are back to discover the mastermind behind the whole tournament, while a few new faces join the fight, including Junpei Iori, Yukari Takeba, Rise Kujikawa, and more. But standing in their way is the dual katana-wielding Sho Minazuki, a huge threat to everyone involved in the P-1 Climax. Worse yet, there's a Sho lookalike who can wield a Persona...

name: Soulstice
detailed_description: The balance of the Holy Kingdom of Keidas is compromised when powerful, feral creatures known as “Wraiths” invade from the other side of the Veil, threatening to consume the living. Wraiths corrupt their victims and can even possess their bodies, turning into unstoppable monsters that prey upon the common folk. The “Chimeras”, hybrid warriors born of the union of two souls, are the only ones who can protect humankind. Briar and Lute are two sisters who have been reborn as a Chimera. The transformation has granted Briar superhuman strength and resilience, while Lute, sacrificed to bind her soul to her sister’s, has become a shade with mystical powers. Voiced by Stefanie Joosten (Metal Gear Solid 5), Briar and Lute are sent on a mission to reclaim a city in ruins that has been ravaged by the Wraiths, only to discover that the Order they belong to has a far more complex plan in mind. Explore a dark world brimming with hidden mysteries, master a diverse combat system, and inhabit the dual forces of two sisters in a coming-of-age dark fantasy story with fast-paced action, vicious enemies, and spectacular boss fights. Key Features Fight in Synergy - Manage sisters Briar and Lute simultaneously. Master melee attacks and combos as Briar and take control of the battlefield with otherworldly abilities as Lute. Combine their strengths to unlock powerful, transformational abilities and tap into their true potential as Chimera. Explore a City in Ruin - A Tear in the Sky has opened above the once-holy city of Ilden. As Briar and Lute fight to reach the Tear, they’ll face challenging puzzles and unveil secrets of the Order while their surroundings become more hostile and twisted. Customize Weapons and Abilities - Weapons are unlocked and upgraded throughout the game and can even be switched on the fly to unleash stylish and highly devastating combo attacks. Battle Different Enemy Classes - A vile mix of Wraiths, Corrupted and Possessed, have poured into the world from beyond the Veil. Utilize Lute’s unique auras to expose or weaken these creatures and adapt to a flow of battle that never feels the same. Learn the Truth of Your Origin - Through a dark story filled with sisterly love and sacrifice, Briar and Lute discover the truth about themselves and their Chimera powers while working together and staying true to their unbreakable bond.

_childDocuments_.review: It's kinda worth checking out, but take a large pinch of discounted salt. And if you run into huge framerate issues right away, give -d3d11 argument a try. Made a massive difference for me.Story is engaging and the art direction creates an enjoyable environment. There's just enough compelling worldbuilding to get you interested in what else is going on outside the main story arc. Characters have personality and charm.Now the gameplay is probably a hit or miss. I don't mind the locked camera, but I do have to agree with the negative reviews about the Blue/Red mechanic. It was a pain in the ass and was hard to keep track of. An even bigger issue for me was that the combat itself just didn't feel very enjoyable. It was long, repetitive and was used as padding. Exploration was very linear and the only engaging bit was struggling to work out which path is towards main quest and which one is the side-path to hidden rewards.There's some helpful accessibility features, but the defaults are kind odd. It pauses conversation after each line, waiting for a prompt. You can make them go automatically, but then you can't fast forward. A lot of UI elements like selecting Continue on start menu want you to hold a button to activate. You can disable that too, but then you run into a problem where you can now insta-skip a cutscenes. Someone must've noticed that problem, so they added an additional confirmation screen for skipping cutscenes. It's a lot of fixing stuff with layers of additional complexity where the problem was just not understanding how to set up reasonable defaults like everyone else does.

_childDocuments_.review: A neat little game in a genre that's far from crowded; despite my 'not recommended' consider going for it if it seems up your alley. The influence of PS2-era action games, as well as dark fantasy anime like Berserk and Claymore is a selling point and almost enough to carry it... if not for some pretty significant flaws in the core gameplay.- Of all the things to take inspiration from, the colour-coded enemies of the Ninja Theroy DmC was not one. It's a tedious system at best and infuriating at worst.- Horrid camera, even when compared to the old titles this is inspired by. A whole lot of enemies throwing projectiles and dashing around, which you can rarely see save for a little prompt/arrow which isn't always available.- Combat ends up feeling clunky due to inconsistent enemy tells and inconsistent stuns/staggers on enemies. - Heavy reliance of gimmicks and swarms of enemies. Individually, these wouldn't be too bad, but when you have swarms of enemies of both colours, combined with projectiles and dashing enemies, combined with the camera... you get the idea.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice isn't close to as good as Devil May Cry, but you almost certainly weren't expecting it to be, as that would be insanely unfair. You'd expect the best thing about the game to be the combat, but it's actually the story that has the most oomph. There's a lot of attention to the narrative here and, truth be told, it's one of the best stories I've seen in an action game that wasn't made by Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio. The combat is the second best thing here and it does provide what I was looking for in a character action game. The weapons are fast and mostly pretty fun and switching between them is seamless. But you can only change out one of your equipped weapons, not both, which is a waste. The MC always has her basic sword on her and there's no good reason you can't swap that for something else. It significantly limits how much you'll be able to mix and match your attacks.The ghost girl attached to the MC is a unique touch, as she helps out and basically hands most of the game's parries. As you unlock new moves for her, she uses more and more of her essence, which makes it much easier for her to overload herself, which causes her to vanish. This can get a little annoying, as can the Ikaruga-esque nature of switching between red and blue alignments to damage specific enemies, especially when forgetting the alignment is active can cause you to overload. The enemies are varied and mostly fun to fight, although certain red enemies have blue ghost enemies leave their bodies when you beat them, which requires you to kill the ghosts or have the red enemies heal and get back into the fight.The weakest aspects here are the level design and the camera. The levels are really repetitive and can go on too long. There are platforming sequences but these are lackluster, as the camera is often so far away that you might not be able to see what you're doing, which also extends to when the camera takes a distant vantage point during combat. The camera in general doesn't feel up to modern standards, as it's hard to lock onto who you want when the area's crowded and the camera loves to whip around randomly or have other enemies or walls obstruct your view. It's messy. As for performance, the game often runs very badly even on good hardware. I often got framedrops into the 40s. If you use Vsync, the game will lock cutscenes at 30 fps, but gameplay was bizarrely unaffected for me. I don't recall any crashes, though. Soulstice is a decently long experience, as it took me about 15 hours. It'll take more if you want to conquer the higher difficulties or track down all the upgrades and challenges. I also have no idea how to do the synergy attacks, as the game doesn't teach you. The help menu sort of explains it, but I never got it to work. Still, this is a pretty good game. It's not nearly on the same level as Assault Spy but the guy who made that is amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: I've wrestled with whether to give this a good or bad review. If there were a neutral option, I would have picked it, but I can't in good faith give it a good review. First, let's cover what is good about Soulstice.The setting, art style, world, and story of Soulstice is wonderful. And because of this I played the game through to completion. I don't think I have ever completed a game and then given it a bad review. You quickly get attached to Briar and Lute and want to see them succeed. So why the bad review? Well, the camera angles are actively awful and make the game irritating to play. They also stop you enjoying the awesome setting. There is a point late in the game where you have to finish a jump puzzle with a time limit and the camera makes it exceptionally frustrating. The same frustration regularly occurs in combat. While we're on the combat, all the weapons are nearly indistinguishable. They might as well not have bothered. I played the game through on the hardest available setting and didn't die until the last act. The challenge in fighting enemies lies mostly in gimmicks (you have to be in a certain 'mode' to kill certain enemies) and these gimmicks are not fun, they're frustrating. I have more complaints about the combat, but frankly I think I'll stop there. To summarise, the story/art/setting is beautiful and compelling, but all aspects of the janky devil-may-cry-esque gameplay are just frustrating.Story 8/10Gameplay 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: Rule of life friends: If IGN said no...... It's a yes.This is one of those games that people will look back really fondly on as time goes on. It’s a love letter to Berserk, Claymore, and Devil May Cry, a fantastic combination of inspirations. The game is awesome, and gave me hope for what a Dante's Inferno remake could be like!Soulstice is one of the most intense games I’ve played in recent memory. I can't stress it enough, this game is bonkers, it is flashy, hard as nails and most of all, it made me break a sweat, and one of those good ones, like when we used to play a hard old school Playstation game where the game is hard, the bosses are insane and larger than life.It felt like old school God of War/DMC with a modern look and feel. It really gives you the best PS2 era vibes with its combat, enemy design and exploration. Only downside is the combat isn't as fluid as I'd like from an action game.   The setting is cool and beautiful, the story is interesting too. There's also no "trudging back and forth" as it's literally linear. Also, the camera work is fine and seems very similar to the og DMC but improved and in battles you can freely move the camera around.   It also doesn't hold your hands, a lot of things are left up to you to find out, like how to make a perfect counter etc. If you enjoy a challenge and insane boss fights and a lot of flashy moves and style, you will love this game.I'm glad these medium budget / "AA" niche titles have been popping up more frequently as of late. Soulstice especially is more than welcome, since it fits into a genre that's criminally underused, being pretty much limited to DMC and whatever Platinum puts out (that's not Babylon's fall).If you loved games like DMC/NIER/CHAOS LEGION, then you will be right at home. If you loved BERSERK or CLAYMORE then you will feel right at home. Anyone who loved that early to mid 2000s era of character action will eat this up. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: A love letter to the original Devil May Cry, Claymore and Beserk.If you enjoy the the classics, then you will enjoy this too. This game stays surprisingly true to the sources it draws inspiration from, and that's a rarity in todays age. Zoomer opinions about "fixed camera" doesn't need to apply. It adds to the charme.The ending hints heavily at a sequel, so let's hope they will flesh out the game even more.A solid 7.5/10 for a 20 hour game. Hope we see more Italian DMC.Pros- A small but diverse enough variety of weapons, which keeps the combat interesting- The atmosphere and design is wild. Especially the body horror was really surprisingly well done.- The story is simple enough to be interested in, but the game doesn't lose itself in it.- The edge- Interesting AI compantion system, but the system will need to be heavily fleshed out for future games.- The combo system has some debts, but it is kept simple enough that even beginners will have fun playing it- several difficulty options. Unfortunately, the hardest ones are locked behind the first playthrough, the default "hard" still can feel easy for curazhee veterans.Cons- Others praise the "exploration" - I found the levels to be quite linear. If that's a good or bad thing, I let you decide. The levels felt too long in general.- The soundtrack was hit or miss.- In fight cutscene (Rapture, Berserk, etc...) just feel out of place and get tedious after a few times- Camera can be wank during combat in small arenas- Not a lot of variety in stage and level design. Pair that with 45-60min stages, and you see why some people call the game "tedious".Others:- Interesting AI compantion system, but the system will need to be heavily fleshed out for future games.- The soundtrack was hit or miss.- The DmC color coded mechanic is back. While it is executed rather well, the later levels especially rely too heavily on it, so you're constantly ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ colors which simply just isn't fun.- Skill tree for AI companion is interesting, but it feels very shallow with the gatekept tiers. Most of the players will probably have focused on the same Chaos/Tricker talents like anyone else before realizing you just max out everything eventually anyway
