_childDocuments_.review: If you can get use to the terrible camera angels, then its a really good game: - musics are awesome, - voice actors/actresses are excellent- hack and slash playstyle are enjoyable (somewhere between diablo and DMC)- even the story is goodAs I mentoined, only downside is the camera (and its not a minor issue). Maybe the Dev will change it later.All in all, its an enjoyable game
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I would like this game. I didn't think I'd love it. But I'm happy to be wrong. This game is amazing and I had a blast the whole way through. Soulstice follows in the footsteps of other over-the-top action games like Bayonetta and Devil May Cry, but personally I liked the setting and story of Soulstice a lot more. The backstory and lore were interesting, and I really like that even though the levels themselves were not actually that big, the devs made them feel epic in scale with backgrounds that stretch way off into the distance. Obviously combat is the most important part of this game, and I loved it. It was smooth and fast paced with a good variety of enemies. A word of caution though - by the end of the game, combat is pretty hectic with a ton of stuff happening all over the screen. You'll be comboing, dodging, countering, turning 'fields' on and off, watching the unity meter, using synergy attacks, and switching weapons on the fly to use the right one against the right enemy. If that sounds like too much then maybe this isn't the game for you, but if you put in some effort to get to where you can handle all that and come out the other side with a diamond or platinum rating, you feel like such a boss. But also, if you still want to experience the game despite the difficulty, there are some options to make combat waaay easier and accessible to more casual players. A lot of people complained about the camera, but patches have since improved it and I was fine with it. It just takes some getting used to. I think a lot of players feel paranoid initially about sometimes having enemies off screen, but eventually you learn how to pay attention to the counter indicators, and you get a sense of what you do and don't really have to worry about, and what enemies to prioritize first. Also it seems like some players had graphical or stuttering issues, but I can say it hasn't been a problem for me. The game runs perfectly fine on my old gtx 1650 laptop.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: The story is set in a dark-fantasy world with developing characters. Following the journey of two sisters, a cautious handler and fiery reject warrior. Sent to a desolate high city to investigate and clear the way of hostile forces found for the main army. They speak to each other while traveling or  fighting, keeping the silence away. Both changing as the story develops.The gameplay is balanced between fighting difficulties, and brain-dead puzzles. You're provided a red-blue color system to match most enemy types, and a few weapons to counter them. Abilities and Weapons upgrades are acquired by purchasing or completing Trials found throughout the game. Completing a combination attack with the same weapon will trigger a "synergy" attack that does higher damage, and has wider/longer hit box.The OST is a sound of Electric Symphonic Metal, fitting the gritty dystopian particle heavy world that will rotate tracks on fights.  The core cons to the game is it's camera positioning for some portions of the game, and animation locking for specific attacks.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible nostalgia scratcher from games like Devil May Cry and God of War.Story is new, interesting and fun to keep up with.Gameplay is fun, impactful, unique. The Red/Blue aura mechanic is new and a challenging kind of fun. The second character acting as a independent support is great plus the parry system feels very nice, being able to parry dozens of enemies around you while focusing on one or more. The scoring system showing up every battle feels great as an instant reward and as a pointer for wether you're doing good or could do better.The animations and visuals are beautiful, AAA type quality.I was very pleasently surprised.IMHO a true hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: A really nice surprise and it exceeded my expectations !Soulstice deliver a good fast paced and satisfying combat system.Honestly chaining combos feels really nice and the last time I enjoyed the combat that much in a game it was with Devil May Cry 5.Of course the combat system in Soulstice is not perfect and it does have it's flaws, most issues will come later in the game though.In the later levels the combat will become quite chaotic with lots of enemies on screen and it can be hard to avoid getting hit by some spinning enemies or AOE attacks.So no the combat in Soulstice is not as good as Devil May Cry, Bayonetta or God of War, it can become confusing and it can get a bit repetitive but it's still really well done.The game also have great characters and monsters design, the animations are top notch and the graphics looks really nice too, there's some pretty amazing vistas to be found here.Soulstice level design is good but very linear, it still does reward exploration and you will get extra items if you take time to explore the levels.Unfortunately the fixed camera angles and some platforming parts can get annoying at times but nothing too bad.Average first playthrough should be around 16-25 hours depending on which difficulty you choose and if you do challenges and explore the maps.If you grew up playing the afformentioned titles and enjoy character action games then give it a shot, pretty sure you won't be disappointed.Soulstice ain't game of the year material but it's definitely a good game knowing it was made by a very small team.Honestly for such a small team I think they did really well and this game feature really high production values IMHO.All in all we get good voice acting, quality cutscenes, slick looking menus and most importantly a great combat system.Now about the pricing, well I think 40€ is a steep price, especially at this time of the year when there's tons of new games coming out.The game is good but considering DMC 5 is now being sold at less than 10€ on sale I think waiting for a discount for Soulstice might be your best option if you are unsure about the game.It's a nice game but it's far from perfect, there are issues and some weird design decisions like how the unity system works, some strange choices in colors which can mess with player visibility.Anyway I have to say congratulations Reply Game Studios I really like your game and I'll be sure to follow whatever you create going forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Short version, this is why I hate the binary 'yes or no' aspect of steams reviews. Do I recommend this game? For the average person, god no stay away. For someone that's a fan of Devil May Cry and wants to play a game like it? Absolutely, but pick it up on sale, this game is far too jank and far too infuriating in its later stages to warrant full price.I beat this game on its normal mode, Initiate.GraphicsThe game has a heavy anime style to it and on the surface it looks fantastic and runs okay. The biggest issue however is that the game only takes place in a single environment... for 20 hours. So you'll be spending 20 hours in the same castles, sewers and monasteries that are all blue or teal. Except the final 3 levels where the game throws you a curveball and makes everything PURPLE. Yeah, not great. This game is already way too damn long, and the fact every level sort of blend into one another does not help one bit. So even though the game looks nice, the lack of variety hurts replayability heavily.StoryThe game has HEAVY inspiration from the Berserk and Claymore mangas, which I'd recommend checking out if you thought this game's story was cool. Claymore is also a story about a mysterious organization fusing humans with other wordly forces to become living weapons, and if they push themselves too far they 'awaken' and become powerful demons themselves. Berserk is present here more in the aesthetics and general vibe of everything instead of actual story content. Briar makes quite a few guts poses on her journey though, so there's that.SPOILERSThe game ends on a cliffhanger with  superheavy sequel-baiting, which is infuriating considering how much padding this game has, by the end of the game it feels like we're only about halfway through the actual narrative, which after 20 hours of fast frenetic gameplay is a bit of a slap in the face. At the same time, I do hope they make a sequel, because this game could really use a further refinement of its ideas and combat. The biggest issue with the story is that there's actually too damn much of it. This is a character action game, not a AAA adventure game like God of War, I'm here to play video game not sit and listen to characters talk for 20 minutes every level. Each and every level is filled with dialogue and cutscenes, damaging replayability severely. LevelsThis game is TOO DAMN LONG. Getting it yet? This game is around 19-21 hours in length on average, which is kinda nuts for a character action game. Most of the ones I've played personally are usually 6-10 hours on average, half of this game, and are usually packed with far more actual story and have a much higher variety of environments to explore. Most levels blend together and don't really feel all that unique, I just beat the game 10 minutes ago and the only levels I remember off the top of my head are the boss levels and the elevator. That's it. I remember 5/25 levels after just beating the game. Oof. CombatThe actual core combat is actually super solid. Hits feel chunky, animations are satisfying, the sounds are satisfying, enemies explode into gore when killed which is fun. You have massive arsenal of weapons at your disposal, including a chain whip, a sword-axe combo, a bow, blade gauntlets, and more. The weapon variety is fun and the combos are cool, but most weapons' movesets sort of blend together and do the same things. This makes switching between them easy, but it also means the only reason you'd ever take out more than just the sword is for the sake of your score, and the fact that enemies have weaknesses to specific weapons.Lute's abilities are cool, but her (aka your) defensive options are severely lacking. When it comes to larger enemies or bossfights, all you can do is use the slowdown counter, which doesn't actually make them stop their attack, all it really does is slow the fight to a crawl and due to the iffy nature of your dodge i-frames, means most fights against larger foes turns into a game of touch-and-go, which is awful. CameraThis games camera is awful. Like im just gonna come out and say it. It's bad. Fixed camera angles aren't the issue here, its more that the camera is so damn far away from the action at times its impossible to tell whats happening. Not to mention, the game expects precision platforming of you with these fixed camera angles, yknow, when you have 0 depth perception??? There was a platforming segment near the end of the game that really drove me nuts because of this, I feel like it wasn't even playtested. A lot of this game's later half feels like that. EnemiesThe enemies have a great variety, which is good. The enemies are also more often than not, a pain to fight, which is bad. You fight way too many enemies, and the enemies have way too much health, turning most fights into incredibly dragged out slogs that can take forever to end. I was only playing on normal, and the time to kill for most enemies was absurd. I thought this meant the health of enemies was shared on all difficulties, which would've been great, but no, I went up to Knight to try it out and enemy health was damn near DOUBLED. It already takes half a year to kill some of the enemies like the summoners, why in god's name would you make that take even longer??? Honestly, some of the par times on some of these fights have to be a joke, I refuse to believe anyone tested some of the combat encounters.Enemies lack any good telegraphs. As you play you get mentally conditioned to see Lute's counter prompt as the indication of incoming attacks, when this isn't shown, you have so little time to react its usually impossible to get out of the way in time. Enemies have such little telegraphing its nuts, no audio cues, barely any visual cues. Even the massive lumbering dudes with the hammers give you less than half a second before they swing, which is just nuts, and incredibly unfair and unfun to fight against. This extends to when they are out of view of the camera, all you get is a red arrow, which doesn't tell you anything, especially if its an incoming ranged attack. You're too busy juggling a million other things to focus on the arrows anyways, enemies need more obvious visual and audio cues, otherwise the combat becomes incredibly unfair really fast. Also they can stunlock you and wombo-combo you into oblivion, which, yknow, that's great. BossesBosses are hit or miss, the first true boss you face in level 14, Jared, is a super fun and satisfying encounter. The next true boss you face, the bird lady, is alright, but she spends too much of the fight running away and she has way too much health, making her a chore to fight. The second-to-last boss is fun, but the final boss. Hoo-boy. Whoever thought it was a good idea to end their game off with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ SAVIOR FROM DMC4, ONE OF THE WORST BOSSES IN DMC HISTORY, should be fired or slapped several times in the face for gross incompetence. One of the only times in the game I ever used an item, I just really wanted it to be over with, an absolutely awful fight and it definitely soured the rest of the experience for me. MusicMusic is good, a solid score overall, though my favorite track, the song that plays in the challenge rooms, is not available in the official soundtrack. Please fix. Voice ActingVoice acting is amateur, but you can tell they’re giving it their all. Hammy performances all around, but I give an A for aeffort. Except the bird lady, her VA was downright awful. Layton’s VA was my favorite.  ConclusionThis pains me, because I did have a lot of points where I had a ton of fun, but also a ton of points where this game absolutely infuriated me. The game is far too long, far too padded, and far too janky. I will not be playing this game again, that's for certain. Which is unfortunate, cause I do feel it has a lot of potential. I hope if that fated sequel ever arrives, it fixes a lot of the issues I have with this game as it stands.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun at some points, but the fun was dragged down by mindless sections with easy puzzles that still required annoying platforming. The voice acting was terrible, and the story was only mediocre. Lots of amateurish problems like glitching in the cut scenes, characters repeating dialogue until you hated them, and thousands of sweeping cutscenes that just showed the room you entered.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fantastic!I was not ready for how attached to the characters I became. There were so many pitfalls the devs could have tripped in but they did an incredible job with Briar and Lute. For example, they NEVER fight or bicker. I can't tell you how utterly refreshing it is to have characters in a bleak setting trust each other like they do - and it feels earned. The gameplay rips. The weapons are cool and versatile with great sound design; and all your enemies explode into nice meaty chunks. Not a lot to complain about. Setting is great. It's kinda a play on the big spooky castle - except an entire city. It gets a little samey, but they mix it up well enough. Soundtrack kicks all kinds of ass. Wish we had more tracks.Camera isn't as bad as many people make it seem. It's an oldschool design choice that carries with it the oldschool problems. The real issue is the lock-on button, which can be unresponsive at times when trying to switch to a new target. The game can be really challenging on harder difficulties. Even when maxed out, one mistake can cost you. The game has got some serious bite which I love.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: I really-really want to like this game, I love a lot of the things it does, but it falls so flat in gameplay that I just can't recommend it.I love the artstyle. I love most of the enemy designs, at least in terms of visuals. The music is great. The characters are decent. The story is alright. I LOVE the fixed camera angles during exploration and platforming, they are absolutely delicious.But my God, the combat is just not good, and combat is what you will be doing most of the time in this game, so it needs to be good. A lot of enemies barely react to your attacks. You hit an enemy with a huge two-handed sword and you might as well be hitting them with a wet noodle with how little they react to it. Secondary weapons don't feel different enough, they all have the same moves, and only real difference between them is the skill price and what type of enemies they deal extra damage to.The proficiency system is also bad because a lot of the times the combat is too frantic to pull off the more advanced combos, especially seeing how enemies don't really react to your attacks much, and since you don't get a lot of opportunity to pull off cool combos you kinda just purchase proficiency upgrades just to deal more damage per hit to specific enemies because otherwise the combat is just gonna be tedious.Also the combat camera is absolutely god awful. Devs had these amazing fixed camera angles that show the entire arena and for some reason they decided to just not use them, instead replacing them with a super claustrophobic free camera that makes it hard to keep track of the entire arena, making the combat even worse as you can't see enemies attacking from behind and stuff. The little warning arrows they put in the game don't really help either.Also the blocking system with Lute is bad. It's a neat concept, but the execution is horrible. It would've been better if you combined the dodge and block button into one, so if you stand still - you block and if you block and move - you dodge, and have Lute be more of a manual thing, allowing you to choose when to shoot her magic blasts instead of it happening automatically. And then instead of having three different types of block you could have Lute freeze enemies on a perfect dodge and stun them on a perfect block, and have her return fire if you perfect block a projectile, not have this weird system where the kind of block you get is determined by the type of enemy you're blocking against. Plus the windows on blocking attacks are so abysmally short, they maybe could've worked with a more traditional block system but they just don't mesh with the existing system at all.Edit: I have re-evaluated my thoughs a little bit on the combat system - it works well for boss fights. Especially when you're fighting the transcended, those fights work (mostly) well with the combat system this game has. But it just kinda falls apart when you're fighting regular enemies, which is obviously something you encounter way more than bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Got this in one of those Fanatical Bundles a while ago. I really liked the dark fantasy atmosphere in this game. Combat is decent since you can dual wield different weapons (sword, pickaxe, whip, etc.) that can each be upgraded. A lot of skills to upgrade also for both your physical character and spirit helper. Not sure about the story since I skipped every cutscene. The color switching mechanic became way too tedious for my liking. The fixed camera is annoying but not a dealbreaker for me. Actually, I think It adds a cinematic flair to the otherwise dull environments. My dealbreaker is the fact that bosses that can heal themselves. They already have massive health bars and to just add that nonsense is a huge slap in the face for the "easy" difficulty I was playing on. Common enemies are already extremely spongy. Seems like most enemies took like 20 hits to kill, no matter what weapon combo I used. If you can put up with the above annoyances, you might enjoy this long indie game (at 11 hours I was not even halfway through the game according to guides) but I just couldn't take any more of the spongy enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a great and polished AA-tier game, but not without its downsidesLet's break it down:1. SettingDevelopers drew inspiration from such mangas as Berserk, written by Kentaro Miura and Claymore, written by Norihiro Yagi. It really shows, especially when it comes to Claymore - what we have is chaos spawns that pose a great danger to humanity and special warrior breed created for the sole purpose of defeating them. What's so special about them, you ask? They are partly chaos spawns themselves! Very dangerous, if you ask me.World is torn apart by those monsters and countless villages and people suffer horrific fate, while it's not even what they should fear the most - The Veil. The Veil is basically, well, a barrier that protects this world from chaos realm, birthplace of all chaos spawns.This sure smells like something I would like, and I was right - I really love this setting. C'mon, it's dark fantasy, after all.2. PlotWell, I will be honest, plot is not something new or unique, it's predictable, although still quite curious and breathtaking in a way. Remember The Veil mentioned above? Usually, just a small quantity of chaos spawns can tear through The Veil, and even they can wipe whole villages, you can fathom what would happen if The Veil is to be torn.The Veil was torn and so chaos spawns rush into this world. But how can this be even possible, how The Veil was torn? What exactly happened here, in Ilden? Find out yourself...I think it's worth mentioning that their story is not quite finished in Soulstice, they obviously have plans for a sequel.3. CharactersCan't say much about characters, there are too few and most of them won't appear until the very end. I feel like they got too little attention and were discarded, aside of a few chosen ones.Chosen ones get some proper developments though.4. Style & MusicStyle is heavily inspired by Claymore and a little bit by Berserk, but still shows something new. Claymore shows almost everywhere - boss designs, special abilities of main characters, some enemy designs, locations.Main character, Briar, is basically a female Guts (Berserk main character). Not a bad thing, not a bad thing at all. I love it greatly!Music? Yeah, about that. It's a little bit unusual to hear electo music mixed up with some epic notes, but it's always used properly and still fits what's happening around you. But also, I love me some epic chorus.5. Locations & Level designThat's where some issues start to appear - locations are pretty, but seem kinda identical. I had a feeling I didn't leave the sewers for like 70% of the game.Locations are mostly linear, but some of them can surprise you.Each level is full of different puzzles and platforming elements, they can be annoying at times, but add to variety of gameplay and it feels nice to do something other than fighting hordes of enemies while you advance further.6. GameplayFirst things first - Soulstice has a system with blue and red auras you can use to destroy crystals that block your path, get some currency or jump on specific platforms. That being said, they also are used in combat - and hooo boy, it's a pain in the ass. Maybe it was a difficulty issue (I completed the game on Knight difficulty), but there were too many enemies and too many of elite ones especially. Elite enemies, you see, have two types, just as well as auras - red and blue. Both of them cannot be damaged without correct aura usage, and that's where the fun starts - red enemies (most of them) spawn blue enemies when they are defeated and you need to destroy blue enemies, otherwise red one you just defeated will ressurect. Now imagine that you fight dozens of red enemies, dozens of blue enemies, you need to block them all, use correct aura and make sure not to overuse it so you can't activate it for some time. Sounds like a bother, right?Weapons. There are seven weapons in total, each effective against certain enemy types, you can freely switch between them and chain combos, it's a slasher, after all. Combos are fine, but main weapon (starting sword) is always with you and has too few combos, which is kinda strange.Devil Trigger? Yeah, we have that! They made it look really cool actually and made sure to make it your last resort - since you kinda go full berserk mode and harm yourself more than usual - you can't block or parry attacks, only dodge them. I won't go into details - see for yourself, it's really cool.7. BossfightsThere are too few "real bosses", they have some questionable design choices but overall they are gorgeous and I love them. Aside maybe one them, I won't tell you which, but this boss is annoying as hell and I spent a few hours beating the crap out of them (there are platforming and illusions involved). What's so gorgeous about them, you ask? Well, they are a walking bullet-hell and melee death threat, and plus, honestly, they are stylish, and I love stylish things.8. Final wordsI think I reviewed everything I had on my mind and I hope it helps you decide on whether you want to pick this game or no. It was a very painful experience, but a very enjoyable one. Will play this game's sequel with great pleasure.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you Devs!Not every action game needs to be souls-like, Rouge-like!Don't get me wrong, these can be fun too, but it's been a while since we got one of these more DMC-like games!** Scroll down to the bottom for a note about older Polaris AMD cards performance.This game will take you back to the good old PS2/PS3 days, with some quality of life additions.So, classic level to level progress, stylish combat, ridiculous* slow mo cutscenes, bosses that talk too much and fixed camera angles!*Not as ridiculous as DMC and DmC, but still ridiculous enough.The combat execution itself isn't that complex, but it offers more and more layers and options as you progress, acquire new weapons and encounter new enemies. It is a bit like Ninja Theory's DmC with it's Blue and Red thing.In general it feels really good when you get the hang of it.One of the biggest criticism this game gets is the fixed camera angles, and how it likes to pull all the way back during exploration. For me, it certainly felt pretty jarring as I started off, even though I've played games like this in the past.And I think it is that this game does it a lot more often, and the levels themselves have pretty big spaces.Although later on it didn't bother me as much.As for combat, they give you camera controls, as well as the options to adjust both camera distance and field of view (which you'll need to max out for some optional challenges).The level design while I liked the design itself, visually, they could have used more variety. Like most of the game is just gray, same castle environment. And I get it is the color palette they choose to set the mood, but in 25 hours I finished the game, it got a bit repetitive seeing the same visuals, same lighting.I played on normal and the difficulty felt fair, only one boss in particular annoyed me quite a bit. But there are many difficulty levels, and even easier ones with assist should you wish.Sometimes the combat can become a bit overwhelming, with the number of enemy types and stuff on screen, and I think some enemies could use a bit of balance. Some are way too tanky imo.There is level replay, and hidden challenges to clear, so there a lot to replay and enjoy this game.You get ranks for combat and level clear, but no immediate ranking like DMC (A, B, C....). Instead you get Iron, Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum and Diamond. The better your rank, the more points you earn to spend on upgrades.Anyway for a small indie team, and for a new IP, this is really really good! I had a great time playing this and looking forward to more!I paid full price for this and I'd say it is 100% worth it!**Note: If you have one of the older AMD cards, like my RX480, expect to encounter a glitch in one of the levels. Due to a certain particle effect, the game locks itself to 15 FPS in a certain portion of the level. It is apparently not something present in Nvidia cards, and probably not newer AMD ones.I've contacted the devs about the issue and they said they could not reproduce the glitch, but they'll do their best to optimize the particles.The game otherwise runs fine.I'll update this review if there is improvement concerning this issue.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a 3rd person action game that focuses on fast and frenetic combat with characters and enemies that have a dark anime aesthetic.The cutscenes are good, even if the voice acting is uneven.  I enjoyed the combat as I improved with it and I was invested in the world enough that I would like to find out what happens in a sequel.  I spent about 50 hours to finish the game--and most challenges--on Knight (hard) difficulty without using items.  If you have any interest in this type of game, it is worth at least one playthrough.There are a couple issues I think kept this from being more popular:INFLUENCESFirst, I think it misses the most important features of the games it resembles (and possibly was inspired by).  The combat system is similar to Devil May Cry in that you are expected to keep up a continuous stream of actions against waves of enemies.  You even get a score and rating at the end of each battle, and at the end of each chapter.  Unfortunately, Devil May Cry fans often cite the creative possibilities of the combat as their favorite feature, and Soulstice combos are relatively simple.  You eventually obtain several weapons, but they mostly differ in that each will do more damage to specific enemies.  Otherwise it's just different animations.  They all have launchers, they all have gap closers, they all have delay combos, and they all have air slam attacks...and they all are done the same way on the controller.  You can switch between weapons in mid-combo, but that isn't to use the weapons for different purposes, it's just because it should increase your score.Since the combos are simple, I thought that perhaps the game wanted to be closer to the older God Of War games.  Unfortunately, the God Of War games were more about journeys through interesting levels and epic boss fights, and Soulstice's levels--while interesting to look at--lack much variety (note that this is also similar to Devil May Cry).CAMERA AND CONTROLS Second, the controls have some weird decisions.  Many of the complaints have to do with the fact that the game uses a fixed-camera at times.  This is mostly only between combat engagements, but occasionally for combat as well.  I rarely had any issues with these sequences, and I had very little issue platforming during these segments.The camera issue I have is the decision to keep the camera up close to your character during combat where the camera is free.  Enemies can and will attack you from off screen.  Some attacks have indicators before they pop, but it's still maddening have to constantly try and take the time to move your character to a position and rotate the camera to see important enemies that you may not be currently engaged with, and that is important because......you have a companion that has the ability to interrupt attacks from enemies.  You may be interrupting several attacks in quick succession, and you are trying to attack and dodge with the main character at the same time, so you can't be expected to learn a specific interrupt timing for each attacks.  Instead you get a button prompt on the screen that you want to press as soon as it shows up.  The prompt looks bad on its own, but worse is that because the camera is so close, they have to give you some sort of prompt for off-screen enemies and it's a tiny arrow that I don't think I've ever noticed fast enough.If they had gone the route of the old God Of War games where the camera would usually be back far enough to see the whole combat area, the issue over what you can see would be essentially eliminated.  (I'm also wondering if they couldn't have a distant camera and still have the interrupt button prompt because it would cover the entire enemy...may have backed themselves into a corner there.)The other part of this issue layer is small, but important, and that is weapon selection.  You select weapons with the D-pad, and since there are six that you can switch between, they put two weapons on the left/up/right parts of the D-pad (down is for items).  The problem arises in that they should have had it where one press gives you one of the weapons and two presses gives you the 2nd weapon.  Instead, it depends on what weapon you currently have!  For example, up on the D-pad represents the hammer or the whip.  If you currently have equipped the bow, then one press up gives you the hammer and two presses would give you the whip.  If you are already on the hammer though, one press gives you the whip, and two presses puts you back at the hammer!  You see the issue?  In the midst of combat, I should always be able to do the same button(s) for the same result.  It's an unnecessary complication for a game with combat that requires lots of quick actions.EXTRA NOTESBosses have great visual design and an epic feeling, but were not that difficult.  Note that the first boss, the big archer, is not indicative of what you will encounter later on.  There is much less chasing in all other boss fights.There is a layer of the combat where your companion has to create a particular color field (blue/red) to damage certain enemies.  It starts out feeling like a pain, but as you go through the game you will gain abilities that make using them easier.  You also learn to think of turning them on and off as parts of your combos rather than leaving them on long term, and eventually it's barely an issue.  I don't see it as a reason to not play the game.Another frustrating part early on is that you will feel like you are chasing enemies a lot.  This is another experience that will get better as you go.  Between the gap closer skill you can get for your first weapon, a ranged weapon, and a weapon skill that pulls you to an enemy, you eventually find that getting to enemies becomes less and less of an issue.This game is worth a buy at full price in my opinion, and don't let a few rough edges ruin the enjoyment you can have with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is the closest thing we're ever likely to get to a game adaptation of the Claymore manga, and this is absolutely a good thing. Soulstice delivers on the fantasy of playing a fantasy supersoldier struggling against the source of her own power to keep her sanity, while also managing to create an identity all of its own with a unique blend of influences and aesthetic flourishes. Camera work and grand vistas reminiscent of the original trilogy god of war games, baseline combat reminiscent of Devil May Cry and a visual aesthetic and setting tone comparable to Berserk, it's not wholly original, but still very fresh.It's not a perfect game. Some of the combat encounters are poorly balanced, certain environmental hazards get overused as combat elements and one or two boss fights have poorly communicated mechanics that led to frustrating ends. And the story, while competently put together and compellingly told, isn't going to set the world on fire. But what Soulstice does right more than compensates for its flaws in my opinion, and it gets things right where it counts. The combat is stylish and intuitive, synergising excellently with the narrative relationship the main characters have. Briar and Lute are as dependent on each other as people as they are mechanically, in a surprising and extremely impressive display of Ludonarrative Harmony, especially aided by the smooth and natural inclusion of Lute's mechanics. And the game's half-dozen true boss fights make great use of these mechanics, standing out as notes of powerful spectacle. A standout moment for me being using the phenomenally cool Berserk Mode mechanic to finish off a later boss, an experience I'm still coming down from the high of hours later.If you're into spectacle fighters, Soulstice is a comfortable recommend from me. Hurrah for the return of mid-range developers!

_childDocuments_.review: After playing the game almost completely (just an assumption) and trying to enjoy the game itself,i cannot recommend the game.The graphics are nice and the overall style is well made.The combat system and combat action is pretty good too.I also like the whole setting, story and characters, which reminds me of Claimore, a little bit of Berserk and DMC.But here are the things that buggle my mind:1) Locked Camera (while out of combat)Im trying to be as objective as possible, so bear with me.Due to the fact, that the camera isn locked while fighting, it's clearly a pure design driven decision.This feature provides a very specific perspective and thus provides partially critical or at least additional informations for the player while walking through the game. If it would'nt be locked, players are likely to miss out loot or other (hidden) content.Using this feature to literally guiding the player through a linear designed game is not an argument and if it's an argument for the developers, it's a bad one.The problem with the locked camera always appears while trying to "explore" the game.Sometimes the biggest challenge in the game are not the fights, but trying to jump on a small levetating platform.What do i mean by that?It happens, that the camera is positioned in a way, that makes 3D-perception and thus depth-estimation very hard.This results in absolute frustation just to try to jump from platfrom to platfrom while beeing vesseled by a limited ressource that sometimes is required to been able to use the platforms as actual (physical) objects to jump on.2) CombatBeen punished for starting an attack but not paying attention to attacks of the enemies is understandable.Provide attack indicators on the enemy or the environment for unblockable, unparryable(?) or that cannot be countered are a huge help.The problem starts, when the player cannot do s**t to avoide dmg from those attacks at all, due to missing delays between indicating an attack and executing an attack.Due to this problem, is faced several messy fights that got very frustating because of their unpredictability and could only proceed in the game due to my own stubbornness and possibly lots of luck with positioning and enemy behaviour.3) Why i stopped playing (highly personal opinion)I hate time-gate events in games.I cannot express how much i hate them because they inevitably cause unnecessary pressure.But what i hate EVEN MORE is when im forced to play over 10mins of progress again if i fail such an event.Yes, I'm not a good player, yes this could all only a "me"-problem, but punishing a player to throw away progress of such a time span is just ridiciolous.And yes, a part of that is related to the first point.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimately, the game's greatest strength is that it tries to be its own unique experience while borrowing from the hack-n-slashes that it's inspired by, specifically Devil May Cry. Excellent combat, cool visuals and a solid soundtrack round out this mostly enjoyable game. However, poor PC performance, obtuse camera angles, a surprisingly limiting 'colour field' damage system and other moments of jank hurt this experience. It's a good first attempt at creating a game like this, and with some feedback and re-thinking, a sequel could be truly great. If you enjoy the 'character action game' hack-n-slashes (DMC, Bayonetta, Metal Gear Rising, or even Castlevania: Lords of Shadow), then give this a try.Pros+ Cool, gothic visual presentation that's both anime and Castlevania-inspired.+ Fun, pumping soundtrack that vibes well with the action.+ Satisfying combat when you get into it. Each weapon feels good to use.+ Smooth, cool character animations and special combat cutscenes.+ Interesting story with good voice acting, engaging presentation.+ Boss fights are cinematic and challenging, cleverly using all mechanics.+ Enjoyable exploration that's rewarding, whilst building atmosphere for the world.Cons- Game performance is inconsistent at best, and straight-up bad at times. Frame rate is hardly ever stable, even with strong graphics cards and systems.- The fixed camera during fights and camera angles as a whole are not well implemented.- Using completion time as a negative for score hurts the exploration that the game clearly wants you to do; to discover items and secret missions.- The colour field system is very limiting to the combat and hard to juggle when things get hectic. Would've been better as a status effect that you have to manage, rather than a limited range 'field' that you need to get enemies into.- In-game character dialogue becomes repetitive, and it either needs to be less frequent or have more lines recorded.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming from the perspective of someone who is new to the hack 'n slash genre, Soulstice was a pleasant surprise. The combat features a variety of enemies and weapons (though there is a great deal of overlap in combo inputs for these weapons, if that matters to you) and enough different systems to manage (Entropy, Unity, counters) to keep it consistently fun and engaging, and it's all backed up by an energizing soundtrack.The game places a surprisingly heavy emphasis on its story and character development, aided by some great cinematics, as a pair of warrior sisters uncover a world-ending conspiracy in the sacred city of Ilden across 25 chapters. Fans of Claymore will be pleased to find that Soulstice proudly wears its source of inspiration on its sleeve, with numerous overt references and parallels to that marvelous manga/anime series. There are nods to other series like Berserk and Warhammer 40K as well.Unfortunately, the overall experience is dampened a bit by the platforming. I found that the combination of a fixed camera (which hindered depth perception) and tight timings on certain jumps made a few sequences frustrating. Thankfully, most of your time in the game is spent either in combat or simple exploration.On the whole, I really enjoyed Soulstice! I very much hope the dev team has plans for a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: it's about time someone wrote a review for this that isn't either a callously phrased "it wasn't for me" or a shallow comparison to other franchises. user reviews were a mistake and i resent gabe newell for making me read through the slop steam gremlins post constantly. anywayit is a side scrolling 3D hack n slash game. what we have before us is a product which does not stand out as fully unique, perfect, or revolutionary. what it does stand out as is adequately designed, moderately priced, and good looking. in the current era of game development and publishing i think people underestimate just how much these AA studios matter and benefit the medium. it is products like this that i never regret buying even if they don't end up having the staying power of the greatest hits of all time.if you enjoy this type of game and the aesthetic speaks to you, you probably wanna play this. that said let me get down and descriptive:you play as a sisterly bond that transcends life and death. you are a super soldier in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up fantasy military. a nuclear bomb has detonated in fantasy new york and you're the response team. little did you know, exposure to this fantasy radiation makes you become a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up magical girl. also professor layton is there? i understand now why back covers of books are the way they are....the game consists of a pretty tight game flow: traverse the linear levels, gather two types of currency and secret collectibles, while fighting increasingly complex and chaotic battles, and watch some cutscenes in between. you only have one profile, so you can new game+ before finishing the game on a different difficulty.now the meat and potatoes. does it game? does it POP? eh....mostly. let's get the bad stuff out of the way first. i won't lie to you, the camera angles are irritating. they are not good. no amount of genre-boner and love for the DmCs and Bayonettas of this world can fix what is broken. you will get annoyed at camera angles many times. you will have to do tedious platformer puzzles over and over because the stylistic camera and stark contrast lighting will make your spatial awareness fail in the most "OUGH" inducing way. the combat itself is quite nice. you can easily intuit how things work, the control scheme is well thought out, and getting a good score after a chaotic and breakneck fight feels very satisfying, like you did genuinely earn that badge (though the scoring system is still a little inscrutable to me). if you love to REACT FAST and PRESS BUTTONS GOOD you'll have at least a passably good time. you will be pressing a Lot of buttons, fast. the bosses are all fairly unique and well designed fights. however thanks to the chaotic nature of regular encounters they tend to feel a bit underwhelming in terms of challenge sometimes. the weapon skills are a bit boring and generic, and tend to simply repeat across weapons. the weapon variations are actually required for dealing with certain types of enemies. this one i find interesting because a major point of criticism in these types of games has always been weapons feeling unnecessary. having to switch weapons in an already very chaotic fight is certainly a challenge, much more so than juggling all the other commands, to me personally. i would have preferred to memorize different combos to deal with different enemy types, but i digress. there is also another set of skills which i will get into less as it ties directly into the story. these magic skills work a lot more passively and actually add variation to the game. by making use of a points alignment system, which skills you pick in these categories will have aesthetic and gameplay effects which is pretty cool. some closing notes on other aspects of the game's quality: -graphical fidelity is nice, framerate is stable throughout (i will post my specs below the review). -the voice acting is stellar, if you can stop yourself from blaming the voice talent for some woefully generic lines with hollywood emotions (they're all lute lines. i'm sorry lute. you are the weenie, i still love you)-the art direction is nothing special but very enjoyable. also a bit out there sometimes, definitely not afraid to be abstract and silly at times. -the music is perfectly middling most of the time, but then they bust out some bangers for powerful moments. -tasteful non-pornographic nip slip includedso overall i would say this game has a target audience. yes friends, it's another one for the queers and the auties. see you next time!

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - It's a good character action / spectacle fighter game. It's not without its flaws, but it's worth picking up on a sale.For fans of character action games, it's known that major releases are few and far between. Fortunately, Soulstice does a good job of reaching for some of the rather lofty heights of games like Devil May Cry, Ninja Gaiden, Bayonetta etc. The first and foremost important aspect of any of these games is combat, and they've done a rather good job at it for a first showing. There are 7 different weapons, each serving a different purpose and having their own strengths and weaknesses, both in literal "this does more / less damage to X enemy" and "slow + hard hitting vs fast + weak hits" ways. Swapping between them mid-combo is very simple and can lead to some pretty flashy moments. However, the weapons themselves aren't too terribly complex, and there are only a handful of moves for each (which may be a positive or negative depending on your preference). Being able to mix in counters while doing your moves is very satisfying, and makes it so you don't have to disrupt the flow of your attacks by mashing guard or dodge. Dodges in this game do have some generous i-frames, but use the Bayonetta system of "punishing recovery frames with 3 in a row" so you can't just spam it. The enemy variety is solid, and higher difficulties actually mix up the enemy placement rather than just making everything have more health + deal more damage, and I was pleased to see they avoided the pitfall of spongey enemies. They implemented a similar mechanic as the DmC reboot, with red and blue enemies requiring you to put up a red or blue "zone" buff respectively. It is fortunately significantly improved over the DmC implementation, and there are other aspects of that system worked in to the combat to make it more exciting as a resource management element. Even better, there's an option in the Accessibility setting to let the game handle that switching for you, if it's not a system you want to interact with. This isn't a perfect solution, and can get you in some trouble during platforming segments or general exploration, but the penalty for overuse of the buff is incredibly minor.Other Accessibility features include Auto Combat, and Auto Counter, both of which make this a very...well, accessible game if you're struggling. That, combined with 5 difficulty options, means there's a difficulty setting for just about any skill level of gamer. Lastly for the positives, the music is pretty good. It's not something I see myself listening to outside of the game or anything, but it serves its purpose well.As for negatives: there are a LOT of cutscenes. Not just in the story sense, but every time you use your "power up" form, and every time you use the "ultimate" out of it. You can disable the "hold to confirm" requirement, but if you do so, you have to hit two buttons every time you do either one of those things, which is frequent. Additionally, some levels have cutscenes that appear to be hiding loading screens, but do some in a little bit of a gratuitous manner (e.g. you may finish a fight, run a few steps, jump on a platform, then a cutscene plays of you jumping across some more platforms). The story is really nothing to write home about, it's full of lots of CHAOS and CORRUPTION and takes itself seriously. On top of all that, the voice acting ranges from decent to "embarassing for a Power Rangers villain" levels of bad. The main characters are what you're going to be hearing most of the time, and they're fine enough, but there are very few lines and it gets rather repetitive hearing the same ones over and over again. The last downside I have is that the first 1/2 of the game really drags on, and is full of sewer levels and overall just very "samey" environments.All negatives aside, I enjoyed the game. Personally, I don't see myself really revisiting it on the higher difficulties or going for any achievements, and most of the issues I have aren't something that can realistically be patched out. Overall, for a character action game there's a good foundation, and that's very commendable for this genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's fine generally, it really is but there's some minor bad points that quickly add up for me;- The controls have questionable stuff, like having a hard lock-on like Souls or DMC but your launchers and your "Stinger" type attack being two buttons pressed together. That makes it impossible to comfortably remap the light attack, which traditionally is on the left face button, but is now on the top. Why? It makes no sense, especially when you get other skills which make you, get this, stretch from the left button to the right button to do an instant parry. It's not possible, who the ♥♥♥♥ designed these controls? Once you get to fighting it devolves further...- The combat's really annoying, the enemies don't take turns like they do even in DMC, they have very badly telegraphed attacks sometimes with vague animations or instant hitboxes that don't match them, especially the bosses. All this while you manage your barrier so you can get invisible/invincible enemies damaged. It gets really egregious when the game has a mechanic dependent on seeing the moves and the button prompt in time to hit it so you can avoid an attack. This all works out really great when put into practice in a crowded room where you can't see what's going on and you're fighting with no eyes which leads into...- The camera. The camera is the worst part. Even if those other systems worked perfectly the camera would ruin it all. It's vomit-inducing. It's actually atrocious and the fact that they pick the WORST possible angles to do the PS1/DMC/GoW/fixed cameras is crazy. It's the worst part of the game and it's ever-present. It affects the combat, it affects the movement, it affects finding bonuses/challenges/items. It's extremely janky in ways I can't word properly.Edit: Scratch that, I'm not gonna finish this and I would refund it if I could. The way the encounters and enemies are set up later down the line is just too annoying. It's hard to see what you're doing, who's attacking, what's blocking your path, and you take free hits only for the game to be extremely strict with its ranks which in turn means you can't upgrade your options, on top of all the other issues. The controls, the camera, the enemy animations, the placement of things, etc. This game is bad, plain and simple, and while a lot of it is the camera, that's not most of it.

_childDocuments_.review: A really surprising well polished game, with that name I was expecting a Souls Like, but learned quick that I was playing a Devil May Cry Like instead, to the point of having even the fixed camera angles.The game is really competent and has a really engaging moveset of weapons, the start is a bit too slow and has a lot of sewer levels that feel samey and clearly padding. Once you get inside the city the game starts getting a bit more varied in its levels, but the asset reuse permeates a bit too much some areas making some levels be a huge blur on your mind. Overall Incredibly fun game though. Clear inspirations from Claymore, Berserk and Devil May Cry 4. The early bosses are terrible, but the main cast is incredibly engaging to fight against, albeit with a couple tough fights that really tire you. If you're fresh out of DMC's to play, this game scratched that itch so well for me that I actually went and beat it in three sittings. This game is pretty hard and I can see people who enjoy cuhrayzee games really feeling satisfied with the level of mastery you can get to with this game.tl:drGun TonfasGutsShierkeBerserker Armor Devil TriggerSpirit Rave mashing with L2 R2Please support this game, the passion and love is clearly felt throughout the entire game. The story was pretty fun to play through and it reminded me a bit of Nier Replicant in tone. Specially Briar's demeanor through the whole thing.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hyped for this since it was announced and it's pretty much just like I thought characters are a little flatter than much of what inspires the game but I love the world, from creative use of many dark fantasy tropes like Berserk to the store brand Gastu clones working for a shady organisation which is straight out of Claymore (that's how I'd describe the claymore too, not just the Ashen Knights)combat is pretty tight, with certain enemies requiring a different field from Lute, some people think it's annoying when wraiths (blue field) and possessed (red) are in the same fight but I just enjoy the challenge of switching targets. while Briar doesn't have a range of combos for each weapon like Dante from DMC does she has quite the range of weapons where the limited combos work uniquely for each weapon then there's the berserk mode. good lord the berserk mode. for one thing, it's actually a berserk mode wrenching control away from the player entirely with the only input being trying to make it stop as Briar screams death threats to a detergent or something and murders the rest of the game. the Donovan boss fight didn't stand a chance when I used itfrom the creative use of dark fantasy tropes to some older character action staples that can still age pretty well, Soulstice is  a great use of it's inspirations between death and transcendence a chimera chooses DEATH/10 would turn gameplay into a basic plea for reason again

_childDocuments_.review: (TLDR at the bottom) With the combat and hidden objects ripped straight out of GOW, and the situational mode switching Ikaruga, Soulstice doesn't do much you haven't likely seen in other games. That along with the lackluster exploration and the late game performance issues, one might wonder why i put so much time into this game, and why i recommend it.Graphics: Beautiful particle effects. The levels are modeled well. Its perfectly serviceable and i have no complaints in that aspect.Audio: Pretty good. The music brings the epic score you would expect from such a game, I was never annoyed or muted the audio.  The Voice acting was solid but . . . . sometimes Briar says some things like an English person, and most things like an American. That was weird. It could just be me but it wasn't a huge deal. Also, one time the main duo commented way too much on the level where the building you are in is collapsing. Other than that, no complaints.Story: There are 2 sides to this one. On one hand, the world. The story is epic in scale, with dark powers derived from chaos, A religion that permeates the entire story. It was never able to grab me in the same way something like Final Fantasy X did with a similar vibe to how the evils of the world, affect the culture of it. Most of the characters who inhabit it are uninteresting, which is fine because most are enemies. However, as I faced down the final boss, I was wondering in the back in my mind "Ok but how does this accomplish our goal?". In essense, I was confused. But, there was one shining beacon for me in this story. The relationship between the core duo was fantastic! I have never in my life cried over a video game relationship like i have with these 2 characters and i have played HUNDREDS of games. I mean it. This relationship is probably the best aspect of the game and certainly what kept me going to complete the story to the end. Chef's kiss.Combat:Movement across the battlefield feels fluid and consistent. The enemy designs are all interesting and best dealt with in different ways. Some enemies must be dealt with in incompatible ways while on the field at the same time so you must focus on one before going to the other. There are ranks given out after every battle, with a reward based on the rank you get. This incentivizes strategy, switching between weapons for optimal effectiveness. Fights are fast paces and chaotic so even though you are kind of given a "Dodge, block, or cancel most things" button prompt, it doesn't feel too easy because you are focusing on so many things. To speak about the fields briefly because they are such a big part of the game, You can switch between red and blue throughout the game. Both are able to do different things with the environment and some enemies can only be damaged when their corresponding field is up. There is no beneficial effect of having a field up. Only a way to bypass an obstacle. You have a limited time you can keep a field up, which can be upgraded. This of course, furthers the amount of strategy required during fights. I like all of these things.Exploration:This is the worst part of the game unfortunately and it can't be skipped when replaying. This dread replaying levels to unlock more things. The level design looks cool from screenshots and trailers, however the game takes place over a relatively small physical space. You fight through 6 environments that repeat as the story demands. This means environments repeat. alot. The levels themselves are filled with spots where you think "maybe there is a secret over here?" only to be met with an invisible wall. You can go down that ally but not THAT ally. This means unless you use a walkthrough, you are going to be running into invisible walls like an idiot all the time looking for extra stuff. The levels also seem to repeat themselves alot. No joke, i was using a walkthough to find extra upgrades and i thought one part of the level was a completely different part because it looked so similar. You can really see the reused assets in this game. As a result, its VERY easy to get lost. Sometimes a fight will break out but i would say about 50% of this game is platforming, and using the right fields to unlock/reach the end. Lots of upgrade materials are to be found, but its still a slog.Control Complaints / Suggestions: The combos are dumb. On a controller, it wants you to use Y+A  to use 2 different combos across every weapon. You realize i need to use my pointer and middle finger or thumb, to crab claw my controller? During combat and trying to avoid ♥♥♥♥? Ya i never used that once. Y + Y (pause) Y + Y + Y for your biggest move for the majority of the game? I feel they shouldn't have bound the sword to ALWAYS be X and allowed switching it like the other weapons. This would allow more things to be done with that button. Also move item wheel to (hold) D-pad down to free up that button as well.TLDR: I have complicated feelings about Soulstice. It does so much right, However it also fumbles super hard on half of its gameplay for me. There is a way to make it work and i hope in Soulstice 2 (hopefully) we see alot of its shortcomings ironed out. I want to see this duo again. Its worth it for them alone for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game for free on Epic and beat it on the hardest initial difficulty. I straight up purchased it here on Steam because these devs deserve the support more than 99.9% of the other studios out there trying to push out 'AAA' titles that end up having sterilized games devoid of any 'soul' in terms of lore, story telling, or even quality gameplay.Fair warning, the camera angels are fixed in alot of places, and I am quite happy with that personally because it feels like a callback to older games such as Castlevania: Lords of Shadow or the Devil May Cry and God of War series pre-Viking era.In terms of storytelling the game is like a high quality anime through and through, my only regret here is that there is no Japanese voice over for the whole thing but the English VAs do an amazing job, better than most high budget dubs out there.In terms of gameplay this is a genuine love letter to all the old school hack n slash titles I mentioned above. Once the action starts it doesn't relent except to allow to explore and each encounter feels like a step up the ladder from the last until by the end you are feeling amazed at yourself for pulling off wild combo strings while avoiding an insane number of hits in the thick of chaotic combat.Anyway... the tl;dr of this rant is that the devs care for their game really shows in every possible way and I can only hope this series continues because it is a true joy to play and immerse in.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a terrible game but it’s pretty basic in comparison to other games in the genre, you're better off playing Devil May Cry, or Bayonetta, or Metal Gear Rising, or the original God of War games, or Transformers Devastation, or any other highly regarded hack n slash that i forgot to mention.This game has got lots of weapons that you can switch between on the fly but all of them have pretty limited amount of attacks, every single once has a ground combo, an extended ground combo, a launcher, and an air knock down attack with the same inputs across all of them.The slowdown can also be a bit crazy as the game goes into slow motion whenever you do a stinger or end most extended ground combos. The worst problem of all I’d say is the different coloured enemies that you can only attack if you have a field activated which you can only have on for a limited time before it needs to cool down, there are upgrades to help prevent it from getting to the point of needing to cool down but it doesn’t fix the problem outright.The story isn't anything i could really get invested in either.Pretty disappointing because I really wanted to like this one especially considering how few and far between games in this genre are.(Funny enough for all the reviews complaining about the camera that's actually something i didn't have problems with, although the lock on system wasn't very good.)

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun spectacle fighter with fun weapons, an interesting open ended story and great visuals. There are two problems with the game. The first is that the static camera makes using keyboard and mouse for some of the platforming and combat a bit more difficult than they are with a controller or than they would be with a free camera. The second is that there aren't that many variations in attacks within a weapon but being able to switch between all seven weapons at once almost makes up for that. Still a great game, hoping for a sequel to see how the story continues!
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst Soulstice has it's flaws in places, it's still a must play for any character action game fan.Combat feels great and rewarding to master. Whilst there isn't much in the way of combos, your attacks still feel good to use with great animations/game feel, and you have a wide variety of weapons at your disposal which you can switch between on the fly. Which lends it's self well to the combat system, as battles tend to be more methodical, with different enemy types requiring different approaches and weapons being stronger/weaker against different enemies. However it certainly doesn't force you to use certain weapons against certain enemies. For example, the hammer weapon is weak against flying enemies, however I still find my self using it against them as it's upper cut will launch you into the air, and it's slam down attack will bring flying enemies down with you.As for it's flaws, the ones that stand out are the camera (it's always the camera) and the implementation of Lute's abilities. Lute is still handled well enough, but I feel like it could have been done better. The main issue is how her attack abilities are all automatic, which is never a good approach for these types of games. And that her defensive/control abilities are all reliant on her counters, and the type of counter will change depending on which enemy you are fighting, and what animation they are doing. So in the chaos of combat it isn't really possible to tell which counter she's going to use, so it becomes difficult to plan around it. I feel what would have worked better is if she didn't have any automatic attacks, and if her counter always had the same effect of just blocking an enemies attack, and maybe staggering them depending on the enemy, and if her crown control effects, such as freezing enemies, locking them in place, knocking them in the air .etc, were active abilities you could use.To just add a note about the camera. Whilst it isn't perfect and sometimes does impede the game. I personally really didn't find it to be as bad as many of the other reviews make it out to be. It certainly isn't a deal breaker.When it comes to the visuals, story and atmosphere in general, all of it is amazing. Whilst the game definitely wear's it's influences on it's sleeve, it still maintains it's own identity. It looks gorgeous with a great sense of style. The story is simple yet still intriguing, and the characters feel very well done, with amazing voice acting, particularly Lute's VA's performance is phenomenal, and conveys her character well. The only real flaws when it comes to the game's presentation are that some of the environments, particularly at the start are a bit samey, the OST whilst good, sometimes doesn't fit that well, and they didn't make Briar at least somewhat buff. Which like... come on, come on. She's swinging that gigantic sword around she should have more meat on her bones.Overall, despite it's short comings, I am greatly enjoying Soulstice, and will likely be playing again on higher difficulties and hunting for high trophy ranks.

_childDocuments_.review: The cinematic trailer is misleading. This is a Devil-may-cry-like game and not a soul-like. It borrow's alot of aesthetic character visual design from the Claymore and Berserk Anime/manga series. I found the developer's take on visual to be very nice.  A good game, but I would wait for a sale if you wanted it. Combat is definitely a step down from devil may cry, but its better to rein in expectations as this is at best an AA game as price point suggests. Overall combat is enjoyable with relatively enough depth to it and a good enough assortment of weapons. Much like the the devil may cry games you'll find you might fight with the camera as the camera orientation is already pre determined by the areas/rooms you are traversing. It probably borrows a little too much in terms of puzzles and enemy design from the reboot DMC. Need red colour for red puzzles and blue colour for blue puzzles and the same can be said about enemy types. This colour with enemy types can get annoying to frustrating; it just isn't for everyone. There are 5 difficulties with the hardest difficulties only unlocking as you complete the game on the lower difficulties before it. The hard difficulty called knight is quite hard, so if you think you just want to enjoy the story then play difficulties 1 or 2. The story itself is a personal tale between two sisters and generally the game has a small cast of characters. Fairly interesting story, fully voiced in English and has nice story cutscenes and action traversal cutscenes. My general only gripe with the game is that its kinda short. Probably around 15-20 hours if you decided to play the normal difficulty instead of hard mode. The game ending sort of sets it up like there is suppose to be a sequel, but that'll vastly depend on this games sales figures.Overall performance is acceptable. 3440 x 1440 p with locked 60 fps with mix of ultra and high settings. I was able to also get anywhere from 90 to 120+ fps when adjusted to medium at same resolution. This is on an r7 3800x and rx 7900 xtx. My only problem with this game is that i experienced random crashing when sometimes in the between chapter menu screen; very bizarre as this happened about 3 times total before i finished the game. As overall i did not have instabilities when in the game itself. At MSRP at 45 CAD it is a bit steep for what it is in my opinion. Get it when on sale at least 35% off.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat was enjoyable (though some of the challenges were BS enough that I started skipping them). Some nice twists and turns, and I was always looking forward to learning the next tidbit. Character and monster design were fantastic, loved seeing all of them, especially some of the later bosses. World design was sort of samey, could've used more variety through the first half, although the last half got a bit better.Combat is, at its core, pretty simple, but the game kept adding new monsters, new weapons, new environmental hazards, and it clicked pretty well by the end. Monster design was good enough it was easy to tell at a glance, in the chaos of a fight, what enemies were what and who I wanted to target (although the actual targeting was sometimes frustratingly difficult). _childDocuments_.review: Soulstice----------------------------------Soulstice feels like a blast from the past, with fast, action-packed combat just like the old God of War and Prince of Persia games. But don’t worry, it has some modern twists to keep things fresh.You control two sisters, Briar and Lute, who work together in fights. Briar does the heavy hitting, and Lute uses magic to protect and attack. It’s a fun combo, and switching between them keeps things exciting.The game’s world is dark and gritty, with clear inspiration from anime like Berserk and Claymore. The characters and monsters are big, creepy, and full of that edgy style.Combat is satisfying, with flashy combos and special moves. The boss battles? They’re epic, but don’t be surprised if you get smacked around a few times.Levels are a bit more straightforward, but there are puzzles to break up the action, and exploring for upgrades is rewarding.It’s not perfect—sometimes the camera makes it hard to see what’s happening—but overall, the gameplay is smooth and engaging.If you miss the old-school hack-and-slash games, Soulstice brings that vibe back with a cool new twist.Just be ready to button mash like your life depends on it!Enjoy !!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: A potentially great game with a myriad of glaring problems.I really want to love this game and I do think it is a good game, but I think there's just too many issues that make it hard to recommend. 1. It Looks Great. The game is gorgeous with great character, enemy and level designs. Some fantastic visuals and amazing looking moments, though the facial animations look a bit odd most of the time (hint: people's upper lips aren't supposed to move that much when talking), not a deal-breaker just a bit odd.2. The Story is Cool. Honestly the best bit of the game for me and sadly the only reason I kept playing it. I really enjoyed the story and although the voice acting wasn't the best at times, at least the main characters are good.3. The Combat is Half Baked. This is the big one and not what you want to hear from a character action/spectacle fighter type game. There's a good fundamental base that I think a sequel could build on and make some of the weapons feel a bit more fluid and punchier.  Sadly there's not a lot of depth to the combat, all the weapons only have 1 basic and 1 unlockable combo and they're all the same (XXXX or XX - pause - XXX) as well as at most 3 special moves (usually stinger and a launcher), DMC this is not but pretty good for a first game. I also think Lute, your Ghostly Sister, could be built on a lot more. She usually runs on auto pilot, tickling enemies for small amounts of damage but mostly exists to put up colour coordinated fields to let you damage colour coordinated enemies. Red for Red enemies, Blue for Blue enemies. It's not difficult to understand but when you have a dozen enemies on screen it can be a lot to keep track of and ultimately is a very dull mechanic, it could do with being more interactive, maybe instead of just a field that you have get near enemies, it could be a blast or attack that makes them vulnerable instead, would at least feel cooler. 4. The Enemies are Frustrating. Technically still under the combat umbrella but its a big problem. The game has pretty good pacing at the start, beginning with small enemies then drip feeding you bigger and more complex enemies so you don't get overwhelmed and the enemy variety is good. However I think the balance of the game goes out the window in the second half. A handful of enemies have attacks that are just too quick to dodge and can't be countered and it just throws too many enemies of different types and I find it hard to find openings to attack since tougher enemies can't be staggered until you do enough damage to them. Also mines are the worst, every combat that uses the Red mines is awful and unfun.All in all, I would love to see a sequel, I think they could easily fix all the problems and build on what makes the game great in much the same way Devil May Cry has over the years. Sadly I don't think the game has sold that well so I'm not sure we'll ever see one but I do think it is just a sequel away from being genuinely fantastic.Now for some very specific complaints:Weapons. Some are very hit and miss. Sword is good, no notes. Axe is good but very slow sometimes attacks don't link if you don't mash. Bow is awful, it just doesn't feel good, like shooting water and its use cases are few, make it punchier, make it pierce enemies, anything. Chain is cool for what its for, wide attacks on small enemies, though is could be bigger and faster to make it feel better for its intended purpose. Fist could feel Punchier (forgive the pun) but it's supposed to feel strong and kind of... doesn't. Never used the knives. But they did save the best weapon till last; Cannon Tonfas, amazing I want more.Camera Angles are pretty awkward and I often found myself missing jumps because depth perception was very difficult to parse.Berserk mode was an odd design choice. I get it in concept, "Losing Control", it makes sense. Doesn't mean not being able to control your character is fun.Dodging could be more fluid, I think it would benefit from shortening the window between attacks and dodging. I often found myself unable to dodge an attack because I was still stuck in an attack animation with no window to react.
