_childDocuments_.review: Edit: This used to be a positive review which I'll leave below, but I've done a total 180 on this game and now can comfortably describe it as bad and not worth your time. It's sad to say this.The focus of a character action game should be the combat. The fun is found in doing fun exciting combos against cool enemies in a nice environment. This game refuses to let you simply fight enemies. The game constantly puts up barriers between what should be the foundation of the gameplay. There's always some dumb hoop for you to jump through. You have 2 "evocation fields" you can turn on. It puts a bubble around you and whether you have red or blue bubble up, it allows you to hit red or blue enemies inside the bubble. Red or blue enemies can't be hurt otherwise (outside of very specific circumstances). But having an evocation field active raises a "Entropy" meter and when the meter is filled completely it lowers your score, lowers your special meters and *turns off the bubble for a few seconds*. This meter also fills up when you Counter, Deflect, Slow down, or otherwise interrupt an enemy, meaning you are *constantly* toggling this dumb bubble off and on just to hit an enemy.Further to this, they also put environmental hazards in which react to what field you have up. There are mines that activate if you have a red bubble up too long (so you have to toggle even more) and there are blue mines which only don't explode if you have the blue field up or destroy them (they respawn). So you're forever either herding enemies away from these things or turning on bubble, hitting an enemy two times, turning it off, waiting a second, turning it back on etc etc.It's like the devs are afraid of simply letting you PLAY THE GAME (as evidenced by them removing the demo!). I just want to do cool combos and hit guys with my sword. I don't want to be flipping the triggers constantly just to interact with them.Further issues; there are only two combos with each weapon I've seen so far and they are the same combo. XXXX and XX(pause)XXX. Boring. They make a number of unique weapons and essentially make them feel identical outside of speed. Even the bow is basically just the whip which is basically just the sword because the bow can't hurt coloured enemies outside of the bubble, so you have to get close anyway!Some enemies also have completely unblockable attacks, they're annoying but they are technically telegraphed. Unblockables are indicated by about 1 second of yellow/black flame around an enemy, so you have time to evade. In theory this is fine, but when the terrible, terrible camera and lock-on system get involved you'll be lucky if you can ever see that one's been telegraphed. Getting hit by an unblockable attack that you couldn't see is annoying.There are special challenge rooms like in DMC4 where you get rewarded for winning in a specific way, e.g. kill everything in under a time limit, or survive X seconds. The majority of these are totally fine and normal, but some of them you will fail through no error of your own. Your companion, Lute, fires ranged attacks at enemies completely of her own volition, unprompted by you. When you have to kill only certain enemies first, or only kill enemies in a certain place and your ally forces you to fail a challenge because they randomly kill them, it's f*cking annoying.The absolute core of this game is good, but for a reason I will never understand, the devs buried it in utterly awful gimmicks. I hate that I don't like this game.Original review below.Red flags: when the game became available the devs delisted the demo. After day one they also seem to have increased the price. Make of this information what you will. It's okay. Feels like an early breed character action game (think more Devil May Cry 1 than Devil May Cry 5). The combat is fun and stages have a grading system like Bayonetta. I don't truly understand how the combat grading system works, you seem to get points based on things like hitting an enemy in the back instead of doing multiple varied combos, some fights I seem stuck at 5x multiplier and I can't for the life of me figure out why it won't go higher, but I likely haven't read enough on it I guess.Platforming is clunky like dmc 1,camera is absolutely atrocious. Unforgiveable. Voice acting is unusual. Game is perfectly playable and overall I'm enjoying it.

_childDocuments_.review: Badazz. You like the original God of War? Boom! Here ya go! Graphics are very clean! No stutters / frame drops. Runs very smooth. Interesting characters too. Played 90 minutes and I am happy to find out more. IssuesI had to force the game to accept 4k by using NVIDIA Control Panel. IrritationI cannot figure out how to turn off subtitles. Two hour refund is more then enough time to figure it out. Do not sleep on this one (Please read below for updates). UpdateThe camera can be a b****...  Another Update!I am now late in the game with still some to do (making this list as I go). One thing that has me dumb founded is the parry system. The main parry option is Lute. Briar (MC) younger sister (blue ghost). Issue I am having, there is either certain attacks or she just randomly just doesn't help. So the devs were nice enough to allow parry on a weapon. But so far, it really is just ONE weapon. Sadly, for me, it is the worst weapon at that (Gauntlets). One of, if not the, slowest weapon. I rarely use it if at all because of the hammer. Really though, my issue comes with giving it parry. The sword is the only consistent weapon. You cannot remove it as an option. It is always sword plus one. Whats driving me mad is the sword gets by far the least amount of upgrades then any other weapon. All that said, my question is why on earth did the devs not have the sword parry? You could look at it like a trade off, not a lot of combos, but you can parry. Heck in some of the cinematic you literally watch Briar use her sword and block... So I just sit there, wondering why I cannot do that. I doubt this will be adjusted, but if you're a parry feign as myself, I would personally give up on this idea. Dodging is your main source as Briar.. However, this is limited to, two side steps and one roll. The roll locks you into place for about two seconds Point is, there really isn't an option that feels satisfying. Dodging is very limited, forcing you to get cozy with those gauntlets, all the while Lute just doesn't seem to care at times. Be nice to have an option that assists by keeping the combat going. Help keep the fight running smooth. To top it off, there is no attack cancel. So once you start a combo, its going to finish. Until an enemy has had enough of you and hits you. Ruining the entire combo and your Unity. To summarize my point, when it comes to your defenses, this game is sorely lacking. You may think it wants you to be aggressive. Which I do not mind, but that cannot be the case. I'll explain more down below in another point. Swapping weapons. Using a controller the left, up and right directions of the Dpad is a weapon slot. Each slot gets two weapons. I noticed if you swap to the second weapon for that direction, then swap away and come back, it doesn't save. So you always have to press twice to get the second option. It would be nice if the last option used was saved. In a hack and slash, every second counts towards the combo. The Dpad being on the left side, it is on the side of your movement. Swapping weapons means you're not moving. Unless you reach over with your right thumb, but then you're not swinging your equipped weapon (face buttons). Too cumbersome in my opinion to not have it save. Later game enemies get BEEFY! Taking a load of hits (granted I am playing on the hardest difficulty offered for the first play through, which I do NOT recommend). I hate to say it, but there not all that fun. In fact, most really ruin the flow of combat. It's like the game is trying to turn into a SoulsBourne without that high of damage output from the enemies, extremely limited dodging from you and a fixed camera. So Devs, please, either unlock the camera, unlock the dodging, parrying, or tone them down a bit. Altogether and it can almost get you to punt your controller... I haven't! And won't! But I have thought about it. No lying on this review no sir.I've also got to admit. I wasn't against the color coded enemies / fighting at first, but I have since changed my mind. This mechanic requires you to use Lute and put either a red, or blue aura around Briar to be able to attack and kill the red / blue enemies. In my opinion, this is used FAR too often. I would easily say 90% of fights require this. I mean, I get it Devs, it uses Lute. But she already is our parry / block system. This WILL annoy you. Why? You ask.. Well, for example. There are red and blue mines in this game. They work opposite of each other. Blue mines require you to use the blue aura and it stops the mine from going off and damaging you. However, the red mine goes off if you use the red aura around it. Now take a red enemy and place them on a blue mine... This ladies and gents is what I like to call, "f***ed". No matter what, you WILL take damage if you attack. Even after the mines go off, they come back. So no, you cannot cheat. Keep in mind, if you're not attacking, you loose Unity (your special). If you are hit by anything, you once again, loose Unity. This sucks. Period. (Aggressive Fighting)Poor, poor Lute. Look, I like the sisters. I like their coming of age, under dog story. But man, I cannot lie. If I rated the sisters now, before beating the game, I can already EASILY say Lute is by far the weak link. She holds Briar back too much. Lute can get exhausted while fighting. She can be forcefully taken by the game to go rest if used excessively. She does warn before this happens, but I promise you now, there is so much going on, you will not hear her at times. Loosing her at the worst moments. When gone, there is NO way for you to hurt red or blue enemies. Granted she is gone only for 6/8 seconds, but still! That is a long time in a HACK N SLASH! You cannot hack, NOR slash. You are truly stuck if there is not a neutral enemy in the arena with you. Most the time, there isn't in the mid to late game. So you're stuck running around till she comes back. All the while you're loosing, say it with me..... Unity (I know you nailed it you Chad you). I hope they fix this because it can be mind numbing. Heck I too have to go rest after some of these fights dealing with Lute. All this does is stop you from being aggressive when you need it most. Tracking! One of the parries Lute uses is her freeze ability. Does just as it sounds. Before an enemy unleashes their attack, Lute can freeze them in place. Nice. Then comes the time you're one on one with an enemy, so there isn't much else to look at but them. You parry/freeze them and discover YET ANOTHER design flaw. When an enemy unfreezes they, no joke, snap back to you finishing the move they started. Meaning, you freeze them, go to flank from behind to keep that combo going, they unfreeze, instant 180 attack. And I DO mean "instant". The attack is now coming at you even faster because it is already half way complete. This game is blowing my mind on so many bad levels. Why is this a thing? If I could parry (with the sword) or attack cancel, I still wouldn't like it in a HnS game because of how hectic it can get, but okay. You gave us the tools, I just have to use them. This means when you freeze, you are allowed another 1/2 hits then the only option is RUNNING. Because a hit IS coming. Ruining, once again, that combo meter. This, in my opinion, has to be patched out. And finally, another MAJOR issue. If you do pull off combos and fill up the Unity meter (FINALLY!), you will unlock special attacks called Synergy. Each weapon has one. Once achieved, the game will focus in on Briar as she pulls off the move. Cool as hell cinematic and I love doing it! However, there is one huge flaw. Enemies do not freeze in place. As the game takes control away from you and Briar attacks, the enemies are free to move as they see fit. This INCLUDES the enemy you're attacking. They just WALK OFF during the move every time. Meaning some of the move, does zero damage. FINAL in comments.

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game on hard difficulty, experienced the full story up to the post credit scenes and with all that said, I do recommend this game. Its not without its flaws, some of which are very annoying, but if you're a fan of stylish action and anime inspired designs, you're in for a good ride with this one.STORYThis game with its story, character designs, world and even gameplay takes heavy inspiration from Japanese games and anime. With regards to the story, if you're a fan of works like Berserk, Claymore and dare I even say, The Witcher, I think you're gonna like this. Its not the most complex plot in the world, but its enjoyable enough to keep you hooked from start to finish. The ending was really good and they caught me off guard with one of the big reveals too. I think its fair to say they were on the right track with this fantasy world they created here. The world building was pretty good too and I liked the little touched like characters wishing each other well in the name of the three heroes of their land. Unfortunately though, I feel the pacing is way off and especially at the middle part of the game, I feel it drags on for too long. Yes, I did dive into this game on Hard difficulty right off the bat and that would result in a longer time to complete the story, but I still think they could have trimmed the game down from 25 chapters to maybe 20. 26 hrs felt like way too long for this story for me.GAMEPLAYCombat is fast, flashy and Briar, your main character, moves with a lot of finesse. There are a lot of weapons to unlock and the animations for all of them are stunning! There are also a crap-ton of powers and skills to unlock. I sometimes wished there was a more extensive combo list like in DMC, but it was still really impressive the many things they were able to add in this aspect.Unfortunately, there are some issues with gameplay. First, forget about all the dope looking monsters in the game (I would get to that in a bit), the camera is your number one enemy. Many times, it messes up your flow by getting hooked on walls and honestly, I didn't find the enemy lock that much useful, especially in situations where you get overrun with enemies (And trust me, you would). Also, there were quite a lot of instances where I got attacked from behind and it just left me like, "How the hell was I supposed to see that???"Enemies here aren't playing around though and they will hand you your butt especially on tougher difficulties. There is the option to counter here, which i love, but sometimes it doesn't appear and the enemies just hit you anyways. The platforming is fine at best because not only are your controls stiff mid-air, but in some scenarios, the game doesn't make it easy to jump from one block to another in a 3-D space because it's hard for you to tell what position you're at relative to the platforms (or absence of one) beneath you.The upgrade tree is good, but kinda expensive though. You can reset your choices to try different builds, so that's good.But with all that said, there is still a lot of fun to be had here with many challenges, move sets, weapons, enemy types and upgrades you can add to your style of play. AESTHETICSThis game is beautifullllllllll! It's sont fully lip synced and some facial espressions can look a little off, but this is a AA game so I'm not really bothered. Actually I'm hella impressed cuz DAMN, they really got the art style down. All the characters look very well modelled, the environments are very detailed and my, my, the music is a dreaaaaaaaaam! I'm so in love with the music here that I wish it could easily be found to stream. It is available to purchase here and I do recommend it, but I just wish it was a bit more accessible. Still, it's way too dope and you'll love it if you're a good fan of electronic music.I still can't wrap my head around how beautiful all the character models in this game are, especially the enemies. They are just so intricately designed and are nothing but the product of pure talent.Unfortunately though, the environments, while very detailed do very little to distinguish themselves. Don't get me wrong, you CAN tell when you're in a different location, but only if you focus. There isn't really a change in colour the palette until the end and for a very long time, you'd be stuck with nothing but dark grey brick walls and maybe some ice.Nonetheless, this game looks and sounds beautifullllll! I think this is where they really hit the mark!PERFORMANCEIt was okay for me. I played it on medium to high-ish settings on my 3050 laptop at a near constantly locked 1080p 30 fps. I could very much push it to 60 fps, but you don't really need that for this game, so I saved my SCREAMING laptop some stress. Overall, it was alright. Not the most optimized, but good for me. Your mileage may vary depending on your setup. I only have a 1080p 75Hz monitor, so almost anything works and looks fine for me with my setup.OVERALL SCORE - 7/10I really do recommend this game and although it's not perfect (Far from it actually), I still think it's very much worth your time at a good price. I had very few rage moments with this on HARD MODE and that's a lot coming from a guy who can easily get enraged at video games. I got this game as part of a Fanatical bundle and think you'd be happy if you get it at a good price. THANKS FOR READING THIS VERY LONG REVIEW AND I WISH YOU ALL THE VERY BEST! HAVE A WONDERFUL DAY!!!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty sweet!  If you're a fan of spectacle fighters, this will be right up your alley.  It's closer to DMC than any other of the big ones in the genre, but still manages to do its own thing and put a spin on the whole combo management system.  I would say if you do not normally play games in this genre, you might have issues with the camera and possibly the difficulty of the game (your performance is rated based on how much score you achieve, how fast you beat an encounter/stage, and how much damage you sustain during combat).  I'm running the game on max settings at 1440p on a decent rig, with no issues.  There was some stuttering during the prologue but once I actually started Act 1 it has been flawless.  Currently on Act 2 and looking forward to slaying more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game certainly has a lot of promise, what with it's incredibly compelling world building, fast, fluid combat and mature themes and dialogue. When it does require you to utilize other abilities, it can tend to make some combat encounters into a bit of a chaotic mess.- The missions, while certainly fun to play through, feel much longer then they need to be, often continuing on even after I reach points that seem like good stopping points.These don't make the game unplayable by any means, it's still a decent time, but I still feel as though these aspects could've been refined a bit more.

It's sad...-I will admit the world and story while predictable was not that bad. Not great, but acceptable.-The exposition was terrible in some places tho. Like. PLEASE. SHUT UP! A HACK AND SLASH GAME, TREATS FIGHTS LIKE A PUNISHMENT, but then at the end of the game I felt like maybe that is the case. So if that was they goal, they did what they wanted to. _childDocuments_.review: Despite the name and the obvious Berserk reference, this is not a Souls-like. Instead take your mind back to the classic hack-and-slash games of older generations such as the original God of war and Dante's Inferno and you're on the right track. With the DMC/Bayonetta style scoring system and the game's mechanics of using fields of effect to attack possessed or wraith enemies, you must use everything in your arsenal to beat the hordes coming at you. With a massive arsenal of weapons and supported by your spirit sister, you fight through a city on the brink of destruction, facing corrupted humans, wraiths and possessed, while you lose your own humanity the more you fight.  Level up your weapons, unlock new moves and build your spirit's abilities as you see fit with collected resources as you face greater foes, harder challenges and solve more complex puzzles. This is a game with a brilliant blend of fast-paced anime style action, a dark/grim, end of the world setting  and the conflicting duality of morals between the two sisters, generates a great foundation for the story. Granted, the voice actors in parts are a bit cheesy and the story is a bit basic, but the lore is rich and the efforts of the devs shine through the fog of its draw backs. The fixed camera when traversing through this world is obscuring at times, but it is necessary for the cinematography the devs have intended. The graphics are great and a real step in the right direction for high-res skins with the cell-shaded foundation for character models. Awesome level design and the fixed camera helps to guide you through the destruction of the landscape, yet the invisible walls can pull you out of the world from time to time. The views at times are breathtaking and the ever-escalating challenge of the enemies will have you on the edge of your seat and hyped up to go back into the fight if you fail.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much cool stuff in it, there are multiple accessibility toggles such as color blindness mode, font size change, and other features that give off a good first impression. The move-list is basic and easy to perform thanks to the addition of visual cues and controller rumble that facilitates the learning curve for moves that have a “pause/hold”  (e.g. X,X,(hold), X,X,X ). And it is a good thing that the inputs are easy since main characters will have up to 7 weapons by the climax of the game, making it comfortable to return after a long break and refamiliarize w/ the gameplay. But by far, MY FAVORITE thing in this game is their implementation of a Devil-Trigger Mechanic called “Rapture Mode”, where you have to raise your stack up hit counts and raise what is essentially your Style Meter to unlock the prompt to do the equivalent of Bayonetta 2’s Umbran Climax. Before the release of this game(and after playing the demo), I was hoping to encounter great boss fights, and y’know what?!  it definitely delivered a lot of spectacular bosses. It’s cool that the devs draw inspiration from Berserk, Claymore, DMC, Bayonetta,  and Astral Chain, unfortunately, they also carried some of the flaws from all of those titles(along w/ flaws of their own). Such as fighting red and blue enemies in ‘DmC Devil May Cry’, teleporting enemies that breaks the rhythm and combo, and just like how this game has the best DT mechanic, it also has another DT mechanic that I’m not a fan of, called “Berserk Mode”, where the characters automatically attacks the foes in an invincible state and all the player do is align the left-stick with the direction of the prompt and mash a QTE. Although this is a personal thing, I dislike that I can’t deselect items in my D-Pad and get my score docked due to accidentally using a healing(or any other) item, especially when I’m playing a Character Action Game.Other than that, I only have mixed feelings about some other aspects, the most divisive point being the fixed camera, though I’m fine w/ it since it is used to direct the player to their next objective along with making the shots look cinematic, but it is a problem for platforming sections. Also, when you enter a fight the camera is free, there was only 1 fight that was fixed camera and it was fine. Most of the issue w/ the camera is the same problem as other action games where they make you fight in tight spaces, and you have to put in the effort to avoid getting cornered by your foes. Controller remapping is cool but not ideal due to certain inputs requiring you to press 2 buttons at the same time, and therefore you need to get used to something approaching the default controller scheme.In short, I love this game, despite moments that frustrated me, it is one of the biggest surprises of this year for me. AND I WANT A SEQUEL REAL BAD.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the Boomer Shooter of character action games.There's a lot to find charming here, but most of it will likely come off as clunky or aggravating, especially if you aren't coming to it with a predisposition for PS3-era action games. You've got a "main attack" that feels mostly like a combo filler, a "secondary attack" that mixes things up, and a dedicated Counter button where your ghost sister will block or debuff enemies when counter QTEs appear. The main gimmick here that might make or break things for you is using your ghost sister to deploy red or blue fields in order to interact with environmental objects and attack specific enemies. So the idea is for you to be wading into it mashing out combos and dodging attacks while also playing the support role for yourself.  You're being pushed to articulate the bond between the two sisters yourself through combat asking you to master maneuvering these two characters as one. It won't be for everyone, but there's something neat there.My only real gripes are that changing the controller layout doesn't seem to apply until you back out to the main menu, and the environments so far can be pretty bland and repetitive.Oh, also there are plenty of barrels and crates to break for shinies.

_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, game's kinda fun. Not very far into it right now, but combat feels challenging enough to feel mostly satisfactory. Exploration is a neat feature, bit of trial and error, another decently challenging aspect that I find myself somewhat interested in. Really pretty backgrounds; I love the vibe, how it feels like a healthy combination between Dark Souls and Final Fantasy.But this game is so pointlessly complicated and nuanced.Camera angles are wonky as hell. Not a fan of the constantly changing angles when running around the environment. Makes it complicated to look for the environmental challenges and hidden treasures/pathways.The incorporation of the fields is clunky and anti-climactic. Cool for exploring the semi-open world, boring while in combat. Functions like a resource bar while in combat, but you get the ability to extend its duration while in-combat almost right away with the first tier of talent points, so it removes almost all active tracking of the mechanic.Not being able to buy talents when you accrue the currency for them is kinda pointless. Can only purchase talents while in a shop or between chapters. To be fair, though, there are a few checkpoints scattered throughout the chapters, but I find it to be an obnoxious form of pacing the game's talent tree functionality. What are the developers intending with this feature? Why disallow talent point accumulation without the checkpoints?Lock-on functionality is bizarre. It's incentivized to focus a single enemy because you can only see their health bar when you have them locked on, but it creates the worst in-combat camera angles. The game is very high mobility, so there's a lot of running around/aerial combat/etc, which blows for the camera if you're trying to fight locked on. You're forced to turn off the lock-on feature and then reposition yourself in the arena, but once you do that, good luck finding the target you were focusing before.I'm finding the challenges to be the most infuriating process in the game so far. Researching answers online will only give you paper knowledge; executing them in-game is either impossible or the dumbest ♥♥♥♥ ever, which detracts from the game's combat system. For example: The perfect counter challenge. It was somehow impossible to complete even with high reaction timing, so the way I managed to overcome it was clear out all other enemies until there was only one, and then stand completely still and mashing the F key until it almost broke in order to obtain my "perfect counters". For a game that has extremely high mobility, what's the point of mandating a "perfect counter" system if the only way to accomplish it is by standing stationary?Having similar issues with the synergy attacks challenge. The combo is supposed to be [left click + left click + pause + left click x4] when the icon in the upper right hand corner "merges." It's a resource bar that's not tracked in the game whatsoever. I've only ever accomplished a synergy attack coincidentally, never intentionally.Maybe it'll get better with future talent tiers being unlocked as the story progresses. Maybe. If it does, I'll change the review. But so far, this game has potential, but isn't impressive mechanically.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated Review - 12/10/2023:This game popped up in my mind multiple times throughout the year since I did want to know how the story played out. So I buckled up and pushed through the garbage encounters to thankfully not see as many terrible ones past Chapter 17. Did end up finishing the game and liking how ridiculously messed up the characters became as you got closer to the truth of what happened. Delightfully twisted insanity going on here. If they do manage to get the green light to do a sequel, I may play it and pray they do away with the messy red/blue swapping battles since it does get really tedious having to do that on the fly so much. The main combat itself is good, just need to tweak or remove the extra baggage that was holding it back.Previous Review:Plays like old school Devil May Cry, without the heavy emphasis on humor, which is honestly a good thing. The story takes itself seriously and only has the occasional quip here and there that I welcome since I feel Devil May Cry leans way too far into the comedy that it can be cringe at times, even if it is fun to watch.After progressing further into the game, I have encountered some truly frustrating enemy variants and combat scenarios. The most frustrating enemies are the ones that play keep away with for the entirety of the battle, making the battles take longer than they need to. There are also large enemy types that produce multiple enemies when defeated and if you fail to kill ALL the enemies they spawn, the larger enemy will revive itself, drastically inflating the battle length to a frustrating degree. Does not help that the enemies that are spawned have the same color as the environment, bright blue, making them really hard to find on the field, which is wasting your time in such a terrible way that are you likely going to get at least 2 enemy revives before you can finish the fight.Then there is the annoyingly stupid traps that get involved in the battles, forcing you to switching from Blue to Red fields every couple seconds to prevent the traps from exploding in your face while fighting enemies that can only be hurt by a specific colored field that so happen to trigger the traps on the field since they have the same color, or different color, depending on the trap in place. These type of combat scenarios are downright nasty and stupid.I cannot in good faith recommend this game anymore after seeing how immensely frustrating the game gets the further you progress into it. it started off good and balanced with some nice enemy types, but the game just got worse and worse over time, making things way too frustrating to even be considered fun anymore. The constant issue of being unable to see an enemy attack coming while there are multitude of other things happening around you just becomes to ridiculous.

_childDocuments_.review: You know how Frodo's journey in Lord of the Rings took a year or something? Soulstice's approach would be to show you all of it... This game has no editing. It sure feels like a winning formula: DMC, Bayonneta, Metal Gear Rising, the old God of Wars and even Darksiders all received at least positive critical reception. Would be hard to mess this up. Soulstice messed it up. It's not a disaster, it just feel so poorly thought out. 2. After the opening chapters of the game I though this took heavy inspiration by Ninja Theory's DmC. After a couple of more chapters I realized this is what a game that would've inspired DmC would've looke like. It's unbelievable that a game 10 years newer would be so much worse.The main problems of the game are that it lacks spectacle and colors, environment diversity, the story is poorly told and the dialogue is most of the time pointless and the game is faaar toooo loooong. These problems would not be so apparent if the game wouldn't drag itself out and show some restraint. The combat is functional and wouldn't be terrible, but the enemies you fight have no discernible identity.

_childDocuments_.review: I’m not sure why, but it feels like this game has received very little attention (which is unfair because it’s really good). It has that single player 2-in-1 vibe from Nier also (or like GOW/A Plague Tale/TLOU) since you mostly play as Briar but Lute is partially controllable, too. The structure of the game is similar to Bayonetta, where you get a rating for each battle that you complete. I wouldn’t compare the two much beyond that though, since this is more hack and slash and less beat ‘em up, and all my opponents so far are roughly the same size as Briar (player character). No fights with screen-filling monsters. The story is somewhat interesting, but not amazing (at least so far, for me). The world is intriguing, as I’m learning about the lore. It kind of seems like it’s set in medieval times or maybe beyond that…like the dark ages, but in a world with magic and demons and whatnot. So far, I’m enjoying this game and hope it gains more popularity. I’ve been playing it on Steam Deck, initially I was struggling to get the game to hold 30-40fps, but after the last update, it’s virtually locked to 60 with everything set to low, except AA and textures set to high, @720p with FSR on balanced. _childDocuments_.review: I need Briar to step on meOkay, now for my actual review:Soulstice is going for a LOT clearly. The amount of ambition and content on display is nothing to scoff at. It's a double A game that would have fit in perfectly well coming in around the PS2/PS3 era, and it does that surprisingly well. If you like Devil May Cry and want more content like that, this is an easy purchase in my opinion. It's not without issue, but it's fun enough, and has enough going for it that's unique and is really doing it's own thing quite well. The negatives:-The voice acting is inconsistent. It's hard to fault the devs, since of course, they are based in Italy, but Briar in particular is particularly inconsistent during 'struggling' scenes or ones where she needs a broader vocal range. It's not bad, but it's clear the direction for the english actors isn't the best. Lute though honestly kinda killed it.-The camera is pretty inconsistent. During fights, especially when they let you free cam, it's quite difficult to see anything. I think the cameras during exploration were used to surprisingly good effect though.-Kind of a slow start, this isn't too big of an issue, but it took about as long as my playtime is to start getting fights that had any sort of challenge to them. It's not an inherent issue, just something worth mentioning.-Targeting can be inconsistent, and the lag after a triple dodge is NEEDLESSLY punishing. Especially when you can use the rollstab infinitely and go an absurd distance. Positives:-Character designs, I **LOVE** women with big swords. I need Briar to beat me up-I actually think the story is somewhat compelling. Normally stories like these don't really do anything for me, but I found myself at least mildly interested, genuinely that's a feat to behold for my ADD brain. -The combat feels pretty good, I tend to strongly dislike games that have a 'grading system' after you finish combat, and I wish I could just turn that off, but it's not too intrusive, as little as it seems to actually fit with the world. Something more melancholic would've fit the game better, but it feels like the combat designer and story designer were very much two different people. Maybe it's to show Briar is a creature of combat? Idk, but it feels kind of ill fitted either way.-The sister mechanic is very neat. It seems genius both as a feat of character design AND gameplay where she protects you mid-combo etc. Very cool, used well, and I think the ghost/color matching enemies are foreshadowed well and allowed you to practice that mechanic in a safe environment first. Kudos.I think the game is good, and deserves more praise. It's not perfect, but if you go in with the notion "This is like a PS3 era action game, jank and all!" You'll probably have quite a bit of fun. Anyway, the devs are lucky I'm not giving this a negative review, because they didn't mail me a Briar figurine yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed ReviewPros:🎵 Music: The music in this game is the unsung hero, weaving a spell that enchants and captivates. It's a saving grace in an otherwise tumultuous journey.🎬 Cinematic Bliss: I can't help but applaud the high-quality cutscenes that unfolded like a movie. Each frame was a visual feast, showcasing the artistry that went into their creation.Cons:👾 Sturdy as Fort Knox: My excitement turned to frustration as I faced enemies with health points that seemed insurmountable. The relentless onslaught of spawned adversaries turned battles into a chaotic frenzy, with no joy. Honestly, way too many on the most narrow spots.⚔️ Combat: The combat system, my oh my! It's like trying to dance in quicksand. Mistakes are brutally punished, and the limited combo options per weapon make achieving any form of fluidity an uphill struggle.🗣️ Dialogue: The narrative fell flat with poorly written dialogues that left me yearning for depth and connection. It's disheartening when a game fails to draw you into its story.🌐 World: Exploring the game world felt like navigating a maze with no surprises. The lack of camera control added insult to injury, restricting my view and engagement with what should have been a vibrant environment.🦄 Enemies: Where's the variety in enemies? Facing the same foes repeatedly became monotonous, robbing the game of the excitement that diverse adversaries bring.In the end, my journey through this game has been a mix of awe and frustration. The captivating music and stunning cutscenes couldn't quite salvage the overall experience marred by clunky combat, uninspiring dialogues, and a world that felt more like a narrow corridor than an expansive realm. It's a tale of unmet expectations and missed opportunities.

_childDocuments_.review: Played the game on Knight mode.This game is the dark souls 2 of character action/spectacle fighting games.Other action games ask  "how well can you react and pay attention to enemies and their queues"This game asks "how well can you play stiff character action while also controlling your environment"this game feels stiff in terms of combos. A lot of animations go on for too long and cant be cancelled into dodge or a parry. the DmC devil may cry idea of "oh you can do two hits of this combo and finish it with a different weapon" is novel but it makes a lot of the combos short, where as in other games its more fun to see a combo continue because of different moves. Theres some other moves that you can do to avoid knocking enemies out with a different weapon finisher, but there's like idk 3? that keep the combo going.This game keeps the stagger punish of hitting the wrong color gets you punished. when DmC de removed that stagger idea because NO ONE LIKED THAT. on top of this, the game also adds environment hazards that punish you for using the wrong colors and not managing them properly, and this wouldnt be so bad if it wasnt for the constant knockback. The sewers was one of the worst spectacle fighter levels I've ever dealt with.But after the sewers those things are gone and now the only thing left is the enemies, and they're fine. none of them are really annoying, its only when they get in the way in the middle of different colored auras.anyway this game is alright and it does a lot to filter out players in the sewers, none of the bosses or enemies get as bad as the boss in that area lol.final score: play a ps2 game instead/10

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent DMC-like game from a AA developer. _childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: I personally like fixed camera angles and their retro feel, or the way they're used to subtly show the way forward to the player. But Soulstice uses it very poorly, either making it simply uncomfortable and a nuisance, or trying to make you observe the backgrounds (which look quite good, don't get me wrong) in a game where all your attention should be focused on your character.The combat feels dull and too simple and easy, not varied enough. The levels seriously lack legibility. The UI/UX is just weird, why would you make me confirm I want to proceed playing after the loading screens are finished? The story is yet another Dark Souls wannabe, with your classic high-medieval-fantasy "ooooh there's a whole mythos to this corrupted land only you can save, but it is obscure and not meant to be understood fully, and we'll keep throwing sterotypical fantasy words at you to keep you hooked", which is proof that they have not understood what is so good about FromSoftware's (and Miyazaki's) storytelling. Although, they can't be really faulted, as few developers actually have.All in all, many glaring flaws make Soulstice feel like an amateurish work -- which it is. It is not actually bad, don't get me wrong; it can even be enjoyed by most people who aren't as nitpicky as I am (being a game designer myself definitely does not help). It has true potential, and I hope the studio keeps making games and perhaps even a sequel, in order to relentlessly improve upon what they make. It is their first work, and is far better than one should come to expect from a first endeavour, in many departments so. I simply didn't enjoy it enough to keep playing, but I really recommend you try it out for yourself and see if you can look past the lack of polish :)

_childDocuments_.review: Received from humble bundle code.The gameplay is genuinely mind numbing. This is shockingly boring even for a hack and slash. One dimensional combat and janky controls to the point that I can only assume this is a console port, or made specifically with controller in mind. Which would make sense given the controller diagram in the loading screens.There is almost nothing positive I have to say about this game, the intro cutscene and fights are extremely generic exposition followed by a bunch of flashing lights and poor fight choreograph. Then into a boring, flat looking environment on some docks where you're presented with the automatic camera. The camera/controls are horrible, no camera control at any point other than combat, and even in combat it feels terrible. While 'exploring' what little there is, the camera automatically snaps to various angles depending on the area you've entered. This feels terrible and is visually jarring. The combat mechanics are also massively hampered by how strongly each action locks you into an animation. Everything you do, from dashing to attacking, to countering etc all lacks agency. All of it locks you into a momentary animation and ruins the flow of combat. The combat in this game boils down to pushing a button, and then waiting for a bunch of flashy lights to happen on screen before you're allowed to push the next button. The performance as well is somehow terrible for such a visually simple game. Although the fidelity of textures and effects is reasonable, the performance impact isn't. Both loading screens and gameplay peg my pc at 99% GPU utilization. Running this game at medium/high settings, especially in combat with just a few enemies on screen results in about 100 fps at 1440p, with a 7800x3d and a 3090. With DLSS quality enabled, the lights and reflections stop looking specular but you have to live with the blurry result of dlss, on top of the incredible 0% performance impact. Somehow the developers of this game managed to implement resolution scaling in such a way that it has zero impact on performance. My gpu still sits at max util, with the same fps in world and in combat (300/100). Not to mention running hotter than in any other game I play, games like apex legends or overwatch at maximum settings still net me a consistent 200+ fps with sub 50c temps. While this game runs inconsistently at best and nets a 65-70c core even on water. The story also seems extremely generic and poorly thought out. Like a 15 year old's first attempt at writing a fantasy, unaware that they've been influenced by other, better works. If the game was like 15$, I might give it a pass for being visually competent and thematically consistent but at 40$ it is just generic and offensively boring.0/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a strong entry in the Devil May Cry / Bayonetta style of games. Strongly recommended.The game stars Briar (a human knight styled after Guts) and her ghost sister, Lute, who fight as a pair in a third person action game.  This review will assume readers are somewhat familiar with the genre.Slight spoilers to follow: The two character system is very cool.  It plays well into narrative character interaction and battle mechanics. Briar does most of the fighting, but Lute helps control the battlefield through powerful magic counters and a field that allows exorcism of wraith enemies.  Each of them has their own customization with Briar focusing on weapons and Lute on magic, which appears to be fairly deep. This feels VERY similar to DmC games (has Stinger equivalent, many XX, wait, XXXX combos), with 7 total weapons.  The weapons feel good and have their own niches because of both movesets and a light rock/paper/scissors mechanic.  Some of Lute's counters are hard counters and others do a time stop field that adds complexity to the game as the enemy will eventually unfreeze and finish the attack.  Just like other games in genre, you’re rewarded for not being hit, good combos, etc.  Enemy variety is substantial and most are very fun to fight. Like DmC, there are red and blue enemies and environmental puzzle elements.  This system is vastly improved, as it has a clear in game lore reason for existing, and the color swap is a magical aura set down by Lute that can be rapidly toggled. This game has one of the best “forbidden powers” I've seen.  If you tap into Rapture mode, you get increased speed, damage, and a modified move set, etc. temporarily.  If you go Berserk, you stop controlling Briar entirely, who begins an assault that will certainly overwhelm the  enemy, and instead shift control over Lute who tries to make sure she doesn’t permanently become a monster. This gameplay implementation peerlessly sells the power fantasy of tapping into a dangerous power to win a battle. This has a chapter select mode which also shows how many hidden items / challenges are left in each map, which helps with completionism. I recommend this game for every DmC / Bayonetta fan. It’s an interesting new entry in the genre which takes strong inspiration from existing games but sets itself aside through the 2 character mechanic.  It is also cheaply priced from launch.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very solid Devil May Cry-Like action game that deserves to be played by more fans of the genre. The combat mechanics are simpler than most games like this, with all the weapons having the same 2 combo strings and button inputs to juggle enemies and do the other attacks, but they all feel different enough from each other that I don't mind. The unique mechanics they bring to this game are interesting and set it apart from the rest. Only being able to defeat certain enemies when they're in a particular aura is the biggest difference and takes some getting used to, but to me the coolest aspects are related to the game's different versions of devil trigger. First there's Rapture, which feels like a standard devil trigger-like status, but you get different finishing attacks when you exit this state depending on what abilities you spec the character Lute into on her ability tree. I really liked this, as it made me feel like experimenting and changing up my play style. There's also a berserk state you can enter when you trigger rapture and your health is very low, where you play a quick time event to keep Briar from being taken over by the corruption in her and she just wrecks everyone. I'm not a fan of quick time events normally, but it was pretty satisfying to go berserk in the middle of a fight that was giving me trouble. And then there's another status you get much later that gets into spoiler territory so I won't elaborate on it but I also thought it was pretty cool.The story is good, better than it needed to be for being in an action game like this, and I was surprised by how much I liked the characters, especially Layton.It's not a perfect game - the environments do get pretty repetitive and I feel like a few of the middle chapters could have been cut out entirely without detracting from the plot at all, but if what you want is some slashy fun then those things don't matter that much anyway. There are also some very light puzzle mechanics that gate your progress through some levels that I could take or leave, but they never ruined my experience.I started on the hardest difficulty available from the beginning, Knight, but I eventually decreased it to the "normal" difficulty, Initiate, because the harder enemies later in the game felt too spongy to me, and I hadn't yet invested in all the proficiency upgrades for the weapons that make them more effective at countering certain enemy types. So, I would recommend people start on the lower difficulties, or if you really want to start on hard mode, invest in the proficiency upgrades as early as possible before you get all the additional moves for them so when the harder enemies start showing up more often it's less of a slog.To all the people that bought this game but gave up on it - give it another shot!  According to the achievements at the time I'm writing this, 73.3% of people who own this game have beaten the first chapter, but only 34.4% have gotten the achievement for meeting Donovan, which is in chapter 4! Out of 25 chapters! It gets better people! You don't even get your devil trigger ability until you beat chapter 5 and that's when the game settles into its groove! Give it another chance if you like other action games like this and I'm sure you'll get more enjoyment out of it, even if you don't wind up liking it as much as I did.As for me - I beat the game, had a great time, and I hope they get to make the sequel they set up so clearly at the end.

_childDocuments_.review: You Play as Briar and Lute, Sister whose village were ravaged but the evil Corrupted and Wraiths, due to foreseen circumstances during the invasion Briar the older sister was injured which corrupsted her into becoming a curropted as well. The only was to save her was to become a Chimera; Those who are sworn to defeat the vile curropted by the orders.. Or it seems. After a while both Briar and Lute are sent to close of "The Tear" which has spread Chaos around one of the main Cities/Castles of the world. Join then as they uncover to truth in this action packed adventure full of challenges .  Do you enjoy the fast-paced action of Bayonetta and the chaotic weapon switching of DMC series, with the tad annoyance of the Blue and Red system where you can only attack specific enemies who are inside of the aura like the DmC series of needing to use the right weapon for those enemies. This game will be right up your ally. As you progress you will unlock a total of 5 new weapon (with 2 already unlocked) for a whopping total of 7 Weapons to switch and around and make combos. As you dodge and block your way in battle, your meter will slowly build up where if you wer to finish a combo, a cinematic attack occurs for high damage. As you also continue to play you will unlock two new special skills but using this could ruin you ranking system if you are wanting to get the best rank through the game, know when to use them and you got the game's core mechanic all set! I for one enjoyed the environment.. at the beginning, it later got a little too stale with how often you visited the sewer, castle bridges and indoor the castle area. Later levels have this awkward blue tint due the whats is going on around the city and it just gets a little tiresome. Character design can be hit or miss, and can make it or break it for some people, i for one did not have an issues and it really gives off the indie charm.  Performance can be a little hit or miss. there has been time while playing the music could not keep up and ended up being a little choppy, cutting in and out. Load screen were also a weird one where even with and SDD or a NVME it felt like it wouldn't load as fast as it normally should, but i don't really care about the load screen, game me enough to take a small sip of coffee as i wait.Now comes to the next big thing...  It reminded me a lot of the first DMC game where it would show an area at an angle and it could look a little weird, but i for one am already use to this. I have played multiple game with these kinds of camera angles to know what would happened when it switches. As long as you continue to hold the direction you were face when it does switch over you character should continue to move the save way unless you made an sort of adjustment when it does happen.There has only been 1 occurrence where this was an issue during a boss fight, but it did not make it too much of a problem. The camera isn't trying to fight with you, and its definitely a great artistic choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: AA games have always been great, and Soulstice is no exception. There are way too many low-effort indie games and definitely too many complete, absolute GARBAGE, money-grabbing, buggy AAA games. AA games on the other hand usually bring the best of both worlds.Soulstice is a very polished experience similar gameplay-wise to games like Devil May Cry or Bayonetta, but more focused on story. Fortunately, the story, characters, writing and voice acting are all very good. The game is also quite long (around 20 hours).The combat is quite enjoyable, you can feel the weight of your blows and there are some interesting gimmicks, like the two color-coded barriers used to defeat some enemies and your Shade, Lute, who can help you with both defending and attacking. There are some aspects of the combat that I would change, like shortening the recovery time for some actions and how focus works, but overall the combat is a very strong part of Soulstice, especially later on when you get used to it and you unlock more skills for your weapons and Lute.It seems like the most controversial thing about the game is the camera. I assume that people complaining about it missed the best era of gaming. However, I understand them when they say that a normal 3rd persona camera would've been better. I personally did not mind the camera for the most part. The only exceptions were some platforming sections when it was difficult to judge the distances and one or two fights when I got locked into a corner. It DEFINITELY is not a good reason to disregard this game.Graphically, the game looks great, especially the environments. The character models are stylised so they should not look dated even in a few years. I saw some people reporting performance problems, but fortunately I did not experience any. The game kept smooth 60 FPS throughout the whole game.The thing that I dislike the most about the game is the fact that the developer removed the demo version. That is a very suspicious thing to do, and I strongly disapprove of it.Taking everything into consideration, Soulstice is a solid action game, definitely worth the price, especially if you compare it to GARBAGE $60 AAA games that I would not play even if I was paid. I hope that the remaining flaws will be fixed in the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a game of gorgeous visuals, a touching love story between siblings, and ridiculous hyper violence, dashed with body horror.The locked camera, when it works, feels like the best of Bayonetta or Dante's Inferno. Like all games of this genre, however, late game enemies dashing in and out of the camera will start to demand a level of "reads" from the player that can be frustrating.The hyperviolence is over the top. Your claymore turns into a sledge hammer mid combo, your tonfas are also cannons/flamethrowers, and the demonic enemies rip off their own body parts to use as weaponry. Flowing between your absurd weapons and stringing the combos together becomes satisfying as the game rewards the "cool" style of play. Also, being graded in every encounter does spark the desire to push for diamond each fight.The story is simplistic but respectable. Our protagonist carries the guilt of her dead sister both figuratively, and literally as her ghost is the second protagonist, and your spiritual half on this anti-demon crusade. The demons corrupt people, and our protagonist is a warrior of the church (Also corrupt) struggling to push them back. Enough ground work is laid for a sequel, that I would jam, if it ever arrived.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my time with Soulstice. The world, while HEAVILY inspired by Claymore, manages not feel like a simple knockoff, but instead builds something original and engaging. The only problem is the length of the campaign, which starts slow and drags unnecessarily at the mind point while repeating too many times some fights. Luckily it rapidly picks up its pace in the last third, and then ends with a bang. The gameplay is like an old style DMC, with a fixed camera, quick weapon switching and the addition of a red/blue mechanic like the DmC spin-off. I didn't mind the camera, it added a certain nostalgic feel to this and made finding secrets pretty fun.Graphically, you can tell it's no a AAA game by the lack of environment variation, the repetition of many segments and the lackluster quality of some models/animations in cutscenes (poor Layton). Still, the game has its own style and most of the times it manages to look cool and stunning.The voice acting is very good, as are the sound effects. The score is appropriate, but it doesn't have any "banger" that stuck with me after playing. Overall it's a great game, and is definitely an excellent pick when discounted at around €20.

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the game story I can safely say I have no intention of coming back.I like the story and can see a lot of it inspirations.  Thats about the only good thing I can say about it.  That was enough for me to push through for one play through...Outside of that...  The camera system is something ripped out of the PS2 era.  Its clunky and unrefined.  By design it obscures certain things you might want to pick up, but it also makes any platforming or puzzles a flat out pain - not to mention when you are in an enclosed space with 4 2 story tall enemies that literally block the camera and you can't get an angle above the arena so you can actually see.  ♥♥♥♥♥♥ camera angles also makes it difficult to judge distance, making any jump more difficult than it needs to be.The sewer puzzle deserves a thumbs down on it own. Combat is repetitive.  There are a handful of enemies, most are jokes to handle... and then theres the electric shade.  Hard to stun, teleports frequently, constantly emitting a damaging aura.  To summarize, general enemy design ranges from bland to frustratingly.  Mix that with resource management and a god awful camera and you find yourself ready to drop the game with less than an hour left in it.  Bosses are OK though.  Wish there was more to them(all bosses repeat the same pattern until they die).Platforming and movement is fine... when not being actively hindered by the camera.  You've got all the staples.  Double jump, air dash, ground dash...  As mentioned above the camera is actively working to screw you over, and that kind of makes any platforming flat out miserable though.The world and art design is serviceable.  Its a bit grey, but its well put together.  Shame I can't view it a bit better... Thanks again, ps2 era camera!Sound won't knock your socks off, but its fine.  The battle music gets kind of repetitive, and I wish I can duct tape the character's mouths shut when not in cutscenes, but meh...One last note - if you do play this game turn off rumble on your controller.  You will thank me later.If they fixed the camera system the game would get a recommendation for me.  I could tell a lot of hard work went in to the game, and with a little more TLC it could shine.  But for now... Well, at the very least I can say that I'd be willing to pick up the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Let’s get this out of the way: Performance issues. They are there, but not for very long...After some reading, it seems to be an artifact of Unreal Engine 4; when something is loaded into the game for the first time, I lagged. During the prologue, it was a slide show. I adjusted some settings, restarted the intro, and it lagged for a few seconds, and then it was smooth. Every time I fought a new enemy, and they used an ability I hadn’t seen before, the game froze for a split second, and then smooth again.Review: Soulstice wears its inspirations lovingly on its sleeves: Claymore, Berserk, and obviously Devil May Cry (a few notes of Dragon Age and Darksiders in there as well); but the game also puts in the effort to be its own thing.The soundtrack and voice acting are competent; and the worldbuilding, dialog, character design, and pacing are all top notch. It’s the exact kind of dark fantasy stuff that I like and the boss designs are insane.The DMC style combat is pretty good. Starts out simple, then gains complexity as you unlock more stuff: Easy to do, tricky to master.There is a kind of “snappiness”, for lack of a better word, to the attacks where it tries to pull you to objects it is prioritizing which can be mildly annoying when you’re trying to smash stuff out of combat. *In combat* it’s not a problem and attacks work fine.I played the game with a PS4 controller (you can switch the button readout in the setting) and didn’t like to control scheme at first, but as I unlocked more attacks and abilities, it started to make more sense and grew on me pretty quick. You can change the controls if you want though…In short: I loved it! It’s good. If you like dark fantasy nonsense, mature characters, hack & slash combos, mild platforming here and there, and gradual upgrading like I do, then you’ll probably like this.I’m definitely keeping an eye on Reply Game Studios, and I hope they do more.
_childDocuments_.name: Soulstice

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not used to writing reviews, but I wanted to give Soulstice a recommend. I had a great time with it.I beat the game a few weeks ago and have only poked around for a minute or two after the latest major patch dropped (1.0.3), so I can't really speak to any changes it made.I'd call the combat distilled character action. All your (secondary/non-sword) weapons have more or less the same toolkit, and the combat encounters demand that you constantly switch between all of them throughout the course of a fight.You don't start out with a lot of weapon and mobility options, and for a while early in the game, it's a bit of a hassle chasing after mooks or trying to hack away at them with a tool that wasn't meant to deal with them. (Regarding mobility, I strongly recommend buying the whip's grapple immediately.)But once you unlock your full kit and fill out the upgrade trees a bit, with the way Briar (the player character) handles, the encounters turn into these hectic, fast and loose free-for-alls where the challenge is in prioritization and maintaining crowd control. Really rewarding to eventually get into the flow of a fight.In terms of performance, I use an AMD graphics card and think that might have caused some hiccups. In the Low Town part of the game, I had to drop my graphics to the lowest settings to get it to run smoothly, and later ran into a really gnarly technicolor visual glitch during a miniboss intro cutscene. Beyond that, nothing that personally bothered me much.I loved the boss and enemy designs, loved the soundtrack, and I'm honestly hoping we get a sequel or story DLC to show more of the world. Good game.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews for games but after, I finished Soulstice felt like It's deserve it.So as a Berserk fan when I first saw the trailer my opinion was like "A hack and slash with a female Guts" and I kept my eyes on it The game atmosphere is similar to Berserks and the gameplay is like DMC. I played all DMC (Yeah DMC2 too. God wish i wouldn't). So I would describe a game like Berserk and DMC having a fun night and bumm Soulstice was born.As I said combat system is similar to DMC. Fancy combos mean higher scores but there is a twist. You have a partner who act as your main defense and crowd control "tool" or even you can make her a dmg dealer too. Lute is simply amazing and she have a tons of upgrade path so you can build her to match your style. You have a stylish...I mean Unity meter which you build with combos and the higher it is Lute is become more and more effective. For me this system is amazing.Story wise the game stands on strong legs too. It's starts simple then It's become deeper and deeper.Briar and Lute are amazing characters. The creators did an amazing job with they personalities and sister bond.I don't write more about this because there is a lot of cliffhanger in their stories.The other characters are not as good as the sisters but they are build up correctly.Graphic is nothing extra but there are areas which look amazing.The game is optimalized? Well Let's just say I have a 5600x and a RTX3080 with them the game was rarely went under 80 FPS on 1080p with max settings ,except the last level. There somethimes is went under 60 FPS when the fight became chaotic.The only bad thing I can say about this game is the camera.Sometimes it can become your enemy. I don't saying it's an issue in the whole game but there are some fighting areas which ones become a little harder because of it.As final thought. This game was made with passion and love. You can feel it as you play it.If you like Hack and slash games you should give this a try and I'm sure It will not disappoint you.So thats all from me. _childDocuments_.review: I just completed Chapter 6, so this is going to review what I've seen and not the whole.I like the game, it is very much a return to Devil May Cry and Bayonetta style games aka Spectacle Fighters.  The pacing in the first chapters is certainly not something I'm accustomed to any more.  I've been playing Dark Souls and basically any Souls-Like that catches my interest over the past decade, so this is a drastic shift of gears.  The Opening gives you an in medias res fight that I believe is close to the final climax.  In that the combat is giving a taste of how it can flow between the two characters.  After that it takes you to the characters entering the city via the Docks.  Outside of combat, you are allowed to explore from a stationary 3rd person perspective.  This is directly reflective of the 1st Devil May Cry game and I think several others from the time frame, Resident Evil 1 through 3 might be the other big example.  Inside combat, you can move the camera around your character or lock on to a specific enemy.  I believe both will be necessary as some enemies have moves to disappear from the battle or speed away and break your lock on.  I think the make or break for personal experiences is going to hinge on whether you like the grading that the game is presenting you.  Each combat is given 4 scores, Combat Moves/tricks, Timer, Damage taken/done, and an overall rating.  The end of chapter collects all of these scores into a total, as well as present a blacked out medal for an optional fight that was missed.  I know the end of chapter rewards upgrade currency for story and I think it gives a bonus for good scores.I think the upgrades are expensive, but I would guess I'm 1/5th through main story progression.  Rewards and costs could get inflated later.

_childDocuments_.review: 🎀This title needs sequels, a trilogy. No dlcs!I loved it from start to finish and it took me back to the Bayonetta days, more for reasons of how the game is told.Soulstice is very reminiscent of the Claymore animated series that introduced me to my son, seeing all the episodes together.I would say that although completely different stories, there are very marked references such as transcendence itself.🎀In Soulstice there are two more crystals, in Doran and Rheim, in the final movie, even in the movie after the credits there are many confirmations and many doors open to a possible trilogy, this title must definitely expand, Briar and Lute are transcended both in one being?Briar is sure, Lute I don't know, but I'm very fond of both, two completely different characters but with a very deep bond.What will happen next? A dlc would be too little and it wouldn't be enough to finish/explain everything, the story is much wider and longer than it seems.🎀The ending of the game makes it very explicit that after the portal in Ilden closes, two more open, one on Doran and one on Rheim as mentioned above.Briar and Lute are quick to face whatever challenges arise in these cities. Then, a new character shows up on final movie, Kordelia the Reaper, in the employ of Lord Dugal and with the stated goal of killing Briar and Lute.Dugal is the real problem and he doesn't deserve to exist after what he did.🎀I think Soulstice was designed to be a trilogy. It would work great if each game would focus on one of the three sacred cities.For example:Each city can have a unique aesthetic and layout, a perspective that is less resource intensive when split across three games than crammed into one. By focusing on just one city like with the first game, Reply Game Studios can fine-tune the look and feel of the city and keep the whole game somewhat coherent.🎀I really think this is intended as a trilogy, but I also think Reply Game Studios is waiting to see what the reception will be for this game before fully committing to a second one.Whether or not Soulstice gets a sequel sort of depends on the player base.The reviews are very positive and this title really deserves a lot.I absolutely want the series to continue.🎀Small additional notes:Graphically beautiful and clean, light engine because the game has been programmed properly, satisfying and fast fights but you get the best trying to create combos by changing weapons, ok no spoiler about transformation.The semi-fixed camera during exploration, and mobile during fights never bothered me, as some mentioned having had problems with it.I tried to explore everything well in 26 hours of gameplay to look for as many collectible and secrets as possible.

_childDocuments_.review: I will recommend this game as it is pretty decent for its price. You're getting an okay story, some nice gameplay, and some decent graphics all for 40 bucks. Now, this game had ISSUES, but none of them can't be fixed in the sequel. My gripes with this game include the following - The whole game is spent in the same drab location, either in the cities or in the sewers, setting doesnt change much.- Get rid of entropy in the sequel... entirely. This red/blue color matching mechanic, while interesting at first, became nothing more than a nuisance after chapter 14 which is only about halfway through the game. I hated using it during combat and never once found it fun, just annoying. It was alright for puzzles (more on that right now)- Way too many puzzles. I like puzzles and they can be fun, but when they're simple and there's a LOT of them? They slow the game pace down a bit too much for my liking and the platforming for said puzzles weren't bad but also weren't the best- Briar and Lute stay the same throughout the whole game. There's no real character development despite what's going on around them. They stay the exact same from beginning middle to end. The voice acting also lacked emotion and tone in most situations- Lute as a partner was an interesting mechanic, but i'd rather just do the blocking and parrying myself as Briar (since you know I'm supposed to be a knight) and have Lute just be my auto-casting mage. Her skill tree was very nicely done too! - The weapons were eh... they spiced the gameplay up a bit by giving you more options in combat  situations, but ultimately they all played the same and had the same combos which was disappointing.Overall not a bad game, however I was just waiting for it to be over by Chapter 18 which is never a feeling you want for a video game. Lot of small issues that they could easily fix in the sequel with some reworking and some design changes (maybe a bigger budget too idk) A solid 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to buy this game on a whim because I had just finished Evil West (which was also great) and I was itching for more character action goodness. I had already seen some gameplay and I really like the visual style of the game but I kind of ignored it when it released (boy was that a mistake).I was not expecting this game to take such huge inspiration from og DMC games (DMC1 and 3), with things like fixed camera angles (which I love because it brings me nostalgia from early PS2 games), secret challenge missions, multiple weapon types to upgrade, new moves to unlock, a combat system that allows for creativity/freestyling (and ranking system), good enemy variety and designs, and probably the cleanest looking artstyle I have seen in a while.This game has exceeded any expectations I would of had and so far the game is on par with games like DMC 3, DMC 5, Ninja Gaiden Black/2, Bayonetta1/2, God of War 1-3 (original series)...etc. The wide shots of the world look beautiful, and the combat effects are very nice looking too without getting in the way. I'm just finding very little I don't like about this game, and the quality is what really surprises me.Pros:+ Visuals and Art-style are beautiful and a very clean looking.+ The animations and cutscenes are very smooth and look really nice.+ Combat is very unique with the addition of your sidekick and the synergy attacks (they feel really really good).+ Combat variation is excellent with you always unlocking new moves or getting a new weapon.+ Enemy variety is great and the enemy designs look great as well.+ Very classic DMC feel to exploration, with challenge missions to find, and character upgrades to find.+ Good pacing, and good balance between exploration and combat.+ Good voice acting+ Great cinematic cutscenes, with good animations, and over the top action like a DMC or Bayonetta game.+ (So Far) The story is engaging and making want to find out what happens next+ I actually like the fixed camera angles, because it reminds me of the PS2 era of the character action games.+ I have NOT experienced any bugs or crashes in the 7hrs (at the of the review) I have put in.+ Good atmospheric music along with some banger combat themesCons:- The Lute assist mechanics could have been explained a little more because early on I was a little confused on how to use her defensive mechanics.- Performance is decent but when performing the over the top super moves the framerate can drop a bit under 60fps (Specs: RTX 3080, Ryzen 3800x, 16GB RAM, Win10).- Enemy hit/stagger animations can look a tiny bit stiff at times (being very nitpicky here).Overall this is an excellent hack n' slash character action game. It actually surprised me how polished and how clean the art style is in this game, especially coming from an AA developer, that from my knowledge, was their first big project. If I did not look into the Devs I would have assumed it was from a AAA studios (that is how polished it feels and looks). It holds up with the best of em imo and the inspiration/passion oozes from this game, from the obvious Berzerk inspiration of the main character design to the DMC style level design. If you love the original DMC games (1 and 3) or just like character action games with fun and deep combat systems this game is 100% worth a try. I could not recommend this game enough!

_childDocuments_.review: To the Point======================Mid tier AA beat'em up with some frustrating gameplay choices that keep it from being great.Beaten on Knight (hard) difficultyGood Stuff====================- The minute to minute combat is good and with a game like this that's really all that matters.- The weapon variety, while sort of standard to these DMC kinds of games, is still pretty solid - Unity mechanic - This may be a deal breaker for some but the game rewards you for playing well and switching weapons. When you do well for long enough you do a super move and later on unlock a Devil Trigger like super mode.- The designs - Its a souls-like world thats well fleshed out with lots of interesting looking creatures and characters inhabiting it.Bad Stuff=====================- The Unity Mechanic - I know I just said this was a good thing, and it is, but it's like invisible how good you're doing, they should have a bar or somehow make it more obvious when you're in a unity state.- The fields - Like DMC ( the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Tameem one with DONTE) there are red and blue enemies at points in the game you need to kill by generating red and blue fields, however these don't last forever and can turn off from over use, which leads to the next point...- Emnity - This is the mechanic that turns off the fields I just mentioned. It builds slowly when a field is up and eventually maxes out, shutting down for 5 seconds or so. Later upgrades will, for some reason, cause it to fill faster. These abilities are used automatically so in endgame you can find emnity filling to fast for you to stop it and losing the fields for a short while. You can lower emnity by hitting enemies inside the field but it's nothing compared to the emnity generated by these abilities. I was constantly toggling fields on/off in endgame.- Damage - you do very little of it on hard difficulty and enemies are like sponges, could be I just don't know how to play but some of these fights took forever- Combat Penalties - This is a personal one, I'm used to being docked points for using items etc. but this game actually penalizes you for using the Devil Trigger Super Mode. I don't understand why you'd only let players use this mode when they're playing well then take points off for using it.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:Beautiful Graphics.   Great Storyline.   Interesting Characters.Cons:-  The combat system is mainly structured around your reaction time.
