You can't train and make your character's stats stronger in order to beat higher difficulties.-  All chapters are timed.  If you like to explore and leave no stone un-turned, you will get a lower score at the end of the chapter.-  I also don't like the tech tree.  It feels very linear.   For example:  In chapter 2, 95% of skills and abilities are unattainable regardless of how much time you pour into chapter 2, or how many monsters you kill.And I HATE the way the camera is practically fixed on each room/area.  You don't see the world through your character's eyes, but instead through a camera lens that's permanently fixed on one corner of the room. _childDocuments_.review: Soulstice : By Triple F"Soulstice," developed by Reply Game Studios and published by Modus Games, is a dark fantasy action game that takes players into a world torn apart by monstrous forces. At its core, "Soulstice" is an action-packed journey about sisterhood, sacrifice, and redemption. Players control Briar and her sister Lute, who are merged into a powerful entity known as a Chimera, tasked with defending humanity against monstrous entities called Wraiths. The game draws clear inspiration from titles like Devil May Cry and Nier: Automata, bringing stylish combat, impressive world design, and an emotional narrative to create a memorable experience that appeals to fans of hack-and-slash and dark fantasy genres.The game’s combat system is the heart of "Soulstice," balancing fluidity, complexity, and strategic depth. Players control Briar as the main physical fighter, with a range of weapons and combos at their disposal. Lute, on the other hand, exists as a ghostly presence that assists her sister with defensive abilities, crowd control, and support. This dual-character mechanic is unique and requires players to balance offense and defense, with Lute capable of interrupting enemies or casting shields while Briar unleashes powerful melee combos. The interplay between the sisters’ abilities becomes essential, especially in higher difficulties, and adds layers of depth as players master the synchronization of their attacks."Soulstice" emphasizes versatility in combat, allowing players to switch between different weapons mid-combo, unlocking new moves and abilities as they progress. Briar can wield a range of weapons, from heavy hammers to quick, nimble swords, each of which has its own strengths and can be swapped in real time. This variety keeps combat fresh, as different enemy types require players to adapt their strategies and experiment with weapon combinations. Coupled with the need to manage Lute’s support abilities, the combat system is both intense and demanding, rewarding players who take the time to understand each weapon’s nuances and the timing required for combo chains.One of the most interesting aspects of "Soulstice" is its Unity system, which tracks the sisters’ synchronization in battle. As Briar and Lute work together seamlessly, a Unity meter builds up, allowing players to unleash powerful synergy attacks that deal devastating damage to foes. However, if players miss attacks or mistime Lute’s defensive moves, the meter drops, weakening the power of these combined abilities. This mechanic encourages precision and rhythm in combat, challenging players to balance both offensive and defensive strategies to maximize damage output. As Unity builds, players also gain access to a “Rapture” state, which grants temporary boosts in power, adding an extra layer of intensity to the game’s most challenging encounters.The setting of "Soulstice" is equally impressive, taking players through a dark, Gothic-inspired city filled with ominous architecture, sprawling cathedrals, and haunting landscapes. The art direction is a standout feature, creating an atmosphere that feels oppressive and tragic, reflecting the sisters’ struggle against overwhelming odds. The environments vary from decrepit streets to cavernous ruins, and the color palette of muted grays, blacks, and blood-red accents adds to the sense of foreboding. The level design is mostly linear but allows for some exploration, with hidden pathways, collectibles, and optional challenges that encourage players to delve deeper into the world. These details add to the immersion, giving players the feeling of being trapped in a decaying, hostile world.The narrative in "Soulstice" is surprisingly emotional and centers around the relationship between Briar and Lute. The game explores themes of sacrifice, family bonds, and the cost of power, drawing players into the sisters’ journey as they grapple with their unique existence as a Chimera. Throughout the story, players witness flashbacks and moments of introspection that reveal more about the sisters’ past and their connection to the larger conflict. Voice acting is well-executed, and the writing, while occasionally leaning on fantasy tropes, does a solid job of making players care about the protagonists. The stakes feel personal, and the story is driven by the sisters’ bond, making it more compelling than a typical hack-and-slash narrative.Visually spealing, "Soulstice" combines a striking aesthetic with smooth animations that enhance the overall experience. The design of the Wraiths and other enemies is grotesque and imaginative, giving each encounter a sense of dread and intensity. Despite its overall dark color scheme, the game uses lighting and particle effects effectively, especially during combat sequences where powers and spells explode with vivid detail. However, performance can sometimes stutter during more crowded battles, particularly on older hardware, which may slightly break immersion for some players. Overall, though, the game’s visual presentation is polished and evocative, amplifying its dark fantasy appeal.All in all, "Soulstice" is a refreshing take on the action genre, combining fast-paced, combo-driven combat with an emotionally resonant story. Its dual-character mechanic is unique, challenging players to master a complex, rhythm-based combat system that balances aggression with careful timing. While its linear level design may not appeal to players who prefer open worlds, the game’s immersive art direction, engaging story, and intricate combat make it a compelling experience. "Soulstice" stands as a strong entry in the hack-and-slash genre, delivering both style and substance in a world that is as haunting as it is captivating. Fans of dark fantasy action games looking for both challenge and narrative depth will find "Soulstice" to be a rewarding journey.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Skip to the last paragraph.When the trailer for Soulstice was first released you could say I was pretty excited. I thought "A story heavy souls-like game with a female protagonist and interesting partner mechanic?! Count me in!" I got my first copy for free from Epic but didn't get around to playing it till more recently when I received a second copy from Humble Bundle. Upon looking a little more into the game I realized it was hack and slash and not so much a souls-like but I wasn't too worried about it. I thought it'd be a nice break from Elden Ring and maybe take me back to my early days of hack-and-slash games on the PS2 and Gamecube. So while I was excited I came into this game without any real expectations, yet, it still disappointed me. The intro cutscene was a little unclear and a huge info dump. MC's voice acting is pretty bad and the shade has issues enunciating some words but is great otherwise. The dialog reads like a Discord conversation rather than characters who live in this grim-dark world. Cutscene after cutscene after cutscene. I like visual novels, I like episodic series, and short animations but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ LET ME PLAY THE GAME! Cutscenes upon entering combat and mid-combat even with trash mobs. Cutscenes where your character fights and runs around the stage you were on not really doing anything you couldn't have just so MC and the shade can talk which they COULD do without the cutscene. With all the cutscenes I'd think the animation would be a little better as well or maybe they'd lean into a low frame rate style as you see in claymation. Semi-regular stuttering on higher-end hardware. Camera angles were abysmal. The combat is salvageable but as it stands it doesn't feel snappy and is just kind of there. You often have to press the target button multiple times to target an enemy even if it's the only one on the field and goodluck target swapping. To supplement the slow boring combat I tried using the "dodge" as a dash but it isn't designed to be used as a gap closer so it still didn't feel quite right. Tool tips don't always tell you what button to press and the ability names don't match up with the button layout. Finally, the 'knight' mode is the highest difficulty available to a new player and it felt like I was playing in a training mode with incoming damage disabled on beginner bots.I would take more time to better explain and condense this mess of thoughts but I'm running on fumes at the moment.I REALLY want this game to be good and if they at least addressed the combat issues and excessive cutscenes I'd be happy to continue playing. But, as it stands I don't feel this is worth its $40 price tag. You're better off picking up something like RWBY Grimm Eclipse while it's on sale to scratch that early to mid-2000s hack-and-slash itch.

_childDocuments_.review: Played on Epic, decided to give it another shot since I got it from Humble this month.This game VERY badly wants to be Devil May Cry, and it does not actually do a very good job of it. The combat is aggressively okay, though I found the counter system to be extremely inconsistent. I may have simply been doing something wrong, but it felt as though sometimes I would only get .2 seconds to react to an attack, and other times I would get several seconds to react to the exact same attack from the exact same enemy. The weapon variety is fine, but everything you unlock later isn't really useful except in niche scenarios, so you just default to the sword/hammer weapons you start with 99% of the time.The story is alright, but just doesn't really leave an impression. There's a few too many cutscenes that last longer then they have any right to, but it's inoffensive.tl;dr do not but this game at full price, get it at a steep discount, and don't expect it to blow you away. This is a game specifically and really only for fans of the genre

I really want to give this a positive review, and until about half way through the game it DEFINITELY was a fun and engaging game, with a few bits of jank that werent show stopping. And I have the upgrades to slow it down from being lost* Im noticing less sense of direction - the goal (avoiding spoilers). Previously there was a real sense of the world failing and we needed to get to the goal, and save people. But these recent levels just feel meh - generic burning houses we have seen before. Same bridges and gates and buildings. Same stuff scattered around the streets. It does not feel any different than about chapter 3. _childDocuments_.review: So I had to drop this game. The combat itself is pretty good at a baseline. It reminds me of every action game I have played, which is actually a positive. I upgraded this meter and found ways to lower it through those upgrade but after a while it didnt matter. _childDocuments_.review: This game was pretty uneven experience, sometimes was awesome... sometimes bad...It takes a lot of inspiration from old God of War and DmC (Ninja Theory one, not the GOOD DMC) with some Berserk inspired aesthetics.- The story is intriguing and pretty unique, the mystery is unfold through the course of a game and main cast is written well with Briar and Lute in the spotlight.- Quite impressive for such a small team to pull out AAA graphics, it has a realistic look with stylized characters.- Soundtrack is pretty decent, it's composed with atmospheric ambiance and blood pumping combat tracks (I only wish there was more of them).- Unique combat, Briar controls like a standard melee character but with Lute as a companion that has a lot of offensive and defensive abilities with plenty of synergies between sisters.- The camera is your constant enemy. It works inconsistent during combat and exploration. I have never seen more clunky lock-on system, sometimes is just impossible to lock into exact enemy you want to follow. I hope this will get patched as it was the biggest issue of this game for me.- Color coded combat with flying enemies. Huge pain in the ass to deal with them, makes bow weapon most of the time useless, some types even teleport constantly which makes you run across arena back and forth all the time.- Inconsistent enemy telegraphs and Lute defense. You never know if you can block/parry attack with Lute or you have to dodge them. To make this more annoying, some enemy hit boxes are huge that even perfect evade distance won't escape it.- Game is paced very uneven. There is a lot fat that could be trimmed to make this game shorter but much more enjoyable experience.Despite flaws that mostly can be fixed with patches, I recommend giving Soulstice a try if you are fan of spectacle action fighters. I also hope this production will be successful enough for sequel to be made because I am eager to see what might happen next.

_childDocuments_.review: Utmost sighs. I really wanted to like this game, but the game seemed determined to convince me otherwise. The combat is fairly competent enough for what I believe is this studio's first game in this style. Which is a long-winded way of saying it's just okay. It clears the (low) bar of No More Heroes combat, and falls short of DMC1 combat, which falls short of every other DMC game except 2. Of the four weapons I unlocked, none of them felt very distinct from each other. Lute's moves were interesting in concept, but poorly executed, since all her attacks are mapped to the same button, so she's basically a glorified QTE robot. I will be a contrarian and say I don't mind the color coding, since it's a neat way of keeping you cognizant of combat. Would be even better if the camera weren't a tad sluggish. So, I was hoping that the game could make up for the mediocre combat with anything else, which it couldn't. The level design from all that I played, up to about chapter 8, is very repetitive and dull. You'll be seeing a whole lot of blueish grey ruins throughout your adventure, and not much else, (it sticks out a lot more to me since I just played Dante's Inferno a few weeks ago, a game stuffed to the brim with diverse and lively environments and levels). This wouldn't be too bad if the levels weren't so obnoxiously long. The longevity wouldn't be obnoxious if there was much to do in these levels. There's not. Outside of the token three to four battles per chapter, there's some trivial platforming (with invisible walls to hold your hand as much as possible), and occasional crystals to destroy for currency. Ultimately, the biggest sin of the game is its length, what should be a five-to-six-hour game that's stretched out much longer than it needs to be because quantity over quality is the name of the game these days, sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: Clunk fueled nightmare with too much focus on weird and un-fun aspects of gameplay. Saw the trailer for this game and thought it looked insanely cool. Grabbed it on sale, because I was a little bit cautious. At first it has some cool call backs to classics like Devil May Cry, but that get's tired really fast. The combat tutorial that's supposed to "wow" the player into the game was just like being given an invincibility star, and then being told to mash buttons until everything is dead. You unlock new moves by picking up currency in each chapter, but simple things like a combo ender from a launcher aren't a baseline ability? Your sister is a cool idea, but in combat it really just amounts to mashing out the block button any time it's on screen, and forget about perfect guarding if you're trying to play the game even slightly casually. You also have to activate a number of gimmicky combat mechanics to make your shade seem more effective, but if you're not managing a number of poorly designed looking gauges you lose the ability to do anything with her for a period of time. I'm obviously in the minority on this game, which is good, because the environments, and the artstyle are really incredible. Hopefully if this game gets enough attention the devs can iron out all the needless complexity and bring back a more distilled hack and slash adventure experience. For now it's just too much work, for no real reason. Also if you're going to get voice actors who sound as good as these ones, write something good for them to act! Just because it's a style of game born in the cringe infested waters of the 1990's does not mean you have to write the dialogue like a preteen focus group high on Twilight, and vape juice. So much potential.

_childDocuments_.review: #1 Rule of Soulstice. Turn off screen shake. The screen shake may be too much to bear and may cause a headache or eyestrain.This game is incredible for what it is. It takes inspiration from the Devil May Cry/Bayonetta/Platinum Gmaes shenanigans and made Soulstice their own. It has your bread and butter hack 'n slash with good range of difficulty(I'm getting my butt kicked, and loving it)The voice acting... *insert Pacha meme*The voice acting is incredible. _childDocuments_.review: I like to style myself as a writer, but I do not have enough words to say how much I loved this game. The world is so full of lore and detail - the weapons, the people, the monsters, the places - it feels completely fleshed out and everything has a reason. There's even lore-backed explanations for why/how certain game mechanics work and the limitations on them. Every fight, every chapter, every challenge is ranked from lowly iron to lofty diamond based on score, time, and damage taken, with respective medals for each. If you loved the Claymore anime or manga, you'll love this game. If you loved the earlier God of War or Devil May Cry games, you're probably going to love this game. As someone who doesn't often play fixed-camera side-scroller style games, the only problem I ever had with this game was down to depth perception. Where targets were and where attacks would land, and one specific bit of parkour. With not one, but TWO difficulties locked behind completion barriers, there's plenty of replayability and opportunity to push your limits on getting timing and resource management right. And that's not to mention the over a dozen challenges to test your limits. I would absolutely recommend this game to everyone. Amazing story, wonderful gameplay, and a surprisingly detailed setting, considering how desolate and ruined it all is. It was 100% worth every penny, and I can't wait to sink more hours into it, completing the harder levels and working for higher scores. Absolutely stunning. Aside from my issues with depth perception, I really have nothing bad to say about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but it's just not good. Each trigger is bound to a color change that does nothing but allow you to interact with objects and enemies of that color, blue and red. They are on a shared timer. That is so artificial and pointless it's actually disgusting.Some elements they did well - the pause type combos have an actual pause and vibration for combo timing, while some they did poorly - the classic "stinger" move that is meant to quickly get you back into a fight launching weaker enemies. Overall aggressively mediocre and core elements (everything ghost partner related) executed so poorly as to actually hold the game back from being good. The dual protagonist thing was what sold me on the game as well, because that could have been used for a unique or at least more fun and stylish combat system, but instead actually makes the game worse.If you haven't played metal gear rising or devil may cry, play those instead. This is a depressingly mediocre clone.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my biggest problems with games is not copying, it is when they copy poorly. If one is aware of the reputation of Euroshmups, this game is the Euroshmup of the Stylish Action genre. Ill-conceived, overly-complicated mechanics; unnecessary skill-trees; more thought put into the plethora of accessibility options than making a camera fit for this genre; too much focus on story and ineffectual attempts at characterization; and boring enemy design. Also, cinematic sequences are anemic and sluggish imitations of stylish choreography found in that Capcom/Clover/Platinum pedigree.I played through three missions to fight the first boss, and was rewarded with a fat, armored giant wielding a hammer... so that's a perfect zero on the originality scale. This enemy plays like a mid-boss who gets demoted to mook status mid to late game. If we're generous and count Bayonetta's tutorial Prologue as the first real level, then the second level gives you the equivalent of this guy (whom you kill with a cool cinematic finisher), along with a preview fight for the upcoming boss, and level 3 starts with a Jeanne fight. In the first Devil May Cry, you get Devil Trigger in second mission and the third mission has you fighting Phantom, an enormous spider-scorpion hybrid made of magma and stone. We're 20 years out and the grand-daddy of this genre is still regularly schooling newer entries. Imagine scoring lower on a middle-school math test than your knuckle-dragging, missing-link ancestors who scrawled on cave walls with charcoal. Another example of taking without understanding is Soulstice's prologue chapter: an in medias res fight where you have a bunch of upgrades and no idea what you're doing other than waling away. In a metroidvania, this might allow you to sample your eventual power level, or introduce you to mechanics you will need to be thinking about when you come across environmental puzzles later on. If your game has diverse skill-trees, you can experiment and decide what you want to invest in going forward. In an action game, this confuses you because you're about lose 90% of this and gain it back in a linear fashion. It also rushes you through the encounter, so any real experimentation is out. Other than learning which button attacks, this level does fails as a gameplay segment. It hints at your "Devil Trigger", but I only know that because I've seen the anime Claymore, and I had no way of telling if this was having an in-game effect at the time or purely cosmetic.If you've never played Devil May Cry or Bayonetta, go play those. If you have played those, you're unlikely to put up with the fumbling missteps of Soulstice. If you're absolutely all out of stylish beat 'em ups, are you sure? Have you tried Fight 'N Rage? It's reeeeeally good. Have you tried Marlowe Briggs? It's a lot more entertaining. Have you downloaded an emulator and played God Hand? Fine, fine. After all that, you could do worse that getting this game for $10, maybe $15 on the outside, if you're desperate. It firmly sits in that 5 or 6/10, just squeaking into the mediocre but playable category.As for the lore, I just want to say that there's homage, there's wearing your inspirations on your sleeve, and then there's sub-contracting your story out to your favorite Japanese manga-ka without telling him. Soulstice is pretty firmly in the latter category. Too bad the budgetary saving created by this five-finger discount didn't go towards better voice acting.

_childDocuments_.review: I am changing my review for a second time after beating the game and am going to cautiously recommend the game. It is a really cool experience with a lot of love put into it in a genre that doesn't get many releases. Learning to deal with the camera and the enemy combinations that make scenarios fairly chaotic (with said bad camera) takes time and a willingness to put up with frustration... which just won't be worth it for many. I have kept my original review with my original criticism (most of which was alleviated with control scheme changes and learning to play this game as a true hack and slash and not a spectacle fighter. The game is more about threat management than stringing together combos and you just have  to accept that)Original Review: I really wanted to like this game but the camera and lock on system are truly a disaster. Also every 20 seconds there is a cutscene to interrupt the flow of gameplay (said cutscenes are disappointingly 30 fps).For good aspects. the art direction is cool if a little monotonous. The characters look great. When the combat flows (which wasn't too common in my case) you do sometimes get that zen feeling from other genre greats. The game ran well on my PC as well.I think this game is having a hard time deciding if it wants to be God of War or DmC and it lands in no man's land and it really doesn't feel good to play.My fixes: So based on reading other reviews I disabled vsync and that did indeed make the cutscenes better. I personally limited it to 60 fps on a 240 hz monitor so the screen tearing is "mostly" unnoticeable.Secondly. I use the following controls to make combat manageable (and dare I say sometimes fun haha). The goal of this scheme is to acknowledge that the lock on sucks and to instead keep your fingers on the sticks. Unfortunately I was only able to accomplish this with a controller with back buttons so I could jump and dodge with A and B on the back of the controller.A - JumpB - dodgeRB - Base attackRT - special weapon attackLT - Lute actionL3 - Blue fieldR3 - Red fieldThe rest of the buttons don't really matter. Note I have LB as lock on but I don't really use it so LB could be used for dodge or jump but you would still be one short without extra buttons :(

_childDocuments_.review: Giving the game a negative review because Reply Games Studios is ESG-compliant.Criticisms and suggestions:Dialogue - Remove the need for a speaking character to finish his/her animation before switching characters. Ideally make all dialogue continuous, with the option to pause if need be. If not, allow the characters to move during their dialogue, but let said movements continue during the next piece of text. For reference, Darksiders 2 comes to mind. TL;DR: make the the dialogue more seamless and smoother.Camera - Don't be afraid to zoom out more, especially during combat. Low-angles are great for cinematic shots but they can get in the way of traversal sometimes; and - Open up the environments a little more if need be. They look great, and nobody is going to notice if the streets are a bit wider just so the player has a better time fighting enemies.Combat - Needs anim cancels in more attacks. As a hack-n-slash, responsiveness is key. Follow-through on attacks are more important in soulslike games.  - Take control of the camera away from the player and instead spend time framing the combat arenas well. For reference, God of War 3. - And on that note, I'd suggest attaching directional-dodge to the right analogue stick. That way it can be functional all the time and not just during combat. Getting that tiny camera-move input from the right stick frustrates a lot more than not having it at all. - Stinger + dodge with every weapon, not just the sword (as in, Dodge+AltAttack, not just Move>Move>AltAttack). - Force Wraiths (and off-screen enemies) to move into the player's FoV before they attack. Alternatively, frame the combat area better (see above). - Increase the hitboxes for crystals and random corrupted humans walking about. Of all things, these shouldn't be a trial to hit.Music - Electronic was the wrong way to go about combat music. Orchestral or metal would have been better fits. Not saying EDM-adjacent music can't match the mood of the game, but it fell short in this case.Lute's Fields - Make them more diegetic. Make the colour drain or the field vibrate as Lute reaches Overcharge and remove the need to look at the icon on the top left. The vocal queue is fine. - Using the fields in combat is an interesting idea. Unfortunately, it should have been simplified. Ideally, the enemies that can only be fought with fields should have a 'shield' system instead: the wraiths should become corporeal for a few seconds after the blue field is activated (like the Sirens from God of War 3 when exposed to Helios' head) and the 'red crystal' enemies should have a breakable barrier (like the Abomination boss) that allows the player to deal damage for a few seconds. The fun should be in the fighting and the combos, not in juggling the active fields.Other: - Just found a feeble fillament by accident. Make them more obvious once you're in their vicinity. They blend too easily with the monotonous blue-white cityscape.Overall, a very flawed game with some fun combat. Difficulty is inconsistent, and you'll often find that bosses are easier than elite enemies. Becomes boring and monotonous before long.

_childDocuments_.review: The game at best is mediocre and while I normally wouldn't bother with a review for a mediocre game, there's a couple things in it that make me have to recommend against getting this game. One of the first challenges you find in the game is to do 5 perfect counters within a minute. That wouldn't be a problem, if they actually gave you more than a milisecond to get a perfect counter in. They have such a high requirement to get it in that if you don't press the button the INSTANT the prompt shows up, it doesn't count. I had to stop trying to depend on them showing the prompt and had to go by enemy movements and guessing on when the prompt should show up to hit the button before the prompt even showed up and only by doing that could I actually get a perfect counter. That mechanic alone is enough for me to give this review, but there's one other thing that I find to be a terrible design decision: the reward system. You are given no way to improve your attack power between chapter 1 and 2, yet they some how expect you to do more damage in chapter 2 and due to you not having increased attack power, your score suffers, when your score suffers, you get less rewards, when you get less rewards, you can't get more upgrades, when you can't get more upgrades, you can't do more damage... it's a perpetual cycle leading to you getting and worse and worse score and an awful design decision. Similarly, they also force players to rush through the game because the timer is always counting while you're playing, even when talking to NPCs or exploring. Yet you're also supposed to explore to find all their challenges and such.Also, I don't like fixed cameras, they're never in a good spot.

_childDocuments_.review: The balance of the kingdom is compromised and now it is up to you to save it. You play as Briar, someone granted superhuman strength and resilience with the help of Chimera. Explore a dark world brimming with mysteries and master a combat system filled with fast-paced action and grand boss fights that reeks of the inspiration from Devil May Cry and Bayonetta. With a unique arsenal of upgradable weapons that can be switched on the fly or insane combos, it is time to unleash and plow your way through this dark story to find out the truth behind it all.While I do believe there is a good game hidden in here, it is definitely not ready for the Steam Deck. We were warned by the developer that it wasn't optimized for the Steam Deck, but people are still going to wonder how it runs! Soulstice struggles to hit 30 FPS and when it does, it still has stuttering issues. On top of that, it will require a lot of power to stabilize that 30 as much as possible, which we felt drained way too much (20W). I did want to make mention that changing the settings did require exiting and re-opening the game for the new settings to take effect. This generally isn't a bad thing, but there were no prompts that the game needed to be restarted for changes to take effect or anything. Just a small oversight, but one that I want to make note of.I can feel a good game trying to get out, and I think it would shine on the Steam Deck, but it just isn't ready yet. We were warned by the developer, but I wouldn't call this one yet. The game does implement DLSS, which means it COULD have FSR 2.0 implementation later down the road. On top of that, we submitted a couple questions to the dev team about Deck support, we will update the review and our article once we hear back. I believe there is a good game underneath all of this, but since we are rating solely on Steam Deck performance, I would wait on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is direct proof that in gaming, looks aren't everything.  Sure, in order for a game to be considered one of the best, the graphics have to be there, but the gameplay and design need to be there, too.  The fun needs to be there.  The whole package has to be complete for the game to have, well, soul.  Ironically, Soulstice lacks soul.  Plotwise it's a B-grade anime style affair with a girl carrying a sword shaped club (seriously, it doesn't have sharp edges, it's like they got a midjourney like AI to design the main character).   Actually that's what most of the character and enemy design for the game reminds me of. Usually at this point I'll embark on the technical defects in the game... I can't do that so much here, there's 4K graphics, a lot of tweaks and customisability, colourblind modes, pretty much everything you could ask for. This is a sloppy, lazy console port with terrific graphics, but some of the shallowest, most mindless and definitely unenjoyable gameplay imaginable.  Combat is a dry, third person brawl where skill is irrelevant and button mashing is king.   You'll spend your time doing some light platforming and pretend-exploration through the nicely presented, linear, boring levels. The real killer, the worst part of this... no mouselook or true mouse camera control.  What a joke!  Do we look like console peasants?  Fixed camera controls like the ones in this game are a direct limitation because consoles lack the processing power to render complex 3D scenes properly... yet the developers here, instead of just designing and optimising their game to work properly on real PCs and not gaming appliances, decided to inflict those limitations on us. As a result, the game is very, very unpleasant to play as you twiddle around imprecise and changing direction and perspectives that the gamer has no control over.  I have no idea how console peasants survive under those conditions, but the best part is, I just don't have to put up with them. There's a story to the game, but the gameplay itself is so painfully poor that I just couldn't get into it.   They want $40 for this, and that's not okay.  $40 bucks spent wisely would get you several older AAA games with far better gameplay than this, with money to spare. It really is such a shame that so much development money (and time and talent from the fantastic artists and 3D graphics guys) was wasted on a bland, joyless button mashing train wreck that seems to have been designed to entertain 8 year olds.

_childDocuments_.review: A very decent PS2 era DMC type action game. I enjoyed this game despite its faults. The combat feel is actually good. The main character can switch between a heavy Berserk-like claymore and a more Dante-eseque broadsword and it's conveyed well enough in the weighty feel of the attacks. There are of course other weapons each with their own unique uses, but my point is the action feels right and good. So many action games never achieve that. Hitting enemies has appropriate feedback.But also in general the game looks solid. The environments can kind of be a drag, as they are samey. Yet when the game wants to have a visual set-piece it can muster up the energy. The character's berserk transformation sequence is a beautifully rendered manga-inspired infusion that looks to capture the Berserk manga's pencil shading during intense moments, and it does it well. It may be AA but in general, the presentation and production values put some major studios to shame. Cutscenes look good, monster design is interesting, the final bosses especially look great.But it sits at decent to me because:The core gameplay is good, but the camera and lock on truly do remind me of the PS2 era. Static camera angels I can deal with, but a camera and lock on that feel like they have no idea what they are doing during battle is a harder pill. It just kind of leads to some headaches as there is a lot going in combat.It throws a lot of enemies at you, but also your astral sister kind of plays crowd control. So during combat enemy attacks will put up a qte essentially that you press the button that corresponds to your sister where she blocks, counters, and stops the attack. Which adds a neat lawyer as it helps fans of these games that complain about attacks not being visible.  Well, here you stop them and then have a clear amount of time to position and dodge. It puts emphasis on that and it's smart because it never feels like your stopping the attack.But your sister is also shooting astral laser attacks that you upgrade for her to even more, so lots of light show ♥♥♥♥ towards the end of the game.But a less smart choice is color coded enemies, but see it's not even like you switch to red or blue weapons, you turn a blue or red area of effect where enemies have to be in that area to fight them. For example, if the blue enemy is out of the field, your ranged attack won't damage them until they are in your blue aoe stance. So thats annoying.What's really annoying is the possessed enemies. Red enemies are possessed and when you defeat them the blue ghost comes out and you need to take them out before they "repossess" the red enemy and bring them back. This is for most enemies later in the game and sometimes multiple ghosts. But that means you have to switch stance(hoping your gauge is not empty) and quickly kill them. That's made hard by the ♥♥♥♥ lock on though. So there were plenty of annoying moments.The story was ok.....like it does come off as a story the writer came up with when they were 16 and thought fantasy ♥♥♥♥ where the religion is evil is still edgy..But they are very invested in their world and characters which is admirable, but I don't know if ending on a huge big "the adventure is not over" type ending is a bit silly.Good game though. I enjoyed it. I like PS2 era action games and this is of that ilk.

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely solid action game. I greatly enjoyed my time and will probably revisit it to grind out a few more of the optional items.The big selling points for me (after beating the campaign):* Fantastic fixed-camera controls in open world (combat camera is player-controlled except during certain big boss battles). It just always felt really good and responsive, like a refreshing look back at older game design with modern polish* Great combo and weapon system that is paced well enough for you to get a real feel of each weapon and ability's contribution to your kit. You can have your favorites but you'll probably end up using a bit of everything as the balance is quite solid* Kickass soundtrack that sets the mood just right. Nice work!* Surprisingly solid story that I ended up caring about waaaay more than I thought I would based on the genre. It's not mind-blowing, but the execution is extremely solid.

_childDocuments_.review: I gave this a fair shot, but it's just boring. The game itself hasn't shown any real difficulty in the first 3 levels so far and the main antagonist seems to be the camera, plotting against you and tunneling into the environment randomly. It also doesn't feel great moving around platforms, nor do your attacks have enough impact to keep the general gameplay interesting. The enemies take far too long to cut down as well, since I was getting "Diamond" rating, I'm assuming that's just how long they take to deal with efficiently for some reason.There also seems to be a myriad of audio issues I noticed, the mixing is also terrible with the main characters being quiet, then the shop keep comes onto the scene bass-boosted. During one fight when a lot of enemies were on screen, the audio also just died entirely, it did come back afterwards though at least.I don't want to keep playing for much longer and after seeing it takes an average of ~17 hours to beat, I'm calling it here. The best way to describe this game is that it's a spectacle fighter that has mediocre fighting....

_childDocuments_.review: So after going on it for almost a month for about one to five hours three, four times I finally finished the game with 12 hour all-nighter straight today. I did not expect this game to be this long. I though it would be short but it excelled my expectation.This game is a hidden gem, that I am sure most gamers don't know about. If you are a fan of souls like game this is something you would actually enjoy more than getting frustrated like in other games except for the challenge missions. The combat and gameplay is over the top and the map is made so well with invisible walls that you can just enjoy the game without worrying about falling out and dying. But the most interesting part of the game was the story and the cut scenes as well as graphics. To be truthful I did not though this game would be this good. It totally blew my mind, the action packed gameplay the maps and the awesome movie like cut-scenes with perfect voice lines except for the main two characters few repeated lines which should be limited to one to two times maximum else it feels like a broken record. Except for those few lines awesome story line.The way the game went it can have two sequels in future for the two cities and more.  I pulled an all-nighter because I wanted to finish the game and the gameplay and boss battles were awesome so I loved this. Though beware if you never played PS2 games then the camera angle will cause you a lot of trouble. For me it was ok except for few stages where I had to do it over and over due to not making it in time but except for that this game is excellent. So feel free to give it a try and thank you devs for making this game and I hope we will get some sequels or similar games in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is heavily inspired by Claymore, Berserk and PS2 era Devil May Cry games. There were some complaints about the camera, but if you are familiar with early DMC and similar games then you will feel right at home. I really enjoyed the character designs, story and atmosphere. I've completed two playthroughs, completed all challenges, and completed all upgrades. At this point I think I have pretty much finished my time with Soulstice.I do wish there were more variety in enemies and level design, but this isn't a AAA game. One thing that did get a little annoying over time was how the characters repeated the same lines again and again throughout the game when traversing the levels.I liked the Rick and Morty reference from the big giant head boss ("Show me what you got") and Armina's design reminded me of Sirene from Devilman. There are probably references to other things out there that I missed.I recommend the game and hope the developers are able to finish the story with a sequel - I liked the game enough that I would support a Kickstarter.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice scratched an aesthetic itch and brings some cool new ideas as a character action game. I love Briar and Lute, I love the quickly introduced ideas of Chimeras and the Order of the Ashen Blade that define the characters. The enemies may have their distinct origins making them samey aesthetically, but there is great variety in the gameplay. A lot of criticism about the camera choices is valid, but not too bad in combat sections. Some combat mechanics  could have been better, but it's got some neat specialties like some Melee-esque fight bonuses and mechanics that directly play into high style rating, to compare to DMC.I really love a lot of the story beats and get why it progressed how it did. I wish it ended a little differently . There are extra challenges and higher difficulties, but I don't see much incentive for non-trophy hunters. I'm glad I tried it out, it's definitely earned its own spot on my shelf.

_childDocuments_.review: Although the game sometimes fights itself with a not always reliable lock on system and a lot of knock backs with a not always reliable gap closer, the combat is by and large fun. I won't even pretend to understand exactly what I should have been doing in fights, but switching weapons and finding openings for the special attacks was engaging. Nice to play a game with two characters that actually feel like they're fighting together as well. Having a block/counter button that didn't fling you over to other enemies was a pleasant change of pace from the more usual Arkham style combat. I don't have a lot of experience with Dmc, Bayo or anything else, so maybe the game isn't as mechanically deep as those. Was a blast playing through on the highest initial difficulty though. The story isn't anything terribly new if you're familiar with other dark fantasy works, though the world building and characters did enough to differentiate themselves from similar works. Briar and Lute were endearing and have some nice growth over the course of the game. It was very nice to hear a different VA compared to the usual suspects, just for a change of pace. A lot of really neat views of the city as you travel through it. The scenery is a little limited by the location, though the environments do change as you progress. I'll be hoping to see a sequel somewhere down the line. I am invested in the sisters journey now and it'd be a shame if this is all we ever got to see of them.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a double-edged sword. I had a tremendous amount fun with the combat. Character models are crisp and environments are incredibly detailed. Performance is generally... fine. I had a few problems with stuttering when i first started, but they were ironed out after a few tweaks. HOWEVER, the level design is so repetitive that it makes me want to scream. It felt like half of the combat encounters in the first half took place on the same stretch of ramparts. It's not great. Also, the voice acting and story were very boring to me. I enjoyed it at first, but around the halfway point, I noticed that i was just watching cutscenes while eagerly waiting for them to be over so that I could return to the substantially more fun combat. _childDocuments_.review: I have quite mixed feelings about Solstice. While the story turns out more interesting than i initally thought, there are some flaws that have wasted my enjoymentCombat works well. Mechanics are introduced one by one, and are intertwined as you progress. It is a beat em all that does its job, rather accessible. But it does lack variety, despite the 6 secondary weapons Briar wields. Their respective upgrades (bought at the shop) unlock new skills, dash, air launcher, slam, and a long combo that is nearly unusable most of the time. And that's it : all weapons actually all the same skills to use. Once i realized that only three weapons actually mattered, despite each having their own strategic advantages against certain enemies, all the others were forgotten on the spot. Also, switching between them during the fight is kinda awkward. On the other hand, our ghost sister, Lute, has a large skill tree, all passive abilities, with which we easily see the increase in powerExploration is another sigh-inducing point : the sole purpose of exploring the city (read "corridors") is to find health upgrades. otherwise, everything looks the same from the first chapter to -nearly- the last.But the worst abomination of this game is the camera. Derived from the old Devil May Cry, this atrocity will never be at the right place. Even set at the max speed, finding enemies is a challenge, as enemies will turn invisible if the camera is too close, or unreadable if too far, which both happens too regularly. Lock doesn't help as it tries desperately to juggle between moving targets, and fighting without the lock will make many fights terribly hard, as some wil lrequire to target a specific enemy.The camera is really the one thing that drove my patience to zero, despite the OK game Soulstice is

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this game it seems to be strongly inspired on Berseker and Claymore manga, I heavily recommend to check it out if you like both of these sources, If you like Claymore over it, even more. The gameplay is based around old school Hack and slash games of the ps2 era, with of course, updated graphics, amaizing cutscenes and polished artistic departure, involving around the idea of grimdark anime.Pros:-Visuals and cutscenes.-Good variety of weapons and skill three.-Narrative is strongly based on Claymore.-Good finishers and different ways to break trought the enemy lines.-Great main boss fights.-Multiple ways to aproach different enemies, synergies with weapons and switching is required during combat.ConsThings to improve:-Some semi-boss fights feel a bit unfair, excesive lower enemies attacking at the same time as the semi-boss (Abomination felt really bad, since his attack range is huge and the timing is hard to read when you use the freeze counter on him)-The parry system works most of the time, but the game doesn't properly explain what is a perfect counter (its blocking with "B" before the enemy starts an attack animation, NOT later)-The afinity system between the sisters, sometimes can be annoying due the multiple enemies at the same time attacking you and aoe effects from bigguer enemies. Also it doesn't work to much if there is only one enemy with small or non consecutive counter openings (takes more time and its harder to fill the bar, if you have to move around the bigguer attacks and they don't let you stick near them to make chained combos)-The weapons chained combo it's most of the same for every weapon, but there is complexity in to know when to switch between weapons or make more complex air combos. (But also mention that the air combos give less afinity within briar and lute, so most of the time you gonna stick to the ground to apply these combos, with a few exceptions like the bigger panthoms that you find during the second half of the game).-One of the main flaws for me during the gameplay, It was that lute skill tree can be a long run problem if its not revised and take the correct upgrades. For example, any hability that increases entropy can be a potential bottleneck for you. If you don't go for a overload build and you take to many of these skills, you can be stuck on boss fights due that the entropy will be always at 70-80%, so you can't mantain lute energy field for more than 4-5 seconds, leaving you in the middle of the fight doing nothing at all until lute recovers and let you attack again (This is kind of horrible in a hack and slash dynamic, were you have to be constantly attacking the enemies). So you have to check other options for lute (prioritize the ones that reduce entropy), and also at the end game it's heavily recommended to complete the distance counter for hight level enemies, this lets you counter even boss heavy attacks or projectiles.-Transformations, (this section has slight spoilers and my main problem with the game)I enjoyed playing this game overall, and the themes presented during the history were great to follow up. Sometimes Briar was too edgy and lute was overreacting, but it's ok for me. The gameplay is enjoyable but a bit frustrating at times (the telemetry of the enemy attack after being frozen by counter is hard to read), the main boss fights are huge and I see the dedication and love to make this game possible. I hope for the best if a second chapter can be reached at some point.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Chimera May CryIn a dark, Gothic fantasy universe, humanity struggles against the creatures of Chaos, commonly referred to as “Wraiths”. These blue energy beings cross over across the Veil, and their mere touch is enough to turn hapless humans into mindless, bloodthirsty Corrupted. Sometimes a Corrupted and a Wraith join together and become a red coloured Possessed. In order to fight these spawns of Chaos the adepts of the Triarchy- the 3 gods that separated Creation from Chaos and created humanity-have commissioned the Order of the Ashen Blade to create Chimeras- a symbiotic union of a human Knight and a ghostly Shade. The Knights can heal deadly wounds with ease, double-jump and dash, and hit evil things with sharp and pointy bits of metal. The Shades can manipulate Chaos to create colour-coded Fields that make both Wraiths and Possessed vulnerable to the Knights' weapons. You start the game playing as a novice Chimera made up of knight Briar and the shade of her sister Lute. A massive Rent into Chaos opened up over the holy city of the Lightbringer (one of the 3 gods of humanity). Along with several other Chimeras, Briar and Lute must investigate the source of the Rent and find a way to close it, killing many different enemy types in the process. The game is a typical character-action game, complete with scores for each encounter and varying fixed camera perspectives. Basically think Devil May Cry 3, but more anime. Briar starts with 2 weapons- a sword and a warhammer, and can unlock 5 additional weapon types as the game goes on- a gauntlet, a bow, a whipsword , dual daggers and powered gun/gauntlet hybrids. Each weapon has a moveset that needs to be bought, but they have identical button inputs. Different weapons are more effective against different enemies (gauntlets smash armor, whip and daggers do better airborne damage to bring down fliers, etc). And in addition, Wraiths and Possessed can only be harmed when the appropriate Field is active- and Lute can only keep a field going for so long (until you get upgrades for it). Altogether, this creates a neat twist on the traditional character action combat system.  The game's version of Devil Trigger gives Lute a  sped-up and increased damage form- but if you trigger this when you're close to death, you Frenzy- your damage increases, but unless you successfully perform QTEs, Briar goes Transcended and then it's Game Over. Combine this with some neat boss encounters, bonus challenge rooms, a ranking system and a VERY anime and unnecessary convoluted story, filled of twists and betrayals (that show up seemingly out of nowhere) and you end up with a surprisingly compelling experience. I did not experience any bugs or crashes. The game has platforming and puzzles (typically you need to destroy colour-coded crystals to clear obstructions, or find levers to open paths, nothing complex), and the game takes place largely in a very similar environment- the various districts of the destroyed city are largely samey-looking, so there's little real environmental variety. Some platforming depends on Lute's fields making them visible, which is a timed thing, so those can get annoying. Overall, though, the run on Normal difficulty took me about 25 hours, trying to explore every corner of the level- and I still didn't find about half-dozen of the Challenge Rooms, so there's plenty of content. Anyone who is looking for a good Devil May Cry clone and likes dark Gothic settings owes it to themselves to check this game out

_childDocuments_.review: "Another Transcended walks the land" is the message that pops up when you fail to revert Briar from berserk state.Solstice excels in character design and world building, it would have been great to explore world prior to **events** of game, but alas, ravaged version it is then, there are lot of areas that felt that they had potential like audio/boss tracks and a ton of controversial game mechanics, first of all, the weapon combos for default great sword are lacking (only 2 combos for what it briar's lore weapon). the weapons each have its own strength and weakness and the game  you hard if you use wrong weapon in wrong place. and the fields are overused to extent of me raging cause LUTE CANT HOLD THEM FOR 5 SECS WITHOUT UTTERING "I CANT HOLD THEM FOR LONG", maybe its just me not finding upgrades but, the color coded enemies makes the game feel more like a puzzle, this in turn makes player focus on solving the puzzle rather than focusing on "style". A huge amount of mechanics crammed into a character with lot of "ifs" attached to those mechanics. The boss battles, most of them are meh, but the ones that stood out are the archer one(would have been better if not for handholding mechanics), nemisis (visuals were gorgeous, the fight itself is meh tho), and final boss (harbringer?, mainly cause, the backdrop was amazing and fight was also pretty good relatively, i see devs took a huge inspiration from DMC 4's savior fight)I liked the whole "claymore/berserk" vibe and the cutscene that plays out when you activate berserk is just **chef's kiss**.all in allPlot -- 6/10Gameplay -- 5/10 (are fun, but get tedious fast)Immersion  -- 6/10 (lets see how immersive it gets when you get triple combo'd by enemies from across the arena)OST -- 6/10 stands out at times, could have been betterBugs  -- 8/10 -- it crashed on me few times at a specific spot, had to search for fix online.Grind -- 9/10 -- game is quite generous with its currency Character designs(special) -- 8/10 -- especially transcended designs.Final verdict: 6.8/10 (worth playing if you are bored or need a case study for your game design class)

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a DMC/Bayonetta-like action game (Hack and slash? Character action?), and I recommend it. Despite its flaws, the core gameplay is great. Weapons/enemies synergies work well: you need to always choose the right tool for the job when you're approached by different types of monsters. This, together with the blue/red aura weaknesses/hazards, makes the combat always fun and engaging. The problem is on the camera, in certain battles, it's a pain in the ass. _childDocuments_.review: Played only a few chapters, but I can feel the charm of the game. As many other reviews mentioned similarity to anime/manga Claymore then the collection of orb (red/blue) for skill/item purchases akin to DMC. But the camera are fixed at 2.5D for platforming, while only during other times outside combat the camera follows your character when you move.  Full camera controls for combat in non tight space fights and that's the weakest part of the game. Same issues with the latest Valkyrie game, due to the free camera control fights with mixed range enemies from close, mid, long range and flying enemies can be a chore. Both thumbs are used on movement and camera/enemy lock while your primary attacks are X & Y with B to deflect. Without back paddle buttons controllers, early gamers not used to it would probably  be"All Thumbs". The background settings is nice too, just a bit confusing within buildings where every other background platform seemingly to be climbable but not. Still, I can't fault that since DMC seems doing that well enough. Now the good part is it's really enjoyable to play and the voice actors are really good. Graphics are quite good though I feel the art would be better off with anime like  cel shades. Overall if one is prepared to get used to the "All Thumbs" controls, it will be way better then most games in the same genre. Looking forward to what this dev can come up with next with more simplified control mechanics. 7.5 / 10.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great for fans of the Berserk and Claymore mangas, It's gameplay is a fun hack and slash similar to Devil May Cry with a world, characters and story inspired by the two previously mentioned mangas. The game has many interesting mechanics that are present in both puzzles and combat. The combat itself revolves mostly around chaining combos without getting to build up a meter that allows you to unleash powerful attacks, and when filled allows you to enter a berserker like state where you are able to attack rapidly with much more powerful blows, though this state is locked at the beginning and will be available by progressing through the game. In combat your main defense is your shade Lute, in response to enemy attacks you can time a button press to counter, doing so also builds up Lutes meter which if filled will stun her making her unable to perform actions. The game contains many different types of enemies all of which fall under one of three types, Corrupted, Spirit and Possessed. Corrupted are standard enemies which will take damage without a barrier activated, spirits can only be harmed while you have your evocation field activated. Possessed are similar where you will need to have your banishment field up to harm them, both these fields build up Lute's meter over time. Overall I do recommend this game even to those who are not fans of Berserk and Claymore, as long as you enjoy hack and slash games that is, personally I would give this game a 8/10 though I might be a bit biased as I am a huge fan of Berserk and Claymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Soulstice is a capable atmospheric dark fantasy hack'n'slasher.  The dark, grim, and gory environment with well-executed if chaotic combat fill a void for me that's been left empty since Reaper of Souls, maybe even since the gory spectacle that was Travincal back in the day.  The static camera takes some getting used to but ultimately is easy to work with and does a fantastic job of showcasing the world's art.  Combat is fast and unforgiving but nuanced; i-framing through attacks and popping counters while tossing grotesque monsters around is very satisfying.  Bosses are challenging, relentless, and cinematic encounters.  The story is mainly delivered passively during gameplay and is engaging with an acceptable voice over.  I have very few complaints about this game and those few issues are minor compared to how many things the game gets right.  I wholeheartedly recommend it (if you're a fan of grotesque monsters, gory combat and piles of corpses littering the world that is).

_childDocuments_.review: A game which you can feel the developers poured their love into. For fans of Devil May Cry, Berserk and Claymore. But that doesn't matter, because it does exactly what it needs to do and maybe even more. The combat is fast and satisfying. The story is surprisingly deeper than some would expect. Likeable characters. The only flaws I could think of are: -the overall campaign could be a tad shorter. There's a lot of padding. -combat, even if satisfying, can feel a bit clunky, sometimes. Need to get used to the timing of attacks in order to properly cancel into other action. -the world, even if beautiful, gets a bit repetitive after a while. Other than that, it's definitely worth it for anyone who enjoys the very unused genre of character action games. Also, finally amazing to see such a good Italian game on the market. I hope they'll get enough recognition to work on more projects.

Not sure what else to add... Oh yeah the camera and the targeting may or may not be annoying during combat fyi. Some boss fights later on started to be better over others and changes things up a bit. 9/10I played this game at 1440p on an Rtx 2070 Super and it ran fine at 60 to 140+ fps with no issues with Dlss on the quality setting. _childDocuments_.review: 6/10While I do like the game and finished it , there are some serious problems that could hinder you in your enjoyment of the game.1.) Combat: The combat does make fun but only when you master it. Isnt that the case in almost all action games ? Yes but not to this extent like in this game.There's this mechanic where you can execute certain synergy attacks if you dont get hit and uphold a combo for a certain time. With it the combat feels fluid and you can get cool executions but without it you have limited options , especially at the beginning of the game. And that leads to the second problem , there are far too few combo variations in my opinion.You have 6 weapons but with each you get the same combo each time and need alot of resourcers to buy them. Even worse is that you have to upgrade each weapon up to 3 times for just a damage bonus that doesnt give you any extra combos ,purchasing these over the combos just doesnt feel rewarding at all.2. Story and Cutscenes) I like the concept of the main characters very much , especially how it affects the gameplay aswell. Thats the best thing about this game. The effect the story has on the gameplay. I just love it. The presentation of the story is rather bland though. The animations inside the cutscenes feel mechanical and the voices dont let you feel the gravity of the situation. It sounds like they recorded all the voices at the same day with the same emotion. _childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty ok 3rd person action game in the vein of DMC, not a whole lot of games like that on Steam, and although it has some issues i think its good enough to warrant a buy.Combat:This is the main issue of the game, see you get quite a few different weapons throughout your play through, and these weapons are your basic tools for the enemies you face: whip deals more damage to basic enemies, hammer is good against shields and fist is good against armor etc etc. The problem is you will face enemies that you are missing the weapons for early on, dont fret too much because the difficulty doesnt ramp up until about half way into the game, but on the higher difficulties you might struggle on your first time.Here is my suggestion though, if you start on the lowest difficulty things will go much smoother. I had never played any game like this before and it helped me immensely. This also helps with the other problem it has, that being the blue and red colored enemies. It can get pretty hectic and only being able to hurt some of the enemies that are surrounding you is a big pain, but on the lower difficulty they will have less health and deal less damage so that helps (also you can increase the difficulty mid play through when you have all the tools and some upgrades).GraphicsPretty good. Unreal engine is put to good use in the art style they chose and the main characters in particular are well done. There are a lot of samey hallways and rooms but the vistas of the city are great. I did enjoy the way they went with the enemy design, a lot of crystaline monsters that look very cool mixed in with a lot of fleshy monstrosities, very cool designs. There are some lip sync issues though on one character when he has his close ups but that was the only issue i noticed. Overall nothing to complain about with some standout boss fights but a lot of mediocre areas. MusicLove the orchestrel stuff and the boss music is sometimes rock mixed in with some synth and electronic. Its somewhat different for a fantasy type game but i really liked it and it definitely gives the game its own style. LengthA bit too long overall in my opinion, there are quite a few sections that i think stay past their welcome, the sewers comes to mind, but the end of the game certainly feels like it accelerates quite a bit which is nice, but would have been nicer had the pacing been a bit faster for the beginning and middle chapters. Theres also a few puzzles that were a bit annoying but only a handful of them that i actually remember so not too bad. Final ThoughtsI think they designed this game to be played through multiple times on different difficulties. Unfortunately this is not obvious to a new player but putting down the difficulty really helped me get through it and overall i enjoyed the story and characters. Combat is fun too once you get all the weapons and some upgrades. It can be hectic but also a good time. To me this was 40 dollars well spent, in this age of studios buying (and closing down) smaller studios i enjoy when a AA game actually turned out pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: DMC in a fantasy setting with a touch of dark souls for flavour, but definitely a little harder. 	Briar and Lute’s journey through a city damned by chaos is a good one. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR - Soulstice is a great game with a few flaws, which did not prevent me from having overall, an enjoyable experience. Soulstice is a spectacle fighter in the veins of DMC/Bayonetta. While its combat doesn't quite reach the complexity of aforementioned titles, it does get quite busy when stuff opens up. There's quite a few weapons that get unlocked for you, which seem to be a bit of a focus in combat. All weapons have strengths and weaknesses to certain types of enemies, so you gotta switch them around often. Also, while weapons have similar inputs for combos, you can switch them on the fly in each step of the combo and continue with the move that should be at that combo step of the weapon you switched to. Combined with launchers, air finishers and a few unique moves on some weapons, this does offer some matter of complexity if you really wanna get into it. As the game’s unique twist, you play alongside a "helper" which provides passive and active help. With timed button presses you can slow down or repel enemy attacks. You do need to get used to this, since slowing down a telegraphed attack doesn't negate it completely, but makes it attack later, often more unexpectedly than if you tried to dodge it normally. It does offer a small bit of freshness to combat, as you can predict where the attack is gonna land and reposition yourself to continue attacking. Passively, the helper will attack enemies on its own and occasionally counter enemy attacks that you missed, this one sometimes does more bad than good though and I wish it could be turned off. There would be instances where I would want to just dodge a specific enemy attack, but it would get randomly slowed down, throwing me off a bit. You also have two types of fields that you can temporarily activate and make specific enemies vulnerable to your attacks. Combined with a skill tree that has various passive perks and abilities that can slightly modify most of these mechanics, you do get a pretty decent combat system that gives enough stuff to keep track of for you to stay engaged.There are moments where camera puts a damper on things, it's actually somewhat weird, since in the beginning of the game, in most of the combat encounters you are given free control of it, while in the latter parts of the game, arenas where you fight have a locked or semi-locked view, which where it really can get annoying. Especially considering that if you use lock-on in those areas, sometimes it does move the camera at more angles (occasionally at pretty weird ones though) than without it, which asks, why not just give you free control of it in the first place. Also, if you have teleporting enemies in your game, when they teleport, it would be better to automatically disengage lock-on rather than suddenly flip your whole view around. I recommend not shying away from using supportive items if you happen to get yourself in a sticky situation due to the camera, it's not a solution per se, but it can help alleviate some frustrations.Graphics / design wise I'd say is where the game shines the most. The game really just looks gorgeous. Design-wise, obviously, a lot of inspiration was drawn from Berserk and Claymore, which I'm quite a fan of. So I really enjoyed it in the form of it being a way to get more content in the style of those works. The environments are pretty detailed and portray a dark, morbid atmosphere really well. Unfortunately, there is not much variety in locations, as you are mostly confined to a specific area. It does make sense story wise and on the upside it does make for an immersive experience of you traveling through a huge city one step at a time. For example, there's a great bridge connected to a city which is considered an impressive marvel in the lore and it takes a while for you to travel through it, you have to go through a prison and a guard post located in its undersides, which gives you a sense of how big that thing actually is. While some more variety could definitely be implemented, I'd say developers did a good job with constraints they probably were working with. Overall, the game is done very cleanly and neatly, performance seems fair and I haven't encountered any bugs in my playthrough.Story starts slow, but I'd say, if you give it a chance, you will find that it escalates pretty well and in the latter parts of it, it kept me pretty engaged. Even though there's only a few characters in the game, they use them well and I really liked getting to know more about them throughout the game. There doesn’t seem to be too many music tracks, but they are good, maybe there’s nothing that particularly stands out, but they serve their purpose well. More ambient tracks fit well with the atmosphere and the main combat track has a nice beat to it. In the end, despite its strong stylistic inspirations, the game began to feel like its own thing and I really got sucked into its world. If there’s a chance a sequel might happen I will be all up for it.

_childDocuments_.review: For one, I was really excited and looking forward to this game ever since I saw the previews. I am a lover of action games, specifically action RPGs, but I also enjoy character action to an extent as long as I like the characters and design, and certainly do with Soulstice. I have also played plenty of DMC, Bayonetta, etc., nothing too surprising.The atmosphere, art, and presentation really unite and hold the entire package together by themselves. Character and enemy designs are all fantastic, and the settings are moody and beautiful. Even all of the bold close ups of the characters in cutscenes failed to betray much of any blemishes and that honestly impressed me, full stop. Indie, AA, AAA, whatever, doesn't matter, I was simply impressed. Overall, a visually stunning piece of art, and major props to the devs for sticking to their guns and going all in on some of their character designs and moments. You know what I'm talking about, and it is a rarity. Thank you.Unfortunately, and with a heavy heart, things fall apart for me in the , and I am writing this days after finishing and giving myself time to mull it over rather than go in with raw emotions. I'll start off by mentioning that I played through on Initiate difficulty, which is the middle of the 3 initially available and the recommended tier for experienced players of the genre looking for some challenge; That's usually how I approach any new game, as I just want to experience the baseline recommended gameplay and enjoy the overall experience first before I go nuts with achievements and mastering things, even if it's too easy. Spoiler alert, it was definitely not.To preface the following, I have not read very much in terms of other reviews and thoughts yet, so these critiques are all from my personal experience in a vacuum after completing the story on Initiate difficulty.Maybe this is just a really unpopular opinion and that's fine, but I strongly feel that , and I mean this in the most respectful and hopeful way possible for the devs if they are reading this; There's already a lot going on by the time you get to the middle of the story, and that's not even when you've unlocked all the weapons or seen all the environmental mechanics and enemies.I actually LOVE action games with lots of depth and crazyness. I mean, I was addicted to fist weapons in Nioh 2, and the skill ceiling doesn't get much more blissfully insane than that in an ARPG; That's a title with a fair number of mechanics too. I have been playing these sort of games for a very long time, but I'm not exactly fond of fumbling with all of the pretty much mandatory combat systems stacked on top of each other in this game. More to the point, I didn't particularly find the "challenge" worthy of the difficulty or the enjoyment I got.The stark difference between Soulstice and something like Nioh is that you don't  to interact with many of the numerous systems in Nioh as they are extra and optional. I'm not knocking Soulstice for having necessary systems by any stretch, I'm just saying that there are sometimes too many other things going on around them that muddy what I feel could be a more crisp experience while still remaining challenging.To be clear, I love all the weapons, they are all very fun and very cool looking. I love the entropy system concept with the dual fields that you manage, and it's obviously integral to the everything. I love the unity system and synergy attacks, they look straight up DOPE. The parry/counter system is cool, sometimes a bit cumbersome and other times really flashy and satisfying. The controls feel good and responsive (except the double-tap analog stick dash attack that can be very difficult to execute at times, when there is a perfectly good double-button-press combination on a few weapons). And here's the thing, I loved the boss fights. I really did. They were big and fun, and the combat felt great in those situations.Literally every other combat situation, which is the vast majority of the game, is where my issue lies, because ALL of these systems are coming together to bombard you with the responsibilities of frequently swapping between 6 different secondary weapons with their own strengths and weaknesses (3 of them require double-tapping the d-pad), maintaining two resource-sensitive entropic fields in order to even interact with certain enemies, enemies that require swapping from one field to the other just to chase around and finish them off, environmental hazards that can really mess you up depending on which field you have up (or none), constantly worrying about parrying/countering/slowing tons of attacks coming at you from all directions, dodging uninterruptible and slowed attacks, trying to build Unity for your best attacks but having it get severely depleted when taking any damage, and dealing with a camera that requires locking on to see health bars but greatly limits your field of view and requires constant toggling or awkward swapping between tons of available targets.I think the thing that really throws the biggest wrench into this pile of systems is the variety of enemies that can be thrown at you at once. Some of those combinations are really nasty and require all of these responsibilities to be managed to the max and in quick succession or you'll be in trouble. This is on "normal" difficulty as well. Even if "easy" is much less punishing, there is still a lot to manage and that is a fundamental issue in my eyes. I can  of see an argument towards not needing to use every single weapon, which sometimes is a fair case to make, but some of them are just WAY better at dealing with specific situations.Again, it's not about being too simple or taking away the fun and reward of combat depth, it's about knowing where to draw the line. I don't have any specific suggestions at the moment for the current build, but I hope this will at least be taken into consideration.I want to end on a positive note and say that I really, really like this game, and I will definitely be looking out for post-launch content like DLC, or even a sequel would be amazing. Admittedly, even if the combat hasn't changed much down the line, I will still probably be checking out any future releases, which is basically saying Soulstice has earned a fan in me just based on how well presented it is. , I really can't stress enough that I feel there is some work to be done about the things I mentioned, and I would be very ecstatic to see that happen in the future.
