name: V Rising
detailed_description: Experience a Vampire Survival Action RPG adventure like no other. Awaken as a weakened Vampire after centuries of slumber. Hunt for blood to regain your strength while hiding from the scorching sun to survive. Rebuild your castle and convert humans into your loyal servants in a quest to raise your Vampire empire. Make allies or enemies online or play solo locally, fend off holy soldiers, and wage war in a world of conflict. Seize your destiny! Defy Dracula! Rule the night! Now with native gamepad support and a reimagined interface, prepare for action-packed, hands-on gameplay! A Gothic Open-World Explore a vast world teeming with mythical horrors and danger. Travel through lush forests, open countryside, and dark caverns to discover valuable resources, meeting friends and foes alike along the way. Traverse the world with vampire comrades or hunt solo as you pillage villages, raid bandits, and delve into the domains of supernatural beasts. Fear the light - Rule the night Stick to the shadows during the daytime, or the burning sunlight will turn you to ashes. Roam the night and prey on your victims in the darkness. As a vampire, you must quench your thirst for blood while planning your strategies around the rising and setting sun. Raise your Castle Gather resources and discover ancient techniques to uncover forgotten knowledge. Use your newly acquired insight to build a castle to store your loot and grow your army of darkness. Personalize your domain, exhibit your vampiric style, and make sure to craft coffins for servants and friends. Strengthen your castle to protect your treasure hoard from vampire rivals. Compete or Cooperate Travel alone or explore the world with friends. Fighting side by side with other Vampires will give you an advantage in the fight to conquer the greatest threats of Vardoran. Raid other players’ castles, play the diplomat in the game of blood, power, and betrayal, or craft an indomitable retinue of insidious allies. Compete or cooperate - the choice is yours. Master your Vampire Learn and master an arsenal of deadly weapons and unholy abilities. In V Rising, you aim skillshots and dodge projectiles using​ precise​​ ​WASD controls ​and cursor-based​ ​aiming - no click to move. Tailor your vampire to fit your play style by combining weapons with a variety of spells earned through vanquishing powerful foes. Find and master your personal, perfect blend of sword and sorcery to become the ultimate nocturnal predator!

_childDocuments_.review: No sugar coating here - this is hands down one of the best games on Steam. It conquers it's own genre in all categories: Mechanics, Story and Graphics. From start to finish, there have been zero bugs. The devs are clearly very professional and care greatly about their work (Creating awesome stuff and connecting with fun players). The community is fair and fun as well. However, don't expect to poke and not be poked. Ha - It's worth a start over n over again. Play for the achievements - not the stale persistence of, "power" that so many other games offer. If you're okay with always staying fresh, this is the game for you and the community will welcome you, warmly.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, one of the best survival open world games that I have played! Acceptable grind. Ofcourse more fun if you have friends. But I don't have friends. It has feeling of MMO-RPG as well (IT IS NOT A MMORPG!). and it is quick hack and slash with spells which makes it an interesting game-play and you really enjoy PvE elements so for those who are not into PvP, the PvE has enough content to keep you going!Also it makes you feel empathetic toward vampires so next time one of them comes to you in real life, you will let them suck it (your blood). + makes you officially hate and avoid sun, more than you already do as an average gamer! Graphics are very nice considering it's a top-down game. The fact that you are a vampire, makes the day-night cycle special to you and it is quite balanced with addition of blood moon. The PvE elements have their own beef with eachother, so you can always be creative and use the environment to your cause. The character creation is decent enough but don't expect Conan Exile level to set the size of your wee-wee and boo-boo.As I said the grind is decent and leveling system is fair. So by the end of the day you will not be smelling sweat and piss all over the room.I would rate it 8/10. -2 deducted because I don't have friends and I want to take it on developers. Please fix!UPDATE on 01-Jun-2024: +2 added back because you can play Single-player if you are a poor miserable ♥♥♥♥ who doesn't have friends, just modify settings to make it suitable to your play style so this game is really cry-proof and sweat-proof if you want to!So 10/10! Definitely give this game a try! Wonderful castle building with lots of options to decorate and the PvE quests are just very must rewarding and keep you going as this is how you gain new blueprints! By sucking it (blood)!

_childDocuments_.review: Loving V-Rising Pros:  Combat feels good, boss fights are very well done,  a ton of options to run on your serve ie. higher material drops, make bosses harder or easier  (it's like having built in mods), for this game being early access it's in a really good state, seems to be a large game (map), the whole world is hostile and makes the world feel alive, love the vampire take (having to look at the enemies blood value% to see if they are worth draining) very cool mechanic  Cons: lack of controller support, not a fan of the fact they have dlc as an extra charge already and the game isn't even fully released (a game should be completed before dlc is started)This developer has done a great job and deserve the money I paid.Thanks for a very interesting and fun game

_childDocuments_.review: I did enjoy this game though some problems.1) This is very much designed as a Server game. 2)The combat is all ranged. Bosses hit super hard and your only dodge is locked to a long cool-down. With no real dodge mechanic, You take crazy damage when in close combat.3) On that, Your healing is heavily restricted in combat. Maybe only getting 15-20% that you can heal. Fine for PVP but in PVE it makes the final 3 bosses No fun at all. 4) Progression is on unlocking recipes dropped by bosses only.5) Leveling up is based on Equipment score. (Icluding Health Pool)6) Equipment to increase this score is locked behind a random recipe unlock system. You may unlock 10 or more before getting equipment you need to progress. Overall it is not a bad game. The combat needs a rework like a proper dodge and the ability to heal more. The recipe system should switch to a point based (Knowledge points). Grinding the random system to only get Decos for 3-4 hours can be a massive pain.

_childDocuments_.review: Grind for repairs: the gameGrind is the only goal in this gameThe combat is fun and satisfying when the game isn't chugging at 10 fps or registering hits you dodged on your end, but the game does everything it can to discourage you from partaking in it. The durability system is overtuned to hell and back.You get trapped in a vicious cycle of fishing for the next upgrade to your gear and then the next repair for your gear, but beyond the grind there is not a lot of content. The boss fight mechanics and presentation are pretty mediocre and short lasting. Endgame is a handful of clans raiding each other in an otherwise dead server when the other party is offline.If you're looking to waste away your life doing meaningless, menial tasks with the looming threat of losing it all if you don't keep performing, this is the game for you. If not, turn around and don't look back.

_childDocuments_.review: I've spent 141 hours in "V Rising," achieved all the achievements, and completed the game on Brutal difficulty. This game is a gem that I initially tried during its beta release and have recently revisited, and it continues to impress.The developers have done a fantastic job polishing and adding new features, including an exciting collaboration with Castlevania. The improvements and additional content have made the gameplay even more immersive and enjoyable.: The game perfectly balances the need to manage your vampire needs and the thrill of avoiding the sun.: Building a castle and crafting various items feels rewarding and essential for progression.: The combat system is engaging, with a variety of vampire abilities that keep battles interesting.: Playing on a PvP server is where the game truly shines, offering the full spectrum of what "V Rising" has to offer. The competitive environment enhances the thrill and challenge.: For the full experience, I recommend playing on a PvP server. It’s where you can truly experience all the content and dynamics of the game.: Choose a server that suits your comfort level and time availability. While the default servers are fine, you can opt for ones that cut down on crafting and refining times, saving you a lot of grind (converting a servant for 10 hours can be a bit much at times)."V Rising" is a wonderful game that I highly recommend to anyone who enjoys survival games with a vampire twist. Despite a few minor time-consuming aspects, the overall experience is rich, engaging, and thoroughly enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: While I cannot deny that this game is great - I do feel like it has been polished into something that is worse than what it was before version 1.0. The game progress seems to have been slowed down, the bosses are hard, but mostly because you have to dodge their attacks while you have too high cooldown and too few abilities - so its mostly the only reason they hit you, cause youve been slowed down which is frustrating and doesnt at all feel like youre a powerful vampire anymore.Im at level 57 and have played 23 hours since release and Im finding myself not wanting to play anymore cause the whole game seems like a chore about now.You need 1 special item to be able to get 2 more gear levels by upgrading some of your gear - that item is only available if you defeat a boss, so you go do that - get the item... farm items to get to build it too, then you rinse and repeat 30 times along the duration of the game.Im sorry, but that is just not a fun time for me anymore, it feels like a nerfed version of what was earlier where it felt exciting and you felt powerful... Thats simply not a part of the game anymore unfortunately.Ultimately, the game is great - but it doesnt feel good to play anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start off by saying that I don't like Steam's binary review system. Yes, I recommend this game, but there are a few caveats. For starters, this is a very multiplayer oriented game. It seems like the devs REAAAAAALLLY want you to play with friends. It is possible to play single player, but it's almost impossibly difficult. Enemies swarm, spam, and quickly kill you, especially at a low level. Furthermore, there is no pause button. If you have to do something, you better find a safe area and hang out there for a while. Secondly, the fast travel is heavily restricted, but the map is huge. You are not allowed to fast travel if you have any resources or valuables. That's pretty much anything you loot. I don't know why this system is in place, but I hate it. I do like a lot of things about this game, though. The atmosphere is perfect, and I like the top-down Diablo style of gameplay. I also really love the concept of starting out as a fledgling vampire and rising to the top as an all-powerful dark lord of evil. I only wish it was a little easier to climb that ladder. I also wish there were a few NPCs that helped players along without the need for multiplayer.

_childDocuments_.review: So 31 hours in and I'm enjoying this quite a lot. Here are some of my opinions, take them as you will:It scratches an itch that games like Valheim, Don't Starve, or Terraria do but in a completely different way. Being the bad guy for once is nice but at the same time it follows the usual formula for all survival/craft games. The speed of progression is not entirely dependant on your server settings, but by default, it could use some slight tweaks and not much else. Recipes for new gear are discovered from random drops or getting enough of a specific resource to roll the dice on a new recipe. Gathering resources is by far the easiest part of this game.Getting stuck trying to grind out resources for a random chance at something that would help you progress is a little frustrating. More gear options would be nice to help alleviate this.The building requires some pre-planning and while I haven't played multiplayer yet, I can see how it might be a little frustrating with it's predefined build areas. That said, it has a real Dungeon Keeper vibe and I am very nostalgic over that game.The combat is decent. As there is no worrying about trying to aim at something slightly higher than you with melee weapons, it is already a step up from Valheim. It feels like it's missing something though as the DotA style abilities don't appeal. It works, but it's not satisfying to me.It is a well polished game with so few bugs I couldn't even tell if there was something off. Hell, for a comparison, it's more bug free than a Bethesda or Ubisoft AAA game.TLDR: It's good. Could be better, but it's got solid foundations and consistent with it's gameplay. Worth the time and money in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid gamer with limited free time, V Rising has become my ultimate go-to for a deeply engaging and exhilarating experience. This game brilliantly combines the thrill of survival, the strategy of base-building, and the action-packed combat of an RPG.Awakening as a vampire, you'll relish hunting for blood, constructing an imposing castle, and mastering a wide arsenal of weapons and unholy abilities. The gothic open-world teems with mythical horrors and treasures, making exploration rewarding and immersive.The combat system is exceptional, providing a satisfying mix of strategy and skill. Whether solo or in co-op, every boss fight is a uniquely challenging experience. The day-night cycle adds an intense layer of strategy, forcing you to navigate threats and plan your conquests.V Rising offers a perfect blend of depth and accessibility, making it a standout in the genre. If you have a few hours a day to immerse yourself in a richly detailed vampire saga, this game is absolutely worth your time. Highly recommended for those seeking a mature, captivating escape.

_childDocuments_.review: I have gotten to about mid-game by now and honestly this is well worth a $20.00 price tag. Even with it being an early access title. The game is very fleshed out and rather fun. Mostly revolving around resource management and killing bosses to get their powers/loot/blueprints. It feels very akin to games like Valheim. Albeit the gameplay itself very much varies from that title.There is something for pretty much everyone here. Base building, resource gathering, fishing, cold-blooded murder, and playing with your friends to terrorize the night. Now this game is far from perfect mind you. There are several bugs that I have discovered and several quality of life areas that need improvement. Not to mention at times it feels a little too grindy, though having friends helps with that immensely.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR- V Rising is a great game with an amazing atmosphere and concept that pulls you right into the world. It's well worth the price point and has quite a number of hours of game play. While there are some flaws, which is expected with early access, those flaws don't overshadow an all around positive gaming experience.  I recommend giving it a try.I don't usually write reviews but I enjoyed this game so much I wanted to give it the credit it deserves. Keep in mind I haven't tried the PVP mode yet so this is mostly a PVE related review after nearly 100 hours of game play. I have compiled some pros and cons listed below if you're still on the fence to try it out.Pros:-The atmosphere is amazing and I loved the world I was thrown into. I liked the backstory and lore of how your character ends up in the position it does and it lends itself well to the 'start from nothing' trope you see in most survival games.-The combat can be challenging at first especially if you're new to the genre. Once you get accustomed to it however it's rather fun. I enjoy defeating bosses and learning new skills, as well as exploring various zones with different debuffs you have to contend with as a vampire. -Servants are a great game play mechanic and I've enjoyed hunting down the best NPCs to send out on missions. The missions themselves do have lengthy timers though but I understand why considering how much valuable stuff they can bring back.-The voice acting is nice and it makes the world feel alive. I admit I was surprised when I first encountered a villager who was begging for their life and it made me reconsider harming them. It was both strange and cool at the same time, so good job there. The boss voices are also really engaging and that added a nice touch to their fights.-The sunlight mechanic is a bit hit or miss with me but I do think it's necessary for the flow of the game. It makes complete sense from a lore perspective and it's a unique system I've not seen before so overall I enjoy it.-The character creator is nice with a fair amount of options. The male vampire design is a bit off putting and I assume it stems from very old vampire appearances which I get. Once you get gear the over-sized shoulders and necks become less prominent at least, so that's a plus.-I enjoyed the castle building element here. I've made several castles with different themes and I am really hoping they expand on it in the future.Cons:-Fishing. Fishing just isn't very intuitive here. I'm sure it's by design to gate your progression but it's still a frustrating element. To me fishing is meant to be one of the more relaxing elements of any game. Yet chasing down fishing spots that disappear after one use and half the time getting items over fish becomes frustrating. If the loot table is going to be so broad then please let us stay in one spot for a while rather than running all over the place looking for glittering water pools.-I mentioned enjoying castle building and I do. However, I do hope Stunlock adds more options to it later on. In PVP bases are built more for defense than aesthetics, but in PVE I'd enjoy making mega castles. Right now you can't make multiple floors unless you find a multi-tiered plot of land and even then it's disjointed. The furnishing items are also a bit limited and there are no beds. Vampires sleep in coffins but I'd like to make pseudo guest rooms just for theme purposes. Outdoor items are especially limited in number. I can only imagine the amazing builds people could do with more options.-The end game feels artificially gated and it becomes a slog. During any other tier of gear you could reliably gather most things. The gold necklaces, however, are much harder to farm and considering how many you need for certain things it definitely doesn't feel as good as earlier tiers. -Sometimes the repetitive sound bytes your character makes can get a little grating, especially while gathering. I've gotten used to it but I do hope they add a bit more variety later on, or maybe reduce the amount of 'uah uah uahs' they do. -No mod support as of yet but I do hope it is in the works or at the very least being considered. Once I reached the end game I felt sad I had no where else to go as I wanted to stay in the world. Mod support may help extend the PVE side of things a bit more.I understand this is an early access game and it is subject to change with improvements later on so much of this review may not be accurate in a few months time. As of right now though I love the game and I am eager to see what improvements or additions they make in the future. What downsides there may be are small compared to the many great things that suck you in and keep you wanting more. Thank you for making a great Vampire themed game!

_childDocuments_.review: In it's current state at the time I am posting this review, I enjoy the game but it is hard to do so. You will only enjoy this game if you already really enjoy the genre. It will not persuade you to play it easily, and I feel like the reasons below are part of the reason why.There is also no way to delete a server that you created. Sometimes the server fails to initialize and the game sends you back to the create server menu. If you try to initialize it again, you will have TWO servers with the same name in your continue menu with no way to delete the extra one. It would also be nice if there was a way to tell them apart other than time, like a look into what your character is on the server, or some kind of distinguishing factor. It would also be nice to be able to edit server settings. At this point in time, if you messed up on one setting you have to make an entirely new server and have this unusable server in your list forever because you can't delete it.Updating your saved ruleset always fails. Once you create a ruleset it cannot be updated, only deleted and made again. It does say save in the bottom corner, but this does nothing to the ruleset you are editing. If you load the ruleset back you will see no changes.If these bugs are fixed then I will update the review.For reasons why individuals won't like it, it is a GRIND, if you do not tweak the settings to suit how you want to play. This is not obvious to the new player to the genre. I personally love how much you can customize the servers. I made a server that makes all of the enemies incredibly hard and made the grind almost non-existent. If a new player to this genre was given these settings then they would really enjoy it I think. So maybe a tutorial on encouraging different play styles would get new players hooked. This game shines on PvP, but the average player's first experience would be trying to figure it out alone or with friends, and be met with a huge grind and quit playing. Only speaking from experience with my friends. I love this game, they do not as much. So I found myself tweaking the server a lot to get them into it, but this requires a knowledge that you do not start with. If more beginner friendly stuff is added, this will definitely turn into a positive review.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the concept of the game, and initially enjoyed the vast, open world and extensive crafting systems.  There are a lot of things to like about V-Rising.That said, good lord these camera and character controls are just unforgivable.  I have never experienced such janky, unpredictable strike patterns.  Hours into the game, I still had trouble attacking things right in front of me.  Given that your very limited abilities are all on medium to long cooldowns, this made combat utterly unbearable.  The camera is not smart at all, and is basically impossible to move without causing your attack/harvest direction to veer wildly off-course; yet another aspect making fights frustrating and random.  I cannot fathom why this game does not have a lock-on feature; I have literally never played a game that more desperately needs one.I beat a couple bosses, but didn't feel like I really did anything to earn it.  I just tried a few times and kept trying to click and attack the target, until I got a fight where less than half my attacks decided to swing at the  air nowhere near where my cursor or the enemy is.  It was not much less than half.  Everything good about the game is overshadowed by the awful controls.  As a crafting/mining/gathering simulator, it's ok.  The whole being a vampire part (ie the reason I got this game) is insufferable.   Vampires are supposed to be graceful and deadly.  This game makes you feel more like you are fighting blindfolded, underwater, and drunk.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great potential but in my opinion it has 3 major problems (two are interrelated) that mean I cant thumb it up. The problems for me are 1) the grind 2) linear progression 3) frustrating boss fights I really like the concept of combining isometric POV with survival and vampire lore. Progression is interesting in that you cant really grind to progress in this game and progress is tied to your gear rather than your character. However this is also where the issues start for me... You MUST take on bosses to progress as killing them unlocks new abilities and blueprints that essential things are locked behind. The problem is that some boss fights are insanely hard even when well over their level and often you need to kill a lot of enemies around the boss to even get into a fight with them. You also need to avoid sunlight since you are a vampire, so taking on bosses will need to be done at night. However because you need to clear enemies to get to the boss you often need to get started during the day, so you are dodging sunlight while grinding through dull enemies to get to a frustrating boss fight you may well lose many times over. Sure you could say 'git gud' but it appears others suffered this same frustration. Even worse, bosses will ENTIRELY REGENERATE their health in seconds mid battle, should you step back a few feet and they get just out of your reach. So you lose all your progress in seconds and this feels very frustrating and is unforgivable in my opinion. When you go through this many times over it starts to become a chore as you may need to grind for say explosive ingredients to gain access to the boss, kill many surrounding enemies and time this all around daylight only to die very fast and have to repeat it again and again... sighThere is no other way to progress so if you are stuck on a boss that gate keeps items you need to learn... you have zero alternate progression options. There is no way to grind your way through, you take on frustrating bosses who completely heal themselves in seconds, or you don't progress. Anyway... I love the graphics and sounds on this game, though the performance can get a bit dicey around your base etc but this isn't unusual for survival type games. It pains me to thumb this game down as it is a great concept and is probably the most complete early access game I have played so far. I got 45 hours gaming so far which is less than a dollar an hour for entertainment - a metric I base value on with games. However I am close to just giving up and stopping the game as the grind and frustrating bosses start to feel un-fun when I just want to explore and build an awesome base but I am struggling to go through another frustrating chore of an infuriatingly hard boss fight. This also limits any replay value for me as I know that next time I play it there will still only be tedious boss fights to progress through the game and why would I want to repeat these frustrating encounters again in the future?So much potential but so frustrating and limited progression wise :(

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:- Combat is fun, interesting, and decently challenging. Enemies feel like they use actual tactics instead of just walking at you at attacking. Bosses can be pretty tough but can be overcome with practice and build choice.- The aesthetic is superb. I absolutely love the art style. It perfectly captures exactly what I want to see in a Vampire RPG. It's appropriately dark, but does so in a way that doesn't sacrifice visual clarity.- The building mechanics are fresh and interesting. I really like the concept of certain buildings receiving bonuses for being in a separate, designated room for their type. It gives you a mechanical reason not only to expand your castle, but also to organize it in a way that makes sense from a sort-of-roleplay point, too. You can still smash everything into one big room if you *really* want to, but you'll miss out on bonuses that make it more efficient to make separate rooms and organize. I love that it gives incentive on building something that feels more like a grand castle and not, like, a META base build in Rust. - Two "official" PvP modes as well as a PvE mode let you pick just how good you want it to hurt.- LOTS and LOTS of customization options built-in to server settings; gather rate, craft rate, and stack size are just parameter tweaks when setting up a server. There are PLENTY of other options to let you tailor a server exactly how you like.The Bad:-   It was a ping issue. Even then, that server was at around 160-180ms ping (I was playing with friends across the pond) and that was the only issue I noticed. I'd say the game handles higher latency very well! After moving to a low-ping server, the issue disappeared.- My BIGGEST complaint about the game is the random tech unlocks. It's not  since all the most important tech you gain by hunting down and killing bosses, but it's still very annoying to be stuck on a boss and farming research materials hoping for gear upgrades but getting every base decoration first. I would very much prefer being able to choose what to unlock, even if they increased research cost to balance it out.The Weird:-   This makes more sense as you progress, can't really explain why without spoilers.- Blood type and quality is FAR MORE IMPORTANT than it lets on. Certain types are useless at low quality but feel overpowered at high quality. For example, a good type at high quality will let you stomp a boss that you've been struggling with otherwise.  This one is still mostly true. The game could benefit very much from some sort of in-game info that gives more detail of how the blood mechanics work and how important it is. The balancing makes more sense now; some blood types are going to be better for you in the early game but others will outshine them as you get better gear, but early on you should care less about the type and more about the quality. Later on when you unlock more and better weapons and settle into a build, then the synergies with certain blood types becomes more apparent - and important.-   I'm taking this one back, mostly. The pacing can still feel out of whack when the first handful of missions only take a few minutes each and then you hit one that takes several hours. The thing is, those missions aren't  your progression - that comes from killing bosses. The missions are just to help you along in the early game, introduce features and mechanics, then later give you a nudge toward your next steps.Other Stuff: - Material requirements for the mid- to late-game items look daunting at first, but they're far easier than they look. You just need to explore to find the good spots and utilize game mechanics (Waygates, cave tunnels, servants) and it's not much of a grind at all.

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising has fluid combat, lots of areas to explore and pillage.  You gain power by crafting, looting, and stealing powers from your foes.  The is a fairly diverse set of weapons and abilities to use, allowing you to find the best combination that works for you.  You can play either PvE or PvP, both can be fun in different ways.I think this game has a good foundation to be an amazing PvE experience.  There are a number of different bosses, all with their own behaviors, locations/patrol routes.  Not all enemies are friendly with each other, so sometimes you can come across random battles.  There is also rare loot to be found for those lucky enough to get them to drop.As it currently stands, the PvE is good.  It has everything it needs to be taken to the next level.  I for one hope the developer recognizes the potential that is here, and builds upon it.A community manager has responded with about the concerns with the advanced settings.  It was mostly miscommunication:"We've made it easier to get into your directory and adjust private games by giving buttons straight in the "Load Game" menu that will take you directly to the folder where you can find your Server Settings text file, as well as access to the Advanced Settings menu right in the client. In that way I think we've been successful in what we were trying to accomplish, however I think there are ways with the implementation that were not so successful and that's what's causing friction here.Our documentation isn't up to date and we didn't properly communicate how to edit these settings that now APPEAR to be missing but still do exist! In fact there are more settings than ever, but you can't be expected to KNOW that if we don't properly tell you, so that is entirely our fault and you are right to be upset with us about that.I just got done talking with our tech engineers, and we're going to be getting that documentation together to get to you guys as soon as possible so that it's as easy as we can make it for you to edit these settings and get exactly the experience you want.TL;DR: Our intentions were to make server hosting more accessible and less intimidating, but we didn't provide the proper tools to implement some advanced settings. We're working on getting all the info for you now!"As for the languages, the community is hard at work trying to get everything localized.  It may have been taken away due to standards, but better late than never.You can check here if your language is supported:

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising is a unique and engaging twist on the survival genre, blending classic gothic vampire themes with robust base-building and satisfying combat mechanics. In this game, you awaken as a newly-born vampire lord tasked with restoring your castle and amassing power by defeating enemy factions and cultivating a clan of loyal servants.One of V Rising's biggest strengths is its progression system. Starting from humble beginnings, you'll gradually unlock new abilities, gear, and resources that allow you to establish a formidable stronghold. The castle-building aspect is incredibly rewarding, offering players a high degree of customization and plenty of room for creative expression.Combat is another highlight, with a skill-based system that rewards timing and strategy. Whether you prefer melee weapons, ranged attacks, or devastating spells, there's a playstyle to suit every preference. Defeating powerful enemies and bosses is a thrilling challenge, made even more rewarding by the ability to turn slain foes into obedient minions for your clan.The game's atmosphere is top-notch, with gorgeously rendered environments that capture the gothic ambiance perfectly. From gloomy forests to foreboding castles, the world of V Rising is a delight to explore, particularly at night when your vampiric powers are at their peak.While V Rising shines in many areas, it does have a few shortcomings. The lack of a dedicated story campaign may disappoint some players, and the game's pacing can feel a bit uneven, with periods of intense action punctuated by extended stretches of grinding for resources.

_childDocuments_.review: After 15 hours in this game and surely I have only scratched the surface, I cannot in good faith recommend this game. That's more than really anyone could ask for an game in EA. The only problem is that foundations don't really make a game fun and engaging. V Rising is missing that it factor that makes me want to come back. I will undoubtedly return when it hits 1.0, but not any time before then.

_childDocuments_.review: Hi,V Rising has a lot going for it, there are a few issues that I had with the game.The game is lengthy, which is fantastic for those who love a deep, immersive experience, but the grind can feel overly demanding, especially as you progress. There’s also a forced fast-travel limitation in PvP, which requires you to empty your inventory if you want to use the vampire waygates, a design choice that can feel frustrating for solo players. So they do not say to you that you server is played solo but with the default option that you cannot travel with materialls.Getting to know the mechanics, bosses takes time. I found myself frustarated in the early game than sprinted trough 60% of the game with no issue. than the very last encounters started being too much time consuming and somewhat difficult.I played the game on the hardest difficulty and it seems like difficulty options have a huge impact on how the bosses behave and the fights playround as I found it out on varies videos of other people that they beaten up bosses fairly easily than me. Taking advantage of your spells weapon type alternative weapon atacks, potions is essential.Overall there is not much to say, because it is a solid game that takes you from the beginning and brings you to the end with new fresh encounters, bosses, maps, locations, weapons etc. it offers a lot as you get more into it.

_childDocuments_.review: is a mesmerizing game that immerses players into a captivating world where they awaken as a vampire, tasked with surviving and conquering a land teeming with mystery and danger. One of the most striking aspects of   is the sense of empowerment it bestows upon players. As a vampire, your insatiable thirst for blood drives you to hunt in nearby settlements, carefully navigating the night to avoid the scorching touch of sunlight. The game masterfully captures the essence of being a creature of the night, with each decision and move adding to the exhilarating gameplay experience.What truly sets   apart is the ability to raise your own castle, becoming a true lord or lady of the night. This feature adds a layer of strategy and personalization to the game, allowing players to shape their own domain, gather resources, and expand their influence. Building and fortifying your castle becomes an addictive endeavor, while also serving as a symbol of your power and domination.While   can be experienced as a solo adventure, the game truly shines when you venture into the online realm and form a clan with fellow vampires. Conquering the land of the living becomes a collective effort, as you strategize, cooperate, and face off against other players in epic battles. The multiplayer aspect adds a dynamic social element, making every encounter a chance to forge new friendships or test your mettle against rival vampires.Visually,   is a treat for the eyes. The dark and brooding art style perfectly complements the game's theme, with attention to detail that brings the world to life. The haunting soundtrack further enhances the immersion, creating an eerie and captivating atmosphere that lingers long after you've turned off the game.However, it's worth noting that   might not be everyone's cup of tea. The game heavily focuses on the vampire experience, and if you're not particularly drawn to that genre or find the concept repetitive, it may not offer enough novelty to captivate you.In conclusion,   is a thrilling and immersive vampire-themed game that allows players to awaken as powerful creatures of the night. With its captivating open world, castle building mechanics, and engaging multiplayer features, it offers a unique and enthralling experience. If you're a fan of vampires and enjoy exploring dynamic worlds filled with mystery and strategy, then V Rising is a game you shouldn't miss. Embrace the darkness, gather your allies, and conquer the land of the living.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of small details in here that makes it annoying to play. It feels like having better equipment is the idea of the game and not the ability to play the game well rewards the players. Towards the end, most the enemies are the same gear level as the player and its frustrating to have to clear the area since it takes a long time. It definitely isn't a singleplayer game because there's little in terms of being able to outplay enemies/bosses.Gameplay just feels very clunky. I've had a much better time just riding my horse and cheesing the bosses by running circles around them. In no way did I feel like there was enjoyment for taking down any boss, only other than being able to craft new items (getting new abilities become stale after a certain point). The bosses are equipped with a bit too much different abilities and AOE damage abilities that having only one way to dodge them every six seconds isnt really fun for the players experience. And as some of them get to summon help too, there's no way to dodge the boss attack and the minion attack properly. I feel like there just needs to be one more ability slot or something added (taking minions to battle) to make the combat better.Weapons: nice to have a bit of variety, but what reason would i use them other than for farming the proper resources? I mainly use the sword and nothing else is fun to use. - Swords, give a small invulnerability window which makes it better to use than any other weapon. - Axes, never would I use it other than to chop wood. The passive for the axes are pointless too. - Crossbow, winding up the bow feels a bit unnecessary, dps is probably the lowest of all weapons.- Spear, one of the abilities is good and the other one not so much.Abilities: somewhat feels like all of them are just the same thing but with different effects (which do little to no damage difference)I can't pinpoint it, but it feels like it's missing a key point in making the player movement/ability/action feel nice and fun to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Great top-down open world game where you play as a vampire with magical powers and servants to assist you. Massively multiplayer but can also be played singleplayer which is a great option.Semi-strategy and RPG, where you will need to build your fortress with resources around the world. Players also need to "feed" your fortress, if playing multiplayer and abandon it after finishing the story, your based will basically implode. Practically farming and hunting to improve your resource gains which is relatively tedious, but not bad.The graphics is extremely good and light, no issues on low-end or mid-end machines. Extremely detailed compared to most games.The music and themes are very good with the gothic vampire themes. Action and attack sounds are quite nice too, except, too bad there is no speaking voices of your characters.Controls are realatively easy and fine tuned both for Controller and on Keyboard+Mouse1. Sometimes items dropped by enemies go through terrain, cannot be picked up2. Sometimes get stuck in certain animation(s) like attacking or morphing3. Controls on horses feels kind of wonkyOverall a great game with extremely high replayability, a lot of fun when playing to play with friends PvE. If you are competetive, PvP is also available where other players compete for resources and attempt to destroy your base. Once the main missions are completed, nothing much to do except farming endlessly. Now that there are new major updates, may continue playing, as finished the main storyline ages ago.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, good game. However, there are a few things to note before purchasing this game.1.) It is meant to be played cooperatively, so single players will want to modify the details and characteristics of their sole serve to make it less grindy.2.) This game's controls, thou finicky, are relatively good but can be a bit of a issue for newer players.3.) Bosses and enemies in this game can be very tricky for new players; and new players may wander into an area where higher level opponents will mop the floor with them.4.) This point is more for the older players who purchased the bundle edition prior to the Gloomrot update. But the purchasing of the original bundle won't give you the new Gloomrot cosmetics for free. You need to purchase it, but it'll be at a 10% discount if you purchased the original bundle.5.) This game is really what you make of it. It can be a building game for some, a multiplayer game to others, or a over-powered vampire lord simulation for another. 6.) Frame rate issues can be a big issue and my computer froze upon changing the settings in options. So proceed with caution. 7.) Be sure to adjust your graphical and game play settings prior to beginning a game. This is to ensure your computer functions normally and that the game is still playable without bricking your system.Overall, is the game good? Yes! However, the beauty is in the eye of the beholder, so my opinion is not the end all be all for reviews. There are issues, but the developers are seemingly responsive and actively adding features players want in the game (multi-leveled bases for instance). All in all, I am mildly curious what is next to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Recently finished the game running a solo playthrough on Brutal difficulty. Played a bit of co-op PvE with a group on a different run, but the majority of my review will be based on my singleplayer experience since that is where I spent the most of my time.PROS:-Fantastic survivalcraft that takes advantage of the vampire theme.-Combat feels well refined, enjoyed using most of the weaponskills and spells, especially counterattacks.-Bosses are challenging, tense, and well varied. Defeating them on brutal solo usually gave a great feeling of accomplishment. Bosses also have more moves/mechanics on brutal difficulty compared to normal.-Good building system. Easy to place stuff and get things going if you want to just build a functional base quick, but also with plenty of optional aesthetic decorations if you really want to invest alot of effort into a badass vampire mansion.-Crafting economy feels good, anytime I have a surplus of something I feel I have multiple ways to repurpose it to something useful.-Your "level" is determined entirely by your equipment ilvl. No need to grind xp, just the crafting materials to make and maintain your equipment.-Can tune all sorts of gameplay settings of your playthrough/server to your liking.-Just the right amount of worldbuilding. The tone and setting of the game is well constructed and deliberate, while not bogging the player down in detail-heavy lore.CONS:-Bosses don't scale well to multiple players. Even a second teammate on Brutal difficulty will significantly reduce the challenge. Tried some bosses with a team of 5 once and the bosses became trivial and got melted in seconds.-Once in awhile, bosses have moves that don't have accurate move warnings. Usually not a issue but some frost moves in particular have a radius much larger than their warning circle.-Wandering bosses have very finicky de-aggro distances. Very frustrating to get a boss to almost defeated then they either de-pop or run away and regen all their health despite making a conscious effort to stay close to the point of engagement. Easily one of the worst parts of the game.-Similar to the above, some bosses have toss moves that have the potential to send you flying out of their arena. If you are playing solo, this will immediately cause them to de-aggro and get all their hp back and effectively ending the fight attempt.-UI could benefit from a option to display your skill cooldowns overlayed atop the character. Especially since alot of this game is dodging layers of boss mechanics while keeping an eye on 5 or 6 cooldown timers.-Finding enemies with good blood quality for capture is entirely RNG. For me, finding 100% scholar blood was a bigger grind than the grind for any material resource.-Some boss fights will have junk items scattered all over the area of engagement due to environment collateral damage, making health orbs difficult to pickup as they use the same key.I didn't touch pvp for this game so I can't comment on the player experience for that.If your interest is PvE, either solo or duo is the way to go imo. Select brutal difficulty if you have a deathwish but normal is also plenty challenging. Good game and though it can feel like hitting a wall at times, breaking through that wall felt great and kept me coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent survival action game with a flavouring of RPG combat, although somewhat under-cooked in each aspects of its undertaking.The game's presentation is great. Although the setting itself isn't unique, featuring very standard fantasy genre trope creatures, set pieces and designs. There isn't anything here that you haven't seen in other fantasy games, but this time you are playing as a vampire, so your castle exudes very Gothic styles and furniture. The graphics are nice, the lighting works well and night and day are remarkably different experiences visually. The only major dissonance here is really the use of low poly character models for the bosses and enemies, visually clashing with the detailed world assets.There is a decent amount of foliage and clutter, and each biome feels distinct enough from one another to encourage exploration and provide diversity. Sound design is decent, although nothing too memorable.Moving on to gameplay, the strengths and weaknesses are more pronounced. You play as a vampire with explicit goals of hunting down special bosses that award you new blueprints and powers on defeat. Similar to other genre staples, you can either use an altar at your castle to create a tracking trail that leads to the boss, or you can simply head to the area and find them as they are either always in an arena or have a set patrol route.The bosses are varied enough to feel fun, although the first half of the bosses are simply just enhanced mobs, and the last few bosses are where it gets more interesting and challenging. There is a need to plan the time you engage these bosses, as the game's day night cycle means that in the day when the sun is out you can possibly be caught in an arena basked in sunlight, which casts a deadly ray on your vampire that can quickly finish you off.The castle building is decent, and utilizes a gridbased expansion and construction system. This means that you can quickly build structures and alignment is easy, though it also means that the more avid builder might feel limited. There are a decent amount of crafting stations with your standard forge, woodwork, chemistry and sawmill, and a few other specific stations that involve blood refinement. Where the base building gets unique is the introduction of prison cells that allow you to lure charmed NPCs with a high blood quality back, imprisoning them and turning them into livestock. There are a number of farming stations available, although the steep material costs involved to even begin production of other materials can be off-putting. Crafting is one of the weakest points here, and while its generic tiered weapon crafting system is serviceable, the problem of the material acquisition rate rears its ugly head often. As an example, the mid game to late game crafting utilizes a lot of scourgestone in almost any high end crafting materials. Scourgestone is either found in graveyard areas, or crafted with a set of lesser materials that are still specific to find. Almost the entirety of your progression will be locked by scourgestone production rates, while other materials accumulate well into excess stacks. After the scourgestone drought ends, you will run into the next issue, scrolls, which are needed to randomly unlock a blueprint on your research desk, hoping for armor and weapon unlocks even as the RNG decides to unlock a furniture blueprint instead.All these crafting woes lead to a massive grind for resources, one that can only countered by playing in larger coop parties or if PVP, raiding other castles. There needs to be more loot spots or more enemies and loot drops per spot for some materials, especially ones that bleed into multiple recipes.The combat is quite engaging, it allows you to pick two spells, an ultimate and you have three weapon skills preset based on what weapon you are using. There are some neat combos here, and the telegraphing and real time evasion of attacks provide for a rather fun combat system that you can get better at with play. Much of the spell options are however, locked behind boss kills, and there is no other customisation which means that most players you encounter would be running similar builds that lack variety. You can select a class in essence by drinking blood from a creature or human of a particular class, and the quality of the blood determines how much buffs you receive. While interesting, it turns into a micromanagement game that can become annoying later on.Loot is mostly restricted to more materials for crafting, and bosses do not drop unique gear outside of the one or two that do early game. Gear scales upwards with pure stats, so a higher level sword does nothing but increase your damage, and adds nothing else. This bland tiered gearing system can rear its ugly head later on when you begin to feel like there is a lack of motivation to earn new gear.The game does have a lot of potential and is a blast to play with friends, but at the end of the day it feels like a lacking title that only slightly innovates from the standard genre tropes and then completely stops and doesn't take the game further. The systems work well together, but they do not work at the levels needed to make the game stand out. Early Access, keep an eye, decent for its price.

_childDocuments_.review: I've gotten a good amount of fun out of this game, but it's still not even remotely close to being done. Devs did in fact improve a number of issues between early access and now- that's great. The game still has no replayability from the perspective of someone who has only done PVE. Gearing up requires little to no thought and each gear upgrade feels as though it looks the same as the last. Weapons are only vaguely visually distinct between upgrade tiers as well. Ability choice is largely the same between trees- two ranged moves, two defensives, 2 aoe options of some kind, a directional ult or a defensive one- but Chaos gives ignite and Blood gives leech! You don't notice any of that in the end. World exploration is better than it was in terms of world size, zones are either unremarkable or ugly, and flora variety as well as seed collecting is a terribly huge pain in the ass. Farming Stygian Shards is terrible, painful even. It's here in particular where mob variety feels at its absolute weakest. PVE basebuilding is pleasant enough, though you're left constantly hankering for more decorative options all game long. Unfortunately 30+ decoratives are locked behind needlessly expensive DLC(4 of them). In addition to this, once you do finally unlock all things decorative, I would describe a feeling of the game already being over. And even then, the last few available boss-locked placeables are so laughably unimaginative or far too late in their arrival that it hardly matters. Nearly level 90, everything long-since unlocked, my gear doesn't have a single good chroma tied to it, three bases built out of boredom- time to fight Dracula! It's the only good fight in the game. What would I change overall? Add more systems beyond the limited resource crafting we have. More decoratives is awesome but there aren't really any meaningful things to place them around in the end. Three different versions of the same desk rendering it's predecessor obsolete each time feels... questionable? And this happens several times. Make upgrading gear feel rewarding, and actually make decent looking sets with good visual variety. Increase the difficulty level across the board. Spend some time contributing to the basebuilding parts of the game even more, maybe even consider implementing a server option to allow people to connect bases that are already basically on top of each other. Add meaningful options for different building blocks, pillar designs, outer wall designs that are weathered or varied. Consider adding greater NPC variety- it sucks that none of them are really voiced. Not even shopkeeps? Anyways. Give it another couple of years, and if the studio hasn't abandoned it by then, maybe it'll legitimately be worth playing more than once.

_childDocuments_.review: A Vampire's Survival MasterpieceV Rising is a fresh take on the survival genre, blending gothic vampire lore with open-world exploration, base-building, and satisfying combat. As a fan of survival games and vampire themes, V Rising has delivered in a way that’s both innovative and addictive. Here’s why I think it stands out:Immersive Vampire FantasyV Rising nails the fantasy of becoming a vampire. From the moment you awaken in a crypt as a weakened vampire, the game draws you into its dark, gothic world. Everything about it—whether it’s hunting for blood to stay alive, avoiding the deadly sunlight, or building your own castle—makes you feel like you’re truly living the life of an ancient, powerful creature of the night.The way the game integrates vampire mechanics into the core gameplay is fantastic. You’re constantly balancing the need for blood to fuel your abilities with the dangers of daylight and enemy hunters. Feeding on different types of blood grants buffs, adding depth to how you approach combat and survival. This gives V Rising a layer of strategy that goes beyond traditional survival games.Engaging Combat SystemThe combat in V Rising is fast-paced and satisfying, blending elements of ARPGs with real-time action. You have access to a variety of weapons, spells, and vampire abilities, each with distinct styles and strengths. Combat is fluid and responsive, with plenty of room for skill and strategy. You’ll find yourself weaving between dodges, casting powerful spells, and unleashing devastating vampire abilities.Boss fights, in particular, stand out. Each one has unique mechanics and challenges, making them feel like rewarding encounters rather than mindless hack-and-slash. Defeating bosses also grants you new abilities, which gives you an exciting sense of progression as you grow stronger.Open-World ExplorationThe game world in V Rising is vast and beautifully crafted. It’s filled with dark forests, cursed villages, and dangerous human settlements that feel alive with danger and mystery. Exploring the open world is one of the highlights, as you’re constantly uncovering new materials, enemies, and secrets that enhance your journey.I love how the world is dynamic, with day and night cycles that directly impact how you play. Being forced to navigate through the shadows during the day to avoid burning in the sunlight adds an interesting tension to exploration, making nighttime the prime time for hunting and gathering resources.Base-Building & CraftingBuilding your vampire castle is one of the most enjoyable parts of the game. You start with a simple structure, but over time, you gather resources to upgrade your castle into a sprawling fortress. The customization options allow you to design a unique and menacing stronghold, complete with crafting stations, storage, and even prisoner chambers to extract blood from humans.Crafting is also well-integrated into the gameplay loop. You’re constantly collecting materials to improve your gear, weapons, and castle. The progression feels smooth and rewarding, with each new upgrade giving you a sense of power and readiness for the next challenge.ConclusionV Rising is an exceptional survival game that brings something truly unique to the genre. Its combination of vampire fantasy, engaging combat, expansive open-world exploration, and satisfying base-building makes it a standout title. The multiplayer aspect adds replayability and keeps things exciting, while the vampire mechanics give the game a fresh and strategic twist.If you’re a fan of survival games or just love the idea of becoming a powerful vampire, V Rising is absolutely worth your time.Rating: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: To explain V Rising simply, imagine 3D Terraria through a vampiric lens. The gameplay loop is roughly the same:Kill bosses to unlock gear/recipes/crafting stations -> Build a base with the new unlocks -> Farm materials for new gear to prepare for the next boss. Repeat until the game is finished.Might sound simple, but it's an incredibly enjoyable experience when taken into the vampire fantasy. You live in a castle of your own design, you abduct people to convert into your servants or lock in your dungeon, you drink the blood of creatures and get different benefits depending on their type, you shapeshift into different animals and you burn in the sun.To explain those on a more mechanical level, every living creature in the game has a blood type and different blood purity. Depending on those two factors, you get different buffs ranging from taking less damage, dealing more damage after you dash or having a chance to reset your spells immediately upon casting them. This does mean that you may run into situations where you won't have good blood for a certain boss which can be frustrating, but your blood is just buffs and not capable of carrying you through a lack of skill.Getting on that, the game has several difficulties and allows you to customize almost every aspect of it. Don't like the amount of time it takes to pass from day to night? You can change it. Think the material farm is too slow and grindy? You can change the amount of materials dropped by mobs or gathered. Custom-make your own experience to perfectly suit your needs. This applies to the premade difficulty settings like Brutal as well.Speaking off Brutal, Brutal difficulty adds new moves to every boss in the game and generally buffs them by giving them a +3 gear score, this games leveling system. If you've played any MMO before, this functions similarly to Ilvl, but if you haven't: every piece of equipment comes with a gear score that adds to your total, dictating your level. For example: if you have a full gear level 6 armor, a level 18 weapon and a level 18 necklace, that adds up to a gear score of 60, dictating which areas you're suited to be in and which bosses you're expected to be able to kill. This again, makes the game a bit rigid in that progression is only tied to bosses. Stop killing bosses, you're not progressing.To help you the materials to craft said gear however, you're given the ability to convert humanoid creatures into vampiric servants. These servants can then be equipped with their own gear (same as you would use) to give them enough power to go on hunts in different areas of the map, returning with loot after 4 - 22 hours depending on how much loot you want them to come back with. This gives you the ability to avoid farming entirely and effectively make the grindy part of the game into an idle game. Log in once a day to collect your servants loot then send them back out to get you more, which is EXTREMELY WELCOME as the material grind in the game sometimes feels too intense. To give credit to the dev, it's a lot better now than it was before V1.0 release, especially regarding knowledge.Knowledge is the main grind for most of the early - mid game, as it's what allows you to increase your gear score by upgrading your gear. Without the correct recipe unlocked from knowledge, you can't craft the upgrades to your gear. This used to be extremely infuriating as the drop chance for books was very low and meant you had to go out and farm paper/scrolls/schematics for *hours* in the hope that the random unlock would give you the gear upgrade you want over some decoration like Vases or Paintings.Ignoring that frustation, the bosses are generally pretty simple. The bosses all have 3-4 attacks and sometimes a gimmick mechanic to keep you on your toes. Keely shots single arrows, a volley of arrows, drop down arrows with circles and goes invis. On Brutal, she does a mid-sized AoE around her when she comes out of stealth as well. Most if not all the bosses have their own tempo that can be learned similar to soulslike bosses. Most of the tempo can be cheesed through uses of high purity scholar blood for the reset chance on your spells to pump out massive damage quickly for minimal risk. The special bosses are a bit different however.The final 4 bosses of the game are much, much more difficult than the rest of the game. This is to be expected, they're the final bosses of the game after all. You're expected to have prepared potions to buff yourself up and have 88 in gear level minimum to stand a chance. On Brutal, some of them have entirely new phases added to prolong the fight and make it more difficult. They're, by far, the most fun part of the game in my opinion, absolutely due to my enjoyement of the souls series. Despite the high level of difficulty, all of the bosses in the game are beatable by whatever strategy you wish to use, and there are many.7 melee weapons and 3 ranged weapons, each with 2 unique skills and 1 basic ability. 6 schools of magic with 6 basic spells, 3 unlockable passives and 2 ultimate spells each with jewels to modify each of them. You're bound to find a playstyle that you enjoy.Heavily recommend and only slightly biased due to swedish devs. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I cannot recommend this game currently. PvE is boring, because there is nothing to do apart from killing brain dead bosses and increasing your stats, which don't mean anything apart from killing more bosses. There is just this: killing bosses and more gear to kill more bosses.PvP on the other hand is truly awful. If you are not among the first players on a server start and you dont have a full clan (depending on the server this is either 4, 3 or 2 people or solo) you cannot win in pvp. It is a simple numbers game. 2vs1 = lose. 2vs3= lose. 4vs3 = lose. You constantlly need a full clan, otherwise you risk losing everything. The grind is so immense after losing your gear (on full loot pvp) or your items in your castle, that you basically can never recover, because people can just continue to raid your base with siege golems. Siege golems cost basically nothing. You can easily produce several of them a day and keep other players who could pose a threat weak, so they never stand a chance. If you are not online during siege hours (or if it is a server that has siege permanently turned on) there is no way to defend your castle. And even if you are online, you require your entire clan to defend, because remember: if you are not the same amount of people fighting the attackers, you instantly lose. So 4 or 3 or however many people need to be online during these siege hours EVERY day.Also if you are not online for a week, your castle and all your stuff is just gone. It decays, unless you "feed" your castle heart blood essence. This lasts for about 6 days real time at maximum. After this, everyone can break into your castle, steal everything and then destroy it for free with one click.And as this was not enough: If you are not playing solo offline or on your own server, there is a good chance the host will at some point wipe the server, resetting everyone's progress to 0%. Now that is a good thing, because it evens the playing field again, giving everyone a chance. At the same time, EVERYTHING is gone. Your character too.Some recipes in this game make no sense. Research is completely broken. To research one lategame tech. you need 100 schematics. One schematic reqiuires several scrolls and other materials.. One scrolls requires several papers and other materials. So unless you farm research schematics, scrolls and papers (as well as sometimes book, which instantly unlock a technology), you require thousands upon thousands of materials. And not just mundane trash. Some of this stuff is in highly contested areas with dangerous NPCs. If you don't want to craft these things, you have to kill enemies in the according locations and hope they that drop schematics, scrolls and papers. And then even if you get enough together and don't get mugged by a gank squad 20 levels higher than you on your way back, what exactly you unlock is random. There are several cosmetic "technologies" that do nothing. And they make up about 2/3 of the technologies. So about 66% of the time you just get crap.The first 10-20 hours really feel amazing and you think you are actually accomplishing a lot by building your fancy castle, killing bosses, unlocking new bosses and crafting machinery to process items. Then you slowly realize: either you are just DONE in Pve after about 20-30 hours. And I mean DONE in every way possible. Or you are playing PvP and after getting mugged for the 30th time by people so much higher level than you, that the game does not even tell you anymore, that it is just a painful, unrewarding, boring grind with nothing at the end to reward the player apart from getting all your stuff stolen, while you are offline and trying to live an actual live.If the developers want to save this game, they do not have to change everything I mentioned here. I understand that everyone likes different things. But there is just so much wrong with the game at this point, that the first 10-20 hours just don't make up for it. People compare this game to DayZ, Rust and other "hardcore" games. If you like those, maybe this is for you, but if you want a some reward for your efforts and some way to protect these rewards, then stay the hell away and just play Minecraft instead, if you wanna play a good crafting game with survival elements.Currently this game is either boring or broken.

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising is a vampire-themed castle builder with a beautiful art style, atmospheric soundtrack and a lively world. You can spend countless hours designing a perfect garden or a perfect throne room, with DLCs adding even more stuff to build, Sims style. It would be a great game if its other part was an RPG - with a proper story, proper classes and proper progression; or perhaps even a life or a dynasty sim. Unfortunately, in V Rising the castle builder cohabitates with a hardcore survival crafting PvP game - and every single design decision is influenced by that. You can't properly heal in combat, you can't teleport while carrying resources, you can't... well, there's many other things you "can't" in V Rising because it makes sense for a PvP-focused game. The main problem is it's absolutely antithetic to other part of the game I just described - why would you ever commit dozens of hours building a perfect castle, if anyone is able to trivially raze or steal it, not to mention the regular progress wipes?As a result, we have the game with an identity crisis, one that tries to sit on several chairs at once, but does it in a very clumsy manner and ends up falling to the floor. Of course, you could play on PvE server - but it feels like an afterthought as there's literally no reason why you'd want that - bosses scale in power depending on how many players are fighting them, and outside of that it's just competing with other players for castle and farming spots. You could also play solo on a private server and tune the settings for the game to be less grindy and less annoying - but at the end of the day you still won't be able to fully get rid of PvP-focused game design. In conclusion, V Rising is at its strongest when you're exploring the world and building perfect castles. However, all that does not exist in a vacuum and you will inevitably have to engage with the rest of the game - combat where the way to win is not getting hit, your dodge is on cooldown and most skills are like "slows the target for 1.1 seconds"; survival where you have to take 5-minute breaks every 10 minutes because of the sun that cripples your ability to play properly, not to mention silver, garlic and holy radiation - after all, this is definitely not a vampire power fantasy; very slow movement around a huge map with fast travel pretty much nonexistent by design. So it's a conundrum - playing the game the "proper" way is simply tedious and unfun and ultimately a "one and done" deal as progression is on rails with no replayability. And if you cheat the hell out of it with infinite resources and one-shotting everything then building castles becomes a pointless out-of-context endeavour just for the sake of it.

Progression:I would welcome more depth to the proggresion. _childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game for anyone looking for a change from the equivalent survival experiences you find in Rust, Ark Survival evolved and Valheim alike. Been seeing some negative reviews which literally prompted me to make this review. For all those who find the system of a games economy slowing down during the approaching end game of the current content seem to not be aware of everything the game has to offer in terms of farming resources, crafting recipes, etc. Within this game you essentially have personal farmers at your disposal through the servant system, unlocking an entirely new method of being able to send your servants out to farm the resources are you lacking - For you. This opens up your time to invest your efforts into things you find more engaging only to come back after a set period of time to find a wealth of materials your servants have gathered for you. I personally love this mechanic and I am surprised to  have only ever seen it in this game. The combat system is rewarding as you will find harder challenges to your average gameplay in the easier regions when you traverse the map through to much deadlier regions, even just with the mobs which patrol the areas. The blood system is genius, making you really think about everything you do and how to manage your character's longevity. I don't want to go into too much detail because the enjoyment I had from avoiding spoilers to the content made my experience the best I've had with a game in a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not your typical vampire game, this is one of a kind. It's more of a MMORPG/Action MMO than a Vampire Game; very little if any storyline, mostly combat and action along with significant base building.This Video shows actual game play (albeit edited): The 1.0 Update Added Lots of Stuff to try out, but I am kinda remiss at the devs for removing easy access exact combat tweaks and replacing them with 3 "generic" levels of difficulty.Generally the game plays like Diablo III or Torchlight II, but with Bases, and with a more open world, open-ended storyline. Optional PvP Servers mean you can either risk it all in player invasions of your castles or find some kind of middle ground on the private servers (which are numerous), to allow only KO'ing of your character and not invasions of castles, or go fully PvE. Also For server hosts, everything is customizable settings, including the (some what rare) support for scheduled PvP Options. And as of 1.0 you should no longer crash your server just because you edited the wrong value (supposedly).For those wondering, No There are not "instanced" dungeons. Instead Caves and such spawn on the open world map, and Bosses (V Bloods) can be found by in-game tracking features (as some of them move around)Solo mode IS an option, and I highly recommend you use it to firmiliarize yourself with the game BEFORE attempting to join a PvP Server (if you even go for PvP, most people here are looking for PvE)

_childDocuments_.review: I was worried after Battlerite, a game I loved, was handled poorly. Stunlock Studios have an AMAZING combat engine, developed and refined over two arena brawler games. With this early access, I can safely say they found their calling.V Rising is an amazing combination of Valheim's building elements, Battlerite's combat engine, and Diablo's hack and slash replayability.  The bosses are staggeringly well designed, and I find myself fighting them again and again when I pass them in the open world. Could I avoid them? Sure. Fighting them is more fun. Each of them have such unique boss fights, some with their own areas designed to show off their unique gimmicks. The best part is how many bosses there are. For an alpha with a future ahead of it, there are already fully fleshed out ability pools to choose from, solid base gameplay elements and an addictive gameplay loop.To conclude, V Rising has managed what Battlerite failed to do: Create a gameplay loop that is fun. I'm relieved beyond words that a talented studio like Stunlock was able to properly apply their strengths before being consumed by the unfeeling market. I look forward to this game's future.

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising is an absolute triumph of a game. It brings the responsive and flashy combat of a good MOBA into the Action RPG style in a way things like Diablo4 could really stand to learn from. It's fast, its fluid, its genuinely skilful and there are many many different kinds of build to try out .The graphics are the best kind of stylised comic book theme - and there is a huge amount of content available to the player across a beautiful crafted environment map. At the core of the gameplay loop is your re-awakened Vampire who needs to explore the land and fight and drain a whole progression of bosses (dozens and dozens of them) to incorporate their powers and magic and learn their skills. These skills form the basis of the crafting and base building part of the game - and here again V Rising has massively benefited from a long and successful early access period to create one of the best systems for loot and resource management and flexible base building in the survival genre. Honestly in a desert of rubbish AAA releases V Rising is a blood filled Oasis of quality and player enriching design excellence. The entire game can be played SOLO, or COOP, or even with PVP and base Raiding. For me its up there as an example of superb game design made with care and quality and attention to detail that stands proudly beside the likes of BG3. Mate of mine calls it "Valheim with Vampires" and it kinda is - while also being an entirely different grade of fluid action combat and massive quality of life boosting base building dynamics. The world itself also feels more alive (ironically for a undead game) with npc settlements spawning victims, villagers, militia and patrols and even the bosses moving around the landscape getting into fights with monsters, and each other. Its got that kind of emergent chaos in combat that you get in the Grand Theft Auto games where everybody ends up wanting a piece of an ongoing conflict. Btw - all the DLC's are cosmetic - they look excellent but its also extremely possible to live out your goth vampire edgelord dreams with the core content and drops available to everyone who buys the game. Massive recommend from me!

_childDocuments_.review: I love a survival game that challenges you without being a slow, frustrating grind. Building in V Rising isn't a minecraft-esque race to have a full castle built within the first hour, I don't feel as though I've wasted an entire evening chopping down trees, and the battle mechanics are very fluid and intuitive. The day/night cycle is a welcome challenge that really brings the world alive, and the voice acting for named enemies is phenomenal. I can't say for sure if this is going to be my favorite survival game of all time, but I do think it can give the AAA titles a run for their money.
