_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game.  Time will tell if they do the usual "survival game abandonment" thing but for an early access release it is very polished and full of content.  For perspective, ~5 of us have been playing on a private dedicated PvE server and we are almost 40 hours in and getting near the end of the PvE content.  I'm sure you can rush much faster, but being able to enjoy 40+ hours of PvE only content in a game like this is a very good sign.Jumping into a public server with PvP would only open up things much more... if the PvP rules were setup and balanced correctly.As long as the developers continue to improve the game, add some more quality of life features and flush out the content and balance this will be a great game to play.   My main concern is that they release the game as 1.0 with the content we see now and call it done forever and abandon the game.  I think a game like this would really benefit from continued support, more added content, new  areas to explore, harder content to push, dynamic events, raids, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: What a strange choice to go the Rust route with a game design like this. I dont think it works very well.The game has a lot of polish for an early access game and it seems like its mostly a complete game already. However, the balance is just stupid. The early game will feel like a cake walk and the late game will feel impossible. There is not significant story or campaign mode as this is a rust like game where you build bases and pvp and I think that was the dumbest decision made by the devs.This game would be AMAZING if it had an actual story and was balanced around a single player or co op mode. It doesnt have the depth needed to be a base raiding/pvp game like rust. Customization in terms of combat and your characters power are extremely limited. Your abilities and power are mostly determined by a linear upgrade path with no loot RNG. That means each level of item will be exactly the same every time you play.The design of daylight hurting you makes sense as a vampire game but the result ended up feeling awful as you cant really do much during the day when the sun is out. Effectively limiting my ability to play the game half of the time. Other games will have time cycles that make it harder but not impossible. For instance, in 7 days to die zombie waves would spawn at night and make it very dangerous to do anything outside of your base at night. However, you could overcome this limit in many ways and even if you were stuck in your base you would always have something to do. That is not the case with V Rising. There isnt much of a reason to expand/improve you base outside of needing more space to put benches and forges and what not. The only threat to it is other players so if you arent playing with people or on a pve server, you dont have to worry about it. If you are on a pvp server, the main way to defend your base is servents which actually require you to go out to hunt for them so thats not something youd be able to do from your base.Server settings by default are insane. For some reason stack sizes are TINY, crafting takes literal hours to complete, hunting missions takes literal DAYS to complete, you get very little loot when compared to what you need to upgrade and for some asinine reason, you cant use teleporters if you have any resources on you. Thankfully you can actually change these settings but it will require you to make a new game with the settings you want and then replacing key files in your appdata to apply the new settings to your old game. I cant imagine the reason for this as all other games like Rust will have a built in UI for adjusting server settings. This should not be hard to change as its all there, they just need a UI to connect the option in game.Lack of variety with spells, There is a big ol book of spells you unlock as you play but they end up being very samey. For instance, you will have like 5 different dodge spells to choose from and they are all different but practically are all the same. One will heal you if you do damage after dodging, one will explode for a small amount of damage, one will make you target take more damage for a bit, ect ect. A few of the spells are actually unique and feel great like one where you can summon a snow knight who wacks people with a big knockback swing and slows them that you cast from a distance. The biggest variety combat wise actually comes from the weapons you use which each has their own abilities. I think the knocked the weapons out of the park but kind of dropped the ball on actual spells. For instance the first "ultimate" spell you get is a charge that stuns at the end and it SUCKS. I actually didnt use my ultimate until I got the second one that gives you a shield. I have a feeling the spells are far more balanced for pvp than they are pve and I think its a big detractor from the fun that could be had with them.I will be keeping an eye one this game as I really do want to like it and its so close to being great, but if they keep trying to chase this base building online multiplayer pvp rust crap, I have a feeling its going to flop hard.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like so many great games rolled into one incredible experience. It feels like they took dark souls, diablo, the witcher, monster hunter, terraria, minecraft and rolled all of those aspects into one of the best ARPG games I've ever had the pleasure of playing. It has super satisfying, crisp, weighty and responsive combat with a high level of skill expression. Every boss is unique, every weapon plays wonderfully, all the spells are fun to use. I've had a ton of fun playing on both PVP and PVE servers alike. I highly recommend Brutal difficulty if you want a more dark souls / elden ring type of gameplay.The building is intuitive and easy to get the hang of. You can put up an entire castle very quickly once you know what you're doing. The materials and resource grind is not that bad, but it is there. You can usually get most of what you need when you're out hunting and exploring so this never really bothered me. Building and decorating your castle is addictive and rewarding. Hands down my favorite game of the year. It's a solid 9/10 with incredible concepts that hopefully show other studios what ARPG and even MMO combat should look like. Stunlock Studios knocked this one out of the park.

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire games are in short supply, and thankfully this is one of the better ones.It's a vampire survival game, so you do vampire stuff, drink blood, and have a good time. You can play this in multiplayer, but I recommend bringing friends along. Honestly most of the battles are challenging and entertaining without being too much to conquer if you're by yourself, the Castlevania crossover is a fun little tidbit and Simon Bellmont lives up to his reputation, and if anything about the game personally doesn't sit right with you, you can adjust just about everything from the server settings to make gameplay easier or harder for yourself. I will give a warning to people who like me do not have friends to play this game with: there are some bosses that were not balanced with singleplayer in mind. I'm sure someone with enough practice and who's skilled enough could overcome that, but I personally hit my limit right towards the end of the game. I tried turning the difficulty down just to be able to experience the combat but aside from a lower damage output, the bosses didn't really change much and I was still stuck at that point. Maybe a 'get good' moment, maybe a 'fight the boss until you learn all their mechanics and die a few hundred times until you win' moment, or exactly what it felt like it was meant to be: a "bring all your friends, cause this is going to be a tough one" kind of fight. Ultimately up until that point, I've had easy fights that left me with my ego feeling inflated. I've had tough ones where I survived with about 1 hp more than the boss I just killed has by the end of the battle. I've struggled, sweat like a pig as I tried for the fifth time to kill a tough boss. After the full release when I lost my save and had to start over, some bosses I struggled with a lot wound up being ez claps because of how well I knew their mechanics, and others that I remembered as being easy I let my guard down around and got smacked around as a result.This game has a lot of content, and you can spend a whole lot of time in it and not get bored. There's almost always a new challenge and up until I hit the limit of what I could beat by myself (f*cking Adam) there was always something more to reach for and look forward to. EDIT: it takes a lot of time, effort, and getting good but you can in fact solo every boss in the game. The sense of achievement is worth everything.I definitely recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I have played this game for 3 hours at the time of this review. For an early access title, this game is absolutely fantastic. I had honestly forgotten this was an Early Access title after a bit since things were going so well. The way this game portrays vampires is great. You are strong, but do have weaknesses. Silver coins hurt you if you try to carry them. You have to hide in the shadows of trees to avoid sunlight during the daytime. I enjoyed being a Vampire even with these hinderances.The crafting and building systems are great. Easy to learn and have a decent balance of what you need. I also didn't have much trouble finding resources early on.The only thing I didn't like was that you could encounter high level "skull" enemies so early on in the game at the starting zones. However, it did challenge me, so I forgive it.In the end, I couldn't really find anything bad to say about this title. I think it is a fantastic Vampire survival game that I hope goes far with the ball here.

_childDocuments_.review: (This review is based off a 2 player PVE experience)It was extremely surprising to find an early access game with so much initial depth and content available to play. This game is a blast with a friend giving tons of options to have fun and is well worth its $20's.Pros:- In-depth open world: I found exploring the map to be very rewarding either giving important resources or boss locations at every turn.- Being a Vampire: This is what makes this game stand out from most base building open worlds available adding a great theme and tone for everything you are doing in the game. With special spells, morphs, and abilities to the danger of being in sunlight, holy radiation, and garlic.- Combat: While not the greatest it is satisfactory enough to make combat enjoyable. It becomes more intricate with special equipment and blood quality of enemy types to make it more than just a simple overhead game combat experience.- Boss Fights: Wow I did not expect this amount of boss fights ranging from large monstrosities to wandering vampire hunters. All the bosses felt as though they had value and felt rewarding to beat either unlocking new spells, materials to craft, or buildable items.- Castle Building: Great building mechanics with a VAST amount of options for not only forges,workshops, and gardens; but also an extensively large amount of decorating available to make your castle a home.Cons:- Somewhat Grindy: You will find your self frequently going on loot runs for a hour taking out large periods of time you will want to spend hunting down bosses or new items. I feel this is mainly due to travel time taking longer than needed due to so much space given for people looking to build castles.- Occasional Bugs: While most of the game is very well optimized for a early release you may experience bugs such and enemies stuck on props such as bridge columns, bosses freezing in combat no longer attacking you for a free kill, or even worse being unable to use your throne to send your servants on missions to collect loot (this happened to the partner on my server and his own for a week).- LONGBOWMEN: They will kill their wife and kids just to knock you out of wolf form.Overall this game is 100% worth the $20 value and I am very excited to see what updates are on the way such as new biomes, (demons?), and hopefully more bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute must-have for any Survival game enthusiast!       Whether you want to play solo or with friends, this game covers all your cravings; Harvest, Build, Attack and Defend.Even though the progression is pretty slow-paced, you can still get satisfactory results by relying only on your mechanics and game sense. At least until the mid-to-late part of the game (circa lvl 40-50). Being able to ass-whoop an enemy which you can't even see the level, while only being lvl~15, is probably the most heart-racing moment you'd have experienced in a while.While it's not my favourite, gameplay-wise, with its camera choices and skills usage, you quickly adapt to it with little difficulty.       The only con I would allow myself to write about, is the fact that; After a certain point in the story/questline, special items and abilities become less varied/usefull or even nonexistent (Yes, I'm looking at you named item blueprints and purple skill tree). I used the same spells from lvl 50 onwards since they dealt the most damages.In my opinion, the last few bosses should have a drop rate of recipes for special cosmetics or weapons.In conclusion, buy it and play for a bit to see if you like the gameplay. From start to finish, the only thing changing will be the degree of mastery you'll have over the controls.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure; anything and everything is fun with friends, as a twenty buck flavor of the month game for you and your mates? Sure. It isn't bad, but it has a lot of little hang ups.It's a PvP minded game, so it keeps pace by making everything slow and the crafting ratios obnoxious, if do-able. For example, glass. Glass is used in a number of things, recipes usually call for ten or so. Glass is made by smelting quartz (#vampires) and it takes 15 quartz for a glass. You get quartz from crystal nodes, which drop in total 80-120~ quartz per node and they're usually alone, although clumps of two to three spawn in certain enemy infested areas as a reward for pushing through. You also use three glass to make what amounts to the upgrade from an iron ingot... which takes ten or so scrouge ingots to do anything. Etc. There's a lot of grinding which feels put in place so that PvP servers have excuses for players to run across each other in the wild often enough.There's also the general progression. Like in Valheim and Conan, you progress and unlock both abilities and crafting recipes (and stations) by defeating bosses. The bosses are hit or miss and some are hella obnoxious and some are cakewalks but whatever, it's about the reward. The crafting stuff is by and large always good, that's whatever. The abilities are the issue; so many of the spell abilities you get are just... bad. They leave you vulnerable with a big wind up in a punishing combat system, they don't do much damage, whatever. You gain one of the most powerful, both in ease of use and damage, spells in the first boss or two and chaos bolt stays on your bar the rest of the game, so the carrot for all these boss fights starts to fall short.Combat also is a little lacking. With some exceptions, there are three broad enemy types; guy who does a slow swing in melee, guy who does a wind up announced charge you dodge, ranged guy who shoots you with a wind up and sound cue. Starts to get stale, but fine. Bosses are near universally the latter two intermixed, as an aside. It's a lot of things to dodge and fancy footwork is the name of the game, but... your dodge is on an eight second cool down. Your shield spells drop if you do anything else, like attack, and then have an eight second cooldown. You have a slow walk speed and can juke some attacks, but sometimes you need to dodge a giant frog landing where you were and the only thing that can avoid it is in the dodge move and oh he did it twice in a row whoops-Bosses are also kind of all over the place in one respect; the game scales their moves and health based on how many people its fighting, fine. Except some... don't? Some are absolutely hellish with one person, and a cakewalk with two just by nature of splitting aggro and offer no new moves, etc. On the flip, some bosses get an outright one-shot move with multiple people and are otherwise a breeze solo and there's no real rhyme or reason to it. This feels like an early access issue, but my other complaints are baked in gameplay choices so shrug.

_childDocuments_.review: Fighting bosses for crafting and processing tables is what this game seems to be about. The power progression system is all about gear and the player does not gain levels.The control system took me a while to get a feel for it. The first few hours I was always attacking in the wrong direction. Probably because of the camera as the direction the player is facing is not the direction you are attacking. It's different but if you play long enough you get the hang of it.Playing this game Singleplayer is probably not what the developers intended. It's probably why I find myself getting bored. I feel like I'm forcing myself to play through taking breaks tabbing out of the game and doing other things then coming back to unlock another crating table after beating a boss. The gameplay loop is somewhat like this. The player needs a new material to upgrade a weapon or armor. Go fight boss to get the ability to make new material with processing table. Then fight another boss to unlock the table that makes the weapon or armor. Now you need another material to actually make the weapon. Go fight boss to unlock another material and processing bench. At first I thought fighting was the most fun part of the game but I think building the castle is more enjoyable as you have many different options and can make something interesting.  This is a mixed one for me due to the lack of making Singleplayer more interesting. Even something as simple as adding story for each boss would help. Maybe even a tug of war system where you are fighting the humans for control of the map like the intro suggests.

(normal might be a bit too easy) I see some people complaining about the resource grind, but that's actually one of the more relaxing aspects of the game. I also enjoy the base building/crafting aspect. I've played 5 hours at the time of this review and I have only really fought 2-3 bosses, since i have spent alot of time on the base building aspect, but the bosses are fun on hard mode.35 hour review: Fighting bosses is probably the best thing about this game. The combat is really fun and I am enjoying all of the different abilities that we have unlocked. I'm playing on a private PvE server with 4 others and I believe the progression is spot on. When i'm not fighting bosses, designing the bad-ass vampire castle is also super enjoyable. The crafting in this game is alot deeper than I thought. I will definitely be sinking 50 more hours into this.80 hour review: Any game I can sink 80 hours into is always recommended. However I believe i will be sinking alot more time into this. I am taking the game pretty slowly because we are only fighting bosses when we have enough friends online, but I cannot recommend this game enough. If you like open world PvE games with crafting and bossing, or if you are looking for a game to play with the squad, buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game but I just can't. Progression in the game is locked behind boss fights, and the boss fights are so overpowered that the player ends up in a turtle of looking for help from admins or dumbing the game down for a glimpse of the next chapter only to find they have to dumb it down again. The difficulty is entirely artificial in that bosses have an overwhelming amount of health and friends in the fight from the start, summon additional friends multiple times mid-fight, and the player is overwhelmingly underpowered and can't do anything about it by grinding for something better; because in order to get anything new or stronger they have to kill the bosses... see the problem here? Online, you're going to have to ask for help because most servers are running default difficulties, and this is if you're a skilled gamer. Singleplayer on default? Forget it. Multiplayer with 1 or 2 friends on default? Forget it.Simply put, V Rising is ♥♥♥♥. It needs balanced or the average gamer will just refund it. You have to find a happy medium and this just isn't even close. If you're a glutton for punishment, believe zerg rushing is the only way a game should be, or are possibly just plain insane, feel free to check it out. If you're just shy of the gamer skill level of a Korean multi-tournament world champion, probably better to spend the money somewhere else, because Stunlock sure as hell hasn't earned it yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a lot of Early Access Survival Crafting games.  This is one of the most polished, deep, engaging, fun Early Access Survival Crafting games I've ever played.  I havent had this much fun since Valheim last year.Not only is the combat fluid, responsive and DEEP, but the moba/ARPG hybrid that it is means enemy and boss fights are fun and challenging.  Leading into the blood and spells system, this is a really need and deep system which enables you to choose blood that you're "filled" with to grant different buffs and may aid you in taking on the bigger challenges; the V Blood holders.  These are basically unique bosses that are exciting and engaging boss encounters that grant you a unique blood skill/ability once you have consumed them, such as the ability to shapeshift into a Wolf for faster movement speed.The daylight mechanic means a raid on a town or settlement during the night can turn you from behind the hunter during the night, to hunted when sunrise arrives.  Its a really unique risk reward system that isnt too punishing.The crafting systems are well rounded and deep enough that you don't feel it's tedious as your castle assists with refining alot of base materials like wood and ore.The world isnt procedurally generated like the aforementioned Valheim, but I think this is OK as it allows you to learn where certain materials are, where camps and settlements of importance are.For the price I fully recommend picking this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Marathon'd through this in the span of a week and a half, solo, after getting it during the sale. Cranked up the crafting and refinement speeds to 3X to offset the grind that you'd expect on a normal MP server, and raised the floor limit on bases to 5 from 3.There's so much to say about this game - It's Conan Exiles, but Isometric, with a gothic theme, a slight hint of Diablo, and fun lore. The base building (as of the last updates) is amazing. I built a 5-story castle with rooms themed around ♥♥♥♥ ala The Sims.The combat is fun, the bosses can be extremely tough solo (if you use Unholy spells and build yourself around that, you can usually tackle them with 4-6 skeletons/skeletal mages), and the progression through each area feels nice, with you constantly uncovering new resources and materials hinting at what you'll be unlocking next, equipment and crafting wise.I came into this expecting a hack and slash. I finished it wishing they would release a spin-off that let you play as Vampires, Werewolves, and Hunters. This game is ripe for expanding with extra playable races, and the groundwork is there to make each of them work. (Switch blood to Faith for humans, Hunger for Werewolves, etc). This game already scratches a aesthetic itch I've had since the 2D Castlevania games stopped being made, so my hope is that they'll eventually expand it out in that way in some form of follow-up, after they wrap up their vision for this one.I really can't recommend this game enough - especially on sale - for people who like the aesthetic, or the idea of "Vampire Conan Exiles". The mechanics are tight, the game itself is fun, and there's a lot of tweakability if you feel it's too hard solo, or too grindy.

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising is a thrilling dive into the world of vampires that's captured my attention unlike any other game in the genre. The freedom it offers is unparalleled. I love how I can customize every aspect of my vampire's abilities, shaping my own unique playstyle. Whether I want to focus on stealthy hunts or all-out combat, the game accommodates my choices seamlessly.The open-world exploration is breathtaking. From eerie forests to ancient ruins, every corner feels meticulously crafted, drawing me in with its hauntingly beautiful landscapes. It's not just eye candy; there's a sense of discovery around every corner, be it a hidden treasure or a challenging enemy encounter.What truly sets V Rising apart for me is the multiplayer aspect. Teaming up with friends to conquer challenges or engaging in intense PvP battles adds a layer of excitement and unpredictability. The social dynamics make every session unique, whether we're forming alliances or competing for dominance.Sure, there are a few bugs here and there, but the developers seem dedicated to fixing issues and listening to the community. The potential for this game is massive, and I'm excited to see how it evolves with future updates.Overall, V Rising is a gem for vampire enthusiasts and open-world lovers alike. Its customization, immersive world, and multiplayer elements make it a standout experience in the genre. I'm hooked and eagerly anticipating what's next for this dark, captivating world of vampires.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game. It's one of my all-time favorites, seriously.If you play this game solo or with a friend, it's an absolutely delightful experience. Combat feels satisfying, though the dash CD is a bit too long imo which can be a bit frustrating. You unlock more and more fun abilities to spice things up as you go, with each V-mark you kill you get a fun new ability to play with. The V-mark bosses are awesome too, with legit mechanics you can't just brute force. Building a castle is VERY fun, the decoration options are awesome, and it looks pretty damn nice overall. Animation is smooth and natural, and mob/enemy models are very nicely designed. Some cosmetic/armor items still clip here and there on my character, but that's about all. The game runs decently even on a lower-end PC (running with a gtx1050, 8gb ram, and an i5, for frame of reference), I can crank everything up to high/medium, the only thing slowing things down a major amount is shadow quality, but it looks great even with it on low. Sometimes the game kind of stutters when I enter new areas or areas where stuff respawned, but it's not debilitating and doesn't last more than a second or two. One thing I dislike is that servants are practically useless in private servers, since they need 24 in-game hours to complete their tasks. PvE/PvP servers are more like a Rust type of experience, so prepare to face that if you want to play in online servers. Private servers don't suffer from the deterioration mechanic like official servers, since the timer only runs when your server is active, so you literally dont' have to worry about that at all, making it play more like Valheim instead.Solo it can be a bit of a grind, so I highly recommend changing your settings up to make progression less grindy (if you want), but 2+ players really shortens the grind, and it's a really really fun time. It's still grindy, but again, you can really modify a lot of the settings (teleporting with mats, more resource yield, etc) so it's not really a problem for me.Overall, this game is a blast, IF you don't play on PvE servers. Play private, modify some settings, get a friend in there, and have a fun time!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying we started playing this 4 months ago. It was a bit rough around the edges so we gave them a few months to fix the issues. Now we're back playing.There are definitely some fun things about this game, and it is polished for what it is. There are however some fundamental flaws that make this game incredibly frustrating to play. Probably the top of the list is the balance of the bosses. There is no linear scale between the entire rest of the game and the bosses. You walk through all the other enemies like they aren't there and then the bosses wipe the floor with you. That would be OK, if you could just load up on healing potions or gear up or grind. That is the fundamental issue. The gear progression is entirely tied to the bosses, and it is completely linear. So you just can't get OP and take them out. You just have to frustratingly try them over and over and over and over. There is literally only 1 set of equipment as you level up, and every character goes through them in exactly the same order. This includes weapons. The only real difference is there is a few limited choices for abilities. But the ability tree is so limited its just not satisfying. The other issue is there are so many gates that are there to slow down progress, and they end up just being annoying. They are supposed to be gameplay mechanics but they are just annoying and frustrating. Like imagine playing Diablo and not being able to teleport back to town because you have some things in your inventory that just wont' teleport. Sorry, i guess you just have to walk. They give you wolf form to go 20% faster, but you're still walking.This game is a neat idea, however it wants to play a little like Diablo but it plays more like Valheim and that's a problem. With one issue, there is no real exploration or any point to exploration. You don't get the excitement of finding cool items like you do in diablo. Or the excitement of exploring a world like in valheim. The crafting is almost cool, but then they have weird things like the floor you choose for a crafting station gives it a bonus which is really hard to do in the confines of some of these castles and given how many stations you need. I almost rage quit today, and then we decided to just edit the server settings and crank up the damage we are doing from 1.0 to 5.0. Its more manageable now, I probably won't play for much longer as having to edit the server settings to fix balance issues feels bad, and i'm walking through the trash mobs even faster now so its boring. But at least we can get through boss fights, although they are still challenging.Its not a horrible game, if we'd changed the servers settings earlier we'd maybe not be as frustrated. As it stands I probably won't play much more just because I've already passed my level of frustration.its too bad. The devs have clearly put in a lot of energy and its polished. They can still fix it. Just smooth out the balance on the bosses, and get rid of some of the artificial barriers that make it annoying. Add some gear variety, and a bit more progression to the abilities. The linear progression of Valheim doesn't work with a Diablo style game.I'll revisit this game in a year or so and if they've fixed some of this I'll change my review.

I played a solid 20 hours before i caved, and it made the game so much more enjoyable once i enabled that. I get having that setting for a pvp server, but to me it doesnt make much sense for pve servers - especially for a single player.Second is your resources/crafting times. I played up until like 35 hours in the game with normal crafting times and resource gains. Felt like it was ok but eventually it started to get to the point as a single player I was feeling like i needed to keep my game open just to let things smelt. If you are playing with multiple people you probably wont feel the need to increase resource gains, but you may still find yourself wanting to increase crafting speeds.I wont rant about bosses too much but there are some bosses that feel like you hit a wall, i'd recommend trying others if you get stuck. Especially in the second area, go ahead and do yourself a favor and beat the undead guy in the iron mines that gives you the undead shield spell.Anyways cool game like the theme a lot, just needs some adjustments made for a single player experience.

The pulmonary artery with venous blood exits the right ventricle and divides into two branches: the right one going to the right lung and the left one going to the left lung.From the site of the branching of the pulmonary artery to the aortic arch, the botall duct departs — an overgrown vessel that connected the pulmonary artery with the aorta in the embryonic period.In the lungs, the right branch is divided into three, and the left branch is divided into two branches, according to the number of lobes of both lungs.The branches of the pulmonary artery run parallel to the bronchi to the pulmonary vesicles (alveoli), and form a dense capillary network on their walls. _childDocuments_.review: After playing the Early Access, now playing the Official Release, and having a large amount of playtime, I believe the development and planning team could make this game better.Style:The aesthetic and vampire base building is the only thing that keeps me playing.However, I've wasted so much of my time and given myself extreme frustrations on this game, it's left me angry and bitter.Bosses and Environment and Minions:When playing through and fighting against the V: Blood Bosses, you'd think the developers changed the skill system after Early Access.However, you just get a point into the spell wheel that essentially does nothing. Before, you got a spell from the V: Blood Boss, but now you get a point to put that into an element tree.It's not a free point mind you, as the V: Bloods only dish out a point into a specific element.Chasing some of these V: Bloods around the map, getting killed from everything that wanders into my battles has gotten beyond annoying.Some of the boss battles rely on you figuring out how to cheese them, and if you mess up and die too often trying to figure out the patterns, you'll need to restock and repair, which costs you even more time as you now need to go back out and grind for materials.The bullet hell mechanic they're trying to make in this game doesn't lead itself to tank or fight anything up close.Some of the bosses, like General Cassius, will place his sword into the ground.However, there is a glitch to this, as his sword (which you'll need to interact with) will go into the ground and past the collision so you won't be able to hold down the 'F' key to interact with it. You'll never be able to stun him or get him out of his invincible state because of this, thus making you have to repeat the battle all over again.Ungora the Spider, spawns a bit too many spiders for you to keep the pressure on, all while covering the floor in poison.Some of the enemies on the map, and even the bosses can track your movements a bit too well.While you have to dodge around from all sides, you might have one enemy out there you didn't see, charging up it's attack. While starting the charging animation phase, the enemy will track the player until release of the skill or attack.Some enemies even have a trajectory system where they will aim at the location you're going to. It's a bit annoying, especially when you've got so many enemies you might run into at once.Character and Skills:Your character in this game doesn't get to specialize into any weapon set, or spell set.Once reaching into late game Act 2, the weapons and armor you get don't matter much and the only way to get higher tier armor and weapons is by progressing and killing the mentioned V: Bloods, in an almost linear fashion.If you get to Act 3, you won't really notice much of a change in your gear as it soon seems to not matter. Not much of an increase in stats.I would like to see a specialized build tree, instead of unlocking spells with points. If you're going to give me points, allow me to specialize into something. Don't penalize me for wanting to play a melee build, which seems to be the case here.Your character, being a vampire, can't outrun certain enemies. Like the night creature in the Cursed Forest.And when that frog and night creature tag team you, good luck, you're dead.Items and Potions:They need to change the animation time for the drinking of the potions.Some bosses will continue to pressure you, not giving you enough time to even consume the potion, as you have to wait for the animation to complete before you successfully drink from it.Then, if you get hit once, you stop healing if you even got to drink your potion.All-in-all, I think the game is cool, but it needs more polish.I know you can lower the settings and adjust things to customize the way you want to play, but I still think one big improvement would be the ability to create your character the way you want to play.Don't make me have to use the crossbow to fight enemies if I don't want to use the crossbow.Allow me to melee these bosses, and don't make me have to be cheap and find a spot to cheese them with a ranged attack.

_childDocuments_.review: Dont play this game solo... if at all.If you do you realise the games not meant to be played solo, then you realise that while this game is similar to Diablo in a lot of ways, having your own characters that migrate between servers isnt one of the similarities, strangely enough.Not being able to migrate characters is stupid, lets say you want to swap servers, if its PvP you would be worried about established players, you would think you would be able to at least rely on your unlocked abilities maybe and maybe what ever resources you can bring along to get you set up, but you dont get any of that, you have to start fresh... on an established server... I wouldnt touch PvP with a 10ft pole, youre just asking to be griefed.Balance is pretty meh, by the time you get out of the first area you realise its going to be quite the slog to get anywhere, enemies are scaling faster than your gear is, your abilities are all damage focused with no viable sustain, which makes no sense because you cant heal all your damage in combat anyway... the entire game just becomes instantly tedious once you enter the 2nd area.Talking about abilities, there seems to be no build other than damage... debuffs essentially dont work on bosses, so the most you can get out of a support character is party buffs, shields, maybe spam healing would work if you can focus on an ally, but its generally only viable to play a damage build, especially solo.Unlocking abilities through boss fights is a dumb idea... because you have "the build", theres no "oh I've levelled up, I like these end game abilities in this skill tree, I'll work my way down to them", its not like that, you dont even know what abilities you will get, and thats the same with core weapons too, so hopefully you like the 2nd and then 3rd ability unlock for your weapon, or else you just wasted your resources making it.Dont worry about the wasted weapon, I guess you can give it to the awful follower system they ripped right out of WoW:WoD, where you can send a follower or 3 out to get resources for you that takes from 8 (-10% success) to 24 (+10% success) real world HOURS, who need PLAYER GEAR to level up, and they bring back LESS resources than if you had just gone yourself for a fraction of the time, and that time DOESNT tick while the server is offline, so again if youre playing solo youre SOOL, you might have them return once before you finish (or more likely quit) the game.Also why is blood quality so rare? I dont get it, it doesnt make you incredibly powerful... except for worker blood it scales based on your own stats, so enjoy your extra 20% damage from good quality blood, on your 17 base damage... IKR its amazing, but dont worry, you wont have it long because you constantly lose blood and need to burn it to heal... you just end up getting w/e crap blood you can find, because if youre bad enough to need the bonus it gives, lets be honest, you probably wont get much help out of it anyway.Maybe if I had joined a PvE server originally I wouldnt be annoyed with the game, thats obviously half my issues with it, but thats assuming the community is good, and that there are similarly leveled characters there... honestly maybe PvP is better because constantly wrecking players until they have no base and cant afford repairs which sets them back to the beginning of the game, because I realised I havent mentioned this but theres no levels in this game, its all based on gear score, but if the players dont just quit that server from essentially bullying at that point lol, they might need help to work their way back up, IDK.This game is maybe 10 hours of solid fun, the rest of it is a roll of the dice, because it might be better if the stars align, but it might not, and who knows if they will line up for you or not, maybe you'll join the wrong server, then are you going to create a fresh character and start again on another random server?If you have dedicated friends to play with, you could probably ignore the majority of my complaints.

_childDocuments_.review: [Early Access Review]NOTE: This review is based on solo-play experience. I tried this game out largely because the popular tagline was "Valheim with Vampires." So let's get the elephant out of the room here; V Rising is -not- Valheim with Vamps. The game play focus, flow and general attitude is completely different. This is as much Valheim as Duke Nukem is Doom; Similar genre, but that's about it. V Rising is a lot more akin to ARPG's like Path of Exile or even Wolcen mechanically, with its focus on movement and  fast , flashy combat. The base building is important, but the game wants you to go out and fight more than chill and watch your fields grow. If you go in understanding this, you're going to have a blast, because the combat is spot on. This oddly feels like the kind of game the Castlevania anime would be based on (despite that being based on something else entirely). Now, another thing to address is the general notion that this game is basically done. Again, it is not. A shortlist of things that should be kept in mind if you think you're buying a finished game; - The game does a terrible job of on-boarding the player. As part of your progression, you'll be given objectives to build certain things, but those things require resources you never saw before, and have not been clued in to how to refine. You need to bumble around and sort a lot of that on your own. This is by no means a game breaking issue, and it does lead to a lot of discovery, but it's not as smooth a process as it ought to be. Expect a lot of guesswork as you move, especially in solo play. - Content with which to build your base is mixed. There's a lot to play with, but there's also a lot of stuff that's conspicuously absent. Walls being of only one height type and structural style (wallpapers aside), window and door shapes being limited, etc.  I'm fairly certain that this will be layered on as the game goes through it's EA phase, but it is a point to note. - Random glitches. Ranging from performance issues to the very random inability to load ones save. The latter problem resolves itself after a retry, but I'm noting this to point out that this is still very much an early access title, despite what some people are saying. Expect as much. So all of that aside? This game does in fact rock. Not since Dungeon Keeper have I enjoyed a game that lets you indulge your inner dark lord quite as much. Raiding villages - especially on horseback- is tons of fun, as is growing your very own dark tower to loom over the hapless farms. The game also has a fair bit of tongue-in-cheek humour, with one boss fight being especially hilarious. I wont ruin it, beyond noting that it happens in a quiet town by the farms, and plays on the classic tale of vampires targeting a woman of important lineage. All in all, the game is worth a buy, even in its early access stage. Again, just expect some rough edges, and do not go in looking for an isometric Valheim.

_childDocuments_.review: 4 out of 5 stars.I got this game for $16 and there is a lot of good in it, I still feel like I might have spent a little too much on it.  I've only played PvE.tl;dr: it's a good game with a lot of promise but is hampered by some strange choices.  Worth checking out for $15ish.  There is plenty to love but let me get the negatives out first:- Waiting: you are constantly waiting.  Waiting for the game to load the world.  Waiting for the sun, waiting for the Forge, waiting for your thralls, etc.  Waiting.  Waiting.  Waiting!- Travel: your character is too slow and things are spread very far apart.  There is a fast travel system but it doesn't allow you to carry anything on the teleporter so if you are on the other side of the map collecting iron, you have to run all the way back with it.  This is only exacerbated when you have a follower.  Not only do you have to run the whole distance but your powers are locked and you are unable to do your "cool stuff".- Unclear goals: the early part of the game feels like it is missing something to ease the player in.  You just run around, get spotted, get killed, repeat.  Once you start building a castle the goals become significantly more clear but the first few hours I felt lost and didn't really have anything to hook me.  Even laying the foundation for the castle was more difficult than it should be, IMO.  - Lacks a lot of Quality of Life: menus are clunky and confusing with construction recipes tucked away under strange categories.  No Auto-Loot pick, tons of stuff gets dropped especially during a larger fight, the "pick-up" key is bound to the "F" key which makes it very hard to pick up loot while evading.  The camera seems to work against you, maybe it is too close?  I feel like I never have a good angle of the action and end up hovering over something in the HUD that pops up and covers most of the screen.  - Not a large selection of weapons: you can use any weapon but Spears are buffed against creatures so I end up just using my spear in combat, axes for trees, hammer for rocks.  Ranged weapons are worthless, RoF is too slow, no autofire, hard to get a lock, projectiles have a slow travel speed, and the fire distance is ridiculously small.- Not a large selection of armor: that's all I have to say about that.- Early Access: in the 39ish hours I've already played I encountered one glitch that ended up having me jump off a mountain and get stuck outside the map.  Had some loot that I would have liked to have kept but it was unrecoverable, just stuck outside the game map.  Taunting me.The positives far outweigh the negatives:- Beautiful game: the world and environment are fun and filled with stuff to destroy, break, kill, loot!  - Once you start getting Vampire Powers you do feel pretty powerful.  - After learning the basics, you do feel very very overpowered, very quickly.  Once you learn to treat mobs like you would in a MOBA (kiting them out and picking them off one by one) it is a blast to drop three bandits without even breaking a sweat.- Feel like a vampire: IDK if that's your deal but I catch myself saying weird stuff like "I need to get back to my coffin to sleep", "Ugh, the sun is about to come up and I need to feed", etc.- Sunlight: the sun mechanic is a lot of fun and adds a ton of strategy.  If you stay in the sun for too long, a beam of light hits you and you start to steam/smoke for a bit before rapidly taking a bunch of damage.  The window before damage starts is long enough that I find myself slinking from shadow to shadow, hiding behind trees and buildings while I try to figure out the shortest distance across open areas.  And heaven forbid you get into combat when the sun is up, you are dodging attacks and trying to dip in and out of shadows while trying to land hits-very exciting stuff.- Castle Building: this is just a lot of fun.  Fairly intuitive, buttery smooth, and way more complex than you'd assume at first.  I have completely rebuilt my castle a few times after unlocking some new tech, or just because I wanted to make my throne room look cooler.- Compulsively Count: I just like that the developer included this (what I consider to be) fairly obscure vampire lore.  It comes from a European belief that vampires are compelled to count spilled seeds or grains.  So people would scatter rice around graves or their house to force vampires to waste time.  IDK, thought it was cute.If the length of this review is any indicator, I do think it is a good game and would recommend it.  I do hope the developer continues to work on the game and definitely hope to see QoL improvements!

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising is not a typical "Open World Survival" game. The closest comparison would be Valheim. Namely through tiered resources and tiered crafting appliances, that are found or unlocked by killing bosses (V Bloods). But it´s not as competitive and "ugly" as games like Rust for example, where you build bases to survive and progress as rapidly as possible. There are those who wish to grind hard and reach for harder regions, and there are those who spend entire days building and decorating their castle. Servers are available in pvp and pve, but i recommend pve for beginners (more on that later). The graphics and environments are surprisingly stunning for such a young game. The map is "relatively" small, but the bioms (various forests, climate regions and of course a poison swamp) and ways of movement make it feel quite a lot bigger. V Rising focuses a lot on aesthetics. There are loads of decorative items to be found and built in your castle. Your castle, aka your base, is limited in size, depending on its´ heart´s level. You can only build two hearts by default. Castles automatically degrade, unless you feed the heart ( it takes a few days). What´s left are really pretty ruins, that fade into the environment. So you dont have to worry about the whole map being filled up by ugly "dirt and metal sheet houses".Some people might not care about aesthetics, but then this is probably not the right game for you.Of course, the game has some negative aspects as well. In the beginning, there´s quite a steep learning curve. You´ll spend the first hour thinking "what kind of game is this? Is it a fantasy mmo? Is it a dungeon crawler? What should i be focusing on?". There are a set of Beginner Quests, that help you navigate through crafting, castle building, and bosses. But often enough people will ask "what´s this, how do i do that". So new players should consider playing PvE first. You can focus on exploring the world and chilling in your castle garden without worrying about getting jumped by some mid-game player looking for his daily dosis of "i´m better than someone else". More often than not, PvE-players will answer you willingly and even trade with you or help you out.As with most early access games, it has major balancing issues. The bosses go from very easy to very hard very quickly. When a clan of 4 lvl 55 players need 6 tries to kill a lvl 58 boss, you start feeling a little stupid. Personally, i enjoy it. This way you won´t finish it in a few hours - instead it sometimes takes a few hours to kill certain bosses. But many players might not expect a new take on "Dark Souls meets OW-Survival".Also, especially in mid- to late-game, it gets really grindy. Like "resources take 4 different items from 3 different regions and 4 minutes to be crafted"-grindy. All in all, it´s an amazing game for early access. Everything is pretty well thought through, there are not that many bugs, and as a bonus, graphics are amazing. While hardly comparable, it really puts the rest of 2022´s release to shame. Easily worth such a small price. But it still needs some work and could use some more variety in equipment, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is limited to my experience playing in a narrowed format, which is to say with me and a friend on a private server.This game seems to have some qualities of Diablo and something like 7 Days To Die. Emphasis on Diablo and not Diablo III, as the combat is limited, but not in a bad way. You're limited to two normal powers, a travel power (which might be better named 'evasive power', as it doesn't help you get places that much quicker, but does help you dodge attacks), and an ultimate power (which I haven't unlocked, except for the seemingly useless Howl and Roar of wolf and bear forms, respectively.) Combat isn't the only focus of the game, so I find this simple selection of abilities to be just fine. You also get to build your own castle, claiming land like something like Atlas, which I can only imagine can get very congested in public servers and violent in pvp servers. Speaking of PvP, you need to remember to sleep in your coffin when you log off, as your body will remain in the world. Allies can drag you around to someplace safe, but I'm not sure what enemies could do to you. I'm not the PvP-enjoying type, so I don't intend to find out. Overall, it's a very nice experience that tickles a few fancies, but doesn't seem to focus on any one of them in particular.Now for the bad news. The game doesn't seem to load everything it might need at once. If you or an enemy uses an ability that hasn't been used yet, it seems to lag the game while it loads those assets. Additionally, as I've just unlocked a bear-skin rug, I've found that it seems some calculations are missing. The game says it increases your speed by [movefactor], but this seems limited to these fur rugs, as the Halloween DLC carpets report 15% just fine. There's also an unfortunate thing where difficult V Blood enemies (bosses) are just roaming the roads, one that seems to be mid-game roaming the early-game area. There are also golems and treants that are significantly more difficult than the area they're in, and late-game werewolves that seem to roam the mid-game area. I'm generally fine with this, though, as it's just a lesson to pick your battles carefully and not just charge blindly around.Overall, though, I'm very happy I found this game on a free weekend, as I don't think I'd have looked into it otherwise. It's well worth the price, and I'm looking forward to what else gets added (except more cosmetic DLCs, though they're cool, too.)

_childDocuments_.review: I will start by saying that I have not tried PvP, and have no intention whatsoever to ever try PvP. Therefore, my entire review is based on playing the early access with family and friends in a purely co-op PvE format.....and the game is amazing.The graphics and decor is all so gorgeous that even a subpar basebuilder like me can make a beautiful and royal-feeling castle.The boss fights are fun and interesting and most importantly different, so it could take a couple of tries to figure out attack patterns and builds to fight each one.I really enjoy that the server is entirely customizable, so I can (and do) turn off features like being unable to teleport with a full inventory, and having servant conversation and expedition times be drastically shorter so I don't need to keep the server running. These were obviously made with PvP in mind, and since I have personally chosen not to play that mode, being able to turn these things off is a perfect solution for me.On repeat plays, I can choose to start at midtier level, with some basic resources and a few Vpowers unlocked just so I don't need to grind out the beginning of the game and can set up a running base faster. Material costs get quite steep in the mid-late phase, but that is also adjustable on server creation.Overall, this game is as sandboxy or hardcore as you want it to be. At default settings, the game is beautiful and fun, though slightly grindy, but with full customization capabilities of your server, this game is the perfect start to something great. I've played through all of the early access content so far and can't wait for more content updates.

_childDocuments_.review: "V Rising" presents a captivating blend of action, strategy, and survival set in a dark fantasy world where players embody the role of a vampire lord seeking dominance. It's a game that immerses players into a realm teeming with danger, where every decision made can either elevate or jeopardize their quest for supremacy.At its core, "V Rising" revolves around the player's endeavor to construct and expand their own castle, a stronghold that serves as both a sanctuary and a symbol of power. This aspect of the game introduces elements of city-building and resource management, requiring players to carefully allocate resources, construct buildings, and fortify defenses to fend off threats from rival vampires and other hostile entities that roam the land.One of the most intriguing aspects of "V Rising" lies in its interpretation of vampire lore. Players are thrust into the role of a vampire lord, endowed with supernatural abilities and an insatiable thirst for blood. This premise opens up a wealth of gameplay possibilities, from hunting unsuspecting prey under the cover of night to commanding legions of undead minions to carry out their bidding.The game's mechanics offer a delicate balance between solo and multiplayer experiences. While players can chart their own path through the game's vast, procedurally generated world, there are also opportunities for collaboration or conflict with other players. Whether forming alliances to tackle formidable foes or engaging in PvP skirmishes to assert dominance, the multiplayer aspect adds depth and unpredictability to the gameplay experience.Visually, "V Rising" impresses with its detailed environments, atmospheric lighting, and meticulously designed characters and creatures. The world feels alive, brimming with untold secrets waiting to be uncovered and challenges waiting to be overcome. From lush forests to desolate wastelands, each area exudes its own distinct ambiance, further immersing players in the game's dark and foreboding atmosphere.However, despite its many strengths, "V Rising" is not without its flaws. Some players may find the game's progression to be slow-paced, particularly in the early stages where resource gathering and base-building activities dominate gameplay. Additionally, there may be balancing issues or technical glitches that detract from the overall experience, requiring further refinement and optimization by the development team.In conclusion, "V Rising" shows considerable promise as an innovative addition to the survival strategy genre. Its unique take on vampire lore, coupled with its engaging gameplay mechanics and immersive world-building, sets it apart from other titles in the genre. With continued updates and improvements, "V Rising" has the potential to captivate players and establish itself as a standout title in the gaming landscape.**Rating: 8/10**

_childDocuments_.review: Fully recommended for solo or coop play.(Experience from PVP server with standard settings)Went in completely blind with 1.0 and had a blast clearing everything on normal difficulty. What a cool and entertaining game.The world and systems feel fleshed out, castle building is atmospheric and has plenty of depth. Spell and weapon customization are amazing and everything can be swapped on the fly to try something new. Stats are meaningful and easily understood.Simply just a well designed experience from start to finish.Progression: The first few hours are a bit on rails in terms of ability variety and boss order. After that it gradualy opens up with more systems, abilities and passives becoming available. The actual "endgame" in PvE allows for a variety of builds and bosses often challenge you to try other setups.Progression is tied to boss kills and connected blueprint unlocks (manufacturing leather for example). Playing solo I never really needed to go way out of my way to farm for hours to advance but I certainly took some time here and there to flesh my equipment out a bit more.Once the endgame hits, oh boy, the posibilties were really staggering at times and some skill, gem and weapon combinations were just fun to try out.What I disliked:- Horse unlock at castle tier 4 feels a bit out of place. I upgrade to T4 right before Dracula as I simply did not feel the need before nor were aware of the system - some pointers/hints would have been niceHonestly, that's about it. I had fun in my first playthrough and look forward to brutal difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising is a game about vampires. And not just any vampires, but the kind of vampires who are really into crafting. Like, really into crafting...So if you're the kind of person who loves crafting/base-building, then V Rising is the game for you. You'll spend hours gathering resources (unless you get your minions to do it for you), building your castle, and crafting weapons and armour. And you'll never get bored because there's always something to do... such as turning humans into minions. But V Rising isn't just about crafting. It's also about combat. And the combat in V Rising is pretty awesome. You can use your vampiric powers to transform into a bat or a wolf, and there are some pretty cool bosses too. So if you're looking for a game that's both fun and immersive, then V Rising is definitely worth checking out. Just be prepared to lose hours of your life to it. I give it 9/10.

Little things that tickled me that I noticed:* Grass that doesn't get sunlight because you are blocking it out with magic bone fog with wither over time. I REALLY hope this was intentional, because holy heck I was impressed.* The assets are all lovingly made, and it is easy to make castles that look like something you could find in a AAA title.* The floor tiles have randomized dirt and grime for the workshop, so it doesn't just look like repeating tiles. Had this been a full release, it would have garnered a 9/10 for me. I am so excited to see what is coming next. I'm a huge vampire lore fan, and this just hits all those good buttons for me!

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising puts an interesting twist on the resource gathering, base-building survival game. Your character is a vampire who is damaged by the sun and must either only go out at night or stick to the shadows during the day. To progress, you must kill bosses to unlock recipes for stations, materials, and abilities. V Rising's bosses are each unique in that they generally have a different specialty related to the recipe they unlock. For example, Clive the Firestarter unlocks a recipe for explosives. While V Rising's ideas are unique and the game has lots of potential, much of that potential is squandered by the game's execution. Boss fights are retardedly difficult, even with more than one player. Much of the difficulty stems from all your abilities being locked behind an animation. For instance, your character has a healing ability in which you can sacrifice some of your blood for health. However, the healing animation takes so much time that it is rendered practically useless. When your character does finally begin healing, the animation must continue uninterrupted. If you get hit, you instantly stop healing. There is also a craftable healing potion. But, like the healing ability, your character must complete the potion's consumption animation to begin healing. Also like the ability, the potion immediately stops healing you upon damage. V Rising's camera mechanics are also poor. The game's default camera controls require you to hold the right mouse button to move the camera's angle. Fortunately there is a mod that makes the game's camera functionality much better. Unfortunately, it seems that the developers can easily implement or have already implemented and are just not enabling the camera settings that the mod allows you to use. V Rising's poorly executed mechanics make progression nearly impossible at certain points. I was essentially stuck in a mid-game rut, unable to kill the next bosses I needed to progress until a friend and I discovered and began using the camera mod.This brings me to my next beef with the game. The developers have made poor choices with the game's execution, and neither they nor the game's community seem to care. Simply put, the community is AIDS. The game's official discord server has channels for feedback and suggestions. However, if you provide any even slightly negative feedback or make any suggestions that would even slightly alter the game, you will be ♥♥♥♥ on. It is unclear whether the developers are actually involved in the discord server, but if they are, they are only seeing an echo chamber affirming every poor decision they made with V Rising. To be clear, I enjoy the game overall. I love V Rising's progression system. I think the game has some great ideas. V Rising should have exploded in popularity. The only things holding the game back are its ignorant developers and cancerous community.

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising will still be good in 20 years.Its stylistic art design will remain beautiful even as technology advances. It isn't dependent on a constant influx of battle passes, microtransactions, or other infusions of content to keep it feeling fresh. It is a standalone, survival-crafting experience, blended with ARPG-style combat and well thought out boss battles. Its PVE crafting system is elaborate and intuitive. Its gear progression is natural and constant. You, the player, will never feel starved for resources or overwhelmed by options.The premise: You are a young vampire, and you need to hunt down powerful enemies to drink their blood, build your arsenal, and level up until you can take on Dracula. You are given an impossible enemy, and an expansive world you'll need to explore until you can find something to kill him with.You can do this with other players, or against them, turning what was once a straight-up survival crafting game into a tense, cat-and-mouse experience. You can do free-for-all PvP, or even allow players to group up for larger scale clan v clan battles. You can create your own servers, and tweak any setting you like to have your ideal experience. A challenging world, where you have to scrounge for every last resource to get a leg up, or a thrilling romp with abundant materials and constant combat? The choice is yours.You can customize your vampire, as well. Appearance, playstyle, castle, everything. You are the evil overlord, and the land is yours. The base-building aspect is robust without being too complex or demanding. You can maintain a very low-effort, utilitarian home base while still making it look great with little effort. Or, you can lean into the roleplay, making your sanguine manor a multi-floored monstrosity. In gameplay terms, the combat feels like a cross between an ARPG and an MMO. Fights are usually not over quickly, and your positioning is key. You will constantly be lining up shots, dodging telegraphed swings and evading ground effects while managing your cooldowns. There are gear sets to be crafted, spell gems to be farmed, and ability points to spend. All of these will allow you to create a build to your own playstyle. The build depth is not overwhelming, but your choices feel significant and will drastically affect how you engage enemies or bosses.This is a complete experience, an easy 100 hours of joyful exploration, by yourself, with friends, or even against them. The design is elegant, but deep. Easy to understand and fun to explore. The art style is beautiful, the combat is tight, the crafting is intuitive. If you like exploration, crafting, and base-building, you will like this game.Simply put, V Rising is a good game. V Rising will still be a good game in 20 years.

_childDocuments_.review: The Format of the game is an open world survival action rpg with a goal of reclaiming your rightfully owned places from the last boss of the game. The game has a good balance of Survival through the creation of your castle and combat that complements the open world.If you played Battlerite, then the combat will feel right at home but if not. Let's just say that it is engaging enough to make me actively look for hard foes to test my skills.The progression is semi-linear like Terraria where you choose which target to pursue with the goal of fighting the very last boss. And the game revolves around these core mechanics. You gain skill points by killing them and you get to choose in a set Tier which skill to unlock, allowing for a flexible build early in the game and throughout your gameplay. Getting these targets is also the way to unlock certain crafting recipes and tools to further empowers you gear or to make your Castle more better. Most bosses in the game will be in set places that make sense (eg. early boss that is a bomber can be found in a quarry) and so on. It is thematically correct and cohesive story wise. But other boss also roams and can be accidentally meet on the road and such, making for a dynamic world to play.Now talking about the bosses, they themselves are pack with cool mechanics that make you quick to your feet. All of projectiles in the game are non-homing so it gets to a point of just playing dodgeball with an enemy. Almost all of them have unique mechanics that sets them apart to each other. Making the encounter fun.There is more to talk about but all in all I will say is that this game is perfect for solo, co-op, or pvp centric players to get.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing EA for about a year or so and witnessing the full release, I can confidently say that V Rising is a shining gem in the dirt of modern gaming.The game gives you lots to do, lots of area to explore, huge amounts of options in terms of combat, a wide variety of castle building and little to no bugs.If you want to be a spellcaster, which school of magic will you focus on? Blood, Illusion, Frost, Storm, Unholy, Chaos?If you choose to be a fighter, what's your weapon of choice? Greatsword, Reaper, Crossbow? (I won't list all the weapons, you can look them up, but there's a lot of variety.)Once you've eventually chosen from the above options, where will your castle be? How many floors will it have? How will you separate your rooms? Will your forge be next to your workshop?Without a doubt the single greatest feature I've ever seen in a survival game is the ability in this one to instantly move all your resources and structures from one area to another with a couple mouse clicks. Literally everything will be transported to your new castle area should you find the old area was lacking in resources or you simply need more room to expand.The only single caveat I have with the game is the inability to change how many tiles are permitted while in the game. Once a server has been started and the rules have been set, even if you're playing solo, that's how it is. Besides that, I literally have no complaints about this game and truly think it's a modern masterpiece.Solid 9.9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks great, and gameplay is interesting, being a little more off the wall than similar games of this type. I like the combination of the top-down hack n slash game with the crafting/survival element. I have only had one CTD since playing, and no game breaking bugs or annoyances. Unfortunately i have lost heart now, because I have become fed up of the stupid Souls mechanic in the game, whereby every time you are killed you drop all of your loot and have to plod all the way back to pick it up again. Today after this happened, i resurrected but then had to answer the door and when i came back to the game I had been killed again - no problem i thought, until I realised that I had lost ALL my loot forever, it has totally disappeared and no loot marker remains any more. it wasn't just simple crafting items, there were some rare items, recipes and gear I had accumulated during that gaming session. OK, you could argue that i should have crafted another chest and kept returning to my castle to off load, but fast travel is not permitted whilst carrying loot either (!), so it makes even simple things like squirreling loot away to be time consuming and tedious. Basically the game looks great and feels good to play, and I would love to spend more time with it, but these mechanics of shedding loot when killed and being unable to fast travel whilst carrying even one item are just not for me. MANY.☐ There are pretty many☐ I didnt find one myself this far☐ It's okay☑ a fewFun:☐ It's never getting boring!☑ It could get boring after many hours☐ Its gonna get boring after a few hours☐ It isnt fun from the beginningStory:☐ There is one, but its actually endless☐ Yes, and it's good☑ A little bit..☐ Yeah, but it's bad☐ No, not really☐ It's just multiplayerSkill Level:☐ Join eSports and come again☑ Normal Gameplay☐ Hard to learn, hard to master☐ Easy to learn, hard to master☐ You just need 2 handsSearch time (only if it's multiplayer):☐ You find a match immediately!☐ There is a short wait time☐ Around 1 minute☐ Long wait time!☐ You'll find one in 30 minutes if you're lucky☑ It's server based, so you'll always have somewhere to play with players in itCommunity (only for multiplayer):☐ it's hard typing "gg" in the chat without getting called racist☐ people are pretty butthurt☐ there are some nice people after all☑ pretty nice community in total☐ you feel like you're in a church when playing this gameDevelopers:☑ The game just came out duh☐ Still releasing frequent updates☐ They could be more active☐ The game is finished☐ They ruined their own game with the updates☐ This game has been completely abandonedPrice:☑ Worth buying!☐ Only buy it if you have spare money☐ I would wait for a sale☐ No, just dont buy it.I was selected to play the closed alpha for free, and now after it came out i bought it, refunded it after not being able to get into it, and 2 days ago i bought it again. In those 2 days i played for 14 hours in total, you can imagine how that went.Compared to the closed alpha, there's a lot of things they added in. The closed alpha already captivated me and had me playing for a lot of hours, and now that it's fully out and I got into it again I'm gonna sink a lot more hours into it.You have your PvP if you want it. (You can still destroy someone's base if it's decaying though, watch out for that)So basically, everything you want from a vampire game. You have to suck out blood from enemies in order to stay alive and gain unique temporary bonuses based on the type of enemy you sucked out, you have different abilities like transforming to a wolf for speed, transforming to a human to get through villages undetected, charming enemies to make them your followers etc.You also need to avoid sunlight during the day by quickly hushing between (thankfully well programmed) shadows of trees/structures/rocks etc.You can find bosses and suck their V Blood after defeating them to gain unique new abilities and transformations.You can send your servants out to areas to scavenge for loot, you need to equip them well though in order for them to return successfully.If you want to craft resources more efficiently, you need to split and manage your castle space strategically since you have to separate your crafting machine types in rooms for them to work with 100% efficiency (which is a positive point because this is really fun for some reason)You need to feed your castle heart with blood essence in order for your castle to stay reinforced.You can start with building a little unprotected base with wooden walls, and then start with reinforcing those walls by replacing them with castle walls, which when complete will automatically turn your before-weak looking base into an actual castle with a roof and everything to keep you protected from outside influence.Very good game overall, and considering it's still in early access, this is probably gonna be a big one. I hope this doesn't happen again, I have a lot of hopes for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I review exclusively the singleplayer aspect after 6th iteration.Juicy game with great satisfaction into efficient runs. Unique mechanics allow to play with both abilities and environment making every fight exciting. Build diversity is encouraged and handy to get because fight is not always stright forward: you might need to kill fast some and totally spare some in order to get a servant or a good blood soruce.Farming is included but beware: stacking any excess amount won't pay off, on contrary, game will reward you if you manage to underrstand the threshold. To give an example: my first iterations i needed so many containers, on my 6th one i live easily with 8 small box because i can process most of resources as soon as they're collected. If anything looks a chore, then there is a better way to do it. However i reccomend to discover it by yourself.Starting over is a featured mechanic, don't be afraid to start fresh, gonna be exciting everytime. Castle building is lovely, go big and will be beautiful, or go efficient and will be beautiful too! Tips:Plant seeds (and figure out yourself the way to collect a big amount of flower with 1 hit), maybe not trees.Use coins asap: will reduce the lottery effect of discovering important recipes.Rename containers and craft station to visually see what's in there.There are no useless items (maybe clay if you're not looking into fancy deco) and none should be overstacking.Servants takes time to figure out. Worth, they can passively generate resourcesThe biggest farm is about research: plantfiber+sawdust -> paper ; paper+corase thread -> scroll ; scroll+gears -> schematics! you need tons of them to unlock all the fancy stuff. Previous tiers foundaments can be done with coins.
