_childDocuments_.review: If there were a neutral option I would select it. This game isn't bad, depending on what you're looking for in it. I played this game in a solo private server. I did this because I don't game consistently anymore and didn't want to play PVP. If you're looking for a crafting/building/exploration game this game leaves a bit to be desired. Here's what I liked as a solo player:-lots of content. This game has a lot of bosses to beat-Cool graphics. I like the art style in this game.-Combat is fun. There are lots of weapons and spells to choose from. -Bosses are fun to fight and are interesting. There are a ton of them, and I liked all of the fights. Here's what I didn't like:-lots of traveling. About a quarter way of my play through I started teleporting via console commands. You have to run all over the place. Literally every corner of the map. There is a wolf form but lots of aggressive mobs patrol the roads and can knock you out of it with one hit. At some point you can become a bat, but way too late. Even with all the speed buffs available via blood, passives, etc it still takes too long. I get that there are waypoints, but if you're carrying valuable materials they might as well not exist. -Grindy as hell. I bumped up the resource farming rates because I don't really enjoy hitting trees and rocks in this game. It can be satisfying in some games but not in this one. -Sunlight mechanic. Look, I get it. Vampires and sunlight do not mix. It does not take very long to queue up your materials and craft what you need. Once all the busy work is done, you really can't do anything important outside of your castle until nightfall. Once again I used commands to skip the day because I have better things to do than wait out some arbitrary game time. -Storage is kind of annoying. You get small chests at the start, and eventually unlock some resource specific storage which hold a bit more. That's it until mid to late game. There are resources that don't fall into any of the categories for resource specific chests. These clog your tiny little chests and there's nothing you can do about it. It's tough to say "Just skip this game". If you use commands to teleport and skip day and tune your settings just right this might be a wonderful game for you as a solo player. If you like PVP and MMO style grinds, it might be great for that too (I never plan on playing public servers). There are unfortunately too many gripes to recommend it either. If you have nothing else to play, give it a try. If you're deciding between this and another game, get the other one.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is overall not doing enough of anything fun or interesting. It's all dull. That's the best way to sum it up for me. I could really go on about almost every aspect of the game but the bigger things are such: - Combat and movement don't feel fast and strong enough. Why do you move so SLOW?!- Camera movement is awkward AF. It should just follow over your shoulder by default.  - AI is dumb as bricks. They ignore you until you are so close to them and you can even pull one of the two enemies. They both will run at you and then one will run back while the other pursues. - You can't jump and it feels like I should be able to jump on rocks and up the side of hills- There's no skill tree so I have no idea where anything goes. - The sunlight mechanic is a great idea that isn't implemented well. It started to annoy me quickly. - Crafting is boring and you're forced to do it. You are ONLY crafting your gear from what I'm shown in game- You can't put a roof on your initial building. Do I get a roof? I don't understand. So you have to use this stupid mist maker to darken the area and guess what, that takes 'bone' as fuel. And to "generate power" for the base?...that runs on blood. Wow. - The whole game a big loot / farm fest and combat and movement don't make up for it. Inventory looks like it's going to get tedious. It all feels a bit contrived. - It was almost painful to navigate the world. I got the wolf and it was lame. I want to sprint and jump. The game needs to be third person without the isometric view. Graphics and lighting are solid.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game, I'm so glad I got it on early access. The music and sound design are amazing. I love the game mechanics and how you can gain spells and do boss fights with friends. I love how each boss fight is a different unique character that requires a different approach, it's a lot of fun! However, I have two main beefs with this game. The first one, which is very simple, is that I really wish the developers added more body types. I honestly dislike the male body type, the neck is MASSIVE. What if I wanted to make a twink?? Ultimately, I wish there were more body options. Like at least one more option for gender.My second main complaint which actually impacts my enjoyment of the game, is that I hate how I'm forced through a tutorial practically the entirety of the game. It's extremely annoying. Why can't I do a small tutorial to make the castle heart then be set free on the world? If I join any game with my friends, and they've already progressed farther than me, I NEED to go through all the steps to be able to build or craft. If an experienced player gives me a recipe for a weapon from later on in the game, I still have to redo that same step later on. This very negatively impacts my experience and has made me actually stop playing the early access because my friends got so much farther ahead, and I was practically just wasting hours crafting to get through the 'steps' to catch up and not actually getting to play or have fun in the game. I expected with the full release, this issue would've been addressed along with the linear spell progression issue.Overall, I am happy I got this game. It's got a lot for it's price point. I still have a blast playing with my friends. I really wish with the full release, they would've fixed the frustration I feel with joining a game late and having to catch up to everyone else. Why do I need to build the wooden walls when my clan already has access to stone walls???

_childDocuments_.review: Time for a review on that gem.I won't go with "CONS and PROS" this time, will just share my very personal opinion on the game, as I have seen (and played) it.hope it helps you in any way :)First of all - have to note that I've played it with a friend, and on hardest available difficulty.No "googling", only "tryharding".I don't really know if it would be interesting in any other way (I'm sure it will, just can't say I've tried), but THAT way - it's a GEM.Progression is hard-locked behind bosses, which usually just pisses me off, but in THIS particular case, it forces you to challenge bosses with "as-good-as-you-can-get-NOW" equipment.It's a part of the balance.And it shines like worst tryhard bosses of Souls-like for sure XDThere where bosses we've been tryharding for a few days.You wanna win - you gotta "git gut", "minmax" what you currently have, and try, and try, and try, and try until you win XDLike literally EVERY boss's first pull goes "How you can dodge that?... This is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥..."And then, several pulls later - sweet reward of finally beating that boss XDSome require specific weapons, some - specific skills, and some even - specific "arenas" to lure enemy into.Each boss is a tactical, and skill challenge.Have to note though, that some bosses feel more challenging than the others due to boss-specific ingame mechanics. Kinda "balance issue", but not too big imho.Each boss have a story, not just nameless "bad dud, kill it". That also gives points in my eyes.Each boss, even each strong enemy - have it's own patterns, and skills, and is definitely unique in it's own way.I love that.Quite big variety of skills and weapons, and tiers, you can really tune-up "your own way", which is also really cool.Also one thing that pisses me off (usually) in games - hard lock on some aspects of the battle, like - very limited amount of dodge-skills f.e.But again, in this particular case - it's a very damn clever part of the balance.MAKES YE THINK WHEN TO ROLL BOI XDOverall - quite "OK" balance on resources, and gathering in general.Nothing that would cause severe "dam we're out of fairy tails again..." moments.Building aspects? Well, I liked the aesthetics, nothing fancy, but - cool.Not too big fan of that in general, but game sure have the possibilities to create masterpieces, if you have the patience.But most of all - THIS IS A COMPLETE, POLISHED GAME WITHOUT BUGS (at least for us, we had only 1, not too severe).IT LAUNCHES. IT WORKS. GRAPHICS ARE DECENT. NO SUDDEN FPS DROPS OUT OF NOTHING. THINGS.WORK.Like, in 2020's - that's nonsence... No one does that anymore XDJokes aside - really, I love how polished and "complete" the game experience is.Overall: I would definitely recommend for those who like tryharding, but then - it's definitely high difficulty for you, and - better bring a friend XDHappy... sucking?...

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10. Tight game design. One of the few survival-style games that actually gives you a goal and a level grind that is felt justified. Only downsides: Its better done in multiplayer and Dracula as a boss fight felt way too over tuned for it.I did the whole thing in single-player and by modifying the server to better fit my speed, ramping up the multipliers as i leveled. It's hard and I get the feeling it was built for having someone there to get you back up when you inevitably go down. Made me wish your thralls could accompany you in to fights.

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising has done a great job at creating an immersive world that nails the vibe of each of its distinct locations of Vardoran. The combat is (mostly) smooth and engaging. You can really tailor make your character to fit any play style though you may need more specific builds for some bosses. I've put a lot of time into the game and have mostly enjoyed what I've played. The following are complaints that I have regarding the game:-Without building from chests, you spend a lot of time walking around your castle, bouncing between each of your storage units. It's a much needed QOL change that would save tons of time. -Some bosses just do not feel fun to fight. You need so many spells and weapons with iFrames that it forces you to use unenjoyable builds just to get through the fight. Valencia, Adam, Dracula. -Legendary weapons appear way too late in the game. Currently fighting Dracula without having found one. By the time I do, I'll mostly be ready to put the game down.-The paper/research grind is not fun, especially when the last few items you need for a build or the weapon you want aren't coming up and instead you're being treated with castle cosmetics. -Most of the endgame content comes down to Stygian shards. These are tied to world events with one location being farmable for a small amount of them. To create endgame gear, you have to wait around just to participate in the world events to get the needed mats. The game definitely needs some balancing and QOL updates. Overall, I love the world that's been created, I love being able to experience such an expansive Vampire game, and there's been lots of content to keep me busy.

_childDocuments_.review: FINALLY this game comes out and have been waiting for seems like forever. Was able to create a character and log in with no issues then played about 1.4 hours till apparently a random person can easily destroy everything you have in PVE game mode at your castle.The only tutorials at the beginning is telling you what you need to craft for your character and then you'll be able to construct your castle but if anyone see's "red" on the walls of your castle make sure you figure out how to claim it. I had followed the tutorials that it gave but the game never told you how to claim your castle once the heart is placed. After I spent the time figuring out where to go and apparently the more north you go you'll hit higher levels and if you think the open plains are safe your wrong it'll spawn level 18 monsters there. But once you place your heart down you'll be able to pick it back up which is a good thing the developers added. But I'm a little peeved at the moment when a random person in PVE mode can destroy everything you have if you haven't claimed your castle heart.I would recommend the game for anyone to try it out but be warned that some of the tutorials and the map doesn't help much. One day when the game is fully released I'll play it again.P.S. I didn't have any game crashes nor any lag issues. Everything was set on High and Ultra settings.Laptop specs:CPU: Intel i7 10th genRAM: 16 GBGPU: RTX 2060

_childDocuments_.review: THIS IS NOT A "PVE" GAME, borderline unplayable solo, you have been warned.But it can be played PVE (solo, small group) but every mechanic and design and decision making is focused around larger servers PVP .I've had great fun with a friend progressing, building and 'finishing' the game with a couple tweaks to settings. But this game is clearly meant to be played in a "rust" style. You can feel this every second playing, to make a "satisfying" survival craft experience in PVE this game is lacking a lot of things.The gameplay loop consists of endlessly farming your current "tier" mats and kill bosses in ascending order to get their abilities (you can go slightly out of order) such as spells or new forms, which, with default settings, is an inhuman amount of ressources and thus traveling, increasing astronomically per 'tier', and yeah you gotta avoid the sun, which usually is no issue unless you try to fight bosses during day time.Obscene grinding requirements, making old school MMOs look like a casual stroll, with extremely low inventory space (stack size) and more or less semi-same spells, with identical gear (no player expression/playstyle) make this game feel like the worst parts of league of legends and rust combined, you can't even use any form of quick travel (like valheim ores) if you have any loot.The static open world is a bunch of locations (most of them 'empty' to have space for player castles) connected by tight corridors to 'encourage' PVP. In which BTW, other players can gate keep you from important core progression ressources with gear you have no chance of surviving against, since those ressources are effectively only available in ONE location (with ONE entrance) each, this isn't even touching on the fact that other castles can literally box you in with no way out.This game is extremely polished with good gameplay, i just think the design decisions in pretty much every way that isn't "controls" is going wrong. The castles are great though.

_childDocuments_.review: Its a good game. Satisfying combat and survival, interesting vampire mechanics, awesome castle building mechanics. Very glad that the world options are customisable, you can increase drop rates, damage modifiers, how long days and nights last for - the only missing option I would add would be to change the chances of higher blood qualities spawning as the grind can be quite tedious for 100% blood quality.  Otherwise, just keep adding new interesting content, improving what already exists (like what has been done with magic), and perhaps more weapons & cosmetics (both player and castle). 9/10 solid game to keep coming back to.

_childDocuments_.review: V Rising ReviewPros: - •	Fluid Combat System•	Excellent Crafting •	Tons of content for an early access title•	Large Open World with different biomes•	UI is good and information is relayed properly to the player•	Communication with other players on the server is easy •	Option between PvE and PvP•	Lots of interesting bosses who are fun to fight.•	Base Building is extremely easy and fun but more freedom could have been there.•	Great price for the amount of content you are getting.Cons: -•	Performance has to improve and changing settings doesn’t seem to affect performance that much.•	More player customization to make your character feel unique•	More Variety in Armors and Headgears is needed•	Sometimes the screen will be filled with all these effects during a big fight that it’s hard to see what’s happening.•	Teleportation mechanic sucks as you cannot teleport almost anything.•	Occasional bugs and glitches which should be expected at this point.8.5 / 10V Rising is a game that can be played for hours without getting bored. If you like games like Valheim or Diablo then this game is for you. I play with two other friends on a PvE server and we are having a blast. Playing solo is also fun but it can be grindy and some fights can be tough.Can’t wait for future updates and see this game grow. This is one of the best early access titles you can buy right now.

I was building up everything and had a wonderful base, with great servants and literal cabinets full of 100% blood of various types, and ...  all gone.  On a no-wipe server.So, I thought, OK!  I'll bite the bullet and go back to my single-player game, even though this game is not designed for single-player.  Lo and behold, they wiped that too.  What is wrong with this company? _childDocuments_.review: V-Rising is a fun game with a lot of potential. Great for co-op, and nice mechanics that allow for creativity in building and design. I think there are a handful of changes that will improve the game. These would be balancing certain enemy types/damage types, fixing hit boxes for attacks (both npc and player), balancing garlic, removing pvp inspired rules from pve worlds. The pvp restrictions come into play a lot with the transformations in game as a lot of them feel weak or useless, and some prevent you from traveling/using the ability while certain items are in the inventory. There also needs to be item-pulling from chests when crafting in the base, it feels bad not having that. Overall the game is fun, the exploration is fun, and it feels great to play with friends. I think it will continue to get better the more updates come out with it, especially QOL changes that just make the game a bit more fluent.

_childDocuments_.review: Before reading, most of my points are based on single player experience.If you want to play it with friends or on a server, don't mind my cons.It's a great survival game, currently in my second playthrough due to the update.It does many things right, I would really recommend it to you.But there are still things I don't really enjoy: It is multiplayer oriented in a very heavy way:The combat feels like it's optimised for multiplayer. You do have a dodge with a cooldown (5-10secs), but for the PvE experience it just isn't very effective. This is fine if you're playing with others, but if you try to beat a boss alone there wil be unavoidable damage. For the most parts it is not that bad, but if you're unlucky you simply die to this.To be honest, you can plan fights very, very precisely, use strategies to beat enemies with nearly no damage and everything, but this is where the other big parts plays in: Grinding.Grinding is the key gameplay loop. Grinding is everything you will do in late-game. You want to have a full new armor set? Grind. You want to have better servants? Grind. You want to get the best equip for a boss, as he needs a specific weapon to be easier? Grind.Early to mid-game it is not that bad, but late-game is pure hell, where you grind hours and hours to get a single new entry in the athenaeum. And there are ~50(?).I honestly like grinding in every game, idk why, so I don't mind it.BUT, and this is the biggest con, the game is affected by realtime.Smelting any bar takes times, later on way, waaaay longer than you would like.Servant hunts take 23 hours. Yes. This is ridiculous. Late game can and will be "wait x hours to progress", and that is the worst mechanic in most games, if its present. It will take your entire flow and you'll loose motivation, as it happend on my first playthrough, where I just wanted the best armor for a single servant. And to be completely honest: I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hate the mid/end-game v bloods. The difficulty in this game is so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ artificial, it just isn't fun anymore. Bosses spam attack after attack which are impossible to dodge, enemies randomly respawn during boss fights, even though you cleared them a minute ago, sometimes they just run away randomly, loosing aggro and healing. Beating bosses doesn't leave with you the impression you actually did something, you are just happy this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of a fight is over. They don't feel fun, they don't feel fair, they feel like "oh, hopefully you have others with you to fight this clearly 2-4 player oriented mess of high dmg AoE attacks, which you cannot possibly dodge."Straight up disappointed with this. They aren't hard to be hard, they are unfair to be fought with others.This is NOT good game design.TL;DR its a great game, though it is set for servers and servers only. If you want to play it alone, don't.If you want to play it with friends, go get it, its worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this with my friends and with what's currently available, it was worth it's cost. V Rising's main draw for me was its combat system which works similarly with games in the MOBA genre with its limited ability keybinds and focus on dodging and positioning. Choosing your combat abilities already offers a lot of choice; adding to it is the blood system wherein the blood you ingest gives you buffs depending on what type it is and how potent it is. Adding to this is the very interesting sunlight system wherein you have to rely on shadows to avoid getting burnt during the day.V Rising's other systems are decent. Building is very simple, though the menus are a bit unorganized for my tastes. It's simplicity means that there isn't much creative freedom though; maybe adding options such as more floors or even underground levels may increase the creative possibilities of the game.Its main drawback in my opinion is the grind involved in the game. A lot of materials are needed to keep your equipment up to date, especially since repairing them isn't free. What compounds this is the difficulty of transporting resources around the map. There are restrictions when it comes to teleporting materials across the map. Namely, you can't really use the waypoints when carrying most of the resources. You'll have to rely on horses and need to spend a few minutes just hauling yourself back to base whenever you try to gather resources. Another point of frustration is how long crafting can take. There were times where we just leave the server on while we wait for things to be crafted.Of course, the game allows you to modify this (although some of the sliders don't work properly). Removing the teleporting restrictions, increasing the yield, modifying sunlight hours are just some of the options available. Now, there is probably a debate if you're removing the challenge of the game by doing this; but that debate is for another day.Regardless of all my misgivings, this is very much worth the cost. It's really polished and rarely had any bugs when we played. Hopefully, the developers would build on this foundation with more updates as this goes through Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: Game Start(0-10h)- +Fun, easy to learn, clear quest line with achievable goals and realistic requirements.Getting Started(10-20h)- +Base building is by far the best of any game I have ever played. +Organization is optimized to a point that you only have to spend about 3 minutes at your base to offload   and head out again (INCREDIBLE). +Quests continue normally with no break in timeline for gear requirement.Heating Up(20h+)- +Gear progression gets more difficult, fighting enemies becomes slightly more challenging due to gear score   being generally lower than enemies since unlocking the next set of gear is barred behind a boss fight which,   personally, I like a challenge, so this is great for me. My friend however, did not like this because he was   constantly dying in boss fights being that he is not an avid gamer. +Travelling about the map starts to become a bit more time consuming and plays a role in how you spend   your time at your base. +Base building gets an upgrade with a second floor and many more work stations to fill up your rooms. +Chests (Storage) progress very well, just as I feel that I am running out of space a new upgrade for chests   drops from a v blood. Overall, one of the best games I have played in the last 10 years. Please keep the content coming and consider adding a few more side line requirements to break away from v blood hunting and castle building. Great job.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't particularly care for survival games, or vampire themed entertainment.... but V Rising has made me completely forget about those reservations, and I'm enjoying it immensely. Which is fine, especially since there's plenty of decorations you can acquire in the base game, it feels more like supporting the developers than being squeezed for cash at every opportunity. The game play itself feels smooth, has lots of build variety depending on what weapons and skills you choose for your character. You can also transform into different animals, like the wolf for faster travel or the rat for hiding. You can glammer human npcs and then turn them into your minions to protect your castle. Oh yeah, yuo can build a castle, and a damn big one at that.For $20 this game is a steal, and it's no wonder that in a week of it's launch, with relatively little to no fan fare on arrival, the game has already sold over a million copies.

I was also pleased to find that the game is quite challenging, without being overly difficult. Overall, V Rising is an excellent game, and I would highly recommend it to any RPG fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. I am vampire. Mostly came for the building and ended up Getting Good just so I could unlock all the cool stuff for my castle.  Gameplay is fun, challenging and the rewards feel so so sweet when you get them. It's still Early Access but I had no issues with running the game AND there's loads of content. I played solo on a private server so no knowledge of wider online/public experience, but this made it mostly a chilled out building and resource management game which I could break with occasionally to do awesome action vampire ♥♥♥♥ like turning into a bat or suckin blood or ripping through 10 guardsmen and watching them explode in a shower of viscera. Teenage goth self approves. 100% would roleplay Castlevania again.

_childDocuments_.review: Needs adjustment for private play, to have server settings available even after you made the game or just have servants convert in less than 2h.Online play feels bad, you never know if a server will shut down and have all your progress go down with it and as I have already mentioned singleplayer isnt really a solution either... _childDocuments_.review: A very well thought and well executed vampire survival game. Does not feel like an early access game at all, it is filled with content and is quite polished. _childDocuments_.review: BOOOOOORRRRRIIIIIINNNNNNGGGGGGGI Much rather NOT go to work in a video game after I get home from work. Collecting, crafting, only to unlock more collecting, crafting is a lame cycle of tedious boredom. Sure, some of the mechanics are cool as you are playing a Vampire, however this is easily overshadowed by the amount of tree chopping, stone working, and base building you HAVE TO DO. _childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: After 100+ hours in this game, I managed to beat all the bosses, made the bloodkey, and finished the game with all 3 soul shards. Built 2 castles with 250 tiles maxed each, designed, etc. rare servants strong weapons. Everything there was to be offered, I explored.So how was the experience? Bit grindy I must say, but it was a pleasure. The crafting was tough, specifically getting the scourge stones for dark silver. I ended up putting my workers to gather the scourge stones mainly, but eh. The game itself was insanely fun, with each boss fight feeling unique. I spent 9 hours on the gonecrusher or whatever his name is. 9 hours of constant defeat until i realized that you can just use a reaper to go invis everytime he does his ult to buy precious time.The atmosphere of this game was my favorite however. With the ability to not teleport with items, it forces you to go out and explore the map, coming across cool things such as rock golems and tree ents or what they are called. wild wolves that give you 100% creature along the way are a gem, giving you sun resistance if you need it.Each main boss fight, gone crusher, solarius, and winged horror was insanely challenging, specifically for me who decided to do this all solo. But it IS possible, with preparation. The soul shards you obtain are very good as well giving you a much-needed boost for fights. This is only early access too, and Im very impressed with it so far. It's not overwhelming and the game is plenty of fun. Unfortunately about the castle feature though. 1 story castle looks like poop from above in bat mode. But the devs also realized this and will release a multi-story castle feature in the future. I'm looking forward to everything the devs will have to add to the game. Money was well spent here. A more in-depth story would also be nice. It's clear that there is the foundation to some lore here. All we can hope is that this game goes well.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Day Three of V Rising:I have abandoned any hope of going back to civilisation. It might be better to lose all hope now. My dark room is has only one source of light that shines onto my face and fills me with a mixture of joy of and pain. It is now hours after midnight. The labour of the burning sun starts soon, but I cannot stop. I don't want to stop..
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun, great theming, love the combat mechanics. Versatility and flexibility of play-style is exciting with the mix of weapon base stats, weapon abilities, dashes, offensive/defensive spells, potions, and ultimates. Fast travel is effective, but doesn't make the world feel small. Castle building offers much more than expected. Boss fights are all very different and challenging, but not brutal if you have the right gear/abilities/potions active. Not a whole lot to the plot/story of the world it seems, but what there is is interesting.Looking forward to more and more content as the developers move forward with the potential of V Rising.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best put-together, well balanced RPG's I've ever played. You feel each gear improvement. There's no "boring grind" spots in the game, always something to look forward to that's close. They're adding QOL changes such as minimum blood quality on elite enemies to increase chance of finding that 100% blood type, genius as this doesn't effect gameplay at all. ONLY saves time running around the map hunting that needle in a haystack. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: Not my type of game. Should really emphasize in the description that this game is %90 gathering resources to craft stuff.You're a newly awakened vampire.  You have but one goal:  Hit things in the environment with different weapons to gather wood and rocks to make better things until you have access to different things to hit with a weapon for 9 hours so you can make the next another thing.Repeat. This is... V RISING
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenominal in every way. The gameplay is so innovative and fun, it scales really nicely, the graphics are beautiful, and it's so easy to come back to over and over. I really hope they add some customization to the servers so I can turn the wait times on resources way down on my pve server with friends.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this game before launch and I'm really happy with the end result. I'm returning back to it with pleasure.The combat mechanics are really great and lots of options to change things up.The survival part is not as advanced as other survival game but good enough to scratch that itch. You can build a very nice castle fairly easily and the grinding of resources can be outsourced to your Thralls. Like most survival games the story and game lore is minimal. However since this is a vampire game they could add to it. It's not why you would play that game and come back to it but it could increase the audience.The game is really well balanced. There is a lot of things to do and it doesn't feel too repetitive. Boss fights are forcing you to improve your equipment and skills naturally.The game is very well polished and performed as expected. Only one or two quality of life items could be added but I'm nitpicking. I'm on my 4th play through and nothing is game breaking.I mostly played solo and with friends PvE.

_childDocuments_.review: I am one of the weird non pvp players who plays on a solo server. This review is for other weirdos who do the same. The game is playable solo and is fun to build and gather resources. As I got closer to end game, I did notice where that fun was going to end. If playing solo, once you get through all the bosses, there really isn't anything else to do other than make your base look nice and run around repeat killing bosses that made me mad at earlier levels. Basically waiting for the next update to release with more bosses and map to explore. If this was just a solo game, the time it takes to get through everything is solid. I give it 9/10 with the missing point just being that it would be nice for something to be made for solo servers for a forever type play similar to the pvp servers. Do not buy this game, look for alternatives as there are many others much more worth of your time and money, And I say this after having over 30 hours of both co-op and single player game experience where both modes failed to deliver (co-op more than anything).

_childDocuments_.review: Love how this game does PvP. It feels very fair for casual players (unless you're playing the hardcore mode) while still having some consequences to PvP. The Bosses, the way you level up, the castle management, the different biomes. It's all really fun. And with the release coming out soon all of this will be expanded. When I think of a living a Vampire fantasy I think of this game. This game is a good example of just trying to design something fun rather than addicting.

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks for free weekend, but no.At first glance there are lots to do and progressions looks interesting you do quest and something is unlocked.. but then it just say "go kill V blood bosses".. and there is nothing to do, really, only to go and kill bosses "very far" away. Fun? Not for me. Coupled with certain game mechanics it's a no from me.+ Polished game, music, atmosphere, surrounding.. cool.+ Huge map, many enemies, lots of loot.- The fast travel is VERY limited, many resources prevent from fast traveling.- Navigation is HARD. On purpose. So that experienced players learn map and shortcut. But I am not experienced player and and sorry, no way I'll become one with such terrible navigation in a forest maze.- Loot disappears. NO way to stack loot nearby and come later.- Constant inventory micro-management, so many items, long trip to base, empty, go fight, full again.. ><- Sun mechanics is at minimum VERY annoying. I hate days. I can't skip them.- Just one base and huge map with limited fast travel.. you got the idea? LOTS of running.- Combat is just meh. It demand to all time run away/aside and way too limited: 2 spells and 2 weapons skills (no idea what is ultimate).- Base building is.. meh. Many crafting stations, very slow processing.- Moving around is slow. I've got wolf form, but it takes time to become a wolf, no hotkey, so terrible.Game is trying to just waste my time for something I don't want to do, but I have to: producing rats (1 every minute) to craft healing things, running around, slowly, mining/chopping, avoiding enemies marked with skull... there are too many of them, patrolling or sitting at certain spot, I couldn't build my base further, because there is a golem, whom I can not kill. Nice? Nope..Blood mechanics I don't understand. I want to get bonuses, so I start eating only one type of enemey.. and no progress. I don't want to google AGAIN for tutorial explaining game mechanics, such explanation SHOULD BE inside the game, because it's IMPORTANT.After playing a bit I got boring, 0 interest in pvp, 0 interest to run and fight next V blood boss and otherwise I am stuck with progression.. Sigh.. I'll go play some other "open world" or "base building" game.. sorry.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing with 3 friends on a Official PvP server. Got to power 20 in 2hours.Fun things:Tons of available land/plateaus to base on.Combat is fun with cool "class" building by unlocking spells and certain weapon specials (need higher tier weapon)Easy to learn with a quest/tutorial system on the top left of your screen.Voice chat is awesome, cant go wrong.Graphics look nice.World is huge.Tons of different enemies.Wild enemies fight other types (hunters will fight the wild wolves as example)Things that are kinda meh:Cant move camera to get a nice look at your character/s and friend/s. Would be awesome for screenshots.Some stuttering if you keep that AMD setting too high (i have a 1070, 7 1700 and 16gb of ram on SSD)Conclusion: Worth the 20$ and great with friends. _childDocuments_.review: From the little pve Ive experienced, it felt really tiresome and boring. There seems to be enough customization to balance the game out to your preference, and the controls are actually pretty decent, but still, overall extremely tedious gameplay. Cant explain, but felt like an extended/improved version of some mobile game.
_childDocuments_.name: V Rising

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say that I expected a little bit more PvP oriented game. The game is grindy and you will find yourself trying to gather and find materials all the time. The game is very similar to rust in how you interact with other players, building your own stuff and grinding the resources to build bigger and better things.PvE:Fun, sometimes challenging. You need to pick your fights wisely. Depends only on gear level. The more you grind, the better you will be at smashing common NPC units. Even bosses are not a problem if your gear is good enough.PvP:Lacking depth. Big plus for Battlerite-like fighting. Everything is a skillshot. There are escape skills.PvP requires a grind. You need to unlock skills and gear. Get ready to get destroyed by people with many levels more. They do more damage, they have more skills and are tankier. I don't understand the part where you can't have skills. It's impossible to fight when you have worse and less abiltiies. Even running away is hard if you don't have a form yet (wolf for example). PvP is not pay to win, but the more time you put in, the more you can do. That destroys the beauty of this game for me. PvP should be fair and balanced.Conclusion: Good game. Good for casuals. Not so much for PvP, skill based oriented players. I am looking forward to PvP oriented modes or incentives as this is what game lacks the most. It will get boring as a grindfest.

name: Dune: Spice Wars
detailed_description: This is your desert, your Dune. Lead your faction and battle for control and dominance over the harsh desert planet of Arrakis. Spice is the most valuable resource in the universe. The spice extends life, expands consciousness, and makes interstellar travel possible. Found only on Arrakis, it is sought by the most influential forces in the Imperium… Scan the landscape for wormsign or risk losing your troops and spice harvesters to colossal sandworms who will burst through the dunes to devour them whole. Crush your opponents in combat, best them through political intrigue, and undermine them with your network of illusive spies. Experience the unique Dune universe, one of the most influential sci-fi settings ever created. Lead your faction to victory with iconic characters, such as Duke Leto Atreides, the Baron Vladimir Harkonnen, the Padishah Emperor Shaddam IV, Esmar Tuek, and Liet Kynes. Stay alert as opposing factions seek to gain the upper hand and the planet itself threatens with vast deserts, huge storms, and the dreaded sandworms. 4X in real time. Balance open warfare, subterfuge, political influence, and economic supremacy to prevail and gain control over the most important planet in the universe. Use secretive agents to sabotage the plans of your opponents. Vote on political resolutions in the Landsraad to further your strategy. Or dominate your opponents by overwhelming them with an all out assault. Explore Arrakis with ornithopters to discover resources, villages, and points of interest. Expand with your troops to take control of regions. Exploit the resources through buildings and spice harvesters to dominate the economy. Deploy your spaceships and aircrafts to exterminate your enemies but beware as outright aggression can have high political repercussions. Embark on a strategic journey where you can choose the path of honor and politics or embrace violence and deceit. Choose from various factions with unique abilities and playstyles. Each faction can be customized by selecting councilors who enhance their strengths and mitigate weaknesses. Whether you choose survival tactics, shady dealings, military might, or dominating the spice trade, there is a faction and councilor combination for every player's preference. Explore the possibilities and shape your own destiny on Arrakis. Conquest mode. Take control of one of the major houses and fight through a number of unique scenarios and situations. Personalize your starting house with a variety of perks and upgrades to tackle the many challenging objectives of the Conquest mode, ensuring you a unique experience every time you play. Band together in 2v2 matches or face each other in a free-for-all of up to four players. Tailor the parameters of your multiplayer match to your preferences, including AI difficulty, map size, victory conditions, sandworm aggression, storms, and number of Sietches. Team up and try different faction combinations to identify synergies and dominate Arrakis.

_childDocuments_.review: Dune: Spice Wars is a 4X/RTS hybrid set in the Dune universe. Developed by Shiro Games and published by Funcom released on steam and only available on PC at time of release. You take control of one of 6 possible factions in a variety of game modes as you attempt to take control of the planet Arrakis. As always the first question we as is if Dune: Spice Wars is worth the 35$ asking price. I am happy to say the answer to that question is yes for me.    Shiro Games maker of Northgard, Wartales and Evoland showing off they can make a 4X/RTS hybrid game. With great music, good control, interesting tech trees with each faction having unique techs, and great graphics that run smoothly. Spice Wars allows you to find a faction you enjoy and play to your hearts content. With three different game modes (Duel, Battle, and Conquest) there are a number of ways to play. Controls are responsive and allow for smooth control when needed. The RTS element is more tactical then click fest and means you can use actual tactics to turn the tide of battle. In addition with world effects such as sand storms and yes the giant sand worms affecting the RTS side it means not only do you have to worry about your enemies but the world Arrakis having an effect on your game as well.   The three modes offered are Duel mode which is just a 1v1 vs AI, Battle which is a FFA vs AI, and Conquest is a risk style semi story driven mode that sees you attempting to take of territories and take over Arrakis. While the Duel and Battle modes allow you to use any of the 6 factions, Conquest limits you to only 4. In addition while the Conquest mode is enjoyable with some unique ideas. All the factions have the same goals. This can be a bit jarring when both the Atreides and Harkonnen want to make friends with the Fremen, even though traditionally, the Harkonnen want to kill all the Fremen.   Luckily each faction gets unique bonuses and unique techs in the tech trees. This means there is enough replay ability to easily get 60+ hours out of the game. The only other downside is that there is no cinematics outside of the intro one to the game. While not a game breaker, it is like I said disappointing.   All in all I found the game easily worth the 35$ asking price, and would highly recommend you give the game a try if you’re a fan of 4X, RTS, or just the Dune universe in general.

It looks lovely and I live the overall look and feel of the game.Its pre release so still has come kinks to work out but its definitely ready to play. It is sufficiently different from other games to earn its niche. Don't buy it expecting it to be an upgrade of the original. (If you can remember that far back).

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game. I love it. It's challenging, but not hard if you don't want it to be and its just right for anyone who is new to the RTS genre (like me) and doesn't expect the same pacing and ideas found in games like starcraft (II). It takes the amazing story and concepts from the books and obviously the movie (that which probably prompted the creation of this game) and does a pretty decent job of making them work for a game. Just right for a first RTS game, can increase in difficulty as you gain more skill Beautiful UI. Amazing stylized landscapes. Practically perfect. Icons could need some work though. I stuck with it and eventually came to realize it has a serious problem. The world has events or "natural attacks" such as revolts, sand worm attacks and rebels attacking random cities. At the same time the enemy A.I. also makes their own decisions and attacks you at what seems random. However as you progress you will soon find that the "world events" and all the enemy A.I. are on the same team.. As soon as i attack someone, i get back doored at the same time by another A.I. team. Whats worse is countless rebels will attack or sand worms at the same time i have battle elsewhere. The timing is very noticeable and to me it just feels lazy. Why not just say its you vs everybody instead of making it sound like its 4 unique teams + world events, because its not. Very lazy a.i. imo and the a.i. always has the advantage. Im sure there are some crazy ways to push through but just starting on normal difficulty and having the entire world rip you to pieces at the same time of all the a.i. teams didnt really feel right. _childDocuments_.review: I finally finished my first game of Dune Spice Wars after five failed attempts that I started and abandoned (I had to reduce from three to one opponent and reduce the AI ​​difficulty and it still wasn't easy).For an Early Access, it's pretty round and I haven't caught any significant bug.Strategically for me was a breath of fresh air. Some people may think as another installment of Dune 2, where you build a base, mine a huge amount of spice, and use it to build hundreds of troops...it´s not (even because building troops and maintaining them is very expensive). In the end game, I should have about eight troops.The idea here is different. Instead of a full open war, you need to gradually expand your influence over Arrakis, conquering villages, building structures that will help you increase your hegemony and resources, and finally defending them with militias.The game offers several options for victory. Destroy the enemy base (a huge task), reach 25k hegemony (the victory condition I achieved), remain as governor of Dune for 60 days (controlling a good part of the territory), and even use agents and infiltration to assassinate the enemy leaders.The game has other interesting mechanics that you have to pay attention to as you try to expand and defend your territory. You can participate in Landsraad council audiences, using your influence to vote on propositions that can give you some benefits (or harm opponents). You can infiltrate agents in different forces of this universe to gain benefits and even create espionage operations that can help you on some occasions. (I used a cease-fire to buy some time and bring more troops to a battle), developr a tech tree, paying a montly fee to the emperor, control rebelions and of course evading the storms and sandworms that can swallow your best trained troop in a blink of a eye. The game give you four houses to choose from, each one with their own quirks and flaws and differents styles o play. I eager to try a new house after my victory with the Atreides.Overall it's pretty cool game with a lot a thing happening at the same time. Dune Spice Wars requires patience, perseverance and a little bit of lucky, a perfect analogy for the desert you have to face. The game still in early acess and I just can´t wait to see what surprises the final version will bring us.Long live the fighters.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews, but I it's been a long while since I played a RTS I enjoyed, let alone a Dune game. I grew up on all the Command & Conquer games, Starcraft, Starcraft II, Dune 2000, and have played many other genres throughout the years.Dune Spice Wars isn't focused on building one or two bases and amassing an army or zerging to win through combat like a traditional RTS. That's not the point. It's more slow paced and methodical, with a variety of win conditions (4X). You can win through traditional combat, or by using agents to infiltrate your opponents and assassinate them, winning politically through Governorship, acquiring points (Hegemony) through objectives, or by holding the majority of CHOAM shares. If you try to brute force a base, you're going to lose a lot of units and probably won't be successful. Instead of building up one or two main bases, you capture villages which provide various perks and let you customize your resource control. The main bases have upgrades which cater to your play style. Each faction also has its own perks, so this is important if you want to do things like build mechs or ally with the fremen who want to trade water. There's also tech trees, and various agents which let you choose what resources you want to acquire first.That's a basic summary of the game. If you ever wanted to play an RTS where you had multiple win conditions aside from pure combat, this is for you. For example, you could truce your opponent, then infiltrate their villages with agents before ultimately setting up an assassination. Alternatively, you can aggressively dominate the map and amass resources so you can buy out all the shares. There's a lot of flexibility in play style. My only nitpicking would be the mesh and graphics could be better and more well defined, like in SC II. The graphics do look great, but the units are kind of basic when you zoom in. There also isn't a campaign or story. Funcom could easily fix that by expanding upon the conquest mode (territory control with objectives) and adding cut scenes and dialogue before sending you to the next mission area. There's a lot of potential to be even better, but it's pretty fun as is.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access April 2023 Review:The good:The game is incredibly atmospheric, with high end graphics and pleasing background soundtrack.The Bad:But that's about it.The game, at onset appears to present significant depth and interest with various mechanism of control and avenues to victory. However, as you begin to master the elements of play you realize that a lot of this is a facade. Combat is not well balanced at all, and lacks any sort of impact whatsoever. While the adage applies "Don't fight a war on two fronts" this game forces you to literally corral most of your army into a spear and attack and defend en masse. These skirmishes are of minor impact, as truly as long as you turtle well and amass the technology to increase your defensive turrets you can sustain yourself until a victory condition is achieved. Unit pathing is atrocious and large armies suffer the same overlap problems as Northgard did. Micro is nonviable in active combat. Armies path into the deep desert on a whim and are lost due to supply issues. Replacing fragile units takes *time*, so losing skirmishes to random unit loss usually waiting a long time to build up again, because often your opponent can't threaten you that well either.The intelligence / spy system seems of great benefit until you realize the rate spys are acquired, brutal RNG for success and the fact that you're better off slotting them in for their economic/control bonuses.The Landsraad is minimally impactful, with the randomizer presenting with little opportunity for strategy. You ability to alter or control resolutions as you gain power makes this forgettable as well.Spice collection is not intensely rewarding and dangerous, but rather banal and your spice gathers can be (mostly) automated. The threat of failing to meet your spice delivery plays a part of minor economic victory. Similarly, Worms whether in combat or spice collection are more a nuisance than a thing of legend to be feared and respected.Build economic production early, push to cap and you'll find yourself with more authority and resources than anyone can feasibly challenge mid-late game. A strong economic pushes the CHOAM victory out of reach of other players as you can use your surplus Solari to manipulate the markets. Hegemonic victories are a minor threat as your great wealth affords you all the room you need. Eventually, certain resources become "obsolete." For example, plascrete in particular is useless after you've established a foothold. With no market, or exchange systems really in place at the moment this further limits strategy or trading.Research trees make... minor sense? But there's no real way to easily increase / trade tech and research a meaningful amount. You can enter into any number of agreements but like a lot of this the major influence it has is essentially to sue for peace. More frustrating, it appears there is no way for allied victory, it is winner take all *only* meaning your alliances are essentially set pieces in the facade of diplomacy in this game. AI cheats rather than gets better, requiring human opponents at the moment for fair play.Shiro games appears to not have really learned any lessons from Northgard, which is another game that appears to have gotten the same surface level treatment. Systems are set in place, pleasingly appropriate to the lore and at first glance appear more complex than they actually are... until you realize there there is very little variance in strategy and whether purposefully or not, appear to have very little attention paid to their balance. A lot of both works speaks of passion, but little in refinement, and an unwillingness to spend the time necessary to build a fully fleshed 4X. This results in long, boring and repetitive game sessions with unfortunate unbalancing elements popping up in later patches and dlc. This is something that be rectified with more time and attention spent to the systems in place and that they are modifying or opening this up with mod tools/customization to allow the community to take these rough cut stones and polish them into gems.Given that Northgard's strategy was to present an unfinished game, and "finish" it through dlc purchases - I honestly can't recommend that you purchase this until final release reviews come out. Time will tell whether the valid criticisms (look at the reviews) are taken seriously, or whether they intend to milk cash out of extended development on a framework with potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Dune is not a game of subtlety. It’s a 4x real-time strategy game, where you lead your faction in an attempt to create the most powerful, vast, and (mostly) mutually exclusive empire in the entire galaxy. It’s a cross between Civilization and Starcraft where war, espionage, diplomacy, and sabotage are the core tenants to success and survival.As the leader of one of 4 factions, you must lead your armies and battle for control and dominance over the harsh desert planet of Arrakis. Your greatest resource is time as it leaves traces on everything you do. You must choose between immediate actions, or making better use of it with research or building improvements. Opposing AI factions will fight to defeat you and take what is yours.Story Plot -In Dune Spice Wars, The players take control of one of the several factions that are vying for control over the planet Arrakis and its precious spice. The spice is a drug that makes interstellar travel possible, but it also expands consciousness and extends life; it's the most valuable resource in the universe. The planet Arrakis, which is also known as Dune, is the only place in the universe where the spice can be found.Gameplay -Players start with a base and some troops and harvesters that they can deploy onto the board to collect spice or attack other players' units. Players also receive cards that grant them special abilities or let them cause trouble for their opponents. Each faction in the game has a special ability that makes it unique--for example, House Atreides increases their ability to use spies when they're not holding any spice. After setting up a network of harvesters and troops, players can launch attacks against each other to take over more territory or steal their opponent's spice, but there are no dice rolls during combat; rather, all combat is determined by adding up power points from various sources and then comparing them to a combat table on the board. During gameplay, players can also negotiate alliances and trade resources, though these deals are not binding so they may be broken or renegotiated at any time, depending on how the game progresses.Key Notes -If you're after a spiritual successor to Dune 2000/Dune 2, then please don't buy this. This is not that game and the developers were not just going to jump into making what people expected. It would've been poor PC ports and poor gameplay, and no one wants that. If however you are like me and want a slicker game that captures some of the political elements (through trading with Houses/Species, or by forcing them through War), then you might find this game enjoyable.Pay attention to every notification or else you will miss out on a trade opportunity or something even better.Time management is crucial in this game, every second matters so make sure you have a plan in motion.The most important thing in the game is the spice. You need to harvest as much of it as possible to win, which means placing your spice harvesters on tar pits in the desert. However, you also need to protect them from sandworms, which can pop up at any time and devour your harvesters whole.The game has a few different paths to victory: crushing your opponents in combat, besting them through political intrigue, or undermining them with your network of elusive spies. It’s best to choose your faction wisely and pick the right set of counselors to assure your success .Conclusion -While the game will certainly take a serious amount of time to play through, if you really like a challenging strategy game that requires some creativity from you to succeed, you will likely enjoy Dune. It takes some straightforward concepts from other games and puts it in one package that is supremely fun. The classes for the units are unique enough to make them feel different even though the names may resemble something similar in other games. The game is easy to pick up and difficult to master.Pros -Great graphicsSimple combat mechanicsDune Inspired universe ( not a spiritual successor though )Cons -Too many notificationsThe Political influence at times feels overpoweringToo many resources to manageIncredibly Slow Paced to the point that 1 playthrough will take at least 3+ hours or even more which is not feasible for everyone.Overall Score - 7/10

Anyway, this is a great game with lots of replay value, and I'm really looking forward to see it in final release.
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing RTS even in Early Access! It still lacks in content and depth imo for being a Dune game (so much lore and the potential to customize units are vast), but this is fine in the current EA state. The game right now is very solid and I can recommend it at full price. It pays homage to the OG Dune RTS (father of all RTS games) and does so splendidly! Faction balance needs tweaks, but it isn't terrible as of right now. If you're a fan of Dune this is a must have in your library and if you're a fan of RTS games and never played the DOS Dune then this is a great game to pick up to see a modern take on what actually started RTS games as we know today.
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

Sadly, Shiro Games/Funcom showed a spectacular lack of solidarity with the victims of war: not only the game hasn't been pulled from the Russian market but it's actually cheaper to buy it in Russia than in Ukraine! _childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: So far, this game is amazing.  I'm a fan of both 4x games and traditional, competitive RTS games - and for early access, Dune: SW is amazing.That being said, while I understand the reasoning of not adding more combat units given by the developers in that they don't want to overwhelm players with a ton of units when there are so many other things to keep track of - I do believe there need to be more units in general.  Mechanized units, ariel combat units, exc.  Dune: SW isn't nearly as complicated as some 4x games, and I think that the belief of "we expect players to be overwhelmed if we add additional units" discredits player's capability in handling Dune's systems.
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: Dune Spice Wars is a excellent mix of a RTS and 4x game with more focus on macro than micro. That is not to say there is no micro in the game, but I feel the macro in the game far exceeds the micro.As for what the game is, you pick one of 6 factions in either a 1v1 mode, a 4 player map that can either be FFH or teams, and a conquest mode which is Shiro campaign mode. Then you start out with a base and then expand your borders to nearby villages you want to get control of using authority and like other 4x games you have other resources you will want to increase such as water (food upkeep for buildings), energy (upkeep for many things), Plascrete (used for buildings) etc. There are several victory conditions in this game too which is expected for a 4x game.The factions themselves play differently from each other and they really spice (see what I did there) up the game with which one you pick. Overall I would highly recommend the game to fan of 4x games and I think this is an excellent Dune game. I can’t wait to see what we get in future updates (hopefully 6 player maps one day).
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is great, and a fairly faithful tribute to Frank Herbert's Dune universe. It's a deep and satisfying strategy game that scratches the itch of both tactical maneuver and also broad macro strategies.It's unreasonably hard on your graphics card for an RTS, and will crash your computer if you don't turn fog and shadows way down.
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: Plays like a board game in a way, think Crusader Kings but shortened down to last only 2 hours instead of 50.That isn't a bad thing - those 2 hours are some of the most engaging hours you'll have. And then you replay it with different modifiers, as a different faction, different seed, difficulty, etc.Spinning plates: the videogame. There are a dozen different things to manage at any given time, and you're on the knife's edge of being in a deficit in any one of them. Which makes it all the more satisfying when there's a surplus and you really start steamrolling.
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DRA great game bringing back a refreshing change to the RTS scene while being immensely true to the story that Frank Herbert told in the books. I can't state enough how much fun I have trying to figure out the "puzzle" of solving certain faction's build paths for randomized maps. I highly highly recommend this game to anybody who enjoys RTS resource management games.Review:A wonderful and refreshing game based on the Northgard predecessor recipe. If you enjoy a complex RTS with various resource management that is faster pace than Sid's Civilization I feel you will really enjoy this game. This version of Dune is a lot less about making a ball of units to smash your opponent's base like Westwood Studio's Emperor: Battle for Dune and far more on assessing what you as the pilot of the game need to do to capitalize a win. The strategies can be vastly different depending on the map seed as well as the faction you are playing. Each faction has a unique twist that is very fitting for the current movie series while also paying homage to the books. If you like Northgard I feel you will enjoy how much more indepth this game is in comparison. If you like how relentless Northgard can be by it's adaptive events that punish you then that is where this game deviates from Northgard. Both games utilize a smaller tactical force while having to manage your people as well as your hold on various regions for particular resources. Additionally Northgard can at times feel like a stalemate because of the hold that the AI has on particular resources and hidden bonuses. In Dune this is not an issue at this current state of the game. I have never felt the game has unjustly punished me and the objectives that pop up are optional.If you don't like complex or how much micromanaging is required in the current trend of RTS games then you will not enjoy this game. Starcraft 2 will be more up your alley for a traditional troop ball smash your enemies bases and destroy their factories before they can rebuild style of game.The story/campaign of this game thus far is very similair to Westwood's Studios conquest mode just like in Northgard. Albeit without the cheesy videos that Westwood was known for. Conquest mode requires you to take control of regions of Arrakis with specific limitations for each region/mission. You can choose a few different battles each turn of the conquest and react accordingly to what regions the AI takes. Do you continue to take over new regions or do you defend against the AI attempting to claim a region you control?I am so happy Shiro Games has created what I could argue is a wonderful spiritual successor to Emperor: Battle for Dune. If you haven't played an RTS before this game will be quite a challenging learning curve but if you have played the recent version of the Dune boardgame and enjoy the complex paths to winning the board game you will understand when I state how indepth this game can become. I truly hope you will give this gem a try. I know you won't be disappointed!Funny side note when I was younger I use to think Fedaykin was stated like "Fe-Da-King!" This brings back the nostalgia for the books all over again for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem. If you're into things like Civ and the Total War, AoE and city builders -- then this is your game. Really fun addicting gameplay loop, good graphics with a fantastic art style. Enough depth to keep you hooked, stays true to the Dune lore, and is heading in a great direction thus far.
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: A strong and flavorful combination of 4X strategy with light RTS elements. While it likely could have been positioned better as primarily a real-time 4X game, it succeeds at what it sets out to do: make you feel like you're maneuvering a faction in the dangerous political world of Dune. I like to compare this game to the board game Root - each faction is fairly asymmetrical, and the game shines in multiplayer which becomes a tense game of playing table politics to convince everyone else you're not as close to winning as you really are.
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: Although I have never read the Dune Novels, I'm a player of the origional Dune 2 PC game. I was 10 years old when the game released and as for a lot of people, it was THE game that got me hooked on RTS games. I have played some other games like FPS games (and WOT), strategy, basebuilding, simulation and some 4x games, but RTS alway's remained my go-to and favorite genre.At first, I was really excited to see that a new Dune strategey game was in the making. But after looking into it a bit further I was disappointed that it was not a 'pure' RTS game and I disregarded the game. I also didn't like the graphics from the screenshots I saw.The lack of anything worthwhile to play and a YouTube review prompted me to have another look at it and I decided to take a gamble and pruchae a copy of the Early access.I'm glad I did! :steamthumbsup:I realize that the game is still in early access and at some points a bit rough around the edges, but the gameplay is pure fun and addictive! I've had to pull myself away from the PC to go to bed, something that hasn't happend to me in a long while :steammocking:I really like the blend between 4x and RTS ellements. In my oppinion this works really well! The pauze button helped my out in a lot of instances and also helped me to findout how the game works and what to build/research next. I'm also very curious the find out how the Multiplayer of this game will work, as I'm thinking about introducing this game to some of my friends whom I sometimes play with.A compliment to the DEV's for a really nice early access game and please keep up the good work!Keep listening to the relevant community feedback during the further developement of this game and I'm sure that the end product will be a 10 out off 10 from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: Once you got your economy rolling and become a shrewd diplomat, the game is too easy. Easy breeze to victory. Not much to do other than sandworm micro management and the usual voting. You just wait for time to pass, which kinda gets boring.I love the game, so I hope the game will get more mechanics and more to do mid to late game
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: So far, I'm loving it. Complex enough to have depth to its mechanics and such but not too crazy, so you can also enjoy it. Graphics are very nice and fitting.For me the only drawback [edited] so far is that the votes of the minor factions are pretty random and at least during the campaign missions you barely get to reach any of the end-game content.Other than that, great game!EDIT: After playing a good amount more (SP only), I gotta say the balancing seems well done and the different mechanics are pretty clever. And there are so many ways to even play just one faction. In regards to the campaign, I really think this is one of the most well implemented campaigns in any strategy game I've played (and sure AoE campaign missions are cool). Spice Wars is so refreshingly versatile when it comes to the mission goals. This allows for many different approaches to playing your faction, encourages players to change their playstyle as well as make use of different research upgrades etc.

_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very polished and not buggy at all. For an EA it's rare.Pros: it catches well Dune atmosphere, it's a good mix of 4X and RTS (with pause), autopause added with the last patch is perfect. Cons: The game even with the biggest size map is relatively short, for a 4X. I reached victory with Harkonnen in about 12 hours, albeit playing on easy to learn the game. Speaking of which, tooltips are insufficients, most icons are not explained at all, a second layer of information is needed, could be done with hover+ALT or something like that. All special word text is highlighed but not clickable, and it should go to a sort of encyclopedia. Lastly, after the last update early game nerfed Harkonned units too much: they are squishy like mussels. Constant save/reload is needed for a satisfactory experience. Autosave every 10 days is way too long an interval.I will do another playthrough with a different faction (yes add more!) after the next major update. So far the game is a solid 7/10 and will become a must for any Dune fan soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great- even in early access. Many of the interesting and unique 4x gameplay aspects from Northgard have been brought over to this game. The exploration is similar but slightly more advanced, the unit movement and "apm" requirements are the same as northgard, and the flavor of DUNE is very well presented in this game. As a long-time fan of the DUNE series, this game does an incredible job of bringing the flavor of the universe into the game, and many game concepts were very easy for me to grasp because I read the books many times.This is an excellent game, and this review comes from someone who is a large fan of both the DUNE universe, and the Shiro Games dev team.
_childDocuments_.name: Dune: Spice Wars

_childDocuments_.review: I know this is early access but the game just didn't do it for me.  There is just so much lacking from the game that sure could be added later, but the game systems are flawed, which means whatever they add is still being put on a wobbly table.  ProsIt's Dune.  Great atmosphere, great feel.  Love the graphical style of the game.  It's simple.  Early game and learning is quite fun.Con'sAfter you get through the early game everything slows down and I'm a guy who loves games like civ on marathon.  The problem here is everything is slow, and repetitive and tedious for no reason.Too many currencies are needed for building and upkeep.  It is really punishing for any sort of expansionist ideal.  Also the currencies are so inter-connected that your always struggling to keep them going.Only 5 unit types really.  No armour, no flying machines.  Scouts that are useless once the map is explored.  And good luck trying to get any number of units because that ain't happening, which means that if you do expand, you're constantly moving units, very slowly, back and forth to defend from the indigenous raids or attacks.  Well defended towns aren't worth attacking because as soon as you do, reinforcements come and another faction is attacking you across the map and you have no units to fight them.  So you build defence buildings.  But then you have too much upkeep and no resource attainment to keep it all going.Its just repetitive, boring/not fun and my god worms aren't even a worry.It will take alot to make this game good, overhaul it.Edit:  I have put way more time into this game from my original review and to be honest, it's not gotten better.  Sure things have changed but this is just not a good game.  I don't know what genre they are trying to go for.  - rts?  no city building really.  Sure there are things you build but all in all buildings arent used for anything but resource gen which makes it so 1 sided and boring.  Unit battling is more akin to live action 4x fights than anything lose to an rts.  In an rts building placement, troop positioning and movement are major, major things.  In this game, not even close to "the devs don't know what these things are i think."  - 4x?  Resource management is just dumb.  Manpower is now a non factor not that far into the game it seems.  I'm afraid in saying this they will just put some more restrictive modifier on the resource so that you have to use more of your "city" (loose term) City building and customisation just doesn't exist.   You're main city has some variation with you being able to get most of the buildings anyways and really you only choose between a couple of different, and very negligible buffs.  I civ 6 mod that is only a skin of dune for a faction in that game is better than this whole game in any 4x category. - strategy?  I guess except what strategy is required when you expand to 3 territories and then you can't do nothing for 10 mins at a time because of the resource required to gain cities.  Can you imagine if the movie was like this game.  "The emporer wants you to run arrakis because everyone is just making a mess of it.""Sure but can you call us in a week?  We'll have enough authority by then to do it."  (authority is your expansion currency fyi)The game is just a slow slog of ♥♥♥♥ mechanics that is piggy backing off of a beloved title to make money.  If they allowed returns in steam over the 2 hour mark for long games like this, you would see a massive drop in revenue and they might have to fix the game.  Unfortunately by the time 2 hours goes by you don't even know what the ♥♥♥♥ to do still (tutorial is garbage) to even know if you will like the game or not.  Steam is becoming the place where devs go to make money no matter what their ♥♥♥♥ is.   One day steam might actually (i mean there is no chance they do this) take responsibility for the ♥♥♥♥ they help let enter the market.DO NOT GET THIS GAME UNTIL ITS FULLY OUT AND YOU READ REVIEWS AT THAT POINT because the only way this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gets better is with a massive, massive overall.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've finished my first playthrough, I feel like I know enough about the game to form an opinion. PROS:- Looks and feels like Dune- Good variety of strategy, map is big and packed with exciting zones to explore.- Very polished and mostly bug-free for EA- Micro is not really needed. This is very much a macro / worker placement game- Factions and their starting "heroes" allow for a variety of meaningful ways to go for victory although in my experience, just wiping out the enemy faction homebase has been the easiest.CONS:- Some balance / performance issues. Occasional stuttering despite good performance otherwise.- I can't see how they would be able to add many more factions to add diversity to the game like they did with Northgard.VERDICT: - If you're a fan of Northgard, this feels like Northgard 2.0 in the Dune setting. It's more sophisticated than Northgard in most aspects.

_childDocuments_.review: Considering it's a beta... I think it's really quite nice.
