_childDocuments_.review: Perfect for anyone looking for a low-stakes and incredibly charming time in a platformer! In Mail Time, you're a Mail Scout in training! The game kicks off with one task that you'll need to complete to officially claim your Mail Scout badge: delivering a letter to Greg. BUT that's easier said than done! Greg is nowhere to be found, so you'll need to get to know the neighbors in the cozy Grumblewood Grove, perhaps help them deliver some mail, and see if they can point you in the right direction to complete your quest. I found the controls a bit 'soft' (kind of like Mario, where your lil mushroom character won't come to a pinpoint stop). I personally found the movement fine and didn't find it too hard to navigate or jump around. Occasionally the camera would get a little wonky, but it didn't detract from my overall experience. Gliding around was my favorite part of the game, and (in almost BoTW style) I would find myself climbing as high as I could simply to enjoy gliding back down again and seeing the sights. The game excels in visual personality and style, and finding all the details of the Thumbelina-esque world was my favorite part.  I primarily played this on my PC, but have hopped in with the Steam Deck to see if it would run smoothly, and it did! I didn't encounter any major issues or game-locking bugs (although on PC, objects sometimes took a second to load in, leading to some areas looking empty for a moment). You can feel the care and love put into this world, and I enjoyed the arcs and personalities of the different characters! Mail Time is a bite-sized game that I completed in about 4-5 hours (moving very slowly through the world and quests, taking my time to explore).

_childDocuments_.review: Mail time is an adorable game! I love the character customization and the designs of the other characters is incredibly charming. I laughed at the dialogue quite a bit, since it appealed to my humour, and also found myself feeling uplifted by a monologue by a certain character at the end. For spoiler reasons, I won't say what the message is (you'll just have to play it to  find out!), but it came to me at a very difficult time and was really comforting to hear. I also really enjoy how casual the LGBT+ representation is. As part of that community myself, I am a bit tired of my only rep being negative or overtly sexual in nature. It was also nice to have they/them pronouns be an option as well! Not something I see everyday.There are some bugs, and from reading previous forum posts there were bugged achievements. I managed to get 100%, so it IS possible to get them all, though I had to start a new game for one in particular, which required a delivery under 30 seconds. However, this took basically no time at all. I did come across some bugs where a mushroom-gathering quest was considered complete, but my inventory still had items and the last two hats were locked for me. Also I had to go find my mentor near the end of the story and it skipped directly from where I was to finding her at the end of the game. Not game-breaking, but still a bit disappointing. However, the dev team is responsive to bug reports and clearly trying their hardest to get patches out as quickly as possible with their small team. A lot of love was put into this game and it shows.My biggest complaint about the game? It's not long enough! I was just so enamoured with the environments and characters that I was so sad when I realized I had completed the game. I'm not sure what could be added, really, aside from new towns and characters, perhaps with different abilities you can gain as you deliver more and more letters. Another idea could be expanding on some of the lore within Grumblewood (like the mysterious well voice, who I tried so badly to get more info on, but found nothing. Unless a storyline is present already and I just couldn't find the trigger for it). Overall, this game was thoroughly enjoyable and I hope to see more like it in the future! Definitely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this game is absolutely wonderful, the art style is so cute and coheisive, the music is brilliantly designed for the different areas and feels of the game, and the gameplay is calming and smooth. The humor is very silly and matches the vibe of the game wonderfully, and you can't help but fall in love with the characters. I also enjoyed the minor commentary on capitalism as well as the gender and sexuality inclusivity, which is there without feeling like it was forced. (my favorite kind of representation is truly when its just there and treated 100% normally) On top of that I think the ending really is touching.Since it is a new release I did find a couple bugs that I feel I should comment on, however I should state, they are very minor and do not effect gameplay.- Sometimes when you click into your book, the cursor comes onto screen and makes moving the camera a little awkward (only fix I've found for this is saving and exiting the game, than re-opening it)- Occasionally after delivering a letter, the letter icons in the top left corner disappear (this can be fixed by opening and closing the book)- For some reason I couldn't deliver the final mushroom sample to Toph, the game still gave me the badge, however every time I went near them, they had the orange exclamation points, and the icon on the left was still there, yet when I clicked on them, they'd just talk about the mushroom hats. (I did not find a fix for this one)- I'm not quite sure if this is a bug or not, but despite having finished every quest all the way through, I was still missing 2 post cards in the credits for some reason (no fix for this)Other than those few minor bugs, It was insanely well polished, which is inherently impressive for such a small team, you guys really did amazing. A few things I'd say to people who want to play this game, explore EVERYWHERE, and don't forget that some of the artifacts you can get are from completing missions, so if you can't find some of them, try focusing on missions for a bit!Overall if you are looking for a charming adventure-quest type game, then I could not recommend this game any higher for you, it is 100% worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: I would consider Mail Time one of the most fun times I have had with a Steam game that falls into the 'wholesome' category. Everything in it is so endearing and charming that it made me perhaps too engrossed over time. Every single element, from the characters to the nature to the music to the oxygen atoms in the air is infused with a high amount of magical whimsy. It put a smile on my face the entire time and lifted my mood instantly, so I highly recommend playing this if you're having a bad day. I also recommend it to play as a game in general, since it hits a lot of sweet spots in the 3D platformer format.Gameplay is exactly what I expected with a couple of surprises throw in. You jump on platforms, you locate people and objects, you deliver things for fetch quest, rinse and repeat. It works for a reason. However, the twists keep things more engaging. The first one is the introduction of a glider to get around the area when jumping from up high. It even comes with a double jump if you time it right, helping me get up to hard-to-reach places with ease (so I guess they're not hard to reach anymore). The next is how each objective to meet is displayed on the right side of the screen with a portrait of the character you are supposed to talk to, making it easier to identify who's who and remember names. My favorite addition is the ability to jump onto any plant in the environment. Rather than reaching something my going along carefully placed platforms that stick out from the rest of the surroundings, you have to get creative with using the natural plant life to get up there. Half of the fun for me came from finding out how to get from one location to the next.The aesthetics are always pleasing to me. I love how the world looks graphically, since everything has a hand-drawn look that fondly reminds me of Winnie the Pooh. There's tons to see and interact with, and no space is wasted, making things much bigger than they appear to be. The Cottagecore theme is brought about well by the character designs, each one of them incorporating some sense of warmth and invitation made to make you feel at home. Character customization is fun enough just to fidget around with before the game proper. Changing the color of something doesn't just add it on, it fundamentally changes the entire outfit or backpack, increasing the variations without having a ton of sliders. The animations of the playable character especially impressed me; this might be the first time I have seen Squash-and-Stretch used on a 3D character that isn't a blob of goo, and the walking from holding shift is immaculate.Usually I don't get affected by cutesy games due to finding it cute from an artificial standpoint. Something that was deliberately drawn to evoke the emotional pleasure receptors in my brain will never outdo something that is naturally cute, like a baby animal or tiny colored mushrooms. Mail Time was able to break that streak for me by coming from a genuine place. Not only did I feel the cuteness from the artwork, but I sensed the personality of the creator shining as bright as the sun. It's like her worldview came through the internet and landed on my screen, which is more rare than you think. I think this elevates the game above most in a way that can't be completely replicated, and makes it worth giving a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cute little mail game where you the mail scout, is traveling around to deliver letters as well as a few other interesting things!Pros: -The game is really beautiful! I was amazed the moment I opened the game.-I think that the dialog is rather funny at times. It definitely gives zoomer vibes.-Without spoiling too much, the little quests that you do with the Hamster is both hilarious and interesting.- I really do enjoy the customization for your character! You get a pretty good amount of starting choices for outfits and hats ect. I enjoy that throughout the game as you collect mushrooms you can then get new hats to choose from!-I like the choice of pronouns while making your character. I haven't seen many games that do that.-I think that the glider was a really cool addition to the game! Made traveling wayyyy easier. -Again without too much spoilers, I like the relationship dynamics between the characters. I like that the mother rabbit Daisy will ask you to bring her any pictures her kids have drawn. I also enjoy a few other relationship dynamics but I will let you explore those yourself without my spoilers. -The capybara? great addition no other commentary needed lol.-There was no set time limit so I was not concerned or rushed to go quickly to finish all the tasks.  (took me a total of 3.8 hrs to complete the story line to get the end credits).Cons:-There were a few glitches for me. 1. I used mouse and keyboard and sometimes after completing a quest/delivering the mail all the sudden my mouse clicker was visible and I could no longer use my mouse to move around the screen or to change my camera angle. (Saving to the main menu did fix this for me whenever it happened)2. When I finally got to Greg's cave I noticed along the way the rocks and mushrooms would just disappear until I was right on them. It didn't do this anywhere else other than the cave. 3. At the end to talk to Janet and be able to end the game I wasn't able to click on her for a while despite her having the yellow (!!!). I was once again able to save and close to fix this issue. -Game instructions- I am personally someone who needs a little more guidance. I had a really hard time trying to find certain people or how to get to certain areas on the map. I do wish that when it said I had a letter to deliver that it also showed where I could find this person. A few characters would like send me in the right direction but not all of them did until way later when I had already found the person I was looking for. I think that I would have finished the game within the hour had I been able to find my way easier. -Reachable areas- I feel like some of the areas I was meant to reach to get items/to get somewhere were not that accessible. I plan to try another save with my controller to see if jumping around proves easier or not. Overall I still feel that even if I was good at jumping it was still not an easy place to reach/seemed impossible. I do enjoy a challenge but at times I felt like it was no longer a fun cozy game when I can't even reach where I need to be. - Getting to Greg. I may have just had a massive brainfart but for me? Getting to Greg proved almost impossible. I tried for a good hour to get to the broken bridge with no avail. The frog implied that I needed to jump around but no matter where I jumped I could not make it.  -So I get the end credits so I assume I have finished the game yet after it still says I need to chat with Janet as well as deliver Greg's letter. So I guess the game isn't done? Not entirely sure what to do about that. I may just be missing something. Overall I would give this game a good solid 7.5/10. I do recommend the game and I think the person who made this game did a lovely job at it. I would say to wait around for future updates as I assume they will add more things to the game and most glitches will get fixed sooner than later. It's not even a week old so I think that there is plenty more exciting things that will be seen/done in the future! I think the pricing was pretty fair. (got it 20% off)

_childDocuments_.review: Mail Time is a fun, comfortable little adventure wherein you deliver mail to some cool animal friends. I bought it on release day having been previously aware of it, but having not played the demo, and have put in 4 hours thus far - I can see myself replaying this multiple times though, so I imagine the number of hours I get out of it will be well over 4.Positives:-The design is really cute and cosy - such a lovely art style-There's excellent character customisation options-The characters are WONDERFUL - if you've played the Frog Detective games, they remind me of the characters there-The collectables are really interesting and fun-The map is quite big and has lots of nooks and crannies to explore-The game has excellent replayability-There are a variety of accessibility settings, something rarely seen in indie games. I truly commend the devs for their efforts in inclusivityNegatives:-There are a lot of bugs (one is getting stuck in things, but there is an option to move your character to a safe spot in the options menu, so this isn't a softlock). One bug softlocked me from completing the game and I had to restart. -The map is very confusing at first and there is no in-game mapOverall, this game is EXCELLENT, and I highly recommend buying it. It's a fun little game with lots of secrets and little bits to discover, and there's IMMENSE scope for future updates or DLC. I love it and am excited to play and explore more, and am hopeful for patches for the main bugs I've encountered. A fun, high quality, cosy, comfortable game, with no pressure, just calm fun. Also, anti-capitalism, hell yes. Redistribute from the cat (who reminds me of Big the Cat from Sonic in appearance but not personality).Edit 21/11/23 - This game remains delightful and patches have fixed the main bugs. I still hope for more content in this game in future!

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute game. The things I would change (besides the bugs) which is common in a new released game. It would be the lack of interaction with this really cool little world.  I just wished it had a little more "world playability".  For an example ---  There is a quest to get sticks from the only apple tree in the world, yet you never walk over any sticks or pick them up you just need to run to the tree and it doesn't even show an update. So....I was a bit confused that I couldn't even find a stick at all by the apple tree yet somehow I competed that quest? So it would have been nice to interact more with the world/quests.Ending thoughts -  Kela made this adorable little world and for that I give her lots of praise! Hopefully in the near future... crosses all my fingers and toes that maybe we will get an update with some more world interaction.. (like those carrots are so adorable I just wish I could help pick them and deliver those!) haha Maybe a Future amazon mail time type of delivery :P!
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: 7/8/2024 UpdateFinally got around to playing this in full. Most of the major bugs were worked out. I thoroughly enjoyed it, very charming game. But man, still really unpolished at the end. One of the badges says {fan mail}/1 fan mail instead of 1/1 fan mail. No real explanation or story around the bottle caps and crystals. The animals that are supposedly playing instruments are just dancing, but your character mentions their instruments. One character has a chat dialogue at the end but says nothing. Notebook still bugs out if you hit esc to close instead of the check mark. I totally recommend this game, but I hope the next game from this dev gets more love and attention all the way through (or they give themselves more time to work on it, the ending of this feels real rushed). _____________________________________________________________________I have been following this game since before the Kickstarter dropped and have been very excited for its release. I still am. I say I still am excited for its release because honestly, and unfortunately, this game is not finished being developed yet. It has a ton of bugs still, that you encounter really early on. Some really hinder the experience (and some make it impossible to progress or understand what is going on). For a game like this, that de-emphasizes complex mechanics in favor of rich atmosphere, dialogue, characters, and vibes, it is all the more important to have those things polished. Right now they are not only not polished, but not finished. Pop-ups blocking dialogue bubbles while the dialogue still progresses. The hair or outfits in dialogue not matching the chosen settings, etc etc.This is a very very cute game. I love the player customization. I love the art and music. I'll even recommend getting it...and waiting a couple weeks, as I will be, for the (first time dev, so cut them some slack) dev to fix these bugs before I jump back in to get really immersed in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cute, fun little game. The style is unique and I really enjoy the characters and world design. Unfortunately though, I did experience some bugs which essentially broke some missions I was trying to do, so I ended up having to start over twice, before some other people found some workarounds for the bug I was having trouble with (If you get a pop-up stuck on your screen, open your journal and use your mouse to click the button!). There are also some problems with a couple of missions, such that I wasn't really able to complete them.Overall I'd say it's a very good game, and I feel it's worth the price, but I'd strongly recommend holding off on buying it until there's some bug fixes and updates. I'd hate for someone to have their experience soured by a bug like what happened to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: There were some glitches but I overall had a great time. I enjoyed the characters and it was certainly relaxing and adorable. Now it took me about 2 and a half hours to complete the entire game going at a casual pace. To some that is enough for $20, for some it may not be, had I not got it on sale I may have felt a little disappointed.  I was a little sad there wasn't any type of post game, even just being able to talk to the characters or complete busywork. The main glitches I experienced were:Whenever I got an achievement I wasn't able to get rid of it without missing dialogue. The fix for me was pressing H, clicking it, and then going back to the dialogue.I glitched through a floor plank and fell when I shouldn't have.Sometimes pressing E wouldn't let me talk to a character even if I was directly in front of them, I had to walk away and walk back.
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in about 3 hours. It's very cute and super easy once you figure out where you are going. The soundtrack is perfect to vibe out to, especially if you are like me and needing something to decompress after studying for finals.I would go easy on the devs for the bugs, it only JUST came out--not even a day. Bugs are to be expected with brand new games. To avoid certain bugs, I would just play on a controller. Anyways, I hope a DLC comes out for the game in due time. I would love to see it be expanded!
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: well, i accidentally finished the game early. i wish when you reach the end it would give you an option first to complete your previous quests before being forced into the ending. i accidentally beat the main quest earlier than i wanted and it immediately went into the cutscene just from me landing in a specific area unintentionally. with that being said this game is incredibly cute. it was just the wholesome getaway i needed during a stressful time. the controls are a bit difficult without a controller imo, and i should've waited to play until i had access to my controller again. it got kind of frustrating at certain parts not being able to maneuver my player just right to make it where i needed to be. with some extra bug updates, i can see this game being really fun and worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game for a good while now, and it finally released. I loved the demo but the game itself was so much more fun! I love the slice-of-life feel. There is a lot of representation in this game from gay relationships, to being able to choose my pronouns to customization of my character. I had such a great time playing. If you want a cozy, relaxing game that is all positive, this is it! Seriously, play Mail Time, it's so worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super cute, cozy, and pronoun friendly! The game play is super chill and it has major cottagecore vibes. This game is full of nature and fun! Beautiful colors, charming character design, and thoughtful game play. This is a chill, rest, and recover from the day kind of video game. So much to do and see, so many friends to make. This game is just super wholesome. It also includes diversity and representation which is a must.
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and cozy, but buggy. I expected some from a new game that just released, but the bugs I encountered were rather disappointing to deal with. I am sure those will be fixed with time, though.One bug made it so my hair color customization did not save on my character, which, while annoying, I can deal with it. However, I highly recommend not trying to get to a certain spot in the game before your progress actually allows you to, because (spoilers for end of the game ahead) Again, please be cautious poking around in a certain area of the game. I would hate for more people to have the same thing happen to them that happened to me. However, I suppose that's what I get for poking around where I probably shouldn't have been. :P I still highly recommend this game. It's cute and cozy and a nice way to spend a couple of hours or even a day depending on how slow/fast you go at it. I recommend doing everything you can or want to before going for the obvious story progression point, though. Please learn from my experience and don't do what I did. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who just finished the game:Let's just put it out there: it's a little buggy. I mean, it's launch day! Of course it's gonna be a little buggy. So, you can't 100% it as of typing this, but the game is adorable and the difficulty is super low. Definitely one of those one off, "I need to play something slow and easy to relax." Replayability (outside of most likely replaying later to get currently bugged achievements) is low in my opinion, but I've been following the developer since 2020 on TikTok when Mail Time seemed more like a pandemic pipe dream than a published indie game. I can easily see them and their passion for the game leading to free or paid DLC that could bring players back.If you like cozy fetch quests games, this is just a cottagecore version of that with a cute story. There's some quality of life changes to be made, and (like I said) it's currently a little buggy, but I think it's worth the time and price for the target audience.
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: Just started this game and I'm already in love! I play on steam deck and for any others who do, it works perfectly! I did have a couple glitches so far but that's to be expected from a game that has just released. The graphics are adorable and the world is stunning, along with the characters being super cute too! _childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: So charming and exciting to explore! Lovely music, adorable art, and hysterical writing. The game just needs a few fixes. The ending can accidentally be triggered early, which cuts off plenty of incomplete quests. I got stuck on an item menu once as well, which required a reset of my game. _childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: I was so excited for this game and it truly did not dissapoint! the artstyle is adorable, exploring is so interesting (very glad there is no time limit for anything), the characters are very fun to talk to and some of the dialogue actually made me laugh out loud. generally you can just see how much love and care was put into the game, there is so much detail in every object you come across too. cannot wait to play more!the only bug I have experienced so far was the hair colour changing after starting the game
_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.name: Mail Time

_childDocuments_.review: Loved how cozy and comfy this game was, there are still a few bugs such as character customization not being reflected in the game however I did enjoy it overall. _childDocuments_.review:
Mail Time is a relaxing, cottagecore adventure set in a peaceful forest, far, far away.

It's your first day on the job as a newly minted Mail Scout. Equipped with a mushroom hat, a pack full of letters, and unbridled enthusiasm, it's time to deliver letters and packages across the Grumblewood Grove.

Their recipients eagerly await the sight of your mushroom hat, so don't tarry! Run, jump, glide, and make your way across the forest to deliver parcels and joy to the cute critters that inhabit these woods.

That's right. It's Mail Time!

name: Planet of Lana
detailed_description: A planet that used to be a place of undisturbed balance between human, nature, and animal has now become something else entirely. The disharmony that had been in the making for hundreds of years has finally arrived in the form of a faceless army. But this is not a story about war. This is a story about a vibrant, beautiful planet –and the journey to keep it that way. Key Features Unique companion-based gameplay. Solve puzzles with diverse challenges and quirky twists. Carefully navigate dangerous situations using stealth and wit. Use your reflexes and survive challenging action sequences. Discover an epic story that stretches across galaxies and centuries.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just brilliantly written. The artwork is excellent and the music/sound is superb. A little short but for the price you can't complain. _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Another one of those rare gems that serves as a strong argument for "games as art". Absolutely gorgeous in every respect, with cute puzzles following familiar themes. A bit short at "only" 5 hours, but has a compelling plot, touching interactions between characters, some fascinating world building, a couple utterly unforgettable moments, and an absolutely beautiful soundtrack by Takeshi Furukawa (composer of The Last Guardian among others). This game is absolutely worth your money and your time.Buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a beautiful game with a simple story and easy puzzles. I love that it doesn't have any talking, so I can understand it even though my English isn't very good. I hope the developers will add more content to the game in the future, like side stories or new levels. I would recommend it to anyone who enjoys adventure games or games with a unique art style.Updated: I hope the game wins the 2023 Steam Awards
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended for anyone who's enjoyed games like FAR:Lone Sails or Minute of Islands - it's a simple puzzle "platformer" with an obvious amount of care dedicated to telling Lana's story through her reactions and huge set pieces that allow the player to learn about her world as she does. Absolutely amazing and beautifully crafted - awesome blend in art direction, puzzle-pacing, and sound. The "tiny" touches too - Lana looking at giant objects as she passes by, Mui surging forward when areas are safe, distinct birdsong from area to area, among so many other touches that bring Lana, Mui, and the world to life - an amazing story to play - thank ya'll!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous puzzle/adventure game. The graphic stylization is one of the strongest points of the game. It looks like an animated watercolor painting, with stunning depictions of natural beauty. Animations are fluid and give a lot of character to encountered animals and robots. Music is beautiful and there are few scenes where the game just takes a break to let a song take over.  Puzzle design is solid and logical, with use of two characters, some abilities, physics and sneaking. I never got stuck. Aside from puzzles there is some basic platforming with cooperation between characters.  The story is told without any intelligible dialogues or writing, characters use a simple made up language. The background of the world is shown through some cave paintings and ruins. Despite that it is easy to grow to like the characters and enjoy their journey to rescue their kidnapped family.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game. Of course, the puzzles could be more challenging and the story could be deeper but I believe that this is still a great job for such a small dev team.One thing I didn't like is that even in a neutral game like Planet of Lana there's a pinch of DEI. There're 4 pictures of some leaders/generals on the spaceship: a white man, a black man, a woman and a robot. Now, take a look at the dev team on their Instagram - all are white Swedish males; yet, they think this game needs some diversity which literally no one asked for. It's sad that nowadays so many men don't have balls anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: To be fair: Planet of Lana offers beautiful graphics, gripping sound fx and an emotional story. It has no bugs, is technically solid and has perfect controls.BUT it only has a play time of 5 hours and it's very easy. In addition, it is absolutely straightforward and offers hardly any development opportunities for the player. If you can get it for $10-15 you might want to give it a try, but other than that it's just too flimsy.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished this game and I am quite honestly blown away. From the beautiful graphics and incredible soundtrack, to the challenging at times (but not too frustrating!) puzzles, and from the emotional roller coaster this adventure takes you on to the pitch perfect sidekick Mui, I honestly consider this to be one of the most flawless, cinematic side-scrollers I've ever played. For a debut, Wishfully should be incredibly proud of themselves, and I absolutely cannot wait to see with what they come out with next.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: "Planet of Lana" is a beautifully crafted puzzle game with a breathtaking art style, emotional music, crisp sound effects and an adorable little companion. It is an excellent game to play on the Steam Deck.You initially only control Lana in a sidescrolling fashion reminding me of the original DOS game "Prince of Persia" while running, jumping and climbing obstacles. Lana is soon joined by a little creature that behaves like a very well trained dog but looks like a cat, to help out solving puzzles. Those puzzles are not particularly hard but engaging and satisfying to solve. While Lana or Mui can die due to being caught by enemies or by falling from height the game quickly resets to the last checkpoint and you can continue on. Those checkpoints occur often and make for a very fluid gameplay.The game looks absolutely gorgeous with its painted art style, and on a couple of occasions I just stopped to take it all in. When the camera zooms out to reveal the vast area around you and the music comes on - that was incredible. And it runs great on the Steam Deck - I had it set to Medium graphics quality for a solid 60FPS. Everything top of the line. The music fit perfectly, the voice acting using the alien language was great and the cute noises that Mui produces will stick with me for a very, very long time. :)At around five hours of playtime for one playthrough plus a bit of replayability for people who want to get all the achievements it is excellent value for money. The puzzles are fun, the graphics a sight to behold, the music just lovely, and there were no bugs that I encountered on my playthrough. I am actually a bit surprised that it isn't rated "Overwhelmingly positive" just yet. I think it should be and I can highly recommend it.Thank you for making this fantastic game! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely wonderful game. Lovely graphics (mostly) and exquisite music make this a such dreamy experience. Leasurely (for the most part) gameplay, puzzles and action scenes aren't overly difficult - the game is clearly designed for younger kids, but as an adult I can say it was  never boring - it's simply too immersive (and though I found the puzzles overall not too hard, the few harder ones were never frustrating and always fascinating, which tells you a lot about this game's worth). To top it off, the storyline reaches for our common human essence in a very honest way. Beautiful! Either way, everyone who plays this will have fond memories of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: The standout feature of Planet of Lana is undoubtedly its breathtaking visual design. The hand-painted art style lends an ethereal quality to the world, immersing players in a vibrant and imaginative universe. From lush forests and sparkling waterfalls to desolate wastelands and ancient ruins, each environment is a work of art that draws players deeper into the narrative. The attention to detail in character designs, architecture, and natural elements showcases the dedication of the developers to create a visually captivating experience.At the heart of Planet of Lana is a touching narrative that explores themes of friendship, loyalty, and the resilience of the human spirit. The story follows Lana, a young girl, and her loyal animal companion as they journey to save their world from an impending threat. The emotional bond between Lana and Mui is portrayed with subtlety and depth, making players genuinely care about their journey and the challenges they face. The game's ability to evoke genuine emotions through its characters and storytelling sets it apart from other titles in the genre.Planet of Lana offers a blend of platforming, puzzle-solving, and exploration mechanics that keep players engaged throughout the journey. The puzzles are cleverly designed, often requiring players to use both Lana's abilities and Mui's unique skills to overcome obstacles and progress. The gameplay strikes a balance between challenge and accessibility, allowing players to enjoy the experience without feeling overwhelmed. The integration of puzzles within the environment seamlessly aligns with the narrative, creating a cohesive and engaging gameplay loop.The game's sound design complements its visual beauty, enhancing the immersive experience. The ambient soundtrack captures the mood of each location and situation, creating a sense of wonder, tension, or melancholy as needed. The sound effects further immerse players in the world, from the rustling of leaves to the distant echoes of alien creatures.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: sometimes the simplest of games make for the best gaming experiences.rating system is arbitrary for this one. It's just a really good, simple story game. If you want a challenge, look for it elsewhere because this game wasn't made to be challenging, it was made to tell a story and imo they absolutely nailed what they wanted to make.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I think the beautiful art, music and environment is the game's biggest strength while the rest is a little disappointing. Perhaps I am personally just not a fan of this type of gameplay, but I expected more than just run, jump across some rocks, hide, do a small puzzle or a stealth section, rinse and repeat. There was no exploration either; we see this beautiful world around us but it's all just a background. Finally, some of the controls were quite frustrating, especially the one to control robots. It was like controlling a heavy pile of jelly. Overall, I can certainly see the love put in this game but I can't say it really stands out among other fantastic indies.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This is going to be difficult. I tend towards a recommendation, but with caveats.Planet of Lana is a cinematic puzzle platformer in the style of LIMBO and feels quite similar in the final part of the game. Unfortunately, it takes a few hours to get there.The story is very basic and does not pick up until the final 30 minutes and the puzzle/platforming sections until then can be described either as "cozy casual" or "subtle padding", as the solution is almost always obvious and it becomes a purely timing-based challenge whether you can reach the safe points before the enemies find you. It's not hard and it does not have to be, but it's also not very satisfying either. The story meanders for a long while and there is little variety in what you are actually doing. At several points I had to force myself to continue as I was close to getting bored. The final 30 minutes or so are then, finally, where the story and the gameplay picks up, invoking memories of the aforementioned LIMBO in both the environment and the setting.Visually and audibly, Planet of Lana is stunning. The visual quality of the backgrounds is top-notch all the way, which generates a number of opportunities for beautiful screenshots that have strong desktop wallpaper potential. The music and sounds are great as well, although the gibberish spoken language does nothing for me.Controls are flawless and the character has some real weight to her, which feels natural in both movements and jumping behaviour.The price is the game's biggest hurdle. I got it on sale and even that was a 14 € price tag, which at ~4 hours playtime heavily exceeds my "one hour per euro" rule for whether a game was worth it or not. There is also not really a reason to replay the game either -- at least not unless years down the line I completely forgot the story and really feel the urge to play it again, although I doubt that.Lots of negatives, but I feel I needed to point this out for other potential buyers, especially since the needle overall still points to "yes" for a recommendation, largely due to the technical excellence (graphics, sound, controls) and the final game and story ending on a strong note.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I  this game! I liked how everything worked very smoothly, the music and the graphics were really beautiful and the story became clear through the visual storytelling. Definitely took some concentration, playing when tired was always a wrong choice especially when seriously avoiding dying. This game fits well with casual players who like subtle and touching stories.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is an absolutely beautiful piece of art, but is a pretty boring GAME.  I really wanted to love it because the visuals were so alluring, but ultimately the simple and uninspiring puzzles and platforming sections...you know...the actual GAMEPLAY, couldn't match the gorgeous setting.  The game would have been significantly more enjoyable if more of the puzzle areas were better incorporated with some of the more striking visual environments.  There were far too many static/flat areas that felt like a slog to get through.  Ultimately, Planet of Lana just made me wish there was a longer, deeper version of the game with more mechanics, more story, more interactive elements...just more everything...but keeping the same graphics and art direction.  I give it a 6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely one of my favourite games I've ever played. It's like playing a movie. Stunning art style / visuals and the most beautiful music. Story is simple but effective and emotional. As some other people have said the puzzles are simple, but the focus of the game is much more about the story rather than the challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game. I am only sorry that I completed it so quickly (over 3 days. 14 hours). I loved the atmosphere. I loved the relationship between Lana and Mui. I loved how they pulled at our heart strings at several points when the energy of the story became intense. I loved how intuitive each level and stage of the game was, while still keeping it interesting enough that we had to carefully problem solve. I would love to see more games like Planet of Lana on the Steam platform. This game reminds me of some of my other favourite puzzle platformers in terms of artistry, style and dynamic playability. Notably:  Ori, GRIS and INSIDE. 3 games that rate in the top of my favourites list. Well done to the creators, for putting together such a pretty, heartwarming and dynamic game.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely little platformer gem! From what I recall, this is the first game of this Swedish studio, so: congratulations guys!I very much enjoyed my 6 hours stay on Lana's Planet. The game tells the story of a kind and well animated girl, Lana,  trying to rescue her dear friend after a robot invasion.  As in games like INSIDE or Planet Alpha, the screen scrolls horizontally for the most part,  and the platforming goes strictly in 2D (unlike Little Nightmares where you have a 2.5D kind of environment).As is typical for this genre, Lana will have to solve several puzzles and obstacles on her way, as well as encounters with enemies that want to kill her.Thankfully, however, Planet of Lana never tries to be a Limbo-Clone. Death isn't waiting for you behind every corner. The game is colorful and pretty, Lana has a voice and a likable personality. She will have a super cute companion, the story isn't a big riddle full of wtf's and questionmarks, and it will have a proper ending. The journey itself is the highlight of the game. I have to admit, there could have been a greater focus on the puzzles. There are only very few somewhat challenging puzzles, and the majority of them are quite easy and obvious to solve. You pretty much do the same thing over and over, and you will never go "Holy cow, now THAT's clever!". The puzzles are neither hard nor overly creative. It's the path, the journey, which is beautiful and often heart warming. And that's what this game is all about.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very beautiful, but that's about it. The puzzles are okay, but very scattered. Basically you go right, then left, then right for 2 minutes, a small puzzle, right for 2 minutes again, another small puzzle, repeat 10 times and the game is over. The game tries to connect emotionally with the player, but completely fails. It's the kind of game that is more of a work of art than a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: LOVELY GAME!!!Stoked to be amongst the first to review. The devs did an incredible job here.It's super intuitive to play, the story is gripping from the start, a total indie-price-winner-vibe. Clever new gameplay mechanics between a hero and her pet. Interesting world, beautiful style, fascinating creatures. I usually stay far away from games that have little puzzles to continue, but this one stole my heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Easier than the likes of Little Nightmares, Inside and Limbo. But certainly not a walking simulator. Requires a lot more "skill" and player input than something like Journey. Platforming does not require pixel perfect timing, and for the most part, puzzles were straight forward. I only got stuck on a puzzle once.I played quite slowly, walking a lot rather than running everywhere, and stopping to admire the beautiful scenery sometimes. It took me 5 hrs to finish. I will play it through again though, at least one more time.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing 2.5D puzzle platformer set in a rather beautiful environment albeit with a pretty generic sci-fi story tacked on.You go throughout most of the game controlling a child with his newfound alien pet that would help the child solving puzzles while the child also basically has to provide a way for both to traverse the Gameworld.However you don't directly control the pet, you can only give it commands to go here and there while the pet very often help the child kicking down ropes or distracting the robot enemies.The environemnt looks beautiful although perhaps not looking alien enough, the soundtracks are also good although not that amazing, there's no earth dialogues in this game, in the fee moments that characters in this game speaks they speaks alien language, but don't worry because the story works without you knowing what they're talking about.My only complain would be the game is a little too short, people can complete this game under 10 hours, some will complete it under 5 hours...
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Quite unpolished when it comes to platforming and controls for other characters, with horrid animation for tree movement and annoying quick time events (there are like 5 in the whole game), the start is a slog to get through, action on the screen is very often, unnecessarily, interrupted, BUT it has a soul, it is pretty to look at, music is decent etc.Overall, I quite enjoyed it and I hope they make some more, but much more polished and with more focus.

_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: An utterly enchanting puzzle/platform experience.  This game is really the ‘ying’ to Inside’s ‘yang’. Where Inside was dark, brooding, and nihilistic, Planet of Lana is exhilarating, joyful and optimistic (which is not to say there aren’t dark moments).  If you enjoy games where the story and the visuals are as important as the gaming elements, then treat yourself to this work of art. I have had the soundtrack on repeat for months (it’s composed by Takeshi Furukawa who created the music for Star Wars the Clone Wars). For me it’s up there with Ori, Inside and Stray for a perfect synthesis of aesthetic, narrative and gaming experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: You play as a mentally challenged little boy that constantly yells "Eeee-looo" and likes jumping and running around. And while he has certain earthly charm, he is fortunately accompanied by a cute spiderpig, I mean blob-cat-dog thing. Together, they engage to save their village from menacing evil robots that randomly appeared on their planet.EDIT: Congratulations, it's a girl! Silly me, I didn't read that you play as a girl, and in the game,  you have absolutely no way of telling it's supposed to be a girl. I'm keeping the review intact, because I think it's funnier this way, where I've only discovered you play as a girl after finishing the game.I got reminded of Inside at times, although PoL isn't anywhere near as polished as that game. The pacing is a bit off, as the game sort of drags at the beginning, but then throws an abundance of puzzles at you, which aren't that engaging and the challenge is usually in figuring out how the game works, as most of them are one-offs that wouldn't work the second time, when you already know what you're doing. I don't particularly enjoy these types of puzzles, as they are easy when you figure out what the developers actually want from you, but getting there can be infuriating at times. Not my favorite kind of level design - some of them are good, some were meh.On the other hand, the presentation is appealing, the puzzles try to be different every time at least in some aspect, and the game has nice atmosphere. There are several epic moments that I wasn't expecting, but they come out of nowhere and are quickly gone.The atmosphere is unfortunately there only sometimes. The gameplay revolves around climbing rocks, running away or figuring out how to get around a robot. That's the core of the game. Forget the cinematic stuff you experience at the beginning. There is some story and evolvement through the game, but it's rather small scale, and even when you're exploring ancient bunkers of the previous civilization, you aren't involved, you're just sort of moving through motions, unfortunately, it doesn't have the weight, as the game doesn't allow you to stay and take in the atmosphere.It's also sadly very isolated. You have your cutesy blob-cat, but that's about it. You won't meet any characters, aside from one that has a brief, random appearance towards the end, mostly it's absolutely nothing. Your boy just sort of runs through area after area, without any consideration why he's doing what he's doing, he just accidentally finds ancient technology and just accidentally saves the day - obviously, this is a game, it's not that deep, but I felt really disconnected from anything, because that's just sort of what happens, even if your character has some basic motivations, you are disconnected from the main goal of the game, and things just sort of happen in a very old-school video-gamey way.There are too many basic repeated scenes that just serve to prolong the game, needlessly so - it's short, but still feels like it drags - at times, it turns into a legitimate walking simulator, or you will be waiting for like a minute until something happens. At times, it can be nice, other time it's just a drag. And this happens over and over.You don't really get any answers to the behind the scenes - unless you collect all the tablets, which I suppose explain some of the "why and who". I still have no idea what was the drive behind the plot, I can only assume that it was some automated program of sorts, carrying over from the Earth, at least that's how it looked on the illustrations - ultimately, the ending is a bit of a letdown, because it makes it feel like very little has happened and nothing has changed. (The devs also pull out something very cheap to get a brief reaction out of you.) Still, a lot more satisfying than Inside's ending. There aren't really any secrets to discover, anything from past to unearth, just one simple set of collectibles that isn't really important.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a puzzle platformer, but! Those two gameplay elements are made simple enough, so that the music, art and the storytelling can take center stage.It's something to keep in mind, in case you're expecting head-scratching tasks and big-brain solutions, or dexterity checks for the platforming parts.Absolutely not.Planet of Lana doesn't want you to get  stuck or frustrated. You're meant to have an easy gameplay time, so you can enjoy the other elements:The story is simple, yet effective.The art, level design, animations, everyone who worked on it deserve 10 raises, because the visuals make this game shine. Same goes for the sound design and the music. They elevated the game experience to an animated movie I actively took part in.All of Lana's pieces work beautifully together, and I couldn't recommend it more.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This was a fun little puzzle platformer and I'd recommend it to others. Quite visually appealing, it (for the most part) makes it clear what is what so the objectives are clear.  I do admit looking up the answer to one puzzle that involved moving bars into specific positions because I had trouble making out some of the obbscured clues, though that may so more about me than the game.  None of the puzzles are so challenging that they can't be broken down and eventually solved.  I appreciate that while timing was needed for certain spots pixel-perfect timing was not required.  The one thing that I had trouble with even near the end was getting a handle on was what the limits of my companion were.  It reminded me of the game Black the Fall, where you also have a small non-human companion that opens pathways and distracts guards. Then as in here only via trial and error could I gauge if a leap or fall was too much for the companion.Overall I'm positive on the game and I'm sure I'll come back to it again once I've forgotten most of the puzzle solutions.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This is very much cut from the same cloth as Limbo/Inside/Little Nightmares.    Similar gameplay, similar length, and in some sections, even similar art style, even though the store page doesn't tell the whole story.  If you liked those, you'll probably like this.  The puzzles aren't quite as inventive as in the others, which is reflected in its somewhat lower Metacritic score, but the art design is top notch and overall it's a solid choice if you're looking for more of that style of game.      Also, it runs pretty well on Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot help but be charmed by the kitty cat. It's demeanour, and whimsical aversion to water added an endearing touch to the narrative. The game's auditory and visual elements are nothing short of phenomenal, effortlessly absorbing the player in its mesmerising universe, making the passage of time feel rather insignificant.While the majority of the puzzles are crafted to guide players through an elegant waltz, a select few snap you back into consciousness, brilliantly disrupting the game's otherwise trance-like aura. The mechanics, despite being predominantly effective, suffer from a certain degree of repetitiveness, thus diluting their impact over the course of the game. A more diverse assortment of challenges would have contributed significantly to the overall experience, perhaps something that can be improved upon for Planet of Lana 2 :)However, it is essential to consider "Planet of Lana" as more than just a conventional video game. It represents an experiential journey, stirring profound emotional responses, and inciting empathetic connections. Despite minor inconsistencies, the game proves to be a heartfelt narrative experience, weaving an ethereal tapestry that lingers long after the credits roll.Overall I give this game a 9/10 Planet of Lana pawsitively claws its way to the zenith of video game craftsmanship, landing a whisker away from the coveted pinnacle of purrfection. It is a tail to be remembered, and undoubtedly one of the most captivating yarns in contemporary video gaming.Note: Game was purchased on this account, family shared with alt-account I use exclusively for streaming, which is why I only have 0.2 hours on record.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you developers for a lovely game!Played it with my daughters (9, 12), completelly suitable for them, we had a great time. Loved the story. _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana doesn't do anything unique and those who have played the original Prince of Persia or Inside or Limbo are familiar with this game. However, what sets Planet of Lana apart is its ability to tell a story without saying a word. Combine this with great visuals, engrossing gameplay and thought-provoking puzzles, and a compelling soundtrack and you have the makings of an instant classic. Unfortunately, with platformers of this type the controls are clunky and can sometimes feel stiff. However, that does not detract from Planet of Lana being a good game. And for the low price of $20 you can't go wrong with adding this game to your library.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game beautifully uses a silent yet compelling narrative, all show, no tell.  Not to mention the story is so heartfelt and powerful, it may even make you cry at the end for how beautiful it is.  The main force that drives this narrative is its amazing soundtrack!  The soundtrack for this game has got to sit within my top 10 soundtracks of all time, it perfectly compliments each monumental point in the narrative and excellently emphasises your emotions to feel more for the characters of Lana and Mui in that moment.   The mechanics of this game are very simple and the puzzles aren't too hard so its an excellent sit back and relax type of game.  If you're looking for a compelling narrative, this is the game.  If you are looking for a challenging game, unfortunately the most challenging thing this game has to offer is the flawless achievement to complete the game without dying.I absolutely  this game, I went as far as getting 100% achievements, and

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a remarkable cinematic puzzle adventure that takes players on a captivating journey through a beautifully crafted world. Developed by a talented team, this game offers a unique and engaging experience that combines stunning visuals, innovative gameplay mechanics, and an epic sci-fi narrative that spans across centuries and galaxies.At the heart of Planet of Lana is the story of a young girl and her loyal friend who embark on a rescue mission in a world that has been overtaken by a faceless army. The game presents a planet that was once a harmonious place, where humans, nature, and animals coexisted in perfect balance. However, the tranquility has been disrupted, and it's up to players to restore harmony and preserve the planet's beauty.One of the standout features of Planet of Lana is its companion-based gameplay. Throughout the adventure, players control both the young girl and her trusty companion, utilizing their unique abilities to solve puzzles and overcome obstacles. This dynamic adds depth to the gameplay, requiring players to strategize and coordinate actions between the characters in order to progress.The puzzles in Planet of Lana are diverse, offering a range of challenges with quirky twists. From environmental puzzles that require clever thinking to intricate mechanisms that demand precise timing, each puzzle feels satisfying to solve and adds to the immersive experience. Additionally, the game incorporates elements of stealth and wit, allowing players to carefully navigate dangerous situations and outsmart adversaries.The visuals in Planet of Lana are truly breathtaking. The hand-painted art style creates a mesmerizing world that feels alive with vibrant colors and intricate details. From lush forests to desolate industrial landscapes, each environment is beautifully realized, enhancing the sense of immersion and wonder. Combined with a hauntingly atmospheric soundtrack, the game's audio-visual presentation sets the perfect tone for the epic journey that unfolds.While the game primarily focuses on puzzles and exploration, it also features challenging action sequences that test players' reflexes and survival skills. These moments of intensity add variety to the gameplay and inject a sense of urgency into the narrative, keeping players engaged and on their toes.Planet of Lana is not just a visually stunning adventure; it also boasts an epic and thought-provoking story. As players progress through the game, they unravel a narrative that stretches across galaxies and centuries, delving into themes of harmony, preservation, and the consequences of disharmony. The storytelling is expertly woven into the gameplay, creating an emotional connection with the characters and their journey.In conclusion, Planet of Lana is a standout title that offers a captivating and immersive experience. With its unique companion-based gameplay, diverse puzzles, stunning visuals, and an epic sci-fi narrative, the game is a must-play for fans of the puzzle-adventure genre. It seamlessly combines elements of strategy, stealth, and action, resulting in a rewarding and unforgettable journey through a vibrant and enchanting world. Whether you're a casual player or a seasoned gamer, Planet of Lana is sure to leave a lasting impression.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Its a really cool game! The challenges and Puzzles ain't hard which makes it a bit different from other games as it focuses on adventure and its cool soundtracks . _childDocuments_.review: I took a chance on this game after I saw it in an ad before a YouTube video and boy am I glad I did. Lastly is the orchestral soundtrack that just demands to be purchased yet is criminally unavailable. Do what I did and take a chance on the game right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice and simple puzzle adventure game with an interesting premise and artistic and stunning visuals. While very pretty to look at, it is not very engaging to play. _childDocuments_.review: Outstanding! I absolutely loved this game. Beautiful art, incredible music and sound design, I loved spending time in this world. The puzzles never get particularly hard, but I liked that aspect. There was one short flappy-bird like puzzle that was annoying, but otherwise I enjoyed it all. _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I spent a leisurely 3 months playing this game, with a total play time of 10 hours.Unlike Inside and Limbo, I didn't feel any urgency or trepidation for the character.  In fact, during the early stages of the game I found it difficult to engage with the character or to care about Lana’s plight. After all, it is a game of puzzles, and feels more like a puzzle game then either of the aforementioned two games.The early puzzles were easy to solve. The greater challenge was finding how to reach the shrines – that was until the game progressed further. Eventually the puzzles increased in difficulty. I stepped away from some of them to think through them. They were certainly not impossible but required some good thinking.As for replayability, I will probably give this one another play some time, just to try to gain some missing achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not essentially a bad game, but it's a bit boring. The images are pretty nice, I'll admit, but the puzzles are easy and sometimes even repetitive. This made me think about Inside a lot, but Inside has a way more compelling story in my eyes, and some of the puzzles are really challenging.Planet of Lana didn't hold my interest for long enough. Not a complete waste of time, for sure, but there are better games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: "This game possesses several noteworthy aspects that contribute to its overall appeal. Firstly, the visual artistry is commendable, boasting stunning backgrounds that capture the player's attention. However, I found the designs of the main character and her sister to be less impressive, which slightly detracted from the overall visual experience.Secondly, the inclusion of a companion creature, be it a cat, dog, or monkey?, adds a unique charm to the game. The interactions with this little creature enhances the overall gameplay experience, creating moments of endearing connection between the player and their virtual companion.In terms of gameplay, the focus primarily revolves around platforming puzzles, which are engaging albeit relatively straightforward. While the mechanics are basic and occasionally repetitive, I never found myself growing bored, although I wished for a bit more complexity to deepen the challenge.One aspect that did pose a challenge was the use of a (possibly artificial) language for the main characters, which initially put me off. However, as the game progressed, the dialogues became sparse, allowing me to overlook this aspect and immerse myself in the gameplay.In regards to the game's duration, it's worth noting that the overall playtime is relatively short, clocking in at around 5 hours for the main story. However, completing the game to 100% may require additional time and effort, making it suitable for players seeking a moderate yet enjoyable gaming experience.In summary, while the game may have its minor flaws, such as repetitive gameplay and peculiar language choices, its captivating visuals, endearing cat/dog/monkey-thing, and overall charm make it a good choice for those looking for a heartfelt and relatively brief gaming adventure."
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Short, sweet, huggable. Art style is beautiful, the soundtrack is enchanting, and the gameplay is simple enough that anyone could play it. Puzzles are a core part of the gameplay, but if you're even dimly aware of how to jump and manipulate objects in the fore/background, it'll be a cakewalk! It honestly felt like it was a long animated short film that someone glued game mechanics to, but that's coming from someone who has beaten some of the harder challenges in Hollow Knight, so my expectations for challenge are probably a bit skewed! Controls and movement are solid, and the narrative -while unspoken and fairly simple- are that of a hopeful journey! Give it play, or at least buy the OST!
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw a trailer for  a year ago, I was immediately engrossed by its mysterious world, mainly due to its vividly colourful presentation. I knew I wanted to dive into this experience full of glamorous landscapes and menacing wildlife that have their natural habitat interfered with by emotionless machines. Perhaps it is an over-explored theme at this point, maybe even slightly exhausted, but it can still make for an intriguing journey if done well, and my first impressions were quite positive.Sadly, that did not last long.Even though  introduces a bunch of solid premises, it never builds upon them, as if it was afraid to actually reach its initial vision and rather preferred to stay in some kind of wishy-washy safe zone that is perhaps sufficient enough – not being inherently terrible – yet still is rather monotonous and uninspired to keep my full attention. It feels like it is doing the bare minimum and counts on making up for it with marvellous audiovisuals—and that hurts both the narrative and gameplay.Let us start with the storyline first. On a distant, foreign planet, Lana and her relatives enjoy a relatively peaceful and harmonious way of life with nature. Needless to say, it does not last long, as their world begins to crumble with a sudden invasion of hostile robots, which kidnap everyone they spot. Thus, Lana’s goal is simple: to find her close ones and free them before it is too late. Sure, probably no one will praise such a premise for its unimaginable creative spirit, but I would say that it is adequate for this kind of game, and nothing stops it from being told in a captivating way.Moreover so, when a cute, cat-like being called Mui joins your adventure. Both of you are on the run, after all. Unfortunately, there is barely any narrative interaction between these two characters; their relationship does not grow. They simply stumble upon each other and continue forward, whilst any hint of possible development is only present at the very end. Instead, it focuses more on the background of both humans’ and robots’ origins via environmental storytelling, which is done well for the most part. I do not mind that – I welcome it, in fact – but it completely overshadows Lana’s character and journey. Therefore, any emotional scene or a possible sign of development feels rather superficial.Where  actually shines are its abovementioned visuals that beautifully portray each new environment you visit, making them distinctive and lovely to look at. The playthrough’s overall flow profits from that tremendously, helping with the feeling of discovering something new each time. And to give credit where it is due, these vivid visuals are perfectly complemented by a top-notch sound design, mainly by an astounding soundtrack, whose charming compositions pepper up many encounters. But it is more than that, as various natural sounds, Lana’s made-up yet inspired language or droids’ tones help with building up the atmosphere, as well. This audiovisual pinnacle was the sole reason I was still somehow semi-motivated to progress further, as at certain moments, it felt like a relaxing odyssey.Alas, the gameplay does not manage to use that – or the said premises – to its advantage and instead drags the experience down with a repetitive and simple loop. That is especially regrettable due to its short length of three to four hours. Now, the issue is not necessarily the fact that it is relatively easy to play nor that the puzzles do not require much thinking—the problem is that there is barely any variety. Any obstacles in your way, whether it is enemies or puzzles, are reused far too often. To make matters worse,  shows most of its tricks within its first half, so the latter chapters fail to surprise, with one exception, and feel the same. That is more astounding, given the fact that your companion Mui is often required to help you. Yet, its presence mostly wearisomely revolves around dropping down a rope for you, whereas you move a box or lift a platform. Any longer or more elaborate interactions are rare, which is a shame.These shortcomings arise from the presentation, too. For example, while you will spot quite a few machines in the background, you only keep engaging with just two types during the encounters. It seems like a waste to come up with various models and then not use them for imaginative and exciting situations, perhaps not introducing them as a foe to avoid but as a platforming section. The same can be said about animals. I mean, one would expect some varied wildlife on a distant alien planet, yet you keep hopping into a bland take on boars and some slime-spider things. The heavily promoted large creatures are barely there. Thus, nature feels lifeless, even though it should not be that way. And the fact that you actually kill  animals than destroy robots undermines any kind of harmonious message this title wished to promote. What a weird decision.So, while the journey and core of the game are perhaps somehow solid, it all feels so basic that I barely found any enjoyment in it. Perhaps if it focused more on the actual journey, I would like it much more. At this state, however, I was bored halfway through, and nothing that happened later on changed that. Simply put,  stagnates since its very beginning and fails to deliver on many fronts. Still, it can be somehow enjoyed as an audiovisual spectacle, but I would advise waiting for a sale for that.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw the trailer for this game a few months ago and was intrigued by the visuals. And the game definitely does not disappoint in this aspect! Planet of Lana is a very aesthetic game with beautiful backgrounds and rich colours. The sheer size of the robots in the background, combined with the music gives the game multiple “highlights”. In some instances, I wished there would have been more cutscenes so I could have taken in the full picture without having to react to the enemy attacks. (An option to skip the cutscenes would however be helpful for those who want to replay the game for all the achievements.)But as visual astonishing the game might be, it isn’t completely without fail. The animation of Lana is very detailed and very fluent but the more the puzzles start to rely on good timing the more the animations got a bit annoying. Lana pulls herself up ledges and only starts moving again when completely standing. So if you are even a few pixels late, you cannot outrun the enemy view. Also, if you jump off just one pixel to early you will not reach the ledge. At least it was for me – but maybe it was just my controller as others seem to be praising the precise platforming. But the game is very forgiving and only sets the player back to the beginning of the puzzle or to the midway point of the puzzle. However, if you wish to finish the game with no deaths you might have to learn to jump pixel perfect.The puzzles themselves are not to hard an in some instances were not really a puzzle and just a timing game. Something I didn’t mind as you can let the visuals better sink in when you aren’t frustratingly scratching your head wondering what to do next. Most puzzles are solved by using your little companion. Even though Miu doesn’t say much you just have to like the little fella. Lana herself is also very likable and the voice actor did a good job relaying Lana emotions, whispering to Miu when enemies are nearby and sounding sad when calling out to her kidnapped sister. Personally, I would have liked to stay in Lanas village a bit longer to actually start caring about her sister and the villagers. The story itself is also very basic, but I haven’t seen a game portray the story with such good visualisation. Everything is conveyed though the backgrounds and character interaction so no boring text dumping and unnecessary “on the nose” conversations. There is also a "music theme" throughout the game. I wish they would have leaned more into the music theme as the two puzzles which were slightly related to the theme were my favourite out of all puzzles. The game is also not very long. I finished it in one afternoon (~5 hours). This can be seen as a positive as you can easily replay the game to go looking for missing collectables (shrines) or as a negative as there isn't much to do apart from trying to reach 100% steam achievements after finishing the game.All in all, I would definitely recommend the game if you are looking for a fun but short game. I would give the game a solid .+ stunning artwork+ great soundtrack+ likable characters+ easy puzzles+ no unnecessary lengthy texts (no text at all, just visuals)(+ short game)- Sometime to depended on pixel perfect timing- No deep emotional connection to Lanas sister and therefore slightly missing reason for the player to by invested in the actual mission(- short game)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really good.That's the last time I write a review saying I personally disagree with a review someone else made.I got angry in heat of the moment, and it bit me.CONTEXT: If anyone cares, I wrote a passionate review heavily disagreeing with a negative review. so I deleted it after properly thinking about what I said. I didn't say anything bad or insulting, dw lol. Off note, it's not clownish for a person to disagree with someone that you agree with. And people providing their own reasons for liking a game makes both sides (negative and positive) helpful to people who are thinking of spending their money on a game. Applying to any game, not just this one.Pros:- Cool concept.- Art-style is beautiful (obviously).- You get to pet Moi.- Environments felt unique and well designed.- Character and animal designs are really well done.- Story was wholesome and awe inspiring.- Soundtrack was great (loved the motifs).- In my opinion, as repetitive as the stealth sections can be, there were some new things added with each environment, which helped refresh a little.- Visual storytelling was really good, especially with the abandoned ship.- I did like that Moi (your little buddy) helps you with puzzles. I thought that was pretty unique gameplay- Runs really well (for me at least).- It feels like a breath of fresh air in a sense. Since this game 'get's in and get's out' with what it's doing. Personally, I think too many games try too hard to make their games lore so unnecessarily deep and 'vital to learn' to understand whats going on. With this game, the story is simple. And I love a game with a simple story from time to time.The gameplay is good enough, has the basic necessities. Run jump, crawl, pet, etc. Basic side scroller stuff.Cons:- Stealth sections were repetitive, didn't really bother me, but I can see how that would be an issue for other players- Human models admittedly look a little weird IMO. They almost don't fit to me. Moi and the animals looked good. The humans just looked a little soulless.- There needs to be a sprint button. The game felt really slow at times when it didn't need to be.- The final stretch was a tiny bit less intense than what I felt this game needed.- I do get why people are not a fan of there being only one collectable that only offers lore. It personally didn't bother me, because I just like the hunt, but I do see why people don't admire it.- This game is a tad overpriced. For what you're getting out of it, I don't view it as entirely worth it's price tag. To fix that, I think this game could've offered more variety in gameplay and puzzles. Take that and make the game a bit longer, then the price tag would make more sense.The puzzles were kind of easy. Which can be seen as a good or bad thing. If you want an easy experience (puzzle wise), then you're in luck here. Although I wouldn't recommend this as a beginner puzzle game due to it's price tag.Overall, the game is good, and I would recommend it. Compared to back then, I do understand a lot more now on why people don't like this game at all to now. My initial review was 9/10. But now it's  a 7.8/10.
