_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's a fan of the travelling from left to right puzzle/platformer genre; this game feels lacking.If you compare it to games like Limbo/Inside the puzzles are almost nonexistent. There were only two puzzles in the whole game that actually made me recognise they're a puzzle and stop to really look at what it was I had to do. Everything else was just going through the motions. Though games like Limbo/Inside managed to also have a sense of tension, a kind of unease to push you forward, even just a curiosity about the world that makes you want to see more. I'd even say the Far games (Lone Sails and Changing Tides) manage to capture a sense of almost panic, pressuring you to succeed. Where Planet of Lana I just never felt any real engagement from the game, no reason to feel like I wanted to see more. The game just feels slow without that special something to make it stand out. The game also does the telling the background story through the... well background. Finding collectables to explain whats happening in the world but, it all feels very surface level. You can ignore the collectables as it's very easy to predict the plot just from a few hints the game drops early on. There's no twists, no turns, just what you'd expect it to be.If this game existed in a bubble where there was nothing else like it I'd recommend it, but if you compare it to similar games I just can't recommend it. It's just it feels like there are a lot of repeated scenes and puzzles to stretch out what little play time it has. There's even a few slow panning scenes with emotional music with nothing really happening just to admire the scenery if that's the type of thing you're into. Oh there's even some QTE sections which, for me, kinda killed the tone of the scenes. Like there's a scene from the early trailer but it's not gameplay it just has some button prompts plastered over the top of it.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is an art-first, gameplay later experience. This doesn't quite mean it's a walking simulator. The puzzles, while simple, are substantial enough to hold player interest across chapters. Gameplay feels like a mishmash of Inside, Hob and Far: Lone Sails. Controls work fine. The end game has a couple of challenging platforming & navigation sections but they're manageable. Including a no-death achievement however is counterproductive and unnecessary for a game of this nature (see also Bramble: The Mountain King).The visuals, painterly and gorgeous, will take your breath away. Wishfully intentionally uses a minimalist art style for characters to redirect attention toward lavish background set pieces (forests, caves, oceans, deserts) because PoL is about the journey, not the one who takes it. Takeshi Furukawa's sublime score substantiates this. The atmospheric compositions are engrossing and distinct musical motifs mark key moments. 'Horizons' is devastatingly beautiful.PoL's characters use a unique language which is a pleasure to acquire through context; the protagonist Lana often uses 'iimo' (stop) and 'olai' (follow/come) with her animal companion, Mui. Mui is unbearably cute and playing PoL will make you want a Mui of your own. Don't say I didn't warn you. The overarching story centres around the intersection of technology and nature, which, in my opinion, is overused in fantasy media and especially games (see RiME's sentinels). Despite this, and the short playtime, PoL has a message that's worth pursuing: even the corrupt can be healed through great personal sacrifice.

_childDocuments_.review: As side-scrolling adventures go, it's a good one.  A great one?  Debatable, but still very much worth your time.It's got some competition; many years later both Limbo and Inside still loom large in this field and indeed they will take some beating, for me at least.What Planet of Lana has in buckets is twofold - one is the sheer amount of polish and love that has been invested in it.  It looks amazing with a classic colour palette, visual style and sense of journey.  The second thing is the animation, which deserves a point of praise all of its own.  While I get a *lot* of Conrad Hart from Lana herself (and that's not in a bad way at all), it's the, ahem, guests and their machines which feel so well painted and designed, they move incredibly and a big hats off for that.As a game I spent around 5 hours all told, enjoyable hours at that.  From Lana's seaside fishing village, the land of sand, the underground and so on, before being welcomed to the machine.  The levels are distinct and all look great.If there is one criticism I have, it's the variety of gameplay throughout that isn't all that varied.  The puzzles, which take up the lions share of the game, are good.  Not too tricky that one must find a youtube solution, but just enough that you might have to spend a few minutes figuring out what you've got and how to use it - a sense of progression was welcome and kept me going.What I missed though, and maybe Inside has spoilt me, is a set-piece.  I can bring to mind any number of scenarios from that game many years later but for Lana, I can only think of one about 3/4 into the game and perhaps another which uses music and sand.  Both of these were very good but I couldn't help feeling, as I sent Mui to another ledge to knock down another rope, that I'd like to be on rails experiencing something a little more cinematic, just a couple more times would have done it.Anyway, great game well made and all involved should be proud.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't remember when I saw this game for the first time, but I still remember that I was instantly captivated by its charming graphics and a setting that filled me with intrigue. I tried the demo at one of the past Steam Fests, and I knew it was a game I was going to love. Planet of Lana will take us along a fantastic odyssey, putting us in the role of a young local girl and a cute creature; they will be the ones who’ll rise up in the face of adversity and try to put an end to a looming threat.The  is one of those that are not told, but shown, and follows the adventure of Lana: a small villager of the colorful planet where the game takes place. At the beginning, we’ll find ourselves in her village, where we’ll gradually learn the basic controls while we follow another villager playfully. Abruptly, we’ll observe how some huge objects fall from the sky in the distance, and soon we’ll witness the identity of these phenomena: some giant robots that seem to have invaded the planet, and who promptly kidnap the rest of the villagers, leaving Lana all alone. She will try to chase them, making her way through the wooded paths of the area, until she runs into the other main character: a curious and adorable little black animal, like an ink spot with white eyes and little ears, who will accompany us and help us from then on. With this new companion and following the same goal of finding the villagers, Lana will travel through this planet full of secrets from the past, dangerous fauna, interplanetary enemies and beautiful landscapes. It's a story that I really enjoyed from beginning to end, even though it's not of the conventional type (being non-narrated), and has several moments that range from adorable (thanks to our beloved little animal) and captivating to tense and exciting; it's a concoction of emotions that I gladly soaked up in, and it's ending left me super satisfied.The  is that of a side scroller, where we can move sideways and jump on some platforms along the way. The controls themselves are very simple, since in addition to the arrow keys we will have some interaction keys, such as activating mechanisms. However, the twist that gives this game to these mechanics is that we can ask our adorable little friend to help us, giving him indications of what we want to do. For example, tell him to activate a switch that we can't access, throw us a vine to climb, or stay somewhere in particular to attract the attention of the enemy. The use of our cute companion is the key mechanic of the game, and we will have to help each other to advance, since sometimes it will be up to us, as Lana, to activate these switches to be able to meet the little one again.As expected, there are several puzzles of different types, but most of them are very simple and give way to organic progression; and, although perhaps some make you think more than others, I feel it is unlikely to get stuck in one of them. Among these puzzles we’ll also have stealth scenes, moments where we can move machinery, and even send the cat (I don't know if it's a cat but well, the word came out of my soul) flying around in drones to activate distant mechanisms. On the other hand, not only will we have to deal with invaders, but also with more hostile wild creatures that want to eat us (or our little friend). Even so, there are not many direct encounters with enemies, but rather we’ll have to avoid them, although from time to time you can defeat some of them; what I mean is that there is no combat per se. Truly a creative section, somewhat simple in some aspects, but extremely entertaining; I want to add that in some moments there are quick time events, but those who are not fans of this mechanic can disable it in the game's options menu.The  are beautiful, drawn in a very aesthetic and colorful style, like watercolor for backgrounds and environments, and more detailed for some areas, characters and enemies. The scenes that you can observe in the distance help to create a very fictional atmosphere, showing us from desolate fields and cemeteries of giant bones, to jungles that hide vestiges of imposing civilizations that fell with the passage of time, and give an air both beautiful and catastrophic. I can say that everything mixes together very well, from the leaves on the trees and bushes, to huge robot creatures looming on the horizon, and these differences blend together to show us a welcoming and captivating world, but that has its dangers when you look for them.The , on the other hand, is a delight. Once again I fall in love with the music of a game, which has several melodies of all kinds, such as the tense classical violin tunes, or more relaxed ones with a piano or guitar. There is one song in particular that features vocals, and that detail always gets me; I loved it. The sound effects and the voices of Lana and the little creature just fit, and although they speak in another 'language', they express their intentions very well. The atmosphere that is created between the visual and sound section is excellent, going at a pace that balances the various moments of the game perfectly; two sections that shine on their own, but together they stand out so much more.In , Planet of Lana is a game that radiates effort, with very elaborate and carefully done sections, and that generated many emotions in me. I experienced super tense moments that made my skin crawl, realizing how immersed I was in the moment, and others that made me smile, like when I noticed how Lana talks in whispers with the little creature when there are enemies nearby; it's a detail that may seem simple, but I found it very cute and that it made sense. I found the animations of both our eared ink blob and the enemies, especially the robots, to be very elaborate and detailed, and I liked the puzzles quite a bit even though I'm not the biggest fan of them. I loved the cat (I know I don't know if it's a cat, let me be, but it's incredibly adorable whatever it is) and Lana, and I adored accompanying them on their adventure. It's a game that left me very satisfied with everything, and I totally recommend it to those who want to experience a charming sci-fi odyssey.

_childDocuments_.review: I've come to call these type of games 'adventure platformers', of which classics such as Another World, Flashback and Inside belong to. But even though this one doesn't bring anything new, it's serviceable enough for the genre.It should go without saying after watching the trailer that the animated art design is quite charming. Unfortunately that's the best I have to say about this title as everything else is fairly standard. The story, controls and puzzles all feel very familiar compared to similar games. All of which left me feeling a little bit bored and disappointed, leaving me with not much else to add.Don't let my play time fool you as I clocked a bit up on the Steam Deck. After playing this I'll say it's done well, especially for fans of the genre. However, with the indie space being what it is, there is a lot of stiff competition out there that have a lot more to offer. So maybe on sale if you are a die hard fan looking for a new 2D action/adventure.

Lots of interesting puzzles and also lots of opportunities to die in many different ways despite the seemingly kid-dish appearance :-)  Loved the gentle introduction/tutorial that introduces some of the basic actions, but also the remaining ones, while not explicitly mentioned, feel very natural and are easy to discover. _childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana, is a stunning and immersive experience that stands out as a piece of art in the world of gaming. This cinematic puzzle adventure takes players on a heartfelt journey through a vibrant, colourful world brimming with both charm and danger. The game's visuals are nothing short of breathtaking, with every frame feeling like a painting rich with color and detail, creating an atmosphere that's both captivating and otherworldly. The contrast between the lush, beautiful landscapes and the cold, mechanical invaders enhances the story's emotional impact, making every moment feel significant. Planet of Lana excels in its unique companion-based game play, where the young girl and her loyal friend must work together to solve a variety of puzzles that are cleverly designed and diverse in their challenges. These puzzles are not overly difficult, making the game accessible and relaxing, yet engaging enough to keep you invested. The use of stealth and wit to navigate dangerous situations adds a layer of excitement and requires thoughtful strategy. The story, which spans galaxies and centuries, is both epic and intimate. It is a tale of harmony disrupted by a faceless army, yet it remains a story of hope and resilience. The narrative doesn't dwell on war but instead focuses on the beauty of the planet and the journey to preserve it, giving the game a refreshing and poignant perspective. Playing Planet of Lana is a truly relaxing and enjoyable experience. The controls are intuitive, and the pacing is perfect for those looking to unwind and immerse themselves in a beautiful world. The game is a brilliant blend of art and adventure, making it a must-play for anyone who appreciates well-crafted games. In conclusion, Planet of Lana is an absolutely brilliant piece of gaming. Its gorgeous visuals, compelling game play, and touching story make it a standout title. Highly recommended for players of all ages, it is a testament to the potential of video games as a form of art.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick and simple: If you don't mind spending 20 bucks on a game that you complete in 5,5 hours, go get it. Otherwise wait for a sale and still go get it.Here's why:The graphics are gorgeous. You can basically stop every 5 minutes, take a screenshot, and you got yourself a new desktop wallpaper.The soundtrack is really nice, too. Not exactly a banger like Frank Klepacki's Command & Conquer music or Ben Prunty's FTL soundtrack, but still solid. And it fits the game's overall atmosphere perfectly.The gameplay is the usual liniear platforming and puzzle solving thing in the likes of Limbo, Inside, Abe's Odyssey and so on. Straight forward, nothing too complicated, nothing too fancy, but it still gets your head scratching from time to time. Especially coordinating your and your pet's abilities to solve some areas is quite fun.The story / environmental storytelling works pretty well for me, too. I won't spoiler anything here. There's no dialogue except for the made up language, there are some discoveries, there's room for interpretation. I liked that.And here and there the game just pressed the right buttons to make my cold black heart feel some genuine emotions. Well done, game, well done.Overall I can recommend this game. My only complaint would be that it's too short. I would have loved to see more of that beautiful world. But as someone with very little time for gaming nowadays I have to admit I do appreciate a short and well crafted game that can be experienced within a couple of evenings.So yeah, go get it, already!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SUPERB, from art direction to music and puzzles.Flawless ~4-5h of fair challenges in gorgeous environments interacting with characters that evoke their own personality by the way they look, move and sound. MOOD - You are the whole game on a run to save your brother under danger from unknown creatures. Despite that, there is no fear evoked but a climax of alertness, as well as many moments of tenderness and epic scenes (v.g. facing a colossal spider or running in the desert).- Character design and sounds play a big role in creating a link with the characters: cute dialogues in an unknown language (soft in danger, loud otherwise), the tender responses of your companion, or even the broken bones when the protagonist falls fromhigh.STORY- Story is explained without words, making you part of it. It is simple but good enough for a platformer, and it gives meaning to running the whole time and hiding and sorting robots and creatures. - Some disperse elements give a bit more depth to it, but do not open questions, provide a complex narrative or offer alternative paths or ideas. The story is simple and superficial.- Don't play this game for the story, as it is not its focus nor it is worth discussing it. Characters are plain, do not evolve nor have an interesting story behind them. They are not defined by their actions, complex personalities, or their own story, but by how they look, move and sound.GAMEPLAY- Every level feels new and requires more and more complex mechanics. It combines environment elements with a coordinated action of you and your companion. Timing becomes important after the mechanic has been introduced and tested by the player.- Giving orders to your companion and controlling robots and mechanical elements of the environment adds a lot of fun to the game.- Puzzles are fair and make sense. There is a little challenge, but no frustration. It is rare that help is needed, as the design and rhythm at which mechanics are introduced make it easy to follow.- Puzzles are dynamic. There is a lot of hide and seek and distraction involved in many puzzles. It requires good timing, but not infuriating precision. - Each new enemy character introduces different mechanics and approaches: the way you make them move; how they make you hide or run; how to tease or control them; the effect they have on the environment (v.g. changing water level)...ART- All levels have a very nice color palette, and there is a variety that is big enough to not get bored.- New creatures keep being introduced, all of them with their unique design style, sounds and mechanics. It is not just how they look, but their mechanic and essence that is different.- Animations are very fluid and give a lot of personality to the characters, which have a unique look and behavior, in the way they look, move and sound. - Character design is great, and varied enough. Each new character is unique for a specific reason and adds a set of game mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: Since everybody insist on comparing this game with Limbo and Inside, this is how I came to play it, and I my negative impression is mostly based on the comparison with Playdead's two games. Like in Limbo and Inside the puzzles are very simple, however the story and environment are much less interesting. There is no sense of mystery at all, fiew from the characters interactions (it's obvious what will happen with her sister at the end), and absolutely none from the environment. Always the same rocks, the same trees, the same setting that has nothing to tell us but "I am lush and wholesome Ghibli-palette nature". This kind of game is the 2D equivalent of walking simulators, there is no gameplay so the story better be interesting. Imagine playing Firewatch or Death Stranding but the story is not interesting?  That's basically Planet of Lana.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not the game I thought it was going to be. While I knew going in that this seemed to be lifting some of it's aesthetic from games like Limbo (which I've also played and enjoyed), the character of the game and the pacing of it's gameplay do not always match up.It's understandable that Lana and Mui have to put themselves in harm's way, but so many puzzles involve Lana and Mui using themselves as bait to lure away the robots or boars or something else. Not only that, but many of the puzzles can only be solved by Lana running headlong into the maws of death, just so I can learn what the pattern is that I'm trying to break.Which is to say; the puzzles have such tight tolerances as a means of creating tension, it actually takes me out. More than once, I've had to put the controller down, not because the puzzle was hard and I wanted to get it right, but because to succeed, I have to be throwing Lana and Mui-shaped dolls into the shredder. My girlfriend asked me to stop streaming the game, because of how unfun that tension turned out becoming.The oddest thing about this is that this is not remotely necessary. The game has more than enough atmosphere to keep me playing and there's already plenty of moments of tension for me to get a feel for the tone. The puzzles are just designed needlessly tight with not enough margin for error to the point that you think that you did it wrong, when you did it right, you just didn't do it slightly fast enough.I hope I will finish the game, but I have to discourage others from buying it. Some puzzles are like running into a wall and with no clear solution, until you've killed the small child character on screen enough time that the game deigns to let you pass.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm conflicted. I want to like the story, I want to like the ending. But there's just not enough to tie it together. Gameplay is not this game's strong suit, aside from some QTE cutscenes there are  only one or two challenging sequences, everything else is your standard analyse patrols and evade kind of difficult. So naturally the focus for this one lies in visuals, story and music.You can tell a lot of passion went into the graphics and music. The kind of beauty you see on the screenshots persists all the way through with some heartfelt soundtrack to go along that, no complaints there. Now let's talk story. I believe a strong combination of the 3 aforementioned factors can create a truly investing experience that can make you feel something for the characters and maybe even shed a tear during emotional points. Planet of Lana has a solid idea with a good start and end to the story but has connected these 2 points with a flimsy little string. Maybe you can dig up some lore in the little details but on my casual first playthrough things were just.. happening. There were some very vague clues dropped here and there but ultimately I had no idea what I was doing until I apparently was in the final boss room. Various interesting plot point questions were raised throughout my run but the game only ever grazed the surface in terms of explanation and rather spent more time showcasing pretty visuals. This wasn't helped much by the fictional language (which isn't bad per se, don't get me wrong) used in this game. Now I'm not saying I want a 15 minute lore dump sequence but some more clues sprinkled about as to why these machines and lifeforms act the way they do really wouldn't have hurt. Regarding the ending, it is well done and I do want to like it. But there was a certain lack of world building and I ended up feeling like that one office handshake meme for not really knowing how I just saved the world. At the end of the day being good in almost all other aspects it can certainly be enjoyed by most people but if a strong and cohesive story progression is as important to you as it is to me then this isn't your game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely gorgeous, a cinematic experience that made me think of Ghibli movies at times. I spend a long while staring at the backgrounds (and sometimes almost missed some quick time events because I stared too long at the art). The soundtrack is great and does well to elevate the scenes impact. Honestly, I am a little bit sad that there isn't a movie or show based on this game. :DThe story itself is about Lana and her loyal companion Mui who embark on a quest to rescue her friends and family who have been abducted by an otherworldly threat. It's simple, there isn't much dialogue (and most of it is in a different language tho you can get the gist of what's said) but it works for this game imo. The puzzles itself are easy to figure out but due to the stealth and timing aspects just difficult enough for you to work for success. And I do like that you have to take advantage of the abilities of your companion Mui to pass through the levels. (also!!! you can pet Mui!!!!! 10/10 i love it)Sometimes the controls felt a bit clunky to me and I got frustrated a few times because of failing to time things right and falling to my death or being caught by a threat. I did play with a controller, so I can't say how the game feels played with a keyboard.All in all the game just scratched a spot for me and I enjoyed my time with it! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I went into to Planet of Lana very hopeful. I love this genre, from Prince of Persia, Another World, and Flashback to modern renditions like Limbo, Inside, DARQ, Black the Fall, etc. This game *almost* fits the bill.It's gorgeous, to be sure. Smooth as silk and just as shiny, with music to match. Beautiful set pieces abound. But beyond that, I didn't walk away from the basic 4.5 hour runtime with any lasting impressions.The encounters are what you'd expect from the genre. The story didn't give me anything new, (but that may just be because I play and watch too much sci-fi).If you're totally new to the genre and the themes, AND you've already played Inside and Limbo, then you might enjoy Planet of Lana.For $20 though? I'd want more. Granted, I have 5 of the 10 secret collectibles to find, but the gameplay already feels too slow to want to suffer through it just to find the last 5. It's with a heavy heart I say wait for a deep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing and beautiful game. And the award for one of the most cinematic and astoundingly epic moments in video game history goes to: the desert chase sequence. Just wow! The composer, Takeshi Furukawa, needs to write music for all media; it's that amazing. Will definitely replay this game soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful experience all round. If you’re a fan of Inside, Limbo, and from the past Another World, you’ll likely love this. _childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a beautiful side-scrolling adventure that follows a young girl and her cat on a search for a lost friend. Lana witnesses the destruction of her village by an extra-terrestrial invasion and manages to escape. The rest of the game is traversing a variety of landscapes with natural challenges (chasms, hills, etc.) while evading the invaders (death ray drones, mechanical spiders, etc.).  You also find alien machinery to puzzle out and use as you make your way. The game feels a bit like LIMBO or INSIDE but has less violence and seemed a bit easier.  Your alien encounters are interspersed with long walking sequences that provide respite.I am not a cat person, but I could not help cheering for Mui - Lana's feline companion who responds to her commands and has special powers. Lana is 'the last child standing' and the cat provides friendship and assistance. All dialog is in a fictional language but the game manages to create strong emotions about love and joy, fear and loss. It also does a good job of creating an atmosphere of true menace when Lana is at risk.Typically, I do not excel in this genre. However, Planet of Lana was manageable. A couple of the evasion scenes are quite tricky as you coordinate the movements of Lana and Mui to survive. My timing failed more than a few times before I finally hit the magic combination and moved on.For me, the hardest task in the game was when I had to load Mui on a drone and fly him about without killing him. The drone controls are very wonky and keeping the drone steady without sending Mui into an electrified wall or industrial fan was quite daunting.  After several days, Mui survived my drone piloting and we were headed towards the final chapter. There is no true 'boss' battle at the end. However, there is a QTE-like exercise which almost gave me carpal tunnel. I played with a controller but there was still a lot of button mashing.The game autos-saves frequently, after each collectible (10 shrines to locate) and each major scene. Although there are some exceptions, progress on incomplete puzzles is not saved. Failure usually meant starting from the beginning of the exercise. SIgh...The art is beautiful, the music is passionate, and the story is sweet. If you don't mind some running, jumping, climbing, and stealth, then I'd highly recommend this game. Completionists have their work cut out for them... 100% requires that you survive the entire game without dying (a lofty goal, indeed!).

I am not one to play games that require fast reaction and/or quick hand/eye coordination. I also am beyond the ability for critical thinking and abstract puzzle design. Bearing those in mind this game is perfect for someone like me. Really enjoyed it ! Thank you WishFully Studios !

_childDocuments_.review: Lana is clearly inspired by Inside and similar games, and it does a good job of living up to its inspirations (but it's no Inside, which I consider a masterpiece). Lana has beautiful graphics and plenty of different biomes, so the visuals never disappoint.The story reminds me strongly of Somerville, another game clearly inspired by Inside and similar games. I think the Somerville story is quite a bit stronger, but the Lana story is interesting and has some unique elements like the relationship with your "helper." The story is straightforward, but enjoyable.The gameplay is much stronger than a game like Somerville, but not up to the level of Limbo/Inside. There are plenty of puzzles, so this is not a walking simulator (except for a few interludes), but the puzzles are not challenging and are a bit repetitive. The secret shrines are fun to find, but don't give any additional lore or endings.At 5 hours for nearly 100%, this is a pretty short game, but I enjoyed it and recommend it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: What a profoundly excellent example of how special games can be when there is love put into them. This game was made with love. I haven't been moved to write a review of a game in over a year - this broke the dry spell. Planet of Lana is a must play for ALL people, no matter what. And just like Journey was, this is the kind of game you will experience once in your life and be thirsting for something similar for the rest of time. Thank you, developers. Should there be more released for this game - DLC, whatever - I would happily pay full price. And that should go for everyone. _childDocuments_.review: Currently playing Planet of Lana.The game was inspired when Adam Stjarnljus drew a picture in 2017 and got so attached to the project he decided to start a game company and make a full game with the picture as the main inspiration and focus. He created the indie developer studio Wishfully Studios to fulfill this vision.This game is visually beautiful and the music is beautiful too. The gameplay is simple sidescroller puzzlesolving so it is a chill experience to play. To see the handpainted environments come to life through animation as you walk through the world is at times breathtaking. I highly recommend it <3
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a great piece of visual storytelling. It is, of course, extremely beautiful - this should not go unsaid, but really, a lot of games are. What really gives meaning to Planet of Lana’s beauty is its worldbuilding. It’s not pretty for the sake of it, it’s not an art exhibit either, it’s a whole meticulously thought-out world. From the vibrant colors of the forest, to the dimness of the swamp, the bareness of the desert and the black-and-white factory level, the game’s visuals mean something.As for gameplay, I had a very good time with it. It has enough puzzles and platforming to remain entertaining and is by no means an auto scroller, but it manages to not be about its challenges - ie. the element at the forefront always is the visual storytelling, as it should be in my opinion. I do have a gripe with like four levels in which the relative jankiness of the controls made them a chore to go through, but aside from those I had a great time and especially appreciated how many elements you could interact with - from Mui to the boxes to the water level to the robots, etc.Planet of Lana is a relatively simple and straightforward game, which is 100% worth experiencing.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana a cinematic  puzzle platformer with some quick time events and some precision jumping. The game play is solid but nothing spectacular. The puzzles are too easy for my taste, and the platforming is less about mastering a system a system of play as learning what buttons the game wants you to press when, an issue with cinematic platformers going back to Out Of This World.Why do I still recommend the game? Because of the CINEMATIC part of this Cinematic platformer. The music, art direction,  backgrounds, and cut scenes are of exceptional quality and show the strong influence of Miyazaki and Spielberg. This team and story may have been better served by making a film rather than a game, but when the film part of a game is of this quality, it deserves notice.   The alien monkey cat is really cute, too.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a gorgeous cinematic based 2D platformer centered around a girl whose planet has been invaded by robotic aliens.From the presentation aspect, it excels in its art style akin to games like Inside but much more colorful and full of life. So many times I had to pause in my track just to take a screenshot that might be a desktop wallpaper candidate. From the rustle of grass to the particle effects, the art direction is really well done.It's also worth mentioning the soundtrack whose melodies play a key part in setting the scene for enemy encounters, mood changes and plot developments. With the main tracks played by violins and actual lyrics, the game doesn't shy away from showing it off particularly in some transitions throughout the world, making us feel like a part of Lana's journey.Then there's the gameplay that controls similarly to others from this particular genre such as the old Prince of Persia games or Limbo. The player must take into account the delay of their actions shown through the animations while solving the accessible to somewhat clever stealth puzzles that are sent in their way. While in my experience none of them were particularly troublesome, my biggest gripe came with the flawless achievement (beating the game without dying) which goes against the trial and error nature of some of these obstacles.Regardless, a playthrough of it can be enjoyed by both the player and their viewers. For its price I'd say it is worth checking out even in the midst of a great year for game releases.

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous, well-made little limbo-like, with a nice twist around controlling a cat-like companion. It's worth noting that the puzzles don't ever ramp up in difficulty, which while making it easier to get through and enjoy the simple narrative, was also a little disappointing. It's a fine balance and I'd certainly prefer Lana's approach over other games I've played that get too challenging, taking me out of the narrative and sometimes leading me to give up.Well worth the 5 or so hours I put into it!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a mixture of an interactive novel/movie and a puzzle platformer. I finished the game in just over 5 hours and it was neat, but not really satisfying. For me it feels like by trying to mix three genres, all were done okay to good but none fulfilled their potential / promise.Story: The story is cute, the visuals GORGEOUS and it has a few unexpected twists, but its rather straightforward / predictable most of the time. There is no dialogue so its mostly environmental story telling. In some cases this is done really well, and I could order things I'd seen at different times into the narrative, but it still felt lacking in detail and depth. It is also quite slow paced, even when there's no puzzles; many sections are just walking through wonderful graphics.Platforming: The platforming has beautiful animations but pays for that in precision. That makes puzzles often tedious. Sometimes you can play as other entities than the player in the game, which I always found a lot more fun than playing & moving as Lana herself.Puzzles: I did have several satisfying aha moments and I really liked how each section of the game added a few new mechanics that changed up the puzzles. My deal breaker is that, while It is mostly easy to figure out what to do, it's then difficult / tedious to actually do it. I found the vision cones of enemies a bit ambiguous, fall damage hard to estimate plus had the above troubles with the not-so-precise platforming.Accessibility: In my opinion, it's straight out rude to provide a warning for photo-sensitive viewers at the start of the game but no accessibility setting to turn it off, nor a second warning before it happens. It was only one scene in the final cut scene so it wouldn't have been so much work and an ambiguous warning at the start is extremely unhelpful and seems more like a legal protection than actual care or consideration for photo-sensitive gamers.In summary, this game relies heavily on its amazing graphics and beautiful music, but the game play was not very satisfying to me, and the story not as gripping as I'd hoped. It's still a pretty good way to spend a couple of hours on the weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - Beautiful Game. Optimistic and light in genre full of solemn heaviness.- Simple, yet solid story carried through by wonderful world-building and lore.- Doesn't over stay its welcome and drives forward. There isn't really weak part of the game.Cons:- The movement is rigid. You're given all the tools you need to complete the game, but you definitely feel how limited it is.- Its definitely a "first game" not many chances were taken with game play or presentation and even though its a completely satisfactory game, it can leave you wishing Wishfully Studios had allowed themselves more room to be creative and experiment with new or unfamiliar mechanics.Planet of Lana is a great addition to the PlayDead style narrative-driven side scroller. It approaches a genre mostly comprised of somber, macabre and stark artistry from the complete opposite angle and gives you a optimistic, lively and vibrant world to traverse. It keeps the tradition of using the camera to really show case the vastness and beauty of the game from time to time. You'll find yourself hitting the screen shot button more than few times.As the title states, it is an odyssey (in about 5 hours). Unlike its peers, its fairly straight forward with a definable beginning, middle and end. Though the story is simplistic, its wrapped in pretty enthralling world building that boast a fun blending of humanities and classic sci-fi.The music is good, maybe not Bastion or Spiritfarer good, but definitely notable. I'd put it a step down from Inside. It is also very important for game play, keep your ears open and pay attention to what you hear!The controls are simple and while it gives you everything you need overcome all the challenges Lana faces, you'll definitely feel the rigidity of her movement that will leave you wondering why they just didnt add sprinting or why she can only jump a foot off the ground. The double sided puzzle solving with Mui is very fun though and though the limitations make actions themselves feel stiff, the responsiveness allow you to correct mistakes as they're happening if you're quick enough.Most of the puzzles are classic platforming with just a couple of hint/deciphering puzzles. Nothing to write home about, but enjoyable none the less. There were definitely times were I made it harder than it had to be because I forgot a key piece of information (despite it being reemphasized through out the game) or because I didnt believe I could jump the distance needed (again, the movement gives you everything you need. Believe in Lana, you can jump that gap or reach that ledge without doing any cheesing)As far as technical stuff goes, I had only one noticeable hick up and that was loss of frames during the Coastal Town level, which is a little puzzling for a rather undemanding game running on a high-end PC. This was only momentary as you dont stay there long, but definitely caught my attention. I'm not sure if Wishfully intends to do a optimization pass on the game, but if they dont Im sure that issue will be addressedOver all this, is a great little game and a wonderful first impression by Wishfully Studios. Their artistic abilities cannot be overstated and while I enjoyed the story in Planet of Lana I hope that they spread their wings a little more and allow themselves as much creativity with the plot as the do their lore crafting. I enjoyed my time and I think others will too. If anything we'll all be yearning for that simple life in lush beautiful world.

_childDocuments_.review: This game can be summed up as:"Mom can we play Inside?""No honey we have Inside at home"Inside at home:I am almost completely 50/50 for loving/hating this game.Pros:Absolutely gorgeous game. Provides an immense sense of scale, with towering titanic enemies moving past in the distance, and beautiful vistas stretching to the horizon. Absolutely wonderful to look at.The lore is sparse but very interesting and immediately understandable through very little communication, which is very impressive and well done. This is very much a "show not tell" game. You can pet the companion, which is always nice, and overall the game has a very cute feel to it.The cons:The character has only one speed of movement, and it's not agonizingly slow but it's far from fast. This game desperately needed a sprint button. The enemies are all much much faster than you, which if done well can heighten the tension of a game, but unfortunately instead of tension I got frustration.  There were also multiple periods of just walking and looking at the background, (including an odd out of place 4 minute music interlude) no puzzles, no interaction, just hold the left joystick to the right. Get ready to hold that left joystick to the right *a lot*. With how simple a lot of the puzzles are this game is almost a walking simulator. There's a ton of puzzles that require almost frame perfect timing, and with your character's movement speed, enemy patrol patterns and save points, those three elements often combine to equal waiting for upwards of 30 to 40 seconds to retry a frame perfect moment, missing, dying and getting reset and having to wait 30 to 40 seconds for another chance at a frame perfect moment.  None of the puzzles were *super* complex, but were however difficult to solve due to timing and platforming. This often led to me having solved the puzzle logically in my head, but then needing to execute in real time, and dying over and over due to requiring frame perfect jumps or timing enemy patrols.There was a huge amount of repetition, it seemed like they made you send the companion up a cliff to toss down a rope to you at least 30 different times.If it were longer than it is I wouldn't recommend it. But if you get it on sale it's fun to kill an afternoon, if a little tedious and frustrating. But I'd rather play Inside.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is the first game that truly awoke my love for gaming on PC/laptop and for that alone I'm grateful to have played this beautiful game. I got this game due to its bright and illustrative art style, and cuz its not scary lol. I'm very satisfied with its entire premise. The story was not explained as well as I thought it would but the aspect of being able to interpret the story subjectively is fun too! however, I was the most satisfied with the intriguing, clever and slightly frustrating puzzles tbh. I used to think puzzle games are no good for me, but after playing this game I'm sure they are fun af given they are not mind-numbingly difficult. And I cant express how much I love the landscapes when coupled with the gentle and smooth soundtracks!! It all really adds to the magical feeling of being swept by the game and brings peace after a particularly challenging puzzle haha!Lastly, the characters Lana and Mui are ones to be remembered, especially Mui!! _childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a breathtakingly beautiful adventure game with a cinematic focus. Featuring simple, but clever puzzles, awe-inspiring landscapes and a poignant soundtrack that culminates into a memorable sci-fi odyssey. The protagonist is a young girl named Lana who lives a pleasant and comfortable life within a small community. Unbeknownst to her, a looming threat is becoming nearer, a threat that will destroy the harmonious balance between mankind and nature. Before long, the tranquillity is abruptly shattered, and her best friend Ilo is taken. The village is in shambles and malevolent robots have taken hold of everything she once knew. This begins Lana’s adventure to pursue the robots and find her friend, but she does not face the journey alone. It is not long before she meets a small and adorable creature named Mui. Mui becomes Lana’s companion for the remainder of the game and plays a fundamental role in the gameplay. There is no dialogue, as the characters appear to speak a fictional language, but the narrative is told through the beautiful surroundings, landscapes, soundtrack, and the tone of Lana’s voice. The story is not something entirely new, moreover, similar stories have been told many times, but it provided more than enough intrigue and mystery to keep me interested.  It is a story about friendships, courage, and cooperation. A heart-warming tale that mixes the essence of these themes, and thrusts them into a puzzle, sci-fi adventure.Before going into detail, the gameplay is more on the simpler side of adventure-puzzlers. If you are looking for something challenging, something with multiple different solutions to puzzles, or a game that may leave you stumped for a few minutes, this may not be the game for you. Planet of Lana excels with its graphical beauty and atmosphere, and whilst its gameplay is not bad by any means, it is not complex.Gameplay is almost solely based on companion-style puzzles, light stealth elements and platforming. Lana cannot directly attack the robots, so she must sneak past them, hide in long grass, and utilise Mui to reach higher places, hit buttons and so forth. Mui must be directed to stay or follow, chew through wires, jump up to a certain spot and more. Timing is typically the biggest challenge with these segments. I did feel that developers aptly introduced new mechanics as the game progressed, expanding players options so it never felt repetitive. Mui learns a myriad of new skills and Lana uncovers new ways to control the robots. There is no inventory management or puzzles involving picking up objects and the simplicity helps keep the game in motion. Becoming stuck on a specific puzzle would feel out of place to me, as this would ultimately deduct from the wondrous atmosphere that the game oozes. The game is also very forgiving and autosaves frequently. If a robot spots Lana or Mui, unless blocked, it will automatically kill them. Despite being heartbreaking to watch Mui die, there are no real consequences to this, as you will just respawn almost exactly where you died.The entirety of Planet of Lana mostly follows the same formula of companion style puzzles, however there are some quick-time events splattered in latter sections. The ending of the game also felt unusual and slightly out of place, but I can only deduce that the developers were trying to do something different for the finale, and it wasn’t too jarring to negate the game's previous accomplishments. There are also some collectable shrines to be discovered throughout the levels, but this is the only extra content the game offers, and these are also linked to achievements. I did not find all the shrines, but I still took approximately 6 hours of playtime to finish. Stopping momentarily to soak in the gorgeous environments surrounding me. However, I have seen some people reach the credits in 3 hours or less.  Bugs were very minor and scantily impacted my experience, however there were enough to be noticeable. During a scene that is supposed to be a swell of emotion and triumph, the foreboding eerie music from the previous scene was still playing, detracting from this moment entirely. In retrospect, this ill-matching audio only happened this one time. Another bug that I encountered a handful of times seemed to be caused when trying to exit an animation too quickly. Resulting in the character staying in a statue, unable to interact with objects or jump, just stuck forever in a T-pose until I reloaded my save.Undoubtedly the most standout feature is the gorgeous visuals. With a plethora of motley landscapes to trek across, ranging from deserts to lush green forests to barren caves and factories. Another impressive element that cannot be fully appreciated from screenshots alone, is the excellent camera and cinematography. Despite being a side-scrolling adventure, Planet of Lana does not feel limited by this. Often in large-scale areas the camera will pan or zoom out, giving an entirely different view to players. There were never any issues with this, it never felt unresponsive or awkward, it just worked, and it worked flawlessly. I also must mention how utterly delightful Mui is. The small cat-like creature bounds gleefully at Lana’s heels throughout the game and is simply adorable.Whilst there is no dialogue, the soundtrack matches the level of quality seen in the visuals, aptly capturing the highs and lows that Lana encounters. Understandably so, as this original soundtrack was composed by Takeshi Furukawa, a highly acclaimed composer known for his work in  and many more. Six hours whilst taking my time but can be completed in as little as three. Yes, the developers also recommend this. Being a linear puzzle adventure, not really. However, there are some achievements and collectibles that may warrant a second playthrough for some.Planet of Lana is a gorgeous cinematic adventure game that when combined with its emotive soundtrack, radiated beauty in every scene. Puzzles are not too challenging but had a great balance in difficulty and were an adept medium in storytelling. Being  debut game is an impressive feat, and I am eager to see what else arises from these developers.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game, and judging by the player reviews, you might like it yourself. And if so, great. But I do want to say that how much you like this game might depend on your experience with other cinematic platformers and other tearjerker games.Basically, this is a standard game of its genre, except the puzzles are simpler (I was stumped only once), there are a bit too many "keep running to the right while you see scenery, for dramatic effect" moments for my liking, and it tries to jerk tears in predictable ways involving an alien that you adopt as a pet, which follows you around and becomes required for puzzle solving. (If it dies, you lose.) Can you guess what happens to the alien later? Yup. Can you guess what happens AFTER that happens? Yup. But if you've never played a cinematic platformer before, or a game which tries to jerk tears, then this is a good place to start. Because it still does these things well enough. Graphics are beautiful and downright stunning at times. The story is told through the environment and occasionally cutscenes without dialog that only zoom in the camera, if that, as the characters emote through animation. The camera freezes in place when in a puzzle or action zone to fit all of it on the screen, until it's completed, which is a feature I really like: basically, the camera moves when you're traveling, but stops to show everything that's important when you need to solve a puzzle or evade an enemy. Being a cinematic platformer, you move almost like a real human, with movement limited to climbing and dropping down, jumping only as high as a real (albeit athletic) person, and pulling and pushing things - or controlling other things remotely. And giving commands to your pet, for the game's many puzzles which require the two of you to work together.It's a competently made cinematic platformer that tries to make you cry a few times. But I've played games that  jerked real tears, and this one just made me roll my eyes in annoyance and think, "I get it, it's supposed to be sad." That's not their developers' intended effect, but I'm sorry, the storytelling just didn't work for me. I never felt attached to Mui, the little animal you adopt for a few hours. And I know everyone talks in a made-up language, but their language seems to have like ten words total, which I also find hard to take seriously.So, just keep in mind what you're getting if you decide to buy this. If my complaints are about things that wouldn't bother you, then hey, buy this game and enjoy it more than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a classic case of style over substance. Sure, the art is stunning—almost distractingly so—but that’s the only compliment I can muster for this game. It’s as if the developers thought that pretty pictures could mask a complete lack of creativity and gameplay depth.The puzzles are mind-numbingly simplistic, bordering on insulting. I found myself wondering if I was playing a game or just watching a glorified slideshow of vibrant backgrounds. The story tries hard to be poignant but ends up being as flat as a pancake, leaving no emotional impact whatsoever.It’s hard to believe that a game with such gorgeous visuals could be so utterly forgettable. Planet of Lana is a beautiful waste of time, where you’re left staring at the screen, wishing you could shake some life into this lifeless shell. If you’re looking for an engaging experience, keep looking—this is not it.

I played on a keyboard which made things more difficult at times than I would have liked, but I progressed at a steady enough pace that the two or three times my fingers weren't up to what my brain had figured out weren't too frustrating. To this effect, it took me 7 hours to solve the game and I may go back to gather achievements after a week or two break. This was just what I needed. #TotallyCharmed #HighlyRecommended

_childDocuments_.review: This beautiful game is such good desktop wallpaper material that I rebound my controller to have a dedicated screenshot button.Planet of Lana is a visually outstanding, mechanically minimalistic cinematic platformer with a straightforward yet engaging 'silent' narrative. The themes of nature versus unknown/amorphous technology are well executed and the style is definitely up my alley. For gameplay, it's the standard cinematic platformer affair: lots of holding right, rudimentary box puzzles, and basic stop-and-go stealth. Thankfully, Planet of Lana manages to have a few interesting ideas for puzzles, but the game is mostly worth playing for the 'cinematic' elements alone. Anyone who finds themselves enjoying games of this likeness will find a few hours briskly walking through Planet of Lana to be a quite pleasant experience.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a simple enough 3D side-scroller puzzle platformer. It offers a pleasant soundtrack and engaging atmosphere. It does have an interesting story delivered without words. _childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what I would label as a "simple masterpiece." It's not anything groundbreaking in game design or story telling, but it's just so well done and so simple. The graphics and art style are amazing. It's a very simple art design with more minimal detailing that looks clean yet beautiful. The sound design is also incredibly well done and really helped pull everything together into a more immersive experience. The story was done without any spoken dialogue or written text, yet it was both cute and very moving throughout the whole journey. I felt really attached to the characters and kept wanting to see more of where the journey was headed. The end of the journey was so captivating it had me in tears (not going to say if they were happy or sad tears). Not many games make me feel much emotion, especially the way Planet of Lana did.The game isn't very long; it can be completed in several hours. The gameplay itself is simple. Jump platforms, solve puzzles, evade enemies. The puzzles are not too difficult but sometimes will make you think a little bit which adds a feeling of accomplishment. There's no combat, but you will have to figure out ways to evade enemies or they will straight up kill you.If you like any of these things mentioned you will probably like this game. I felt so immersed, I usually have videos or live streams on the background when I game, but I had to keep pausing it for this game just to experience what was happening. The sound design and art style played a huge part in making things so captivating. I would put this up there with games like Outer Wilds and Stray, which are very different games, but similar in the sense they have a unique art style and unique way of telling a story which breaks out from the typical gaming standard.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: The fact that "PlayDead-Like" makes any sense as a moniker is a testament to the strength of that studio, and this comes closer to the ludo-narrative impact and polish of Limbo and Inside than almost all of the many puzzle platformers inspired by them.If Somerville played like an awkward and arrhythmic imitation of what makes these games tick, Planet of Lana manages to feel like a beautiful celebration of the form, despite the narrative playing things somewhat safe and the puzzle design being merely "strong" to PlayDead's "inspired."One of the nicest side effects of narrative puzzle platformers being insanely hard to execute at this quality is that they almost never drag on or overstay their welcome in a market filled with live service "forever games" competing to become your next habitual lifestyle...Fans of the form should enjoy Planet of Lana today while dreaming about the third PlayDead game of tomorrow.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: - You love story focused games- You love beautiful whimsical worlds- You enjoy clever simple puzzles - Don't mind a game in the 3-5 hour range- Are a fan of both INSIDE and Ghibli- You want tremendously difficult puzzles- Prefer crunchy mechanic focused games- Aren't a fan of games where the main reward is the story- Nothing about the world portrayed in the trailer sparked curiosity in youI love an infinite AAA game that you can pour years of your life into without ever scratching the bottom as much as the next person. Sometimes that's what I want, sometimes I really just want to be somewhere else for weeks at a time, to have an experience that I know will always be there with something new for me to do.And sometimes I want Planet of Lana.I've been desperate for something to scratch the INSIDE itch since it released years back. Planet of Lana scratches that itch with a more adventurous upbeat tone that still has a fair smattering of dark spooky moments. The puzzles aren't going to make your head explode but the way your companion is integrated into them leads to some super clever and satisfying solutions.Plus the composer worked on The Last Guardian, the music really really makes the game and helps reinforce that wondrous feeling of adventure.it also has some of the best alien wildlife ambiances I've heard in a while. Each location feels like it's full of very diverse alien creatures, most of which are conveyed through sound alone.I had a great time, some very tense moments, some very tender moments, some slightly frustrating moments, overall well worth 20 bucks if you meet the above criteria.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game in all aspects. Reminded me of Limbo, crossed with the golden oldie Another world, in its earnest simplicity and visual storytelling.Mechanically, the game plays spectacularly. The controls are well thought out and precise, and the environment almost always communicates clearly about what options you have in every situation.The visuals... Oh the visuals. This game is extraordinarily beautiful, especially when you see the environments in motion. Together with the music, and the unwaveringly cute voice, giggles and squeaks of the main heroine and her pet make for an excellent game atmosphere.Overall, the game is exactly what I hoped it would be - light platforming, some light puzzling and an excellent story told entirely in subtle visual clues, so your mind is free to fill in details.Overall score: 11/10.(The extra point is because YOU CAN PET THE PET and it's super satisfying! :-) )
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: The artists did a wonderful job with this game... but that's really the only praise I have.The puzzles being so repetitive was honestly one of my most minor criticisms (in fact, I thought they were pretty good for the most part). The whole idea of the story in this game just felt so lacking and dispassionate: you have this beautifully painted world invaded by robots, but as you progress through the story, it becomes clear that the natural dichotomy of nature vs machine which one might expect to be explored in a game such as this, is actually too complicated for the storytellers to bother with: animals (aside from your eventual companion Mui) are portrayed largely just as """bad""" as the robots themselves (and ) and in the end,  There seemed like a lot of potential for lore in the shrines and the "communication" with the machines, especially in , but in the end it turned out to all just be an effortless tack-on perhaps for the collectathon minded.The creators wanted a world reminiscent of a Studio Ghibli film. They achieved the beautiful paint, but got lazy with everything else. I was very disappointed in this game, and would not recommend it. If you want a puzzle-exploration game that is actually inspired and full of heart, I would recommend a game like Tchia.

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game that takes you on an atmospheric adventure of friendship and brevity. The story simple yet well told even though there is not a single word spoken in any language you speak. Whilst playing you discover a fantastic world full of fascinating creatures. You can feel right into the characters and you might shed a tear or two.The game plays similar to  or , but in a much brighter, colorful way. It is way more forgiving than LIMBO and less just running than INSIDE, yet you get a fair amount of just running, which I'd say is the only downside to this game. The puzzles are easy and logical, the shrines are not too easy to find but also not unfairly covered and if you tread carefully you might even manage to not die on your first run - although I'd recommend a backup copy of your savegames, just in case. It had light puzzles, a fantastic soundtrack, and incredible storytelling; my favourite combination in a game.The puzzles kept me engaged as a player, and weren't too difficult  in that they would lead to frustration. It struck just the right balance for me. As a video game music fanatic, the OST was a must for my VGM playlist. _childDocuments_.review: I liked the game overall.Positives: 1. Art is amazing, animations are cute, the world is alive with small animated details. The story is clear and easy to follow, while also developing over the course of the game and revealing nuance. The music can be relaxing, but also tense at the right moments, and I liked the original songs.2. Puzzles are usually interesting and varied, especially because you play as two characters, Lana and Mui who each have their own strengths and weaknesses. Puzzles generally have one solution and can't be exploited. Only 1 or 2 puzzles stumped me, but not so much that I needed to look up a guide. I only feel like I solved 1 or 2 puzzles in an "unintended" way.3. SPOILERS: "Boss battle" at the end is pretty fun.Negatives:1. I only really have one. At times, the game seems to drag needlessly. I understand the more cinematic moments that show the great lengths Lana goes to save Ilo, but sometimes puzzles are repeated verbatim or there are long sequences where extent of the gameplay is holding the right arrow. Some (few, but still worth mentioning) of the rooms seem repetitive, rehashing the same puzzle with no added story or gameplay element. Then the next room the puzzle will make me think about the environment in a completely new way, which is awesome. I just want less of the former and more of the latter.It's hard not to compare this to INSIDE, and if I were to do that, I would have to say INSIDE is the better game. However, this game is quite good too, but I have more here to criticize.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to go with a light recommendation for Planet of Lana. There are a few stretches of this game that could have been trimmed down big time. It feels like it's about an hour too long. There are only a handful of types of puzzles that you and your little cat/alien buddy named Mui solve, and there was a point about an hour and a half into it where I just wanted to feel some kind of progression. It was just the same puzzles over and over again and that section definitely overstayed its welcome. It picks up again around the middle, but then it falls into that same pacing issue a bit towards the end, but the third act pretty much overall, is really nice and emotionally satisfying, and really saves the game. But, there are definitely a few badly paced, repetitive chunks. Sorry but I need to go on a little tangent here... any RedLetterMedia fans might be reminded of the movie Nukie (a terrible 80s b-movie that they watched and was referenced in their videos for years). I only say that because really all the main character does is call out for her sister ("Elo!!!!"), and the opening of the game there is a section where they are calling out to each other over and over, ("Lana!" "Elo!!" "Lana?!" "Elo?!", etc etc)  and it just immediately reminded me of Nukie, which gave me a laugh. If ya know, ya know...With that said, the art design, the score, the sound design, and the narrative (which is all visual storytelling) are all top notch. There are defintely several moments of real beauty, awe, and emotion, and I have to give the game a lot of credit for engaging me in that sense. If you enjoy these types of games (this is very similar to something like INSIDE, which I loved), then I would definitely recommend this. Definitely stay away if these artsy platformer puzzle games are not your cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: Planet of Lana is a captivating masterpiece that seamlessly blends stunning visuals, an engaging storyline, and thought-provoking gameplay elements. Set in a mesmerizing hand-painted world, the game takes you on an emotional journey alongside a young girl named Lana and her loyal companion, a small alien critter named Mui. Together, they navigate through a beautiful yet perilous universe, unraveling the mysteries that lie within.The game's art style is a breathtaking work of art, with vivid colors and intricate details that transport you to a realm of wonder. Each frame feels like a carefully crafted painting, bringing the world of Lana to life with every step you take. The atmospheric soundtrack complements the visuals perfectly, immersing you deeper into the enchanting experience.But it's not just the aesthetics that make Planet of Lana compelling. The gameplay mechanics are equally impressive. With puzzles to solve and obstacles to overcome, you'll find yourself challenged while still feeling a sense of tranquility. Instead of focusing on fast-paced action, the game encourages you to take your time, observe your surroundings, and approach each situation with a calm and collected mindset.The game has also great support for ultra wide resoltuions: Planet of Lana is more than just a game; it's a work of art that transports you to another world. It provides a sanctuary where you can escape the chaos of reality and immerse yourself in a beautifully crafted universe. With its rich storytelling, stunning visuals, and serene gameplay, this game invites you on a journey of self-discovery, reminding you to appreciate the beauty that exists in both the smallest moments and the grandest landscapes.
_childDocuments_.name: Planet of Lana

_childDocuments_.review: My name is Lana and that was the sole reason that I became initially interested in this game. However, that being said, I was overjoyed to find that this filled an INSIDE shaped hole in my heart. I love 2D platformers, such as Limbo and INSIDE, especially of the abstract / surrealistic variety. This checked all my boxes. Stunning artwork? Check. Gorgeous soundtrack? Check. Abstract and avant-garde execution? Check. Bonuses: You get an adorable cat companion that you can pet. Also, there are some moments that really hit hard emotionally. I got teary eyed a few times. There is a plot line, yes, but the game definitely urges you to use your own imagination while you go on the journey of unraveling the plot. In my opinion, the plot was loose and very abstract for most of the game, but towards the end, everything came together and everything made sense. The game is 90% about the journey and 10% about the actual plot. Like I said, by the end, it's very obvious what the whole journey was about and everything starts to completely make sense. I highly recommend it. It's such a relaxing and chill game that's embedded with occasional moments of tension and dread. Definitely kept me on the edge of my seat. The game had a slow start for me, but once it gained traction, I couldn't put it down. I finished it in one sitting and can't stop smiling and gushing about how wonderful it was.

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game,  I don't so much recommend it as not *not* recommend it.  But I can only give it a thumps up or down, not a "meh," kind of handwave. TL;DR:+ The game is pretty, colorful, sentimental and whimsical.  The art and music are fantastic and it has a good 'feel' to it. - It feels like a more colorful and sentimental but ultimately lesser version of the game Planet Alpha.  I spent MOST of my time playing through going, "Yup. Feels like a Planet Alpha ripoff."  I try not to make direct comparisons to other games while playing because I think that even similar games with a lot of overlap can provide rewarding experiences!  In a somewhat niche market of sidescrollers like this though, it brings nothing new to the table and generally offers less than its competitors...more of which named below.  The Likes:The graphics are whimsical and very pretty at times.  The sound and music is very well done :)  The 'story' progression is nicely told through scenery and observation.   If you've had limited experience with these types of games (others being Limbo, Inside, Planet Alpha, (arguably) FAR: Lone Sails etc) it'll probably all feel very novel and charming!  Dying (which will happen a lot no matter how careful you are as  you sort through things) is a zero penalty affair, which is good for this sort of game.  You typically start back with little if any progress lost.  Controls are simple and the required button pushes are often labeled for anything more complicated that jumping.  You WILL NOT find yourself getting stuck or hung up because you can't remember the buttons for a specific action.  If you've never played a game like this before, it's a good primer to the genre :)  Now the criticisms:   Total gameplay if you take your time is probably 6ish hours?  I have 9.5 hours logged but think I left it running in the background while I ran errands somewhere so the timer's a bit off.   If you liked it enough to play through it again and search for all of the secret locations you'll clearly get more out of it.  ....but understand that a normal runthrough will only last you an evening, maybe two. ...not much in the way of puzzles. There were a few which made me scratch my head for a minute or two, but most of the game involves virtually identical types of simple setups to navigate through.  "Instruct your companion to climb up there and throw the rope down.  Climb the rope."     "Hide in the grass, find a way to get the robot to get on the other side of you, run to the next hiding place."   Often LITERALLY identical setups.  There is very little variation. The flow of the game can be frustrating.  Almost every bit of terrain you'll encounter throughout the entire world will require you to jump and climb with little deviation.  No casual jumps which allow you to keep moving at a regular place while providing variety to the terrain and ambiance..   Just lots of completely unnecessary standardized up and down and ups and downs as filler which can feel very unnatural as you move through the world.   Transition between playing and cutscenes feels awkward and also upsets the flow.   Instead of shifting naturally from character movement into the cutscene, the screen goes black and comes back...but it's the exact same kind of animation and camera control as the game.  I know it would have required a bit more effort to move seamlessly from one to the other and there are limits to the time and resources devs can put towards things.  ...but it bothered me every single time it happened and devs from other projects have done it pretty well. The 'story' itself...if you've never played any other similar games, is somewhat charming.  To me it felt like a less involved version of Planet Alpha with fewer puzzles and less interaction with the terrain and surrounding world in general. Overall: It's a cute game with a bit more sentimental/whimsical feel than most of the other games I've referenced .   ..but that's ALL it has setting it apart.  Given my play history with other similar type games which I feel did almost every element of playstyle better than this one, I can't really recommend Planet of Lana.  BUT.  I can't in good conscience *not* recommend it just because I think that many other games have already done almost literally everything this game set out to do and did it better.  It's a decent game and despite what I consider an overall lack of creativity and over-reliance on the same few tricks, clearly a lot of love and effort went into it and it shows.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely, wonderfully crafted masterpiece. It's fun, relaxing and enjoyable. _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game a lot. It's a beautiful cinematic platformer with an excellent soundtrack, fun puzzles, and a heartfelt story. This is an example of how to tell a story with no dialogue. The speech featured here is in a probably fake language, but the message is clear nonetheless. The presentation is the highlight here. The visuals and soundtrack mesh perfectly. Its art direction reminds me of Studio Ghibli with the vibrant colors and cutesy models. Despite being 2.5D, the environments have a lot of depth to them. The backgrounds are full of detail and showcase impressive scale making the world feel huge. There are moments that feel like I'm watching a good animated movie.As is typical of the genre, there are chase sequences, semi-realistic movement, puzzles, and one-hit deaths. It's not a difficult game at all and can be beaten in a single playthrough. The controls are tight and platforming isn't as complicated as some other cinematic platformers like the old Oddworld games. Directing the companion is simple and easy to do. It's also very adorable and you can pet it whenever. There's a good variety of locations like underground caverns, the swamp, a desert area, and a high tech facility.I don't have many complaints, but I thought the quick time events were out of place. I'd prefer more gameplay or just another cutscene. The final boss is rather lackluster. You just time some jumps and do an easy QTE. I also found the repeated fade to blacks distracting and odd since it fades to black before a cutscene plays following whatever you were doing in gameplay. Nonetheless, I think it's a great simple game. It's definitely style over substance, but the style is really incredible and the substance isn't bad. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is made by an Indie Developer, and so I definitely give this game a high score probably a 9/10. I look forward to the next episode in the series. It's a mix of a walking simulator with some light puzzles, some nice music, and a cool heart warming story.Pretty good game with at least six hours of content. I'd recommend playing through this with some friends or some young kids if you have any. There are puzzles that aren't too difficult, some platforming challenges, and a pretty cool Sci-Fi flavored storyline. There are no words or reading in the whole game, so anyone of any age should be able to play along with you as you run through this. The only challenge would be one part, which is a mathematical puzzle that involves binary, and I think that will be probably be the most challenging part.I had a good time and enjoyed the storyline. It warns about flashing lights, and that's mostly at the end of the game besides some bright flashing when you launch the game. I have some eye sensitivity so I really wish games had an option to turn off bright flashes, but it didn't bother me too bad.
