_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a middle option for reviews, as having only yes or no kind’ve forces you to swing a certain way. So, despite enjoying the game myself and certainly recommending it to some, I’m voting ‘Not Recommended’ in hopes the devs will take notice of some critiques. I wrote down my thoughts, and would be remiss if I didn’t post it and add my voice in the mix in hopes things may change for the better!NOTE: I have unlocked all the characters and put in a fair bit of playtime, but I've yet to beat the 'story' mode, or play online, and I’ll try to keep this review ‘spoiler free’, but I want to lay out my thoughts as I go through the game, as it hits a sweet spot for me and I just HAVE to write a review, and hopefully give others insight if they're on the fence and maybe the devs will notice if this game picks up off the ground. I try to go into detail about my reasoning for things and can be a bit long winded, but if you're fine with all that, read on, else check out my final thoughts at the bottom!Pros:+ The soundtrack, obviously. It’s varied and there’s a whole bunch of variety in genres.+ Soundfall lets you drop right into the entire playlist of the game’s ~100 songs, with the added bonus of being able to import your own. (Note *1)+ Controls are snappy, it feels like a blast to play. The game itself seems very polished.+ A decent variety in character abilities, there's bound to be something there for every type of player to carve their own play style. (Note *2)Cons:-  Some of the equipment mechanics are locked behind rarer loot tiers (e.g. double/triple dash, longer ultimates, more range, etc.) which make the lower tiers immediately feel bland upon trying them out. There is also no infusion/upgrade system to bring your favorite weapons up to par. This leaves players out of luck later when they find a rare weapon at low level.- The game too slowly drip-feeds you exp, mechanics, characters and difficulty, which could bore some players at the outset before things pick up in the late game. Character unlocks are tied to story progression, which makes getting to 'new' things feel a bit sluggish. Plus, if you  play free play and ignore the story, you’re stuck with  playable character. (Note *3)- Levels within the same 'biome' feel samey, procedural generation could be to blame and might benefit from more varied path 'tiles'. For a game with procedural generation, the song is the same, every time, except via higher difficulties, but that only changes the monsters you encounter, not the layout. Every time I know exactly what to expect, and while it can be good for mastering a song in a rhythm game, it does not work well for a grindy looter-shooter with freeform movement and gunplay. (Note *4)* Note *1 - One of the characters is nearly identical to another with some seemingly minor tweaks to their skillset, while not game-breaking, feels a bit underwhelming after playing the others, which are more vastly different in comparison.* Note *2 - The imported song generation can work great on some songs, but is also fickle, as some songs will straight up be off beat on import. Though the devs have posted a third party workaround which is neat, albeit a slight bit convoluted for the 'average' gamer.* Note *3 - I feel the exp curve should be half of what it is, as unlocking higher difficulties can feel grindy and slow. It’s also unfortunate that because of the way the game is structured with power level, lower difficulties become ‘obsolete’ because you gain power over time, so pairing someone new to the game with people who’ve already mastered it just doesn’t mesh well. Unlocking characters is tied to story progression, so while jumping into freeplay play from the get-go is nice, you can’t unlock the more varied characters, so you may as well just play the campaign if you don’t want to import music. Speaking of importing music brings me to my next point.* Note *4 - There is no way to customize an imported song’s biome - Sometimes an EDM song can make a volcano biome (usually attributed to Rock), sometimes a rock song can put you on the beach, or in the jungle. As stated above, most biomes feel samey, and would benefit from a bit more variety of path and battle tiles. There’s also NO way to play the ‘arena’/gauntlet type levels with custom songs. They seem to be tied to the end of stages in story mode, and that’s the only way to play them. Slightly disappointing, as the option to play a wave-based type stage with your own songs would be a very cool addition to this type of game considering you only need to spawn enemies in a designated area, rather than generate level tiles to walk through. Speaking of walking through levels…* Note *5 - The game incentivizes completing a stage before its designated song is over, but there’s also explorable areas off the beaten path that could yield some reward. The better rewards are tied to better rankings at the end of the level, which seems sort of counter intuitive to exploring a level for more loot- Though getting loot this way can also yield rare items, and can in turn de-incentive people to getting good at the song and just rushing for the hidden chests.* Sometimes on the menu songs wouldn't keep previous difficulty, as in I'd start a song on Challenging, and either swap menus or win, then the song would be back at Warmup.* When a song ends, it takes a few seconds to start again, which can throw off players trying to keep a beat against mobs of monsters in silence.* There is no option to ‘favorite’ a song. While not game-breaking, this is kind of a standard in most rhythm games, being able to load up your favorite toons quickly is one of the reasons folks come back. Without it, it feels like a bit of an annoyance. Some quality of life updates would really help this game survive in the long run.* Upon researching, this game started as a backer game on fig.co, there are some stretch goals that seem not yet implemented, or stripped entirely. There’s no DJ or playlist mode, no playable instruments, or new skins for the playable characters, and no Twitch integration to speak of. Either way, it seems the game’s been in development since even before the last part of 2018, so they’ve clearly had time to iron out some kinks, and seem to have some community presence. 2020 took its toll on a lot of people, so perhaps some things had to be scrapped for the sake of putting the game out. Take that for what you will.This game overall has a lot of love put into it, and clearly shows there’s thought behind all the systems and is not only gorgeous and fun to play, but also technically sound, it's unfortunately held back from greatness by some seemingly strange loot/exp mechanics and shallow replay value, that hopefully could be rectified if enough people speak up and the devs take notice. Due to this being a unique, possibly niche game, and an indie developer, I want to be able to say I’ll cut Soundfall some slack. It’s a very good base, and I would definitely look forward to a sequel, though I feel this game might have benefited from being early access or playtested more by their target audience for feedback before release. In spite of that, the game feels polished, structurally sound, and is of decent quality.If you're new to rhythm games, or are put off by the loot system or procedural generation,  I love this game's premise, and it's really up my alley. I personally enjoy it, and despite the ‘Not Recommended’ label, if you enjoy things like Just Shapes and Beats, Crypt of the Necrodancer, Diablo-esque games, or twin stick shooters/bullet hells plus rhythm games,  you can handle the gripes I’ve listed here, I can recommend giving this game a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game, although far from perfect. Just putting up front I actually recommend this game, and if it looks fun you should buy it. The rest of this review I've GOTTA complain though. Just a couple points that are kind of worth noting before you purchase:1. Some of the music is very poorly chosen for a rhythm game. Very early into the campaign you hit a forest area that mostly uses orchestral music that is VERY difficult to follow the rhythm of, and in some cases have BPMs that are ridiculously high that seem to be incorrect and make the game WAY harder?? The choices are occasionally baffling. Most of the music is great though and works great but especially in world 2 so far there are some songs you just have to drag yourself through.2. Importing music barely works. If your song has ANY tempo changes, breakdowns, or anything that takes a consistent hard hitting kick out of the song expect the beat to get thrown off. There's a guide on how to make your own beatmaps that is really appreciated, but it's a hassle and in my experience also sometimes doesn't work at all. You'll create your own beatmap and for some songs the game just will refuse to use it and will instead use the very bad in-game algorithm instead. If you're looking at this to play exclusively your own music, i'm not sure I can really recommend it.3. There's a lot of sound effects that don't hit on the beat and also only really serve to throw you off and make the game less fun. My honest suggestion is before even starting to go into the settings and turn sound fx volume to around 40%, and also enable the metronome to play when you haven't hit a note on-beat in a while. It really helps.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for about 7 hours, and there is a lot that I like here. Very satisfying action gameplay, and I hope it goes deeper the longer I play. The ability to add your own songs is very awesome and I wish more games did that. One of the nitpicks I have is that at the end the the level, the music just abruptly stops, and for a game all about the music, there has to be a more elegant way to fade out the level gracefully. I also know that there is a way to edit the BPM for custom tracks, but I haven't been able to make Audacity work like the Devs did in the video, I feel like they skipped some steps on how to install the plugin. With custom songs, this game is practically endless, and I wonder how deep the rabbit hole goes with progression. Speaking of progression, I do wish there were just a few more variations of weapons, I feel like I'm just trading between two weapon types any time there are stronger ones. Anyway, there are more pros than cons, and I am looking forward to sinking my teeth into the rest of the game. 8/10, would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: As a lifelong musician, I find this game really fun. I'm usually not really into shooters but this one has managed to keep my attention for 6 hours at the time of this review. It's just so satisfying to play! Graphics are nice, singleplayer runs very smoothly despite a lot of stuff happening on screen, and I was pleasantly surprised to find that its soundtrack has many different styles of music. My only critique is that a lot of the songs don't loop properly, so you end up with several seconds of silence in the middle of battle, which makes it incredibly hard to keep the beat if you're playing with no metronome. Also some songs have weird intros/outros where it's impossible to hear the beat because it's just ambiance. I've died many times due to losing the beat because the song stopped playing in order to loop itself. That can be really frustrating. But if you're playing with the metronome on at all times I'd say I recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The first time i saw this game was at Pax Australia in 2018/19. It was a beautiful demo of the game showcasing the mechanics and style of game play i would come to expect. The way the game felt then was absolutely amazing, I loved doing everything in the game along to the beat of the music! Shooting enemies, dashing through obstacles, jumping up to different areas, even going as far as to having the character's walking pace matching with the music!Fast forward to 2022, having waited 3 years for the game's final release, I have to say i'm nothing less than amazed at how far the game had come. The story is amazing, the art is beautiful, and the game play is even more fluent than the demo i played those few years ago!Not only that, but the ability to put any song I have into the game, load it up and the game will automatically generate a map for me to play along to the beat of that song just makes it all that much better!Sound fall is a beautiful game for any and all to enjoy! You won't regret getting this!

_childDocuments_.review: This game mixes some really neat game mechanics to create a really fun and unique experience. The core premise of tying all of your character actions to the beat of the song is actually very satisfying when timed correctly. I think this is in part due to the excellent sound design of the game, which gives some really nice audio feedback with on-beat attacks and dashes. Once you get in the groove of it, you really start to feel like your playing a part in composing the song, using the notes from the weapons and dashes mixed together. Overall, I think this is a fantastic game so far. The mechanics and aesthetic are combined artfully into a must-experience package.That said, I do think there are some design elements that feel a little rough around the edges to me. They don't detract from the experience as a whole, but I think these are some things that could make the overall experience of play just a little tighter and feel more complete.1. The cursor for item select is difficult to see with the current ui design. The box-in-a-box-in-a-box thing it has going on could really benefit from a bigger visual distinction between the cursor and the item slots (like maybe a beating red dot inside the selected item or something like that).2. The Gold tracker feels out of place where it currently is. I think it would make more sense to put it near the store page, since that's where its spent.3. Speaking of the store, I don't think it serves much purpose to close the inventory/store page when the cursor is over the current inventory. I think it would streamline the visual inspection of your loot if that panel is just always open.4. I'm not sure if this is an issue later in the game, but it feels weird that the rythmic blaster (a submachine gun) and the scattershot (a blunderbuss) share the same weapon skin when the stable scattershot (another blunderbuss) is visually different from the former version.5. It would really help with item experimentation to have a training area in the menus to try out equipment before setting of on a deployment.6.  The character swap tutorial spoils the whole cast! It should really only have Jax and Melody as the example characters in there.7. Lastly, this is probably a non-issue since it likely only comes up once early on for everyone, but I feel like the prologue cutscene was too terse. It went from Melody talking to her room mate about having to drop her audition to keep her job to a cutscene where she puts on headphones, without some sort of story transition like "I'll think about it later, right now I just wanna not think about anything for a while." or something to that effect. The way it reads to me as it is right now, if feels like Melody blew off a heavy subject with her room mate to go to her own world (literally haha).Anyway, these are my personal thoughts on the first few hours of the game, and overall I think it was a very positive experience. I'm looking forward to seeing what else the game has in store for us players!
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: I have been having a blast with this game.  The music choices are wide and varied, and even require some additional skill when the beat isn't quite so obvious.  They have a metronome mode to help you find that beat in case you're struggling.  It is a refreshing take on the looter shooter and requires patience and timing.  You can't just spam buttons to get yourself out of the situation you find yourself in.  You need to feel the music and react accordingly.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: It's repetitive, and it's just the same weapons, gears etc with different rarities and unique passive.At least you can import any songs and it can generate levels for you based on your own imported music, but it's not really working in online yet, overall it's 7.6/10Maybe wait after they fix and add bunch more stuff to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: In the running for my favorite rhythm game ever.  You're twin-stick shooting on the beat with the entire world bopping in the background, all while trying to get a decent rank to get better loot.  The loot system is varied and interesting, with damage typing and bonuses such as increased on the beat damage, augmented movement, etc.  It's clear that the same amount of care that went into making the game also went into selecting the (pretty lengthy!) soundtrack.  There are some amazing songs on here from artists I will for sure be checking out on Spotify.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Game is cool, but has a lot of potential. Many bugs to squash, and a lot of small quality of life things that would significantly enhance our playing experience. Fun so far, but I am a little worried about the long term replayability, even after these bugs are fixed.Would not recommend to anybody who is unfamiliar with music however, as core gameplay is based around performing actions while staying on the beat, which can be tough if you are not well versed in music theory or have played a lot of rhythm games in the past.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: So much fun and so satisfying, a little addicted within the first 5 levels. It's a chill game to play solo, just tapping my feet along with my mouse clicks! Absolutely in love with the ability to import music of my choice. So much fun to jam to my favorite songs and strike a perfect game-to-music vibe. In the imported songs, the game beat has a tendency to change halfway through and it is jarring. It's not that easy to analyze the beat but I'd prefer it to one rhythm the whole way through.A few small changes desired: Not a fan of the dash sound as it's not punchy and distinct like the other sounds and can sometimes throw me off. Also, there's a pretty long space between song end and song start, so losing the beat is a problem there.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is pretty fun and a new mix of genre. I love it that they have custom songs import because you may get tired of the original songs, and you can edit (kinda) offline. Else, it would be AI-generated but it does a pretty good job. I think the UI is lacking abit where reading the info of the equipment may be a bit of a hassle. The local co-op works pretty well and can play up to 4 players, would be a good party game as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun but weird bug when i go full screen i sync better with the game but i lose the ability to shoots on the right hand side of the screen. windowless screen i get a big delay in the game. when you get to the screen to change items you cannot access the menu on top because the right hand side of the screen is unusableI'll play it again sometime when that gets fixed
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just awesome... I never heard of it until the release, but it should get way more visibility !!I love rythm games and game that have loot, this is the best of these two worlds ! The music selection is huge (and you can also add your own music too !) The gameplay is smooth and the design of the characters, weapons and menus are really great !You guys made a really good job, it's fun to see games like this, really refreshing ! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following the development of the game since years ago so I already knew what I was getting and I really feel the love and dedication of the game, it is really polished and fresh. The concept, music and aesthetic are really pleasing but the level mechanics and enemies feel a little bit repetitive and too easy, music is what still makes me want to play it and also the urge to have all the characters. Still a really cool game where you can even play your own music! but be sure that the song you choose has a constant tempo. Hope the game continues to update and create challenging and innovative levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really, really good for a whole lot of reasons. Simple controls, fun enemies, perfect adjustable difficulty, wonderful music, and unlike other rhythm games it doesn't punish you for missing one (1) input - to lose a chain you have to make a whole bunch of mistakes or get hit. Keeping chains is easy and not wildly stressful!You guys did great.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of fun, difficult, and really charming. Combat's tuned well so that when you find the rhythm and know what you're doing, everything just works.I keep getting blown away by all the musical genres I'm finding in here and how well they work: indie-pop, samba, ska, metal, funk, and more. Much better quality and variety of songs than I'm used to in rhythm games.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: The game is amazing and fun. But in my opinion it needs some little changes.I think it would be better if you had immunity while using the abilities. No point on spinning around with a giant sword while losing +100 hp sometimes, and even worse, that at the end the character stays in the place to receive even more damage.And Lydia needs a HUGE buff, I had a bad time trying to pass 3-5 on easy.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: disclaimer: i backed this project on fig!short summary: action rogue-like dungeon crawler with a focus on music. rng loot system, multiple characters, playing with friends available!my initial delight at this product was in its desire to craft levels from one's personal music library. and it certainly delivers! i'm 7 hours in and most of my time has been in playing music that i've found and plugged into the system. that said, the polish on this game is impressive. i quite like the quality of the art and story (despite it taking a back-seat to the main gameplay). the support for creating a game based around beats per minute is also inclusive in settings, and tuning takes generally once to get it right. you really do feel amazing when you time your movements and attacks, especially when you pull off an amazing string of moves all at once in time to the music.my qualms with the game might be the automated mapping, though i understand there is a manual mapping tutorial to guide one in adjusting their experience (i'll take a look at it soon!). another might be in the levels' clearance ranks; there are 4 ranks depending on how you clear the stage, and the top two 'difficulties' (gold and platinum) cater towards players striving for a 'no-hit' run. overall, i'm really enjoying my time with the game atm! tackling the different stages input by my own music library is super fun to experiment with.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Great game hard as nails at first but the metronome setting is a godsend for me. It gives me crypt of the necrodancer feels with a hint of Enter the Gungeon. Very great game. But what puts it above others is the custom song importer.  Very user friendly one click your done. They dont always come out 100% beat accurate but damn close. I highly recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Very addictive! Has that "just one more level" quality to it that keeps you playing well past your intended stopping point. Songs are fun and each world has its own unique style and variety. I only wish there were a little more variety within the levels themselves, but the gameplay is enough to keep me hooked.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible! I really like the combat and the gameplay loop. The story is interesting too and the music is all bangers. Great job devs!The only suggestion I have is to tighten up the feel of the middle three characters a bit. I don't like the other characters as much as Melody because their primary abilities feel a little counterintuitive. I don't think the charge or hold primary abilities fit with the combat style too much. I think an easy solution to this problem would be to allow for a quick press like the other two characters have along with the existing charge attack. I know you can do single beat attack but it feels off and not as snappy as Melody and Ky's melee. Also I don't feel as much weight with the middle three characters' ultimates as I feel there should be. It should feel powerful and, at least with no rare modifiers, those ultimates don't. Melody's and Ky's ultimates do feel powerful though.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: A really cool mix of dungeon crawling, loot collecting, and moving to the rhythm of the backing soundtrack.  I've seen Crypt of the Necrodancer comparisons, but I'd say a key difference here is that character walking isn't constrained to the beat like that game (Which makes it way more manageable for me, though there's still a decent challenge on the higher difficulties).  Bonus points for all campaign songs being unlocked for Free Play mode as well as an MP3 import option for custom levels, though it'd be nice if in the future they patched in more options for that like specifying the level theme.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game, with a beautiful combination of rhythm and combat. As a lover of rhythm games, this one immediately caught my eye, as something different than standard rhythm games. It met the hopes I had for it. The combat and loot system is great as it is, with the added complexity and attacking and moving to the beat, making combat, and victory, all the better and more enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: The aesthetic really reminds me of a old game I used to play - Spiral Knights. The game itself is polished on release inputs feel smooth, AoE/dash indicators is simple yet effective in telling the player it will happen in three beats. Visual indication when enemies will spawn, Stray from the main path to find secret loot just to name a few. I could think of a few improvements that could be done.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy the game despite my lack of being good at rhythm base games. The co op is fun the game itself is enjoyable the music not terrible. I was talking with SonikBuster earlier on my stream and told her flat out I had to get nit picky to find things to possibly be annoyed with about it. I mean if you like gauntlet and rhythm base games than give it a shot. If you like to see some gameplay of it before you buy go look it up on twitch or youtube. But I think it a nice game so take that how you will because people will find reason to dislike something if it not their cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly solid rhythm action game in the same vein as Crypt of the Necrodancer and BPM: Bullets Per Minute, but without the roguelike elements. Instead, Soundfall has a 10-world campaign for you to run through, unlocking new characters, leveling up, and getting new randomized loot. The music is excellent, it's satisfying to land shots on the beat, and the whole experience is quite enjoyable. I've only finished the first world, but I'm already looking forward to playing more and getting to see the rest of what this game has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: this game is very fun but id does have somethings i dislikemainly the fact that weapons and equipment are totally random ( in tearm of quality)meaning you will have to just be lucky to get the item you want while also having to constantly check your (limited) inventory because you keep getting worse verions of a weapon you already have the weapons so far are pretty fun but not a lot is explained, some weapons can do a rapid fire witch would have been nice to be actually shown somewhere other then a loading screen tip and who knows what other special weapons i missed.generaly if the game would give the option to give more info about items and enemies. aswell as a more controlled way of getting the weapons you want then i cant find any problems with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing rhythm game with simple twin-stick looter shooter mechanics. Both the art and music are amazing. You can even import your own music and have it automatically generated! Now I can shoot some baddies while listening to all my favorite songs. There are multiple characters with unique playstyles, a decent variety of weapons, and different elemental attributes that make your builds a little different. I really hope this game gets the attention it deserves. Keep up the great work!
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start this off by saying I have no sense of rhythm. I am not good at keeping on beat, I cannot play an instrument, etc. While that may be true, as a fan of bullet hell, shooters, and roguelites I thought this game had a nice appeal.It is relaxing and bubbly, but also at higher difficulties is very tough. For me, I struggled in the beginning, but by hour 10 I could hold my own. I find the story to really just be a gateway to the game, but the game itself is impressive. Fun combat, catchy songs, beautiful art and real difficulty (to whatever extend you like).Shoot some guns, hear some music, and just hang out!Overall, I give this game a 9/10, a real gem I never knew I needed!
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to put an early review in, as i'm currently under 2 hours. I'm really enjoying this game. Each map is around 3 minutes long, about the length of time for each song. Each biome comes with its own genre of music. The weapons all have different feels, and come with a borderlands-esque random attachment to it. The gameplay is simple and enjoyable. There is the capability to add your own songs, but i've not touched this yet. As you unlock the 5 main characters at different stages in the campaign, i've yet to play around with any besides the main, but i can see that they will all have a differing feel to them depending on how you want to play. I'm sure i'll be trying out the multiplayer at some point soon. So, just for a small game with quick matches and enjoyable music, i'd recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: The songs have been really good! i was impressed by the difficulty that keeps ramping up! I wish the customization was a little more flushed out but other than that the gameplay is solid and responsive if you do the calibration for the audio and visual setup. I am impressed by the sheer number of songs in the game at launch and cant wait for more to come maybe multiplayer specific maps that have special bosses! Its a great start for an early game and I love that you can do custom maps with your own favorite songs too! Good work Devs!! you should be proud of the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: I love rhythm games and I have to say I enjoy when you can import your music into the game and Soundfall delivers.I don't write may reviews and I don't have a huge amount of playtime when writing this review but I feel I had to help boost this up so others can feel good about at least trying it. Only thing I wish you could do is set up a playlist and do those levels back to back solo so you can just play nonstop and I hope that is a plan down the line. Overall a solid game and a welcome addition to my library
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Still early so I'll probably write a more concrete review later.But so far early impressions are incredibly strong. This game looked interesting from the trailers but as someone who enjoys rhythm games and a variety of music, actually playing it feels much better than I expected. It has a nice early and forgiving progression and I definitely felt myself getting better even after the first 30 mins. The music so far is a great and the loot collecting isn't intrusive so far which was a concern I had before. That's thanks to loot being collected automatically and only being able to manage it between songs/levels.It's honestly shocking how well this mix of looter shooter and rhythm based combat works so far. And the ranking system feels just right in how difficult it is to achieve the highest ranks.Other games that have similar combat tend to be on the very difficult side but so far this feels like something I would recommend even to those that didn't like those other games. While I haven't tried it Co-op, it sounds really fun and is a big part of why I'm likely going to recommend it to friends. Hopefully I can try it out soon!
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Its a pretty fun action RPG that could be summed up as a Rhythm based Diablo game, with a good variety of music packaged with the game. You also level up all of the characters together, so you dont need to worry about levelling up the cool new character you just got. They also share the majority of gear, aside from their unique melee weapon and ultimate attacks. However the one downside I've run into so far is also a big upside to the PC version: the ability to import your own music. The game, while able to read the artist and album names, does not separate your imported music based on them. Instead it just lumped all of them together in "unrecognized". Additionally, you can only import a single song at a time, and you need to click off of the imported song as the "Delete Song" button replaces the "Import Song" button while an imported song is selected and it automatically selects the imported song. So if you have a few dozens songs to import it will take some time to add all of them. Thankfully importing each song is near instantaneous, so its just tedious rather than sitting around and waiting. Another big downside is that imported songs need to be re-imported everytime you open the game, it doesnt save them.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: So far the game is a lot of fun. Initially I was having significant issues with timing the beat correctly, which is strange since I play the drums and have good timing, but I figured out it was due to my bluetooth headset. If anyone else is having issues with this try using non-bluetooth headphones or just the computer speakers. This changed the game from frustrating to me having a blast.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of rhythm games and looters, I was excited to hear about this today. Awesome game, somewhat comparable to crypt of the necrodancer / cadence of hyrule. Has custom song support, on top of a beefy and varied track list, plenty of loot to grab. With co op, both local and online, you are in for a good time. Hope it gets plenty of attention
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game.It's a nice spin on the dungeon crawler genre where you have to attack and dodge to the beat. I'm not great at it, but I'm getting better with practice. When you pull off a massive combo it's super satisfying, and you can even import your own songs in a free play custom generated level which any loot, exp or money you gain carries over to the main game.If you like rhythm based games, and also enjoy looting and dungeon crawlers this game might be for you. The combat is really fun once you get the hang of it. And as expected of a rhythm game, the soundtrack is great!
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal! It is so incredibly satisfying shooting up enemies to the rhythm of the music (which by the way, is also incredible!) The loot is satisfying to collect, the world and character design is great, it is just really easy to see how much these devs cared about putting out a truly unique and amazing product.Absolutely, 100% recommend checking this one out!
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Soundfall so far is EVERYTHING I could have wanted out of a rhythm-centric action game. The game does a great job at blending it's fast-paced combat with it's soundtrack that has a ton of variety. All of the different characters, weapons and equipment you can find allow for a ton of customization and different playstyles as well. Everything about the themeing and character designs are SO much fun and the soundtrack has a ton of bangers from across a wide variety of genres. Being able to play custom imported songs is such an awesome addition too. I can easily see myself putting in MANY hours into this game and is a must play for people who love rhythm games infused with other genres!
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun so far. Character control and enemy design feel a lot like Hyper Light Drifter to a beat, which is high praise. Unlike some rhythm games, firing a shot off-beat doesn't completely punish you, just weakens your shot, which keeps you very in flow through the course of a level. The mission based system offers very nice pauses to stop and get your head back together before the next level. Had a bit of a hard time with the first level, found it quite long and difficult compared to the second through fourth levels, but equipping stronger weapons that I had found in previous attempts before diving back in got me through it just fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Only play a very short amount of this game, but its the best rhythm based game I have played in a while. Looking forward to unlocking the other weapons. Being able to load your own music into the game and play those songs is almost always an instant buy for me when it comes to rhythm games. Very cool concept and seems like they nailed it so far.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Crypt of the NecroDancer meets Zelda: Four Swords Adventures. VERY very good game so far, lots of polish and a fun romp of a story with great music. There is a real rhythm to the game and it changes with your loadout and it all just feels SO good. This is absolutely worth checking out in my opinion.

Check!Light but fun Story? Check!Interesting graphic? Check!Super Mario Bros. world map style? Check!Loot drop? Check!EXP and Level up system? Check!Good music? Check!Fight to the beat? Check!Co-Op Online? Check!Different classes? Check!No Micro-Transaction? Check!Work with Controller? Check!Nintendo Switch, Xbox, PlayStation controller buttons? _childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw this game had no user reviews, I was a bit skeptical. Game studios without a large following in the rhythm genre are very hit or miss in my experience.However, after spending about an hour on the game, my expectations were blown out of the water. This game's music library is ! Like, I'm not talking about volume of songs, there are plenty of rhythm games out there that have just a huge library of songs. I'm talking genres from Latin funk to hardcore drumstep, neoclassical to pop, and every song affects the enemy attributes differently, depending on its intensity, bpm, and instrumentation. The library isn't very large, but for a new release, I wouldn't expect it to be with the amount of time that would be needed to map, encode, and create triggers for every new track.Here are my initial impressions, categorized roughly into positives, needs improvement, and negatives:To summarize, if you love rhythm games, and looking for a break from the regular Quaver/osu!mania genre of hit the notes really fast, this is a refreshing game, and I highly recommend it. However, if you're on the fence, and aren't sure if this is for you, my advice is this: Wait a month. Let the developers get some community feedback and improve the overall experience, and  go for it. I have very VERY high hopes for this game, and hope to see the community grow and flourish.
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Soundfall is a fun rhythm-based shooting game. It kinda reminds me of BPM:Bullets per Minute but top down - works good and runs smooth. There are a lot of songs to explore, but my favorite part in this version is the option to import .mp3 files from your PC to create custom levels. I always appreciate that option in rhythm games :)
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

_childDocuments_.review: Soundfall is a dungeon crawler that combines looter-shooter action with rhythm-based gameplay. Venture out solo or with up to 4 friends locally or online. Collect loot and time your actions to the beat to become all powerful. Play the Campaign Mode, Free Play 100's of songs or import your own music!
_childDocuments_.name: Soundfall

name: Minds Beneath Us
detailed_description: Story Embark on a thrilling sci-fi journey in a futuristic Asian city with MINDS BENEATH US. In a society fully automated by advanced AI, you find yourself trapped in a foreign body, alongside the subconscious of its original owner. As society evolves, a new industry emerges that replaces the hardware needed to operate AI-automated systems with human brains. Consequently, the most disadvantaged citizens have had no choice but to sign up one after another. Against the backdrop of this mad society, a conspiracy gradually unfolds. Features Players can make their own dialogue choices and shape the relationships between characters throughout the journey. The combination of dialogue choices and actions will continually affect the story. Observe environments, pay attention to the dialogue, and then look for hidden clues in every scene. This way, you can even unlock new dialogue choices. With hand-drawn animation and smooth camera movement, a unique cinematic experience is created. The game combines 2D characters and detailed 3D environments to present the streets of a near-future Taipei.

short_description: MINDS BENEATH US is an emotional sci-fi narrative game. Through the eyes of a humble individual, experience a mad world where humans are exploited as computing devices for AI. Listen to the concerns of those you meet and offer guidance. Together, face challenges and confront an uncertain destiny.

_childDocuments_.review: Have never written a review for a game. This slaps. Got so invested in the story and characters that I feel obliged to promote it somehow. Feels like a while since I played something with such an original take on the cyberpunk/hopeless sci-fi genre. Tells you a lot that a game that is 70% dialogue has been enjoyed and played to the end by so many people.Hope there's DLC or a sequel, so many questions left unsolved - in a good way. _childDocuments_.review: I've just finished the game and wanted to leave some of my impressions here while they're fresh and my memories not too blurred from the passage of time.First of all: I did really enjoy this game - more than I actually thought possible after the long wait. In general: it's beautiful - the storytelling, the characters and the whole artistic vision were put together nicely to make you feel like you were part of a future that feels familiar in some ways and so foreign in others. All the while tackling very human, very contemporary issues that sometimes hit harder to home than I felt comfortable with. I don't really want to spoil too much as the story is pretty much what makes this game great. Let me just share this one thing that I really liked about all the dialogue choices and conversations with characters: Things were rarely black or white. Most of the time MBU offers a very "gray" perspective to the world - even the ending is no exception to that. What is right? What is wrong? How do we determine that? For us and for others? MBU further emphasizes that fact by giving us a whole bunch of loose ends that do not ever lead to a satisfying conclusion. Whether this is intentional or not - of course - can be put to debate, but in general, it felt right to me that the game - rather than explaining every tiny little detail to me - ended up leaving me in the dark. Which made "finding the right choice" even more of an obscure thing to achieve. Sure, there are certain philosophies and thoughts presented to us that do come up more often than once, but never did I feel like those were pushed onto me as "the right beliefs". As a lot of those things come up in conversations with others, it just felt "ok" for people to have certain opinions and principals they live by - and them sharing and defending them vehemently is something most people, I think, should be able to easily relate to.The gameplay itself is minimalistic which I didn't mind at all, but for anyone going into this game: It's more of a visual novel than an action adventure or anything. I'd dare say that point-and-click-adventures offer more interactivity than this game. To me this is not a bad thing, to some others it might turn "Minds Beneath Us" into a very boring and tedious endeavour though. Just be warned. If you yourself have little issue with reading in videogames, I'd say: Go for it!I hope you have as much fun with the game as I did. It's well worth the money,  imho.

_childDocuments_.review: Minds Beneath Us is a strange and complex story-driven cyberpunk adventure game that’s light on gameplay mechanics but staggeringly heavy on branching, choices-matter dialogue. But who could blame it for being longwinded when Minds Beneath Us (or M.B.U.) has  much going on?   You’ll play as Jason Dai: underachieving, unemployed, and uninteresting on the outside; possessed by a rogue consciousness that gives you superhuman reflexes on the inside. Together, your original consciousness and this surprisingly agreeable mind-controlling rogue consciousness (which refers to itself as an M.B.U.) will work together to juggle a borderline impossible list of competing interests, including a work-obsessed and pretty out of your league fiancé-to-be, a super-involved multi-part interview process at a local “flop farm,” a freaky, supernatural specter with unknown motives, and a corporate underbelly run by rival super soldiers you and your gf inadvertently stumble into headfirst. Before you know it, you’re working alongside one of these super soldiers—the uncompromising and philosophically-driven killing machine, Nin Situ—and her eclectic support staff. Simultaneously, Jason must learn the ins and outs of Silencio, a flop farm that (and this is real) generates power by hiring predominately poor, desperate people to willingly chain themselves for  to a hiveminded supercomputer that converts brainwaves into electricity. What could go wrong?  Go figure, Silencio is a controversial operation, even internally, and during your interview process you’ll get caught in the middle of an existential office politics battle between Silencio’s two operational halves: Screening, the group in charge of contracting all the poor people or “juicers” as they’re derogatorily referred to in-game; and Ops, the crew tasked with racking those juicers—a process so disturbing that Ops would rather see the flop farm shut down entirely. Along the way, the choices you make in each of these storylines will dramatically affect MBU’s plot, characters, and dialogue, all of which I’m giving very high marks for originality and memorableness (if that’s a word).  Alas, while its Story is excellent, it’s about all MBU has to offer. As noted earlier, MBU plays like a visual novel first and a video game second, so if you don’t like reading while you’re gaming, you can probably stop reading this review right now (please don’t). For everyone still here, MBU only features a handful of quick time event combat sequences, and they’re pretty bad. If you somehow manage to lose one, the game will just reload and let you try again. There’s equally little in the way of non-combat mechanics, here, which surprised me. Not once does MBU—a game about cyber-stealth, heists, and hacking—ask you to... do any of that. You’ll never hack a computer, disable an alarm, rewire enemy AI, solve a simple puzzle... it’s bizarre how  gameplay there is here.  As a consequence, you’ll rarely have to have to interact with MBU’s subpar user interface, which lacks some basic accessibility options and makes clicking through the game’s thousands of dialogue prompts a real chore. What you  have to interact with are elevators! Good gravy does this game love trapping you in an elevator and forcing you to click through minutes of unskippable monologuing from Silencio’s troubled employees, all of whom seem weirdly ready to disclose their innermost thoughts to you, a nobody who started working here two days ago. To clarify, the actual dialogue is good (if a little heavy on the exposition)—what pisses me off, however, is the inability to skip it. Time and time again I’d accidentally lock myself into a rambling NPC speech that I really wished I could cut short. It doesn’t help that MBU’s world, despite its incredible premise, consists of about eight tiny locations you’ll visit dozens of times each, and several of these locations are near-identical floors of the same flop farm. While the game’s final act opens things up, it’s arguably too little too late.  That leaves us with style. MBU features an interesting blend of faceless, hand drawn 2D characters and 3D environments. I very much enjoyed this aesthetic and can’t recall seeing anything like it. The same cannot be said for MBU’s simple if atmospheric synth soundtrack and unremarkable sound effects.  In the end, Minds Beneath Us is a fresh narrative take on the increasingly saturated cyberpunk genre. While it offers little to nothing in the way of actual gameplay, I still found myself engaged and intrigued 20 hours later. I think the game is appropriately priced at $20, so I'm giving it an aggregate MEGA score of 3.08/5 (full scoring breakdown from "Plot" to "Sound" available in video). Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Good game! Got some good hours out of it, and I'm jumping back in to explore a couple of things after this. The game play isn't complicated, and most of the difficulty comes from picking the right dialogue choices. It's definitely more like a visual novel in that aspect, which is to say that  If this is what you want out of a game, look no further!For those of you who needed a little bit more information, let's talk a bit more.Simply from the little clips and photos in the product page, you can see the general aesthetic and art standard of the game. This quality is maintained throughout the entire game, which takes the players to many different kinds of locations, from clean office to dystopian scifi labs. The atmospheric and cinematic tag is not for show. Every shot is gorgeous.Music and sound design is decent. OST suits the theme, location and mood, and sounds designs all make sense. I regret not being able to give a more comprehensive look on it, just that from a layperson's view point, none of it feels out of place.The plot is truly riveting. It's not a detective game, but there was a mystery you must unravel by the end of the game, a mystery that appeared to be who you are and what you consider to be important. As Fran, your girlfriend character eluded to at the beginning of the game, the more massive the scale becomes, the smaller you, an individual in the system begins to feel. And somehow, that can both empower and enfeeble you.  Haha, I don't know if that makes sense for the plot section, but that's all I have without spoiling. You try and do something even as the scale grows terrifyingly larger. I think anyone who ever tries and cause a change in a bigger system gets it. There are a couple of hard decisions in the game, but you generally are told if there are extra things to do, as long as you pay attention to the dialogue. I must say, I'm pleasantly surprised by the dialogue. I felt the weight of my decision when it was plot relevant, and I felt represented when given the opportunity to give my opinions. There were points when I felt like I was debating with a friend. The characters are brilliant. The character growth, the decisions they made, their emotional outburst and climaxes... Boy, it's hard to gush about it without spoilers, because they are the core of the game (imho). The characters are pushed into their limit, forced into conflicts and confronted with hard decisions. You, as your character, can sit there and judge, help, or be pulled right into their mistakes and fights. World building is solid. the futuristic technology, terminology, social movements all have their basis in reality and seems well understood. They know what to expand on and what to leave vague. I think some people have found it preachy, but from the perspective of the game, where you are a relatively helpful if self-regarding man whose girlfriend is involved in social movements.... I mean, It's a game about helping people, and how you would actually help people. It's complicated. I think a lot of people consider just talking about morals and social movements preachy. To me, the game feels more concerned with corporation crimes, and how it's hard to fight for what's right against gigantic entities with infinitely more resources and power than you, as well as the thousands and millions of ways it will grind you down using everything from ethics, moral, money and violence, leaving you to carry the weight of the decisions and hundreds of tiny mistakes twisted into a knife in your back while they sit on the throne of blood, committing way worse crimes intentionally and without a care. But that's just me. Ok, you have read too far down, TLDR, I thought the game was good, very solid, lots of choices, pretty. Have fun if you get it! Oh, right. Almost forgot. I look forward to your next game, devs. Definitely would love to come back and visit these characters, and see some of the loose ends tied!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best indie game I have played in the recent years, absolutely adored this game. I'm a huge cyberpunk/sci-fi fan and this game delivered on those themes perfectly. Enjoyed every single second that I had with the game.The art style of the game is what hooked me at first, the game looks really good visually. The atmosphere is amazing and immersive. What kept me going was the game's story and the characters, both of these aspects are written really well. The characters really enhance the game. The story as a whole is really good but one of the sub plot wasn't explored/explained really well but it's not a big issue. _childDocuments_.review: I bought this game attracted by its particular art style, something that reminded me of the golden age of adventure graphics in the 90's, but what I found was not a puzzle centric game, but rather a very well written graphic novel. As a matter of fact, Minds Beneath Us does not require you to solve puzzles or mix together inventory items, you just need to click through rather lenghty dialogues and make decisions that could slightly change the final outcome of your journey. That's it, this is not an hard game, there's basically no action or deep gameplay mechanics, apart some basic quicktime events. It is like reading a very good sci-fi book, that will accompany you for something like 20ish hours. If you approach this title knowing all this, and accepting it, then I can recommend it with a good 7 out of 10 as a personal score. If you are searching for a challenge for your intellect or reflexes, please look elsewhere. I really enjoyed my time with this story and its characters and I hope the developer will be able to write a sequel in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: TIGHT TIGHT TIGHT YEAH.P.S. Frances <3 Updated review after 2nd playthrough:On a more serious note, the game is a cyberpunk dystopia sidescroller with some.. visual novel aspects. I hesitate to use the the term visual novel because there's enough player control and interaction to differentiate it from a typical VN. The gameplay can be broken into as walking from point A to point B, talking to characters, making choices, and the occasional (and very simple) QTE for combat scenarios. If games like Life Is Strange and Detroit: Become Human aren't your thing, you can skip this game.The meat of the game is through its story and characters. MBU takes you into the life of ordinary and extraordinary people trying to make the best decisions they can in a continuously, morally gray world. Some people are compassionate, some are self-serving, some are morally corrupt, some disagree with others on morals, some are simply victims trying to get by. Navigating the drama, politics, conspiracies while questioning yourself and others in a system that doesn't care about anyone is your role in MBU.Your choices can affect the relationships of the characters and their endings. However, the overall plot will remain the same e.g. choosing a major choice in this specific area will not change the how the next story beat begins. The game is much more linear than let's say Detroit: Become Human. That is probably my one real complaint about MBU: there aren't diverse branching paths that drastically change the story based on the choices you make. That's not to say that your choices don't have impact at all, but don't expect a vast decision tree.Regardless, I found myself caring for these characters and invested in the story. It kept me on my toes and the world remained interesting throughout my playthrough. The characters felt like real people with real problems and it was genuinely enjoyable listening to what they had to say.I usually don't write reviews but if this review can help persuade someone to support this game (because I'm really hoping for a 2nd game) then I will have done my job.

_childDocuments_.review: I would give the game a careful recommendation.Positives:* Very well written game, offering up a LOT of moral questions to the player. Even the 'golden options' (there are a few) do not diminish the questions you had to answer to get there, and a lot of hard questions aren't avoidable. * Some very intelligently written dialogues that make you question some fundamental aspects of society, justice and humanity. * Excellent soundtrack and use of the soundtrack.* Great characters. It is always to the credit of the writers when 10 speech bubbles and a featureless face can turn into a 'someone' we care for and want the best for - and how you guide the different characters feels very meaningful.* The general plot progression keeps a good pace and there is very little that feels like busywork. * Leaves a lot of plot threads hanging, but in a way that is not invasive. I really like having a little bit of mystery left. Negatives:* The game mechanics are 99% dialogue, and I wish they had just leaned fully into that. Some of the 'mechanics' introduced very early in the game, like looking at items in the environment and using the information unlocked from that, is basically immediately discarded. Choosing certain dialogue paths or choices to unlock different options later is surprisingly rare, and rarely seems relevant. And the game somehow believes that the combat QTEs rise in difficulty because I need to press Space 4 times instead of 3. * The game is significantly more linear than one might think on first look. This is NOT purely a bad thing - the game is very reactive to choices in the smaller things. But compared to some other VNs, choices are for roleplaying more than for significant deviation. * The game is sometimes very, very verbose. I usually credit the best visual novels and roleplaying games with not dropping essays on the player in dialogues, and the game has a tendency to monologue at you fairly often, locking you in minute long periods of characterization, exposition or philosophy where your only options are "..." or "Generic 'keep going' message". For the same reason, I was honestly ready for the game to be over by the end.It is a good game within its genre (which is really just a VN with extra steps) but the player should approach it with that in mind. Well worth the price though.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm close to the end but I need to make a review already. It's everything I've wanted in a game since forever. This will be a (99%) spoiler free review for those who want to know what you're heading into without ruining the surprise.(I am dyslexic so mind the grammar errors sorry.)TLDR: The game is well thought out in almost all of its creative process from plot to art direction and it's worth every penny if you liked the demo.Warnings: This game includes flashing/ glitching imagery for sensitive viewers. Non-graphic violence, injury. Mentions of torture, human trafficking and general abuse on people of all ages.And lots of reading for people who don't read the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tags. >:/ Visual NOVEL people! C'mon.Minds Beneath Us has a hooking plot with many moving parts that keeps you on your feet, guessing and going over information. It makes you question everything and everyone around you.There's no strict line of good and evil and having those shades of grey to everything makes the story really interesting. It honestly makes you think about what *you* want, how do *you* see the world, and where do *you* draw the line? Having the story constantly moving behind the scenes and out of the players control at times honestly makes the world feel real and bigger than you started off thinking it was. This isn't about you, sure you're the main character, but to YOUR story not everyone elses.One would think comedy would be sparse in a philosophical cyberpunk drama right? No, and that's great! The moments are placed in laid back situations or to lighten the mood before and after a serious moment and I found myself actually reading things OUT LOUD because of how much fun I was having.The writing doesn't keep you holding your breath all the time which makes important and serious moments feel natural. Although the writing isn't full proof and you really have to think and focus on the things being told to you to understand a lot of the plot beats, it's still really good and having moments to relax and understand the things happening around helps you you and ease your brain for the next time.You might not notice it on a first play through but your choices matter and they can and will come to bite you in the ass or help you later on in other chapters, that's right, you're choices can effect you further on in the game! This isn't one of those lazy "your choices matter" the developers and your main characters are expecting you to make actual choices and not skin through everything to get to the next story marker.The characters are really intriguing and slowly finding out what makes them tick through your choices and the information from everyone around you if you take the time to slow down and listen is really rewarding. On the topic of slowing down and listening: having people you pass by interact with each other makes the world feel full, these aren't random npc's to fill up space or continue the plot they have opinions and lives and those details are worth listening to.The combat is simple but don't mistake it to be easy, you can catch the auditory and visual patterns though. The combat mostly consists of pressing SPACE and E when the prompts tell you to "Quick time events" in short and although some of the combat can be sudden because you're not told beforehand when new things are introduced. but you'll get the hang of it. Think of it like mortal combat except you can't spam your power attack and knock down the other person until they got no health left (I see you >:C). The combat is honestly fun (but could become repetitive if that isn't your style.) and the quick time events outside of the combat catch you off guard which keeps the player's skills sharp for the next QTE or combat situation.I might ramble about this... THE ART? Chefs kiss I love the style. the animation is amazing with little details and stunning action scenes. Exaggerating proportions and using visible smear frames during combat and quick movements was an excellent choice and on top of the audio, the impacts feel hard.Not having faces in the style is also a good choice: it leaves the player focusing on body language and thus the beautiful style details the animating team added in. This also means the actions are very expressive and coupled with the audio and good dialogue faces are hardly an issue. It makes you rely on the main characters inner thoughts too because he sees humans. *You can't.* This also could be related to the story for various reasons you might figure out yourself as you play.I don't have a lot on the audio, I'm not that kind of artist, but the music is very unique, very cyberpunk and casual electro beat. Audio is used for almost everything from character "voices" (The different sounds accompanying different characters when their text is generated.) to footsteps on different surfaces and audio ques for combat. There's a lot of little details that add to the atmosphere. It's nothing show stopping compared to the rest of the game but it's definitely a good and well thought out touch.There is some clunky dialogue and at least 12 different grammar/ spelling issues that happen later on in the game but it's nothing game breaking.My overall opinion? I love the game, it has replay value and that alone makes it a worthwhile purchase. I struggle to read but I've enjoyed this game so far and have found something that's hooked me where most stories don't. I couldn't recommend it enough and my friends will never stop hearing about my ramblings on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I don't do long reviews but this time I'll do it because I want to support this studio and contribute my two cents. At first, this game caught my attention because of its visual and interesting premise (I'm a sucker for cyberpunk/future dystopian stories, don't ask me why). I have to say that by the end of the story I officially became a fan of this game. What a pleasant surprise! I'm looking forward to whatever this studio has in store for this universe.What I liked the most about it was the dialogue and world-building. Just a heads up, this game is dialogue heavy, has some quick time events, and no real combat (you just have to press a certain button when prompted and that's it). Regarding the combat, I don't view it as a negative thing. Not every game needs to have combat. Moving on, the world building is top notch. If you're a person who doesn't like to read, or has no patience and is looking forward to combat then this game might not be for you. Sure you can finish the story in 12 hours (according to the developers themselves, see FAQ), but I think you'll be doing yourself A HUUUGGGEEEEE DISSERVICE and it would not be as enjoyable as if you took the time to examine everything and I mean EVERYTHING. That's why my first playthrough is 26 hours. Examine each magazines, watch every news, listen to every bystanders in each floor level after each cutscenes (sometimes you get the chance to play a role in it). I promise that if you do that, the world become more alive, you will be more invested in the story, and by the end of the game you will crave for more. And finally the star of the show was for me the dialogue. The dialogue between each character are what truly carry this game. The dialogue feels authentic, well though out, and human (which is an odd thing to say) in the sense that you feel like you're talking with real persons who has their own personality, ideology, and feeling. It will make you feel a variety of emotions. I laughed, was dissapointed, sad, angry, smiled, confused, conflicted, etc. It's also at times, thought provoking, and it will make you think hard about certain things. The options given to you to respond back are also well thought out. Most of the time, the respond will fall back into the category, either you can: agree, be neutral, or disagree with the other person. What you choose affects what kind of relationship you will have with each character, and in turn will have good or bad consequences (such as it might make your playthrough more harder or easier. You might unlock alternative paths/secret dialogue that gives you a bit more context about the story/certain character if you play your cards right). Here comes my only nitpick with this game and that's it doesn't give you chance to get a bad ending prematurely. While the endings itself (4 in total) were satisfactory, sometimes the game will present you with certain choices where you know if you pick that choice, the game will end early and I would have just liked to see how these alternatives bad ending might play out. Is it important to have those prematurely bad endings? No, but it just goes to show how invested I am in this story.That's all I can say without spoiling the game for you. All in all, this game gets a solid 9.8 for me and if the developers are reading this, good job guys. Keep up the good work!

_childDocuments_.review: I've played it just a bit, but I'm already absolutely mind-blown. Not only does it have an engaging plot, but it also looks incredibly delicious while not requiring a high-end PC. In fact, to me, visually, it appears better than any of the AAA games I've played recently.The game is essentially a point-and-click adventure, supporting both keyboard + mouse and controller. With keyboard + mouse, it would be better if most of the game could be played with just the mouse. Currently, movement requires the keyboard, though the character moves in two dimensions, which should be easy to control with a mouse. For the controller, the scheme is mostly good, but using the right thumbstick for the cursor feels awkward. The cursor is only needed to examine items, which is crucial for learning about the world. The game should be fully mouse-controllable, and for the controller, hotspots should be automatically highlighted instead of using the right thumbstick as a cursor.Another issue, and this is the only real issue I have with this game, is the save system. The game uses one save slot per playthrough and doesn't allow manual saving. It only saves at specific main plot points, not during side content, potentially leading to long gaps between saves. Manual saving on the same slot should be allowed, as it wouldn't affect gameplay and should be easy to implement. Or at least, automatic saving for the optional content. Because I tend to go for all possible side content, sometimes I have around thirty minutes between the saves, which is less than ideal for the way I tend to play games.This is incredible, really, the more I play this game, the more I like it. I am incredibly grateful to BearBoneStudio, and I hope they will make more quality games in the future. I will definitely tell everyone I know about this game, recommend to buy it, and hope for the bright future of the creative power behind the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely play games that don't include some sort of action element, so was hesitant to start a visual novel; however, within the hour, I was hooked and wanted to learn more about the characters and world.The plot was immediately gripping and the characters are all very distinct. I genuinely had to take breaks to ponder my choices, and while they don't ALL cause major consequences within the game, I truly found myself pondering my own take on these topics as opposed to being concerned with how it may affect the outcome of my own playthrough. The game's strength is definitely in its writing. It can come off preachy, but it really does make you think about how AI will eventually come to affect our real lives.Gameplay-wise, there could been more to interact with and minigames to break up the very dialogue-heavy nature of the game. There are some QTEs but nothing beyond pressing a few keys here and there. I wish there had been more usage for the various items we were inspecting, though some did present new dialogue options if you were a scrutinizing player.The music was charming, if not a bit basic "cyberpunk lo-fi" vibes. I did find it comforting to listen to while debating which side of the fence I was on with the multitude of factions that exist within the world.The art was beautiful, though I wish there were more scenes. The animations and environments are all hand-drawn and the locations that do exist feel very lived-in. I felt a bit empty, like a piece of me was missing after I completed my first playthrough. To me, that's a great sign of impactful media (games/books/movies/etc.). Overall, incredibly pleased with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Minds Beneath Us is a game that picks up piece by piece all the fears you may have about our future and sets them on a plate for you to reflect on, one by one, or all together at the same time.Its wow factor does not come from its graphics (though they are pretty for being so simplistic) nor its gameplay (though they could have made an effort, maybe?) but from its stellar story, dialogue, and character development.In MBU, you are.... essentially a mind agent, that can move from body to body in order to extract information from predetermined targets. You are, at first, tasked to extract some information from a guy, only for everything to break lose, leaving you stranded in another man's body, this time however... without a goal, a target, or information to extract, you are just.... there.From there, you live in the body of Jason Dai, a guy who is about to start a new job in a Flop Farm (basically, where people provide their brains to feed an AI), you have to learn the ropes, the nice side and the really ugly side of what that job entails, the great and horrible people, the different departments, their judgements, and how each character views this morally ambiguous world that surrounds them.That last part is what Minds Beneath Us really strives for; moral dilemmas. You are constantly being pushed to, more than to make decisions, to discuss morality and face the reality of how people move in this world, both from the perspective of someone who just wants to make their pay grade to that one executive that thinks of you as a number, and that alone is a fascinating thing to be able to express in a videogame.The biggest downer for this one, IMO, is the gameplay -there is action, but the one you make is pretty bland and repetitive- From there, you could argue that, being a text-centric game, it may not be for everyone, and for those only interested in graphics, this may not be the biggest art showcase either.Also, disclaimer: I found a few minor bugs, mostly with translation and missing lines. Nothing too big -it was easy to draw them out from context, and weren't important to the plot-, but I think it's better to say this. I did see many updates prior to launch, so this may not be relevant.But yeah, totally recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow…like I’m just stunned.  This feels like it came out of nowhere and is just one of the best cyberpunk games I’ve ever played.  It reminds me a bit of ANNO: Mutationem as far as style goes.  However, it gets rid of the worst part of that game (the combat).  I love that this is an adventure game where you just spend the bulk of this game living in this world and talking to people.  The QTE fights you get in are an excellent way to have a combat mechanic without bogging down the game like in Anno.  The world feels so alive and lived in.  The background environments are gorgeous and the soundtrack is stellar.  I love the character designs, it took a bit to get over the lack of faces…but it honestly didn’t bother me.  I also really appreciated that it didn’t use that garbage pixel design that a lot of indie adventure games use these days.Where this game really shines though is the narrative and writing.  For one the relationship you have with Fran, no matter what dialogue options you pick all feel extremely realistic.  The writing conveys perfectly the type of relationship these two people have, but this also extends to literally every single character in this game.  I love them all, each feels like a real person instead of a stock character…which is shocking given that this is a 20hr adventure game and not a 100hr RPG.  I would say the writing is on par with Haven, which I think also has just incredible realistically written characters.  I was so disappointed when this game ended because I knew that was probably the last time I would see any of these characters.  The puzzles were also the best type of adventure game puzzles.  They relied on you remembering things and exploring the world, instead of some obtuse math substitution puzzle or the typical Sierra adventure games of the past where you were combining super weird objects.  There is basically no puzzle that you’ll get stuck on, but how you go about solving it will certainly change your relationships with characters in the game…because the game cares about story so much even the puzzles are story beats.The game does have some drawbacks.  While there are constant dialogue choices that can affect character relationships, the choices in the game don’t really affect the outcome of situations in the game.  It certainly will change the ending, but it’s not like you can go down completely new paths to explore this story.  The story is going to play out the same, still the characters are so well written you will care about how the individual characters in the game are affected by your choices.  The other issue I have is that the story does not seem complete even after 20hrs.  There are some pretty major questions remaining…which I guess could be answered in a sequel…but the way this game was heading it is shocking that those questions aren’t answered.  Towards the end it almost felt like the developer got tired with the story they started out with and then went all in on a different story.  To explain the rest will have to be spoilers. Those issues notwithstanding, this game is an amazing accomplishment.  This world feels like a real possible future and the characters you meet are easy to imagine existing in reality.  Any fan of either adventure games or cyberpunk games should be immediately buying this game.  It has one of the best cyberpunk stories told in a very long time…I wish Cyberpunk 2077 had a story even half as good as this game.  #Worth any price.
