_childDocuments_.review: is a prime example of what indie game developers can do and eventually surpass most of the triple-A titles that have come out in recent years. I went into Minds Beneath Us blindly and, having no prior knowledge for this game (I only saw it on the releasing soon page), I was instantly drawn into the game's dystopian world and captivating art style. The game acts out as a visual novel of sorts, and although you move your character and get QTE for the combat parts, which are pretty easy and lets everyone get through them to focus on the story. Nothing in terms of gameplay is truly mind blowing and we've already seen in other games. What Minds Beneath Us excels at, is The developers have created a truly gripping story, start to finish, with a future that seems terrifying and maybe not so different to where we are heading. With the technology progressing fast and AI affecting everyone's lives, the world is still plagued by inequality and poverty. The ones on the bottom are forced to rent out their brains, to give a platform for this AI to function on in exchange for a sum of money.Minds Beneath Us deals with one of the most important things that games these days seem to forget; the lives of everyday people. Relatable characters that have different opinions, moral dilemmas and problems of their own are often what bring the world alive and give you that reality check, making you really think about the game world. It delivers a strong, coherent story with some really hard hitting, emotional moments. It has  of dialogue, none of it actually voiced but the writing is exceptional. The lack of facial features might throw you off but the characters manage to show a wider range of emotions than ones that do have a face in other games. Every side character, no matter how small of a role they have, has some kind of development that you as a player can contribute to. Minds Beneath Us gives you this illusion of choice and although most of the things you do certainly affect those around you, how much can you actually change the world?In the end, after all, you are one person, insignificant in the grand scheme of things. An astonishing thriller/mystery that I got a decent amount of hours out of and is so far my favorite game that released this year. Can't wait to see more from this studio.

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't enjoy serious Visual Novels but I'll always make an exception for deep cyberpunk (last time was the interesting Eliza).I very much enjoyed the themes of corporate appropriation of progress, of workplace dynamics, of the role of the individual in a corrupt society, the quest for meaning and all the humanist discourse around these points. They were always tackled in a tactful and meaningful way and, as a European, seeing something written from the perspective of the Chinese-speaking world was a breath of fresh air.The presentation helped a lot, everything about the art and animation style, lighting, music was right up my alley: colorful, sprawling, industrial cyberpunk at night, what more can you wish for? Well, I would definitely have wished for more outdoors environments such as the one next to the main character's apartment. Just gorgeous! Character art was also a great success, loved the faceless style.Also contributing to my immersion were the few elements of gameplay. As I said, VNs are not usually my thing as I think the medium (linear text boxes with unnatural dialogue, limited conversation choices) tends to limit the quality of the writing. By offering the player some degree of sidescroling control with a few quick-time events and the occasional object search, I felt less compelled to think about the way the text was delivered.  These added elements were not perfect though, I especially regret that the idea of using the cursor to look at and interact with the environment seemed to have been abandoned pretty quickly: some of the later environments didn't contain any interactive elements which made the world feel less alive. I'm tempted to think that the game would have made a stellar point & click more than a VN, but I also understand the need to deliver a lot of dialogue for the sake of the story.And the story was good, sometimes great! Most of the time, it felt like the brilliant narrative arc of a Ghost In The Shell: Standalone Complex season. I felt however that it could had been tighter and stretching it over 15 hours was unnecessary, especially as the finale felt surprisingly rushed and gasping for air, quickly wrapping up loose ends without revealing much about the story's greatest mystery.But not to dwell on this, I had a good time and I wish the developers a lot of deserved success, I am looking forward to your next game!

_childDocuments_.review: I had a lot of fun with this one. Reminded me of games like Detroit: Become Human or Citizen Sleeper. The story was really engaging and unlike a lot of decision-making games I actually enjoyed the dialogue. Usually in these types it's frustrating because I don't have the option to actually say what I'm thinking, but I rarely had that issue here.  I really liked the characters and their character arcs as well, with a couple exceptions.A few things soured me on it near the end. There are several combat sequences in the game and they're QTEs. I actually tend to enjoy those usually, but these fights got super dull. It was always the exact same thing: space to dodge, E to attack (with the same sequence of blows practically every time). Supposedly my guy is a great fighter. Not sure how he beats anyone by spamming the same moves.I also found the ending to be pretty unsatisfying. I won't delve into it too much, but many questions were left unanswered and it feels like half the plot-line received no real resolution. My best guess is they're setting it up for a sequel? I hope so because the questions they left in the air are the ones I was most interested in. :/Despite my dismay at the ending I had a great experience though. Really enjoyed the mystery and spent all weekend thinking about it. I'd play a sequel in a heartbeat, both to tie up loose ends and to spend more time in this cool world they've built.

_childDocuments_.review: Criminally underrated, this game has brilliant world-building and really made me feel like every choice I made matter - how I spent my time, who I talked to, etc. all felt like they mattered.The premise reminds me of the donghua Link Click and the dystopian capitalist society within the game reminded me of the TV show Severance - so if you enjoyed them (or if u enjoyed this game) please play this or vice versa. I'm shocked nobody is talking about this, I totally recommend, it's very immersive despite the simple character designs and the art and music are beautiful.There are heavy political themes in this game that I may be too illiterate to fully grasp, and it really makes you consider what your priorities should be, and how sometimes wrong cannot be overcome without hurting good, and sometimes there are necessary evils. This really annoyed me but also got me questioning my own morals, so that I really like. The end choice is a STRUGGLE, but I felt satisfied ultimately, despite the MANY unanswered question. The game hints at a sequel so that might be good, but I'm happy either way.PLEASE PLAY THIS.

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect glimpse of a possible future where almost everything operates more efficiently with AI (and not the general AI I suppose). Technological advancements integrate seamlessly into everyday life—even into public transportation. However, the downside of this world is its heavy dependence on the technology that enables it.With its narrow level design, the game lets you learn so much about this world through the interactive elements around you. What it accomplishes within its genre is, in my opinion, very successful. Tackling issues like socio-economic divides, politics, and corporate exploitation is what makes this game so fulfilling.There are two main plots. You finish one, while the other remains somewhat ambiguous by the end of the game.Mind Beneath Us is a heavily dialogue-driven game. Even with that expectation, it can feel stifling at times due to a few limited gameplay mechanics—almost like reading a book with animations, if you will. One major drawback, in my opinion, is that sometimes the dialogue feels like a writing exercise for the creators. Characters usually give more information—or just can't stop yapping— than they should. It feels more like a director’s cut than a theatrical release.Overall, I am glad what the creators achieve here. This could be adapted for a feature film. One last thing I can't miss mentioning is that this new 2.5D trend is just awesome. It elevates the game genre to another level for sure. I hope to see more of these.

_childDocuments_.review: Mind Beneath Us act similar to a visual novel, however, it is a side-scrolling game. Until then is a game that utilize a similar format, however, it is a completely different game by itself. Mind Beneath Us was able to capture the interactions and emotions of the characters perfectly with seamless transitions. Compared to a visual novel, there are usually static transitions between a character emotion changing between each frame by the click of the mouse.M.B.U (Mind Beneath Us - Shortening it) was able to develop a complete story while leaving a lot of loose questions about the world's lore and several characters. M.B.U frequently give you a third option to solve character's quests/problems without outright telling you where to do so. I love the fact that M.B.U tries to make you recall about past events and try to complete a quest through a different method. I was listening to a conversation between characters, then those characters noticed me eavesdropping on them. Hence, I feel like my presence has a place in this world influencing other characters and their choices. Each game attract a specific fandom or people by its mechanics or storytelling. M.B.U acts as an interactive novel for players that enjoy reading a story and having an impact in its world's characters with your choices.

_childDocuments_.review: Minds Beneath Us is an indie sci-fi narrative game, by BearBone Studios, that immerses players in a dystopian world where the lines between humanity and technology are blurred. Set in a vibrant cyberpunk city, players navigate a storyline filled with mind-swapping technology and a criminal underbelly.The game begins with our protagonist waking up in a hospital, amnesiac and bewildered, only to discover they are not truly human but rather a consciousness that's been left to inhabit a human form. This revelation sets the stage for a journey through various lives, offering a unique perspective on a society dominated by AI and shadowy figures.The game is absolutely rich in story lore, requiring players to invest a significant amount of reading. The narrative is intricate and thoughtfully crafted, drawing players into a world filled with philosophical questions about identity and existence. The start of the game is deliberately slow-paced, designed to establish the tone and atmosphere for the unfolding story.While this approach effectively builds anticipation and immersion, some might find the pacing a bit drawn out, which can make it easy to lose interest before reaching the more engaging aspects of gameplay.In terms of gameplay, Minds Beneath Us functions primarily as a visual novel, but it incorporates elements of mystery that set it apart from traditional point-and-click games. However, much like many point-and-click adventure games, you might find yourself clicking on items that are no longer relevant to your current story path. For example, I clicked on a book on a shelf, expecting it to reveal a new clue, only to find it was the same old text I had read before, which at times, can sometimes feel redundant.Most of the choices and decisions are based on text interactions, and while there are several branching paths, there’s a sense that they often converge back to the same story arc. For instance, choosing to confront a character either aggressively or passively might lead to slightly different dialogues, but ultimately, the story circles back to the same plotline, leaving some narrative branches feeling a bit incomplete.Combat mechanics and interaction rely heavily on quick-time events (QTEs), a design choice that adds both excitement and frustration to the gameplay. For instance, when confronted by a hostile attacker, a quick-time event might require you to press the space bar to dodge an attack and then E to counter.While these sequences can inject a burst of adrenaline, they also highlight the limitations of QTEs, as they often reduce combat to a test of reflexes rather than strategy.This approach can oftentimes feel like you've turned on 'invincibility mode' because the player's success hinges on reaction time rather than tactical decision-making.On the visual side, Minds Beneath Us is stunning piece of art, with graphics that create a captivating and immersive environment. The combination of 2D drawn characters and 3D backgrounds, particularly the cityscapes inspired by tech heavy Taiwan, adds depth and vibrancy to the game.The city skylines and meticulously designed neon signs create an artistic atmosphere, reminiscent of heavy brush strokes on dark smooth canvas. The graphics invite players to wander and absorb the views, bringing each scene to life with dynamic life-like energy. The color palette is particularly striking—notably, the prevalent use of purple seems to be a hallmark of this dystopian world.It seems like every cyberpunk game I've played has embraced various shades of purple, and Minds Beneath Us is no exception. This focus on the everyday rather than the typical power fantasy seen in many games is a refreshing change, allowing players to connect more deeply with the narrative and its characters.The sound and musical composition significantly enhance the overall gaming experience. Sound effects add a rich layer of immersion, with intricate crafted audio that draws players deeper into game world. The music is thoughtfully integrated, from moody to dire, which matches the game's tone and pacing.For example, during intense moments, the score shifts to pulsating, fast-paced tracks that heighten the tension, while more light-hearted scenes are accompanied by upbeat tunes that provide a welcome contrast. This careful attention to auditory detail complements the visuals and shifts the focus back the depth of the story.In the end, Minds Beneath Us offers a unique and challenging blend of storytelling, visuals, and philosophical exploration. While it may require some patience at the start, the game ultimately provides a thought-provoking experience that invites players to reflect on the nature of humanity in a technologically advanced world.Despite its minor flaws, this title shines as a significant achievement in the indie gaming landscape, particularly for those who appreciate games with profound narratives and deeper meanings.PROS:CONS:If you found this review helpful, hop over to   for more game insights and the occasional chuckle. We're serving up fresh content faster than you can say 'loading screen'!"

_childDocuments_.review: Generally speaking,  stands as a character study on how to write dialogue and meaningful interactions without it feeling forced or making the illusion of choice obvious. Characters have distinct personalities and are designed to be thoughtful with their choice of words. Thus the characters you interact with will come off as likable, as each person is well meaning or true to themselves in such a regard as to feeling human. Very few characters are just rude, nice, or thoughtful. Rather many thoughts and feelings are expressed in a single interaction to make the characters more than just an archetype or existing to fill a role.Too many stories are written with one tone in mind for a character and never change, thus dialogue with such a character end up being unpleasantly predictable. Meanwhile, in  characters fully express their thoughts and feelings, which might not happen in real life but is refreshing in a story instead of creating needless drama. You might have someone say something that comes off as rude, but then recognize what they said might come off as harsh or even apologize and better explain why they meant unless they were provoked. Characters are all rather thoughtful which is nice, and explain what you need to know to push the dialogue forward without making the conversation awkward or making you hate a character too often.Despite all of the praise, the dialogue is  perfect. The characters and dialogue is only well done for the first 2/3rds of the story and the quality of character interactions and dialogue slips later on. As a general rule during the first 2/3rds of the story the characters are well designed, often avoiding falling into pit traps or stumbling over themselves to force you feel a certain way. There are exceptions, like at the start with your neighbor going on about his opinions on women which was out of place and clearly the devs were intent on trying to make you hate the character. Another example is when a character that fairly early on blurts out he has a boyfriend which is not relevant to the dialogue at the time and should have been left until later in the dilemma though is very obvious the plot is nudging you to side with him. Needless to say the devs front loaded certain information to bias the players interactions with certain characters which is bad writing. Same ends up being true when Lawrence uncharacteristically nudges you into romantic drama when it is revealed 23 has a romantic interest, it's forced in at a time it wasn't right for the story just to make sure you as the player knew without being subtitle what was going on. To make you feel like you had a part when it was purely an illusion of choice.I'm not going to talk too much on the devs using the story to push their own personal values because while it's not hidden, it's not uncomfortably in your face all the time like a lot of game developers do these days. Though it is there and it is not hidden, and added nothing of value to the story.Another bad example would be with Nin Situ when she explains her view on doing the right thing, then ends up starting a philosophical debate without being asked about how principles only hold you back for a good 40 dialogue blurbs that added nothing to the story that is relevant at the time. If you cut out that entire conversation, nothing of value would have been lost. It was not needed for the story to expound on the characters personal philosophy without being asked and it had no importance to the situation it was brought up in. This situation ended up feeling like a book where the introduction of a character comes with 3 pages of explaining the entire backstory and world view of the character instead of allowing it to reveal itself through the characters actions and short dialogue during the story.On the contrary, when 23 does the same thing it does make more sense because at the time, place, and circumstance in which she chooses to do it it is relevant. The character is having a casual dinner with friends with drinks involved and it is already known that she has a moral dilemma through the story about the situation she has been put in. Now that is not to say it should have gone on as long as it did in 23's case, as the problem later became that you were trapped in a long conversation that had no real story relevance as it became about your thoughts on OWL and other topics when you did not ask about OWL. It was forced dialogue that was not directly related to your current situation in the story, and thus should have been optional instead of forced into the interaction.Two examples side by side of characters dropping pages of dialogue about philosophy on you done wrong and okay, but could have been better. Forcing the player into dialogue that has no relevance to the story should always be left to optional dialogue, and pushing romantic drama only works once. It should not happen when the plot thickens and there is suspense lingering about the plots main danger lurking which should be the primary focus of the story.I could point out many more examples, like with HELPER who's a ♥♥♥♥ right out the gate unprovoked without a need in the story in order to turn the player against him instead of being more subtle. I am not saying you can or can not make a well written one dimensional character, but the reason the character is one dimensional needs to be understood by the player and well written.In terms of personal taste, there are times the story has you be a match maker or forced bystander to inter-character romance, which ends up feeling more suited for a rom-com than a dystopian spy thriller. This takes away from the seriousness of the story. The first time was okay, because it was optional and before the plot had gotten into the spy thriller side of things, meanwhile the other three were very forced and I have no illusions as to why it was intentionally forced in for the developers personal reasons because of how it was written in at poor opportunities in the story.Guess you can say I am quite the critique despite the positive review, and it's not without reason if you read everything up until now. Before I became a writer and game developer myself, every interesting idea was some candle in the dark. As you are all familiar with the saying "the light shines brightest in the dark." Which inverted once I got into writing and game design myself, as now all of the flaws and little discrepancies are impossible to miss, same is true any time I look at art. It's like a dark candle in room of pure light, and there is no way I can miss how that dark flame flickers. It's a shame, but I suppose it's one of those things you end up with once you have seen the other side. Though that's enough about me, I just felt the need to explain why I see things the way I do to help you as the reader better understand where these incites come from.- Overall, well written dialogue and interactions which is worthy of being studied by writers in the games industry as a whole to learn how to make better inter-character dialogue and better characters.- The art style complimented the themes well, and is distinct enough that it would not be easily mistaken for another game.- Overall, likable characters and character growth served to push the story forward without being too overt about it. Letting the story move along naturally instead of having to be forced in a way that reveals the illusion of choice in many situations.- Despite the praise there are a few one dimensional characters, and interactions bent on biasing the reader for or against characters. Which is bad writing if you want a character to be more than just some plot device.- There is no hiding what the devs political political view are on many topics. It's not hidden, but also not in your face all the time.

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece. If you love story games in cyberpunk settings, you'll love it.- Story and plot: 9.8/10. Well written, with enough suspense, plot hooks, and world building. It's a deep story about humanity, morale, duty, class struggle, idealism, corporative power, tech dependency, etc... All the cyberpunk classics, but deeper than one could imagine.- Visuals:  9.7/10. Never saw so much emotion with faceless characters. The artstyle is also very good, with great colors, and fluid animations for the action scenes.- Characters: 10/10. Every single character is well written, deep, multi-faceted and fits in the world very well. The dialogues are excellent, and convey a lot of emotions.- Gameplay: 8.5/10. It's a biased mesure for this game. It's mainly a story game, so you go through dialogues, move left or right and interact with the world. Sometimes there will be QTEs, I find them balanced, not too hard or too easy. But it's not demanding gameplay, as it is story focused.- Rythm / Boredom: 9.5/10. Very few slow moments, as most of the time you can skip dialogue options if you're not interested. Overall very well paced. When you finish the game once, you can skip through dialogues, so you can replay it easily.Overall: 9.7/10. Excellent game, will be looking forward other BearBone games.

_childDocuments_.review: Well first off, I don't really play games like these. I usually like playing shorter games that have more instant results with more action. However, as soon as I played the demo for this I was really interested in this world the story have started to carve out. When I started beyong the demo, this entire ecosystem of the world opened up to me slowly through interacting with the environment, people and how the system works. As someone who enjoys a good story, this is definitely one that draws you in. The art is polished and immersive, the characters you bond with stay with you after you finish the game, and the gameplay is quite simple- you select your choice of answers and questions and explore the general area. What still impacts me is the characters- the game makes you care for them and connect with them, and the choices that impact them negatively or positively will affect you as well. There's a couple of moments in the game where I gasped out loud and was stunned :p I feel like after I finished this game, you feel this sort of (good) empty feeling after reading a good book- where you went on an adventure and it finally ends.. and now what do you do with your life? haha Overall really enjoyed this game and I am very hopeful for this studio's next game- I think they're really creating art and I can't wait to see what else they will create in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been on quite a Visual Novel binge lately, and I have to say that 2024 has been one of the best years for this genre that has created a genuine impression of authentic emotions, story, and character development, not only with Minds Beneath Us, but with so many others. While the game is extremely slow in terms of interaction time and progression more so than action and adrenaline, if you can stick with it throughout those long sessions, you'll be greatly rewarded with a gripping emotional story. Your choices here have a huge impact on your connections with coworkers, love life, and general interactions with people all around the world, especially with the persons life that you are currently taking over. Everyone has a personality, rather than just being background characters making it feel very real in a sense.On the surface, the game appears to be simple with its expressionless figures, yet they are capable of conveying a wide range of emotions through body language, which is wonderful. Simply put, this is a slower-paced iteration of the Visual Novel genre similar to things like Night in the woods, very engaging, and emotionally connected with your moral responsibility to the authority and yourself in this dystopian society.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: It has typical cyberpunk style of story, where "corporations always win, necessary evil and you're the loser no matter what" etc etc...Not very much of a game as it is practically a visual novel and I can see that it could possibly get boring to some people, since there's a lot of dialogue and no voice acting.But at least in a visual novel, I'd be able to go through entire different routes, but here, although I do get to choose one of two different departments in MC's work with its own quirks for a tiny part of the game chapters, in the end, all the choices in the game boil down to same 4 ending options, no matter what, with the difference being the aftermath of your game choices shown before the credits...And I really wished they made proper CGs or something, since I did like character art shown in the game page, but there's nothing like that in the game...Now I do have to inform, it is essentially a woke chinese game, which is kinda weird, but it is. Nothing too extreme, didnt annoy me too much, except for the dialogue in first 2-3 chapters. The "woke" part is light, but quite typical. While I expected them represented in a game that's set in 2049, LGBT couples get more highlighted in the game, you can withness their confession and talk to them about it, even hinted at almost catching them having sex, but main character and his girlfriend doesnt get as much romance or at all, just few short conversations. Game character art made me think 23 and Nin Situ are male characters, until I played the game to learnt those are female (as of course lesbian) characters in the game's cover art. Every major authority character is a female and of course the male authority characters are one or two and they are the villains, it was kind of funny in a way considering the age we're living in. But none of that made it too bad of an experience for me, what actually pissed me off is when they started talking about politics in the first few chapters, like for real, I get that its a chinese game, but the MCs girlfriend promoting communism was just dumb, props to the game allowing to call that out, but it was pushed aside at laughed at, as if we're just "misunderstanding". Same with other conversations promoting one side of politics over the other, but its being done in a way that almost seems like a parody, a meme or a criticism towards it, considering how idealistic its being portrayed to the point where the characters look delutional, but you can tell the developers want to promote those things to you, but dont realize what they are actually saying or what it means. Once they were done talking about politics, the game felt much better.To top it all off, the game tries sequel baiting. There were things that were left unanswered on purpose.It wasnt too bad, but if I could choose again, I'd probably not buy the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: A nuanced and refreshing take on the cyberpunk genre where the priority is not violence and combat mechanics, but rather on journeying through ethical and interpersonal conflicts that make you question your own value systems. Story is well-paced, engaging, and full of wisdom. 100% recommend--this is a GEM. I'll be keeping an eye out for future releases from this studio.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and loved playing out the story that the devs developed. The story, and the things that you find out as it unfolds, is engaging and I loved the concept. It was unsettling enough to make me care about the characters and the outcome of the story. I also loved the art and the combination of 2D and 3D. Overall, I would definitely recommend this game to anyone that is looking for something new to play.With that being said, there are some negatives/cons of the game that did stick with me.I think it's quite evident in the trailer, but this game has NO voice acting, so you will be reading all of the text dialogue on your own. As someone who reads to help myself fall asleep, I will admit that I fell asleep during some parts of the game. Partly due to having to read the dialogue and partly because I was at a boring part. I easily put 10+ hours into this game, so if you think this is going to deter you from playing the game, then maybe don't play it and watch a playthrough if you're really curious about the story.The middle of the game/story is the weakest section of the whole game, in my opinion. Beginning and ending of the game are engaging since you're finding out new information and fighting to end the battle, respectively. However, I think the middle of the game is kind of lackluster and I feel like it's not very memorable. Once you get through the middle, it does ramp up well and the story gets exciting again.This is more of a smaller issue, but when I got to about the last quarter of the game, there was this glitch where characters were disappearing and flickering during conversation. I saw that at least one other person had this issue in the Bear Bone discord, so I hope this is an issue that they patch soon. Closing the game and restarting it fixed the problem. Also, some spelling and grammatical errors for the english version, but again, not that much of an issue.TL;DR: There are some issues, but I think they're minor in the grand scheme of things. Give the game a shot, it's pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: From the narrative and visual perspective, I would definitely recommend to play through the game. Even though it is mostly a book, really. Visual novel would probably be the best tag for this game. However, I do feel a little lied to, as the entire story feels like it's building up to the main character becoming someone bigger and better. We are left at the end of the story going in that direction that I expected to start with. In that sense it was a let down. The real lesson I've learned after first playthrough is that the main character is not you. Without giving up any spoilers, your job in this story is to team up with the main character in this story. Yes, you do make important choices. But all choices that actually impact the narrative are shoehorned into the story precisely to give you the false sense of being the center of it.It's really hard to be satisfied with this story when you're in chapter 4 and still waiting for your character to start being "the hero" of it. Again, despite my disapproval of this decision, I would still recommend the game because its very affordable and it has a lot of positives going for it. I just would wish someone told me before playing that I should not expect to become the cyberpunk equivalent of Captain America, which is literally something the story tells you you WILL become. Just off screen after the end. This felt cheap.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty hard to find video games with compelling and moving narratives like this that make me reflect on my life decisions thus far. Without going into spoilers, I can say that this game is very philosophical, with strictly no right or wrong answers. It will force you to make tough choices. Moral dilemmas will be forced onto you. Sometimes even make you feel guilty for doing the "right" thing. Perhaps there is no black-and-white except for the principles we make for ourselves, and Minds Beneath Us will make you re-evaluate them in uncomfortable ways.It's with this setting in mind that the game's narrative is mostly built around the perceived illusion of choice in the grand scheme of things. Unless you happen to be extremely rich and/or powerful (and you probably aren't, otherwise you wouldn't be reading this), you are nothing. Even the choices you make seem insignificant because the world keeps spinning regardless of your actions, but Minds Beneath Us reminds us to be kind to ourselves and the people around us. At the end of the day, we still matter. We are our own most important person, and it's not necessarily wrong to be selfish. The game's narrative constantly reminds us that the world can be a cruel cesspool, that we inevitably do what we can to survive, sometimes even stepping on others, but also subtly urges us to make decisions with empathy. Because no matter how screwed up and hopeless everything seems to be, we can still make small changes that feel like they mean the world to ourselves and those we love and care about. The consequences of our actions, no matter how small and insignificant, still fully exist in tangible ways that we may not be able to predict. Minds Beneath Us reminded me of some moments in my life when I felt that I should have just ceded control of my life to the whims of fate, only for me to decide to stand my ground in the end. Things didn't always turn out favourably in the end, but at least I was glad I tried. What mattered the most was that I could live with myself and the decisions I made. Accept myself for what I am, mostly. I could look myself in the eye with some degree of pride at least, mixed with some shame. Still proud nonetheless.Admittedly, when I first saw the reviews for this game, I wasn't convinced that it could be so well-regarded with 9/10 or 10/10 scores everywhere. Feels like I'm jaded, cynical and bitter enough to regard everything online with a pinch of salt, what with rampant disinformation, echo chambers and state-controlled media these days. I'm glad I gave this one a chance. I think you should too.  Oh....and there's plenty of unskippable dialogue, veeerrrry heavy on the philosophical, political and anti-establishment side of things with some rather repetitive QTE sequences. Solid translation work from Chinese to English with minor typos here and there....while keeping emotional nuances in dialogue mostly intact. TLDR:   PLAY IT. IT'S A STEAL AT THIS PRICE POINT!

_childDocuments_.review: From the viewpoint of someone who's incredibly picky about sci-fi writing, especially in videogames, this game is a relief.Oh, sure, the art is nice and the characters feel decently written, but what really struck me was how the writers actually put thought into the concepts they came up with. So much sci-fi is essentially an aesthetic skin on an ordinary story, or possibly a clumsy metaphor for something else; Minds Beneath Us is a work that's interested in exploring its premise and examining different what-if angles on this world they've created.Even the little lore drops in the form of magazines and TV broadcasts were thoughtful and presented a setting that felt both interesting and grounded. Offhandedly, a single article mentions that scientists are searching furiously for a reason to say humans are unique and intrinsically special after discovering brains aren't that different from computers. Another article mentions cybernetics as first and foremost a disability issue, which is probably the literal first time I've ever seen a videogame understand cyborgs as disabled people.It's also wonderfully refreshing that the writers have clearly thought through arguments you might actually want to make in a debate. I was amazed to see dialogue options that included things I wanted to say, rather than feeling like I was limited to a set of bland stock lines; I also never felt like the narrative tension depended on the protagonist not wanting to ask questions, which is something that annoys me a lot in other games. Often other characters might refuse to answer or might not give you good answers, but just being able to ask at all feels good.The game does have its weak points. Sometimes you can make choices that feel like the game clearly didn't expect you to make them, such as , and seems to proceed assuming you did something else. The  have the weakest writing. The entire mind parasite premise doesn't ultimately seem necessary when the game really shines most in the parts that could also be experienced by a basically normal guy.Nothing's perfect though, and overall, it remains absolutely head and shoulders above almost all other sci-fi videogames.Subjectively, if you don't like VNs and really need there to be robust gameplay, look elsewhere -- this is basically a VN. It has even less gameplay than a simple point-and-click, which is probably for the best -- it focuses entirely on its writing without trying to pad itself out by making you hunt pixels or collect keys.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has to be one of the best RPGs I've played this year. The amount of thought and emotion put through the dialogues are something else. The questions of morality and how far do you draw the line in what is right or wrong, how much can you give or lose for what you think is the greater good. The characters are well thought out and express their emotions towards choices you make are pretty well done. The characters all have their motives and background fleshed out that makes you care whether or not your decision really is the right thing. It's not everyday that I write a review like this but I believe this game deserves it. Only thing that I would say that's not much of a con is the amount of reused settings. I think it would have been beneficial to have the story go to other place other than just the company and the house about 70% of the time. But other than this minute con, this game is good, I hope a DLC or a sequel comes out for it to further develop the ongoing story! 9.8/10!

_childDocuments_.review: Holllyyy crap. An entire game that sets you with morale choices left and right. Are you a survivor? Are you a pragmatist? Are you an idealist?It sets you up over and over again with lots of little tests to make you actually live into your professed ideals. Little tests: do you sacrifice for the greater good? Do you sacrifice to improve your own standings?  Do you just keep your head down...And then in the final act it sets you with a brutal trolley problem, an "unwinnable" moral quandary that makes you really put your money where your mouth is. When your life is on the line, will you stay on your high horse that you've been riding all game or will you tuck tail and run?Hot damn. Finally a morality system done well.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing The gameplay is simple and intuitive, and the story keeps you engaged very hard. I can't remember the last time that i got so focused in a story-focused experience like i was in this game, i played most of it (around 18 of my 20 hours) in 2 days, and during gameplay overall i was extremely engaged with the story. The worldbuiding is okay. The plot you think you will explore in the prologue actually is not the focus of the story, but that didn't matter much because the actual story quickly clamed my interest and became the focus. Indeed the fact that you are actually some type of player just controlling other person did not came to me anytime except the few moments that you are detached from the character.The vibes, musc and visuals are also pretty good, contributing a lot to the atmosphere and helping the player engage even more with the game. The combination of this and the awesome characters made feel a lot harder then i would usually feel for characters in a videogame.Personally, in a smaller/simpler way, some obvious differences aside, i felt like i was playing some small version of disco elysium. This game does not have a lot of content to speek of (around 20h to 100%, mostly don,t need to play it again to see the stuff you have lost), but the price isn't saying it should have. For the first game released by this developer i think it have a lot of quality.The story was amazing. The characters are very good and have a very nice development (provided you want them to develop, as you can ignore some very important stuff regarding this matter). The whole thing, unfortunely, is a bit short compared to my expectations. I understand that they may had limitations and could not make a game twice the size, but i hope they are able to make some good profit of this game to have the ressources to make even bigger projects. Also, i felt that, except by the side quests, your choices didn't really matter that much. I did not make any stupid things that could obviously hinder the main objectives, but overall i think it didn't make all that much difference. And the endings are all a choice you make in the last scene, witch isn't a thing i actually hate, but i think it would be better to tie these ending choices to at least some of your deeds in game (for example, situ just offer you her mentor's weapon if you did resolve the conflicts in her team).OverallGameplay: 5/10, very simple, but is not the focus anyway, just think they could bring more variety to quick time events, and also bring more puzzle-like sections like the very start in the prologue.Vibes: 10/10, the atmosphere is very engaging, even considering the simple graphics and lack of voice acting, the music is beautiful and the key moments of the story are very well built into the scene to make a breathtaking experienceStory: 8/10, I really made an effort to pull out everything i did not like about the story, and overall i think it had more potential, but is amazing nonetheless

_childDocuments_.review: Minds Beneath Us is rich in story and kept me hooked from start to finish. This is exactly the game I needed to play right now. _childDocuments_.review: Finished this game recently and it was absolutely fabulous. I would definitely recommend this game to my friends. The ending was shockingly tremendous yet very sad. That feeling you know you could change nothing and the world still goes on the way it was, it just hurts. The script of the game is what makes it stands out. I like it a lot and it involved many things. Morality, responsibility, justice, etc. The background is set in a futuristic world where AI systems are in charge of almost everything. It's kind of like the Cyberpunk-style world, with all those cutting-edge technologies yet people's life is still rough. “High tech low life” is the foundation of the cyberpunk world. The struggle, the desperation… society was built on people's misery. The AI system needs energy supply, and the cheap, easy-to-get resource? People. The game made it clear as one NPC points it out that humans are actually the most convenient resources they can get. See? Human beings are just a kind of resource, a useful tool for that rotten society. When playing the game, I couldn't help but constantly think of the iconic movie series Matrix. The red and blue injection bottle from the chapter 1. And also using human's brain as energy. All that similarities. I've always liked the Matrix movies and I'm certainly happy to see such a game. I've made so many choices along the way and every decision leads to the ending. What is free will. Does it really exist? I guess some questions are hard to get an answer. Like Delores said in the show Westworld season 3 “Free will does exist. It's juts so f**king hard.” This is life and this is the world we living in. Guess we are not so much different from the people in this game. Words being said that "every road leads to Rome" but the truth is, some people are already born in Rome. Some choices are hard to make, and some people even don't have a choice. This is life. The harsh cruel life.

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly brilliant.I love complex, mysterious, choice-driven narrative games.  is up there with  at the very top of the mountain. The 15 hours of my playthrough went by so damn fast and I was so heavily invested in the characters and the multi-layered story that I played most of it in one sitting despite hellish heat in my computer room.The final two chapters had a larger number of spelling mistakes that the earlier chapters didn't have ("Chamleon"), but that is literally the only (small) negative I can think of. Even the fact that the game contained quick-time events didn't really bother me, because they were fortunately fair and really easy (I think) to master, so that they wouldn't become a showstopper. I cannot say enough good things about the graphics, the atmosphere, the dystopian cyberpunk mystery story and, most of all, the characters. What beautiful character design from a writing perspective, with side characters and their stories feeling just as real and alive as the main characters.This is a GOTY contender for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Minds Beneath Us brings together storytelling, beautiful visuals, and interactive gameplay in a way that keeps me hooked from beginning to end. I enjoy sci-fi stories and games that test my thinking and decision-making, this game is definitely one that check out all the boxes and leaves you thinking for a while after finishing it!I was taken bsck by how much I enjoyed it it's a fantastic game. Hopefully the studio creates more games and sequels in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game for almost always giving me the option to say nothing (the option ".........."). As an introvert person, I often prefer let the other person finish their whole argument or opinion before express mine. So this ".........." option is great for me. (some other games though.... force you to choose one option from ones that you all dislike)BTW, great storytelling. A super rare case of cyberpunk style story based on modern tech development (2010+). Love it. 3/5--My own rating criteria: 1: Terrible; 2: Average; 3: Good; 4: Awesome; 5: Miracle.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: saw it in recommendations so I decided why not and played it, had an absolute blastit's a "choices matter" game but leading up to the final choice you have a lot of control and the game lets you go outside the box a few times and it's very satisfyingthe game is very morally grey and it's not always easy for me to pick a side and I think it'll test your principles to some degreenarrative is fairly complex with a lot of good foreshadowing of future stuff in hindsight.I really hope the dev makes other games with a similar style cause this was extremely unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that was so heavily worked on, over the course of 5 years, by a small team of people. I feel very proud of the developers at Bear Bones Studio, for putting something like this out there, that made me think that it was a good game from the start up until the end, and I found little to none as many flaws with this game, as with other games, when I played it. It's vibrant with its locations and designs, comedic with it's moments, and heart-warming in the moments you get to bond with characters and see them grow in the short time you are there with them. As well as being dramatic and upsetting in it's major moments, even towards it's final moments.I have seen people complain about the combat, I really didn't care about the combat, I know the story was the main focus. To me this game feels like it's a final cut on it's story. But to a lot of us, it feels like there isn't enough. Just like other people, I would also like to see more content or a DLC added to this game, because we want to see more with these characters and the world they live in.Besides from that. I truly enjoyed this game. And I highly recommend it for anyone that wants to play something like this. That for once in the reviews I make, I'm not going to make a funny review about it, like I do with other games. Because I loved this game when the demo came out, and I loved it and 100% it after I had finished the full story, So, thank you.10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Superb story, decent twists, amazing world-building, interesting characters, and great art and animation. Very interesting style though, as all the characters have no face.The game does start out very slow, and there's a lot of reading. Things do pick up near the final quarter of the game. The story does branch out depending on your dialogue choices, and there are multiple endings. Gameplay is a bit lacking. You only get to make dialogue choices, walk around, inspect things, and engage in very very simplistic combat.Would love a sequel, and hopefully next time the characters have faces and there's more to do in combat and exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Really amazing diversity of choices and characters have great personalities. Your decisions impact many choices later on, even when I didn't expect it in many ways. Worth the price for a great choices matter story. I would love a Minds Beneath US 2 release with a continuation. Game is about 20hrs long.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Oh I love this game SO MUCH and IT's A TRUE GEM.  The visuals, music, the choices, the long length, the inspectable objects, the not so hard fight sequences, the trials you undergo, the missions, the characters, it's just one heck of a sci-fi game - I recommend Sentience the Android's Tale that's like this but RPGmaker.  The Orwell series and Simulacra are like this but the Orwell series is really like this with no action but a great story.  Personally this has become one of my favorite games.  I only played it 9 hours though I got really emotional about it at parts because it's just so realistic with its metaphors.   If you go to work, this will resonate better with you especially if it's an office.   I recommend Moonless Moon for realistic metaphors and music videos instead of fighting scenes and a short length for one playthrough if you want that but this is about four times longer and less philosophical but these go good together one after another.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible narrative game in a genuinely thought provoking cyberpunk setting. The story has interesting characters and moral quandary's that it spends a ton of time fleshing out and examining from every angle. The game does have action here and there but ultimately the star of the show is the games efforts to consistently challenge the player to take a moral stance on the various issues it's presenting to you and ask you to rationalize your thinking. The only real negative I would call out is the small writing snafus such as rare grammar issues or a letter missing from the end of a word here or there. I know that anytime someone calls out translation errors it can be a bit of a red flag but I want to be sure it's clear the translation is fully legible the entire way through the game and the occurrence of these errors is a rarity and in no way the norm.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game and stared at the wall for a long time.An incredible experience that was worth waiting for for two years (since I first played the demo). Amazing soundtrack (I especially want to mention two compositions that were mainly played during the conversation with Lawrence, I’m extremely delighted), beautiful locations, some quite disturbing (yes, the Cellar with the Matrix vibe, I’m talking about you), characters, you empathize with... All this made every hour of my play the best thing I've done in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Very detailed, rich cyberpunk-style game with a dark story and an amazing soundtrack. Throughout the playthrough, this game will test your morals and raise many philosophical questions by presenting various situations that happen to characters in the story. Emotional depth is another important aspect, it's filled with moments that will make you question the nature of society and the consequences of your actions. Not to mention well written dialogues, and choices that they have, although most the choices lead to the same outcome, some of them actually alter the story and the ending. I would highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys deep, story-driven experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody of Taiwanese descent who almost completed his tech-related Master's, this game felt like it was made for me. Minds Beneath Us goes into a lot of hard-hitting topics such as a black-box nature of machine learning algorithms alongside societal issues such as how the poor are forced to do unsafe work to make enough money, or that a company's conditions are deteriorating due to budgets. If dystopias and sci-fi/cyber punk is your jam, I highly recommend this game. The writing is top notch, and it's been a while since I've agonized over various in-game decisions.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: A very narrative heavy game with minimal gameplay elements, but enough to keep you engaged. The story and the characters are the main reason you will want to keep playing this game. I easily became invested after just a few minutes and with each chapter came new revelations and even more questions. Highly recommended if you like dark mystery type stories.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I personally loved this game. It might not appeal to everyone since it's more of a 'Playable Narrative' with a few action and combat moments. But if you give it a chance, it's very likely you'll get hooked on the story, the graphics, the characters in general, and the exploration of new events/choices and everything else.It's a 2D game with 3D aspects that also stands out for its carefully crafted atmosphere, featuring a beautiful, detailed, and vibrant setting that greatly contributes to the game's immersion.Overall, the game is well-designed, though it has some gaps, as is often the case. I felt they could have explained the most important part of the game better; it came across as vague and even a bit lazy when you think about it. But in the end, it paves the way for improvements in the future (I'm already waiting for a second title, if possible). The exploration is well-balanced, offering a satisfying gameplay experience, and it incorporates many psychological aspects into the gameplay, which adds an extra layer of depth to the game, creating interest and even a sense of responsibility and fear when making certain choices. It's definitely worth giving the game a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Tl:dr This game has fantastic dialogue, colorful characters, a truly impactful choice-system and amazing writing.This game provides a truly engaging, action-filled and thought-provoking experience from the very start to the finish line. The characters are all very well fleshed-out even if they only appear for short periods of the game and all of them feel *real* which is impressive from a writing stand point no matter what.This game has a lot of dialogue seeing how it is a choice-based game, however what most choice-based games tend to fail at I find this game does amazingly, that is it doesn't hold your hand throughout the process, you are left to explore the world, notice hidden meanings and motives behind what people are saying and unlock choices by thinking outside the box rather than just following the set path. The dialogues themselves are truly well written, the interactions between characters feel real enough that you could easily see people out on the street having similar interactions, barring the more deadly and threatening ones of course. What really gripped me personally was that the choices you could make always had consequences whether small or big, but not only for you the player, the consequences affected the character and their life in a way most games fail to realize. A lot of the choices really had me questioning my own morality and doing my best to find a middleground between my own wants as a player as well as what I percieved would be the best for the characters themselves. Overall this was an amazing journey that gave me a lot of insight into myself and many hours of enjoyment, I highly recommend this game to anyone who likes choice-based games with heavy moral themes.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Narrative choice and morality games I've ever had the pleasure of playing. My suggestion... play the game through without resetting the Autosave file. play through it and accept the fate of your choices as if you were experiencing this yourself. there are no redo's in life. treat the choices in this game the same way for the best experience. though this is just my personal opinion. there were times when i did reset but after getting back to that same dialog option... i wanted to know how much my choice at this moment would affect me later in the game.  some choices do carry through to later in the story. The characters are written so well to react like actual people. even closing off dialog and discussions based on your responses. incredibly philosophical and makes you question your own ideals and morals. the dialog options reflect core ideas of people and you will almost always find an option that reflects what you're thinking and the characters respond appropriately. the setting feels alive. there are pivotal moments where paying attention to details makes or breaks certain story elements. exploring is absolutely encouraged and rewarded. analyzing these characters while you play is also a key element to knowing which choices to choose for your own personal outcome. only a few grammar errors dotted throughout but doesn't impact the story terribly. very minor mistakes that can easily be translated to what was intended. Now... time to replay it and see alternative outcomes and see how much foreshadowing was present. also unlock remaining achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

Help 2 best friends make up after years of conflict. 5. Expose a corporate conspiracy to , , and thus , for the sake of . 6. Adhere to the bro code when pissing at some urinals.7. Not actually find out what you are exactly.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: The art and music were amazing. I enjoyed the story but many of the character's felt flat, repeating their motives over and over again. Some story lines were discarded midway through and it honestly felt like many of my choices didn't matter. Characters that are so important one minute are never seen or mentioned again. The plot twists were good but they just kept coming over and over again to the point where I couldn't form logical answers because whatever happened was a trick or lie anyway. I enjoyed the game but there is definitely room for improvement for future games by this studio. I appreciated the philosophical messages in this game and I thoroughly enjoyed the world building and characters. The ending was pretty disappointing though.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: I waited nearly 4 years for this game and it was worth all the wait!The art style is awesome. The scenes have so much detail and the background characters give life to the world.While the ending of the game does leave open a few questions and feels a tiny bit rushed at the end, I would still recommend this game to anyone, be it just for the general world and art style, buit also for its characters.The characters are very well written, some cliches are there, for sure, but overall I had the feeling that they are very believable and I was rooting for some and hating others. Which is great :)Please support this team in any way you can <3
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first play-through, and wow. The art and visuals are very stylised and I love the mix of 2D and 3D assets I think it really helps give a sense of scale to the large rooms. The themes and messaging are consistent throughout and honestly, it reminds me of a lot of Cyberpunk 2077 but if you had to play as Johnny Silverhand. It will make you feel awful for the situation that neither you nor your host have control over. Make no mistake just like any good game based in a cyberpunk world, you are just a grain of sand on a beach. There are no happy endings for people like you, not without losing something important. I think this game captures that idea perfectly and doesn't have a single point in the story where I felt bored. Now the ending (or at least the one I got ):I have a feeling people will have mixed thoughts about the ending its sudden, but fitting. You don't really get a payoff, some reactions but nothing like a full epilogue and honestly, I like that. This was never your story, never your body. Does it matter where you came from? What an MBU is? No, I don't think so, if you want a game about an outsider taking over another's body and finding out about the secrets of your existence, this isn't it. I'd compare it more to parastye as this game more tackles what a human is, what thought is, and what gives a life (no matter how seemingly unimportant or how short) meaning.100% recommend for any fans of omniscient readers viewpoint or Parasyte or psycho passspoiler for the ending:
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely surprised by this game. Not my usual as I prefer fantasy role-playing games generally but recently been branching out and boy am I glad I am. So far I'm in the early stages but I'm instantly hooked. I can't wait to explore this game and see my ending and go back and see the other choices. If you like story-driven games this is a must grab IMO. The mystery, the small details I've seen so far, it all is so compelling I lost three hours in the blink of an eye.

_childDocuments_.review: i honestly really love this game i loved the demon and i got the game the day it came out i do wish the new game option was not the highest option in the menu i just lost a bunch of my play through cause of it and that really sucks but imma force my self to try to get back where i was but i just wish the new game option wasnt so high up on the menu

_childDocuments_.review: Story is so amazing i was hooked from the start still going through it , i love the characters the world building the relationships its like reading a very good book or watching a super cool tv show, gameplay wise its super simple you get to make choices though i havent tested how much it matters to the overall story, id totally recommend for anyone looking for a good sci fi storyEdit: finished the game god what an ending i was on edge the whole time, definetly worth a try
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Detroit Becoming Human, you while love this game. It is not exactly the same but out of all the games I've played I would say this game comes the closest. Your choices can have a major impacts on the story allowing you to see different sides which gives this game lots of replayability. The only thing I wish the developers of this game would add is a story decision plot tree that branches off like in Detroit Becoming Human, or at the very least more chapter checkpoints that you can load into so you can start closer to where certain decisions are made in the story without having to completely replay the whole chapter. Overall this is great game that is perfect for visual novel lovers.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

_childDocuments_.review:
Minds Beneath Us is an adventure about a guy and a data ghost who lived in his head and controlled his body.

After society has become fully automated with AI, a new industry has emerged that replaces the hardware needed to operate the internet with linked human brains. As a result, the most disadvantaged of citizens have had no choice but to put in their bid to sign up, one after another.

Against the stage of this mad society, a mysterious conspiracy gradually unveils.
_childDocuments_.name: Minds Beneath Us

name: Monster Energy Supercross - The Official Videogame 5
detailed_description: Hold on fast to the handlebar of your bike because a new chapter of the series has finally arrived. Try Monster Energy Supercross - The Official Videogame 5 and discover the quintessence of indoor supercross! BUILD YOUR SUCCESS The road to become a true champion starts here. With the new career mode, you'll have to prove your skills on two-wheel bikes to be able to win glory! Win the first races in the 'Futures' Category. Improve your technique as a 'Rookie' by starting out in the 250SX class. Create your team after signing with a sponsor or join an existing one. Throw open the doors of the entire championship by becoming a real 'Pro' to challenge the heroes of the 450SX class and achieve ultimate success. SHAPE COUNTS Keep your rider in shape by going through 5 preparation levels. In Supercross 5, training sessions, race results and injuries affect your rider's conditions. Are you ready to keep everything under control? COMPOUND Explore, practice and improve your performance in the new Compound! Do it alone or with 3 friends, or race against them on one of the 5 fantastic tracks available. TRACK EDITOR Unleash your imagination and build the perfect track with the Track Editor. Use and mix together the modules inspired by the tracks of the official races, share your creations with the community and race on the tracks made by the other players. MULTIPLAYER Discover all the ways to enjoy Supercross 5 with your friends. Challenge other players online in breath-taking races by putting your abilities to the test. And, finally, the very much in demand Split Screen mode has arrived, providing double challenges to the last jump. Fun multiplied by 2! E-SPORT For the second year in a row, E-sport is confirmed in the Supercross series. What are you waiting for? Are you ready to accept the challenge?

name: MXGP 2021 - The Official Motocross Videogame
detailed_description: All the power of Motocross in your hands: the new MXGP 2021 is finally here! The official MXGP videogame is ready to show you what it's made of: warm up your engines and get ready for the most realistic, exciting two-wheeled experience ever! CAREER Strap on your helmet, hop onto your bike and go full throttle on your path to becoming a true MXGP champion. You can create your own team or choose to join an official one, starting from the MX2 category in the new career mode. Your career results will affect game progression, as well as the contracts you can sign with teams and sponsors. LOST IN REALITY Everything is so realistic in MXGP 2021 that it's easy to get confused. More than 40 riders, plus the official MXGP and MX2 2021 season bikes and teams. Sponsors, accessories and all the 2021 championship tracks. Plus three iconic tracks from past competitions: Ottobiano (Italy), Ernee (France) and Leon (Mexico). With MXGP 2021, you'll feel like you're riding your bike instead of watching in front of a screen! MAKE YOUR MARK ON THE FUN Make your dreams come true, letting your imagination run wild with the track editor: choose the terrain type, build the track and customise every aspect of your dream track. Share your crazy achievements online and download the most exciting tracks created by other players. NO LIMIT CUSTOMISATION With more than 100 authentic brands, there are endless possible customisation combinations for bikes and riders. Make your mark on Motocross and add your own special touch to the game! PLAYGROUND 2.0 A fantastic new Playground lets you explore new landscapes and hone your riding skills. You can create your own route by placing multiple checkpoints in sequence in Waypoint mode: race and challenge your friends online. MULTIPLAYER Online competitions are taking on new horizons: now you can challenge your opponents on custom tracks. You can also create your own events and interact with other players in Race Director mode. Are you up to the challenge?

_childDocuments_.review: I am all about supporting moto games and have purchased every milestone mx game to date but its getting real old year after year seeing the same gear, same compound, same game, an slightly jacking up physics each time. The whole game seems like the next lazy addition in the series. Please, please bring something new to the table. Add the terrain deformation and improve air physics like we have been asking for years. Anyone reading this comment, stray away from purchasing, there is nothing new here, head on back to MX Bikes and enjoy it, cause you wont find that enjoyment here.
_childDocuments_.name: MXGP 2021 - The Official Motocross Videogame

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played a Motorcross game since my PS2 days. After some research of other titles I went with MXGP21. I've seen people comparing the copy and paste formula that EA uses with Madden and FIFA.I've never played a MXGP game before so i cannot weigh in on that comment. Yet, I would assume, like any other chain franchise there may be some truth in that statement.If you're brand new I recommend this game. -Soundtrack is great-Physics are challenging (to me at least) -Graphics look clean-The Tracks are fun-The Bikes sound sick.I don't have high expectations with games and where other people might be highly critical, I'm just happy to play a Motorcross game again. Big nostalgia boost from me.
_childDocuments_.name: MXGP 2021 - The Official Motocross Videogame

_childDocuments_.review: Have many hours on MXGP 2019, picked this up on sale. How can a game that is essentially the same as the previous end up worse? For reference, in '19 I played on the most realistic physics and difficulty possible, after learning how to ride it became a fun challenge, eventually steam rolling the AI on the highest setting. (I prefer career mode only). Was hoping this game would change up tracks and new bikes/gear. To their credit they did change up tracks and gear (maybe less amount of gear IMO), but holy moly are the physics terrible on this one. Tried running all realistic settings like in '19, but attempting a lap is challenging in the way that you have no idea how the physics engine will react. The bike and rider do not behave like one would expect, even from a game, just nonsense. Like cartoon glitch wackiness nonsense. Its ridiculous. Again, bunch of hours played in '19....now to just bouncing around like gravity is on a smoke break. Then there's the animation of the rider. It only makes sense to pair the Gary's Mod physics with what looks like Raggedy Andy with Moto GP style riding on a dirt bike (I've raced dirt bikes in the past and ride motorcycles on the road, so I have little idea of what rider form looks like). Its hard to enjoy this release when games from over a decade ago did better.Other small things like engine noise are annoying as well. 2 strokes sound like a weed eater, I'm almost thinking that they actually recorded a weed eater. 4 strokes are ok. The sound of the revs just don't match what the bike is experiencing.For a player expecting a realistic outdoor (MXGP/Nationals) style of motocross, look elsewhere. Heck go play 2019. For casual players, buyer be ware is all I can say. It became so frustrating after an hour, that I pulled the plug on the game and requested a refund.P.S. I miss THQ and Rainbow Studios
_childDocuments_.name: MXGP 2021 - The Official Motocross Videogame

Handling is terrible in this game and so are the physics. If you still want to buy this game just buy it on sale but I would just wait until Supercross 5 since that seems to be the series they care more about.

The first moto looked like mf 2006 Millville and I was there lookin like my i'd been dressed up for pre-season press day still. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR - MXGP Pro is much better for racing real life tracks, this game is only (insanely) fun for the track editor.I'll give it a yes, because I am absolutely in love with the track editor. My only complaints in that department are the camera and interface (worked great in the SX games, and it's the same company, right? Just use that...), and it could use more features (although I'd probably say that regardless of what's offered). Other than that, the track editor, with it's real-world-style maps, is crazy addicting. There was only so much you could do with the flat-floored stadiums in the SX games, but building in the hills adds a whole 'nother dimension. Literally.As far as the actual racing/career mode, I don't like it. The physics aren't terrible, I've definitely experienced much worse, but it just doesn't work with the tight, twisty, narrow, bumpy real-life tracks. However, the physics are fine, just fine for the the big, wide, smooth, fast tracks you can make in the editor. The AI is much harder than in previous games as well, without being bulldozers. In fact, if you get lucky and grab a holeshot, you can stay out front until you make a mistake, even if you're not as fast as the AI. They'll stack up behind you instead of running you ever. And, if you collide, it's actually a fair chance between which rider falls, it's not guaranteed to be YOU every single time anymore! It's a very surprising and pleasant change, but now I can't lap the field on 'realistic' difficulty haha. Definitely an improvement if you want a fair, but difficult challenge (and if the physics suit you). Also, even with the graphics turned down some, the game doesn't run too great with all the other bikes out there. I'm using a 3060 12gb, Ryzen 5800x, 32gb ram, and it's still stuggling to get 60 fps, running 3440x1440 with the bells and whistles turned down/off. Just another reason the racing is difficult for me. Runs fine in the editor though.I'd say, if you want to have fun racing on the real tracks, go with MXGP Pro. The physics in that game are some of the best I've come across, as far as a balance of fun/challenging. MXGP 2021 is honestly pretty similar, but something's off. All I know is, in Pro, I didn't have to rewind 30 times because my rider doesn't understand the concept of exiting the inside rut of a tight hairpin, heading in the general direction of the track. Instead, we wanna slide over the rut and likely bounce over all the other ones and off the track, OR we wanna turn WAY too tight and spin a 180 and start ripping backwards.Anyways, If you like to build tracks, buy this on sale. And I'm sure I'll be uploading a few LONG ones if anyone wants to watch for em. My first track is a 4:47 lap time on a 250 haha!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely a step forward from the last game, which was amazing. The physics seem to be completely new, there is actually track deformation that effects the way you ride and the AI are very tough. But all of these improvements have there downsides though, first is the track deformation, while it makes a huge impact on how you take every corner every lap, it sometimes gets absurdly difficult and makes the bike do very strange things like spin out randomly, hit an invisible wall while turning and it seems like you cant really catch the ruts most of the time, you almost just bounce out of them, however it is very fun to actually have to search off the main race line in order to find a smooth line. Next is the AI, they are extremely challenging, but as soon as they get a 2 second gap on you they will begin to absolutely leave you in the dust, I think it has something to do with the track deformation not rendering for them because they are too far ahead? But you can have some amazing battles, as long as you don't crash which at the end of the race if super hard not to do. Finally the physics, they are an improvement, but super frustrating. If you are going too slow through a turn and lean too far you will drop the front end and crash, this can make you feel cheated in some circumstances. Also the swapping physics that every one hates are actually really good. It will get your attention if you land sideways but you also can save the bike as well. Overall the game is great but has a few quirks that can ruin your race and make you very angry, but my advice is to at least finish the 250 season then try to fully upgrade your 450, then decide if you like the game or not, If you liked last years game and want something more realistic then you will love this game
