_childDocuments_.review: I find it necessary to express my profound disappointment with the apparent negligence displayed by the developers tasked with adapting this PS5 console game for PC. Their indolent approach is clearly evident in the misalignment of the mouse cursor with the menu interface - a blatant oversight that does little to inspire confidence.Moreover, the imposition of a user agreement, whose terms are relegated to an external website, ostensibly to obfuscate them from the player's immediate scrutiny, introduces an additional level of inconvenience to the overall user experience. Furthermore, the curious decision to commence the game with a tutorial race instead of the main menu, while lamentably commonplace these days, only serves to exacerbate the situation. Regrettably, the necessary equipment to ascertain the functionality and efficacy of "adaptive triggers" and haptic feedback within the game lies beyond my immediate reach, rendering me incapable of conducting a comprehensive examination of their performance. Notwithstanding the aforementioned observations, it would be remiss of me not to acknowledge that one may, in fact, elect to use the keyboard to play. This option ensures that even those who might eschew the use of more novel control schemes can nevertheless derive enjoyment from this gaming experience. Additionally, it is noteworthy that the optimization of the game's graphics allows it to operate smoothly on systems of a more modest specification, thus providing an inclusive experience for a broad spectrum of users.Despite some reservations, I can cautiously endorse MXGP 2021 as a game worth considering. However, it is important to note that my personal preference lies with the 2019 iteration, graced with more vivid and enthralling graphics, albeit perhaps skewing towards an aesthetic that may not fully align with the most stringent standards of realism.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing the game on the hardest difficulty with advanced physics makes getting a single player championship impossible. Why? Because if you lean to the left or right, you quite literally instantly fall over. The AI do things that are literally, and I am not overexaggerating, LITERALLY impossible for the player to do because if you did it, you would crash. Oh, but if you don't do it, you still ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crash.I love this game but at the same time all it does is infuriate me because I KNOW I can win, the game just doesn't ever ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ want me to.In retrospect and after uninstalling the game I will admit things like air physics and general bike handling are VERY good. Hell, even the A.I. is golden. So golden that I really hope Supercross has the same... "dynamics" with their A.I. where the grouping isn't so.. together, but instead spread out. Able to lap other riders. Maybe not on a short race (depending on the length/complexity of the track) but 100% definitely on a medium race and so on.This is a good game. Just like the previous titles they're slowly getting better and better. Clearly there's obvious issues like the fact that there still isn't track deformation, but for me it's alright because the tracks do feel like they get bumpier throughout the duration of a race. No ruts, but still, they're getting there. It's an arcade game, not a simulator. On that note I do think there should be different game modes for realism specifically.Air physics are better; still no free control in air but it's not the worst. Graphics are obviously a bit better than last year, which goes with the gradual increase in game quality that we're familiar with in Milestone games.Again, it's a good game. I recommend giving it at least a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Scripted gameplay. The bikes pivot in the center and any feedback from the road goes straight to lateral grip. Nothing to do with vertical physics. Ever notice how there's no wheel hop or struggle leaning forward when launching? Nothing to do with suspension unless you're mid-corner. To clarify an example: Fast bump will help with the small grooves, but not "extension", which would be fast rebound. Slow bump helps a minor bit for grip in smooth corners and large jumps. And that's all. The animation of the rider also over corrects like a sob at every given chance. Guess that's their way of pretending "speed wobbles". All this really does in effect is remind you to keep 4ft from the edge of the berms or the rear will step out. Doesn't matter if you're on the gas, how fast you're going or if you're even in the air. That rear-wheel steering will be sure to finish you off. And don't bother racing will computer, they drive on rails and reminds me an awful lot of Grid Autosport. The "physics" which are scripted act like the lie of Forza.Okay, rants over. I meant to keep it short, sorry. It might be fun with friends and I really had my hopes up for this game. HDR is also forced on so everything is bleached out. At least it allows full screen though and runs fairly smooth on fps. It certainly is a challenge, but after playing Tourist Trophy, MX bikes and so on, this could've been much better by comparison. I had a lot more for with MXGP2 & 3.

There doesn't seem to be much terrain deformation, but the tracks are already nicely rutted and feel great. The animations and rider movements all look really good and natural, and the whips and scrubs feel nice, although it's a shame they're still not completely free. Graphically the game is stunning, and is easily the most optimised Milestone game I've played, it runs like a dream!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic update. I own MXGP 2020 and this entry is totally worth the price. The track surfaces are more realistic than ever. Real ridges form as you ride (in 2020 some tracks were just flat), water from rain fills in the tire ridges, and weather can really change the surface in a noticeable way.  The riding surface will look totally different by the end of the race. This is something I've wanted to see for a long time.  Actual dirt degradation.  The tracks also have more detail and a more varied usage of 3D space.  Lots of tilts and twists, again moving farther away from the flat feel of past entries.  Controls and physics are challenging but you can really get in a groove once you master them.  The mud and sand each have a unique feel and you can even hear the difference when throttling the rear tires against them. I love it and totally recommend this, for new players or those who enjoyed 2020.

name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters
detailed_description: Grand Master Edition Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters - Grand Master Edition contains the acclaimed base game, Execution Force Pack, Duty Eternal Pack, and Castellan Champion Upgrade Pack. Castellan Champion Edition The Castellan Champion Edition includes Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters, the unique playable character Castellan Garran Crowe*, and the Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate – Daemonhunters Original Soundtrack. *Unlocked through a timeline event in the main story campaign. About the Game Lead humanity’s greatest weapon, the Grey Knights , against the corrupting forces of Chaos in this brutal and fast-paced turn-based tactical RPG. Root out and put a stop to an insidious plot to infect the galaxy with the Bloom , an intergalactic cosmic plague capable of rotting worlds into oblivion. Armoured in faith, shielded by devotion, the Grey Knights ’ very existence is rooted in mystery, enforced with mind-wipes and executions. Experience life in the 41st millennium and follow the journey of these elite warriors in a narrative penned by acclaimed Black Library author, Aaron Dembski-Bowden . SHAPE THE FATE OF THE GALAXY Upgrade your base of operations, build new facilities, conduct research into arcane mysteries and engage in combat missions across multiple worlds to purge the spread. The Bloom corrupts without prejudice; your choices will affect which planets succumb… and survive. FORGE YOUR CHAMPIONS Command your own, personalised squad of Grey Knights ; learn a range of diverse skills and psychic abilities, unlock powerful equipment and specialise your champions into four unique standard and advanced classes. Each of your warriors can be customised with voice, armour and facial options to make them your own. PRECISION TARGETING Grey Knights are an elite chapter of Space Marines and are not in the business of making mistakes or missing their shots. The Precision Targeting system puts you in control of your tactical decisions, allowing you to plan your strategy with confidence, whether by taking shots from afar with sure-fire accuracy, or dismembering and dismantling a foe in brutal melee combat! MUTATING MONSTROSITIES AND THEIR MINIONS As the Bloom corrupts worlds, environments will evolve and erupt with deadly hazards and minions, cultists and the infamous Death Guard Chaos Space Marines will mutate with pestilent boons and blessings, giving them new attacks and abilities. Adapt your tried and tested strategies to overcome unsurmountable odds against towering foes and their servants. CINEMATIC SLAUGHTER Charge headlong into fast-paced tactical combat. Eviscerate and execute enemies up close in gory displays of prowess, or strike from afar with blessed bullets and powerful psychic energies. Use the dynamically destructible environment to your advantage by tearing down pillars or slamming vehicles into unsuspecting enemies.

My main complaints are the bad performance (FPS drops made it near unplayable frequently) and the time sensitive nature of the campaign. You don't really get to play around with all of the different customization options (gear, abilities, squad combinations etc) since it's literally game over if you don't finish in time.  You can't take your time and try to unlock a lot of cool stuff; the narrative is pushing you to do everything as quickly as possible. Once you do finish, you  can't continue playing after the campaign to enjoy all of the stuff you've unlocked either. I've been through the campaign twice and still haven't had a chance to try a lot of the armor/weapons and even two of the advanced classes. I haven't felt like starting over a third time so I've just been reloading saves, but that's already gotten old. The moment to moment gameplay is fun and I want to play more, but due to the choice to limit gameplay to a single campaign playthrough, I can't see myself playing this much longer.

_childDocuments_.review: Way underrated. 20-ish hours in, this is a beautiful and polished game that I recommend to fans of the genre.Compared to other XCOM-like games, this one feels much closer to Firaxis' game, with many aspects directly parallelled, if somewhat darker and maybe a bit grim. When you scratch the surface though, you'll find many of the less popular aspects of XCOM have been addressed in interesting ways —  • Turn-after-turn missions will become harder by adding mutations to enemies, debuffs to your units or other general hazards, which nudges you against taking your time between engaging new groups of enemies • Some enemy groups (patrols) move around the map, adding another thin layer to your tactics — it's rare, but possible that an enemy group will stumble into your battle with another group if you're not careful. • The skill tree you upgrade your units with is engaging just enough to make you excited to experiment with a different path on few more units of the same class.Those and smaller gameplay and UI decisions, to me, signal professionalism and creativity from the team behind this game, and I love it.I am early on the campaign, so I can't speak about the story much — so far I can't say I'm losing sleep over it, but the sort of earnestness of the characters and I enjoy reading their takes on what's going on, and their occasional banter.

_childDocuments_.review: I've had to revise this a few times.  The more I play the worse it gets.  I want to like this game, but I can't.  It's beating a head against a wall.   1) LOS Rules - Terrible.  Enemies 15 squares away are triggered, but sometimes it's more than 15.  There's no LOS tool to determine range.  Counting squares is challenging at best.  So fighting one group, you can suddenly trigger another group.  And that group that is triggered has a full free round of action before any of your knights can do anything.      2) There's no ability to go back one combat turn and correct.  Make a mistake and your knight is out of action for a month or more, or you are restarting your mission.  A game like this requires a go back one round in combat.  3) There's no auto save between missions.  Make a mistake with your knights on a mission, for example, you forget a key piece of equipment, and you have to go back to the last time you saved  4) The turn management is downright bizarre.  You move units one at a time.  If you aren't really careful, you can move one knight way out in front of the others, trigger the enemy, and then combat starts with the rest of your force way behind.  And look at point #1 and #2.  Easy to trigger enemies accidentally and no ability to go back a turn and correct.  Also you can move 3 of your knights 3 AP, have the 4th knight trigger the enemy (also moving up to 3 AP) and all of them get another 3 AP within the same turn.  Like I said, bizarre.   5) Random events are awful.  I just got my last seed on a mission, and suddenly 4 enemy reinforcement groups show up.  Then a warp surge giving them ALL +5 armor. Oh, and they all get a turn to move/attack before I can do anything.   6) Lack of differences between missions.  There's one mission so far (and I haven't gotten past day 180 before almost all my knights are critically wounded or wounded), that's different.  The rest are all the same with different maps.   That's gets dull quickly.   Solid graphics, great maps, good concept, but the mechanics just don't work.  There are better Warhammer 40k games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big Warhammer 40k fan and I am making an effort to like this game. It's nice-ish and has potential. Unfortunately there is some seriously annoying stuff. The in game graphics are nice and I personally even like the sligthly cartooney style.On the plus side ..+ .. I get to equip my knights+ .. action sequences are nice; like throwing that one hand grenade+ .. switch around weapons, pick out my team and all that.+ .. Upgrading the damaged ship with limited resources feel thematic and enjoyable.+ .. The research might be a bit weird, but lack of inspired progress is definitely the imperial vibeNow for the parts that NEED work- JERKY CAMERA, CENTERING IN AND OUT OF COMBATas of the time of this writing, the camera has only two settings: action camera always on or sometimes. The camera jerks around needlessly. Even when my knight is right there already on the screen it will violently centeron him. In combat that only gets worse.Smooth(er) transitions would be nice.+/- STARTING ENCOUNTERS, SURPRISE PULLS WITH 1 TILE DIFFERENCEA severely mixed bag. On one hand, it is nice that you get a full contingent of action points when you encounter / pull new enemies while out-of-combat. That is a welcome departure from XCOMs "whelp .. that's where you moved your last soldier are and now it's the enemy turn! Enjoy!"Sometimes the enemy is detected from far enough away. Sometimes you just move that ONE square farther up the line than the rest and you pull a new batch. Whit is especially unfortunate when it is one of those 3-turn-rituals-start-NOW things. So you try and stay sort of in position as well as keep up the wardings.And here we come to stuff that feels tedious: cycle through everyone and their inevitable greetings just so everyone can get their ward and we can move on. Then you move everyone 1 action point and then a 2nd round for the 2nd action point. If you do not do that, you will start the encounter more scattered or with a shield down.So if you want 3 AP fresh on the pull (without having to waste one on a shield) that's the tedious 3 cycles to do.Also, I have to wait for one knight to finish running to his destination before I can even start to command another. It's single player. Just let me switch once the command is given. That works in XCom and feels much more dynamic.- SHOOTING, LINE OF SIGHT/EFFECT, COVER AND ASSISTANCEA good thing is, that for every square you select, some sort of line is shown that usually - but not always - indicates that you can shoot a target.Sometimes that line is bullsh*t and you end up being unable to shoot from that position.That straight up sucks.I am guessing some general line of sight / line of effect issues remain. Since in one mission I had high ground and unobstructed visibility down on two targets. Lines and all shown. Turns out I can't shoot them. Fine.A nice mechanic is fire support that triggers from friendlies. Which is less fun when the friendly in question cannot actually shoot the target. So they end up shooting precious ammo into the wall... Thanks for nothing Thule!Do not get me started on the full cover wimpy edge, that I can clearly see a chaos space marine sitting at. somehow he is in full cover. Apparently not only the emperor provides! :)- DEACTIVATED PORTRAITS AND LACK OF CRITICAL INFORMATION Portraits automatically deactivate when all AP have been spent.Regardless of whether or not you could still do actions that do NOT cost AP.Certain abilities do not cost action points. Certain abilities and stratagems refund action points.Unfortunately, once a knight's AP are spent,you do not get to use that servo skull this round.You need to do that BEFORE you spent your last AP. Unfortunate.The whole thing just turns super annoying when you want to use your AP restorative.Did that guy have ammunition left? No idea. I forgot and I am not aware of any way to find out how much - if any - ammo that grey(-portrayed) knight has once I activate them. Maybe I just get to reload. ;)Even when the knight is active you actually need to select the shooting action to have the ammo displayed.Because if you are not in that shooting action, it will show you an icon displaying your meele weapon next to an infinity symbol. For those people that want to be constantly reassured that their knight can hit things infinitely.You might only have 1 of 3 shots left. Who the hell knows? At least you get to read up on how you can always infinitely bash things. That is even true for Purgators. Who do not have a dedicated melee weapon.- LACK OF COMPARISON FEATURES: WHEN SPENDING REQUISITION AT MISSION ENDAt the end of missions, you get some random gear and personnel to spend your hard-earned requisition on. Nice!Especially at the start, these improvements may be marginal. Unfortunately there is no comparison option for your armory or even only against the items carried on the mission. Did I already have a strength 4 bolter with range 12 or is that a slight improvement? .. Especially difficult with weapons you do not routinely use.Also your knights get bonuses that mean the range displayed on the weapon is not the final word.Same with knights. You get the level and class shown. you accept him. And then you get the info that you do not have any room and need to discard an existing one. Comparison ... hm. Well the name and level.- EQUIPMENT, LOADOUT, THE LACK OF SETSThe game shows me if I am equipping something for the mission that another knight has. OKbut it only replaces that with a standard weapon if I switch it out. Not really relevant.Ideally I would like role-sets. My mission apothecary uses that narthecium with those servo skulls. The purgator gets that psilencer, this one suit with plague resistance and the psychic hood, etc.I managed to bring only 2 of the 3 plague resistant suits because I did not pay sufficient attention on a team rotation. You will want to rotate wounded team members. And then you will spend time individually going into all the sub menus for ranged weapon .. stormbolters .. select; back; back; armour .. power armour .. that one; back; back; melee weapon .. swords .. the ones I always use. Yes, that one with 75% parry, as always.Tedious. Ideally I pick standard role mission equipment sets, equip those with a quick select and only swap out grenades / servo skulls / whatnot when the mission profile necessitates it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've read some of the Warhammer books and understand how brutal the universe is, then you'll have a good impression of what to expect. It is not Mechanicus where your Tech Priests become insanely strong, it is not Dawn of War with Hero characters. The intro mission sets the tone, and you becoming commander is not a fluke but a veiled reminder of the universe you are entering.Overall the progression of your knights into killing machines are awesome to see. But the chaos gods have an answer to everything you try prepare for. Luckily additional classes become available later in the campaign to assist in dealing with the ever increasing challenges you face. I will say that the difficulty increases steadily with your own power growth and it is only in the last 25% where you might have confidence knowing you can finish missions cleanly and efficiently. Beware that the closing 10% will quickly destroy all that confidence and personally I loved that twist of desperation. I honestly thought I would have to reset my 2 hours of final mission at several points.The story does a good job explaining the ever increasing difficulty and desperation of the gameplay. I was also surprised more than I thought I would be at the turns the story decided to make. In Xcom and Mechanicus the story is somewhat easy to read before hand, but I must say I was pleasantly surprised at what the writers decided to do with the story and how the characters felt genuine.If you understand and enjoy 40K and enjoy turn based strategy, then this is an awesome game. Replay value is there, but after the amount of time I put in in my first campaign I'll be taking a break. But I can see where there are ways to replay and take different paths with the classes. Way more variety than the other titles mentioned earlier. And on the sale price it really is a no-brainer.

_childDocuments_.review: XCOM meets WH40K, the right way. I found the mix of game systems and risk/reward management inherent to keeping your roster of marines healthy to be enjoyable. The AI can be very clever and punishes bad or risky plays very hard. There is no 'aim %' system, so everything is based off of range and no/half/full cover systems, and it works well. Every class has a ton of skills you can level up and build into, there is a wide variety of gear and wargear to equip on your guys, and you will be forced to try out a variety of things due to getting wounded and having to take backliners often. Certain skills are of course overpowered compared to others, but finding out what is good and what isn't is part of the fun.A unique aspect of the game would be the manner in which each mission unfolds thanks to the warp timer causing random effects that can seriously change how you approach a situation, such as spilling a swamp of poison between you and the enemy, randomly giving mutations to enemy troops that make them much more dangerous, spawning in reinforcement squads, depleting your casting resources, or evne giving all the enemies a huge armor stack for a turn. It makes for some very wild twists in missions that I find very welcome and in character for the setting, considering it takes place in the middle of a demonic incursion into the sector.My one small gripe so far is the very punishing wound system that results in a lot of downtime for team members, from pretty routine amounts of damage. However, if I had been able to use an A-team the whole way I probably would have complained about that instead. Some people take issue with the cartoony style of graphics, but I actually like it and think it suits the setting. I've played enough 'realistic' 40k games to last a lifetime, and this take on the aesthetics is refreshing and welcome. Despite the graphics, the story narrative is spot on setting wise, and fairly engaging, especially for a WH fan.Overall I would say a lot of care was put into this game. It does the source material justice and is also decent from a gameplay perspective. Yeah it has its quirks and some aspects are not executed all that well, but I can say its a good game and mean it. Doing a blind run has me fully engaged and interested in learning how to make the best squad possible, and it feels like all the information and resources I need to do that is in the game itself.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are an XCOM fan, you'll love this. The difficulty even on standard feels balanced, to where remove the enemy buffs and whatnot, they will hurt just as much as you do unbuffed as well. There really isn't any difficulty scaling aside from what kind of mission your on and the threat level of the system, until you drop in. To put simply, when your on a mission the phrase "If it is possible to go wrong, than it can go wrong." I can't say how many times that in particular happened, but I wasn't mad at it either. The buffs and debuffs that basiclly run the entire game, feel really nice, especially all of the empowered stuff as well. As for your Grey Knights, or in XCOM terms your Team, to me really and truly feel like there is kind of a difficulty when it comes to class synergies. In the end however, you will start to kind of see a little pattern of what works for your kind of style. The main thing that I really loved was how it takes its Risk/Reward gameplay to a whole new level that I don't really want to spoil much about aside from it puts you in the mindset of if you are confident enough or think you can get in, do whatever Grey Knight boogalo that you do, and survive. Reminds me of how XCOM does the same thing. In short if you love Warhammer 40k, if you love Grey Knights, or you just want to spend time on something trying to find the perfect class build, or you just want to tell some funny stories of you encountered a new enemy or things like that, play this. You will not regret anything (PS. be careful with Crowe pls)

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I feel this game suffers from the "annoyingly/frustratingly difficult" issue.Yeah, difficulty itself is fine and all and can be fun, but this game has some frustrating BS in it that bogs down the fun of the core game. I've been playing on "normal".Not only do you deal with multiple enemies that surround your units, they can be ressurrected and summoned in within just a few turns, or seemingly at random. This means if you don't go straight for the objective you're stuck dealing with a ♥♥♥♥ ton of enemies that just dont die. Doesnt help that these guys dont go down as fast as you'd like. Sometimes it takes just one hit, sometimes two, but then they respawn, hit your units and slowly chip away at their health. Then they set up an overwatch, stopping you entirely unless you want more health chipped away.Need a healer? sure, you just gotta sacrifice more damage for it. And that heal doesnt last, as you just repeat the previous and your units get chipped down to 0 again.This shouldnt be too big a deal, right? Ok but now we add in extra annoying stuff.The objective of the map is the main focus. Kill a specific thing.Ok, cool. Now you're dealing with the above, plus the thing you have to kill which is a damage sponge, and has high area damage attacks with a good deal of range that screws up your units. And in some missions these things have helping hands with the same high damage attacks. Theyre health sponges as well.Ok, now you have 2 of these objectives, far apart from one another, you will certainly lose one or two guys doing the first objective and now you have to do the second with what little you have left.I dont mind difficulty, but this just borders on wasting my time.Unless you go out of your way to savescum you're forced into doing these missions (low danger btw) and cant retreat or redo. If all your guys go down, mission fail, life moves on, other missions get harder.I have other issues with the game besides this, mainly the UI needing a lot of work as it's a bit big and cluttered at times, and I think the mission structure (not being able to just go into a lower-level mission to skill-up recruits) could use some work. My problem with the difficulty is the thing stopping me from enjoying the game however.If you're an Xcom player, then you'll probably like this, but for me this just aint what I was looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not bad per se, OK graphics, sound, OK voice acting. It is pretty brutal difficulty wise, which is not a bad thing, I like the challenge, but it get repetitive very quickly. Boss fights feel unfair considering it takes two hits with the power sword to kill an unarmored cultist, each single demon and chaos space marine takes a team effort. This is my biggest gripe  with this game, it punishes you hard for making a wrong decision but it does not really reward you for good tactical play, the best you can hope for is no critical wounds. Story is interesting but not very compelling. Overall Grey knights don't feel like demon slayer powerhouses they supposed to be, which is sad. On a bright side, upgrade tree is very nice and offers a lot of tactical options. The variation of classes and weapons , including weapons visual aspect is great, but in the end it all comes down to doing same thing over and over, struggling to survive on every map. I think it would benefit from rebalancing, enemies, making them hit harder but also go down easier, this would push players to utilize more skills and environment and plan ahead better with less frustration. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Any turn-based tactics game these days will be compared to the XCOM reboots (XCOM: Enemy Unknown and XCOM 2), but this game is actually closest to Gears Tactics (3AP and stun/execution system). This is to its credit, and if you enjoyed Gears Tactics like I did, then this game offers a similarly fun tactical formula with a more fleshed out strategy layer on top.The player and AI take turns commanding all their troops each turn, like in XCOM, Gears Tactics, Phoenix Point etc (as opposed to individual characters taking turns based on initiative, like in XCOM: Chimera Squad, Battle Brothers etc)Each character has 3 Action Points (AP) per turn. All actions cost 0-1AP and can be used to move/attack/activate skills in any order, which offers a great deal of flexibility. Certain abilities can provide bonus AP as wellEvery attack that applies damage is guaranteed to hit (no XCOM-style missed shots). All attacks have a single default damage as well. However, the damage actually applied by an attack varies according to the following:The UI nicely shows you how much ranged damage your character can do to each potential target as you mouse over each possible tile you can move to, which is an excellent featureOverall, having no hitchances completely eliminates frustrating moments of missing 95% shots and adds a bit more predictability in the game so you can focus on other interesting aspects of combatWhen your Knights perform melee crits or special ranged crits with "Precision Targeting", you will have a choice to disable different body parts of the enemy to debuff them in different ways. This varies from enemy to enemy. For example, you can shoot off a Plaguebearer's arm to disable their main melee attack, or shoot their head off to inflict the "Crazed" effect which gives them a 50% chance of attacking their allies each turn. This system is most similar to that of Phoenix Point (minus the manual aiming)Non-mechanical enemies have a "Stun HP", which refers to how much Stun damage they can take before they enter the "Stunned" state. Most attacks deal 1 Stun dmg by default, and the game will tell you if an attack will deal 0 Stun dmg or bonus Stun dmg. All melee attacks on Stunned enemies are guaranteed crits, and if the melee attack has Precision Targeting, there is an additional option to Execute the enemy, which immediately grants +1 AP to all Knights that turn. This enables a fun combo playstyle you can wipe out the enemy force in a single, well-planned turn. Note that at higher difficulties this becomes a lot more difficult as all enemies spawn with higher Stun HPBasically a mana pool. Each Knight has an amount of Willpower (WP) which can be spent to perform special abilities. Killing at least one enemy in an attack usually grants +1 WP to the Knight who made the attack. This system means that most non-DLC abilities don't have any cooldowns (except that you might only be able to use the ability once per turn), while still encouraging thoughtful use of abilities. Note that many WP abilities contribute to the Warp Meter, which is explained nextEach battle has a soft timer, where as the battle goes on and as your Knights use Warp abilities (that cost WP), a Warp Meter is filled up. Whenever the Warp Meter reaches 100%, a random debuff is instantly applied, ranging from enemy reinforcements, reducing maximum HP/WP of all Knights by 1, temporary buffs to enemies etc. Hence, although there's no hard timer in battles like XCOM2 (where you will instantly lose the battle when the timer reaches 0), the game does motivate you to complete the battle as soon as possible, as it gets increasingly difficult as the debuffs stack upEnemies roam about the map in pods similar to XCOM/Gears Tactics/Phoenix Point and have the free "scamper" turn upon contact, where they will take cover, go into Overwatch, or even attack in rare instances. This game mitigates this effect by full refunding all player AP when a pod is activated when no battle is currently taking place. As soon as all active pods have been defeated, all characters instantly reload and regain their max AP as well. The UI also shows a radar icon showing the position of nearby enemy pods that have not been activated yetMany players really hate free "scamper" turns in tactics games. While this game doesn't do away with it, I think this game offers a more forgiving system that doesn't make players feel like they have to resort to the slow Overwatch crawl popularised in XCOM: Enemy Unknown. Moreover, Overwatch distances are much shorter in this game and enemies typically will be well out of your Knights' Overwatch range when the pod is activatedLimited-use "spells" that you can use to heal/buff/debuff depending on what cards (Strategems) you selected before the battle(Steam Reviews have a character limit so this section will be less detailed than the Tactics section)You control a single ship (which you can upgrade) and move between nodes on a Star Map. Time passes as you move and missions appear on the map that follows the tried-and-true XCOM formula of You Can't Be Everywhere At Once. On top of that, many events can happen that basically require you to choose between different debuffs, such as reduced XP growth, limited roster, reduced research speed etc. You're basically fighting a campaign with one arm tied behind your back most of the time, which can be frustrating for some but definitely poses an interesting challenge each campaignYour Knights gain EXP and level up, allowing them to spend Ability Points each level on a branching skill tree similar to that of Gears Tactics. There are 8 classes in total with 4 available from the start. Each class promotes different playstyles and are restricted to certain equipment, though there is some overlap and a bit of flexibility depending on how you level your KnightThis feature kept me  on this game each playthrough. At the end of every battle you can purchase randomised gear for your Knights. Starting from the midgame () you can upgrade the gear as well. The different types of gear and their upgrades can drastically alter how you play. I found that between 2 different playthroughs, how I played each battle varied greatly depending on what gear I had at the time. Every time I play this game I want to play Just One More Mission to see what cool loot I'd getThe devs have continued to update the game with free new missions and enemies. To date there are 2 content DLCs (Duty Eternal and Execution Force), each adding new missions/enemies and classes. I highly recommend playing a vanilla playthrough first to get a feel for the game before buying or activating the DLC. This is especially true for Duty Eternal which many reviewers complain as being unfairly difficultThis is a fun, well-designed, and polished tactics game. You don't need to have any knowledge of the WH:40K universe to enjoy it. I look forward to more updates and DLCs from the devs!

_childDocuments_.review: I beat Chaos Gate: Daemonhunters - played halfway through on Ruthless then restarted after learning about some dumb gotcha moments and beat it. This is a positive review but I'd recommend waiting for a sale price, personally.(Relatively low number of hours is due largely to using cheatengine's speedhack to play the game at 4x speed - it's sloooooooow paced by default)Like most good Warhammer games it's really held back by being a vehicle for Games Workshop's lore instead of taking advantage of the things the IP is known for, like designing and painting your own armies. I understand the lore reasons why they went with Grey Knights but because you're forced to play Grey Knights, you can't recolor any of your armor or customize soldiers much and you're locked into everyone being a psyker.But there are other ways this sucks even more - like every X number of days you have to give a report to your Grandmaster. This can go a number of ways - but one example is that since the Space Marines are all ascetic weirdos he'll do things like berate you for stockpiling resources (seeds), and demand you hand over half or all of your resources. You can choose to say "Nah, I'll keep them" but then this entirely locks you out of earning new gear until the next Grandmaster Report (which is ~4+ missions away), and the game autosaves immediately after your choice (and only keeps one autosave slot). So a number of times throughout both playthroughs I unexpectedly got locked out of earning new gear and oof that sucks. Another thing he will berate you for is claiming too much gear from missions that you're not actively using - if your inventory starts to fill up, he tells you what a bad space marine you are and demands you hand over random pieces of high level gear, with similar penalties for saying no. There was never any indication that this would come in the future or that I should limit what I take, and since I had no idea what gear I'd want late-game I just took everything that seemed interesting.Another way the game ♥♥♥♥♥ with you like this is with soldier death and advancement. If a soldier 'dies' they get a Critical Wound. After too many Critical Wounds, they die permanently. At any time before they die permanently you can retire them to get a Requisition bonus. The obvious gameplay avenue here is to retire any soldiers that reach 1 Critical Wound because you get resources for them and they're about to die permanently anyway. Well, once you get one of your marines to max level, you learn that you can respec their skills or gain additional skill points on them... but it requires 'communing' with permanently dead marines. So late game, I hit max level on my first playthrough and find out I had no way to respec or gain bonus skillpoints because I never actually let anyone die. Then I had to restart and game the system by intentionally hiring marines whose sole purpose was to eat up enemy hits and die an actual death so that later on I could mulch their corpses into bonus skillpoints for my party. This all sucks because you're punished on a gameplay level for lore fluff reasons and the accompanying gameplay mechanics are just bad and frustrating.All of that being said, by late-game my marines definitely did feel like invincible space marine ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ who could shrug off a thousand suns, on Ruthless by late-game the Marine:Enemy ratio feels much more appropriately space-mariney, with engagements often being 20+ enemies closing in on my 4 marines and my marines dispatching them handily. It felt too easy toward the end because of how absurdly tanky your units get but that was also probably my fault for continuing to grind out bloom missions to get powerful before taking on the Reapers - by the time I fought them I basically just dogpiled them, ignoring all their gimmicks and killing them in a couple turns each with overwhelming damage output. Since I restarted to kill level 1 marines off to turn into bonus skillpoints later I took advantage of it and maxed out a couple characters' entire skill trees :v:Overall I enjoyed it a lot, it was some of the better tactical strategy RPG combat I've played and the production value is high. Great presentation, marines feel weighty and punchy. The Strategic layer is extremely shallow compared to even nu-XCOM and the way it handles strategic resources is frustrating at best, and the entire time I felt kind of sad at all the ways it was held back from being great just to tie into the IP lore.

_childDocuments_.review: This game... Really makes me wish there was a mid option for reviews. I "enjoyed" the game for the most part. The base gameplay is rather fun. But it seems for every positive this game has it has a matching negativeFirstly the game is easy. Extremely so. I started the game on the easiest difficulty because people were saying it is extremely hard. I stopped halfway through that run because I hadnt even lost a single knight. So second run through I go for the next difficulty level up and same thing, easy as hell 99% of fights are over turn one or turn two as the knights just blend through enemies as if they were nothing. The only challenge is that the enemies pile on a million debuffs onto your units, rather then just making the enemies deal more then like 5 damage and have more then 8hp, they decided that they would rather make every encounter extremely annoying as your units get hobbled forcing you to not be able to reach the enemy so you waste a round doing nothing, Or completely disabling all spells (Somehow? Like seriously how does a bell make up to 5 grey knights unable to cast spells???), Or literally everything plaguing your marines so you have to have a million cleansing abilities or servo skulls. But probably the most annoying thing is that by the end of the game literally every enemy reduces your knights armour, or entierly bypasses their armour. On both my runs I went for things that increased armor alot, turns out that was all a waste because everything ignores armour. Seriously one grenade hitting your squad and suddenly your 4 terminator armored knights are now equal in protection to a normal power armor knight. Not that it matters because the enemies die immediatly from a stiff breeze assuming you have a functional brain and can spec your knights out effectively. I didnt even look up what the meta is or anything, I suspect if you do you probably will take literally no damage as everything crumbles in your pathWhere the challenge of the game comes from is the absolutely absurd RNG in the game. I suspect if you are very unlucky you could die by day 100 through absolutely no fault of your own. Your knights can just up and vanish due to events "Oh you have a level 9 knight that you love. lol hes just dead now not through combat through a random event!". These happen constantly and have zero skill to them. And random events that damage your ship can happen constantly. To the point in my first run I ended up with a ship almost completely destroyed entierly through random events. I of course maintained a massive stockpile of servitors on my second run and that mostly fixed that issue. The way mission spawns seem to also actively screw you over. It seems impossible to actually reach all 3 that spawn most of the time, and half the time you can only reach one. This makes it less of a be careful with how you deploy your knights and more of a "Well you can only reach one mission anyways may as well only have a A team and no backups because when will you ever need a B team". Turns out you ABSOLUTELY NEED A B TEAM. Two of the final missions basically are impossible without a decent B team. Luckily I had a few decent ones but it was extremely annoying. Speaking of the missions. These are sometimes fun but spoiler there are exactly 4 types of missions. Seed carriers, Bloom spawn, Bloom Spreaders, And boss fights. These get stale fast, and worse they get LONGER not harder, they get LONGER later into the game. You go from needing to kill one seed carrier to needing to kill 3 seed carriers spread across the whole map. Needless to say the fact that the game doesnt really spawn more units or really make you face anything tougher then two terminators in these missions. Well yeah its just annoying to the point 90% of the time I am in a mission I am not thinking on how I could beat it, but instead how I could cheese the map to get it over with faster. Saving teleportation abilities to cross gaps or teleport past enemy patrols. Its just not fun, zero challenge in these random missions and they just drag way too long. There is also no way of skipping enemy actions, you can speed them up but the animations still play out and enemies all have to move individually. Same thing with your knights. It takes like 5 minutes of just watching your fat ass knights jog their way across the map one by one to actually get to the fight. It would be WAY more fun if every mission just had one objective and that objective was actually hard. Rather then a million scattered easy as ♥♥♥♥ objectives that you clear in one or two turns tops. The enemy variety is also a bit lacking. There are like 3 demon types that spawn, and 5 marine types, along with 2 cultists. They are pretty basic, the only interesting ones are the 2 big terminators that have unique abilities. Unfortunatly one of them is just straight ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ allowing ALL UNITS to bypass the armor of your knights. As said earlier this is just annoying. But really it is rather unfortunate that you dont see any of the more unique demons or more threatening marinesBuilding a squad is very fun, there is alot to do there and is probably the most enjoyable part of the game. The problem is ITS 110% RNG. There is no way to pick what you want ever, you cant craft items, you cant choose upgrades, and you cant even pick what knights you want. I beat the game once almost twice, I still havent seen a librarian. Not even once show up as a recruitment option or a reward. I havent gotten to play with a librarian. The worst part is the completely RNG weapons give so many cool unique builds that would be awsome to mix and match if you could craft your own or modify weapons or just actually pick from a option of 4 at least. By the end of both of my games I had upwards of 40 requisition points because I simple never got any decent equipment rolled that I could actually use past a certain point. The game would massively benifit from a crafting system, and a level system that let you start with basic strike marines and spec them into paladins or librarians or purifiers down the line. It also feels like the game is missing a commander. You are the commander but you never actually join the battle. Having a main character Captain or Librarian that you can spec out with various team buffs would be very coolThe ending and post game are bad and none existent respectively. Slight spoilers but nothing major. The final boss is sort of interesting but over all is way too weak, the only good part about it is that you get to play the best character in all of 40k (Fight me) Kaldor Draigo. Unfortunatly Kaldor is a MASSIVE PUSHOVER, he has like 2 unique abilities and is overall weaker then a single paladin. Half the health and basically no armor. Seriously what? Like really why did you make him weaker then a level 9 paladin? He 1v1 mortarion in the past and a million demons, but no hes straight trash that has to be protected by your random marines. Probably the worst part is that you dont even get to kill off the main sorta bad guy Kadex, like sure you kill him but no true death for him. Come one Kaldor is right there with the titans sword just have him kill off the annoying bastard. Kadex isnt even a major character, he doesnt even have a model on tabletop. It would be so easy to have Kaldor just say ♥♥♥♥ this annoying ♥♥♥♥ and banish him from existence. And finally you dont even get a final chapter master report, not even a final "good job you get to keep the ship and stuff". Or a triumphant return to TitanAlso post game content. Why isnt there any? You have Khorn daemon models in the game. Just like have a gauntlet type deal where you fight them in randomly generated missions along with nurgle units and hell since it seems like they make new units as if its nothing (Seriously literally made Khorn models for the intro that you can skip and they never show up again) why not flesh out the other gods for this sort of mode as well?

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fun clone of a certain squad based tactics game that has "X" in its name. Helps a lot if you want a Warhammer game, because then it will be good enough, and stand out from the competition with its focus on melee combat. The bad:- RNG - enemies get bonuses every couple of rounds. Some are fairly mild, some can cripple you- irritating scouting mechanics from XCOM games is here as well. Exploration is its own mini game. I prefered the standard, old XCOM model, not 5 enemies jumping out all at once- Grey Knights are super duper warriors among space marines, which are super duper warriors themselves. They shouldn't get a scratch from most weapons the enemies use, yet they do get wounded fairly easily- I'd rather see another, melee focus chapter. Would make more sense from the mechanic's point of view (grey knights feel underpowered for what they are in lore)- I love warhammer for chainswords and bolters, not high sci-fi weaponsThe good:- a lot of melee which is refreshing- the timer pushes you to rush, and eliminate enemies quickly- you outclass the enemy instead of the reverse - its a change from the genrea's classics- nice and rich ability tree- nice class selection- Nurgle is the enemy - best antagonist in my book

_childDocuments_.review: Too many people compare this game to XCOM. It is FAR more akin to Gears Tactics and makes me realize that not everyone plays as many tactical/strategy RPG games as I do. It's an amazing genre - go play some more games than just XCOM. HMU if you need recommendations. Overall I have been enjoying the game. I like the art, the music, the ability to literally disarm your enemies, and once you get the first healing upgrade and to around level 3 things really start to open up.The first part of the game IS pretty rough on you (I had some salty words on stream about it NGL). If you just push through that and stop thinking of this game like "Hide in cover" XCOM it really grows on you. There's a lot fun to be had here. I think so far Teleport Strike is my favorite ability. Man that one is just awesome fun to use. The only mechanic that irks me still (at least as of writing this) is that when you Overwatch you step OUT of cover. I got shot a lot needlessly figuring out when Overwatch is (and is NOT) helpful. Final note: You don't have to kill everything. In fact you RARELY have to kill everything. Focus on your objectives and then GTFO. I know that's a different mindset than some of you are used to in this type of game and it's a bit of switch. Once you make that change though... it's fun times ahead!

_childDocuments_.review: One day this could be a great cross between 40k and X-Com.Today is not that day. The game is hella janky as it stands.Cover is very wonky. People will shoot you from below while you stand three tiles back on an elevated ledge. Overwatch will not trigger on people running backwards and forward through it - except sometimes it will. Enemies will shoot you from positions you were certain were safe. You won't be able to shoot them back.And then there are the missions.Spoiler Alert: The first time you take the inquisitor out for a mission you have a nice long slog through constant respawns. Get to the end and you have a long fight against the toughest nurgle fellow so far. Kill him and all that's left is to channel the inquisitor on his altar. Oh wait! It turns out you need to channel for 6 turns while fighting off waves. What a lot of pressure! What a long tough mission... and then. You realise that despite explicitly positioning your inquisitor between two gigantic plague towers so that she's channeling on the altar and not getting hit by them... they just seem to hit her anyway. Every turn. For a bunch of damage . And corrupt her. But wait! She can't take actions! The game has locked her channeling! Just standing there taking massive damage but you cant walk her away. Can't stop the ritual. You desperately drop all of your remaining heals on her. It's a miracle you have any left after this giant slog of a mission. You try giving her armour but this stuff pierces right through... of course. Turn after turn the out of range towers smash her and she dies, Enjoy that kids! Some great design there. I genuinely don't know what they want you to do. Perhaps sit wailing on the two towers for a number of rounds before sending her in? But that seems kinda insane. They're basically scenery. They don't move. They're tough as hell. Why would you waste the time? You know... if you don't have to.I'll say this much. No human being has play-tested this campaign through from start to finish because I'm really not that deep in and already there are some glaring issues... Give this one a few good patches because right now, you'll want to punch the screen.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played for 19 hours, and have only done 7 or 8 missions, so I'll edit this recommendation based on more gameplay, if necessary.  Even those 19 hours are misleading; I played the first mission on easy mode, unintentionally, so I started over on Standard mode.  Then I made several bad decisions due to not understanding how the various mechanics work (their documentation / explanations are very terse), and decided to start over again.  So I'm only half as far as you might expect I am.I am not a Warhammer or Warhammer 40K fan; I do have some residual resentment towards Games Workshop due to their pricing model and some of their business tactics within the miniatures hobby, it's pretty low-key.  I don't dislike either of their main franchises; I just don't know much about them.Even without knowing the lore or the backstories, I'm still enjoying the plot and story elements of the game.  Actually, one of the reasons I've only played 19 hours is that I found the lore and references so interesting that I started reading 'Eisenhorn', one of the most-often recommended series in the extensive line of 40K novels.  I've been enjoying reading that during some of the time I otherwise would have been playing the game.  I'm normally enough of a snob that I wouldn't read an RPG tie-in novel, or usually even a franchise (Star Wars, Star Trek, etc.) tie in; the fact that 19 hours of game play convinced me to give one a shot is pretty impressive.  The mechanics are X-COM-worthy.  The action point and willpower economies are fun to manage, even with the limited amount of control I have with level 3 characters and a single strategem; I can see how I'm going to get more and more tools to manage both in-battle currencies in the future.  There is a Ship tech tree, and a Research tech tree.  Each marine has their own individualized Ability tree; I believe what they did was define a bunch of mini-trees, each one of which can be placed in the North, South, East, and West positions relative to your starting point in the center of the tree.  I also believe they came up with similar mini-trees that could slot into the NW, NE, SE, and SW locations, and I think that which one goes into a particular marine's final tree is at least partly determined by which of the "primary, N/S/E/W" trees are on either side of it.  In any event, it makes each marine distinct, and with the same class and the same level, two marines can play completely different roles.It plays well with both gamepad and mouse-- I use the gamepad while playing on my laptop in bed, and the mouse when playing on the PC with my widescreen monitor.My two significant complaints so far are:1. As ridiculous as this sounds, there's actually no way to inspect the battlefield.  You always have one of your marines selected, and anywhere you place the cursor is in relation to some action that marine would take-- moving, firing at range, teleporting, healing, whatever.  You can't hover over something that looks like it could be just artwork, or could act as effective cover, or whatever, and get a name, or a description of its effects.  This is super irritating.  Even if you could get all the info you need while having a marine selected (and I don't think you can), it's needlessly awkward.  It would be so simple to just have a button you can press when a square is highlighted to get information, but there isn't.  It would also be normal an convenient to have a button you can press which would outline items of interest in some color, like movement penalties, what kind of cover it supplies, etc.  2. I can't figure out how to re-read the text that appears on the screen-- sometimes in battle a message will get displayed in a or edge of a screen that I'm not looking at, and by the time my eyes track over, I only have a moment before the text disappears, and I'll miss part or all of the meaning.  Similarly, in the Options, I have Combat log turned on; but I can't find any way to view the log, which I'd *really* like to do.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I think the game still needs some optimization work. The framerate on some levels drops as low as 10 from 60 during the enemy turn in particular. I have a suspicion this is Denuvo related. Further, even for minor wounds, the wound recovery time is way too long and needs to be balanced better. I have had some at 40+ days for minor wounds. This means you cannot use the same character and build them up as per the RPG element of the game. The audio in-game is very good, but not outside of it. The story doesn't make much sense lore-wise either. So while the author is, in my opinion, qualified, I am left wondering if it was double-checked by somebody more familiar with the lore? The interactions between the Imperial factions stand out to me as lore-breaking in particular. Special mention to the outrageous price for two items, one character and all the twitch loot you can get by watching streamers for hours on end. I think they need a better marketing department, to be honest. Charging people so much for things that should be in the base game is not acceptable. Full review:Do you like X-COM? Do you like 40k? On paper, this should be the game for you. Overall the gameplay is good, though wound recovery time needs balancing. 40+ days for minor wounds isn't acceptable. I mention this as even weapons that lore-wise would damage Aegis Armour rarely do so regularly. This would be forgivable if wound recovery did not take so long.  Some of the abilities that show up at random are either useless or absurdly powerful. Due to being randomized, they often affect mission outcomes greatly. Imagine fighting through a mission that was super hard, only to know you likely have to reload and hope that ability does not spawn again. This is incredibly frustrating. Otherwise, I think the game is very good; though I'm not too fond of cover being up to 100%, I think it should be capped at 80-90%.Sound-wise, the voices and battle sounds are great. Honestly, they are some of the best I have seen from a 40k game. Outside of battles, minus the voice acting, it is subpar. This takes away from the immersiveness of the setting. I had hoped for better. Story-wise, I think several missions come across as filler and do not contribute meaningfully to the story in any way. When you have the Inquisitor, Astropath and other characters written so well, it sucks having to grind through meaningless missions that do not contribute overall. Dawn of War 2 at least had missions that were grindy, but there was a purpose overall to do them. Here it feels like you get a small reward, but that is all. I would like to see that improved. The interactions between the Imperial factions also needs to be improved as well. Performance-wise, it can be all over the place. My system is high-end, so getting frame rates as slow as 10 on the enemy's turn is not great and takes away from gameplay. I note this only happens on some maps, whereas others are near perfect 60 across the board. I would hope the developers optimize it some more and hopefully remove Denuvo. Finally, one cannot neglect to mention the marketing team deciding to make players watch over 10 twitch streams for items. Who thought that was a great idea? Further, the items + characters in the special edition could have easily been included in the base game. Neither adds anything meaningful to the experience, as far as I can tell.In conclusion, I would give this game a 7 overall, but it is a 6 due to the crappy marketing and value for DLC proposition. I hope the devs know that this would be a solid game with more optimization. Perhaps market it better next time? Buy it on sale.EDIT: The Devs were kind enough to give the community the twitch items in an upcoming update. I am bumping my overall score to 6.5/10. It is good to see devs listening to the community. Now please remove Denuvo.

_childDocuments_.review: So I never post Steam reviews but after putting in some time on this game I felt I had to warn people NOT to buy this. This is my review after 30ish hours on normal difficulty. Initially, I was having fun looking for an XCOM-like and boy did it scratch that itch. I'll start by saying that on the positives that the tactical side of this game is extremely fun. The missions play out like a more aggressive XCOM, the Knight classes are well designed and balanced and each mission has tension and more often than not that the line between sweet victory and catastrophe was a one move difference. Now for the negative. This game's random event system is utterly broken, unbalanced, and unfun. This makes the strategy side of the game a complete dumpster fire. The game withholds information from you and peppers you with so many random events that you are constantly digging a hole in the sand as it relates to managing your ship. Here's an example. After the Craftworld mission (basically beginning of Act 2) I got three random events in a row, the first was a cryptic message about my construction being disrupted for infinite days until I "resolved" a situation. There was nothing in any of the menus about how to resolve that situation (e.g., special mission, repair) so my halted construction project stopped 1 day before completion. About 35 days later I received a message that I had failed to resolve the situation so my construction would continue to be delayed (current project knocked back to 10 days), hull integrity -1, gun batteries down. Great. So more projects stacked on top of each other to get back to 0. Then, another random event this time an enemy ship encounter. I had to board the ship otherwise I think any other action would have been an instant game over. I complete the mission by the skin of my teeth and it's fine. Then a THIRD event. I opt to send knights to investigate after consulting a guide, which seemed like the least negative impact (3 knights inaccessible for 10 days). _childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game on Legendary. First play through on Regular was super fun, and I learned a lot. Love the story line, the graphics, the voice acting, but most of all, the tactical combat (like Xcom as everyone says) combined with the strategic pressure building relentlessly. The music is repetitive, like all of these games, but I frankly don't even notice it any more. Like Gears: Tactics, it looks like you'll be completely overwhelmed, but somehow, if you figure out the sequencing of your knights and their abilities, you can often pull it off. In the 2nd play through at Ruthless, it was pretty dang hard but I somehow squeaked through. I discovered the trick of standing on the bloom warp and sometimes being able to stop a reinforcement squad from appearing. I learned which weapons and armor were worth spending precious requisition on, and I avoided certain builds for abilities that I didn't use very often. I got to try a few of the harder classes to recruit: Chaplain, Librarian, Paladin. At the end of game 2, I read some online guides and realized I had been missing out on some other tactics, like making Interceptors into melee machines instead of primarily using them for fire support as I had done originally. I learned about how to really double down on certain knights' strengths and rely on passive equipment and auto abilities much more, instead of active abilities that suck up WP and limited supply items like grenades. So in game 3 in Legendary mode, I was much more picky on which weapons / armors I would pick up. I got a lot more knights from the missions instead, so I could send a squad of knights to battle for some of the strategic encounters. I still didn't quite sequence the ship construction correctly - should've focused on getting to the 50% faster construction ability sooner. I never used an Exterminatus, but maybe I should have. My Morbus level got to 3 when I finished the game, but it felt a lot riskier at the time.Though I've spent way more time on Xcom 2, I dare say I love this game even more. I am itching to restart a new Legendary game to see if I can do it better / faster. I really didn't know for 99% of the Legendary run through whether I could live through the final Boss battle. Turns out I had a little more buffer than I had thought, but I was definitely swearing and sweating through the multi-hour fight.Awesome game. Great job developers. Scrolling feels jerky.-	Readability of the maps and characters is not good, the art design itself is OK-	The UI looks very soft. It seems like it is designed for FHD and does not scale to 4k. On top of that additional (update: not cosmetic, actual Tire1 items with better stats) content is gated behind streamer drops. _childDocuments_.review: After 64 h of play time on day 617 at game time, I finally completed the game. Overall, I enjoyed very much the game. I bought this on pre-order. On the release, there were some silly bugs, like cursor disappearing and some of the character abilities was not usable due to some bugs, but those got fixed on later patches which were released rather fast after the release. The game balance and AI was adjusted during the patches. To be honest, I don't know how much they adjusted the gaming experience. Perhaps to the better since I was middle in the game when largest patches were released and none of those caused any issues for me. So personally I feel that the game is worth of even the full price. It was great fun.Generally speaking about the game. Now that the game is completed and looking back, there's actually pretty much nothing that I dislike. I think that I managed to do right choices during the game since there wasn't ever really a need to go long way back using saves and redo the choices. Some minor choices I did need to do, like go back couple of days per game time which were like 15 to 30 min play time. And usually those kind of redo things I had to on the top level strategy view. The one where you need to choose your research, where the team goes and decide ship upgrades. I think the game requires two week of game play time to get the real grasp with the game rules. After that, everything comes rather fluent. Before that, you are going to make some mistakes which costs actually just some game play time. People complain about the difficulty. I completed the game on standard and I didn't use any spoilers or strategy tips from the forum. And as said, I never had the need to go further back and redo some choices that I did during the game play. The end game, I did beat on single run. It perhaps took like 3 to 4 hours. Which actually tells that the combat is not that difficult if you just take your time and think your moves. I think that at the core, the game is really fair. It's actually like a game of chess, where you just need to do the right moves. If you do your choices too hastily and just run guns blasting and expect enemies to fall just because you feel that the marines should be totally op compared to the chaos, you're dead wrong with the game.The general game concept is good, low level strategy is almost perfect for me, top level strategy is enjoyable and it's actually cool to see how the choices you do conveys the story on.  I really did like the story. Got even fond of the inquisitor, lol. I think the game could be so easily on par with the classics such as Jagged Alliance 2, Xcom and even Civilization in to some extent, but pity that at the overall, the game is not really a classic status. I could say, close but no cigar, which is a true pity. I hope there will be a sort of sequel, similar like how Jagged Alliance evolved from 1 to 2. By minimum I expect a DLC.There is however one thing what I really wonder. The game has rather large amount of RNG, and even some decisions what you do during the game has rather large impact at the end game. Considering that, I actually managed to do almost the perfect choices during the game. I can see that if you have done poor choices, you can easily see at the end that the choices you made wasn't sufficient in order to complete game, lol. Then the fact is that you need to do the whole thing once again. But I suppose that has been the thing at previously mentioned strategy classics as well.Anyways, this is actually my first review and did want to write something because I think the game totally deserves it. I think that I will do another run to get some killer combination in the team and upgrade ship better and try to beat the game in less amount of days.

_childDocuments_.review: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters - that's a mouthful. It makes me hopeful for a "Chaos Gate - something something Aeldari", though. I think this game is so good, I would insta-purchase future campaigns based on other 40K factions. I love TBS games, and I think this one is top tier. Unlike tabletop 40K (and games like XCOM), RNG isn't really a factor. The benefit of this is that the developers were able to balance the game exceptionally well, and that leads to really satisfying gameplay. I initially started on Legendary difficulty, then restarted on Ruthless. I just completed my first playthrough, and not only was I addicted to the excellent gameplay, but I was deeply impressed by the writing and the story. (Note: dealing with COVID, so apologies if this review is a bit scattered.)The story incorporates an impressive amount of lore from the Grey Knights, Nurgle's Chaos Demons, Adeptus Mechanicus, the Inquisition, and there's even a little Eldar love. So that was fantastic. Top notch voice acting brought the story to life, and the story arc was not "Hollywood predictable".In this game (no, I'm not repeating the too-long name), there is a strategic level where you manage a ship and team resources - but the level of granularity is just right, meaning, it's not too much. The focus is on the tactical squad combat. I played much of the game with a team of Interceptor, Librarian, Purgator, and then a rotating 4th which was at times a second of one of the above, and at other times a Paladin. And I pretty much played the entire game with that team (I did have 2-3 of each role, so I could swap them out when one of my guys got wounded). But there are many other classes, leading to different team dynamics and playstyles: Apothecary, Chaplain, Purifier, Justicar, etc. - with DLCs adding more as well. So, good replay value.On Ruthless, I started strong, and wasn't defeated on a mission until quite deep into the game. I appreciated that, if things start to get rough, the game remains balanced in a way such that you can fight your way back to the top. Defeat doesn't inevitably snowball into further defeat. There are also random events that require you to make some interesting choices without any indication of how those choices will impact your game. This is exciting. At first, I was frustrated by the fact that I couldn't save-scum during battles. One thing I love about TBS games is the puzzle-like aspect, and I like to be able to rewind and "figure it out". But I got used to the inability to save frequently, and actually game to appreciate the game design here. Not being able to hit the rewind button every other turn forces you to commit - and then learn from the overall experience. And as I said earlier, if you lose a battle, you get the opportunity to evolve and do better next time. Defeat is only temporary.What can I say, I loved this game. Great art, music, acting, writing, gameplay, balance. A little note on sound design: many of the combat sound effects are incredibly satisfying. Okay, I'm going to go buy the DLC now and play it again. High praise indeed.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game. And I would definitively have given a thumb up, if that was an actual sequel to the cult game Warhammer 40K: Chaosgate from 1998 developped by Random Games Inc.So, the biggest fault comes with the name. No big deal would most say. So why do I freak out?Simply put, there are two kinds of Warhammer Games:1) The ones who follow somewhat the Warhammer rules (Shadow of the Horned Rat, Dark Omen, Space Hulk, Chaosgate 1998, and so on) and offer the real immersion. They are the best imo.2) Those who are under a Warhammer License but mimick some other game or license dynamics. You've got good and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ things there. And Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters belongs to the good games from the second category. It is actually a very good XCOM-like game and I enjoy it for that. But else, compared to the dynamics of the original Chaos Gate:- it lacks a proper squad number of units (5, not knowing the Grey Knights, I don't know if they actually are based on a 4-units squad system). It might seems weird to some, but overall I don't like that much games where you control only 3 or 4 characters. I had always a preference for 5+ playable-at-a-time characters games. It just feel more real.- you control only 1 squad. in 1998 CG you controlled more and more squads as the game advanced in plot, with vehicles (unfortunetaly a bit buggy or not adapted to the maps, but there was potential there for a sequel).- the ambiance of Daemonhunters, true to the XCOMs, is too much comics/funny-wise for my taste. 1998 CG was a lot darker and I prefered that.- Musicwise, Daemonhunters does not hit a spot by me. 1998 CG did. And it was a looong time ago. And still it does if I am to believe the comments of some retro-gamers).So, dear developpers, why did you actually manage to no deliver a sequel - probably condamning at the same time any future hope in that regard -  and still used an existing name? Lack of inspiration?You did a good game, don't get me wrong, but you killed my hope for a much promising sequel to the 1998 version of Chaosgate. Yes you did. And for that only reason I give you a thumb down.

_childDocuments_.review: Xcom meets warhammer 40k. You are charged with commanding a strike for of Grey knights space marines in purging worlds of Nurgle's taint. (God of Plagues and decay so he is bad news.) You have serveral different classes which focus on a skill. It can be melee, tanking teleportation, ranged or support. Each of those roles is important to countering the forces of nurgle from the swarms of cultists to the elite death guard chaos marines to the daemons of nurgle. As Grey Knights are pyskers (magic users), they can all have special magic abilities which can cause damage or support team mates. You can use the terrain such as exploding barrels and knock pillars on your foes. Your knights will not miss their shots. However cover does reduced the damage you or your foes take. Some equipment (such as grenades) or just shooting can destroy cover. On the campaign you decide on research, requitment upgrading your ship and marines and which battles to do. The battles give different resources. I enjoy this game. I really enjoy the sync kills your knights do when they kill someone in a "critical damage" hit. If you are a warhammer fan you will certainly enjoy this. If you are new to the series, there is an in game "wiki" the explains the terminology used in the game. (Tip for beginners. When facing cultists, engage them in melee. They will use cover shoot you and throw grenades. You want to wipe them out quickly as possible or they will whittle away your knights health. Your knights are much better in melee and gain buffs by killing their foes.)
