_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting game, some good, some bad.The good parts: Theme: Being a casual Warhammer fan, this feels right. The flavor is good, space marines, inquisitors, chaos, all that jazz.Sound/Music: Fine. Nothing spectacular, but nothing detrimental.Graphics: Fine. Nothing to blow you away, but it definately gets the job done. Gameplay: Its split in two.Tactical combat; deceptively deep. It seems like a very simple version of Xcom at first look. Not so. There is way more depth to this, with critical hits playing a role, chains of Action point boosts, Buffs, Armor piercing, armor breaking, stunning, aoe attacks, knockback, executions...there are a LOT of possibilities here, and the game is rather difficult. You better make use of your options or you will get punished.The bad:"World Map" traversal; the second part of the gameplay. Building your spaceship is cool. The details around it, are not. There is some dialogue to be found, mostly for lore it seems, and you get to choose what to build/research, and when. This is fine, but there are also some story choices to be made. They have STAGGERING consequences, and you have no idea what they are before you choose, and you get zero hints as to what they may be.As an example, you use "Servitors" to build things in your spaceship. Medibays, barracks, engines, shields etc. At some point in the game, 20 hours out or so, I get a story choice. I can support either of my officers in a dialogue choice, or reprimand them both or something like that, the details escape me. I choose what I feel is best from an "RP" standpoint, what I would say as a commander, and suddenly I have 200% increased build speed, and -50% xp gain and -50% research speed. At that point I had zero servitors, so I couldnt build anything. And thats what I was stuck with. I had no idea what I got into before going into the conversation, and afterwards it was too late. The game is cheap when it comes to saving/autosaving. There is also a plague spreading in the system you are in. At timed intervals 3 planets will become "attacked" by plague. At the start you can only do 1, so you have to choose. Thats fine. After a while I had upgraded my engine, could fly faster and hopefully do more missions. But you get afaik ZERO hints as to what planets will be infected, so you cant position your ship to make the most of your upgrades, making them feel like a waste of time and resources. I dont like that at all, the map also becomes bigger, and specific story missions appear that you have to do, with NO hints as to your time-frame or the penalties for not completing them in time. Way to much randomness.I also have to say, that while the tactical action is fun, the variety in missions are very small. After 30 hours played, I've played I think 2 specific story missions, and probably 60 "grindy" protect the planet from the plague missions. Some variety would go a long way I think.As it is, it is a soft recommend. If you crave Xcom like gameplay with a warhammer flavor, definately check it out, but be prepared for some things to ♥♥♥♥ you over completely.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. Everything looked so good, and the story seemed interesting. I was excited to see the mechanics of the game at play in the 40K universe. Sadly this is one of the more frustrating turn based tactical games I have ever played. For some reason the developers of this game thought it was a good idea to omit a few simple but essential elements. Such as the ability to know what the limits of your squads vision are, or any kind of indication as to how much of the fog of war will be revealed when you move your squad around the map. This leads to you being constantly thrust into ambush like engagements. Even when they give you an indication that the enemy is close you can very easily trigger combat prematurely, because of not knowing where the edges of your vision are. During combat if you use Over watch your supposedly elite Spacemarines will step fully out of cover in order to cover the field of fire you setup. Seems like elite super soldiers would have figured out at some point this is a bad idea. When engaged with enemies good luck knowing what sort of range they have on their attacks, because this game gives you zero idea if you are walking into range of your enemies attacks. The simplest solution? A superimposed preview of movement, and ranges for weapons as well as seeing the edges of the squads vision so you know how much of the fog of war you will reveal. The same goes for the enemies. Scroll the mouse over a known enemies position so you can see what their effective range is. The worst part is that they will give you this kind of information if it has to do with AOE attacks like grenades and other explosive elements on the map, but not anything else. Sad to see what could have been an outstanding game hamstrung by poor choices by the developers. I am not sure I will ever pick this game up again. If you don't mind putting up with the aggravation and frustration created by these bad developer choices then play away.

_childDocuments_.review: While there is a lot of fun to be had playing Chaosgate, the game needs to get out of its own way. You are constantly being pushed forward in the story, with very little control over what you actually do. Random events pop up often and almost invariably penalise you for making the "wrong" choice, with no way to understand the consequences of your choices before you make them. I enjoy the action in the game, and it looks pretty good, but I've also taken to keeping a book next to my computer to read while the enemy takes their turn. In my first play through (failed the campaign) I finished the first half of Rabbit Redux by John Updike doing this. I hope that this game is developed into something better than it is because at the moment it is a fun X-Com clone weighed down by punishing and grindy mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable Warhammer 40k game, which falls flat after around 10 hours.The missions are repetitive and there are only three of them: a timed mission, kill seed carriers (enemies), and destroy chaos spreader, and there are  only a handful of gated story missions.Power-up-pogression through research exist, but for an experienced player it's a no-brainer what to pick.Missions reward loot, and depending on the loot, the tactics can be limited. Like in Gears of War Tactics, a mechanic grants action point. For that you have to kill a stunned enemy. Depending on your gear, you outdamage the stun meter.A big "buy it during a deep sale or never" is the lack of mod support. There is a reason why games are played even years after it's release. Once you have beaten the game, the only reason to replay it is on higher difficulty: more bullet-sponge enemies and a lower win-timer, yet still the same.The reason why I have such a high gaming time is, I did other stuff (watching, browsing, etc) while the game was running. I bought it on a deep sale from an other legit seller than steam. I don't regret spending my money, but the money could have been spent better!

_childDocuments_.review: Even if you took away all the trappings of the WH40K universe Chaos Gate would still be an excellent turn based strategy game.I expected an XCOM clone but was pleasantly surprised to discover that the tweaks that Complex Games have made to the formula go a very long way to making the combat feel unique. i.e. the extensive use of environmentals, the general lack of RNG and the aggressive playstyle encouraged without the use of game-ending timers.The sound design is overall quite spectacular. Weapons feel impactful, Bolters sound punchy, Space Marines sound like big stompy Space Marines without coming across as slow and clunky. My only complaint is that some of the enemy dialogue seems a little weak, especially compared to the Space MarinesVisually it's very pretty, it somehow captures that Grim Dark feeling despite having a very saturated colour palette. If anything it makes it feel like tabletop figures come to life. Some of the lighting is particularly impressive and explosions in particular are quite funIf you have any appreciation whatsoever for the grim dankness of the 41st millennium then I wholeheartedly recommend this game to you.If you have no idea what Warhammer is then I'd say this is a good place to start and I'll still recommend this game to you

_childDocuments_.review: I like the gameplay. Customization is nice, the classes feel unique and each have a specific role they fulfill. The game can be cheesed like any other game that allows total freedom of group comp. The basic missions can get repetitive but new enemies appear and get harder as the game progresses. The Story missions stand out and for a AA game the cutscenes are very well done and the characters are immersive. The lore seems accurate from what I can tell but I also am still fairly new to the 40k lore universe so if there are minor mistakes I didn't catch them. Overall I love the 40k universe and this game scratches that itch for a 40k game where I can customize a space marine and go to town on the forces of chaos. Purge the heretic and hail the Omnisciah. Also one word.... Terminatus. You'll thank me later :)

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy did they make some stupid decisons with this game. This could have been an awesome plowing trough heretics game but its so hard braked with artificial difficulty. You are a Grey knight, your armor is papper and common autoguns can shoot trough them. Meanwhile, your basic chaos counterparts has 3 armour points (AP) meaning they ignore the first 3 dmg done to them, this resets every round. Why could you not have the same?Its a rush against time as there is a warp clock that ticks up every round, and when you use abilites, when it reaches 100 then your enemy gets a buff/boon or you get a debuff.On top of that, you move your guys in turns all the time. The annoying part is, that as soon as an enemy is revealed they get their first turn and move into position, but you dont. This means that the guy you moved last or the guy/guys you didnt even have the time to move can be very far away from the fight.When you take enough damage even if you heal it you get a condition that sticks for a really long time early game, first gives you -3 max HP the other -6, so dont think you can lvl up that grand kill team.I could go on and on. The game looks awesome, music is great, enviorment is great, but the gameplay is trash, a pity... The 40k games really falls ito the wrong hands these days.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could do a neutral review I would, but on balance - it has to be a negative one.Pros:- Devs have listened to the community about Twitch drops and back tracked.- The art style is unique and cool.  Even though it is bright and cartoony - and generally very un-grimdark - it fits well.- Heaps of research, tech, base management, troop management options.- Story is workable.Cons:- ♥♥♥♥♥♥ marketing.  The Twitch drops were an interesting idea and I respect the desire to try something different to build up interest and support - but this was poorly executed.  How do I - a gamer in Australia - watch the Angry Joe live stream to get that unique item?  It wasn't clear how it worked and was needlessly complicated including signing up to websites and linking accounts.  The thing that most people are annoyed about is the dishonesty (although I lean towards a genuine miscommunication) around the fact that they weren't only cosmetic.  This this said though, the Devs have backtracked.- Denuvo.  You harm paying customers while pirates will get a version soon enough with out it.  It is also becoming pretty apparent that it is messing pretty badly with the performance.- Day 1 DLC.  Sorry, but I'm over this ♥♥♥♥ in my games.  It's just greedy at this point.- Performance. Its terrible.  This game is terribly, terribly optimised.- Balance that is breaking immersion.  I understand that 40K games can never be lore accurate, but some random dude, hitting my terminator with an iron bar really, really hard, that injures him for weeks, is just garbage.I would leave this game for now.  There is a good chance that in a little while it will be better.  Xcom is still a far better game, and I had a lot more fun with Mechanicus also.

While the game constantly punishes you either through intervention attacks or resources being pulled, or with warp surges on the ground, I never really felt crippled. Honestly I think you can pretty much fit the entire Grey Knights Codex into this game, and you have a Strike Cruiser! Where are my dreadnoughts and DreadKnights! Where are my Storm Raven strafing runs, why Cant I field a Techmarine and some heavy weapon servitors? Where are the ancients, highly elite with more levels like the pre order castellan? Anyway, I never really had any bugs, the most consistent annoyance was the execution camera going into terrain, and one case where a dreadnought threw one of my paladins off the map and he was gone for the rest of the mission. Also a time where reloading a ground save made my heroic deed disappear, (but it was still active) I just couldn't see it or if i failed it with the other objectives. _childDocuments_.review: These are my first impressions after playing for one evening:This is a fun game, with some small, technical issues. Combat keeps you on your toes as it is not forgiving: not staying in cover can easily get you cut down. Keep that in mind as recovery is slow. Feels a bit like an XCOM mod, but that is not a bad thing as that means it can compare with it favourably.On the tabletop game and in the lore, the Blood Angels are one of my favourite factions. They want to get into melee and kill stuff as bloodily as they can. Do not try to do that here. Cover is important and overwatch is quite powerful! If your Knight is not in cover, the enemy is smart enough to target him and grind him down. Melee is powerful, yes, but should only be applied when tactically sound. Which is something I really like!A small gripe that I have here is not so much with the combat, but with the recovery after combat: Knights take damage easily and take a while to recuperate. In combat, the first time a Knight's wounds reaches 0, he goes down but not out. He will stand back up by himself after 3 turns or you can heal him. That is forgiving, but he will only have half max wounds left for the rest of the battle. The second time he goes down, he actually dies. If a Knight does not die, it will take time after combat to recover. And this is my small gripe here: this takes quite a long time (depending on the severity of the wounds) and speeding up that process is quite deep in the building chain. Luckily, all but the severest injured Knights can be put into combat with a wounds penalty.There are some neat little tricks you can do in combat: stratagems. They are one time use only and are powerful tricks on the battlefield. A nice touch!One other trick you might have to get used to if you played XCOM a lot: Knights have lots of abilities, and almost all of them can be used every turn. But some take action points, others use willpower. You start with an x amount (based on ability upgrades), but can be recovered by killing enemies. But not all enemies, or my game is bugging out. Summoned poxwalkers for example do not give willpower when killed. This regeneration of willpowers makes for a good dynamic where you can keep using powerful abilities, rewarding you for fighting.One of the major technical issues with this game is the sound balancing. One moment you are turning your volume up to hear speech. A second later you hastily turn it down again as other speech or music will start, but at a  much higher volume. Sometimes the ambient music is even louder than the speech volume.The music is good and appropriate, but I feel the voice acting is sometimes lack lustre, and could've used slightly more feeling in it. Sound effects are great too: shots sounds powerful, Knights stomp around, voices change if you put them in Terminator armour, getting shot sounds good.During the tutorial though they really miss the boat with sound and it irritated me a little. The end of it was lacking in appropriate effects. Something implodes, but there is no implosion sound effect. A Knight dies, but the music stays the same as far as I could tell. Emotionally, the whole scene (in terms of sound) did very little to invest me in the moment.The game has a slightly cartoony vibe to it, especially the characters. This is not a bad thing, as the 40k lore is slightly cartoony, and I like the style. But characters do have a small issue with expressiveness: sometimes only the mouth moves as they speak, other times they emote just fine. This just feels like a slight lack of polish.One small design decision here that I disagree with: characters seem to talk to you directly, but you are never shown. In cutscenes, you (as a commander) are missing. There was one where a character walked right up to the spot where I could swear that I was standing, based on how they were talking to me. Complex Games should've added some generic knight as an avatar so you have some presence in those moments.Also, small thing, but the font seems to be not very consistent. It feels sometimes as they use 3 different ones, which feels kinda off.Buildings are actually parts of your ship you must rebuild, there are about 10 of them, and each has upgrades. All of the buildings and upgrades are dependent on how far you have upgraded your power core. The tech tree is fine, nothing special here.There is of course the Shadow Co... I mean Grandmaster Report, every 60 days where you can upgrade mission rewards. During such reports, there is a lot of conversation and at the end you get a choice. You will not know what the outcome is and some of the options are dependent on you having something available. This will give some weight (to the first playthrough) to them as you hope you make the right choice.There are other such events as well, randomly occurring. Even some space combat (though only in text form). These will impact a lot of things, like hull integrity, research speed, gain of equipment etc. A nice touch.Unlike this header would suggest, there are very few bugs. The only one I found so far is this: I restarted a mission through the menu, and my objectives were altered. Where I first had to recover something from 1 of 3 sites, it was now only 1 and my mission specific challenge that I accepted was removed.And this is not really a bug, just inconsistency: the game told me I could only recover said item with a critical hit. But it seems just killing the target was just fine as well: I still got the item.So, all in all I would say this game is fun to play! Even with its minor technical issues, I had fun playing it. The learning curve is not steep (on normal), it just takes some getting used to. Knights are very powerful beings, but still can get taken down by chaff if not careful.

_childDocuments_.review: Any update to the XCOM formula is welcome, and chaos gate has massive quality of life improvements that speed up and streamline the xcomalike gameplay in a significant way. Add to that some epic visuals and a surprisingly excellent use of the warhammer license and you have yourself a downright excellent game. I did not see bugs until the final mission where my save file exploded, but thankfully I had a backup not long before.Many complaints ive seen about the difficulty seem baffling, as even on ruthless difficult I had a knight get critically wounded twice in the entire playthrough. If anything I would say the difficulty is so easy it made the game drag. Again on the ruthless setting my knights would 1 turn kill every single patrol they encountered every time, and once I had a librarian midgame missions would only be 2 or 3 turns long at most as I gated across the map in a nonstop massacre.Perhaps the perceived difficulty is from xcom like tactics, which will result in failure. Grey knights throw themselves at the enemy with unchecked aggression, all out attack is always an option, because the other patrols are so far apart you rarely if ever take a risking diving into the fray.overall, a fun game, with big story missions challenging enough to break up the samey standard missions and some really cool boss fights.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes and No.  Daemonhunters is a great isometric X-Com-style game, but it suffers from a measure of Darkest Dungeon Syndrome, heaped upon a failure to properly represent the characters you are portraying. Daemonhunters has many wonderful systems in place to engage you, including of course its excellent tactical combat, refitting of your cruiser, and research of The Blight plus the beneficent abilities that will help you fight it. It uses an Action point system of very tiny scope i.e. 3 pts. per unit to divide amongst movement, interactions, attacks, and special abilities. The totality adds up to make a very good game. BUT...  ... The game hammers you. The Warp Surge mechanic - a timer that bestows all sorts of negatives upon a player, from plagues to weakenings to reinforcements - is an omnipresent tiring thing that always has you under the gun... rushing from A to B to C. As such, a player does not have much luxury to employ certain stratagems, like luring enemies into an area full of destroyable architecture. You have to bull-charge forward, and the more effectively you do that, the better. Some researches, some cruiser technologies can help. Still though, you never get a break, and the aforementioned bull-rushing is almost  your best option. That aspect plays into the main gripe with Daemonhunters.  You aren't playing Grey Knights. As an appreciator of the lore we are immersed in either from dabbling in tabletop days or from playing the MULTITUDE of Warhammer 40k games out there, many of which are quite good, you understand the place Grey Knights have in the Empire Of Man: Grey Knights are the most potent cloned stock of engineered warriors, the most dedicated, augmented by their super-human psychic abilities. They are the demon-hunting special forces from amongst the special forces of the Space Marines of the entirety of The Imperium. ... in Daemonhunters you are no better than a regular Space Marine with a couple of interesting psyker traits. In 40k lore, Lasguns and Stubbers (conventional ballistic weapons) are at the low end of the tech pole. Plasmas, Meltas and Bolters (gyrojet round weapons) are at the high end. From the very beginning of the game, you are confronted by hopeless human Cultists with primitive Stubbers. You should wipe the floor with them.  These Cultists will out-range you, pin you, lay low your psychic shields, strip your vaunted elite armour, and tear you a new one. While playing you will fear the appearance of run-of-the-mill Chaos units, nevermind anything like a plague priest, a vehicle, or a buffier demon. You play in constant terror and dread of such. Compromises were made to make a (good) challenging game that works. And it works very well. But the compromise always rubs you the wrong lore way: these are trusted Marines who have occasional superior tech and interesting powers, not at all the Grey Knights of 40k lore. And that reality constantly gnaws at you, especially as entirely conventional Chaos enemies pound you into the earth. One who knows more than I about 40k lore put it this way: a single Grey Knight wouldn't be challenged by 3 to 4 Cultists and their Stub-guns... he'd be sweating against 500 Cultists. 500. Daemonhunters always feels off because of that. I played up to point X on Normal. The combination of that lore scope and the unrelentingly brutal treatment of those aforementioned mechanics made me quite decisive about abandoning my Normal Campaign in favour of starting a new Easy one, whatever such a setting may bring. Just not interested in  so much, Darkest Dungeon-style. Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters is still a great game, just not quite what it should have been.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very mixed on this game, if there was a neutral option I'd take it.   The TLDR is that I struggled to learn the games systems, and that combined with a fairly grindy first section of the game has just left me feeling burned out.   I'll be pointing out things that I struggled to understand below so if you do decide to play, you can maybe avoid my mistakes and have a better first experience.Before I go into that though, I want to take a moment and point out some highlights of this game.  This game has better combat than XCom in many ways, with good ability trees, environmental hazards, targeting body parts, and no random misses.  The art style is very colorful, kind of feels like a more Blizzardy version of Warhammer but I dig it.  Animations are satisfying, and the writing is decent.   So again, many redeeming factors, there's a reason this game is mostly positive on Steam.   Long VersionI'm not entirely sure why this game has been so difficult for me to learn because it takes so much inspiration from XCom.  It's possible that I wasn't careful enough in learning this game because of that,  or maybe the UI needs improvement.  Or both, not mutually exclusive.   But I'll list my failure highlights in the early stages of playing the game.First fail on my part.   Missing critical ship repairs.   After the tutorial you go to your ship and the game tells you that the ship is damaged and some systems are offline.   There are three systems are broken, FIX THESE BEFORE YOU DO ANYTHING ELSE.    It doesn't help that I think the list doesn't appear until you go into the Manufactorum, open up ship improvements, and the quest is in the upper left corner while the build options are in the bottom right.   Also the broken systems are red and my brain was like  "Oh I can't do this project yet".  You can do them, and you should.   Don't be like me, you will suffer if you do.   XD   My suggestion to the devs on this, please lock out construction on other systems until these first repairs are done.  Its pretty standard to lock features until first steps are complete to make sure a player understands how a system works, you should probably do that here.    Second, and related to the first, not using prognosticators...  This is one of the three broken systems at game start.   Prognosticators are like satellites in XCom.   They reduce corruption on the planet you place them in the galactic map, and give you more time to reach a planet if a mission pops on it.  This gives you the possibility of eliminating two threats rather than one when a batch of missions appear, which means less corruption and more XP for your marines.   The game does explain some of this to you but only AFTER you fix the augurium.  Again, the game should probably lock the player into fixing the three basic systems before cutting you loose and should really hammer in that prognosticators are a vital part of the game.  For players who are new, make sure you fix the Augurium in the Manufactorum quickly and get those going.  You are going to need them.   Third fail, not understanding the combat system.  This one could very well be on me.  So you get three action points in Daemonhunter for each marine.  You can move or shoot with each.  What's new vs XCom is that you get all your AP BACK when you enter combat and again if you kill all active enemies.   This is extremely important because there's a gauge that fills and debuffs you every few turns, so the more aggressive you play the less debuffs you take.   To the devs I'd recommend making an icon appear above all marines every time this happens.   I don't believe you do currently since there are usually cutscenes that appear over this.Fourth, struggling to learn how the ability trees work.  Mileage may vary but I REALLY struggled at first with the level up screens.  So for new players each class has four ability trees in a compass layout on this level up screen.  Within each path there tend to be blocks of four, first an ability and then three relevant perks.  The problem is that whole compass is blue and seeing what block each ability is attached to takes more work than it should.  It isn't clear at a glance what each tree does, and there's also sword icons all over the thing.  Each tree has a little near it that shows what it is, but it's buried under other details and the uniform color scheme.  Separate the blocks by color and design the trees so it's more clear what everything improves at a glance would be my recommendation here.   These were my biggest learning frustrations.   Maybe I was inattentive but it really feels like I had to work more than I should to understand the game's systems.   And it definitely stole some of my initial enthusiasm.   Now we get to the story pacing.   Without spoilers, all I'll say is there is a mechanic where you extract resources from certain enemies.   This eventually leads to the first big story mission and a really tough boss fight.   This then unlocks a larger galactic map where there's more types of resources to harvest and missions are spread much farther apart.  So my first problem is that it feels necessary to get to fairly high level to have a good chance with the first story mission.    I lost my first attempt with level four and five characters.   I restarted my campaign since i had learned a lot about the game's systems and tried again around level 6 and 7.  I won, but it was not a pushover encounter.   The level cap on your Marines is 9.   So frankly it feels like I had to level excessively.  And this is with missions that all play out fairly similar, and with enemies that require a fairly routine set of strategies to counter..   By the time I reached the story mission I felt kind of bored with the repetition of the missions.And now that the story has expanded I don't feel excitement at the new larger map.  It feels more like I finished a workout and now I have an even longer workout ahead.   And I just... do not feel like continuing.  And it's unusual for me to burn out on a game that I'm fairly invested in.   I'd recommend a more evenly paced experience in the future, with more special missions spread out over the length of the campaign.   I'd like to finish by saying that I'm glad I tried this game, and not opposed to playing it in the future.  I think with improvements to the game's UI and pacing Daemonhunter could be improved, and another entry from these developers could build on this game's successes.   There really isn't anything wrong with the bones of the game other than the scourge of Denuvo.  I'll be looking forward to these developers future work, and I hope we see lots of good things from them in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: + W40k setting+ Xcom-style turn-based combat, but with its own improvements+ atmosphere+ many options for customizing weapons and character development+ challenging campaign- minor technical problems- the side missions are too much the same at timesThe tactical game from the small Complex Games team surprised me. Games from the W40k universe are often weak titles using the strength of the brand, but Chaos Gate is one of the few exceptions. The game is strongly inspired by Xcom, but it goes its own way with its own improvements and the result is very good. The player takes the reins of the Imperial ship Baleful Edict of the Gray Knights Astartes chapter. Instead of returning to the home Titan, the damaged ship is taken under the command of the Inquisition and tasked with investigating the Chaos infection that has broken out in the sector. The basis of the game is tactical combat, where the player takes command of 1-4 marines, who perform story or side missions to reduce the spread of infection. For start, 4 classes are available, each with its own development tree. 4 prestigious classes will be added later. The combat system is based on AP, which are basically 3 per turn and can be used in any order within the turn and characters, and the variety is also enhanced by the possibility of using the environment to eliminate opponents. Requsition points are earned for successfully completed missions with the option of a bonus challenge, which can be used to obtain new recruits, weapons and equipment from the chapter. As a basis for operations, strike cruiser serves as a base, which can be improved in various ways.The game is challenging, of course the most fun is in the form of one save, grandmaster mode, when you need to be very efficient and careful, because it is not a problem for an inexperienced player to fail in the campaign even after dozens of hours. The knights themselves are haed and killing them is not that simple, but injuries are frequent, which subsequently reduce their maximum hp in missions or make their deployment completely impossible. The game also randomly loads events that mostly affect various parameters of the ship or crew and sometimes generates very unpleasant challenges.Enemies and their AI is very straight forward, but not bad. Their counts and types are put in play gradually and story bosses spice it up.Chaos Gate is a very good game that I can only recommend to fans of XCOM and similar tactical games .8,5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Daemonhunters could be described as a game that gets better after you sink ~10 hours to it, which by itself makes it very difficult to recommend. Combine that with some severe or even game breaking bugs, the miserable slog through repetitive missions for the first ~10 hours along with bland combat - i'll be blunt here, this is a pretty tough sell for 45€/$ in its current state.Game suffers from an extremely frontloaded difficulty curve and much like the recent XCOM games, campaign gets easier and easier as you progress further. So what makes the first ~10 hours such a slog? In my opinion this is a combination of few things: - Mission duration in the beginning of the game is far too long due to the Grey Knights being utterly pathetic at level 1-3.- Early research & construction take too long- Leveling total of 8 knights to level ~4 (the level it roughly takes to get your build started) takes too long- Game holds back the access to "advanced" classes for far too long.Once you break past those early stages and progress a little further you arrive at sort of a golden zone where you have decent builds, better gear and enemies start to appear with some more advanced abilities as well. However it does not take long before you start to become more and more powerful, eventually being able to dispatch enemies with ease...Unfortunately at that point I was already really bored of the game due to the lack of mission variety, while there are some story missions and special missions, the regular missions that make up the bulk of your playtime consists of only 2 mission types: Kill seed carriers or kill big plants - no matter if you introduce new enemies, repeating the same two missions over and over and over again is woefully inadequate to keep the player interested throughout such a lengthy campaign.For now I would recommend keeping an eye out on what aspects of the game get worked on in the patches, perhaps in a few months time it will be in a better shape and if not, then at least likely you'll find it sold on a discount if you still wish to try it.

_childDocuments_.review: The difficulty level with this one is all over the damn place; even at normal difficulty the game hits you with mandatory missions where INFINITE waves of enemies keep getting spawned all around you, with enemies that heal and regain armor EVERY TURN, while you spend your limited resources literally tickling them for entire rounds; and once you are finally scraping the bottom of the barrel; here you go spawn 6 more of them on your flanks and rear and just r**e you to infinity.UI also does his best to NOT let you know when you are out of ammo until you are out of position and ready to (not) fire your weapon.To add insult to injury all the enemies have at least DOUBLE the range of your guns making overwatch and careful positioning simply futile, as they simply sit out of your range and wait until you expose yourself, splitting your group and guess what, spawn another enemy squad behind your back.Key game design format of this game is clearly "troll them until they are ready to hit that refund button".

_childDocuments_.review: You know. I've done a lot of testing in this game by now, and I have to say I think it fails pretty hard. It tries to be X-com, but it takes out certain rules, and changes things that were there for a reason.There are less tactics in this game. I'll try to explain a general overview of what is wrong with it.In X-com there is a chance to avoid fire when you are in cover. In this game, all hits are automatic and cover just offers you damage reduction. I'll get to why that is a bad thing in a bit.Enemies tend to completely outnumber you in this game. They are weak compared to you, but I don't think the developers really know what action economy is. If every enemy hits you, they are all guaranteed to do at least some damage. Through no fault of your own, you can end up in situations that screw you over. Why? This game has random events. A patrol you are not aware of somehow sees you through a wall while you are fighting another encounter. Or a warp gate opens up which spawns in enemy the game doesn't really indicate clearly as to when these reinforcements will show up, just that they will at some time. You can quickly get completely overwhelmed by the sheer actions of so many enemies and worse yet, this can even happen when you are fighting far more elite enemies, that actually aren't significantly weaker than you, especially during early game. The game is focused around being defense as far as I can tell, but you are actually rewarded far more, for being almost recklessly offensive and just killing as fast as possible, while spamming heals. While this doesn't make the game impossible to beat, far from it, I feel like the design leaves for far less strategy compared to a game like X-com. This game kind of forces you into a corner, to play a very specific way.There are also other problems. This game doesn't run as well as it should, the graphics are passable, but the faces just look awful, and the game has Denuvo, which I am pretty sure they didn't mention until after release, and is likely causing the slowdowns. I'd probably not have purchased this game at all if I had realized it had Denuvo to begin with as I know for a fact it tends to cause problems. I've experienced it in other games, and had to use cracks on my legal version, to remove Denuvo, just so I could play the game, so don't tell me Denuvo doesn't cause it.All that said, I think this game is a good first attempt. There is a lot here that is quite nice, and I like the customization. The art style isn't really Grimdark, but it's not bad either. I think with a second entry if they change some things around they can have a much better game.Also, is it just me, or is Nurgle like... The enemy in the majority of Warhammer games now days? I am getting really tired of facing the same enemy in every game.(Oh. And the other reason I mentioned the auto hits, and action economy, is because the recovery time of units in this game, is absolutely atrocious. If they were going to do auto hits, they need to really balance that out as it is way easier to get a wounded soldier in this game, than something like X-com.)Edit: If you play on easy difficulty, nothing above is relevant. As I have found so far, the game is laughably easy. It especially helps that you now one shot most enemies, which makes it far easier to manage the enemies action economy. I tested easy just a little, but it felt kind of like X-com 2's zombie like enemies I can't remember. Except without the mechanics that let you keep shooting as long as you one shot them. I actually think that X-com2 mechanic would be quite good in a game like this one, considering Grey Knights would basically walk all over most things I've seen in this game so far. The only real exception being traitor marines. Except... Grey Knight are all Psykers and would still walk all over them.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy turn based tactics despite really, really disliking X-Com, the granddaddy of them all. Daemonhunters had potential, but around the 15-20 hour mark there are some massive difficulty spikes. More importantly, there are far too many enemies placed on the maps and the maps are far too large. You can easily go multiple turns without engaging in combat, then get a squad of space marines wiped out by a handful of cultists and mobs. The game started with a great concept, only to be marred by updates and tweaks to make it more difficult and more of a pain than it's worth to play. Watching the AI take turns and destroy your squad for a solid couple of minutes, only for your turn to last a minute tops, is a waste of time. At no point after the 10 hour mark did the game feel remotely balanced. If the entire game is an uphill battle, it isn't fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The concept is great, the execution needs significant work though. The difficulties are almost nonsensical in how punishing it can be. While games like this do tend to be on the more difficult side, the amount of punishment your characters will receive is almost constant, while the amount of damage they can take feels very minimal, which is odd since they're space marines. They feel like they're as squishy as an Imperial Guardsmen. 100 pox walkers wouldn't touch a space marine, let alone a grey knight, yet if you're not careful in the early stages of the game, you can lose a marine to 1 or 2 pox walkers. The other thing that makes the "difficulty" setting feel like it either wasn't tested or simply doesn't work right is the amount of RNG in a map. The enemy seems to be able to call-in endless reinforcements, and the plague marines seem to be able to just heal whenever they want, even on the "easy" difficulty, the RNG can make the experience a slog to get through. If things just don't go your way, you're better off restarting the mission until you get it right or just abandon it all together. The game balance really feels overwhelming at times, where one wrong mistake means you've basically lost the round.You'll find that your characters are constantly chasing the objective to keep up, and complete the mission before the game spawn too many enemies for even a space marine to defeat. Weapon balances don't make any sense unless it's simply to make the game more difficult and unnecessarily tedious. A trashy cultist auto-rifle of stubber does more damage than a storm-bolter, Plague Marines can just hang out in psychically charged promethium fire and only get a little warm. There are annoying mechanics that allow stationary enemies to just get free, incredibly powerful attacks on your characters with almost no recourse and they're harder to kill than most of the actual enemies. Their range of attack is also probably close to if not double the range of your own characters. The Purgation Marines you can field have a laughably short attack range, making them nearly useless considering how much you have to move characters. The design makes the Grey Knights and Space Marines as a whole feel significantly weaker than the lore, and even other games in the same universe suggest. While I expect X-Com clones to be difficult, it feels like they made this hard in all the wrong ways. It's frustrating. Developers completely ignored lore to make the game more difficult unnecessarily. After the time spent with the game, I can only come to the conclusion that the developers think a Space Marine is just some normal guy with cool looking armor on, because that's what the Knights feel like.It's not a bad game, but it's also a far from good game and not worth the $40.00 price tag. If you're interested in this game, wait for a sale, a very big sale. It would ironically feel like a much more consistent, and less frustrating experience if you simply changed the Grey Knight characters into Imperial Guard, at least then their lack of starting abilities and generally weak feeling characters would make sense. There's not been a great representation of what a Space Marine is in a video game since the 40k Space Marine game released over a decade ago, and I'd love to play another game where a Space Marine feels like an actual space marine. Your low-level prisoner in Warhammer Darktide is going to feel much more powerful than a Grey Knight in this game. I want to like this game, it's just doesn't do itself any favors. The presentation isn't bad, it looks like a 40k game, they look like Grey Knight Space Marines, except at the end of the day the game doesn't play like you're a Grey Knight, or even just a Space Marine. While the game looks the part, at the end of the day it certainly does not play the part of a Space Marine well at all, and to a frustrating degree.

_childDocuments_.review: I have shelves full of 40k minis and hundreds of hours of in the Firaxis XCom games. So this seems like the perfect game for me. Which makes it particularly disappointing that I'm just not having fun. The main problem is that there's basically just one mission to play. Walk across the map while having your resources slowly ground down by swarms of enemies and a constantly ticking timer of hostile passive effects. Kill something at the destination. Repeat a couple times. Sometimes there's a timer. You will play this mission a lot. Often 4-8 instances for each research unlock, and research doesn't do much to change-up the dynamics of the fight. New enemies unlock, but they're all similar Nurgle units with more hit points on top of the same tricks. It just becomes a chore.Other issues:- As best as I can tell, all weapons are unlocked form the start. Makes sense from a lore perspective, but doesn't make for much progression. If you work really hard you can get the same gun with +2 damage on a critical hit. Yay?- New recruits usually come pre-leveled. Which is necessary for them to stay relevant, but the game assigns them skills when you buy them. Even at the start, you're often getting level 2-3 guys with 4-6 skill buys that lock you into a build you may not want, preventing you from customizing your squads in a way that fits your playstyle.- Maps are littered with environment effects that you can use to help even the odds. Which is really fun. Unfortunately, encounters are random and you can't really control where they happen. So you seldom get an opportunity to actually trigger these effects. Plus, once you get beyond basic enemies they don't really do enough damage to be worthwhile anyway.- Every enemy seems to have three action points, just like your squad members. Even basic cultists. Since you're nearly always outnumbered, often by 2-3x, you may have to sit through 30+ elaborately animated actions each turn with nothing to do but wait. - Enemies overwatch far too much. This seems to be a way of balancing out all the actions. Otherwise, the would too easily swamp you with attacks and kill you off. Usually the overwatch with one or more of your marines in the fire cone without bothering to fire one them. This bogs everything down into an uninteresting movement puzzle. - Oh, and enemies often get to act immediately as soon as you trigger them. Not just moving, but buffing or attacking and, of course, going into overwatch. So there's no way to start an encounter with any sort of workable plan.- Overwatch is nearly useless for you, though. The range is shorter than standard weapon range and in a narrow arc for which you can't control the vertical. It's usually blocked by terrain and often difficult to judge where the blockage will occur until you're setup. If an enemy does trigger it, you throw out a few desultory shots and then give up without doing meaningful damage to anything but trash tier enemies. - Enemies are slightly too tough relative to your ability to do damage. For example, I once caught a cultist with a heavy stubber with no cover on easy mode. I shot him with a 4th level purgator armed with a relic psilencer. This was not enough to kill him. Why? Similarly, plague marines all have at least three points of armor regenerating each turn, better than grey knight terminator armor. They will often get more from warp surge effects. Killing each one requires slowly grinding them down over multiple actions.- The net result is like playing in quicksand. The AI gets an almost endless wave of actions, each slowly wittling down your resources, while you only get twelve most turns, which quickly disappear to movement and the need to attack multiple times to kill one basic enemy. Then it's time to wait again while the AI takes its actions. Rinse, repeat. Sorry, that was longer than I intended. I actually think this is a very good game, and clearly a lot of people really enjoy it. There's clearly a lot of skill and care that went into designing the characters and levels. It's just not a game that I can really enjoy, for all the reasons listed above.

_childDocuments_.review: I am very glad to say that I really enjoy this game and I can't stop playing it! Experienced a lot heavy crashes about 5 times out of my 50 hrs play time, specially after starting the mission after I completed assigning my strike force. Fortunately, there were a lot of auto-save functions after each of your selections in-game so that you can just reload your game when it crashes. And also the application always starts-up regardless of the heavy crash and did not corrupt your saved games unlike other games.- Yep I knew that WH40k should be bloody and gritty. I also initially thought that this game seems "way too clean" not enough blood, grit and weathering. - But the game already have all of those details. the graphics shader was just too bright/colorful(?) or something comic-like or overwatch-like. Still way better than League of Legends graphics in my game standards. A dark, gritty, and bloody graphics mod should be made available soon. Personally, I think the graphics fits the board game origins of it.- Yep I knew that it only takes 100 Space Marines to conquer Earth against its United Earth Armies.- Yep I knew that Space Marines are genetically engineered Super Soldiers like Captain America but came equipped with Vacuum sealed Space Powered Suits made out of Ceramite, an armor made out of a combination of Cement and Metal.- Yes, I was frustrated seeing that a regular human soldier with firearms can just kill a space marine, not just a space marine but a Gray Knight, an elite spec-ops army of the Emperor dedicated on fighting the Army of Chaos with magic powers in the shadows.- But I also knew that the lore was very difficult to translate and balance in a game so give the developers a break. - Don't get me wrong it can be done with proper writing, planning, and time or just introduce it as an easy mode in the game.I did not played the WH board games nor do I own the model kits (but I do own some JoyToy articulated and highly detailed Blood Angels Death Company figures). I am a huge fan of Starcraft and ever since I saw the Astartes/Space Marines knowing that they pre-dated Starcraft. Since then I knew that Starcraft and all its races was based on or ripped-off from the Warhammer franchise. But unlike Starcraft, the Warhammer franchise was extremely and painfully mismanaged with very poor business decisions made in the past. By now Warhammer should have been bigger/popular than both Starcraft and Warcraft games that was based out of it. Warhammer should have been bigger than Starship Troopers, Star Wars, and Star Trek. With multiple CGI or live action movie trilogies or movie-verse and various game styles made out of it. Yep, very painfully mismanaged. Originally I came here just to support the WH40k franchise knowing its possibilities and was surprisingly satisfied with the gameplay. Coming from my all-time favorite turn based games like Disciples 2 and Tactics Ogre: Knights of Lodis.But I have these few nitpicks or proposals that the developers can help improve in the game in the near future:1. Do not limit the screen rotation in just 4 corners. It could have been dynamic since this is a beautifully colored and detailed 3D graphics game. A complete camera 360 support should have been made available like the other 3rd person action games.2. The game was extremely detailed and the current Zoom-in limit was still a bit far. The player should be able to zoom-in and see all those beautiful and wonderful character designs and details while in the game map. 3. Yes I am aware of the Character Info screen, but even that it was only limited to the front view. The player should at least be able to rotate the character in that screen.4. More Mouse control support in the settings. The user should be able to rotate the map using the mouse, zoom-in and zoom-out. The accept and decline function currently was a great touch.5. The unit HP HUD was severely underutilized. Other than the selected Unit HP it could also already show the unit Ammo Capacity, Action Points, and Warp/Will Points. thereby allowing the players to clear out some screen clutters and show the complete  beautiful game map and units with less screen clutters. 6. The Character customization screen should have mouse scroll support for an unlocked manual zoom-in and zoom-out. A and D keys should also be supported in rotating the character.Regardless, overall I'm very satisfied with this game. Already looking forward for DLCS like:1. An Ultramarine version or various different Chapters selection.2. Other races defend against Gray Knights invasion or invade a planet fighting Kriegs and etc. A complete reversal of this game.3. A new story or new game exploring the Emperor Origins from the Thunder Warriors, The Hunt for each Primarchs on different galaxy sectors, Horus Heresy, and so much more!

_childDocuments_.review: Big time fan of modern xcom tactical squad games here-There are so many players leaving negative press citing "optimization, difficulty, etc..."I haven't had a single issue, 4 hours into the game. Too many people want to say it's the devs fault that their "3080" can't run a TBS...SMH. I'm running a 2070, at max settings across the board, and this game plays buttery smooth. No frame drops that are even close to what some people are claiming.Further, the difficulty level in the beginning of these types of games is meant to be challenging. Until you've spent hours leveling your team and investing in strategy development, expect a learning curve. Nothing wrong with the UI other than I don't know where to look for the ammo counter. TBF, the game tells you to reload, so you reload. Graphically, some wild commentary about this community aside, it's like looking at animated versions of models in great detail. I'm satisfied with the SFX and audio too. The music is good quality. Voiceovers are par, but really, I don't expect massive perfection from a WH game anymore. I set my standards too high years ago and finally realized that even if the voice acting was brilliant, another aspect of the game might get outshined.Buy it if you're a fan of TBS games. Quit being a follower and listening to reviewers that only want to blast works of love that didn't get that one thing right that they have a bone to pick with. I'm no perfectionist, but I will sink time into a good game and if I really enjoy it, I'll play it again and again. This is one of those good games that you can miss out on because of negative influence. Don't be that guy/gal.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for three hours all I can keep thinking is "I wish I was playing Mechanicus".I really wanted to like this. I love 40k and I love xcom-style turn-based combat. And the idea of playing Grey Knights as fight chaos with customisable marines really ought to be awesome but somehow this game ruins this opportunity.From a gameplay standpoint, the UI is extremely confusing. Between battles, the game doesn't do a great job of explaining the different options. It runs a tutorial mission and then offers XP progression but doesn't explain what the different classes do so you're making decisions without really understanding the consequences. In battles, it's not always clear what uses what Action Points and you're making basic mistakes because it's not obvious that the action will end that character's turn. None of this is helped by terrible graphics. I'm not sure if it's the art style or the way it's implemented but its really difficult to differentiate between your marines and make sense of the battlefield. The camera pans and moves in a non-sensical manner. Regularly I've been in battles where you take a ranged fire action and the camera will pan behind a wall so you can't see anything. But worst of all, you just don't feel like you're playing Grey Knights. These are supposed to be amongst the baddest of badasses in the galaxy. Not just Space Marines, but the toughest, hardest, Space Marines there are. In the intro, you see the Commander go toe-to-toe with Greater Daemon of Khorne. So why is it that a few rounds from a cultist and my guy is down to less then half health? I get that you need to make the game a challenge, but if you substituted the Knights for Imperial Guard it would be more realistic!Everything that Chaos Gate does, Mechanicus does better. Much better: from graphics, gameplay, story and music there really is little point in Chaos Gate unless you really want a game where you get to kill Nurglings.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an excellent XCOM "clone".  I put "clone" in quotations because while superficially this looks almost identical to XCOM 2, the changes in mechanics make this an enjoyably different game.  Daemonhunters' tactical combat is determinate and extremely deadly.  There is no missing 90% shots, no making 20% Hail Mary's.  Your Grey Knights either win the day with your tactical brilliance or fall to a hail of stubber fire from flanking cultists.  The battle against Nurgle's forces is not an easy one and the penalties for making mistakes in combat are severe.  Thankfully, the battlefield is strewn with interactable objects that can do massive damage to enemy formations.  All of the other regular XCOM trappings (research, gear, base building of a sort) are also here to help in the fight against the Bloom.  Overall, this is a great refresh of the XCOM formula that fully embraces the 40k theming.  I have almost zero complaints.  I have not run into many performance issues, only one map with inexplicably low fps so far.  No crashes.  The UI could use some improvements but it's serviceable.  Why do I need to press the I button to bring up crit chance (the only RNG mechanic) and damage explanations?  Give me a checkbox to always have it on.  Why can I only see my ammo when I have a gun selected?  It's quite difficult to tell when an enemy is behind full cover or half cover until you go to shoot them.  The UI screams "made for console".  The soldier recovery time is quite high but I found that an early barracks upgrade allows you have enough Knights to properly cycle out wounded Astartes.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game I have very mixed feelings with a 3/5 experience even as an old Ordo Malleus enjoyer back in the 4th ed.If you want XCOM in 40k, go for it.On the other hand the game is decent in most aspects, if you can get past the few first painful hours and the absolutely cringe and forced tutorial that "teaches" you all the self-evident things, but none of the important and non-obvious things.The game mechanics are basically cloned from modern XCOMs, both the good and the flaws, including the silly pod system that actively prevents any depth the missions could have. Throw painfully scripted story missions on top of everything to break the flow of an ok fight you finally got for a change and yeah, that's the experience most of the time. On the flipside Chaos Gate throws some of its own ideas and twist to the mix successfully. Campaign (ship and your knights) is nicely done requiring a modicum of strategic thinking and random events throw some needed curveballs every now and then.However, my main issue throughout the whole game was the alleged difficulty - there was none. I regret playing my blind run on ruthless instead of legendary difficulty, as soon after the early game in all the missions I was consistently wiping out enemy encounters, including  even some bosses, in a single turn or two tops, which turned the game into a slog of trivial missions you just had to wade through. Repeatedly. Over and over again. Just to wait for the new story mission to be unlocked.

_childDocuments_.review: At this point I think I've played almost every 40k game, at least since 2000, and imo this is one of the best ones. Get it on sale though. If you're a 40k fan I think this is a must play, especially if your a fan of space marines or the grey knights. The main gameplay loop during missions is something similar to X-Com, but with less chance. But combat is punishing, and you'll need to learn positioning for encounters. But its rewarding, there is a lot of loot to collect to customize your knights, and their progression is fairly deep. It can take a little while to get access to some of the higher level mechanics and units, but its worth the wait. The narrative is fairly up-front which is nice, with quite a number of 1-2 minute cutscene's, especially in the first 5-6 hours. Then there's smaller narrative moments that you can interact with at your convenience on your ship, adding to ships immersion. I also really like the way they handled their voice acting, seems like a logistics choice but it insured every piece of text has at least some of it voice acted. The story isn't anything overly compelling, but for fans it has a lot of cool moments and characters I was stoked to see. The random events slot in really well with the campaign, adding to my role-playing experience and giving you the opportunity to further personalize your units with event rewards. I'm not a fan of the DLC's integration, when those missions start they are just integrate into the normal campaign, and probably WAY to early for the enemies you come up against. And a few bad defeats in a campaign early on can really derail the whole playthrough.I'm a bit bias as a 40k fan, a fan of the Grey Knights, and a fan of XCom. But, I think this game is the closest anything has come to letting you feel like you're controlling your own chapter of space marines. Also, the maps are pretty awesome. I didn't think they'd be this varied.EDIT: I've since completed the campaign and all my original feelings remain, except I'd give a few extra points to the story because near the end it really picks up again with a lot cutscenes and cool moments and characters appearings. My only gripe to add is that after completing the main story the game is done, with no open ended mode or anything to continue playing any mission you may have left unfininished (I had a few Mechanicus quests still to do). So take your time unless your going for the 500 day achievement. Fingers crossed we get a sequel

_childDocuments_.review: This is X-COM made in the Warhammer 40K universe with a few exceptions:-More Buggy-Smaller variety of enemies-Confusing layout for customizing squad members-DLC that isn't worth the $Given all of this, I have to say that this game is incredibly fun. I played on the hardest difficulty and it is very, very unforgiving. I had to walk away from this game several times from frustration/misunderstanding. Having 5 available save slots per campaign is nice to be able to return to an earlier point if necessary.The most incredible part of this game is the lore, VA, and character customization - an astounding amount of work went into casting, voicing, producing, and referencing the main Warhammer characters as well as the squadmates. The wonderfully produced cut-scenes made for an excellent intermediary between moments of rage and fury.Ultimately, I would highly recommend this game if you 1) Enjoy X-COM style games, and 2) Enjoy the Warhammer 40K universe. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed the game, completed the campaign on merciful (easy mode) snowballed through second half (DLC's probably help). Just some ideas for the game I had.New battle types, at the moment it's generally move your guys through a map and kill x, y, z. That mission with the imperial guard where you have to protect the four bases, more of that please, here's some ideas.Hold The Line - Hold a trench and repel waves of enemies.Under Siege - Hold a single fortification and repel waves of enemies.Dual Battles - The final battle was epic, where one squads action impacted the others, made it feel like a war, more variations of this would be great.(These missions can all include Imperial Guard too)Speaking of Imperial Guard, I would love if in a future DLC, this was the unit you could recruit. _childDocuments_.review: Warhammer meets Xcom with one of coolest groups of space marines against some of the fiercest foes humanity has. If that doesn't sell you, nothing will. Tactical combat is great, environmental hazards work well and are incredibly cinematic, and with the fixes to recovery time and likelihood to get wounded the game is better than ever. I would rate it a solid 8.5 out of the 10. It does what it sets out to do well, the story is good, and the moment to moment gameplay is great. My only real gripe is with enemy and mission variety. It gets somewhat stale fighting the same servants of Nurgle repeatedly (which makes sense story wise) and just going around collecting seeds mission by mission. There are hints at larger activity happening around you (such as mentioning a group of ultramarines is currently fighting off an Orc invasion on one planet) but because the Grey Knights are a "secret" faction they never interact with anything outside of demon spawn. I hope the devs are extremely successful with this project because over all it plays fantastic. I would love to see this idea expanded more in the future with more variety.

_childDocuments_.review: The first half of this game is great fun, you get most of the good with very little of the bad. The second half is the opposite, just tedious and frustrating. You don't have to deal with the randomness of chance to hit, but nearly everything else is left to rng: items, knights, augments, space events, battle events, warp events. Sometimes you'll lose a knight that you need or really enjoy playing for several missions because the game just randomly took them. I haven't played many turn-based strategy games, so I'm probably not as good as some people, but the game gets much more frustrating, if not more difficult near the end. Every enemy inflicts 2 status effects on every grey knight every turn, so you're constantly unable to even play the game at times. Enemies love to hobble you so you'll be spending half your turns just slowly moving towards an enemy. The game makes you fight the last two bosses in a row without time in between, so if you make any mistakes in that first fight and don't have enough good knights to take the spots of injured knights, then you're screwed for the final fight. The game also strips you of stratagems in the last couple missions, despite spending the entire game collecting resources and spending time researching them. In case that wasn't miserable enough you have to spend the whole last mission protecting one guy who is the only one who can really do anything to the boss, so I hope you have multiple high level apothecaries to babysit this guy, and god forbid you don't have disrupt abilities, because then the boss can kill him the first time he goes down and you fail the mission.

UI could do with some work and refinement.The game needs optimising as there are random chugs and frame rate drops, some say its the drm they use I dont know enough about it say one way or the other.The Good:For the most part they are keeping this lore friendly as far as story is concerned.Not a bad story so far.The aesthetics are good.I hate the Grey Knights as a chapter but they have made them palatable.Overall I would say this is a good effort but needs some finishing touches to call it a finished game. Nothing too great but certainly not awful either I would give a 6.5 - 7/10 if they cleaned things up a little.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like Imperial Guard Simulator, except you're cosplaying as Grey Knights.Did you know regular bolters do more damage than storm bolters?Did you know that human cultists are more durable than space marines?Did you know that Chaos Marine armor is far superior to what Grey Knights wear?If you enjoy watching the finest of the Astartes hit a regular human with a force halberd and repeatedly fail to kill him, this is the game for you.It's actually not a terrible tactics game, aside from the clunky UI and slow animations and transitions, but it manages to make the Grey Knights feel grossly incompetent at every turn. Power armored marine took a punch from a one-armed cultist? Wounded for thirty days. Cultist crouching behind a box? Essentially invulnerable to ranged attack. Every mission type requires you to push push push relentlessly, so you spend most of your AP trying to catch up to enemies who spawn in by the half dozen, then fall back into cover to shoot you to pieces. Because yes, human cultists are better marksmen than Grey Knights, their rusty stubbers outranging even your purgators.Hence Imperial Guard simulator. Were I running a dozen lasgun monkeys, I'd understand how digging gribbly cultists out of their cover could be a rough fight. Instead, I'm watching terminators get punched and take damage.The ideas in it are interesting, but this is a game where their only ideas for challenges are to put a timer on every mission and reward you for bringing fewer soldiers. As a result, every fight plays out the same: rush forwards at full speed, because the enemy gets more actions than you and is almost guaranteed to use several of them to fall back, drawing out every fight so the bloom can spawn in more of them or buff them to insane levels. The devs response to this was to nerf the mobile classes.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially gave it a negative review because the early game is fairly awful and personally I still find the amount of negative events to be overdone, but mid game it dramatically improves. Early game is just a little bit off and lacks hook, GK feel extremely weak and the enemy has double the amount of toys you have at your disposal. You pretty much just slowly move towards enemy formations that outrange and outgun you, avoiding overwatch, and hope you don't get plague or shot once with a stub gun which will put your GK in the hospital for 30+ days. It's not exactly challenging or engaging, it's mostly just tedious. And this is on any difficulty, so it will be a turn-off for quite a few people. But there's a bit of a difficulty cliff then precipice as it becomes dramatically easier once you pass the early game, for better or worse, but I found it a lot more rewarding than limply throwing grenades and seeing my stormbolters have half the stopping power of a lasgun. If this were a game where you played the IG or even inquisition pawns akin to Darktide, I think the ludonarrative dissonance would bothered me less. However by the time you start getting access to advanced classes and get your GK to roughly rank 5, it picks up significantly and feels like a genuinely well done tactical experience where you get to play some genuine-article GK, though it's a bit easy depending on your choices. There's a lot of options for how to approach missions and loadouts and tweaking of your GK into unique units, and every class, except apothecary which is mostly useless after the early game, feels like it has its own playstyle and use. Bosses are fun, but by the time you fight them you can pretty much mow them down if you build correctly. The meta-strategizing of directing your ship and upgrade paths is fun, but frankly, almost every random event on the starmap is negative, which gets a little old. They removed shot chance and replaced it with a wheel of misfortune on the map. I didn't like it, but someone more masochistic might.

_childDocuments_.review: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters isn't perfect but it's fun and has a ton of heart and atmosphere.  It can get aggravating to wait for the computer to make all of its moves, most notably at the end of the game when it has 20-25 units on the board, tactical play at that point can become tedious and repetitive. But overall the game is engaging, immersive and, as I mentioned above, fun.  If you're a fan of the X-Com reboots and Warhammer 40K in general than this game is for you.  The art direction is great, the lore is on point and the campaign is interesting and full of twists and turns that do the writers a lot of credit.  I should mention that the designers opted out of the frustrating RNG combat model used in X-Com.  Every action's outcome is predetermined and you can see what that outcome will be before selecting the action you want, no more missing at point blank range, hallelujah.  The game has a lot of re-playability and I can see myself playing through it a second time.  A solid 8 out of 10, have fun, stay alert and keep your boltgun handy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good. There's some folks who are very loudly complaining about things that do not matter, or would not make a good game. A very common complaint is that your soldiers -- Grey Knights -- get wounded by low-level enemies. That's because this is a game first, and Warhammer 40k second. It wouldn't be a good strategy game if you just plowed through enemies wholesale with no consequences whatsoever.So, as a strategy game rather than a pubstomp power fantasy, it's a good game. The abilities available to the player are varied and mostly very useful. The enemies also bring to the table a pretty varied collection of abilities, each of which requires some special thought. Chaos Space Marines aren't very dangerous if you're in cover, but heavy stubbers can destroy your cover. If you plan out engagements and set up properly, you'll be able to handle what the game throws at you with the tools you get. I'm playing on the "hard" setting and am doing just fine. Its not without its issues, of course. There's still some bugs yet to be fixed, and they're frustrating when they come by. There was one bug that made the game unplayable for myself and many others, but it got fixed one day after it was introduced (patch 2 to patch 3). I don't particularly enjoy the game's events, as they're often very feel-bad and give you two or three options that all, seemingly at least, have bad results for you. It'd be nice if events more often felt like a positive occurrence, or at least a tradeoff of one resource for another. I'd also like a greater variety in random missions, there's only three-four varieties on random missions. The map variety, at least, is pretty large. Of course, more maps would always be better, especially as these are specifically designed maps and are not procedurally generated.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game and assuming the developers wake up it will be a great one.Pros:- The game has great 40k lore and polish.- XCOM style gameplay with the knights works well- A fair bit of variety in locations- Well written story- The metagame of the strategic layer with the ship adds another layer of needed depth and variety- Graphics are well styled and fit the 40k universeCons:- Its unity so the performance is trash - to be expected and moving on.- Supposedly there is time limit on the campaign length - this is a universally bad idea.  Why the developers would think they are the exception is beyond me.  Remove that crap or provide a option to (FYI - your "vision" doesn't outweigh my game play style when I drop 40+ bucks)- There needs to be more variety in the enemies honestly.  It could be worse but it could be a lot better.- I think the squad size is too low for deployment - if modeling on XCOM we need to look at 6 member squads.- Some TLC needs to be given to the abilities you pick when leveling knights.  Many of the options seem rather redundant.  XCOM options had more meaningful oomf to them.- There needs to be a way to skip action animations because after the 500th time your no longer needing to see the run animation in full glory every time.- I think wargear needs to be possible drops from combat vs just mission rewards.  Not a ton of Dawn of War 2 level drops but I think some randomness added from combat would be a boon to the slow grind of acquiring wargear.- The Twitch fiasco with their gear and unlocks at launch is absurd.  Release the game you built (including the skins and crap) to be above board.  Build good DLC and charge for it.- Lack of modding support.  Seriously - it's 2022 so you need to support modding which doesn't mean releasing a full mod SDK.  It means making the game configurable via JSON, XML, etc the way you can with XCOM which on it's own opens a lot of doors to the modding community.If the game adds modding support, fixes the issues above and releases some decent DLC to add more meat on the bones I think this title will set a high bar for XCOM like and 40k titles.UPDATE:After finishing the campaign I still recommend the game but not quite as easily.  The lack of variety issue and more importantly, lack of meta game depth really made the last quarter of the game drag.  If you compare to XCOM then you have this much deeper metagame with deeper research, construction and special projects that keep you interested even after your troops have developed to a high level.  Chaos Gate just didn't flesh it out to the same degree and it hurts the model.Maybe they left it out to give it broader appeal (because of that foolish notion people buying strategy games struggle with depth or complexity) or it's left out due to DLC plans.  Not sure but right now im not sure I would replay the game in it's current state.  I don't regret buying it and playing it through but it needs some more TLC to seriously be compared to the XCOM series.
