_childDocuments_.review: The Main Game of Chaos Gate: Daemonhunters is excellent. It is unfortunate that I cannot put it into as elaborate of a review as my negativity towards the Duty Eternal DLC, because this game deserves the praise it gets.Chaos Gate takes the Xcom formula of turn- and squadbased strategy and refines it in my opinion. Getting all your action points back before hitting a pod of enemies is a much needed change that even Xcom2 would benefit from, because it speeds up gameplay. Melee combat is integral and works. Executions are a fantastic way to encourage players to leave cover and get in there. What is there more to say than free turns? The Story is overall very good. We get a believable narrative set in the 40k universe, albeit without sufficient introductions to catch newcomers completely unfamiliar to the setting. All the original characters created for this game are fantastic, and while the characterizations canon 40k characters isn't on point, the overall narrative suceeds in telling a fantastic story about the Grey Knights and the Death Guard. On a technical level, the game looks fantastic and is probably the closest a video game ever got to depicting a 40k miniature as a 3D model. The visuals are less focused on depicting 40k artwork (like Dawn of War 2) or realism (Darktide). Chaos Gate chose to look exactly like the miniatures on the table and that pays off for me. My last point of praise has to be the free downloadable content. Even without purchasing a single DLC, Chaos Gate is quite frequently updated with new features, enemies and even missions. Each of these new additions shake up the play experience and come free from any paid DLC. This effort is NOTHING short of absolutely commendable. And if you hate the Meltagun Plague Marines as much as I do, you can disable the extra enemies in the main menu before starting a new campaign. Buy this game. Unlike the DLC, I have nothing bad to say about it. But I wish it had mod support.

_childDocuments_.review: I get that the appeal of Warhammer to some people is the purposefully obtuse terminology - er, role playing. That's cool. However, at some point, this is a video game that presumably someone wanted people to play, which in corporate-ese is measured by "sales." There is a loving skillcraft evident through much of the game, that is wholesale ruined by two huge, painful, bleeding spikes of brutality that should never, ever, ever be apologized for in a game:(1) There's no parenthetical to explain what a thing actually is, or provide some loose analogy to draw new audience in. This sin breaks into full on bad UX design when looking at the level up screens for the Knights. What. Does. This. Level. Up. Do.(2) By way of example for this point, let's talk about the bonus mission challenge I took on voluntarily, "Don't use a frag grenade." Interestingly, I couldn't _take_ grenades and fail the requirement, I had to unequip all grenades. Fair enough, I guess? It takes 20+ clicks to swap out grenades for other gear _on a team of 4_. 20! I'm all for Warhammer is about "attention to detail" and getting really INTO customizing your units, but it is straight up F- design that it takes so much navigation to perform such a basic task.If you really want to play a game that disrespects your time, the actual "my Space Marines move around on a cool, reactive tactical map" part is great, 10/10, awesome. It's just that every. other. part. of. the. application. fails. to. be. a. game.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to “screw you gate”, the warhammer 40K game where you will get rewarded with punishment and annoyance on top game difficulty. The game itself tries to be a X-COM rip off with not even a close match to the delightful work that the X-COM remaster had.  While X-COM has a fast-paced campaign where mistakes can be really punishing, this game skips all that and even if you make good decisions and you manage to keep everything straight for some time, it will still kick your nuts, because screw you.  The game fancies an artificially created difficulty with the “ warp surge” mechanic, which can basically hinder you every few turns, or buff the enemy every few turns, this is on top of the fact that all enemies usually have much more range than you, they are also  more than you, and practically all enemies have one or more special skills (which can combo with the mentioned buffs or debuffs) The game campaign also aims to bother you at every step, for example: Are you doing well? Have you stocked hard earned samples that you pretend to convert into much needed upgrades for your equipment? Well, what about we take half of those from your hands because of no bloody reason? That’s nice of you, grand master. At least the storytelling for campaign is not bad, plus this is a Warhammer 40k game. To make a general balance of the game, I would say:  Cons: Learning curve is steep and punishing, get ready to start over a couple of campaignsCombat feels a penance because of the horrible design of the mechanics, especially the warp surges. It feels like as if they could not get to balance the game and as it felt “too easy” they artificially added the Warp surges to make it artificially harder. Campaign would be ok if all the events were not just to screw you, some of them REALLY HARD You need to mostly “live off the land” because better gear can be only obtained based on the planet you make the missions, and the missions trigger randomly, so you may not be able to make a truly polished build for your characters I think they saw how bad this was and changed it when introducing the assassins and the dreadnought, but that is too late for the main body of the game There is a game mechanic to “enhance” your characters, but requires them to be mortally wounded, which makes them unavailable for a very long time. At the start of the game, you don’t have many characters and they heal really slow, causing that if you get them some mortally wounded, you might find yourself in a situation where you can’t complete missions  PROS:  It is a Warhammer 40 K game with a very good ambience, they really got the lore right The story is interesting, and it is well told The boss fights are fun, quite fun, to be honest To wrap things up, if you are not into BSDM, just try to avoid the game because it mostly feels like a torture. If you decide to get the game, absolutely not worth to buy at full price, wait for discounts.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all a solid tactics game that could've maybe been more challenging. And some subjective art style gripes on top.Gameplay-wise i think it takes some inspiration in its tactics rules from recent Gears Tactics: you have 3 actions per character, cover, hero progression and loot. On top of it the game goes into a much better direction (in my opinion) by ditching hit chances completely (yay!), which makes ironman playthroughs much more enjoyable. Where i think it falls short is difficulty. The game is just too easy when you figure out its rules properly. And i think the major problem lies with basically no consequences for getting half your squad nearly killed during the mission. You can still deploy a wounded character with an HP penalty, which is totally fine most of the time. Turning that into full downtime for the character would have made the game much more challenging, forced you to invest into more replacement squads, etc.The main gripe i have with the game is art style though. It is consistent and well done, but it's too cartoon-y for a 40k game for my taste. It looks more like 40k for your 8-year old. I never got used to it and it hurts immersion in my opinion. Another thing that hurts immersion is how the hell can a random cultist dude with a rusty autogun punch through power armor and even freaking terminator armor. That's just silly.

_childDocuments_.review: A satisfying XCOM clone that manages to not have some of the more annoying traits of such games.Gameplay is pretty systematic with a 2 turn system, namely you and the enemy. You move your pieces then the enemy does etc etc...There are a handful of different classes but the only 3 that truly matter to you are Apothecary (medic), Purgarator (heavy ranged) and then everything else (hammer and bolter with varying flare)The melee classes all feel rather satisfying, if you play your equipment and abilities out correctly you can create a execution machine that grants additional actions every time he attacks it.On that note the game has a Stun system for the enemy units, after a number of hits most units will stagger and be open a variety of debuffs or even outright killed. Its a important tactic for some boss fights and if you string it right you can annilate entire waves of enemies in one turn.Sound and visuals are fantastic. There is a number of cosmetic choices one can make to give each knight a sort of unique look to them though this seems to be a tad buggy with the unique units (Chaplin and Librarian) but its not really noticeable outside the actual customization screen.Sounds are crisp, clear and nasty. You fight forces of nurgle throughout this and he is VERY gross and with units that sometimes sound like a backed up toilet in a crap factory you get to almost feel the nasty.Explosions and gunfire have a powerful punch to them and the loud foot falls of your knights (and even enemy marines) never gets old.The badCutscenes feel almost last gen, despite being pre-rendered models move extremely stilted reminding me often of animatronics rather than people, though thats the only real complaint there.Sometimes the amount of enemy units moving even with the fast mode on can seem to DRAG ON, but short of a button to outright skip their animations altogther theres not a easy way around that.There are a variety of random circumstances that can occur during travel around the systems and some of these can be good but most of them you either break even or just take a penalty after doing it with the rewards rarely outweighing the costs. Othertimes the game punishes you for something you didn't know it could do so save regularly after each mission and do any customizing or upgrading before you travel to that next planet cause you never know when the Grand Master is going to decide you have too much stuff and need to get rid of some of it (yes this happened, yes it was frustating and no i didn't save beforehand shame on me.)There is also a ticking clock element to the entire game where worlds can get progressively harder and harder each one reaching a breaking point and if you don't intervene to stop it after a number of times its just game over. Story wise this makes total sense but gameplay wise...well no one likes time pressure. Despite that there ARE steps you can take to stop the ticking clock or at least slow it down so its more a nitpick than a actual issue.TLDR: Do you like XCOM but hate missing shots at 95% chance to hit? then here play this.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is the best warhammer 40K game that has been made. It has been likened to X-com in 40K and at first this seems to be all that it is, but if you dig a bit deeper you do see that it is it's own game. Additionally, it captures the feel of the 40K universe. e.g. the dogmatically religious grey knights vs the "bordering on heresy" free thinking inquisition. Even the ship design and the feel of travelling through the warp with it's warp storms is great to experience. There are some rough spots where powers or quests or ship upgrades are unbalanced (I think a few things in particular are unnecessary like how executing enemies gives you a free move), but over all this game was great. I'm thinking about playing it through a second time, which is something I haven't done since battle brothers and darkest dungeon. High praise for me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice Xcom meets 40k type of game with plenty of neat innovations to set it apart, especially regarding the melee combat and the psychic powers you get. The game also has a pretty nice story line with some important characters from the lore of 40k showing up through the campaign. The developers put a lot of time designing and staying faithful to the world of 40k with some exceptions being made for the sake of gameplay regarding the grey knights power scale. The game does have some performance issues, I get some frame drops every now and then when I have a rig better than the recommended one. On a side note I've been seeing people complain about twitch drops weapons and even give a negative review solely based on that when it honestly makes little difference because you quickly get better alternatives through playing the campaign. It's worth mentioning that the game does provide a decent challenge too. Overall I'd give it a 7.5/10 and it's a 8.5/10 when the frame drops eventually get fixed

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: the game has its issues; but, I am having FUN! (I would imagine it is ultimately what one hopes to get from a game.) Would rate the experience 8/10.Longer version: I'll start with the negatives.The wound system is utterly frustrating and at times I cannot figure it out. If your marines finish the mission with less than full health, they get a penalty to their maximum health for future missions until they heal up. But sometimes I do heal them to max before the mission ends and they get wounded anyway, whereas sometimes a marine will finish missing a few points and they'll be just fine. The problem is really bad at the beginning of the game when your roster is limited and upgrades to your ship are slow to come by. Later game it is not so much of a problem. I would understand if you finish the mission with 10% health and doing this kind of mechanic, but finishing with only 20% missing and my marine needs to be in the medbay for 40+ days? Again, I say frustrating.A lot of hit and miss on the aesthetics. The customization tool for your marines itself is pretty cool, but for whatever reason the font of the UI and the font on the marine's armor just throws me for a loop. All the upper tier armors have these weird pauldrons with strange text (why is an Space Marine sporting something inscribed with deamon and unrighteous?) and you can't change them like the base armors; or at least, you don't have as many options and those weird pauldron/greave pieces are always there.Some game mechanics are not explained very clearly. I was super surprised when I was notified of my first Morbus event because it was not clear you do not want your planets to hit level 5 of bloom corruption (you will never be able to hit all planets that have bloomspawn events because your ship is not fast enough, this is especially true early game where resources for upgrades are slow to come by)Lastly (for the bad), it seems a lot of others are mentioning that a whole bunch of items are unlocked via watching streamers. Complex Games and Frontier Foundry, a good portion of your customer base doesn't have copious amounts of free time. If we do, we want to play the game. At the very least, why not unlock that content for those of us who forked over the extra money for the Deluxe Edition? This problem is a little more pertinent to me given the limitations of the customization option's aesthetics.Alright, so why have I given the game a thumbs up?The bread and butter of the game is the combat and this is where everything shines for me. The classes of marines each have their own strengths and abilities that you can upgrade. I really feel the uniqueness of each and every one especially as they gain in levels. You cannot grab every upgrade as your marines have a level cap of 9, so you need to have a clear idea in mind of the role you want each of your knights to fill. There is a lot of value in forming a diverse party with a wide array of abilities; however, you can also laugh maniacally as your four Justicars all juice each other with additional action points and you mass charge a boss with power hammers. Some combos are more effective than others, but nothing is absolutely useless.I usually do not like it when games try to implement environmental mechanics, but Chaos Gate does an INCREDIBLE job. You can topple statues to break through walls and crush your opponents. Lobbing a grenade next to a crate of plasma coils a couple of cultists got to close to is extremely satisfying. Send your enemies tumbling over ledges for those sweet instant kills.There was the miss with the aesthetics; but somehow, while in combat, there is a sort of narrative flow to the movements and looks that makes me feel like I am hearing a story unfold. Kill animations seem a bit comical, but somehow fits the grimdark insanity of fighting Chaos. Landing criticals are extremely fulfilling, and I love that you can inflict unique and specific wounds that hobble the enemy in someway or even straight up execute them rather than just being additional damage.I enjoy the crafting system (when you unlock it). It is simple, but it allows for very significant changes to your weapons that can radically alter your marines' effectiveness, depending on how you specialized them. You can get by with the basic weapons and speccing your marines all the same way, but the game really rewards strategic choices and carefully developed knights.And most important of all: YOU CAN PURGE HERETICS IN THE NAME OF THE EMPEROR!!!Go forth my brethen! Cleanse with fire and sword in his name!

_childDocuments_.review: I have played a bunch of different X-Comalikes and they've all had a bit of a problem hammering their square-shaped game into the X-Com round hole. Chaos Gate doesn't do that. It's changed a bunch of different mechanics to reflect the 40K setting and the feel of handling a group of Space Marines. You command a bunch of ultimate warriors so you don't miss shots, but better positioning does more damage. Your marines are godlike, so while they can die they aren't squishy and have a chance to soldier on even after being knocked down. The universe is insane and uncaring so you can destroy the environment to hurt your enemies, knocking over statues and blowing up crates. The game has really put effort into being its own thing rather than follow X-Com's example verbatim, and it does so extremely well. Combat is tough but fair, fights are quite dynamic and require you to think on your feet (rather than rinse and repeat), your choices impact your progress, and its dripping in 40K tone and lore. The only downside I feel is with gear allocation, where I'm tediously re-kitting every member of my squad before almost every mission with equipment off their wounded comrades or something better I've gotten since I last sent them out. Otherwise, I find this a great experience for turn-based combat fans.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun albeit punishing turn based 40K game. Four Grey Knights versus swarms of minions of the Plague God Nurgle. It is very easy to get overwhelmed if you aren't paying attention or if you get to cocky. You start out relatively weak and you don't feel like you are a superhuman space marine, but you are suppose to be an under strength strike force coming back from a crusade. For those who have played 0.1 hours and said it sucks, you have to play further in then the tutorial. As you progress you gain new abilities for your knights and better gear. Then you start to see the type of game play that lets you kill whole groups of enemies at a time. You also have an incredible level of customization for your knights from the skill trees to their appearance. I loved the characters on board the ship and as the story goes you will talk to them more and more and slowly see their stories unfold. If are on the fence then watch some let's plays, but I don't think you will be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t think I’ve played a game that feels so similar to X-Com, yet plays so differently. Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate – Daemonhunters looks like X-Com and dialup up to 11 with the breach sequences, but absolutely punishes you if you take a wrong approach to combat, and the errors compound quickly. Its base difficulty is fairly high, and with its unintuitive gameplay mechanisms and clunky UI can lead to frequent campaign restarts (or at least going back a few saves). Recommended for Warhammer 40K fans, or those who like tactical turn based combats who don’t mind frequent difficultly spikes.You play the role of a newly elevated Grey Knight commander, leading his decimated ship and forces back to Titan when an Inquisitor intercepts you and “requests” the Grey Knights assistance with stopping a demonic plague (the bloom), from spreading beyond the current subsector that it has been detected in. This is the start of a much larger story, and involves many well-known characters from both the Grey Knights and Death Guard, and what you think could be a major battle turns out to only be the start of a much larger conflict between the two opposing factions.I found the story good, choices you make affect gameplay and squad readiness significantly, it doesn’t go against any of the settings established lore and having to manage relationships between the main characters on the ship (who are often at ends with each other) while constantly fighting running battles, random events and reinforcing you current squads gives the feeling of always being 2 steps behind the enemy and severely under resourced. The 8 troop types you can pick all have abilities that align to the tabletop game, and give you fairly free reign in how to develop your squads. Losing experienced squad members can be devastating (at the time), but at least you don’t lose their equipment and the game does have mechanisms to get you up on your feet quickly if you invest in the right technologies. If you are fortunate enough to have the right resources on hand, you can exterminate planets, which is very much in line with what the grey knights and inquisition would do.Gameplay is similar in most regards to X-COM titles, though differs enough that you can easily set your campaign behind if you play it like X-COM. There are a few instant game over conditions, which requires careful management and progression of resources and research. You can’t always avoid the events that cause additional damage to your ship, and need to keep a handy stock of servitors (resources used to upgrade rooms), and possibly planet destroying missiles if you don’t want to do the Morbus mission that seem to constantly appear. Failing a mission isn’t a game over, though the squad will be in recovery for an abnormally long time, and it can lead to the death of a marine, and is more likely to happen on a Morbus mission (where enemies are constantly reinforced) or during a bossfights where there are instant death pits and you have to choose between mobility and firepower. The actual missions are where the largest departure from X-Com is felt. You have free reign to pick any 4 squad members before deploying, including their equipment and weapons. Gameplay has you generally performing 1 of a few mission types (these do get repetitive quickly, even if the terrain and layout constantly changes), which either involve killing 1 large well protected target, killing 3 wandering targets then surviving for a few rounds, or defending priority targets from multiple waves of enemies. Increasing levels of corruption increases the resistance found in stages, the available buffs enemies will have, and you are punished every few rounds by a debuff that hits your team or a spawn of additional enemies for you to fight, which is a kick in the pants as the games already difficult enough without handicapping you more.The game doesn’t seem to know if you it wants you to play cautiously or hard and fast with your Grey Knights, punishing you every few turns, but also really wanting you to hug cover and avoid taking any damage all at (or at least only taking damage against armour that regenerates every turn). Enemy patrol usually consist of between 1 to 6 enemies, and they all activate together. You generally want to be stunning enemies to unlock a execute move (which then gives the entire squad another turn), or if killing the patrol isn’t an option using precision attacks to perform critical hits (which then allows you to remove an attack or inflict a debuff on the enemy). It’s another kick in the pants that enemies regenerate from these easily enough, undoing your planning. Overwatch takes you out of cover, making it practically useless (unless you are only left with enemies who will melee you), and the units you really want to overwatch with, can’t (Purifiers). On the system map, you can control the routes to each planet to take on bloom missions. Each mission advises you of what your rewards will be (either in weapons, armour, new recruits, resources or requisition), as well as the mission type and it’s a fine balancing act between going for the mission that has the correct rewards vs what you can reach before the missions expire (the planets corruption increases). You can also purchase ship upgrades, research abilities (that either help in missions or help further the story), and upgrade and reequip your recruits and equipment. This is also where you will death with Death Guard fleet missions, random events, and receive your regular dressing down from your grand-master. Most of these events generally have a negative impact, which can start taking its toll on your campaign, but on a positive note it does fell like there are hundreds of these and they don’t seem to repeat (even if they are random).The game does a great job in animating the corruption of Nurgle across the stages, with increasing corruption warping each stage more. Enemies look great (though each enemy type is exactly the same), and battle damage is shown against the enemies. The execute (instant kill) moves are very cool, and the different bosses are varied, have vastly different attack patterns and offer a good challenge. Each Grey Knight is customisable, giving you a decent range of options to edit. Stage design is good (even if the missions are repeated frequently, and offer plenty of tactical choices). The animation of enemies and units busting through the environment is great, and the environment is mostly destructible (cover can become very rare in prolonged firefights).This is a nightmare to play on normal, you would have to be masochist to want to play this in the hardest settings. You require all the DLC, and need to play multiple playthroughs.For more reviews please visit

_childDocuments_.review: Chaos Gate is a must play for anyone who is a fan of turn-based, tactical combat. The character builds, the item customisations and the synergy between classes makes Chaos Gate and absolute gem to play. I love the story and the setting too. I've played a few other Warhammer 40k games, but have never considered myself a fan of the Warhammer universe until this game. The Grey Knights are such bad asses and a great introduction to the 40k universe. Plus the science fiction / body horror setting and story appeals to me a lot. The Grey Knights are fighting some of the coolest looking demons and monstrosities I've seen in recent games. All animated and brought to life with a lot of great details.You can read about whatever flaws the game might have in other reviews, because honestly, I'm having such a blast with the game that nothing is ruining it for me. If I really had to pick something it's that some missions can get repetitive, but I enjoy my teams and trying out different compositions so much, that I just use these missions as a chance to try different strategies.Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters is a great game that demands your attention and planning. And it's well worth the investment.Edit: Finished the game and am rushing into my 2nd play through with the DLC on. Also, reading some of the negative reviews is crazy, because a lot of the stuff they complain about is what I love about the game. _childDocuments_.review: First mission forces you to make every single move exactly as they tell you to.  Like, literally everything. _childDocuments_.review: I will start by saying this game is brutal. I love the 40k universe and a tactical strategy game is a perfect fit. Combat reminds me of Gears Tactics, while base management is closer to X-COM. I reached 10 hours into my first attempt and I'm in a position that I don't believe is recoverable. As I said, this game is brutal.Research and construction takes a long time. I'm talking 28-48 days. Injured units you've invested in and leveled up can take over 30 days to fully recover from injuries. In the beginning your ship won't be fast enough to reach most missions and so planets become even more corrupted when you don't complete them, making the following missions on that planet that much harder.The battles take a long time. I'd say I average an hour or so per battle. They can be stressful and frustrating due to how hard they are. Often times they feel unfair. One thing I really don't like is that after each turn the corruption level rises. When it reaches 100%, an event such as extra powerful groups of enemies warp in to join the battle, enemies gain a buff, or your marines gain a debuff. After that occurs, the meter starts to fill again and doesn't stop until the mission ends.  The corruption meter is my least favourite part of the game. I hate timers in games. I don't want to be rushed through. I want to enjoy the game at my own pace. In a challenging game such as this, each turn needs to be weighed carefully. The meter forces you to constantly move forward and make reckless decisions because the longer the battle lasts, the harder it gets. You will likely fail any mission that you allow the meter to fill three times or so.Though I do recommend this game for strategy fans and Warhammer 40k fans, keep in mind that it's unforgiving, you're facing a timer, and failure is quite likely. You can spend 10 hours like myself and realize you have to start the game all over again because you can't recover from your loses, nor deal with the challenges ahead. They have since added an easier difficulty, but I haven't tried it. I'm sure it will help, but I also enjoy the challenge and trial and error for the sense of accomplishment, despite my frustrations.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to recommend this game, I've tried very hard to like it and in many ways it has a lot going for it:+ The audio is great, both effects and music.+ Character design is generally good,if slightly too cartoonish for my taste. + The combat is weighty and satisfying. + The decision to remove chance to hit RNG is great. Sadly, I can't recommend the game, and wish I could get my 80+ hours and money back, for the following reasons:- RNG has been removed from chance to hit and instead injected into every other mechanic in the game, resulting in frequently, brutally unfair encounters and enemy spawns that take it from satisfyingly challenging to a pointless waste of time.- Optimisation is non-existent in this game. It runs poorly while looking mediocre.- Environments are very similar and consist of 1 or 3 template arenas that get randomised slightly for each mission. - The unit upgrade tree is full of choices that aren't meaningful, or sub-optimal and will get you killed.- The game is more stressful than fun. Like many people, I play to relax after work. The chance that I will get steamrolled in any given mission due to unlucky enemy spawns, or warp events, is totally off putting and will make me want to play anything else 9 times our of 10. TLDR - I wish I could go back in time and never have bothered with this game. It's an un-optimised mess that's full of petty mechanics designed to ♥♥♥♥ on your day, rather than present a genuine challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR at the bottomI am writing this review right after finishing my first play-through on the standard difficulty in Grandmaster (Ironman) mode. I'll try to keep this review spoiler free, but if you see , be advised.The story is pretty good, for a Warhammer game. It's no masterpiece, but it at the very least makes sense. The characters, on the other hand are.... pretty weak to be honest It feels less like they're battlehardened Warriors with centuries of experience and more like Children, or Rookies at best, with their constant bickering. But, since you can skip almost any cutscene and most dialogue, this isn't too much of a problem.The Voice acting, on the other hand, is amazing All cutscenes (and boi there are a few of those) are completely voice acted and the optional dialogue is at least partly.Overall, a 5/10 in this categoryThe Gameplay is, similarily to XCOM 2, split in two parts: The Strategic Layer and the Tactical LayerThe Strategic Layer is pretty boring IMO, all you do is fly around the map,  and complete 1 (or two if you're lucky) out of 3 missions every now and then. You do eventually get better equipment, which can be upgraded at some point but the Strategic Layer really isn't that exciting.As long as you focus on the important Ship-Upgrades you'll be good to go.The Tactical Layer is amazing, I would say on par, if not better than XCOM 2's (amazing game as well btw). Unlike similar Games, there is no chance to hit in this game, you will always hit. This is compensated by damage penalties on long range and cover. Additionally, your strongest abilities and weapons will be melee focused, promoting a much more agressive playstyle than similar games. My only gripe is, that your units, especially in the early game, feel pretty weak, but that is something you need to accept, if you don't want half of the game to be a walk in the park.Overall, a 9/10 in this categoryFirst of, the Game looks amazing, the enemy gore looks good, the facial animations and cut-scenes are phenomenal.But the game requires a really beefy PCI will admit, that my PC is not the best in the World (16GB DDR4 Ram, GTX 1060, Ryzen 7 3800X) But i could not get the game above 60 FPS even on medium quality. I am pretty sure that my Graphics card is the bottleneck here, so keep that in mind.Overall, a 7/10 in this category IF you have a good PC, otherwise maybe stay awayThe story is decent, the Gameplay is really fun, the game looks gorgeous but you need a beefy PCOverall Score is 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is the first time that I'm going to change my verdict from recommended to not recommended.I had big hopes for this one. I love XCOM, and the mix of XCOM and Warhammer 40k sounded really good. Having watched the preview gameplay and reviews, I decided to preorder Chaos Gate Daemonhunters. It was a bad decision.First of all, preorder cost me around 40 euro since I chose the version with the DLC - thought that it would give me some story, customizable items, anything? Nah, you get a character with some items. Paying 30% of the price just to get a character is very bad market practice.Next is the gameplay itself. This game is a literal copy of XCOM 2 in terms of research, building, soldier loadouts and abilities. And I don't mind it. What I mind however is the terrible gameplay on the battle map. I liked the idea of going through systems and purifying the plague nests, but battles are another thing.Bloom meter or whatever it is called is such a bad mechanic. It gives your enemies buffs or gives you debuffs, and that would be fine, except it fills up quickly... VERY quickly. Around turn 5/6 the bar is filled and by this time you are probably fighting two groups because it is impossible to isolate the groups - spawns are designed in a way to force you to fight two groups at once because the detection range of your marines is big.At this point NORMAL difficulty turns into LEGENDARY. You essentially end up fighting around 10-20 enemies with 4 space marines, whereas half of your enemies are pox minions that do nothing except waste your AP points. Even if you do win the battle, it probably cost your soldiers their health, and because of that, your campaign is ruined.That is because the wound recovery time is absurdly long. Your soldier walked through a small bonfire? Unlucky, he needs 50 days to recover despite the fact that his body was made to withstand literal gunshots. This forces you to use less-experienced soldiers, but as the game goes on, the difficulty is higher and the enemies get tougher. In my last mission I was forced to use one healthy soldier with 16 health and 3 wounded soldiers with 6 hp each. Obviously I lost. You barely get any soldiers, if you do it is after you win a battle and these happen every 20-30 days or so.I'm not even going to mention the twitch drops scandal because I'm too tired for this.Overall, I'm just frustrated. I really like the idea behind the game, but mechanics are just so so bad and frustrating and because of that there is no fun. I have faith in the devs of this game, so I'm hoping that the game will get patched and receive mod support and hopefully, in few months it will be playable and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: There are some traps at the start of this game and I can see how a lot of people with only a couple hours of play time would come away with a negative impression. They're not wrong.While XCOM 2 is the single biggest influence on the game and clearly the starting point of the design, it mixes in other modern games like Gears Tactics and has enough ideas of its own that you'll be very frustrated if you try to play it just like XCOM at the tactical level. The game does not introduce you to its systems well either. Not from the perspective of a new player, and very much not from the perspective of an XCOM veteran who's chiefly interested in the things that are different. Cover, overwatch, armor, RNG, critical hits, action points, movement, skills, etc. are all quite different and need to be re-learned. Optimal play patterns are very different in this game compared to the games that inspired it.At the same time, while in many ways this game is devoted to the 40K lore, the developers treated it as only a suggestion when they were tuning the early-game combat and progression. If you come into the game with lore based notions of how tough Space Marines are, and expect that power fantasy out of the gate, you're in for a rude surprise. Cultists with mere slug-throwers are going to damage and sometimes wound your marines, even those with terminator armor, with one or two hits. Your level one and two guys with the entry level gear, despite looking, walking and quacking like Space Marines, are closer in power to XCOM recruits you need to keep behind cover. It feels bad.The far-from-purely-cosmetic pre-order kit, the cheat-code marine in the special edition and the twitch drops all leave a bad taste in the mouth as well.But if you can get through those bad initial impressions, and engage the game on its own terms, there's something really special here. The game isn't just copying other tactical shooters, it's in conversation with them, mixing things up in some very interesting ways. The combat systems they've changed largely feel like improvements and after the rough opening, fit well with being elite Space Marines. The skill trees and the gear system allow real builds to emerge. As these builds start to take shape and you personally start to master the game's systems, the power fantasy kicks in and then some. Your squad of marines will be able to roll through tough encounters with some real momentum, not getting shot at all, or only getting shot when you intend to on troops with enough armor to shrug it off. At the strategic level, it feels even more like XCOM 2 out of the gate, but finds its own identity as the game goes on with constant and interesting tension in your choice of missions and how to spend your resources. The interplay between tactical and strategic are great, with the strategic often asking you to take extra risks and leave your comfort zone in the tactical for some extra resources.The story is better than anyone should expect from a game like this. In the now familiar pattern, it starts with XCOM and finds its own voice from there. Like XCOM, it's told largely by your supporting caste in your HQ. Unlike XCOM, there's some real tension between the characters and you make decisions that have real, if sometimes opaque, impact on your campaign. The writing and voice acting are solid. Cut scenes are fully voiced. The interactive dialog has about one sentence per paragraph getting voiced. My one complaint in this department is that that one sentence isn't always the first sentence of the paragraph, creating some real dissonance where you either need to just listen to their line without the context of what they were supposed to say before it, or try to read their response as written while ignoring what they are saying. It's a baffling choice in an otherwise very well produced story.This game is not without flaws, and they are unfortunately very front-loaded in the experience. But it's loaded with love for the genre and setting, and some real ambition to be its own game and create new thrills and challenge, even for those like me who've taken many a lap around its tactical shooter predecessors. There's a reason, I think, for the disparity between the near universal critical acclaim and the mixed player reaction. Critics had to get through the opening to write their review. Normal players are under no such obligation.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a mediocre clone of X-COM, with many mechanics not fully polished or tested. The clashes, central to the game, get boring quickly. It is due to the small selection of opponents, low intelligence, and predictable move sets. Schematic approach forced by the solution of renewing action points - fights start with an alpha strike, mopping up, free moves before finishing the last enemy, and then making as many moves before triggering the next group. Leveling up your Grey Knights is also quite dull - the game encourages you to use only a few builds, with many options being so clearly suboptimal and not introducing anything. Events resolutions are quite absurd - it is recommended to use a guide to them because quite a big part of them is counterintuitive and gives you the opposite result than selected. Overall, missed potential - better to play X-COM, Phantom Doctrine or in case of 40k game - Mechanicus.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - PASSABLE: 6/10Same gripes as most of the players. Marines are fragile, ranged weapons hardly have range, 4 member squad limit, it also follows XCOM style of gameplay instead of staying in line with the first Chaos Gate game.Yeah, I'm one of those salty Gen Xers that's been playing 40k since "before it was cool", so I'm a little more opinionated than some other fans. The first game was one of the best 40k games ever(still available on GOG, btw). This feels like more like XCOM than Chaos Gate. Enemies move in clusters which once spotted break up into individual units. It makes the most important part of your strategy positioning your team before combat starts.Cover is broken. You either have 100% chance to hit, or 0%. If you are behind low cover and use overwatch, works fine. If you are in high cover and use it, your knight will peal out to the side of it, completely exposed, instead of just peaking around and still using the cover.Armor is a joke. Your power armor has a rating of 0 standard, where as the Chaos marines have 2-3 standard. This means all damage is done to your health(more on that) with basic power armor, where as Chaos marines have 2-3 points that regen every turn.Fragile marines. If you stub your toe, or scuff your knee, expect to have 2-4 weeks of recovery time for the most minor of injuries.Ranged weapons. A cultist with a an autogun has better range than your highly trained knight with the best weaponry the Imperium can build.Strategy is lacking. With only a team of 4, and limited range it just turns into a scramble to find cover every turn. Especially with an enemy that goes into overwatch with more range than you.Personally, I've never been a huge fan of Grey Knights, but that's just me.If you're a 40k fan than you'll find some enjoyment of this. If you're looking for a strategy game, just do XCOM, which does it better. Hopefully the devs will fix the armor issue, reduce chances of being wounded, and balance out the ranged weaponry.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't really write that many reviews, but I saw this sitting around 80% and I'll sometimes write one for a game that isn't getting it's props. I honestly enjoyed this more than any of the recent X-Com games. It's so much more enjoyable to start off with units that aren't made of paper and can still get a lot of killing done right from the first battle. And the way you can spec your units out lets you recover action points during a turn, meaning you can often chain together attacks. It lets you play increasingly aggressively compared to X-Com where you feel like you have to play conservatively to protect your soldiers. You have this real feeling of forward momentum as you annihilate the enemies in brutal fashion. And doing away with hit percentages is a great move.Brilliant game design.It looks and sounds good too and the narrative is just the right balance of grimdark and ridiculousness. I really wish this team had gotten the Necromunda license.

_childDocuments_.review: Ehh, it is ok. Good cartoony graphics and smooth game play but that is about it. I found a bug in the first few minutes - I could not start repairing the ship, I had to save and reload (thanks to the info on the Steam forum). The game totally ruins the effect of playing as the very tippy tip of the Emperor's spear when a lowly cultist will easily kill one of your Grey Knights. You do not have the feeling of being powerful at all. None. Zero. Zilch. This game needs an injection of something thrilling. You need to feel powerful, you need to feel like you are doing something. The game cut-scenes and battle maps do not convey the awesome universe of 40k. The huge scale of slaughter, the huge scale of buildings, the huge scale of war.  I would love to mow down cultist, but the game mechanics are built from basically one on one combat. Every character in the game is almost on par with your Knights. The missions need low level troops that you can slay with a few mid level units mixed in. This would increase the scope and scale of the game and add some excitement. My Knights want to spread the Emperor's light, but the game decided a half dozen cultists should be a match for my Space Marines. There are some choices in the game, but you always (and I mean ALWAYS) feel like you are playing exactly the path the developers want. It is the illusion of choice. The interface is clunky. A lot of "ok" or continue buttons are fairly small and appear in the bottom corners of the screen. The first time I loaded a battle I didn't see the button and I thought "wow this is taking a long time to load. The game needs more chances to skip cut-scenes. In general it is not good UI design, but the UI is smooth running.A cultist with a rifle, cowering behind a barrel will make you question your life and your Steam buying choices.Edit 1: The more I play, the worse it gets. I just realized that the super cultist slackers have way more armor than my Space Marines. What the...Edit 2: The game revolves around giving your Knights only short range options and all of the enemies long range weapons. This game needs mods bad. Bad. Please mod this horrible game. Shorten the enemy ranges and give the Knights more armor and longer range attacks. Before someone says, "Well the game just has a hard difficultly level...". No. It is not clever or good game design to just lower the stats on one side and raise the stats on the other side. That is laziness. The core of this game is just lazy design. Edit 3: 2 more bugs found. 1. When I restarted a battle, the game did not display the special objective, "Glorious Deed" (?)(it was "do not use willpower"). I am so tired of this game, so I said you-know-what to the game (I told it what I thought of its parents and where it could stick things) . I beat the mission using every power I had anyways. The game displayed the COMPLETED bonus objective in the mission summary screen and gave me the points. 2. My game now freezes at the end of day 164. I get a feeling that the game want to load an event, because some of the UI goes away, but some of the other buttons can still be pressed. Needless to say, I told the game you-know-what again, just to see if it helps this time. *as a note: I realized that this game is just a cash grab by the developers, so I did try to get a refund, but I ended having a slightly long play time. It was rejected by Steam. We need a "game stinks, tried to get a refund" tag.I feel the Chaos Gods sucking the life out of me the more I play it.

_childDocuments_.review: X-com in 40,000 universe.  It should have been great, but Chaos Gate has serious flaws that mar what could have been an excellent game.  Firstly, user interface and strategy; what should take one click takes three, there are to many nested menus, research and construction seem unnecessarily opaque and the requisition system is complex for no good reason that I can see.  Lastly the voice acting is, odd.  There are frequently paragraphs of text with only one line voice acted.  I found this much more irritating that I thought I would.  A quick word on the graphics, they are not bad but they feel not right for 40,000, they are cartoon a bit like someone put a world of Warcraft style filter on the game, its personally but I prefer the gritty realism style in the 40,000 universe.Secondly, the difficulty spikes are massive.  Its not just a case of the game being hard but that it goes from being easy to incredibly hard from mission to the next.  This is not challenging but poor balancing and mission design.  To go from a difficulty of (out of 10) 2, 3, 1, 9, 3, 2, 10 feels uneven, punishing and off putting.Lastly, performance.  I have a pretty beefy machine with a 3090, and the not only is the performance sluggish, especially on the enemy turns, but my rig sounds like its trying to take off and fly.  Am sure this will be patched at some point soon.To sum up this is an amazing premise with solid underlying game play marred by what feels like a very rushed release and muddled design.  Hopefully this will be a great game in 6 months time but I wish I had waited until them to buy it.  I would recommend that you hold of purchasing at least until you read feedback about the next patch.Hope you find this helpful.

_childDocuments_.review: Look I wanted to like this game a lot. I love 40k and I loved X Com, and that is what this is.Except the balance is way off. The game forces tactics out the window and makes it a melee and aggression fest. The enemy always:- Outnumbers you- Deals the same damage as you, despite the lore- Out ranges youAnd the random number generator meter ticks up constantly, and then dishes out a random surprise every few turns. Sometimes manageable, sometimes totally F'd.The maps dont allow for tactical movement in the way X Com does.Your characters are always wounded, too. Unlike Xcom which encourages tactical play, this is a war of attrition where you will always take damage. That isnt too bad on face value, because you almost always survive, however they need an insane amount of time rested after the mission, basically necessitating 2-3 full rosters.The game was fun for just long enough to not be eligible for a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: (Will do updates via comments)Played on Steam Deck. I preemptively set the video options to low since the the game was listed as unsupported as of the writing of this review. Game plays smoothly and seems well optimized for Steam Deck controls. Which begs the question, how do users flag something as it DOES work well on deck that is mislabeled? My only qualms are occasionally the game itself will have minor flubs like claiming a target is in range and will take damage but ignores that there is terrain that is blocking. Or occasionally it may be off on the amount of damage something may take (leading to an awkward position where you planned for that enemy to be dead and executed but they are still alive and well).The game itself: XCOM meets 40k and minus the % hit shenanigans. You either will hit (or at a reduced damage due to distance) or are unable to hit (unit has too much cover from you). There are story elements (primarily a Grey knights faction vs Nurgle story), base construction (no minigame like xcom 2 for optimizing layout, just optimizing opportunity cost in the form of time and servitors), research (both tech to progress story and stratagems), different units, and various complications that arise during gameplay that keep things fresh.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent XCOM game in Warhammer 40k world. :) During tactical engagements, the game looks pretty, it's challenging, tense and engaging. Strategically - there's research, there's character development, there's base development, there are random events during which you are supposed to make difficult choices. Dialogues and interactions between characters are not childish. Voice acting is ok, especially your Space Marine warriors sound really badass. Sound and music is fine. There's really nothing more to expect from AA game. :)I strongly disagree with people who describe this game as lore-incosistent. It's exactly opposite - unless all your knowledge about WH40k in general and Space Marines in particular comes from novels. Yes, in novels Space Marines are god-like killing machines who anihilate anyone not equipped with power armours and bolters by thousands. But actually in the "original" lore - WH40k tabletop rulebooks - the Space Marines ARE in fact very powerfull, true - but they are FAR from being invincible and it's entirely possible for them to be overrun and beaten by a force two - three times their numbers of "lesser" oponents. And this game simulates this perfectly. :)

_childDocuments_.review: The game and the lore is not in sync. The Grey Knights in the game is weak and can be killed by cultists. Do not mistake this game for another XCOM like game. There is no hit percentage, no flanking bonus, no high ground bonus. Farming research resources are random, Most missions are just repeating itself just to farm even more random resources and random wargears. So if you are unlucky, you will find yourself in the stage of grinding.The game expects your knights to die so you can use the the dead to upgrade your other knights by a little. Too bad if you are good at this kind of game, you will know that it is not worth the sacrifice.The gameplay is difficult in the beginning which makes you train your knights to a very specific build to win it, especially in timer based missions. Meaning another dead lock on the specialization on some of your knights. After that, you can finally be free of building more knights of your liking, But for what? 8 classes of knights with different builds but in the end, you can only bring 4 to a mission.The skill tree in each classes looks interesting but after observing it, half of them are redundantly useless. You may think that each classes have many builds but no, most of them is only 2 kinds of build, and respec'ing takes too long.The gameplay is slow and those random interventions while travelling the map is just to make the game even slower. It is really a pain to go through the wargears every missions, could have save a lot of time if it were not the random one-kind-only loot. It is always hard at first while progressing steady and well but turns out easy and grindy slow at the last part of the game. Guess what... some bosses can be killed within the first turn.The lack of maps is what make the game bored since once your remember them, you know where the strategic points are but what the heck, just blast everything to ashes since the AI keeps wasting your time by pinning. That's right, kill before the battle even started. This don't really feels like a strategy game, more of a stealth game.The AI basically pins you instead of finding a way to flank you if they are ranged or crawl towards you if they are melee. So how do they try to kill you? By not making you act and throw many afflictions at you. Really? Putting so many enemies in a wave to scare you but somehow thinking firing at you is too OP against you so they made them pin you.The game could have been more creative in its development. I rather stick to XCOM. You still want to play the game, Get it at a discount. But don't regret if the game is too slow for you.

Tactical map rotates in 90 degree chunks and is off-set 45 degrees from the grid axis, this makes using a controller in tactical super annoying (unplayable for me).3. Squad selection and inventory interface is set up for controller meaning it has a bunch of unnecessary button clicks to get anything done: select warrior, select load out, select ranged weapons, select the type of ranged weapon, select the ranged weapon you want, hit back a bunch of times to back your way out of this ridiculously deep hierarchical process.4. No sorting or filtering on the unit or gear screens. Why not "sort by class" for units? Why not have all ranged weapons with sort by type and only display usable .and only display tier 3?5. Sector map, after expansion does not all fit on screen and there is limited zoom functionality (insufficient to zoom out far enough to see all systems at once). _childDocuments_.review: So far having a blast. _childDocuments_.review: A few things.First of all, this game is great fun. XCOM crossed with 40k is a match made in heaven. I basically bought this game because I wanted to experience the power fantasy of commanding humanity's finest weapons: the Grey Knights, and this game delivers very well on that. The overarching narrative of the game is great. Very simple, but very effective. All NPCs are extremely well voiced and are actually interesting; with my personal favourite being our resident Tech Priest.The art style is really nice, the environments are exceptional, and the animations and art assets (especially our Grey Knight terminator armours) are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ perfect. The only issue I have experienced thus far, is that this game is EXCEPTIONALLY punishing. I started my first play through playing on normal difficulty, and man - the game ♥♥♥♥♥ you up real good and fast. As I said, I bought this game because I wanted to play as the most overpowered chapter of the Astartes and experience the power fantasy of them wrecking ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ left and right... I have no shame in saying that I dropped the difficulty down to easy to achieve those ends. Even then, if you forsake tactics in the name of a more run & gun approach on this difficulty, you will find yourself outflanked, outmaneuvered, and outgunned a vast majority of the time - which is great. For what I wanted out of this game, easy difficulty is perfect (it'd probably be more considered 'normal difficulty' in other titles. Game is very punishing.)The game has various spikes in difficulty too. For the first 3-4 hours, it's pretty smooth sailing. Then, you start to experience a vast array of various hard hitting units that give you a pretty rude awakening that you better stop ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ around and start approaching your missions with actual tactics.Great fun, I enjoy this game a lot. Hopefully you will too.

_childDocuments_.review: just absurdly hard and unnecessarily punishing, odds are stacked against you in a way that you have very few options to leverage a team's strengths to mitigate being outnumbered and outgunned at ALL times. At no point in any map will you be able to seize any advantage and the game routinely pushes you into eat sh*t moments that have you ending missions with one survivor even on the easiest difficulty. fail to stop a ritual of a priest guy who's got like 5 plagued marines protecting them? enjoy a 15+ armour enemy with 30+ health when all you have is some level 3 newbies to deal with him. the warp surge is just a horrible mechanic that makes missions stressful rather than fight and you spend more time scrambling at your enemies and trying to melee them down since your ranged attacks just tickle even trash enemies leaving your squad exposed all the time. oh and you'll be outflanked during warp events too so don't even bother with cover just back yourself into a corner and set up overwatch and pray to god that the AI doesn't path around your overwatch overlaps. there's no way to feel good about your outcomes here compared to something like xcom or phoenix point. Save your money and time and play one of those games instead. balance is just wayyyyyy off and the game has been out long enough for it to be clear that this is just how it is.

_childDocuments_.review: Its good. Has its problems but a very enjoyable game overall. To deal with the elephant in the room. Yes this game is very much Xcom in 40k.  But its also so much more. Xcom is an obvious inspiration point, but the devs added a lot to the mix to differentiate. The enemy design is very different, most enemies are rather reactive, forcing you to act (like suppression, slow  area bombs, etc) and your starter units are much stronger. Also lot of the "roll to hit" parts of the game are gone, Not even mentioning the genius Bloom mechanic. I also genuinely  enjoy some of the animation touches and the VA and audio design is in general really good.  So that was the good. Now the bad. The game runs kind of bad, not super well optimised. And the higher fidelity graphic settings seem to clutter the game instead of actually make it look better. (Also oh my god that greater demon in the tutorial looks horrendous) I had a number of crashes and bugs, usually related to audio or loading. A few animation jitters too. I recommend not alt tabbing at all while playing this game. It gets WYERD,  But once the game is going and running it seems pretty stable. I played games with much worse problems (just the Xcom enemy unknown to start with). Hopefully they get fixed however.  Overall its a fun game. And the story and theme seems to click well with 40K's vibe.Big recommend to any fans of either tactics games or 40k. Pick it up on a sale. Maybe not on full price until they fix some problems.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. The story is good, the characters memorable, the tactics work fine... Original take in that there is very little random in a fight (apart from crits): Distance and cover influence the damage you take/inflict and not your chance to hit.Many different classes with different upgrade path means no two knights will be the same, and there are lots of strategies you can use.Boss fights are interesting and have nice mechanics that change the way you have to think...Overall, a very good turn-based strategy game!
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very good turn-based tactics games. The closest comparison for this game is XCOM 2. For those tired of the unpredictability of XCOM, you'll be happy to hear that Daemonhunters has very little RNG to worry about. All shots hit. Combat manages to be remarkably cinematic for a turn-based game. Environment interaction has a much greater impact than in XCOM and is very satisfying to use.  None of your units ever feel completely useless in a given situation, although certain classes seem almost like a necessity for virtually every mission (Justicars).As for the negatives, the maps can get a bit repetitive. Unlike XCOM, the maps are not procedurally generated. There's also not a huge variety of enemies, although I expect both of these things to change in future DLC, assuming there is any. I did encounter several bugs, the most notable of which involved my Interceptor: I somehow managed to teleport inside an enemy and get stuck there. Had to re-load a save to undo it. Same character also never showed up on the final mission, meaning I had to do it one knight down.Advice for new players: be as aggressive in combat as you can. Players that are generally good at tactics games should probably start at a higher difficulty than they might usually do. Unlike XCOM, this game appears to reward you for getting soldiers severely wounded or even killed, although I'm not sure if I understand the mechanic correctly as I went the whole campaign without losing a soldier.TL;DR: overall a great tactics game with some minor flaws that should hopefully be fixed in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate - Daemonhunters

_childDocuments_.review: What if X-COM 2 was a good game without needing mods for that?That's pretty much the question answered by Chaos Gate in those early hours for me, so far.They have better implementations of pretty much exactly all mechanics of X-COM and X-COM 2 that bother me.Like the turn limits that result in an instant gameover - here they cause mutations that increase the difficulty instead, makes a lot more sense.Or the awful, awful pod mechanics of XCOM - here the enemies are not the only ones that get a free turn when a pod is activated.Or the boring RNG-fest of accuracy. There's no accuracy mechanics here. You still have some rng in the form of Crit Chance and similar, but there's no missing the target; neither for you nor for the enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: If you played Battletech, you'll probably see many similarities. As the XCom comparisons miss on a couple aspects: 1) RNG is nowhere near as brutal in this game as the XCom franchise. Either for you or the enemy. If you miss a shot, you took one at someone in cover. Same if they miss. In general, your Grey Knights will do more damage. Be hardier. And can wade through chaff with relative ease. But the AI has brutes of its own. And will use the hordes to whittle you down until you walk into them. 2) The tools you have in the beginning have all the essential gameplay elements you'll see throughout the game. Unlike XCom, where you unlock bigger squads, new types of weapons and methods of attack, in this game, your tactics will be decided by the mission. And your gear by the character build. Which you'll probably have a strong idea of when you see what each character's trait and class are. There's more variation than the game tells you. And that's good and bad. Good because it rewards you for investigating the systems and becoming familiar with the mechanics. Bad because the game could do a better job of telling you some of these items. For example: Character Traits. Nowhere are you told each character has one of these. And if you don't hover your mouse over the center of each character's progression tree, you would never know it's there. The gameplay is very good. The story is solid. The music is YMMV. But I like it. The interface is Unity engine style. Which is another reason I say Battletech is a good point of reference. As both are Unity games. The game doesn't have near the performance hits of typical Unity fare though. So hats off to the developers for that. All in all, a solid game anyone who likes either Warhammer or Tactical RPGs should enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has alot going for it and great potential, however I've run into a couple of problems.Just to clarify I've been playing RTS and turn based strategy games most of my life, so I hope my opinion will help.Pros: - Great cinemtaic combat animations, you can see care has been taken with them. Great voice acting for the most part- A linear story that still allows you to feel you're steering it's direction through in game choices.- The fun logistical challenge of managing your time and resources between your ship and Grey knights, it gives a true sense of desperation and urgency, couple this with event decisions and it adds weight to every choice you make.- A new  style of gameplay that awards aggressiveness not seen often in the turn based genre, forces you to really think about your next move.Cons:- UI seems a bit much for me, there are options to turn some components off but there is just far too much going on.- Enemies never seem to stop coming on most missions, and do too much damage. Little cultists can leave a big dent in you with machine guns even with Terminator armour. I was only playing on normal and I'm used to playing Turn based games on the hardest difficulties. Safe to say I wasn't feeling like a Space Marine.- Wound times are far too long, especially for how easy they are to acquire. 40+ days to recover my grey knights, after I had to make an in game decision it increased their recovery time by a further 50%- Buggy in some places, there are freezes and FPS drops. Doesn't seem well optimised atm but I'm aware this is an issue that will likely be fixed. I've had no crashes yet.Summary:In conclusion Chaos Gate has alot going for it, it's tried to break the mould and be different from other turn based strategy games and it's working. Enemies defintely need their damage or numerity tweaking, it needs some quality of life improvements and optimisation. But at the foundation is a really good game that you can tell has been made with care by people who love Warhammer.I hope this helps 🙂

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, having finished it once and now going for the rest I can safely say that this is one of the good W40K games.If you like W40K and X-COM then it's an absolute no brainer to get this.I'm not sure about full price. as well as the DLCs, but on a sale the basic game is a blast for fans of the above.Gameplay is pretty good for a turn based game (and you won't have the 99% miss chance).Visually it's its own cup of tea. Nothing amazing that will make your jaw drop in awe, but the direction they took on the design is still pretty satisfying.What shines the most though for me is the story. It is absolutely awesome for someone who likes W40K. Starts of slow and picks up the pace with some twists and the usual futility that humanity faces in this franchise. _childDocuments_.review: Ok.....So:- Grenades trigger overwatch (because reasons)- Your troops get fired at, even outside of the enemy's overwatch 'screen' (because reasons)- Your troops get fired at when shooting the enemy who is triggering the overwatch, not only that, there is only a slight chance of you actually disabling the overwatch by shooting the enemy.- The warp can spawn multiple reinforcements (4/5 each or even more) and that multiple times during 1 mission...- Early on there is no healing against plague over-time damage or even healing itself, only 'resurrecting'- The enemy has more range than you do (because oh so powerful knights - not -)- The Terminator armor does not give you 2 permanent armor without activating Aegis shield (is it something that needs to be equipped? If so, why does the game not inform me about it?)- Early on you only have 4 deamonhunters at your disposal, sometimes against 15/20+ enemies a mission.- The battles are filled with minutes long unneeded animations, it even takes long when activating the 'fast' enemy turn speed.- The camera sometimes does not record both ally and more often enemy actions- The sound of suppression is dampened and is only hearable when it is your turn.Limited repairs on the vessel early on, limited weaponry, limited units, limited information...I sincerely just don't get the hype around this Warhammer 40K game. _childDocuments_.review: It is a good XCOM style squad TBS game with overworld elements.  It is not great, as there are flaws, other reviewers have vented about many.  Off the top of my head, the difficulty curve can be severe based on some RNG.  Specifically the servitor missions.  Those shouldn't exist before the first chapter is complete, you lack the tools and experience to handle 3-5 fronts spread across the map with up to 8 enemy squads attacking, starting with 2 and gaining 1 per turn.  It's alot to ask of new Grey Knights.  You also start from almost zero, and because of this, if you don't know what the game will require of you, you could make some bad first decisions.  As an example, perhaps a new player just kept going to planets with grimoires as rewards, so their entire ship rebuilding is crippled because they didn't realize they have to front load on servitor reward missions until you fix up your own factories to a decent degree.  As others have said as well, the encounter system is not well thought out as well.  You cannot surprise or be surprised really.  Either the enemy patrol reveals you, gets a free turn to move and attack, or you reveal the patrol, and they get a free move into cover along with overwatches and other abilities BS.  Your knights have none of these options.  The absolute best you can do is creep 3 knights to just out of sight, overwatch them, then send in the 4 that one step extra, and watch as the enemy all set up just outside your overwatch, setting up THEIR OWN overwatches, so you wasted a turn and still have to dig them out.  It could have been much better with a few tweaks to incentivize setting up ambushes, or rolling in hard and fast and catching them by surprise.  As it is, you  are basically just trying to avoid giving the enemy a free turn to attack you.So in essence, the game operates an iron curtain against new players by punishing decisions they make when they are unaware of the consequences, offering or forcing mission types that are beyond fresh knights capabilities and making encounters within those missions frustrating for new and veterans alike by the lack of tactical tricks regarding engagement.With all that, you'd think I'd not recommend it, but I still do.  It is still a good game despite those flaws.  If a new player is able to surmount that learning and difficulty curve, the mid game is just fine.  The end game can be a little tedious with the number and resilience of the enemies they throw at you, but you actually have the tools to handle it, so its not bad.Boss fights are all unique and fun, the characters are great (I call Lunette 'Toaster Grandma') and once you get some gear and experience on your knights, they can be great fun for power fantasy.  A purgator with psycannon, using psychic onslaught to wipe out a whole enemy squad of pox walkers.  An interceptor teleport blinking behind a dreadnaught and smashing it to pieces with an F-all thunder hammer.  I still enjoy the grenade throw animation, hundreds of times later, lol.It is hard.  It will likely require trial and error or research out of game to succeed, a 'dark souls' of xcom genre, to use the overworn trope.  It is not perfect.  But it is good, and it is fun and it is 40k.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game, though it's quite flawed in many ways.  Forget tactics in combat, it mostly comes down to action point spam - the more you can generate, the better and later on allows you to have one knight kill everything in one turn.  You need only think about how to spend the action points efficiently.I would also say this game is about twice as long as it needs to be, taking over 30 hours to finish.  You will play the basic missions a lot e.g. seeding the bloom and they become very boring.  It's unnecessary grind.Graphically, it's a bit disappointing with fuzzy low res textures.  I'm playing on max detail on a 3070.There's far too much story in this game and the dialog is hammy.  Cut scenes get boring and I didn't even bother talking to the characters between missions after the first time.Some other things are a bit jarring, such as your 8 foot tall knight with an enourmous sword can't kill a cultist in one swing.However, it is still fun despite the above and the one-off missions stand out as being a lot better than the regular ones with some good ideas that make them more interesting to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't listen to the negative reviews that claim the game is too difficult. It really isn't. After you learn how each class works and how they synergize with others gameplay gets pretty smooth. You'll learn when you can push forward and when you need to fall back, which makes this game so much more engaging. You'll have enemies thrown at you left and right at times, you have to analyze your surroundings and create strategy on your own. There are even ways to pump all your resources into one marine to wipe entire squads with just one person. The tutorial really needs some work, it misleads you into thinking you can play recklessly, they don't really showcase real strategy. Yes, you can run in guns blazing, but only circumstantially. I'm almost willing to say this game is better than X-Com. Mainly because if you do things right, you completely turn the tides of battle and you're not really a victim of rng when it comes to this game. My only real complaint about this game is the dlc. It's hot garbage and not worth it at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit2: developers did some uneccesary balance changes, my campaign is now too hard again on normal. Changing my review to negative and it will stay negative. Developers unfortunately have no idea what they are doing. Moving on to next game.---------------Edit: Restarted my campaign and with the new knowledge I am now doing much better. Also haven't encountered a lot of bugs anymore, maybe due to changes in my playstyle. Turning this review into a positive as the game hooked me! It's just bloody hard, even on normal and takes some time to adjust into. Really love the whole polish on the game, from the graphics to the sound and music. Also lots of enemy variety, building stuff on your ship and doing research!---------------As you can see I have a lot of playtime. This game was really scratching the X-com itch and I wanted to give it an extensive, positive review. However, at the moment I have to give it a thumbs down, which is rather unfortunate. There's two issues that's really killing my enjoyment:1. Difficulty - it's off, I am playing on normal and I was hitting a brick wall at first and then later in the game again. Really frustrating, especially with the limited savegames. Related to this: you are supposed to be crack commandos, however you never feel like that. The difficulty scales in a way that your knights never really feel powerful. This is not a flaw easily fixed...2. Bugs. Later in the game I started encountering more bugs: Hellbrutes running around getting stuck and not progressing the turn, a knight which I sent away to become a Paladin vanished as in the meantime my Barracks was full, etc.So unfortunate, because it's almost a great game. You can nicely customize your characters, there's research and some production and the missions and enemies are pretty varied. Graphics are good as well, with a large destructable environment.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a great game, just has some minor issues that could be worked out if the Devs got some time to focus on it. To resolve this you have to disable all in game overlays (Steam, Nvidia etc..) Lots of potential for this game! Same with the missions where you have to protect some friendly guard squads with seeds.... would be cool if later game missions, you could control these units to actually make them useful.
