_childDocuments_.review: From the developers of Behind the Frame - The Finest Scenery, comes yet another great masterpiece by Silver Lining Studio. The Star Named EOS is like a picture worth a thousand words: its beautifully framed narrative takes unexpected turns and twists, and much like a photo being developed, it takes its time to reveal the beauty it has to offer. Just like its previous title, the game is a simple point-and-click game with engaging puzzles that keep you intrigued and weave a story throughout its game-play. The game’s art direction is truly amazing yet again. It’s the kind of beauty that makes you want to snap screenshots constantly (which i totally did with both of their games) the visuals and the clarity of it could totally be used as a desktop wallpaper. Or if you're crazy enough, print it, frame it, and hang it onto your wall.The music in this game perfectly blends with the ambiance to set the tone and atmosphere, and it also enhances the more emotional moments, making them even more impactful. The gorgeous art style makes it feel like you’re experiencing a living storybook, you’ll definitely be in tears by the end, and the game really hits you with valuable lessons that resonate deeply just like its previous title as well. Thank you to Turn Sound Studio for executively producing the music for this game!Also, to mention, the VA for Dei's mom and Nat is voiced by 3 very talented woman who are well known in the VA industry. Aoi Yuuki, Suzie Yeung and Shandy Ma. For now, i have only played with Aoi Yuuki voice over and i could say she has done an incredible job at setting the tone and voice for the role she is playing as.Although it's a short game which could be completed in an hour or two, is it worth the money? In my opinion, yes. I fully enjoyed my time playing it and would see myself coming back to this game again in a couple of months or years.

AAAAA Also the subtitles got stuck on my screen several times and got overlayed on top of each other. For now quitting and re-entering fixes it if anyone else has this issue. It's quite short but very pretty, and the story and puzzles are good, so I will recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: "Mixed feelings" is the best way that I can use to describe my attitude towards this game (100% completion). On one hand it is stunning visually, the story is intriguing, and the music serves as a bow on this gift of an aesthetically pleasing game. On the other, I really disliked being "pushed" by the game to progress in a very specific way. There was so many interesting things I wanted to click on but no, no exploring beyond the "necessities". And the biggest let down of this game were the puzzles. I think we are far beyond the point where the towers of Hanoi were a fun thing to solve.Side note about achievements: full play-through takes about an hour, if you aren't nearly blind like me, you'll get almost all of the achievements right away; some of them are... tedious? a reach? unnecessary? I'll let you be the judge but I love maxing games and this one felt like a chore at times.All in all: at this price point + this much content = sorry to say that, but mid for me. However, it could be great for you if you're more of a "vibes" person and not "give me your toughest  puzzles" person.

_childDocuments_.review: The Star Named Eos is an aggressively sentimental point and click puzzle game where you play a young man named Dei who is trying to replicate the photos sent to him in the mail by his mother. In order to do this, he has to navigate several elaborately constructed rooms where everything he owns is locked behind a puzzle that requires him to decipher secret messages encoded in his childhood books, or move his clothes around following the rules of a tile puzzle rather than simply lifting them like a normal person. The Star Named Eos was released in 2024 by Silver Lining Studio, developers of Behind the Frame which is a similar explore-the-environment and ”why does my bedroom have so many puzzles in it?” game.You navigate the game by rotating a 360 degree view around the room you’re in, clicking on interactable items in the surroundings letting you pick them up, examine them closer, or use items on them. Standard point and click adventure stuff. Occasionally, moreso towards the latter half of the game, you will need to use your camera to make progress through the puzzle by finding a specific point in the environment to take a photo of, though this is always clearly telegraphed.The art is beautiful and hand drawn, and the voice over narration is quite good. The story follows Dei recreating his mother’s journeys, as well as replicating her photos, and uncovering more about their relationship. Everything is accompanied by tinkling pianos music and strings. It’s very cinematic.I did run into one bug that soft locked me out of continuing the game (I took a camera out during a specific moment, which then prevented me from interacting with an object I needed to interact with as well as leaving me unable to close the camera view.) However reloading put me right where I left off pretty painlessly so it wasn’t a big deal. The game otherwise functioned perfectly and the controls and UI were well designed.The Star Named Eos costs 14.99 USD, and I was able to complete it in about three hours. There are a number of collectible photos you can find as well by taking photos of interesting things in the different environments, so you may get more game time by 100%ing it and looking for these collectibles. Also, I want to say that as an admitted point and click adventure dumdum, I was able to solve every single puzzle in the game except one without needing help (and that one was a doozy in my opinion.) So the puzzles are challenging enough but with patience the game is quite solvable.My biggest problem with the game was its sentimentality. Endless voice overs about finding beauty and never giving up hope and that amid darkness there’s always light and so on and so on. By the end of the game I was writhing in agony anytime a voice over started because I knew I was in for several minutes of platitudes.The one time I did get a bit choked up by the story I felt more manipulated than moved. Take me with a grain of salt here, less cynical people seem to find this game very moving. I just thought the game was all gentle reassurances with no real point. However if you enjoy point and click puzzle games, or games that get described as “cozy” then you will likely find this game in your wheelhouse.I’d love to hear your thoughts on the game, and if you’re interested please follow my Steam Curator page  for reviews of lesser known titles like this of all genres.

_childDocuments_.review: This one didn't land for me.You explore the story of a young man and his memories of his mother. Both of them are photographers, and the man reads his mother's old letters, retraces her steps, recreates photos she sent him from her journeys and in between solves some logic puzzles.There is a break in the story when it turns out that maybe we haven't seen reality quite as it was, and from there on, things move in less predictable ways. I won't spoil much more.What bothered me about this game was that the narrative was confusing. I think I got the main elements - spoilers:   . But the way they were conveyed was strange and I don't quite understand why it was done this way, visiting similar locations multiple times and at times becoming fantastical. Also, the pseudo deep statements characters made took me out of the story - even when granting poetic expression and sentimental exaggeration, a lot of that stuff just isn't true.And lastly, the logic puzzles ... at some point, I no longer understood how I was meant to come up with the next step (e.g. how do I know that I'm meant to photograph the window in my dilapidated childhood room? Because I've photographed it in a previous chapter?).It all doesn't come together for me as it was likely intended, as a touching, calm and wise story.

_childDocuments_.review: Another beautifully drawn game from Silver Lining Studio with an emotionally impactful story.The puzzles aren't too hard for the most part, though I did get terribly stuck on one of them. There are also these diary entries you can unlock if you take certain photo shoots in certain chapters; this is an unprompted feature, & I feel like this should be prompted as it adds context to the story. Not everyone will complete all the achievements to discover this feature after all. That aside though, I have no complaint for the game: it took me just under 6 hours to 100% it & those are six hours wonderfully spent.P.S. Another thing that might be easy to miss: the main menu changes a bit every time you complete a chapter. Just one more thing to appreciate about the game!

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely charming aesthetic.  Really enjoyed the environments and the presentation of characters.  The trailer shows it upfront- putting an animated 2D character in a 3D environment with free camera controls is a bold choice, and I thought it worked very well.The puzzles, especially in the first half, were very charming and satisfying.  Like most hidden object / escape room-esque puzzle games, a lot of the later difficulty starts feeling a little more like Where's Waldo than solving an actual puzzle, but I was definitely still engaged.The last puzzle room unfortunately took me out of it a bit, as it was suddenly a lot less clear how to move forward (or what moving forward even meant).  Specifically, solving the only puzzle I had access to didn't seem to do anything, so I thought I was missing a step or a button or something.  Nope- once this puzzle is solved and starts glowing blue, that means it's time to look around the rest of the room in Camera Mode until you find something new.  (Devs: I would maybe consider adding some flowing particles toward the newly-activated puzzle.  Something to draw the player's eye to a place they've already written off.)  The same room had one other puzzle that took a much larger leap of logic than any before it, but as pretty much the last puzzle in the game, I can't fault it too much.Despite losing momentum during that scene, I enjoyed the game and strongly enjoyed the ending.  Recommend to any fans of short, polished puzzle / narrative games.

_childDocuments_.review:
Ever since he was young, Dei regularly received letters from his mother when she was traveling, and each letter came with a beautiful photograph of the location she was visiting.

One day, Dei notices something strange in one of the pictures she had left behind, and everything he had believed is challenged. Now, guided by his mother's voice deep within him, it's time that Dei sets out to find the truth and finally move on...

Delve into a beautiful hand-drawn world and capture the fleeting moments that shape one's life.

Recreate old photographs and uncover the long-lost truth of a family mystery, and fragmented memories will help you find a love that was long left unrealized.

With a perfect blend of a gorgeous hand-drawn artstyle and story-heavy puzzle game mechanics, The Star Named EOS will take you on a dazzling, fantastical journey of reminiscence.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're thinking about getting the second game which is also on Steam, you can forget about it. Because this game feels like the complete definitive version compared to the first and second games which felt lackluster. This game is no Mario Kart or Crash Team Racing, but after playing it I have to say this is pretty damn Solid for a licensed game.It's not great, you have to grind and collect in-game currency in order to unlock the other characters in the Garage. The race tracks themselves (While most of them are recycled/reworked from the second game) are fun and full of life. And I'm really glad this game has voice acting, but it has no unique dialogue it's literally taken from the characters respective shows so it gets stale after hearing it for a while. It kinda sucks that Zuko is only playable in the " Turbo Edition " and he's not even voiced by Dante Basco.(It's Vincent Tong who voiced Kai from Lego Ninjago)No story mode, No cutscenes, (aside from the intro and ending when you completed the challenges) and Not even a gallery showcasing concept art and other neat stuff (More Licensed games need to have those)Nick Kart Racers 3 is by no means a bad game, but it's certainly one of the better Licensed/Nickelodeon Video games I have ever played. Is it worth your time ? YES, Is it worth getting this game full price ? NO. You are better off saving that money for a better game. If you are a fan of Nicktoons or you wanna play something fun with friends for 2 hours. Then give this game a shot, Who knows maybe DLC will improve this game.Also Online doesn't work properly, so you're better off waiting for 2-3 weeks until the devs fixed it and of course there is no Crossplay (because that will make the game good now wouldn't it)

_childDocuments_.review: Can't recommend this game at it's current price for it's current state. $50 is WAY too much for whats being offered. The game is definitely fun so I highly recommend picking it up IF ITS ON SALE. Got it plus the DLC for around $15 which I believe should be base price. I'll go into a bit more depth on some of its issues below if you are interested, but the basics are what I've said above.- Ridiculous GrindIf you want to 100% or even unlock just some specific parts or characters, you are looking at an asinine amount of grinding, ranging from ridiculously unfun and annoying to basically impossible. A great example of one of the more grindy unlocks is Judy Neutron, who requires you to win 97 games of arena. Now keep in mind, these have to be WINS, not just games. And with each game taking around 3 minutes this can take an upwards of 5 hours for one unlock THAT ISN'T EVEN A DRIVER. Not to mention that 5 hours is assuming you WIN EVERY GAME and not even factoring in wait times. On the side of nigh impossible we have The Spittle Runner, a bike that requires a whopping 138 online wins, which already sounds absolutely daunting but then you factor in the fact that no one anywhere plays this game online. In my nearly 60 hours of playtime as of writing this review I have found ONE online game that had only ONE other person in it, after nearly AN HOUR of searching. So go ahead and accept the fact that you will never unlock any online items which include not only a driver but also some high tier equipment. And god forbid you want to unlock everything in the shop. With the only way to unlock coins being to play a whole track, and you only being able to unlock 10 coins per track, and items ranging from 30 to 200 coins and there being around 100 items to buy with most ranging around 40 coins you can quickly see why only .6% of people who play this game have purchased everything in the shop. Especially considering 90% of the shop is just lazy recolors to pad for playtime.- Annoying ChallengesAlong with the usual online, timed, and grand prix modes present in most racing games, Nick Kart 3 comes with a unique challenges mode, which consists of several mini races in which the player is given a specific kart and character combo and a specific task to complete while winning the race. This sounds fun until you actually try to do the challenges and realize that they seem to have been thought up and thrown in with little to no testing because they are some of the most frustrating things I have ever had the displeasure of trying to grind through. For starters the character combos they force you to play as make most challenges completely luck dependent, for example in one challenge you are required to pull off a few max charge drifts which doesn't sound too bad until you realize the combo you are stuck as is bulky as all hell and has terrible traction on one of the worst maps for drifting. Take this, alter it slightly 47 more times and you have this games challenge mode. Just 48 ridiculously annoying tests of luck and patience. After grinding through it painfully to unlock Jenny, I never went back to touch this mode as there was no point. I can only pray for those poor souls who really really wanted Powdered Toast Man because having to go through what I went through even just 2 more times sounds like torture.- Wack BugsIt would take far too long to explain every bug and wack ass movement this game has thrown at me, but ill name just a few. The timing for slime stunts ranges randomly from incredibly simple to literally frame perfect with seemingly no reason why, The game will just decide "hey you are going backward now" and spin you around with no reason why, the game will completely deny you use of your chief power with no reason why, items seemingly roll a pair of dice to decide what to do when deployed because they rarely ever act the same each use I.E The football randomly switching from tracking to just running straight into a wall, the game will just throw you off course, the game will give your drifts delay, and that's not even the start of it.- Useless StatsStats are pretty standard in racing games. Certain stats handle certain aspects like how fast you go, how much traction you have, how well your kart handles, if you are able to take bumps and dish them out and a lot of games handle it well. Nick Kart Racer 3 is not an example of one of those games. Pro Tip, every stat that is not speed does not matter. If you want to win then you are basically forced to play the combo that gives you the highest speed stat (Sandy Cheeks, Johnny 13, Slime Wheels, Ecto Turbo) I made the mistake of playing with absolutely atrocious speed stats for nearly 20 hours before realizing this and during those 20 hours, I accomplished massive migraines trying to brute force my way through grand prix after grand prix. - Useless CrewmatesAn interesting mechanic that I surprisingly enjoyed unique to this game are crewmates. Crewmates consist of three characters that the player can choose to give themselves boosts in a race. One crew chief and two crew engineers. The engineers give passive buffs while the crew chief unlocks an boost that can be activated when your slime bar reaches max charge (which can be filled by doing stunts, collecting coins or going through slime on the map). This is a very unique mechanic which I found extremely fun. Especially considering the large amount of crewmates the game gives you, it actively allows for some strategy and combos focusing on specific strengths and weaknesses, however this system is not without its flaws. A big one being how useless and stupid many of the crew members are. There seems to have not been much thought put into a lot of the abilities because so many crew members are either reskins with slight changes or just straight upgrades of other options. A good example of this is that there is a crew chief, Brad. Brads power gives you a few seconds upon activation where you can earn coins after hitting enemies with items. Not really a great power but a power none the less. But now consider that there is a crew engineer whose passive buff is to provide coins after hitting enemies, PERMANENTLY, so why would ANYONE CHOOSE BRAD??? He is lit a direct downgrade in all conceivable ways.- RubberbandingIMO the worst offender of anything I have encountered in this game is the absolute braindead way they handle rubberbanding. For those of you who don't know, rubberbanding is a mechanic in racing games that essentially boils down to "if you are super far in first, racers behind you will get a boost to prevent the match from being too easy", it's a decent mechanic in most racing games and serves to prevent you from completely wiping the floor with AI but this game seems to have no clue on what balance means and just jacks rubberbanding up to ridiculously insane amounts. Be prepared to never 100% the grand prix modes because rubberbanding in those is completely screwy. Rather than boost other cars to put pressure on you and punish you for making a mistake, this games rubberbanding chooses to launch every car way way way in front of you, give them a crazy speed boost and actively punish YOU for not getting lucky item boxes. This game will just straight up give unfair, impossible to beat advantages to AI because YOU are doing to well, to punish YOU for actually being good at the game, they chose to just make it a game of "can I get a lucky football to hit the guy in front of me and if I don't I lose and have to restart".Despite everything I've said so far, this is a decently fun game. I love some of the ideas they have, like the slime bar and the unique chiefs and engineers as well as just the loyalty and references to a lot of shows they added. Just remember to pick it up on sale and stick to offline grand prix on any difficulty below hard unless you want to play something so annoying it'll make you want to tear your teeth out one by one.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite several inclusions like voice acting, this game falls flat of succeeding it's predecessor. You're better off grabbing the second game. I'll probably finish unlocking what I can in this one, but getting 100% just isn't happening for reasons I'll get to in a moment.Pros:+ Voice actingWe can finally hear all of our favorite characters being the chatterboxes we know them as, and the vast majority are all voiced by their original actors.+ Good lineup of characters new to this game.At long last, Jimmy Neutron is finally in one of the Game Mill Nicktoons games. Hopping over from Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl is Jenny, Garfield, and Powdered Toast Man.+ Massive improvements on graphic detail from the previous game, as well as resolution options.If you played the second game, you'll notice a lot more detail in the environments of tracks that returned for this game.Cons:- Questionable character choicesWhile it's okay to take notes from Mario Kart, maybe don't include the part where minor variants like Baby Mario or Pink-Gold Peach are included. That's pretty much what Purple Reptar and the Kamp Koral versions of SpongeBob and Patrick are for this game. Also, why remove Tommy? Was E.G. Daily unavailable to voice him? Speaking of being unavailable, why bring back Jojo Siwa if she's still silent? If you're gonna cut corners like that, give us Carl Wheezer since Rob Paulsen is already here as Raphael.- Tedious or impossible to unlock charactersWhile most characters are available for purchase with slime tokens earned during races, Donatello, Raphael, Helga, and Cindy are far more annoying to unlock. Methods include completing fifteen cups, beating all 36 time trial ghosts, playing 80 arena matches, and winning 20 online races. Why change what worked in the last game where most characters were unlocked from completing individual cups?- Some challenges are near impossible.I only managed to complete the challenge that unlocked Jenny by pure luck. Compared to the last game, where you could pick power-ups and your racer to help you, here you're stuck with whatever the game gives you. Often times, past the third set of challenges, a sole racer will be WAY ahead of the rest, and it is increasingly frustrating having just that one opponent ruining you from completing a mission. One mission with Kamp Koral Patrick is also impossible because you can't focus on using speed boost pads and simultaneously find a way to pass that one annoying fast racer way ahead of everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - I'd rate this more down the middle, but I'll lean a bit towards "Recommend" as I don't feel this is a BAD game. Though I'd wait for a big sale, as I don't feel this game is worth its asking price. It has a lot of issues.I played through Kart Racers 2 on Switch about a month ago. Found it to be a fairly enjoyable little game. There are things this game does better, but there are also things I feel this game does worse. There are also a few creative decisions that honestly just baffle me.In terms of driving mechanics, I honestly don't find this game to be much different from the second. Physics and general responsiveness still pretty much feel the same. Drifting can take some getting used to due to its weirdly loose nature, but I never had too much trouble with it. However, one big difference from the second game is that airtime/tricks are much harder to pull off. I can't say I'm a big fan of this, as the fluidity of stunts was a big part of what made the second game so fun. Here, I never really feel like I'm getting that many opportunities to pull off some nice chains.Speaking of gameplay mechanics, I fail to understand the point behind the slime slides. Yeah it's kinda cool blazing through some slime loop, filling your slime bar, hopping over obstacles, and getting a speed boost at the end, but a lot of these slime slides are located in bizarre places that give you no edge whatsoever. In a fair number of cases, it's faster/generally better to just take the normal track.Everything in the shop is just too damn expensive. There's an easy way to grind coins (one of the challenges allows you to back up and collect 5 coins, collect them again, and then hit a wall to end the session), but the fact people are using this method just says it all. A single character costs anywhere from 150 to 200 coins. There's also tons of karts, bikes, paintjobs, wheels, exhaust pipes, crew chiefs, and crew members to buy, most of which is priced similar to characters. You can only get 10 coins out of a single race. Do the math. There's at least no microtransactions, but that should never be something worthy of praise. The in-game prices really need to be brought down a little. This game is fun, but its content does not justify the absolutely abysmal amount of grinding you have to do, and I'm getting sick of racing games that require you to unlock the majority of content through sluggish currency systems.I have a fairly powerful rig, and yet this game still faced truckloads of performance issues. I had to tone down the graphics to "Low" for things to finally run at a consistent FPS, and even then there's sometimes minor frame drops on some tracks. For the record, I can play a game like DOOM: Eternal at its highest graphical settings and pretty much never lose a single frame. This game is sincerely just optimized like crap. I hear console versions suffer similar performance issues.I've also encountered a good number of glitches. At one point I just fell through the floor and had to restart the race, and several times I'd hit a bounce pad or a geyser and just... go right through it and fall off the track. Particularly annoying when I'm dealing with tougher AI and I'm just trying to take some shortcuts, only for the game to decide, "Nah. You didn't hit this."I'm also baffled by some of the character choices. Most of them are fine (there's 42 characters if you get the Turbo Edition), but there are four omissions from the second game. Shredder, Angelica Pickles, and Heffer are now crew-related. I'm not sure if Tommy Pickles is as well. I haven't seen him yet. But he's also no longer a playable character. I don't understand why these four would be omitted when we now have the likes of Kamper SpongeBob, Kamper Patrick, Eastman & Laird Raphael, and... Purple Reptar??? These feel like completely unneeded characters, and I'd much rather have Shredder, Angelica, Heffer, and Tommy back. The rest of the roster feels fine.I can't speak on the online as I haven't tried it, but it wouldn't surprise me at all if it's exactly as bad as people here are saying, considering the amount of issues I've encountered offline.I've been talking a lot of crap, but I'll address a few good points to cap off this review.Despite performance issues, this game still does look good. A little unpolished in some areas, and it won't take your breath away, but it's mostly pleasing to the eye. Environments are detailed, characters have a lot of fun and bouncy animations, and even the karts have some fun cartoony wiggle to them.I feel this game is a bit more balanced than the second. Jellyfish in particular are nowhere near as horrid to deal with as they were in the second game, and while item spam can still be a thing, it feels a lot easier to maintain an edge over the AI when playing on the harder difficulties. At the same time, the AI can perform well enough that they still provide a good challenge.The boats are cool. I'm pretty indifferent to them, but it's a neat aesthetic thing.I'm personally a big fan of the voices. They really do add a lot of much-needed life to the game, and they're varied enough to not be annoying. You'll hear a lot of repeats, but it's not like every character just has two lines or something. Some characters also... don't really sound like their originals, but it didn't bother me much. It's just standard budgeted-voice-acting-in-a-karting-game affair, and that's all I could really ask for.As I said before, there's 42 characters, and there's also 36 tracks. Tack on the fact there's so many karts, kart pieces, and crew members, and there's an absolutely wild amount of content and performance-related customization you can pull off (y'know... provided you put forth the effort to farm for all this stuff).The music is inoffensive. Not bad, not good, just inoffensive. Personally I just found myself playing my own music in the background.All-in-all, it's really not a bad game. There are things I actually prefer over the second here. However, the myriad of issues (mainly regarding performance and the horrendous shop system) reeeeeeeeally holds this title back. It's not worth its asking price. Despite the large amount of content, this is still very much a budget title. The gameplay itself is fine, but it doesn't have the mechanical depth that say... Crash Team Racing: Nitro-Fueled or Mario Kart 8 Deluxe has. If you're looking for a similar experience to this game specifically but at a cheaper price, then yeah. Just get the second... or Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed.Wait for a big sale on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I am thrilled to write a negative review for this game. I loved Kart Racers 2 and honestly this game is better in almost every way. Most of the people leaving negative reviews here haven't put enough time into the game to see that it is far superior to the second. The controls are better, the graphics are much better, there are more tracks, the jellyfish can be blocked by bowbow, and we finally got voice acting.Why am I leaving a negative review then? Yes, the game is SLIGHTLY buggy. I have fallen through maps on more than one occasion. But that is not the reason I'm going to leave a negative review.My main gripe is the game's AI. Dev's PLEASE pay attention!!! The design philosophy is to make every grand prix and every challenge be decided in the final moments of the race. The AI is always adjusting to stay competitive. You have no idea how annoying this is. The first few laps are irrelevant because the AI will almost always allow you to catch up. My girlfriend doesn't steer or drift as well as I do but she is always able to catch up to second during the final lap of most of the challenges. What this means is that in order to win the last several challenges, skill isn't the only factor. You WILL need some luck. When playing a grand prix on fast or insane, you will notice that getting first place in the first 3 races is much easier than the final track. On the final track, the AI increases it's skill level dramatically. How do I know that it's the AI and not just my ability to play consistently? Here's how. If my girlfriend and I are playing a fast /insane track. I can almost always pull ahead by a wide margin. If I'm playing a grand prix by myself, I rarely have this opportunity. It's obvious the AI is adjusts to the level of weaker players. It's much easier to get 3 stars on fast/insane if a weaker player is playing with you.Some of you may say, "Well that's just to make it more challenging." Let me tell you, it's annoying as heck to get first in the first 3 races only to have the AI dramatically increase during the last lap of the last race. It feels like such a waste of time to beat the AI with skill for the first 3 races only to have luck determine the final outcome. And all of this is avoidable if you're playing with weaker players. Devs! Make a consistent AI! Don't waste our time for 3 tracks only to dramatically boost the AI during the final lap of the final track.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a bit of a Mario Kart snob, and I REALLY enjoyed Nick Kart 2! But Nick Kart 3 fell flat for me.Refunded mainly because you cannot change the controls for gamepads and cannot use the d-pad for steering. That was a huge dealbreaker for me, as these were both features present in the previous game. (I am aware I could remap my gamepad outside of the game to achieve the layout I wanted, but that requires more hoops that I would care to jump through and results in on-screen prompts to show "the wrong button".)Other changes I disliked are:-Coming out of a driftboost handles very differently now, not intuitive like how it does in Nick Kart 2 or Mario Kart 7/8.-Steering is smoothed, which makes it less-responsive with rapid changes in joystick direction or when using binary input from keyboard controls.-The new purple slime slides seem like an odd side distraction. Didn't seem advantageous to take them.-The Cups tried to group tracks thematically, but ended up making incoherent assortments or stale/repetitive aesthetics.-The game kept launching SteamVR for some reason, and could not exit unless I ended the program in Task Manager.Some positives:+Any character can use any kart, adding a new layer to stat modifiers.+Significant graphical overhaul, with returning tracks featuring new assets for less-repetitive visuals.+The random Double Dare race objectives are a fun way to spice things up.+Characters are now voiced! (But a lot of their in-race chatter is too lengthy to fit most situations and gets repetitive pretty quickly. (Can be disabled.)I was extremely disappointed in this to the point of returning it. I overall recommend Nickelodeon Kart Racers 2 over this one, even though this objectively should've been an overall bigger & better game. _childDocuments_.review: It's clear that this was made for a paycheck, not out of love.I wanted to give this game the benefit of the doubt, I really did. I was chalking the hate up to the stigma against licensed games. But unfortunately, the game is just as bad as many people say it is. It's not terrible, but it clearly lacks polish that the THIRD iteration of a game should have. There really is little excuse for it.- It really is a grind to get anything in this game, the rate you earn coins is pathetically low, even when dominating.- Lots of unlockables are locked behind online only play. If you don't have friends to grind with or a stable internet connection, you are effectively locked out of a lot of customization options.- The game really is pretty poorly optimized, even for Unreal Engine standards, and may crash semi-frequently.- The boasting about voice acting means nothing because the voice lines are just common quips associated with the character that have almost nothing to do with racing, and it is very distracting. Like they just rung up the voice actors and said "Say the thing from the show we didn't watch, who cares that it doesn't have anything to do with the context of racing?"+ There are some neat innovations here at least, the pitcrew and item systems are neat.But overall, this game is of poor quality, and you shouldn't buy games made by Bamtang. Get All Star Brawl 2 instead, that is made by people who actually care and aren't just shooting out licensed, souless cash grabs like Bamtang. Gamemill, you should be ashamed.

_childDocuments_.review: A bit of a mixed bag, when this game works it's extremely fun and delivers one of the best mascot kart racers experience out there, however bugs are plenty and vary from slightly annoying to incredibly frustrating and almost game breaking, I've hit many invisible walls where I was just driving in a straight line, I've had instances where my Kart sank through the floor, there were races where the placement tracker  looked like it was having a seizure because it didn't know who was where, (I also played offline so those glitches weren't because of lag) I love that the characters now have voices compared to the previous entry,  but some of the roster choices are questionable at best, Angelica and Tommy Pickles are gone (or in the case of Angelica is now a crew member) but we now have 2 versions of Reptar? I actually don't mind that they brought back Jojo Siwa (I get I'm not the target audience) but now that all the other characters have voices, it is incredibly Jarring that she remains mute the whole time (I'm assuming they couldn't get her to record lines, which is understandable, but then why have her be part of the roster?) 2 Versions of Spongebob, 2 Versions of Patrick and if You get special edition 2 versions of Raphael?  Don't get me wrong Mario Kart did the same with Metal Mario, Tanooki Mario, Baby mario etc... but it still feels like there are many more nick cartoons they could've pulled from. Overall I Still have fun with the game and I would recommend it albeit with Major Caveats

_childDocuments_.review: I am not the biggest fan of Kart Racing games and although I may be slightly biased to the game because of my love for these iconic characters, but I can't stop playing this. I have never actually enjoyed a Kart Racer as much as I have this one. It's a Nick game and with Nick games come bugs and things needing to get patched because Nickelodeon is known to not give their devs enough time before release especially now that they are aware games can be updated from what the day one release is so although I can't claim this game hasn't bugged out a few times in my play time, I know that it's something we will see fixed and isn't necessarily the devs' fault nor do these bugs get so in the way that it makes me enjoy my playtime any less and neither should you. It is also honestly a serious dose of eye candy! Anyone who watched Nicktoons as a kid can't be anything less than thrilled with how these iconic locations were adapted for race tracks! Seeing these characters in a bright and shiny new style is also quite amazing and never a dull moment on screen. Some may say its far too chaotic and unstructured but honestly, that's kind of what I love about it and really makes it feel not just like a Nickelodeon game, but a NICKTOONS game! One that captures that wacky and classic feel of the best Nicktoons from the 90s on in a way I don't think many games in the past, even the best ones, always captured so perfectly. So, if you are someone who like me worshiped these characters as a kid, you won't be disappointed with the game! The voice lines make it feel like not only a cherry on top as well, but at least the whole jar of them! I definitely don't like paying big amounts for video games but who does. At the end of the day if you enjoy these characters and you enjoy racing games (which I don't even enjoy them that much so please take it from me that it's incredible!) then you'll be getting your money's worth!

_childDocuments_.review: Nickelodeon Kart Racers 3: Slime Speedway exhilarates both nostalgia and excitement, delivering a captivating racing experience. _childDocuments_.review: I feel that the third Nickelodean kart racer is as good as the second (which I really liked), and definitely better than the first. This one adds voices to the characters, which was sorely missing from the previous ones.                **  In spite of having a max resolution of 1440p, the graphics are bright and colorful and, due to the art style still look great on a 4k display.                                                                                                                                  ** The music is upbeat and energetic.  None of the songs really stick in my head, but they are definitely        fitting. Some of the voices can be a little annoying, but I'd rather have them than not.                                       ** The controls are great.  The drifting feels a little different than other kart racers, but it did not take me        long to get used to it.  Sometimes the drift button doesn't seem to initiate the drifting/boost build up,        but for the most part it works well.                                                                                                                       ** Slime Speedway has a great sense of speed, especially once you get going with boosting, jump boosts,        slide slimes, item boosts, etc.  The speed gets pretty crazy, which is great in my book. I have have mostly        been playing on the middle difficulty.  The higher the difficulty, the higher the speed.                                  ** There are several single player modes (traditional 4 race G.P., "challenges" which are individual events        with varying objectives, time trials, single race, and arena, which has a few different group battle types).        There are also a lot of unlockables which can be won or purchased from the garage using slime tokens        acquired from the races and events. So there is a lot of replay value.                                                                    **  For me, the biggest negative is the lack of cloud saves.  It'd be nice to have my saves carry over to my laptop and steam deck.                                                                                                                                               **  I purchased the game on sale for $19.99, and definitely feel it is worth that price.  It could be worth the          full price depending on how much you like kart racing games and how hungry you are for them.          Thumbs up!!!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a cool game, but one thing is making me contemplate getting a refund while I'm under 2 hours, and that's the fact that as of this review, the game doesn't support cloud saves. To be honest, I don't think it ever will, but it feels like it should. I started playing this game on my GPD Win Max, and when I went to swap over to my main rig, I was unpleasantly surprised to start off at the tutorial again. I tried to think nothing of it, but then all my unlockables were locked again too. That's really lame, epecially in this day and age where PC handhelds are more prominent than they ever have been. So now I basically have to choose where I play this game. The modern convenience of having this game be on a handheld, or exclusively tethered to my nicer looking OLED television. First world problems, am I right? But still, how lame. It really is a cool game from what I played, so I'm kinda beside myself here. FYI, if you're looking for a more critical review, I'll just say, this game does not dethrone the king. If you're looking for a game that's better than Mario Kart, I don't even think it exists. Although this is definitely a competent kart racer for sure, if you aren't particularly attached to any of these Nickelodeon IP's, this is a skip. Straight up, even if you see this on sale, put that money towards Mario kart instead. You'll be a lot happier with yourself for doing so. This game is a love letter to Nicktoons, some of which are ancient by todays standards. I doubt very many people who were born in the late 90's will know Ren & Stimpy, Hey Arnold, Ahhh Real Monsters, Rugrats, Rocko's modern life, Invader Zim... now that I think about it, this game might have been made for 90's kids in particular.Edit:Okay, so new info, and VERY IMPORTANT: Apparently, this game has a ton of unlockable characters unlocked via online play only, and the online is dead. I've tried it all three matchmaking modes, and not a single person joined me. That's going to be a deal breaker to a lot of people, and something to consider when buying this game. I only have 11 playable minutes left to make a choice regarding keeping this game or refunding it, and now that I know this new info, I think I'm going to refund it. Even for the 20 bucks that I paid, this is a bit much for me. Maybe when it goes on super deep discount, I'll revisit this title, but even for its current sale price, I just don't think this is worth it. Too many of the characters require online play, and you'll just never get them without a community to connect to.

_childDocuments_.review: Nickelodeon Kart Racers 3 is a successful attempt at replicating the classic Mario Kart formula with a vibrant Nickelodeon splash. There's a wide variety of characters to choose from, both playable and non-playable. The vehicle customization is robust, letting you choose your kart/bike, wheels, exhaust pipes, and even a cosmetic paint job! You additionally get to choose 3 other characters to serve as crew members, which will perform various things whenever something else happens - think spirits from Super Smash Bros Ultimate! The gameplay itself is as fun as any other kart racer, with a little bit of jank. In Mario Kart, your standard turning radius is small, meaning you'll be frequently using your drift on tight corners. In NKR3, your standard turning radius is huge in a way that makes drifting seem negligible. Also like in Mario Kart, there's a small hop between pressing the drift button and starting your drift. This hop lasts only a little bit longer than in Mario Kart, but that extra little amount makes it easy to mess up your drift direction. You could be holding right when you press the button, then tilting a bit to the left for adjustment, and once you land you end up drifting to the left instead. Or if the stick ends up right in the center when you land, you won't drift at all. The game also mentions drift chaining, meaning once you release your drift you can instantly press the button again to go into another drift without the hop. This was added with the intended effect that chaining drifts together would make you feel almost unstoppable, but because of how loose and sloppy drifting is in this game, most of the time I get thrown off expecting myself to hop but instead I immediately go into another drift. This is another example where the hop length has a negative effect. Thanks to this sloppy drift mechanic, races are filled with plenty of crashing into walls. The items are also a slightly mixed bag, as some are fun references while others are slightly confusing. I found it hilarious when the photorealistic hand from Spongebob blocked my view, but I still don't understand what the purpose of the bowling pins is. Another addition in this entry is that all the characters actually have proper voice acting so races are no longer deathly silent, although sometimes these lines can get repetitive. The final thing I have to point out is the price tag. While this is undoubtedly an enjoyable kart racing game, its $50 price tag is way too steep for what it's offering. However, if you can catch it while it's on sale (like it is as I'm writing this review), it'll definitely be worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though it feels more like an enhanced re-release of the previous game, the changes done to the gameplay and presentation make it a significant improvement. For one, characters are now fully voiced, which adds a nice level of polish. In addition to improving the visuals and a solid soundtrack, a handful of new mechanics were introduced to add some variety to the races.Bikes are now available as an option alongside karts, although I have yet to tell if there's a difference between how they behave. There are boat segments similar to those of Sonic & All-Stars Racing: Transformed, and slide segments where you go on-rails and attempt to dodge obstacles. However, It feels like half the tracks from the previous game got carried over, but they were retooled to include the new boat and slide sections.The only issue I have is that, as of this writing, there's no cloud save support even though it was available in Nick Kart Racers 2, but it's not a deal breaker for me.I realize there's not many kart racers on Steam to begin with, but I'd put this one right behind Sonic & All-Stars Racing: Transformed in terms of how the overall package feels. If you've already played that one to death like I have, this one is worth a look.

name: The Forest Quartet
detailed_description: The Forest Quartet is a puzzle adventure about a gone, but not forgotten, lead singer. Play her spirit and travel through 3 acts unique to the members of her band for a final concert. Face their emotions, solve puzzles and fight the corruption plaguing their souls. Something strange has taken over the once green and lush nature that Kirk would draw his inspiration from. The fungus slowly creeps and turns growth into decay. Use the power of your voice to restore the forest. The forest has become an abyss of darkness. Creatures have awoken from the depths of the underground, swarming JB's house. Find the light that once existed to reignite JB's musical spark. A volcano has erupted, spitting lava out into the nearby forest causing fires and destruction. Find your way as a swarm of butterflies through a maze of pipes in order to reestablish a system of water in the deep underground. Sing to interact with objects, create light with your fingertips. Glide, float, and transform into butterflies to explore the band members' psyches. Environments and objects add unique layers to the soundtrack. Whether it be crackling forest fires or the cold winds from the deep caverns. Live through heartbreak and loss. Recover from grief and restore the band’s musical spark. No written descriptions or instructions, progressively gain powers for your travels. Short and sweet. Can be played in one evening or picked up for a little while every night of the week. Note from the developer: The Forest Quartet is a personal and family made project. The original jazz score is composed by Mads' father (Kaspar Vadsholt), Nina is voiced by his sister (Nina Vadsholt, artist name: NV-4), the soundtrack is performed by select musicians from The Danish Radio Big Band based in Copenhagen, Denmark.

_childDocuments_.review: A melancholic tribute to a deceased singer. I don't know her, and never knew her until I played this and listened to her music, but with heavy heart, I'm glad I came to know of her and her beautiful voice. The game seems to be an homage to her effect on others, and concludes with her song .Unfortunately, this game focuses more on the people that were around Emma, which to me seems to be at odds with what a tribute should be. Most exposition throughout the game is of friends, I'm not sure if they're allegorical or real, talking about themselves. The game in of itself is very short, not more than 2 hours long. Playing as the ghost of 'Nina', you try to bring the remaining 3 members of the Forest Quartet together for a final concert. The gameplay grows in small iteration with each level. The 'puzzles' in the game are very simple and straightforward, but nevertheless it was an enjoyable experience carried a lot by its ambience and art style.

_childDocuments_.review: is an emotional puzzle adventure about a spirit helping the ones she left behind deal with their depression, anxiety and anger in the aftermath of her passing away. It’s a short and touching story about grief and finding the motivation to keep going after suffering a big loss.You play as Nina, the lead singer of a jazz band called The Forest Quartet, who passed away due to an unknown illness. As a ghost, you wake up in a dark and mysterious forest which appears to be an astral projection of the place dearest to the member’s hearts, the place that inspired all their creations, the place that they call “home”. Floating through bizarre shapes that seem to have their own unique heartbeat, vibrating as you pass by, you encounter various broken mechanisms. Using your abilities to float objects, you will reassemble them and then power them up using your voice. Soon enough you will discover that these puzzles have a symbolic link to the broken hearts of the fellow members and by fixing them you will implicitly help them overcome their grief.The game is structured into 3 short chapters, each of them having unique mechanics. Despite the fact that the puzzles have an abstract nature reminiscent of Amanita games, they’re overall quite intuitive and fairly easy to solve. They usually revolve around finding missing components in the immediate proximity of the puzzle area and putting all the elements of a machinery together, activating light pillars in a certain order based on visual clues, or shape-shifting into a swarm of butterflies in order to go through pipes and access certain valves or levers. has not only stunning visuals, but also a remarkable sound design. The elements you interact with produce peculiar sounds, and as you float through the forest you can hear how the entire forest resonates with your moves. I’ve never been a fan of jazz music but the soundtrack and the ending sequence really touched my heart in a way in which few music scores manage to do, especially not tracks belonging to genres I’m not keen on.Despite being short (it took me a bit over 1h to finish the game),  is a memorable experience. It’s simple but beautiful, heavily symbolic and touching.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: There were some parts of the game that I enjoyed, it has a compelling tragedy as a group of musicians lost a lead singer and their passion for playing music, but I feel like too much of this game is 'giving' you a story right away, and not letting you discover it, there is no mystery, there is no suspense, it's more of a healing experience for the characters - the grief is the only thing that has to make an emotional connection, and for me, it wasn't enough to carry the entire game. Now I think a concept like this could have worked better if you showed their relationship with the singer more, we see the characters but we don't see them interact with her in a meaningful capacity, I am usually not a fan of flashbacks, but I think this game could have used more context so we could experience the grief from their perspective. The game is very short, I would say 60 to 90 minutes with no replay value or collection content. There are 3 zones with various puzzle mechanics, although once you understand the controls the game has almost a negative level of challenge, you can pretty much glide your way through the game, which is not necessarily a bad thing, I prefer to play the game for the aesthetic anyway. It's a bit unfortunate that you didn't add any optional collection content, with the game having that vertical movement you could have made some hidden areas for various memories or perhaps some trinkets that would change the color of the character, just to add a bit of a 'game' into what is essentially a linear experience. Maybe a subjective take, but I don't think the game looked all that great overall, with the exception of the second zone where the light would bounce nicely off the narrow paths. This is another thing that I think was good in theory, I think you had the tools and the gameplay to make an interesting level design, but ultimately I feel like you didn't take advantage of it. The most fun I had was when I had to hug the walls in mid-air and connect the dots, I really think you should have utilized verticality in the game a lot more than you did because those few moments were great. (+) I mean as an aesthetic/narrative experience I think you did a decent job, but I think you didn't take all of the opportunities with the gameplay and the visuals that you created, there are so many games on steam that are all about the experience, and so many of them are more compelling, I wanted to get more out of it. Like there are parts specifically in the second zone where the lights create these cool-looking dioramas, I just wish you took advantage of it more, played around more with different color swaps, or have more escapism in the verticality of the scenery. - I enjoyed the game the most whenever you would make big changes in elevation because of the dynamic movement system, I think this is something you should have been doing a lot more, creating navigation escapism by letting the character float around the scenery. Also, I wish you played around more with the color changes and the lights, the second zone feels more immersive because of how the shadows create small dioramas whereas the third zone feels a lot cheaper with the open spaces and bright glowing. - there was no point in the story where I was compelled to speculate or question anything. It's okay to have a simple narrative, but you could have added some optional memories to provide more context for the characters. You want me to understand their grief but I never really learn about their individual connection to the character, perhaps it could have used some individual flashbacks. I think it's better to design the narrative so the player can discover it, like following the breadcrumbs, but you kind of give everything right away and there is not much space to improve. Even though it's obvious who we playing as, you didn't even need to say it, just could have started with the remaining characters and let the player figure it out.Even if you make a linear game about visual/narrative escapism, it's still a video game and you have to understand how the player experiences your game and what makes it more fun. I like the dynamic floating movement in the game, but you don't use it all that much outside of the second zone, you can create so much enjoyable navigation by changing elevation. Even with a linear narrative, you could hide some optional memories and have more context for each character and their connection to the singer, the world is so much more fun to explore even if you make small extra trinkets around the areas. Overall, the game is okay, but there are a lot of pretty games on steam that do the same thing, you can make it a lot better if you make the navigation more meaningful. I liked the concept for the story, but there was no place to go down or up after you gave me everything.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: After losing their lead singer to a mysterious illness, each of the remaining three members retreats to their forest cabin to deal with the loss, the emotions and the doubt about the future of the band. Out of love for their lost band member, they want to play a final goodbye concert as a tribute to Nina, whose spirit you will play as while guiding your former group through dealing with these emotions and lighting their way in the dark forest to the stage.The gameplay is very linear each act, one for each character, contains its own set of simple puzzles that all have different mechanics.You play as Nina’s ghost and use energy blocks on pressure points, turn switches and valves, connect lights in a specific pattern, and chase a shadow figure because they have something you need; use your voice to sing and activate things, even turn into a beautiful stream of butterflies to reach different areas.You’ll never be stuck for too long or grinding your teeth if you are having trouble when solving these puzzles, which in my opinion is very lovely; it makes it so that you can focus more on the overall tone and story.I have a short first look Beautiful painterly art style that is dark but with a core of brightness; would I dare to say almost glowing at the same time. It blends in perfectly with the story and the aesthetics and it only contributed more to making it a great atmosphere and experience. I didn’t know I could like jazz, I never once saw it as my style. Yet the mellow soft jazz has captured my heart. The song at the very end where Nina sings is very beautiful. I enjoyed the music in the game very much.As for the overall sounds, they’re very nice and fitting to the environment and atmosphere.You can either play with a controller or keyboard and mouse.For me, everything went smoothly, no issues and the game does a good job guiding you through what buttons you need and what they do.More of a personal gripe than an overall game issue is that it was a bit on the short side. I wish the game would’ve had more story, more info about each band member, their time together and the fun stuff they went through and so on.Besides that no issues, everything ran smoothly and nicely.In all its simplicity with the fitting jazz tunes, the beautiful visuals and the authentic feeling of the wonderful voice acting; It just all added up for me, I can only conclude I absolutely loved it to bits.I couldn’t keep my eye sockets dry at the very end, as it made me wonder if this game comes forth out of a very personal experience.Yes, of course I do wish it was a bit longer and we got a bit more but, that’s something I always do with games I adore. The 80 minutes I spent going through the game is an experience no one will ever take from me. It felt relatable as it hit home and a powerful message came through. Grief and loss can be horrible and they’re experienced differently by everyone, but know that you’re never as alone as you may feel or think you are.Somewhere along the line, I read that this game was a family effort where the dad helped with the music and sounds. The sister did the lovely voice of Nina. Even if this doesn’t influence my opinion about the game, I still found it very worthy to give it a mention, as it is a lovely detail.There are 14 languages you can choose from at the time of writing this. I also saw an OST and achievements are on the way. And perhaps in the far future maybe even more, who knows.So, if you’re looking for a touching narrative-driven game and it doesn’t bother you that the puzzles are simple or the gameplay is on the shorter side and you like a nice jazzy tune while at it, then this may very well be your cup of tea.I truly hope you can see the beauty of it all as I did if you pick it up and play it.With love, Tchii
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: the puzzles arnt fun.doesnt matter that pretty much everything else (music,story,art style etc.) is done really well the GAME portion of this game isnt good so cant recommend. if you dont mind basically all the puzzles feeling like filler content that requires no brain power and you think the story is cool maybe you will like
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: -  Really liked the music and sound design of this game. Ofcourse the story is about music so there were a lot of opportunities. The song at the end of the game is a great ending.-  The Danish narrator in the beginning really sets a good atmosphere and the radio interview that plays in snippets through out the game was also very well done. It gave a good feel for the different characters and what personalities they had.-  Everything has lots of personality in the game. Whether it is something you are doing or the environment. It all has their own sounds and movements that give it personality.-  I really like the grey guys that walk around and make moppy sounds. They are incredibly silly and tricking them feels funny.-  I like how simple the mechanics of the game are. Nothing is explained with text. There is just imagery. You really get to put things together yourself as the player. Even though the puzzles are not very challenging. It is more about exploring the world.-  Some of the writing could have been better. The pianists levels were a bit forgettable, I didn’t really see the connection with the level and the theme of depression. The bassist portrayal of anxiety could have also been better. It was more acted out as paranoia.  It’s a great small experience, a bit short but with a great ending. Don’t expect to be challenged too much. It is more about the experience and the story.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: There is an honesty to the sort of documentary interviews heard at various moments that make them sound authentic, though ultimately does not lend to very deep characters as everything remains shrouded in a bit of a mystery.Each of the three musicians has its own little special puzzle type, where you activate light machinery to dispel darkness and depression. All are very short stages that lead to approximately 2 hours of linear discovery. None of the puzzles are meant to be challenging. All use very simple mechanics best played with a game controller. Keyboard controls are very awkward and do not lend to an enjoyable experience.This game has to be experienced for its relaxing vibe, sublime visuals and audio. If the trailer does not speak to you, the rest of the game also won't.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks good and sounds good but in terms of story telling it is not that good. I don't like writing negative reviews for indie titles but I really don't think the story was told well. It felt rushed and it didn't left an emotional impact. Look, at the end of the day it is only my opinion. I bought this game and I don't think it is a bad game, I usually like similar games soooooo.....maybe you will like it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: The Forest Quartet offers a special experience by telling a story of sorrow, grief and loss, deals also with topics such as depression and self-doubt. Game and level design is appealing, fitting and artfully created. In my opinion, sound and musical score in general, as well as the sound design for itself, was well done and deserves the most praise, and I say this even though there are also a few points that could be constructivley criticized, when Nina sings in the game, it sounds a bit synthetic and plastic, it would have been much nicer to hear her sing properly, and maybe in a few variations so it's not always the same. In the scenes with the other band members, there are a few places where you can't understand the dialog very well and there are always gaps during the game that could have been filled with more background sound. The puzzles are extremely easy to solve and the game can be completed very quickly. Nevertheless, it is a special game in terms of the idea and the story, as well as the artistic implementation.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: The game is about the death of a loved one and how people struggle to overcome grief but without being too heavy. It is a Triumph. I thought the puzzles were abstract but intuitive and helped pace the narrative well. I know the developer suffered the tragic loss of loved ones and this directly inspired this game.It is a very special game. It speaks of loss, hope and perseverance in a simple and elegant way. Infused with a jazz score and excellent sound design this is a game of feelings and vibes. The dark, scary, creepy figures are very well done. When I became a flock of moths I stayed in the space for a while, taking it in. This game was peppered with beautiful and inspired moments like that. Full disclosure, I am biased because I followed the development of this game as I filmed a documentary that included the developer, Mads. However, I was not prepared for the high quality, originality and overall tone. This game surpassed my expectations. I feel I got good value for my money as a lover and supporter of narrative, indie titles that have depth and meaning. 10/10. Not a long game, not big replayability but a really well crafted experience and one that is worth your time being immersed in, like a good film.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: An ode, a requiem from a family that lost a loved one, for those that have lost a loved one.A very artistic approach on coping with your own brain, while being pressed and tortured by the thoughts of your lost one.Mental issues, grief, self-control and other serious matters are discussed with an amazingly respectful and touching way.I wouldn't really consider the Forest Quartet a video game, but rather a form of digital art. It contains some form of gameplay, but it is rather light and quite uninteresting. The script - although quite sparse - along with the great atmosphere, are two highlights of the experience. Each solution to a (very light) puzzle solving routine, leads you to the next part of a two to three sentence dialog that continues a thought-provoking and touching story.Although the script and atmosphere are some highlights of the Forest Quartet, the sound design, soundtrack, mixing and mastering are from another world. They reminded me of GRIS, another absolutely amazing non-game experience.If you have lost someone dear, the Forest Quartet will offer you a very touching trip to a dark, dark world. If not, since you'll be there at some point, play it with an open mind.It is very short, offering a playtime of about 90 minutes. So, instead of going to the next pop corn muncher movie on the cinema, spend the same amount of money for a unique experience.The whole team that created this gem deserves both the money asked and the admiration of its audience/players.Thank you for sharing, Mads (and Family) and Friends.I hope the Forest Quartet was a way to ease your pain, as it was a way for us to feel it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: As I was playing this game, this *gorgeous* game by the way, I had this sinking thought in the back of my mind. I was enjoying myself as the bulk of this hour long experience is a visual and audio feast, the audio design in particular was kinda blowing me away. But I had this nagging thought. That nagging thought at the back of my head was, "I really hope this one final show is good."You spend the majority of the game quite literally bringing the band back together. A 4 person jazz quartet is now 3 as their singer and sax player has passed, and you play her ghost, slowly breaking her old bandmates out of their homes and neuroses to go out for one last show. I want to mention that there are these interspersed bits of commentary as you play the game, that seem almost like a panel interview of the quartet while their singer was still alive, and working in an industry where I get to see a lot of artist, film maker and musicians panels, I'm so curious if this was based on a real band or not because the dialogue in those sections sounds so much like a real panel. Good dialogue is hard to come by so props there. It happens a lot where a low budget or smaller dev team game build up to an emotional finish really well and then don't stick the landing. I seriously can't convey with words how well they nailed it, my worries were completely unfounded. Each of the band members has their own flair and flourish in the final act and it all gets tied together, as the quartet was tied together, by Nina's lovely voice. I do know that the voice actress and singer that plays Nina is developer Mads' real life sister, and that the score is by his real life father. Huge props to them both. The score throughout feels so right and it kicks in at all the opportune times, and that final song where Nina really gets to let loose is phenomenal. Her voice has this gorgeous, very clear and consistent tone to it, and the song choice was perfect for that "one last show" they were going for. I'm always an advocate for short, sweet indie games you can play in a sitting, and this doesn't do anything special with puzzles or anything, but its more for the visual and audio experience, the story. I had a great time with this game and would highly recommend it to anyone thats looking to kill an hour with a great artistic experience. I review all kinds of games both indie and not, so if you made it this far please go follow my steam curator page, it helps a lot to connect me with devs and get more reviews like this one out (plus I go hard at games that aren't good so I'll probably save you some money at some point lol)Thanks for reading

_childDocuments_.review: I don't wanna call this is puzzle... it's too easy and just walk straight all the way.music and the concept is great but as a game this is not fun game it's boring one, so if you look for a challenge and fun game you should find another game to play I not recommended this one.ps. at first I buy this game because the cover that have 3 instrument so I think it will be a fun game with puzzle about musical but it's not at all...
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: The Forest Quartet tells a story of a jazz band struggling with loss. The band is called The Forest Quartet (as the title suggests). You play as Nina, a band member who has passed away. As a spirit, Nina helps her band members cope with their mental struggles and prepare for a farewell concert.The game is really short, only takes 1 hour. You travel through three chapters, each featuring different mechanics and conversations with the band members. The game indeed includes puzzle elements, they aren't too difficult, but I feel the game more focuses on the emotional story of finding motivation after a significant loss.I wasn't expecting much, but it turned out to be a well-spent hour for a short emotional story, considering its price of around $0.60 at this year's Independent Games Festival. For the best experience, it is recommended to play with headphones.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: The Forest Quartet is a small puzzle game about a deceased lead singer. Journey as her ghost through 3 acts corresponding to the members of her band to perform one last concert. It's a really beautiful and wholesome game/story. I really hope for another part. :)+ Full controller support+ Very beautiful and wholesome story+ I love the art and graphic- No Steam Trading Cards
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the sound design and environmental storytelling did a great job of conveying the mood of each band member. Each puzzle had thematic ties to those emotional states in interesting ways. The music was also weaved into the gameplay in masterful ways; the angry banging of drums and lonely piano tune stood out as the antithetical sounds to a quartet in need of orchestration. Nonetheless, a few parts dragged in my opinion, like the finicky sections of gameplay. I also felt like there was not enough to really get me invested in the characters or their grief regarding the loss of their bandmate and friend. Perhaps it was because it is short experience, or a lack of characterization on the vocalist, but the "saying goodbye" through one final concert did not resonate with me on the level the game seemed to be aiming for. In the end this was a concise, interesting experience that I am glad to have enjoyed, even if it didn't get a standing ovation from me!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: A game oozing with style, great jazz and incredibly satisfying sounds and interactions. The puzzles are simple in the way were they are challenging enough but not frustrating. The atmosphere was great, I really liked travelling around in the forest while listening to the narration and learning about the different band members stories. You can tell there has been a lot of love gone into this game, and I tried hard to fight back a couple of tears throughout the end! Really enjoyed this, I would definitely recommend playing it through in one sitting!
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: The Forest Quartet is a very short and simple Danish indie gameThe audiovisual design is the only exceptional part, everything else, game-wise, is pretty primitive.The story is average, the levels represent depression, anxiety and anger well enough.The puzzles are baby level easy and the overall gameplay is too basic.Not bad for $1 quick run.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: This was a very bittersweet, but gentle and emotional experience. It resonated with me a lot in its specific setting and pacing. I'm not the brightest when it comes to puzzles, but those in this game felt easy enough that the flow of the narration never felt like it was interrupted. To me, this felt like a really good moment of reflection guided by the game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Forest Quartet

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful little game. Do you love jazz? Do you love puzzles? Do you love delving into what makes people happy or sad and enjoy a great story, then this game is for you.I hope they release the OST so I can listen to the music while wandering the city on these cold and dark evenings while I explore the town and meet the people in it.

_childDocuments_.review: gonna update this review once I play through the whole game (I have a few others I'm looking to check out before returning to this one), but so far, I've gotta say, it is a beautiful and enchanting experience with impeccable sound design, art direction, and writing.edit after finishing: yeah, this is a wonderful, heartfelt little game. second game this year where the end credits really added a lot of context that made me appreciate the game all the more. I will add that the music is beautiful too, most obviously with the emotionally heavy ending song.this isn't really a game I think anyone will be replaying for the gameplay necessarily, but I'll certainly come back to it when I want to experience its story, visuals, and music again.as for constructive critiques, I did find the connect the dots puzzles from the violinist's stages to be a tad annoying (at least on controller). the hitboxes for the dots felt a bit finnicky, repeatedly feeling like they would either register with the incorrect dot, or not at all. but these minor rough edges are the only real complaint I have with The Forest Quartet. definitely check it out if it looks up your alley.for more thoughtful recommendations of the best games on Steam, check out my curator, .
