_childDocuments_.review: Simply said, I freakin' love this game. The 100% achievements that I got for this game proves just that.Coming from the Ryza trilogy, I find that the synthesis grid mechanic in this game is a lot more in-depth and not as trivial as Ryza's synthesis loop mechanic. You are encouraged to experiment with different traits in order to get a much stronger trait, unlike in Ryza where you can just throw in the same trait over and over to raise a specific trait to its max level. You are also going to be doing a lot of "give-and-take" when synthesizing items for effects/traits in Sophie 2. There are times when you can aim for a max level effect for each effect in an item, but there are also times when I find trying to aim for a max level for each effect a little bit too difficult since I am focusing on using materials with better traits. Hence I only focus on getting the effects that I truly need for the resulting item. This is also something that would happen to you in any Atelier Ryza game, but it feels even more prevalent in this game, especially if you're just starting out.Worry not though, while Sophie 2's synthesis mechanic is inherently complex, they get less mind-numbing over time. You start out by playing some kind of puzzle game on the synthesis grid similar to that of a Rubik's cube, into playing a strategic game of chess where you'll have to focus more on traits and getting some if not all effects for the item that you're going to synthesize.So how are the other gameplay elements though? Like combat and exploration?I'd say that I prefer Ryza 2 and 3 hack-and-slash combat mechanics. I often find myself spammingon every boss every time I get the chance. Even so, this item will only be available to you once you're getting near the end of the game, so you'll still have to plan properly in order to make your way through certain bosses. Some bosses will also bring up Aura (a kind of barrier that blocks any kind of attack albeit not entirely) more often than you'd think so you'd still need to adapt and find better strategies to defeat the boss.The exploration aspect of this game is somewhat similar to Metroidvania, with a small bit of puzzle attached to it. A lot of the exploration mechanics in this game rely on a weather-controlling device to change the condition of the environment and this weather system will be the key to how you'll be progressing throughout a dungeon. I kinda liked this system, it slightly removes the tedium of having to go through a long dungeon like in most other JRPGs.As for the story though, it was quite a bumpy ride. The story isn't for me at the very least. I do like the characters though, they're very charming and are easily likable, but the entire concept of the dream world felt a little dull to me. That said though, still a servicable story if you're not that serious about it.I hoped that Gust wouldn't give up on Sophie just yet and maybe make a third game. Because there's so much to like about this game, but there's also still so many things in the game that weren't as fleshed out as I hoped it would be. There are not many other games that are as unique as Atelier Sophie 2, and it would be nice to see that Gust would keep doubling down on making more Atelier games in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: My favorite game in the Atelier series -- if you haven't played Sophie 1 though, I highly suggest doing that first. There's a lot of references between character interactions and story that require some knowledge of the first Sophie game to really understand.For any newer fans who came to the series from the newer Ryza games, definitely suggest this game. I think Sophie is a much more fun and interesting character than Ryza, I think the plot and artwork are better, and I think overall the game is just more polished and knows its place more than Ryza (I think Ryza 3 tried too hard to do too many things).Biggest plus to this game is that the alchemy system is FAR better than Ryza in my opinion. Having a clear tree with ways to progress in alchemy, two different alchemists to level up, and a system that is far more intuitive and allows for more puzzle solving than mindlessly placing ingredients, it absolutely surpasses Ryza's systems.The biggest downside to this game in my opinion is the weather mechanics. I think it's cool to have some elements of exploration but if you're looking for a more open-world experience, I suggest Ryza 3, as it actually allows for more interesting movement and exploration. However, if you're looking for open-world, Atelier probably isn't your best bet anyways.Overall, great game. Amazing soundtrack, great alchemy system, stays true to the Atelier series (and in particular Sophie 1) and just one of my favorite games of all time.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time Atelier fan, I tried to like this game, I really tried. But I started to fast-forward the cut-scenes midway through the game.: 9/10: 2/10: 6/10Story is weak, like one of those isekai animes but everything happens in a dream-land created by a goddess with a mental age of 5. As you know, those 'happenings in a dream' sort of stories tend to be underwhelming and this one is no exception. Worse, it's a sequel so the scenario writers didn't even try this time. The end-product is a fragmented, soulless game that's only selling because fans loved Sophie & Plachta. The plot is abrupt, and the second half didn't even make logical sense. It's worse than Lydie & Suelle / Ryza 2 if you want a comparison.I played till the end of chapter 8, where you can start building ultimate gears and grind for end-game contents, I then asked myself "what was memorable about the story so far?" My answer was "nothing", I'll probably forget the whole plot in a few month's time, just like I did with Ryza 2.I started to question do I even want to bother making ultimate gear? Something I did each and every year for the past decade. This is the only Atelier game where I just have zero motivation to finish-off the story, even though I'm 90% of the way through.Hey, at least I enjoyed seeing Sophie & Plachta again. If this is what you are after, go buy it.--------------------------------Shout outs to other game designers and artists they as did a fabulous job. The game is very good mechanically and has beautiful graphics and world design, let down by a poor story. It's very reminiscent of Hollywood making sequels to popular films hoping to duplicate its glory but lands flat on its face.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still very early into this Atelier, but first impressions are very positive. It basically meshes the better aspects of Atelier Sophie with some good aspects from Ryza and Ryza 2, and the end result is great.The synthesis system is very similar to Atelier Sophie on the surface, but the few changes have a big impact. Sophie system was very good, this one also is. Might be my favorite crafting system yet.The combat system feels like a good upgrade, especially with how it deals with stacking buffs and debuffs, and I think is my favorite turn-based combat in the series so far (I haven't played Lulua yet to compare it with that one, though). I particularly really like that it makes you use your "reserve characters" as well, I always appreciate combat systems that do that - makes you care and equip your whole party instead of picking just one single team.The "Very Hard" difficulty is once again decent enough that it can be enjoyable, not being the snore-fest that it was on Ryza 2, though I still think they should just let us pick Charismatic right out of the start instead of locking it behind a game clear. I recommend switching to charismatic (via downloading a save or such) around the time you face your first boss fight.The only issues I have so far is with port quality; it carries the same issues that Ryza 2 has. Stuttering, frame drops, and restricted keybindings for keyboard to the point that I prefer playing with a controller. Atelier Sophie 2 has become one of my favorite JRPGs of all time, alongside some past old classics from the SNES and PSX era and a few more recent great ones. Only issues remain the ones I mentioned above, especially the fact that Charismatic and Legendary difficulty should be available from the start to make the most of a very good combat and crafting system - I fully recommend using a clear data file or cheatengine to enable them.

_childDocuments_.review: I was amazed when a friend pointed out to me how Atelier games never clicked with her until she saw me doing synthesis and winning boss battles using mostly (if not only) crafted items in this game. That speaks a lot for the Atelier Sophie 2 experience that I hadn't truly appreciated until now - one with the most engaging and extensive crafting system I've ever had the chance to play with. I find myself lost in the countless hours gathering ingredients in the fields, calculating and synthesizing items with the best effects/traits possible, and testing them out on the beefiest of bosses I could find. Once done right, alchemy and crafted items can trivialize combat with a few item tosses, and take away the grind that I absolutely hate in other JRPGs. It's a satisfying gameplay loop that keeps on giving.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Atelier Sohpie. It was cute, the pacing was good. It had it's flaws, but overall was a great product. I was looking forward to the continuation of the Mystery Series in the Ryza engine, I thought nothing but good things could come from this. I was very wrong. Oh so wrong. There is just too much, too many things to gather, to many enemies to fight, too many things in your way, too many things cluttering up your map, too many corners cut, to many things to do. It was great at first but it's just overwhelming now in the last 1/4 of the game. I want off Mr Bones Wild Ride. TLDR; If you need this game in your life, chances are you've already bought it and played it, and I hope you enjoyed it. If you're waiting for a sale; wait. This is a $20 game with hours of padding between scenes. Graphics: Cute, design is on par with past games but doesn't try anything new. Sound: Repetitive at times but a few good songs. VA is good. Japanese VA only.Gameplay: Mostly generic for Atelier, trying new things for better and for worse. Story: A-dore-able. It's cute, it's wholesome. It's got Shoujo ai, it's got growth, but a sinking feeling it may not matter in the end. -------Typical Atelier formula, there are materials on each map that are unique, and even in each zone, they are unique as well. Normally this isn't an issue, as it's part of the whole point; find what you need to make the thing to do the thing. But there are almost if not more than 100 gathering points in some zones, and then it adds a mechanic that intentionally or not, **Quadruples** this number. You need X? It's in six different zones, with very little clue as to where in said zone. Good luck. Just gather until you get it. Typical Atelier formula, there is a puzzle in your way and you need to it get past it. To do so you need to use item X(spoilers), which is consumed on use and you can only carry so many, to affect literally a 20sqft radius of the map that turns into a unique loading zone with loading barriers in all four directions. You now need to do this 6 times to get through 6 loading zones to cover roughly 80 sqft total, to get to a single point. But oh no, you're out of Item X. Guess you need to go back to the atelier and craft more and do that all over again to get that last part solved. Yes, each loading zone is only 5 seconds, but tell me why I couldn't use that once to do the same thing across such a small area? There's also no way to know which of the 4 materials you will need, the icon on the map for the puzzle is the same for each one. Each time you change the weather, the materials on the field reload and change completely, including the enemies. They're easy enough to avoid, if you don't want to fight, and if you do, they're easy enough to kill. There isn't much challenge, and that's okay. This is atelier, you build the thing to break the game and one shot enemies. Except they brought back a mechanic to slow this down considerably. Certain enemies have hyper inflated health, and only take 15-20% of damage until you remove a barrier, which takes around 5 turns to remove, more if it's a boss. It's a R>G>B puzzle of sorts, where you can pop it faster if you use the right elements or effects, but some barriers nullify their weaknesses and vice versa, so it just becomes a boring time waster. New-ish Atelier Formula, Major gathering points(MGP) are here, and boy are they here. You have a map with 20 icons+ on it at all times, and it's very hard to parse where you are and where you need to go. New weather mechanic icon, major gathering point icon, new movement mechanic icon, and in the end of the game it's not clear where you need to go and what you need to do. Just get lost and figure it out. Which is fine I guess, but my patience is already eaten up by all the other padding and time wasting this has presented for us. The minigames for major gathering are okay, some are clearly better for getting the best results for a material than others. You can get a piece of ore from an ore MGP, and get up to six attempts(using the best craftable pick) at better quality, more links, more elements, ect. Or. Or... Here me out, you can find a similar ore material from a bug or slingshot MGP and get literally everything using the lowest quality net/sling you can make. You have 20 seconds to play a game of cash shower. Have fun. The synthesis from Sophie 1 is back, and it's better than before, but overcomplicated in ways that aren't even worth bothering with. There's no point in using some of the tools you are given because one or two are just so objectively better and simpler. You can brute force you way through using 5 minutes of time and process X and getting results 25% better than expected, or you can spend 25 minutes using process Y and getting results 27% better than expected. If you want that 2%, that's fine, but it's a rube goldberg system that needs to be trimmed down. This was a cute story, that had some good development and was honestly better than Atelier Sophie in ways, as each character felt like they got their moment to shine, rather than falling to the wayside to be out-shinned by Sophie and Plachta. But it's all soured by mediocre gameplay, and intentional padding mechanics to make this feel like a full fledged Atelier game, instead of a summer side project.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall: long, relaxing game. Play to explore, collect, craft items, and repeat. This is my first Atelier game.The menus, font, and text are all current gen, while the level geometry are last gen. Good candidate for Steam Deck, lower graphics and small file size is amazing for it. As long as you don't expect 60 fps (which you shouldn't) then the game is perfectly playable. Helps that there are Low graphics options. Character animations are last gen, but the facial expressions are top tier. Surprising attention to facial expressions for minor things, such as Sophie's cute reactions to successful recipe unlocks and catching fish. Game difficulty is fairly easy, even on Very Hard difficulty with just a bit of gathering and crafting. You do not have to minmax, even on Very Hard difficulty to beat the game. Combat is very fluid, with good use of camera angles and movements to make attacks feel more kinetic and smooth. Recommend turning on 2x speed after a few hours. Note that status effects are absolutely busted against enemies, try to blitz enemies with items before they can attack your party. Your only danger are bosses, they will nuke you if you don't strike first or aren't ready.There is definitely a focus on the crafting system. The crafting minigame starts off limiting, but you will gain new items that let you expand the crafting minigame and create stronger, more busted items. The game requires you to progress to unlock more tools for the minigame, which lets you make stronger items to progress the story. Discovery of new recipes allow you to gain massive power spikes and completely overwhelm bosses with lots of damage. In order of usefulness, status effects > damage > healing. If possible, stack status effects such as frostbite and curse (physical/magic resist down) in order to do more damage as well as gain TP to do more dual attacks, which let you stack more damage and statuses. Rinse and repeat.The weakest part of the game is the story. The story is quite slow and predictable. It falls into several anime tropes, and the characters themselves are one-dimensional. Thankfully, there's an auto button, a fast-forward button, and even a skip button. Don't play for the story, play for the game and experience.I enjoyed my time and it wasn't too much trouble to collect all the achievements after the main story. I would recommend picking up on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful return to form for the Atelier series. The addition of the weather system is also neat, as it kinda makes it a puzzle to travel through the new zones since some paths open and close depending on what the weather is. _childDocuments_.review: Another Atelier game i picked up - another one that's the 4th game in it's Quadrilogy.What can i say about the game...It's a game that almost does everything it sets out to do right!Like, if a series i am into or something more to my tastes was done on the same level, it would probably be one of my fav. games of all time. I can imagine it's one that ranks quite high amongst Atelier fans.I honestly have no big/major complaints with the game.The Alchemy in this game is super fun - the Elemental tetris and how you need to combine everything to get the item you wanted is pretty fun, especially later on when you get the bigger boards with the different effects and you just go on elemental tetris'ing.If i have one thing to complain about concerning Alchemy is that you can't create multiple items at once (like in Lulua) - but i can imagine that's pretty hard to with Tetris - and you have duplicate anyway if you need an item multiple times - but you can't do the wholesale thing.Gameplay - dungeons and the whole weather thing were fun, and i liked the whole Aura thing in combat, but did they really have to give us 4 characters with delay attacks xD. Also weather in combat could've been used better. Wish more boss battles made me rethink my build and use everything in the system like the final boss did. Still, pretty fun!Characters were fun - especially Rami - and story was fine...but ya know, i think worldbuilding could've been done much better. The NPCs should've had names and stuff, and the quests connected to them instead of the whole guild thing. Would've made me care about the world more. I think that's the one thing the game was turly lacking - world building and NPCs. With Dreams being a centeral point of the game, would've been cool if NPCs and their dreams were more fleshed out and we helped some more achieve their dreams.Music good as expected of Gust - but it is the one aspect where i find it weaker than Lulua. But still pretty high quality!All in all, it was pretty fun - and makes me excited for the series' future - maybe i will become a bigger fan of the series instead of just playing a game every know and then? _childDocuments_.review: I'd call this the best Atelier game to date!This game is a decent entry point, despite being a direct sequel to a previous instalment. If you haven't played the first Atelier Sophie, you'll be missing context about why Sophie cares about Plachta so much, but it's easy enough to get a rough idea just from context and dialogue. There's a recap available if you need it.Graphics are okay, though a bit of a downgrade if you're coming from Atelier Ryza. The characters are well-designed and memorable, as is usual for Atelier.The plot is surprisingly good by Atelier standards. It's nothing groundbreaking or revolutionary, but it has some genuinely emotional moments. I legit cried at the ending, and that's not something that many games can do.The gameplay feels like the ultimate evolution of the Atelier formula. Alchemy is the key: you craft your own equipment and items, so you influence how strong they are and what effects they have. This game's alchemy is similar to other games in the Atelier Mysterious series. You place items on a grid, and depending on which color components they have, the effect bars fill up to upgrade your item. The better your materials, the stronger the result can get. At times, getting the desired effects and traits onto a certain item can feel like a real puzzle.The variety of craftable items can lead to some very satisfying occasions when you struggle against a boss, then get a Eureka moment as you realize that making a certain item would make things much easier. For example, I fought a certain boss whose attacks put my party members to sleep. After some frustrating failed attempts, I returned to the workshop and created some items that cure sleep, making the next attempt much easier.If you play on Hard difficulty, things will get pretty challenging at times. But if you remember to keep making new items, you'll eventually find a way to overcome.This is what I want from Atelier: crafting items to solve problems. And it's why I consider it the best game in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Having now finished Atelier Sophie 1 and 2 as well as Atelier Ryza 1, 2 and 3, there is a pattern in my impressions of the first and second games of both subseries. While Ryza and Sophie are quite different in both their alchemy mechanics and as well as their combat, in both Ryza 1 and Sophie 1 I felt like I overall enjoyed the experience, but felt like they were heavily lacking in some areas:In Ryza 1, I didn't like the bigger focus on plot as I felt it was at the expense of individual character moments, and I felt the alchemy and combat systems were a bit underdeveloped. In Sophie 1 I felt the opposite, it seemed a bit too reliant on the character events while missing a bigger plot tying them all together. And the combat felt a bit too simple as well.Then Ryza 2 came and became my favorite entry in the series as it fixed its weaknesses and built upon its strong sides (although maybe the plot took a bit of a hit).Finally getting to the game this review is supposed to be about, and my impressions are the same as with Ryza 2, as Sophie 2 is now tied with it as my favorite game in the series so far. Like with Ryza 2, in my opinion this entry is just straight improvements across the board compared to Sophie 1. Combat has gained a lot more depth, additional alchemy mechanics were added and the synthesis is just pure fun, easily my favorite from all Atelier games I've played so far. There is now a more tangible plot tying everything together in a pretty cool and unique setting. Nothing groundbreaking in the story department, of course, this is still an Atelier game where that is not the focus, but much better than Sophie 1 I'd say.The character events and interactions are still there, although if I were to mention one personal nitpick, this would be it. Since the Atelier series doesn't take itself very seriously, I've come to enjoy the characters that are more on the unique, quirkier and funnier side, rather than the universally friendly or serious types. But Sophie 2's main cast is just a little bit "less weird" than I would have personally liked for me to remember them, like how I still remember for example the clock maker guy from Sophie 1.Being a lot more modern, there is also simply a lot more polishing and quality of life compared to the older and glitchier PC port of the first Mysterious subseries game.TLDR: If you've enjoyed Sophie 1, I don't see any reason why you couldn't enjoy Sophie 2 as I feel it is just a straight improvement in almost every regard. If you didn't play Sophie 1 but are interested in this entry specifically, I also think you can still check out Sophie 2. You'll miss out on some payoffs due to missing some character backstories, but that's not the main reason you'd play these games anyway. Although I'd advise you to check out other reviews that go more into the details of this title specifically to see if it's something you'd vibe with.

_childDocuments_.review: Fourth release of the Mysterious series. The time line is situated between Sophie and Firis. (Mysterious series: Sophie > Sophie 2 > Firis > Lydie & Suelle)When this title got announced, I actually wasn't really hyped for it. I had really hoped for the follow up of Ryza 2. That said, I found Sophie 2 to be a really pleasant experience overall, to the point that I think that Ryza 2 has already been dethroned as my favorite Atelier game. There wasn't a single gameplay element that I disliked, I enjoyed them all. However, there was once again a lack of english voice, which can be a dealbreaker for some people, so there's your notice.You play as Sophie, who has decided to leave her hometown to become a licensed alchemist and help Plachta return into a human body. However, this is a video game, so obviously something happened. Hehe.There is no time limits in this title. The exploration part of the game is very similar to how it was executed in Atelier Ryza 2, with a few things exclusive to the universe of Sophie 2. The similar things are the huge maps that allows enough freedom to extends towards a side map every so often and each gathering spots have 3 tiers of items tied to them, making it so lower level areas aren't completely worthless once you reach the midgame. The unique exploration elements to Sophie 2 are the Major Gathering Spots, an area altering feature and the Ability Points.-The MGS allows for the customization of the item gathered, which is decided by the player, by playing a mini game, depending on the Tool used. This essentially lets you target specific element patterns, allows for more links on the item or even aim for higher quality values. There is also a "currency" option, but I found it to be completely useless from the getgo. -Without spoiling too much, each areas have slight variations to them, which contains different monsters, gatherable materials and certain paths will be different. -Ability Points are gained by a character leveling up, when finding Landmarks or when completing "Party Quests". These points can be spent to upgrade the characters' stats or to improve your exploration experience, and as APs are spent, characters will have their skills upgraded, which gives the player a sense of character progression outside of Alchemy. After having played all of the Atelier titles on steam, I can say that Sophie 2 has my favorite turn-based combat system of them all. Not only does all characters can use items, albeit non alchemists with limitations; like in Ryza series, but standard Assist Commands and Ultimate Skills have been improved by so much. -As usual, Assist commands requires a certain gauge, gained as actions are taken in a battle. You are not longer timed when an Assist Command pops up, which means you can take your time and properly think, and even back out if needed (for Support Attacks). Support Attacks allows you to switch the front character with one in the back, while also allowing both of them to use a skill or an item. Support Guards aren't special by themselves, but the Defend action in this game can be customized a little bit through the use of the new equipment slot: Talisman, allowing you to proc various effects when attacked while defending.-Ultimates in this game are made between a pair of characters, without needing the second character in the frontline. This gives a character 3 options to choose from at any given time. The availability is kept in between battle, like older titles.Additionally, debuffs aren't completely useless in this game, as they can be useful to deal with a certain mechanic that often happens during combat. The alchemy is about as much as you could expect from Atelier Sophie, with some improvements or new features. If you like to do puzzles, you will probably enjoy it, but if you despise them, you will probably dislike the alchemy of this game. As you complete friendship events throughout the game, you will gain link abilities for each element, giving you a bit more control over the board. There's also a "Cauldron" like feature later on.The overall experience was one of the best I've had within the Atelier franchise, if not the best. Same as its prequel, it is a fairly relaxing game. While I did enjoy Ryza 2, there is somethings that I didn't particularly like about it. In Sophie 2, I liked everything, minus the lack of english voices anyway. The OSTs were great. The combat was fun. As I enjoy puzzles, I enjoyed the alchemy too, The story was alright, although be a bit cringey at times. I really like the Ability Point system, and the new Assist Commands behaviors, and hope that they will be brought back in future titles that uses turn-based combat, as it gives a solid progression system for characters that the Atelier franchise usually lacks. I'd say this title is definitely worth the full price. My Play Order at the time of this review:1. Mysterious series (Sophie +, Firis -, Lydie & Suelle +) // 6. (Sophie 2 ++)2. Arland series (Rorona +, Totori -, Meruru ++) // 4. (Lulua +)3. Ryza series (Ryza ++, Ryza 2 ++)5. Dusk series (Ayesha +, Escha & Logy ++, Shallie +)

_childDocuments_.review: There are so many good things that I wanted to say about this game, which make this game the top Atelier game for me, right behind Mana Khemia and Ar Tonelico.The QOL in Ryza 1 are improved a lot in this game: - List of available (obtained/not obtained) drops on every gathering spot are shown on every map AND on every gathering spot. It's not something necessary since there's no time limit in this game so we don't need to be selective when choosing gathering spot. But a very good QOL nonetheless. Very useful when doing requests or hunting specific mats/monsters.- They also brought back the small chibi head icon showing up on maps whenever a new event available. Kinda disappointed they removed this from Ryza 1.- Fast-forward button in events are very useful to reduce the time following the story.- Auto-save feature is available an an Atelier game (finally!). This game crashed several times on SteamDeck and it only ran smooth with low graphic setting, so auto-save is an auto-win solution.Huge graphic improvement especially on characters models compared to Ryza 1. I especially don't like the shading on the Ryza 1's 3d character model faces. They looked jarring for some reason. I'm so glad they don't use the same style for this game.Gameplay-wise, there are many things they brought back from previous Mysterious games and Ryza 1:- Night time doesn't make monsters aggresive (stronger), just like in Ryza. There are traits that can make characters stronger depending on the time of day, but there's no way I use those situational traits on top of Dragon God's Blessing traits lol- The changing weather mechanic make the maps feel so dynamic (different enemies/boss/gather materials/terrains on each weather).- Camping feature from Firis is available here, though it's kinda useless because the game is not open world and we can instantly go back to the Atelier. Using camp is consuming item as well so it's another L.- Love that it retains the usual synthesis mechanic from mysterious series. it was fun because it performs like tetris and easier to get items with high quality.They went back to the usual full turn-based battle mechanic instead of semi-action like Ryza 1. To be honest I like Ryza's battle system a lot, but there are few things that Sophie 2 kind of different compared to other Mystrious titles:- Battle speed x2.0 is available here. I love seeing this feature on my turn-based games.- Twin actions make the battles in early game piss easy. you can just spam it and the enemies die in 5 seconds. Ultimates are called Dual Trigger and are activated with two characters instead of one.- By pressing R1/RB we can see which character the enemy will attack in their next turn by pressing, making the battles easier because you can make the characters guard beforehand. But you'll end up not using it 99% of the time. Sophie 2 OSTs for me are more memorabble here compared to other Atelier games. There are few that caught my attention when exploring. Most of the time though Atelier OST are usually forgettable.Story and character development/interactions are what made Sophie 2 shine the most among other Atelier games. I love the premise. There are depressing moments especially at the beginning. The interactions between not only the playable characters, but NPC are done so well.It has higher standard for a Atelier game for me than what I've experienced before. So I'm glad I've experienced it until the end.The only con that I could give to this game is that container is way too small.There's no way to extend container like in Lydie&Suelle so near the endgame you'll spend some time removing unwanted materials every time you go back to the atelier. This is kind of annoying because every map gives a lot, I mean A LOT of loots to pick up. If you're a hoarder in an RPG like me, you'll end up meeting this obstruction point sooner or later.---Hours later into working, and I'm still thinking about the ending.It's similar to the ending of TLoH: Trails in the Sky 3rd. But this time I cried like a baby. It was sadder than I expected. I didn't believe it when that happened. I cried because of an Atelier game. The last time I cried because of a game is at the ending of Tales of the Abyss.I love Sophie so much as an MC. For me, both her looks and personality are league better compared to other Atelier MCs.I'm sad that her journey has finished long before I played this game, but I had to force myself to uninstall the game today so that I can peacefully move on to the next stories. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is an Atelier game -- a long-running series of JRPGs focused on character interaction, item crafting, and questionable fashion choices. Specifically, this is the fourth game in the Mysterious sub-series. If you haven't played an Atelier game yet, it does feature a "the story so far" option to catch you up on plot details, but it will spoil you on Atelier Sophie. The systems are the most streamlined in the series, making it a good starting point for those who don't mind spoilers, but this review is targeted those who have played an Atelier game before.There are four aspects to Atelier games: exploration, combat, synthesis and story.Exploration: Sophie 2 features solid fast-travel and greatly reduced ingredient grinding thanks to the new "large gathering location" feature. You won't find a ton of interesting secrets but some items are only available in chests. The weather mechanic can occasionally make for an interesting "how do I get over there?" puzzle, while bringing variety to individual areas, but doesn't fundamentally change things. Movement is fast and smooth, though jumping is still a bit weird. Overall, Sophie 2's exploration is satisfying and streamlined if not exceptional.Combat: Sophie 2's combat is excellent. All of the combat features are at least somewhat useful, and difficulty is the closest to "balanced" the series has been in a long time. Admittedly it becomes a bit easy at the end, but only one out of three people who finish the game do so on Very Hard. The new aura system encourages tactical variety and the new stat bonus/penalty system is more powerful, clear, and rewarding than previous iterations.Synthesis: Item creation is what separates Atelier games from other JRPGs and, after the disaster that was Ryza, going back to the best synthesis system in the Atelier series is a relief. The pacing isn't perfect -- an avalanche of new options show up all at once midgame which is a bit overwhelming, and in the endgame crafting perfect items is more a matter of patience than cleverness -- but it's still deeper and more rewarding than the crafting in any other RPG by multiple orders of magnitude.Story: Not in the same class as Lydie and Suelle, which is a shame -- this is the only area Sophie 2 doesn't excel in. It's not a total loss, though: a couple of touching moments and a largely inoffensive cast meant I didn't skip cut-scenes. The single ending may disappoint those who love the series' traditions, but it means a lot less confusing grinding during the endgame.Overall, Sophie 2 is a heavily streamlined, well-paced, enjoyable game. It is certainly in the top tier of the series' 3D entries and even has a claim on the top spot despite its mediocre story and flat characters.  It's a great use of 60+ hours, and a reason for optimism about the series' future.

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed my time with this game. Most of my time was spent preparing as much as I possibly could. 999 quality, the best traits I could get at any moment, and when farming opened up, same there too. Unfortunately, on VHard, playing like this made the game's difficulty an absolute comedy-fest: frequently taking 1 damage from enemies and then proceeding to obliterate them in 1 hit. I didn't use healing items. Let it be known: party level barely matters. Your equipment is far more important. I was underleveled the entire game.It wasn't until the last quarter of the game that I downloaded a system save online and swapped my difficulty to Legendary. A welcome surprise when the next boss I fought proceeded to wipe me off of the map.I've seen a number of complaints about the aura gimmick, and I'll be honest, auras were shattering left and right for me early on, so much so that the gimmick basically shouldn't have existed. It wasn't until later on where enemies started resisting statuses that the auras became a bit of a challenge (though then there were other solutions).The story hit home more than it should've tbh. _childDocuments_.review: For context, I've never played the original Atelier Sophie or ANY of the Mysterious Trilogy games. I had heard that this game doesn't require any background and that the original Sophie hasn't aged as well comparatively, especially coming off of Ryza, the only other Atelier series I've played. So what did I think? Well...I had a lot of fun! Combat is done in turn based style ON the map, alchemy is done via puzzles, and Sophie is just the most adorable thing. The game has so much charm to it that it's an easy recommend for any lover of JRPGs.Now the game isn't without its gripes. In particular by the time I reached the end I was ready for the game to be over, but it was such a slog to get through. You beat the final boss? Well I hope you've been collecting recipes and synthesizing a bunch because now you've got to create a brand new item that you probably don't have the materials for. And after you DO create it...settle in for at least another hour of cutscenes. It doesn't make the game itself any less fun...but I'd be lying if I said it didn't try my patience after a while. Another gripe would be late game recipes are needlessly complicated. The game essentially forced me to choose between Quality, Effects, and Traits...which was extremely frustrating whilst I was trying to make everyone's end game gear. But hey...that's probably just a skill issue.So overall, I do think this was a really good game. I may have even gotten interested enough to go back and play the original Mysterious Trilogy. I'm sure I'll miss some of the QoL features added in this one...but hey, more Sophie can never be a bad thing!
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: With a lot of the recent new releases for older series, it felt like they were just fan service and to a point even cheapened the original games. This game thankfully does not do that. It helps bridge the gap of Sophie going from a novice alchemist unsure of herself, to the confident and strong mentor we see in Atelier Firis. This game has heart and makes you really enjoy the characters. Usually there's at least one main character I can't stand, but I truly loved all of the main cast. This game is definitely a love letter to Atelier Sophie fans, but it's a great title in the franchise and stands on its own.
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: Gust is on a weird improvement spree. Ryza 1 was decent but Ryza 2 was better in every way. Blue Reflection is (apparently) mediocre and Second Light improved everything except battle themes. The first Sophie was just okay so Gust decided to make Sophie 2 one of the best Ateliers instead.The story no longer feels like something tacked on to the game at the last minute. There's actually something going on in the story all the time. You don't even have to find new recipes to progress the story for more than two dialogue lines at a time. The story itself is just okay but it is still better than the almost non-existent story in the first game. Hopefully Gust will eventually make stories that are more similar to the older games. Those were more interesting than the stories in Mysterious and Ryza.Sophie 2 has easily the best combat in the series. Higher difficulties now have proper difficulty curves and there is more than one difficult boss fight in the story. The combat mechanics are great and the higher difficulties show how fun the combat is now that you consistently have to think while fighting. The combat does get much easier at the end though. At least the final boss isn't annoying like in the other Mysterious games though.Tetris alchemy is still the best crafting system in video games. It is still a crime that no one copies the crafting from Atelier. Please, someone copy even one thing from these games so I don't fall asleep while crafting in other series.While the gameplay is the best in the series, the characters are still dull like in other Mysterious games. Their personalities and side stories aren't interesting. It is also weird how generic the male characters are since the previous Atelier actually had interesting personalities. Dull characters must be the price for Tetris alchemy.The only actually disappointing part of the game is the soundtrack. Gust's games have always been great albums with a bonus game but the soundtrack in Sophie 2 is just okay. Unlike what I used to write in this part though, the old soundtrack is actually free DLC. You can ignore this complaint now since you've got other 10/10 Gust soundtracks to listen to.The boring party members and okayish soundtrack don't ruin the game though. Sophie 2 is still one of the best Ateliers. Ayesha is still the best Atelier though. (Is this a good time to ask for Ayesha 2?)
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: Chronologically this game takes place after Atelier Sophie and before Atelier Firis. So I think you can play this without playing the other Mysterious series games ("Atelier Firis" and "Atelier Lydie & Suelle")Overall I had a really good time playing this game, but it was a bit of a time sink. There is a lot of variation between ingredients which makes it take longer to pick and organize ingredients for alchemy. The actual alchemy system is quite puzzle based, and it can take time to solve the puzzle compared to other games.The combat is fun, and they brought back the system of swapping characters mid battle, so you will actually use all your characters. one slightly annoying thing is that most of the random enemies have "Auras" which are basically shields that you need to break. These auras are interesting in boss battles. But these make regular battles unnecessary long, at least until later in the game when you have abilities to break auras faster and deal enough damage through them without needing to break them.In terms of story  this is a very a very slice-of-life feeling game.
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: *Spoilers for the first couple hours of the game*If you're quick about it, within the first 5 hours of the game, you can tear open a hole in the fabric of reality to reach a realm beyond space and time to beat the hell out of god in an attempt to save Sophie's teacher/"family" member, Plachta, who, in turn, had her soul ripped from her automaton body of which Sophie was trying to replace with a living breathing human body, ignoring any possible moral ramifications that may come in creating such a vessel.Everything in this game is so metal, but the way it presents itself is so feel-good, warm and friendly that I can't help but witness in awe as Sophie, one by one, fells both demon and god in her quest to help her companions and sort out their problems with the wonderful power of alchemy, family, friendship and good fun. Pick it up if you're interested, and if you're not, pick it up on sale, it's a nice feel-good experience!
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game. I hit 140 hours, but I'm a really heavy crafterIt was an overall wonderful experience. The game also gives you a lot of slack. I eventually had it at max difficulty. If you played the other Atlier Mysterious Games, get this one. This game also felt pretty easy, but then again, I did play the entire Arland saga.  Some complaints: you start out at Level 20 and there's a Level 50 limit, though it kind-of makes sense because everyone is experienced. I would feel more growth if the level limit was 60-70. That might stray from the Mysterious limits though (Sophie is in the Mysterious universe). Lots of nice interactions, especially with Ramziel.
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: Our "mysterious" waifu is back!!This is my 10th Atelier game I play. Sophie is super cute, beautiful!! I ran out of adjectives to describe how cute she is LoL xD, a gorgeous and colorful world!! even the NPCs are cute, the central town and indoors are exquisite detailed!! And even the Sophie clothes are very detailed too, and moreover, her skin is a different model than her coat, for example look at her arms and you will notice, even the fabric seams project shadows over her!!! Check in her back, the seam in her coat, its shadow changes if you move around... I really like how much love they put into even those details!Gust already offered a high quality technical level on their games with Blue Reflection Second Light in past November 2021, and now they improved even more!! I'm happy for them.As always, a cast of female characters charismatic and cute, and also interesting male characters, you know, the "bishounen" type.The combat system was improved. We have back the turn-based system and I think is totally right because the Mysterious series always had it. I can't imagine a Mysterious game with the real-time combat system of Ryza series, for example. So a good decision of Gust, fortunately. +1 for them.Melodies: beautiful, orchestrated, totally connected with an Atelier game as always, so much that I could hear the soundtrack in my free time or even at office. I like it.But, by FAR, the BEST aspect of this game is the story, or at least its foundations: Even though we already know about how the Mysterious series ends in Lydie & Suelle, and specially what happens with Plachta in the end, Gust really managed to tell an original story about one of many adventures Sophie faces throughout her journey, so it feels refreshed. No previous knowledge of previous Mysterious games is required and it offers a decent summary of how Sophie decides to embark herself in that journey with two objectives. A simple but effective way to get into the plot. Of course, I would recommend to play the complete series to enjoy even more. So if you get interested, go ahead.I'm happy Gust brought this beautiful game to us, the fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist & The Mysterious Dream is both a love letter to the series’ past and a bold step towards its future. I was thoroughly impressed by the game’s ability to merge gameplay found in Ryza with the gameplay of the older titles without ever feeling as if it needed to compromise either. Nearly every new element it introduced felt like a logical evolution of past ideas, to a point where I’m surprised that some of them had only been introduced now. Although it has a small number of cracks holding it back slightly, Atelier Sophie 2 was an absolute delight of a game, and easily my new favorite in the series.

_childDocuments_.review: Best Atelier game yet. Has the great duo of Sophie and Plachta with all of the quality of life improvements of the later "Mysterious" Games and the graphics of Ryza. Perfect for a comfy grindy rpg afternoon.The main story, never really the strength of these games, is still somewhat lacking but is more interesting and gripping than any of the Atelier games I've played. We still get the variety of characters and the mini interaction cutscenes with them as we get to know them more.Combat is a bit like Lydie and Suelle but more refined. 3 people in battle and 3 in support with skills allowing you to swap them more or less at will.Crafting is the Tetris style "fit all your materials in the pot" of past Mysterious games with "Links" being the mechanic to increase max effects. Can be very in depth if you want it to be. The trait transfer and combination system works just like the previous games.My only real critique so far is the weather system. Although I like the idea of changing the areas to allow different places to be explored, the items to do it have to be recharged between uses. The items hold 20 charges each... but you end up changing the weather A LOT and it can be a hassle having to stop and go back to refill. That and weather can be changed in battle which feels a little shallow and more of a binary "Either the enemy is buffed or debuffed" system. I feel it could have been fleshed out more.
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Sophie and Ryza, you'll love this. Nothing radically new, just an improvement and refinement to the crafting-heavy rpg format. l The combat sees the biggest improvement, bringing back features from Dusk trilogy: you can now have allies block or assist with an attack, and basically choose who takes the blow. You can also see who a monster is targeting ahead of time, so you can plan strategically. Also further visual improvements and minor QOL changes to crafting. As someone who has played every Atelier game released - this is their best work and possibly the best place to start the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: I am just barely at 1 hour in and I can safely say that this is the best Atelier I have ever played. For one, Sophie! Shes my favorite alchemist and being able to see her story continue is amazing. Second, the story is extremely intriguing and is very unique. Third, the graphics are simply breathtaking!
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: Great addition to the series, One of the synthisis I liked the most was Sophie one because it required some thinking about how and when to put certain items into the recipe in order to squeeze the best results out, but it also took a lot of time because of how important item order was to where you could spend a long time trying to figure out how to get two different things to the next threshold. This new synthesis (of what I have unlocked so far, none of the advanced stuff yet) keeps the puzzle aspect but does it in a way to respect the players time a bit more. The item refreshing took a middle ground between the more punishing when it is gone it is gone and the too easy of return home and it gets fully recovered and added a cost to recovering items charges, so somewhere right in the middle of the two extremes making gold actually useful something I never really used in other games since I always crafted my stuff. Now to the more unique part of this entree since Synthesis and item counts are basically tweaks half way between Sophie and newer games.The changing level mechanic, it is an interesting way to add a lot more maps without adding a lot more maps, I am not totally sold on it yet but it does add a level of puzzle design to the levels. All in all a great addition to the series.

_childDocuments_.review: TENTATIVELY, yes, I recommend this.  Having finished the previous game, though, many things starkly stand out.1.  NO ENGLISH DUB.  For those who, like I did, started with Sophie DX because that's when they removed the time limit on the games, going from a good English dub to no dub at all is not only a shock, it's downright annoying, as I'm used to hearing the English and watching facial expressions.  Now, I have to read everything, and the graphics of conversations are a total waste, because I can't see them for all the reading I have to do.  If you have a problem with reading captions, this is NOT your game.  This wasn't a problem in Sophie DX.2.  Significant lag in the input process.  In the previous game, my XBox controller inputs are fast.  In this game, I find myself having to hit a button 2, sometimes 3 times, because there's a delay in processing my input for some unknown reason.  This should have been tightened up prior to release.  Mind you, my computer is less than a year old, and pretty much top-speed.  This shouldn't be happening.  When you have to gather tons of crafting resources by hitting the A button each time, this annoying frustration builds up rather quickly.  This wasn't a problem in Sophie DX.3.  Camera controls are FUBAR.  I had to disable the auto-follow feature because the camera would get "stuck" at times, resulting in repeating camera jumps so bad it could cause motion sickness.  I have to control the camera at all times.  This wasn't a problem in Sophie DX.4.  Run speed in the open world is way too slow.  Yes, you can warp to sections of the main map, but you have to find the warp crystals first and activate them.  Even then, the open world maps are huge compared to Sophie DX, and the run is a LOT longer than it was previously.  While the scenery is beautiful, the long time it takes to traverse a map makes me feel bored eventually.  I'm used to the smaller but more numerous maps of Sophie DX.5.  You can't talk to everyone, and you can't go in most buildings.  You have to look for conversation icons to talk to people, and you have to look for location icons on the map to see what buildings you can enter - and you can't enter a lot of them until the story progresses.  I call this "GTA 5 Syndrome", where the majority of the gigantic map is useless scenery.  I know a lot of places will open up soon in Sophie 2 DX, but it's annoying to not have them available from the start.6.  LOTS of invisible walls (especially around the Dream Tree).  Also, you can't jump off of small hills in one accessible area to land in another accessible area - why even have the jump function?7.  One of the first craftable items in Sophie DX was a healing item (Berg Medicine, IIRC).  There isn't one at first in Sophie 2 DX.  I'm afraid to get into most battles, because I only have 3 weak characters and no way to heal them.  Mind you, there are boss-class monsters on the map FROM THE BEGINNING.  I ran into one, and just barely managed to run away.  I've made over a dozen recipes, and still no decent heal items.  Considering this is Dream Land, you'd think they'd have heal stuff available from the beginning.8.  The new synthesis process is a bit random.  Your cauldron exhibits different bonus symbols that make recipes better, but they differ by recipe and probably at random (I haven't checked in detail).  I've gotten some outstanding items, and then some mediocre items from the same recipe due to placement and number of the bonus symbols.  If you want to understand how to make items of high quality, you will need to go over the process more than once, as the tutorial is not enough.  The whole links vs. lines thing just doesn't make much sense.  This was not a problem in Sophie DX.9.  The beginning of the game is running back and forth a LOT.  Also, when you complete quests, it likes to teleport you back to town, even if you don't want to go yet (you know, pick up a few more ingredients on the way out then fast-travel back would be nice so as not to have to make two trips in short succession).  The game drags you around a lot, at least in the beginning.  This was not a problem in Sophie DX.10.  The combat system is radically different.  If you skip the tutorials, you will miss out on the combo attacks that the characters now have (as opposed to the characters auto-assisting in Sophie DX).  Also, the combat selection menu is a tiny vertical menu on the lower left side of the screen, and not very visible, unlike in Sophie DX.All in all, it seems from my very limited time playing this game, that this game is more like a beta-test rather than a full game.  Many of the functions that were smooth in Sophie DX are clunky now, and slower to use.  Problematic controls that should have been fixed were left as-is.  Some design decisions should have been re-thought.  It's unlikely that these problems will be fixed, based on the game's update history, so if any of these things are a non-starter for you, don't get this game.  I hear the Ryza series is better, but I haven't played it yet.  If you're into the story, though, the story seems as good or better than Sophie DX.  You just have to suffer through all the jankiness.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is unimaginably SHALLOW and REPETITIVE, everything becomes a chore after 20 hours of gameplay when the novelty value has gone. The major problem is the broken combat mechanic and shallow alchemy mechanic, I beat very hard mode using the same simple tactic, don't even care what bosses do.Pros:- Voice actingCons:- Repetitive gathering. Even though you know most of what you're gathering are useless, you still need to gather a lot materials. How to gather? Just press 'Q' or press with timing.- Shallow crafting (alchemy) mechanic. It's all about accumulating traits to get better number, you can get +20%, +30%, +100% critical hit rates, or +20%, +50%, etc item damage, or +1 +2 +3 DEF buff. In early game, I crafted one item to get +2 DEF +2 ATT +1 SPD -2 DEBUFF +100 HP to team members, and everyone can use it. Using this item throughout the game makes very hard mode pretty easy. You can craft much more powerful items like bombs, but it's just about accumulating traits together, becomes boring quickly. I don't have any end game weapon because the I'm tired of crafting and I know they just have better number, nothing special.- Repetitive crafting (alchemy) gameplay. It was fun during early game, you can think of it as a little puzzle game, but playing it throughout the game for 100 hours is boring, I literally don't wanna craft anything in late game, but the game force you to upgrade your alchemy level to progress.- Shallow combat mechanic. There are many elements in the combat like passive skills, switching party members, breaking shield, etc. Looks complex, but all you need to do is to keep buff on your team members and keep debuff on boss, and to follow some simple instructions like using fire if boss is weak to fire, not using magic if magic triggers counter-attack.- Similar team members. Everyone is tank with block pose, everyone is dps, healer, etc. Buff/debuff is the only thing you need to consider in combat, and everyone can use crafted items to buff/debuff. Anyone died in combat? Don't panic and no hurry to rescue them, because everyone else can do the same thing.- Shallow upgrading mechanic. There is NO skill choice, you spend upgrading points (TP) on something like +5 attack or +10 speed or +2% critical hit chance, etc. Yes you feel you grow each time, but it's not fun.- Repetitive map and puzzle. Throughout the game, you solve puzzles by using the same skill called changing weather, it works like this, go to place A to change sunny to rainy, now you can access place B, change it to thunder, then the door in front of you will open. Repetitive and boring.- Repetitive boss. There are 4 or 5 elite mobs and 4 or 5 bosses throughout the game, very few, huh? And their skills are quite similar. And they REPEAT. You fight the boar boss 3 times, the dragon boss 3 times, the goddess boss 3 times. How lazy are the game designers?- Cliched story. It's ok if it's a bed time fairy-tale for 12 years old, but it's way too shallow for a 100 hours game.- Tons of meaningless small talk cutscene. The game uses the slow paced small talks to pad game time, even the positive reviewers skip those cutscenes.Maybe there are some more cons I forget to list.After beating nice RPG games like Final Fantasy X, Dragon Quest XI, I feel sad because it's over.After beating RPG games with deep combat mechanics like Octopath Traveler, Divinity II, I wanna play it again to try different strategies.After beating this game? I feel good because the repetition and boredom is over, I deleted it immediately and will definitely not try any atelier game.

_childDocuments_.review: Atelier Sophie 2 The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream is the latest installment in the Mysterious games despite it being a sequel only for the first game, which is Atelier Sophie. My thoughts are: This game felt more of a side story arc compared to being part of the main games' timeline, which makes sense because of the events in the game. The plot wasn't bad at all but it was kind of lacking, could have been better. Either way, I enjoyed every bit of the story and its characters, both the "old" and the new ones. As for the gameplay, The battle went back to being the classic turn-based type, so nothing changed much compared to its other Mysterious games. But for the alchemy, in my opinion became harder but funner. I would not be surprised if people dislike Sophie 2's alchemy gameplay even thought the Mysterious games' alchemy has been quite disliked in general.Overall, I give Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream a 6/10 for its decent story but the gameplay made it enjoyable for the most part.~

_childDocuments_.review: So if you're familiar with the atelier series you already know most of what to expect. Relevant points for people who play these games, there are significant quality improvements in this game in terms of graphics, the fast travel is unlocked early and is fairly designed, the port is great and runs well. In terms of combat mechanics, its about as good as turn based gets with a mixture of mechanics from Firis and Sophie along with some of the things Ryza did well. One drawback is that you cannot do charged swings against trees like Ryza but otherwise the gathering is arguably easier and even comes with fun mini games.Besides this we get to beat up a cute butterfly goddess so thats a huge bonus point.
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: To me, Atelier Sophie 2 has shown an all round improvement in terms of combat flow, synthesizing, and a new form of exploration system that brings simple puzzle experiences that does not hinder one's progression . Similar to older titles of Atelier games such as Lydie & Suelle and the beginning of Sophie, it heavily focuses on the aspect of gathering and synthesizing, unlocking recipes or making key/items to progress through the story, and utilizing different materials to bring out the best of your equipment for your party. As combat (turn-based) and exploration/story still plays a big role, it acts as a secondary toppings to the core of this game, of being an alchemist synthesizing and mixing whatever great traits/quality materials you have gathered from your adventure. It was enjoyable and engaging when every item or equipment I decide to make brings me to think and formulate ways of putting down tetris-like patterns on the board and min-maxing their ability traits, and it gets even challenging as catalysts are introduced and the board expands. I'm not exaggerating when on average I could last mins to an hour synthesizing one item, and I definitely enjoyed it.I'm a fan of Atelier games and I've played a lot of its series, and there are moments I would love if the combat could have been more engaging, the monsters could be more unique, especially against bosses. If you are looking for that, Atelier Ryza 1 or 2 could be a better option in terms of that aspect. However, if you love to experience the world of being an alchemist, overpowering items and equipment, apart from this title, older titles as mentioned are also some that I would recommend as well!All in All, a 8/10 for a great sequel experience of Sophie's unexpected adventure into the Land of Dreams.
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend this. 80% of the "game" is spent watching cutscenes. There are seriously places where it's 30 seconds or less between cutscenes. You enter a building, and get a cutscene. You walk through a door and get another cutscene. Which might have been ok, except that the story has some of the worst writing I've ever seen in any medium, ever, game or otherwise. It's one contrivance and coincidence after another. Flashbacks to things that happened mere minutes ago, people suddenly remembering that they run an alchemy store after you, the alchemist, have been adventuring with them for days, people randomly walking up the moment they're needed, etc.Even the problems to be solved tend to be monumentally stupid. For example, there's a huge quest chain where you're looking for somebody and get blocked by a waist-deep river with some boxes by it. Neither you nor the other alchemist in the party have any idea what the boxes are, but action-girl remembers that she saw the person your'e after use those boxes that one time to stop the rain. You go back to the guild, and everybody knows all about these alchemy-rain-stopping boxes except for the alchemists, and they explain that you need some super rare recharging tool to recharge the boxes, and nobody knows where to find them. A guy who is also not an alchemist walks in right that second and mentions that he has the item you need and gives it to you...but oops, the recharging item needs to be recharged with some rocks that only an alchemist can do that. Suddenly you remember that you know how to make the rock you need to recharge the boxes you had no clue what they were for. You make the rocks and recharge the item and use it to recharge the boxes...which makes the rain stop. Instantly the river dries up and you can cross. Oh, and now you can make rocks to recharge boxes whenever you want, no special item needed anymore, and these boxes suddenly exist all over the place whenever you need to raise or lower a river.This is immediately followed by a mountain pass that you can't get through because a dragon attacked a caravan travelling through it. Does the dragon stop you? Do you have to level up and fight it later? No, of course not. The dragon's already gone, but during the battle he knocked some bags off the caravan, and the bags are blocking your path. So you can't simply help move them, so you'll just have to come back later, never mind the fact that the bags are also waist-high and have huge visible gaps between them.That was about when I gave up on the game.I'll grant that the alchemy minigame is mildly interesting, Drop shapes on a field and try to line up special symbols, score better to make better equipment. But it seems kind of useless, because combat is easy and mostly optional. You can walk around most monsters in the game, and boss fights are easy enough that after 7 hours of play I've yet to lose a battle even though it took me four hours to figure out how to equip anything and I haven't bothered leveling because I can walk around everything that isn't a boss.As a plus, none of the characters are unlikable. This is basically a "cute girls doing cute things" slice-of-life anime, with little bits of running around and easy battles in between. If that's what you want, you might like it. But don't buy this expecting much of a game. Or much of a story.

_childDocuments_.review: My only previous knowledge of Atelier was Ryza 1 and 2 which I loved, so I thought I’d jump into the Sophie games when Sophie 2 was released. I played through 1 first as 2 was a direct continuation of it, but unfortunately, I wasn't a fan of Sophie 1. It was extremely dull and boring, and about 16 hours in I decided enough was enough (a certain red enemy that autoheals for 200HP) and ploughed through the rest of the game to complete it. I was debating whether I should even play Sophie 2, if it was going to be much of the same I wouldn’t. But I gave it a shot and ♥♥♥♥ it’s so much better, the world is beautiful and feels more alive, characters are so expressive and the cutscenes are well made in general. I finished Sophie 1 in 20 hours, and I’m only 20 hours into Sophie 2 and I feel like I’m barely halfway in! Definitely didn’t need to play 1 to enjoy this game, there’s a intro on the main menu which covers the first game, though I do appreciate the few mentions to the characters and world from the first game thanks to playing it firstThe devs must have jumped into Erde Wiege to find a PC from the future to test this on though because performance is all over the place – on an RX 6700xt I can easily reach 120+ inside, and about 70-90 in the main open areas on all high, but there are occasional stutters and framerate dips seemingly out of nowhere. Don’t even think about running this on a Deck: with a 30FPS cap, lower resolution and everything on low it still manages to go lower than 30 sometimes, stutters like crazy, and draws a lot of power. (Edit: actually after further testing it runs okish and looks decent with FSR, but def would rather play on my actual PC) Also, the antialiasing in the game settings is complete garbage, no AA looks a lot better imoAll in all blew my expectations away coming from Sophie 1 and Pirka is adorableEdit: Just finished the game, honestly it was great, glad I played it. _childDocuments_.review: This review is PoV: 18 hours into the game and done but will probably finish it in the future once I'm bored enough.I played this after Ryza 1 & 2 because many were saying it's better than both, only to find that such people were all shills. Everything in the game is worse than Ryza 1.Ryza 1 alchemy was a simple loop with a lot of depth. You could eventually break the system entirely which was half the fun. Sophie's alchemy feels far more on rails; you have to play Tetris with your elemental values instead of just dropping items into loops which while fun at first becomes just annoying later where you need to have X amount of lightning and you want the shapes to match so you can fill your whole Tetris  board. Even then, doing optimal alchemy in Sophie is nearly irrelevant.The best item you can make in Sophie is the items base stats + the stats from 2 ingots + (some) stats from elemental value + some stats from traits - that's 90 damage. It's very easy to make the optimal weapon. Meanwhile in Ryza you could eventually break the alchemy system entirely and make +500 all stat weapons through Loop Morph and optimizing the materials.Ryza alchemy was simple in idea but complex in the sense that you had to gather specific materials, craft specific alchemy ingredients (eg. Effect Spread) to optimize recipes to optimize other recipes. By playing it smart, you could break the system progressively more throughout the game which was half the enjoyment for me.Sophie's is really just "gather random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that kind of fits the criteria of this item". Eg. You want to get grass with lightning, but you can't directly control how the lightning is spread out on the Tetris board so you just kind of get a bunch of grass and hope it works out. It feels bad, the Tetris board is okay at first but just limiting later, and the limits of Sophie alchemy are unbreakable. You will make the 90 damage item and that's it.Learning new recipes in Sophie is also just "pick up random ingredient and fight specific monster." Ryza's Recipe Morph made way more sense overall, and Ryza's skill tree was  actually mattered tbh.Progressing through Ryza's alchemy made sense. You make a Crystal Element with (Gemstones) and Effect Spread +2. It's useful in every recipe that has (Gemstones). Meanwhile Sophie's is like, you make a (Poisons) item with 5 Wind element in an U-shape. It's now useful in... Recipes that need (Poisons) and Wind and other materials that fit the Tetris board with the U-shape. It never really felt like you got a significant item, just kind of "side-grades that kind of work in the right situation".Combat feels bad mainly because it's just item spam. Playing Ryza on Very Hard, you'd run up against a boss, go craft the best gear you can right now and some utility items like Ice Bombs to slow the boss and you'd just barely beat it. It felt like everything matters.Meanwhile in Sophie, you have no CC limit on your items meaning you can just zerg them. You run up against a boss, go back to craft the best gear only to realize it doesn't matter because the boss has an aura. The only optimal way to break the aura is to make 6x () and spam them every single turn. No CC limit means no punishment for just spamming your bombs, and once the boss's aura breaks, how do you punish the boss while stunned? By spamming more bombs. Gear is only to keep you alive and farm low level enemies.Auras are a boring cancer mechanic that forces you to spam the opposite element of the aura or deal 0 damage, then once the enemy is stunned it takes super damage so you just burst it with bombs. Seeing an aura ruins every single fight, and you guessed it, every single fight has an aura!I remember thinking Ryza should've been turn-based as that would've made the game more strategic. Sophie 2 is turn-based but the combat is so trash it's actually 3 letter grades worse than Ryza's system.The world feels far more hollow in Sophie. It's a random isekai land with no NPC's of note. The main characters are fun, sure, but surrounded by nothing but props. Ryza had a lot of irrelevant NPC's as well, but it didn't feel hollow the same way Sophie does. The other issue is the world is too large and you progress through it too fast, which makes memorizing materials and specific monsters also irrelevant. You just wing it through all areas and gather what you happen to get while running through. Years after playing Ryza 1 I still remember many of the mini-bosses and items found in areas because you actually had to learn those things.Story is okay, it's far too "♥♥♥♥ it we ball" for me though. You go to Isekai World only for everyone to group up with you instantly and breeze through situations with bizarre reactions. eg. A jellyfish monster slowly floating away from you? Let's go back to alchemize Monster Bait to keep it in place. "Oh Sophie, can you go and alchemize an item to break down dimensional barriers real quick?" The story is probably the main reason people recommend this game, and it's okay, just okay.The important characters are okay but just kind of fall flat overall compared to Ryza 1. There's also less of them, eg. there's 3 non-playable characters you actually care about. Ryza 1 & 2 had far more.No one has human dialogue in this game. It's painfully apparent in some cutscenes, but more or less on par for the course for these games. Still, Ryza characters felt far more human and reacted to whatever is going on somewhat understandably.It also feels even lazier than Ryza did in animations and that kind of stuff. Sophie ate some food, they CBA to make the food or even an artwork of the supposed food in the game.The new mechanics in Sophie 2 are all kind of just annoying, like the weather system just forces you to stock up on weather change items and go through every map multiple times with multiple weathers at multiple spots. Oh there's a treasure chest under water here, you now have to run back halfway through the map to turn the weather to sunny to clear the water, then run back. It's unnecessary complexity that just makes it harder to keep track of the few things that actually matter.I especially hate how nothing in the game is retroactive. You're constantly learning recipes by going back somewhere to re-discover an ingredient you already found before, or crafting a recipe you already crafted before. You can't do multiple character talent quests like "Use X ability 10 times" at once either, but slowly one at a time. If you enjoyed Ryza 1 for the systems and alchemy, play Ryza 2. If you only cared for the story and vibe, I guess Sophie 2 is okay for you. For me personally, this really feels like it was released 5 years before Ryza 1, not after it. It can't even compare overall to Ryza 1 as a whole package, and I thought Ryza 2 was boring but it was still much better than Sophie 2.There's clearly a psyop of people shilling for this game. I know not their long-term plan for such action. Anyone who actually enjoyed the alchemy and combat in Ryza 1 & 2 can't possibly enjoy Sophie 2.
