_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this review as a first-time Atelier player. To be honest I didn't really know what to expect, but unfortunately the first half hour of the game was enough to tell me this just isn't for me. I just really dislike how slow-paced the game is. Firstly your character is as slow as molasses relative to how large the environments are. I suspected something was off when I saw they were actually selling running speed as DLC (no joke, look at the Digital Deluxe version features), and as it turns out your base speed being obscenely slow is simply due to malevolence rather than incompetence. But that's not all. Characters will talk endlessly and say so little--60% of every conversation can be safely ignored. I'm fine with slice of life but that should come with interesting characters with interesting things to say--this game rides so hard on its moe aesthetic that I guess it's just supposed to make up for the bland dialogue and characters. Yeah the girls are cute but how long can I be expected to endure their one-note innocent kawaii 10-year-old shtick and not get a little tired of it? And would it kill them to include honorifics in the translations? If you're not going to have an English dub, just go all the way and keep the translations literal. The more dissonance between what the characters say vs. what the translations say, the less immersed I am and the less I can transpose the character's Japanese voice to the English words on the screen in my head.Ok now moving on to the graphics--they're not very good. The game looks like a PS3 game. I wasn't expecting a masterpiece but if you're selling the game for $60, it should look nice right? It's actually really jarring because, while the lighting system looks fairly modern, the geometry and textures are easily from 10 years ago if not more. Anyways I'm half an hour in and experienced no gameplay, and I figure I won't even really be in the gameplay loop until 5-6 hours into the game, at which point it's too late to refund. Sorry but I'm not taking that chance. This one is probably best left for the fans. Any newcomers who are interested in buying this game--even if the gameplay seems appealing, you will have to deal with an RPG that is slow in pacing and generally uninteresting. If you're ok trading substance for saccharine character interactions, i.e. you just want to turn your brain off, this might be worth checking out. So what's the takeaway? Am I stamping my feet, demanding the next entry in this series to cater more to me? No. Who am I to come into a niche series with an existing fanbase and say it should change? It shouldn't. It's just not for me, and I'm happy for Atelier fans who get to celebrate another entry in their franchise. I just think it's good for prospective buyers to get an opinion from someone who was new to the series who did not like it. I think most should steer clear, maybe steer clear of Koei Tecmo as a whole as they seem more than content to fleece their customer base (seriously--there's the Atlus tax, then there's these guys).

_childDocuments_.review: 5.1 out of 10, yeah it was a close call between a positive and a negative review.There's so much to like in this game. It has great characters. A very enjoyable story filled with positive messages. Beautiful music and artwork. A challenging battle system that you can use synthesis to overcome the challenges of.The game and the community that supports it have their challenges though. Most of my frustration involves the random elements surrounding synthesis. I could not find any guides (let alone good guides) on strategy for placing components on the synthesis grid. I was eventually able to piece together bits of several posts to understand how to leverage assist skills and the restricted panel to be able to perfect many of the recipes, but when it came to a few end game items I couldn't find any way around the major gathering mini games. I'm old and I am incapable of any amount of success in those mini games. The only way I could see to achieve items with the number of the correct elements with enough link stars on them was by playing the mini games.  I had perfect seeds with perfect quality, and utilized element lv +3 and element lv Max +3 every chance I could but there were still some recipes that I wasn't able to perfect because I didn't have enough link stars. The random chance of rare items dropping from seeds caused me also considerable frustration. I would find myself needing a high quality rare item to complete a recipe and when I'd try and get it from seeds it sometimes took over 100 attempts to get the item (I noticed that the same rare items never seemed to be in short supply after I no longer needed one, I felt like the game knew what I needed and was withholding it). Super Success, what a pain. There's a super success gauge that's supposed to represent the probability of getting a super success at the end of synthesis, but even though I regularly had the gauge above 90% my success rate was about 6 out of 10. I found myself save scumming my synthesis so I didn't waste components when the RNG was mean to me.Synthesis and gathering should have been the stress free safe haven that could be retreated too if the stress of battle became too much and I needed a break. Instead they were in their own way even more of a frustration than the challenges of battle (not that that was much of a challenge once I used seeds to defeat traits and built decent equipment).If random number generation was more accurate and if there was some path to synthesise around the mini games, This game would have been a 9 or 10 out of 10.It's a nice game, probably worth a play for most people, but not as enjoyable for me as the Ryza series (all three of those are an 11 out of 10 for me). Good luck, and I hope you enjoy the game if you decide to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes I recommend this, it's the best crafting system in the Mysterious series. However it doesn't get over the central problem that series had, namely the total lack of plot and uneven combat.Pros:- Crafting system. I'm not sure if I prefer Ryza's loop system or this one, but for what it's worth this is the best the mysterious system has.- Gameplay tweaks. I might be imagining it but I think they have taken some gameplay ideas from Ryza and applied them here. They work well and help exploration.- Fast Travel. You get it early and it's everywhere.- Sophie/Plachta. This dynamic makes up for a ton of story and character flaws. It's so strong, especially when the 'plot' get's going.Cons:- Story. Yeah I was never going to like this prequel business but even considering that it's not got the plot or worldbuilding the Ryza series had, nor does it have the small, central goal and lack of plot the mysterious series had. What you're left with is some loose nonsense and a ton of small cut scenes which break flow.- Side characters. The mysterious series never really cared about its side characters, this isn't any different. They're fun and ok, but this is no Ryza.- Combat. The turn based system works, but basic enemies are easy and bosses are a real challenge, so I'm already in this weird position where I rarely bother with combat unless I have to because it's boring. It's uneven, though as I say the powerful enemies/bosses are where it shines. It's shame 90% of the combat is against boring peons.Overall this is recommended for fans of the series, but I still prefer Ryza by miles. The crafting system is what saves it.

_childDocuments_.review: I also have specific complaints about the design of certain core elements, which have a significant effect on the gameplay during your first playthrough. The issues I have in mind are the invisible walls on the maps, the alchemy system/gameplay during the early stages of the game, and the amount of backtracking required to progress. These are just some of the issues I will address in this review.The alchemy part of the game itself feels very good once you’ve reached the later stages of the story, but it is too restrictive during the early stages. In the early parts of the game, you do not have access to the catalysts, which I consider the core component of AS2’s alchemy system, holding AS2 together with all the other content the game has to offer. It's acceptable not to have access to them until the later stages, but missing out on the core part of alchemy until around 50% into the game’s story is quite disappointing.Another issue I've noticed in AS2 is the amount of backtracking required to progress in the story. This is primarily due to the introduction of the weather devices as a core mechanic. The amount of moving back and forth needed to solve the weather device puzzles becomes tiresome when you don't have access to a set warp location yet.Combat is another crucial aspect when playing a JRPG. If I have to summarize how AS2 handles it, unfortunately, I have to say that Koei missed the mark on this one. To put it simply, it sucks. I would even recommend playing on easy mode just to minimize interaction with it. The game’s aura combat mechanic feels stale and slow, which becomes very boring throughout your playthrough. The aura numbers themselves are not bad, but the sheer amount you have to go through during your first playthrough is the main problem. After a certain point in the story, every fight encounter will have such an enemy, which significantly reduces the game’s combat pace, making it unenjoyable. Personally, I would prefer fewer enemies with set combat mechanics, but with higher aura numbers, to make this mechanic feel more special.Firstly, the game’s atmosphere is amazing. I had such a great vibe while playing it. The atmosphere of the various areas you explore to progress the story is phenomenal! The music and the overall buildup of each area are amazing to experience. Additionally, the music in each area is really good! While I wouldn’t consider it the best Atelier OST out there, it is solid overall.The story and side stories are what you would expect from playing an Atelier game. Slice of life, comedy, soft shoujo ai vibes, and a main plot with a secondary b-plot caused by the main story plot. This is what you could consider a certified Atelier classic. Because of this, there isn't much to say about it. The game contains what the franchise has always offered, and I'm completely fine with that.Another improvement I noticed in AS2 is the reduced number of cutscenes that can occur at once compared to the previous Atelier games cough cough Atelier Lydie & Suelle cough cough Atelier Firis. This is overall really pleasant to witness. It's nice that we don't have to endure four cutscenes in a row during your first playthrough, but only one or two occasionally. However, this also has a slight downside, as it makes you feel slightly less connected with the characters in the story, aside from the ones the story is centered around. But to be fair, one can't have it all, and it is what it is.One thing I particularly enjoyed while playing AS2, aside from the alchemy post-story, was the different character designs showcased throughout the story. As expected from a game involving time travel, it is awesome to see characters with distinct aesthetics. Each main character looks great and unique, adding another layer to the game's atmosphere, which is truly enjoyable.

I particularly liked the theme for Thunderbolt Palace.This is the 3rd Atelier game I've played, the first two being Sophie 1, and Ryza 1. As expected of a sequel, it plays much more like Sophie 1 than Ryza 1. Sophie was 16 at the start of Sophie 1, and is 19 for this game, so timeline-wise, it takes place not long before the "original sequel" Firis.Every item, piece of equip, and monster, all have commentary from the characters for them in the in-game listing, which can be pretty entertaining to read. It was actually pretty disappointing to realize when I'd all but filled that listing, since it meant the end of the game was near.I had two very minor complaints. One was that while every other place in the game had a menu detail on the world map, listing which enemies and items were present, in what rarity, in each available weather type, the Heartscapes did not get such a listing, so it was much harder to keep track of what could be obtained there. Even the bonus area from the Atelier Plachta DLC had its own listing, but not the 2 Heartscapes. Pretty annoying.The other minor complaint was that several of the achieves were pretty grindy for me, such as planting enough seeds to get all the greenhouses, and then waiting out the time needed to harvest every type of seed from each type of greenhouse. Crafting enough to get both Sophie and Plachta up to 99 Alchemy level was also pretty tedious.All in all, it was a great time. I think it would be fun, in future games, to see what happened to the various supporting characters after the end of this game, especially since they officially came from all times and places. Hearing the commentary from the voice actors (game completion bonus), from the point of having finished recording, but not yet being able to play it themselves, was also fun.I can see myself playing it again at some point, though next I'll either finish off Ryza (~85% done), or restart Sophie 1 (50% done).
_childDocuments_.name: Atelier Sophie 2: The Alchemist of the Mysterious Dream

_childDocuments_.review: I played Atelier Ryza 2 along with this game and can confidently say this is by far the better game.There are obvious comparisons between the two, most of the icons are the same, the art style is the same.The exploration I felt was better in Ryza 2, you could pretty much go anywhere, could crawl (ohhhh yeah) and had a mount for moving around faster. In Sophie 2 there are invisible walls everywhere and a moronic weather system that brings nothing to the game other than annoyance.The alchemy is superior in this game, rather than relying just on item quality now items have tetris like blocks that you need to put in place to get the most out of any particular item. The depth of this crafting system cannot be understated, you can make a normal item, or an awesome item, or anywhere in between based on the items you use, the quality of the items, and your attention to detail in the tetris grid.They seem to have reduced the number of cutscenes. It's still feels intrusive rather than bringing anything of value to the game (instead of thousands there are still hundreds), but it doesn't feel anywhere near as annoying as in Ryza.The combat in this game is far superior. Rather than a quasi realtime nonsense in Ryza they've opted for a much better turn based system with link attacks. Even though you'd think turn-based might result in slower combat you'd be surprised. Combat in this game is much quicker and smoother. You're not sitting around waiting for a "it's your go" gauge to fill like in Ryza.In summary the game still has some issues, they could easily reduce the number of cutscenes to 5% of what they are now and nothing of value would be lost. After the 10 hour mark I literally skipped every single cutscene and still knew exactly what was going on just from the TLDR mission screen. All in all though I'd recommend as it's pretty good.Hopefully for Ryza/Sophie 3 they're more like this game than the former, and they blend the exploration of Ryza with the crafting/combat of Sophie.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the best Ateliers maybe the best if you aren't into some of the changes the Ryza games introduced. It combines the more 'modern' feel of the Ryza games with some of elements of the more traditional Atelier games. Gameplay -- This one doesn't have real time battles as it returns to the older turn based system before the Ryza games. The big new mechanic that they added is the aura system in battles. Essentially you have to use certain types of attacks or items to break the enemy's aura faster and if you don't break it, you don't do any damage. It works well and is balanced well for higher difficulties and bosses. You have to manage the whole party's items more. You also have to think about the the positioning of the characters, whether you want them in combat or in support. I think the aura system is a better implementation of a 'weakness' effect in these games. Specifically, I'm talking about Persona and Octopath, where the weakness system in those game take center stage and it almost becomes a chore to manage because you are not playing the 'right' way if you are not exploiting weaknesses. However, the auras do have a downside and its that they don't just apply to bosses, random enemies also have this mechanic which just wastes your time to be honest. This actually creates a bad gameplay loop because you need to waste more items/mp in combat when you are just farming, and then you also need to farm for more currency as well because you need to replenesh the items you just used.Story -- Like Ryza 1 & 2 or even Lydie really, there is an actual plot and plot progression. The older Ateliers (before Lydie) don't really have a cohesive plot, and stuff just kind of happens and you go along with the ride, which is fine, but there is just more of a story this time around where you can follow along. You don't need to have played the other mysterious games to enjoy this, but you will be more appreciative of the older games, mainly Sophie 1,  if you have played them before this one. If you've ever played the Tales games, its like Berseria making Zestiria better because you are able to put certain plot elements that seem unimportant in context.

_childDocuments_.review: An overall successful sequel to what is one of the best Atelier games ever made. Not as good as the original, but in the same ball park. Here are what I thought some of the pros and cons were:Pros:Combat was very fun in this game. I'm usually not a huge fan of turn based combat but the addition of barriers and the variety of skills this game offers among characters and their combos really made it engaging.The addition of changing the weather to environments was also really cool. it helped in combat like in Atelier Lydie and Suelle, but also exploration was impacted as well on maps. This does have a slight downside that I'll get to in the ConsSide characters are as charming as ever, and I really enjoy doing their side quests and getting to know them.Graphics in this game are very good for an atelier game, and the sound track is one of the best.Main story was actually really good unlike Ryza 2. The ending struck me in the feels which I did not expect, even more than Lydie and Suelle. It was coherent and progressed wellThe variety and how upgradable the catalysts for the cauldron are makes for convenient synthesis and more thought into which catalyst you should use.Cons:Though the addition of weather is cool, it does make exploring some maps tedious. These maps are big, and there tend to be 3 - 4 subsections in each map.They tried to use more dramatic shots for cut scenes, but it was like a child with a brand new toy. It was a bit much to see a zoom in to someone's grin for dramatic effect every time, or to the fireplace.I know it's an atelier game but the friendship is magic and believing in each other dialogue was reeeeeeally over the top in this game. just made some of the key cutscenes a little less interesting to watch.Having to level up the Alchemy level of both Sophie and Plachta was a bit tedious.I wish it scaled in difficulty like in the original Mysterious trilogy. The only difficulty spike was somewhat 3/4th the way through the game and other than that you really didn't have to worry about losing a fight.Items didn't feel as engaging in this game, though still useful. You could really get by with just skills alone in this game.Overall solid game, definitely worthy of being a sequel to Sophie. The ending was just spectacular, and you get so much gameplay in the main story alone.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet another wonderful experience from the Atelier series. I've left reviews on a couple others, but I may as well restate what I said in those reviews here.First and foremost, Atelier is a different breed of JRPG. Most JRPGs center around chosen heroes fighting to save the world, but Atelier is a bit more humble. Ultimately, Atelier games are meant to relax, stow away your worries, and spend dozens of hours gathering materials and making gear and items with an exceptional crafting system. Though combat can be fun, most of your strength will be gained by creating powerful equipment so you can bash through whatever challenges are in your way.Atelier Sophie 2 is a prime example of an Atelier game. Each party member has their own dream, and they bond together as friends as they work together to achieve those. Combat and crafting are interspersed with many scenes to get to know the characters, and the story is as heartfelt as ever from this series. The previous entries of Atelier Ryza and Atelier Ryza 2 were a bit experimental, but Atelier Sophie 2 feels like a return to form for this long-running series (it's almost as old as me, if you count Japan-exclusive entries that never got localized).If you like pretty aesthetics, relaxation, and a crafting system you'll spend more time in than the rest of the game combined, you'll like any Atelier title, and Atelier Sophie 2 shines as a perfect example of the little things that have made the series one of my favorites, ever since I first picked up Atelier Escha and Logy many years ago.

_childDocuments_.review: Ryza was my first Atelier game and while I thought the alchemy and world were really (really) well done, I just never really got attached to Ryza. I think that game is probably the better game, but I was held back by feeling so meh about Ryza. However, I immediately fell for Sophie. She is the driving force of this game and I am immediately going to go play the original Sophie game, and probably Lydie & Suelle because I hear Sophie is playable there too. I can see why she won the popularity poll in Japan that got this sequel made. She's just a joy to be around. Without her character being as strong as it is my interest in the game might have slipped a bit. I felt the alchemy was a bit simplistic compared to Ryza, but it was plenty of fun to craft anyway. The weather gimmick was cool at first but then clearly became just a gimmick. Even still, I'd adventure anywhere with Sophie.

_childDocuments_.review: Picking up Atelier Sophie 2 I anticipated a focused, plot driven, signposted experience (in line with how Atelier has been evolving since Lulua). Guilty on all three counts the result is perhaps the most approachable entry in the series yet - one that will not disorient regular JRPG players, and will delight if you're after a bright and cheerful, yet solid experience. Bright and cheer aside Atelier Sophie (first entry) was none of the above; more chill, less predictable, more lived-in, it did a ton with so much less; and like many other Atelier games, succeeded at creating a sense of freedom and serendipity that seems to be disappearing in the process of going bigger, and going mainstream.Isekai-wise Sophie 2 offers a meek rendition which frankly does no justice to the theme; this coming from the maker of Blue Reflection 2, clearly is a choice (but why???); world kinda big but shallow - no lore, barely anybody to talk to outside Roytale.Unsure about future direction, but for now I still recommend this game; the crafting is truly awesome, and the battle system is everything a modern TBRPG should be (raise difficulty whenever you stop feelin it).

_childDocuments_.review: My goodness... I have played many many games here on steam. I have hundreds of hours in games like Rimworld, Oxygen not Included, Skyrim, ect. And I have to say... This game has drawn me in like no game has for a long long time. The alchemy system is easily my favorite part. You can go out and collect all sorts of material, and each material - including duplicates - are very often completely different. The game is super clever with the game progress of such materials as well. You often have to make one item in order to craft another. And there are qualities and traits that can transfer through the crafting trees, leading to endless combinations of traits, and stats for equipment and items. Combat is super satisfying as well. Brings me back to the FFX days. Getting to try out a newly crafted OP item and seeing it wipe the floor with the enemies is quite satisfying.On that note, this game WILL give back in difficulty what you put into it. I finished the game on Very Hard on my first play through ---- without losing a single battle. But I am a puzzle nut, and I put a lot of time into upgrading equipment and crafting items. There is a difficulty beyond hard, but I have yet to try it as of this review. Long story short, the game can be as hard as you want it to be- depending on just how much alchemy you want to do.I don't know how this compares to the other games in the Universe as this was my first one, but as other have said, I could see this easily being the best. If you love exploration, puzzles, and Turn-Based Combat, this is a MUST.

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to touch upon three big topics that I feel cover the majority of this game and will give both new and veterans a quick glance and what Sophie two has to offer. Story, Crafting, Combat. In that order of what I feel is prioritized by the game to you as you play. The story and how it supports the other aspects of the game, Crafting changes and how it elongates without essentially changing anything, and the changes to combat from Sophie 1. As a more direct Sequel compared to Finris what will you get with Sophie 2? Well if you enjoyed Platcha and Sophie before this is wonderfully more of that. The teacher student dynamic between the two get swapped in a bizarre way which leads to a new lens to view them thru. We get to learn more about Sophie's Grandmother and her roll which is wonderfully sweet. The cast as usual is lovable even the two I thought at the start "OMG Snow and Edgy the hedgy dear god no." Yet by the end I was crafting not for stats for myself to continue on, but I was gonna make a sword that could cleave the planet for my friend to help him achieve his dream. Speaking of dreams. It would be poor of me to not address the lazy way the get the story going. The over arcing setup honestly was just an excuse to get these chars to this situation so you can explore their lives in this new setting. I forgot about it till I read my notes, but at the start and end it does hit the immersion. However, since it does bring some really touching Sophie and family moments that can melt your heart I do forgive it. So the Crafting then the main gameplay loop you will be sucked into and spending most of your time doing! How has it changed from Sophie 1. Well.... it's gotten longer. Not necessarily more complex or even harder. The materials you gather now will have a variety of shapes, colours, amount of components up to four which can also vary in colour, traits, and specific link parts in the shapes to connect. You also get the same cauldrons just in different forms. What this all equals too is it will most likely take you longer to gather specific parts with the specific shapes, colours, amount of links, and traits you want and need to pass on. See it isn't harder, but it will take longer if you aim for specific things on specific items. It also means a lot more materials you will have around and have to shuffle thru to find the ones you want. The filter/sort system is decent, but lacks sort by links which was the one I wanted the most almost 99% of the time. You do make this up somewhat by gathering a LOT more boasting a massive basket and I honestly never cleaned my garbage. (Except when I failed a mini game particularly poorly then they hit the ground.) So in the end Crafting is longer, but if you could do it in Sophie 1 then nothing here is gonna give you grief. Combat this part hurts me, but I personally feel they downgraded the combat. I was really hoping they would have taken the previous turn system in Sophie one and really worked being able to move around the turns based on attacks to make chaining easier. They instead just made a link attack gauge that lets you choose when to do so. This means now the turn order is just listed with no blanks. Seems like an odd thing to draw attention to, but I honestly thought the haste/speed up didn't work in this game for around 40 hours. See if you use a speed/low wait move, but it doesn't do enough to over take another person on the turn order it will seem like nothing happens. On top of the huge amount of buffs Debuffs tossed around constantly it can be hard planning out turns on a stunned enemy much less understand the skill is working. That being said you will never need that level of precision. I played on Very hard and ... this game's combat is kind of a joke. I've never wiped and only had two deaths. 80 hours in I had tier one gear and tier 2 bombs. I was waiting for a reason to craft some new gear, but even on Very hard nothing till post game hit me for enough to make me feel the need to craft the next item. Just raw stats and HP on my gear no dragon blessings no demon bombs. Just the tier 2 bombs and Stew to heal. This is particularly disappointing as the crafting allows for some amazing mixes and ideas. I just want a reason to actually do so. Thankfully the characters were so likable I did find myself doing so in the end over the silly things. Olias got a elbow scratch on a job. I made him Dragon god armor and a F-off cannon with auto heals so I knew he was safe. Edgy the hedgy is after a dragon. I lost 3 hours failing at swords to get one I felt was worth it. I bring it up cause it is a positive point in the games favour that it has characters to drive you to do so. Just the combat itself does not till post where it just nonsense anyways. TLDR; Sophie 2 gives you more slice of life scenario with Sophie Platcha and a cast of new friends. The crafting may be longer, but all the good bits are there and it does feel good to just nail everything perfectly and it all comes together. Many unique ways to deliver devastation though the combat even on Very hard will not ask that level of you till post game. -1 points for removing the Jump voice line. You know the one. Sophie 2 is an easy recommendation for those who are still new to the Atelier Series and want more Sophie! No time limits just lovely fun. When you are done Give Finris a Try and tell her Fayt said hi!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is brimming with potential. I love how laid back, simple, and stress-free it is--yet, at its core it offers so much. The alchemy is by far the most addictive part and the depth you can get into is is awesome. It's not just "adding ingredients", you can specify which traits of said ingredients you want focused on during the mixing. It's so fun to improve quality/level of gear, the series does great on that.I actually really liked the free-flow of combat from Ryza 2 (played on Playstation), but going back to the turn base hasn't been a hindrance whatsoever. The combat is a blast and the combos feel amazing. I'm still working on itemization for each character, but the gest of comboing attacks, both in offense and defense and in element weakness/strengths feels so good to watch unfold.The game is centric upon relationships between the world and its characters and Sophie. If you can get over or into the anime-style art, I highly recommend if you're like me and enjoy a game that you really can just chill through. The progression is just enough to where you're unlocking new stuff throughout the game. I have really come to appreciate the Atelier series, even if my first entry was Ryza 2 and now Sophie 2. I feel like the mechanics behind this game have absolutely so much potential and man alive I'd love to see them expand into creature collecting late/end game. Just like gathering enough new materials unlocks more alchemy, to have it where fighting enough of a creature allows you to capture and farm its resource and that eventually lead into taming/assigning fetch quests (similar to Ryza 2) with intent on eventually becoming an alchemy monster collector xD #dreams

_childDocuments_.review: This game is both a great follow-up to the first game, and an awesome modern Atelier.  Hell, it's probably one of the best of the series, period.  The game looks incredible (the character models especially).  The only complaint I'd have in this department is that I feel there is less Event Art than in Sophie, and previous Atelier games I've played.  I wish there was more.The world this game takes place in was really cool.  It was both a smart idea, using it to make the game fit nearly in the timeline of the Mysterious saga (Probably, I haven't played Fyris or Lydie/Suelle yet).  The weather system is really creative, and part of me wishes it would be possible in future titles.  The interconnected world is fun to explore and complete objectives in.  ...Mostly.  Near the end of the game, I got tired of trying to remember what way to traverse the map in order to get to a specific spot, since changing the weather can change what paths are open and closed.  Alchemy is the most fun as it's ever been.  The puzzle alchemy is so much fun to try and make happen.  I've spent hours just tetris-ing the best configurations of some items to get certain traits.  It's so much fun.  This game probably contains my favorite Atelier battle system, too.  I love the ability to include your entire party in battles directly, it's a really smart system.  And I love when these games allow you to use items with non-alchemist party members, too.And the story...  Kind of one the weaker side as far as Atelier games go.  This world's logic is kind of wishy-washy sometimes, and the ability to magically solve an issue with alchemy kind of goes beyond the realm of believability sometimes.  I'm not a huge fan of the main antagonist, either.  They are pretty infuriating at times.Gripes aside, I'd like to once again reiterate this is one of the best Atelier games made to date.  You could probably play it without having played Sophie 1 (though it is probably way more rewarding to do so), but if you don't, there's a catchup option on the main menu.  Not that there's a lot to catch up on, since the first game's story is so basic.  Anyway, if you're interested, definitely check this game out!

_childDocuments_.review: Atelier Sophie 2 tries a lot of new things for the Atelier franchise and it does it well! The game takes place between Atelier Sophie 1 and Atelier Firis (both parts of the original Atelier Mystery Trilogy). You don't need to have played Atelier Sophie 1 to play this sequel as you get a TLDR of the first game. I would still recommend playing Sophie 1 to appreciate the references in character conversations and just the fact it's a great game as well. Gust and Koei Tecmo try a lot of new things that take aspects of the original Mystery trilogy and combine them with aspects from the Atelier Ryza duology that had good feedback from the community. There are new aspects of exploring the different regions of this game's dream world by having different control methods for the environment as well has harvesting methods with implemented mini games. Most of it is really clever and fun! The battle system is by far in my opinion the biggest upgrade for the franchise. Taking aspects of Lydie and Suelle and the Ryza games made the combat so smooth and easy to go back and forth on. It's super satisfying to rack up a good rotation of characters, abilities, and items to do some great setups of attacks and damage. Of course we can't talk about an Atelier game without mentioning the Alchemy synthesizing system. The boards feel familiar yet have a few changes with implementing components that works really well. At first it may seem convoluted or tedious to some, but after awhile you get used to the different catalysts and methods of using the board and super success rate to make some great items. There were times were I got so wrapped up in making items, time would pass by in an instant which made it both relaxing and enjoyable to do (especially when thinking about the great stats / abilities / damage that certain items would do).The game gets a solid 9/10 for me because of how much I ended up enjoying the experience. I must preface that the original Mystery trilogy series is my favorite in the Atelier Franchise, and so I had a lot of motivation to 100% (achievements) the game. It took me about 80 hours (in game time), but it didn't really feel drawn out until the very end (trying to max out alchemy levels). Had I just played the game casually, I believe most ppl can expect a solid 40 - 50 hour journey. My only real issue was a few hiccups in performance for the PC version. Some areas would have dropped frame rate or some stuttering while transitioning between connected gateways. The other thing I have to mention is the mini games involved for harvesting via certain tools. Most of the mini games are clever and nice to have, but there's a couple (like the fishing rod) that were nonsensical at best. I appreciate the effort in trying new things, but that specific mini game wasn't the greatest.The story was quite enjoyable and had many moments where I couldn't help but smile, laugh, or even get teary eyed from various aspects of the character's stories (especially Sophie's story two key characters). It's nice to have a straight forward and digestable story where you can follow through and still take time on the side to explore and get to know characters and make a lot of items. By the time I finished the game, I had feeling of joy for a great experience, but also sadness that this alchemy journey would be over.Overall I would highly recommend this game!TLDR: 9 / 10 Great game, well worth playing for fans of the franchise and fun enough for me to 100% the game!Positive - Fluid battle system, enjoyable characters, straight-forward story that made me both smile and get teary eyed, catchy soundtrack, amazing voice acting as always, and intricate systems like weather and mini games to spice up harvesting materials,Negative - A few performance issues for the PC version including some stuttering and frame drop on some maps. Certain harvesting mini games are probably best left out for the next Atelier game, but I appreciate the effort

_childDocuments_.review: It feels solidly like an Atelier game. The crafting system gets more complex and different ways you can approach it as the game goes on. The combat is fun, not too terribly challenging. If you find yourself hit a wall, go back and craft some things :D Put on your alchemist hat and go! There's still some graphical flickering when you move the camera at times, but they've been patching every couple of days so it makes me believe they're working on fixes to things like that. Took me 60+ hours to beat on Hard, not 100% but fairly close. These games are awesome! Definitely worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Atelier games have always been a comfy series to play after a long day. In most RPG games, you would often play as some medieval, world-renowned hero. However, that's not the case with games like these.You're playing as an adorable alchemist who brews potions and whacks monsters with your staff. I love it for what it is. Every Atelier game is unique in a way, and if you're ever the type of player who likes a mix between RPG and Comfy, this is an excellent game to start on that.9/10, would recommend

_childDocuments_.review: As usual with the Atelier games, it's more about the gathering than the combat. This is a level up from the first game for Sophie. I've only reached so far in the game, but it's quite lovely. If you're looking for a deep story, skip it, but there are several hilarious moments (mostly involving the hazards of time travel, so awkward.) The subtitle translations are excellent. Whoever did the translations went for the feel of the characters as much as literal word for word, and it comes across well in English. I do miss the original cast from the first game, and feel bad for people who don't know Japanese enough to enjoy some of the nonsense shouted in battle. Main complaint is one that I had with the first game. Why oh why do Sophie and Placta constantly babble during alchemy. If there was a toggle to switch that off, I'd click it. It's the same bloody thing. Argh. Secondary complaint is the total lack of musical variety. I just turn off the BGM and play jazz or the soundracks to other games. TLDR; Cute girls and alchemy puzzles, slightly different JRPG, boring music, great translations.

_childDocuments_.review: A 7/10 game, but a 9.5/10 Atelier game. Highly recommended for fans of the series, otherwise might wait for a sale.Art direction and game performance were much improved from Ryza 2, A more expansive world, beautiful lighting, improved in-game cinematics, overall stable FPS (albeit there are some minor FPS drops in certain menus), and much less GPU-consuming. Ryza 2's outdoor lighting turned my 3080 into a helicopter but Sophie 2 is really optimized. Regarding visuals, GUST has managed to strike a perfect spot between fanservice and wholesomeness. This could be the benchmark for future Atelier or even other GUST games.Much of the game's core mechanics including synthesis and material gathering were swapped to the original Sophie. I can't really decide if it improved the quality of life or the overall playing experience, it's simply changed rather than improved. Players more familiar with Sophie would find it better, while those more familiar with Ryza might not. As with previous Atelier games, Post-Game is present and offers higher difficulties, a set of swimsuit skins that looks the same for all characters, and a new difficult boss.Story is much more substantial than previous Atelier games. There were some false climaxes which makes the story feel a bit dragging, but the ending was really emotionally moving and provides a sense of satisfaction rarely felt in the series. The story, as with tradition, is gated with a series of quests. Some of the quests feel tedious and sometimes break the momentum generated by key plot points. This results in a poor story pacing, unfortunate for the beautiful story it tries to tell. This is unpleasantly common for GUST titles so fans of the series would probably be familiar with the pacing.The game also suffers from HORRIBLE balancing. Previous titles, even spin-off titles like Nelke, were always on point in balancing enemy levels with player progress. In Sophie 2, you can smoke regular enemies in one turn, and get absolutely wiped in a boss fight without the latest equipment. I tried not to synthesize too much equipment because the regular monsters feel really too easy to take on and I was afraid being too powerful would ruin the immersion for me, only to get crushed by the chapter boss. In most parts of the main story, you fight bosses in unexpected places and circumstances, often leaving you unprepared. You need to be massively overpowered all the time to make sure your equips are adequate against a surprise boss fight. However, this could be a good thing if you consider battles against regular enemies as just a different form of material gathering, removing extra stress and tediousness, so you can just breeze through small monsters and focus on stage bosses.Regarding the combat, Sophie 2 abandons the real-time turn-based system of Ryza and introduced a fresh take of a pure turn-based system, more streamlined than previous titles but more satisfying. The introduction of Twin Actions and Dual Trigger made sure every character in your party is usable and useful. No more leaving out half of your party in a battle again, everyone has a chance to contribute now. This should be the standard of not just future Atelier games, but also party-based JRPG games in general.Conclusion: Beautiful visuals, good performance (for a Koei Tecmo port), superb story, poor pacing and balancing, a revolutionary combat system, and a great soundtrack, all packed in what can be described as a definitive Atelier experience.

_childDocuments_.review: 117,75hrs spent on my first playthrough. This is by far the most emotional title in the whole Atelier series that I've played, and I've actually played more or less every title from Marie, Elie, Iris, etc. onwards (this means through Mana Khemia, Ar-Tonelico [even though this isn't really part of Atelier series, but it IS by GUST and it DOES have the "alchemy" system], and every more-recent title [those available on STEAM now], oh even Nelke).I've actually followed the Japanese sneak peeks and news before the release of this title so I already knew some stuff and what I could expect before buying and playing the game for the first time. For those of you who don't know on the other hand:- The synthesis system follows the good ol' Mysterious trilogy style, but is much much more Alchemist-friendly and simplified.- Navigation, map touring, etc follows their latest engine, so it feels like Ryza, Lulua and Ryza 2.- Transition between combat and adventure is seamless and immediate without loading / long transition times. Combat is turn-based like older Atelier titles so you don't have to deal with frantic button presses like in Ryza and Ryza 2, which to me was a pain in the a... err.... thumb.- The story ties up TONS of loose ends and fills in the blanks for a lot of stuff that happened throughout the Mysterious series like why Sophie is such a cheat in Firis and Lydie & Suelle, and explains how tons of stuff that happened back in Sophie 1 came to be. I won't fill in the details here, just play the game to find out.- You do  to have played through Sophie 1 in order to play Sophie 2. If you've NOT played Sophie 1 before but wish to jump straight into Sophie 2, just do it. There's a short synopsis available in the main menu of the game. Just select "Story So Far".- For those who might ask, No, you won't get to see Firis, Lydie, Suelle or other characters because this happens RIGHT BEFORE Firis.For fans of Atelier series, this is definitely a must have. The story and game mechanics are just excellent. Although it may feel that the whole story might be a bit short (just like in many other Atelier titles), it had taken me almost 120hours of gameplay to go through the game at a casual pace and this is no mean feat as I tend to finish any first playthrough of any Atelier series game in around 90hours.As at time of writing, there are still a few problems with the game though:- A pretty nasty fail graphic screen ghosting can happen sometimes.- The game had CTODed on me a few times  this only happens after long hours of continuous gameplay and FORTUNATELY the game autosaves VERY OFTEN so I didn't lose any progress at all.- The game will jitter if it doesn't detect a controller. If you have one but don't really enjoy using a controller, just connect it and play on mouse/keyboard anyway, it's no biggie.All in all, I'd highly recommend the game if you're into this sort of game, especially if you're a fan of the series.

_childDocuments_.review: My initial expectation was something along the lines of A20/Lulua, where the effort, budget, and creative energy felt very scaled back from the more traditional mainline releases like the Mysterious trilogy games. I'm not very far in yet but I have done my research and been in this business for over a decade now. Music is definitely scaled back, with a return to VSTs from the mostly live instruments of Ryza 2, and with the entire tracklist being loaded onto two familiar series regulars (except one track by the ACRYLICSTAB guy and the opening vocal song by our beloved Yano). However, it's perfectly fine as comfort food and Yanagawa is such a monster he still has lots of pleasant surprises spread throughout.By virtue of being so much more recent than earlier games like the original Sophie, most of the graphics look super good. I can't get over how good Sophie looks now in 2022. However, I don't think I can get anti-aliasing to work with this game. The borders of character models look extremely rough except from a comfortable distance (then they get a warm glow and the issue vanishes). I'm extremely used to this after so many games, if anyone has a magic solution to it that'd be neat though. The movies drag REALLY hard for me, will check a few settings but for now I am just overlooking the issue since I can view them outside of the game anyway and they're mostly extraneous flavour. The grid alchemy from the rest of the Mysterious trilogy makes a return. Personally, I'm a HUGE fan of it. Ryza's node system felt a little too straightforward particularly in the lategame while earlier series didn't have much room for "active alchemy", mostly relying on just tossing traits back and forth in long strings. The little grid puzzles are fun in seeing what you can squeeze out with some obscure materials. I liked the combat in A19 so much and I have yet to delve into it enough to make much judgment on how the lategame parties shape up, but I am optimistic. Very solid release so far, just recognize it's not the same scale of product as Ryza 2 or Lydie & Suelle. I'll take it over a Ryza 1 for sure...

_childDocuments_.review:
A mysterious story of a mysterious dream...
One of the stories experienced throughout the Alchemist Sophie’s many adventures, as she continued her travels after leaving her hometown of Kirchen Bell.
This is Sophie’s adventure as she searches for her friend Plachta in the dream world Erde Wiege, where they become separated, and shows the bonds she forms with the people she meets and passing of hearts.

■Evolved turn-based battles & seamless transitions!
In the 6 member party turn-based battles, the 3 members in the front and 3 in the back form 2 teams cooperating “multi-linked turn battles”, and transitions from exploration to battles without loading times in “seamless battles”, the entire game can be enjoyed at a great pace.

■2 types of panels for everyone to enjoy synthesis!
This game uses panel synthesis, the synthesis system of the Mysterious series, where materials are placed in the panel slots to create new items in this puzzle-like feature. By placing the certain materials in the slots, various effects can be produced.
There are 2 types of panels in this game that players can select from : a regular panel and a restricted panel that has a higher synthesis difficulty level.
The board of the restricted panel is fairly complex, but when materials are placed just right, items with high effects can be synthesized, which can't be generated from the regular panel.

name: Core Keeper
detailed_description: Roadmap More Great Games! About the Game Awaken as an explorer in a long-forgotten cavern teeming with untold secrets. In this award-winning, 1-8 player mining sandbox adventure, your choices shape an epic journey. Harvest relics and resources, craft advanced tools, build your base, and explore a dynamically evolving world waiting to be unearthed. Level up your skills, defeat legendary Titans, and unveil the power of the Core. Grow your garden, fish in mysterious waters, master a vast array of recipes, raise and care for animals, encounter the Cavelings, and carve out your own unique world in an enchanting underground adventure. MINE RESOURCES Delve deep to harvest precious resources and unearth hidden gems. Craft tools to help you survive, from pickaxes, fishing rods, and shovels to traps, bombs, and mortars. Upgrade your arsenal and equipment with advanced tools like the mighty Obliteration Ray, and automated machinery to streamline mining, smelting, storage, and more. Level up your skills and unlock powerful weapons to conquer the depths. DISCOVER AN ANCIENT WORLD Explore diverse biomes with unique ecosystems and long-forgotten lore. From the living walls of the Clay Caves to the crystal caverns of the Shimmering Frontier, discover more about this mysterious world as you uncover the secrets of the Cavelings. Build a boat to set sail across the Sunken Sea, race across the Desert of Beginnings, and encounter the remnants of ancient civilizations. BUILD, CRAFT & GET CREATIVE Create a totally unique base using a variety of different materials and customisations. From the ultimate adventurer’s lair to a cozy underground cottage, shape the underground your way. Customize your character’s appearance and choose from an array of powerful armor and unique outfits to suit the moment. BATTLE TITANS Face legendary Titans that hold the secret to this long-forgotten world. Sharpen your combat skills against a variety of monsters and mini-bosses, spend talent points to level up your abilities, and plan your strategy to conquer these colossal creatures of the underground. Discover rare and powerful loot to help you on your journey and power up the Core. EXPLORE WITH FRIENDS Enjoy the adventure solo or team up in 2-8 player drop-in/drop-out online co-op. Play your way and explore at your own pace — celebrate the seasons, trade with merchants, hatch your new best friends, design the ultimate base, automate resource gathering, host your own dedicated server, create music on playable instruments and discover an unforgettable sandbox adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: So far the best game with balance in farming (managing hunger), base-building (creative way to mix combination with paintable props and colour paint), and fighting (boss battle, exploration, mobs).I know many would think this is like a combination of so many similar games, but it's really difficult for me to find the a game that can focus on both the importance of farming & harvesting and fighting/bossing, as other games tend to lean on one aspect than the other.Looking forward for more contents to come. _childDocuments_.review: A delightful 2D title taking the best of Terraria, Stardew Valley, and even topdown exploration titles like Classic Zelda’s? Count me in! Even in Early Access, Core Keeper never gets tiresome or repetitive, with genuinely challenging yet rewarding simplistic combat and exploration mechanics baked all throughout the adventure. The progression system is linear enough to avoid getting lost, and any Minecraft or Terraria player should find themselves at home with ore and equipment of advancing status. Meanwhile, like Terraria, it has enough opportunities to stray from the traditional path and take certain opportunities early, for the daring! Alongside these, the farming and hunger system is quite simplistic compared to Stardew Valley or traditional farm titles, but just neat enough to be a warm addition without becoming a barrier or issue. It really is like Terraria in a top-down perspective, in the best way possible! My sole complaint is in the lack of a fast travel system (railroads are too costly and other non-spoiler travel methods are locked too far into progression IMO), and I occasionally wish I had a faster way to go between some already-visited areas. Even with that, easy 9/10 even in early access, can’t wait for the full release and updates to come!

_childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper is spectacular. My friends and I are consistently baffled this is an Early Access title. It has way more content than we expected, has been free of bugs or issues in our experience, and has an incredible amount of charm and personality. As a longtime modded Minecraft player, I've often felt that Core Keeper has taken all the best parts of Minecraft's gameplay progression and loop, and made them better. While you can't build elaborate structures, the little creative things you can do in base-building are satisfying and fun. If you've got a group of friends to play with and you like survival crafting games, I can't recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so my fiance roped me into getting this game. I thought it looked cool and started to play. Within the first 10 minutes I wasn't sure this was for me (keep in mind I haven't ever played a game like this/terraria which is the closest i thought to compare to) my fiance has had lots of experience with these kinds of games so he was instantly hooked. A few days passed and I said "lets try that game again" and we started to play... and let me tell you I was HOOKED.  This game is addicting in the best way. Whether you like to grind it out, decorate, fish, casually play, fight bosses/foes, garden, this game has it all. I truly love this game and would recommend to anyone who loves pixel art and the chance to explore endlessly and practically do whatever you want.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a whole review typed up but Steam decided to yeet it into the abyss, so a tl;dr is all I'll do.Fun co-op survival-crafting game which takes some of the best elements of similar games (Terraria, Starbound, Minecraft, Stardew Valley) and in my opinion mixes them up perfectly. _childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper is an immersive open world crafting game. It has farming, base building, and smooth combat. You're not limited by certain mechanics (e.g. Stardew Valley's sleeping and stamina system) and encouraged to gradually develop alongside your workbench level. I'm at 73 hours playtime yet I'm only now preparing for the final biome's boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to give this game a good review. I love the survival crafting genre, but there are A LOT of improvements that have to be made to make this game more enjoyable. But let's start with what I DID like. (Keep in mind that I'm a pretty casual gamer, so complaints about difficulty may be less warranted.)PROS:-The music is nice. It's relaxing when it needs to be, and epic when it needs to be. Fitting all around.-Collectibles make the game more interesting to play, and there are more incentives to explore.-The weapons are pretty cool so far. -Most of the boss fights are pretty fun. Ghorm gave me quite a spook when I first saw it, not gonna lie.-I love the durability system. You don't have to toss out an item that breaks, you can just repair it at a station! No wasted materials here!-The concept of an ancient underground energy as a plot point is very interesting. Can't wait to see where it goes.-Overall very cute concept with a solid art style.CONS:-PLEASE do not make me craft ten thousand tiers of crafting tables. It's a pain in the butt to have to hunt down materials to upgrade. Wood, tin, iron, scarlet, it literally never stops. I have two rooms in my base dedicated ONLY TO CRAFTING STATIONS. It's utterly asinine. Other survival games like Minecraft and Terraria tend to leave three main crafting stations for common items like weapons, tools, and armor. Maybe a few extras for things like potions and magic items. -The grinding is exhausting. ESPECIALLY when you have bosses that require items to summon them. Namely one of the titans in the Early Access. You need ten pieces each of four different ores that require you to explore different biomes on opposite sides of the map. It's a chore. Straight up not enjoyable.-Some of the enemies are ridiculously overpowered, even when you have the best armor and weapons available. -Some of the bosses are enemy spam/bullet hell. Please don't.EXTREMELY FRUSTRATING:-Supposedly a softcore character does not lose items upon death... Uh, they do. your ENTIRE INVENTORY OUTSIDE YOUR HOTBAR is lost and you have to retrieve it. No. Just no.-Boss items take a ridiculous amount of ore to make. Some of which, RNJesus does not make it easy to find. It should not take 45 pieces of ore to craft a freaking egg. Some games such as Terraria only require five of a particular item, maybe ten of another. And such items are much easier to find. SUGGESTIONS:-Game rules such as keep inventory--hunting down your items after you die is a pain in the ass when you die on the very edge of the map and have to make a LONG trek just to retrieve them. -Game difficulty settings--I am a pretty casual gamer so if you intend to make the game this difficult I'd very much like to play on baby mode.-Tone down the enemy spawn rate during boss fights.-Consider nerfing the titans a tiny bit.  Their fights don't need to be that hard.OVERALL:Early access is literal hell. I'm optimistic about the full release. I understand Early Access is just testing your demographic and receiving feedback on how to improve. Hope my review helped. Because as it currently is, Core Keeper makes me want to fold my monitor twelve times. Unfortunately had to request a refund. I will consider buying it back once the full release is out, IF some suggestions are honored.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Gardening tools are some of the best tools in the game for adventuring. Enemies spawn out of slime and moss on the floor and tilling the area picks up a bunch of it instantly. Remove hazards, control spawns, reduce lag. Always carry a gardening tool with you and make sure it's reinforced.Struggling with a boss? Don't neglect the cooking system! Food buffs are insanely powerful and can turn any boss into an <1 minute encounter. Fishing in the clay biome can give a fish that negates slime slow when cooked."Stationary drills" are found in the automation table. You can find extremely simple setups for them with one google search. Mining boulders will save you a ton of time grinding ores.Glow is an awesome stat. Always remember to upgrade your lantern and maybe cook some food with glow tulips sometimes. Save your sanity, you don't need to cover the map in torches anymore!

_childDocuments_.review: Shockingly good for early access. I've encountered minimal bugs, and most issues can be resolved with a quick search or just keeping on the discovery path.Great balance between exploration, battle, crafting/discovering, and base-building, with that last one being largely optional- though you probably want to get your chests and crafting stations organized at some point. If you enjoy games like Terraria or Minecraft, this has a huge chance of being a hit. The progression seems really solid so far, and bosses seem to be just the right amount of challenge (for when I encounter and fight them, but I have to admit I haven't beaten all yet), and if you're struggling you can just run away and try again later. Death is punishing, but not so much so that you get frustrated and give up. It's a bit of a search through crafting stations when you know what you want to make but not where to find it, but it's not enough to be an issue, at least where I'm at. The lack of guidance in the game is a charm instead of a point of frustration, but a bit more help with, for example, a Terraria-style bestiary would be nice (I had to go to the wiki to find out how I could get the king slime summon). If graphics/looks are your thing, this game PROVIDES, it's the most stunning pixel game ever laid my eyes on so far. There's some awesome-looking pixel stuff out there, but for me this takes the cake and slams it in my face at the exact speed it takes for me to unhinge my jaw like a snake and swallow it whole.All in all, this game is already fantastic (I would go as far as to say one of my best purchases) and has great potential to become even better. I feel like the devs know what they want and have a great chance of getting it if they keep at it like this.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice cozy game! good break from no audio apex or stressful elden. no riot here~ far less tilting even if you die you just go back and pick your stuff up. your not completely helpless tho! all your armor, your pet, and equipment slots 1-9 is still on you upon revive. its  also nice you can break early game terrain like dirt or rock with your fists or a torch. later game you will need pick axes but it helps for early game starters. raged fighting seems more reliable but i started warrior and adapted quickly and you can just pick up a staff or bow and start ranged fighting if you wanted later in the game so the starting class really doesnt matter. im just a tanky mage now lmao. if you break things put them in your pocket and take it back to base. what you kill is yours now. so thats nice. huge map to explore so that will take a while and you have to find the boss locations thru exploring. i highly enjoy this game since i love the customizability of terraforming my base

_childDocuments_.review: In short, very old school game, like playing SNES Zelda/Minecraft on steroids. Huge maps, lots of enemies, items, and materials. Very good basic game with a lot of cool stuff in it. My only complaint would be a more fleshed out class system, the game feels very difficult to level up traits for a class, its just a whatever levels up situation from what I can see. Clothes and weapons make the class basically. I just end up playing ranged class because melee is too risky and mage eats too much mana to be fast enough for farming. I would like to see a real healer class. There is a chef, and fisherman, and those are not really worth being a class, they are more like side jobs. There should be a fighting class and a job pick imo. Anyway, there are mods I haven't tried but I hope a little more goes into this game, I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game but feels like a beta instead of a full release. Too many missing QoL features and content. There is a ton of ideas that could be taken from terraria/starbound that would be super easy to implement but weren't.Some of the gripes I had:- Hardmode feels like terraria Expert > Master rather than Normal > Expert, only increases monster HP/DMG.- Can auto stack into chest but no way to favorite items.- One of the starting Ores (tin) felt insanely hard to get early game.- Teleport home available way too late.- Loot system feels like terraria with half the inventory space.- Lackluster/uninteresting weapons, armor, and accessories. Ex. Summoner spec only has 3 weapons available, counting the starting weapon, and the 2nd one I got was borderline worthless.- Pets/minions don't auto attack- The game is very dark, torches/lights don't illuminate a wide enough area.- Didn't find fishing enjoyable (only fished when I seen bubbles)- Food system is atrocious, too many varieties. I just want to fill my food bar but have to waste buff food (this is a me problem).- couldn't figure out a way to use food/buff potions from inventory. When doing bosses have to put all buffs on hotbar and use them individually when boss spawns (only lasts 1 minute). (b to use all buffs in terraria).- Didn't find the crafting system compelling. Lots of useless feeling crafting stations.- No workshop modding support yet.- Frequent crashes while playing (Multiplayer + both running Linux so might not be an issue on Windows)- I didn't get immersed into the environment/exploration to the extent of terraria/starbound.Hopefully they continue to update the game. Still a decent play, my expectations are simply set very high due to other games in the same genre.

_childDocuments_.review: The progression of the game is very confusing at first but once you beat the first three main bosses and get past the wall this game is fantastic. I found myself comparing this game to terraria quite a bit initially but now that I've played more of it, it is an entirely different game with it's own unique mechanics. that being said, i'd say it's much more difficult than terraria, pretty much no matter how much progress you make it feels as though you're never truly safe while exploring new areas. The biggest downside of this game in my opinion is probably the lack of unique weapons and equipment, there's only a handful of items for each "class" in the game which is a negative in my opinion because, to me one of the most exciting things whilst playing a game like this is getting fun new items to use at each stage of the game and furthermore having a variety of different items to choose from based on your play-style. perhaps the worst of this is summoning because there are only  3 summon weapons in the entire game and the only real difference between them is their attack mechanics they all fundamentally do the same amount of dps and only exceed or fall short of each other in specific scenarios. Regardless I think this game is a great addition to the open world survival craft genre and I'd recommend purchasing if you are looking for something fresh with a fairly high level of difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Aquatic titan is not a well designed boss if all it does is spit an ungodly number of tornadoes at you that suck you toward them, limiting movement thus making it so you can't outmaneuver them easily if at all, and then get three shot with no hope of recovering using healing items. 'Course this is as a single player mage with a max level pet, fairly decent stats grinded out, and gear that is supposed to be at level with this boss rather than overcompensating by venturing into arguably more dangerous areas that are sequentially after this boss. Lest I'm missing something, it's a new and unhinged mechanic to have to resist bullet hazards sucking you in. And if they're stacked up or you get combo'd because you didn't react fast enough to falling into one and getting pulled into others, GG you die with no hope of healing. And if this is only a midgame boss? I actively shudder to think what the end game bosses are going to do.Everything else is a well done and a fairly well constructed experience up to this point, yet it feels awful to keep dying to the same boss and then have to grind out the materials you need to resummon it because it killed you. It's not the only boss that does this, had I perished to two of the required bosses before this I'd have to resummon them as well. Only the first two bosses, Glurch and Ghorm, and a couple of optionals so far, the larvae queen and the toxic slime, don't require an item to summon them or to rematch if you die on the first fight. The toxic slime actually required a bit of thinking because healing in its arena is off the table and the slime slows you down, but that's surmountable. Having to grind out materials for a rematch? That will always feel awful. I know the ever comparable Terraria does that too and it's not excusable there either.So either bosses need rebalancing or after they've been successfully summoned once you need to be able to refight it without expending more resources. Provided the expended resources are difficult or otherwise time consuming to acquire.Core Keeper can do so much better than this.

_childDocuments_.review: I found that this game had a lot of grinding and a slow item progression system, which was fine for the most part. However, I had a problem with the gameplay between the third boss and the fourth boss. If the developer doesn't rework this section of the game, I think a lot of players will stop playing after beating the third boss. The issue is that the gameplay between these two bosses is just not as enjoyable as it could be, and it can be frustrating for players who are trying to progress through the game. Additionally, I found the character job feature to be largely useless, despite the fact that it grants additional skill points and items at the beginning. This is because it requires five skill points to unlock new abilities, regardless of your character's job. This means that you'll need to grind for skill points in order to unlock new abilities, which can be tedious and time-consuming. One potential solution to this issue is to adjust the skill point requirements based on the character's job. For example, a miner character might require three skill points for the mining skill and four skill points for the running skill, while a cook or gardener character might require six or seven skill points for those skills. This would allow players to specialize in certain areas and make the progression system feel more balanced and fair. If the skill point requirements are the same for every job, you will eventually reach the same level of progression as other players, which can make the game feel less unique and rewarding. It could also enhance the experience of playing with other people, as players could choose different jobs and work together to progress through the game. I would recommend that the developer consider implementing this change in order to improve the overall gameplay experience. Despite these issues, the sense of accomplishment that comes with slowly working your way up and unlocking new items may still make the game enjoyable for some players. Keep in mind that this game is still in early access, so there may be additional updates and changes in the future. Overall, if you enjoy games that require a lot of grinding and have a slow item progression system, this game might be worth giving a try.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting one for me...while i enjoyed much of the game, after nearly 70 hours (defeated 10+ bosses - including optional - still more to go) decided to call it quits. The game has many fun elements and several components that differentiate it from Terraria and Stardew (as it's often compared to). However, they really need to consider introducing some quality of life changes. Having to farm a rare item to locate a boss on a very vast map can feel like a chore, after a while I realized I was in a loop. Beat boss, determine next boss, farm ore in that biome, upgrade items, find rare items to "locate" boss, beat boss. Losing a boss fight was a bit heartbreaking toward end game as I knew I'd need to farm to find that one element, to craft that one summoning item again. Really took the joy out of it for me.I'm still giving the game a thumbs up, though I won't be finishing it. It has enough dynamism and unique content to make it a good game, overall. The graphics are beautiful, discovering temples and other hidden places feels genuinely rewarding and exciting, and it really is its own game. Hours passed by...I was immersed. It's not a copycat - they've done well here and it's worth a look...hope they continue to fine tune.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ridiculously good. It's well balanced, there is enough content to keep me interested, clearly, since I am at 400 hours. Although the main concept is pretty easy to pick up, there are different types of monsters to fight, and definitely the opportunity to figure out strategies for each type - ie ranged, hand to hand, and develop on those over time, like building walls, laying traps, digging moats, etc.  Core Keeper is a lot of fun individually and with a couple of friends. I like the new features, and unusual for me - I even made a couple of hardcore characters, one death and *poof* gone for good, I normally am not skilled enough at games to enjoy the challenge of hardcore, so this one really does cater to a wide range of gaming ability and allows enjoyment even if you aren't the most dexterous with the controller or keyboard. One nitpick, there are a couple of "bottlenecks" in the game where you have to complete certain tasks before you can progress. Like the tasks needed to gain access to drilling for example. I started to get a little frustrated at this point but eventually figured it out. Initially I was dubious about the "old school" look - I am not a fan of minecraft - but I actually quite like the simplicity and it certainly doesnt detract at all from the gameplay experience.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun.  Hitting walls and enemies feels good.  Building your base is awesome.  There seems to be plenty to explore.  I think this will be expanded on further as time goes on.  You feel like you are getting stronger.  The crafting isn't overly complicated.  It is just good ol' exploring, fighting, and getting stronger.   When you die, it was your fault, not the game's fault!  I generally do not buy Early Access titles, but this one was irresistible to get.  Get a group of friends together and play the game.  It is a GREAT multiplayer experience.The one gripe I would have is that it did not run very well on an older computer that had no issues with Stardew Valley and Terraria. _childDocuments_.review: Also have about 250+ hours of play time on PSN.Minecraft meets 2D top down zelda with lite RPG mechanics. Level is tied to gear progression and skill/talent tree that players can reset at any given time with ingame currency. XP is earned per action performed (IE, mining blocks is +1 xp gained, same withing melee, fishing,... etc). There is no colony sim management, but there are NPC merchants that spawn the same way they do in terraria. Speaking of which, the game is filled with many easter eggs and references to other popular indie survival games such as terraria and deep rock galactic (not sure if DRG counts as indie). Nostalgic 16-24 bit visuals, ambient BGM, and impressive ray tracing (shimmering water is a little too blinding in large open space, take caution here). Highly recommend for what it's worth, game has immense potential comparable to minecraft's earlier days.

_childDocuments_.review: ‣ 8/10 – The 1.0 update added a lot of good content.‣ Thoughts: The first time I played Core Keeper; I wasn’t a big fan of it. Some aspects really rubbed me the wrong way and left me bitter. However, the recent 1.0 update fixed almost all of the issues that I had with this title.Today, Core Keeper is a full game with an ending and plenty of content to experience. At first it was a really grindy game with a few boss fights but not much else. Now these problems are addressed and removed. Once you start a new world you get to choose how the world will be shaped. You can select the number of ore that will spawn, how the biomes will mix into each other and how many rivers there will be. These changes allow the player to create a personal experience both in world design and gameplay grid. The game still looks beautiful and has better ray tracing than any title known to me. Combat still has its issues and some boss fights are just poorly designed, but the overall experience is way better.Now there are tons of new weapons to play with, armor sets to try out and classes to experiment with. Depending on your difficulty the game will roughly take you about 50 hours to complete and that depends on how grindy you made it for yourself in the world editor. The story here is simplistic, but enough to keep you going. I’m not saying this title needs a deep narrative, but considering the developers themselves said: “Core Keeper is about exploring and uncovering the story an ancient underground world” it does come across as a bit silly. The best part of this game is just simply exploring the lands and acquiring new gear to play with.Overall, Core Keeper is a way better game than it was a year ago and a must try if you enjoy sandbox survival games with fantasy elements.
