_childDocuments_.review: Okay, you are reading through the reviews to determine if this game is worth buying, and for you. I'll try to be very brief (LOL) and address what you will see in both the recommend and not recommend comment sections.A lot of people compare Core Keeper to Stardew Valley, which if a fair comparison because Core Keeper does have a very similar farming process, but is a much smaller aspect of the game, and not the central game loop like Stardew Valley was. The crops can be sold for in-game currency (not much) but this isn't their primary purpose in Core Keeper. The different crops (which there are quite a few) can be cooked in different ways to create food that gives a large assortment of status buffs (in the late game all your buffs look like a World of Warcraft buff list for a raid boss).A lot of people will also make the comparison to Terraria, which is a much closer comparison to Core Keeper's central game loop. You explore a randomly generated map (which is massive) with many different biomes, and slowly discover new materials --> upgrade equipment with new materials --> fight new Boss and repeat. However, I enjoyed Core Keeper much more than I did Terraia, and I suspect it has to do with Core Keeper being designed in a angled top-down perspective VS. Terraria's Side-scroller perspective. I just think the game play works better and is overall more enjoyable. The crafting system in Core Keeper is pretty "standard fare" to other games like it. However, I did enjoy and find the Automation systems, in particular the electrical circuit stuff to be rewarding. The game doesn't force you to dive very deep into this aspect if that isn't your thing. However, I think this is the one aspect of Core Keeper that allows the most creativity and a little problem solving when trying to conceive mechanical belt/robot arms/smelting systems etc. It is slightly similar in a sense to Factorio except it is more of a "Factorio Lite" version (which is a good thing in my opinion). MAJOR ISSUE: one thing you need to consider prior to buying the game is how much story element is important in your gaming experience. I know Core Keeper bills itself as a sandbox game and not an RPG. However, I was really shocked by the absence of any kind of narrative at all.... I mean there is not any "meat on the bone". You are presented with 2 or so sentences at the start of the game. Maybe another 2 simple sentences around mid-game and that is it. Don't misunderstand me either, there is no passive environmental narrative going on either. The few NPC don't give a single sentence of flavor text; which would be so simple to put in the game, and go a long way for overall user experience.I think if you are playing with someone else or better yet, a group of people, you will not notice or take much issue with the absence of any kind of story. However, if you are playing solo (like I did) then you really need to consider this prior to purchasing the game. EARLY ACCESS: The DEV team seems to steadily be pumping out new content (biomes/bosses/machines/quality of life) every 4 or so months. They appear to be socially active and taking community feedback and actually adding things in. All great signs for any early access game.

_childDocuments_.review: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐Core Keeper is the delightful love child of Minecraft, Stardew Valley, and Terraria, and it has quickly become one of my favorite games of the year! 🌟From the moment you start exploring its charming underground world, you'll feel the same sense of wonder and adventure as in Minecraft, with a focus on building and resource gathering. _childDocuments_.review: It's a hard game to rate, because there are a lot of nice things in the game, but ultimately where the game falls down at the moment is that there is no content. Aside from 12 easy boss fights, there is some progression in gear and capability, but that's just chasing ore blocks in different biomes allowing you to craft the necessary pieces to go get the next ore blocks from the next biome, not really content. There are some collection goals and "quests" that require you to find items from the world, but that is not really content either.Trying to find things like Threads of Fate (one of those "quests" that asks you to locate multiple items from the game world) is entirely at the mercy of the random number generator, so you have to comb the biomes with a fine brush for hours and hours hoping that the procedural generator decides to generate you a block with the necessary shrine in it, or click digging spots on the ground for hours upon end hoping that the rng decides to land on the right item from the loot table, which wouldn't be so frustrating if there was something to spice it up between, but there isn't. The biomes have little to offer and chasing the random number generator becomes an exercise in frustration.Some of the "quests" and such are guaranteed to spawn on an exact distance from the center of the world, which is alright because you know you will run into it eventually, but when things can be literally anywhere, or the results are entirely up to loot tables with low chances to roll, then the game stops respecting your time and it stops being fun rapidly.There is nothing to do in the Core Keeper sandbox either. The only way you can "get creative" is to build a base, that is, put some walls down and decorate as you please. While games like Minecraft and Satisfactory are sandboxes as well, the major difference is that their sandboxes offer a lot more in terms of logic. You can build cool machines, you can automate, and get clever about problem solving through the use of logic and machines. In Core Keeper, you don't really have those options, so there isn't really anything cool to build or invent. I think there is a lot of power in allowing the player to get creative about problem solving as well (and present them with some problems to solve), not just base decoration.I put a lot of hours into the game because I'm a bit of a completionist, and I've played grindier games too, but I think I might be done here until there is substantially more content. I haven't had fun in the game for a long, long time.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not understand who they thought the intended audience for this game was. Every aspect is subpar.This does not feel like a 1.0 release, but rather an early access release. Once you complete the first 3 bosses and open up the rest of the map, the game slows down to a snails pace. It's incredible how bad the pacing is, this is very much a wiki game if you want to do things in any reasonable amount of time. This is in large part due to the fact that bosses either need 90+ of an item that is not a guaranteed drop from a certain enemy type. The other item needed for the important bosses, that you need 10-40 depending on the boss, is a static object that blends into the ground, and is very easy to miss. It was not until I was agonizing over the 10 feathers that I realized they were on the ground and needed to be broken to be picked up, because the seashells were always just on the ground as a dropped item whenever I saw them. So I wasted a ton of time just killing enemies hoping for the 1% drop chance.You will not fight another unique boss for 10s of hours because of this. For some reason, you not only have to use boss scanners to find their location, you have to make the summoning items as well. Unless it's a certain repeat boss from the first 3, then you just need to scan.Exploration feels pointless for the most part as the main goal is looking for big ore nodes that you can drill, it is pointless to mine by hand. Btw, this is where most of my playtime comes from, waiting for the drills to mine nodes, I just left the game open and would occasionally do a bit of farming.There's really no weapon variety either. there's basically 3 kinds of weapon for each class, unless you decide to play summoner, in which case there might as well only be one and it does not scale well beyond the first couple bosses.This game obviously took a ton of inspiration from stuff like terraria and stardew, but for some reason took none of the QoL that made terraria fun and took the negatives from stardew valley.Farming is the most annoying thing because despite being able to harvest a 5x5, you can still only plant 1 by 1. You can't just right click replace flooring either, it is a very slow and tedious process if you want to change how your base looks, having to smack each tile 2 times to pick it up and then replace it. The sledge hammer lets you hit them in an aoe but it's still not enough, and would break walls, chests, and crafting benches as well.I'm assuming every missing QoL feature is missing because there's a mod button on the main menu where you can see what the missing QoL is very easily, they're just too lazy to add them to the game and instead rely on modders to do so for them.One of the most egregious is that hitboxes are where the enemies feet touch the ground. So any of the taller enemies are only a horizontal 1x2 tiles at their feet, and just feel bad to fight with ranged weapons if not standing above or below them.---You can't use items from your inventory, you have to painstakenly stop what you're doing, move an item to your hotbar, use it, put it back, to get buffs that only last 1 minute.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like the game itself, especially after 1.0.The atmosphere, the music, the graphic design, everything just fits. Simply running around in this game just feels right. But man, once you progress past the outer wall and get to the higher tiered materials the game gets progressively more and more grindy and tiring. The more advanced the resource, the more you need of it. Copper armor is around 6 bars per piece, Solarite armor, which we are at currently, needs around 30-35 bars per piece. And this goes for everything, equip, craftingstations. boss spawners, everything just gets more and more tedious the farther you progress. The resources you need get more and more harder to acquire due to beeing farther away from spawn, stronger enemies, etc., yet you instantly need more of it than you needed of the ore before. This just keeps you stuck in the "my gear is too low for this biome, but i need to get the resource of this biome to get the right gear to survive this biome"-Phase for way longer than it should. It's no fun progressing if everything progress gives you is just a longer list of stuff you need to get. As said, i really like this game itself, i love building little cottages, decorating and simply just enjoying the wonderful soundtrack while doing some fishing or farming. But the grind in the later stages really muddies the water for me, so much in fact that i just cant give it the thumbs up it should deserve. It's also not that i dont recommend it at all, it really has some redeeming qualities, the grind is just not for me personally, that's more of a preference thing i guess.

_childDocuments_.review: Good light-action game with digging and gear collection for your character. Feels like a top-down version of Terraria, though this game is still relatively new compared to Terraria.=Combat= Pros:Combat is smooth and responsive, with different weapons featuring unique attack motions, all of which feel satisfying to use. Hitboxes are surprisingly well done—better than you’d expect for a top-down action game. Navigating your character is well-paced and fluid, neither too slow nor too fast. The movement and combat feel even better than Hades, in my opinion.Cons:There are limited options for combat in each "class." For example, as a ranged archer, your best move is your basic attack for most of your playthrough; only one skill per weapon is available, and often, the skill isn’t particularly useful so better just focus on dodging. This is similar for Summoner and Sorcerer, although each has unique armor sets. I think this will improve as the devs add more item variations and unique abilities for each class.=Exploring= Pros:Exploring and mining are decent, with lots of beautiful places and buildings to discover, plus side-quest-like areas with mystery-solving elements. These structures add atmosphere to the world and look really cool.Cons:As this game is still relatively new compared to other sandbox games, there aren’t enough items to make exploration feel rewarding. Especially with chests—after a few, you start finding the same items: potions, basic materials, and one green gear most of the time, and that’s about it.=Building= Pros:Building is the best part of this game. The range of materials all look distinct and pretty, and different light sources really change the vibe of your room. The controls for building, rotating, and breaking objects are well-designed and user-friendly.Cons:Many special furniture and structures can only be obtained by exploring and breaking the environment. While this isn’t necessarily bad, as it encourages exploration, from a building perspective, it limits the variety of items available until you explore and collect limited quantities of simple structures, like just a campfires.Overall, this is a polished and content-rich game, and it is going to be a new Terraria alternative for the next 10+ years with mod support. That’s why I’ll hold off finishing the game now and come back when it’s more fleshed out, maybe even with insane mods like Terraria’s Calamity mod.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I thought I'd enjoy this game, but there are just some things that make this game lacklustre.- The music and art are both quite good, but the music gets repetitive very quickly since there are so few soundtracks.-The map is far too large for the amount of content that the game has available. -Combat is dull and ends with either you killing enemies with little to no difficulty or getting killed immediately. -progression was a drag, and all of it required "Exploration" which is miserable with how little there is to explore.-Leveling system was so dull that I've seen better in bad mobile games that popup as ads on youtube-transportation is a nightmare since not one moment is spent where you're not dragging yourself through floor slime-Boss fights are uninspired and really remind you how bad the combat isWith a $30 price tag and almost three years to get the games ♥♥♥♥ together, I don't have high hopes for what is going to come in the future, though I don't think the game is abysmal. _childDocuments_.review: The game was quite fun until I ran up against three major issues that are deal breakers for me.#1 I could not find the next boss - Malugaz the corrupted. He is in a throne room that you have to find manually in a massive part of the map. The only way to find him is by doing hours of mining in columns. Other bosses have a way for you to pay special items in order to locate the boss automatically. Not this one.#2 Everything becomes extremely expensive. You really have to grind for hours on end to get enough resources to buy the next level of upgrades. The game was pretty fun until this point.#3 I wasted so much time walking around the ginormous map. The map could easily be half the size. You have the ability to build portals later in the game but they are super expensive to build and have a 20 minute delay before you can use them once they are built. I also built an expensive railway system that took hours to build and only went across 1/4 of the map.The game is no longer fun and I won't be playing it anymore because of these reasons.

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh. Maybe it's my fault. Because I don't like down-voting games. Somehow i keep coming back to build/adventure games, wanting to like them and mostly I just don't. I think i'd rather more of a level of adventure, and less 'craft this, you need that' kind of gameplay.It's in EA, so it may get better, but i think this is the style. Think somewhere between things like Stardew, Rimworld, Portal Knights/Minecraft (minus the 1st person view) etc. The other issue for me is - and this may be just because it's EA - it's just not really clear what you're doing.  Read the wiki, go kill the slime boss, that's a start, but now what. If there's no real hints and you have to go explore everywhere by tunnels to find more stuff, then it's just not for me.TO BE CLEAR, the game isn't bad, but it's not for me. _childDocuments_.review: 2024 - Aug 30th 2024Ultimately this game fails to be outstandingA decent game marred by some unforgivable sins- Extremely poor inventory management will plague any experience... you have dozens if not hundreds of useless garbage items you are forced to always pickup... items of utterly no value that you are forced to stash in very small chests or discard...  But every 1/1000 of these garbage items is needed to use to craft, nothing tells you or sets these pieces of trash apart from one another... and your inventory is to start minimal and at the end still painfully small especially when you encounter hundreds of other trash items by thenYOU WILL spend 20% of the game throwing useless garbage away out of your inventory- Extremely poor leveling / gameplay balance... for reference, it won't take you long to realize that melee, ranged, magic, and summons all pale pathetically to mining for killing enemies...Lemme make this abundantly clear... Melee SUCKS... not only do enemies do 75 - 400% of your maximum health per hit, but they are all rangedRanged is MEDICORE... as above, but they move randomly to avoid attacks while randomly attacking youMagic SUCKS... imagine ranged damage but lower, slower, and with a limited useSummons... my god... summons are beyond garbage... like I struggle to come up with a game where summons are this bad...Which leaves Mining... fast attack, range attack, melee attack, allows for healing... massive damage... yeah don't bother with regular weapons...- EXTREMELY poor enemy balance... imagine dark souls... now suck out all the skill and expertise that you can use to overcome enemies... now make most enemies one hit kills though the entire game... NOW make MOST enemies use ranged attacks in random patterns often 1.5x - 7x faster than you can move... NOW make most enemies take 5 - 125 hits to kill... NOW make most enemies drop garbage that clogs your inventory... NOW make most enemies spawn in large numbers... NOW make healing utterly garbage until end game where it becomes so utterly pointless that you can tank the final boss- EXTREMELY poor world map layout... sure you can get 9 permanent health buffs in the game... oh 1 per world... randomly thrown into the map... good luck finding that literal needle in a haystack- EXTREMELY poor base management... you have to interact with individual chests to actually deposit or use things... yes structures can pull from something IMMEDIATELY adjacent to it, but that is extremely small in scope and you have oh so much to surround it with... farming... no that is painful and a joke and ALSO NECESSARY TO SUFFER through... enjoy micro managing this boring aspect... Fishing barely a footnote, Digging barely a footnote... etc- I would go on but this is a 6/10 game that people have rated highly because it DID have promise but they biffed thatEdit - 2022 EA reviewYea, its got promiseKeeping for relevance

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. Has elements similar to many others combined together to make something unique and interesting. The similarities to other games means a lot of it's mechanics will be very familiar and easy to pick up. Despite that there is some learning curve as there is no hand holding or tutorial but you often get moments where you think "oh, this works like" [insert game the mechanic is inspired by]. I have seen elements from Valheim, Minecraft, Moonlighter, Stardew Valley etc. however it doesn't feel like I'm playing a knock off or inferior version of any of those games - it is it's own thing with enough mechanics and content to make it worthy of your time. I actually didn't enjoy Terreria or Stardew Valley but enjoy this much more. Plays great on steam deck too.

_childDocuments_.review: I have no friends so this review is only about singleplayer experience.I bought the game on the day it launched in early access.Seems like a dumb idea, huh? NOT THIS TIME!If you're a fan of sandbox games like Terraria, you will definitely enjoy this one.Gameplay is somewhat of a mix between Terraria and Stardew Valley (graphic style also gives me slight Starbound vibe) - The main objectives include exploration, mining, fighting enemies (and a few bosses), crafting items, farming, building your base, as well as leveling up your character in few different skills: mining, gardening, fishing, melee and ranged combat, vitality, cooking, crafting and agility/movement. The world is procedurally generated and I especially recommend getting into the game with knowing as little as possible. Feels like the day I played Terraria or Minecraft for the first time.The only problem (what actually may be a pro for some) is that first two bosses are very easy to cheese (I still havent fought others).Definitely worth the money :) I'm looking forward to see how the game grows in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is dramatically mis-billed. It bills itself as a top-down, 2d, cutesy sword-swingy pickaxe-the-earth-and-build-your-base game.It is in fact Factorio Underground, which you will only get to enjoy after reaching "endgame." The community for this game is  to anything which would enhance the "I am a Valheim Dwarf building a Dwarf Fortress" experience because "it would constitute a penalty for not playing your way." They like to tear down and rip to shreds anyone who proposes any such things on their Discord server with a combination of fallacious and disingenuous arguments.I was so frustrated and attacked by the community that I left their Discord server and uninstalled it. This game is no longer fun to me, in vast part because of how hostile the community was to me.----Original review for posterity below:If you're a fan of Valheim-like single-character-control action and building/crafting, and a fan of top-down 2d sprite-based games with a look reminiscent of the 16-bit era without being slavishly confined to aping 16-bit hardware capabilities, and most of all, if you yearn to be a Dwarf, digging a hole, a la Dwarf Fortress...Then you will like Core Keeper. Excuse me, I need to go diggy-diggy hole.

_childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper is a decent game, but it doesn't really stand out in any way. The story is almost non-existent. The crafting system is ok, but doesn't coordinate as well as it could. For example, farm animals provide one type of good. You don't typically need many of these goods and they don't really coordinate into something more complex. While early game ores let you build a large number of tools and buildings, the later ones are much more limited. Crafting stations could've been combined or upgradable to save space too.The gameplay is decent overall. I don't feel like the fighting is a strong point, but it's not a bad one either. You get several options for playstyles, though some can feel a lot weaker or stronger unless you've really optimized your gear. Most gear is found by RNG though as the craftable options are quite limited. So you might need a wiki and patience to find what you need.The late game started to feel tedious to me. Lots of wandering hoping that whatever material I needed would eventually drop - and the world wasn't interesting enough to make the grind fun. It'd probably be better in a group though. Also, many bosses require spending resource to create an item to fight them. If you die, you need the item again. I prefer boss fights where you don't have to waste a bunch of time just to have the right to fight them again.Overall, it's a fine game if you've got time to kill or don't mind grinding, but it's not amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: 5/10, November 2022. So brutally grindy. If you are someone who likes to 100%, please avoid this game. The grinding requires a stupid amount of hours. I'd say of my 250 hours played I have probably 100 looking for legendary item pieces, to which I gave up on Thread of Fate (Dynamic spawn gtfo). Mining required a script and multiple 24-hour days of CONSTANT mining to get to 100. Really wish I didn't desire that 100%. would have saved me a lot of peace and time.Solid 7/10 in current stage. Lots to do. Lots to change.The game itself plays very similarly to Terraria. Mostly 2-track gameplay, either ranged or melee, with not much in the way of weapon variation.Basebuilding, farming plants, cooking foods, unique bosses, massive world exploration, plethora of time-eating secrets, minor automation of mining.Things that need to changeMining and automation feels uncomfortable and useless at higher levels. With one single node on automine, I had over 1k of every bar.Farming - Autoharvester. Watering increases, but nothing else. Replanting every seed was awful. Make some sort of machine, tool, something to plant 5x5 sets of seeds at a time please. My plants finish growing by the time I finish planting.Food - More tiers of combinations. Maybe an improved cooking station or talent that allows 3 food combos. Maybe a reward for # of recipes discovered. There are so many that after a few dozen I lost interest in completion.Achievements - Generally needed but I assume its on the roadmapTalents - I have like one boss left in the game and my ranged combat is only at 40, seems like it raises disproportionately to farming, cooking, running, mining, vitalityStill, a great direction and a fun time all around. I'm at 70 hours, and I have plenty more to do with whole areas not even unlocked yet.

_childDocuments_.review: This game as all around satisfying to play with good controls, a very in-depth and creative food system, and a nice little splatter of automation. Its fun and rewarding with a fair difficulty curve and would definitely recommend to my friendsThe Bosses (for the most part) are fun and rewarding to fight with a variety of different approaches to each, that being said there is ONE boss that i need to address because he is so far the only boss i have encounter that was not fun or interesting to fight, and that is the sea Titan. There's no nice way to put this, the sea Titan needs a rework, up until him the only things we had to grind for was materials, but the sea titan is just a slog, hes only attacks are spawn tornadoes which aren't that difficult to avoid or predict and spawning 3 2X2 tentecles that can take a quarter of your health away, take way too many shots to kill and can rapidly box in players at the rate he spawns them. this boss was not fun or interesting to fight and so far the only advice i can find is "grind your stats to max" and i am not doing that, leveling a stat takes forever and i see no reason to continue playing this game until the sea titan is reworked to match the more skill based bosses rather than just a nonsensical war of attrition where victory is not reliant on your skills as a player but weather you grinded yourself to max and painstakingly min, maxed your gear for a specific boss, which as i mentioned before i do not have either the time or patience to do, it was rather demoralising and rather Jarring to me to encounter such a poorly made boss after the others have been very creative and interesting, and furthermore FAIR to fight, the fights were harsh and punishing but in a way that made me go "i made a mistake there" or "welp that death is my own fault" but not Mr Sea Titan, when i and my friend who was with me at the time died to the ridiculously high amount of tentacles that we couldn't kill fast enough dispite being in full Octarine gear and haveing our core stats at around 50 each, we got completely overwhelmed and after we both respawned neither of us want to try the fight again as again as i said before, this boss doesn't feel like a test of my skills i have learned and fighting him didn't take any real skill or challange it was just a game of whack a mole that i had no chance of winning.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty great. It really limits you on choices though, obviously holding your hand and guiding you through the first couple of bosses, bronze for Giant Slime, tin for Giant Centipede, iron for the Hive Mother, respectively. My review is also based on .The map is randomly generated and there are a few bosses that you need to beat to progress to the next biome. The biomes itself are pretty well made, though 80% of the time all you do is just dig through walls non stop. You see, the map is generated in pockets/rooms and between them there's rarely any path. Ores also only generate inside walls so The combat is pretty basic. Your melee just swing right in front of you and you can shoot with range weapon. Most enemies have basic AI so they just . I don't know if the end-game weapon will change this (as of writing I'm still roughly 1/3 of the way) but so far its . Boss fights just end up depending if you have enough heals to tank some hit or cheese it with range.The game have a skill tree but it can get really grindy to get some of them to high level. Some skills level up on their own (like Mining and Running because thats all you do in this game) while some needs some heavy commitment to grind (looking at you Fishing).You dont really play this kind of game without some cool base building involved. Though if you are lazy you can always just make a Lawn Base and drop all crafting bench and chest sprawling about, I wont judge.

_childDocuments_.review: ====================================================Edit:The creator of Core Keeper, Prantare responded to this review.As I stated in the beginning of this review, I genuinely do love this game, but it has a big drop off in quality in the latter half. From the outside looking in, I barely saw any reviews about the lack of content in the outer layer, and as I've been playing since EA release on March 8th, 2022, it looked as if they were set in stone in going that direction. Promises can always remain unfulfilled from EA games, but after hearing that my issues are being actively thought about and addressed I have genuine trust in the team developing Core Keeper that they have the capability, and most importantly will actually follow up with the improvements to the latter half of the game.So, I've elected to change my review to positive, since I don't want to leave a negative review on something that is both a (mostly) good game, and I have actual faith in having it's major flaws fixed.Of course, games still deserve to be reviewed in their current form, so I've left the original review here to be read. If you want a trial of a great game, i'd say buy Core Keeper. If you want a finished product, wait for release.Also, I guess i'll just catalog the original ratings on this review here, just for it to be known what my fellow players thought about this opinion that brought up the drop off of the outer layer.Ratings:50 People found this review helpful3 People found this review funny4 People gave me the Jester award3 People gave me the Wholesome award2 People gave me the Extra Helpful award1 Person gave me the Treasure award====================================================Honestly man, I love this game. But only the first half of it. The first half of this game is amazing. Decently varied biomes, enemy variety in those biomes, and fun bosses to fight. The Quality of Life is great too, (although damn do I wish this game had Magic Storage or something like it) I love that you can hold shift to hold out your torch without needing to give it a dedicated slot. I love that this game has fun accessories and progression like Terraria. The Boss Fights are well-designed and fun as well. It feels good to just start the game, make a base, start mining, start fighting, and get tons of cool gear to expand your capabilities, from inventory space to defense.But damn, does this game drop hard at the "Hardmode". Once you've beaten all three bosses, you finally get to take down the walls surrounding the map, and you can start fighting the Titans. Issue is, all the amazing variety and decently paced progression in the "pre-hardmode" part of the game completely drops off. Instead, you get four ABSOLUTELY MASSIVE biomes, that are all the exact same. It's so boring. All you do is mine and see the exact same enemies, the exact same tiles, the exact same dungeon, and rarely see a structure which isn't even worth going to because the loot is boring. The enemy variety also gets worse.- Forgotten Ruin Cavelings are basically the same as the Cavelings in Azeos' Wilderness. See you, charge an attack, attack, repeat. See you, shoot a projectile, downtime/reload, repeat. Yeah the farmer guy drops a flower but it doesn't make him any different.- The Mold Tentacle in the Mold Dungeon got reused as the Tentacle in the Sunken Sea.- All the slimes are the same, the slime bosses are also basically the exact same.I mean Azeos was a fun fight, Omoroth was a pain but it was still unique. I didn't bother playing to the Desert Boss cus I just got so bored during the grind to do Azeos and Omoroth. This game just becomes an absolutely boring mining grindfest after the first three bosses. I don't entirely mind the idea of having massive biomes but they really needed to put a lot more effort into making them feel way more varied for the amount of time you'll be spending in them, getting the materials to create the scanner to find the boss, and then mining to get to the boss, then making the boss summoning item. I just can't recommend this game for $15 if the best part of the game only lasts for the first three bosses. If the ENTIRE map was like the beginning of the game, with lots of expanded biomes with unique enemies, bosses, and resources, much like the underground of Terraria, I'd recommend this game in a heartbeat. I mean I love the idea of unlocking the rest of the world, but it's like they gave up at the end, and just threw their hands up and said "Make an entire quarter of the map just one biome, with the content of only a single biome.". I'm disappointed to see how this game ended up. The last half just feels completely phoned-in. The first half is the jam-packed beginning of a masterpiece, but the second half is just a huge dropoff in content and quality.Honestly, I feel bad for even giving this game a bad review. I mean, I enjoyed it, and I respect the developers for the fun game they made, but it just seems irreversibly screwed. They already made the entire rest of the map just 4 giant biomes with a single small biome's worth of content, they can't exactly change it. I'd love to be proven wrong with an update that fixes my issues, but I doubt it'll ever come.

_childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper is a hidden gem in the indie gaming world, offering a refreshing blend of adventure, exploration, and survival. From the moment you start digging into the mysterious underground world, the game captivates you with its unique gameplay loop, balancing resource management, combat, and base-building in an incredibly engaging way.One of the standout features of Core Keeper is how it rewards exploration. The procedurally generated world is rich with secrets, biomes, and treasures, giving players a constant sense of discovery. Every session feels different, and no two playthroughs are alike. This element of unpredictability, combined with the need to adapt your strategy based on the resources you find, keeps the game feeling fresh even after hours of play. The variety of enemies and bosses also ensures that combat remains challenging and fun as you progress.The crafting and base-building systems are equally impressive, offering endless possibilities for creativity. Whether you're crafting new weapons, setting up an automated farm, or designing the perfect base, there’s always something rewarding to work towards. It's a game where you can lose yourself for hours, refining your base or exploring deeper caves for rare materials.Replayability is a huge strength here. With different character classes, multiple progression paths, and the random nature of the world, Core Keeper offers something new with every restart. Multiplayer adds another layer of fun, allowing you to share the adventure with friends or tackle the underground challenges as a team.Overall, Core Keeper is an absolute must-play for fans of survival and exploration games. Its fresh gameplay mechanics and near-limitless replayability make it a standout indie title that will keep you coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: It is a fine game. People like it. I'm just not one of them. Consider this review a drop in the bucket.This game is a management nightmare. You end up with 30 different tables/anvils/crafters that all have some unique crafts that you always end up needing. There is no centralization. The ability to draw items out of adjacent chests while crafting is brutally undercut by the waking nightmare of organizing this mess. Minecraft and Terraria showed how to manage this a decade ago. Make a crafting menu bigger than a 2x6 grid. Make tables include the contents lower in the tree.The having the map open while travelling feels mandatory due to the zoom and scope of the world. That is fine. You can not interact or attack while running with the map open. Explored areas have no transparency options. An almost good idea that fell on its face.You need to craft four tables and setup a generator to power a lumber mill... to make a plank of wood. One plank per 10 seconds. 40 planks for a special map table. You need this table just to know the currently explored map. This is a terrible. A living hell when playing multiplayer. When you have people screaming their heads off about getting jumped by a dozen miners, and they are a mile into the unknown... Either turn this feature ON or OFF for the server. Gate keeping it is terrible.The game is fine. It is a fine 2012 game. It looks great. It has a lot of character and unique designs. I have played dozens of early access survival crafting games. The fundamentals are rough in a way that will never be addressed. Technology scope will increase. You will get more mechanics and tables. If the above does not bother you, then the game is up your alley.

_childDocuments_.review: I like that the game just starts us in a dirt room and leaves us to figure things out, but that also seems to kinda be the whole game. Most games let me press the right stick down or something to sort or deposit.  Instead, I have to navigate to the deposit button and then navigate to the sort button, which are somewhat far away from each other on the UI for some reason.  Or if I want to throw something away and not immediately auto loot it back up, I have to select, haul it to a corner of my inventory screen where the trash can is, drop it there, then move down and select the trash can and then repeat for whatever other trash I've auto looted up that's stopping me from collecting the things I do want. _childDocuments_.review: I have never reviewed a game on steam as I am selfish for my own time, but I believe you seriously need to have a warning before you decide to start this game. I recommend you check the wiki to fact-check my information if you do not believe me, or look for videos.I have played it for 45 hours. We started as 4 and ended the game being 2 as we wanted to "complete" it.I did not enjoy the experience: many people here describe the game as a survival/craft game similar to Terraria / Minecraft / Don't Starve.This game is nothing like the aboves: it is empty in its core.Combat is uninteresting with very limited movesets. All weapons pretty much do the same thing.There are only 3 different summoner weapons in this game.There are only 7 mage weapons in this game.Melee patterns are the exact same, all the time. The same spear/axe/sword you find early game will have the exact same pattern late game.Coop experience is flawed: the only way to upgrade health permanently in this game is to consume almost-unique items found randomly in biomes or very late through boss fights drops and fishing.There are 8 in the game. (I am excluding the christmas-specific item)4 are biome specific, so you could not obtain them twice, meaning only one person in your coop could have the increase. In our world, we only found 2 of them as well as they are tied to biomes in game. The biomes are extremely large and you do not need to explore them entirely (would take a while and ressource-wise not necessary)There is a slime boss in the game early on that has only one attack pattern: a jump towards you.You will encounter a reskin of this boss 4 times in the game, and the pattern is always the same: a jump towards you + one unique pattern per slime reskin.Other bosses are pretty bland: the Shaman is probably their best boss design.The titans are going to be very disappointing: each titan has the same pattern as the last one with one additional clone.On hard difficulty, you will die from regular mobs attacks post early game in one hit. This may be tied to the fact we did not have the chance to get many health upgrades.This does not make the game challenging though: it makes it really tedious to play.Food cooking / farming experience is not fun, but necessary to do in order to have stats buffs (movespeed/damage) or any form of health regen if you have the chance to survive a hit from an enemy.I would seriously recommend checking out the skill tree to understand what kind of game this is: the "skills" are ALL passives and are extremely boring. They are a % increase to a stat or a chance to proc an effect that gives you a %increase to a stat. Unlocking a skill is not exciting in any way.Overall, the mining & exploring core loop is not very fun or interesting as there is not much to discover by exploring: the weapons upgrades are the same things with higher values (+dmg).There a lots of "cosmetic" biomes found without interesting loot/chests/rewards, which is probably what attracts some people in this game. For a sandbox aspect, I would much rather play modded minecraft or Stardew Valley as a cosy game rather than this.I still do not understand why and how it was allowed that cosmetic items like herbs are destroyed by our attacks on mobs. Whilst exploring, there is so much inventory clutter createdPlease make sure to put a timer when you start the game to ensure you can have it refunded after you play it a bit. What you experience at the beginning doesn't improve but fades more and more through the rest of the playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Early Access:Just a great game without any cons. If you´ve enjoyed Minecraft, Terraria, whatever game in the scene, this one is definately for you. The game itself is nothing but fun. First you´ll be like "Just another farm - build - simulator.... and yes it is in some way, but it has a lot of depth so far. Your character progress permanently in e.g. exploration, mining, gardening and so on. Weapons and items have different tiers from uncommon to legendary. Some are dropped by bosses, the others can be found in random dungeons. Set-boni are included too. And well, the game has bosses... stuff as you know from Terraria possibly. I don´t want to spoiler, but all of them have different mechanics and are well inscenated. Housing has a lot of possibilities so far. I mean... you can plant EVERYTHING on a podium as deco. It´s great!Nevertheless, the game is just in early access state... but it does a really great job for what it is and especially for that price! New content is in development and you clearly see, that the devs love and support their game well. All what we need is more stuff to farm, more bosses and more housing items. (QoL options are well implemented aswell...)Thumbs up for this and anybody should seriously ignore the handful of bad reviews and give it a try at best with friends!Now:The game is no longer real fun. It starts well but falls off really fast. The reasons are simple:- The world went from infinite to finite and on top even inner biomes got cutted in half if not more. - Progression got overbuffed. - Enemies got nerfed.Since the world-size got hard reduced, exploration feels kinda pointless. While this was not enough, the devs nerfed walls, YES WALLS, so the player can destroy them faster or even earlier (like stonewalls with a wooden pickaxe just because...), which let you "explore" the small world even faster. While the more fast-paced gameplay is not enoug, enemies got nerfed, even bosses. They also drop way more loot now. Your inventory is pretty full every couple blocks with enemies in between. Different gearsets are pointless to craft, because enemies drop way better gear way to often and too easy. "Rare" isn´t rare anymore and pretty much pointless anyway. On top XP-gain got increased and needed XP reduced, which will cause the player to outscale the actual environment anyway.Some poeple might find it fun, i can´t. The progression is so hard ♥♥♥♥ now, that you can and will skip whole biomes or needed tiers now. Earlier traps, drills, portals or whatever, which you either became lategame or needed dozens of ores to create, are now easily and early to obtain, which makes grinding and farming kinda pointless. Right now the game feels more like a boss-rush, because it has nothing else to offer. The finite world just kills the whole exploration-factor for new dungeons and other stuff, because if there is something, it´s almost next to each other. Also... they removed a minigame. Nearly every game with fishing has a minigame and it was unique in this one. They removed it, because players couldn´t boost the fishing-level to 100 fast enough. Was it tedious before? Yes... definately. But they could´ve just reduced the needed XP and give more XP for more rare fishes, but no... they reduced something unique for some dumb reasons. The game will still be fun for newcomers for sure. Even EA who fall in love with this will still like it, but in general the progression is completely off, the world got hard cutted, the exploration feels pointless and even building is limited now since you can´t farm endlessly, unless you jump with you character through multiple worlds and collect with whatever you need. While this is not enough... old bugs still remain.I can´t recommend it right now and i feel sorry for it. The game is beautiful, but it losts its magic and possibilities it had in EA.

_childDocuments_.review: A friend of mine who knows I like this kind of game (Terraria, Crea, etc) got this for me. The idea of turning Terraria into a top down, semi isometric dungeon crawl is pretty cool. The beginning is easy enough. Dig around, make stuff, dig and make stuff. Things start to get annoying once you have made all the normal copper and wood stuff. Then you realize that tin is super short of supply. (of the 300 or so ore I found 9 were tin, the rest were gold and copper. Gold isn't useful until much later.) Finding enough tin to make the upgrade table is just not a fun process. You will probably end up running into mobs that you can't handle despite full copper armor. You might even run into a super slime (I managed to avoid that but jeez that thing is huge). The nth time dying to a series of mobs that are too hard to fight (one had many hundreds of health, another had nearly as much.)  was enough to chill my enjoyment of the game.I would definitely sideways thumb this if there was an option for it, despite my own misgivings. If you love Terraria you will play this and recognize similarities. You might enjoy it. It certainly was fun for a few hours before the grind set in. And I do respect that the game is by a small developer house, not some gigantic AAA producer.The graphics are fairly awful btw. I don't love pixel graphics in general but Terraria's definitely is the way to do it. More antialias, less fuzzy lines would make it a lot less ugly. That said, graphics are typically the least important aspect of the game unless they interfere with the game play and they don't here so I would not base my no on that. Just a note that you might or might not like them. Overall: buy it if you have a fondness for survival crafting games. Be aware that combat is twitchy and not well tuned to be fun. And it seems like there are game balance issues, especially with creature difficulty vs resource availability/tech upgrades. The lack of a ranged weapon option at the beginning is especially egregious as it somewhat leaves out the ability to kite enemies. I'd give it a 4 out of 10 stars with a definite eye on improvement over time since it is still Early Access.

_childDocuments_.review: Already, even in Alpha, this game is refreshing and exciting to get my hands on.I discovered this game when talking to one of my friends. I was talking about how supremely awesome Terraria is (and it is), and how I hope something like it will appear in the future. That's when he told me about Core Keeper. Funnily enough, I was thinking of a more isometric, Stardew Valley type of Terraria where you in the cardinal directions as opposed to up down left right, whilst keeping the same sandbox and combat oriented gameplay of Terraria. If you are looking for it (and you might), this is it. NPCs, biomes, bosses, enemies, ranged & melee combat, mining, equipment tiers; a lot of what I, and many others, have enjoyed about Terraria is here. If you are here because of the Stardew Valley comparisons, there is some there too, but beyond the isometric style, the farming, and some gameplay mechanics (such as the fishing), there isn't too much similar here I would say with the warm, relaxing, Stardew Valley. This isn't to say, of course, that a Stardew Valley player won't like this game, I like it, it just means that it may not be for you.One last comparison I want to make is with Starbound. It isn't as well known, so that's probably why I haven't seen too many comparisons, but Core Keeper has a striking resemblance to Starbound. Apart with the already mentioned Terraria similarities, which Starbound shares basically all of, the sound design, visual effects, and some more subtle game mechanics that Core Keeper has are very reminiscent of Starbound. Another big similarity they have is in their pre-release. Like Core Keeper, Starbound had a very polished and well made pre-release (many even think the Beta was better than the current version!). Only time can tell if Core Keeper will continue being improved on and developed for years to come, like Terraria, instead of being neglected and having so much lost potential, like Starbound.tl;dr: Great game, especially as it is only in Alpha. I can only hope it continues getting better, and development neglect is what I'm afraid of.

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't bad but I can't recommend it until it's at least out of early access and the automation system is actually fleshed out.What makes these kinds of games fun to me is the automation systems that the player will unlock and figure out throughout the game. The problem is the electrical system used for automation doesn't have much to it yet, and in some cases if you try to use it you get punished for it. There's a leveling system in this game, but it takes far too long to level up skills. I have a little over 100 hours at the time of writing this and only 72/100 levels in farming.I tried to use the automation system to automate my garden, but there is no way to automate planting or watering which takes a long time. Harvesting can be automated but then it won't count towards leveling your skills that already level far too slowly AND you won't benefit from any perks the skills would give you.At this time the game is like playing Stardew without sprinklers or upgraded watering cans. Or like playing Minecraft where the only things red stone can do is open doors. It's not bad, until you get to the late game and feel like you don't have anything to show for it except a fancier sword.

_childDocuments_.review: I've dumped so much time into this game, it's roped me in and I can't escape.My first impressions based on the name alone was that Core Keeper was a mixed procedurally generated dungeon crawler, tower defense style game. I regret to say I judged a book by it's cover.Akin to Terraria, Core Keeper takes a boss-centric, mining-and-exploration heavy approach to progression and didn't miss the mark when making procedurally generated worlds fun to BE in. Core Keeper, on it's launch, also already rivals Terraria in terms of customizable character progression AND cosmetics. It has a unique upgrade system, making gear relevant even into the end-game akin to, but further developed and integrated, than Starbound. Some might even compare elements of these systems to Stardew Valley. In particular, the leveling system rewards you within skill trees related to your various tasks, which may be grind heavy at times. But, this is more than made up for by it being so gratifying to have multiple viable options to choose from in not only a multitude of skills, but ways to play the game. It has an absolutely eye catching art style, which although maybe said too often about pixel graphics games, is completely true here. It's simple, but highly polished and refined. Core Keeper is worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: So far this has been pretty enjoyable. I have not defeated the first boss (there are three "first bosses", but one is going to be pretty close to your base). I have been *killed* by the first boss plenty, though. Looks like I'll be hitting it with giant bombs. Not all biomes of higher levels will be safely behind lower level biomes. I found the rock biome way before I found the clay biome. The key to combat here is hit, run, hit, run, hit, run. You can't stand there and just swing till something is dead. You'll be one or two-shot. Not all skills level equally easily. You'll probably have mining and running maxed out. But jeez, it's taking forever to level cooking and gardening. And I'm doing A LOT of both. I started the game out even as a gardener. It's early access, so keep that in mind. Things are going to be tweaked and patched and possibly outright changed. But as it is, even with some skills not leveling very well (which could be easily fixed with a retuning on their end), it's fun. And the price tag isn't bad either.*edited to update*Ugh, and the downside to early access. They changed the repair system and it's tedious as hell now. People whined that repairs were too easy. _childDocuments_.review: It's good. If you like things like Terraria, Stardew Valley, Starbound, even Minecraft, you should get it.The main focus is on combat, but there's a decent variety of build options and non-combat activities that can each help you get stronger in their own ways. I haven't played multiplayer yet, but it seems like that's where the game would really shine. The graphics are nice without being too demanding, I've had very few glitches, and I think I'm about halfway through at ~52 hours. I probably could have beaten it in 20, but I like just exploring and farming and such. There's also an in-game mod manager that I haven't really checked out.There are kind of two unofficial class systems in the game, and each person could play their own specific build. Outside of combat, you might focus on fishing, farming, crafting, building, exploration, and/or automation, all of which are helpful to the whole group in their own ways. In combat, you can focus on melee, ranged weapons, summons or magic (or a mix of whatever you like). In single-player, I've been taking my time and exploring each of the non-combat systems (except automation, but I'll get there).The biggest disappointment so far has been the lack of weapon variety for a summoner/mage playstyle. In 50+ hours, I've found 3 simple summons and 5 staffs that shoot some kind of ball that does damage on contact. I guess those classes were added really late into early access, so hopefully they get more love but we'll see. I haven't played melee or ranged yet, but the weapons I've found seem to have a bit more going on. The problem is that I've played a lot of Terraria, and the weapon variety there blows this game out of the water. It's probably not fair to compare a game that's been getting updates for 10+ years to one that just came out of early access, but it's still something I've found lacking.My other issue might be a limitation of the top-down, grid-based style, but some of the biomes get pretty samey after a bit. There are a ton of handcrafted 'scenes' scattered around, many of which are really cool. The space in between is often completely indistinguishable from 100 other places in that same biome.Overall it's a really solid little game. Well worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: -- Updated for 1.0 Release --With another 40 hrs in the full game I can now say that I recommend this.  The price is great for what you get, and it's a steal on sale.  The map is huge, which can be daunting at first - but it gives you lots of space to play in.  There are a variety of things to do, from combat to automation, and several distinct zones to explore.  Nothing here is too deep, the skill tree is there but fairly simple, likewise combat is serviceable but not complicated.  Which is perfect if you like a casual drop-in, mess around experience.  The developer has kept up with the game, so this looks like one of the Early Access titles that is going to be around and worth investing in.  Great for multiplayer too, since everybody can run off and do their own thing, come together for a boss fight, and then scatter again.-- original review --I'm not going to recommend this right now, just because this is very much an Early Access game. Fun for a while, but if you like it so much you dive into it, you'll quickly hit the end of available content. The first few patches make me wonder about the developers, exactly what they plan for the game, since they've changed things that didn't need changing (in my opinion), like dodge and repair, but have barley touched things I feel need a big revamp, like fishing and the skill trees. So while I have enjoyed my 60 hrs well enough, I would wait on this to finish development or if they open it up to the modding community.  If this game sounds interesting (being crafting, exploring and light survival), I would recommend Terraria, Forager or Littlewood instead, for the 2D style, or No Place Like Home for 3D.

_childDocuments_.review: 1.0 update: Progress is pretty ass. A lot of cool concepts here, but overall I did not have a good time attempting to grind materials to find where a boss is mindlessly for hours.I'm really only recommending 'cause I like the idea of Core Keeper and want to support the devs. There's a charm to it, but there's something... missing. After 7 hours I still haven't had that magic 'click' moment.Early game grind is pretty rough, as one would expect of the love child of Terraria and Stardew Valley, would like to see some tweets to that, along with maybe bigger ore patch spawns?The Skill system is pretty bare bones atm. The skills are also pretty grindy (or at least it felt like it was for some skills, ie fishing.) Would like to see either EXP adjustments, or ways to help increase EXP gains, either through in-game means ala exp boosting potions, or through meta means like a server/world setting you can manually tweak.Cooking is quite nice and I like the variety of foods you can make, which also give a little variety in buffs, depending on what you cook. The heals per second are quite nice, but the alternate buffs like increased Mining damage are pretty minute and unnoticable and makes them not desired, so some changes would be nice there.Combat is pretty good, but it would be nice to have a ranged weapon at the start of the game if players wanted to do that instead of being melee. The 'face mouse direction' option is really great for combat as it allows for kiting in a much smoother fashion than other games who do combat in a similar isometric point of view.A few too many crafting tables with different uses and styles. Would nice to see a unified upgradable table.Overall, I'd give the game a 6/10 with lots of potential and I can't wait to see where the devs go next!

Boss fights require careful planning, especially in multiplayer. Speaking of multiplayer, you can team up with friends, which always makes the experience more enjoyable. Building a base—whether alone or with friends—is a lot of fun, with plenty of options for decoration and crafting to make it your own. And while exploring, always keep an eye out for cool finds like vehicles, which are great for getting around faster.One of my favourite features is automation; it’s been fun learning how to automate essential tasks for survival. _childDocuments_.review: TL:DRVery well done. It is most similar to Terraria in terms of game play and story progression with some moderate automation potential, if that appeals to you. Beautiful biome design, incredible soundtrack, decent combat, gets a bit grindy for the last third or so of the game. Bosses are overall good, later bosses are better. 8/10, very satisfied with my experience, well worth my money.I like simple lists soPROS: - Soundtrack. Seriously, the tracks for the outer biomes are superb (though they are all top notch overall). The Sunken Sea music reminds me of the Terraria mod Calamity and their Sunken Sea biome. Additional shoutout to all three tracks in Azeros' Wilderness; I was honestly floored by how good they were, especially when compared to similar games. - Lighting. Gorgeous lighting, most notably with ceiling holes, they "shafts of light" visual is wonderful. - Water. Honestly some of the best water graphics I've seen, even outside of pixelesque graphics. - Automation. While the automation is fairly light (some drills, conveyors and robot arms) the developers included the ability to easily utilize logic gates meaning that those with the know-how can really go hard, which is something I feel a lot of games could use. I may not necessarily be creating massive circuit systems like factorio, but having the option to use logic gates opens up a gargantuan amount of possibility. Note that while you can automate a ton of stuff, it isn't necessary. All you "need" to automate would be 8 drills on the big ore rocks which is a piece of cake. - Built-in Modding. At the start menu you are linked directly to the modi.io portal for Core Keeper, makes using mods super easy and convenient.  - Story presentation. While I wouldn't really consider the game to really be "story heavy" I *do* appreciate how lore elements are presented. There isn't some character waxing on and on about stuff, its in item descriptions, looking around locations, looking at murals, paintings and walls...honestly very well done.  - Scenes. Essentially the pre-fabricated pieces of each biome. They are quite detailed; honestly some of the best pixel-graphic work I've ever seen. - Since the scenes and audio and visuals are all superb, exploring was incredibly fun.CONS: - Mage and Summoner classes were added in the 1.0 release, but they still don't feel as finished or effective as ranged and melee. I did my playthrough as a mage and you, quite literally, are always mana-starved. If I didn't always work on melee at the same time I'd end up spending 50-60% of combat running around waiting for my mana to recharge. So if you go mage you *need* to be using a melee/range set-up as well. Melee and Range each have a hidden multi-step legendary weapon you can find and re-forge. Mage and Summoner do not. I used the same staff and robes for the last 40% of the game; armor *heavily* favors melee and range. Mage is definitely viable, don't get me wrong, it just feels lackluster compared to all the sweet looking weapons and gear that melee and range get. - Some weird mechanics. In every other game under the sun, if you are holding a stack of items and you right-click, you deposit one item from said stack. In Core Keeper, you *pick-up* one item instead. That got me the entire time I played. Shift-clicking an item while you have empty hotbar slots also does not move said item into an empty hotbar slot; that would've been nice, especially as... - Lack of some obvious QOL. When you eat/drink for stat boost prior to a fight you have to cycle through each potion/food/drink and partake individually. Your hotbar will already be crowded with tools and weapons, meaning you consume each item, open your inventory, swap items out, close inventory, and continue consuming. I need my "B" hotkey from terraria that just...consumes all boosts in your inventory in one go. Re-boosting during a boss fight is....difficult. - Grindy at the end. First third of the game is fine in this regard. Map is big so you gotta make "scanners" to find the Titans which require certain rare  increasingly larger numbers. I'd spitball and say like 15% of my total time was wandering around trying to find the stuff needed to summon the titans, not very fun.

_childDocuments_.review: It's sideways Terraria with a top-down digging exploration that may remind older gamers of Dungeon Keeper. It also incorporates a major Stardew Valley feel, with farming elements. Later, there's a dash of Factorio, with basic mining automation and electronics.It's very polished for an early access game (as of version 0.3.3). I only had 2 random crashes, which lost no progress. And I think I only saw one glitch (an invisible mob).It's got a whole lot of content already: 46 hours worth of core progression, for me. That's playing almost entirely alone. Although it was definitely a bunch more fun when a Steam friend joined my world for a bit, near the beginning.I was able to defeat all the bosses solo. But there was a bit of a learning curve with that. And I had to cheese the last two using environmental... adjustments; the spike trap is a rather core gameplay mechanic, at this point.My biggest criticism is that a few of the biomes feel dead and boring: particularly the stone area, after one's been through killing everything, nothing seems to respawn there.The movement and combat is not intrinsically as fun as a side-scroller. And a *lot* of the mechanics and content are very clearly derived from Terraria (and Minecraft). But the change in perspective, various novelties, etc, were enough to keep me engaged. Just about. Having not played a similar game for a few years.Overall highly recommended. Either to play now, or to wait until the next couple of bosses are released. Presumably with a whole lot more content besides, given the rate the devs are currently pushing out updates.[Edit: 120 hours further in!]So, after checking out some YouTube, Steam community and Reddit content, I realised I'd entirely missed 2 optional bosses, hidden away! Plus a load of higher end and rare gear. So I jumped back in (for lack of any other game I can currently be bothered to pick up)...The game becomes wildly time consuming, searching the vast swathes of map (alone). And in terms of levelling up the skill-tree of your character, through grind the various activities. And catching the less common fishes, etc.Then I got into aesthetic builds. Reorganising my base for more optimised crafting flow. Experimenting with wood auto-farms and enemy mob spawn mechanics. Plus making a couple of guides to apprise players of the lesser known aspects of NPC housing and, today, the wildly expansive cooking system - currently there's 1785 unique dishes can be made!The chunky pixel graphics have grown on me even more; I feel like this might be the most pretty retro graphics of a game I've seen. Particularly in parts of the wilderness, with the water shimmering there.And I've revised my #1 pet peeve: the clumsiness of fine interactions (on PC). It's trivially easy to break the wrong thing, like the punching the floor off, instead of harvesting a veg, or picking up a torch, or mine cart, or mining a wall. All the same interaction. And it auto-targets something else off to the side, sometimes, even when your character is looking at what you want to do. Sometimes even when that thing is highlighted! So hopefully there might be some refinements there. But either way, I'm fully hooked into this game and community, now.[Edit: over 400 hour in.]Short video review here!:

_childDocuments_.review: It's a GREAT start!I love this game. The gameplay itself is fun, the decor items are super creative and great for styling bedrooms and making beautiful looking spaces in bases (my love in any survival/exploration game). There are some really creative bosses! I love the individuality and the amount of items and armour sets surrounding each different area and the amount of weapons, tiers of tools as well. I think the early/ mid game is super fun! The late game however is in need of attention. Now this may sound stupid as it is in early access, I know its not finished and still being updated and added to regularly (Which is great to see). The game gets way too easy way too quickly. I have used the same weapon since the 2/3rd hour of playtime and every time i pick up a new weapon its either not at good as the weapon I have or the perks/ incentives are not worth changing my weapon for, that might just be me being stubborn but I just have no desire to change to a weaker weapon imo. I've written some suggestions below for some things i would love to see in the future and again I love this game an have had a blast playing it, I think im reaching the point where the grind is just too long for an armour set with a faster dash as its crowning feature.1) The armour set bonuses need a rework or an update, some of the sets in general (ESPECIALLY a certain armour set that takes quite alot of searching for in the late game) are quite weak, or not that impactful in my opinion to switch from the set I was using 20hrs ago. I also think that all sets should have a bonus, but the sillier sets should have funny or more jokey bonuses eg, chef set: cooked food has a change to multiply, caveling set: your character makes caveling noises 2) Late game instructions! Yeah there are parchments which tell you what items you need to collect but they give no hints or instructions on where in the vast map they could be. I don't want to be guide reliant.3) More decor! I am just a sucker for funky looking decor so more would be great!4) Better weapons, better scaling, more risk for more dangerous weapons, and more variations of ranged weapons5) More bosses / mini bosses! There are some really fun bosses. but more optional ones would be cool,6)More subareas! Having more variation in the different sections would really make exploration more fun, and feel like you are actually moving forward progression wiseAll in all I will be playing every update and seeing whats new, and will hopefully be playing this game for a long time! : )

_childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper seems like a pretty great survival crafting game. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: kind of like Terraria. It's a fun game and I recommend it if you like digging/exploration kind of games with rudimentary combat.This game satisfies most of the same itches Terraria scratches, but with several differences. Lots and lots of digging to find ore to gradually beef up your character, fighting bosses that gate content, building farms for mob drops and food, fishing, etc. That's pretty much where the similarities end. Equipment takes durability damage and needs to be repaired pretty frequently. Farming crops is more reminiscent of Stardew Valley requiring you to till the dirt to plant seeds and maintain a water level in your watering can. There is a very basic talent tree and makes you want to experiment with different things, or look up build guides on youtube.Regarding areas for improvement: - Some boss battles. One in particular, somewhat early on is more challenging than the others. There used to be a way for the player to effectively remove one of the mechanics from the battle, but it has been patched out of the game, requiring the player to find another way around some of the annoying mechanics. It's just a very dull encounter that feels like something you have to do just to progress. No real fun in it.- Playing on hard mode seemingly has one benefit only: more drops from bosses. Doesn't seem worth it seeing as how everything in that mode gets more HP and hits way harder. If there were more benefits to even out the hard mode difficulty slightly, or various exclusive mob drops, it would be fun to take on the challenge. - There is no way to transport the various liquids in the game to fish in apart from digging extensive trenches back to your main base. The way around this is to have multiple bases in the different biomes. [EDIT: this has been addressed with the addition of water buckets to transport liquid.]This review is based on the early access version, so I'll try to update when ver 1.0 releases. Overall it's a lot of fun and I see myself spending many more hours playing Core Keeper.

_childDocuments_.review: Please Note:I've had this game for a while now. Played it in early access and let go and it was  years before a 1.0 release.1.0 Release and it does not feel like a 1.0 release at allAllow me to say I think the game is charming. I do like this game and I would like to come back to it WHEN it is actually fully released. See, its quite evident that when you are in a sea of overwhelming data for what does and doesn't work and then make the mistakes regardless of the data that is already there is just another form of stupidity. I am not blind to the fact this game isn't Terraria or what ever but that does not matter. At the time of writing this review, an update for summoner type weapons was released. Sure it does work to fix problems, but its a band aid for a large issue. The point is, this game needs so much QOL, QOL that other games just have and people praise those simple things that every time I played this game, it felt lacking. Armor and Health stats are just garbage feeling, Melee weapons across the board fail to register to hit or fail to feel good ontop of having brutally short ranges (you need to kiss the enemy with your model just to make sure the melee weapon hits), Magic Weapons cost too much and because there is no good way that realistically scales with your Mana or way to increase your Maximum Mana without the aid of armor you constantly run out should you pursue upgrades that give little to no benefit. Upgrading feels worthless at time. It feels like upgrading gives 25%+ to base stats only after 7+ tiers of upgrading. I do not care to do the math, someone else can. Physical Ranged Weapons are the only weapons that felt any good. The issue then is the weapon selection is far too small. Accessories, for offhand or the majority of rings and necklaces give far too little of a buff that the time and effort to acquire them isn't worth it. I think this game just needs more. More of just everything and there is nothing else to it. It's not ready for a 1.0 release and i do not think it deserves to be labeled as a full release. I do like the design of this game but there needs to be a lot of work done before i consider coming back. Having read the positive reviews for the game and having actually played the game, I am at a loss for what i read vs what i played.
