_childDocuments_.review: This is game is amazing. It's basically Terraria from a topdown view, which (in my opinion) makes the map so much bigger than in Terraria. The world generation is really nice and has a good number of settings to it as well. What I really liked in particular though is the story behind the world you navigate. Each biome has its own set of structures that each tell their own stories of who might've lived there/used it. The bosses in this game is what truly amazed me though. The slime bosses were very basic (although I liked the Terraria reference to king slime), but the bosses that I really liked in particular are the hydra bosses. When I first saw these bosses spawn in I was amazed at the animation of these bosses for a game that has pixel graphics. I also really liked that each time you kill 1 of the Hydra bosses, their soul fights alongside the next hydra boss you face, making you eventually fight 3 hydras. Although this game is great, there are aspects to this game that I think need improvement. First off, why are there so many different crafting stations? You start off with a workbench for regular crafting, a furnace for smelting ores and an anvil for crafting gear. But then you have an automation table for automation like conveyor belts and drills, a bait workbench for creating bait for fishing, a carpenter table for decorations, a jewelry workbench for necklaces and rings and a lot more crafting stations. The one that ticks me off the most however is the glass smelter and glass workbench. The glass workbench is only there to craft with glass which in my opinion is mostly useless since you don't need glass to look through a wall since this game has a top down view. And the glass smelter is hilarious. It only lets you smelt sand into a glass piece and that's it. It's things like this that make me wonder why the glass smelter was even added in the first place. Why not just add this recipe to the furnace? And better yet, why don't you just add most of these recipes to crafting tables/furnaces? Why do I need to fill my base to the brim with 20 different crafting stations just so I can get the 1 item I need and then never touch it again? I get that you need to lock certain items behind something for the sake of progression, but you couldn't have made something like a crafting scroll that you can find after like defeating a boss or just exploring the world to unlock the recipes for certain items? Another thing I really didn't like is the gardening mechanic. On the surface level gardening is fine. You plant stuff, it grows pretty quickly and then you  harvest it. Easy. But it is when you start making bigger farms where the main problem starts to arise. Planting things takes forever on a big farm. There's no automation for planting crops, so you'll have to do it manually. This wouldn't really be so bad if I could place more than ONE seed at a time. But since I cannot, it really just discourages me from farming at all, which disappoints me since I like creating giant farms. Hopefully they expand on farming and specifically automated farming in the coming updates.And lastly to top this already too long review off is the baffling summoner class. When I found out that there was a summoner class I was excited, since I like being a summoner. Although in my experience very few games actually manage to pull off a fun summoner class. So I was curious how the summoner class in CK is like. After playing through the game and checking the wiki to make sure I wasn't hallucinating or really unlucky, I found out that there are only THREE different summoning books of which one is almost completely useless (which also happens to be the highest leveled one of the bunch). But there is plenty of cool looking armor for the summoner class. Why? There are 32 different melee weapons, 20 ranged weapons, 8 magic weapons and only 3 summoning weapons. Really? On top of this, something I really didn't like (and this also applies to most magic weapons) is that you have to get these weapons from exploration or killing enemies. You cannot craft magic weapons. You have loads of different crafting stations for very specific things, but couldn't make one for magic/summoning items?And that's my review. Great game with some flaws, but definitely addicting. Highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game per se, but I cannot give it a recommendation either for a few reasons in it's current state. The main issue Core Keeper has right now is that it doesn't offer enough variety with it's gameplay. It's the same gameplay loop you're asked to do over and over again, with the same tools every single time, enemies that play by the same rules and bosses that are very one dimensional. The game runs out of steam around the third boss, which is sad because it's a pivotal moment in the game's story and progression (at least they try to make it look like that), but what you get instead is you are asked to do the same thing you were doing so far, again.I will make a reference to Terraria here to try and explain what playing this game is like in it's current state: Imagine the very first version of Terraria and how barebones it was. Then take away everything that isn't the underground layer and leave only a few pieces of findable loot and unique things. Now you have an idea of how simplistic and basic this game is in terms of the gameplay loop and what is there available for you to do as a player.So, what does this game need to actually be interesting and have more staying power? As I said: variety. That can manifest in multiple different forms: More weapon and tool variety to make combat more dynamic, different objectives other than "kill the next boss", more interesting loot and unique things to find to give you feed your spelunking drive, different kinds of progression other than dig-new ore-same gear but stronger stats-repeat, new gameplay systems that give you things to do. There is so much design space here that the devs have luxury of choice in what they want to work on. Any of this would make the game significantly better. And the best games in this category (like Terraria) have absolutely all of it and then some.As it is right now, you might get about 10 hours of gameplay out of it until you arrive to the point I've mentioned when the repetition starts to wear on you. I've played the game two times so far, and it stopped being fun around the exact same point. The way the game is being developed right now, I don't think this is going to change, adding higher tier content is not going to change anything if I never get to it in the first place, what Core Keeper needs is a proper midgame section when ti opens up with possibility and varriety, not an infinitely stretched early game with the same gameplay loop. And I hope the devs realize that, because it would be a shame for a game with so much potential to remain in it's current, gimped form.

_childDocuments_.review: -The game is sorely in need of a way to automate seed planting, like a seed cannon or seed disperser because it takes me 10minutes just to plant my seeds on my current field, and that's 10minutes that I could be out exploring the world.-Coins don't stack, so I have 4 chests literally just filled with coins.-You can't see what's in a chest at a glance, so you always run around opening each of your chests just to find the material you're looking for.-You can't craft from nearby chests, which is sorely needed.-When you want to destroy an item, it takes two clicks into the trash box, when it should only be taking one.-The price for items/materials isn't displayed, until you take it to the merchant, which is terribad.-The game is for sale in ruzzia.-The regional pricing in the 3rd world is disgusting.-The skill system can be improved a lot and you gain nothing anymore if one of your skills reaches lvl100, so you literally waste experience at lvl100, instead of that experience being passed to other skills.-The game has seasonal content, which is always bad since the devs spend development time on something that players will only 'enjoy' for a few weeks out of the year, and that development time could have been spent on permanent content instead.I'll play the game more during the EA period but right now the game has too many missing QoL features which makes the player's life difficult, and the crazy regional pricing & ruzzist support push this game even further into the red.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: If you liked Terraria and need a new game to play, play this.At the time of writing this (version 1.0), it'll probably take most people around 50-100 hours from start until the final boss, going in blind or mostly blind. One huge plus to this game is the ability to let you do that; everything is fairly intuitive, never felt like I had to go to the wiki in order to figure out how to do something.It's a fair critique to say this game has less content than Terraria and I'd say that's probably true, but you also gotta remember Terraria has been out since 2011 and has had tons of updates since then. The way they've laid out this game you can definitely tell they've set it up to receive plenty of updates in the future. And even if you just do your 1 playthrough and stop, $20 for 100 hours of fun isn't exactly a bad deal.But for those who are still enjoying the game after they've beat all the bosses, there is still time to be spent in optimizing your character re-farming bosses for rare loot, trying out different builds, and customizing your world in general. Also tons of different world settings you could try out if you wanted to test out playing a new world or a harder difficulty.If you don't know too much or haven't seen too much content on this game and you're considering getting it, I'd recommend going in blind. This game has a lot of little details and surprises that lead to cool moments.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge potential, as many have probably said, game is VERY much like terraria, but not in the "oh terraria has this but better" way, its familiar, but has something new to offer that can't be found in terraria. With that out of the way, this game has potential to become one of the greats in terms of survival/crafting multiplayer. I appreciate how easy it is to start a world, copy one code and have a friend join a game, looking at you minecraft. As for the gameplay itself, it offers fair and ramped up challenges as you move along in the game, the more bosses you defeat the more powerful you must become before facing the next. Crafting can be pricey but as is the nature of crafting games; at first it'll be tough to get rid of your items, but soon you'll be drilling the ore cluster and have hundreds of said ore. On top of that, a skill tree, personally one of my favorite upgrade aspects in video games. My only complaint, I wish it was a longer list, but if it there was more upgrades perhaps the points should be a bit less between upgrades, fishing can be grueling where as running and gardening will be a breeze. Combat is simple, but still thrilling, when you first start off even the basic slime can be a bit scary. This is also one of the first games where an ax or bow is much preferred to a sword as they tend to lack range, which is interesting to see. As this game gets more updates, and more content, new biomes, new mods (there seems to be a fostering community for it which is awesome to see), new items etc., I could easily see this being right next to terraria, or even surpassing it in quality. Amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: Thanks to the change in the repair mechanic from scrap parts to partial recipe costs a lot has changed, rare items like the mining grenade launcher are no longer priced posessions but something that will inevitable become useless since there's no way to repair them without recipe materials since they aren't crafted. You can forget spending your first of a higher tier material you worked hard to get on your favorite tool, why bother till you can get lots? it's just gonna break and need stuff you barely managed to scrape together instead of scrap, ducktape and prayers.  Since ores are a finite ressource, you will be forced to mine ever further out just to repair your gear , overtime reducing progress speed because a portion of your gains will be spend on repairing your tools. The game has promise but that change made a massive difference in the negative. Some people might find repairs with material "more realistic" but they certainly are not more fun. I play games to have fun. If I want drudgery with little progress I'd get a extra part time job in a factory.

_childDocuments_.review: Actually, I'm an opponent of early access, which always smelled to me of how to take money from players.Core Keeper was a birthday present and I have to say after only 120 hours of play I searched here extremely, I have a lot of games I enjoy playing but I keep coming back to Core daily because it just occurred to me you could do this room Y design like this or search the area z times.You also notice, when you do certain things, how which "people" suddenly gain strength and you have to fight it harder.I think it's great that you can do a lot in co-op, whether alone, in pairs or in a large groupdigging around, creating real ingenious infrastructures.Digging, mortaring, building according to free ideas and looking for new items, equipment, designs in the same dungeon.Great job so far, the game should actually be out of Early Access, there are still a few bugs that other games that have been released also have and sometimes even worse.If you like digging, building, dungeons, farming, grinding, fighting, this is right the place for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing multiplayer, game crashed 4 times in 5 hours which isn't really that bad especially for early access. The BIG issue is that the last time it crashed one of the people had there characters bugged out and they were unable to load into the game with that character from that point on. We spent hours trying to figure out how to fix it and ultimately the game has a few problems that need to be overcome.All the userdata like character info etc is locked behind encrypted data files and not separated from other main data making it impossible to copy characters to try and solve issues like that. Sure there are some duping issues there but anyone can cheat the game if they want in any number of ways. Better to simple just let users have access to non critical game data (which would also allow for easier modding) then to run into an issue where the game gets in a poor state and then after many hours of playing in multiplayer the world map is no longer usable because one of the players characters will load into other worlds but no into the world you have been building up.The game is decent but there are some BIG issues that need addressing. It's a buff system in disguise. Each raw food item has a stat buff and you can cook any two raw foods together to make buffs that work for your character or build.Characters have  like Terraria or Valheim. You can make a new character per world, but you don't have to.There's  for the green-thumbs that has a really nice feeling skill progression. Combining skills, tools, and equipment to make even a little go a long way.The  is almost the crux of the game in a way. The progression path is led mainly with breadcrumbs in the crafting system; find a new item, craft a new thing, now you can find even more items or defeat even more enemies, repeat. And crafting is separated into different tables which allows builders to really go to town on bases. Which leads to...There are so many  options; walls, floors, sub floors, lights, furniture, decorative items, equipment stands / item pedestals, etc. You can even paint some of the blocks to really let your creativity shine.For the animal lovers, you can  for fun or for crafting ingredients. _childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. You'll find a lot of elements from other great titles like Valheim, Ark, Zelda, Stardew Valley, Diablo, Minecraft, Terraria, Harvest Moon, Animal Crossing, Forager, etc. It's a balanced mix of mine, grow, gather, and hunt. As you find relics, kill baddies and bosses, you'll get to upgrade and customize everything along the way. You can run up to three armor sets at a time utilizing various rings, necklaces and offhand gear. This allows you to change stats and abilities on the fly for various enemies and tasks. It's a huge world and it easily accommodates the 8 player option to venture with friends. There's only been a few visual bugs and a handful of times items around the base decide they don't want to stay in place. It's just a matter of breaking the ground with a shovel, replacing it, and laying your item back on it. I'm sure it'll get patched at some point. It overall feels like a polished and very finished game compared to a lot of titles that have released in recent years, so if this is just early access, we're off to a great start!

_childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper has a ton of pros IMHO compared to its cons.  It feels as though Stardew, Valheim, & Factorio had a baby and called it Core Keeper.  Assuming you're not looking for a first or third person style 3D modern-looking adventure, and you like the general crafting-survival genre,  could be right up your alley!TBH, I really had to think about the 'cons' list above.  The devs fix glitches pretty quickly that do arise, and release great content every couple months.  Like I said in the BLUF, if you like this genre, you won't be disappointed in Core Keeper.  It took the farming satisfaction of Stardew Valley, mixed with the crafting/survival/biome-bosses/progression of Valheim, mixed with some automation of Factorio/Satisfactory. _childDocuments_.review: Definitely really tried to like this game. The art and music is amazing, but the game is EXTREMELY grindy. The game definitely feels like it doesn't respect your time with a fairly large map that takes awhile to move around in. Making things such as a minecart network feels like a hassle, since mine carts  / boats aren't equipped to your character, but placed on the rail network, so if you die, you'll have to walk all the way back to get your vehicle.  Fast travel points are few and far between, and the only way (As far as I know) to create an additional fast travel point is extremely resource intensive and has a TEN minute cooldown.You'll also need a large amount of materials for a lot of stuff in the game, which the game seems to flirt with automating the process a bit by having automated drills to get these resources for you.  The way you can automate things is extremely basic however, and will require you to just randomly explore until you find an appropriate node you can place your drills at. The gearing for combat in this game also feels pretty basic, and doesn't have as much synergies as I'd like. For example, I equipped an armour set that increases crit chance upon poisoning an enemy. However I found that this trait doesn't proc when using a range weapon that poisons enemies, when using a character skill that inflicts poison whenever you deal damage, or when using a pet that poisons enemies. It seems to only proc when using a poison melee weapon - which wasn't mentioned in the description of the armour set. The breaking point for me in this game was Ultimately, I was looking for something to scratch my survival crafting itch, but there's not enough here to justify the massive grind.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game!!!Valheim meets Path of Exile meets Zelda.As a fan of Valheim and Path of Exile, this game totally hooked me even though at first the pixel art wasn't really my thing. However after about an hour I felt like the pixel art was charming and now after dozens of hours I LOVE THE PIXEL ART!!!It has a similar progression/crafting system to Valheim, which the devs even stated was their inspiration for the progression system. Yet it's even more in depth than Valheim. Each new biome and boss require strategy and upgrading your gear and cooking better food along with some forethought as to how to approach the fight and even how to manipulate the terrain prior to engaging the boss in order to give yourself an advantage. And of course the combat and isometric camera angle reminded me of PoE a little bit even though it looks more like old school Zelda at first glance.The boss fights themselves are intense, especially if you play on hard mode which is quite hard in the beginning stages of the game. Each boss has interesting and challenging mechanics and it's chaotic at times but still the mechanics themselves are very 'readable' with good visual clarity unlike one of my favorite games of all time Path of Exile which while being incredible itself lacks visual clarity and it's one of the biggest downsides to that game (unless you use a broken build and trivialize the endgame bosses, LOL... but back to Core Keeper).Man this game totally grew on me to the point where I got my buddy to try it and at first he was like "meh, I don't know about these graphics" but then after about 30 mins he was loving it as much as I do. Being in a group (up to 8 ppl can play co-op) is even better than playing solo although solo is enjoyable as well of course.Do yourself a favor and pick this game up. It's great and yet another great example of how much better indie games are nowadays on average than most AAA titles with bloated budgets and 100's of devs. Fun is fun and no amount of "investor capital" and massively over-staffed studios can manufacture fun any better than a few dudes with passion and focus. Just buy the game. You won't regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper is a delightful indie title that masterfully combines the charm of pixel graphics with the excitement of exploration. The art style is vibrant, detailed, and perfectly fits the atmospheric biomes that range from lush forests to eerie caverns. The music complements this aesthetic, creating an immersive experience.The gameplay shines with its variety of bosses, each offering unique challenges. The thrill of exploring new areas and stumbling upon unexpected secrets keeps the game fresh for hours.However, the game could use some balancing. Warrior melee builds dominate with their damage output and survivability, making them feel overpowered. Meanwhile, summoners and wizards struggle to keep up, often requiring more effort for less reward. Additionally, some skills demand an overwhelming number of points to unlock or upgrade, which can feel like a grind.Despite these shortcomings, Core Keeper is a fantastic adventure for anyone who loves exploration-driven gameplay with a retro twist.

_childDocuments_.review: So with the release of the 1.0 there came a slew of patch notes that many of us in early access hadn't heard about or were expecting. The biggest ones was the gutting of the endless map, the removal of the fishing mini-game (i know that's a controversial one but it was one of my favorite things) and the tacked on magic system (still no clue WHY it wasn't tested in EA but...)The Map getting limited makes it smaller. SO much smaller. I'm pretty sure the entire dirt biome in a Classic world was the same size of the entire three zones inside the unbreakable wall. Gorm the Devourer had to be made smaller (The big worm thing from the above trailer. Hes like...1/4 his old size) and exploration feels so much worse when you realize how much less there is to explore.For the Fishing Mini-game, I'm biased but I personally loved it. Just simple pattern recognition, sit there, and relax. I know a lot of people didn't like it because it kept them from grinding up to 100 as fast as possible, or because they couldn't slow down for a few minutes, or simply because they just don't like fishing mini-games. I understand its removal is overall a positive for most people, but what makes me the most upset is that it came with no warning. No notice, no communication, no polls outside of a discord (assuming they did one there, i don't join too many discords due to personal reasons) they didn't look at maybe revamping how fishing exp works (easiest way would be to double exp gained when catching fish at active fishing zones, hell just fishing at those whenever you see one is an easy way to keep fishing even with your other skills) but no, lets just nix the entire thing. I guess the auto-fishing mod is going to get more popular since the system isn't worth interacting with now.Speaking of systems, Magic is OBJECTIVELY terrible. It basically boils down to "ranged, but with extra steps." The new magic guard is neat and is kind of a balance between dodge and armor, but its not strong enough to carry you very far, especially in multiplayer with how much harder enemies hit. (The fact it ONLY on gear an doesn't go up with skill level or other skill trees doesn't help its case)The Magic system took a few range staff weapons an made them their own skill system, but they're bad. They go shoot, shoot but bouncy, shoot a few, shoot or explode, and shoot.AND, unlike ranged, your LIMITED in how many times you can shoot by a mana pool. It just doesn't feel worth it, and the devs lack of creativity when compared to most of the game is shocking.Staff for tethering to an enemy and dealing damage over time? Nope too creativeStaff for laying traps at your feet that attack enemies who step on them? Nope too creativeStaff for a chain lightning spell? Nope too creativeStaff for healing allies or self? Nope too creativeIt's just not a system worth levelingSummoning is actually decently enjoyable, despite the devs having tacked it on at the last second. (There are only THREE summoning weapons) The first and earliest weapon you get summons a little ranged bat that lasts 30s, and if your running around with melee or ranged its a nice little helper, shooting at things. If you get summoner gear, you can summon more than one, which sounds good on paper but their targeting of whats hostile and whats not still needs to be worked on (surprising.) The fact they cost mana to summon isn't an issue if you're just relying on the one, but when your limit goes to 3 or beyond that, you're mostly running around trying to get your attention deficit helpers out onto the field. An easy fix would be having the mana cost of summons passively go down the higher the skill level is (the tree is fine, don't change it) but until a change happens its basically worth using as a side skill, not a main play style.While I'm happy to see an EA game leave EA, a few baffling changes that SHOULD have been looked at in the EA long before 1.0 was on the map are dulling this gem of a game.

For example, me and a friend spent 3 hours trying to find an alien challenge room for the nuclear battery, an item required to fight the Atlantean worm. Not only that, a few scenes are once per map, like the paradise fruit item, which is one of the few items that increase max health permanently, which can be a problem when you are playing multiplayer. If we didn't dupe these items, we would have probably fought over these items as playing the game on hardmode, getting more max hp is really needed. _childDocuments_.review: I remember buying this game for my sister a few years back. Didn't think much of it at the time, but I thought it would be a nice gift for her. I remember seeing her playing it from time to time, the message indicating that she'd started playing it popping up on the corner of my screen. There was always a certain small pride in seeing that, because to me it meant that she was enjoying my gift.Last September she committed suicide.After everything had more or less settled down from that, I sat down and booted up her computer. All that was on there was Chrome, Steam, Word, and a few games. One of them, of course, was Core keeper.She had played this game to pieces, clocking over 170 hours and owning practically everything the game had to offer. She had used every square inch to its maximum potential, and was making ridiculous amounts of loot. It was only then did I see just how much she loved my present. No other game she played quite captured her affection as much as this one. None of her friends really knew about it, however; it seems like she preferred to keep it to herself. Like it was her own little bit of heaven she could turn to whenever she wanted.And because of that, I can't help but smile whenever I play this game.I cannot recommend it enough; every bit of hard work the developer put into this masterpiece shows in every single aspect. The music is catchy and memorable (I'll often find myself humming certain tunes from it), the world feels lived-in and natural, and the gameplay is incredibly laid back and enjoyable. It's hard to stop once I get invested in the game; minutes can easily turn into several hours. And now, with the multiplayer beta, I play for even longer with my friends, each of us dedicated to our desired jobs. Most of all, however, we're all just happy to be together.

It does have some small minor elements of Lite-RPG into it but nothing more than standard numbers going up to make mining/fighting/fishing etc alot more easier in the late game. The combat seem's very hit or miss and not very layered in terms in depth approaches or enemy variety but just simple you either health and damage mechanic. The pixel art is cute with the controls being very basic but this all ties together like a simple mobile game. If you're playing this expecting this to be something around the corner from Terraria or Stardew then you might not be be 100% into this game as of now. It's a very one-dimensional gameplay loop that you either love or don't.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a shame to rate this low as it's clear a lot of effort has gone into it, but survival-craft games are only fun when there's a REASON to continue the gameplay loop of "get resources to build better equipment in order to get better resources, ad infinitum". This one very quickly becomes stale as there's no motivation to keep going - no story, no mystery no lore. The constant need to mine to get anywhere becomes tiresome, even with the equipment upgrades - particularly when you're searching semi-aimlessly for the next boss.Other elements of the game also feel a bit thin. Building bases is fun for a short time but it's let down by a lack of variety compared to say, Terraria. Other game elements such as farming and fishing are ultimately unrewarding as the food they provide, when cooked, provides buffs that aren't necessary to progress.

_childDocuments_.review: As an early release, it very much shows. The game plays fairly well if you only play in small bursts in a solo world/with a friend, but the state of the dedicated server shows just how glaringly bad this game is programmed. There is seemingly no memory management, and a game is hard capped at utilizing 4gb of memory, dedicated server or not. This would be fine in most games that purge items and enemies, but this game does neither. A server cannot exist for more than a few hours before hitting the cap and crashing, and there is no way to notify people on a server of an impending restart to mitigate this. The complete lack of basic server functionality shows this game is still needing a lot of polish before its release, and they just announced they are going 1.0 in Summer 2024. This suggests the dev team has utilized early access as a means to finance the game, something Steam actively tells devs not to do (but doesn't stop), and are pushing 1.0 to get financing from consoles for either continued development or dropping support entirely.I do not have high hopes for this game's future, even if I enjoyed the first few dozen hours.

_childDocuments_.review: After beating first 3 bosses i have no interest in continuing to play. At the moment i can't really recommend this game.My main gripes are:1)Biomes are boring. There is nothing interesting to biomes. Biomes are mostly walls of various durability and pocket of mobs, sometimes slowing slime or damaging acid puddles on the ground.2)Mining is tedious. Ores are too few and are too scattered out to much to be fun to gather. While i know there is a way to automate gathering from nodes that scattered about, i got bored and stopped playing before made to the point where i had the tech required.3)The game is grindy. Skills are levelled solely by hitting/wall/vegetable or in case of fishing playing some tedious minigame.4)Perks are boring. They mainly consist of +% to damage, those that add something more are mostly "Stand still to get +100% to crit", there are no perks that affect gameplay in any meaningful extent.5)Progression is boring. It mainly consists of "get ore> smelt ore> craft workbench> repeat for the next ore". Even worse recipes are not inherited from previous tiers of workbenches. They are still required to process/use material from lower tiers.6)Smelting ores takes a long time (27 seconds for a scarlet bar). Why? I genuinely don't understand this. There is no automation prior to this ore. Even if there was, what the point? This isn't MMO that needs to waste players time with useless waiting.7)Automation come into game too late. When i got crimson ore i already was getting bored from tedium of gathering and smelting ore that i needed up to that point. Even then Crimson ore takes too long to process without automation.8)Combat is boring. For melee it mainly consists of hitting something few times and the running/dashing away to avoid attack. For ranged it consists of shooting something then running around waiting for the  to finish, making having more that one gun useless.9)Worst of all mobs have a "anti cheese" mechanic where they start to regenerate health if they cant get to you or you are attacking from outside their attack range. Why? Half the fun of these games are making mob farms or otherwise automating the combat. I would have understood if bossed had this, but not trashmobs. This is only decision i consider truly moronic for devs to implement.I genuinely have a hard  time understanding why this get so much praise.

_childDocuments_.review: Just a quality video game. The art style is simple and beautiful. Progression feels fast and meaningful, but not so fast that the game becomes too easy. The devs were thoughtful about quality of life features to keep you immersed and make the game loop and grind feel like a challenge, not a chore. Exploration is exciting. You never know what lurks around the next corner. Enemies and bosses are unique. The gearing and food system is excellent. Fans of Terraria and Valheim will love this game. _childDocuments_.review: Exploration: Fantastic (I really loved the Biomes)Progression: Fantastic (until towards the end of the game)Music: Fantastic (I will be listening to this OST on Spotify)Combat: Fantastic (It gets fast and intense)Gear/Loot: Very Good (The loot that they have currently is great but there is not much of it/It's the same thing just better stats)Sound Design: Very Good (Sometimes there are audio cues from monsters that play multiple times at the same time making it loud)         I strongly recommend this game if you like exploration/isometric combat (especially if you like Terraria). The pacing and progression of this game is fantastic.         I had a solo world and character for when my friends were offline and while I enjoyed playing with friends there was something magical with exploring the deepest dankest caves and biomes while being alone. It created a terrified feeling of what is hiding around the corner that will kill me next.         I played on normal difficulty and while some fights were easy because I progressed past them I still enjoyed all of the boss fights. The final couple of boss fights were pretty tough.         I have pretty much nothing but high praise, but there are a couple of things that I noticed that I hope gets fixed down the road. The final two biomes did not really have much going on in them. the second to last biome felt fine, but there was not that extra push to keep exploring once I realize there was really only one thing to do outside of getting the ore and getting out. The final area felt like it was rushed or the devs felt like they needed one more biome to make the game bigger. While I like the visuals and the encounter in that biome, it felt really empty once I realized what it was.         With those minor complains out of the way, I really hope these devs stick with the game and continue to progress the game/fill up the current map. They have plenty of space to work with with adding new things to do. I will keep my eye on this game going forward and will immediately jump back into it if they release new content.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: 1/29/2024With numerous updates adding new features that smooth out the overall gameplay, especially with the QoL change to the multiple crafting stations being able to craft all tiers below them, the game has become significantly more enjoyable. There's a lot more variety in equipment, and the inclusion of pets and more unique collectables adds a lot more colour to the adventure. We've been surprised multiple times over how many new offerings and quality of life changes there were to play with since we last played.Sadly, the game still feels very on-rails after the initial starter bosses, but it's a very enjoyable game these days with much more to find than before. I can definitely recommend the game now, but it still could use some more of that same level of variety in exploration introduced toward the start of the game for its later areas, as well as more unique items/weapons to find at each tier to allow for more playstyle diversity.-(OUTDATED) Old Review:It's a bit checklist-y after the inner ring of bosses, even though it started out incredibly promising. I have more issues with the overarching game design than I do the direct gameplay, and it's really souring what would otherwise be really enjoyable.Really felt like a worthy Terraria-esque RPG where progression doesn't just go in a straight line and had a lot of cool things to discover at your own pace, but it kind of hits a wall (ironically) after you open the literal wall in the game surrounding the inner circle.Once you're beyond that, progression feels incredibly linear, with a pretty defined path of which bosses to fight or where to go because of how dangerous everything is. That, and materials required to tech up are found in specific biomes leading up to one another. Any attempt to skip or explore beyond the intended path at this point gets stifled by strict game design discouraging exploration through limiting your options.After playing for long enough, you also kind of realize there isn't anything unique to really collect that does anything noticeable besides useful passive bonuses. As far as weapons go, they all feel pretty much the same, and there's no creative magic like Terraria or wacky weapons to find like modded (or even vanilla) Starbound. Just some speed/scaling variations but no particularly differing movesets/summons/gimmicks. There's almost nothing to differentiate players' playstyles, especially when playstyle-relevant things like dodging/shielding or role-encompassing stats are strongly dictated by the resource/tech tier you're currently in, too.Building leaves very little to the imagination as well, with most essential components to a base being made irrelevant by other things in the techtree or just requiring too many things something else also needs- so they end up crammed in the same room as each other instead of encouraging us to sprawl them out elegantly. The inventory management leaves a lot to be desired as well, as managing chests and limited space even with upgrades feels frustrating when moving large amounts of items. Not to mention that the game has an incessant need to fill your inventory with valuables that do nothing but sell for currency, yet there's so many of them.I just can't recommend it. It starts out strong but the direction feels a little confused. It could change, but for now I just can't recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game and very much enjoyed pouring hundreds of hours of my life into it, and plan to do more in the near future. I finished my Normal mode playthrough and am just about to clean up and finish my Hard mode playthrough so I think I am just about qualified to put what I've gathered thus far:The game's storytelling is incredible. At the very beginning, you are thrown into a room with roots, dirt walls, and an inactive core, and even though nothing is explained to you, the design of the game is so intuitive that I went a really far ways into the game without even needing to look anything up on the wiki, which is incredibly rare for this style of game.I can clearly tell that the game was balanced incredibly well... for normal mode. I can feel myself getting stronger in a directly proportional relation to how much effort I put into growing my character, and the dopamine hit is insane as I walk into an area and get to participate in a mini bullet hell, only to come out on top. I think that that is a big part of the charm of the game.I love the way that food was implemented. There is an incredible amount of variety that comes with the choices you are allowed to make as a player when it comes to what you eat. I'd say that after 30 minutes of playtime, food becomes less of a hindrance and more a huge part of what gives this game its character. When I say that I can feel my strength increasing directly based on how much effort I put in, the food system plays probably the biggest role in that. There is no limit to the amount of buffs that you can have on your player, besides the amount of effort you are willing to put in to coordinating them. One caveat that I will note here- I play with the Keep Farming mod, which allows me to reliably fill up my tummy with a variety of Golden Crops really reliably once hitting farming 80, so my relationship with the food system isn't *entirely* vanilla.This does bring me onto my next point. The Mod Integration is also a really cool thing to have as a default setting in the game. There is no alternate version of the game to download or anything, or a third party to manage all the files through. Everything is hosted natively, and many of the mods exist solely to improve the game in ways that I think the base game could benefit greatly from. For some examples of mods that I really appreciate and why:-Keep Farming: Pretty self explanatory, allows me to take Core Keeper from a game where you can garden into a game where you can Farm, which is a huge difference. I do think that the game could benefit from a way to create more seeds from the ones you have planted (Maybe increase base seed reclamation % by 5%, so at Gardening 25 you get 105% seeds from crops?), especially since getting more seeds in huge quantities is pretty tough at all stages of progression.-Placement +, I think its called. I have a giant base in my hard mode run, and without this mod it still wouldn't be finished. Increase the scale of placement and shovel actions with keybinds and then alter greater parts of the world with it. This small QOL mod played likely the biggest part in shaping my experience in my latest playthrough.-Faster Minecarts: The world is infinitely large. Minecarts don't get any faster than the one obtained in the Forgotten Ruins. I think this is pretty self explanatory, as it keeps Minecart tracks both relevant and useful to the player, especially as the slower minecarts typically aren't fast enough to avoid getting killed by the Tentacles in the Sea or the Assassins in the Desert.Anyways, there's far more to this game than the modding, and I love every single thing about it, besides one important, glaring one.One of the complaints that I saw in the Core Keeper subreddit a couple of days ago was that the Bosses in hard mode were so incredibly easy and the mobs were too hard, and that one of the devs was confused by this since they hear a lot that the bosses are too hard, and the mobs are easy. I agree with both of these, and it stems from the fact that Hard mode is definitely in dire need of some balancing assistance. I get that its hard difficulty, but that is no excuse to be getting consistently 2-shot at EVERY stage of the game. The slimes in the dirt biome deal a good chunk of health, but its nothing to really worry about. I stepped foot into the clay caves and got dropped immediately into dangerously low health by a single spear, dealing 130 damage in a place where there are not many options to increase the health pool or armor stat of the player. I immediately hid back in my base and fished for a while to gather some resources and try again. Despite preparing, 2 shots still would've killed me, just for stepping into the second area of the game.This is a constant story throughout the whole game. From what I can see, Normal difficulty is balanced so that by the time you make it into a new biome, a roughly equivalent amount of hits will kill you based on the relationship between your Max Health, Armor, and enemy damage. The thing that really changes the game is the enemy mechanics, which makes for a game that doesn't get more damaging, just more technical at a rate at which the player can pick it up.This balance falls apart immediately on Hard Difficulty. If you had 80 points of armor on Normal, and an enemy deals 150, you'd take 70 points of damage. That's fair, as it gives you as the player room to make mistakes and still feel like you are growing in strength. In Hard Difficulty, the damage doubles. This seems like it should be fine as a difficulty increase, but in practice the amount of damage taken is far more than double due to the fact that none of your defensive stats become more effective. With 70 points of armor, you don't take double damage from an enemy that deals 150 in normal, you take something closer to triple due to the fact that your defensive stats consistently lag behind in all stages of the game.At no point in the game can I feel myself as a player getting stronger, just that I am barely holding on. Just as enemies in the Clay Caves 2 shot me, as so enemies in the Forgotten ruins, the Azeos Wilderness, the Sunken Sea, The Desert (to an extreme degree) and the Shimmering Frontier (at a point where it just feels insane.) Whenever engaging with the combat system gets you sent home every 10 minutes, players are incentivized to play defensively at all times, and are punished for spreading their wings. This led me to a gameplay loop where I would play a little bit in the zone to find a boulder, hide in my base and upgrade, and then run to the next zone and do the next. By the time that I had gotten to the point where I was running out of upgrades to do to my gear, I was still getting killed almost immediately by random events outside of my control. I think that if the damage stats were identical on paper as it got processed through your defensive stats, and THEN got doubled, instead of being doubled already when it ran through, the difficulty would be a lot more consistent and manageable for players such as myself (i.e. 300 damage - 70 defense = 230 damage vs. (150 damage - 70 defense = 80 damage) x2 = 160 damage. I think this would be far better as, in late game areas, I'm consistenly taking what feels like 5-6x the damage from enemy attacks, instead of the double I was told to expect.Besides the (imo) poor balancing on the hard mode side of things, the devs have put together an incredible game that is filled with some of the best gameplay and most enthralling visual storytelling I've ever encountered in a game, and for incredibly cheap at that. Definitely recommend.Oh and, dodge chance maxes out at 90%, but defense only blocks up to 75%. Was this intentional?tl,dr: Incredible game, immediately became one of my favorites of all time. Could use some more QOL, Hard Mode balancing is wack (or personal skill issue tbh), but still a 9.9/10 normal mode.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best game in this genre. I really don't think it's close. This is one of the few early access titles that felt worth it immediately. It hasn't ever felt like an early access title to me because of all the polish. I've come to realize that I kind of hate a lot of games. Each company seems to exist in a separate universe. Every company needs to reinvent the wheel or mindlessly parrot what others are doing without understanding the design behind it. Why am I mentioning this is a positive review for this game? Because Pugstorm didn't fall for that and very clearly sat down to think deeply about even small aspects of design. After playing for a few hours I realized I didn't want to look up mods to fix the UI or add super basic QoL features. Then I remembered I was playing an 'early access' title. Most games in this genre feel really bad to play without mods (Terraria anyone?). I've had plenty of moments playing this game where I've gone "wait... why isn't this the standard everywhere".  For example, enemies hitting you when you walk into them in games is kind of crap. This is a holdover from the 'before times' when having attack animations was literally not possible due to cart size limitations. Most dev teams will just stick with that because thinking is hard or something.Combat feels good overall. Usually melee builds tend to feel bad in games like this, but they do a good job of not making melee too punishing. Clear attack animations mean you aren't also playing a secret game of tag with every monster, so that probably helps.  Also, the unique weapons you can find are usually interesting. Either they're a bit better than what you can make or have a usable gimmick. They've added some new combat styles I haven't had a chance to try, but the ranged combat options were varied and interesting before, so I'm sure it's only better now. I don't usually expect boss design to leave an impression on me in games like this because I feel like I've seen a lot of the same things over and over. I was pleasantly surprised with most of the boss encounters.Progression hits a sweetspot between having a grind and being rewarding. Using a skill levels it up and you get to spend points in a skill tree. Each skill has it's own builds that you can reset any time for a small amount of currency. This adds a lot because otherwise you're totally reliant on gear for character customization. Armor/Accessories were kind of basic at first, but they've added a wonderful upgrade system. In most games, you have to make a new set of gear at increasingly higher tiers. This game lets you take early game gear with you into the endgame. That low level ranged set with the cool set bonus you like? Just upgrade it with the materials from each tier and watch those stats you like get bigger. Core Keeper says "no" to fast fashion.  The gardening and cooking are maybe a little more basic that I would like, but I think this is an intentional choice because the game rewards you for going out and exploring. I do think they do a good job of using the plants as crafting materials outside of cooking, so you are rewarded for planting a good amount of certain crops. I'm not sure exactly how to improve cooking, but that is the only part of the game that feels even remotely underdeveloped to me. Also, the game looks really good. It's actually 3D which is probably why the lighting looks super crisp. I'm not usually much of a builder, but this game gives you enough aesthetic options that it will probably inspire you a least a little bit. This game looks like art.   Again, the biggest thing to me is that the game hasn't ever felt like it was in early access. Launch is coming up soon, but they aren't loading up a wheelbarrow full of broken pieces to dump at the finish line on launch day. I've been burned by a lot of early access titles, but Pugstorm have continued to deliver quality updates since I picked it up.  I hate a lot of games, but I really like Core Keeper. If you're a fan of the genre I would recommend checking it out.

_childDocuments_.review: This game seemed unremarkable when i first encountered the early access, but i was quickly charmed by the gameplay and especially charming graphics~if you like Terraria, this is a must-try! I love the innovative map generation thats kept in rings, which makes it really fun to explore in all directions! Even the building aspect of the game surprised me, because from first glance it seems that you dont have many options besides your average brick and hay walls, but the generated structures and painting option offers alot of variety to cook up some absolutely beautiful builds (not to mention the gorgeous gernerated builds all across the world, i love stopping by these and taking screenshots)!The ore progression is not too slow, and also not too quickly overcome, and i like the creativity with the in-game metals after you get past gold.The combat is fun and not too clunky, and the upgrading of weapons into late-game is something i wish other titles would do as well.HOWEVER:There are two gripes i have with this game, and they are a kind of annoying thing to deal with...The first being the durability system. In my opinion, these just straight up consume more time than you should be needed to put in. It become annoying real quickly, especially when you're working on large scale builds (there is a skill in the mining tree that lets you regain durability points when mining ore, but its not broad enough to fix the issue, like with weapons or armor for example).There have been one or two cases where my armor broke through a boss fight, and i had to take a larger  break in order to renew the items i needed to beat the boss...Speaking of bosses, there comes my other main gripe with this game. and unfortunately, this one really stings. Call me a bad gamer but this thing needs a desperate rework. Im talking about Omoroth, the boss residing within the sunken sea. Let me ask you this, if you die to a boss, you probably try to get back there as soon as possible to give it another shot, right?Well, unfortunately, with Omoroth, that can be pretty difficult. His arena consists mostly of water, and thus, making a boat to fight him is essential.Sure, you could cover the entire area in walkable tiles, but Oh-Oh, you didn't account for the tentacles that spawn, which break tiles in a 2 by 2 area wherever they are summoned. And he summons *alot* of tentacles, Pair that with his absurdly unfair vortex attacks, and you have the recipe for a downright unfair and unfun Boss, thatll force you to go on a major collection detour to get another boat, or tiles, if you die to him.Unfotunately, Omoroth in my eyes takes this game down quite a few tiers.Despite that though! I still love this game!!! Its charming, its cute, its well-packed full of stuff, but not at all overbearing, and not too grindy whatsoever! in my opinion, 7/10, and a deffinate recommendation to people who love sandbox games and terraria lovers!

_childDocuments_.review: What I wanted:A comfy mining/farming game with some cool exploration and maybe a few interesting boss fights.What I got:Digging up 10,000 identical slime tiles one at a time to stop them from respawning and stop my character from moving 0.01 mile an hour, all the while my tools keep breaking from durability that would make BOTW blush and my character hungrier than the average Ethiopian while constantly crying they're hungry because the hunger system was designed by someone who clearly hates fun.Half of the stuff in this game is a chore that feels tedious to engage with, and the controls feel kinda imprecise and clunky. The kind of "i'm just going to let my character die instead of eating to reset hunger" tedium because eating food gains you barely any hunger back, food is far too few and far between and digging feels so garbage that I really don't want to engage in farming.In games like this such as Minecraft, when you want to create safe areas to navigate through you pop down a few torches and it's done, the whole ordeal took 5 seconds and you can move on with your life.In this, you come across a room of slimes, have to one by one clear them out in awkward combat because I can't find a dodge roll for the life of me (so instead it's just awkward hit, walk back a bit, hit, walk back a bit...). Then spend 20-30 minutes digging up slime all around you so they don't respawn anymore, though better make sure you brought like 6 shovels because lol they're all going to break before you're even half way done through the room. And make sure you brought like 20 mushrooms or you're prepared to die and walk all the way back, because otherwise your character is going to constantly screech that they need something to eat while you desperately fumble through the settings menu trying to find the option to either completely turn hunger off or slow the rate of hunger down because you're wondering why is it even in the game in this state and are the developers and people praising the game actually having fun with that mechanic.Oh and then when you're done with that one room, dig a few more down and there's another completely identical one to waste your durability on. Enjoy!Do I only have 2.8 hours in this game? Yes.Did I enjoy it? Not a second.Will I be coming back? Not unless there's been a massive overhaul, because what's here so far just isn't fun in the slightest.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed my play-through of the game, solid 20-30 hours of content. This game shows a lot of potential and could be really good if it had more content as the base is already solid.The game features a skill system where you individually level certain traits such as fishing, melee combat, etc. Fishing and gardening skills even reward the player with combat buffs at a certain level. Combat is interesting; enemies have different attack patterns and you have to learn them to effectively defeat them without taking damage.Lastly, one can change the tiles, build walls and bridges and even collect unique decorations to put in the base throughout their adventure. There are many hidden collectibles spread over the huge, seemingly infinite map, and provides for lots of exploration.Overall, the combat system may be limited (so is the weapon variety), but it is still fun given the restrictive movement. (Think Terraria's Eye of Cthuthlu shield in the early game) There is still much more in this space that can be explored by the devs and I look forward to more interesting and challenging enemies in the future.Next, decorating the base is quite limited. There are not many different kinds of decorations. You can paint your base different colours though!Lastly-lastly, the game has a bit of mechanisation - robot crane arms and automated belts. This unlocks a totally different kind of gameplay that I look forward too as well.In conclusion, I recommend this game but with the caveat that I suggest waiting for the next one or two content updates before playing. If you want to play right away though, it's good for a few dozen hours - a long time in its own right.*Edit*: There's multiplayer too!

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game, I just finished the first boss and I thought I would write down my initial impression. It reminds me strongly of Keplerth It also reminds me of Minecraft and TerrariaOne of my favorite features of this game is it is absolutely pitch black underground and if you don't have a light source you can't see anything. Some games will make it really dim without a light but not this game. Definitely makes the first boss more terrifying as it keeps smashing your torches; plunging the world into darkness.The cooking setup is fun, so far it seems you can combine any two ingredients and you will get a unique food item that looks like a combination of the two and gives you bonuses from each part. _childDocuments_.review: Core Keeper is a little like Terraria, but for the most part its it's own thing.Worth full price, you'll get many hours of enjoyment out of it.This game has twin-stick controls here, you use your cursor to aim while moving.Scrounge for resources, collect rare loot, make better gear, and fight bosses to progress.Try to be prepared for a fight before you go in, but bosses don't reset if you die, so it's not very hard.The only penalty for dying is anything that wasn't in your hotbar is left inside a grave where you died, you can go and collect it whenever you feel.Your presence isn't required for enemies to spawn and die, sometimes they'll fight and leave item drops behind for you to find later.Items also do not despawn, so you can just leave things behind and pick them up later, this is also useful for conveyor belts.Conveyor belts are useful for item farms such as  and mob farms, you can place drills that'll automatically mine ore for you from boulders placed around the game world.You can make turrets that'll kill enemies when they spawn, having them be automatically delivered to your chest of choosing no matter how far.By far the worst part of the game, skills take a very long time to level up, often you'll have to basically grind for XP. After 79 hours of gameplay the only skill I managed to max was gardening.It's not a requirement for beating the game, so it's not too big of a flaw unless you wanted to get 100% without mods.Pretty good stuff, some decent jams.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. As you probably know, it's basically a top-down version of Terraria or Minecraft, but in my opinion vastly superior to both. Minecraft has hideous visuals, while Core Keeper is beautiful to look at. Terraria has the infuriating issue of being CONSTANTLY bombarded by enemy attacks, always preventing you from doing what you are trying to do. Core Keeper, conversely, is much more respectful of the player, typically allowing you to engage enemies on your own terms. It's also easier to prevent enemies spawning where you don't want them to be. So you have the freedom to build a house, craft items, farm animals and plants, and cook food without being constantly bothered (unless you set up your base in a spot with a lot of enemy spawn tiles, but you can remove those to "cleanse" it anyway as mentioned above). 10+ hours in so far and 2 bosses defeated, and I haven't been pestered by the stupid bloodmoons, goblin hordes or any crap like that that happens in many other survival crafting games. I've had enemies appear around my base 2-3 times causing minor damage, and that's plenty; enough to give you a reason to think about traps and securing your base, but not so much as to detract from your main goals. So this is a welcome difference that makes me want to keep playing.If you've never played either of the abovementioned games, but think you like the idea of survival crafting and building game, it's excellent for the asking price (especially as it's 50% off on a couple stores), so give it a go. Beautiful graphics; a fun and engaging gameplay loop of exploring, collecting resources and building; easy to jump into and back out of on your own time, and great fun either solo or with a friend(s).

_childDocuments_.review: 1.0 just released and I gave it a try, and I'm rewriting my review. The thing I enjoyed the most about this game is exploration, especially secret areas like the royal tombs. However it does get a little old after I've seen almost everything each area has to offer. Overall the experience was alright, not mind-blowing, but it's an okay game to kill some time with. I'll probably play it again some time in the future whenever I feel the itch.I feel like this game has so much potential but there are so many aspects of it that are so lackluster. It's such a shame. It's the kind of game that doesn't have enough to get me fully invested but pretty cozy to play for some casual gaming.Here are some things that I wish were included in the game or could be improved upon: -Quick-storing items to nearby chests. I was playing with a controller and inventory management has been such a pain. -More weapons choices. Melee weapons have such close range that I didn't even bother with them 'cause it's just too dangerous.The fireball staff is just so much better than bows that I've been using it all the time since I got it early game. The summons don't do much so I stopped using them when my pet got strong enough. The weapon design just lacks certain creativity. Combat gets boring when I'm using the same staff 95% of the time because of how good it is. The upgrade system sounds like a good idea at first but then it just gets boring since it means I'm still using the same thing. No ability upgrade or extra perks or whatsoever. Only the number grows bigger and bigger.-Cooking lacks creativity too. Being able to cook with any two ingredients sounds great but it really isn't. I just end up stuck with 3 or 4 dishes with my preferred buffs and don't bother to make anything else. I think it would be great to have like an advanced cooking station that allows you to cook certain recipes with better and more interesting effects.-Enemies don't despawn. It's especially annoying when you're visiting an area that you haven't been to for a long time, then you're gonna find the entire place crawling with enemies. There might be a limit to how many can be spawned in to an area, but I'm not sure.-Something to stop enemies from being spawned near my base. There's this new giant mushroom enemy now and it freaking destroys blocks. It's such a pain that I can't keep my mushroom farm the way it is. -Collection system. Something like a museum or whatnot for all the insects, critters and treasures I find. I don't think there's anything you can do with the bugs you catch except for feeding them to the animals but I could be wrong. _childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game! The game is 100% worth it at it's current price point. Like everyone said it's like a love child between Stardew valley and Terraria. The game has a lot of potential. At the moment while it's a great game, it does lack the polish that both Stardew Valley and Terraria both have (but both games have had YEARS of development). As development progresses I can only see the game getting better and better.While the game says it's built for 1-8 players, the game is completely playable SOLO. That was my biggest worry that it wouldn't be fun solo. I had a nice relaxing time playing at my own pace. Currently there are 4 main bosses, and 2 side bosses. You can beat the 4 main bosses within 30 hours. The game can be kinda grindy to collect resources, but it's actually not that bad if you listen to a nice podcast/youtube video as you play. I found it strangely therapeutic.EDIT: 4/16/2022: Their new repair mechanic makes the game less fun overall. I wouldn't recommend the game to new players especially solo players unless they fix the repair system.Edit: 4/27/2022: They have been making strides to fix the repair system. The game is still relaxing enough to warrant a recommendation. It's nice when a development team listens to their audience and corrects mistakes.Edit: 6/16/2021HIGHLY Recommend the game. It is pretty amazing when the dev team implements every SINGLE quality of life improvement that was suggested by the community. Many of these quality of life improvements have made me come back to the game after their first major update which did in fact add a lot of new content. This is a very relaxing game. Props to the developer for actually putting in a lot of effort into making a quality game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to recommend this game if you enjoyed any of these games:Stardew ValleyTerrariaMinecraftWith an *.This has a lot going for it and the fact it is in Early Access and has quite a bit of content already is fantastic. Other Early Access games dream of having this much content on an EAG release. However, while there is plenty of potential, the game has a long way to go before it becomes a hit. The gameplay loop does start to get a little monotonous. NPC character interaction, more bosses, more items, basically more of everything, and WAAAY more trash mobs are needed. I also feel the difficulty (I only played by myself) is pretty easy. I've heard it can be difficult but for some reason I found it easy until I got to the 3rd boss. But up until that point it was a breeze and I almost put it on the shelf. That boss was great to beat though. The awesome thing about that particular boss was I didn't need to "level up", I just needed to adjust my strategy - WHICH IS AWESOME for a game. I love the fact that you have to approach a boss differently and figure out a SMART way to beat it instead of just... oh let me gain more levels and mash my way to defeating this boss (lookin at you Eldin Ring) then using your actual brain to defeat said boss.I have to say, if there was a way to invest in this game through stock options I would be buying up a sh&* load because this game has HIGH potential. Let's just hope the devs don't pull out and release lame patches until the end of time....NOTE: I've seen others compare this game to these: Valheim, Factorio, Satisfactory, OxygenNotIncluded, and Don't Starve. I feel these are not good examples to compare to as they barely have any similarities in my opinion. _childDocuments_.review: Although I don't have a huge amount of time played in this game, I can honestly say that Core Keeper is quite a wonderful piece of artistry. It's a incredibly beautiful environment considering it's pixel style graphics. From what I've played, I've come to enjoy the fact that there is no doubt in my mind when I've crossed over into another, new, portion of the world. It's incredible seeing the distinct differences in each biome that I've traveled too so far. The eerie change in music, the different shades of color, the quirky responses of some new mob that I've yet to uncover because their beady little red eyes put me in a sense that I should tread carefully. It's quite comedic how I've responded to new enemies in this game. It's also comedic at how many times I've died thinking my brand new armor would outmatch their damage....yeah, that was a mistake lol.The general feel of the game is enjoyable. I've found myself a few times smashing through walls for 30-45 minutes at a time without any real purpose other than trying to see if I can find some odd little hideaway for mobs that I can exploit. The music really set the tone for me when digging around like that.The entire game is one giant quest which is great because I don't have the dragging feeling when I leave my base. I know undoubtedly that whatever I do outside of my spawn will offer some sort of reward towards moving closer to unlocking something new. The general gameplay doesn't have that grind feeling that I got from other sandbox games.Like I said above, the environment and design is quite amazing considering the games pixel graphics style. Vibrant colors, interesting mob designs, and the overall theme throughout the different regions are definitely topnotch. Each regions music really sets the tone as well.Not everything is obviously perfect in this game and of course, there isn't a single game out there that doesn't have its drawbacks. The largest of which is none other than it's optimization. The games optimization is mediocre at best. Lighting in this game really puts a strain on your system. (of course, if you happen to have some top of the line gear, I'm sure you'll do just fine.) There are points when I run into my base and physically see my fps drop to what feels like an oncoming crash of the software. Keep in mind, my system is nothing in comparison to what a lot of serious players out there may have, but it does seem quite odd that I can load up a similar title and have zero issues when it comes to how smooth the game operates. Another drawback that I've found is that the cursor seems quite clunky. I'm not sure if it may just be my system trying to handle the game itself or if it's the game, but I've noticed at times that when I have my cursor directly over the top of a plant I'm trying to harvest, it decides to hit the tile next to that plant instead of the one I'm selecting.As of right now, that's my review for Core Keeper. I don't have too many complaints regarding this game and I intend on continuing to support this game and the future development of it. Top notch devs! Thanks for a great game!

_childDocuments_.review: The game doesn't autosave and it has spiralled me into a progression depression twice now.Corekeeper doesn't fail as a game, it has a charm akin to Terraria. In Corekeeper you grind endlessly to level up your skills and get gear, I'd say the majority of the game is spent on this. Which in itself isn't the worst, many games do this. The problem is that the game only saves whenever you exit your world, so if the game ever crashes for any reason before you save and exit, you lose ALL your progress; in your world and character both. And while it doesn't crash all the time, when it does it is DEVASTATING. I've lost countless hours of progress to this issue, I am beyond infuriated.For me, until they fix this issue Corekeeper is simply too risky to invest your time into at the moment. _childDocuments_.review: A must have for Terraria fans, Stardew Valley combat enthusiasts, people looking for a game to play with friends, or anybody looking for a challenge! Also lots of customization and base decorating options, and awesome scenes that can be found randomly around the world that makes exploration refreshing every time you have to go out.The only downsides, in my opinion, are that: It can get a fair bit grindy at times, but I think this can be avoided when playing with friends. _childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game more than I actually do.  I played both during first release during early access and after 1.0.  The game is a fun, casual, survival/mining romp up until you get passed the content that was available at initial release.  The grind significantly increases, the new biomes actively work to be "unfun," and the bosses at that point are miserable.  It is simply not fun having to grind up 200x of various not-so-easy to get resources that take forever to refine just to build one important structure or even a faster version of vehicle. It's also not fun getting to a water biome where it's safer and easier just to build land bridges because going out on the water with a boat will inevitably end with you needing to build a land bridge to get your body/boat back.In short, much of the newer content is padded out with grind/difficulty rather than anything unique.  Once you've done a few iterations of "find new biome, get new flavor of ore, beat boss" you won't find much else offered.  The early game will make you think otherwise because you get mazes, puzzles, and other scenes that give you hope that your experience will be varied going forward.  Sadly, if anything, it gets simpler as you go.At the very least, I would suggest the developers seriously consider the cost of late game items.  Requiring rare drops for upgrades, hundreds of resources, or drop-dependent items just for one try at a boss, is not fun.  Many items need to be re-balanced to feel meaningful and purposeful in the game.  Choosing to try the warlock/mage class will lock you out of many crafting options because you simple cannot craft magic-relevant armor or weapons and the ones you find are of limited use (e.g., summoned mobs barely engage enemies, staves that can blow you up as fast as they can enemies).  Lastly, there are a lot of seemingly "unfinished" ideas with crafting benches that could give this game a healthy boost.  Automation could be a lot of fun but there is little point with the available tools provided (need load balancing at the very least).In short, I'd wait for the developers to refine the game further before diving in with your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks cute and fun on the surface but underneath is a hilariously unbalanced and anti-fun grindfest. There's a point where some bosses are literally unbeatable with skill. You just need to spend hours grinding for higher stats or making specific builds, It feels much less like a game and more like a puzzle at that point. I'm sure part of our issues came from playing on hard but that's another problem in it's entirety. When I think hard I think "can be overcome with practice and more skill". Not whatever this is. We specifically struggled with the boss "Omoroth". It's sad because the core gameplay is fun, the visuals are beautiful, the soundtrack is good. But the balancing and grind are just godawful and feel like they needlessly prolong the game. We loved the experience past the first three bosses,We typically enjoy hard games. Unfortunately this games difficulty doesn't come from requiring more skill but requiring more time and knowledge, which is just not fun. Again it'd be acceptable if time and knowledge were a substitute to make it easier for those struggling and not a base requirement.All in all I believe the game's worth keeping an eye on. At the moment the gameplay just starts to deteriorate past the 5 hour mark.

Too bad, I would say wait for it to get better. But its had long enough in early access to get better.

Ranged dominates and Melee is only useful if you enjoy taking contact damage from the garbage range all melee weapons have.The leveling system is something that can basically be ignored, it only really serves to reduce the time spent grinding and doesn't really impact the gameplay in a significant manner at all.Inventory management is awful, this is terrible for a game where at least 20% your time will be spent just managing the myriad of useless items and drops. The item progression system just feels like a skinner box time sink if you ever played a crafting game with more depth like factorio. Base building feels absolutely pointless because the NPCs do nothing but wander around uselessly and get in the way, don't engage with enemies, don't talk, and there are only five of them anyway. Nothing they sell is really needed or worth the time bothering with.There isn't really a need to fight the bosses multiple times since only 1 or 2 drops are worth anything per boss, and they always drop those items. They aren't interesting enough to warrant fighting again because the mechanics the player is limited to never expand beyond anything you'll see from the beginning of the game.Weapons are also really boring, and unique weapons are pretty rare and aren't much different from any basic weapon.The game gets really boring, weapons never become interesting, enemies never become interesting, the bosses are easy, the mechanics are extremely basic.
