_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this game in early access, and was immediately charmed by it. The art is adorable, the sounds are intuitive yet unique, and (my favorite), there's a lot you can do to build a base however you please.Core Keeper has a lot going for it. It takes some of the best features of several games I have loved over the years (Minecraft, Starbound, Terraria) and found a way to make satisfying progress without too much grind. So far, it feels pretty well balanced.I am a particularly big fan of the scrap mechanic of this game. It was taken out, and then returned to us (more on that below) so I really could feel how much it impacted things. It's a great way to allow for a slower play style, which I personally really enjoy. Not a lot of games out there let you go at your own pace without penalizing you somehow, so I'm very glad it's there in Core Keeper.(Note: Up until the time that I updated this review, I did NOT recommend this game, due to a poorly-managed major change to the repair system. They have since removed that change and went back to the formula that worked best, building off of that to make an even better system than before. I believe the team have been a lot more mindful of updates since that point, and my personal faith in them has been restored. I only leave this in for now to be perfectly clear about my complete 180 in my review of the game. It was a bit of a bumpy road here and there, but I do feel like the developers are listening to their player community.)

_childDocuments_.review: First - don't let the hrs on record be an indicator of the grind involved.  About 2/3's of my played time has been OCD related developing/changing my base, acquiring EVERY item in the game to display on pedestals, etc. etc.  That is not to say there is not countless hours worth of content to experience just playing the main content.  I picked this up shortly after their first EA update a few years ago and have been hooked every since.  A great example of a game where the devs have a continued passion to make a great product and iterate/update on it, listen to community feedback and (because I feel it needs to be said given the state of much of gaming) don't feel the need to push an agenda and then complain when their game fails.  The volume of content released during EA has been nothing short of remarkable, consistently updating their living roadmap and I look forward to all Post 1.0 content.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking at this game and thinking it will scratch your terraria itch PLEASE GET IT, an incredibly surprising experience that I have loved almost every second of. The game is very intuitive and I haven't needed or really even wanted to look at the wiki for anything, not too difficult at all and allows for a decent amount of creativity with both character builds and base building though hopefully more to come as its still in EA. The game is very pretty, lots of nice bouncy animations and lighting that reminds me of octopath traveler, I like a lot of the enemy designs and having holiday themed ones is fun as well! Plenty of easter eggs and references in flavor text as well as achievements, the game so far obviously has a lot of care put into it and I can't wait to see it grow. Now for a little bit of the nitty gritty, I think not having certain weapon types per ore upgrade feels a little bad if you're focusing building around one, it has sucked to spend time making a new anvil just to find out I can't make a new dagger or ranged weapon or something, I like the focus on exploration but inventory management can sometimes be a chore in this game, quick stack is making it mostly fine but I would love to favorite items so they dont get removed (like wood) when dumping my inventory. I would also say that copying a bit more from terraria and having a button in inventory for quick stacking to nearby chests would also cut down on inventory management. this last bit is completely out of pocket but while I enjoy having to go get different wall or floor types for decoration, maybe some expensive way to convert wall/floor types into different ones would help encourage being a bit more creative with base building? halfway through and we have thousands of dirt walls that just aren't going to be used for anything, maybe a new kind of machine in scarlet or octarine tier? those are just mostly random thoughts while writing, the game is a ton of fun and I highly recommend anyone to give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: 6/10. I give this game a lukewarm yes.For the price, I would recommend other games such as Terraria, Valheim, and Stardew Valley as they have way more content to enjoy and a more rewarding experience. This game is in Early Access, so there are still elements to be added, but the overall core gameplay cycle (ex. explore new biome, farm resources, kill boss) is unrewarding and therefore boring. The game is very grindy, but doesn't reward the player adequately for all their hard work. Bosses will drop items that are significantly worse than items you can find on basic mobs. The boss fights themselves are ResidentSleeper. The main goal of the game is to kill the bosses and outside of that there isn't much else to do. So if you are a goal-oriented player, then I think you'll find the experience lacking and un-fun.The positives are that the game isn't buggy ~ especially considering its Early Access state. The graphics are cute. And playing with friends is fun and makes the game playable. There's a lot of potential with interesting elements like pets, shopkeepers, and automation. If you buy this game, I don't think you'll hate it. I don't think you'll love it either though.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually like this better than Minecraft for reasons I don't fully understand yet. It seems perhaps more streamlined or less confusing. I'm playing this with my two kids, aged 7 and 9 and it is complex enough to keep me, a 40ish year old man entertained, but easy enough for small children to grasp. Unfortunately there is no split screen type co-op, but that is understandable imo because otherwise you'd be tied to the same area or the screen would be too small. The upside is this motivated me to smash together a couple of old PCs into a new frankenstein gamish. It is an interesting evolution, from iPad kids, to playing on PC with Xbox controllers, and now eventually somewhat with the mouse. At least they're seeing it is way easier to navigate and aim using mouse rather than the controllers. Anyways, we're currently 4 hours in and having a blast. There is enough decorating and building for my daughter, enough exploring and fishing for my skittish son, and enough logistics, organization, combat, and complexity to keep my adult gaming sensibilities fulfilled. That's a pretty tall order if you think about it, and it makes sense why this game has such great reviews. Another benefit to the devs (and Steam for that matter) to this more cheap co-op game is now each kid has their own Steam account, own PC, and own copies of Core Keeper. Nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Review at Patch: 1.0.0.7Hours Clocked: 70.7Face it, if you are into this genre you have probably already played Terraria, Necesse, and Don't Starve (Together). You have probably clocked hundreds of hours at the least and like me you were hungry for more.I have checked in with Core Keeper since it first became available, stopping at the first titan that was originally available. While I enjoyed myself then, I really wanted to wait until the game was fully released before I dove in. Since then, I have doubled my time in game and for good reason.If you are new to this style of game, the premise is simple. You start with little more than a backstory and a mysterious set of statues. I will touch on the backstories in a moment, but essentially you are now tasked with getting your bearings and eventually downing all the bosses in order to get home.With that in mind, let us return to the backstory you can choose at the beginning.  From professions like Fisher, Explorer, Chef, Fighter, Mage, Warlock, etc you are getting a small bump to start in that  path. Some get early gear, and if you are going to min/max or speed run, these choices matter a little. No matter what you choose, you can do all of it.As you play, you will accrue skill points just by doing "that" action. Your mage finds a sword and now you have decided melee combat is the better path? You will earn the respective points as you go, so mage start or not, you are not stuck with that choice. Conversely, if you find a sweet mage staff, you can go back to slinging magic or decide both is a fun option.As you level up, every so many skill points will move you up a tier. This lets you choose an associated perk and instead of being cumbersome, it is small stat boosts to lean into your style of play. In Co-Op this means you can lean into being the group farmer, or generalize and do whatever. No one tree is overpowered or underpowered and getting skills as you go means your character is always adapting to how you are playing.That said, there are also pets you can get that will also get skills in the same manner. These pets can buff your stats to further specialize your character, or to round out other skills. For example a melee oriented player might want a pet to buff their movement speed and pick a pet that buffs that, or they might choose a pet to buff their ranged attacks for when melee is not ideal.Combat for the most part is attacking with one click, but some weapons do have an alternate attack. Otherwise, it breaks down to simply dodging or attacking. There is enough depth that a mage will play differently than a melee, but shallow enough that playing with friends does not require them all to be able to clear a no hit run in a souls like.In addition to all of that, food and potions further specialize your character. Add in a variety of weapons and armor, and you will find there is a lot you can mess with but not get bogged down.Exploring the world is mostly gated by gear or skill. While a boss is not gated, you might find tackling them in a mild order is easier if you are geared up with the materials found in that biome. There are a lot of good looking biomes, and while some enemies are common like slimes and cavelings, there is enough variety that each area does not feel like a reskin of the last one.Last but not least, builders will find lots of options to decorate, design and paint their new home. You can transport a biome's block, water, and decor to suit your tastes. Want to theme it? Go for it. Want to make a cozy fishing hole? Absolutely. Want to make it a dystopian hellscape full of monsters? Yep! There are even traps to farm them.Overall my recommendation of Core Keeper is Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: So the game isn't completely bad, but if you believe reviews saying it's like Terraria, you'll be disappointed. It's not an adventure, it's a farming and mining game.After almost 2 hours I still haven't found anything interesting in progression or exploration, the game felt like chores. I'm not going to wait another 2/5/10 hours more just for a chance that it might get better.This is purely as if the Hill-top(mining) farm from Stardew was the whole game. It's just tedious mining, planting, and hoping you'll be able to automate it soon so that you can go look for something more fun to do.Terraria was about the mystery of exploration and treasure hunting. There you always expect treasure with unique materials, gear, new unique weapon. Entering a new biom you can always expect some new materials for crafting and (mini)boss or special event. With that gear you want to always try something new, something different and not just next tier set.Here it's all missing. - Get wood - craft wooden gear, then get copper - craft copper gear, get iron - craft iron gear. There is no horizontal progression, only stats upgrades. There is no variation or side-grades, or character building beyond choosing a class. You get a class specific set with a set bonus, which is like 1/3 of total set's power so you really don't want to mix it with anything else. - Combat feels boring. You have 3 basic classes with boring weapons; melee, range, magic. Weapons in each class don't have much variation and all feel the same. Summoner might not exist at all with how awful it feels: resummon pet every ~20 sec, broken AI that constantly stops attacking, pathfinding issues, needs a full set buff and 3 minions to be close to basic mage staff. With summoning frequency and amount of mana it requires, you can’t really mix it with mage.- Exploration is extremely boring. There is no interesting or unique loot, ruins only give the items that you could craft on your crafting bench. Just points of interest with increased quantities of the same materials. - Farming feels extremely clunky and tedious. You can't hold the mouse button to till the soil since it will then automatically turn it back to dirt, and you can only till the adjacent block. Plants growing time is in a weird spot where it is too long to just keep planting, gathering, and planting again with new seeds, but it's also short enough that when you are done planting and crafting, it will grow just a few minutes after you leave the base to explore. So there's a lot of time your farm is not growing.- The UI, controls and missing QoL features just make it feel like an early access game. Interactions are a mix between cursor aim and character position, interaction range is extremely limited, so you often have to adjust character position just to interact with something in front of you; inventory is tiny and not in an interesting way, you can't lock or favorite items, controls for splitting stacks/moving/equipping etc. feel random and unintuitive. There is a lot of unnecessary text with an awful font. Hunger system is very annoying with very little use. You have to constantly cook and eat, but the buffs are barely noticeable.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall this is a good game, however it does have issues which can make it stale at times.Pros:+ Great art style and overall aesthetic+ Good spread of skills (fighting, fishing, mining, farming etc.)+ Gameplay is nice, similar to stardew valley with a larger focus on combat.+ RPG elements where skills level up through use+ Bosses to kill+ Discovering new recipes is satisfyingCons:- New patch repair system means you can no longer use salvage and have to use ores. This would be fine, however ores are not all that common, tools are expensive and break quickly leading me to not use tools, especially when high mining skill can make bare hands decent enough.- Exploration/mining can be dull as you have to tunnel everywhere making finding new areas a bit of a chore. On top of this, ore locations are highlighted so you know there aren't any surprises for you to uncover in your exploration.- melee combat purely relies on kiting making each encounter just a hit then run away experience which is not very satisfying.- Skill trees really only offer stat bonuses. It would have been nice to have abilities or more interesting skills that allow you to lean into a certain playstyle/build more.- Very little driving force to make you progress. Hunger is easy to beat and mobs won't invade you so you don't need to upgrade your base and only need better gear to beat bosses.Overall this is an early access game with a lot of potential. I am confident that more things will be added and am excited to see where the game goes hence my positive review. However until I either get some friends or the game systems become deeper I will probably not be playing much.

_childDocuments_.review: Seriously, if you have ever liked any of the relevant survival games from Minecraft, onwards, buy this game. I first played Core Keeper in early access (I'm talking EARLY access when it first launched on steam) for about 14 hours. From day 1 the foundation for game was entertaining and fun, but didn't necessarily feel like it stood out yet. Fast forward to the launch of 1.0 and I'm honestly fascinated. This game has so much charm. I'm in my 20's now, and Minecraft launched when I was about 10 years old. Growing up, MInecraft was that game that really got me excited about gaming as a whole and opened my eyes to how magical a quality game could be. As I've grown up there have been many great games that have brought innovation to the Minecraft-like, survival genre. Terraria, Starbound, Stardew Valley, and to an extent Satisfactory come to mind as titles that really stick out. This game draws inspiration from all of those games, all while putting it's own wonderful spin on it. Core Keeper removes little inconveniences that are common through out these types of games, but delivers these quality of life features in such a natural and seamless way. For a small example: Tools have durability, but it doesn't feel like nuisance, because the materials to repair them are the same no matter what tool you repair. Additionally, with a couple of extra materials you can double the durability of said item and make it stronger.  Crafting stations draw resources from chests that are placed next to them. Shortcuts and hot keys are readily displayed in menu's so you don't have to stumble around inventories. The pixel art is so cozy and full of character. The sound design is peak, the music is stunning. I can't quite put words to why, but this game gives me the same feeling I had when I played Minecraft and Terraria as a kid. So basically digital crack, delivered in a warm, pixelated, apple pie. TLDR:Exploration is rewarding, mining isn't a chore, as you do things in game, your character levels up. There's loot that feels meaningful, armor that looks cool, unique bosses, pets you can tame and level, gear to collect, and I could go on. All of these features feel well thought out, and created with intention. This game combines elements of Minecraft, Valheim, Terraria, Satrisfactory, and Stardew Valley in a way that is seamless and beautiful. If you have ever been a fan of any of those games, do yourself a favor: skip buying starbucks for a few days, and buy this game. These devs have made something truly special.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: When i saw this game i immediately fell in love with the graphics. Those lightning effects and reflections - simply amazing.At first i enjoyed exploring the game, but the deeper i went the uglier it got (not visually), leaving me with no desire to play until most of the issues i have are fixed.Here are the issues:1. World is too big, and there is no setting to make it smaller. I once decided to find a piece for a sword recipe, the one in the jungle. But after seeing how damn huge that jungle is i just gave up. Biomes also get very repetitive because they are so big.2. Ore deposits are not infinite, making you move your whole drilling and automation setups, and there is no option to make those deposits infinite. Hey devs, why don't you add a soil depletion system for farms? So that farmers would be forced to move their farms every once in a while. I bet it would be fun.3. Hotbar is anti-handy. For example, to plant seeds you will have to remove all your potions and stuff from hotbar, put your seeds in there, plant them, then put your stuff back on the hotbar. Same thing you will do when building. Every. Single. Time.4. Classes and combat sux. I've played with several people in several worlds, and most of them were playing as ranger. Because the rest of the classes simply suck!As a warrior you will see one swinging animation the whole game, mages constantly have no mana, summoner is a joke without multiclassing (and devs are not sure whether he is ranged or melee). There are some failed attempts to make a rogue.Only ranger is the strongest and the most interesting class.Btw the game has almost no active skills. Such a boring and disbalanced combat system in a game where you constantly fight.Those are the big four for me, but there are a lot more minor issues. Like "valuables", or huge unnecessary amount of food recipes, or tedious unproductive fishing. Why you can automate farms, but not fishing, if you need a lot of fish too?And all that can be fixed with a series of QoL and balancing patches, it's not like the game needs an overhaul.But until those patches arrive, i'd stay away to avoid the bitter taste of disappointment.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, Needs some improvements:It's good, it's worth getting and playing now, but it's even more worth getting in order to support what I think this game could become down the line. This is as terraria was in it's early days and that spells out good thing for this game's future. The Good:- HUGE MAP, I think its limitless technically. - Lots of Bosses to fight.- Nice mix of some of terraria's open ended mining, Valhiems Boss system, Stardew's farming, and Factorios automation. - Cool Skill treesThe Things That Need Improvement:- REALLY needs more armor sets and weapons and needs to likely add some new combat elements. It seems 'Ranged' is really the only way to go if you want to survive. Melee really sucks and unless you go ONE very specific build. Its really uninteresting. Combat needs a lot of attention. - Server Control: We really need more parameters in the configuration of a server. We need server commands. We need to be able to control how long items persist when left out on the ground. It would be wise if we could have the timer not apply if the items were on a conveyor belt.- More NPCs Please! There are really only like...3.5 NPCs, it would be awesome to get more. Even if they were just pets. Terraria's NPCs make it's worlds feel more alive, while this game's world feels a little empty despite being bigger. - More enemies and mini-bosses. Having more types of enemies per biome would be awesome. Adding unique much stronger enemies in each biome as sort of mini bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Game starts out fine, but quickly turns repetitive, and completely loses the plot once you get to endgame. None of the final few bosses past the first Hydra are fun to fight. Defensive stats might as well not exist because everything is just going to oneshot you regardless on hard mode.The bosses are massive damage sponges (on 5 player scaling) even against players wearing the best armor and weapons available to them. Standing there for 5+ minutes holding down M1 while the boss cycles through the same 3 attacks over and over is simply not fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge Terraria fan who sunk in a bit over 2000 total hours in modded Terraria, Core Keeper is SO ADDICTING and rarely gets boring! There is so much to this game! Skills with their own Skill Tree of perks, lots of bosses, and amazing underground biomes, and as of the current version, Pets that you can get! They work like Minions in Terraria from the Summon Class! They follow you and fight for you (except for one)! Not to mention on the topic of Terraria, Core Keeper and Terraria had a AMAZING crossover collab for both games! Core Keeper received King Slime from Terraria as a boss that can be fought at any time but is challenging early on! Also speaking of that, the game lets you take your time! Want to make a farm, level up more of your Skill Trees, and get to the stronger bars in your point of progression before fighting the first bosses? Sure! Want to rush in and go straight to the first bosses? Sure, even though you would need to be very skilled with the bosses if you want to rush to fight them asap. I also forgot to mention, the game has A VAST INFINITE AMOUNT OF COOKED FOOD COMBINATIONS to the point it's crazy! You have a recipe log in the Cooking Pot that shows you all the different recipes you made! Every food item temporally gives beneficial effects such as boosting Melee or Range damage, Movement Speed, Critical Hit Chance and Critical Hit Damage, higher Health Regen, and much more!This game is one HECK of an adventure that is waiting for you to explore it!
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Needs QOL updates.Summoner AI: 1/10, Made summoner nearly unplayable and where is the magic summons?Structure Rarity: 1/10, I understand that it's a big world but with having spent 4-6 hours straight to not find a single structure needed to progress a weapon which seemed almost needed to progress in the game is unacceptable in any game.Boss fights: 10/10, was slow off the start (understandable to get used to the mechanics) I was blown away by the boss designs and how dynamic they were. Even using the same titans they had different mechanics.Scenery: 10/10, this game for it's size was able to display beautiful biomes and diverse mobs.Progression: 8/10, can't give it a 10 with how difficult it was to find certain parts for end game gear, QOL fix would be to make crafting recipes available upon beating the bosses in that zone.Difficulty: 9/10, with having beaten it on the max difficulty I can say it was immersive and made you think on how you would approach certain bosses. Only complaint is the builds felt to reliant on food for buffs.Overall: 7.5/10, I can't give it a rating any higher with the prolonged problems I've seen and having forums complaining about these problems and they are from more then 1 year old. If you want to push it to a 10/10 you need to address these problems. It's understandable that you want to expand the game, but you need to fix the foundation of core keeper when it comes to combat mechanics. Nice game would recommend just be aware of these issues.PS: NERF THE FLINTLOCK, SHOULDN'T BE DOING 20K+ DAMAGE WITH ONE SHOT AS A GREEN ITEM.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly.. I want to love this. I really do. But, I don't.It runs well, it's interesting, the bosses are unique. So what's the problem?It takes AGES to level everything.Want to level running? Make a big tunnel and run back and fore for a few days. Fun?Want to level fishing? Don't bother, the fishing minigame is absolutely dreadful.Each and every fish follows a different wiggle pattern, if you click while it's wiggling, the red bar goes up. How do you know which fish is which? You don't. Good luck.I want to like the game. I even have a plushy from the game, it's adorable.But... I don't like the game.And as I don't like the game.Maybe in future, when the game is finished, it still says early access.Maybe in future, when mods are less finicky to install. (It's not on Nexus. Lame!)Old, outdated review:Yes, Yes, All of the yes!I only recently started and I love this game.It's only major flaw I'd say is the combat is pretty difficult, but it's early access, we'll get stronger bows some day!It's a lot of fun, lot's of building and digging. It's like Stardew, but instead of farmers, there's slimes. And they want to kill you, okay, it's nothing like stardew.I'll make this review better some day, I just wanted to start off by recommending the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played Terraria, but this gives me the same kind of enthusiasm I had when I first played Stardew Valley. As in I put around 12 hours of gameplay in the first day and keep going back for more. I've only gone through the first three bosses at this point, but I'm getting too much of a kick out of setting up drills, conveyor belts and robot arms currently to care. I'm looking forward to exploring more of the game and fighting the remaining/additional bosses(eventually). I'm also enjoying being able to take my character to my friend's server and help them out without remaking a brand new one, similar to Valheim.It's still in EA so things may change, but hopefully they'll just add more fun and fix the bugs. Only thing that annoys me currently is the occasional crash, but the auto saves make is so only like ten or so seconds of gameplay are lost.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: For a pixel game it's very addicting. I would say it is much better than Palworld. You've got all your base building systems, profession skilling, talents, and smooth combat. Some of the bosses are very difficult when your doing them for the first time.The only thing the game needs is more biomes, monster types, and weapon types. Some kind of a class system where you can maybe choose 1-2 spells from a list of like 6 per class would also add more depth into the combat. Probably a good idea for a DLC! I hope the development doesn't stop with version 1.0 and we keep receiving DLCs and content updates with just more stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Many different objects and combinations, a good difficulty and the chance to use one character in different worlds. So you can play the same char in a singel game and in a world with frends. But same bugs as well. It is possible to become max-LVL just out off norwhere. Sumtimes objects will be duplicate or become a 999 stack.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome to the hate child of minecraft and terraria, where luck and grinding are your only way of winning. For the majority of this game you either rely on dodge build or crit build till you somehow find the stuff for their legendary gear. If you want to go melee good luck as most bosses will destroy you if you don't know them well enough. If you love grabbing achievements good luck as most you either have to search up or get lucky goofing off. As well as the tips and guides online are severely outdated, so mods are the answer to your prayers to make the game manageable. The drops for some of the good gear is abysmally low and how you can spend hours or days trying to find stuff, so roll up your sleeves and get ready for self torment.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game, people may say it's a "watered down Terraria" but I strongly disagree, I see huge potential in this game. If you plan to buy this game, it really depends on your preference but if you enjoy survival games with friends I'd definitely suggest this game. Personally I give it an 8/10, It's an overall simple but fun game with a little risk to it because there are lots of things trying to kill you. If you consider it, buy it, you can always refund it later. (If you have less than 2 hours of playtime)
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing the top down view is very different that other games. Its like if Stardew Valley, Terraria and Minecraft came together to make this master piece. Its all of my favorite games in one and i'm a a huge survival game fan. I have been playing it for a year now and I have seen the beautiful things you can build and immerse into the adventure.    Here are the features of the game:     1. Combat: Enemies have health bars, and there is bosses as well and you can attack         both with weapons.    2. Gardening: You can use sprinklers, grow crops, water manually, and hoe your own         garden to plant crops.    3. Multiplayer: You can play with lots of friends for more fun via steam.    4. Somewhat Infinite Map: The forgotten ruins ends, the clay biome ends, the regular earth         biome, ends, But the Azeos Wilderness is infinite so is the ocean and desert biomes.    5. Survival like character being mortal: Needs food, Repair items, And effects on         characters body and health. You have to gain and collect your own items.    6. A great development team and Updates/Road Maps: They update and work on the game        greatly as there will be so many future updates.    7. Top down view: You look at yourself above and play in a really cool different perspective.       You should really check out the game as it has a Early Access title which i think is cool because you get to play and give feedback as the game develops. Anyways in conclusion this game is the best buy I have and you should totally buy it if you have the money and play it with friends for more fun and laughter.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Early game Core Keeper is absolutely a blast, to be honest. I'd go as far to say as it's nearly perfect. Those first few biomes feel wonderful, have plenty of enemy variety, and lots of options for weapons and armor for all the classes. After making the outer wall fall, the wilderness was also, in my opinion, nearly perfect. They filled that biome with plenty of content, equipment, scenes, and enemy variety.This is the issue. Everything past the wilderness feels incomplete, and a bit empty. Visually, all of the biomes look incredible. However, the enemy variety continues to shrink as you continue through the biome, and gear becomes more scarce for summoners and mages. It ends up with you being in the passage, where they are only two enemies, minimal structures, and one boss. Funnily enough, the final boss isn't even in the endgame biome. Why?The game is not worth playing through to the end, as there isn't enough content to satisfy the part of me that enjoys survival games. I'd rather play Necesse or Terraria until the developers add more content, or until significant overhaul mods are developed for the latest version.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: I been having a blast with this game so far. I am taking my time but I have been also playing with some people and we have had nothing but fun. I would say that if you enjoy games like this to give it a try. I am excited to see what they have planned and what will be coming in future updates. I cant wait to play more of this game
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: I heard that it's like Stardew Valley and Terraria, so I bought it because I thought I'd like it since it was meant to be similar to Stardew Valley. I had some reservations since I didn't enjoy Terraria, but I thought I'd try it out anyway. Unfortunately, in the short time I've played, it feels like a purely underground Terraria and I've not enjoyed it. Also, the game drops you in without much to go on. At least Stardew Valley has the basic opening of your grandpa leaving you his farm, and you turning up and being welcomed in, told to introduce yourself to everyone, etc. Whereas this just drops you in it and leaves you to get on with it. So, unfortunately, I don't recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: I think I can recommend this game but currently only during a big sale. The game looks and plays very good, exploration is insanely interesting but the entire charm vanishes completely once you realise (and maybe check on wiki) that there is nothing to find. Aside from boringly standard crafted gear for melee and ranged weapons only, all you get from drops is a tiny amount of gear to be found throughout the entire game, and what there is doesn't even influence your gameplay - it's just stats! That is absolutely horrible and defeats the purpose of progresssion. That is not worth of 1.0 official release.If you plan on beating this game - play a melee build. That has the most items to get. If you're a summoner you're looking at THREE summoning weapons.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game for Early Access. It's similar to Terraria but for a top-down perspective rather than a 2D one. The biggest thing I don't like about it is how insanely rare some items are, and how much players need to grind to max out their skills (especially fishing). It is still in Early Access so the issues the game has will likely be fixed.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really solid survival game, with the top-down one layer perspective keeping exploration streamlined compared to a lot of other ones and keeping the game going at a nice clip. The art is charming, the pacing is deliberate enough that you won't exhaust the content too quickly, and there are bugs that are cows. Do you not want to meet the bugs that are cows? They're pretty cute, and I like them. Good game.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Such a cute little game to play with friends - never played it alone ever since. With each gameslot, the setup is different, and with hard work and a little luck, it's possible to build one's own base camp in a way that leaving the underground doesn't even seem desireable anymore. The only thing I don't really like is that there is no option to make the helmet invisible. One has to decide whether you want a protective helmet or see the nice avatar you made.Edit: Since it is now possible to craft and equip vanity items, which make you look fancy without compromising on the armor rating, I fully recommend this game. It's so cute.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: I had tremendous fun with Core Keeper in Early Access but purposely chose to "stay away" until 1.0 dropped, This is such a fun, addictive little game. Does it reinvent the wheel? Not particularly but the handles the elements it cribs from other titles pretty damn well whilst cultivating enough of a unique identity. Very aesthetically pleasing too. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: So, Core Keeper, is it worth it? You're probably thinking that, if you're looking at reviews before buying the game. Short answer: If you like building bases, exploring, and enjoy progress, then I would say yes. The game offers a nice progress system, and allows for a simple multiplayer system for coop. If you want to know more, you can keep reading.Having a feeling of Stardew Valley and Terraria, You start in a dark cold cave world, filled with mysteries, creatures, and bugs worst of all. You'll have to diggy hole your way around to collect various resources for progressing against a various amount of bosses.Although the game has a fun unique experience, you should know that there are issues that I have to address. As I write this review, the Desert of beginnings update has been out for not too long, so things might change. So firstly, my biggest issue is that although the game has lots of content as it is, none of it is really fleshed out. Let me give you an example:The game has different transport systems such as minecarts, boats, and cars. Despite what you think, they are very basic, as in you can only use them to move around, and don't offer extra inventory space or use to make moving unexplored regions easier.-Minecarts are simple, yet they ask a lot of resources for how little use they offer. It's best to use other modes of transportation.-Boats are currently the most useful for simple navigation, but there's only 2 variants, one of which is quite expensive just to go faster.-Cars are the most recent in the game, and offer more than the 2 others. They have 3 variants. The first one, being the primitive car, can be found in the world, and is overall the weakest. Second one is all about turning good and having a quick top speed. Lastly, the third one is way too fast, which I personally find impractical, since you can't really react in time before crashing into a wall and getting butchered by 9 daggers in the back (you'll know when it happens to you).Despite this, it is just an example of what I think the game has issues with. It's best that you do not base your entire view of the game on it. The game still has a lot to offer in terms of entertainment, with plenty of updates to come. I hope to see you all out there exploring the deep dark caves of Core Keeper.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't a full release yet. Mage and summoner "classes" are barely a single class together, and are honestly just a reach in calling them fully enacted classes. Especially since the summons are paltry wastes of mana that don't target anything. Terraria made summons actually good, let alone making magic viable compared to just ranged. Top end there is no real reason to equip anything but the final drill, as it just kinda does everything and never breaks while doing it. The devs have managed to make their full release feel like this game is just a knock off of everything else in its field, it doesnt have enough appeal or character on it's own to get people in. It's a look alike for terraria meets stardew, that can't be either. Not really close to either. Core Commander needs a craftable or purchaseable scanner. Full stop. Needs more work, needs the dev's to be serious about "adding classes" if they bother to come back to flesh out their work at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game, but it does get repetitive since there aren't any exciting events like in Terraria (such as raids, blood moons, etc.). The loot system also feels a bit limited, with only a small selection of drops and not many unique items. That said, I still enjoy the game, especially the top-down view, which sets it apart from the usual 2D or similar games in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: This is simple, slick, addictive, and fun.  All the things you want in a game.  Great to watch and play. There is enough flavour in this to suggest that something interesting is going on, while you can spend as much time as you want building your little base and home. I'll be keen on seeing how far the content goes just now, and how much gets added.  I would normally comment about things I think need adjustment but so far, and this is a rarity - I can find no bugs with this game. Well, lots of icky bugs on the end of my sword, but there is nothing that doesn't work exactly as advertised, and everything is intuitive and clear. I had a brilliant time with it over the weekend!At the price, it is an absolute steal! Go grab it, and you won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: The farming & gathering from Stardew Valley meets Terraria exploring & fighting. It's a fun & chill combination.Bosses and tactics of how to deal with them are essentials of the game. Waiting for game to be completed.Worth the money and there seems to be a steady flow of content arriving in the future!This game has a very bright future. Already a masterpiece. I could write more but I need to get back to playing!!! Cheers!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this solo: Fun for what's there, your usual get thrown in not knowing what to do and craft everything and climb the tech tree. Fighting is fairly easy and simple and there isn't anything really too difficult to deal with besides breaking down walls. Boss's are pretty easy as long as you fight a little safe and figure their attacks. Was easy to lose 6 hours just mining and gathering and exploring, so the game is at least a good time waster and I had fun.  As of this review I've beaten the current final boss and eagerly awaiting further updates.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun! Definitely worth $25 bucks, I was hooked for 2 weeks straight. Major selling points for me is the exploration and progression is really good. Bosses are kinda meh and there's alot of reusing assets, IE: like 4 of the bosses are just variations of the same slime boss. a few of the fights were decent though. I bought this the same time I bought Age of Mythology and ended up completely ignoring Mythology for this.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: What a delight. The graphics are cute and cohesive, the mechanics make sense, and the story, while a minor part of the game, is compelling.This game is fully playable, which isn't always true for early access games. I haven't encountered a single bug during my time playing, and as of right now the developers are actively adding new content on a regular basis. If you enjoy exploring, upgrading your gear, and the occasional boss battle, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like Terraria but better, honestly. I got so bored with Terraria after early game, when fighting bosses is basically the only thing you can do in the game. This game mixes bossing with other fun things like gathering and crafting. All the content I loved about early game Terraria I found in this game - for a much longer period of time. Plus its super fun to play with friends :P
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

_childDocuments_.review: Explore an endless cavern of creatures, relics and resources in a mining sandbox adventure for 1-8 players. Mine, build, fight, craft and farm to unravel the mystery of the ancient Core.
_childDocuments_.name: Core Keeper

name: Stray Blade
detailed_description: CHECK OUT THE NEW DLC 'VALLEY OF STRAYS' JOIN US ON DISCORD! About the Game Prove yourself in this action-adventure and master intense combat while exploring the ancient ruins of a mysterious civilization. Legends tell of Acrea the Lost Valley, a wild and overgrown place but unmistakably powerful. You found this forgotten land yet died. Time passes, and miraculously you are brought back to life. The price you pay: You are bound to this land. Regain your freedom and embark on the quest of restoring balance in this ravaged and war-torn place guided by your trusty companion, Boji. Explore towering throne rooms of giant god-kings and long-lost cities. As you uncover their secrets, prepare to face even deadlier foes. Get ready to explore a world that is constantly altered by your discoveries and the waging forces! Set off for an unforgettable adventure. Embark on an unforgettable journey and discover the story of Acrea and its ancient legacy. Discover the whole history that turned the peaceful valley into a place of war and death. Use this knowledge to destroy the relics of the past and restore peace in the war-torn valley. Change is part of your journey where every victory leaves a mark in the world. Time keeps moving forward even if you die. Revisit the places of former victory and experience the changes you brought to the world. But beware! Your actions will lead to even greater challenges. The hyper-responsive combat system allows quick reactions and precise attacks to fully control the flow of battle. It merges strategic anticipation of enemy attacks with split-second blade-to-blade reactions — the High Noon of melee weapon combat. Encounter the God-Kings that ruined the land in the past. Bring their legacy to fall and free the land from the shadows of the old era. Harvest their powers and use them to unravel the mysteries of Acrea. New domains are waiting to be unlocked. Both the adventurer and Boji have individual talent trees. The Adventurer is a fighter who gains experience through battle, whereas Boji is a craftsman who increases his experience by finding pieces of ancient lore. Acrea's colorful world ranges from overgrown city ruins to frozen caves and winding canyons. Together with your companion, explore the deepest corners of an ever-changing world bristling with adventure. Every discovery holds treasures. Find rare materials, recipes, weapons, lore pieces, and beautiful places.

_childDocuments_.review: Classic example of a kickstarter being overambitious - The first 1/3 of the game (First major zone) is amazing, so many weapons to play with (20+).The remaining 2/3 of the game contains a grand total of 6 weapons and all the same enemies, but recolored. The boss fights are decent but there's only 4 of them.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game horrible to a point you would want to call it hot garbage? - NoIs it a good game - also no. Had a great potential to be something cool, yet either the budget or talent of the studio was not enough. Starts pretty nice - there's a world to explore and everything looks nice. You check out the combat and it feels ok: you exchange hits and dodge at right moments -> this gives you stamina boost. Yeah, I see where this is heading. Then you discover there are dozens of weapons. Maces hit hard, spears are reaching far, daggers are fast & crit, etc. Oh, and all those floating glowing stones in the sky and locked doors. Hmm... It's pretty clear I will use those to move around, so I need to find and unlock some abilities first. Nice!Exploration feels great, revealing the maps and finding secrets - satisfying. Man, this game feels good. Why all the negative reviews, I wonder? Couple of hours in the game you start to notice stuff. Like why all the enemies feel the same? You got knights, bugs and rats. Several variations of them, yet still. Why different spear weapon acts like if you didn't even change the equipped one? What's up with all the items dropping from enemies? I got tons and tons of them, even after crafting everything I could, yet my inventory is full of junk I never use? Maybe it'll get better as I progress?Couple more hours in the game you unlock multiple new regions and guess what? Copy the above and paste it here. Everything stays the same: enemies, surroundings, loot... The scenery doesn't change a bit. But you also notice even more problems - performance issues, bugs, bugs and bugs again. There are plenty. You can get stuck in textures just jumping around props. You can make enemies teleport around and insta regen health if you kite them out of the spot where designers meant them to spawn and operate, you can kill a mob and spawn their loot in the sky above you. And more. And more. And more.Finally, you open your abilities and that is the last drop of your patience: there's a bunch of glowing-portal-like rocks floating around, connected with beams of light. They serve as "grapple" points so to say. And to get to one - you press R3 (to focus on the spot), hold Lb and press Y to teleport to the stone. Guess what? It's so random that at some point it's just insane. You could be standing 1m away, 5m away, 4m to the left, 13m to the right of the thing and it won't highlight. Do a step in a random direction - "Ok, oh. You may use it now". LIke how was it supposed to be? Feels broken to the core. Summary: this is a game that totally deserves it's current Mixed rating. Full of bugs, poor game mechanics implementation, poor AI, poor variety of species and combat equipment. It has a decent exploring element and a somewhat good level design (if all the game features would work properly). Could be your game, yet for me it's just disappointment and frustration the further I play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game taught me to pay less attention to steam reviews. Yes, the game needs some patching in some aspects, but really only minor things. Also I have seen the reviews say it has a almost nonexistent story, with less that 2 hours of gameplay... _childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I do like this game, combat is satisfying and exploration is always rewarding, but as of right now, its bogged down by technical issues. Performance is bad, seems to take a huge toll on my machine running basic effects, and there are all kinds of bugs and glitches. I think I'm softlocked out of progressing in the skill tree, because skills are passive and unlocked by mastering the various weapons, but you have to craft the weapons first. After I hit the halfway point I straight up stopped getting blueprints, so I can't craft weapons. There were moments were the controls became straight up unresponsive, which is a huge problem for timing based combat. I want to recommend this game, I think its a good idea and I would like to reward smaller yet ambitious titles such as this, but I simply can't when there this many problems.

_childDocuments_.review: This game sneaked upon me from nowhere, and without a friend's recommendation, I'd have never even found out about it. So far, it pretty much feels like a souls-inspired take on Fable/Kingdoms of Amalur, with easy to grasp yet somewhat difficult to master stamina-based combat with parries, dodges and poise break. The world is visually attractive, and there's tons of stuff to discover while hunting for the next boss. Really fun surprise so far!
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I very rarely make reviews but this game i felt deserved some positive ones considering the amount of complaints it had. I think there's a problem with how players treat souls-like games and that is because a lot of them expect those games to be well... Souls games and so they create for themselves those high expectations like every above-average quality souls-like game should be as good as it was made by Fromsoft themselves.While personally I appreciate any and all different approaches to this kind of games that makes them both similar to Dark Souls and also different from Dark Souls and let me tell you Stray Blade does a lot of things right but most importantly it really is fun to play. So now that i know the gameplay is fun lets get into more detail.World/level design - Aside from your classic exploring - which the areas are beautiful and they also can change drastically with your progression through the world and it's interesting and cool to see how the things you do influence the world. Tells you a lot how powerful the original dwellers of the valley were.But aside from that It feels like Stray Blade took a page from DS1 and made the world map a fun convoluted mess of interlocked areas - where you explore an area and move on and further on you discover a shortcut/gate/vine/bridge which leads back to the previous area except where in DS you would meet there the same enemies and environment you did on your first go through the area in Stray Blade the areas change, sometimes you will se Golden Order move in on a turf you yourself cleared, sometimes you will see wild animals nest up in the Order's former camps - you may also find some loot that previously wasn't there. I really enjoy that because unlike Souls' world this one isn't dead or dying and thus it's subject to change and in story it's cool and makes sense that when Farren blazes a trail and clears out an area - some faction follows his in footsteps finds decent ground for camp or stronghold and sets up.Tl;dr - Backtracking can be fun and good if done right which Stray Blade does.Story/lore/characters - It's likely that the story is not the main focus of the game and yet it's not lying forgotten in the dust. I enjoy the fact that Farren despite his general skepticism and loner mentality expresses genuine curiosity about the area and the history - as a proper adventurer should. It's a very natural way for the player to learn the lore and the history of Acrea - Farren being an adventurer and Boji being a local and it's also natural way to break the ice between Farren and Boji. Which i do also enjoy the dynamic between the two, i enjoy how much personality they both display in anything from Farren being revived to them smithing a weapon/armor together. Even though i saw the forging cutscene tens of times at this point it's still fun to watch.I will not talk about lore too much, because naturally better to find out by yourself but i will say that Acrea isn't huge, decorated with weird visuals, metals and ornaments purely for the aesthetic. A lot of what you see while exploring has to do with the original residents and the elements and metals that they used, the more you learn the more things start to make sense.Combat - I heard all the complaints about Stray Blade's combat and apparently soon it's getting a bit of a rework so i don't know how relevant my opinion here is going to be but here it is anyway.First off I am a Gothic 1 and 2 veteran so your combat would have to be really really bad for me to have problems with it. As it happens personally i really do enjoy Stray Blade's combat, i like the amount of weapons i can get, i like that mastering each can boost my character - i think it has something to do with the fact that Farren is a melee weapon nut as much as i am - i also like that i'm better with some weapons and i suck with some other ones. I do actually find it a little weird that some red attacks that don't look to heavy(animation-wise) can't be parried, i think most enemy attacks should be able to be parried, maybe some elite enemies and bosses should have red attacks and that's that.I would also enjoy more killmove animations with different weapons as some of the different weapons share the killmoves - but that's a minor thing that's purely aesthetic, doesn't lessen the combat fun.Which as a final note on combat/killing end of the game - the killmoves are cool, extremely fun and make winning that much more satisfying.To sum it up i believe Stray Blade is a great game as a whole, one of my favourite souls-likes in fact and i'm gonna support and shill it every chance i get and with upcoming updates and fixes it will potentially become even better as even i have to admit that few things like camera work could use improvement.My two biggest complaints would be clunky feeling cameraAnd lack of photo-mode.I highly recommend this game if you're looking for fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Blade is a souls-like with heavy focus on the story/characters and weapon variety. It has unusual system of progression where you unlock passive upgrades for your character by mastering various weapon types, this technically forces you to use every weapon you find which is a double-edged sword as one one hand you have a decent variety in armament, while on the other you're often forced to use a weapon you might not like just to unlock a damage or health upgrade for your character. Entire combat system is heavily melee focused as there are no ranged weapons and you only have few magic abilities that are story-related. Average playthrough should take around 20-25h. I've waited till latest patch to write this review and unfortunately I can't recommend the game in its current state. It does run better than it did on launch but that's only because the game was shipped in a very bugged state. For a souls-like game, a genre where timing and precise inputs are crucial the gameplay feels very clunky and unresponsive. It doesn't help that you often have to face multiple enemies at once with some of them attacking you from range, a design decision that makes the game even more frustrating given the lack of precise input. The game's performance is also quite odd, even when not much is going on the screen the game fully utilizes my R7 5800X, which is a sign of poor optimization.Hopefully the developers can solve at least some of these issues, they are quite active on Discord and open to feedback so there's hope for improvements in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable hidden gem!To get the bad out of the way, performance should be better relative to my hardware.No big deal, but I have to lower more settings than I should.Visually I find it very appealing, reminds me of good old Amalur.It´s not open world, but the hubs are big enough to make for rewarding exploration.Combat is challenging but fair. Fortunately other game mechanics, e.g. the progression, are not "souls-like".There is no harsh penalty for death, just retry and keep leveling up as you do.I like it when games respect my time. ;)Lots of different weapons to unlock, and the game makes you use each of them at least for a short while.Cut short, Stray Blade is a nice Action-RPG with a bit of Souls-DNA.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: A solid open world game, maybe a bit rough around the edges, but neat ideas like clearing out a location of enemies lets the world evolve and other enemies take over, sometimes building new things for traversal.Ran into a small bug that was annoying me a bit, so headed over to the game's Discord and asked about it, got help directly from the devs and solved it quickly. That alone is worth a recommendation, in my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game.  It's dripping with ambiance, and there is a huge amount of potential, but alas it goes mostly unused. The two biggest gripes I have about the game:- the 3 factions, there's little to no backstory about them -- what are they doing in Acrea?   What is their origin? fleshing these little details out a bit helps immensely. (granted there's books / notes which hint at these things, but it's not enough)- for a game that hinges so much on exploration and finding secrets, the way the map and compass currently work makes it far harder than than needed.  What do i mean?1. face a direction2. open your map3. You'll now notice you are not facing the direction you were facing in step 1.  I'm going to be shelving the game until this bug is fixed.. c'mon guys, bugs like that should never have made it out of QA.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Verdict: On one hand the game is fun, on the other finding new collectibles and fighting the same enemies for 20 hours is beyond dull. Get it on sale if you are into action RPGs, stay away if you want something souls-like +Steam trading cards (7 drop, 13 to make a badge)Steam achievements (52, 46 base game and 6 DLC, a lot of collecting things)Visually beautifulThe landscape is gorgeous at times Solid execution animations A lot of work was put into the story and how you learn about the world There was a lot of care put into the worldArmour sets and weapons are beautifulWeapons feel different when it comes to their light, heavy and special attacksCombat is not half-bad itself and you feel the weight of your weaponsColour palettes for your armour are quite nice Voice acting and soundtrack are enjoyable to listen toThe few bosses the game are well put together -Levelling is a lie - level up means 1 skill point and 1 new weapon blueprint drop from the first human enemy you encounter 90% of my deaths were due to falling into the abyss Serious lack of enemy varietyI got stuck in loading several times after dyingThe story is pretty much the most basic fantasy I have ever seenThe pacing is off - with exploration it took me 5 hours to meet the first boss and 2nd one was 5 minutes after himI have no idea what is going on with the sounds as it sometimes plays combat queues including parry soundThe game uses 'increase X' without telling you what that means, hence making informative decisions impossible Armours have armour/dodge stats, but once again without explanationsStory bits = stop and listen,  you can either skip everything or wait for 5 minutes on a spot
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I tried this game when it first came out and thought it was aesthetically pleasing, but there were some performance issues, and the combat at the time was not the greatest. I'm so glad they went back, revisited it, and altered the core gameplay to what it was to what it is now. I think what they had was a cool concept. Parry blue attacks. Dodge red attacks, but combat in between that was not as rewarding. Now it plays very fluidly, they have indicators where poise breaks are going to be on enemy attacks, and each weapon feels really cool. The finishers are absolutely amazing. The voice acting in the game is great. My only gripe is that the lack of pauses between commas and periods causes the character interactions to not seem very lifelike. Either it is the voice actors are not given a full script, reading and acting sentence by sentence, or that between each sentence a new "cutscene" is produced that may load too quickly. Which that honestly isn't a big issue. The story is cool so far, and it's a really cool take on an RPG with light souls-like elements. If you are a Souls fan and are looking for a game, just note this is very light in that category. There isn't much of a loss when you die, the real souls-like elements are just the combat, memorizing enemy attack patterns, dodge, parry, and stamina consumption. They do a lot to make the game their own. It amazes me how little attention this game has gotten. I'm really glad I gave it another go. I understand how it may have been hard for the devs to want to alter a core gameplay mechanic, and I just want to thank you all for putting the time and effort into reading and listening to both the community, and providing a top-notch game that I hope get's more traction soon. It's much deserved.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. There is a deep love at the core of this game. I felt that.I play a lot of games. I tend to enjoy an open-world experience with a little bit of platforming, as long as it includes stuff u get from the game as mechanics. That is not all, but the rest is not relevant to this review. This game, from its entry to you, does not pretend to tell you anything you haven’t heard already and cuts right to the chase of the character’s heart. Goals are established and you understand what it is you are to do. There are no side-quests or countless lost minutes searching for what it is you set out to do via a “journal page”. You’re very aware of what to do, and if not, there is helpful tiny staff guiding with magic fingers to guide your clueless ass to which area you are supposed to look in. It’s not embarrassing as that same character will play on the world around you.That said, this game is horrible on my ADD, undiagnosed, at this point because I will find myself filled with child-like amazement at what is next or actually noticing a crevice that leads to another area the map doesn’t show. The map is seductively chaste in its disclosure of info. You are not burdened by weight mechanics, or fractions of % increase in stats when you find items. The mechanics, at core, are present and work well. The game has not crashed on me yet. I highly recommend this game to those missing the heat or excitement from the early days of Fable 1, or those that have been sold this same journey, lone chatacter vs the world, with less effect, on other indie titles.In the end you have to at some point give credit to 505 games for putting weight behind this title that might not have got the polish that is delivered to you on day 1. Are there bugs? Yes. Does it really impact your play when you lose nothing when you die? No. Can you play it on your potato? I currently can’t upgrade to windows 11 due to my hardware, so yes, if you have a recent gfx card and all else, it runs as smooth as butter. Is this a souls-game? I am no expert, and am quite dumb at moving my character around, but this has no resemblance to that genre other than a dodge mechanic? This has more similarity to Kingdoms of Alamur:Reckoning than that. A lot of fresh talent looking at these games these days without the memory of anything other than a blockbuster reviewing these hidden gems, I think, results in the “mixed” review status.If you have fresh eyes on this game, try it. It’s not as hard as you may hear and it may run on an older system hoping for a new adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Won't give you a grand slap across the face, it's an unpolished game with little ambition. It just wants to give you a lot of stuff to explore (about 30 hours to 100% the map) and a nice, sometimes touching banter between characters along the way.It was clearly made with a lot of love, only the very end of it feels like something to be done with.Regarding the soulslite debate, allow me to explain: you can adjust difficulty in real time, putting it anywhere between "baby's first Zelda" - I mean don't give it to babies, it's pretty brutal - and "damage sponges kill you in one hit".This title has nothing to do with the design of a Souls game, but it does provide decent challenge if you put the mob's health and damage sliders somewhere around 1.5, and leave the poise sliders at Standard values.That way you actually can get killed and have an incentive to get parries in and practice your combos, but you will have enough wiggle room to power through the - many - animation glitches and won't end up stuck on even end game fights for more than a few minutes. Most mobs are just too inconsequential to take more of your time than this imo.All in all, it's a sweet little game if you've already combed through Horizons/Zeldas, Elden Ring and the like.Final point because I couldn't find anyone talking about it: the flying orbs across the map are teleport beacons that you eventually activate with an ability called Intium Flash. When you see two orbs linked by a blue beam, the farther one is generally impossible to lock on. You'll have to flash to the first one, then to the second in mid-air. Nothing will happen if you try to just stand under the closer one and press keys.Either I'm dumb or the game doesn't explain that clearly, so I lost a bit of time assuming these things were for an upgraded version of the skill. Until I just hit the thing like an angry ape, because that's the right thing to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: So very close to being a good game. The combat is addictive, especially with the vast range of weapons at your disposal each with their own movesets, and the voice acting is surprisingly good, but... there are so many little quirks/bugs and general lack of polish which get in the way of it being anything other than a frustratingly unenjoyable experience. Performance also leaves a lot to be desired, with regular framedrops and a disappointingly low overall framerate to boot.In the end, the issues are the kinds of things which could be patched out, but given that the game has already been out for 9 months and is still in this state, I can't imagine it's going to happen. Hopefully Point Blank can take what they learn from this and put it towards their next game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so glad I ignored the negative reviews on this one. I'm loving this game. I think that gives players certain expectations that this game does not fulfill or provide. I am NOT a souls player, and I love this game. But I'm sure if someone comes in thinking it'll actually be souls-like, they will likely be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Stay away from this game. This game plays like a test build and runs like one too. On low settings it will dip to 30 fps very frequently whereas I can run elden ring at 60+ fps on epic settings. You can backstab enemies and then throw them into walls and sometimes they will just bug out and get stuck in the wall. Some enemies will just straight up spawn in the ground and despite what it might look like, your weapon can't hit them. This entire game is running around a map collecting materials and fighting the same enemies until you reach a very VERY mediocre boss. The world itself looks nice but is boring to explore because eventually you reach a point where all you find is bonedust which has no use if you have nothing to craft. I find it odd how almost every recipe required claws for some ungodly reason and I never had enough for more than 1 or 2 items. To that I just say why are you only not giving me 1 material when I have an ungodly amount of everything else? You also eventually gain nothing from leveling up because if you don't have the weapon recipes you can't get any more traits. Leveling becomes useless after that point because nothing is improving. I really gave this game all the time in the world to shine but it's so exceedingly good at being boring and repetitive. I say stay away because it just sucks the life out of you, for me the only redeeming quality is that it works sometimes. If you absolutely love soulslikes like I do then sure play this game when it's on sale for $10 because a game in this state is not worth more than that.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Blade is an adventure game with souls-like elements. But that description doesnt describe the way the game is. I will go into a few of the main aspects of the game and give the good and the ugly about it. Combat:-The game has a parry, a dodge and with certain weapons a block. Perfect parries stagger an enemy for a second, deal poise damage and give back stamina. Parrying at just the wrong time blocks the damage, but doesnt stagger the enemy and leaves you open to a second attack. Just like parrying, perfect dodging recovers you some stamina but doesnt stagger enemies. And blocking is well... blocking. -The combat can feel clunky at times due to its unforgiving damage and stagger when you dont perfect dodge or parry and the stamina economy also requires you to do perfect parries and dodges. Some weapons have slow attack combos and dont have enough hyper armor, nor can you increase your poise like in a Fromsoft game. It takes some getting used to but eventually the flow of combat will become more of a dance then a battle. If you can find the patience for it that is.-The abilities you unlock troughout the game (Intium, Manninite and Xhinnon) have their own uses in combat, Intium is fun, Manninite seems fun but doesnt do enough to make it worth it and Xhinnon turns on easy-mode.Story:-The story is pretty good if you read all the extra lorestones you can find around the game and talk to Boji whenever you can. Without the lorestones and Boji the story does become confusing, and the ending becomes very confusing and a bit weird.-The valley of Acrea is very rich in its culture and history, and you can find out quite a bit about how the society was before their fall. Many areas have interesting tid bits of lore regarding them. The valley also looks very pretty.Exploration:-The exploration is this game is quite fun and reminds me of metroidvanias. You go trough an area, see some stuff you dont have the ability to get and come back later to find some nice customizations or other secrets. -The world as noted before looks great and each new area is great to look at and run around in. Performance:-I ran the game on high settings on a 3070, Intel I-7 10700k with 16GB ram. I only noticed minor performance issues in certain areas. (Have to go back and check the areas again to give acurate and recent statistics on this since my info on this is outdated)Final Thoughts:Stray Blade is a good game that I am going to be replaying a handful of times with some fun challenges for myself. There are aspects that could be better or design choices that couldve been made differently but looking at the game as a whole its 100% been a blast and I cant wait to see what the future brings to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: After doing 100% of this game. Its an alright game for what it is. Not sure why some people would call this a Souls-like, it isnt. Its more similar to action adventure games like Immortals Fenyx Rising. It had some metroidvania-type elements which I enjoyed though. As of patch 1.7, there are still a lot of bugs and janky movement, in combat both me and enemies get stuck alot, on various terrain or on each other. I didnt like some other lack of reponsiveness in combat, also the running animation looked really wierd with some weapons. The story is really generic and while it had some hints of potential, it didnt really do anything with it imo. The best thing about this game for me was the art direction, and the last bossfight was really the best in the game, so a nice fight to end it all on. As I said, its ok for what it is. Worth it on sale.
