_childDocuments_.review: first 10 hours: funsecond 10 hours: fun but.... where is my progression goneeverything past that: please let it be over!Its kind of fun watching the devs first run out of ideas (for more than the weapons) then out of money (for custscenes instead of concept art)  and last out of time (to fix bugs). Though I shouldn't complain about bugs too much: At least the final boss dropped through the floor with 1/3 HP left and died instantly giving the credits.The saddest part is that it could have been sooooo good if only they tweaked a lot of nuisances. It has so much going for it: Acceptable storyline (which isn't just a rehash). Interesting maps with a good amount of secrets collectibles and places to revisit. But its just too rough to recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: My first ever review! I will try to be short and to the point:Most will read "souls-like" and expect resting at shrines to refill potions and/or respawn enemies. While resting does respawn some enemies, it does not refill your health consume item. These are gathered through harvest. The enemies are very simple. The combat is very simple. The art is very simple. The game is very simple. It's the simplicity that actually makes the game tough. You need to know when to parry and when to dodge. Most of these are through wind ups that are kind of hard to get without getting hit one or two times before learning the timing. This game is very pleasing to the eye. It feels more like an RPG than anything. You gather blueprints and materials to craft said items. This is a game where I can turn on and relax through the vibrant colors and take my time enjoying the scenery. It can feel a little "cluncky", but this isn't a big budget game. If you miss your parry or dodge, you will be stuck in a frame you can't get out of and probably get hit. The enemies also take no impact. Hitting the enemies feel like hitting an impenetrable wall, but its easily able to be adjusted to. The finishers are so pleasing and feel so rewarding. I've yet to reach a "first boss", but I've come across some of the difficult enemies and they were a blast fighting. The game isn't for everyone, but if you enjoy an enriched environment with a very relaxing setting, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: This week, I had the opportunity to dive into the game of Stray Blade. While the game certainly has its moments of brilliance, it falls short in certain aspects, preventing it from reaching its full potential.One aspect that stood out in Stray Blade is its visually striking art style where I realized the detailed effort that the developer has put into it. The forest and the dungeons were all of high quality but sometimes it was put down with technical issues such as frame rate drops and minor graphical glitches, which was a disruption to otherwise a seamless experience.In terms of gameplay, Stray Blade offers a mix of exploration, combat, and puzzle-solving throughout the game. The maps that I explored had plenty of beautiful scenery and spots which were fantastic. The combat mechanics, at the beginning seemed to have less of an excitement but this grew as I have played more and found tons of skills that changed the move of the hack and slash. There was an absence of a skill progression system but the combat visuals was what really got me sunk into playing the game.Ultimately, I felt that those craving a truly immersive hack and slash type of game would love this game to the fullest but should be warned that the current patch there may be little bit more to.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Blade is a stylyzed souls-like where you play as a softspoken woman, Farray, and her newfound accented companion Boji as she brutally finishes off enemy after enemy in an attempt to leave the world of Acrea.Pros:- Combat is fun: Why I recommend the game, the combat itself I found to be pretty fun, rode the fine line for me between being challenging enough that I can't mindlessly go through but not so hard that a single npc felt like a bossfight. The finishers are a cool mechanic. - Good graphics and performance: game has a cool style and ran pretty well. Had some bugs and some exploration is cheesable but didn't have anything game breaking during my playthrough. (And I like cheese)- World evolution: the world changes slightly in some places as the story progresses and that was kinda cool to see.Ehs:- The story is what it is. Its ok, I ended up skipping some of the scenes if i thought they were too boring. Its quite predictable.- Character and skill progression was ok thought eh pacing of it was not great (see below). Skills are tied to weapon collecting and crafting which is quite cool in itself and the individual skill and attributes to make a difference but they felt a bit like a odd chore to get, especially the last special weapons which require a lot of backtracking.- Shrines and the Flux mushrooms separating save points and fast travel is not something I found compelling unlike in most other souls-like games where the "bonfire" point does both, but it didn't bother me that much overall.- Unskippable death cut-scene. Fun the first couple of times then they become a waste of time.- Odd behavior sometimes with the lock on. It works mostly as intended and sometimes you try to lock on to an enemy right in front of you but it selects the furthest enemyCons:- Low enemy variety. "I was supposed to go much ...further....." - yeah I've heard this before....- Progression pacing weird and not in a great way, its tied to what weapons you get and the game gives you basically all weapons expect for a couple few before the 75% mark. This made the only thing left the guided exploration and the new repeated npc fights which got a bit mindless and made exploration disappointing as I mostly got rewarded with crafting material and armor (which doesn't contribute to skills and attributes, only weapons do).Conclusion:After completing the story on Adventure Mode and 100% character progression (all weapons and skills) I'm going to recommend this game. Though probably at a discount. I had a decently fun 20 hours and that was with exploring enough to get all the weapons and skills so this game doesn't overstay its welcome too much (I did feel like it dragged on a bit at the end).
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game, but boy does its combat feel stiff and limiting. Hitting enemies often feels like it has no weight to it, so you end up just falling back on learning each enemy's 3 moves and parry&countering them, over and over, because going aggressive overcommits and punishes you due to your hits having little to no crowd control. That's... not terribly interesting. The execution animals are nice, at least.Also, the performance is surprisingly bad for the technically simplistic visuals going on (the art style itself is nice). And I wasn't fond of having to wait almost 30 seconds between getting killed and regaining control of my character as the game lingered on showing my corpse for a while, then after the load screen had me sloooooowly pick myself up, and take a step, and look around, and finally I can play again.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: The Mixed Reviews accurately describe the state of the game.While the bones of the game are quite good, there are some polish issues and tweaks that need to happen before its great. What you see in the trailers and such is how the game looks and feels, most of the time. The combat is fantastic with a slight learning curve, but needs to be smoother and more weighty. The levels and map design are great but need tweaks to be great. Overall, this game feels like an early access that's a couple patches away from being done. I hope they come soon and people keep supporting this game because I am a fan of this art style and world.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Not one to make reviews but this felt like it deserved one. Story is a little short considering I beat it within 17 hours, collected and mastered all weapons and hit level cap of 50 pretty quickly but all and all game was surprisingly good considering the mixed reviews. Combat definitely takes getting used to but if you can get a hang of it its very satisfying to parry the bosses over and over. Didn't quite 100% completion it but this is something i'll definitely end up completing fully.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to try this game, but unfortunately, the targeting system is terrible and the lack of mouse movement when locked on target is disastrous. Swapping between multiple targets is very inconvenient. I will try a couple more times whether I will get a taste of it otherwise not well spent $40 I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: The good:- Various environment, tons of stuff to explore.- No punishment for dying so even if the map is super hard to navigate through, you still won't need to recover your resources.The bad:- The devs waste your time abundantly with ridiculously SLOOOOOW chat and an extremely dumb revive unskipable animation you have to watch every single time you die.- There is some bugs that kills your game progress: -- In the DLC after you kill the final boss there is a chance you don't get to see the ending because the game gets bug and forgets about it. -- If you progress a bit, there is a good chance your game will get stuck in loading after you die, thus you lose all your progress as your progress isn't saved if you die, only if you rest at shrine or get a random save trigger point.- TONS OF INVISIBLE WALLS, and jumping is bugged asf, meaning you are likely to get stuck tons of times in walls and objects of the map.Did I had fun?First hours yeah, middle of the game gets boring, ending is so damn insufferable because you have to walk a zillion miles form point to point with nothing interesting in between.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Blade for is like an open world crossing of Kingdoms of Amalur with a combat and shortcuts in the line of Dark Souls games.Story is nice, characters are interesting and voice over in english are pretty good (played female). Not a lot of bosses but they're interesting too.Character progression has a very interesting twist that favors using diferent weapons which leads to diverse gameplay styles during the same playthough.Overall I really loved Stray Blade and it's the first game I bought the DLC because I wanted more of it :)Please note: I played the game in 2024 and on a recent ROG laptop with a 14 core CPU and RTX 4070 GPU. I don't know if the many complaints about performance were solved after release, or if the game just requires a more capable computer to run well on, what I can say is it ran flawlessly for me on 1080p with Ultra settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: From what I've played so far this game absolutely slaps, and it is a shame it seems to have been given an underwhelming reception. It's a hidden gem and it deserves attention equal to the amount of work this game has in level design, bosses, voice acting, and most importantly combat! The term soulslike has been used so liberally that people are probably tired of seeing the term, but it feels like Dark Souls 1 with some charm from Fable and Kingdoms of Amalur thrown in. Two bosses down and 4 hours in, it's already been worth it, highly recommended!Edit after beating the game: I loved it. A labour of love has been made through the entirety of the game. Beautiful levels, clever boss designs and a satisfying end of the game. Again, worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: It's just another souls-like / action RPG, this time in a more colourful zelda-like world. You'll find the difficulty spikes and precise timing to hit/block that fans of the genre love. There is not really so much more.It's an indie game that tried to sit at adult's table. But it's not time yet: over demanding mediocre graphics, gameplay that gets boring after a while, only 4 bosses, "on rail" tracks, repeating enemies, far from perfect hit boxes and lagging parrying times. And the asking price of 35$ is absolutly unjustified.I won't waste my time on this one, but I won't judge you if you will.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I gave it a good go before making sure I wanted to leave thumbs down because the setting of high fantasy world (instead of dark) in a souls-like title was an interesting idea in my eyes. Sadly the game itself is just mediocre (at its best). It is not a very bad game but nothing stands out and with so many better games out there playing this one just feels like a waste of time. Looking back I do not see a single reason why should I finish it.Pros:- Fighting system is the best this game has to offer. It is not great with stupid enemies that can be easily tricked and defeated and just few move sets for each weapon type. However I like what this game has done with skill sets. So in order to level up and get new skills you need to master each weapon. With many weapons the game has to offer, the fighting does not get stale. You have few favourite weapons but you are keep changing them in order to get more skills unlocked. I think this was the main reason why I did not leave this game after 1 hour of playtime. - Skill system like explained above- Fully voiced protagonist in male and female versions. However the protagonist itself, dialogues and the story are all bad so I am not even sure if that is a real "pro" - deserves a mention tho because usually you just get a silent hero in souls likes In the middle:- The world looks beautiful. Nice high fantasy setting. However it also feels flat with poor level design and nothing really stands out that much. There are picturesque landscapes that are easy on the eye but still when you start exploring them you have that feeling that you just explore more of the same. World is just uninteresting and bland.The bad:- Protagonist is terrible. TALKS a lot to her/him-self. It just feels forced. There is another NPC in the game you meet your sidekick. After you meet him the dialogue becomes unbearable. They talk to each other so much and the dialogue does not feel natural. After a while I just started to skip everything. Most of the time dialogue is about lore, those two characters relationship and about the story (which is quite bad)- The story is bad and silly. I could not care less about it- Enemies variety. It feels like this game had just few type of enemies. Human enemies reskinned in many ways, plant traps and moster enemies (big monster, spider and fast monster). It gets stale really fast. It is like someone had 0 imagination- Game is terribly optimised. The graphic isnt even that good. I would say it even looks dated but it runs just terrible on steam deck. And it should be locked at 60fps on high settings. Instead when everything is maxed you get 10-15fps, on minimum it still isnt good most of the times 30fps but there are a lot of areas when the counter goes below 15fps like next to a fire etc. There are games out there that have much superior graphics and run at 60fps on steam deck at all times at high settings. Looking at you dishonoured 2 and Prey.I rate this game 4/10 - waste of time. Maybe 5/10 if feeling generous.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy this game so far. I am not the biggest fan of souls and such, but the simple yet challenging nature of this combat system speaks to me. It is very much based on read and react. But where in a lot of games you react to blinking visuals, here you react to actual movement and position of your enemies. Presentation of the game is organic and has its own style. Fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun combat open world ish metroidvian/soulslike game. Kinda reminded me of Kingdoms of Amalur Reckoning in art and combat a bit. Lots of weapons for different play styles and once you get the dodge/parry mechanic down the combat is very rewarding and fun. Some bugs here and there but overall a fun game. Played on Challenge difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: A light mix of a souls like, metroidvania and an action RPG.The game is pretty straight forward and at least in my case there wasn't ever a situation where I didn't know where to go and there is a map and a compass that shows the general direction where you are supposed to go. Along the way you pick up three new abilities/skills that let you keep progressing and allow you to go back and collect some collectables that weren't available before without the abilities. The soulslike elements are rather light and there are no souls or equivalent to collect and you just get XP by killing enemies and you don't lose anything when dying.There is a nice variety in all the weapons. However, some are rather useless either because they have very little range and do no more damage than the weapons with longer range, and in actuality tend to do less damage, or they have a rather long charge up time even in basic "light" attacks. The upgrade system is largely connected to "mastering" each weapon, which means you kill a certain number of enemies with said weapon and you gain mastery and then you can upgrade an attribute or skill tied to said weapon like health or the ability to carry more healing items. On the technical side everything seems to run fine. No crashes or other major issues and the only problem I ran into was a case of the game not saving during my first 15-30 minutes of playing the game, but that was a singular occurrence.On the whole I had fun with the game and I'd recommend it as long as you know what you are getting into and if you are expecting a soulslike game you are most likely going to be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: A genuinely enjoyable game. The story is well-done, the environment beautiful, and controls smooth. My favorite part is how the various zones will change as the story progresses. For example: if you go through an enemy camp and wipe out the enemies, then hit the next story checkpoint, when you return to that camp, structures in it will be wrecked, there will be bodies around, and it'll be populated by either wildlife or a different brand of enemy. Likewise, when you go through 'untamed wilderness', the next time you return it could be built up into an enemy camp and that camp can keep growing as you progress. It makes exploring and re-exploring the map just so fascinating to return to places and see what has changed since you were last there.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Was a fun game with great combat system. i really enjoyed the way skill point were used in mastering each weapon. my only disappointment was how short the game felt. i really don't understand why developers put a "point of no return" in these games. you do all of this work to make the world right and to never see how it all turns out. i would have liked to at least finish collecting everything without the insane storm after killing third boss.

If you hit "new game" by accident, it instantly starts one and saves in the only existing autosave slot. This just happened to me.7 1/2 hours of progress gone thanks to a single pressed button.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Despite its enchanting setting and captivating storyline, Stray Blade does have a few technical issues that need to be addressed. While the game's art and level design are both impressive and beautiful, there are a few bugs and glitches that detract from the overall experience. The main issues revolve around the camera. The camera lock on seems to flick randomly between enemies you're currently attacking and others that are patrolling in the distance currently unaware of your presence. You can turn this option off in the settings, but even then frequent and random camera resets take you out of the action and make combat difficult; especially when fighting multiple enemies.It basically becomes more luck than timed parries and dodges.The game's dodge, parry, and roll mechanics are a bit sluggish and imprecise, which can make combat feel clunky, floaty and unsatisfying at times. Overall it just doesn't feel as responsive and polished as say a genuine soul's game.There are some nice execution cinematics but there are also some pretty rubbish ones it can get a little repetitive as can the final narrative of the enemies. A seemingly Greta Thunberg inspired "how dare you!"  seems to play over and over again as you dispatch humanoid enemies. Despite these issues, Stray Blade still manages to offer a very immersive gaming experience in the soulslike vein. Stray Blade has plenty of loot but not in the traditional sense of these types of games. As enemies are killed they will drop varying levels of materials needed for the games very comprehensive crafting system. The different variety of weaponry on offer give you plenty of opportunities to customize your character and create a truly unique gameplay experience. With three Acrean metals to master, you'll have plenty of challenges to keep you engaged and entertained.Overall, Stray Blade has the potential to be a truly amazing ARPG. With its colorful fantasy setting, engaging storyline, and innovative crafting system, it's an easy recommend . While the game may still have a few teething issues that need to be addressed, there's no denying that it's a thrilling and engaging gaming experience that's sure to keep you coming back for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: The game is extremely mediocre in every thing it does. That the best i can describe it in one sentence. It has many potencial to be higher but it mostly subpar. But if I had to rate it, it still a 7/10 which is a passing grade in my book which is why it a thumbs up. Note that I played this game on the "Farren must die" difficulty so I know this game pretty well since I must midmax and figure out how to beat the game that trying to kill me. Many problems become clear especially when you play on higher difficulty but here a list of pro and con.Pro:- The art style is really good! I love the vibrant color and landscape design. - The land can sometime be gorgeous at times- There are many cool weapons and cool combos and ult to mix and match- The game feel fantastic and solid when you unlock "powers" later. It really smooth things out for combat- Customization is cool, especially how I can paint my armor and look- Variety of armory with cool design- Pretty alright combat with decent impact.- Game got solid excellent execution animation- The metroidvania part of the game pretty fun and make you want to explore old zone- Story is ambitious and i can see a lot of work was put into the lore and world- Map changes as the story progress which is an amazing and innovative ideaCon:- Art direction is a bit contradictory at time. At time the game quite colorful and wimsicle like Fortnite, but there are scene in the game that are really dark lie bloody bodies scatter everywhere, lacerated, hang on treee, impaled dead corpse, lots of blood. It feel so mix tone especially with the art direction and writing.- Boji not as interesting as I thought and I hate having to pause the game and talk to him whenever he got something to say, I wish he just said it as I'm moving through the map- Story is a mediocre and really predicatble. There wasn't much interest in the lore or incentive to learn more from the monster and wild life since they pretty basic "wild beast" that are pretty large monster. Only the human faction lore seem flesh out.- The Combat can be very annoying with badly time window of attack, delay attack and VERY small parry window that can realyl extend farther. Sometime i feel like parry is not worth it since it stun the enemy for half a sec and I hardly got time to counter hit before they begin the NEXT attack. it probably safer to dodge and hit instead which is dissapointing for parry freaks like me.- Enemy are extremely inbalance, atleast on hardest difficulty since ESPECIALLY the range enemy can 1 shot you the majority of the game. The archer also CANNOT be parry and often shoot you point blank. Since you can't stagger them fast enough, if you swing at the wrong time, you shoot you point blank and you're dead in one hit. - Boji and Farren banter is a good attempt but I can see people get annoyed between their.... mediocre banter- The story drama between boji and farren isn't that great, often time it feel like forced drama. - The map and idea of metroidvania is cool since you want to return to old area HOWEVER, as the map "changes" as you progress in the story, sometime it changes so drastically that I get lost in where I was, and i'm someone who GOOD at navigation in other video games. It didnt feel balance on how much is change after certain story beat.- There no better way to "upgrade" a weapon you like and it often get powercreep by some other weapon, like a halberd since it can stun while other "ult" leave you in such a vulnerable state.- The land design despite being beautiful can sometime be mediocre. generic grass ruin land, generic snow land, generic desert. It the second HALF of the game where the land get a little better. - Many weapon not well balance since it is unusable in harder difficulty since you are stuck in an animation for too long leading to death.

_childDocuments_.review: Not for me.As someone who doesn't have time for multiplayer games, the recent resurgence of SP has been a blessing. This game has been on my wishlist for a while and I was aching for another gem like Kingdom Come: Deliverance or Greedfall.Since reviews have never been a metric I can rely on, I decided to give this game a try. However, there was nothing keeping me in or pulling me back to the game - no hidden area unexplored, no tough boss that I am *this* close to defeating nor a storyline that gripped me so hard I need to follow it. I tried again after a few days, to see if it was simply a mood. Unfortunately, no.

_childDocuments_.review: People got spoiled by Elden Ring and now think everything needs to be compared to it. This is a good game on its own, brings new ideas to the table and is just good fun.Highlights: - Skill progression system tied to mastering weapons, so you get encouraged to try all of them out and find your own playstyle. - Gorgeous artstyle (subjective) + nicely structured world allowing you to open up shortcuts to past areas everywhere, making you feel like everywhere you go and everything you collect is progress.- Quite in depth difficulty settings.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't been playing long but I can say just from the beginning I am loving this game. The animations are nice. The combat integrates blocking and dodging in such a way that it increases your ability to attack. Also a big bonus is the climbing up or down animation is not just automatic but is done in such a way that you can easily believe this life long adventurer has in fact adventured for a long time. Loving it so far.Update: I play a lot of souls like games. Love them frankly. That being said they have this thing where no matter what you do you never feel more powerful that the enemies you fight. Not so in this game. I have been playing for just a couple hours at this point and the skills I got to boost myself have already made a big difference in a big way. Im just loving this game man. That being said please fix the controls customization. I changed my dodge and parry keys and they keep resetting themselves. Very annoying.Regarding the loot system. I love the fact that loot is basically mostly crafting materials. Most games do the color thing for loot and it doesn't always land well. In this game though I don't feel like IM picking up a high rarity item only to trash it the moment a new one shows up.

_childDocuments_.review: 6h in, never played before 1.7, the combat feels great, I really like the characters, Boji and Farren have a good chemistry and really really good voice acting, the environments are good with good variety for now, and it is way better than reviews would have you believe, we'll see how it goes. bonus points for armor customisation
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a ton of potential and you can see that the devs tried making a good game, but it just falls short. The combat is clunky to say the least. The enemy AI is bonkers and has issues with path-finding. The attack animations are very inconsistent (some look great some are terrible). The game also suffers from a very  large amount of bugs, the biggest one being that the camera is constantly re-centering itself making normal gameplay almost impossible. The world building is pretty good, but the main character is unlikable.My biggest gripe with the game is the combat! There are no 'normal' attacks - all opponents either attack you with a blue attack that you MUST parry or a red attack that you MUST dodge making the combat feel like a big QTE instead of giving you tactical options and the choice of when do you wish to simply block or now risk for a parry but potentially get a bigger reward. And since this game tries to be a souls-like, the combat makes or breaks it...Had the game launched without some of these terrible bugs and had the devs made some adjustments to the combat itself, this game could have easily been a 7/10, especially for its asking price...EDITED: Changed the score to a thumbs up. The 1.7 updated (as well as the minor updates before it) have drastically improved the responsiveness of the game as well as the camera issues. The combat has also been redone and the enemies are no longer changing colours from blue and red constantly like a light show. Instead, the combat now behaves much more like a traditional souls combat would and is in line of what one would expect from a souls-like title. I will leave my original review to show the state of the game on release.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: About 3 hours into it and so far I am actually enjoying it. I had this game on my wishlist for a couple months because I just kept reading negative reviews and decided not to buy it. Well, I caved today and so far, it's been quite enjoyable. Depending on the difficulty you set it to, you can for sure make it a Souls like game, otherwise I haven't really come across anything hard on Adventure mode. The atmosphere and graphics overall have been pretty epic on High settings. My only downfall is I don't like that you have to master each weapon in order to spend your level up points to get more energy, hold more potions, have more health etc. Of course that is the name of the game "stray blade" but gets annoying because I would much rather just enjoy the weapons that I like using and level them up specifically. Maybe they can take the mechanics from Kingdoms of Amalur Re Reckoning. Also, if you are interested in super fast paced combat, this game is sort of like that but with delays. You can't smash the dodge, parry, attack button as you would in other games. I mean you can if you want, however, there is always like a split second delay between certain buttons so when you Parry, Dodge, etc, you have to be really precise or you will get slammed to the ground. As far as the story goes, hasn't been very the most exciting but I'm still eager to see what is upcoming in my next few hours of game time. This game does provide that open word itch ive been wanting since FFXVI though. The game could also use a minimap (even if it has to be toggled) instead of having to open and close the menu. It would also be nice that If I do open the large map, maybe you can have it auto focus on my icon (facing the proper direction please) instead of me having to click a button to make the map move towards my cursor. Just a few little QOL changes, and this game would be super fun! But I am going to continue my journey now!
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: While it's not flawless it is one of the better games of this genre, within that price range. The artstyle is very pleasing and the game overall looks good. Armor, weapons, enemies, animations mostly are very solid. I didn't really cared for the story after a short time so i cant say nothing about that. The combat which consists of attack, dodge, block and parry is fun most of the time. Enemies have interesting movesets, even tho some can be quite annoying, mainly the animals. Humans are fine. You get a ton of weapons like sword, some with shield, axe, hammer, spear, other polearms, daggers, dual swords. Most are fun to use, some are less fun. The game kinda force you to use different weapons because you need to master them to unlock abilities, like more HP, attack power, and so on. But i didn't mind that. Most weapons are fun to try at least once and the others you can max out quite quick. You can even use a rune skill to make that process even faster. You can also just leave out weapons that will unlock skills you don't use in your playstyle. For example I never really blocked in this game.Level and world desing as well as the traversing mechanics, which you get new ones throughout the game (metroidvania style) are solid. World is fun to travers. Some sections can be a bit irritating at times but that could be just me.There are difficulty settings so you don't need to be afraid you wont be able to finish it. I went for the medium difficulty and that was pretty okay. You can even adjust separate parts of the difficulty, (like damage scaling) but i didn't really looked into that. Technically I only had minor bugs, and it could run smoother on high end gear but it was still alright.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Bunch of armors so far, decently unique weapons, wide selection of enemies that aren't just copies of each other. Some of the more elite soldiers you come across are an actual problem. The executions are very very satisfying. Highlight of the whole game hands down. The bosses tho are straight up 0/10. They're the easiest thing in the game, straight trash. And the story hasn't been worth my time to the point that after 6 hours in, I just stopped listening. Overall I think the game was just mean't for a younger audience. Story isn't that deep and you have a furry companion who makes jokes sometimes. Big Jak and Daxter vibes. 5/10. Good game to play if I want to get through an audiobook.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. I put about 50 hours into it with the DLC included. I liked the way weapons unlocked the skill tree and the map was fairly helpful. The story was decent enough and I found myself actually paying attention to the dialog. The combat was fun and each weapon played a little differently. I had a few instances of enemies freezing up but nothing game breaking. I hope they make more DLC or a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic, extremely fun and satisfying to play.It's aesthetically gorgeous ~ The music, sound design & voice acting are phenomenal. The story and relationship building between the two main characters is fantastic (you can choose to be a masc/fem character AND masc/fem voice lines separately. Wonderful?!) - There are so many weapon varieties and attack combos. Parrying & dodging are extremely satisfying; as you regenerate stamina from performing perfect ones, as well as cool combos and animations for stance breaking / finishing moves. You can color customize and mix and match gear pieces & weapons to your preference. There are so many awesome & unique aspects to this game!!I would describe the combat as relatively slow & cinematic. If you go into this game thinking it's just another souls-like, you're doing a grand disservice to this game. It's so much more; I'd hardly even call it a souls-like. Respect the game and play it as it is, don't try to play it like a souls game. 7 hours in, with thorough exploration; and I'm not even 1/4 of the way through. this game is well worth the full price; if you catch it on sale, it's an absolute must!
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Blade is here, I have been waiting for this game, Like ever since it was announced.Tame your expectations if your expecting this to be a souls like, some elements of it are, while others aren't, My suggestion play until you unlock the first few skills and weapons, then the game becomes more faster.Story: Meet Farren West, Adventurer Traveler in search of the valley of legends, the greatest discovery ever, But what awaits them in this mysterious land remains to be seen.Combat: Stray Blade combat, How to describe it, you can either mash attacks, learn the timing of the dodge mechanic, learn the parry system, or you can just tank the damage and hope you come out on top, on higher difficulties, the enemy's hit hard, and you hit for less. With a variety of weapons, skills to learn and help from Boji, you grow stronger.Art: The art in the game is amazing, from how the lands change after certain events, to how enemy's you fought later move to earlier area's conquering there foes, to the animals art styles.Music: The score of Stray Blade is beautiful, from how it matches the combat, to the cutscenes, somber in sad moments, and intense in the boss fightsWeapons: My lord there is alot of weapons to choose from, My favorite being the Lighting Blade, this weapon packs a mean punch. Other weapons include daggers, hammers, halberds/spears Armor: Farren comes across lots of different armor sets that provides benefits to his overall armor and energy meter.Overall look: The overall look of the game is beautiful, from the environments, to the enemy's design, to Farren's armor and weapons.Give the game a try, it is Point Blank Games first game, Once you sink your teeth into it and get used to the combat and the wittiness of Farren and Boji banter you will grow to love it like i do.Also yes there may be a few bugs, but the devs are working hard to fix them.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game quite a bit, people are comparing it to Kingdom of Amalur Re-Reckoning which I think is a very appropriate comparison, the combat and feel to the games are similar for sure, I wouldn't necessarily compare it to souls-likes as readily however, it doesn't really have that same feel to it in my opinion. I thought that the combat was interesting, the variety of weapons was fun and the story was good. I didn't go into this looking for story so I didn't necessarily go out of my way to engage in the story, but there seemed to be a lot there, so if you want to, there is probably enough there for you to enjoy. With regards to gameplay I thought there were some minor issues that made some enemies frustrating, due to visuals making you think they would attack sooner than they would. The example that comes to mind is the spiders who will charge you, then raise up and then strike down, except if you're standing in front of them they run until they reach the end of their animation, not until the reach you, meaning that you can watch them run at you in place for a few seconds, thinking you need to parry the incoming attack only for that attack to come much later than you would have thought. With regards to the difficulty, I thought the difficulty with the bosses was earned, as in I lost fights because I didn't know their combos or didn't time something right, unlike sometimes the difficulty in the 'open world' which I found could feel a bit unfair. For example, if your focus gets stuck on the wrong enemy, it can be quite difficult to fix that in time before you're hit from behind. I potentially found the difficulty a bit low on the hard mode (but I am yet to play on the hardest difficulty so take that with a grain of salt), it took me no more than 5 attempts at any one boss, which for me felt like a happy medium for this sort of game. All in all, I enjoyed this game. It lacks polish but if you're willing to work within some awkward gameplay here and there, and enjoy the good stuff that is here, there is a lot to enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Overall have enjoyed playing. Has some jank and needs some patching. Needs optimization for better fps. The attack color notifications take some getting used to and I'd rather have them pop when the actual attack occurs. Fun to play, though.Devs are on top of patching issues. Also found the custom difficulty settings helpful for getting used to the parry/block features.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: After completing the game and dlc plus all of the achievements, I can tell that both the game and dlc especially were really underwhelming. Some of the good: Story, world exploration, looks, voice acting, customization, weapon variety, progression, boss fights. All of those are great. The combat is mid, but does the job, the exploration is ruined by enemy variety and how repetitive it is. There are some cool ideas, how the environments change after some progression, ability to upgrade every single weapon you come across, your companion being useful and having his own abilities, runes you can add to weapons, and so on. Some weapons, armours and other collectables are very well hidden, which is annoying if you are trying to 100% the game, but feels rewarding when exploring. Ability to chose a difficulty is nice. Performance isn't too great, some stuttering. Revival animations is annoying and unskippable. Personally haven't encountered any glitches or bugs and can't say the devs didn't put a lot of love into this game, maybe should have let it cook a tad more though before releasing. Price is good for the amount of content, especially on a sale. At the end of the day, I did enjoy it even though it is just above average.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. Combat is alright (AI can be bad/glitchy) and a big part of the game- light and heavy attack, dash, and parry. The cool part about the combat is the vast number of weapons there are, about 40. And you need to master the different weapons to upgrade your characters stats. But my favorite part of this game the exploration and world!! It's a 3D metroidvania. And the exploring is always rewarded. The atmosphere is cool with nature around you usually and birds singing when you're outside. I would not call it souls-like but instead a metroidvania action adventure. Combat is not as difficult as a souls-like, at least on normal difficulty. The game does overstay it's welcome a little and gets repetitive but still a good time. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I was super excited to start but very quickly into the game it felt to much like a elden ring knock off. I decided I’m going to stick with it even if the timing on blocks and dodges didn’t make sense and the simplest enemy’s were handing me my ass. Where I drew the line and decided to go no further was when I died in a cave right after an auto save and when I revived, the only way I could move was to press the jump button over and over and I couldn’t do anything else. The only thing that fixed this issue was to uninstall completely but by then I didn’t feel it was worth the hassle and again all this happened very early into the game. I did receive it for free for testing it from the creators which I am thankful for. Maybe in future I’ll try again but not any time soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I will update this later, but for now I just want to add a positive review for this game because it deserves a lot more attention than it got. I have to wonder if that was due to lack of advertising and public awareness. In short, this is the most stylized soulslike game I've played that didn't try to be all dark and grim/gritty like Dark Souls/Demon Souls. It has exploration that I would compare to Kingdoms of Amalur or Zelda with labyrinthine, complex levels (You can get lost, but there's a world map and a toggle-able compass to assist), which I have found to be enjoyable rather than cumbersome. There is some jank and you will have to have some tolerance for such, but that also comes with the territory of large scale games with relatively small dev teams. And let me say, the art department did a phenomenal job of making the story and world pop. It's the thing that got me interested in the game, but the gameplay has been fun and engaging as well. I believe I'm around 25% of the way through the game and I look forward to finishing it. If it looks interesting, give it a shot! Oh and side note, there's adjustable difficulty if you find the game to be too easy or too hard. If you've played other soulslikes, I'd recommend Challenging while also turning up enemy health to 1.5 or higher.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: It sounds great: both the music and the voice actors, it looks great (if getting my CPU a bit hot: even getting the FPS to 30 still got me from 76-80°C O.O) and I'm sure the wolf-like companion is great, but I quit before we met because: the combat sucks. This should have been a game like Beast Quest: block or dodge in time with color prompts and attack when you see an opening because that's the blueprint I'm seeing in it. As it is it's too slow to be souls-like: the animations are very slow and exaugurated, but there's no fluidity to make it work - Dark Soul 1 did this way better.  The other bone I have to pick with this game is that shields are tied to certain weapons, e.g. if I want to use the earliest available shield, I'd need to use a spear. While it's less clunky here, I'm not a far of spears, give me a sword swing over that any day.  Since I can no longer refund it, I'll wait for the devs to figure out how they want the combat to work and maybe try it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Blade is a great rogue-lite game. Combat takes a little getting used to, as it doesn't operate like a typical hack 'n' slash. Some skill and timing is required to be successful and it can take a little time to develop. Overall, the game is graphically interesting with a wonderful artistic style. Enemies feel threatening (and definitely are), but the environment isn't overly dark and heavy as with some games in this genre. Leveling your characters skills, upgrading/enhancing weapons, etc. all have natural and understandable progressions and add to the game play experience. I am enjoying the game a great deal and definitely recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you, dear developer team, the 21 hours were really worth it, I wasn't bored for a minute.The game often reminded me of old classics like AC (because of the finishers), Darksiders (graphics) and a bit of a Souls-like-light (depending on the difficulty). Also the atmosphere in general reminded me of old PS2 games as well as the gameplay in general, game is not too packed.Short, tight, but full buy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Got about 7 hours ingame time so far and got to say I love a lot of things about Stray Blade.The gameplay feels smooth, like a somewhat simplified (not in a negative way) hybrid between a classic darksouls and sekiro.The items so far are feeling decent and you really can notice the differences between them, got like 10 and a lot more to discover.The skill system is nice, the fights are fair and feeling smooth.All in all the game feels way smoother and really finished, whats great for such a small studio behind it.The story and the audio (english) are awesome, I really like the visuals as well.Also the development of the story, the characters and the world are feeling natural, well thought as well.All in all I really like this game and I can call myself a souls veteran since the beginning, got many other soulslikes under my belt as well.I would recommand this game to anyone who is into somewhat tactical fighting, cute visuals, and a nice narated story with well spoken dialoges.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game; An easy favorite! This game offers some advanced combat that requires a great deal of attention. If your not good at that, it also has a very wide range of difficulty level. Anyone can play this, even if you never parry a single attack. I greatly love Farren West and Bojji as characters. The game requires players to spread out their weapon variety to gain more health, energy, or stronger attack damage by gaining 100% mastery over each weapon they forge. This is super cool, because you will love everything from the speedy swords, and heavy axes. I really hope it gets more added to the story.This game doesn't get the credit it deserves, and all these "problems" with the camera, I cannot fathom. I have no issues, and it may just be a settings fix. Please give this game a try. It may not be the greatest thing ever to be played, but its a solid fun game, so give it credit.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely enjoyed my time with the game. I'm not much for story driven titles, but even trying to skip the story, I found myself stopping to listen from time to time. I also find the price to be right on point. Just casually playing the story with a little bit of exploration on the side, you'll easily get at least 30 hrs out of the game. To me $1:1hr is a good price point.I also had a lot of fun around the end trying to one-shot bosses with a certain rune+weapon combo =).
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Having way more fun than I though I would (according to older reviews). It's a Metroidvania with Souls-like combat and really nice finishers.The beginning is rather hard until you get to know the parry mechanic, which is way easier than in Dark Souls. You can also opt for shield builds, but parrying is more my forte.The story is also quite entertaining by having the interactions between you male or female character and your sidekick Boji.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Fun action RPG with a different take on leveling, pleasing art style, and relatively decent combat.  Pros - Great looking game- Combat is good enough- I like progression and skills being tied to weapons but others may not- Exploration is rewardedCons- Dodge/Parry system falls apart with multiple enemies- Some minor bugs- times where you have a lot of skills points available not able to spend
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Blade is a fun action RPG with relatively simple but surprisingly satisfying combat. The counter and dodge system takes a bit to get used to at first but once you get the hang of it it's very fun and engaging. I'm personally a big fan of the aesthetics and the level design is fun and interconnected. The weapons are pretty unique with their own play styles, featuring a special ability, and feel good to use. Your companion adds to both the combat and the story and unlike many other games isn't annoying or grating. There are still some issues that should be worked out, targeting can be wonky and there are some performance problems but I think the game is well worth the asking price. If you are looking for a cool action RPG with relatively simple but engaging combat and a cool aesthetic, I would recommend Stray Blade.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: The game could definitely need more polish but i would already recommend it. The combat system is a bit clunky but it mostly works. The animations are nice - the enemies mostly clearly indicate their attacks and all the weapon types have nice animations. I really like the Weapon-mastery system that "forces" you to use all the weapons at least for a bit to unlock all the skills - even though the skills are just passive like more health or damage.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: The best thing about this game is the combat system, it's so rewarding when you can parry and finish the foe. I love the fact that you can try so many new weapons with tons of personalization. I rarely get into single player games but this is my style! Not the best performance wise, I get some frame drops but usually not a big deal, I mean not in the middle of the fight but just when changing areas and I got an high end pc. I hope it will get better in the future.I hope there will be some kind of arena or atleast NG plus but I doubt it, I would love some kind of replayability because the combat system is what makes me complete the game :)
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: i dont usually write reviews but i feel compelled on this because of the vast mixed reviews/very negative reviews i feel are overblown. This game for sure has some flaws that could have and probably should have been ironed out but they are not game breaking. Most peoples problems with the damage and combat are no where near as bad as said once you start upgrading your armor and your hp/stamina pool. i am playing on the 3rd difficulty (there is 4) and im at a point i feel like i could be on the 4th if i want more of a challenge but could still progress. the actual issues with the game are your weapon "special attacks" feel like they were an oversight. like whoever created them was like "oh lets add a decent strong attack with a cooldown for brownie points" but never actually field tested them. they are like a 2/10 on usefullness. they are god awful slow animations that can just be and WILL BE interupted by an enemy attack and do not do enough poise damage or hp damage to be like "man i NEED to get this move off". yes of course i still always try to use them lol but they are implemented horribly. they parry/dodge system is actually pretty good and cool except if there are multiple enemies attacking. again i think this was an oversight without field testing. you can only parry one attack and HAVE to wait till the parry animation is done to do another meaning if a second enemy is attacking you ARE getting hit no way around it which takes away from skill expression. the fact enemies can constantly interupt/daze you compared to you BARELY ever is just a forced way to add difficulty but take away skill expression/immersion when even the littlest creatures/humans use a light attack and do it yet you used a massive hammer heavy swing and they just swing right through it like yyeeeaahhhh OK not going to happen. its comically bad and frustrating as it breaks your combat groove but again its not gamebreaking and can be worked around. everything else is great. the scenery changes between darker battlegrounds to lush colorful nature. voice acting is fine as long as you dont mind british sounding accents. besides the weird battle flaws i described battles are actually satisfying learning movesets and the finishers are nice looking and quick (most of them). the parry/dodge thing everyone complaining about the game telling you not to look at the color but the movements is i think just a description mistake and the part of the devs. the best way to explain it is you dont HAVE to just react to blue=parry and red=dodge. like you can still dodge backwards on a blue overhead swing. no you cant parry a red attack but you CAN block every attack with a shield wepon. the story isnt too deep from what ive gathered so far but it is unique and interesting so it makes you want to actually uncover the whole thing. if you like adventure/exploration games with action combat this is a very nice and fun game for sure worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Liking it so far... I will say that the combat can be annoying.  The combat moves from most enemies are hard to see the telegraphs and it makes it more frustrating than your average souls game is.  A lot of them will use the same start to an animation and then switch it up at the last second to do a delayed move thus causing a missed parry.  It becomes really frustrating instead of fun.  Take this with a grain of salt because my reflexes are slowing as I age so this could just be me needing to git gud.  One of the first hard enemies killed me like 30 times.  It was "harder" than elden ring or even sekiro.Beyond some of my frustration with the combat moves I like the game a lot.  The story is good so far, the environments are cool.  Despite my earlier comments on combat I actually still enjoy the fighting, it can just be frustrating sometimes.  The game is performing great, no issues, but I have a really good cpu and gpu.Really enjoying the game so far.  Definitely worth the $30 price tag.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd give this game a 5/10. The Pros:Combat is funYou get new weapons often enough that adds a slight change in combat styleThe Cons:The game is poorly optimized. I have a fairly modern gaming computer and I couldn't go 4k with Ultra graphics without low FPS and stuttering. I had to turn it down to regular HD and the game would still hitch occasionally.Your abilities would sometimes not work; the special powers that help you navigate the terrain. The main driver behind the game.I'd wait for the game to drop in price to about $10, because you'll get at least that many hours before either quitting from performance issues or deciding to tough persevere through the problems until them end.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, the negative reviews are mostly people who are mad cause bad.KBM controls are fine, just turn auto targeting off.the combat's not awful, but being forced into parry or dodge is rather annoying, when one's for the enemy's poise, and one for your stamina respectively.  Makes the whole stamina/poise system a dice roll against the ai instead of something you have any semblance of control over.Buy nioh 2 or sekiro and play those first, if you like the art style, try asterigos: curse of the stars.then if you're still looking for more, buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I just heard about this game on release day and was interested enough to purchase it right away. I am really enjoying it! The voice acting is great, I love the clothing customization and large skill tree, and the combat is challenging. I find the story intriguing and am looking forward to more adventuring. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty great! The art is different and stands out. The game play is pretty damn smooth and feels good. If you're looking for a different take on somewhat souls-like combat mechanics with a twist and an absolutely lovely story-line, Stray Blade is definitely a damn good place to get it. Yes, my copy was provided for me, but that holds no power over this review or my feelings of the game. I genuinely enjoyed myself 95% of the time. I am very excited for this full release and fully intend to go through the game again as a completed title. It's just that good!!
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: It's like taking Elden Ring, making it a bit more accessible and giving it a more artistic, colorful art style and you have Stray Blade. While the environmental art up close looks good, the distance terrain could use more detail as it looks backgrounds found in the old PS2 era. Combat is what you expect in the souls-like genre with easy-to-understand dodge and parry system. The finishing moves are satisfying as well. The skill system rewards experimentation with other weapons but at the same time, it doesn't reward those who just want to stay with a specific weapon. A skill tree refresh in a future DLC could be most welcome here.Is it work playing? I think if you enjoyed watching Elden Ring through streams and videos but thought it was to difficult to enjoy yourself, you might enjoy this approach. The story is entertaining and the voice talent is quite good. Solid 7/10 but easily higher with future content, patching and additions to make the game reach its full potential.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first.If you enjoying this game, good for you, I'm happy for you, this is just my experience what I'm writing down.This game made me really mad right at the beginning.On 1440p, epic settings, this game ran 35-45 FPS. Even FSR on, the max was 55.Why?! I have no clue. I got a RTX2070 and I played Cyberpunk 2077 on all high, dlss on, 1440p with 75-95 FPS, or WD: Legion very high and some ultra settings, dlss on, 1440p with 65-100 FPS. There isn't any reason why this game ran so ♥♥♥♥♥♥ on my rig.But I was very generous, so I went back to 1080p with FSR on and the game ran with 85 FPS.I wasn't really happy about this, but ok.Let me tell you one thing: I've finished Elden Ring, Remnant from the Ashes, Code Vein, so I'm not totally unexperienced with these kind of "souls like" games.But the combat in this game...maaan...Dodging is somewhat ok, but parry. It's broken AF.The game warns you to not react to the flashing indicator (that seems pretty stupid to me, but ok), but man... I died 3 times because I coudn't parry at all. Even when I tried to react on the last second of the animation, nothing happened. I just took the hit. So after 3x of dying + the problem with the graphics I asked for a refund. So, this is my wonderful experience with this game. :D

_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely neutral on this game. The good:1.) Stunning world visuals2.) Interesting and often clever characters3.) Simple Crafting and Upgrade System4.) Multi-tiered fully customizable difficulty tuning that can be done at any point in the game.5.) Decent Boss fights (though few)The bad:1.) Not enough variety... You fight the same 4 enemies over and over and over again. With boss fights few and far between.2.) Optimization in this game is awful... Even at low settings it chunks on the deck and on my chonky uber PC it is a CPU cruncher at 120fps. 3.) Enemy models slightly in the distance always stutter even at high fps. I guess they thought this was  a way of optimizing but it is jarring in most cases looking like they are skipping animation frames.4.) Lastly graphics settings are annoying with no monitor setting and FPS choices of 30, 60, 120, or infinite. So if I want my gaming room not to turn into a sauna when running at highfps (see aforementioned comment about high CPU demand at high FPS), my choices are cook at 120 or have to drop all the way to 60 or limit it the monitor externally.Again, having a beefy PC and some know-how I can work around most of these, but the game running too hot at low settings on the deck is the biggest bummer. I think with some focus on optimization they could make this game more accessible to steam decks and low end PCs and this title would be a banger. As it stands my recommendation would be if you don't have a really nice PC maybe pass this one by for now. If you do it is a decent play.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: A great AA title with a lot of heart. I honestly don't get all the negative reviews. While it may take a while until the combat system clicks, the world is vibrant, dynamic and full of stuff to find. Easily recommended, especially if you crave that oldschool feeling of classic action adventures with a little souls mixed in.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like we're back to the past with this one, in a good way. I feel nostalgic of the good old RPG games, reminds me a bit of Kingdoms of Amalur and that's a huge compliment because I loved that game.However, I feel like the game is not completely polished. The camera on mouse and keyboard feels a bit clunky and not as smooth as it should be. Camera centers itself to see frontally and it's annoying, it cannot be disabled right now. Combat is a bit boring for me, but maybe it will become more interesting later on. Some animations are a bit too basic and simple. Sound effects could be better, but overall seems like a promising game, especially if we consider the price!Not recommending it would not be fair, but if the developers really want to improve it then I am willing to wait until the gameplay gets better.My advice is to give it some time and maybe grab it when it's below 20€.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Version:This game is a great addition to any players library whom likes Souls like combat, and Great world depth with a few flaws at this price point. Extended Version:Game Rating - 7.8/10.Stray blade has its eyes set on the prize for being a Souls like, semi open world combat game and it storms the castle and makes it in the door at this attempt. The combat is engaging, however I personally would like to see it a bit more fluid. Players who are well antiquated with Souls like games will enjoy the Dodge/ Parry system and the game does a great job of allow you to "scale down" if you are not good at that or like me have a disability that just makes you not that fast. environments and sounds are both above average in my opinion and while there is some asset reuse (Items in areas I just don't feel belong/Match the vibe) it is not extreme. The one thing I would love to see more of is enemy types or maybe affixes to add some variety to the game. There is many weapon types to choose from from sword and shield (My favorite) to great swords with each weapon having its own style. Over all this game is a recommended play for anyone who likes souls like games and enjoys supporting small dev teams.

_childDocuments_.review: Stylistically Stray Blade reminds me a little of Kingdoms of Amalur, but it plays a "little" (I stress a little) like a From Software game.To succeed, you'll need to master the dodge and parry systemNot enough control of the camera with auto repositioningJumping feels jankyThere is no visual indication of fall damage or low health - though there is the obligatory heartbeatGraphically, it's OK.  Which I like better than something like ThymesiaDefinitely a game you want running at 60 FPS or more.  Turning down shadows gives you a massive boost in FPS.  I was dropping into the 50s with a 7800x3d and 7900 xtx at 1440p using ultra.  Lowered it to high and get at least 45-90% back.VA is pretty good.I kinda like it, but to say it's 'one of the most anticipated action-adventure titles of 2023' would be an overstatement.  Considering I just heard about it today.  Anyway, it's got some jank in the combat.  Though I would say it's more nuanced than anything.  I'd recommend it at it's launch 20% off.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Blade is like a slightly better version of the original Lords of the Fallen, I think. With a goofy little twist and a little too much monologue, for the first hour at least. I wanted to go and fight the first big baddie, but I think I want to get a refund, at least for now. The combat is okay, pretty simple, but solid. With some creatures, I struggled a little to get the parry or dodge timing. The human enemies were much easier. It has this Metroidvania feel to it as well, but you can probably tell it was going to have some elements as you can see the Metroidvania tag. The skill tree seems fine and the game promotes using and mastering different weapons to get their passive abilities permanently. But I don't know, for the premise, I think the areas feel a little... big? I was expecting it to be a little more linear. This review is all over the place, so I think maybe giving it a rating will be better. I'll give it a 5/10 I guess. Not great, not awful either. But what I can definitely say is that the optimization is not really good.I also did not enjoy being British for the past hour. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a bit too harsh on my previous review so i sat down for another session and tried to get into it a bit more while deleting the old review. It seems that the recent patch addressed some of the issues i initially had with the parry system as it was just rng based and unfair. Now with a bit more time to parry it's a bit better. It still needs tons of improvements with camera, lock-on and it is a mess with multiple enemies so i'm still not fully enjoying combat. At least now i am able to progress so i could enjoy the world and lore a bit more. It's visually pleasing, has a good sense of exploration and decent character customization. I do wish it was not a souls-like and would just be a proper action rpg, but it is what it is...I can now at least recommend it due to the few fixes they've made. Still hope they will fix more stuff as it has potential to be a great game overall.

_childDocuments_.name: Stray Blade

_childDocuments_.review: My First Impression (and this review might change depending on the devs work)After the first few hours of play, I feel like saying that the game might have potential, but right now there are many problems:1. The enemy aiming camera does not work well and often remains fixed in the middle.2. Weapon special attacks are non-existent, with horrible animations and very little variety.3. Fatalities are realized in some cases very well, in others too hastily and sloppily.4. The equipment coloring system is poorly done, because it applies to all weapons and armor, instead of applying as it should only to the set being used at the time, forcing the user to have to recolor all pieces every time he changes armor. Instead, a coloring system should be created that allows each individual weapon and piece of equipment to be colored separately.5. Too little variety of enemies and poorly crafted bosses so far (until the general initium)For all these reasons I cannot recommend the game at the moment, but I hope the developers will seriously consider my suggestions because there is potential in the game, if they will do patches to improve the gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Blade is a good game and worth your time.  It takes a little bit to really get into the story but then when Boji reveals himself, it starts getting good.  I have yet to finish the game but so far so good.  The mechanics of the gameplay are not too complicated.  The ability to forge weapons and upgrade them is appealing to me.  Unlocking spells for Boji to cast to help is also neat.  There has been an update since I played last so I won't talk about some minor glitches it had (which all new games seem to have anymore).  The discord group is helpful and through there I feel like the devs will take notice and work on fixes if you have any issues.  I'd highly recommend, especially if you are able to catch it at the current discounted price.  It is worth every penny.  Also it is not a short game which I'd hate to spend more than $20 on a game I can finish in 5 hours.  I have over 12 hours and from what I can tell I'm maybe a third of the way but I did some poking around which did not advance the story.  It is open worldish and I managed to get lost a few times but if you like open world then this game is for you.  There is a map and a compass to help you get on track if you want to advance the story.

_childDocuments_.review: I found this to be a boring third person sword slashing game with poor optimization. No matter what I changed the graphic settings to (even when lowering the resolution percentage to 60%), I still experienced constant frame rate drops in 4k resolution with an RTX3080 and i9 processor. Some of these frame rate drops were actually below 20. From searching the Steam discussions, this seems to be caused by the Unreal Engine 4 shader compilation stutter that can only be fixed by the developer, which has still not happened. Other issues are that the graphics are low-res and sort of cartoony, combat is often unresponsive and requires absolute perfect parry and blocking, there is no crouching, the only form of sprinting is to toggle it on/off, you don't get ranged weapons yet are constantly being shot by ranged weapons, there is no manual save, you spawn way back at far away shrines, and the game always looks the same taking place in boring outside fields. Overall, I did not enjoy my time spent with this game and I therefore cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, has more replay value than soulsgames.If you wanna experience everything, you have to die, mostly due to gravity.Enemies are basically simulating an ecosystem, if you clear an area of enemies, and if you die, then those areas mostly will be later on devoid of those enemies or switched out with another type of enemy, basically fiends vs humans, humans build new stairs, platforms, chests, forges, also sometimes block some pathways, while fiends will destroy said stuff.Defeating story bosses also alters the world and brings in new and stronger enemies, bosses sadly can't be stunned, but they are affected by certain weapon attacks that can stagger them, allowing you to stagger lock them, there are some secret boss type enemies too, which grant you permanent healing buffs.You also have some metroidvania stuff too, when you get new powers to get access to old areas.Speaking of old areas, loads of shortcuts that you can unlock, on the fiend side you grow down vines or grow vines over a gap to form a bridge, and on the human side you open mid sized gates from the other side.Combat is also okay, mostly the game wants you either to dodge or parry enemy attacks, but you can try to interrupt the enemy, before getting hit yourself. Timing is still essential, you can use the wrong type defense, but you won't get energy back from it, nor parry an unparryable attack, but you'll at least take less damage. You can also disable the color coding for what type of an attack is incoming, but then it just becomes a trial and error mechanic where you have to remember every attack and if you have can dodge it or parry it.Lock on mechanic is needed here if you want to see the enemies health/stun bar, but it's not needed for doing parries or dodges.You start out the game with fists, you get a your old rusty sword back which also hints how much time passed after your first cutscene death, you can also find another starting weapon, these two don't have any masteries for them. Later on you'll only find blueprints for weapons and armor, so you have to use the enemy forges to craft yourself new gear. All the weapons that are crafted come with an unlockable passive skill for the character even when not using the weapon. Each weapon also has a special attack.You can also craft rune that act as temporary buffs for the weapon you have in your hand at the moment, or the hand slot (haven't tested yet, if it's weapon bound or slot bound), the buff itself so far doesn't seem time based, but more about how many times it activates.Nicest part of the game are the finishing animations, which can be done forcefully after stunning an enemy or automatically sometimes when killing an enemy. You also have your backstabs, which are pretty brutal. Each weapon type has similar backstab animations for human enemies, or similar finishing animations for fiend enemies. The rest are much more varied.Oh and also some weapons come with a shield, and only with those weapons you can block attacks, the rest of them will only do a parry with the block button, though there is a separate parry button.Performance is pretty good, can play it at 1080p 60+fps mostly with Ultra settings, though Ultra shadows are too much, better to use Epic, some areas become slightly demanding, but you can get only around 10 extra fps from lowering shadows even further and view distance, the rest don't do much in terms of performance.So yeah most optimal would be just using Epic View Distance and Shadows, the rest ultra.Using RTX 2070 8GB, i7 8700K, 16GB ram.Sadly the game doesn't have dlss, and amd fsr is just an on and off option, which doesn't do much.

_childDocuments_.review: Stray Blade is an action-adventure game that combines elements of exploration and combat, set in the vibrant yet perilous Valley of Acrea. Players assume the role of Farren West, an adventurer accompanied by the mystical creature Boji, as they uncover the secrets of this ancient land.Pros:- Dynamic Combat System: The game offers a responsive and engaging combat experience, allowing players to master dodges, parries, and a variety of weaponry. - Rich World Design: Acrea is brought to life with a colorful and detailed environment, encouraging exploration and discovery. - Compelling Character Dynamics: The relationship between Farren and Boji adds depth to the narrative, providing both emotional engagement and gameplay benefits. Cons:- Technical Issues: I had a glitch with a puzzle that led to me having to restart it.- Repetitive Enemy Encounters: Some players may find the variety of enemies lacking, leading to repetitive combat scenarios. - Map Navigation Challenges: The in-game map can be difficult to interpret, making navigation and objective tracking cumbersome. In conclusion, "Stray Blade" offers an engaging blend of combat and exploration within a beautifully crafted world. While it faces some technical and design challenges, it provides a rewarding experience for fans of action-adventure games.Score: 7 out of 10 enchanted swords—A sharp adventure with a few nicks.

_childDocuments_.review: While it is far from perfect, it is a decent game. Combat is solid and weapon selection is good. There is also an interesting story. I would say the game, dlc and soundtrack are a good value at $30 but I wouldn't pay anymore than that. Overall I would recommend it but I listed some things I dislike about it below to take into consideration before buying it.1. There is no cloud saves. The game saves are stored at C:\Users\"Your Username"\AppData\Local\Lingcod\Saved\SaveGames. There are the save files with SG in the name. The ST files store the display configuration. So if you play on multiple computers, you will need to constantly transfer them back and forth.2. The performance is pretty inconsistent. The further you get into the game, the more stutters and frame drops occur. The DLC is also like that. This happened on both computers I played on it. One of them being a newer high end system and the other a mid range laptop. 3. The harder the difficulty you plan on, the worse the combat feels. It is decent but that tends to fall apart when facing multiple enemies. I played on the Adventurer difficulty because I heard someone else say that about that game. Everything seemed fine until the third area when the difficulty spiked. All of the sudden my weapons were doing poor damage and it took a long time to kill enemies. Leveling is also automatic so if you do a lot of exploring and stuff, your character levels more and in turn, so do enemies.4. The third area is just annoying. The whole thing is like a maze, the enemies seem much more difficult than the previous areas and there is poison clouds to deal with. I did not like the area at all. It was more frustrating and tedious than interesting.
