_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off with the most important part, the controls.It feels a  off. I think it all comes down to how long an attack takes to come out before you can move and swing again. In another adventure game with dungeons for the Super Nintendo that shall not be named, you can attack REALLY quickly. I think you could maybe get out 2 to 3 attacks in the time it takes to get out 1 in this game. It feels a lot more sluggish because of that.The movement speed feels kinda slow too. This might be a personal preference thing, but I wish the little chicken was like, 10-20% faster.All of that being said, I'm a big fan of the creation tools.It's a very good foundation for later updates.For a game like this, I feel like the important part is the variety of tools that a player can find in a dungeon. As it is right now, there's bombs, a hookshot, a shield, flippers to walk over water, and an item that lets you dodge roll. If more are added, then the possibility for creations skyrockets, so I hope we see some interesting items implemented in the future. There's 10 or so enemies. Not a bad amount if you ask me. They're varied enough to challenge the player in different ways.I wish there was a larger variety of cosmetic things to place. There's over a dozen right now, but they almost all take up space in the world. There's only one basic floor pattern per tileset, I think having different decorative patterns and maybe even stuff like rugs you could walk over would go a long way to giving more options to players.And I've unfortunately encountered a few bugs that make dungeon creation somewhat annoying. I've submitted 3 bug reports in the hour or so I've played, and I guess we'll see how long it takes for those to be fixed.I've mostly talked about negative stuff in this review, but that's mainly because I wanted to bring up stuff I think should be fixed. There's not much to say about what I enjoy about the dungeon creator, it's just fun to work with. If content updates and bug fixes can be pushed out in a timely manner, I could see this game getting a lot of players in the near future.And add an overworld creator!!! Or at the very least, a way to link dungeons together and have items carry over into the next ones.

_childDocuments_.review: IMPORTANT EDIT: Since my review got a bit of traction, I NEED to add something. The game is officially dead and abandoned. I consider this a quite sad development, it had huge potential. As much as I said in this review, that the game is giving a good framework and base to add further elements, we seem to never see what these additions might have been. It might not be a bad game in its current state, but it's also not enough to still recommend it to that degree. I'll let my review on "Recommended", since my "helpful"-votes would go away, if I would change it. Less people would see this edit and I don't consider this good. Buying at your own risk folks!ORIGINAL REVIEW:After over 20 hours I have spent most of the time building and I need to say it's giving a good basis for now, but still needs features to be added. I don't need to say which since a lot of other players have already pointed the issues out.The framework gives a lot of freedom and allows to make fun concepts to play with. If you are interested in making dungeons in a Zelda-style this will give you pretty much that. Some QoL changes need to be made to make it easier, as example selecting multiple tiles and move them around or to spawn the chicken into your hand to test instantly in the area you are working in (EDIT: Haven't seen it myself, but the Devs said they have added these features). Making something original is a bit difficult but possible.There is a lot to desire, the concept is great and can be build even further to make it a great game.Right now, you will get to the point where you are unsure what to do. Playing other dungeons is nice, but only for a while.Most of the time I see questionable dungeon designs (perhaps also unfun), with occasional softlocks and also cheese potential, since death means a respawn at the start with all keys and equipment you gathered. This leads to a lot of soft-locking and cheesing potential, which not every builder has in mind. To fix this, there needs to be a checkpoint system. A negative voting option would also be an idea, but I believe the devs won't do it for the time being, since this would discourage players to build levels and I also dislike the idea, even if it would be a good one when the game becomes more crowded.Also right now there is a motivation issue. You can only build or play other builders dungeons. Sadly you can't pick a random dungeon instantly, only if you already started a dungeon you picked from a list, what makes it a bit tedious to get right into the fun times. There is no mode like the 100-Mario-Challenge in Super Mario Maker or the possibility to make multiple dungeons and create your own adventure with a world map. I would even say there are the possibilities to make your own overworld at some point, since your game menu is basically an overworld.Again there is a lot to add to make a game with long-time enjoyment out of it, but this will not be an issue.The devs are extremely responsive about ideas and criticism. There is almost not a single steam thread where the devs haven't responded to and they are working hard, to give us the best experience.With time this game will become only better, with what it's already doing. I believe with a mode beyond "Pick dungeon from list" this might already become a more fun experience.If you like the old zelda-titles this is a game you will most likely enjoy. I am not even a fan of the old titles and spent quite some time in this game already.Have fun building and enjoying other players creations :)

_childDocuments_.review: For everyone who grew up playing classic action games with top-down perspective, this is a dream come true. Sadly, it functions more as a tool than a game.Everything begins with a chicken awakening in a dungeon. There is no tutorial or information on the screen. But if you've ever played a game like this before, you'll be fine. The controls are simple: move the character with the direction pad, attack with the A button, and pick up pots with the B button. By holding the A button for a few seconds, you can even charge the attack. The charged attack hits everything around you. However, all objects within the range get hit at the same time. This is very noticeable with grass. When you release the charge button, all grass gets cut at the same time while the attack animation is still playing. Later you get access to items (X button) and dodge move (shoulder button).You arrive in the village with numerous locations after completing the introduction dungeon. The first is a playground that is built like a normal tutorial, but there is no way of knowing if you're doing it correctly. All tools are available right away, and you can speak with NPCs who can explain each mechanic. You, on the other hand, are never taught anything. It's largely just a matter of clicking on things and placing them on the grid.The five build icons located on the left side are divided into doors, objects, usable items, enemies and floor type. It should be mentioned that building using a mouse is considerably easier, but you may play with a gamepad as well. The left mouse button is used for selection and placement, whereas the right mouse button is used to delete items. Undo is also available, but only for a limited number of actions.The save button, brightness, and environment are the other three icons. You currently have three types of dungeons to choose from: forest, desert, and castle. The only distinction is the types of objects that can be placed. You can't put a cactus in a castle, for example. I’d like to nitpick and complain that you also can’t place NPCs, which would really breathe life into individual levels, but then you’d have to change the name of the game. There is no single-player mode, as stated in the description. NPCs don’t have anything to say except for some tips and there are no secrets. The only thing worth noting is the village's three pre-generated dungeons, one for each environment.Some smaller observations:-	Water has strange animation when you get close to it. It looks like your character attracts water like a magnet. -	I’d like to have an option to change my character.   -	Sword’s range feels very short due to the avatar’s size.-	Enemies can’t be knocked into holes.Overall, the tool works and is easy to use. This means good news for the previously-mentioned classics as well. It probably won’t take long before someone transfers entire levels into the engine and gives us an opportunity to finally play them. Or make them harder and create "What if?" scenarios.On the other hand, the tool doesn’t offer you a lot of resources, even in early access. I’m sure there will be a lot of content added with future updates, but you’re still limited by what you can actually use to build your levels. I understand the ability to import your own creations might create all kinds of copyright issues, but I still think there should be some kind of editor included in the package.

But its not listed as one on steam which is not fair towards the customers buying something that's listed as a initial release. _childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately my review couldn't fit in Steam's character limit, so I'll be doing a shorter version. If you want to see the full thing check the game's discussion forum on steam, it addresses everything i want added in the game and also the stuff i think should be on high priority.I'm a huge Zelda fan and a huge Mario Maker fan, so you might imagine my excitement when Steam recommends me a game called "Super Dungeon Maker" for an affordable price. I've played the game for a while and it's pretty fun. The online levels people have made are already really good and they fit perfectly into the Zelda vibe (well, at least some of them), but there's still a lot missing.At the time of writing, Super Dungeon Maker has the following main items (as in, items used for exploration purposes that you can use):These items are cool and all, but a lot of them are missing, mostly the bow and arrow and boomerang, and although the grappling hook can hit switches and paralyzes enemies just like the boomerang, having these items increase the creativity of the levels by a lot, and honestly this same logic goes for most of the game. It's great, but missing things.For instance, your character automatically starts with a sword. What if level creators could choose to remove it initially and put it on a chest later on? or heck, not even use it at all. It's these type of stuff that i think would benefit the game immensely, and honestly, it has a potential to be one of the best maker-type games out there.Because the devs are apparently working on a switch port, which is really cool, don't get me wrong, but seeing at least signs that they're alive and what they're working on would be great. The only reason we know they're still working on it is because they respond to the questions in the discussion forum on steamThe game is being developed mainly by two people. Yes that's right. TWO. People. The amount of work they've done is nothing short of impressive, but i still think it's important to talk about the game's problems or things that should be added/fixed, because to me, listening to the community's opinion is the most important part of game development, and so far they seem to be adding a lot of stuff through content update, having introduced 3 bosses already with a fourth one already implemented but not placeable on the level editor. I honestly think no one is allowed to criticize them as "lazy" or "irresponsible with time" considering the amount of updates this game already received and the fact they're porting this to the Nintendo Switch. It's honestly impressive what they did here.This game is worth your money, especially because a lot of the community made levels are really good, but keep in mind it'll take a long, long time before this game becomes the masterpiece it can and, should the developers keep working on it, definitely will be.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished making my first major dungeon.  This game, both in game and in editor is too glitchy for a 1.0 release, but most of it can be worked around.  I'm guessing it was getting patched as I was working on it as some of the glitchiness (like with permanent staircase removals) stopped happening.There are also limited dev options but that is true of most game-maker games...that's why you are playing the Zelda dungeon maker instead of building dungeons from the ground up in Game Maker (which is a lot more work and a lot more things going wrong).  You lose versatility for the sake of efficiency.  This is still a lot more robust than trying to make maps in Timesplitters or something similar.  A good designer can definitely still express unique and interesting ideas with this, but on the surface a basic dungeon is going to feel the same as a lot of others.It lacks rewards for the player, making it difficult to add hidden or optional sections as there isn't much reason to explore.  Some kind of in game economy would fix this, even just a simple score board that shows how many rupees (or it's equivalent) a player got with maybe a few other metrics.  I would love to have this because I want to have the ability to put in more optional content, places where I would stick harder puzzles or tougher encounters that might be a roadblock for players otherwise.  Plus, it's Zelda, exploration is a key part of the fun and there isn't a great way to encourage it.Tool-wise, it definitely could use some features, notably a better fill system, the ability to select select, drag, and copy/paste multiple tiles at once (I was really surprised this isn't in the game tbh), and the ability to 'save' what you copied to reduce future work.  Dungeon wise, I would like the ability to control individual sound effects and lighting changes with triggers.  Just these two changes would allow for a far greater variety in the feel of dungeons and would extend the shelf-life a ton with the game, and since they are just aesthetic, it wouldn't over complicate the basic dungeon making for the average user.  These should be easier asks than adding, for instance, another boss monster type.I'm leaving a positive review as I have wanted a proper Zelda dungeon maker for years and this does deliver that, but the appeal is limited right now.  As I noted above, unless you are invested and work well with limitations, you probably aren't going to have a masterpiece dungeon pop out in front of you, and playing random dungeons has limited appeal.  While some dungeons can be excellent, this isn't Mario Maker where you are looking at a 5 minute commitment usually, so playing even one mediocre stage feels like a lot and creators also have to put in more work to make something passably fun.  What this means is, you'll be playing more rough than diamonds.BOTTOM LINE (TLDR): If you like Zelda dungeons and have ever wanted to make your own (and/or are worried about Nintendo's ability to keep this style going), go ahead and dive in!  The devs seem to still be putting in patches and features.  It is very close to being 'good', frustratingly so even, but right now it is just 'okay'.  With some updates, this could be great.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game and has plenty of potential, but some of the bugs in the dungeon creator are just too much to handle. I played this game for about half a week before I just had to tell myself to stop and wait for them to patch out these bugs. I was excited to find a old school Zelda/Mario Maker game but was a little let down in the end. The combat is pretty smooth and I have made several levels that I am proud of, but there really isn't any incentive to play other creators stuff. There is no reward other than the feeling of beating a dungeon, and that gets tiring very quickly. There are some good levels people have made, but the game is mostly filled with "my first dungeon" levels, and I can only play so many bad dungeons in one sitting. Another thing is how it feels like you have so much creativity and so little at the same time in the games current state. I will think of an idea to implement in my dungeon and attempt to create it only to realize it is just not possible with the tools available or because the game bugs out. There is a small number of things this game does well with such as the combat as mentioned previously, it definitely has that old top down Zelda combat down, but there are only a handful of bosses and fighting them can get repetitive. I would recommend this game but keep it on your wishlist until more content becomes available or you will struggle to have fun after the first week of playing. Will definitely return to this game when it works some bugs out and adds more reasons to play other creators dungeons.Edit: The game has gotten better. I still check in on it after a few updates. The level builder has gotten less buggy and I have made several new levels since my last review. The builder mode could use some more QOL updates like multi-select or being able to drag and place a trail of objects. Other than that my only complaint now is the level player. There are currently tabs to look at hot levels, top levels, new levels, and a search option. There is no place to see your currently uploaded level to check how many plays or how many hearts they got. This leads me to my next complaint. There still is not really an incentive to upload levels or play them for that matter. Once you upload a level it will get a couple plays, maybe a heart or two but no reward for creating an amazing level. A solution to this is if as you got more hearts on levels you unlocked more characters or pets, or more level objects or themes, but in its current state there is not anything. Also, there is still no incentive to play other creators levels. A similar system as mentioned before could be implemented into a golden egg shop or something because you get a golden egg once you complete a level. Definitely still recommend keeping an eye on this game cause it has potential.

_childDocuments_.review: As a rabid enjoyer of Nintendo's Mario Maker 2 (I made an entire 8 world set of levels) this game has quickly become an equal obsession.Super Dungeon Maker is an underdog with a chicken as its protagonist.  Entering the ring for the very first time, and seemingly out of nowhere Super Dungeon Maker easily knocks out every contender in the level builder genre especially among other dungeon builders.Super Dungeon Maker relies on its bouncy, colorful, retro graphics, and beginner friendly UI to clear itself a place in the genre. There are many different themes you can give your levels, there's sure to be something you like. A decent set of power-ups can turn the most perilous levels into cake walks or your very own Metroidvania. A large roster of original enemies and fresh takes on tropes also make their way into this builder.But unfortunately just like any underdog that enters the ring they're bound to have bruises.Super Dungeon Maker relies on no pre-existing IP giving a lot of flexibility which it is able to harness to some extent. But sadly as I see it this gem is yet unpolished, a large rough cut emerald without shine. Many enemies you may expect to find in the level editor are simply absent or are unable to have a trait edited to make them perfect for your level. Another strange absence is the lack of magic or ranged attacks or even weapon variety.  Between the pitiful two characters you can play as both are stuck with the same simple sword that only boasts only two attacks. In conclusion, Super Dungeon Maker has done great carving out a space in the genre with its graphics and UI alone my only hope is that it can fill the space. Also play it, it's fun!(P.S. And there should be at least a spear and a bow)

_childDocuments_.review: I originally posted this as a positive review, but after learning that this game was abandoned and Quest Master exists, I've decided to change it.I don't think the two game studios are connected. The enemy variety isn't very good, and the three bosses here all are ripped off straight from ALttP and Link's Awakening (Wormeon is so shameless a Moldorm ripoff I'm surprised it's legal)But even more so this game heavily lacks in puzzle variety. You have sliding block puzzles, button puzzles, and color switches, but that's about it. No torch puzzles, gem switches, etc. Half of the maps I've either made or played suffer heavily in puzzle variety and are almost always just combat gauntlets.If you want this game, buy it with Quest Master. _childDocuments_.review: After having spent a decent amount of time in the Editor now, I can safely say that the foundation to build a great dungeon is all there, but there are tons of features and improvements this game needs before it can truly become the best version of itself. [!] = Priority- More Channels for Triggers [[!]] - Global Channels that work across all floors- Summoning Fink to your current position in the Editor [!] - Playtest Mode (Select powerups to start with in the Editor so you dont have to place them down all the time)- Custom Health + Heart Containers as Powerups [!] - More collectibles that serve as rewards (similiar to coins in Mario) in order to give creators more possibilties for rewarding the player for exploration [!] - More Themes- Make Themes floor-specific (currently you have to stick with 1 theme for the entire dungeon)- Some Themes have siginificantly better decoration than others (forest > beach), so overhaul them- or what I would personally want to see: make all assets usable regardless of theme (in this case theme would only change the wall design)- NPCs and readable signs so the creator can add worldbuilding and story to their dungeons, which would be huge [!]- More enemy variety (currently most enemies dont do much and there arent a lot of enemies the creator can choose from)EDIT: After leaving the game untouched for about 3 months and coming back to it, barely anything has changed. Old bugs reported months ago are still there and there is a lack of new features or improvement of existing ones. Behavior of certain objects, triggers and switches is not clearly communicated, which forces you to guess, experiment, or ask someone to find out.When I first bought the game, I recommended it because it seemed like it could turn into something really great. But now after 3 months, which is a long time in terms of development, I see that barely anything has changed. You may have a great experience the first 30 hours of playing the game, but it gets very limitting and restrictive very fast, which is the main issue of the game.The game tries too hard to be a low-budget Zelda Maker instead of doing it's own thing. Features that would just make sense are traded in for less-logical options, simply because "thats what it's like in the Zelda games".I still think the game has great potential, I just don't see the devs trying to realize that potential, which is why I've changed my opinon to not recommending the game. Ultimately you will only waste your time, longing for more, but not being able to get it.

_childDocuments_.review: The developers of this game (afaik it's just 2 people) quickly patched some of my initial gripes and added a needed  push-puzzle-mechanic to the game, to add a bit of polish and variety to an already fun game. So I decided to refresh my review and change it to: .----I finished building my first dungeon, lovingly called "Listoric's Mini Maze" (ID 1872276), after 17 hours(!) of playtime and I basically put every mechanic I could think of into it. I hummed to the theme of my dungeon and enjoyed my time being creative AND I also found myself wanting to play more Super Dungeon Maker as soon as I sat down at my PC. If you overcome the small few hurdles the game throws at you, it's already an enjoyable time.The dungeon creator is (still) clunky to use, but also still easy to understand. So placing and creating your rooms and puzzles can be done quickly, even though I still wish the UI would be easier to use. Testing the dungeon is also a drag at times. The bigger your dungeon get's, the more often you need to place the required items (bomb, shield, grappling hook, etc.) next to your starting location, just to speed up the test. After dozens of tests on different parts of my dungeon, I found items laying around where they didn't belong, just because I forgot to delete them after testing my puzzles. Same goes for finding and grabbing your chicken everytime you spent a few good minutes in the creator. Not to mention bugs, unintuitive use of some items and the general wish for more options and easier access.Quite a few bugs and clunky controls for your player character as well left me frustrated at times, with some problems mentioned in the initial review below still existing ofc. It's software that needs time.Yet, I spent hours planning, refining and decorating my dungeon. Same goes for puzzles and traps, there are few options available, but with clever placement you can add puzzles in various difficulties for every item you acquire. It's really fun to test things out, create new rooms and try to get the most out of the limited objects you have in your arsenal. Generally it's difficult to tell if the early access problems are a dealbreaker for you or not. After some time you'll get used to the controls, you'll be as frustrated at little things like I was, but you'll love creating your dungeon. I spent 17 hours after the first few fixes in the editor just on my first dungeon and enjoyed the time spent immensly. <3So again, even though it's rough around the edges: . ------ Original Review ------Super Dungeon Maker is a cute dungoen editor with nostalgic look, easy to use tools and a promising outlook from the get go. The game welcomes you in a small town with cute characters that explain almost everything you need to know to start your own dungeon building adventure. The onboarding is well done and entertaining, which is quite refreshing. You can not only create your own dungeon, but explore the village and the nearby dungeons. If you like, you can even jump into community creations right from the start. While all of this sounds great in general, the very short list of placeable items, as well as the clunky controls within the editor and with your hero character as well, quickly dampen the great initial impression.Here is a quick breakdown of the good and bad that Super Dungeon Maker has to offer on day 1 of early access:The positives are easy to list, they are few and fine. It's exactly what you'd expect from the screenshots and videos.------Unfortunately, the negatives are easy to spot once you actually play the game and create your first dungeon. I know it's earliest access, but as soon as it's released with a price tag, people should be aware what they spend their money on.[In my initial review I gave examples and ideas how to improve the game here, but I cut it out as my edited is deemed to long by steam :3]I'm most definitely not the first one to suggest some of the features or highlight those issues, so to be quite frank, I fear there might be an underlying problem with the games direction or understanding of what's really fun about crawling a dungeon. It's close to what I'd imagine it to be and looks promising though.It's said to release in a few months, but as some flaws seem very apparent, so much so that it almost seems like they are working around limitations that are set up by themselves, I just fear that this great and fun idea is not going to live up to it's potential. So yeah, I'm kinda torn.It's super difficult to create software, yet alone a great game, and as of right now, the cons outweigh the pros by a very slight margin. It is a fun game though.Best of luck und Grüße aus Nürnberg! <3

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone who has played The Link's Awakening remake on Switch knows that one of the new additions to that game is the ability to create dungeons. Well, kinda. The problem with that system is that you're limited to the dungeon rooms in Link's Awakening only, so while you can mess with different layouts of the dungeon. there's not the same amount of customization as we would've hoped. And then there's also the issue where you can only share dungeons locally with friends through Amiibo, which is completely lame. Here's where Super Dungeon Maker comes in.This game is heavily inspired by TLoZ, and the writing is very self aware of it. The main character is a chicken called Fink. This game gives you the tools to create dungeons any way you see fit by allowing you to actually determine the boundary of each room with different types of floor tiles, walls and different types of doors. In addition to small keys and the large key, you can also gain access to a Shield, Infinite Bombs, a Hookshot, Feathers to help you dodge attacks and roll over certain gaps and Flippers which allow you to swim. There are also lots of different decorations which changes depending on which biome you use. Each Biome also has one unique floor tile, like Quicksand for the Beach, Lava for the Volcano, Ice for the Tundra. On top of all that, you can also upload and share dungeons you create online for other players to enjoy.Here's the problem though. The developers have stopped supporting this game; a lot of the planned updates that were promised ARE NO LONGER going to be happening. That means we are going to be losing out on Story Mode, any new biomes, new dungeon items, etc. Plus in it's current state, the game still has various bugs in it, especially the Switch version. You're better off spending your money on Quest Master; that game is in early access, BUT, the developers are constantly updating the game on an almost weekly basis and is set for a full release at the end of the year. The developers are continuing to put their heart and soul into Quest Master and it shows between the music, amazing sprite art and the fact that they keep updating the game. Personally I can't wait to see what the full release looks like. Overall, this game was a good attempt but you're better off just getting Quest Master instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Having enjoyed games of this type before, such as Mario Maker, I just had to try this out, especially since Nintendo doesn't seem to want to give us a Zelda Maker. Oh well. Even though there aren't many assets available yet, considering this is early access, there is still quite a lot you can do, and I am very excited to see what new features will be added down the road. The tutorial dungeons are pretty fun and the UI is fairly straightforward. I ran into a little problem once trying to delete a door I accidentally placed in the middle of a room, but aside from that one thing, everything's been pretty smooth so far. This definitely captures the feel of Link to the Past, and if you're going to model your game on Zelda, you can't go wrong taking inspiration from the most popular top-down Zelda ever made.If I were to change anything, I think I might prefer if using the shield item locked your facing so you could strafe, or just make the shield a passive like Link's shield, rather than requiring a button press. Either one of those two ideas I think would be an improvement. I'm hoping that in the future, money can be added and shops can be placed in dungeons, just so there can be more variety to drops/pickups than just hearts.I'd give this an easy 4/5 if you're into "maker" style games. If you're just looking to play user-created dungeons, I think I'd still give this a solid 3.5/5, maybe 4/5. It's hard to give something a full 5/5 while it's still in early access, just because I have no idea how much this might change before the final product, but right now, Firechick seems to know what they're doing.

_childDocuments_.review: Super Dungeon Maker is a wonderfully cozy, creative, and nostalgically fun 2D dungeon designing game created by a team of two talented developers with a passion for gameplay and creativity that is inspired by the Legend of Zelda.  While there are a few minor shortcomings, they pale in comparison to the praise I want to give this game and its developers. The devs set out to simply make a good 2D dungeon designer game filled with love and respect for it’s inspirational source, which I think they did in spades. The devs also are very active in the community responding to bugs and feature requests and they've posted a nice Feature Map for new content coming soon. The game itself is delightfully charming and scratches an itch I've had for a long time about wanting to create Zelda-like dungeons. The dungeon designer itself is a fairly impressive and powerful tool that can be used to create some truly imaginative creations. In large part, the amount of  positive feelings I have for this game (as well as my eagerness to overlook its shortcomings) is due to how well I think they implemented the dungeon designer. It's a great foundational framework that I know future updates will only improve upon. All in all, I've fallen in love with Super Dungeon Maker and can't wait to watch the community and the game itself grow. I would say I Highly Recommend Super Dungeon Maker for anyone that's a fan of 2D Zelda games, cozy games, creating dungeons, practicing level design, or simply just supporting two great indie game developers! _childDocuments_.review: Thank you developers for the amazing game and key!Booting the game, it looks very simplistic and pretty. You're immediately thrown inside a dungeon that also serves as a tutorial. The first dungeon tutorial is straightforward and easy to understand with simple UI. The art style immediately clicks. The spriteworks and animation is done very nicely.The HUB area looks really nice, and the few developer-made dungeon serves as a good playground for those who feels like playing something immediately in the base game without jumping in the internet. The sandbox is an interesting way to serve as a tutorial for the building mode. Having the tutorial served like this is definitely an effective way to make players not bored by a pile of text, but it would still be nice to have an optional traditional help button in the corner or something to help reminding players of each function when they're back into building or help confused players in the beginning. Channel buttons and triggers are especially confusing for beginners in creation tools if they're trying to build more complex dungeon and deserve its own help section.I tried both keyboard+mouse and controller, it both works nicely with the game. The controller also transitioned really smoothly if you change control in between- it does surprise me a bit. I didn't expect the controller option is also very friendly with the dungeon making controls, so it does come as a very pleasant surprise. Playing in the dungeon with a controller also feels very good, each button feels so natural especially when you're doing dodge roll and shielding.The options I'm having during a dungeon making is actually massive, to my surprise. With every map having its own kind of gimmick and not just a reskin, which amazes me. It does offer more variety in dungeon puzzle making. There are so many options to try. Decorating a dungeon is actually my favorite thing to do because of how easy and fun it is do drag and drop pretty stuffs into the room.Looking for people's dungeons online is also made very easy. You can search with both title, ID, and even filter things with tags.The only major problem I'm having is the lack of select button, copy, cut, and paste mode during building. I always end up mispressing a thing or two because a normal select option doesn't exist. You always press an object even when you're planning to only select thing. So when you're trying to select something you've made if you're not doing it on the right area you just end up accidentally creating a new thing or so. It's mainly difficult especially if you're changing between chat program like Discord back into the game. These buttons should also help with certain stuffs like moving certain rooms; as for now I have to move things one by one or recreate things if I want to do that. This option could be placed in the upper part of the object tools or so.Another suggestion I could add is overlay floor map button during building. I'd love to see where the player would fall down if I were to make a pit. I accidentally made a pit that put the player into one of my last areas. This overlay could work like animation onion skin layering. A toogle next to the floor list would be nice.Regardless, I'm having great time building dungeons with the tools. I thought I would get confused on how to create puzzles and mechanics, but I'm never been more glad to be proven wrong! Creating secret rooms and decorating things have been a blast. I also can modify boss battles and their second and third phases.All in all, Super Dungeon Maker is overall a solid Dungeon Maker game people could've dreamt of. I love all the references the developers put into the game and having a great time with it. For the price, everyone who can't get enough for the classic ol' game boy TLoZ should check it out. There's also seems like more to come with the updates, and I'm excited to see what's coming for this title!

_childDocuments_.review: Let me tell you my story.I spent like 1-2 hours learning how to use the build mode because this game's 'tutorial' (which is the tiny bird sandbox on the game's hub area that you could easily miss) is dog water.  The tutorial just consisted of bird NPCs shoving a vague wall of text at your face expecting you to figure it out.  Still I pushed on and had to trial and error + experiment just so I could get a grasp on how to start building a dungeon.So I spent like 5+ hours crafting the most perfect masterpiece of a dungeon.  Powering through the game's clunkiness, bugs, and crashes (I crashed like 6 times making a single dungeon).  Until I finally finished my work of art.  I was so proud and I uploaded it to the world.  Played some other people's pathetic dungeons before heading to bed.  The next day I wake up, excited to see if my hard work was recognized.  I booted up my game.  Looked at the number of gamers that played my awesome level and...One person played it...At least they liked it.REVIEWI would wait and keep an eye on this game instead of buying.  This game feels like early access more than an actual release.  There were plenty of bugs and crashes that I experienced that are annoying, especially if you don't save.  The gameplay was mid and felt... off.  Like the movement and animations just felt wrong and I don't know why.  Plus there is no punishment for dying or resetting so there is no real danger in this game.Music and art used in the game is nothing crazy.  It's not bad but its not particularly unique or good.There is not enough content, assets, and enemies in this game to enjoy it after playing a few dungeons.  You'll feel like you've experienced it all after a bit.  There is little to no difference between the dungeon environments aside from looks and a few tile changes.Combat in this game was either too easy + boring or just annoying.  Example you can stunlock pretty much any enemy if they're against a wall.  Then there is the annoying spear plant enemy that always dodges back when you get close, requiring too much of a commitment to try and kill when you most likely have other things to worry about and do.Bosses are actually pretty alright for the most part.  But there are only 3 of them so don't expect much variety.Items are ok-ish.  -The hookshot is great, you can use it to stun enemies and traverse obstacles.-Bombs are pretty boring.  Rarely useful in killing enemies (They don't seem to do more DMG than a simple sword swing). Only really useful to open paths.-The dodge feathers are actually busted.  They make combat and obstacles 10x easier.  You can dodge through pretty much anything its stupid.  They also make traveling faster.-Flippers are ok, they're just uninspired and not very interactive.  You find flippers and its just like 'hey, you can move through water now.' and I'm like 'wow alright'.-The shield has potential but I still think its lame.  You can use it to block projectiles and some other stuff but the worst part about it is that you can't strafe or back pedal with it.  Whatever direction you move in is where the shield points making you extremely vulnerable to anything that isn't in front of you.Finally, the worst thing about this game is its online dungeon system, the main selling point of the game.Searching by 'hot' just straight up doesn't work lmao.You can search by 'top rated' but as far as I'm aware this is always limited to an 'all time' range with no way to filter by week or month.Then there is the chaos that is 'new' which works as intended but is also where 99% of inspiring gamer dungeons will be.So unless you advertise your dungeon on reddit or have a title like 'sussy amogus', next to nobody is going to play your dungeon.The game also lacks any system like '100 Mario Challenge' to help give traction to new dungeons that are made.It also lacks player profiles to check out other dungeons made by the same creator.Overall, game doesn't have too much to offer.  Either wait for some real big updates or just buy when on sale.

DO NOT BUY THIS, even if it's on sale. it's a terrible player experience. -there is a positive from the map issue, forcing map makers to develop more focused and well paced dungeons that do not rely on the player referencing the map. I have played a few user maps that are like this... they do exist, but it's sometimes hard to find experiences like those.-if you fix the map issue, the lack of official dungeons would not be an issue. solving one iisue essentially fixes the other.-there are bugs, but they werent an issue.-no message/text making(the reasoning is understandable, but still a negative)With all that said... devs looking to use this as a prototyping tool, just grab solasta or original sin 2 orrrr nwn enhanced edition if your looking to develop dungeons with story or campaigns as a whole. Those are all great for prototyping/conceptualizing for your own projects/work.SHORT AND SIMPLE:this is a great tool for developers for prototyping purposes, and a horrible game for players.there are two issues...THE MAP:-no player location indicator/icon makes all larger/complex dungeons unplayable. you WILL get lost and get frustrated.-you can tough it out by mapping the dungeons yourself on paper... but players should be expected to do that if there is a map in the game. -this should have been the first thing fixed. if this was a vision/ideological decision on the developers part... dude, just add an optional toggle for a player map indication with a parentheical note stating the the "intended experience is would the player icon on the map..." or whatever. -this alone ruins the player experience as this game is 90% user dungeons(most being large and rediculously complex).-there is a player icon/indicator when building, so it can be done... why is it not a thing in the general play experience.LACK OF OFFICIAL DUNGEONS:-to be honest, if you fix the map issue... this would not even be an issue being that the map issue would make all user dungeons more playable. that alone would rule this game in a more "content heavy" player experience. but, with the map issue, official content would allow players to enjoy atleast a little more than a few fun dungeons.-it's stated that the lack of official content is due to the dev wanting to focus on the tools. buuuut, official dungeons could be use to demonstrate key tool features(being that the dev would know the tools function and limitations thus resulting the probably the best dungeon crawling experience for players).look, theres a lot more I could say about these two issues but after the initial version of my review was wiped... eh. VERDICT:-for devs looking to prototype, this is great.-for players... without a USABLE map... DO NOT BUY THIS, even if it's on sale. it's a terrible player experience. -there is a positive from the map issue, forcing map makers to develop more focused and well paced dungeons that do not rely on the player referencing the map. _childDocuments_.review: I've just dipped my toes into the world of Super Dungeon Maker, and I've got to say, I'm absolutely stoked about it! I'm old enough to have some serious nostalgia for the original Zelda games on NES and SNES. So, you can imagine my excitement when I heard about this game.Super Dungeon Maker is everything I wished for and more. It's like Nintendo heard my prayers for a Zelda maker and handed it to FireChick to make our dreams come true. Building dungeons, crafting adventures—it's like stepping into the shoes of Link himself.What makes this game truly shine is the community aspect. The folks at FireChick aren't just making a game; they're fostering a creative haven. The updates and constant interaction with the players show they genuinely care about making Super Dungeon Maker the best it can be.I can't help but wonder what surprises FireChick has up their sleeves for this gem in the future. The potential here is boundless, and I'm excited to be part of the journey.In a nutshell, if you're a fan of classic Zelda games and you love getting your creative juices flowing, Super Dungeon Maker is a must-try. _childDocuments_.review: In it's current state, this game is well worth it's price tag, and it has endless potential. I can't help but wonder what some of my favorite creators from Mario Maker 2 could do with this game, especially those with a knack for making puzzle-based levels. As far as I'm concerned, this IS the definitive Zelda Maker game that Nintendo may very well never give us, bc the demand is too high and they like to be mysterious and unpredictable, or something. Growing the Super Dungeon Maker community to help this game reach even more talented creators will have the greatest impact of all. I feel like creating good, puzzling Zelda-style dungeons might be a bit trickier than say, a typical MM2 level, but this game absolutely offers all the right tools to do it, and it couldn't be more user friendly. All that said, there are 2 things that I would ask of the devs to make this game better, imo. 1) More baddies. Some new bosses and sub-bosses at the very least, though I feel that whole department is a bit lacking. And even more importantly, 2) Something that rewards exploration, like finding an optional hidden area that's easy to miss. Something non-essential to beating the dungeon but cool to find, much like the heart pieces in Zelda games. In fact, extra heart containers would do just fine really. Or it could be a potion to replenish hearts or get a temporary buff (speed, invincibility, etc). It could be a sword upgrade (2x dmg). Just some bonus or assortment of them to say, da-da-da, look what you found! Otherwise, there's not much incentive to add any little hidden nooks and crannies when making a level, or try to find them when playing one. That's actually one pretty key ingredient that's missing from this formula, with this being such a very top-down-Zelda-inspired game, and one that it absolutely NEEDS. But I feel it would also greatly benefit from the addition of some new enemies, bosses especially. Still, great game! Hope it continues to grow!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome. Imagine being able to create your own Zelda-like dungeons with a proper UI. It feels like a perfect blend between something like Super Mario Maker and an action RPG.First of all, the art style is fun. The bright colors and cartoony animations have a lot of life to them. The enemies and our main character all are drawn in a signature art style for this game. While sometimes I think the animations could use more frames to improve their smoothness, notably Fink's spin attack, overall, the looks are very polished.Secondly, the dungeon designer itself is quite intuitive to use. If you have a mouse and keyboard, you can be quite dangerous with the editor. It's very easy to click and drag to draw enormous rooms full of tiles. That said, there are a few bugs here and there, but it seems like the team is actively fixing those as I write this.Finally, there is proper online support for sharing dungeons, unlike earlier betas of this game. I can easily go and find new dungeons to play by entering the Dungeon Eggspedia area and browsing. While it doesn't have a ton of filters or other ways to sift through the loads of levels, there is potential for that kind of functionality to be added.I think what this has going for it the most is potential. There are a few dungeon themes, monsters, and other features yet to be added. Sadly, though this game is a full release, it does still feel a bit alpha at times due to the bugs and somewhat limited dungeon-building variety. If you're OK with that, you will love everything else about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Take all critique with a grain of salt. As of writing this review, this game is still in Early Access, which means that bugs are still being worked out and features are still being added. Is the game *currently* worth the price of admission? Yes. Would I still like to see more, before calling this game 'complete'? Absolutely. My family has left feedback with the developers, asking for several bugs to be addressed and several key power-ups to be added. The devs are a small team and they work on patches and expansions slowly. (I don't fault them for that, I'm just stating it, so it's known.) Every power-up that's been implemented, so far, has been implemented well. There are bombs, swim flippers, a hookshot, a shield, a roc's feather... but there's no bow and arrow. There are no rupees to collect or spend. There's no ocarina/recorder.What's more, there are very few enemies, as compared to a 'complete' Zelda-like game, and even fewer bosses. At present, there are 3 boss types and—by the time you've filled up 3 dungeons' worth of enemies—you'll start to get bored of fighting the same creature types over and over.The ability to craft puzzles, however, is where this level designer shines. There's a good variety of different switch trigger types, including blue/red barrier switches, floor switches, weighted floor switches, movable blocks, rope-pull switches, levers, bombable blocks, keyhole blocks, and sliding ice blocks. These can all be strung together to create simple or complex traversal puzzles to enrich your dungeons.All-in-all, I've spent over 100 hours creating dungeons for my family and the world to enjoy. Again, it's well worth the price of admission.I think the most elegant solution to improving the game variety would be to add a couple more item pick-ups necessary to make this feel like a more 'complete' Zelda-like game, and to increase the variety of enemy types that have weakness to those new items. With additional enemies that were weak to arrows, weak to bombs, weak to some musical instrument, that could have their own weapons reflected back by the shield (or by an upgraded mirror shield), etc... it would add that strategic combat element of dungeon delving which is currently lacking.The devs have been highly receptive to feedback, so I look forward to seeing what gets added in months to come.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of games like Super Mario Maker, and are a Zelda fan as well, then this game just might be for you. While it's clear of the games it is parodying, it does offer something that a lot of people have requested in Zelda titles, and that is dungeons the player can make themselves.The tools that are currently in the game have a lot of functionality and interact fairly well with each other offering many ways to create puzzles with a lot of dimension, and the developers are actively adding even more to this game for even more possibilities.The user interface seems quite easy to follow and intuitive, the trigger events (buttons, switches and stuff like that) are also quite easy to understand and seem to work well from what I've experimented with so far.The current enemies have easy to understand patterns and by themselves can be easy to take down, but of course in groups can be challenging, and possibly more so depending on how a dungeon maker creates their dungeon. The bosses themselves are actually quite fun to implement and fight, a few times it was quite challenging to fight them (in a good way) depending on how I made the boss room.For any potential negatives for the game, it's mostly nitpicks and little things. Mostly it's a request for current items to have more interaction with other things or certain behaviors to be slightly different (and of course more things to have/do). (As a suggestion for the developers, cause I know you will read this, perhaps you could implement for bombs a higher bomb count when you collect more bombs, so when you get 2 bombs, you can place up to 2.)In summary, there was and still is a lot of love being put into this game and I would highly recommend it for people who like to create dungeons or simply enjoy the dungeons created by others. It is in open Beta and not many people know about the game right now, but based on the quality of the current content and the developers reception to feedback, I think this game has the potential to be quite popular and successful.
_childDocuments_.name: Super Dungeon Maker

_childDocuments_.review: I personally really think this game has a great concept, its still early on for it so I expect that much will be added and changed over time as it is further developed, so far I haven't played it very much but only have one complaint, that complaint being the lack of ability to mix and match between themes, for instance if I wanted to make a jungle dungeon where the lower levels are frozen, or use the fog tiles in an ice dungeon, making it possible to utilize multiple themes in a single dungeon would greatly expand the possibilities of what someone could make. beyond that small nitpick, it has a lot of potential and I am looking forward to seeing this game grow.If you enjoy games like Zelda A Link to the Past / Four Swords, you will probably love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I ended up buying this for my Steam Deck (runs great, and handheld is ideal!) It's great fun and I could easily spend many hours playing dungeons from the community and making my own. It is somewhat barebones at the moment - all the Zelda dungeon essentials are there (Link to the Past seems to be the most heavily borrowed from-title, understandably), but it doesn't have the "embarrassment of riches with endless things to try out and be delighted by" feeling of the Mario Makers. I'm particularly disappointed by a lack of variety and amount of enemies. The controls are also not quite as tight and polished as a Zelda game, but that's to be expected given Nintendo has always been the reigning king at that stuff.It's still "Early Access" though (obviously). My understanding is that the developers are committed to making this title as great as can be, are listening to feedback from the community, and are committing to a roadmap for plentiful updates with added elements, themes, enemies, etc. I'm guessing they would be rewarded for this effort by many more people buying the title over time as cool new things get added.This is probably pie-in-the-sky considering the current state of things to be improved on, but I would also greatly wish for the ability to have several dungeons strung together into a "world", or even make a huge fully-interconnected world. I understand that adding an overworld editor to the game would probably be too big of an effort for this release, but even if there's just a dungeon selection screen, how cool would it be if you could have your player move freely between 7 different dungeons you've created, all with different themes and challenges, as they gain skills and open up new places to explore gradually? Then you could really make your own interesting 4-5 hour Zelda-like experience.There's also a certain kind of "dynamic" feeling to creating levels in Mario Maker that means you can make a level, and then be gob-smacked by the results when you play it yourself as different level elements play off each other in surprising ways. But there's not much like that here. They need to have spontaneously dynamic stuff happen in levels. For example, lighting a bat on fire with an arrow that's passed through a torch, and then the bat flapping around fast and lighting other things on fire as chaos breaks out would be cool as hell and give more than just a basic Zelda clone feeling. Or skeleton enemies hurling bones at you, but their bones can trigger switches, extinguish torches, or damage other enemies upon contact. You could set up a cool puzzle-boss fight where the player has to damage the boss by positioning it in the way of bones being thrown. There could be hundreds of little interactions like that. Different level elements need to be combinable and interact with one another for fluid and unexpected gameplay.All in all, though, I'm excited for this game and think it's highly worth supporting this developer on their progress.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simple: you can either play or create dungeons made by you/other people. There is not real progression, so don't expect anything more than that. There are some dev-made dungeons though.If you ever wanted to try designing a 2-D Zel-... "Adventure game" dungeon in a super easy/intuitive/Mariomaker-esque manner, this game delivers exceptionally well. I will say that it's obvious this game is in early access, as I ran into a number of bugs (often with doorways) while editing. Also, there were many times where I thought a certain interaction would make sense/be cool to explore (i.e. guiding a beamos to hit a switch, using jars to break other jars, blowing up jars with bombs, etc.) only to find it didn't quite work out. However, with what is currently implemented I found more than enough creative material to create a relatively large dungeon. I'd say it'd start getting repetitive during my 3rd or 4th dungeon, but I haven't played that much yet. It's perfectly reasonable for Early Access. Regardless, I found this game because I was feeling the itch to see if there was software to craft a Zeld-... "Adventure game" dungeon, and this game scratched it beautifully.I haven't played other people's stuff much yet, but I assume since there are only so many things currently able to be used that the enemies and puzzles could get repetitive, but that ultimately depends on the creativity of the dungeon designers. However, from playtesting my dungeon, all the items were smooth to use and felt very polished. I am very excited to see how this game evolves through development as more options and interactions are added.

_childDocuments_.review: There's a mix of things I like and things I feel could be better, but overall I'd say it's a fun little dungeon maker.Starting with the positive, I'm loving the art style, though the chicken is a bit funky to play and is so big I have trouble figuring out where exactly is good positioning to not get hit by floor spikes. There's a few dungeons on the overworld you can play through, but most of the dungeon content is user generated, and there's a lot of creative dungeons out there.For me the real fun is creating the dungeons, though. I've had a lot of fun just painting a bunch of random floors, cleaning them up into more logical rooms, and then creating a path of progress to the end. You can make pits that drop to lower floors, or some minor platforming using the dodge roll item, a maze controlled by the switch that raises and lowers colored tiles to defeat all the enemies and open the door.That said, there are a few things missing:- Bosses aren't a thing as of writing this. I've read they're planning some kind of visual scripting method of creating boss behavior and attack patterns, which would really spice things up knowing that even if you've fought a particular boss before, it won't behave the same in different dungeons.- There's no "pressure plate" object or anything to make a type of puzzle requiring pushing something into a specific spot. Not a glaring issue, but would add more options to what rooms you can put in a dungeon.- No ranged items outside of grapple/hookshot. Maybe it's more my personal taste and might not be on the table considering the controls need to be friendly enough to work on a Switch, but I like bows and arrows, man.I'd also like to be able to tweak the enemies that are already in the game. As of now, the only input you have on baddies is where they stand when you enter the room. It'd be nice if they had a submenu to tweak their health/damage and speed or something. Nobody would blink at a little fly that dies in one hit. But what if you lost a full heart when it flew at you going mach 5? Unfair, maybe. But it's different.Overall, I like what's there, the eventual implementation of bosses will make it far better, and some more puzzle interactions would go a long way.

_childDocuments_.review: Super Dungeon Maker or 'SDM' is a dungeon builder/crawler designed to be very easy to get into but still offer a good degree of complexity. You can create/play/share your creations with others using the online dungeon finder. Dungeons can be made in less than 5 mins or more than 5 hours, your creativity and time is all you need.  Don't like building dungeons but just wanna play, well there's that option too.The game is currently in EA, there are bugs but for the most part the game is solid. Devs are very active listening to the community, adding features and fixing bugs. So what are you waiting for, pick up a copy and join the fun!

_childDocuments_.review: I really only play on consoles, mainly the Switch. But since it's still a while before it's released on the Switch, I thought I'd support the developers and give early access a chance. Yes, there's still room for improvement, but I have to say I really like what I've played so far. _childDocuments_.review:
The classic action-adventure dungeon experience of your dreams is about to be made... by you! Create and share your very own dungeons, then play a nearly infinite number of highly creative, trap-ridden dungeons made by other creators from all over the world. 

Unleash your creative streak as a dungeon creator and place as many enemies, floors and secret paths as you like. Make the journey more difficult for your friends with countless traps and hidden spikes.

Play built-in dungeons or play the dungeons of your friends and the community. Solve their puzzles and defeat the enemies you encounter during your adventures. Find hidden hearts to replenish your health and make it to the final boss.

Become a hero of the most impossible dungeons the community can come up with. Show everyone that your dungeon is the best!

name: Star Trek: Infinite
detailed_description: DELUXE EDITION Star Trek: Infinite: Deluxe Edition gives you access to the base game, as well as the following: U.S.S. Cerritos & California -class Uniforms Add the ship class with the most heart to your fleet and don the uniform to match. From Star Trek: Lower Decks, take on the California-class ships and iconic uniform of the crew for yourself! Klingon Voice Pack Bringing an extra layer of authenticity to your Star Trek story, the pre-purchase bonus also includes a Klingon advisor voice. Downloadable Soundtrack Take the sounds of Star Trek: Infinite with you anywhere to keep your mind firmly fixed on leading your faction to victory, even when you are not. More Star Trek Music Additional Star Trek music tracks to help explore the galaxy to, added into the game via a content pack. Art Book Like many crews before us, we have documented our voyage for posterity. Explore the birth of Star Trek: Infinite from concept to completion with a 70-page artbook! About the Game With Star Trek: Infinite there is no singular way to play. Whether you wish to take the route of diplomacy, espionage, warfare, or a mix of all of these, there are multiple paths to victory. You are in the command, and the fate of the galaxy is in your hands! Choose between the United Federation of Planets, Klingon Empire, Romulan Star Empire, or Cardassian Union. You will take on the role of the leader in charge of all the major decisions of your faction as the game unfolds. With each faction having their own unique styles of play, your decisions determine how successful you are in reaching your goals. Star Trek: Infinite has been meticulously created to provide an immersive Star Trek experience while allowing you to shape the story of your playthrough according to the choices you make as the leader of your chosen faction. As you take on the role of the Federation, you'll have the opportunity to recruit iconic captains and officers, including Picard, Janeway, Sisko, and Data to name a few. Meanwhile, other factions offer their own set of iconic characters to enlist, such as Gowron, Makbar, Garak, and many more. Beyond the potential cast of characters you recruit to your faction, the game grants you access to a range of starships from the Star Trek universe, tailored to each faction's arsenal. From the Federation's reliable Intrepid- and Defiant-class ships, the menacing Cardassian Galor-class vessels, the sleek Romulan D'deridex, or even the formidable Klingon Negh'Var battleships. Of course, the Enterprise-D can be developed and added to the Federation fleet through the bespoke storytelling system developed for Star Trek: Infinite. Star Trek: Infinite is built upon the core systems of Stellaris, leveraging the deep and complex system and making them its own. Aspects of these systems have been streamlined and simplified to better resonate with the Star Trek franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT April 2024: The game will no longer be receiving support. it is unpolished, unfinished, and unworthy of your money. I no longer recommend this game. TL;DR: Its an interesting game, priced appropriately enough, and seems pretty polished. So, I have like, 1k plus hours in Stellaris, probably more. I'll try not to constantly compare the two because yes this is a Stellaris clone, its been very open about that from the start. Anyone whose familiar with Stellaris will be able to jump right in, although I did do the tutorial just to see what it was like. This game might be overwhelming for someone who never played Stellaris, but I feel like the Venn Diagram of people who love Star Trek and have played Stellaris is almost a single circle. But for the rare person who loves Star Trek and hasn't played Stellaris, this game might be a little much to handle at first. While its not a Paradox developed game, its based on the mechanics of one, and that means there's a lot of depth coming from a base game that's gone through multiple expansions and updates over...what, six years? More? So whats different? A few more additional resources, science is one big pool (I like that), new "mission" tree like HOI4 and EUIV, as well as a galaxy tension mechanic like HOI4 are the first things I noticed. You don't have hyper-lanes that you can see, but I assume its just hidden and the movement is like what you would see in a Stellaris map where he hyper-lanes were turned up to infinite density.  Anomalies seem to be more frequent compared to a default Stellaris map, which makes sense. But then again you play the federation in the tutorial so that seems to be their focus so maybe thats why (traditions that buff it). Oh, there are faction specific traditions and I believe faction specific choices within traditions as well. What did I not like? Terrible voice acting. I am sorry but that's the worst Klingon I have ever heard in my life. This might sound silly, but it absolutely ruined the immersion for me to hear a Klingon that sounds like drug store cashier who's had a long day and just wants to go home.  Then there is the map itself. Pretty strange to put everyone right on top of each other, and from other Star Trek maps I have seen, this is not the way the Galaxy is supposed to look. The general direction of where each empire is is correct, sort of, but Its just weird. I took advantage of that and did what I could to block the Cardassians off from expanding southward at all, which seems like its a bit broken. I would highly recommend to the devs to change the map, spread things out, etc. There's some reused audio assets from Stellaris, and some stuff that looked like placeholder text (when I absorbed the Betazoid Houses, I got their fleet of ships and stuff and they had generic names, which is fine because I don't think anyone knows what these minor faction fleet ships were ever named). Also when I absorbed the Betazoids their science ship was at the very edge of the map for some reason but you don't get to see what they had surveyed or explored. That makes sense from a game play stance, you don't want it to be too OP to annex Minor Powers, but its a little silly otherwise. All in all, for the price, its worth it. You're getting years worth of Stellaris updates content repackaged with plenty of unique Star Trek events and flavor, with a lot of room to grow with DLC and mods. I will try playing some other factions and see what I think, but in general I definitely have a positive feeling about the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek Infinite, a game that bears a striking resemblance to Stellaris, unfortunately fails to stay true to the source material of the beloved Star Trek franchise. One of the glaring issues is the game's misrepresentation of key elements, such as referring to a D7 battle cruiser as a "warbird." This oversight demonstrates a lack of attention to detail and a failure to accurately portray the iconic ships and terminology of the Star Trek universe.Another concerning aspect is the game's initial inclusion of phasers on Klingon and Romulan ships. While digging into the game's code reveals the intention to add disruptors and other appropriate weapons, it is evident that the Paradox company released the game prematurely, without fully implementing these essential components. This lack of readiness suggests a rushed development process and a lack of understanding of the intricacies of the Star Trek universe.Furthermore, the release of Star Trek Infinite is marred by a multitude of bugs and technical issues. These problems can significantly hinder gameplay and detract from the overall experience. It is disheartening for players who eagerly anticipated an immersive and polished game to encounter such obstacles upon release. This raises concerns about the developers' quality assurance processes and their commitment to delivering a stable and enjoyable gaming experience.Considering the aforementioned issues, it is reasonable to question the decision not to release a beta version of the game. A beta release would have allowed the developers to gather valuable feedback from the community, identify and address bugs, and ensure a more refined final product. This missed opportunity to engage with the player base and improve the game's quality is a disappointment for fans who expected a more thorough and polished experience.In conclusion, Star Trek Infinite's failure to stay true to the source material, evident in misnaming ships and providing incorrect weaponry, along with the game's buggy release, highlights significant shortcomings. The decision to release the game without addressing these issues and the absence of a beta version suggest a lack of attention to detail and a rushed development process. Fans of the Star Trek franchise deserved a more faithful and polished gaming experience.Updated 11/23/2023I've been somewhat impressed with the way the Star Trek Infinite team has addressed several game issues since my last review. The improvements have been commendable, and it's clear that the developers are dedicated to fixing bugs and crashes. However, I still find certain lore aspects to be incorrect, and I believe it's essential to address them.Firstly, the portrayal of Klingons and Romulans using phasers instead of their iconic disruptor and plasma base weapons is a significant deviation from the established lore. It's crucial to maintain consistency with the source material, as this helps to immerse players in the authentic Star Trek experience.Additionally, the discrepancy in Klingon lifespan is worth mentioning. While Star Trek episodes have mentioned that Klingons can live up to 150 years, the game seems to overlook this fact. It's important to ensure that the lore is faithfully represented, as it adds depth and credibility to the game world.Another aspect that caught my attention is the absence of faction-specific flagships for certain factions. In episodes like "The Way of the Warrior," the Klingons prominently featured a Klingon Negh'var as their flagship. It would be fantastic to see each faction have their own flagship, as it adds diversity and uniqueness to their respective playstyles.Furthermore, misnaming the Klingon D7 as a "warbird" is a significant oversight. In Star Trek lore, the Romulans were the only faction to utilize a bird-like design, calling it a "warbird." The Klingon D7 should retain its rightful name, as it holds historical significance within the Star Trek universe.Lastly, the absence of the K'vort class battle cruiser, which is a vital ship in Klingon military doctrine, is disappointing. This iconic vessel, is Larger in size to the Klingon Bird of Prey, has been accurately represented in other Star Trek games like Star Trek: Birth of the Federation and Star Trek Armada 2. It would be fantastic to see the Star Trek Infinite team rectify this omission and include the K'vort class battle cruiser in the game.In conclusion, while Star Trek Infinite has made significant progress in addressing various game issues, there are still some lore aspects that need attention. I hope the developers take these concerns into consideration and work towards correcting them. As a passionate fan of the Star Trek franchise, I will continue to remind the Star Trek Infinite team through my Steam review until these lore aspects are appropriately addressed. Let's strive for a truly authentic and immersive Star Trek experience!

_childDocuments_.review: The TL;DR: If you already have Stellaris, wait for fixes and further patches. If you do not have Stellaris yet and are a great Star Trek fan, it it ok to get for 30 bucks.My experience, mostly from Federation play: The good:- It is looks very nice, really gives you a big Star Trek feeling. That is a really, really big plus, they did that so well.- Besides that, it is a Stellaris fork. Automation actually works. It is slow, but hey - you could have done it yourself.- Pirates are an actual menace. They appear from somewhere and I need to scramble to stop them. And no, they did not spawn somewhere, they simply came from where I could not see them- Many, many small lore events and characters you know and loveThe bad:- There are a few ship weapons that are just plain better in all situations. Why even offer the others?- While we are at ships, the auto generated ship designs are plain awful. MUCH worse then in Stellaris. It does not even use all the slots.- The Federation has so many bonuses to not only diplomacy, but also growth and colonization that it actually plays like a rush faction. If the others do not contain the Federation early on, it will blob and snowball- Planets on the other hand are too balanced. Every planet I saw had roughly the same amount of energy, mining and agriculture bonuses, making every planet as good as the other for most things- While the design is really really great, the music is forgettable. Maybe it is not loud enough, even on full blast, but it seems just to be a boring, nice tune in the background all the time- A few textures went missing sometimes, like 1 leader and a few checkbox marks- In popups, a few important words are bold. But you cannot get any info about them. It should have a CK3 like tooltip mechanic or at least some ingame lexicon to check on those bolded words.- There are a few bonuses to be on friendly terms with minor factions, but you can also annex them which is not only plain better but gives additional bonuses. Why even add a bonus for being on friendly terms if you never want to keep that state?The ugly:Many functional issues where I wonder how that came through the QA check. Hell, how that came through dev at all:- The Federation somehow has 2 human species that are exactly the same- It has 4 founder species but for some reason humans are not marked as a founder species- The other 3 founder species all come from Earth...- and the humans have an unknown home planet. Yes, really- And the actual home planets of these races did not have the home world bonus- The federation is only a federation in name, no senate or special events are happening- When a minor faction gets annexed, they vanish (as a faction) from the game. So in the galactic tension screen you will have unknown factions suddenly- While we are at it, you only see that a galactic tension happens and to whom, but not due to whom. Would be kinda nice to know who the baddies actually are- Messages/Notifications are baaaaad: We cannot make our own breaks for e.g. research finished, and messages for construction finished? Appears only once, and has in title and text the same message: "Construction finished". Uh.... where? And what?- The mission/focus tree. So far I only checked out the Federation one, and outside of the question if you like it in general or not, it has big issues. Mostly the pacing/triggers. E.g. the very first mission takes a few years at least, but after that you can have 3 or 4 missions in a row that are already done. On the other hand, I had a mission I could not trigger - because...- It has the old TotalWar mechanic that when you are strong, you cannot do diplomacy well. There is a diplomatic malus for being strong. So I could no longer finish my mission to have 3 commercial contracts at the same time...- Some story events cannot be fulfilled - e.g. I figured out the supernova early, and was told to build some sort of ship I did not have and could not research. Great. I was also asked to do a mission against the Borg queen, but I could not reach the location with my military ships, so the timed mission failed. GREAT. And when I reached the place, my fleet cannot attack the Borg cube for some reason. EVEN GREATER- You cannot play a minor faction or add your own custom faction to the ring
