_childDocuments_.review: I'm enjoying this a lot, but there are some criticisms that I hope will be addressed in updates:1. Some obvious lore stuff. Star Trek doesn't use terms like "voidships," and I'm not sure what those are yet. The game's "authenticity" - appearances by characters like Picard, Worf, Dukat, etc. are why I bought this game. There are obvious terms like "quantum slipstream" and "transwarp" in the Star Trek universe that could explain advanced forms of faster-than-warp travel.2. Bajor doesn't seem to be "working" the way it should. In my Federation game, I went to war with Cardassia, destroyed their station, and landed troops. But I can't seem to find a way to "annex" it. Perhaps because Cardassia fully occupied Bajor earlier in the game. Anyway, it's a bit frustrating to be sitting in a system with your troops all over it and not be able to tell the Cardassians "this is mine now, or I'll destroy all of your fleets again." Oh, and about that station? Pretty sure there was a whole show about the space station in orbit of Bajor, and it did not look like "generic minor state space station 01." 3. Geordi. Poor Geordi. He'll never get to join his friends on the Enterprise-D. Why? I'm fresh out of anomalies. I found tons of them before I unlocked the Enterprise-D, but once I finally paid that alloy cost, the anomalies seem to have dried up. Now it appears that I'm effectively locked out of those campaign objectives. Maybe make it so you can unlock him by scanning debris from battles? That seems a lot more reasonable. Either that, or find some way to create low-reward anomalies that can be done later in the game. There's too much content locked behind the "Geordi wall," like the Defiant and Enterprise-E, so lets pull a classic move and give him a way to roll under the door.4. Poor Romulans. I had no idea how to get that carrier ship I was supposed to have to save those guys. RIP5. The tutorial absolutely brain blasts you with information. It's a little overwhelming to a new player. I figured things out, but, oof.So overall, I'm really happy with the experience. Frankly, I'm just glad that someone is making a game based on my favorite TV shows. I'm excited to do more, but after putting about 8 hours into my first playthrough, I'm hitting these bumps that show that maybe a little more polish could go into the authentic 90s trek experience the game wants to offer. If you can't tell by my profile, that's a pretty big deal (I hope I find the D'Arsay archive sometime soon!)Personally, I hope the game has a big future. I'd love to see Gamma Quadrant and Delta Quadrant DLC, or special scenarios or modes where you do things like fight the Dominion War with mission objectives based on episodes like "In The Pale Moonlight," or command Voyager on its journey home. There's a ton of potential here. Even though I've found my experience to have some rough spots, I'm really hopeful for the future of this game.Edit: Oh, one more thing. The lack of voice clips from Picard, Worf, Data, etc. is a big miss. I'm not even looking for original VO. You obviously have the license. Slap some clips of dialogue in there for appropriate moments.

_childDocuments_.review: The negative reviews I have read make mostly accurate observations and I still recommend this game ON THESE CONDITIONS:- you are a big star trek nerd- you kind of like the idea of playing Stellaris Lite (or are new-ish to 4x space strategy and haven't played stellaris yet)- you don't mind paying $30 for a game in the hopes that it will help fund DLCs which you can buy in the future so that by the time you've spent $70 you've really got a pretty robust game to playI've played thousands of hours of PC and/or Console Edition Stellaris, single and multi player. The game has gotten pretty bloated with things to do and think about nonstop for hours and hours. I miss having chill time in my Stellaris games. This game is a nice easy version of Stellaris, although it can have a lot of busy work also, but it has some idle-ish time and it just doesn't take anywhere near as long to play through. It's a spin off game with a presentation I really like (star trek!) for the same price as a stellaris dlc. I'm in.I agree with reviewers complaining that it's clearly made to end up with a bunch of DLCs - that's true. I agree with reviewers who complain about audio prompts, event text, and other errors that make it clear the game was really not at all polished for launch - that's true too. I just don't care much. I'd rather have something to play (at a low price) now and pay the rest for the DLCs later, that's fine. My imagination can take care of the other problems with ship classes, weapons research, and alien species being in the wrong places. It's fine. That said, if those things would be a problem for you, probably best to hold off. If you can sit down, enjoy what it offers, and maybe rock some TNG reruns in the background? Even better.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Stellaris 0.8: Star Trek Edition. IMHO, the unofficial Star Trek mod for Stellaris is MUCH better. It's forked from a super old version of Stellaris, so it doesn't have any of the QoL updates or bug fixes or lesson learned that Stellaris has picked up over the years. Additionally, because it needs to fit the "Stellaris" mold, all sorts of non-trek or completely broken-trek things are in there, like "Highways" instead of Stellaris' wormholes, the timeline is TNG era, but TMP era ships are researched after VOY era ships, The research tree is completely jumbled, so you'll have Starfleet researching plasma weapons while the Klingon's are using phasers... names for things are are wrong "voidcraft" being the most jarring example, etc, etc. Add to that missing tool tips, unexplained features, broken quests/events, and you have your typical Paradox release. On the bright side, it'll probably get patched, so give it 6mo/year and try again?

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so i ain't gonna go on about how it's lacking features from Stellaris or it's a pointless game like some have made out. Rather my issue, and the reason i'm not recommending the game, is this:Stellaris has been out for more than 7 years now. During that time it has not just added new features but it's, more importantly, really refined it's systems and the way you play the game. There has been a bucket load of changes to the UI and to it's management of things so that you have far greater control over what you do in the game.All of this is missing from Star Trek Infinite.Instead the UI is insane. Text is low resolution, sometimes hard to read. The buttons are all over the place an for some reason a number of them are incredibly small. Tool Tips do not impart enough information. And worst of all the systems that Stellaris refined are back to their basic versions from the launch of the original game (for example you cannot automate Construction Ships nor can you specify how automation works on your colonies).For me, it just boggles the mind how something that has been so obviously been built upon a preexisting system can have NONE of the improvements that system has implemented from it's many years in operation. It is like they looked at a picture of Stellaris and not the actual game as it is today.Fingers crossed that they'll patch it heavily and in a few months time it'll be vastly improved. But as it stands right now i do not recommend this to any Star Trek fan and certainly not any Stellaris ones.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not do many reviews - this one I am doing because I am very torn on the product. I am a Star Trek fan and really hoped for the best!--I want to love this game, have been excited since it was announced but I can not feel as if this game is a husk of what it could be. It feels like either an early access without early access (which I am sure will be fixed after we are milked through DLC), or just a cash grab.There is a good core here that I want to embrace but it is missing various key elements some big, some small, and others seem silly.1) Complete lack of ships is a major let down (dlc incoming? probably)2) The weapons do not have the right effects or sounds (this here while silly is inexcusable 3) There is not enough to differentiate the current races, while they play a bit different major aspects just seem cut and paste4)Random bugs galore...noone died, stop spamming that for no reason5) When playing the klingons, why is Janeway now a captain of one of my ships?? oy... lazy6) The story elements/events are not varied enough for replayability7) There should have been coop8) The biggest sin yet is the complete lack of a tutorial, as someone that has not played stellaris, I am completely overwhelmed. What they gave us was a complete and utter joke.9) The war system seems half baked10) The diplomacy system is also half baked, neither are intriguing. Things I like - The Art looks solid, ships and galaxy are welcomed as well as the elements or lore injected within. --Paradox - I am a longtime fan, however having played all your other work over the years, you guys can do better. Us fans that I know you will "Milk" with DLC deserve better, and this franchise deserves better.Hoping before to long I can wipe this review and recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun: The game captures the essence of Star Trek with its strategic depth and iconic factions, but falls short of fully delivering the experience fans expect.Holding You to the Game: While the overall style and feel are enjoyable, the game lacks the polish and complexity of older strategy titles. It’s fun for a while, but the limited scope leaves you wanting more.Many Enemies to See: The factions and enemies are true to Star Trek lore, but the lack of variety and challenge over time diminishes the excitement of encounters.Nice Scenario: The visuals and Star Trek theme are fantastic, offering an immersive experience for fans. However, the world feels too small and doesn’t live up to the potential of the franchise’s vast universe.Extra Depth: The game has great potential, but it desperately needs updates and fixes to expand the gameplay and address the current limitations. With improvements, it could become the strategy game Star Trek fans have been waiting for.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT:This game is really fun for me. So many nice details. This is a good Star Trek game. Think I even like it better than Stellaris. It's more focused, factions are not as generic, but beloved and iconic Star Trek races. Systems like spying and missions add a lot of flavor. Devs did a good job in my eyes and did a lot of things right. There is room for optimization and improvement of course, but it's fun as is. And they are already fixing and improving bit by bit. Very nice.ORIGINAL REVIEW:- Rough around the edges- Overloaded and cluttered, in-your-face UI - Some really bad design decisionsBUT+ Loads of potential+ Beloved ships and setting+ Nice art+ MODDABLEStar Trek: Infinite is a solid basis with flaws - but easy to tweak. Chances are, it will only get better. I do recommend it if you like Star Trek and maybe even feel the well-known Star Trek mods for Stellaris offer too much content and features. Don't expect a perfect game, but something that is likely to grow and hopefully manages to tap a considerable part of it's potential. Devs seem to be trying. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of most of Paradox's games.  Star Trek Infinite is great for a fan of the source material and is similar in play style to Stellaris.  The devs are actively working on fixing small bugs and improving the quality of the game.  Because of the nature of the Star Trek Universe, some things are a little more set in stone than with similar games.  Your starting location is based on which of four powers you chose to play through as.  The technological improvements and missions are interesting, but some of the features don't feel entirely fleshed out yet, like the Governor ships.  Enjoying the game so far, worth buying with the black Friday discount if you're a Star Trek fan.

_childDocuments_.review: As an experienced Stellaris Player I was actually a little bit hyped for this. Dude,  I've been so wrong.This game has absolutely no  Star Trek atmosphere. The mission and traits system feels shallow and hollow at the same time, besides the fact it's directly copied from Stellaris and somewhat from Hearts of Iron.Besides the automation of planets (which is rudimental at best) everything has to be micromanaged. _childDocuments_.review: **UPDATE JULY 2024**This is abandonware. Although some of the issues were fixed, it is still a vastly sub-par effort that is not deserving of the ST IP. Just play regular Stellaris with the New Horizons mod. At the moment I cannot recommend this game, even though I have put many hours into it. -Lets start with the bugs. There are many. And I really do mean many. If you bought it with the deluxe edition, well done you just lost money needlessly because the launcher doesnt recognise the deluxe edition elements. They claim to have fixed that, but the forums are full of people who still cant access it, myself included. -There is no thought process to the tech trees. Why am i researching plasma weapons as the federation? Why are the Romulans attacking me with phasers? Why does the Enterprise-E have a cloaking device? Why do I unlock Intrepid class ships long before Excelsior class...when they are 100 years apart in other direction? -The map is all wrong. Everybody is VERY close together at the start. And you are all in the bottom of the map. The whole top half of the map is there for expansion into, but as the Federation you cant really go that way without war. -Characters are all wrong. Data died of old age at 83. Data. Old age. -Romulans lose their star system very early on to the Supernova that spawned the vomit worthy movies series. Fine, its canon, but it makes playing the Romulans a waste of your time. -The Borg are about as threatening as my grandma. There is genuinely no threat posed by them at all. It was honestly far more effort to get Bajor into the federation than it was to defeat the entire Borg collective. I have no doubt Paradox will DLC the hell out of this game, and that will inevitably sort everything out. Because thats what they always do. And in a year or two this will be a solid Trek strategy. But right now, it is just a bug ridden mess of nonsense. Right now, stick with normal Stellaris and play New Horizons. Come back to this in a year.

_childDocuments_.review: My old review was a tentative 'no' with the clarification that if you just want a simple Star Trek-ish 4x strategy game without all the complexity of modded Stellaris, this game is a lot of fun and showed future promise. But given its abandonment after only a few months of support, I am sadly changing my review to 'don't waste your money'. Other reviews have highlighted the gameplay issues. For me, the biggest issue was that despite talking a lot about how much they love Star Trek's lore, none of that shows through in the actual game. Every faction has an accumulation of lore mistakes that get annoying over time. It's hard-to-impossible to play through major plotlines from the shows. It's much easier to RP as the four factions available in the game by making them in vanilla Stellaris... even easier with mods. Really strange little disappointment that could have been amazing if it had been supported by the devs and solidly playtested by fans of the franchise. Unfortunately, it seems a bit like they were always planning to just make some money and drop the game. Really sad. Recommend Stellaris or Star Trek Online instead.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is pretty much what I had expected, which is a good thing as a big Star Trek fan. Some people are correct in that the game feels a little shallow compared to Stellaris, but I feel like that's also to be expected upon launch. I had a slight issue upon my first to startups, where the game crashed but the third time I tried it, I switched the game to windowed mode and it launched smoothly. I haven't encountered the issue since and have experienced no other bugs. Now I haven't put too much time into Stellaris, so I am still quite inexperienced, but I feel as though over time I will begin to enjoy this game even more. I am hoping DLC will add a little more meat to the game because there is a lot more they can do with this game. For example, I would love to see the other two quadrants in the game, as well as other playable factions in the future. Even staring off as smaller factions and have each faction start fresh, then having to expand would be a nice mechanic or optional feature to use upon the start of a new game.If you enjoyed Stellaris, or are a Star Trek fan like myself and wanted a new space/strategy game, I would say this is a solid buy to add to your collection. Again, this game is exactly what I expected it to be, therefore I am quite happy with it. I don't understand the negative reviews because you should have known what you signed up for upon purchasing it. It was pretty cut and dry. This game will only get better as time passes and will see more playtime than Stellaris so I'm happy and excited to see what's to come.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 10/18/2023:I've uninstalled the game but didn't ask for a refund. As I logged back in, after playing Stellaris, I was again frustrated by the distance created with the Stellaris quality of life updates. So much was manual again, among other things!The Star Trek connection feels even more forced than my short initial play time. I don't think that Starfleet only ever had 1 type of ship (I don't count construction or science - though that's a whole other problem). Maybe there's a way to get there, but there seem to be several issues:1) The core Stellaris mechanics are not suitable for an established universe that doesn't match those mechanics2) The core current Stellaris quality of life mechanics are not available in this variation, which makes it hard to play when compared against its own predecessor3) The game doesn't match the emotional depth of the Star Trek universeNote, I believe this is my only review on Steam at this point, which is due to the importance of both Star Trek and Stellaris for me.Original:I know it only shows minutes playing on this game, however, I have played over 7,000 hours on Stellaris, and I am a huge Star Trek fan.I was very much looking forward to Star Trek with the Stellaris engine with the best of both worlds (like Spock :) ), but that's not what I felt happened here. Ultimately it felt less than both. The narration seems dryer than any of the computer voices in any of the on-screen versions, almost obligatory. _childDocuments_.review: A pretty decent launch experience, once I got used to the differences between this game and stellaris.It's NOT a mod, like people keep saying. Mods can't make changes like this to the base game. It's much more like an official Star Trek scenario in the Stellaris Engine. You basically get to play one of four factions in the TNG era of Star Trek. I played through as the Federation and had a pretty good time. It's a simpler experience than Stellaris, while still being a respectably complicated 4x game with a bunch of great mechanics that simply aren't in the base game.The developers nailed Warp travel. Minor powers can be interacted with in a bunch of neat ways, and these end up being tied to victory conditions in a compelling way (integrate them to get their civics, get the most civics to win -- or conquer everyone.) There is also a mission tree for each faction, and I liked the one I saw a lot. I do suspect that these mission trees will mess with replayability.As of launch, the game has some rough edges. I got notifications meant for other empires when their spies failed in my territory. Minor powers gave me the same mission a few times. Ship design is fairly opaque and unforgiving, and making ships that work is basically a trial-and-error experience, and the post-combat readout doesn't do much to explain why you've won or lost a combat. There were also some bugs -- Once, the USS Enterprise would just go up to Cardassian ships and not fire at them or be fired upon, but reloading the game fixed it. I also got verbal notifications that leaders had died, but no popup saying who had died or why (I'm pretty sure my spies were dying, but I can't confirm it.) None of it was game-breaking, even when they were irritating or confusing, and I had a good time.All in all, this is a great experience and the price is right. Paradox has a strong history of supporting their games, so I am looking forward to what happens in the future for this game.Bugs and rough edges aside, my only real criticism is that the galaxy felt too safe. Nothing really endangered my explorers, not the way I'd expect from the TNG era of TV, anyway. There's never a reason to go into the neutral zone, for example, nor are there (as far as I know) roaming threats to deal with, aside from a pirate faction that can be bought off. This is a solid 8/10 game, with a bright future ahead of it. The art, writing, pacing, and mechanics all feel like you've been plopped into an alternate version of TNG, with nods to the movies and other series as well. If you're a fan of the show and like crunchy strategy games, you'll love this.

_childDocuments_.review: So been playing it for two days now, Played as the Romulan's and the Federation.In short this is a Star Trek veneer, on top of a trimmed down Stellaris. If you want a Star Trek game find and play the New Horizons mod for Stellaris.For starters, the game is very trimmed down, it starts just before the TNG era which means you miss all of the founding stuff for the Federation, no early starfleet vessels, None of the early content that makes ST have depth. You will start the TNG era with no previous history with any empires. Fed play through: Start with Miranda's, then you unlock Intrepid s before encountering the Borg then you encounter the Borg which the game says is a cube but is actually a sphere which crashes in to a planet. Another sphere comes, takes Locutus then you immediately get him back with a -10 year life span on Picard. Ship enter sol and does nothing, No one else attacks you, then I got a message saying Voyager had returned home, Didn't even get told it was missing but it had destroyed the Borg for us, Gave up as there was nothing there, doubt the Dominion are in it, there's not much other ST content for it.Rom play: Bit more exciting, The Klingon's declared war on me, sent my ships to engage, turns out auto build didn't give them weapons so they got trashed and I lost the war, then I was stuffed for the second war. Gave up after that, Went on to the Klingon's and just couldn't be arsed anymore as it felt pointless.Music is a poor version of Stellaris, it has no grandeur and is definitely not star treky music, Even the Mod has better music.Models are good, but on auto build they quickly give up the race specific weapons so it looks wrong when firing.Feel like the traits for each species are incorrect. In summary, If you like the first hour or two of Stellaris, you'll find this game OK. But don't expect a rich Star Trek experience as it is really only ST from the models and occasional hero's that pop up and do nothing, It would be a good tutorial mode for Stellaris, aside from that I am very dissapointed that it was A. Sold as a new game and not a DLCB. The official content instead of just making New Horizons an official DLC.C. Got my hopes up for being able to play a good Star Trek game again.Don't buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. But if you're expecting Stellaris, then you should play Stellaris.The graphics are awesome and in some instances have features Stellaris doesn't. I love the planetary screens. Managing planets in some ways is easier. On example of this is the little "+" next to districts. That's a nice little bit of QoL that was added. The portraits and models are beautiful and really do add the to game. It LOOK like Star Trek.The sound design might need a tiny bit of work. I was expecting the classic laser and torpedo sounds from the series. It seems they aren't there. While not a deal breaker but it's fine. The voice acting, I really, really wish were better. It's a little jarring. The music is definitely Star Trek inspired and the Klingon voice pack is definitely well made. I have it. It works and sounds good. Over the sound is good but there's issues.Gameplay. This is a slower game. It makes sense because unlike Stellaris you're playing in half a galaxy so everything is slowed down. That said, it's still fun. There's still a learning curve for each faction. Each solves its problems in different ways and each has their own challenges. Thematically, I really like each faction's uniqueness. Also, the economy management is fun. The fact ships need a officers to crew them is a huge plus. I LOVE this mechanic. There's something that feels thematically correct about it and I really wish Stellaris had this mechanic.Is it fun? I think it's fun, depending on what you're here to play. If you're here to play Star Trek in the Stellaris franework, then this is the game for you. It's fun. If you're here for a Stellaris type of experience that just so happens to be Star Trek... you're going to be disappointed.I'd give it like a 7.5 out of 10. Yes, it seems like a Star Trek skin of Stellaris, but that's not what it is underneath. It's Stellaris plus some very Trek-specific mechanisms that make each faction play differently. _childDocuments_.review: I purposely waited for the latest patch to be pushed out (and played on) before posting.  First off, I'm a devout Star Trek fan and was excited enough about the Star Trek Infinite pre-release teaser to pre-order the expanded package.  To me, I don't mind helping support another Star Trek software attempt since "Birth of the Federation" was the last Star Trek strategy game that appealed to me, but evey "long game" eventually crashed due to how big the game had gotten around Turn 220+.  Star Trek Infinite appears to take that "long game" scalability into consideration if the player has the patience to stick around for it. Despite the bugs and very frustrating issues in the first week after go-live, I believe Star Trek Infinite has a lot of potential once more fixes are pushed out.  Having played in the first week (before patches) and the second week (after patches) the second round of patches has made a huge difference in game play flow, reduction in frustrations (Data dying of old age? Inconceivable!), and select actions that now "work" like they're supposed to.  Is it perfect yet?  No, but neither was Crusader Kings II or Europa Universalis IV during their initial releases either.  As a licensed Star Trek offering (in theory), I would have expected more Star Trek-themed music, but most of us are in this for the game play, and how well the game mechanics actually work.  Disclaimer: I have never played Stellaris, so I have no basis to compare Star Trek Infinite to the Stellaris mods.  And Star Trek Infinite does have the potential to grow and refine itself as more of the remaining underlying issues get resolved.   My one hope:  effective patches get completed to the base game "before" the roll-out of DLCs, please!  One more thing; every other Paradox game has the "Pause" key on the keyboard functioning for a quick "pause/unpause" shortcut for players, but not here?

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a lukewarm fan of Stellaris. I wasn't in love with its anthropomorphic animal factions and generic setting.Star Trek Infinite, as a 4X game, is worse than Stellaris, but its fantastically improved IP makes me optimistic for its future. I'm looking forward to where the developers take it.–In detail:I loved the Mission tree. The game gives you goals, in the form of a small branching tree similar to Hearts of Iron 4’s National Focus trees. The Federation mission tree rewards you with an Enterprise-D, a unique ship capable of research and combat. Once built, you get six specific missions to complete with the Enterprise, each rewarding you with a “graduated” member of the Enterprise’s crew, who joins as a Faction Leader. I was partial to Troi, who became my lead diplomat (or envoy), and Data, who became one of my best Science Ship captains.I appreciated the smaller-form, hand-designed galaxy. Star Trek: Infinite gives you the lower half of what seems to be a medium-sized Stellaris galaxy. It’s still procedurally generated, but less so than Stellaris. There’s a design to the galaxy. Personally, I loved smaller Stellaris games, and I prefer hand-designed content over procedural generation, so these are great steps in my opinion.Star Trek: Infinite draws content from the Rick Berman period of the 90’s-00’s, but mostly focuses on The Next Generation. We don’t see anything from The Original Series, Star Trek: Enterprise, or the rebooted classic period.The game is far from perfect. There are bugs. The AI of other major powers is poor. The End Game Crisis never seemed to trigger in my game. Content gets a little sparse as the game goes on. I’d have preferred a deeper internal politics system for the United Federation of Planet, and a deeper character system. I’d prefer better voice acting, especially for the Klingons. No sound effects or music are brought in from the shows, and what we have in the game isn't very good. (Compare, for example, the early 00's Star Wars: Rebellion, which made excellent use of Star Wars' voiced dialog, sound effects and music.)– I enjoyed my 20 hours. I'd love for Paradox to apply this same treatment for other IPs: In many ways, Star Wars is a much better fit for Stellaris than Star Trek. Dune or Foundation would be interesting, and I would absolutely love a Crusader Kings 3-based Game of Thrones game.This is a tentative, qualified recommendation, assuming that Paradox is going to come through with a patch and content update for the game. For me, it was worth $30, and I’d recommend it if you’re sort of like me: If you like 90’s-era Star Trek and you thought Stellaris was at least “okay.” I hope it's financially successful for them, as I'd love to see it improved and expanded.

My expectation with this game was that the Star Trek theme would be pasted on a "dumbed down" version of something resembling the base game of Stellaris. In reality, much more was brought over from Stellaris and its many expansions than I had expected, which left me pleasantly surprised. That's not to say its been a perfect experience, and in many ways I might have considered giving it neutral feedback if there was such an option. I have experienced quite a few annoying bugs, particularly with the voice narration constantly making comments that are not consistent with what's actually going on, and every time a war is going on, it seems to think I am involved even if I am not. I also unlocked a tech for a new starship, which appeared to be bugged, as I could not combine it into any of my fleets or create user designs for it. These things have definitely been something of a frustration for me as I play. Also. a minor quibble, but Commander Data died of natural causes on me at the ripe old age of 85. which just makes zero sense seeming as he should be an ageless android. I found that to be rather annoying and immersion breaking, but what can ya do.I also think that this game could use a fair amount of expansion, be it additional factions, customizable civics, etc. Would love to see content added, but hopefully it will be fairly priced if so.All that being said, I've enjoyed my initial 10 hours with the game quite a bit, despite everything, so although my feelings are a bit mixed, the thumbs up just felt more fair than a thumbs down. The game just launched, so hopefully some of these issues get ironed out, and the game gets properly expanded upon. At the end of the day, it really is a treat to have a game like this as a fan of Star Trek, and I can see myself coming back to this fairly often.

_childDocuments_.review: Spoilers: This will be lengthy.I've played stellaris and now I have played Infinite. There is definitely a lot of differences.One: there is a glaring difference in playability, you are always bound by a pre-set game design that limits a lot verses stellaris. I get that they want to keep this almost like true trek, but adding a random universe setup will do the basics a wonder. Further, there isn't any settings to change for this game. You can't set the crisis difficulties or the amount how things are set up.So if you just want a conquest game, or an ethics game, you cannot change the settings to give you that option. I was winning as the klingons, and then out of the blue within like...40 years, the federation pulled a win of ethics out from under me when I had looked and everyone had 3 ethics like me. I was completely surprised.Two: Computer systems in the game messed up my designs pretty horribly upon getting to the Vorcha class (Tier 4 ships). In stellaris, it tells you the effective ranges that the computer will stay at for longest ranges of shooting. (like artillery, line, and point blank.) Another issue with the computer for tier four ships, You only get "Stay at longest ranges" as an option. Which made my ships sit outside their own weapon ranges and be useless upon fighting stations. (so tier 3, 2, and 1 ships were the ones fighting the stations effectively where the tier 4 just.... sat there... Very Frustrating.)Three: They hinted that the Nebula ship was in with artwork at somepoint, sadly they don't have that ship in the game. They did say they might put in the option to making the ships have optional skins, but really... I feel they are leaving this to modders. Which is highly frustrating to me. On top of that, while claiming to be going canon, they muddled up the order of ships. Further, they are using I believe the avenger style miranda looks instead of the classic miranda that we usually see.Four: Star bases are different in this game verses stellaris. You can build any number of them and it seems to be ok, verses stellaris having you research more starbase amounts. This is probably because of how the warp works for ships being able to attack any system within the FTL limit.Five: It feels like the same missions go across the factions, so it doesn't feel unique like the stellaris beginning story arcs. Maybe it is located in certain areas, because I played the federation, and then klingons, and conquered Sol... But I got a few missions from the federation playthrough.Six: There is not much variation with the ship builds. You don't get to pick different hulls that make different builds per say. Birds of Prey have 1 small weapons slot and 2 medium weapon slots. Mirandas have 3 small weapon slots and 1 medium. (Tier 1 ships) It felt like there was classes of ships in stellaris with the hull picks (where one is a picket class, one a torpedo class, one is a basic class, etc.) It would be nice if they used different ships for this design. (but using such minimal ship designs makes this currently impossible at this time.)Seven: Some of the race missions requires you to be a friend of X empire, like the klingons, in order to progress down its mission ark, you must be friendly with either the federation OR the Romulans. Which if you weren't paying attention before, and went to war with both, it is a pain in the ASS to get to be allowed to complete this missions. Literally ANY war you do, drops both the empire's views of you and you have to wait FREAKING FOREVER to complete missions. Making the game kind of stale.Eight: I have YET to see the end game crisis. Which is supposed to be something to worry about. (Which I doubt seeing how I completely dominated in the game.(Nine: (and probably my last point.) I think I missed the research tree for the exquisite minerals, so it seems like you cannot buy them? Someone correct me if I am wrong, but on my playthrough, I could not buy any dilithium for my better buildings. Very frustrating.Now, on to my actual review on the game.Graphics are pretty standard and they look nice. Very stellaris. Many of the icons is stellaris. If you want to play a sandbox game, definitely play stellaris over this game. There are so many things that could be improved with this game that they are indeed going to let the modders do the work for them. It is unfortunate that this will eventually be just abandonware.Core issues with the game:There is no true flexibility, if something happens, too many of the quest lines get broken. If a character dies, dead quest line. Everything seems to be super interconnected where If you go to war, all of the major empires will have extremely long lasting negative views of it...making say the klingon mission tree fail completely or take far to long to go through.There is no way to change the win outcome, so if an empire beats you on civic wins, you have lost. (yes, you may continue to play through, but its still considered a loss.)There are far too many bugs right now. Infact, as of this day, there's an advice bug that will not remove the tutorial advice, removing the whole U.I. on the right hand side. VERY FRUSTRATING.Concerning ships, the most iconic ships are in (arguably) especially on the federation side, but only has Galaxy, Excelsior, Miranda, Intrepid, and Sovereign class ships are actually in the game. In a latest statement, they pretty much said they are going to let modders fill in the gap. This screams Abandonware to me, and that they are not invested in giving their player base exactly what they want...and want the modders to do the work for free. I am highly disappointed in this outcome.  At this time, I cannot endorse this game. I may update this review at a future time, but as it is, I think the most polished game is stellaris with the mod new horizon for a star trek themed Stellaris. I do not normally want to give a game a negative review, but today is the day I was super agitated by the U.I. bug that was caused by the latest update, and last friday's dev report.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently I cannot recommend this game as there is so many issues.1) Gameplay: It feels "empty". We have some Minors, the most I don't know from Star Trek (ST) btw. They are just there, but I don't see how they contribute to e. g. the Federation like with an unique ability. They don't have any unique traits or whatsoever. Assimilate them, repeat. That's it. The other Majors are even worse. In my last game Klingons were calm, Romulans were calm, Cardassians were calm. As for Federation, the gameplay is sooo boring. Only here and there pirates are attacking and somehow the BORG, but that's it.2) Science:A complete mess. If you are playing Federation at least you can research things (too many things). But a major issue is the complete randomness of junk inventions. Why do we have weapons never seen in ST? Why do we have 10+ different weapon systems? Complete useless. In my last game shortly before 2400 (end of game) I finally could research the solar panels for star bases? Why not earlier? This doesn't make sense at all. You have to research photon torpedoes. Not mark VII or so, the basics ones. While I like that scientists have some research traits, it is annoying to switch them acc. to what is currently researched for the bonuses.3) MapI know that only alpha and beta quadrant are covered, but it is still a complete useless non-ST map at all. In addition, there is a certain amount of anomalies you can discover. So after a certain point in time there is no benefit to uncover every star system at all. The random factor of resources is annoying. Sometimes you have only one system with Dilithium. The other rares are...super rare.4) EnterpriseWhat exactly is now the purpose of the Enterprise D (and if you are lucky E)? It is a science ship, ok, and can make some buum buum. But that's it. The missions are ridiculous. Some are super easy, but finding three fights is more a challenge. You can't even put some other ships to the Enterprise, so it is highly dependent of a proper fleet IF someone is attacking. No "real" missions available, sad.5) EventsWhich events? In the ST New Horizons mod at least you have a bunch of events, but here - NOTHING. Ok, you have this stupid Romulan star system sh1tty thing (I hate this Kelvin? timeline), but even after - nothing happens. It doesn't matter at all. Bajor? If you don't attack Cardassia, they will assimilate it - no prophets, no worm hole. So empty, so boring.6) IntelligenceWhat is the purpose of that? You spend sometimes 10 years with a certain mission, but then, booom mf, you mission failed. Hahaha.7) ShipsWe are starting with something like "Miranda" (lol), and then, due to the crappy science system, maybe you can research for Intrepid, Excelsior (!), or Defiant (which is crappy to the power of 10). Yes, in STNH we had too much, granted, too many versions of subversions, but at least some kind of logic and canon. Here, we have developers not knowing what was there in the 24th century.Taken together: It seems like this is a premature version of what could be possible. On the one hand it is not as complicated as STNH, but on the other hand it is too "empty" to have fun. Also, in my opinion the Devs started as ST fans, but then the team switched and now we have Devs who don't know anything about ST. Shame on you. And Paradox: if you have plans to bring out 1000 DLCs to make it playable: GFY.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:I find the gameplay of "Star Trek: Infinite" disappointing. Although it presents itself as a complex 4X game, it comes across more like a very limited and incomplete RTS (Real-Time Strategy) game with some 4X elements. Despite the uniqueness of the Star Trek universe, the lack of robust implementation of 4X elements could reduce the game's appeal for fans of the genre.Technical Issues:The numerous bugs and technical issues could pose a significant obstacle for a smooth gameplay experience. These technical flaws could be particularly frustrating if they significantly hinder or even prevent the progress of players.Comparison with Stellaris:Engine and Aesthetics:Both games share the same engine, which could lead to similar gameplay mechanics. The aesthetic implementation of the Star Trek universe in "Star Trek: Infinite" could be appealing for fans of the series. However, I think that the game doesn’t offer much new in terms of innovation or unique gameplay elements.Unique Features and Gameplay Structure:Although "Star Trek: Infinite" offers some unique features and a structured gameplay experience with clear objectives and missions, these elements might not be enough to significantly distinguish it from "Stellaris", especially considering the reported technical issues and the perceived lack of gameplay depth.Overall, I find that "Star Trek: Infinite" receives mixed reactions from players and critics, with technical issues and the perceived lack of gameplay depth being highlighted as major points of criticism. The similarities with "Stellaris" could be both an advantage and a disadvantage, depending on the personal preferences of players and their experience with both games.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game.  I am a Stellaris fan and have been playing it for years through all the major updates.  Stellaris is a great game and has amazing mods to make it a passable 4x game with Star Trek elements.  What I mean by passable is that Stellars is a great game in it's own right, but even with the mods it never felt like Star Trek.  Just a great game with a Star Trek skin.  Then, Star Trek Infinite came along.  I was skeptical at first, especially with the mixed reviews.  But  "WOW!", this game really feels like Trek.  It is more simple than Stellaris, but still much more complex than most other 4x games.  I like the balance.  I like that it uses resources from Trek.  I have played for a few hours and already feel like I am playing in the Trek universe that I love.  The biggest problem with the modded Stellaris version "New Horizons" is that after a while it bogs down.  Too much detail to enjoy after your empire grows to a moderate size.  Since Infinite is more simple, it is more manageable with larger empires.  The interface is cleaner, everything seems more polished.  So, big thumbs up from me!  Hope you try and like it.  Oh, and I haven't hit any bugs yet ... they have patched it a few times, maybe most of the bugginess has been addressed in the patches since release.  If you're a 4x fan and a Trek fan, this should be a great game for you!

_childDocuments_.review: As both a very novice RTS/Grand Strategy player and a seasoned fan of Star Trek, this game was extremely easy to jump into and enjoy in the latter sense, and while many of the mechanics were apparently lifted almost straight from Stellaris, it seems that they've been boiled down and modified in a way to make this game much more accessible to those newer to the genre.  Additionally, (as I was playing with someone who had little to no knowledge of the Star Trek universe) I found that the game lays out the lore up to 2346 in an easily digestible manner, and presents a game experience from that point onward that really allows the player to take the reigns of their respective faction and determine the next course in their history. My primary complaint in this field is the lack of thoroughly developed mission trees and unique traditions for factions other than the Federation.Overall, I can say I'm a fan of this game, despite my understanding that its beginnings have been rocky, especially in the opinion of more experienced strategy game players than I, and most certainly in the glitches department. As of the writing of this review, however, this game is very barebones. I look forward to seeing what the devs will do in the future, and am especially excited about the potential for the addition of new factions, such as the Ferengi Alliance and The Dominion. 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I had my doubts about this game due to many people saying it was just a glorified Stellaris mod. I feel like the polish of this is better than the Star Trek Stellaris mods out there. I have not had any crashes, issues with starting the game up or graphical problems. As a Star trek fan, particularly of TNG and DS9, I would recommend this game. I just hope the devs do not abandon it.Now for the constructive criticism:1. Weapons, particularly photon torpedoes, phasers, disruptors, etc. should match the color and appearance from the movies/shows.2. Voice acting needs to be reworked and more believable, although it does not prevent me from playing the game.3. Map size choices, although it sounds like they will be introducing other quadrants at some point.4. More/stronger minor powers; as Cardassians, taking over minor powers to instantly grow my empire should not be so east. Also assimilation of that empire into my own should have other requirements or caveats.5. This may already be the case, but it would be good to have a diplomatic penalty if you cross another empires space, even though your ending point is not in their territory; in other words, just flying through their space should be enough to make them angry (I know this does not apply to "highways")6. Speaking of highways, it would be nice if there was some canon explanation for them or a little more depth there from the shows or movies.7. Needs to have the Briar Patch from Insurrection.To the devs, keep up the good work and please do not abandon this!

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT BUY THIS GAMEAs much as it pains me to leave a negative review, I must be honest. Despite being rather excited seeing this game, knowing it was effectively a clone of the Stellaris Star Trek mod, I purchased it with hopes of it being polished over time and being comparable to Stellaris. The game definitely feels like Star Trek at times, but the controls are very clunky and take a decent bit of time to learn. The lack of playable factions/races certainly didn't help as well. Add to this that the game received less than 2 months of proper support before Nimble Giant went through "restructuring" which left this game with no team to continue work on it, leading to it's official end of all support in March. I wish this game had received the care it deserves, as this will simply serve as another reason to prevent more Star Trek games from being made in the future. If you enjoy Star Trek and have the itch for a proper 4X Grand Strategy, go play Stellaris with the Star Trek: New Civilisations (exact spelling for the mod) and you will have a much greater time. Especially if you can get Stellaris and any dlc as a bundle or on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I have waited so long for a decent Star Trek strategy game! I really enjoy this game, it takes me back to playing Birth of the Federation in 1999. It is highly replayable in my opinion, with four major factions to choose from, then the fact that the resources in each system change with each game, which means you can't spam certain systems that you know contain the best resources. Also, with so many minor races depicted in this game it opens up all kinds of different strategies.The only issue I have is that when I start a saved game for some reason my Energy Credits are always negative, even though they were positive when I saved the game. Still, that's a minor issue that I can get past because this game ticks all the boxes for me and I look forward to many more hours being invested in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoying the game so far, didn't play the Star Trek mod for Stellaris so this is completely new for me.No crashes on 3 machines I tested it on all setting were mid to max from first listed machine to the last:i5-9400 16gb ram 256gb SSD MSI Armored OC GTX 1070i7-11800H 16GB ram 500gb SSD 3070 (Mobile)i7-12700 32gb ram 1TB SSD MSI RTX 3080New NVIDIA driver's were needed.(the old ones I had from a month ago did make graphical load times worse)Not sure why everyone had so many crashes unless they were using older equipment, haven't had a crash yet.The map does feel pretty small at first, and the learning curve is VERY steep if you haven't played Stellaris before.If you are a start trek fan and have the time to learn how to play the game then I can recommend this to you.The ship combat does feel good and balanced at the moment.Diplomacy needs a bit of work as it literally is either yes or no, aggressive or hyper proactive, for the most part. Have only been playing for a hour so far.Research needs some work as it doesn't truly explain in enough detail what some choices in each branch is supposed to do.The graphics are decent enough nothing to spectacular but looks good enough to make you believe your in the TNG Series.The bottom line is you either have buyers remorse because the game isn't what you wanted it to be, thought it would be, or you will enjoy it because its start trek and your willing to put in the time to LEARN to enjoy the game. If your looking for instant gratification this game isn't for you it's a slow burn to heavy action.Good luck.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a die hard Star Trek fan, so when I learned of new Paradox Trek game, I was very excited!When I first saw the gameplay reveal, it was clear it was going to borrow a lot from Stellaris, but after getting a couple of hours into the game now, it's clear that it is, unfortunately, a re-skin i.e UI, same mechanics - everything...right down to the construction ships.Now if you're a Trek fan, will you like this? probably. However be prepared for inaccurate continuity. The game starts with the Khitomer massacre and the events around the TNG episode "Yesterday's Enterprise". However, the Federation is only a small power and you start as though the UFP has only just been formed. So, unlike Stellaris where you expand from a single system out, you control of the 4 founding members but you find established cannon planets like Risa are unsettled planets (which breaks from the timeline too), therefore, they need to be colonised.Would this have been better to start just after the Star Trek: Enterprise finale? and develop the respective "empires" from their?Also, starships can't initiate first contact on their own either, you have recruit diplomats to do the work that a captain would usually do, so you have to sometimes put this on hold until said diplomats are free to do so whilst they complete other tasks etc. The game looks great, but it feels disjointed from the Trek universe so far, so I'm hoping it gets better soon and that Paradox work to distinguish this from Stellaris, and give it it's own personality, rather than having a "copy & paste" development plan. It would be nice also to see empires such as the Romulans and Kingons take on their species traits more too. When I get a Romulan ambassador asking me to open a trade deal and share technology for peaceful means, I get a little suspect (because it's the mid-24th century in the timeline, and they wouldn't do that) especially after they've just wiped out Khitomer, and especially as this event in cannon plays such a huge part in the Star Trek universe.So would I recommend it? Yes. BUT...it needs a lot more work to give it a truly unique Trek experience - as well as making it a lot more different from it's similar predecessor. Paradox have a plethora of amazing Trek content out there to draw from, but we don't even get an LCARS UI. Please, PLEASE make this MORE of a TREK experience.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Great game if you like Star Trek and Stellaris and HOI4. Otherwise it's a glorified DLC.Pros:- Character art- Inclusion of famous Trek characters from Film and TV- Ship and station models- faithful recreation of the trek galaxy and races- the potential for this is insane especially the inclusion of mods- the inclusion of a mission tree is interesting and engagingMiddling:- this is Stellaris with a HOI4 focus tree integration- story drivenCons:- AI is as buggy and non-nonsensical as Stellaris is- Currently not as deep an experience as I would like- no mods and DLC yet- music is repetitive and sometimes doesn't feel 'trek'Conclusion:I really enjoy this game, it speaks to the inner Trek nut in me. However, I'm highly aware that reviews are mixed and some feel a bit put out that it's a 'Stellaris clone.' I think there's a lot of potential here. The artwork is great, as are the ship models. It feels like a lot of love went into the writing and world generation here. You will love this if you've played Stellaris and Hearts of Iron 4 as there are elements of both here. DLC integration and mods will make this infinitely better and a much deeper experience.Is it worth the £26.99? I think so!

_childDocuments_.review: .Ok. The idea of it is fun. I love Star Trek. It's neat to get to command starships and take care of everything from wars, to exploration of the galaxy, to diplomacy, to economics (though, economics gets really frustrating at times).Good stuff:- Heroes like Spock, Picard, and Janeway play a role in this.- Wars starting up was fun- Nice to see other familiar characters and place names- I liked playing the diplomatic role to persuade others to join the Federation- Getting to move the Enterprise around as a hero ship that can be upgradedThe less good:- Late game was dull; I felt like I was running out the clock until victory, having easily outmaneuvered the other powers even though I was struggling to learn this.- Needs more governments to interact with, and for them not to feel so... passive in galactic affairs.- Relationships between powers get permanently strained. I did a war with the Klingons, and they never forgot it. Yet... they survived it, and I made efforts to repair the relationship, but there's apparently no coming back from that (not reflective of the source material).- The Enterprise upgrades get hard to acquire if you don't do them early (i.e. only a finite number of surveyable worlds)Bottom line:Play if it you like Star Trek. There seems to be some potential here, and I hope they expand on it.

_childDocuments_.review: **UPDATE** March 31st 2024. Game is dead and Abandoned. DO NOT BUYAs much as I love Star Trek and Paradox games, in its current state I cannot recommend Star Trek Infinite.there is very little difference between the 4 major species, You dont really do much with any of the minor species. A lot of foundations for what could be great concepts like espionage and diplomacy are there but again, they do nothing. The Federation is OP, Ive tried games as the Federation, the Klingons and the Cardassians and I gotta say they were way easier as the UFP, I mean it does help they get a free hero ship and no one else gets one. It also felt like managing UFP economy was much easier than the others. The Tech tree is a carbon copy for each of the playable species, as the UFP you research Phasers, and as Klingon's you research Phasers. War is cancer in this games current state, armies are useless(normal for paradox) I really hoped the doomstacking from Stellaris wouldnt transfer over but it did. When you go to war your opponent(s) jump fleets all over the space you control forcing you to play an incredibly annoying game of cat and mouse, this is how ever single war went for me. Didnt matter if my fleet was stronger or not when I spend the  entire war chasing ships whos movement is tactically idiotic. Lastly the Pirates(which you cant turn off atm) O boy the pirates, absolutely one of the most frustrating addition of the pirate mechanic I HAVE EVER FRAKING SEEN!!!! Pirate fleets will raid you pretty consistently, unless you have ships waiting for them at your system they will warp in, destroy your outpost causing you to lose the system and then they charge you 1000 of each of the 3 primary resources, all of this happens very quickly as well. I had some instances where I got a fleet there to fight them but they ignore my ships killing them and destroy the outpost anyway. The influence cost to build outposts to claim systems is very high compared to your monthly income. Pirates end up stagnating your growth. I was very excited for this game and the only thing thats kept me from being angry about the crappy half rushed state it was launched as, is the fact that its a paradox game and it should improve in the future. I just wish they had waited to release it. It seems like they didnt bother to play test their own game.

_childDocuments_.review: It was a very promising concept, and there's a fair bit here. It's likened a lot to a fan mod, but the production values are rather higher. Through official licensing, they were able to really replicate (no pun intended) that Star Trek feel. Unfortunately, Paradox's penchant as of late for defecating in its meal bowl has shown its ugly head, with the sorts of results one would expect. This game plays like it was pushed out early and needed more time to polish. Support was also cut for it shortly after launch and it's just sort of languishing in what seems like a very unfinished state. If it hadn't been for Paradox abandoning the game in this fashion, I would probably be giving this game a yes.So, yeah, between this and Cities: Skylines 2, I've really learned my lesson about buying Paradox games pre-release.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Trek and Stellaris fan I was excited about this game and really went in with reasonable expectations. I largely ignored the amount of bad reviews, wanting to give it a shot on my own.  After several campaigns it truly hit me that the fun factor just is not there.Ignoring the numerous bugs and very unstable economics (both of which can hopefully be solved with future patches), the game feels like somebody pasted Star Trek Lite on an older, less refined version of Stellaris.There is no satisfaction in many of the achievements, combat victories or other special moments that should make this feel like Star Trek.   They pasted a few pictures of characters we would know, ships we have seen before (and should love) and factions that are dry and lack real personality.The music is bland and has none of the scores or tones we would hope for in a Star Trek game.  The other factions and minor races have a single, uninspired (and often annoying) phrase you hear when you interact. The new mission feature (for The Federation at least) is so dependent on a few key events happening that if you don't follow up on certain things in time, you simply lose out on what should be a very cool feature.At the end of the day it is certainly not worth $30.00 or any of your time when there are so many better games out there.

_childDocuments_.review: The mighty Star Trek license was badly used. It is too absurd. I bought this game to play the Klingons. And only did play them yet. But... Starfleet declared war on me without reason. The same starfleet that loves to hug and cuddle, and talk out of trouble.But ok, this is something that COULD be done... But why are we in a timeline with Picard, so clearly AFTER TOS (game is in 2400 something) and the only spaceships that are known by my people are Bird of Prey? Why I need to learn how to make a D7 battlecruiser when it did exist already in that time? You simply could make two different starting times like in HOI4.Kird time and Picard time. Call them however you want, but it gives you roughly 100 years of explainable technological differences.And yes, it is Stellaris ultra light. I not understand why people with only one hour in each game say that this game here offers more. More frustration maybe. In Stellaris you also can make races that nearly match those from the Star Trek franchise. Just not in look of ships. I hope this game will not get put in a corner and still get some love by the dev. It COULD turn to something good then. Stellaris also needed time (and DLC) to get better. But why not use the good that was in Stellaris and use here.Also what somebody else wrote...The Starfleet ships need also special exploring ships... No matter their ships were discovery vessels! The Enterprise was never ment to be a war ship, just a ship to explore the unknown and be able to defend itself. Now they kicked all research guys out of the ship and made it a "warship".Lastly... Why would a Klingon research rescue pods? It is a honor to die in battle and not to flee! Again Stellaris... There are also things restricted by different ideologies. Starfleed would be pacifist, Klingon militarist. They had all the mechanics... And tried to make something "unique".

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that is not quite the Star Trek experience I was looking forward too, and too much like Stellaris, which I already own and love. The issue is this feels like Stellaris and not enough like it's own game. I'm happy they brought back the warp drive (which was in the original Stellaris until they tweaked it to include only hyperspace travel between stars), but the ships are not multi-purpose like they are in Star Trek, and instead follow Stellaris' formula for specific ships for construction, science, and military. While I understand this as a way to play the game, I was hoping for the versatility for ships to take on whatever role is needed, like how Voyager (Intrepid-class) was a science vessel, rather than purely a military ship in Star Trek Infinite. And yes, I know you can get the Enterprise-D and it can both fight and explore, but I feel like this should have been the norm for all ships, not the exception.The time of when the game starts also messes me up as well. The game seems to primarily try to aim for the Next Generation Era and afterwards, skipping when the Federation was first founded and also the Original Series era as well. There are alot of star systems and aliens missing from the game as well. And while I understand that adding them would up the scale of the game, it just makes the Star Trek universe I'm trying to play as feel incomplete.I guess that's how I would sum up this game: incomplete. It has the potential to be a better game, but it was developed off of Stellaris and marketed to Star Trek fans as something new. However, it's not unique enough to be it's own game yet. When playing this game, I want to feel like it's a Star Trek experience, not a Stellaris one. If I wanted to play Stellaris, then that's what I would do.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Infinite

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, it's Stellaris. Like any other game on the Clausewitz engine. I have to say that they have added some new features, but not really a lot to make it stand out. Having said that though I deem necessary to say that if we compare Stellaris 1.0 to what we have now we are talking light years of leaps forward. So I would expect the same line of development for this game too. Is it the same game? YesWas it a blind buy? Yes. for me two reasons, Paradox and Star trekAm I disappointed? a bit yes, was expecting more than a re skin, it was a bit... lazy. I would expect this as an early release not 1.0.Is it fun to play? I have to say yes. Its the same mechanics I know and  love and with a similar improvement queue like Stellaris had it can become the ultimate Star Trek game. Remains to be seen of course...edit 5 Mar 24: was expecting to see a good development queue, improvements, fixes. I was hoping to start as a stelaris clone and become something of its own, rather that it remained there, now without an update for so long I am starting to lose hope and get disappointed. Its not a bad game but if you have played Stellaris for so many hours it feels like eating yesterday's leftovers.

_childDocuments_.review: We all knew this was based on Stellaris. It says it right in the game description. Many of you bought it because it was based on Stellaris. Many of the reviews say "I bought this because I loved Stellaris and now I'm mad it's too much like Stellaris" When I bought Star Trek Catan, I wasn't mad because it was too much like Catan. That would be silly. Yeah, maybe some mechanics and writing need to be flushed out. Great, I'm looking forward to some updates. Maybe some mods. I'm having a ton of fun with this so far and it scratches an itch I've had since I started watching TNG in like 1990. I'm going to love this. I hope you look past the surface and do too.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a good game, not as complex and with less Trek story content than in the Star Trek New Horizon mod which makes the whole thing easier but as a die-hard Trekkie you miss a bit.Sadly there were some "asychronities" in the multiplayer and in the middle-game some ships didn't respond to commands and just stood around while the fine fleet shot at them.Also I would find it more fitting if the division of the big empires would be more accurate, the Federation for example is more centrally located and runs in the alpha and beta quadrants, the Romulans are north-east with a parallel neutral zone, the Klingons are more east and the Cardassians more west. It would be nice if this could be adjusted, but of course it doesn't harm the fun of the game.I hope that story elements, the Gamma and Delta Quadrant, as well as one or the other playable faction (Dominion?) will be added via DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek: Infinite sets out to merge the strategic depth of 4X gameplay with the rich lore of the Star Trek universe, promising an immersive experience where players can chart the course of galactic civilizations and navigate the complexities of interstellar diplomacy. Positioned within the Alpha and Beta Quadrants during the Next Generation era, the game invites players to lead one of four major factions – the Federation, Klingons, Romulans, or Cardassians – as they vie for supremacy in a dynamic and ever-changing galaxy.At its core, Star Trek: Infinite embodies the essence of traditional 4X games, emphasizing exploration, expansion, exploitation, and extermination. Players venture into uncharted territories, establish colonies, harness resources, and engage in strategic warfare to expand their influence and secure their dominance. The game's narrative framework draws inspiration from iconic Star Trek storylines, intertwining player decisions with key events from the series to create a cohesive and immersive experience.One of the game's standout features is its narrative-driven approach, which introduces branching mission trees and dynamic events that shape the trajectory of each playthrough. From diplomatic entanglements to existential threats, players are confronted with a myriad of challenges that test their leadership skills and moral compass. The inclusion of familiar characters and story arcs from the Star Trek universe adds an extra layer of authenticity, allowing fans to immerse themselves in the lore and legends of their favorite sci-fi franchise.Despite its ambitious premise, Star Trek: Infinite falls short in its execution, plagued by technical issues and design flaws that detract from the overall experience. The game's user interface feels clunky and unintuitive, making it difficult for players to navigate the vastness of space and manage their burgeoning empires efficiently. Additionally, the absence of engaging visuals and lackluster ship-to-ship combat sequences leave much to be desired, failing to capture the epic scale and excitement of space exploration and conflict.Furthermore, Star Trek: Infinite suffers from pacing issues and tedious gameplay mechanics that can impede the player's enjoyment. Lengthy diplomatic negotiations and repetitive micromanagement tasks often result in a slow and cumbersome gameplay experience, testing the patience of even the most dedicated Star Trek enthusiasts. Moreover, the presence of game-breaking bugs and technical glitches further exacerbates the frustration, hindering players' ability to fully immerse themselves in the Star Trek universe.Despite its shortcomings, Star Trek: Infinite offers glimpses of brilliance and moments of genuine excitement, especially for fans eager to explore the depths of the final frontier. The game's commitment to narrative depth and thematic authenticity is commendable, reflecting a genuine passion for the beloved franchise. However, until its technical issues are addressed and its gameplay mechanics refined, Star Trek: Infinite remains a flawed gem, struggling to live up to its lofty ambitions and the legacy of its illustrious predecessors.

_childDocuments_.review: ** Review Updated**Game is a decent "expansion" on the Stellaris formula. It does a few of its own unique things, but not enough for it to be its own 40$/SAR500 title. However, if you are a fan of Star Trek The Next Generation, there is something here for you, not a lot, but something. I believe this game will be worth it for those interested on a 50% - 75% sale, but before then, its really only hardcore fans and enthusiast who will want to jump in.My hopes is that we will see some decent changes to the game to depart from the base Stellaris formula, where all the current ST:I factions can be role played in already. The one really nice thing about ST:I is the story board section, allowing you to develop the Enterprise and her crew for the Federation as an example. I found that to be a really fun part of the game so far.I recommend the game as a Star Trek Fan, but not as a gamer. I will continue to play, but like i say, I recommend waiting for a sale.** Update **Thinking on this further, I do not believe that purchasing this game is worth it. The product is waaaay to similar to base Stellaris with a star trek mod on for it to be its own game. It is in essence a paid mod. I highly recommend avoiding the purchase on this for now, until they update it with FREE expansions on the content available, like more Story Board Quests and Extended Universe content.They did not even spend a reasonable amount of time making new music for this product, it shares a lot of the same music from Stellaris, which is just mental. I hate going back on my review, but this is just a nightmare. It's stellaris with a 40$ star trek skin tossed on, with some basic voice acting thrown in. Clicking on the klingon contact makes me hate this product more.It truly is a lazy cash grab

_childDocuments_.review: Like: Finally I can blow hours at a time indulging my inner conqueror in the Star Trek universe. There's a lot of callbacks to the various series, and events keep you immersed in the game. The mission tree allows you to either play the usual Federation, or go dark and play the Confederation of Earth or the Terran Empire as you wish. I've not played the Klingons, Romulans, or Cardassians yet, but they are options as well. Dislike:  Finally, I can blow hours at a time indulging my inner conqueror in the Star Trek universe. I need more hours in the day! XDThat said, real problems include a lack of ships in the early game, canonical ships missing until much later after they show up, WAY too many techs in the phaser side of things (are the other techs as well defined?), and some late-era techs really don't fit well into Trek. An example of my current Star Trek Infinite playthrough has Neutronium Armoured, Interdimensional Disruptor-Armed ... Excelsiors. While they are small, they are mighty. But they sure don't fit the Star Trek 2409 motif...Adjust your expectations when you buy this game. You're paying $40 for it, so your expectations should be adjusted properly. ST:I is a new game, and has bugs in it. But it's a fun game, and the dev team is actively squashing those bugs. Give it a chance and you should have a lot of fun with it!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: This is still a great game and I still don't get the hate. Honestly, this is a fantastic, streamlined, Trek-themed Stellaris reskin as intended and it plays great as it, but also really shines with any of the community created mods available. This is Stellaris without the bloat, and I still play Stellaris consistently. This is a great Trek game and you should buy it and play it if you like 4X and Trek.I don't get the hate, they told us we were getting Star Trek with the Stellaris engine, and that's what we got. Player support for this game will translate to Paradox support for this great game. They're still putting out expansions for Stellaris and the game is still strong and a consistent replay. That kind of support for this game could lead to a robust Trek game, which the gaming space sorely needs.Could the game have more? Yes. I think the TNG-centric nature of it is narrow and stifling. I do like how the New Horizons mod covers the scope of Star Trek history, and I hope expansion content for this does that because this build is very well focused on Trek-type needs and would work real well from the 22nd century events through the 32nd century events.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: This game was nothing but bait and switch abandonware.The moral of the story is, don't buy any games on release. Wait 12 months to see if the developer is actually committed to producing a quality product.I wish I could say amazing things about this game.It certainly has some deep and well thought out systems at it's core but at the end of the day it really doesn't feel that good.It sort of feels like those old "choose your own adventures" books, where you basically had two possible outcomes to every dilemma and after doing a few of those you figured out the pattern and the magic was gone. Since I know nothing about this sort of game I've had to restart from zero A LOT and what I'm noticing is that there is absolutely zero variance in events and scripts (at least in the early game) meaning that every game feels pretty much the same. The only real variation is in what research technologies you are given to choose from, and this is actually very frustrating because it means that you really have no regency over what direction your technologies research will take. IE: If you want to play Klingons in a very planetary invasion sort of way, but the tech research options you are given mostly focus on terraforming... well you are going to be struggling.The long and short of it is this, Star Trek Infinite is NOT a sandbox game, it's more of a theme park where you get to ride along on a scripted story that has pretty much been told many times over in tv shows, books and even other games, so unless they give players more regency over how the game is played I don't see this becoming a huge success other than riding the brand recognition and the fact that players have been starved for Star Trek games for so long.OH and another thing, the sound effects in this game feel like they were grabbed from the bargain bin of sound clips. there is almost zero recognizable sounds from the decades of cool sounds Star Trek has generated over the years, it's like they were being restrained by the weird lawsuit from Paramount and CBS a few years back where fan films were banned from making better content than them.At the end of it all this game accomplishes one thing, it makes me want to play the Star Trek Ascendancy board game where you get way more Star Trek in a box than you do here.

_childDocuments_.review: I ended up liking this quite a bit more than Stellaris as a game. It might just be personal preference, but the established start did a lot for the early enjoyment, and I really like the mission trees, as well as the way traditions work in this game compared to Stellaris. It's not for everyone though: if you want something more sandboxy or want EU4 style "million and one mechanics" that allow you to control all aspects of society, this probably wont be something you enjoy as much.
