_childDocuments_.review: As a newbie of Stellaris, I tend to be overwhelmed by the numerous possibilities and am happy that Star Trek: Infinite dumbs it down enough for me. I can identify myself with the species as I watched TNG and DS9 when I was still in school and like the setting and characters. I feel motivated to play it and did not take significant breaks to other games in the last 37 hours. Just fixing some stuff on the various planets of my system always ends up in a full evening spent playing.For the downside, the game's documentation could be better (maybe some Paradox Wiki would help) to get information about how trade works or the technologies (there is no tree as in Stellaris). The only tree where I can decide where to go is strongly depending on what you are given and what kind of species you play. A kick-start with the Romulans is quite slow compared to other species (closing borders only possible with contact to new species). Missing out the technology development for some shield generators in the Klingon tree set me back forever so far. I did never ever get the possibility to research it again. Coming back to technologies, that is a real setback and feels some kind of stupid as you are realistically cleared for other technologies after preliminary research.Other posters already mentioned the German translation which is completely erratic at the moment as some placeholder variables are not fixed and no real text is displayed. For me the German translation is unplayable at the moment and I switched to English.Another thing which I found quite strange is the threat by the Borg collective. On my Klingon run I received Capt. Janeway on a Klingon scout ship (strange!). No support by the Federation even if I was on good terms with them. The best thing is that Janeway died as the scout ship was attacking the Borg Queen's cube. After some time (without re-loading on iron man) I was able to beat the Borg and deactivate the cube. But it is still there. I cannot destroy it nor do anything about it. Seems like a bug to me.Summed up I really like the Star Trek setting and the easier game mechanics compared to Stellaris. I really immerses me into this alternate future. The game feels like it was published too early and did not receive enough testing. I hope that the game lives long enough to improve and play out it's full potential. The bugs bother me but not enough to stop playing. Therefore I would recommend this game to Star Trek fans or people like me who are overwhelmed by standard Paradox games.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, here we are.Sadly, the company had a very strong template here to make something unique and appealing, for not only Star Trek fans, but also the fans of the Stellaris game aswell.In the end though, they missed every single mark they could've aimed for.The game itself feels like a quickly rushed out of the gate Early Access.From the design down to things like actually the missions to finish the game.Sound alerts telling you you have lost a high ranking officer when your leaders gain a new level.War score not being possible to achieve even if you are bombarding the enemies planets.Blunders when calculating the scores for Victory conditions.The list goess on.This, is another prime example of a company riding the wave of a new hype theme (In this case Star Trek general resurgence).It's never been playtested, riddled with bugs and obvious blunders, and generally just a horrible design.Most of all this truly feels like a mod of Stellaris, that got abandoned half-way through its design.I cannot advice people anything else then simply to stay away from this product.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I have changed this review to negative. The game has been abandoned, unfortunately, by the devs per their post on paradox. The game had potential to be quite spectacular but with the state this game was left in I wouldn't buy it for any price point.TLDR: I would rate this as recommended, but to be upfront, just barely. This is due to the yes or no option system. If there was a third option, neutral, I would pick that. What puts it slightly over no, for me, in the 2 option system is the potential the game has.The pros:- The game has most of the visuals down for Star Trek; it helps to build the universe and make the player feel like part of it. There are some problems with this Deep Space 9 looking like a standard Stellaris space station once taken from the Cardassians.- The mission tree overall is an excellent addition, though I feel it needs to be expanded and become more interactive. Having just the requirements and clicking the mission isn't as engaging. Giving stories, events, and additional tasks/decisions would add to the engagement, even if not on every mission in the mission tree.- Many initial bugs have been fixed, so the developers are aware and actively fixing these issues. There are still some but I believe most of the remaining bugs will be resolved within the next few updates.- Hero ships are a nice addition and helps flesh out the universe. I think it could be expanded further, such as interactions with other iconic heros/hero ships, and also an increased number of hero ships (within reason).Neutral/Undecided:- Price, at first, I felt like this was overpriced, given there are Stellaris mods that almost make this game. The reason I have moved to a neutral or undecided stance on the price now is licensing fees. Depending on how much had to be paid to get this license or given per purchase, which I just don't know, the price may actually be significantly lower and closer to a DLC price, when licensing is taken out. Given some of the new features in this title I could see this *becoming* a worthwhile game just as Stellaris has for me after some time.Cons:- Starting timeline... I don't understand why the timeline starts at the Khitomer Massacre instead of putting the player into the original series timeline. The game feels short and an earlier start helps with that issue and also allows for additional problems to be fixed, such as the next point.- Lack of ship classes. There just aren't enough ship classes. Where are the constitution, excelsior, ambassador, etc. classes? This could also allow replacement hulls. As an example instead of moving through what are, in essence, escort, destroyer, cruiser, battleship, etc. hulls give me a cruiser (constitution) and the ability to research new cruiser hulls (excelsior) that are slightly better. This doesn't need to be ridiculous like 200 hulls per faction but the scope should be expanded to further fill out the universe as was done in the series.- Balance seems slightly off. A starter miranda class is only minimally worse (.9 avg. damage per day for a similar build ) than voyager class. Given the cost difference, the feel of these ships doesn't quite match. Not asking for a perfect 1:1 performance ratio for supplies or officers but it just doesn't quite feel right.- One of the biggest problems for me is the lack of an open plan for the future of the game. What are the plans? Are we going to get expanded timeframes? Additional major starting powers? Full galaxy to explore?- Lack of things like megastructures. I know this would be hard for the factions in the game, but it should still be achievable along the end game, and at the least, we see these in the series. (I haven't explored the entire galaxy but I have explored about 60 - 70%  and not found any.)- One final minor issue is that the map in the game doesn't match the Star Trek map. I wouldn't even say its close. I get this is a game, but this could be adjusted to better match while still allowing for some leniency due to game requirements.Again I think the game has potential if the developers stick with this game, take player feedback, and give a roadmap of whats ahead.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Star Trek fan and a huge Stellaris fan.  I've got 2,100 hours into Stellaris.   Unlike most of the negative reviews, I'm capable of reading and it was very clearly and officially stated this game was based on Stellaris.  It wasn't just a "rumor", it was right on the official announcement.  So, this shouldn't have been a surprise for anybody.  Initial impressions is they've delivered on giving it a Star Trek feel so job very well done on that.  If I didn't have 2,100 hours into Stellaris, I would probably be declaring it fantastic right now.  The problem is I do have 2,100 hours into Stellaris and not having Stellaris's QoL improvements is painful.  Don't get me wrong, if I try to pretend I've never played Stellaris, it's a great Star Trek game which is a void that badly needed filling IMO.  If you're coming in as purely a Star Trek fan looking for a strategy game, you're probably going to love it. But if you're a Stellaris player, staring at both titles in your Steam library, Infinite is a tough sell.  Given Paradox is publishing it and it's based on Stellaris, I expect both mods and DLC to follow in quantity as per the norm, so take that as you will.However, I'm not talking about DLC or mods, I'm not even going to touch those subjects.  I'm talking about things like the improvements to science ship automation and adding construction ship automation.  Infinite is basically missing out of years of Stellaris QoL improvements and that makes for a rough sell/transition for Stellaris players because it basically feels like you've stepped into a time machine.  You find yourself going "How did I used to have to do this, I forgot".  Or "Oh, man, I forgot we used to have to do this manually".  I mean an hour in I'm going "I forgot how much I hate researching anomalies stops auto-surveying".  I love current Stellaris' option of auto everything on science ships.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, Not the start in general I was hoping for, but personally for me I'm having a blast. Now while I am having fun, there are a few things that annoy me. The UI Scaling doesn't seem to work great, I have close to 400 hours in Stellaris and since this is based off that engine (At least up to the point that team did Nemesis, then NG branched off from there with their own work), so I know the 1.2 Scale is big enough for me for Stellaris , but here it's still rather small. I'm afraid to go above that since I hear reports on icons not being aligned properly the higher you scale stuff, etc... , so I'm fine with what it is for now , but is annoying that it can't be a bit bigger or scaled better if that makes any sense. My other major complaint is the lack of good planetary features on the Trek planets that are in the game. It's already been said through Discord comments from the team ,etc.. the map itself is 20% static and 80% random, but I expected the 20% static to have really unique planetary features known for those trek planets... Sadly, this is not the case at all.. Risa for example.. The embodiment of a pleasure planet it's known for in TNG and DS9 shows, is in the game, however, it has no distinct features that make it feel like it's supposed to be Risa it's just all generic +1 to commercial, +2 to farming type of planetary features and unless you get it to research, you can't even designate that as a "pleasure planet"  which is really disappointing to see. Vulcan is another one that annoys me a bit.... No Vulcan Science Academy as unique building, ok I get that (perhaps the team didn't want to overload unique buildings for some planets), but why not as a planetary feature at least (that gives a bonus to research for example?) Decisions like that baffles since the discord site has made it very known these guys know their trek lore.. As mentioned in the beginning of the review, outside of those 2 annoyances though I am having a blast in a little over 2 hours I've played so far, the map at first I thought would be small it being 500 stars, but it's actually working on quite well here because the major empires are already formed and the minors don't expand as much, so unlike Stellaris where your border-locked 20 years in, this one appears to have exploration to continue all the way through the mid-end game which is gonna be great. The immersion of the galaxy map with how Nebula's actually look like Nebulas, etc.. is pretty incredible to see, plus the events are very trek flavored which is great to see. Luckily bug or crash wise I haven't encountered much yet, so that's good, but I feel bad for those who have encountered stuff. Although I did have to make that change to go borderless fullscreen (as fullscreen won't load the game up). So in the end I think this can be the start of something great, if hopefully they gets pass the little annoyance bugs that people have reported already and most importantly fix this DLC issue for people who have it as it still says it's not verified that I own them even though it was fine until the hotfix they deployed this afternoon EST my time as for example the Cerritos (lower decks fame) won't spawn in any new game anymore, it only shows in my existing game that I had going before the hotfix was deployed today.

_childDocuments_.review: Stardate 2365.07.23..A combine Romulan and Federation offensive has pierced the boundaries of the Cardassian Union. Legate Dukat, at the helm of the glorious navy that fights our foes and brings death to our enemies, has blunted their offensives. The Romulan offensive was smashed in the Trelka system while the Federation was blunted over Bajor. Actrium, taken early in the conflict, has been liberated. A status quo achieved, but a victory for Cardassia no less!Now, our intelligence tells us that the Romulans have made treaties with the Klingons who now advanced against the Federation, striking deep into their territory. In this peace that we have gained, we will grow stronger as our enemies weaken themselves. In the end, we will be the true victor, we will achieve greater heights! For Cardassia!=========================While pretty bare bones compared to Stellaris, which has the Star Trek mods, this official title is still fun. I was worried about when I saw only four factions as playable. There had been no dev diaries, to my knowledge, of minor factions, yet I was surprised. I saw Betazoids, Bajorans, Nausicaans, and Idanians as minor factions with one Ferengi outpost thus far. The game is pretty optimized and looks gorgeous! The colors, the UI, the music, and more all were given quite the detail.Now, certainly Stellaris has the leg above considering all the DLC and updates, but for a start, Infinite has the potential and solid foundations to become a great title in its own name.For 30 to 40 dollars, you get what you paid for. But, that doesn't mean it's so raw that there isn't much to bite. There is certainly room to grow and improve. It is a good foundation for potential and for what could become an absolutely amazing game. Keep it up, Nimble Giant and Paradox!

_childDocuments_.review: Unlike Star Wars - or Marvel - or DC or most massive multimedia IPs - Star Trek established a... different formula for itself back in the day.Ever play Birth of the Federation (Master Of Orion) ? Bridge Commander (various Totally Games flight sims) ? Elite Force (Quake) ?Knockoffs of popular games with a Star Trek© skin??Long ago - when the internet was young - this is what CBS/Paramount would  when they wanted a 'Star Trek©' game. Rent the IP out to a mid-tier developer - give them a fractional budget - and hope something platinum came out of it. It led to a lot of stinkers - granted - but it occasionally led to something truly special.Though, what it usually generated, was a 'fine' product.This is that.It's fine - it's serviceable - it's a neat little strategy game and if - like me - you're opposed to the idea of having to buy a huge amount of DLC to play one of the Stellaris mods then this might be for you.If you like strategy - then this might be for you.If you like Star Trek - this IS for you. You, like me, will tolerate the unstable launch and diet Stellaris for what it is to get even  in this universe.Buy it - let's see if we can support this game enough to get proper mod support (and by that I mean the STEAM workshop) and maybe a Dominion and Delta Quadrant DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: I've really enjoyed it so far. Haven't had any significant bugs yet, though your mileage may vary. It's not just a reskin of Stellaris, but of course still shares a lot. It looks to have branched off a few versions ago, which is a bit of a shame because Stellaris's more recent leader overhaul would have been perfect for this.There's some great mechanics not in Stellaris, such as officers (think manpower from EU4), diplomatic missions (minor tasks from other nations that give rewards), governor ships/spy ships, meaningful space weather, and neutral zones. It's enough to give it a somewhat unique feel mechanically from Stellaris, while still feeling familiar. If you know how to play Stellaris, you'll still feel your way around here. There's only 4 playable races, but at least the mission tree lets you play each in a couple ways that are at least a bit different (turn Federation evil, or open up Romulan society, for examples).Thematically, the game is a 10/10. Everything looks and sounds great. I think the map looks great; way better than Stellaris. For a game I largely play just at the galaxy map, that's great news. Gameplay events feel right at home in the Star Trek universe (often based on episodes). Music is good, though I wish there was a bit more of the classic Star Trek theme.Can't wait to see where they go from here. Beyond bug fixes, hopefully the game gets the usual Paradox treatment and gets years of updates and new content.If you like Stellaris and like Star Trek, at $30, would recommend, especially once some of the bugs are worked out.

_childDocuments_.review: I held off on reviewing this for a good long while. Probably too long. The game is ultimately incredibly disappointing in how much of a bait and switch I feel it is. The easy-to-market things like beautiful, high-quality artwork and in-engine visuals were front and centre during the marketing campaign, while gameplay wasn't really talked about in great detail. Mostly teasers about different mechanics but never really elaborating on how it all tied together.Well, the answer is, it doesn't really tie together. It feels like it's trying to be a Star Trek reskin of Hearts of Iron 4 rather than Stellaris, but it's no Best Of Both Worlds. The mission trees are ultimately linear box-checking, other than one choice per faction which can change their playstyle a little, or a moderate amount. You can turn the Federation fascist, woohoo I guess? I feel like Stellaris already handles progressive adjustments to your playstyle better and more elegantly with Traditions (Which also make an appearance but don't change your playstyle terribly much either, since they're also a reduction of the Stellaris feature) and your empire's civics (Which are fixed per-empire in this and unable to be changed). You also burn through the story very quickly and then you're left with most of the galaxy unexplored, and not much reason to keep going.Ship classes and their order of appearance make no historical sense, which, for a game that places high importance on progressing through a very specific time period, seems like a bizarre choice to make. The music is also... Fine? But it's not Star Trek. No licenced themes whatsoever. Occasionally you may catch a fleeting tease of a few familiar notes but it never fully commits, so it ends up sounding quite bland and generic. I found myself muting the in-game score and playing the soundtrack to Birth of the Federation in the background instead.I was hoping to see more of a game plan from the developers about addressing shortcomings and releasing any DLC/Patch combos as Stellaris does, but after 3 months of very light bugfixing patches (Their last post is from December as of the time of this review, just over 2 months ago), they haven't made any indications they're working on anything bigger so I guess they're done with it. Now to wait another 20 years until someone makes another attempt at a Star Trek 4x, I suppose...EDIT: There it is; a month after I post this review there's the official announcement that no further work will be done. Paradox are really burning through their goodwill.

_childDocuments_.review: When this game first came out, I had high hopes for a great new Star Trek game. After playing a few hours of the game, I became very disappointed. There are pros and cons to the game so I'll start with the positive notes and then point out the negatives. This is one of the most beautifully designed games which clear images of planets, ship designs, and galaxy maps. I enjoyed see the realist look to the galaxy and solor systems. I did enjoy being able to zoom into the solor system to see the ships in action (scanning planets, fighting enemy ships, and more). I enjoyed seeing the opportunity to build specific ships from the tv series (e.g., USS Enterprise, USS Cerritos, etc.). I did appreciate the tutorial was better designed than Stellaris' tutorial. Then regarding the negative aspects of the game: The gameplay was too much like Stellaris that I felt like I was playing the same game essentially. The tree development process was interesting and did give a more Star Trek vibe but I felt it limited the game play in variability. I also was surprised that Paradox only included four factions to play (Federation, Klingon, Romulans, and Cardassians) and would have appreciated if a few other factions were included such as the Ferengi and the Breen. While there is an attempt to create distinct behaviors and styles among the factions, I didn't really get the feeling that each faction was unique (other than the tree development) but felt like the factions were the same with just different pictures. I think the game designers made this too complex as well, too much micromanagement of all the features. The last best Star Trek strategy game ever designed was Star Trek Birth of the Federation (90s). I think if a game designer sees this feedback, they should review STBotF as a great starting point and game format. Really all that is needed for a good game would need is to update STBotF with current level animation, user-friendly mouse interation, similar links to flow of information, latest canon ships and characters, selecting bridge crews for ships, and allow players to have the freedom to start at different stages of development (pre-federation or post-federation), and allow for wide range of re-playability or players can set the map to match the franchise. A simplier version of the game would be more popular I think among Star Trek fans. If you enjoyed Stelleris and can't get enough of it, this game will be enjoyable for you. If you are a Star Trek fan looking for a new ST strategy game, I don't recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Although there are enough changes that make this a different game, to the point where you can say that if you like this, you might not like Stellaris, and if you like Stellaris, you might not necessarily like this, and because I like Trek, I like Stellaris, and I'm not bothered one way or the other about DLCs, I was on the fence about a 'Yes' or 'No' for this game. Overall, the graphical representations of the IP give a general 'Star Trek' feel to the game, and as a Stellaris player, it was easy to pick up and deal with the new or different mechanics this game offers. There are, however, many QoL features in Stellaris that are frustratingly absent in this game. Manual Empire Capital relocation, or Autobuild for Construction Ships are two good examples.In the end I decided to give this game a 'No', and since it's essentially a Star Trek skin on another game, I want to focus on thae Trek rather than the actual gameplay.The Federation starts with the 4 founder races. There are no Remans. Not at the start, and not later on.I got Janeway as a special character as part of a Borg storyline. Great, except I was playing as the Romulans.People can and will debate the inclusion itself of the Hobus Supernova, but in the game it's utterly unavoidable. In every new game. the Romulans will lose their capital after about 40 years or so. If you've played Stellaris, you'll know why this is might be a problem. If you're a Trek fan from before 2009, albeit for different non game related reasons, you'll also see why this might be a problematic thing to put in the game from an immersion perspective.There are a few notable exceptions, like Singularity Cores for Romulans, but for the most part, everybody gets everything technology wise. In short, there is one tech tree with very little individualisation for the different factions. Romulans can research and use Phaser Cannons, and the Cardassians, Plasma Torpedoes. There are a lot of events and 'quests' to do as you play through the game, which is really good. The trouble is that a lot of them either don't make any contextual sense for where you are in your current game, or else flat out happen in the 'wrong' order.The game is set just after the Khitomer Massacre, and the 4 major powers start off well established (4 colonized systems), yet only the Miranda (or equivalent) class size ship (Stellaris Corvettes) are available at game start. This is partly due to the Tech Tree having been borrowed from Stellaris. It works well there. It's problematic for a Star Trek game based in a particular era. In one game, I unlocked the Enterprise D before I'd researched even the second tier of Starship. Disappointingly, this is the Intrepid Class. Read the first line of this paragraph again.The whole game is oddly specific about so many things, yet really not when it comes to others. Romulus has to die, but can then use Phaser Cannons. Like... is it a 'canon' based game or isn't it? The Borg didn't speak to me like they do in the trailer. I had to... ugh.... read... 'Resistance is futile'.In the diplomacy screens, each Civ (majors and minors) only have one line. The Klingon guy sounds like Brad from accounts - even if you have the preorder Klingon language DLC.There's not a great deal of major Trek related issues. But there are an absolute mountain of minor issues that add up to an overall 'Trek-like' experience... kinda. It's a little too Stellaris and a little just not Trek enough for the whole thing to feel off.So... I played 32 more hours since posting this review, most of that time in multiplayer. I'm feeling very uninspired by subsequent patches. I understand that they're busy fixing more critical problems that should never have been part of release, and I haven't played since 1.0.2, but nothing they've patched so far touches anything that goes anywhere near what I feel are the underlying issues. It's still a 'no' but the more I see, the less on the fence about this verdict I become.

_childDocuments_.review: Thus far, it's exactly what I wanted out of a Star Trek 4x game.  ---------....6 hours later....Playing Federation.Have liberated Bajor.About to help evacuate Romulus before the sun explodes.  Good:  -It is a love letter to fans of the TNG/DS9 era.  I AM the Federation, and I feel like I am.-The mechanics are different enough from Stellaris to feel fresh-Looks absolutely beautiful.  I literally just sat there watching a construction ship build a starbase for 5 minutes when I first started up the game.  -The diplomacy feels a lot more involved than Stellaris ever did.-You get to run around with the Enterprise.-Music is good.Feedback:  -While I agree with the devs reasoning behind not flooding the game with ship classes... having played it now, I feel like it does in fact either need a few more ship classes, or at least they need to have you unlock the classes they do have faster.  I'm 6 hours into the game and I still only have 2 ship types.  -A few glitches here and there, but nothing game-breaking... mostly a few voice notifications that are popping for the wrong events.  -The espionage system, while more involved than Stellaris (good), is bit obtuse.  You keep getting this "silent alarm tripped" event, which apparently is supposed to be your signal to do an anti-espionage mission with your spy ship, but the game never tells you that, even in full tutorial mode.  -I feel like research needs to be a bit less random in spots.  Right now I've unlocked two different types of disruptors for the Federation, and still don't have photon torpedoes.  Overall, I'd say it's at least 8.5/10 as is, and it can only get better as they patch things and adjust stuff like research weights.As of 11/21:  Devs have put out a lot of fixes and respond well to feedback.  Gonna call it a 9/10 now.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I have now played 13 hrs of the game.   While you cant play the other races within ST, they are there.    As the Fed, you can integrate them, as the other starting races, you can conquer them for their civics.   The anomalies need work.  I so far have repeated 2 of the anomalies in the same game with only 13 hrs of play.   How you get the enterprise is interesting as well(I wont give it away).    But I dont like how they do it for 2 reasons.   1, its not the true enterprise D.   Its based upon the tech level of the shields, weapons, etc.   So its basically just a named ship, and an expensive 1 at that.  The traditions are interesting, but make no real sense for the FED.   The ascension perks are decent, I actually liked some of them for the FED.   The research tech so far is a little under whelming.   Now mind you, I havent tried the other races yet, but for the FED, they are not unique in my opinion.   Maybe I havent gotten far enough down the tech tree to see, but to me they seem cookie cutter.  Example, there are no bonuses to diplomacy which the fed is known for.   There is no real tech dealing with the prime directive nor any reason to follow the prime directive as the fed either that I can see.  Also, as the fed, you are interacting with the Borg way to early for the tech tree limits.   If they are starting in this time frame, then some of the tech should already be there.   Also, starting in this time frame, where is the Federation Council.   That should be a big part of it, and they are not to be seen.  Star Fleet Academy seems to be just a building on Earth, nothing more.  The game has potential, but right now it isnt.   Dont get me wrong, I will continue to play it to see if I am missing something later in the game, but I just dont know.For me, play Horizons or Civilisation for Stellaris.   More you can do with those mods and alot more immersive.   What they are doing is gearing the game towards dlcs.   I can see it now, a new race every 2 or 3 months at 12.99 a pop.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Stellaris clone.Worse, it's a fork off of one of the earlier versions of Stellaris, where you could DEFINITELY feel the jank that had to get patched out. And oh boy, the jank absolutely shows here. The UI scaling feature is completely borked, it makes some screens overflow off of your monitor. The game kept crashing on startup for me until I did a full reinstall. The UI is also, frankly, terrible in general. There's too many buttons that don't actually list what they do until you hover over them, which is absolutely dreadful for a game that's all about clicking on buttons to do things.Like open menus.And honestly, I don't really like how the game plays. There's way too much crap you have to micromanage. It's way more tedious than regular Stellaris. Like, hell, they actually managed to make espionage more tedious than in Stellaris. Originally, you'd just send your envoys over to spy. Now you have to recruit spies and physically fly them into enemy systems to perform espionage, and nine times out of ten your spies get murdered when the AI sends a fleet over. So that system's pointless and I have no idea why they'd implement espionage like that.They split governors off into their own little ship class too, so that's another thing you have to micromanage. Governor happens to be halfway across the quadrant when a special timed project pops up specifically requiring one? Welp, guess you're screwed. And on and on it goes. Pick this game up if you're a Trek fan, but just get Stellaris if you're in it for the 4x experience. Stellaris has way, way more features than this game does, it actually manages to be less jank, and it's got a modding community to boot.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a labor of love, in two ways. The devs putting the heart into this game, and the player having to fight the game to enjoy some Star Trek. A very soft "not recommended" from me. Though I don't feel it was a waste of money as Paradox games usually age like wine, I do feel too frustrated to play again in the near future after just 11 hours and 1.5 games. Pros: Where No Man Has Gone Before: The artwork, setting, and attention to detail here are amazing. It's clear the devs have a love for Star Trek that shines through every aspect of this game. Tomorrow is Yesterday: It's Stellaris lite. I've got a ton of time in Stellaris and I've been playing since release, but sometimes the game gets a bit bogged down. It's nice to jump into a game here and not have to deal with a lot of the bloat of starting a game in Stellaris. Lower Decks: Much of the Stellaris engine fits very well in the Star Trek universe and about 80% of the game just feels great. My first five hours felt like a breath of fresh air and just felt Star Trek. Neutral: Deja Q: It's a Stellaris reskin. I don't think that's a bad thing, but you should absolutely be aware of that going in. Hollow Pursuits: The focus trees are a fun addition to the game but are not super fleshed out. Basically a button click for things you were already gonna do. Looking forward to expansions on the concept like in other Paradox titles. A couple times events and focus tree items got jammed up and impossible to continue. If you don't keep on them then key leaders will die from old age before you can complete the line and this will hard stop those events and focus tree items. Unsure if this is working as intended or not.Cons:The Menagerie: Deeply frustrating events. The events in war are exactly the same in all four empires (I assume, they were identical between UFP and RE). And boy are they awful. One of them is that one of your fleets just straight up disappears. This only triggers during a war. It absolutely lost me a couple wars early game when one third of my military just vanishes. Then there are a number of events that occur over the course of the war that are seemingly intended to tell you how the war is going, but trigger randomly. Star Fleet troops are in the middle of invading Cardassia, their fleets burning in space, Bajor liberated, and I get an event pop up titled "We are losing this war." There are at least three others like that that seem to be an attempt to give some flavor to war but are not tied to reality and seem to pop up at random.  I, Borg: Unfinished events like the *spoiler* that seem to hint towards bigger events that never trigger. I played a full game as the Federation and it was so boring after the first half. Once you eclipse the other powers they essentially stop participating in the game. The Federation (correctly) can't claim systems and generally can't be aggressive. This is good from a lore perspective but essentially means the last 200 years of gameplay is Microsoft Excel simulator. Also there was a bug that made it impossible to assimilate minor powers into the federation. Schisms: Diplomacy sucks. This was always a complaint of Stellaris but is unfortunately severely highlighted in this game, especially if you're playing Romulus or UFP. The UFP is relegated to a purely reactionary force on the galactic stage since you can't do anything. Spying also sucks which means playing the Romulans is like playing the Klingons or Cardassians but painted green. Face of the Enemy: Enemy fleets are really jump happy. The enemy will have a half dozen military fleets jumping around your systems like a squirrel on crack. They don't do anything but sit on the edge of the system not engaging with your starbase (even when they could easily defeat it) and jump away as soon as you enter the system. Makes war a very frustrating endeavor.Turnabout Intruder: The pirates make me want to put a phaser in my mouth. They will randomly jump into your systems and early game you cannot repel them. They destroy your starbase meaning you have to reclaim the system and also takes 1,000 each of the basic resources away from you. This is devastating early game and there doesn't seem to be a way to do anything about it until late game when you can repel the fleets or find the pirate system and ask them pretty please to stop. This is what finally broke me into using the console to just delete the fleets as soon as I see them. They're infinite though so it's a temporary measure at best. Balance of Terror: I have literally never seen the AI employ a cloaking device despite the fact I know it's in the game. Shades of Grey: All the factions are boring are seems to be kneecapped by being crammed into the Stellaris engine. I've already elaborated on the UFP. Romulus has an event pretty early game where the sun explodes. It's fun from a lore and universe perspective but even metagaming and preparing for it it still absolutely wrecks your economy. I haven't played the Cardassians or Klingons yet. I think both probably lend themselves better to the engine as they are more conquest focused empires but I'm not very optimistic after the UFP and Romulans. The Trouble with Tribbles: It's pretty buggy. I know that's par for the course these days but still.~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~Edit: Got the itch while watching DS9 and reluctantly played another campaign. I played as UFP all the way to 2650 and got a victory. No material changes to my review but some observations:-Couldn't complete a focus tree because of a bug. It said I didn't own a system that I clearly did. Deleted the starbase and rebuilt, donated the system and retook it, nothing fixed it. -Even as Evil UFP you can only claim three systems at once. I had to spend a couple hundred years chipping away at the other powers despite the fact I could have conquered them all at once. -The borg are the worst. I clapped the "end game crisis" before mid game. I didn't even use all my fleets. -The other three powers are way too diplomatic. The Klingons, Romulans, and Cardassians never even attempted to conquer minor powers. That's like the Cardassians whole thing and the other two should at least be more aggressive and treacherous respectively. -I threw everything into liberating Bajor very early in the game. Bajor responded by hating me and forming several treaties with the Cardassians. I guess Kai Winn won in this universe.

_childDocuments_.review: No, I can't recommend the game. And not just because it's a reskin of another game. Because there's just not much there to it. There's only one galaxy size and one galaxy type, and it's pretty small. You can never explore the gamma or delta quadrants. Game play amounts to sitting around and waiting for events much of the time.It feels like a demo to the game they should have made.And I'm already seeing political stuff in the game. In before "Star Trek was always about politics!" No, not like this. For example, there's one 'event' where a colony becomes a matriarchy and it just magically solves all problems for it. That's it. That's the event. Compare that to the TNG episode about a matriarchy where they're executing people for having traditional relationships. Two sides to every coin etc. (Update: now they are riots on that planet because their polices are too gender "binary". It'd almost be an improvement if it were riots for any other reason, but no Cardassian in Star Trek ever expressed any ideas similar to gender theory. Really, you're making a TNG-era game. Stop inserting modern politics.)Also, now there are Cardassians of every color. Because I guess "gray lizard people with spoons on their heads" was too difficult a description to follow. Not every faction needs to be a mirror of Earth and its interracial politics. Some can be, you know, alien.That stuff is the bridge too far for me. Not because I disagree with the politics of the devs, but because it's not like Star Trek was. I disagreed with the politics of most Star Trek writers and I still loved the show. Because they were good writers who knew how to justify their beliefs and didn't just beat everyone over the head with them. But if a game is sold to me based on nostalgia, I'd expect them to try to make it the way Star Trek used to be, not the way modern politics would have liked it to be.Speaking of stuff that's not like Star Trek btw, the weapon effects and the music are not like Star Trek. You'd think they could have gotten something that at least sounds similar for the music, but it's very generic.So, yeah, this is not for me because it's simplistic and not like Star Trek. Maybe some mods will fix it, if Paradox doesn't take them down, since I know they're famous for doing that.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for something that has a Star Trek taste to it that you can play over the course of a day, Infinite has you covered. If you're an unhealthy Star Trek nerd like me, this won't sate your hunger.I played a game up to about 2405 as the Federation, and there were some aspects I enjoyed:---------------------Being able to request missions from minor powers to strengthen relations is neat, and provides an opportunity to do something with your hands instead of just having an envoy sit in a cubicle on the target's home planet to raise relations is nice.-Some of the events that fire from exploration or from colonization do have some follow-up to them, making it feel like there's some continuity to your story. I'm not sure it'll hold up over multiple plays, but it felt nice.-Art is good to look at, sound is welcoming. Models all looked clean.--------------------There's plenty I didn't like:---------------------I at first thought I was in for a treat seeing a Miranda-class variant (Antares I think), that we would be seeing a great collection of ships that existed up until 2346 when the game starts. Instead, I quickly found out that I didn't have access to anything else. There was clear gameplay reasoning to just have the corvette available to everyone, but it's really jarring to just be researching the Excelsior-class in 2401, a good 120 years after the class was introduced in the timeline.-The tech piggybacks off of that. Some sort of basic plasma launcher, and phase cannons? Starfleet is sporting at least Type VIII phasers and photon torpedoes by this point as standard, even on it's smaller patrol craft.-It feels like there's a lot of tech in the game just to give the inherited Stellaris research system something to do. Scientific discovery is one of the mission statements of Starfleet, but it seemed like a lot of busy work just to make it feel like I was making scientific progress that should already have been made by this point in the timeline.-Mission tree gets fouled up too easily. Really ought to be yanked altogether to let the sandbox live long and prosper.-I'm sure there's more to the spying game if you're playing as the Cardassians or Romulans, but it felt like an afterthought playing as the Federation. Sloan sitting in his ship dropping propaganda leaflets on a planet isn't exactly a great implementation of this. Perhaps spies are on ships so as to facilitate the minor powers missions that come up, but it would be better to just put all the spying stuff into a UI like Stellaris currently does.-Highly static between the major powers. There'd be a treaty here or there, but overall I didn't see much happening between the four of us. Everyone seemed content to explore and expand in directions away from each other. I dissolved the Romulan Neutral Zone just to try and get something started, but not a peep from them. Most exciting thing was the destruction of Romulus, which ended up making us friends since I went down the mission tree for it. Wasn't expecting the Klingons to take over the Romulans, but I was anticipating something more exciting than what I got.-Voice acting needs work. Quality of it was similar to that of the mods we have for Stellaris. I don't mind that for the mods, but I'm expecting better from a product that I'm paying for.-Entire leaders system needs to be either reworked, or removed. Notable characters are something we want to see, but utilizing what Stellaris had essentially a few years ago (which was also clunky then) doesn't do those characters justice.-The Trek universe is way bigger than what's presented. Sure, we're limited to the Alpha and Beta Quadrants, but even those are FULL of other species. Let's get them in there!--------------------I think it's important to make a distinction moving forward on fans versus nerds when we're looking at Star Trek games. This game was made by Trek fans, no doubt there. There's a lot that looks like Star Trek, smells like Star Trek, and tastes like Star Trek. It's unfortunately less filling.What we really need is some deep Star Trek nerds to get together with the grand strategy nerds to put together a game for us.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a real shame that I have to not recommend this game, but given there are some really good Star Trek mods already out for Stellaris, this feels like a major downgrade for a paid title. The gameplay is what you'd expect from Stellaris, in fact, it's almost 1:1 to it, and what's worse it's a super old build of Stellaris without some of the great updates that have happened (i.e. having a ruling council, needing a scientist to lead each branch of research, construction ships not able to auto-construct) That said, where you'd expect this game to really shine - the Star Trek lore - is really poorly implemented. Here's just a few examples of the immersion breaking gameplay:-You'll get the opportunity to build the Enterprise-D, but Will Riker will exist as a separate "admiral" level character that can't be assigned to the Enterprise-Captain Ben Sisko appears but without the Defiant-Janeway can return, but will be commanding a generic, random science vessel "The Fearless" instead of Voyager. -Data can be recruited but is a generic SCIENTIST slot character, who also can't be assigned to the Enterprise-Spock makes an appearance, but not as an Envoy They really clearly just rushed the development of this game and didn't take time to truly create a Star Trek game, but instead, reskin as quickly as possible old Stellaris and its event mechanics. Instead of overhauling the ship system and having hero ships that have multiple officer slots, to recreate that feel of crews like the Enterprise, they just cobbled things together. What's more, you start with Miranda-class vessels and then will randomly get further patterns via research instead of having a tree to follow to unlock later, less anachronistic designs, unlike both ST mods for Stellaris where you get ship patterns based on the stardate.TL:DR: It will wow you if you're a Trekkie for about 30 minutes and if you already own Stellaris isn't really that much of a change to warrant spending money on it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is full of bugs. Like big weird ones. I haven't had any crash issues like others, but stuff like enemy ships getting stuck inside my starbases, fleets that decide they won't fight, multiple instances of the same character running around, big end-game events just being broken, and so forth. And there are TONS of issues where the developers either didn't understand star trek, or didn't care to pursue "realistic" mechanics. The TNG bridge crew are all here, but they won't work together and they're all "admirals" or "scientists" or whatever. The progression from one ship class to the next is super weird and doesn't follow the chronology of the show at all. It goes on and on. So many problems.And yet... despite all this there's a fun game here and an interesting Star Trek experience. We've gotten a ton of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ Star Trek games over the years. This one is very different. I'm going to hang in there hoping for fixes and changes, and I'm going to keep on playing despite all the problems. Highly recommend for any Star Trek fan who enjoys the 4x genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets a lot of comparison with Stellaris and it's justified, it uses the same engine and looks and plays pretty much the same. I have tried to play Stellaris but never gotten really far in a game so I can't really compare the both. I have gotten further in this game and even finished a campaign. Here is what I like about it. - You already start with a few systems under your belt. Which means you have a small head start and skip the slow beginning in a lot of other 4X games. This doesn't mean that there isn't much to discover, the opposite is true. But it's also not that much that you can't wrap your head around it.- It's an open universe in that you can travel to all the systems within reach. You aren't limited to travel lanes which a lot of other 4X games start out with. That also means you can't create a bottleneck where you build up defences. Mixing up things compared to a lot of other games in the genre. - The game still offers a lot in-game systems. Most I properly haven't discovered yet but the mission tree helps with this. It already pointed me towards things I wouldn't have discover otherwise at this point. However I still needed to go outside the game to look up some of the things required. An in-game encyclopedia would have been nice. - But the biggest draw for me is the Star Trek IP. Growing up with Star Trek makes it so much better to play with a known empire instead of something unfamiliar. Is everything perfect, sadly not. The game suffers from some bugs but up until now the developer has been very active in patching the game. Some systems could have been developed a little further as well. Small note on the Steam Deck, it runs good on it. It does require some tweaking in order to get the text more readable but otherwise I haven't run into any issues. In the end however the most important thing is having fun and that's why it gets a thumbs up from me because I have.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is much more than just Stellaris with a coat of paint on it. It adds several cool new mechanics, while streamlining others. It adds significantly more to your library than a few stellaris DLCs and being priced at 1.5 times as the typical stellaris expansion the price is completely fair. And it's also a good entry point into the world of 4x games.What do I like:- all the things i already like about stellaris- Mission tree (OMG I really love that thing, and I'm working on a mod to make it even bigger)- Galactic tension and balance of power influencing diplomacy (although it could be more impactful)- Every nation feels and plays unique- It just feels very star trek- The devs are listening to feedback and continuously improve the game- There is a lively and motivated modding communityWhat annoys me:- Many of the new mechanics are not as impactful as they could be (there are mods to fix that tho)- The steamroll tipping point comes earlier than in stellaris- putting governors and spies on ships was a mistakeThis game might not be for everyone, but if you're a trekkie and a strategy game enjoyer you should definitely go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not one to often review, but the people who take to this complaining that it's "just a Stellaris reskin" are wrong. There are definitely some similarities, but there are enough other mechanics to make things interesting. Yes, I'm recommending the game, but there problems.For one, the game definitely needs some polish that it evidently didn't get before release. For example, when I go to my envoys to see what they're doing, I get the base game code for integrating a new species into the Federation. "vol_INTSPE##" or something like that. I also see that in diplomatic modifications. Today I completed the mission to save the Romulan people when their star exploded and it was like "compmis_ex" +200. Another is "warp_agreement_yes".... Which I don't even know what a "warp agreement" is. (It's not open borders, that's a separate thing.) I figure a patch or two will fix some/most/all of that.For all that, I've been playing the Federation of Planets, and I've gotten to explore a large amount of official timeline and I've decided to do the whole "benevolent Federation" thing. It is possible to make the Federation into a conquering police state by fulfilling different missions in the tree. I haven't touched any of the other three factions, so I can't say what their mission trees look like. Science is handled in a way that I quite honestly like, with just "Science" being generated and applied to all the trees equally, instead of getting specific amounts of society/physics/engineering, though the tech tree is done with "cards" shuffled into those three groups just like it is in Stellaris.There is a complaint that ship advances come far too slowly, and I have to agree. I'm five hours into a game, and I only just got the second ship class. They're equipped with weapons that were FAR more advanced than what they actually had in the show. I'd rebalance those mechanics if I were them.I'm a trek fan, but only from the tv shows and the movies, and I've really enjoyed what I have so far, which is not the complete story. And only from the Federation of Planets side of things so far.Someone in one of the reviews says that the map is always the same. That's not true. The map is slightly different in its initial setup (and does change slightly from playthrough to playthrough, even when you don't alter the settings.) But you do get the basic, Federation to the South, Cardassians to the West, Klingons to the East and Romulans to the North, with the Romulan Neutral Zone making up a significant portion of what would be the Federation Border. The map outside the starting area is different for every playthrough. The map is somewhat less than lore accurate, mostly to prevent the Federation from having a MASSIVE advantage. If the map were lore accurate, the Federation would have empty space to the "North", the "South", and the East, in the North or South depending on where the Cardassian Union is placed on the maps. Even the "lore-accurate" maps aren't all consistent.Yes, I have some complaints about the UI, and I had to work the graphics for about ten minutes to get them to look right on my very small display (I have a 13-inch Macbook Air so it can be tough to do that, but I make it work with all the other Grand Strategy games.) And there are some crashes and some weird things that have happened (some combination of buttons reverted my graphics to what the game originally set them to that was all wrong, and I had to save and quit and come back to fix it.Finally, the music is much more Stellaris than Star Trek. Sometimes you hear a little note or three of Star Trek in there, but if you're expecting to boot it up to the Star Trek: The Next Generation/DS9/Voyager theme, you're going have to do it yourself (it's not hard if you own the music), or wait for somebody to mod it.If you're hesitant about it, go ahead and wait a few days for some of the kinks to be ironed out, but if you're able to look past some of the warts, and you want a Star Trek Game, I would recommend Star Trek: Infinite.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek: Infinite has a lot to offer for players that love the genre, but also for novices as the learning curve is gentle, and the level of immersion is great. The balance of game events and the pace of evolution and progress you feel while doing research, exploring, and doing all kind of things... it's just an awesome, relaxing, and great experience overall. It just keeps you in anticipation as to what is going to happen next, while you are doing and learning all kinds of things.On the Start Trek theme, if you are a fan of course it's a plus. Keep in mind it's done in such a way that if you're not familiar with the story, you'll have a blast anyway. I've only had a few hours played so far, but I can tell it's one of those games you need to be careful not to lose track of time!  Plus, as a dad with young kids, I truly enjoy games that I can just start playing at a random time during the day (or night, sacrificing a bit of sleep - whenever those 30-60 minutes are available really), and be able to get out of it an enjoyable experience playing the game, even if it's just 30 minutes. Likewise,  you can go 1 hour or 2 hours and have a blast without feeling that you "have to" before reaching a specific milestone.I truly recommend this game, and as a person just getting into the genre, I hope folks are not afraid to try something new and give it a try. It may feel a bit intimidating at first, but after the first 20-30 minutes, you'll get the hang of it.

_childDocuments_.review: After time has passed and updates have been released, I would like to say that this game is definitely one of my most favorite Star Trek/Space 4X Grand Strategy game! Stellaris still being my number one favorite though but Star Trek Infinite is climbing up to become second!There is a lot of complaints of this game being Stellaris. But it is not. What people fail to realize that Stellaris was built to be solely about Stellaris, nothing else. Not Star Wars, not Stargate, not Mass Effect and definitely not Star Trek. Are there total conversion mods that turns Stellaris into those games? Yes. But that does not make Stellaris a Star Trek Game or a Star Wars Game, etc. Stellaris will always be a Stellaris game.Star Trek Infinite is its own game. Does it have elements of Stellaris? Of course. Developers were given permission to use Stellaris to build this game. But there are obvious differences that this game has compared to Stellaris.Then there was the hiccup at launch. Who is truly surprised that games come out buggy at launch? It's lately been becoming a thing, which is annoying indeed but at this point, it should be expected. Cyberpunk, Pokemon Scarlet/Violet, Starfield. And more. Did the Developers hop onto fixing the hiccups at launch? Their response to fixing the game so that players can play it, was quite quick.And what others also fail to realize, is that it will always take time to flesh out the bugs, iron out the kinks, and make the game better over time. Stellaris wasn't perfect at start. It was great, but over the years, the developers improved it to where it is today and it is so much better than it was at launch. 25 tile planets...crazy border gore...multiple FTL options that was slogging down the game for most people. Again, the developers spent years improving Stellaris to where it is today and thus have the experience and tips that they could offer to the developers of Star Trek Infinite to help improve it more quickly.But these things do take time.Overall, I was quite excited when this game was announced, very excited when it was launched and not as disappointed as most people were and definitely was not shaming the game either after playing it for the first time. I know improvements will come, and I do quite enjoy the game as it is now and cannot wait for more! We all know there's going to be DLC in the future but I am quite excited to learn what they have planned for the future of this game. Perhaps they could offer a preview to a roadmap?Take my review as you will, it is my opinion after all and if you do not agree with my opinion, that is your choice and it will not alter my opinion or my review of this game in any way.Edit:Unfortunately the latest announcement states that the continued development of this game has ended. Likely due to Paramount but no one will ever know.BUT there is enough for the modding community to keep the game alive! And I for one, who have plans for this game in a group I am in, I too plan to keep this game alive. Games that have been cancelled have been revived and development returned to full force. I hope some day, that too will happen, with Star Trek: Infinite. I refuse to give up hope and no one will take that away from me.Live Long and Prosper!

_childDocuments_.review: The tech is all over the place, early game tech shows up in late game and mid game tech in the early, which brings about massive issues with the economy, as in if you don't get the early game tech for minerals or power you are in a one sided hell of trying to balance out your eco. and your military ends up going to ♥♥♥♥ as well, i played a Cardassian camp in which i ended up unlocking a cruiser type ship before i was able to even unlock basic weapons to use on them, you end up in early game 2500 lvl tech for all of one pick then you get anything from 3500-11000. its insane to me why this is. And then there is the officer cap, and by that i mean every time you build a ship you have to have officers to use with them, and the incoming officers is to start +10 and the most i have gotten it has been +50 so when you build a fleet you run out of officers before you even finish the fleet and thats assuming you have unlocked a fleet cap over 40 before mid game (Which is unlikely). The Federation of all things attacked me and i had to try and pump out fleets to counter (as i didn't have many if any ships at that time) and ran out of officers before even making half the ships i needed, which is an issue as it halves your fleets damage and when you are fighting an a.i that's openly cheating pumping fleet after fleet into your territory.... Right so update 1, turn on the game get the launcher click play, wait for it to load, then click new game, and hit enter... and it crashes, checking the files does nothing reinstalling does nothing, cant play the game.... so why did i buy a game i cant play? (FIXED, go into your anti-virus and put the game in your white list e.i allow list)Update 2, i can load old games but not start new ones, having said that federation end game event is  non stop waves of borg, and you have to research there warp something or other while also fending them off... which you cant because they spawn into any system you have left as soon as you kill there first attack wave, so any ships you build are either immediately destroyed or end up in a never ending fight that makes it really difficult to get said ships OUT of the system, oh and when you go to the area you need to research there is a MASSIVE fleet of borg like 50 times stronger then anything you have fought to that point waiting for you, on my second node i lost an entire maxed out fleet of sovereign class starships in seconds i was only able to get one ship out. (Note: if you do the janeway quest line the borg die out and that end game never happens)Final Update, now that i have fixed most of the issue myself as support is as per the norm useless, the game is... ok, you will need to use the mods that are out to fix minor bugs and make the game more startrek as well as open up better ways of doing things like being able to conquer the other factions as the federation rather then only beating the hell out of them then saying "ok bye!" and nothing else, as well as being able to unlock ship tech in research order rather than time order, etc etcThe game is playable and can be fun with the right mods, is it worth what they are asking? No. would i recommend buying it full price again No, would it be better just getting the startrek mod for stallaris? that is up to you, i don't like that mod as its more cluttered than i like BUT it is pretty much this game but with more junk thrown in.So in conclusion, It is a funISH game if you mod it and fix the minor bugs with said mods, however it would be better if they fixed the issues themselves, which i'm sure in time they will as per the norm with paradox games. if you made it this far into my book of things i did in this then gratz you get a cookie! my rating for the game is a flat 5 not the best and not the worst something i would buy if on sale for 50% or more off.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trek Infinite, stellaris's trek flavored kindred.rating 9/10first i will start this review by naming some of the current issues with the game that the devs have been informed of and are looking for fixes. ~there are some crash to desktop issues primarily involving firewall permissions, and MAC OS~DLC authentication issues that can cause some bugs~loading screen issues related to specific systems which the exact cause has not quite been pinned down. im starting the review with these because of the mixed reviews rating steam currently has listed for this game, to explain that these issues are painfully clear to the devs and have been reported ad infinitum in their discord server and they are currently working on patches to fix them ASAP. onto the actual review nowPros: ~a healthy balance of exploration, strategy, combat and planning. unlike infinite's big brother stellaris, infinite has a markedly higher focus on the logistics side of things, stellaris feels significantly faster because all of the mandatory content  of stellaris IE the primary gameplay loop of explore>colonise>conquer>explore repeating, is distributed into the new logistics systems. this game is not stellaris, it is not a clone with a trek costume on. it has unique mechanics that require additional attention and slow the overall march of the game down. you MUST focus on all fronts or you will fall behind~beautiful visuals and artwork~incredible attention to detail in how systems interact with each other which ends up rewarding careful planning in powerful ways~a basic but comprehensive tutorial to properly introduce a new player to all of the above systems~a nail on the head star trek theme. no expense was spared in detail or design making an overall authentic accurate star trek experience encompassing DS9 VOY and TNG star trek eras.cons:~the game could be considered very slow for some people, especially for people who like the more combat oriented feel of stellaris~infinite is not what i would call "easy", individual mechanics are sometimes simple and sometimes intricate but learning to balance and use them all continuously is taxing mentally and if you arent used to that level of depth or detail infinite will almost certainly run away from you occasionally and leave you reeling to correct some problemsi give infinite a 9/10. any "complaints" i have come down more to nitpicking than genuine criticism. the game fleshes out all of its mechanics, provides a lore accurate and friendly star trek experience mixed with the fundamentals of stellaris with its own evolution on the original concepts that create something entirely new. the devs are also incredibly responsive on all levels and immediately set out diagnosing day 1 launch issues. final verdict: if you dont mind some bugs and troubleshooting buy it now. its certainly worth the full price tag if my pros section interested you. if you would prefer to avoid bugs for now, give it a few days and watch the game in the store or your library. once the launch issues are ironed out infinite will be a masterpiece experience even for new players.

_childDocuments_.review: Since my childhood, 'Birth of the Federation' has held a special place in my heart, making it one of my all-time favorites and a truly formative experience. Nimble Giant, you're incredibly close to capturing the essence of the Star Trek universe, and I commend your efforts. Please, stay with us on this journey.It's essential, however, to consider overhauling key details that avid Trek fans will readily notice. Enhancements to the user interfaces that genuinely differentiate the major factions would be a significant step forward. This includes distinguishing elements such as the colors of torpedoes, the distinctive combat noises of weaponry, and creating a captivating ambient soundscape reminiscent of the Star Trek universe. I understand the potential limitations imposed by licensing from Paramount, and it may be cost-prohibitive at this early stage, but these refinements would truly elevate the gaming experience.For those who may compare this game to Stellaris, consider why reinvent the wheel? The potential for expansion through downloadable content is virtually limitless, and Nimble Giant should seize this opportunity to secure their fan base's loyalty. The first key stage in this process is addressing issues and working on improvements, and with dedication, I believe the game will only get better over time. Please, Nimble Giant, don't give up on us.Nimble Giant, you're on the cusp of realizing the infinite potential of this game. Take the naysayers' remarks on the chin and work this rough stone into a smooth gem, it will pay off for everyone. Please continue your fantastic work, and we're on the verge of something truly 'infinite' in the Star Trek gaming universe.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The initial review above was, as you can see, predicated on the developers taking ownership of the messes, instead they have cowardly abandoned their responsibility. This is a shameful display. Do not purchase this game, as it gives tacit support to these people.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of both Star Trek and strategy games. This game is a good blend of both.Negative reviewers want this game to both more and less Stellaris. This, to me, is a mistake. The game is approachable for players who are newer to the genre, and it foregrounds the Trek universe. Many of the game's discoverable anomalies and events mirror Star Trek episodes. They're cleverly written and help to build the immersion.Players who expect the game to perfectly match the Trek timeline will be disappointed. With so many canonical events, some of them fire out of order or in ways that are anachronistic. These misalignments are occasionally jarring, but I can't imagine the difficulty of keeping characters, events, and conditions appropriately locked together while still giving the player freedom.In its current release, the game has some bugs, most of which are only a little annoying. Dismayingly, my current save file (35 hours in) has become corrupt and unplayable. I expect these kinds of errors will be remedied in patches. Though I can't continue my current adventure, it was fun along the way.As with most other Paradox releases, this one will no doubt have scads of DLC: playable factions, events, mechanics, and more. I'm excited to see what comes. For now, though, I'm happy to have purchased and played this game. Is it perfect? No. But I can't wait to boldly go again soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Tentative recommendation. While it is unpolished and somewhat buggy, I think it demonstrates particular strengths over Stellaris itself -- the set galaxy encourages a very different way of engaging with the other powers, and certain new mechanics like crew being a resource, are something Stellaris itself could stand to port over.The biggest weakness of the game is that it is built on a significantly older branch of the Stellaris engine, with a lot of aspects and issues that Stellaris itself simply doesn't have. It's a fun twist on Stellaris, has a nice Star Trek coat of paint, but it'll only become great if it is polished and fixed up over time.

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly offline play.I really really wanted to like this - and I do, to a degree but not enough to suggest it.As said by others this is basically a Stellaris mod with the gameplay mechanisms all be familiar.  If you like the Stellaris gameplay loop you should find the gameplay loop enjoyable mostly.  It introduces a lot of Star Trek flavor but that's also a drawback in that it's done extremely poorly.The drawback though is that it feels very shallow - small number of ship types, inconsistent lore, limited races, limited meaningful events, etc.  At the end of the day, being the official Star Trek title it's almost more painful to play it than not because of how horrifically far it falls from where it should have been.  If Paradox had taken this seriously this game could have been AMAZING with a massive user base given the built in Star Trek fanatics.  I don't know the details of the development process but I question giving such a massive opportunity to a relatively unknown and untest dev like Nimble.If you like Star Trek you should stay away because it will hurt. _childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: The game has been abandoned while in a not quite finished state."Not quite finished" means: The game works! There are no major bugs or main missing features. HOWEVER, balancing of factions and content (or the lack thereof) suggest there was a plan for more updates and DLCs which now will never happen.Without this, the 4 factions feel quite unbalanced which makes playing with friends... challenging. Two of the factions barely even have reasons to interact with the rest of the main powers.The lack of content, however, is the big issue. After playing one game I didn't have the stomach to go in for another one. It feels like playing a Stellaris mod. There is one way to play (for each faction), there is only one way how the game will go and there is just one end-game crisis. War only happens if players (or the AI!) gets bored since expansion is just more useful. It gets repetative soooo quickly.If this game was just the starting point for years of cool stuff to come I'd say: Go grab it! But as it stands, just don't.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this to someone who loved playing Birth of the Federation back in the day, BUT be prepared for some major issues. This game should be in early access in it's current state. It has a lot of bugs that still need worked out. Has a lot of potential but still needs some work which I'm sure the modders and/or dev team can do to make it better. Can't wait to see what you all can do!!Here are some issues that will stand out to your hard core trek fans:1. Mission tree is more of a goals list than a story line. As Federation, don't resolve the growing the federation goal UNLESS you control Bajor. If you do, the story line will hit a dead end if the Cardasions take control of Bajor. The only way to progress is to go to war with them to take it back.1.2 Why Bajor anyway? Was there a DS9 fan on the dev team? Lets get more Borg!!!2. Feds can't go to war without going down the war mission tree. Horrible mechanic in my opinion. Makes for a boring run through and makes it difficult to have the Enterprise-D gain battle xp to complete Worf's mission. Not to mention you can't free Bajor...3. What the heck are those torpedo sounds?!?! They sound like those saturn missile battery fireworks! Clearly it was not a Trekie in charge of them. Weapons in Star Trek have a VERY specific sound and would easy to correct.4. Give us a tech tree, not a random chance at getting the tech we actually need. You end up sitting around just waiting and waiting after various cycles of repeated research items. Do the repeats even stack? I couldn't tell any difference after researching increased warp speed 10 times.5. Change the names of the upgrade types and make them closer to cannon. Some of the items don't belong in the Star Trek universe. Just pull the old tech manuals off the book shelf, it's all in there!6. Start and middle game are so much fun with tons to do! The end game is very anticlimactic. Make the mission tree a true story line that follows the players progress better. I want to see the exciting big battles, rescue missions, ect to finish out the game.7. Only resource that's an issue is the influence. Pray you find the Freingi that will sell you influence or you'll be waiting around for it to build back up. Not saying it's a bad mechanic, just needs to have other ways to gain it other than time. It limits outpost construction and taking over plants from war.8. I hate the war mechanic, only being able to take 3 plants every war and then a 10 year cool down to redeclare war. Get rid of both of those and rework how influence is gained.9. Ship tech not in cannon timeline. Why am I building Intrepid class before Excelsior? Way off on the Trek timeline.... Again pull out the old Star Trek Encyclopedia off the shelf, it has timelines....All in all, this is a neat start and I'm excited to see where this game can go!

_childDocuments_.review: The game isn't bad, but it isn't really a simulation of the Trek universe. If you just want to play a Trek themed game of stellaris, this would be a premium version of the trek total conversion mod. Its good looking, has lots trek art and stories, and if that's what you want I think this is actually worth it. However, for me I have decided to return the product as there just wasn't any mechanics that felt tweaked enough (or at all) to fit the trek universe. Personally, I really wanted ships to operate more independently like they do in Star Trek. Example of something cool they could have done with ships: Assigning a captain to each ship, and then an admiral per group of ships would have been much more interesting. The ships could have been off exploring and conducting missions (opportunity for more story) within a designated area and then recalled when combat is happening. Unfortunately, ships really just operate like they do in Stellaris. So they just sit around. The combat is also boring because of this and not very Trek. Other weird things like being able to just go to war with Cardassia with the sole goal to humiliate them as the Federation. No real effort to simulate the world of politics in the Trek universe. The map is also streamlined, making it seem kind of oddly shaped especially if you are familiar with Alpha and Beta quadrants.Overall, its just not really that immersive if you know the lore of Star Trek.
