_childDocuments_.review: I consider this game to be an excellent starting point for the future. This is essentially Stellaris in another timeline. However, there are a few major features that separate it from Stellaris in ways I find better. First, the game begins with a scenario more akin to the historical titles Paradox has; the 4X element of Stellaris had always struck me as at odds with most of the themes of PDX's major games and so this starting scenario really seems to fit in. I hope it's developed even further. 4X still exists, afterall its Star Trek, you must explore. The mission system which, I feel, redeemed Imperator: Rome and gave EU4 much replayability is introduced here as well. It can be more fleshed out, but it's here, and it's only here because there's a starting scenario.The aesthetic is very Star Trek, straight down to the combat. Combat looks like Trek, from the shield glow to the weapons fire. This isn't a mod like ST:New Horizons, you aren't going to have base game Stellaris content creeping in and ruining your immersion. Tech is limited by what faction you are; you won't go around seeing Disruptors as the Federation (or, so I think, maybe it's rare? I haven't seen it at any rate)There's a ship logistic range that keeps you from cheesing too hard, you have to actually conquer systems and not just Rush B to win wars. Growth is less explosive, influence income is seriously reduced and you'll be lucky to build a starbase a year. Snowballing still happens, but can you name a strategy game where it doesn't?I sincerely hope the Star Trek modding community from Stellaris considers making the move to this game. It's not fully fleshed out yet, but I feel like this game has good bones.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trek: Infinite

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of Star Trek The Next Generation, Voyager, Deep Space Nine, or Picard, DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. You will be SORELY disappointed in their extreme lack of attention to detail and disconnection from the franchise they attempted to cram into a reskin of Stellaris.The game timeline is all screwed up, events take place out of order, classic technology isn't in place when you start the game, recognizable ships are not in, territory that should be part of the Federation is not... This game is all kinds of BAD.For starters, you have to research very basic things like photon torpedoes and phasers, which were invented in the 22nd Century by the United Earth and by the early Federation in the 23rd Century respectively, so we should have the blue TOS phasers and photon torpedoes minimum at game start. I can see upgrading the blue phasers of TOS to modern orange ones as part of TNG, but those were also installed on various vessels as early as the Motion Picture era.Quantum torpedoes (blue) and transphasic torpedoes (yellow) were the ones introduced in the 24th century, trying to combat the Borg.And speaking of The Motion Picture, where are all the Excelsiors in this game? They were EVERY-FREAKING-WHERE in canonical TNG. As I see it the Federation should have access to those at the beginning of the game, just as we do the Mirandas. After all, they're both from the TMP era, which predates TNG.Hell, they even had a few modernized Constitution-class cruisers still active as sector flagships early on in TNG. Hello, Battle of Wolf 359? Admiral Hansen's flagship?So we start the game with NONE of the appropriate technologies or ships for the era, just replicators. If this is "a sop to gameplay" then they need to strongly reconsider the era in which this game takes place. It would be far more at home as a TOS-era, TMP sub-era game, NOT a TNG-era game, as that is when the game territories, playfield and tech aspects make the most sense.And the Romulan sun exploding is an event in this game, but it occurs WAY too early. By the time the Romulan sun exploded, the Odyssey-class was available canonically! Does anyone remember the USS Verity from the tie-in novel? That's long after the Enterprise-E and approaching the -F! So if they're going to give us that event, then they should also be giving us the Verity from the novel/Odyssey-class from Star Trek Online.Between that and the fact that they didn't even bother to give us the proper territory (Denobula, Risa, Betazed and several others need to be colonized in the game when they should be in the Federation already, the Nausicaans should be known as well) and random, rapid timeline progression unconnected to the actual date in-game, these developers do NOT know their 24th Century Star Trek lore. Not TNG, not Voyager, and not Deep Space Nine. They don't even know their Picard, which was WAY past TNG and the Enterprise-E.They are vaguely aware of the overall events and major cast of characters of TNG, DS9, VOY and PIC, and they know how to make a simplified, reskinned copy of a game (  ) but they are clearly NOT fans of Star Trek The Next Generation, Star Trek Voyager, Star Trek Deep Space Nine, OR Star Trek Picard.I highly doubt they've seen a single episode of any of these series, maybe just the opening title sequence but nothing more than that. They probably just looked at Memory Alpha for all their details instead of actually watching the show.In Developer Log One, the devs claim this was a "passion project", they claim it was meant to be inspired by titles such as Star Trek Armada and Birth of the Federation. After playing the game, all I can say is that that statement is "a whole load of BULL!""Passion" is more like "pathetic". Both of those games have actual gameplay, are well-paced and the events happen pretty much when they are supposed to. I should know, I play both Armada and Armada 2 currently!There's literally not a thing in this game for the developers to be proud of. It's a clone of Stellaris with a Star Trek paintjob and a few bits of Trek lore sprinkled in.What they did with this game... it's like trying to attack a starship with a stick. What you end up with in both cases is an epic, epic failure. These developers shouldn't be proud, they should be ASHAMED. They are clearly quite DISPASSIONATE about Star Trek, and this game is an INSULT to the entire history of the franchise.This game is a waste of money - I wasted mine, and wrote this review so that you don't have to waste yours. It's not worth twenty dollars and ninety-nine cents plus tax, it's worth precisely zero dollars and zero cents. If I could get my money back, I would.However, since I'm past the 2-hour refund time for this game I will continue to play it, but as someone who is actually passionate about Star Trek, and ESPECIALLY 24th century Trek, I can pretty much guarantee you that you will find a better version of this by playing a free Stellaris mod. Don't spend your money on this.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks great and fits the aesthetic very well, which was good for eye candy and frankly not much else. The events were infrequent, annoyingly timed or downright inconvenient, the game itself had way too much menu navigating for my fancy, and the game would be hella confusing for rts newbies. Hostile AI are either too diplomatic or completely impossible to deal with, with the particularly hostile 'end-game level threat' AI (spoilers) is way too easy to beat.Not to mention the launch being inundated with bugs and other issues which seems to have already soured people's opinions (personally the game ran smooth as butter for me). If you like it, and you've wanted a Stellaris clone set in the Star Trek universe, this would be the one. But it's just not there yet in terms of gameplay and overall polish and really needs to be improved, which considering my love for Star Trek and all things Paradox strategy games, is absolutely heartbreaking.For now, the cons outweigh the pros and, sadly, result in a negative review from me and a recommendation to avoid it until some bug fixes and well-needed patches get implemented to hopefully curtail the most pressing issues.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good:  - A Star Trek Grand Strategy Game, the first since Birth of the Federation way back in the day - Uses the Stellaris engine, so players of Stellaris will be able to easily pick up and play - Star Trek related events and story missions - Uses a Hearts of Iron style mission tree, which can lead to ahistorical playthroughs i.e the Federation going bad, or the Cardassians being cooperative - Graphics and music immerse you in the Star Trek universeThe not so good - It's an earlier Stellaris engine so there's still some irritating micromanagement i.e governors and spies have their own ships and you need to move them around. - As your chosen power expands things can start to feel bloated, lots of micromanagement, and it doesn't feel very streamlined The potential - This is the base of a new game, but what it could become with future patches and DLC is exciting! - The Mod community could do great things with this game Overall: A good, though not amazing, game that starts to scratch that Star Trek grand strategy itch with lots of potential. 7/10 (if that potential is realised, that score could very easily go up!)

_childDocuments_.review: While based on a forked version of Stellaris from several years ago, this game is nowhere near as good as Stellaris. Apparently, a bug keep wildly changing the firepower of enemy fleets, so you don't have any idea how powerful they really are -- even while you'e mid-battle! Are they 2k or 5k or 17k? Your guess is as good as mine! This and the other oddities/clunky UX can -- and must -- be fixed to make this game worth my time. The prettiness of the UI and fun Star Trek veneer make this a game I hope will be improved to be great.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has potential. But that potential is not yet realized. My review might change in the future if they implement enough changes. But as it stands now this game is more frustration than it is fun. Here are some of the key problems:1) It feels too much like Stellaris. Now hear me out: I -love- Stellaris. One of my favorite games ever. But to really soar this game needs to leave Stellaris behind. One good example of this: In Stellaris you have to work to research large and larger ship sizes. You start at the bottom, and work your way up. That shouldn't be the case in Infinite. This game starts in the TNG period. Not TOS, or pre-TOS. There is no good reason why each side should only have the smallest ship size unlocked. And of course the ships they picked are questionable in some cases. Intrepid over Excelsior? Yeah... For the UFP at least, they should start with Miranda, Excelsior and Ambassador unlocked from the start. I would also have updated models in the future that replace older ones- same rough size and cost, but better/more features. Think upgrade the Miranda to Steamrunner, as just one example. 2) More divergence between factions. This is where I think the game can really shine over Stellaris. Make each side feel truly unique. Don't simply give them some buffs or incentives towards certain playstyles. Really differentiate how each should play and then reinforce/reward that. The basic building blocks of this are there, it just needs more. 3) More interesting systems and space objects. Star Trek lore is filled with all kinds of possible encounters. There needs to be unique system, there should be more types of space creatures or other things for you to interact with. 4) "Mid" factions. I am talking about a handful of factions that are in between the major 4 and the minor powers. I am talking about the Breen, Gorn, and Tholians, to name a few. Use them for "mid-game" events or other challenges as the game goes on. 5) Bugs and Balance- both need work. Some is already being done, but more is needed.

_childDocuments_.review: Infinite is, for all intents and purposes, a Stellaris total conversion to the Star Trek universe. Sadly, despite this being done by an actual studio rather than somebody's basement, the end result is more disappointing and incredibly superficial.The basic concept is fine. Star Trek would be a good fit for Stellaris after all, but the delivery is lacking. You can build a tiny number of ship hulls (like, five) and the random tech tree means you can easily ignore lore and load Starfleet up with disrupters rather than phasers. Fleet combat is simply dropping a stack in to a system and relying on a bigger number. Speaking of lore, the UFP just sits there and can't declare wars or do anything against aggression, just be a punching bag. Probably on point to be fair, but as a game it just makes it boring.Flavour text is probably the only well done part of the game. Sadly the music is generic and not even licensed Star Trek themes. The UI is just the standard Stellaris UI, no attempt at LCARS or anything else.Simply put, don't bother. I won my first game by score. The Borg event chain ground to a halt and there was no end-game crisis to deal with. I couldn't liberate Bajor after the Cardassians integrated the system. So instead I just endlessly expanded and watched numbers go up.

_childDocuments_.review: So Far I really like the game. It's a very different angle to take on the space grand strat game compared to stellaris. It prioritizes actually entertaining and useful intrigue, mechanics that actually allow your progress to wax and wane not just go nowhere or blast off to an insane lead, and incremental gains through wars. I really like how many of the good systems from stellaris came straight over but others were fiddled with, it made a great combo of new and familiar. The trek flavor is entertaining and immersive if bizzarely and wildly out of timeline order and it all happens much too quickly. All in all It's a fun, addicting game that succeeds at meshing a new settign, some changed mechanics, and some classic mechanics into one cohesive new game.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to lie or maybe even love this game but I can't. After giving it a fair shake I can say it wasn't near ready for release. There's a lot to like. If you like stellaris, and you are a Trek fan, this game has potential. But it has a lot of stellaris at it's core and not necessarily the good parts. Random techs, poor balance, and bugs really prevent this from being something great. The federation is the only faction to get hero ships and are laughably easy to play. The Romulans are pretty much unplayable at the moment of this review due to a ship energy bug causing them to get outclassed by even pirates and a spy bug punishes failed spy missions until the end of time. Almost all tech pool is shared which leads to mundane replays with other factions. Some easy tweaks can fix the smaller issues but I fear a lot more work is needed for me to recommend this over Stellaris.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a dense strategy game - a must for anyone who like Birth of the Federation which was my most preferred computer game of all time.  From what little I know Infinite does appear to be a heavy modification of the Stellaris engine. Works well on my Mac.The learning curve appears steep and it would be worth watching a couple of 'how to' videos before starting the game, but there appears to be plenty of fan service for people who are into Star Trek TNG. A couple of bits appear to be odd relevant to the franchise (can they use the term Transwarp conduit?!) but generally if you are a fan of TNG era then this is a lot of fun to play. I've found it addictive anyway :-)There are lots of things to keep an eye on and as the game develops it thickens the resources and responsibilities. 12 hours in and I am only part way through my first game as I am taking it slow to try and learn the ropes. I expect the major conflicts and encounters are coming soon so I need to improve my military. Well worth a go if you like 4x strategy and Star Trek.

_childDocuments_.review: People are saying in comments and reviews that Birth of the Federation was a great game, it really wasn't. That game was BAD even for it's time and I feel like a lot of people who say this haven't played too many games of this kind then or know what was available. If you own no other space strategy game and you want a Star Trek game like that, then this is good and much better than the highly overrated BOTF. If you own Stellaris and play Star Trek New Civilizations mod that is basically the design of this game. Not overly complex like New Horizons, runs well, generally good gameplay dynamics. However this thing does things that a Stellaris mod can't do. Such as how ships travel is much more like Star Trek and how agents are used is more fun IMO than Stellaris. On top of that you are not overly punished for having a ton of characters like in recent Stellaris updates. But at the same time this is missing a lot of stuff that Stellaris provides. The bespoke events and things like that are not much of an upgrade, especially not over Star Trek New Civilizations mod for Stellaris. STNC is a much more complete Star Trek experience even considering that you have hyperspace lanes instead of warp and all that. The main thing with this game is I hope development continues because there is a lot of potential here, especially with mods. I think this is overall a good game and i'd recommend to buy it simply to make sure development continues, this will probably be the future focus of Star Trek modders.

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of the 90s Star Trek game Birth of the Federation made by Microprose, but modernized to incorporate several series together (TOS, TNG, DS9, and VOY) and play similar to a 4x game (think of Stellaris).Game is playable, but I would wait until the bugs are fixed.Ship and Fleet Management is horrendous when trying to move/organize the ships into specific fleets.  The Ship Designer needs to be fixed.  For ship designs that you don't have researched, it keeps on auto-generating the designs.  Also, you cannot build more than one of the unique ships until you research the ship class body.  The game doesn't tell you that unique ships are their own fleet, which means they are going into battles solo.The DLC is semi-broken.  You get the Cerritos, but you need to research the California Class ship design.  Also, when you try to build a fleet of California Class ships, you realize the ship is a civilian ship and not a military ship...Notable characters die too easily from old age, which apparently the DEVs forgot that old age for humans in the Star Trek Universe is around 110 to 120 years old NOT 75 to 90 years old.  This issue applies to other races as well.Decent game, but would wait until bugs are fixed.  I don't want to sit here listing every little issue that was missed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a money grab based on the Star Trek IP.  I have logged hundreds of hours into Stellaris  (600+).  And have already invested several into this one.  So, I am not throwing out some ill formed opinion.  It isnt that this game is a bit buggy which can happen with new releases.  It just feels like the developers put the bare minimum work into making it.  There are entire conversion mods for Stellaris that change it into a 100x better version than what this game turned out to be.   Minimal minor species were added.  Minimal ST technology.  Minimal overall conversion in my opinion.  The fact that they also made people pay extra for Klingon VOs, I mean come on.   If you are going to add these four factions then flesh them out.  Given the wide variety of Federation starships, why just the handful that we are given.  It was just Miranda, Excelsior, Galaxy, and Soverign.   The science ships in game look like one from base Stellaris imo when they could have made it an Oberth or something like that.   The story elements seem to be the only highlight here and unlocking the turning points just seems bland.  If you are looking for a Birth of the Federation type game I would recommend staying away from this one.  Just get Stellaris and the conversion mod.  Overall, horrible job in my opinion.  The galaxy map is also so small that I cant see much replay value.  Your chosen faction is right up against the other 3 when the game starts.   Final opinion, this game wouldnt make a Star Trek fan happy.  At the very least, it didnt make this fan happy.

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry, but really quite a poor attempt at a Star Trek 4x title.Come back after about a year or two of player feedback. I've had some time to mull over my thoughts about ST:I (a rather apt acronym, honestly) and here are some points I would like to discuss.ST:I starts in the late "Lost Era"/early "Next Generation" time frame, a reasonably decent place to start. Yet outside of your Construction and Science vessels you only start with the Miranda Class.That's it? Where is the Excelsior? The Constellation? Why are we jumping from having just a Miranda Class available to building the Galaxy Class? Excuse me? Slight issue here, folks.Oh, and the model for the Miranda is the "Antares" version, not the classic and more widely used "Reliant" style with the "roll bar". We should not need Steam Workshop mod in an official Star Trek game to make it more like actual Star Trek. The Ship Designer itself is ripped straight out of Stellaris, which is fine until you are dealing with vessels that have an established canon. As such you'll have multiple versions of the same ship running around, even if you manually design them yourself.Also, as it is essentially the Stellaris Ship Designer, your automatically built ships all have a random, wacky name as its design designation. So you end up with dozens of different technology, strange model Mirandas all called "The Xycote" or "Bing Zing" or something.How it  have been done is that the ship designs were fixed based on era, with refits later, and those would be based on what tech you have unlocked. Once all the tech for a ship is open then, and only then, should you be able to build a vessel type.And seriously, fix the damn Miranda model, the Antares type is not what fans think of when someone mentions the Miranda Class.The one, and I do mean , good thing ST:I does is give each faction a small amount of space to begin with, loosely based on Star Trek canon. This prevents early game system rushing to establish borders. However, the map itself is largely inaccurate.Systems and borders not matching understood canon status, scale is far too small and every faction is on top of each other, a faction's space does not seem to reach as far as it should. Complete waste.Again, we should not have to turn to the Steam Workshop to download a galaxy map that is a far more accurate representation of the Star Trek in-universe space in an official Star Trek title. I personally would have limited the play space to the Alpha and Beta Quadrants, increased the scale by 30-50 times and included a lot more minor races as the equivalent of pre/early FTL species from Stellaris.And what is with the bizarre "Warp Bubble" mechanic? Building starbases to extend the range your ships can travel? Why? That isn't a thing in Star Trek. The "free" warping around is good, but the range thing? Daft.This was my initial turn off about ST:I when I saw that Focus Trees were included in a review. Now, Focus Trees are fine when you have dozens, if not hundreds, of factions in a game, some with unique trees, like there is in Hearts of Iron. Each tree will have 3-4 overall end points with multiple ways of reaching the various endings.That is great when you have dozens if not hundreds of factions to play as. Not when you only have four.It really does kill the desire for replay-ability. Taking the Federation on a reasonably canon "good guy" route would work out more or less the same every time, as you have to fulfil the same requirements every time. ST:I does not need the Crusader Kings "fully open, no hand holding" approach of "There's the Galaxy, good luck", but it should be like Stellaris.The Stellaris system allows you to shape your path through the game via your Edicts. How deep or how shallow you go into a tree is up to you. What order you do so is up to you. In conjunction with that and just random events that occur throughout gameplay shapes your story over the course of a playthrough.There really isn't none. In three quick test games I had the same sequence of events in more or less the same systems in more or less the same order. First system you scan? Space whale. Wolf 359 just around the corner? Alien artefact on one of its moons. Every. Damn. Time.I can only guess that will be the case going forward.I get it, it is difficult creating random occurrences in a gamespace that (supposedly) has a hard, established canon and rule set. But .This would have been a decent Star Trek spin-off of Stellaris if it had been released when Stellaris was in its infancy. Given the missing features, given the missing depth, given the "my way or the highway" nature of the Focus Trees, no. No, just no. Not for me.But at least, , if you are doing an official Star Trek tie-in game at least  to be accurate. It is almost as if they bought the rights to Star Trek and then were scared to make it too much like Star Trek in case of legal problems.

(Why am I flying intrepid's well before excelsior's? Even getting around the fact that the federation has canonically have many more ship designs, you could work around it by using the alternative design feature that Stellaris has had for ages to change the flavor of ships the other factions have, this is not a new problem, and it was fixed by mods and even Stellaris has fixed it. The pacing of the game is rather poor and unless RNG is in your favor, your mission tree is pretty much locked behind it. The timeline (The extent of the game, not the setting.) of the game and the size of the map is a joke, you'll never fill up the map and so few of your colonies  Will feel done before the end of a game. Speaking of which. Why is Denobola and risa uncolonized? These are major planets in the Federation... There is so much wrong with this game, that more time and forethought could have went into it. As it stands it's incredibly shallow, buggy and feature poor that I can't recommend this game. Just buy base Stellaris and play one of the mods instead if you want to itch your Star Trek 4X needs. There was a attempt of love here, but the love doesn't match the scope of what was out there.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a dedicated Star Trek 4x game for $30, if you're a ST fan with fond memories of BOTF then get it. BUT IT'S JUST STELLARIS!!!!11!Not sure why people are blasting this game when they've said from the beginning that it's based on it. And they've improved on it in many ways - warp to any planet vs hyperlanes that make you fly through every system in between, logistical range is a welcome addition. Spy ships you send into enemy territory vs just assigning envoys. No ship or starbase limits that never made sense. Overall it's a more streamlined experience especially compared to the mods.I haven't had any crashes or glitches and they released multiple patches already for those that have. We can expect updates and DLC to add more empires and flesh out the game more over time (like all Paradox published games, nobody should be shocked by this).  There are some gripes, like how they kept Influence which I hate here as much as I do in Stellaris. The galaxy is pretty sparse right now with only 4 main players to choose from. It feels like they talked to fans but were not ST fans themselves, so its missing a little something there. I was pretty disappointed for about the first half hour to hour of playing it. I have over 1200 hours in Stellaris, a game I've played since it released. All I saw in this game at first was Stellaris but with a somehow worse, less intuitive, more generic UI. But the longer I played the more this game started to differentiate itself, I started enjoying it more and next thing I knew hours had passed. It feels more challenging than Stellaris, and certainly more so than its ST mods. I'll keep playing it and hope the updates and DLC roll out soon.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: After a bit more time with it, I'm changing my opinion of this game. If you haven't already bought it, you should hold off for now.I can understand the limited choice of ship models (even though some of the Federation ships are too new and advanced for the era the game starts in). However for a Star Trek game that aspires to be the definite experience, the following should *not* have been left ignored.=Lore/Canon-established *Preferred* Empire Techs=At game start, and despite the era the game is set in, every empire starts with Phasers and Plasma Charges... Except Phasers are almost exclusively a Federation weapon and Plasma-based weapons are typically Romulan in origin. In the timeline of this game, Photon Torpedoes have been around for quite some time and are in use with the Federation and Klingons (I can't recall ever seeing a Cardassian ship use torpedoes, not to say they don't have them) yet these need to be researched. The Federation and Klingons having plasma tech and not photon torpedoes makes zero sense.The Klingons and Romulans favour pulse and beam disruptors over phasers. The Klingons, as already mentioned, favour photon torpedoes. The Romulans favour plasma-based torpedo weapons. The Cardassians almost exclusively utilise 'spiral wave disruptors' - at least according to the DS9 Technical Manual. But no, Phasers for everyone...The Klingons and Romulans - empires with proven cloaking capabilities by the era this game is set in - do not have cloaking devices at game start, nor can they be applied to their ships (with specific exceptions) once they have been developed.The weighting of techs can have serious, game-breaking/ending repercussions later - such as if better reactor tech doesn't show up, empires can be significantly weakened with no way of directly addressing the issue, as even if your economy is good and you can produce ships in large numbers quickly, those ships are easily destroyed. In my personal experience, despite having several types of increasingly powerful phaser technology, my (Romulan) ships were either unable to equip them or only able to equip one slot but not the other due to having no power and/or being unable to have shields as by adding shields the starting reactor tech was unable to provide enough energy.To make matters worse, Romulans use a special resource (Singularity Cores) that - while it is a resource required for building ships - has zero impact on the amount of power a ship can generate.=Starship designs=The graphical quality of the provided models of starships is quite good. However, and though it is more an aesthetic 'thing' for me, the lack of 'canon' designs and/or addition of designs that have already appeared in other Star Trek games and/or are 'appropriate to the era' is disappointing. There have been several games which offer - at least inspiration - for designs, particularly for non-Federation empires. This is especially critical of the Cardassian starship designs - the 'STI-specific' designs (i.e. "non-TNG/DS9") do not follow the established Cardassian design philosophy and are instead blocky, over-the-top eyesores.Federation ships such as the Miranda and Excelsior are definitely period-appropriate, as are (arguably) Galaxy-class starships however Intrepid, Defiant and especially Sovereign-class ships are 'too new' to be in-game, especially as a mass-production Federation starship. Yet starship classes such as the Ambassador-class (which should definitely appear in-game, considering the USS Enterprise NCC-1701-C *should* have been destroyed at Khitomer during the Romulan assault - which is when this game starts) and the Constellation-class (the USS Stargazer - the ship Picard was serving on around/just before the time period in-game) are absent. Add to that that the Intrepid can be accessed earlier than the (older) Excelsior...For combat ship models, I would have gone with (as these are period-accurate):1. Miranda (Antares)2. Constellation3. Excelsior4. Ambassador5. GalaxyIf the Defiant, Intrepid and Sovereign are *really* needed, they should be 'one off' hero-ships.From the Romulan perspective (and I can appreciate that, in this era, the only ships 'really known' of this time are the Science Vessel, Scout Ship [which is *not* in-game] and D'deridex), the starting 'Bird-of-Prey inspired ship does not follow the established aesthetic of known BoP types (T'Liss, T'Varo or Malem) and is instead somehow trying to be parts of all 3 at once. Add to that, that the Valdore/Norexan-type ship is available *before* the D'deridex despite being a newer design first seen in Star Trek: Nemesis.=Mission Tree event failures=In my current Romulan (I've had two goes at the Romulans now, and one as the Federation) playthough, I'm about to lose Romulus to the supernova because I can't evacuate the planet, and no one seems to have told the Federation that I'm okay with them helping me fix my problem. It's probably something I've done, however for something as critical as the loss of my homeworld, the event shouldn't be an option (or should reset) if there's issues that prevent it from finishing. I know there are now mods for the game, and one of them in particular is addressing some of these issues itself, but I should have to be relying modders to 'fix' a game that has only just come out. Mods are meant to improve and value-add, they're not meant to legitimately be directly responsible for fixing the game...I still think this game has potential, but I think it has a long way to go before it gets there.=ORIGINAL REVIEW=I'll get the over-hyped obvious out of the way: Star Trek Infinite is built using the Clausewitz engine - the same engine Stellaris is built on. In fact, it's fair to say STI, mechanically, is an older version of Stellaris. As such, it's UI and mechanics are similar, if not identical, and the way it plays is also very similar (though it does approach some things a little differently, with the use of Governor and Spy ships, for example).It has features taken from/inspired by other Paradox games: The empire management, story-telling and cinematic action of Stellaris, with the faction objectives of EU4, and the 'National Focus' (Mission Trees) of Hearts of Iron 4. Combined, this makes STI its own game.It does have some design decisions that I think are a missed opportunity but overall, in my limited playthrough thus far, it has great potential. What it has now works, but it feels like it's missing some things - things that are somewhat glaringly absent in certain areas - but visually, the game is very clean and combat is quite nice to watch unfold before you.I haven't played with the Cardassians or Klingons yet however from my experiences so far, the Romulan-specific mechanic of having to generate 'Singularity Cores' to construct their ships is a novel way of controlling the rate at which the Romulans can build ships. I was underwhelmed with the physical designs of the Romulan starships (except for the D'deridex and Valdore), as there are plenty of designs they could have used, or drawn inspiration from, from previous games - or even STO, also controlled by CBS. Examples of missed opportunities being the lack of Ambassador (despite Enterprise-C being destroyed in orbit of Khitomer as the game starts), Constellation (despite Picard technically being on the Stargazer when the game starts), cloaks not actually doing anything...Klingons not having cloaking devices on their ships...every race using Phasers (when it's widely known, well established and represented in the shows and movies - Klingons and Romulans use disruptors) and Plasma charges - despite Photon torpedoes being in the Starfleet and Klingon arsenals for over a century...Being under the Paradox umbrella, I expect there'll be a number of DLCs as well as changes to mechanics and such over time. Looking forward to seeing the Dominion, in particular, become available.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me first immediately state I can see the Devs clearly put a lot of work in this game, the artwork and designs look top notch.However the problem is the fact the game itself is at odds with its own heritage.As someone who loves both Star Trek and Stellaris, I feel that the devs sadly have made the game lose touch with its own roots.I am well aware this is based on Stellaris and while I do not see a problem with that at all, the issues start with many of the choices on how to balance both sides out.The governor system from Stellaris was perfectly fine for example, putting them on ships which only buffs one planet in specific ways just feels clunky at best.So I started mostly ignoring them altogether.Another example is piracy, since Stellaris got rid of alternative drives years ago for sake of balance piracy is very predictable.Send a lot of trade through unprotected systems and you will sooner or later have pirates pop up there, though they aren't more than a nuisance usually.Instead the devs decided to make some random Nausicaans come at random and trash your systems.So why is that a problem?First of all it pretty much means, and I am not kidding, in my game I had to dispatch fleets every 5 minutes just to keep them at bay, because if they trash your system you will lose it and when that happens you lose that system unless it contains a planet, so they decided pirates use the same mechanics as the Stellaris endgame crisis.And sometimes there is not even enough time to intercept them, and there is no solution either, because if you build a starbase in that system they just pick another one, which thanks to Warp they do not care how deep inside your borders it is.This also extends to diplomacy where the Klingons and Romulans just after Khitomer started becoming best friends, I really feel the Devs should have made this more realistic.And then there is the speed of in-game time, which while working perfectly fine for Stellaris, does not work in Infinite.It immediately became a meme for my friends and I that I got Data, which not even 5 minutes after becoming an officer died of old age.In general when you're dealing with a franchise that has named characters, you have to adjust your game so they don't die off like that, maybe fallen in combat sure, but having TNG suddenly span hundreds of years like that just feels weird.And speaking of Data, the mission system inspired by EU4 is nice on paper, but its execution felt bad in the game.I got stuck on multiple roadblocks, I cannot get Bajor because the Cardassians integrated it and I could not help the Romulans, their supernova happened while I was stuck on not having enough trade treaties.For some reason when the game considers you too strong, they refuse to do trade deals with you. So I was never able to get to the point where I could evacuate the Romulans, so I failed that.So while those missions were an interesting idea, Stellaris as a base is too random for it to work properly and it does not feel good getting stuck like that.So in the end with those issues and many more gripes, I did not feel really engaged with the game much because I was hoping for a more roleplay like experience with a Stellaris flair, but as stated the game is at odds with its heritage.Overall I hope eventually the devs manage to change those things to make more sense, then I would of course adjust my review. But until then I just cannot recommend this.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam would let us post "neither" reviews, because I don't want to actually recommend against Star Trek: Infinite.  I just can't recommend in its favor either.Everything that's wrong with the game stems from a single problem: STI (someone really should've thought that acronym through when naming the game...) is built upon the Clauswitz engine developed by Paradox for Stellaris.  The thing is, some engines are like Unreal or Unity, i.e. they provide a very basic framework and require that developers tailor a lot of their game's core systems on top of the engine.  This is why there are FPS and RTS games both made in Unreal.  Clauswitz isn't such an engine.  It was purpose-built for Stellaris, and it shows.Perhaps the most glaring example of this can be seen when playing STI as a Klingon.  Stellaris, and therefore STI, has a system that was introduced many years ago wherein a player seeking to go to war can't simply start shooting the enemy's ships and bombing their planets.  Instead, one must make claims on an enemy's planets, which you can only make a limited number of, then go conquer virtually all of their territory, and when you win, you only get the planets you made claims on.  The intention of this system was to solve a very Stellaris-specific problem wherein even mediocre players could absolutely stomp very hard AI players by simply rushing a large fleet of cheap ships in a hurry then winning a quick war before the upkeep of those ships had time to bankrupt them, wiping the AI out in a single quick war.  Ironically, the Clauswitz engine didn't have a solution for what was essentially player Blitzkreig, so they created the claim system.Fast forward many years and the system remains in STI, but with an added twist - in addition to having a very limited number of claims that are very expensive, and (unlike Stellaris) no means to increase the number of available claims, STI also has a system that measures the galactic "tension" in the galaxy and further reduces the maximum number of claims, giving you only THREE claims when tension is at a minimum.  The problem with this new tension system is that AI actions contribute to it too, and the AI tends to do friendly, tension-lowering things whenever tension is low.  The AI thus starts every single game already locked into a downward spiral of constantly-lowering tension that effectively locks you to no more than 3 claims for the entire game.  Combine this with the fact that all 3 opposing factions will ALWAYS make a defensive pact with each-other by year 10 and every war is followed by a 10 year forced truce, and you have a situation where you are railroaded into fighting the entire galaxy by yourself, and even if you manage to eek out a win, you get 3 systems.In short, the game is unplayable for Klingons.  By far the most effective way to fight wars in STI is to use your spies to sabotage your opponents' starbases, which destroys them and makes the system neutral as long as it has no colonized planets, then quickly fly in a war fleet, survey ship, and a constructor.  Survey it and claim it yourself, then sabotage another, rinse and repeat.  This is a natural playstyle for Romulans or Cardassians, and the Federation's diplomacy-first route seems to be what the game was intended for.  But the Klingons?  The game's own systems actively work against them.tl;dr STI as essentially a professional-quality total conversion mod for Stellaris, but it's ruined by the game/engine that was selected to build it on top of.  Something like Stardock's Sins of a Solar Empire would've been a much, much better foundation for this.

_childDocuments_.review: Consider this game as the starter box of Star Trek Ascendancy, with Cardassian expansion, if it was put into PC game format. Where the tabletop game does have replay-ability in how it is set up each game, this is where this game sadly lacks that variety. The devs, wanting to retell the TNG to VOY timeline, have made the galaxy a set piece, the board does not move or change, only what territories are snapped up by each of the other races though after a few games the AI can get predictable. Like many others have stated prior this game has the "potential" to become something greater, something more, if given the green light to get out, let's say, the Dominion as a playable but also end game crisis. This would affect all other races and add to their mission trees and what can and can't be done.However in its current form, from what I've played on a previous machine for a good 50+ hours that sadly aren't synced to my current steam account, the base game gets too samey after too many games, as I stated before the galaxy is a set board that doesn't change or alter all that much. Sadly I think, for a while, this game is being sidelined for something else as prior to release there really wasn't much in the way of gameplay footage or youtube previews, but plenty of previews for the pre-order/deluxe content that would be available. So I can only assume there's no credible news on further expansion on the game and we shouldn't have to rely on the modding community to upgrade and finish off the starter game.This does sound like a contradiction doesn't it? That I recommend it yet talk about it in a negative light. The game in its current state is good for someone wanting to play Stellaris BUT are overwhelmed with how complicated that game has become now with all its expansions, as this game's engine is Stellaris 3.0. Not too difficult to get the ideals of the 4x empire building down but also allows for bringing in more mechanics later on. The devs right now are playing their cards way too close to their chests with this game, like they did with previews, and as it stands, with some extra free or paid content thrown our way in the coming months, I could easily throw in a good 10+ hours a week for a decent thorough playthrough, maybe a multiplayer game too, but this won't happen. Buy this if you want a diet-Stellaris with a star trek theme, but do not buy it if you're looking for a Birth of the Federation 2. C'mon Devs, give us something for this game. There's obviously a lot of time, effort, artwork, and thought that's gone into this game wanting to recreate the TNG-timeline and beyond, but as it sits here it looks like a dead shelved game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very disappointing. I went in with very low expectations, and even those weren't metI have completed one full game as the Federation, achieving a diplomatic victory. What I can say is good about the game is the addition of new victory conditions is nice, and a feature that Stellaris unfortunately lacks. Also, some of the UI presentation is excellent, and I like some of the unique concepts (like warp logistics range), at least in concept.But then there's all the problems. The first is the parts of the UI that aren't polished to a shine. The galaxy map is nice, but the alert icons are odd. Ships in transit to reinforce your fleet? Expect to see the icon Stellaris uses for federation XP decreasing. The alert icon stellaris uses for your federation level increasing is also used wrong (although I'll admit I can't remember for the life of me what they use it for).Then there's the voice acting. This might be the most egregious design decision in the game. There's such a comically low number of unique voice lines that I can't take the game seriously. What lines they have don't match Star Trek at all. The Klingon male diplomacy screen voice spoke more like a Ferengi than a Klingon, and only ever said one thing. Every female voice is unbelievably high pitch, and again, only has one line on the diplomacy screen. But the problems aren't contained to the diplomacy screen, because there's a severe lack of alert sounds too. Leader just level up? You'll get the alert sound for a leader dying. Diplomatic proposal rejected? Leader died alert. Sometimes even construction queues finishing would give the leader dying alert sound. That one sound effect was  I always had to check and verify that a leader hadn't died constantly. I know voice acting is hard, and it isn't cheap, but is it too much to ask for unique alert sounds? For women to not sound like a cartoon mouse? Even the Klingon voice pack from my pre-order didn't make the Klingons on the diplomacy screen sound Klingon.Ship design and space combat are also severely lacking. Having every faction just use phasers is already a bit of a simplification. But if they're having the different weapon types be so limited, how come they didn't put in the effort to make the weapon effects look accurate to the show? Only spinal lance phasers are beams for some reason, and it's nearly impossible to distinguish a photon torpedo from a phaser array, since the phasers shoot little red-orange bursts instead of coherent orange beams. The worst part is, base Stellaris can make battles look more like Star Trek using just lasers and missiles, why weren't those effects used more? The weapon progression is similarly absurd, starting you from Enterprise era technology, 200 years after it would have gone into service in the timeline. I'm not normally one to nitpick on canon things, but it's really hard to take this game seriously when I don't even have torpedoes when the attack on Khitomer happens. So many weapon types have such low accuracy that it's just not worth using them.The Borg are nowhere near threatening. I don't know if it's just because I've played a lot of Stellaris, and the basic settings were just too easy or what, but I completely wiped the floor with the Borg. They didn't kill a single ship of mine during the crisis. I stopped them at the source. And based on the missions, it seems I was behind on tech. The missions seemed to expect me to have Sovereign class ships before the Borg arrived, I didn't even have Galaxy class ships yet. I have no clue how much I need to turn up the crisis difficulty to make the Borg challenging, but if the expectation is to have 15 Sovereign-class ships before they arrive, I don't think the slider goes high enough.The worst part of all of this is that the core gameplay concept isn't bad. There's clearly a good idea at the core of this game. But the game concept is so unsuited for the Stellaris engine. I knew this was a Stellaris reskin going in, they're certainly not shy about it, and I can understand why using a pre-existing game as the basis for this makes sense. But using Stellaris as the basis for a game set in a time frame of about 100 years at most is just bad use of the engine. Stellaris mods like New Horizons work by using the full 300 year length Stellaris is built on, and running you from around the launch of the NX-01 Enterprise, through to the events after Picard. At its core, Stellaris is built for those kinds of generation-spanning stories, and the way it implements researching tech and exploration and planetary development reflects that. Star Trek Infinite is not a generation-spanning story. It is set in one era of Star Trek, with tech that never develops beyond about 30 years from the start of the game, but to give the progression Stellaris relies on, it tries to squeeze the entire history of Star Trek technology into 30 years, on only TNG-era ships.Star Trek Infinite would be a better game if it was built like Birth of the Federation, on the framework of a more traditional 4X like Masters of Orion, or even Endless Space. Instead, we have a lackluster use of the Stellaris engine and gameplay, for a story that doesn't fit, and that warps the whole reality of Star Trek to make anything even almost work.If you're looking for a true Star Trek experience in the style of Stellaris, I unfortunately cannot recommend this game. Try out the existing mods for Stellaris instead, Star Trek: New Horizons (my personal recommendation), or the more streamlined Star Trek: New Civilizations. They're more worth your time, and somehow have better voice acting than this officially licensed game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are on the fence, DO NOT get this game.  I've never played Stellaris but like Star Trek and strategy games. In one war, I captured every system and planet from my opponent, but I can't force an end to the war.  Instead, all I can do is wait for the AI to admit defeat or admit defeat myself. The devs stopped working on the game 2 months after launch, fixing only crashes and minor issues.  It's dead.

The bad-No polish and very buggy, I think its safe to say the devs ran out of money/time before being forced to ship-Stellaris tech tree.  Each faction should have their own tech tree path but that's not the case here, its the generic Stellaris RNG tech tree where everyone can research phasers, plasma weapons, etc.  A missed opportunity.-Doom Stacking ships.  Instead of giving us ships that were powerful and impactful we get the old Stellaris doom stacking ships.  This really is my biggest complaint.  Star Trek should have fewer ships but are each highly capable of defending themselves.  Instead we get more Stellaris.  The flaghships are an exception but they have their own issues.-Flagship design.  Mindbogglingly you can't design or upgrade your Flagship with better tech or how you want to arm them.  So for the Enterprise D, its currently bugged with its armaments and just sits back out of combat not shooting for most of the combat missions.  Occasionally it will shoot photon torpedoes but they don't work against shields so... There is a lot more I could list here but I'm not trying to completely nitpick this game.  My suggestion is to skip it, or at least keep an eye on it to see if it gets some much needed updates.   Right now this game was pushed out the door in a barely working state that is just barely finish able...unless your playing Romulans, then you might as well quit because the Supernova from the series happens and happens early wiping you out. =/

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game at launch and liked it but it was a bit buggy so I gave it a few months to cook. Started playing again recently and after a few tries I finished my first Federation campaign (diplomatic victory). All of the bugs I had previously encountered have been fixed and the game is good now (imo).It's a 4X game so it has a bit of a learning curve, but it's not too difficult to learn and is quite fun when you figure out how things work. For those familiar with the genre this is basically Star Trek Stellaris, since it uses the same engine and most of the same game systems/mechanics. The setting for the game is TNG with a splash of DS9 (excluding the Dominion) and a cameo from Voyager (after their return home), you follow the major events from those shows and complete goals related to those events that give you different rewards/bonuses, it gives the setting some story and context and is a very nice touch (I like it alot). Stellaris itself has Star Trek mods, mods that have more content and are still being updated today, but this game is different enough imo and works out of the box (no mods or specific Stellaris DLC needed) so I'm glad that it exists.However I have to say that this developer has recently (in the last couple months) suffered major layoffs, due to them being an Embracer owned studio (Embracer is going through some self-inflicted tough times right now lol), so future support for the game (patches, new content, etc.) is up in the air right now. That being said the game in it's current state is complete and fully playable, and most importantly, fun.If you're a 4X fan and a Star Trek fan especially it's definitely worth a buy! If you're not a fan of these things or don't like how this game may not get more content in the future, my recommendation is buy it, try it out, and if you don't like it within 2 hours refund it and move on... :)

Including but not limited to (only those I have discovered myself):- Federation cannot start offensive wars (I believe some traditions may change it but not at the start)- Romulans don't have military limit as standard races have: they need to produce a special resource which produces a kind of fuel for their ships. This can be produced by planetary buildings (one per planet) or vassalising empires- Europa-Universalis-like mission trees- Hearts-of-Iron-like world tension- galactic balance (basically vicotry points per race) with (important) buffs for the best and the worst race

_childDocuments_.review: Update 3/20/24: I guess updates have stopped. Its been 3 months since we've heard anything. I can no longer recommend this game unless the modding community saves it.Original Launch Review-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------As a big fan of both Stellaris and Star Trek, I am excited about the possibilities for the future of Star Trek Infinite. If it follows the Stellaris model of continuous improvement funded by paid DLC I can imagine Star Trek Infinite to be a fun and refined experience in the future. Where it stands now is far from a refined experience. I've run into bugs while playing and from what I gathered other players have as well. The immersion into the Star Trek universe is the primary reason for Star Trek Infinite to exist and its kind of ruined by poor voice acting and some questionable lore breaking gameplay design choices. Its difficult to be hard on a game that seems to have been rushed to release while seemingly at early access level of development.I do like the dynamics of Infinite's smaller and more focused Stellaris-like experience. The galaxy exploration feels more engaging with all of the major powers next to each other in a central location. It captures a Star Treky feel of exploring into the unknown more than standard Stellaris. I'm looking forward to diving deeper into Star Trek Infinite once the bugs get sorted out. I'm hoping it gathers enough support for continued development, but if not the modding scene can always pickup from the good base that Star Trek Infinite has laid.

_childDocuments_.review: After much thought and deliberation, I believe Star Trek: Infinite deserves a 9.5/10. Although not without its flaws (somewhat clunky war system, poor documentation, etc.), I have had a great experience with the game after 17 hours. The gameplay is very engaging and I have been delighted by my playthroughs so far.Frankly, I'm as shocked as you are. Given Paradox's poor showings in recent years, I had no faith that this game would be any good at all. Joking aside, the development team should be commended on their ambitious take on the 4x genre. They made a great choice to focus on the TNG-era. We all love TNG and it avoids a lot of the cringe of more recent Star Trek media (ST: Picard, Discovery, etc.). The art direction is wonderful and respects the work others have done, while appropriating it into the Stellaris formula. The playing the warlike Klingons feel very much like Klingons, the ruthless Cardassians feel like Cardassians, and so on. I especially enjoy the influence and officer mechanics. The AI is a challenge without becoming overbearing. These are essential aspects to the game that make it worth my time.Is it what I wanted?I wanted Birth of the Federation 2. I knew I wouldn't get that, but I am convinced this is the next best thing. Infinite is a brilliant Star Trek experience from a group that loves the franchise. It is more than worth the cost of admission. Given a robust patching schedule and reasonable DLC (Dominion, please), I think it will become *the* go to Star Trek game for years to come.Kudos to the devs and Qapla'!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - this is a mass of crashing bugs at present and my review stays as not recommended until I can actually play it. And I'm really disappointed to write this because i really want to play it.I'm not going to refund because i'm really hoping they actually get this buggy mess sorted out. Scream day 1 woes (or 2, as it is now), all you like, but i'm entitled to have a moan if I paid £27 for a game on pre-order and expected to actually be able to play it on release day. Not like it's a multi-player game, after all.I'm a big fan of stellaris, but i've really only touched the surface of how deep that game is, but that's up to me. It's my money I spent on it, so i can play it how I like. It may sound like I'm blathering here, but i'm getting to my point. I can play that game, and have been able to since I bought it. I've got a game here which is unplayable, as it stands.For context: Mac M2 Pro here, so system should be more than up for the task. When I had the game running, there were no issues with slow-down or anything like that. If my machine can play Stellaris flawlessly then this is going to run as well, because we all know it's pretty much just a reskin.So, I load the game and decide to start with the tutorial, because it's been a while since I played Stellaris. That loads 2/3 of the progress bar and then dumps me out with a crash report. Not a good start. Give it another shot with the tutorial and it crash bangs out again. Definitely not a random crash then. Restart the Mac and go again. Third time lucky, right? ..... Wrong.Alright, so let's forget the tutorial here and try and play a game. Click on Federation and hit start just to be asked if I'd like to run the tutorial? Nice try, but you're not catching me out like that. Skip straight to new game and off we go.Science vessel going off to explore strange new worlds, make some alliances (hey, i'm on easy mode. I'm rubbish at battles, so usually play diplomacy in these kind of games) and start constructing star bases in new sectors so I can expand my territory. Ok, this is what we came for, and I know enough about Stellaris to kind of feel my way further into the game gradually. Naturally the game then decides to do it's auto-save - which i hadn't bothered to check what the time frame was because why on earth would i need to?Crash bang, here's another lovely report for you to send to Apple, or, more likely, shove straight in the trash can as who on earth reads these anyway?Reload the game and go to the load game option. No games present. Of course there aren't. The game kindly crashed before it could save the last game that I hadn't asked it to do at that moment, after all.Switch off auto-save and cloud saving (just in case, even though the forums report that doesn't work anyway), and give it another shot. Another crash, bang, wallop when i assign a leader to one of the science ships I just built.Yeah, enough is enough, right.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is wildly incomplete. Some features are available to some factions but not others. Such as named ships with special features.Only four major factions are available, a bunch of minor factions that based on the chosen timeline should not be independent minor factions.The locations of minor factions are scrambled every match meaning factions you may be expected to interact with as part of missions may be on the opposite side of the galaxy so you have to aggressively expand your territory due to warp range limits. THis can lead to trying to overextend yourself to the point you can't defend your territory just to complete a mission.The mission trees are kind of hot garbage in how they were designed/planned out.Unlocking senior officers for your hero/flag ship for the Feddies results in them becoming admirals to lead their own fleets instead of them being assigned to your flag ship as the senior officers.Asside from the turbo powered Nausicans that seem to be the most powerful force in the universe, a hundred times more dangerous than the borg; no faction seems to put any effort into conquering or taking territory even during wars.This game would be considered bad in it's current state even if it were to be labeled early access. But yet this is pitched as a complete game.What may even be the bigger offender is that there are only 5 ship classes. Twenty years ago we had Star Trek games with twice that and a more dynamic experience. Oddly enough I would say this game feels like there are more obvious and blatant missing features than there are bugs. Sure, there are a number of bugs that are easily replicable that should never had made it past any meaningful Q&A attempt. But they are less numerous than the content gaps. SOme of them are as minor as names being missing from event notifcations to as major as hero officers that are critical to missions having the wrong traits so the missions cannot be completed without the use of console commands/cheats. Some can't even be completed that way.I want this game to be improved. I am not here to rage and ♥♥♥♥ on it for internet points. I want this game to get to a state where I can change my review and fall in love with this game. There has not been a STar Trek game I have genuinely loved to be released in 22 years. Based on available content, I have to say this game is inferior to a game that came out two decades ago.I want to see better. In genuinely want to see improvement, and for this game to dethrone Armada 2.As of now the game is abandoned by the devs in an unfinished state with several promised features still missing. THis game was abandoned in a state that should have never been released, this game is in a state that should have been an in house testing version not an early access scam, much less a full release.

_childDocuments_.review: Its stellaris, with a mediocre mod and just a few ship types. _childDocuments_.review: Most CRAPTASTIC "Star Trek" game that I have ever played. No Player's Manual is complete BS. (No wiki either) Having to put a governor in orbit of a new colony for TEN FRACKING YEARS to complete an inauguration ceremony is complete BS. Waging war against an enemy empire for several years while obliterating 80% of their territory only to have the war suddenly end and you get ZERO territory for your efforts because you did not click a magic button on some magic sub menu before the war started is complete BS. (Casus Belli is complete BS. The victor makes the rules. ALWAYS.)Enemy ships that escape at the last second is complete BS.  Somehow massive structural damage never disables the navigation or warp drive systems.The entire colony building and district allocation system is complete BS. You need food so you create agricultural zones but NO they would rather starve to death than farm because they were trained for white color work, not blue color work.I love Star Trek. I love 4x strategy games. I HATE this game and most likely so you will too. Far too many HIDDEN RULES that are not explained by the cursory tutorial and they cannot be bothered to publish a game rulebook.You won't know how bad this game gets until it is too late to refund it so . . . just don't buy it. You will  probably be happier that way. I know I would be.Cheers!

_childDocuments_.review: I havent seen a good star trek 4x game ever since i spend hundreds of hour on Birth of the Federation, so when i saw Star Trek Infinite, it was a must try for me. I did immediately realize it is heavily based on Stellaris, which i love and have well over 1000 hours in.Starting the game up was nice. I immediately checked all the ship models and they are really really nice.for the rest, i saw modded stellaris.The game turns out not only to be heavilty based on Stellaris. It basically is a Star Trek mod for Stellaris. Even  the code for events, anaomalies etc. is full of Stellaris code.Still, i want to give it a chance and had 2 playthroughs now. What i noticed:- I barely have any space battles. The occasional pirate attack which is annoying at first and just a bother when you gain a fleet strength over 2k. Used it only to get my mission for worf. - Liberated Bajor in an underwhelming war where the Cardassians just gave up and let me win. Wanted a DS9 spacestation (cardassian model), but just ended up with having to build a federation station myself.- Recruited William T. Riker and used him as an admiral. At 92 years oldPicard dies and helm is taken over by William Riker. Now i have 2 Rikers as admiral? pretty immersion breaking- Encountered the borg, have some easy battles against a 2k fleet. Suddenly Janeway pops up in a scout ship (come on... give me voyager) and kills them and by this ends the endgame crisis. Very underwhelming. in the endgame crisis i want to lose 3/4 of my empire and then suddenly manage to win.- i havent seen any cloaked vessels. no klingon cloak, no romulan cloak, nothing.- it takes ages before the galaxy and sovereign class become available. reseacrhed them well after defeating the borg.all in all the game just feels like Stellaris when it just came out, but way easier. Events are immersion breaking (2 rikers, data dying of natural causes before anyone else from the TNG crew, no cloak etc.)Potential? maybe. its a long way from Birth of the Federation (please someone take that game, ad 4k renders and release it as part 2). Paradox has a good reputation in fixing and long term support, but this one seems very hard to fix.Worth the money? absolutely not. 30 euros for something thats basically a mod is way overpriced.for now, if you want star trek in Stellaris, go for new horizons.

_childDocuments_.review: Having always been a Trek fan, and remembering ST Galaxies i was looking forwards to playing this game...Sadly the game is a disappointment. Although its graphics quality and smoothness are not an issue, the important factor - game play, is where it fails miserably. It is disjointed. You start with an already established set of borders, wars and all manner of other things that appear to be happening without you even gaining your bearings. The tutorial is unclear/indecisive, it does not give you clear instruction on button direction or control options on screen - and there are lots of buttons!Every 30 seconds or so a message pops up, giving you barely time to read the previous. None of the research trees or tech seems to have a point, its difficult to be sure what resource you are spending.The game tries to hard to micro manage everything but does not give obvious indication as to what (if anything) has changed when you do build/change/create/research. When a discovery is made, whether its a anomaly, star system or random event you jump to that place without seemingly being warned.War is declared. I haven't even established contact and already we are at WAR.Didn't notice any bugs in the game which is great but unfortunately it all feels very rushed, almost as if it was just a after thought to rake in cash.Normally ST is a no brainer for me, i am straight in, but this time its a no from me.GR is probably rolling in his grave, my advice, give this one a miss and look at Galactic Civilisation 3 maybe.

_childDocuments_.review: First new star trek game in forever and this company screwed it up massively.  Its supposed to be Star Trek stellaris but its more like an incomplete alpha version of Stellaris . _childDocuments_.review: Star Trek: Infinite SpreadsheetsIt's Civ-in-space with a (quite pretty) Star Trek skin. It pretends to be a Star Trek game that honors the lore, the universe, and the peoples of 90's era Trek, but is only 'skin' deep. Edit: Apparently it's Stellaris, which I do not play because I do not find it enjoyable. Too bad; I thought this was a new game with some of Paradox's 4x mechanics ported over. I guess it's more of a poor mod for an old game, like season one of ST:Pic. (Android Picard; give me a break. *slams head on desk*)It's pretty enough, but last-gen graphics. Starships are pretty static 3d models with some lens flare. Maybe it gets better, but I'm probably not going to find out.The promised story-line is as easy to find as a genetically modified Suliban. I assume it's something to do with one of the multiple mission logs... but you know, just assuming here.No achievements unless you're on "hardcore" mode, so you weak-willed non-Klingons may not seek glory. What a joke. Star Trek was about exploration, not 'hardcore' shi... whateverThe game has real depth and seems to have a lot of care put into every tooltip. The voiced tooltips are horrendous though... I mean it didn't stop even when I exited to menu and started a different game. I'll be honest, this game has some potential but I couldn't make it through the first 2 hours before I got seriously overwhelmed by the bombardment of tips. Aaand the game is unplayable without some guidance in the beginning because there is simply too damned much going on all at once. Put it like this, when I started Civ VI, I skipped the tutorials because you know, SIX, and I beat the nuts out of the first 5, so get on with it already. This is NEW and not intuitive, yet. So, huge learning curve to even begin to discover if it's enjoyable in the mid or late game stages. WHERE IS MY STORY? For real though, there's no objective goal beyond trying to figure out what each of the very tiny (ui scaling sucked) icons does or doesn't do. My god this game's ui is a mess.I won't refund because I will support any game that is Star Trek in hopes of more of them, but this game needs some serious work on the user experience side of things. If there's amazing graphics, show me them! if there is a great campaign, then put it in my face and let me play it! If you expect me to spend 2 hours figuring out tooltips just so I can start my first mission, say so and then piss off back to the Gamma quadrant.So disappointed I feel like I'm watching the first season of ST:Discovery again.

_childDocuments_.review: Huge Star trek fan and gamer for the last 40 years here. I usually like pretty much all types of games. Only made it 16 minutes with this one before putting in for a refund. Apparently this is just like Stellaris, which I didn't play. Looks like maybe I was supposed to have played that as the introduction to this game, because what they call a tutorial was just an AI voice reading me information about whatever I clicked on. Game starts me in a universe of symbols and lines and buttons, and each time I clicked one of those the voice would read me info about it and usually a new menu opened up too. Click on things in those menus and sometimes the voice starts telling you about that too, but they sure don't start you with a story or clear objectives or any direction whatsoever. Basically, if you don't already know how to play this kind of game, you get to click on the countless symbols and such and try to memorize the explanations given for them until you have some idea how to do things. Nope. So I went to youtube to watch a 40 minute tutorial video. Dude lost me by the 10 minute mark on that too because this simply doesn't look fun enough for me to take classes to learn to play it. Probably quite simple if you've played whatever games it copied, but if you haven't, maybe watch tutorials first to see if its something you care to learn before you drop $30 on it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Star Trek skin for Stellaris, not an actual new game. If you love Star Trek, and you love Stellaris, then you'll definitely love this game. I was a big fan of the old Birth of the Federation 4x game, and this doesn't measure up.To be clear, the game is fine. Good even. There are a handful of annoying bugs but nothing out of the ordinary. The problem is that this was sold and marketed as a new Star Trek game. Even in the interviews when devs were asked about the similarities, they seemed to be trying to minimize the similarities, when in reality, it's simply Stellaris with some Star Trek names thrown in. Had they marketed it as "Stellaris: Star Trek Edition" I probably still would have bought it, and enjoyed it, but the dishonest approach to this leaves a sour taste.My other quibble from a Star Trek perspective is that the geography and timeline is very confused. Civs dont act the way they should in-universe, systems are simply not located where decades of Star Trek lore and canon maps say they should be, and the timeline makes no sense.  It's not the end of the world, it just kills some of the immersion.If the game were $15, I might recommend it, but at $39 (Cdn), it's a no from me.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm confused about the reason for this new Star Trek game's existence. We already had a fantastic total conversion mod for Stellaris called Star Trek: New Horizons. It offered a deep and engaging Star Trek experience with unique events, mechanics, playable races, and a challenging gameplay loop.This new game, however, feels more like a modern version of the classic Birth of the Federation. It lacks the variety of playable races and complex mechanics found in New Horizons. There's also minimal story unless you specifically choose the Federation faction.In its current state, I wouldn't recommend this game. While future updates and potentially expensive DLC packs might improve it,  it's unlikely to reach the level of depth and polish achieved by the free Star Trek: New Horizons mod for Stellaris.

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of the Stellaris mods for Star Trek I was so excited for this game. The game itself looks great, the warp effects and smooth looking interface full marks, however lack of ship models, poor music and no Star Trek weapon sounds left me looking back at the Stellaris mods thinking i felt more part of the federation than i do in this game. _childDocuments_.review: I got this game thinking i was going to get the same feel as Star Trek Armada like the good old days with Civilization added on top of that through all that diplomacy. I will be comparing STA (Star Trek Armada) with this. I have played just under an hour just to be able to refund if this turned out not what i hoped or expected in a negative way. I have requested the refund and waiting on it.First of all, the 12 different things you have to manage. Like are you serious right now? I have to not only ensure i have money, food, some version of currency (?), science (thats fine, Civilization feature-like) and then the rest of the things i have no clue about. In STA, you only had two resources you had to worry about, officer capacity, and the building resource (forgot it's name). Research was simple like Star Wars Empire at War. Just research it and wait for it to complete.  In this game however, you cant just research. No, that would be too simple. you need to get a captain/officer or w.e to research it. and on top of that they may not be the BEST at w.e you are currently researching..only "good" thing is you can research 3 things at a time but again your pool of officers might not be the best at those.Now this is the part where the comparison stops as the simplicity (restrictions of technology of the old days) cant be compared to this. The map you play on is small. here it is huge. In order to claim a star system, you have to survey it completely so you are then allowed to build in it. some planets are useful that allow you to build science stations, mining stations and so on. But not all planets are useful, at least not up to what i managed to play. I understood i could terraform some planets so they could be useful down the line but time restriction kept me from reaching that point. The game really did not need to be this complex. Sure some people would rather just build their favorite faction ships, and blow up other faction ships nice and simple like, hear iconic lines and phrases from favorite characters of the show, and the sounds of the photon torpedo, lasers etc. TLDR: Too complex for simple gamer who enjoys simple rts with little management such as STA, Star Wars Empire at War, StarCraft 2 (im a casual player of it, not crazy with those macros+micros) Halo Wars, or Civilization like games.
