_childDocuments_.review: I've always wanted to play an horror game set in an oil rig, something about being isolated in a critical situation. Still Wakes the Deep is a strong narrative driven game where you are a blue collar electrician, stuck in such a nightmare scenario where you go around trying to find survivors and of course, escape!This game has many interesting settings mixed into one, where you can find strong inspirations coming from the movies "The Thing", "The Blob", "Leviathan", "Underwater" and even a non-horror one, "Deepwater Horizon" for the catastrophe of the oil rig.SWTD is mainly a walking simulator and it has a few interactions to be had, like flipping switches and turning valves. You have many "run for your life" escape sequences and hide from monsters situations. The visuals, sounds and voice acting are all spot on very good. The oil rig itself was impressive looking and a treat to explore when you can that is.The game is VERY linear but you do have some opportunities to explore a bit but not enough in my opinion. I found the catastrophe happening too fast and I wish you could had done some more "blue collar" work around with the other oil rig crew but it is not the case.The story is minimal since you don't know much WHAT is causing the catastrophe besides some strange otherwordly "skin filaments" hanging everywhere. I wish you could get to know more about the origins of the "entity/ies" but again, story is minimally explained.Game works very well for Ultrawide screen but as of now, it doesn't have a FOV option and at times, the in-game view is a tad too close. No bugs or technical issues encountered in my playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece for being made by a small studio; however, it's game play, story, and price let it down hard in comparison with the game I compare it to most. If you've played Firewatch, this is basically a horror version of that but without the touching story or most of the charm. It has excellent atmospheric horror and makes good use of the unreal engine, and that is where the positives stop. The monsters, when you even see them, are repetitive and boring, with absolutely no difference between any monster encounter other than their appearance and again that's if you can see them. The game includes a "distraction" system used by throwing objects in the environment, but I never got it to work and found it far easier not to use it at all. The story is a interesting concept but is fairly skin deep with nothing ever being explained and the epilogue being confusing despite the actual final game play scene being fairly conclusive. The setting and character dialogue is charming and well executed but that only goes so far in a game with this many flaws. Technically speaking I had 2-3 crashes over 4.7 hours playing and no other problems so the works okay on release but not perfect as crashes were pretty serious random freezes.Pros:good graphicsexcellent sound designinteresting settings and charactersgood atmospheric horror elementsCons:overpricedlacking in game play that compliments the horror experienceGame play that is present is repetitive and lazily thought outShort playtimelittle to no replay abilityOverall, I do like this game because it was absolutely beautiful in it's own way and I think the idea of a horror game set on an oil rig is really cool. I saw the first trailer for this game and I've been excited to play since I thought of elderitch horror plus oil rig. Unfortunately, this game just doesn't deliver on that promise for it's $35 price tag and frankly I think it's a crime to sell it at that price and I feel ripped off. This is a tech demo for the unreal engine and nothing else is really going for it. Steer clear of this, watch a walk through, or maybe pick it up for $5-$10. Otherwise, it's just a waste of your money. 4/10 If this game was $5 - $10 I'd sing it's praises but at that price tag I've gotten so many better games and even better horror games.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a first-person horror game developed by The Chinese Room. Set on the Beira D oil rig in the North Sea during 1975, it offers a beautifully crafted juxtaposition of manmade, natural, and supernatural elements.Atmosphere and Tension:The game excels in creating a sense of place. The oil rig feels remote, claustrophobic, and oppressive, yet it also holds warmth and life. The lived-in spaces reveal much about the characters, and the authenticity of the world is easy to buy into.The writing is beautifully nuanced, incorporating perfectly deployed profanity, and the performances from the cast are stellar.Narrative and Gameplay:Electrician Cameron McLeary (Caz) receives a letter from his wife, urging him to come home. But duty calls, and he faces a day filled with escalating disasters.The game balances horror with a human heart, gradually allowing unknowable forces to take hold. While the linear structure might disappoint some, the strong atmosphere compensates for it.Visuals and Art Direction:The grim period setting of the Beira D oil rig is brought to life with gaudy fabrics, grubby linoleum, and meticulously recreated details. The artistry captures the bleakness of the rig while infusing it with life.Conclusion: Despite some hand-holding, simple puzzles, and a short story, Still Wakes the Deep is an atmospheric, tense, and gripping experience that I fully recommend. It’s a journey into horror with a very human touch.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in just over 5 hours which is a fair playtime considering the price tag. People have pointed out it's a walking sim but it has more than that. It has climbing, jumping, running, swimming, some stealth and other interactions. Yes, the game does follow a particular path and whilst that's not a bad thing, there were times where I wished for more exploration during breaks between chase sequences. Even a few side paths where you could find collectables or notes would of been appreciated but the game has an engaging story and excellent dialogue, so I never ended up being bored, even if some of mechanics were repetitive. The story and the sound design is what nails this game. The industrial banging and creaking of metal, and punishing gales really make you feel like you're on oil rig. The audio also does a good job of providing the horror atmosphere. I particularly enjoyed the first (sort of) encounter with one of the things and you can only hear it clambering about. This did a brilliant job of making me feel uneasy as I never really knew where it was or if I was under any kind of threat. The creatures and disfigured bodies embedded into doors, and walls look horrific. The voice acting is great with some mixed accents here, mainly Scottish but I heard some Irish, Northern and London accents when chatting to folks in the canteen. Performance is OK with DLSS or similar on balanced and the graphics still look stunning in places, especially the overwhelming size of the rig itself with all the waves crashing against it. This was a worthwhile experience and I hope Chinese Room develop some kind of DLC as I think there's so much more lore and backstories that could be appended to this.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: For those that just want a Score: 6.7/10.There you go.For the rest of you here a bit more (con)text.First off let me tell you that some Reviewers really wanted to sell this Game as one of the classic horror Games.A Hall of Fame Game if you will. A Game that is so deep it belongs with the big boys in the big league.I'm telling you right now, it is not that.Is it a bad Game? No! Definitely not. But it is not the new Horror Classic some make it out to be.It is competent. Even good in some areas. But that's it.Now why is that? Let's get to the good and the "bad".Let me start with the Graphics.The Game looks good, in some areas very good. And here I can tell you, the developers did a really good job with Unreal Engine 5! What I mean is the performance. Everything cranked to Epic and the Game runs smooth as butter. Very few and minor frame drops here and there but overall perfect.And it is not a stutterfest like Silent Hill 2 Remake, so I guess the devs here knew what they were doing with optimization.There are a few minor nitpicks in the graphics department, but overall they are not really worth talking about (for example a strange "dithering"/noise effect on some shiny surfaces but I think this is because of either DLSS or UE5; also there were a few clipping issues here and there, where your body is clipping through things or the monsters clip through walls, all minor stuff).Musically the Game is good. Not overwhelmingly good, just good and fitting.Sound Design is REALLY good here though. The creaking and groaning sounds of the oil rig, rain splattering, the howls and moans of the monsters, footsteps and many more environmental sounds are all top notch and give this Game a great atmosphere.Also, as many people mentioned, the Voice Acting (I played on English UK) is really good and believable! Good Job there. (Btw.: Sometimes when your guy speaks I just had to think of Gerard Butler.)So now, what about the Game(play) itself?! I won't spoil any of the story here, because this is basically almost all that this Game has going for.This Game is EXTREMELY linear. There is literally one path, one way you can go. From starting point A right to the finish line to point B where the Game ends. This is not always that bad but it needs mentioning. You can not explore or deviate (apart from maybe 1-2 small sections where you can explore 3 rooms before you go on your path again).Also the Checkpoints are extremely plentiful, that means if you play on Standard (which already is the "highest difficulty") you don't care if you die (either when a monster gets you, you miss a jump or maybe a small "skill check"/QTE). And that means that all the tension that this Game could've had is gone. This Game has no tension. There is no real threat of danger. And this Game didn't scare me at all. Yes, the atmosphere is top notch (and sometimes that's enough for some) but without tension or a feeling of dread it feels hollow.Also there are no secrets to find and no puzzles to solve. You just go from point A to B and it basically feels like watching a "longer" movie. At least in this regard it feels immersive.So yeah, this is a linear Walking Simulator. I have to say though that the monster design looks really cool.The whole Game gives you "The Thing" Vibes with a few pinches of Lovecraft.The Game itself is really short. It took me 5.9 hours (maybe a bit less since I took a few small breaks while inside the Game) to complete, 27/37 Achievements. Also I really took my time with this because from the Reviews on Steam I already gathered that it's a short Game.A few things that I didn't get...: 1) Why is there an online profile for a purely singleplayer Game?2) Why bother putting Achievements into the Game that warrant multiple playthroughs when this is clearly a Game that you will probably only play through once and not more. (Because there are a few of them.)Overall as I said, this Game is not bad, it is enjoyable, but in my opinion this is just NOT worth either the full price or around 20€/$, maybe 15€/$ at the max. And I want to mention that I did not really factor pricing into this review even though I said it's not worth the asking price.But yeah, still an enjoyable Game but don't get fooled into thinking this is a new Horror Masterpiece. It is not!

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 and without doubt one of the best games to be released this year; especially with the number of garbage games released on Steam over the last year.The story follows an electrician who is trapped on a damaged oil drilling platform in the North Sea, having no way to escape while being pursued by mysterious monsters under harsh weather conditionsI DO NOT understand why people are so critical and the negative reviews are not accurate and more about people who are unhappy with their life.  Because you do not like a game is not reason to NOT RECOMMEND.  My point is that negative reviews with out stating specifics on the good or bad are not helpful; and i would not give them much  weight.  But I knew nothing about this game prior to release.  I went in with no expectations and am amazed on how great this game is....and I having been playing games since Steam started in early 2000. _childDocuments_.review: The ocean waves hide darker secrets than the stars can even imagine.A fine line between classic Lovecraft, where the common people are forced to confront the indescribable, unexplainable unknown. Recite what you saw and be declared deranged.Mixed with a beautiful, more modern edge, where even the most bizarre can make just a sliver of sense through human connection.An excellent, narrative-driven horror game that plays smoothly with light stealth elements and breathtaking environments. Every part of this story is highlighted by its fantastic art direction, where darkness gets warped by bright, colorful lights and the reflection of the water that sneaks into the cracks of the decaying oil rig that's surrendering to the weight and forceful invasion of a mind-and-flesh-bending organic monstrosity.And it wouldn't be fair to leave the amazing cast of voice actors unmentioned, as they put a beautiful, cherry red, satin bow around the delightfully horrific package that is Still Wakes the Deep.I don't want to spoil too much, I just want everyone who's even remotely interested to take their own dive into this fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, truly one of THE best horror stories in a game that I've played in a long time -- unfortunately it's constantly marred by poor game design and a lack of QA. A+ story, C- Gameplay. It kills me to have to set this as a "not recommend". The voice acting and world building is top notch, and the atmosphere is perfect. I really enjoyed the characters and the body horror was perfectly grotesque. Sadly, the most of the actual game mechanics simply felt entirely "tacked on" last minute to me. It feels like it would be a great filmThe game is absolutely FILLED with bugs, with several of them even being game breaking. There were countless times where I found myself infuriated with the controls failing to register properly - near the end I was gritting my teeth through it just to finish up the story. This probably has the worst swimming mechanics I've ever had to deal with, and I even had to spend a full hour doing my own QA testing just to try to figure out how to get around a game-breaking bug regarding an underwater ladder jump. I was frequently glitched through views, or straight through guard rails (to my death) several times. Many of the settings menu options simply don't work at all, which is crazy considering that should be the simplest mechanic to verify. On top of that, the level design is incredibly simplistic with simple paths and very little actual game play. It's very much a walking simulator -- which I normally tend to love ...when I don't feel like I'm having to fight against constant bugs just to make progress.As a result, it felt like I had to actively fight the game just to complete the story. The game mechanics actively dragged me out of it simply because they were so broken. It really got worse the more I went on, so perhaps they focused more on the first half of the game during testing. I DEEPLY wish that I could recommend this game, but with the current glitches I feel like I have to tell people to wait and save their money until the developer spends the time fixing the bugs. These bugs should have been solved before launch -- it's a full month later and they haven't fixed anything?

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Very interesting story, easy to follow along and with a little back history of the main character.- Graphics are simple but rather well done (thank to UE5)- Gameplay is not over complicated so that you can immerse yourself into the story.Cons:- It's a little "hand-holdy." There's no combat, or anything like that and the most you'll have to do is watch for the queue when "holding on."- 60 FPS lock (for those with a beefy GPU, you won't get much more out of this).- It's a bit slow at times. Personally, I wish there was a little bit more than just running, swimming, and climbing.- It's rather short, you could absolutely finish this game in 4 -/+ hours as that seems to be the average play time (via Steam reviewers).Overall, it's an excellent game for what it is. Perhaps it's a little overpriced for how short the game is but, it's 2024 and everyone trying to get theirs. In my humble opinion, this game should be valued at a FAIR price between $20 to $25 MAX before tax.If you're interested, check it out. If it's not your jam, then that's understandable. _childDocuments_.review: Traditional horror has really started to bore me recently. Any new movie that has those clickable words of, "scariest film in years," or "people left the theater terrified" tend to fall extremely flat. One horror that has never failed for me is Lovecraftian, though. If you've seen and enjoyed the movie Annihilation (an amazing film that almost perfectly portrays Lovecraftian horror), this game is for you. I watched Joe Bart play it until I saw the glowing branch stretch out of the water; I recognized the Lovecraftian influence and immediately bought the game. This game has the most realistic dialogue and voice acting I've ever seen in a game, and the soundtrack has moved my emotions from down-right terrified to near balling my eyes out. It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I was very sure I would like, but I ended up feeling quite "meh" about. A strong contender for a neutral rating. Since it's rated so very positive it will survive my thumbs down, I am sure.So why the disappointment? The voice acting is fine, the Scottish accents a welcome change, the oil platform setting is very promising, but what can I say, this is a horror game, and I wasn't frightened once. It just runs on rails; the controls are reduced to a minimum and I never got emotionally involved; I know I was supposed to care about my mates and my wife and probably my character, but it just never happened. So, you are this not-too-bright worker with the heart in the right place stumbling about, but never asking any of the thousand questions coming to my mind when I see what's happening, just uttering one curse after the other - that's, pardon the pun, not very deep. The monster(s) are a stark contrast to all these down-to-earth people, but I for one would have liked to discover a bit more about them; presented like this they were just some arbitrary ugly things doing ugly things for whatever ugly reason. Yes, they can be taken as an allegory for all the evil fossil fuels are bringing to this planet, but unfortunately that isn't solved by one guy sacrificing himself in the end.To me Firewatch or Under the Waves were far more satisfying experiences with emotional back stories that really gripped me, let me identify with the main characters a lot more and which were games that either let me play or at least gave me the illusion of choice. But Still runs the Deep falls short as a game, as a horror experience and as an interesting story. 5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent narrative-focused lovecraftian horror game."Still Wakes the Deep" emphasizes atmosphere over action. It helps, then, that the worldbuilding is fantastic. The rig really feels like an actual place. An intricate place filled with lovecraftian horrors. Likewise the characters are quite human, and thus very relatable, something that's helped along by some excellent voice acting.It also doesn't overstay its welcome, but progresses at a brisk pace, but without feeling rushed. Rather the pacing is just right.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: The Loch Ness Monster isn't real... it can't hurt you...I enjoyed Still Wake the Deep, visually it is stunning, there is some phenomenal voice acting, and there is some clear inspiration taken from John Carpenter's 'The Thing' which is one of my favourite all-time movies.But outside of these elements, the game as other's have mentioned is incredibly linear, ultimately an on-the-rails experience with some obvious quick-time events baked into the foundation. Which is a shame given such a unique setting/environment the game is set in... and it's all over in 3 hours, with absolutely zero-replay value save achievement hunting if you're that way inclined, and for £30 that's way to steep. If you're looking for an interactive love-letter to 80's Horror/Sci-fi, then Still Wake the Deep is worth your time and attention but only if it is on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: It is not a game, it is an interactive story with a lot of repeating mechanics: corridors, doors, crawling, opening/closing valves and pulling triggers with 0 to no challenge at all. _childDocuments_.review: A very compelling game. Great scripting and well produced. The mid 70s vibe has been captured well with good interactions between the workers and  the dodgy rig management. _childDocuments_.review: Wow, what a game!I'm not usually a fan of horror games, I've managed to get through some like The Medium and Alan Wake 2, but others like RE: Village and Alien Isolation were too much for me. However, I do love "walking sims" with great stories (like Firewatch, The Invincible, Edith Finch), and this game delivered exactly that.The setting and atmosphere are superb, and while the core of the story isn't particularly novel, I loved the way the narrative played out, and that was helped by some incredible voice acting and dialogue.On top of that, the attention to detail in the environment is outstanding, the graphics are great, and everything was tied together with a brilliant soundtrack (I’m actually listening to it as I write this).The ending was so impactful that I just sat watching the credits roll. And by doing so I inadvertently saw how many people and how much work went into it. That actually gave me a better appreciation of the high price tag, although I still think €35 is a bit steep for a six-hour game. I picked it up on sale and would recommend others do the same.All in all, this was a very memorable experience. I'm glad I pushed through the horror elements to play it (I think I'll even give Alien Isolation another try now). I’m excited to see what they put out next and I'm looking forward to trying some of their older titles like Everybody’s Gone to the Rapture.

_childDocuments_.review: I did not particularly enjoy this game. The acting and sound design are great, loved the characters, but the 4 hour run time and lack of "video game" present are major downsides. The game ends up being just a long string of coincidences where our main character ends up in the right place at the right time to do various things, there's even a point in the story where one of the supporting cast is literally like "Wow dude you're like the luckiest dude here so you literally HAVE to go do this thing" like it's some sort of tongue in cheek yeah there's no real way this man should be alive self awareness from the devs. It's very predictable from the beginning as well, the moment you realize the entity is some flesh creature from beneath the sea you can easily put OIL RIG and FLESH MONSTER together on the horror game conclusion mad lib and know that you're obviously not getting out alive and you're going to make some heroic self sacrifice where you burn the creature alive to prevent it from spreading to the mainland.It's just rather disappointing this game has nothing to say of it's own, just retreading old ground.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.75/10I LOVED this game.I beat it in 5 hrs on my first playthrough, standard mode. Let's talk about it! SPOILER WARNING!! This is going to be a long one, buckle up! <3Pros:- The story is very well written, easy to understand and relate to, and felt grounded and realistic for the game world. It wasn't over complicated, which I think actually added to the game because you aren't trying to split your focus between a complex story and the scares which take most of your attention in this game.- Gameplay was great, smooth on my rig, with no framerate or lag issues- The horror was BRILLIANT. I never once got bored or expectant of the horror or the scares. From start to finish, I was on the edge of my seat and did not know what to expect.- The monsters felt unique, even though they appeared somewhat similar in model. They weren't overemployed and though there were calm moments, I feel like the scale of chase/evade to free roam time was pretty fair and balanced.- I LOVED that you got to know which monsters were where, and at points I was going 'ohhh don't you dare send me back to Engineering, I don't wanna see Addair!' xD Which was great.- The strategies you needed to employ for each monster felt challenging, and I had to stop and put thought into my next move before taking it, and when I did die, I had to reevaluate my moves. In one scenario against Addair (changing the fuse box in Engineering cage), I died probably 5-6 times trying to go 10 feet to a door. The BEST part of this situation for me, was that after I got to the door and closed it, I walked ten feet and realized the beast was waiting for me in the NEXT DAMN ROOM. That was brutal, and I felt like it flipped the script on the traditional 'hide/run/rest' cycle of horror. We have been trained by horror games to hide or run and once we reach a door or a checkpoint, we get a few moments to rest where the music is light and we can let our heartbeat come down - BUT that moment where I opened the next door and found him there, and immediately had to go back and hide was one of the most brutal things I have had a horror game do to me in a LONG time. It was a nice sequence break that kept me on my toes. (Addair was honestly my fav monster, and I also hated him the most xD I was so thrilled when he burned LOL)- The map was very well utilized! Despite returning to the same areas several times, they were different each time, and I never felt like I actually learned the map because it kept changing and molding as the iridescent goop (as one of my stream viewers called it) took over. I had to find new ways to get around the monsters and form new strategies for the same area because it had changed since I was last there. This made the horror 10x better because I wasn't just running down the same hallways (even though I technically was) and looping the monsters because I knew the map, I had to relearn the rig at least three times, which was scary, but great!- The graphics and art style was beautiful. The world felt REAL and lived in, the map was (to my knowledge) fairly realistic in terms of an oil rig, and I didn't feel 'pathed' as you might say. Yes, this could be considered a form of walking simulator because there isn't much to do besides run/hide and open doors, but I never really felt like I was on a single straight roped off path like some games feel. I felt like I was exploring an oil rig, and even if I couldn't walk around the map freely like an open world game, I didn't feel guided like a carrot on a stick, I was exploring in the bounds of a falling apart oil rig, and it felt genuine. I felt like I was in control, which made it all the more scary, because I was making the choices, and I suffered for my mistakes.- The sound design was top tier. The noises of the rig, the monsters, and the ocean were very realistic and horrifying. The atmosphere it created was bone chilling at times, especially for the under rig sections and pontoon sections. There's more atmosphere than music, but I don't think that took anything away from the game at all. I actually think it suited the game to have less music and more just natural sounds of the rig and ocean. The Leg areas and Pontoon areas were brutal for me because they were so SILENT xD That scared me way more than creepy music would have.- This might not be a 'Pro' to everyone, but it is to me; this game plays PERFECTLY on Thalassophobia and Vertigo.Cons:- The story could have been introduced a little better at the beginning. Why are we there? We don't really find that out for a while and it left me with a slight disconnect. Also, the connection between Caz and Roy was not established very well. I felt nothing when Roy died. I felt more losing Brodie and Finlay because I spent the whole game talking to them and experiencing the horrors with them.- There were only a couple graphical issues, specifically where you got out of a cutscene. Both of those were when the cutscene was showing a monster coming up behind you and you had to run. One was with Trots or Addair, I think? The other was with Rennick. The one with Rennick got me killed TWICE in a row. Basically, when you come out of the cutscene, it turns you back around, so you're facing the monster. I already had my run going, so the moment I came out of it, I ran smack into Rennick instead of running away like I had been before the cutscene turned me. This isn't a huge horror killer, but it did break my immersion/horror/tension when Rennick killed me twice in a row before I got myself turned the right away and barely escaped him from the time I lost to the cutscene turning me.- A couple of the controls were a little buggie (though it may have been user error?) The 'leap forward' while swimming did not work for me at all. I followed the on screen directions and it never worked. I was using keyboard and mouse, so maybe it's just an integration issue. Despite this, I never once drowned in the underwater sections, so I didn't suffer for this issue. The grab and grip mechanics failed a couple times when I KNOW I was pressing hard into my mouse buttons. I am unsure if that was scripted or just a control bug.- The run speed felt... awkward? While I know you aren't supposed to be able to outrun giant monsters, I sometimes felt like I was moving through quicksand (even when not injured). This MAY be purposeful, but I died more than once in places where I should have been able to make it to a safe space or door.- The volume was a little hard to get right - meaning I wasn't actually sure which meter the monsters were tagged to minus the global meter. It was a little hard to get that balanced right - and as someone who uses earbuds, that did present me with a challenge when the monsters were right in my face. They were WAY too loud, but if I turned down the global setting, I couldn't hear anything, so I felt almost handicapped. Maybe add a volume slider for the monster sounds, or make it clear which one they are tagged to for headphone users? That made it really hard to find a good balance between 'i'm scared' and 'my ears are blown out, you just ruined the horror for me', but honestly, it was only a major issue in a couple sections, mostly with Addair in Engineering.- This is specifically about Addair in the Engineering room with the fuse box - I got stuck under the stairs to the door out beside the fuse box cage. Addair was literally on top of me, and would not move or go back to his patrol path despite me being silent. Even when I threw objects to pull him away, he would not move. I ended up having to let him kill me once because it felt like he was bugged there after 10 minutes of just waiting and throwing stuff across the room. I am unsure if this is a bug. Overall, I had a BLAST playing this game* If the Dev's want footage of any of the bugs I mentioned above, let me know, I streamed my playthrough on Twitch, so I can provide timestamps to see the issues I had.- LitaCakes

_childDocuments_.review: Some games are like a movie, they are a linear experience and story with a game just being the medium. The gameplay is not all that, walk/move turn a valve, climb on yellow marking, move to yellow paint. This is not the strongest or weakest lovecraftian tale either. Main thing is as with the best cosmic/incomprehensible horror, this is a sad story. Do not expect explanations of what happening, you are just a man working an oil rig, trying his best as circumstances steadily worsen. That is what this does well, its not some outlandish tale where you are the man and you meet scientists who research or anything. You play through the POV of a worker going through hell and trying to keep his buddies alive, the only thing special about you is you are lucky, and thats only ever brought up due to the fact you haven't been killed like half the rig. Really good game for a one time experience that you may come back to in some years to relive.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10. I played this game on my bro's Xbox on GamePass, and then came home and bought it here so I could own and support it more directly, if that tells you anything, but I might be a little weird.I admit my expectations weren't extremely high, because I wasn't sure what to expect from The Chinese Room.The first thing I want to call attention to is how ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ excellent the voice performances are. It absolutely nails the setting, an oil rig in the North Sea, manned by a bunch of Scots. The accents / dialect / language are impeccable, you will probably need subtitles if you are an average English speaker. The story gets pretty emotional and the voice deliver on that.The game is fairly linear, but that didn't bother me in this case. This game does a lot with its horror set pieces, and never relies on cheap scares. The mystery of the antagonist in this game is at once chilling and compelling. Without spoiling too much, if you like  you should love this.It's pretty short at 4-5 hours, but I would happily pay $35 for this experience, maybe more. 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: So I just finished the game and I'm blown away. Suffice to say, I never expected to be so invested in the whole story but oh boy, it's so much more than that. Still wakes the deep is the prime example that you can create a masterpiece game without any combat or boss fights. It's about the story and the emotion. There's no doubt that UE5 is the main ingredient for a photo-realistic immersion and playing this game can trick you into thinking you're watching some oil rig personnel bodycam footage. It's that amazing. Lots of nerve racking scenes, pure emotion and feels all around. At the end of the day is a blend between The Thing and scottish life.Can we all appreciate the voice acting? Spot on.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: The story is absolutely heartbreaking. The voice acting is phenomenal; the best I have experienced in a game.Level design can be a bit repetitive - go from A to B, dodge antagonists etc. - but to be honest the draw of this game is its story, and the repetitive nature does well to highlight Caz's desperate clinging to hope. Each level is designed differently, and when revisiting the same sites the environment changes with the progression of the disaster unfolding, making it interesting to traverse the site in a different way. It's a terrific use of the limited space an oil rig presents.Visuals and audio are superb and really make the environment of a oil rig convincing as a player.£30 is a steep price point for the approximately 4 hours of gameplay, so I would consider picking this up when it is on sale. However, I am perfectly happy with my purchase and can say that you will likely not regret buying this at full price. I didn't encounter any game breaking bugs, although I am aware of one in Mud Handling. I did experience a glitch where the antagonist was clipped into the wall - he soon freed himself to come and terrify me. I gladly recommend this game; it is an absolute delight.

Lovecraft and others, but also to execute it well in both design and gameplay. I will definitely go back and play through this game again to hopefully get all the achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of this review, I have played through this game twice.It's a very short game. I completed my first playthrough in under 8 hours.Terrible performance. Cannot maintain 60 FPS.Despite having terrible performance, the game looks good. Some of the visuals are particularly great. Even removed from story and gameplay, the visuals are a worthwhile experience.I've heard complaints about how linear the game is. But I believe that's a ridiculous argument. Some games are a linear one-and-done experience. And that isn't a problem.However, despite being linear, the game frequently completely fails at directing the player. And input feedback is barely noticeable or non-existent. Did I press the button in time? Am I supposed to fall down this hole? The path forward is meant to be highlighted with the color yellow. But sometimes there is no such highlight. And other times completely unimportant or unrelated objects are also highlighted yellow. So what's the point?There is no actual story. Nothing is explained or expanded upon. It's all left up to interpretation. However, despite the lack of tangible story, I like the game's concept, and the theme that it maintains throughout gameplay.The game frequently doesn't feel good to play. The controls are clunky. And even with head bobbing disabled, the camera bounces around in a jostled and uncomfortable manner. During both of my playthroughs, I used keyboard and mouse. I have not played the game using a gamepad controller, so I can't speak to how well gameplay feels with that input method.There are moments that are completely devoid of purpose. Like being forced to wait at a heater. These moments don't further the story, expand upon the plot, or explain game mechanics. They just waste time, and otherwise serve no purpose.During both of my playthroughs, there were unskippable title cards. This is an unacceptable waste of the player's time. Title cards should always be skippable or presented in a better manner.You may also be interested to know that this game was developed in Unreal Engine.In summary, I like this game's concept. It's a concise experience with a theme similar to The Thing and Annihilation. However, its biggest flaws are its terrible performance and its lack of clear and consistent direction and input feedback.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: If your flavor of "cozy" is a spooky narrative adventure game, this one is for you. In fact, if you are a fan of  (one of my most favorite games of all time) I HIGHLY recommend you check out . While it has a slower pace than , it will definitely scratch your underwater Lovecraftian horror itch if you're into that. The game will be very easy for you if you're used to the type of gameplay in  (you can only hide from monsters or distract them, and the controls are almost identical), however, if you're fine with that, don't let it stop you from checking this game out. The narrative and cinematic experience more than makes up for it, even with the fact that there are no choices to make in the game. The character development, plotline, and presentation are all stellar.Sometimes the QTE events are a tad glitchy, but that didn't bother me too much. My only real complaint is how short it is. Despite that, I still highly recommend it if you like Lovecraftian stuff. Certainly scared the pants off of me more than a few times, and the ending, , hits soooo good.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes The Deep is a game that I have been looking forward with a lot of hype since it was announced and I can safely say it did not dissapoint!First thing I want to say is that an Oil Rig is a very under utilised environment in almost any video game! Given its secluded nature, its large size and clostrophobic interior - it honestly makes for an amazing environment in almost any video game but it really works in a horror like this one.I loved so much about Still Wakes The Deep: Overall I loved Still Wakes The Deep, it ticked every box for when it comes to an amazing single player narrative driven game and the grotesque horror was the icing on the cake!

_childDocuments_.review: I've finished and at times even enjoyed this game, but I have to be honest I can't recommend it.The game has fantastic voice acting and great atmosphere, and even some good moments but unfortunately that's it. There is nothing here for fans of interactive stories or fans of horror. This is a game that feels like it wants to be about the oil rig, the Beira D. But this isn't a story of "a great ship" or anything. There is nothing to discover, nothing to find, nothing to interact with. Every area is labelled when you leave and enter, with grand cut-ins, levels are littered with maps, but the game is completely linear, so it's all in service of nothing.There is nothing about the crew, or the company or what they're mining, or any problems of the rig falling apart past the opening. All of those things are set up in the first 5 minutes and they're great! But except one, most of those things will never come up again.The family story and the horror segments try their best to be relevant, fighting for screentime, trying to set up something, ANYTHING, but they are constantly kicked to the curb. We don't have time for that. We have to go to another part of the rig, to pull more levers, and push more boxes and do the same "nearly fall off the ledge" quick time event for the 14th time, we don't have time to think about your stupid monsters. It feels like you can cut out the wife completely and replace the monsters with any natural disaster and almost all of the game will remain exactly the same.Nobody in the story gives a ♥♥♥♥ about the monsters that used to be their friends, screaming and writhing in pain. They just tell you to avoid them on your way to screwdriver another fuse box. The monster arenas have so much hiding places that going through them is a casual walk and most of the monster chases are solved by holding shift and running down an obvious long corridor. The monster will never catch you.At least if you're a fan of beautiful industrial setpieces, you will enjoy the view.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I know everyone is saying it's a short game but I don't mind that as much. You buy/rent a new movie for twenty bucks and it's only an hour to two long. Thirty for four hours of great storytelling and fantastic characters? I'm completely fine with it. Each character has their own personality and the voice actors do an amazing job relaying emotion. I want to express my gratitude, however, for the settings! I've never seen a game that allowed me to turn off flashing lights and as an epileptic who has been begging for an option to turn them off -- I have never been happier. I can enjoy a game without having to worry or pause in order to protect my health.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: 𝑻𝒉𝒊𝒔 𝒓𝒆𝒗𝒊𝒆𝒘 𝒊𝒔 𝒔𝒑𝒐𝒊𝒍𝒆𝒓 𝒇𝒓𝒆𝒆;This is what I’ve missed about horror games—linear and helpless. No weapons, just pure survival in a linear horror experience where you’re at the mercy of fate, and fate only...What an amazing game this was. I'm already a huge fan of this type of horror, and it feels similar to SOMA by Frictional Games, which is my favorite horror game of all time. The design direction of Still Wakes the Deep also reminded me a lot of the movie Annihilation. When I looked it up on the Wiki page, it turns out the movie was actually a major source of inspiration for the team! Very cool. The story dives deep into the unknown; you don’t know what’s happening... until you do, and even then, you’re not really sure. You just go with the flow, letting the atmosphere and gameplay take over and see what happens.The level design is incredible. The oil rig where everything takes place is HUGE. Every nook and cranny is filled with detail, really making you feel like you’re on a monstrous platform, trapped in a labyrinth of leaky pipes, water, machines... and some very strange organic matter. I often found myself lost in paranoia—knowing where to go but not knowing what might be lurking in the dark water. You hear grunts and roars echoing in the distance, everything creaks and groans, and there’s this constant strange pulsating sound. The atmosphere is just amazing and so is the sound design.All in all, if you love being thrown into the unknown, and you enjoy a good piece of psychological horror with a linear survival setup, you'll enjoy this game just as much.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best horror 'walking simulator' out there! Visually this game is impressive - the oil rig is amazingly detailed and very creepy to explore. The Devs have really nailed the overall setting and the vibe is very reminiscent of Alien Isolation and The Thing. Obviously this game is more in the walking simulator genre and is therefore very linear, with interactions and exploration being far more limited then games like Dead Space and Alien Isolation, but they've really nailed the genre. Yes, expect to find lots of locked door and only one that is unlockable, only to return later and another door has magically unlocked - but that's the style of game. You're always moving forward and not having to back track to find the right key etc. It's a straightforward game, as intended. What is does, it does extremely well, but don't expect this game to do what it wasn't designed to do - It's not a vast sandbox structure to explore like Dead Space.Sound design is impeccable and really adds to the atmosphere. The enemy type I thought was superb, very reminiscent of The Thing, with some really intense sequences!This really is an amazing game. Its a short roller-coaster ride of a horror, but I love that, and really puts many triple A developers to shame with the whole quality. I played with hints reduced, which I believe removes some of the yellow paint markers. I heard some reviewers being frustrated that the map was confusing, but I didn't find that once. It was always fairly obvious to me, but I guess some people may find the nature of exploring an oil rig a tad confusing. But to me it always seemed logical and not at all confusing. The Scottish actors are amazing and loved the accents and dialogue too. This game was an amazing experience and just begs to be bought!! Easily a contender for Indie GOTY.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t know how to describe this game, but it’s wonderful—the only flaw is that it ends. The characters are rich with stories, and you grow attached to them. The graphics are impressive, and although I’m not usually drawn to games for their visuals, the compositions really impressed me. The story is captivating and intriguing—I couldn’t stop playing because I needed to know what would happen next. The lighting and composition are incredible. Please, someone needs to praise the lighting artist and level designer! The levels are so well done—I never got lost and constantly felt immersed in the game. The sound design is perfect, it worked so well with everything that I’m at a loss for words. You can truly see the dedication and passion of everyone who worked on this masterpiece. Congratulations!I highly recommend this game!Developers, thank you so much for your hard work.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't going to leave a review.  But this game really stuck with me.  I loved the characters, and my only wish is that we saw more of them before everything went down.  The art direction is consistently amazing, and the music is fantastic when is takes the stage, while the story is a fantastic downwards spiral towards tragedy.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a good narrative-driven horror, similar to Amnesia in its concept. The idea of a Lovecraftian horror game set on an oil mining rig is definitely unique. However:- it's a walking simulator, there are no puzzles, only QTEs; wouldn't have been a downside if there was a compelling story (e.g. SOMA has almost exactly the same gameplay but its story is far more complex and deep than this one)- the story isn't bad, it's just very personal and isn't that deep- the horror elements are repetitiveI would recommend trying the game but I would say the gameplay/story balance is lacking as both aren't really there. Visuals, audio and the VO are incredible.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: It is short. Really short. Took me 3 hours to finish it. But that did not diminish the experience in the slightest. I wont spoiler anything, which is why I have to keep it short. Its a perfect horror/adventure game with its own unique story. A bit expensive for such a short experience but bearable for the level of presentation without a single bug.The game has its own unique charm well worth buying if you are looking for a dense immersive experience which is obviously inspired by some of the best horror movies. If its too expensive for you now, get it in a sale. You wont regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: As always, Chinese Room delivers. Impactful stories with simple but engaging gameplay. I highly recommend it for everyone who likes psychological horror and tought provoking stories.Also, the achievements are funny, you get them for being bad at the game! :D Dying in different ways and being a perv... (McLeery)
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I liked:1. The first person viewpoint throughout. No cut aways or extended cutscenes etc. I like games to be a games and not interactive movies.2. Not Scottish myself but I appreciated the localiisation and down to earth (and salty) dialogue. Good vocal performances by all. (English/Scottish version)3. Some tense moments dodging the monsters4. Visual guides to where to go is pretty good 97% of the time5. Doesn't overstay its welcome - There is next to no padding. Although shortish I felt I got my money's worth. 6. Sound and visuals were good (if your pc is up to it). I was impressed by the water effects ,particularly the scummy oily water down below.I disliked:1. The 3% of the time I got completely lost and couldn't figure out where to go in a couple of places.2. Due the the first person perspective you do kinda miss seeing what monster is chasing you. I blinked and  missed Rennicks end for instance.3. Still ruminating on whether it needed the Suze scenes.Other:1. Controls take a little getting used to. Particularly the grab and hold button functionality.2. Not alot of replayability. (Not necessarily a bad thing). I don't know if there are alternative events in the game.3. Nice change of pace from the usual monster outbreak type games. There is no shooting or killing in this one.Overall I thoroughly enjoyed my time in the game and would recommend to anyone who wants to have a gripping short story experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Cool game, first game in a while that I've actually gone through and beaten. Voice acting is the highlight, incredible cast and performance, in the scope of video games where voice acting and performance is commonly mediocre at best I'd say its award worthy in this game. Story was gripping enough to keep me entertained and immersed and it didn't overstay its welcome, I feel like it ends right where it should. Graphically I had no issues, the game looked and ran great on a 7900GRE + Ryzen 5 7600 at 1440p High and the setting of a stormy oil rig only helps to make the visuals better. If you aren't immersed in the story then it could be harder to get hooked on the game for the gameplay, this game is very much story and characters first, atmosphere second, and gameplay third. Its not bad but it could easily get boring and repetitive if you don't care for the story. I do wish they did more with how the controls feed into the gameplay as looking back is neat but doesn't add much and leaning is honestly useless as its never really brought up as something you could do. Its a good story that doesn't overstay its welcome, but does leave more to be desired as a game. If you're lucky enough to be interested when this game is on sale then definitely pick it up, Its a good pickup for Halloween. Otherwise you should either reeeaalllly want to play it to be willing to pay full price or just watch a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: A really solid and engaging short horror game.The Chinese Room is known for their atmospheric story/atmospheric driven games and the story of SWTD isn't quite as complex/meaningful as meaningful as A Machine For Pigs, Dear Esther or TCR's other games, but it stays very engaging throughout the whole playthrough and feels much more polished and higher budget than previous titles.The price tag is unfortunately high for a game this short, but if you think this game is up your alley I would overwhelmingly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: It's aight.I don't have a strong reason to say don't buy this, but i wouldn't particularly recommend it either. This is supposedly narrative horror, but i'm utterly confused where the narrative part comes in because there is no such thing as a story. You encounter the horrors, you run from the horrors. That's as deep as this gets. The presentation is definitely great, but i feel like it's wasted on this because it never goes anywhere or accomplishes anything. I'm left feeling sort of meh. This is basically an overly polished, overly long  and doesn't hit as good. It's a good fit for VR and should imo be primarily sold as that.in short:+ great visuals+ great ambience+ good voice acting- non existent story- bland, barely existing character writing- the yellow plague (you'd be correct to assume bright markings blend in very well on an oil rig, but that's no excuse to go completely overboard with it. i am not a cow, if something is halfway horizontal i can understand it's possible to walk on that, not every piece of plywood needs to be drenched in paint)
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: What a banger of a game. When i first saw this game revealed i thought this was something perfect for my taste if it would be how i'd imagine and here we are, i just played through the game and what can i say, it is exactly how i imagined it to be.Quality is top notch, if it's Graphics design, Audio design or the excellent Path visualizations to keep you in the flow, everything just works well hand in hand to give a spectacular movie like experience.Also here is finally a game again that is very short compared to most games but the more amazing.It's really nice to see all the temporal upsamplers included if it's TSR, XESS, FSR etc. without them i would have played at 20-30fps and massive input lag but with XESS i got pretty much the same experience but with fps locked to 45fps flat on my 1080Ti and 3840x1080p monitor which made the game feel much smoother but noticing almost no visual degradation.The one thing i'd say wasn't all that nice was the amount of quick time events, they are generally very intuitive so they feel very natural which lead me to lock in my buttons for new quick time events before they showed up due to the nature of the task, but the amount of equal quick time events is getting a little repetitive overall i feel.Overall, if you're a fan of horror games with monsters and maybe you liked John Carpenters "The Thing" then this is THE game for you!@TheChineseRoom @Developers @SecretMode awesome Game, you tried something new and you nailed it so thank you for that ! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: While on a technical level, the game is executed quite well, it is really just a glorified "hold W" simulator with a few QTEs and three or four annoying stealth sections. There is very little actual difficulty in the game - there's more challenge in getting all the failure achievements than not. There are also two areas of the game where you can easily get yourself confused on what to do. One is a forced-failed QTE that isn't explained at all, leaving you resetting from checkpoint endless times until you google it. The other is a "parkour" section where you must climb up (against the obvious path which is downward) to trigger an QTE event to then jump down, instead of just climbing down to begin with (which you can but then cannot proceed because you didn't trigger the unexplained QTE).The story itself is good enough, well except the what felt like a rushed ending, but there's no reason to play it yourself at the current price point - just watch it.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible voice acting, breakneck pacing and standout art direction. The Chinese Room has outdone themselves here and seemingly created their magnum opus.The game never feels like it drags and constantly keeps you engaged through minor gameplay interaction, excellently written/performed voice acting and some of the best visuals to come out of Unreal Engine 5 so far.The game is somewhat short so keep that in mind when putting down the 30-40 dollars or so to play this game, personally I found it to be absolutely worth it and can see myself giving it another playthrough in the future just to relive it.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not usually a fan of horror or psychological horror games, but I decided to give this one a try. From the moment I started playing, I was completely hooked, largely because of the captivating story—I just had to know how it would end. _childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with stunning visuals and solid gameplay and story!The game focuses on narration and visuals, while sometimes a bit stressful i found horror to play a smaller role.Similarly to SOMA but with a better execution, even though SOMA's concept was more intriguing. _childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10First of all, I have to call out that the voice acting was just so incredible. So believable. They nailed it in every way.The setting and story was on point and of good premise. Game play was very fun, with multiple different outcomes. The sounds were very detailed. The graphics were great, but that's Unreal Engine for you! I don't want to put spoilers in here, but if you're wondering if it was worth it, it is! I will admit it's short, but just so well made. _childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know where to begin, everything about this game has me stunned.I've never bothered writing a review on steam as i haven't come across a game that pushed me to take the time and post.But this is it.The story line, artwork, characters, soundtrack, soundfx, voice & acting, the SUSPENSE, I don't have a single issue or even a negative point with the game. Finished it in 10 hours, but those hours were well and truly enjoyed and on the edge of my seat.Worth the $45, worth supporting a team creating master pieces like this, it's a rarity these days.Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This was a well crafted video game with a strong framework. The horror element was good but didn't over stay it's welcome (Never explain your Lovecraftian horror, I say). The voice acting was on point and the story telling never gave me a reason to roll my eyes. During my play through I never ran into a glitch that took me away from the experience so kudos to the dev teams for that one (Name a game you can say that about now and days). This is not a challenging game and my playtime ended up around four and half hours which I appreciated as well. The worst I can say about this game is that I don't need a "Still Wakes the Deep 2" or anything of that nature but I do look forward to whatever project this studio comes up with next.

_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Voice acting and sound design is 10/10. Story and character design is interesting enough however there are issues. The trope of a phone ringing only for the person on the other end to be moments away from death becomes more and more laughable by the time it happens the 4th or 5th time. The biggest issues by far are graphics and gameplay. Firstly, UE5 is just plain poor in terms of performance vs end result graphics. The amount of processing power needed to run nanite isn't worth the payoff and if you're running anything less than a god tier spec PC you will have to seriously crank things down to get anything approaching a smooth frame rate. If the end result looked beautiful then it might make sense however once many of the key options such as resolution/internal scaling are turned down the game looks quite average. While a comparison to something like RDR2 might not seem fair since this has been developed by a much smaller studio, the fact remains that the performance to graphics ratio is way out of whack and detracts from the experience. I've no doubt that a lot of the  incredibly poor performance of UE5 is to blame for much of it but this is a poorly optimised game.Gameplay - oh dear. This is the real reason I'm struggling to continue on after taking my time for around 5hrs. The game is of course a linear experience with essentially no choice over how to proceed however this also extends to enemy encounters. Avoiding enemies is at best boring and at worst frustrating as you attempt to navigate hiding spot to hiding spot in the dark. There's no real depth to the gameplay or tactics to be employed. If you ever played SOMA you might draw parallels - though I'd argue there were more moments of 'freedom' or at least perceived freedom in that game. This is not Alien Isolation on an oil rig - as much as I wanted it to be. I'll try and finish it but I think it will go down as one of my more disappointing purchases of the year and I can't imaging it'll get replayed anytime soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I hate that you can only recommend a game or not, it's really a hard choice with this one. On one hand, at it's heart it's got a decent narrative, has well-detailed environments, is good at creating a feeling of tension, and is above all else superbly voice acted.On the other hand, that decent narrative is stretched really thin - at best, it would make a good single episode of television (probably not even a movie's worth.) It's about four hours, two of my six hours of playtime were a break/pause, and by the end I wanted the game to be over. The walking simulator/exploration became monotonous, and had about three hours of 'oh no the thing you need to do is over here, go here, do this, etc'. Some of the 'monster' designs were more laughable than horrific - think giant-head MODOK from the most recent ant man, with more tentacles and less butt cheeks. Lots of chromatic tentacles/viscera. I wish they had gone in a bit different direction with the monster element, it would make for some good cosmic horror but doesn't quite get there in this game. Some of the 'The Thing' comparisons are apt, at least in tone, but not quite. I would recommend it if it were shorter and cheaper, and wish there was a so/so option which I'd have chosen for this.It's an achievement to make a game at all, so kudos to the developers. Bravo again for the voice acting. Graphically, it was fine - environments were great, character models and lip sync/animations less so, but traversal overall (which is the bulk of the gameplay) was alright. I didn't hit any game breaking bugs, and there was no UE stutter/shader compiling nonsense - it worked. A lot of loading screens for such a small map that reuses areas so many times, but they were brief load times at least. For some reason I also only had High and Epic options for the graphics, and the motion blur was atrocious before some tweaks to the upscalers.The biggest complaint besides the length is the HOW DID THIS GAME RELEASE LIKE THIS bug relating to the subtitles. Yes the scottish accents are thick, but I wanted the subtitles off. Every time you move to a new area, every time you die, every time you even open the page with the subtitle options (even if you're just passing that page to get to the graphical options), the subtitles turn back on. I spent probably 20 minutes of my playthrough turning off the subtitles, which by the way, are not even directly capturing what the spoken dialogue is - they change some of the words for I'm guessing clarity? English with an Accent to English is not a translation that is necessary. Either way I assume (and hope) the subtitle issue will be patched out quickly.It's maybe worth watching an edited playthrough eventually for the story, but in the meantime if you want a similar game I'd go with the Dead Space remake or Calisto Protocol - similar vibes, but cheaper and better overall. (FWIW, I'm also kind of skeptical of some of the glowing reviews that popped up here immediately with early/free copies..)
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: A good cinematic horror game of about 4 hours. The gameplay isn't tedious, and it doesn’t have time to get boring since the game ends right on time. The plot, while not sophisticated, is quite good. The atmosphere in the game is a 10 out of 10. Dark, confined spaces where danger might lurk around every corner. Excellent sound design and voice acting. In terms of optimization, I played on ultra settings at 1080p with DLSS (DLAA), the game ran at a stable 60 fps, and I didn’t notice any drops.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I really gave it a chance, but this typical walking simulator just didn't click with me. The whole thing unfortunately is neither scary nor original and just features all the usual "puzzles" for this type of game, including alien-isolation-esque hide and seek sections. The graphics are good, but not exceptional.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, what an amazing ride these horror adventure was. The creepy atmosphere is bombastic and the speakers also contribute. Normally i'm not a fan of so-called QTE's, but in these title they are excellently integrated into the matching situations here. Unfortunately, there are no optional routes here to find, which would make the exploriation even more extensive. Well, of course a demolished oil rig isn't a theme park. Anyone who likes body horror, such as "The Thing", and who can live with less legroom, will be rewarded with a not very long, but very entertaining adventure ride that definitely has it's replay value. -------> ' Very important: be sure to take a look into the “accessibility” option of the game menu; there are many extremely useful settings here '. The only disturbing thing are these awful "flashing-effects" around your view field, which reminds of melting celluloid film material in old movies, especially in cut- oder deathscenes it hurts my eyes. _childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed the heck out of this. Fantastic visuals and amazing sound. Like some others have mentioned, this game reminded me of SOMA which is a favorite of mine. Loved the water effects as they really helped to create a feeling of isolation when your outside. Standing on the platform and staring out to sea was beautiful and terrifying at the same time. Amazing sound design as well. Money well spent. Thanks Devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic piece by The Chinese Room. Playing with a friend we were immersed, scared, and thoroughly disgusted (in a good way) by the horrors this game had. Loved the attention to detail in the music, acting, and most importantly environment. The rig is vast, yet claustrophobic and fairly functional and realistic in the design. Devs did their homework on oil rigs and as an engineer I appreciate that. Overall story holds up well, not a claim for the best but it had us engaged and actually caring about the cast and events.Looking forward to the next one!
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: A masterclass in premise, setting, story, characters, graphics, sound design and voice acting. It's high up there with SOMA among the best horror games I've played. Sadly, the same cannot be said about the game's design.I suppose the uninitiated will find the eldritch cosmic body horror plenty scary, particularly if it's executed to this level of polish, but that in and of itself might not cut it out for the most seasoned of us. Certainly not me. Ultimately, this game could have been so much scarier, but only ended up feeling a tech demo showing me how pretty Unreal Engine 5 is for the 40th time in an hour.  Also came with a neat little feature: every time I died the framerate would get chopped to bits and I'd be forced to QTD and launch the game again to fix it. No amount of fiddling with the video settings would get it under control.Really,  wanted to get scared by this game. Ended up only getting sad...

_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed this game from beginning to end (which was about 4.5 hours) Although the game was short I respected that the game wasn't filled with running backwards and back tracking and remembering where rooms are... the game is fairly linear and tells a very good slightly lovecraftian style (without being generic) horror story. After playing this game I had nightmares I was drowning. So thank you for that. Very good game, highly recommend! Thank you devs , I know horror is a tough genre to tackle and you did it beautifully - literally the game is beautiful and detailed, and the voice acting is *chefs kiss*.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is beautiful and the ending was really well-done, but the climbing mechanic felt just a tad clunky/buggy at times and the short playtime made me wish it was just a *tad* cheaper (even with the 10% off at the time of writing). That being said, I loved the Lovecraft-esque horror, the singular setpiece that slowly evolves as the game progresses, the voice acting really gets you invested in all the characters, and by God the ending brought me to tears! 8/10 for me
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. A stunning game. I find myself crying thinking over things, but this. Truly one of the greatest games i have ever played. The story is fantastic, the visuals is incredible and there are moments i'm physically on the edge of my seat, and yet, i would play it over and over. i have never been hit so hard by a game in my life. I don't regret buying it, the Scottish accent is truly amazing, the sound and music playing keeps you locked in. i found myself in my room pitch-black playing it. if you have to money, its worth every single penny, Thank you Devs, and voice actors. Truly a 10 out of 10. I'm going to go cry some more, and contonplate everything. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this. I usually chicken out with horror games and rather watch Let's Plays, until now. The characters are very lifelike and the phenomenal voice acting really makes them feel alive. Really the voice acting alone is worth playing this. The setting is very interesting and adds to the atmospheric horror. I got really emotional near the end, I did not expect it and to me it contributes to the lovecraftian feel of the game. My only problem was that occasionally the gripping mechanic didn't work right, but I eventually figured out how to not die in those situations. All in all it's a very enjoyable game and very well playable for a horror noob like me. Another thing worth mentioning is the great range of settings for comfort and accessibility, really this should be standard practice in all games by now. Well done, devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Immersive horror about a monster from the deep that wants to gobble up a whole oil rig. It's all just a cover-up story for the real horror - company that skims on materials, security and employee well-being, no wonder it all ends how it ends. _childDocuments_.review: A well executed immersive survival horror.It delivers everything, what the genre is strong at. The environments are absolutely beautiful and gameplay-wise, well designed. You'll be able to explore the area or always find maps of it before... the game puts you under stress. :)The sound design is top notch. The acting is very well done as well. The dialogues are very well written, although the drama didn't really hit the mark for me. Machine for Pigs was way more memorable for the drama and mood elements, than this one.It would spoil stuff if I went into specifics, but the level designers deserve a medal, for they recognize, that level layouts could spoil gameplay features and it shows, that they take that into account.The monsters are creepy as hell, visually very well done! The throwable item mechanic is bad. For one, I've hit extremely large hitboxes on props multiple times, which prevented me from throwing items far enough. The other terrible factor is that crawling, "shimmy-ing" in narrow spaces, climbing waist-high objects make you drop your held item. You can't open/close a door in this game while holding a mug in your hand. Also an immersive game means, HUD should be minimal. Overall, the game delivers well on this aspect (you can disable elements), but interaction icons are too big and aren't positioned on the edges, where they should be. Also, while holding an item, the game constantly shows two huge (smallest setting) icons saying "LMB throw", "RMB drop". This info should be a one-time tutorial, then leave them out from the HUD entirely.Underwater controls aren't good. Quick-Time Events underwater is done even worse. Those areas really dropped the fun factor of the game and it didn't manage to climb back enough by the ending.If you like the genre, I'm pretty sure you're going to love this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a psychological-horror interactive storytelling experience presented in a linear format. The voice acting, sound design, graphics, and scriptwriting are all excellently executed. While the game's length was shorter than anticipated, the quality of the experience remained consistently high. Drawing from Eldritch Horror and Lovecraftian themes, the unique setting on an oil rig enhances the visual and atmospheric appeal.Similar to the developer's previous title, Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs, I found the lack of player agency frustrating. Additionally, the inclusion of various quick time events (QTEs) as the primary challenge on normal difficulty detracted from the experience. Mechanics like hiding and distractions, which could have added strategic depth, felt underutilized, even on the hardest available difficulty for my first playthrough. As a result, unless you have a personal connection to oil rigs, Lovecraftian horror, or Scottish culture, I would recommend passing on this title.

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the game in 4.1 hours. Was it good? It was a 7/10 game for me laddie. There's plenty of missed opportunity to be great. It is only a decent, albeit short game. It's like 6 dollars per hour of content.Positives:- Amazing voice acting, loved the Scottish accent and the voice performance is great.- Visuals and environment looks pretty good, nice attention to details.- Curated and linear storytelling. Horror game should go back to this as there's plenty of potential through this method.- Setting at the oil rig at that time period is pretty nostalgic.- Gotta love my big man Roy.Neutral- Music is average, nothing amazing nor bad.- Story is serviceable for the plot. It is however quite cliche and very predictable from start to finish.Negatives- While linear storytelling is good, it has no branching paths for replayability. - Game is not scary nor thrilling at all. The approach used is similar to countless of other horror games. I feel like there is a missed potential here to reinvent the tired horror cliches and tropes.- Most non-essential NPCs are mostly forgettable, even though you are supposed to know them well. Would be nice to have a regular shift with everyone to establish rapport.- Gameplay is subpar; hiding mechanics is pointless as you can just throw stuff to distract monsters. Platforming is quite buggy. There's clipping and crashes when Caz dies. - All items only has single use (fire extinguisher to fight fire but cant be used against monsters). - Game has a terrible audio bug where you don't hear dialogues at all, ruining the experience for me.- Storytelling could also be better. The game tried hard to make us care or feel in important set pieces, especially in the ending but we weren't given time to be invested or bond with any of the characters in any meaningful way.- The COD-like flashing images are overly used in so many games. Why not replicate what is it like to lose one's mind with playable memories or hallucinating pathways in the oil rig. Yet another missed opportunity here. With that said, I put heavier weightage to atmosphere and overall feel of the game, which was decent. This is why this review is positive. However, your mileage may vary.TLDR: I recommend getting this when on sale just for the atmosphere. For all its faults, it has a unique setting and game deserved to be played IMO.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully sculpted game, top notch voice acting, and smooth as butter gameplay. Only once while swimming up through a hatch did I get stuck, glitched in the floor. A quick checkpoint reload put me back about 15 seconds. Checkpoints are very generous, so repeated deaths aren't bothersome.I always enjoy a game with regular characters; no special powers or unique skills/abilities. Caz is just your average guy with dogged determination in a horrible situation.The game is a puzzler at heart. It never felt overly challenging, especially the parkour. The only times my progress was impeded was due to me turning off the repeated prompts feature, so I didn't recognise the odd interaction that I'd done somewhere else prior. If I could do a first playthrough again, I'd also turn off the yellow paint directional markings for an added challenge.I think the only thing that let it down slightly was the avoidance system. Throwing objects to distract often felt like it wasn't working, or was just not even necessary. The achievement for throwing 50 unique throwables doesn't seem like one you'd ever get naturally. I doubt I picked up even half of that. I started by trying to carry items in case needed, but the crouching, standing, or squeezing through an obstacle automatically drops it, so I gave up quickly. As for hiding in lockers, other than the first time I was prompted to try it, I never had to use it. There was simply never anything near me to even require it.It's not a very long game, but it's pretty polished and an overall, very enjoyable ride. Recommended to use headphones for the ambience. Enjoy :-)
