_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a very good game. I really liked it! And I absolutely recommend it. However, it is not perfect. I think it has some big problems that stop this game from truly reaching its fullest potential.First, the good. Still Wakes the Deep absolutely nails its characters and setting and choking the player in its oil-slick world. Set on an oil rig in the North Sea, off the coast of Aberdeen (the scariest thing about this game), you play as Cameron "Caz" McLeary, a man running from his problems. Speaking as someone who has lived in Scotland their whole life, I have known a Caz. I've known people who I see represented in this game. Hell, one of them has my surname. If you live in Britain and are aware of its history, then there is a lot to unpack in the game's seventies setting.There's Trots, the proper seventies trade-unionist, working on the rig. A homage to a better time of worker's rights in the UK; the kind of man who voted Labour, back when the party actually had worker's interests at heart. Then there's Addair. He has a Britain First poster in his room, and the symbol of the National Front. He's a racist piece of ♥♥♥♥. There's Finlay, the only woman on the rig, and our closest friend it feels. The dynamic between Finlay and Caz is so strong and realistic, I felt right at home. Next is Brodie, a hard worker and dear friend who gives his all. And finally, there's Rennick; the self-interested, unforgiving boss of the rig.Once ♥♥♥♥ goes down, the beautifully haunting gore and viscera and... sinews of whatever you have awoken is able to really evoke a sense of terror and helplessness. Just as colossal and incomprehensible is the sheer size of the rig. Standing impossibly in the sea; a towering hunk of metal and concrete, burning gas in the sky. The game's environment artists have really focused on details, and pushed themselves. The game is simply beautiful. Lastly, I also appreciate the game's further representation of Scotland by actually have the game available in Scottish Gaelic (that's gah-lick, not gae-lick). Such an uncommon sight, but greatly appreciated (even if I can only say hello and introduce myself).Now, the problems. While the beat-by-beat plot is easy enough to follow, and leads to some tense scenes, the overarching narrative is confusing, and a lot is not explained. There's a theme of running away and of regret, featuring flashbacks of Caz and his wife arguing. But that's about as much attention as this plot gets; a few flashbacks. Then it comes back at the end. It just feels underdeveloped. I feel these themes could have taken the stage a bit more, and have actually been elaborated on further. This problem of underdevelopment goes a bit further.A character who I won't name dies, and it's a very emotional scene, with a moving performance from Caz's actor. But... it just falls a bit flat. The character who dies means a lot to Caz, and so the reaction is justified in that sense. But to the player, we have a few good moments with them, but that's it. We don't really see them again until their death. The game expects you to care for the death of a character you shared all of five minutes with.Furthermore, Rennick, the big bad, isn't all that big. He is set up in the game's coda as this big threat, and you really start to worry. But his death is so uneventful. You see him about three times in the whole game, and the rest of his presence is through dialogue. I was really expecting a scarier finale with him, but that simply didn't happen. And I guess that's due to the game's walking-sim nature.While I appreciate walking-sims, I can't help but feel the game could have been improved with some player defence. A better finale could have been done if, for example, we had an Alien: Isolation style flamethrower, or a deterrent of that nature. We could actually fend off Rennick while completing another task and ending him. I dunno.All in all, Still Wakes the Deep is a five to six hour experience, with immense levels of world-building and polish, for £26.99 as of writing. It has some issues, but overall, I would seriously recommend it. Especially given its price. In a world where games with gigantic budgets are asking for gigantic prices, Still Wakes the Deep is a prime example of bang-for-your-buck indie titles putting the triple A industry to shame. You will not regret buying and playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Big heads up, this game is solely focused on story and immersion, the go to term people would use would be "Walking Sim". There are some gameplay elements beyond just walking around but they are very surface level. HOWEVER, the story, atmosphere, sound design, and definitely the voice acting more than make up for the shallow gameplay. This is a game you turn the lights off and play alone with noting in the background or on the other monitor.I was expecting a longer game however, I was also expected a different kind of game and in hindsight after beating it, the game would feel a lot worse if it went on longer. If you beat the game in one session like I did, the game might drag on a wee bit at the end but thankfully not too much.On to the actual review, good story  , and phenomenal voice acting. From the start I was completely engaged and that continued until the very end. The game play leaves something to be desired however this being a story focused game and the length of the game, it is more than acceptable. The price might be a bit of a pain point for some people so I would say wait for a discount if you really want to play it but I must insist, this game is ABSOLUTELY worth playing. 7.5 / 10And one last thing to remember Caz, Jesus loves you, but everyone else thinks you're a ****
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: A story driven horror masterpiece that felt like anything but a boring corridor-walking simulator. Immersive in dialogues and acting, gorgeous in sound and image, I loved every second of it.It has this taste of cosmic, unknowable horror in a realistic setting without sacrificing its mystery to squid-like demigods' names and long dead american writers. It smelled like cinematographic, arctic horrors and submarine despair without being a soulless copy. The characters felt true, respected by the writers and the actors. Kudos for making me love the scottish accent. It's short by today's standards and expectations, even though I felt a hint of replayability. However, I'd take that sort of games for double the price anytime, considering its quality and the emotions it left me with. It's fluid, challenging enough, simple but varied without repetition, well paced, well written, well acted, well crafted.A shame that sort of solo experience is so rare nowadays. Thanks for this journey.A future classic and already up there in my "all times best" lists.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: This product is more like an interactive movie than a game. I think it is a VERY GOOD interactive movie, but I would struggle to call it a game.1. Story - Very good. Writing was interesting and the characters were believable and well acted. 2. Level Design - Impressive. The rig feels very true to life, and the fact that you repeat sections but they play very differently is a testament to great planning.3. Monster design - Wonderful. I love John Carpenter and H.R. Gieger, and I see similarities here that I personally enjoy very much.TThe team is clearly talented and I want to see more like this! So why a negative review?It's really short. I took my time looking around, often times I would stop and just observe monsters or areas and take in the detail, and I still clocked under 4 hours. The game appears to have no replayability value either. You could get the same experience watching someone stream it without commentary. $35 USD is a steep price for what is essentially a long movie (however good that movie may be).I do not regret my purchase for full price, but my love for this type of writing and monster design heavily skews my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Still wakes the deep is a incredibly authentic SCOTTISH horror experience (i am personally Scottish so i find this very entertaining) BELOW THIS POINT THERE MAY BE SPOILERS I HAVE BLACKED OUT EVERYTHING I CONSIDER A SPOILER BUT I MENTION THE PACING AND LENGTH OF THE GAME + TALK ABOUT HOW THE STORY IS PORTRAYED (NO SPOILERS REALLY AS I DON'T TALK ABOUT ANYTHING THAT HAPPENS)The actual horror itself is inspired by a few things the main noticeable ones being   The games story is Phenomenal in my opinion While also being very LAYED OUT / on the nose, what you see is what you get if get what i'm saying which is not a bad thing in my opinion as it is done very well. Another big positive i would like to mention is EVERY Character feels like there is a story to them but not in a forced way, it feels like they are people doing their job just like you which i think is very neat (plus the funny Scottish banter is amusing).One thing i will say while not necessarily a negative, is that it is VERY linear like there are next to know other paths you can go the closest thing you get to breaking away from the set path is looking around for some lore or other random things (it doesn't feel this way though) at least not until later in the game. Now this COULD be seen as a bad thing BUT personally i think it is a good thing for the game as first and foremost the game is a story to be told, AND ITS A DAMN GOOD STORY although because of this linear structure i feel they decided to not make the game that long (i completed it in around 6 hours this is with me doing most of the optional things) and i feel this is because they feared the game play would get boring since it is kinda just sneaking about NOW personally i think they could have taken it a bit farther. ALTHOUGH i understand why they didn't and i still really enjoyed my time and the ending. but i do kinda wish there was more and  anyways the reason i mention this is for 2 main reasons1. it's kinda short for how expensive it is2. it is lacking in replayablity because of how linear it isHaving said that I really like this game even though i normally prefer more free less linear games and don't regret spending money on it IN FACT i would do it again honestly I may even replay it just because of how good it is even if there won't be a lot variance from my first run that is how strong the game is as a experience in my opinion.a few things i wanna rate---------------------------voice acting = 10/10writing/story = 9/10visuals/setting = 10/10music = 10/10 characters = 9/10 (there are some reaLLY good ones but i feel like one was slightly half baked / needed more screen time other wise i feel it was 10/10)horror = 8/10 (some parts are TRULY horrifying and the cosmic horror that is there is on point both beautiful, horrifying and beyond my comprehension lmao but as i mentioned earlier it was slightly untapped in my opinion + in the last few parts of the game a lot of the tension towards the main threat had felt less scary having said all of that if you like cosmic horror or interesting settings/characters or even body horror (and silly Scottish banter) i would recommend playing this game at least once it is worth the money BUT if you are not willing to spend that much it is understandable.

_childDocuments_.review: The best horror game I have played in a long time. Just the setting alone already is unique and an amazing choice for a horror game. Graphics are really good and performance was great. _childDocuments_.review: Worst horror game 2024.Story rich is fine, but when it's all there is to a game, it should be good. It doesn't deliver here. It's another awful retelling of psychological horror great SH2. Protagonist with inexplicable dark past he either won't admit/remember as the world around him changes to the whims of a spiritual power punishing people for their sins and general humanity for it's hubris. It's been done before, and infinitely better. The great mystery of SH2's story was how it told its story through subtly, this game throws it at your face without any nuance or grace. Then this all brought down to even more understandable and relatable terms to just any judeo-christian deity so it's just another angry god story, instead of a character finally coming to terms with his past and what brought him to such a decision, it's just an guy being punished for him being an actual terrible person.Game play could be nonexistent and I'd probably have more enjoyment from just a visual novella. Interact with X place at Y oh no, don't get seen by Z. But making collision and the game eating inputs any task now becomes a chore.The voice acting is fine, it's just a real tragedy they had to act out this horrendous story, apologies to the voice actors.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually review games, but I just wanted to share my opinion on this one because of how much of fan I am of walking sim games normally. This game has a familiar feel to other walking sim games like "Firewatch," but with a horror spin on it and you're of course on an oil rig. In the past, I have absolutely loved games like that, but for some reason this one just did not hit the same. I found myself getting bored with it and stopping regularly, and that is extremely rare with these types of games for me. The horror element wasn't really there for me either. In the beginning it for sure was, but as you progress you realize all spooky encounters are almost the exact same mechanics and the enemies themselves don't change much at all other than the names. However, I can't exactly say the story was bad, but it didn't have me personally hooked. The characters were well written and the voice acting was great, but for a short game it somehow felt drawn out with how many random inconvenient things happen to you like falling through a floor right before reaching a door you needed to go to or your character always being the one that is told to go do some other task that will inevitably fail anyway. Idk, I hate that I didn't enjoy it, cause it looks great, sounds great, has a few cool moments, and people really do seem to like it. In my opinion though, if you want a good walking sim game with a good story, go play "Firewatch" or "What Remains of Edith Finch" sense this one doesn't have much horror anyway. THOSE are bangers, and generally they are cheaper. (Or at least wait til it is on sale.)

_childDocuments_.review: I know this will be an unpopular opinion based on what I have seen already on reviews, but after finishing this game, I honestly felt like I wasted money (at least at the price it's at). I was excited for this and wanted to enjoy it, but overall it just fell flat in a lot of ways for me. I will say the voice acting was great and the music pretty good. Aside from that, it started to just feel like a slog to get through, which I feel should say something given how short of a game it is. After the first encounter or two, the suspense and tension didn't hold up and I felt like I was running through the same scenario over and over. The chase scenes felt very lackluster and linear. I keep seeing people say how phenomenal the story was and how it even made some tear up and it's the best story they've ever played... really?? To each their own, but I just didn't get that feeling at all. I didn't feel much of an emotional connection to many of the characters, I think part of that has to do with the length of the game itself and not having enough time to reach that point with them. The story wasn't bad, the concept of it really intrigued me at first... but in my opinion it definitely wasn't great, let alone the best story I've ever played through.I guess what a lot of it boils down to for me is the price vs. the content you're getting. I definitely do not think this is worth it at full price, maybe if it were at least half off a lot of the complaints I have wouldn't have been as pressing. I have really enjoyed other products from these guys, this one just didn't hit the mark for me. I'm glad others were able to get more enjoyment out of this one, it just wasn't for me. I'm curious to know how many other people share the same take as me, I knew this would be a bit controversial as of now since the majority so far seemed to really enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is one of those rare horror games that is 1. Well written 2. Pretty scary in parts and 3. Emotionally resonate. The wheel isn't being reinvented here by any means and in fact the tasks you're completing can get a bit repetitive (probably the games biggest flaw). What you get though is a compelling story that plays out something like The Thing but on an oil rig and everyone's Scottish. There's so much cultural flavor in this game from the Scottish angle of it all that it does add a sort of quirky charm to the whole experience. But that charm is cut HEAVILY by just how bleak and horrific the game is. I think it's well worth 30 bucks and 6 hours of your time.

_childDocuments_.review: A walking simulator but imo the way they SHOULD be made. SWTD drips with tension throughout almost the entire experience and has top notch presentation when it comes to delivering its scares.The body horror elements are particularly gnarly here. They could have settled for fleshwalls and the occasional limb sticking out at you but you see faces, bits and other parts of human anatomy blended up and sometimes reassembled into grotesque murals of undeath. Which i use that term because i don't think alot of the corpses you see are truly dead and the way the monsters gibber on with occasional bouts of worrying clarity unnerves me almost as much as the horror of being a Irishman in the 70s.Mechanically SWTD feels a tad clunky. I wouldn't use terms like smooth or comfortable to depict how your character controls but it works fine enough, platforming feels a bit stilted whenever you need to jump but it hasn't caused any problems and the regularity of autosaves prevents any loss of progress from a mis judged jump or platform, knowing where to go isn't a issue due to the variety of pathfinding tools you're given (which are optional and can be turned off so haters of the dreaded yellow paint can rejoice)For the most part the game runs well. My hardware is showing its age again but frames for me are usually consistent so i don't think its a optimization issue but i'm also no tech guru.For the price of admission you're getting a quality experience and the game even lets you skip dialogues and has many interactions early on being optional if this isn't your first go around, many things devs seem to overlook.

_childDocuments_.review: This game nails atmosphere and visuals in a way that other horror titles could only dream of. The gameplay can be a little repetitive and the story is missing a certain level of depth, but the voice acting and realistic characterization/writing more than make up for it. It genuinely just feels like you're a helpless oil rig worker trying to survive incomprehensible eldritch horrors. 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the entire game and I have some opinions At first I was skeptical because I'm familiar with the Devs past work with Frictional Games and I couldn't shake the feeling of another Machine for Pigs as I wasn't a fan of that specific game. Despite it starting a bit slow you get an attachment to some of the characters and the emotions get tense as you play. Not too many jump scares most of them are environmental, The scenery is absolutely gorgeous, The anxiety you receive diving into water hoping nothing is down there waiting for you is incredible. While I'm not usually a fan of stealth in horror games this game did it well because lets be honest here you are on an oil rig with no weapons in the middle of the ocean dealing with eldritch abominations of course you're gonna avoid them as best as you can. Incredible story, Incredible setting, Incredible game 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely fantastic display of why using amazing voice talent can elevate your story.I'll just say up front that while I won't spoil anything specific, I will spoil at least the basic premise, so avoid if you don't know anything about this game.  OK, here goes.So, we have seen this sort of premise before.  In fact, I'd call this game "The Thing on an Oil Rig" and I'd mean it in a 100% positive way.  That's because it takes what The Thing does on a surface level, and does it very well on its own accord.  This isn't some cheap knockoff.  What's missing from "The Thing's" paranoia and themes of trust, the unknown of who a person really is and such is replaced by SWTD's murky shadows, constant groaning metal, and overall excellent atmosphere.  And it all works.And truly, what makes this game better than just your typical "Oh look, some unknown eldritch force is infecting your friends" story is the fact that through the acting, I found myself caring deeply for Caz and his crewmates (and deeply despising Rennick.)  Excellent writing, performed fantastically by great voice actors.Indie games - spend your budget on getting good actors - I'd rather your textures don't look perfect, than have an AI spewing out your dialogue with no humanity.In terms of visuals, the environments looked great, were claustrophobic, and lead to the feeling that I could slip to my doom, or have something jump me at any moment.  I found things like ropes and flags flapping in the wind to be oddly uncanny, but I'd imagine that that's a pretty hard thing to get right, so I got over it.  Things got a bit repetitive with the game loop after a couple hours, but as I said, the care I had for the protagonist saved it.I will say that I had to wait for their first patch to get rid of that subtitle reset bug (subtitles in a game completely ruin it for me - it's one of my "things") which took a while to implement, but from what I can tell, they are a small group, so I was fine just waiting it out till the patch came.Finally, top marks for the very subtle little things done to my character's locomotion to really make me feel like I was on a keeling vessel.  I actually had to force myself to pay attention to what the game was doing (stopping me from moving in certain directions as gravity throws me the other way, jerking me left or right, slowing me down as platforms tilted, etc.) because it was quite seamless, and just felt so natural that at first I thought nothing of it.  It's not flashy about it, it just completely works to immerse you.Well done on this, and I look forward to your next project!
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the game. Took me a bit over 6 hours to finish it and I think it's the right length for this game. The pacing is great except in the middle where you have to keep fixing the generator and you start to ask yourself "What's even the point of this?" but it all comes nicely together at the end when they directly address it in the story. And the story itself was fine but the thing I liked about it, it did the cosmic horror right. And the whole game felt like playing through a movie because it was so focused and the acting was good.It's basically The Thing on an oil ring (even the protagonist's name McLeary is similar to Kurt Russel's MacReady) minus the paranoia. Instead of an alien posing as human, there's some kind of growing presence infesting the ship and changing the crew members. The flesh growing between the walls of the rig reminded me of biomass in System Shock 2.The graphics are top level, the environments are full of detail and the monster animation is great. Like I already mentioned, the acting is very good for a video game. The dialogue and the banter between workers felt real and they speak Scottish with so much slang that you'll have to rely on English subtitles for translation lol. You'll interact with a handful of characters throughout the story but I only cared for one of them- your best mate Roy. Expected he would turn into a monster at the end and fighting him would be heartbreaking but that never happened. Perhaps a missed opportunity. You see your wife in the flashbacks but she always acts like a total ♥♥♥♥♥ so I didn't get why he wanted to go back to her so bad, I thought the monsters were a pleasant company in comparison. Such a weird decision to put happy memories where she was actually somewhat charming only at the very end of the game.The sound design is fantastic. They built a miniature oil rig to capture the sounds of the environment. The cries and the screams of the monsters are creepy as hell and getting chased by them was nerve wracking at times. But after sneaking around them for a while and playing hide and seek, the scare factor began fading away.The game is extremely linear and there's no room for exploration. Pretty much every door that you don't need to go through right this very moment will be locked. I thought the use of the color yellow to guide you worked perfectly in this case as that's a color heavily used on the real oil rigs in similar fashion so it's actually subtle but then they kept adding yellow paint and yellow towels hanging out of the hiding spots and it became annoying and immersion breaking instead. There's a constant feeling that the devs are holding your hand throughout the game, even solving puzzles for you. You see a typical looking puzzle in this genre and it seems like you're gonna have to figure it out but it is just window dressing. The solution to the problem is always right in front of you, and all you have to do is press interact and the character will solve it for you. . It would be much more satisfying if we'd have to engage our brains a little. A couple of simple Frictional style puzzles would do wonders for this game. As it is, it seems like the devs have no faith in the players. Everything you do in the game is sort of realistic so despite of all the supernatural stuff, I only had to suspend my disbelief during some of the platforming sections. There were a couple of jumps that I don't think even the best parkour athletes could make - you'd break your arms catching yourself while dropping from such heights. And this guy starts breathing heavy if you run for just 4 seconds but at the same time he has incredible agility, upper body strength and endurance to climb for hours.There were a couple of scenes where the sights of eldritch horrors actually looked very beautiful and awe inspiring (accompanied with music, which I only really noticed during those scenes). These were some of my favorite moments.For me it's  despite how damn linear it is. If you're into cosmic horror, you will love this game. setting and the atmosphere cosmic horror done right realistic visuals and fantastic sound design great acting and believable characters good pacing too linear, almost on rails doesn't require any thinking  In the latest patch they added a toggle for reducing the yellow markers.

_childDocuments_.review: It's okay.Walking sim with stealth elements and a very crappy water section. Interesting story that often feels directionless with how many characters are introduced that immediately die a half hour later. Similarly, your character gets close to escape but is pushed back in with multiple macguffins. Gets tedious and old very quick. Thank god this was a fairly short game.However, the setting is wonderfully unique and isolating; perfect for what this game is going for. Environments are very pretty and interesting to look at and traverse. Listening to the characters talk is very entertaining and is made better with the subtitles on.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a percentage to assign for reviews...oh wait, there is: 49/51 for/against.It isn't a bad game, but it will probably only appeal to fans of the genre. Vaguely reminiscent of the absolute masterpiece that is SOMA, and enough originality to not be a ripoff in any way of that title.But, I found many of the gameplay sequences to be clunky and frustrating. Yellow paint guides your way through mostly intuitive, but sometimes not, obstacles. There is an option to turn this off, which is a nice touch from the developers, but I found it necessary to figure out where to go. Also, thank you to the devs for story mode. This enhanced my enjoyment greatly. This was due in part to having to strain my eyes to see the surroundings. Dodging and distracting your foes would be an exercise in sheer tedium, for me, without story mode.One level has you swimming in slow motion as you flail around with your headlamp (in North Sea water? Yeah, near instant hypothermia aside...) trying to figure out where to go unsuccessfully. I died there more than anywhere else. Perhaps my screen settings weren't quite right, but this sequence was more frustrating than scary by far. (01/99 frustrating/scary; I truly hated this particular sequence which I won't reveal in case of spoilers.)The protagonist's dialogue consists of the lines "Oh F*ck," "Christ," "Oh Jesus," or some minor variation thereof throughout. I'm no prude, but isn't there a little more variety to Scottish profanity?Overall, if you like these horror walking sims, which I do, you will probably enjoy the game and grab it on sale. If you aren't already a fan, I don't think this one is going to win you over.

_childDocuments_.review: The British/Scottish English accent is really hard to understand and subtitles are no fun because you miss a lot if you just have to read all the time.They should have used normal english here.Voice acting is good, but the mumble accent just sucks.The graphics are "good", nothing earth-shattering and in some places rather cheap but overall the setting is good and interesting.The gameplay gets boring after a short time because everything repeats itself.Press button XY, pull lever XY etc.A linear design with backtracking, no real puzzles, nothing exciting to read, it gets boring in the long run.The indicator is sometimes not visible or difficult to recognize.The monsters aren't really smart either, the AI ​​behaves stupidly and always the same, everywhere.Also, and that's a important point for me, I don't support DEI and political agenda. (You know what I mean.)So I returned it.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought it this morning, and finished it within around 4hrs.It seemed like an interesting concept (to a certain extent), but turned out to be completely linear, and didn't really seem to have a point (apart from "suspense on an oil rig").There wasn't really a strong enough story, character development or interaction is non-existent, and a distinct lack of any real challenges to make it exciting.A fairly middle-of-the-road walking sim, with a few dull QTEs thrown in here and there.There aren't many games or movies I've experienced where I feel robbed of both money and a few hours of life, but this unfortunately managed to make the list.10% off the full price - it was still far too expensive.4hrs of lack-luster entertainment concluded with an anti-climax (the title of Santiago's sex tape).I wouldn't recommend, unfortunately, as I think most gamers will likely be ultimately disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep. I'm truly on the fence about it. (My sister recommended it to me.) This game has some seriously great visuals, sound and VA's but in my personal opinion, that's it. After beating it the first time I gotta say, the story is both really good but also really disappointing, Maybe I somehow missed some of it or just didn't get it, for me I felt like it wasn't all there and while I did like the characters, getting attached to them, the feelings just weren't there. (in terms of the story/plot, it might be a case of, something like (trying to explain the unexplainable?)) Main plot point occurs then you just go from point A to point B, not too much story telling, it just happens and things occur then it just kinda ends. at least that's how I felt about it.  As for the game it's basically all on the rails so it doesn't feel like there's much to explore outside of the predetermined path, the playable characters movement felt so incredibly slow at times and the flashlight seemed a little underwhelming even with adjusting the brightness it still seemed pretty dark and some of the controls (about an hour and a half on M&K, rest was on an Xbox controller) felt clunky or abnormal.These are just my thoughts, still plan on 100% completing it. if you think it looks good, you should try it out. I bought it on-sale, but was left feeling pretty disappointed.(edit after 2nd play through)while watching videos and going through the game, while I'm still not too much of a fan of the story. it's significantly better with more knowledge/understanding of some aspects

_childDocuments_.review: In a world of horror walking-sims that feel almost identical to one another (mascot horrors, P.T. clones, bloober jumpscare fests) this seriously stands out as something truly original, albeit drawing clear inspiration from franchises such as It is a walking-sim through and through, I wouldn't recommend this if you are not a fan of the genre, but for what it aims to achieve it does so extremely well. Graphics, sound design, story and pacing are top notch, if not some of the best I've seen in the genre. The experience took me a total of roughly  to complete, it did not feel too short nor did it feel like it overstayed its welcome.It's going to be hard to find another game that tops this as my personal GOTY. _childDocuments_.review: Good game, not great. The setting and atmosphere is really fun and unique. The gameplay is pretty simple - very basic puzzles and a lot pressing buttons when prompted, and very much on rails. This is a level or two above a walking simulator, but it was fun enough to play through. I'd get it on a sale though, price is a bit steep for what it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Tried this hoping for a big-budget atmospheric horror game. I saw the game is 4-6 hours so after 2 hours of disappointment I refunded it.Problems:- Walking simulator gameplay that repeatedly puts trivial obstacles in front of you that universally amount to "take the branch and interact with the thing". There are many forms of this but none are interesting, just feels like they had to pad out the gameplay, which is shocking given there's only 4-6 hours here.- Horror is all pretty generic biohorror in the style of Dead Space or Amnesia, presented to you with no context aside from "it's from the ocean". It just wasn't interesting to me.- Enemies use the most basic AI and forget you were ever there the moment you enter a hiding spot. - Graphics are fine but don't seem to justify the low performance compared to other games. - What I saw of the plot was uninspired and predictable - greedy foreman screws over crew, everyone tries to escape repeatedly but dies, that's it basically. No intrigue was built at all in the first 2 hours.Most positive things I can say about it are great voice acting and environment design.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Giving it a thumbs up due to Steam's silly binary vote system but this one is a definitive "meh" vote from me, in actuality.It's a fine game for what it is, but ultimately I was somewhat disappointed. I'm familiar with the genre but this one just didn't grip me in the same way that others such as Firewatch did. The story was impactful and it most certainly takes center stage here, but I didn't feel that invested in any of the characters. I had hoped that the gameplay would pick up some of the slack but alas, it was devoid of any mechanical variety. Using a screwdriver and pulling levers is as complex as it gets.The game was buggy but it was nothing too unforgivable considering this was an indie game that just launched. My only major complaint was the subtitle bug in which the subtitles reset to the "On" setting every time you re-enter the Audio settings menu, enter a new area, or reload a save. I am easily distracted by subtitles so this really broke my immersion in a game whose sole purpose is to immerse the player.I'm not here to dump too much on an indie game, but this one didn't scratch much of an itch for me, personally. On the plus side, the setting is brilliant as is the Scottish culture and atmosphere. If you suffer from thalassaphobia or megalophobia, you're in for a hell of a time!
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game! The story is very well written, the voice acting (especially the lead) is superb, and the musical score is (as always with their games) mesmerizing. There were a few moments in the middle of the game where some of the game mechanics became a little repetitive but there was always a new story progression around the corner which kept me motivated to keep moving forward. The Chinese Room have perfected the art of creating beautiful worlds and telling well-crafted narratives and, for me, their games are obviously crafted with love and passion. Buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: Best narrative horror game I've ever played! Graphics, story, sound design, atmosphere, are all top notch! The pacing goes perfectly, and the plot is simultaneously horrifying and in parts beautiful and tragic. The writing is extremely good, dialogue felt so natural it was noteworthy, which I have rarely seen. Highly recommend picking this up.

_childDocuments_.review: Not worth the 35 dollar price tag. Don't get me wrong, game looks visually great and has a good story, but the game play itself boils down to click, press w/a/s/d. Completed my playthrough in about 5 hours, and about an hour of it was two sections where the QuickTime event changed from the standard click and hold into a sudden rapid clicking. I would click repeatedly and half the time it wouldn't recognize I was, or would just drop and not let me interact all. Leading to death, reload, and then the same cutscene/dialogue for the 7th time.  All in all, 6/10 for me, if this was cheaper in the 15-20 dollar range I wouldn't have any complaints but 35 is way too much right now. Wait for a sale before you buy.

Believe me, if you work in a stressful job, in austere environments or in any similar position away from your family, the ending is a travesty. Kinda fun while it lasts, but the ending, absolutely kills it for me. Keep my money and next time write a game with an ending that shows proper respect.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Now, I would preface this by saying this sort of experience is not for everyone. It is very linear and railroaded, you don't get much choice in the matter whether story or gameplay wise. It made me laugh a few times on just how much yellow paint was splattered around which serves as a guide for the player to go there specifically. You do not also fight any of the monsters as this is a mainly stealth focused game!However personally? I enjoyed this quite a bit. I ended playing the whole thing in one sitting because I absolutely love stories about cosmic horrors going into places they really shouldn't be. The gameplay itself is incredibly simple in my opinion and most of it focuses on the player enjoying the experience and atmosphere more than anything. The characters I wish we had more time with before they were inevitably infected, but I loved every single voice actor. I still felt awful for them when they'd die! Or worse. So I would say if you love stories about cosmic horrors and also being stuck on something as scary as an oil rig, give this game a shot when you'd like! If anything the characters and story helped it stand out for me and it was a wild ride from start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm posting this review as a do not recommend because I personally did not enjoy it very much. That said, it's not a *bad* game by any means. You might decide after reading this review that none of my criticisms touch on what you value in games; in that case, you should absolutely buy Still Wakes the Deep, and expect to enjoy it a fair bit. If you find yourself shying away after reading any of the following points, however, then consider picking it up only at a hefty discount, if at all.- The storySo, the main draw of walking sim games, and one of the qualities which has earned this game most of the praise offered by its fans. I thought it was OK. There are some contrivances, and by the end little change is made to the status quo compared to early on in the game. But as a character drama, it works well enough. The protagonists are relatable, though many characters are not present for long enough to get truly attached to them. The area I really owe the game props for, however, is the dialogue. The banter between the characters is excellent - there were two moments in the second half of the game that genuinely made me laugh out loud - and the dialogue in more serious moments can be quite moving. No shockers there, from the company that wrote the Mandus monologue in Machine for Pigs.- The visualsWhile much of the game looks quite passable for a modern title, there are numerous issues that break immersion, in addition to just looking plain ugly. Many of the dynamic objects in the world essentially move at a reduced framerate compared to the rest of the game. My machine was not particularly taxed running the game on maximum settings, so I'm not sure why I had to watch dangling cables move at 12 FPS when the rest of the game looked fine and ran at 60+ FPS. I'm uncertain whether this was an issue with the physics engine, as some other physics objects displayed very jerky movement, such as the diving bell immediately after the event early in the game, which was awkward-looking but still at the same FPS as everything else. Somewhat less glaringly, the monster models, They clip through walls and into hiding spaces quite frequently. Other than that, I think they look a bit goofy, particularly the one that's just a giant head. Especially since that guy *just* got eaten when you see him in monster form. How'd his head even get that big so quickly? Come on. Last thing I wanna mention here is a constant lighting issue with the flashlight. Well, two lighting issues with the flashlight. One is that the point of origin for its light source in the game world frequently is occluded by map geometry when you're crouching in an area with low ceilings. I'm talking like, half the time you spend crawling through ducts, your light is in the ceiling and not illuminating your surroundings at all. The other issue is that it doesn't seem to adjust correctly sometimes when going underwater, making it even harder to see in the murky depths, in a way that is more frustrating than challenging or scary.- The audioThe atmospheric sounds are OK. The music is OK, and also quite sparse, which is fine since it probably would have just distracted most of the time, especially with it not being particularly good. Other than stingers, you'll largely only hear music in a scene where something sad is happening. The voice acting is good, which pairs well with the exemplary dialogue I've already mentioned. Are the accents and vocabularies true to life? I have no idea, I've not spent much time around foul-mouthed Scots. It sounds good, though.- The gameplayAnd here we come to the biggest weak point of this game. And I say this as an ardent Machine for Pigs defender-- nay, a Machine for Pigs *offender*, who is quite happy to call anyone who dislikes that game an uncultured nerd. This game just... isn't a very good *game*. About 70% of the playtime (not counting cutscenes) is spent doing uninspired, repetitive parkour. Climb the ladder, leap across the gap, hold the button to make sure you don't fall! Uh-oh, here's a monster, you'd better hide from it and then walk to the next hiding spot when it passes you in its circular patrol route. (That's the other 30% btw). And the monsters truly are that dumb. They just walk in circles most of the time, patrolling around one room until you advance and make a convenient loud noise so they can chase you to end the segment / follow you to the next area you need to do things in. And they can't even do that right, because literally *every one* of the major monsters in the game got *stuck* on my first playthrough, refusing to move for thrown objects or even to come and eat me where I was standing, 5 feet away. That was fine in two cases, because it let me not have to interact with some of the worse areas of this game as much as I otherwise would have had to, but in one case the monster took out a mortgage on the one path I had to take to advance, and so I had to walk into it to reset to the last checkpoint so that I could move on. And if you thought this mind-numbing monotony would be broken up by the occasional puzzle, I've got bad news for you. There were maybe two things in the entire game that could by any stretch be labeled a 'puzzle', and that's with me leaving room in case I forgot a second one. The one I can recall was literally activating 5 things in the right order, with them all shutting off when you activate the wrong one. Yeah.- SummaryIn short: I had hoped, with this being the first game I've played from The Chinese Room since Machine for Pigs, that they might have developed more talent for creating an engaging gameplay experience, while retaining the same quality of storytelling. Unfortunately, the gameplay in Still Wakes the Deep is markedly worse (Machine at least had some puzzles!), and the story is, in my opinion, not as good as that of AMfP either.P.S. Why were some people saying this game has similarities to The Thing (the main reason I bought it)? In only the most superficial of ways, sure. The monster assimilates people, and the story takes place in a setting where the characters and threat are isolated from society at large. But literally the main thing about The Thing is that it perfectly replicates the behavior of assimilated victims, making it difficult to identify and a genuine world-ending threat if it gets back to civilization. Spoilers, but no one in this game is subtly assimilated-- it is extremely obvious in all cases that they have been taken over. The only way you could think otherwise is by making some heavy assumptions about the unexplained crash in the game. For that reason, it's entirely unreasonable to think that the threat in this game could end the world. The army could just kill it with flamethrowers and bombing runs. It's just big fleshy bits, it's nothing special.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is very emotional, I have to say, it wasn't easy playing this game. It was, however, a wonderful experience. Still Wakes the Deep has an amazing and terrifying atmosphere, beautiful graphics and an incredible sound design. But the one thing that makes it truly great is this. Even though the scenario and ultimately the "enemy" of this game are vastly abstract, its deliverance feels very real. I think that is because the people in this game feel like actual people.From the detailed imperfections of every room and relatable reactions and problem solutions of characters, all the way to the absolutely brilliant voice acting and the well written dialogue. Everything makes it seem like this could actually be a real place with real humans. One thing I have to admit is that some specific key combinations can feel a little counterintuitive, and some control choices I don't really understand. Moreover, the enemies you face (while truly unsettling) can be pretty predictable. In any case, path finding and fundamental movement is very simple. And even if confused at times, none of this stopped me from having a great time enjoying the ride. I personally felt like playing a movie. Still Wakes the Deep is linear and not that long (for a game) but it is full of inspirational thoughts and designs, of stories and emotions. So, being the philosophical art loving moron I am, I must recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: :- Atmosphere. The game creates a unique atmosphere that keeps the player in suspense throughout the gameplay. Gloomy locations, dark corridors and unexpected plot twists make the player be on guard.- Gameplay. The gameplay is a mix of horror and adventure. The player must explore underwater locations, solve puzzles and fight monsters. This makes the game interesting and diverse.- Plot. The plot of the game is intriguing and makes the player want to know more. He tells about a group of researchers who go in search of an ancient artifact, but encounter something much more dangerous.- Graphics and sound. The graphics in the game are made at a high level, and the soundtrack creates an atmosphere of horror and tension. The sounds of water, rustles and screams of monsters add realism to the game.:- Complexity. The game can be challenging for some players, especially at high difficulty levels. Some puzzles and battles with monsters require certain skills and abilities from the player.- Duration. The game may seem short to some players. It is designed for 5-6 hours of playing time, which may not be enough for some players.- Repeatability. Some elements of the game, such as puzzles and monster battles, may be repetitive, which may reduce the player's interest in the game.In general, Still Wakes the Deep is an interesting and exciting game that will appeal to fans of horror and adventure. It offers a unique gaming experience that will be remembered for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, rather disappointing. As many others have pointed out, the design and story aren't great. The ending was just embarrassing. Many have commended the writing, but I can't share the sentiment. Perhaps above par for game writing - but that's not the same as 'good' writing. The slick coating of strong language and Scottish slang just didn't cut it for me. The voice acting was great, for the most part. Similarly, the visuals and setting are decent. But it feels like a lazy attempt to remake 'The Thing' on an oil rig - while somehow missing everything that made the film so great. _childDocuments_.review: ➕ It's The Chinese Room - so the VA direction is stellar as always!➕ The visuals and overall look of the game looks great, definitely a glow up for the developer!🟣 Short length, around 4 hours.🟣 Does feature enemy encounters, even though there aren't that many of them and they aren't that complex.🟣 The writing does work at some level but keep your expectations low,.🟣 As of patch 1.2 it's relatively stable experience without many bugs present.➖ Overall rhythm and feeling of engagement, especially from the story perspective, slows down to a hault half through the game compared to pretty strong introduction section. _childDocuments_.review: Bear me with the playtime, my spouse and I played this game on his rig thanks to Steam's family features. I'll probably replay the game in a month anyways.This. Game. Rocks.It's been a while since I've picked up a horror game and felt so fully immersed. The last time I felt this much impact was when I played RE7 for the first time.Pros:- The tension doesn't end. The game keeps throwing new situations at you in a way that it doesn't get boring or repetitive.- It's actually scary! I did feel a sense of dread so many times while playing it.- "How many phobias can we fit in there?" The team was clearly very eager to create many scary moments in very different ways.- Lovecraftian horror. It's not just any Lovecraftian horror though. As a literature major, I felt like the team really understood the essence of this kind of horror and carried it out perfectly.- Colors, graphics, gameplay feeling, art direction. I couldn't separate these points because they're in great harmony. I don't remember how many times I decided to stop and watch the scene and take it all in. Imagine creating such effective areas that the player could guess how it would smell like.- Sound design. I found myself sitting in the corner of a level for a second to catch my breath just to hear sounds and get more even terrified. The atmospheric sounds and the soundtrack itself set the mood very well.- Story. Nowadays whenever I'm playing a horror game, story finds itself a place somewhere in between and just pass by but in Still Wakes the Deep, the story is strong and prominent, the characters and the situations are well written and it keeps the player both physically and emotionally engaged. The ending made me cry. I can't spoil it, but it's a great story to experience.- It's not a jumpscare fest. I know, jumpscare-horror has been a hit for a long time but honestly, we needed more horror games that relied on strong atmosphere and story instead of jumpscares. Still Wakes the Deep helps with this very specific craving.Cons:- Small bugs. I have been following and contributing the discussion forums regarding this. There are some bugs here and there and some of them are even game-breaking if you're not careful. I just want these to be addressed and it's going to be all good.Would have recommended this game with more than two thumbs if I had more.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is an intense cosmic horror experience that lingers long after you put it down. 10/10 - highly recommend to play it, or watch someone play. The storytelling is not spoon-fed, letting you slowly piece things together on your own. The horror build-up is incredibly well-paced, allowing you to get a feel for the environment (despite some calling it a glorified walking simulator) while preparing you for the intense, heart-pounding encounters. Even on the “easier” difficulty, I found myself fully engaged and constantly on edge. The danger encounters are riveting and kept me at the edge of my seat, Although these can be frustrating because of the sudden change of pace/speed, it felt realistic - as in, that is exactly how i would react in a situation where i am running for my life.Bottom line: If you love horror movies, feeling a constant sense of dread, and well-crafted stories, definitely give this game a shot. It’s an interactive experience that lasts around 5 hours. If you're achievement-oriented, make sure to gloss over them so you don't miss out on completion while you're playing the game.  Personal preference: better played on a controller (as someone who migrated from console to pc games).

_childDocuments_.review: WHAT AN EXPERIENCE. Once it got its hooks into me, I needed to finish it. Fans of The Thing or Cthulhu-esque horror will not want to miss this, just so long as you know what you're in for.Still Wakes the Deep offers little in the way of innovative gameplay or narrative. The 1st-person path is exceptionally linear. There are no character skills, inventory management, combat, or even consequential choices beyond "succeed or die". The plot boils down to, "paranormal calamity strikes an isolated location", a time-honored setup that includes Resident Evil, Half-Life, System Shock, and Dead Space. Expect body horror, environmental transformation, otherworldly vistas, and LOTS of switches that need flipping to avoid disaster.Still Wakes the Deep truly shines in the execution. This is an interactive horror EXPERIENCE that respects its audience. While there's quite a lot of incredible voice acting, none of the dialogue over-explains what's happening. You're left to put the pieces together on your own. The specificity of the setting, the lighting and graphical details, the sound design, the music, the level design and environmental story-telling -- all are carefully calibrated to evoke mounting dread, nerve-jangling anxiety, and a descent into reality-disintegrating, otherworldly transformation.If you expect detailed or fast-paced game play, look elsewhere. This is not a survival horror game. But if you want a finely crafted, carefully calibrated, precisely paced horror experience, buy this game. Turn down the lights, crank up the audio, tune out distractions . . . and just let the waves crash over you.

_childDocuments_.review: I write this as someone who's played and enjoyed the Chinese Room's original brand of minimalist, narrative-driven gameplay. The studio has undergone major changes through the years, and Still Wakes the Deep is proof of that. Not just a "walking sim," this has a modern, cinematic flavor. Unfortunately, I was very disappointed. If this game were priced more modestly after some polishing, I could possibly recommend it, albeit with massive caveats attached.Other reviews have mentioned it, but the amount of convenient yellow signposting in the level design really is beyond excessive, making the game unintentionally amusing rather than intentionally horrifying, regardless of the excellent atmosphere. There are also many repetitive interactions throughout, such as breaking locks, turning valves, and opening vents. When you're forced to see the same animations over and over again, it easily comes across as padding. Additionally, I felt no tension in the sequences of danger involving pseudo-platforming and stealth, because they require too little of the player. Even for something that obviously aims to be straightforward, there can always be new elements introduced to replace old ones. Occasional QTEs with the same button prompt during a climb aren't exciting, and neither is tossing objects to distract an enemy. Perhaps a handful of times--not repeatedly over the span of 4-6 hours. I found it strange how areas contain several lockers to hide inside, yet I never had to. Lastly, this point isn't as significant, though staying within the subject of level design: Areas being separated by loading screen doors contributes to a pace that feels less immersive, given that it's another repetitive interaction you're sitting through. I was often underwhelmed to realize I didn't accomplish much and I'm already getting funneled into the next area.On the technical front, I encountered several bugs, a few recurring like the double black screen after dying and reloading, and not being able to grab onto a ladder until I walk away and approach again. In one particular stealth sequence, the enemy got stuck near the objective, allowing me to waltz past and get a nice smell of his tendrils. Besides the bugs, I think the controls could use some tweaking. For example, when crawling through a tight space, you crouch to initiate the animation, but the game makes you stand when coming out the other side. It's tedious to re-press the crouch button during stealth sections.Although I miss the flowery writing from the Chinese Room's previous games, and the story here doesn't have as many thematic layers to it, I was still engaged thanks to sharp dialogue and great performances by the cast. Despite all my complaints, I did have an otherwise convincing physical presence in the setting, connecting with the protagonist. The fact he has a full body and casts a shadow helps, too. If TCR makes another story-driven game, I encourage them to rethink how they balance storytelling with gameplay. As other titles have shown, you can be cinematic without being passive, and you can be minimalist without recycling.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: A poignant story of love and loss, wrapped in creeping, bloated tendrils. If not for Silent Hill 2 Remake, Still Wakes the Deep would easily have been my GOTY. It is a near perfect marriage of tragedy and cosmic horror. The environmental storytelling is brilliant, there are frequent motifs that reward your attention with deeper slices of lore about the world we are exploring and the lives of those who had shared it with Caz. The game also makes fantastic use of vertical space, achieving a sense of immensity while maintaining a state of constant unease as the rapid decay of the rig produces increasingly hazardous conditions to traverse. At no point did I feel safe navigating the Beira D--there was always a new claustrophobic, acrophobic or even hydrophobic element being introduced, an ever-evolving danger as large hunks of the rig collapsed or imploded or worse, forcing you to climb, crawl or swim in increasingly unpleasant (and urgent) circumstances. What's more impressive, though, is that through all this, the game knows how to stay out of the way of its story. It is raw and unflinching yet utterly heart-breaking. It is devastating. I won't get into any story details, however. Plenty of other reviews have dived into the meat of it. I'll just leave this by saying; this is easily one of the best games I have experienced this past decade, and I cannot recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Keeping in mind that this is a linear walking sim (since the ignorant reviewer at IGN couldn't get past that fact for some reason), the game is incredible. First off it looks absolutely gorgeous. The lighting, textures, water effects, realistic and true to life environments create a very believable place. The creature design is very unique to the point you'll want to keep looking at them to try and figure out what it is you're even looking at. This mixed with the beautiful and gory supernatural imagery makes for a truly unique setting. The sound is also exceptional. The music is solid and emotional albeit not memorable. Environmental sounds and groans of the damaged oil rig make you feel like you're there. Enemies sound otherworldly and terrifying. The largest standout is the voice acting. These are some of the most believable character interactions and conversations I've ever heard in a game, especially the protagonist. You can really hear the desperation and fear in their voices more so than any horror game I've ever played.Gameplay wise it is very simple but that's to be expected. You can't fight enemies and instead have to sneak around or run away. Environmental puzzles are very straightforward which is alright with me because I never felt stuck while progressing through the game. This is a walking sim through in through but one with a horror backdrop and some of the thickest atmosphere you'll find in any game. PLAY IT.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely leave reviews, so believe me when I say this is worth playing.Fantastic writing and excellent game design. Great game play and smooth mechanics make it a pleasure to play. I typically hate stealth mechanics but this game executes them amazingly well. Game ran fine, only had 1 crash.The story is also a very strong point backed up with incredible voice acting.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes The Deep is a well-written, exciting, narrative horror game with great pacing, and doesn't resort to near-constant jump scares or common horror tropes, but instead places a greater emphasis on creating an unsettling, disturbing atmosphere, with intense, interesting and rewarding scenarios/set pieces that serve the story and don't feel tedious at all. It's not your typical horror game, and that's so refreshing.Without spoiling too much, the game's story is great and serves its purpose without bogging the game down with overly long cutscenes or exposition. The dialogue and the characters are well-written; I couldn't help but become invested in the character dynamics and relationships. Additionally, the acting was amazing, and I was consistently impressed by the performances.The game is visually impressive, ranging from absolutely horrific to downright strangely beautiful visuals. The sound design and score are spectacular, and really served the narrative. The levels and set pieces are masterfully crafted; they're fun, they make a lot of sense, and often made me feel clever for quickly thinking of ducking into a side room  or escaping through a vent that I saw earlier, and made dramatic moments a lot more impactful and terrifying. Really, in one of the scenes, I felt my soul leave my body at one point, it was great, and I'll never forget it.Overall, this is not only a great horror game, it's an incredible game with a lot of heart.

_childDocuments_.review: Very engaging story, a few points could have greater clarity, more info about people other than Caz, Suze, and Roy would have been nice so that we could get more attached to them and understand their motivations. i.e. Knowing that Finlay has a child or more about Brodie. The ocean looks fantastic and the 'thing' looks stunning! The  also look great.  design and animation were a bit disapointing in comparison. A few graphical elements seem prone to errors: A lot of the ropes/tethers that are meant to flap in the wind glitch and jitter quite oftenMultiple instances of vibrating or floating chainsLighting and shadow glitches occasionally- especially when entering/emerging from water.Caz's arm and shoulder would occasionally stretch across the cameraNot the most engaging gameplay, but there are a few sequences where it really shines. My biggest issue was that there were multiple instances where I got 'soft locked' due to glitches- this wasn't a big hassle as checkpoints are fairly numerous. I shall list the instances I can remember for reference:Blocked into room by an immovable object in the doorway.Blocked into room by  which was stuck in the door.Character got stuck in a small gap between platforms and was unable to moveCharacter's head got stuck on the 'thing', could not move and screen was covered in the proximity effect which made it harder to realise I was stuck.Upon returning to a checkpoint, quest progress had reverted but I was unable to interact with the item required to progress it again (reloading the checkpoint again automatically progressed the quest to the correct stage)Really great accessibility settings, with a story mode and a normal mode. Subtitle settings are very in depth. I made use of the anti-motion sickness settings which worked wonders. Many other settings were available also, including; colourblind settings, a reaction window slider, closed captioning, and a flashing light toggle.A game with a great, engaging story which is well worth playing. While it does fall short in a few areas, I wouldn't let that put you off. Additionally, if the progress halting glitches I encountered get fixed, I would say that this is a very high quality game!

Still, if u dont wanna hear anything the game is about u better skip the following list.promonster design together with the atmosphere are pretty good. There is nothing hidden, no other way to go. Nothing to uncover.That wouldnt be bad at all, u can fully focus on the story path. I played a lot of similar games but some feel more linear then others and this one here feel like u are on rails with only here and there some interaction. There is nothing fresh and the story consists only of escaping the rig after they drilled into a monster-lifeform or smthng.Thats it. For real now. i cant spoiler anything because thats it except of the end. but its an end many many many game Storys allready had.I dunno how people can claim this ist the greatest story..ive done that in serveral games like this before..cinematic masterpice or smthng like that..haha ahm no. but i admit it has its strenghts.There are no dying scenes. if a monster gets u u have a red screen and some wild images and just start at the last checkpoint.Thats so sad, if u walk into those things that look like alien eggs u just get bounced back and after the 3rd time like i said, red screen and restart..Mostly no threat for a horror game player. _childDocuments_.review: *mild-spoilers ahead*I've agonised over my rating - but Valve only lets me provide a binary response, so.. well here we are.Firstly, some parts of the game are fantastic. The sense of place and time - I could smell the stale tobacco that's permeated every inch of that tartan carpet and stained the formica. I'd have happily paid to just walk around and explore the rig. The combination of the desolate exteriors with the endless sea and the claustrophobic interiors let the story wind through the small environment with some variety. The middling things - the story and the characters.As many people have said, it was nice to have some proper Scottish characters and have them well voiced.I did not for one moment however, care about a single one of them though. They're drawn with some very broad strokes (Will the guy with National Front posters, be a nice chap? *strokes chin*). There is the clearly special NPC you're meant to care about (we know this as you have conversations that don't just tell you to go somewhere) - and that ends precisely as expected. I felt infinitely worse about my horse in Ghost of Tsushima.The plot was 'fine' - but not novel and didn't really take anything off in any unexpected direction. After 'the incident' happens, you'll find yourself asking a question that takes the game until the last 10 minutes to surprise you with..The poor.The game is very very linear. Walk/Jump/Swim forwards and aim for the yellow thing.I saw in another comment that they were planning on allowing the yellow to be turned off - that won't help. Whether the yellow is there or not, there's always only one way to go. Without it you're just going to have a more frustrating time finding the single place you can go and bouncing off a lot of invisible walls. Initially I'd got excited when spotting what looked like options ("Do I carry on forward, or duck into that tunnel?") - but there's never an actual choice. A subtle branch spotted simply means the main path is about to be a dead end, or the story will be taking you back through this area. There are no superfluous areas to explore - don't waste your time looking. Follow the yellow. The plot is entirely driven by MacGuffins - Character X will tell you that you need to go to Y, to press something to make Z happen. The character will be behind a window, on a ledge, on a phone, have to remain seated to press a button (as the game clearly doesn't support two characters interacting). Once you realize nobody can ever follow you and every movement that isn't you is scripted, then being told to go and rescue somebody.. well you know it's not happening. There's going to be no cluster of survivors path-finding across an open deck to a rescue vessel.I think there would have been a great 2 hour game, which you rattle through without engaging your brain. I think there could also have been another game, where you spend hours free-roaming the rig getting to know your colleagues, delving into back-story and performing menial rig-tasks, before it all kicks off.What we got here just feels a little imbalanced. Despite the length of my whining, I did enjoy the game and am glad I bought and played it.If you can get this in a sale and come into it knowing what to expect (and what not to expect) - it's a fun experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Listen,I really like the game. I do. I think the premise is quite unique; you can see the foundations upon which the story, creature, and visuals have been lovingly built, while retaining a very unique personality. The characters are very endearing, due in great part to the voice actors. Unfortunately I found the gameplay a little repetitive at times, and possibly buggy? Which made it drag by the third act, which is a shame, because this is also where the art direction truly shines, and the character relationships become ever so ripe for exploration. The ending feels... almost like a betrayal to the themes of the story that made us connect so deeply with the characters and root for them. Undeserved tragedy, unearned nihilism, that felt familiar coming from the studio but maybe disconnected from this particular story. The Chas I was told about and the one I witnessed helping his comrades were completely different, and though my stay with him was brief, he as a protagonist utterly convinced me he was deserving of a more layered finale.TLDR I think the game is worth experiencing, though maybe not playing. Watching it or getting it on sale is much recommended; ending is a Little Flat. :/

_childDocuments_.review: I've just emerged from the depths of "Still Wakes the Deep," and I'm still catching my breath. This game is a masterclass in atmosphere, wrapping you in a claustrophobic blanket of tension from start to finish. The plot had me hooked like a fish on a line, reeling me through its twists and turns.Now, I've heard some folks grumble about the game being too linear, but for me, that's part of its charm. It's not trying to be an open-world extravaganza - it's a focused, narrative-driven experience that knows exactly what story it wants to tell and how to tell it.Speaking of focus, let's talk about the game's length. It's short, sure, but it's all the better for it. There's no filler here, no padding to artificially extend playtime. Every moment counts, every scene builds on the last. It's like a perfectly paced thriller novel - gripping from page one to the final chapter.Visually, this game is a feast for the eyes. The developers have worked some serious magic here, optimizing the game to run smoother than a well-oiled machine. It felt more like controlling an interactive film.It's not all smooth sailing, though. There are a few bugs in the code (please fix the fusebox first, when the game tell you), but they'll be fixed in a patch coming this July. The enemy AI could use a bit of fine-tuning too, though if you're as fused in the story as I was, you might not even notice.My one major gripe? The main character's inability to climb over closed doors outside on the rig. It would be nice too have some visual obstacles, that prevents him to do so.Despite these minor issues, "Still Wakes the Deep" is a triumph of atmospheric storytelling. If you're a fan of narrative-driven games that prioritize mood and plot, you owe it to yourself to take the plunge. Just don't be surprised if you find yourself holding your breath along the way.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I wanted to like STWD I was really disappointed by the mechanics and enemy variety / encounters. All you do the entire game is click buttons, pull switches, replace fuses, and turn valves as interactions with objectives and levels. And of the few puzzles there were, they were extremely simple. I'm not asking for anything crazy difficult but, I just imagine they could have done some more clever interactions.As for enemies, I was really disappointed. I barely play horror games (STWD being the first one in like 3 years for me) and was really hoping for some crazy monsters or something. Just ♥♥♥♥ to scare me. But you quickly find out that basically all the monsters act in the same way, and your interactions with them are no different. You hide in a place for them to leave, and throw something in the other corner of the room to get out of your hole and make distance. Rinse and repeat for the entire game.This comes to me in the end, being barely at all spooked. The only things that really scared me was the atmosphere. Monsters were a tiny adrenaline rush when first meeting them. Before finding out they're all simple and the same.

_childDocuments_.review: A short game, to say the least. I read it was only 6 hours and at the point of completion, I have exactly 6 hours on the clock. It's not up there with the best (Think SOMA), but it's most certainly a fun and engaging addition to the genre. The voice acting is perfect, the story line is interesting and the graphics, whilst not revolutionary, are pleasing on the eye.I felt that the games difficulty modes needed a further addition; I completed the game on standard and often felt like it was far too easy to navigate around the monsters. A lot of the time, I felt like i was playing in casual. The yellow objects guiding you were also a little too over the top and insulting to my intelligence; at one point there was quite literally only one way to go and a little bit of yellow tarp (Or paint) was included to show me "Hey, this is the way to go"; yeah, thanks for that. Anyway despite that I did thoroughly enjoy the game. If you're not into the genre, it's no doubt worth a miss. But for those who enjoy story driven horrors/psychological horrors; you will undoubtedly enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A Deep Dive into the Abyss..“Still Wakes the Deep” is a masterstroke in the realm of psychological horror video games. As someone who works on oil rigs, I found the game’s setting - an oil rig named Beira D in the North Sea - to be incredibly authentic and immersive. The meticulous attention to detail, from the commissary to the locker rooms and the drill floor, mirrors my own experiences on an oil rig, making the game feel eerily real.Playing as Caz McLeary, a worker on the Beira D, I was drawn into the unfolding disaster that threatened both my character’s life and the lives of his crewmates. The narrative is driven by its unheroic characters, making the story feel grounded and relatable. The dialogue and voice acting are some of the most impactful I’ve ever experienced in a horror game, adding to the overall sense of dread and suspense.The game’s atmospheric setting, brilliant performances, and fun creature effects are standout features that elevate the gaming experience. Despite its strictly linear trappings, the game offers an engaging story that can be played through in a night or two, making it a perfect choice for those looking for a short but intense gaming experience.While some players have found the ending disappointing, I believe it adds to the overall sense of unease and ambiguity that the game cultivates. It leaves you with more questions than answers, keeping you thinking about the game long after you’ve finished playing.In conclusion, “Still Wakes the Deep” offers a unique gaming experience that resonates with individuals like me who have real-life experience working on oil rigs. It’s a deep dive into the abyss that leaves you on the edge of your seat, making it a must-play for any fan of psychological horror games.
