_childDocuments_.review: Far out... I turned up the audio using Razer Synapse spacial audio and MAN this game can make you jump. 3D audio seriously brings this game to life and I was gritting my teeth especially during that first major chase scene. The sound effects in this game are also incredibly immersive with the volume cranked.It helps that the voice acting is seriously next level across the board. The main actor is absolutely brilliant and should win an award for his performance its seriously that good... I also loved hearing every slang Gaelic word because being able to see its translation in the subtitles was pure brilliance. It means you can hear a character ramble off a whole heap of slang words but be able to perfectly follow the conversation via the subtitles. And man it seriously helps with the immersion. Bravo Chinese Room seriously next level thinking there... And I'm also guessing they had a lot of input from the actors to make the dialogue as good as it is. It all feels really natural to an impressive degree...Another aspect I love about this game is that I feel like I'm playing through the movie 'The Thing' but just based on an oil rig. And as a massive fan of The Thing, I'm 100% fine with that... The rig itself is a brilliant setting and I really felt that they nailed the time period including the vibe and look. And yes its a very pretty game with nice character models. It's Unreal Engine 5 so what did you expect? Its not Hellblade 2 levels of good by a long shot but it does beat it in another area. Let me explain...So lets set this straight. Yeah a lot of this is a walking sim with some light platforming, stealth sections and some awesome chase scenes. But for perspective... I felt bored for the most part playing through the recent Hellblade 2 - which to me, is also a walking sim with a splash of combat. At least here the story and premise had me hooked. In Hellblade 2, I was honestly running through the game to get it over with. Here, I'm actually engrossed like I'm watching a cool 80's horror flick.So yeah this game is tops. Best walking sim type game I have played in a hellishly long time.Bravo Chinese Room. Bravo...FINAL NOTE: If your not listening to this with the volume cranked so that the creature chasing you is making so much noise you might have to stop & change your undies, your doing it wrong...

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a great entry into the horror genre, more specifically centered around themes such as body horror, Lovecraftian elements, claustrophobia and thalassophobia. You play a character down on his luck working on an oil rig off the coast of Scotland, before the rigs drill hits an unknown entity that sets off a chain of horrific events that results in both the crew mutating, as well as the oil rig itself distorting. While being set in an environment as industrial and bleak as an oil rig, some of the cosmic horror elements in the form of the entity itself bring a slew of strangely visually pleasing aesthetics to the game, despite being hostile and quite frankly disgusting.The story elements are well done, as is the voice acting; it’s fairly uncommon to hear British and Scottish voice actors in a game, but in a strange way it adds a level of authenticity to the games storyline in my opinion. The main character is likeable and the writing is very authentic to the Scottish. You’ll hear a lot of swearing and banter between the crew, and a lot of colloquialism that I personally really enjoy in a game.The horror elements are great, the body horror specifically is quite magnificently gross, yet you can’t help but take a look and really examine the brutal transformations that the entity causes on board. I found myself going out of my way to find most of the dead (or not dead) crew members to see their fates. Most of these dead crew members are essentially either set pieces or hazards, but there are a few notable enemies that force stealth sections. I didn’t mind them too much but some areas did get frustrating, as the enemies movements are actually very hard to predict as they moved around the areas like giant legged spiders almost.In terms of the gameplay, we’re really looking at loop that incorporates walking simulator elements, light parkour and a few stealth sections between, with some very minor puzzle elements of remedial tasks like turning switches off or moving carts out of the way of your path. At its core, it’s a pretty basic game and mostly an enjoyable horror experience, but due to this I can’t really imagine doing multiple playthroughs. Despite that, I would 100% recommend this game but only perhaps during a sale and not for full price – it’s a short experience but a good one nonetheless.Excellent voice actingOriginal concept and settingGreat visuals and weather effectsNot much replayabilityA little on the short side

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes The Deep was one of the more refreshingly dreadful (in a positive way) psychological horror games I've played in recent history, due largely in part to developer The Chinese Room's awareness of the importance of building an atmosphere within your game universe. While the game plays as your standard walking simulator, and at times has its frustrating set of chore-like responsibilities, it serves as a reminder that horror should have a creeping sense of dread attached to it inherently in order to be effectively immersive. Creature design paired with a well-crafted story, tense atmosphere, and unsettling overall vibe make this one of the more highly regarded horror experiences of 2024. Not necessarily for people who require a high-octane jumpscare attached to their horror.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10 The most technically beautiful UE5 game so far, fantastic art design with absolutely stellar environments and character models, with very Cronenberg-like enemies. Gameplay is quite smooth, and a "Story" difficulty is offered if you, like me, don't enjoy the survival horror genre, which significantly eases up on enemy AI in stealth sequences. Controls feel crisp and the traversal punches above its weight class. The story is just enough to move the plot along, with few strong emotional notes, and a satisfying conclusion. For the price and size of the project, it feels more like a 9/10 - if you like cosmological horror, this is certainly worth your purchase, especially at the price it is offered.

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty decent walking sim. Definitely better than most walking sims.  Many people report the game took them a few hours but I am not really sure how.  I did restart the game somewhat early one due to playing with a friend and not paying attention but that only was for like 1 hr.  So the total game time for me was probably fairly close to 7 hrs.  I did get stuck once which probably added 15-20 min.  Even so.  If you listen to all the dialogue and explore a bit. you can get 7 hrs out of this game easily.   (also I paused the game once to do an errand so my true total time was close to 7 hours for a single play)I think graphics were fantastic and monster design pretty creepy.  My only suggestion on monsters is that sometimes less is more.  And I think the creepy horror would have been increased if there was actually less gory viseral stuff everywhere.  That way when you do encounter a deformed human it is more shocking and you don't become habituated to it, too much.  (like in the movie annihilation)Performance: I played at 4k with epic settings. No issues with performance but there were some bugs with the QTEs.  One near the start of the game was borderline game breaking.  It is the first time you go under the rig and you make a jump requiring you to hold RT, in quick sucession the thing you are holding breaks and you need to then hold LT.+RT  But instead of giving you the usual amount of time to do this, the timer is almost up when the icon comes up on the screen .  It actually took me 3 tries just to figure out what button it was supposed to be because it flashed up and off so quickly.  Even after I finally figured that out, it was not recognizing that I was still holding RT.  So it legit took me about 10 tries to guess at the timing.  You will have to quickly release and re-hit RT While also hitting LT and holding at the perfect moment.   Later in the game there are other instances of this, but they actually work properly.  Which confirmed that this one is bugged.  Hopefully it gets fixed and hopefully my explanation helps others stuck on it.   There was another part of the game where I swam under something but then came up through the grating and was stuck in the grating.  There is another time when I was in a long tall room where I was supposed to travel down to the bottom. But the hint icon kept saying I needed to go up.  This is the part I was stuck on a bit and wasted a fair bit of time on as I kept trying to climb back up but I was actually supposed to be moving down to the bottom. I had to watch a walk through to figure that one out.   There are a few times when it is really unclear where you are supposed to go.  There is another one mid-early where you are hanging off of the helocopter and the place you need to jump is a platform that looks way way too far away to possibly be where you are supposed to go. But it is. Overall I would reccomend this game to people who like walking sims.  If you dont like walking sims than walk away.   As for the price tag.  I think its fair.  The game runs really well aside from a few minor issues I mentioned above. I mean those are so minor compared to other bugs I have encountered in AAA games.  I got 7 hours of entertainment out of it.   Maybe you will get less than me, but lets be real.  The devs did a great job and deserve to be paid.   I am more than happy to help out the little guys making unique games vs paying $70 for a bloated fetch quest AAA game, any day.  The graphics are stellar. Art design and monsters are great.  I really  liked the orignal setting of the oil rig.  I was getting Abyss vibes but more sinister.  I thought the casting was stellar too.  Looking forward to more games by the Chinese Room.  Also to anyone who doesn't know.  The dev name "Chinese Room" is a reference to the "Chinese Room Thought Experiment" which is about AI sentience and can be applied to other concepts as well.  I would google that and check out the wiki. It is actually a really interesting thought experiment.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really have any expectations for this game. I did ponder the idea of buying it, and thankfully, my friend gave me a glowing recommendation. I am thankful for it because I believe this game deserves nothing but the highest accolades for narrative-driven horror. Still Wakes the Deep is a love letter to the claustrophobic nature of John Carpenter's The Thing, from the immense body horror, tightly packed space of the Beira D Oil Rig taking the place of Outpost 31, and most importantly, the well-rounded cast of characters making this Scottish rig feel like a grim but lively environment. The story is otherwise a horror-drama that is just The Thing on an Oil Rig, which by no means is an insult, it's quite perfect, especially since very few games have tried to replicate that outside of the official Thing game and Distrust.For its 6-hour length, you will see things so uniquely bizarre that I honestly will plug the concept artist Jef Wall here:  I really wish we had a model viewer since the few monsters you do run into are so heavily covered in darkness or fog that you can't appreciate it that well, so hopefully that link can satiate that interest. On the other end of that, this game does feature moments where you need to face monsters and honestly, their scripted sections that don't last long and are quite easy to navigate for the most part, so for people expecting a Mr. X situation you don't need to worry, everything is purely situational and that's honestly fine. This is a narrative game, first and foremost, and it's some of the best writing I've seen for a game of this nature. I cannot recommend it enough; it's a truly anxiety-inducing experience that is definitely worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't bother with this game. This game is a walking simulator and not even a good one. Hell this game literally has an achievement called WALKING SIMULATOR!! Which you get for not using sprint in the game outside of specific sections. Lets go through some pros and cons.Pros: -This game has excellent voice acting, it's half the reason the characters are so likeable. If only they were in a better game.-The Lovecraftian fleshy stuff has a cool visual aesthetic... I honestly can't think of anything else positiveCons:-This game is utterly devoid of mechanics. You literally just walk from one point to another and press whatever button the game tells you to. There's no items, no inventory, no nothing. The most adventurous the game gets with mechanics is needing to use heaters to stay warm. Except that there's only like three heaters in the whole game! And it's not even a case of you'll die if you don't get warm, Caz will just say that he needs to get warm first before he'll let you interact with the next objective. Effectively making this mechanic just another part of the walking simulator. But hey that's not everything to a game right? Maybe the game has an awesome story?-This game hasn't got a good story. The story can be summed up in a single paragraph. "Oil rig drills too deep, awakens generic Lovecraftian horror. Main character Caz goes around the rig fixing things in order to prevent it from sinking while avoiding monsters and being haunted by his failing marriage back home. But in the end all the work he did means nothing because he decides that the generic Lovecraftian horror is too dangerous and so he ignites the oil in the rig blowing himself, the rig and the generic Lovecraftian horror up."That's it. You might think I've missed out a whole bunch of stuff but I really haven't. The story is remarkably thin and really just serves to get Caz from point A to point B.-The Horror elements are super weak. You never find out anything about the fleshy Lovecraftian substance that causes the whole story to kick into motion. Seriously you never learn what it is and it never does anything interesting. It just spreads through the ship, turns the crew into monsters, and messes with Caz's head. It's basically just the Necromorph goo from Dead Space only half the time you forget that it's even there.-The monster designs are also super weak, they're just humans covered in fleshy goo with tentacles coming out of them. There's no variation between them either each infected crewmate is fundamentally the same. Both in appearance and how you deal with them.-Length. This game is super short. I beat it in a little over 4 hours and I was exploring areas as much as I could trying to find anything of interest. The real playtime is probably closer to 3 and a half hours long. I'm starting to think that the developers made the bare minimum of a game so that it would get players over the 2 hour mark so that they can't get a refund.I'm super disappointed in this game because an oil rig sinking into the North Sea while an Lovecraftian oceanic horror spreads across the rig is an awesome concept for a horror game. That is why this game is so much more disappointing, the concept IS genuinely good and it's wasted on a seriously sub par game with no gameplay, no story and no horror.2/10 If you want to play a good Lovecraftian horror game set on a failing ship, play Dead Space. If you want to play a good lovecraftian horror game without combat, Play Amnesia TDD. If you want to play a good horror game that's a walking simulator, play SOMA.Don't bother with this game.

_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: If you like these movies: The Abyss; Leviathan; The Thing; The LighthouseIf you like these games: SOMA; Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs; Gone Home; the first half of Alien: IsolationIf you like these things: Walking simulators; great narrative; remarkable graphics; likable characters; a memorable protagonist; stellar voice acting; cosmic horror; body horrorThen you will enjoy Still Wakes the Deep. _childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: There's cheap horror, and then there's this. Still Wakes the Deep is a stunning atmospheric visual experience, and if you're into story-focused psychological horror, definitely pick it up. The well-crafted story paired with excellent voice acting and sound design keeps you immersed and engaged all the way through, and while it's not the scariest game out there, there's a near constant underlying sense of dread that is incredibly effective. It's not littered with cheap jump scares, and the creature encounters are actually chilling. This is probably a good one if you're trying to ease into the horror genre. So yeah, this was horrifying and I loved every second of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I will start off positively saying the games graphics, sound, voice acting, and atmosphere was top notch, especially using an oil rig as the environment which is definitely underutilised in horror. Also the monsters retaining some of who they were as theyre yelling out, hunting you was amazing. I really wanted to love this game as it was recommended a few times as being a GOTY contender and after seeing the trailer having "the thing" type monsters I had high hopes. Problem is those monsters barely play a role in the game. Youd expect them to be a bigger threat, sorta like outlast, but you can easily sneak by them with little effort and other characters talk about them as if they're a minor inconvenience or not even monsters at all. You dont even get to see what most of them look like as you never get that close. Even when they kill you its instant with no type of unique execution, which i found disappointing. Most of the monsters look like meatballs or a giant head with lines coming off them which i couldnt take seriously. I also kinda expected the game to have multiple endings or choices to give it some replayability but its linear with little in the way of collectables to help world building.As much as I dont regret buying the game since i do wish to see more games like this, just with a little more depth. I cant recommend it as youd be better off watching a playthrough of it and maybe read some lore as youd get the just of the experiences

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely review games, but this?This is cosmic horror done The voice acting is superb, the atmosphere is on point, and It genuinely terrified me, which is hard for horror games to do to me. A lotta folks compare it to the Thing, and you know what? That's an apt description. The Thing meets Color Out of Space, with a healthy dash of absolute terror that comes from hearing the distorted insane ramblings of your co-workers as their corrupted husks they once called bodies slaughter their friends. Lovecraft thought that being able to describe, or quantify such horrendous creatures and concepts detracted from them.This proves him wrong.Buy this game. Some people complain about the length, but it's worth the price if you ask me.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep is a fun yet honest by-the-books horror game experience.Gameplay-wise the game does not present a lot, as it's mostly fueled by typical parkouring and basic stealth.With the game instead focusing on cinematics and story priority, which isn't inherently always a negative. But it is worth a mention.A lot of the body-horror present feels most strongly inspired by that of Carpenter's The Thing and Annihilation from 2018.And what I really like is how the game takes awhile to build-up the monsters before ever seeing them, which makes it immensely rewarding when it is you finally do. Which is furthermore is also topped with the glimpses of humanity present within the monsters themselves as well, and of course the gorgeously grotesque gore galore.There was sadly a short part of the game where I got pretty hardcore stuck on, as I had no idea how to progress.Luckily, the developers commonly roam the Steam Discussions and were quick to happily help me out. Very awesome! Thanks!Also Scottish is funny.Anyways, the game is pretty good but in the sense that I don't foresee it reaching anybody's top 10s this year.You can play it and be over with pretty quickly and feel nicely satisfied -- some probably in a single session or 2 -- with yet very little motive to ever really return to it or think of it again. That's not inherent criticism, those games are needed in the industry. But it is still worth being considered.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This is an awesome premise, but the game just falls flat.  There's hardly any interactivity along the game's long, linear, narrow path, but there are a lot of invisible walls and knee-high barriers.  It doesn't build the dread or mystique or plot it needed to in order to do the premise justice.  The inciting horror is never explored, the world offers no background or mystery about it, its ramifications are never brought up, and most of the game is a series of chores around it.  The game wasn't scary.  It wasn't interesting.  It wasn't emotional, but it definitely tried at that last one.It's not quite a walking simulator, but it's only a couple steps removed.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Superb atmosphere, voice acting, and level design.The game's detailed use of an oil rig as the setting and being cast amongst blue-collar Glaswegians proves novel and engaging, lending a verisimilitude that keeps the otherwise by-the-book survival horror mechanics both gripping and engaging.If you have an itch for content related to Dead Space (sans combat), The Thing, Eldritch or Body Horror, or 80s underwater horror movies, then I highly recommend giving it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game, bit on the short side and there's no real """substance""" to the game outside of just experiencing it. (by that I mean there's no real lore notes or anything filling out the rest of the world. You just get some phone calls and that's about it) The main monster sections are very basic, you can just throw an item and then hoof it to the exit or next hiding area, but the monster designs are very cool for what they are. The four main characters are FANTASTIC, Caz especially feels like one of the realest protagonists I've ever seen, but I wish there was more to them that fleshed them out. Honestly part of me wishes the paranormal aspects of the game weren't in the game at all and it was just about an oil rig sinking, as i found all of the actual Player vs Environment sections vastly better than the Player vs Monster sections.Do I think this is worth 35$? Eh, probably not, its a on the short side(beat it in just under 4 hours) and there's not a whole lot of side things to see. Am I glad i played this game though? Yeah absolutely. If you got no problem dropping 35$ though, there are definitely MUCH worse games you could pay the same price for and at least this game won't waste your time and will give you a neat little experience while it lasts

_childDocuments_.review: I have only played about 30 minutes so far so I haven't gotten anywhere in the story yet.  I will update this review later once I actually play the game.  I was initially going to play this on gamepass, but the developers have made an incredibly scummy decision to remove the ability to use DLSS from the windows store version of the game.  The game runs very poorly without it on my more than capable 4060 rig.  I purchased this only to refund so I could make this review and alert others to this.  I will be happily sailing the seven seas to experience the game that I cannot enjoy on gamepass.  I will always support indie titles and pay for products, but this practice of shipping different versions of the game to different stores is unacceptable.  Not to mention the xbox app says it supports DLSS so they are literally lying.EDIT:  I have now completed the game after about 5 hours and would change this to a hesitant thumbs up.  As I stated before the game is on UE5 which is a BIG performance hog on even the beefiest of rigs.  Developers know this and often center their performance benchmarks using DLSS Nvidia's AI based render scaling.  I don't quite understand all the specifics, all I know is at a cost of slightly less defined graphics the game runs like 75% better.  At native 1080p with settings on low-medium I was barely hitting 40 fps on my 4060 on game pass without it.  I went to turn on DLSS and I was like "huh. it's missing".  Yup, I am not sure if this was a choice of the development team or publisher but there are two separate builds of the game.  Steam/Epic's with DLSS and the hampered GamePass one without.  This is flat out absurd, and frankly a dangerous precedent if developers pull something like this again.  Anyway, the steam forums are full of games pissed rightly about it.  Once again, piracy is the best way to experience a paid product.  Unbelievable.  It's a d**n shame too, because the game is overall a fantastic experience.  The lovecraftian horrors that appear are downright terrifying.  The voice acting is phenomenal as well as a subtle, but mesmerizing score.  The game is clearly inspired by body horror from the likes of carpenter/cronenberg with some astounding effects that seem ripped out of "The Thing".  If you have gamepass I feel you are morally "allowed" to experience the game since you are supporting the devs indirectly.  I don't need to go and debate the ethics of piracy in this review however lol.  It's 30 bucks on a launch discount on Steam for about 4-5 hours of gameplay.  I took a bit longer actually because some of the mechanics I won't spoil late game were finicky and rather infuriating lol.  All in all it's a solid experience if you are looking for something off the beaten path.  Oh!  And like EVERYONE is Scottish which is really amusing.  The accents are so thick sometimes you LITERALLY couldn't understand what they were saying besides copious amounts of swear words LOL

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best horror games to date. First off, the shining star here is the voice acting/writing for the game. The voice actors were phenomenal and the writing for this game did not feel fake at all. I also thought it was awesome for them to speak multiple languages in conversation. There are some characters that would swap between English, Scottish and Gaelic(?) in sentences and it felt so authentic. The horror in this game reminds me of a toned down version of Soma. There are some chase scenes and sneaking around you have to do but the parts aren't long. The majority of the horror is the mystery of the phenomenon and the random screams, howls, unrecognizable noises you hear throughout the journey. Not a lot of jumpscares, but the environment is completely horrific once the madness happens. Great story, great voice acting, great script, great game. Good job team!

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished it. 3.8 hours and I wasn't "sprinting" through the game though lack of collectables or anything of the sort added to that. Pros: Good initial premiseGreat voice acting/cast Good pacing and tense momentsBody Horror. Feels very "Colour out of space" for the first hour or so. Cons: Areas felt reused (a lot)No elaboration on the "event" whatsoever. Not even notes or in game text (compared to something like Dead Space or Bioshock this leaves a kind of hollow experience) Ending was a bit cliche Extremely simple gameplay loops and a little repetitive. Performance wasn't great. IDK what that 3D resolution slider is but that's where ALL your frames go. 50% I could get 120 fps on a 3080. 100% I could barely get 60. Rest of the options did nothing in terms of performance cept maybe lighting and shadows. Conclusion. Wait for a big sale. £30.00 for shy of four hours gameplay without replayability isn't a good deal. This is the kind of game you give to someone that doesn't mind a slower pace of game with extremely simple controls/game loops. Perhaps a relatively new gamer looking to try a horror game as the game has no combat, crafting, skills of any kind.

_childDocuments_.review: It has been a long time since I played a horror game that did such a good job of immersing me in the story, environment, and setting. Between outstanding visual design, brilliant voice acting, and an incredibly well-realized setting, Still Wakes the Deep makes for an incredibly engaging and positively terrifying experience. Around 7-8 hours for the main campaign, a bit more to do all achievements. Definitely recommend if you're looking for a solid horror game that doesn't outstay its welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: "Still Wakes the Deep" is an atmospheric horror game that excels in creating a deeply unsettling experience. Set on a North Sea oil rig, the game's claustrophobic environment amplifies the tension as you explore narrow corridors and dimly lit rooms. The narrative draws you in with a sense of isolation and helplessness, where every creak and shadow adds to the eerie atmosphere. The game's visuals and sound design are top-notch, effectively immersing players into its grim, mysterious world.While the pacing can be slow at times, especially for those expecting more action, the game shines in building suspense and delivering moments of heart-pounding terror. It’s more about exploration and psychological horror than combat, which might not appeal to everyone, but for fans of games like "Amnesia" or "SOMA," it’s a hauntingly captivating experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Very straightforward linear story with some hard-hitting emotional beats. Feels like a mix of Underwater and The Thing. _childDocuments_.review: Some of the best atmospheres and voice acting I've ever experienced in a linear horror game. I feel compelled to recommend this because other than a few performance bugs this has been nothing short of a great experience. The game conveys well a sense of powerlessness in the face of eldritch horror.I do not necessarily enjoy overdone panic inducing chase sequences, and this game has those spaced perfectly. I have to stress that if you're immersed, the audio design of most rooms alone is incredible. Thoroughly exploring what I could felt rewarding as I love engagement that leads to stronger world building. Some of the areas where you're required to tread water felt a little clunky, and there were some audio bugs I experienced whenever the character was out in the rain and having a conversation which led to lots of overlapping sharp sounds. I experienced a big chunk of the game alongside a friend who has experience working in similar conditions, and they were impressed with the overall attention to detail and the general environment. For me, the story took some really questionable turns towards the very end and did not have a conclusion befitting of the experience.Thoroughly impressed aside from the likely subjective creative differences I hold, so either way well done and more of this please!

_childDocuments_.review: Very short for the price. But honestly I wouldn't want it to be longer. It's an interesting story, fairly easy. No combat, no puzzles really, more like an interactive movie. _childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep does a lot of things right. It has it's moments, a lot of which are extremely thematically resonant, however, for a game to be a walking simulator, I feel like I need a much better and more engaging story.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through Still Wakes The Deep at least three times now and I feel like it emotionally broke me more and more with each play through. _childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the most high quality and best of the "amnesia-like" horror type games. There have been so many lately but this one sets itself apart due to the amazing setting of the oil rig and the fantastic (scottish) voice acting. It really scratches the cosmic horror itch as well. I love that the rig is as much of an obstacle as the "enemy" is, and its constantly changing. This is probably the only of these types of games where I actually felt empathy for all of the NPCs, they feel so true to life due to the excellent voice acting and writing, and they are involved deeply throughout the game.The gameplay itself isn't anything new for this genre, as its mostly navigation or short stealthing to avoid enemies (nothing too difficult, nothing annoying at all in the gameplay). But it does just feel unique as you navigate the rig and the interactions like climbing or jumping or squeezing or crawling, or fixing the electricity throughout the rig really feel weighty and meaningful though. These types of interactions really do to amp up the atmosphere and claustrophobic horror.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: This game is at least 95% crawling or swimming through contrived obstacles for no reason. That's not an exaggeration, it's literally true. The ending is stupid and not only thoroughly unsatisfying but genuinely frustrating. The game never explains itself, even a little. It's nothing more than a very short, linear "crawl now, jump now" mess with a garbage non-story.This is just another stupid game with characteristically stupid design and plot choices (e.g. "You stay here. I'll get to the lifeboats alone and then come back for you, tripling the time and the risk for no rational reason. We definitely should not both go right now together, even though this plan makes zero sense whatsoever.")Just another game that makes you hit the right button at the right time -- basically QTEs -- while you zip through a contrived maze that is absolutely unrealistic.Just another game with ladders that lead to cramped crawlspaces in an incredibly unrealistic way, and with filing cabinets and the like stacked in a thoroughly implausible way for no reason other than to create a pointless maze.And yeah, I'm running for my life to escape a monster trying to kill me, and yet for some reason, the best I can do in this scenario to move a laundry basket that blocks the exit is to gently move it ever-so-slowly, as if to avoid waking a hummingbird. Or how about that my top running speed is around 3 MPH?This nonsense reminds me of how, in Days Gone, the ultra-fit protagonist somehow becomes tuckered out after running 10 steps, even when trying to escape a horde of zombies. This is just contrived, low-effort gaming mechanics trash. It doesn't entertain me, it infuriates me.The swimming mechanics are infuriatingly difficult, even when they work as intended. And at one point, I lost all control of the character while underwater. My hands were out in front of me, but I couldn't move, no matter what I tried. I just had to wait to drown.And the monsters are , ffs.Stupid game. Boring and predictable. The ending -- which comes rapidly since the game is extremely short -- is also senseless and frustrating, and makes everything you did up until then completely pointless. Alternative ending scenarios are easy to imagine but are not even brought up.And the game doesn't even begin to explain what caused all the events depicted!People like this game for the same reason that people raved about the Model T automobile in 1908: There's nothing better on offer. Sort of like how there's nothing on TV but absolute trash, more absolute trash, and just plain trash. The plain trash looks good by comparison. But it's still just trash.Here's a clue, developers, and yes, I know you don't care: STOP MAKING IT SO CONTRIVED!Edit: Cute sarcastic comment, Liam. How "incredibly detailed" should my review be, given that the game has hallmarks that I hate? If you went out for dinner at a restaurant and found a turd in your soup, would you detail everything about your experience, or would you focus on ... oh, I dunno ... the turd?
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Man, I dunno maybe thats a personal thing but this game just did not click with me.I bought it because i am fond of thalassophobia and megalophobia stuff and storybased walking simulatorish games. When I started it, I was amazed by the visual style. And that did not change to the end. Its an immensely detailed and high quality game. They make you want to just walk through their visually stunning world taking in every detail. Surprisingly my biggest complaint is the heavy handed yellow paint. Devs must be ex-Ubisoft employees. _childDocuments_.review: The short short version: John Carpenter's "The Thing", except instead of Americans in an Antarctic research station, it's Brits crewing an offshore oil rig. Narrative-based walking sim with quick time events.Rather than re-tread many of the existing reviews, I will instead highlight what I found most notable.1. The voice acting: it's fantastic. All of the voice acting is great, with special note to the main character (McLeary) and Rennick. I also admit, as an American, I found the dialects and unfamiliar slang fascinating. While most of the terms can be gleaned from context, the subtitles are helpfully in "plain" English. My only complaint is that I wish we spent a little more time getting to know the various characters before the actions begins.2. Game length: somewhat short at 4-5 hours for a normal, blind, non-Achievement-Hunting playthrough. While I don't put this as a negative, some people may find the game to be too short. I felt that it was just the right length - long enough to tell a complete story while not stretching things out enough to ever get boring.3. Gameplay: while I dislike the negative connotations to "walking sim", that is essentially what you have here. Follow the path, flip the switch, do a quick time event, repeat in varying order. This is, first and foremost, an interactive horror story, not survival-horror. Don't take that as a negative - just letting people know what to expect.Summary: All in all, I got exactly what I wanted and expected. 10/10, would get chewed out by my boss Scrooge McDuck again.

_childDocuments_.review: Having just finished playing this over on my Youtube channel (link at end of review for anyone wanting to see a gameplay sample before buying), I can confidently say this is a great horror game.I'll admit I'm a bit biased here, namely because I do enjoy maritime/nautical settings in horror games. So with Still Wakes The Deep being set on an oil rig (the Beira D) off the Scottish coast in the 1970s, I was immediately hooked. The premise is that you're an electrician trying to run away from a few personal problems; after a bit of a crappy morning being shouted at by your boss, the day gets infinitely worse when the rig's drill hits something sinister deep below the water and terrible, alien things begin to happen. Cue a story of desperately trying to survive the unknown horror that has emerged from the depths and find a way to escape the rig...Visually, the game is stunning. The devs have put a hell of a lot of effort into this and the sound design, and it pays dividends; the atmosphere is rich and full of tension as you navigate claustrophobic internal passages and the rig's fog-shrouded deck. Admittedly, even on lower graphics settings this did cause my PC to chug a little; though to be fair, I think this might partly be because my PC is getting a little old and probably needs replacing in the coming months.Speaking of atmosphere, players be warned: if you have nyctophobia, thalassophobia, submechanophobia or claustrophobia, then this game is likely going to really tap into some of these. There are times where you're plunged into dark passages and structures, sometimes flooded with water, often cramped and discomforting. But then again, if you're playing a horror game set at sea, I'm sure this is the kind of thing you're expecting!The other aspect of the game that really makes Still Wakes The Deep stand out, however, are the characters. Perhaps it's the mix of various UK accents (predominantly Scottish, but with a few English and Irish ones as well), but the devs did a really good job of bringing them to life and they have a lot of charm in their own gruff and often-foulmouthed ways. To name a few standout examples, there's the protag, Caz, rough around the edges but ultimately determined to do what he can; Roy, the rig's cook who you can't help but quickly become somewhat attached to; Rennick, the a-hole of a boss; and plenty more. My advice: take your time to explore in the early stages of the game, before the horror kicks off. There's lots of background dialogue to listen in on and side characters to talk to, all of which helps bring the setting to life.All in all, Still Wakes The Deep is a great addition to the videogame horror genre and is well worth playing. Just be sure to use subtitles, particularly if you're from outside the UK, otherwise some of the slang might leave you confused!

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely beautifully written story told absolutely beautifully. It's fairly short by today's standards but, this game contains absolutely no filler. _childDocuments_.review: + I'm not really a fan of horror games where you can't fight back, but I found this game's setting interesting so I gave it a shot. And, indeed, the game's North Sea Scottish-operated oil rig makes for a pretty amazing location for a cosmic horror story. It's surprising how engaging the progression through its innards, as you struggle to fix collapsing infrastructure and save co-workers, can be despite the game being extremely linear. Credit to Beira D's design, it feels like a real-life oil rig (or at least how I imagine being on one is >.>), but also works great from a "gamey" level-design perspective, a tough balance to achieve IMHO.+ The voice acting is incredible and it's backed up by really well-written dialogue, allowing the charming Scottish lingo to shine (funnily translated into basic English in the subtitles). It builds up believable characters and a compelling protagonist in Caz MacLeary, adding a lot of weight to the myriad of emotional scenes peppered along the game's 4-hour playtime.+ Thankfully, the cosmic horror entity is not explained at all, just a terrifying, unknowable thing from the depths of the sea, released by the oil rig's drill, expanding, consuming all, leaving body-horror and tendrils in its wake and turning some of Caz's mates into disgusting monsters. It's also visually inspired by the Colour Out of Space, meshing a certain caustic beauty with the grotesque imagery.+ Audio-visually, the game uses Unreal Engine to great effect for a AA game. The locations look amazing, characters are detailed enough and the horror is impressively rendered, plus performance was without issues. The score is appropriately tragic as well, with a beautiful and sad song in Scottish-Gaelic during the end credits.- There were some animation bugs here and there, but nothing horribly distracting fortunately.* Hide-and-seek encounters and chase scenes are thankfully not tedious, something I can't really say about other horror walking simulators.* And yes, the game is very much a walking simulator, extremely linear and devoid of puzzles or any sort of mechanic difficulty, but I knew that going in and adjusted my expectations. I do understand how that can be deal-breaker for some.

_childDocuments_.review: Very short for the price (I spent at least an hour of my playtime not actually playing), but on the whole a high quality experience with horror elements and some subtle but distinct mechanics, most of which are well done, such as flashlight flickering and fading when pointed at monsters, meaning you never really get a good look at just what is hunting you, the ability to look behind you when fleeing so you can appreciate the drama of the situation instead of just hearing crashing noises behind you, and a parkour system which, whilst limited (the game is linear after all) does help sell the tension of the situation as you deal with death-defying situations.I wouldn't say it's a particularly good pure horror experience though, as it lacks enough openness to feel like failure is likely. Monsters are easily distracted in the same manner every time, so getting caught is unlikely during stealth sections. During chase sequences the game feels tense but not terrifying as the game is so linear there's no real risk of getting in an unwinnable situation, just hold the sprint button and point face in direction away from enemy.Story good, gameplay okay, sound design and visual design excellent (except for a few minor continuity errors where the devs either forgot or failed to realise you could see them). My only real story criticism is there's no real "aftermath" sequence where the outcome of the events of the game can be seen from an external perspective which would help put the events into context.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was excellent, one of the best atmospheric walking simulators I have ever played.Positives and Negatives:+ Jaw dropping gorgeous graphics.  The game ran perfectly on max settings 4K on my RTX 3070, which was interesting because on the forum some other people have been having troubles. Maybe its my beefy i9 CPU or 64gb Ram I am not sure. + The sound design was also fantastic, from the howls of the ocean waves to the howls of the monsters, everything was quality and felt big budget.+ The game moves at a brisk pace, there are no difficult puzzles to get stuck on or get frustrated+ The voice acting is superb, like a Hollywood movie+ Again, art direction and level layout is jaw dropping.+ The jumping and platforming sections were done right. Many FPS games do this wrong and these sections are usually frustrating. In this game the difficulty is perfectly balanced, fun and exhilarating.+ As with the platforming sections, there are a few stealth sections that were super tense and fun. I usually do not like stealth in games, but this game nailed it.  Perfectly balanced difficulty.- I beat the game in just 4.5 hours and actually tried to take my time with it.  So for some players this may be an issue because of the price per length of the game. - The subtitles cannot be turned off as of July 2024, this ruins the immersion and atmosphere of the game a tiny bit - The ending was anticlimactic and felt rushed.Rating: 9.5 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: Dan Pinchbeck is my favorite writer, and my biggest artistic inspiration. I've been looking forward to this game for a very long time, and I think it is well worth the wait. The atmosphere and character of the world that Pinchbeck builds is stunning -- both visually and narratively. I don't think that it's as profound of an experience as  or  but it's still compelling throughout, and the ending is just as emotionally impactful as the rest of his work (seriously, this guy knows how to write a good ending).For what it's worth, I've already played this twice in the past twenty-four hours, and I think I liked it even more on my second playthrough. I'm sad to see that Pinchbeck has left The Chinese Room, but I hope that he keeps up the great work, because I'll play any game or read any book that he writes.

_childDocuments_.review: I clench my cheeks over every beam suspended over the ocean, and hold my breath when I round a corner in the dark.  The atmosphere and sound design is top notch!  Its a breath of fresh air in the indie horror scene.  It was doing so well with the level, sound, and story that it almost took me out of the experience when I sat in a vent looking directly at a monster...a terrifying monster that sounds human, but a *wonky* acting monster nonetheless.  I feel like the "threat" of a monster that is up to our imagination, like going through one of the opening events, is far more nerve racking and intense than looking in the face of a derpy monster that clearly sees me. lol Games are games and I wont hold it against it too hard, i still have the rest of the game to play through,so far solid 8.5/10 for me

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, another great Super Mario Bros game, very nice!......But in all honesty, this is a really good Lovecraftian game without any lovecraftian fanservice (not that I'm all against it). NIce return of The Chinese Room. 8.5/10I enjoyed the gameplay, you walk, jump, crawl and swim trying to get through the labyrinths of pipes and oil rig constructions. You get:- a great feeling of being small and lonely human against an unknown force;- also a feeling that you are on the edge of your abilities, especially with swimming. It's evoking very natural fears and I love it;- portions of the game, where you avoid a monster, BUT it's pretty easy and not frustrating and you don't have to repeat things over and over (I personally hate hide and seek and running away from monsters sequences in horror games);- very sad story. But It's Lovecraftian, you have to understand there's no good ending in such stories;- really great dialog, I'm not good a scottish accent, but, aye, mate, who is? Subtitles helped. Also dialogs and characters reactions were VERY believable and seamlessly integrated; - very nice level design;- nice body-horror.You don't get much puzzles in the game. However you are given tasks to operate some machinery, push some buttons and being a low level worker on the rig you follow instructions given nearby.I didn't like what devs did with yellow paint. Yes, you can switch if off in the settings right before the game starts. But everything else leading the way will still be yellow. _childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. I have never fallen in love with a game so quickly, or connected so well with the characters before. I'm not a huge fan of playing horror games (in fact, I've never really played any before), but this one really caught my attention. The entity, the mutations, the setting, the voice acting, the interactions of the characters were all so  interesting. I so desperately wanted them to live, and the ending was so brutal but also important. I loved the story, and I don't mind a linear game. In fact, I like it more than an open world environment where I don't know where to go and I'm just wandering about for hours aimlessly. I had a little trouble with the controls at times, but it didn't stop me. My only huge gripe, if you can call it that, is knowing I will never see more of these characters and this story beyond what's in this game. I so wish I could see more of them in some way or the other. I loved how they talked to each other and wished I could see more of them, especially prior to the events of the game. The oil rig setting was so fascinating. The game itself played like an interactive movie, which was very enjoyable for me. This has somehow become my favorite game and I will play it more in the future, just to enjoy the story and characters again.

_childDocuments_.review: This was definitely giving me vibes of PREY and also John Carpenters The Thing. So if either of those vibe with you, I think you'll have a good time.It's got tons of great scares and monster encounters, doesn't over-rely on one type of scare or one type of monster experience. The Chinese Room is back to doing what they do best, but I was also pleasantly surprised that this feels more like a graduation from their earlier niche of horror-style walking simulator, to mainstream horror game. There's definitely more game-play compared to previous games which will make the game palatable to a wider audience.🟩 People have elsewhere stated they feel the game is too expensive for the playtime. But this is a product of quality, and I believe it's worth the price.🟩Story was was fairly good, and it avoided the game cliches of "it was all a dream" or "Player Character had a breakdown in the past and the game is them coming to terms with it", which was nice.🟩Characters are well written and crack some funny jokes. It relieves the tension a little bit, and for a handful of the characters I was genuinely caring about at the end.🟩Music and sound were extremely good. Really added to the atmosphere and the music never seemed like it was trying hard to force you to feel either scared, or emotional. The sounds are well done and really do give you that feeling of being on an oil rig at sea.🟩The levels were really detailed and the setting felt realistic, theres plenty of minor details to stop and observe, when your not being chased by 🟩The monsters are truly terrifying creations of guts and limbs. Think of the characters from elden ring that have too many appendages, now remove their skin... now make random parts of their anatomy huge, now make them talk to confirm they are indeed still alive and human-ish, now make it so you can sneak past them or run for it. Truly a lot more dynamic than their previous games.🟧If I had some minor complaints and these are indeed very minor... the game is hyper linear. There were a couple of times where what would seem a very obvious route to take was invisibly blocked, and sometimes when enter a new area, doors will magically just lock behind you. I would hope in future games TCR experiments with multiple endings and branching pathways and choices, there's nothing wrong with a linear game providing this level of detail, story and game play. But it would be nice to see them push the envelope in the direction of replay-ability.🟧Without spoiling too much, there's a certain violent event that occurs near the beginning of the story, after you first speak with the oil rig's boss, and sets everything else in motion. It would have been nice to get a bit of story detail later on in the story about either what originally happened, or at least some character's opinions on what the thing from the deep actually might be. We're left to do that ourselves, and while this game does indeed benefit extremely from having no idea what is really happening, it could have been interesting to have the story explore this direction a little.TLDR: If you are looking for a deep, scary, horror experience, this is one for you.

_childDocuments_.review: First up, the positives. The game looks gorgeous, plays very well, the soundscape and especially the voice acting is top notch and especially in the first part of your adventure, it's an absolute treat and it's a joy to get to new areas, explore them, learn about what's going on.The negatives though, I feel personally, outweigh the positives. The game is extremely linear and the storyline is predictable, lacking in any real depth. I think the linear aspect of the game pushes you so hard to go in a single direction always, there is a single path forward and you either follow that path, or you won't progress. And because a lot of the environmental troubles you face are going to be repeats of the same thing over and over, going over ledges, crawling on beams, swimming from one spot to another. The actual gameplay gets stale because it's not a hard game, the enemies aren't hard, most of the troubles you meet are quicktime events where you hold or press buttons to overcome them.The enemies as well, sadly don't have a lot of variety, they are creepy and cool the first time, but then you're faced with two situations, you either run away from them as they chase you, or you sneak around while distracting them by throwing stuff.What I really miss in a game like this, is being able to make choices, perform actions that change the outcome of certain situations, even if the end result would be the same, it would be really nice if you're not just moving from place to place doing exactly what the story needs and nothing else apart from looking at stuff, reading up.Would I recommend this? Probably a slight yes over no, but mostly for the first part of the experience and the character development that happens there, that stuff is great, everything else beyond that is just going through the motions more and more with every area you go to.

_childDocuments_.review: I know Chinese Room productions from Amnesia: A machine for pigs. That game was OK, just IMO didn't deserve the Amnesia tag. But this isn't about AAMFP.Still wakes the Deep has a lot going for it. I think the graphics are fantastic, and wow finally a flashlight that works like a real one! The sound really makes the game though, there is a ton of work and expertise in it. The mood, overall, really conveys to the player what's at stake, and how bad things are. There's a good mix of different puzzles, albeit they're about timing and simple controls more than anything. And that's where my negative comments come in:Sure, the game is designed to be "on rails" and you'll find that out after 30mins of play so if that's not your deal, just refund. But I went along with it. It bothered me more when I found out, than it did later in the game where it was obvious that the story telling needs the pacing, which requires "rails."I would have liked to see a few more "options" especially in the chase parts of the game. It always just comes down to timing.My review of this is a 8/10. Graphics and sound are really brilliant, story is good and carries itself to a logical conclusion. A bit more mechanics around dealing with the threat would have been very nice. I loved the playthrough, and I'm OK with the price point given the production values.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd love to be more positive, but this has been a bit of a disappointment for me. It's what you would expect from The Chinese Room: a walking, crawling and climbing simulator, - which would be fine if it wasn't as repetitive as it unfortunately is. There is little story progression and almost no variation in scenery. And what story there is didn't really grab me. I am a big fan of A Machine For Pigs as it struck the right balance of interactivity and walking simulator for me, - but most of all, it had a fascinating and often thought provoking story. That final monologue is still one of the most haunting things I've ever experienced in a game. Sadly, Still Wakes The Deep has none of that.Another thing that A Machine For Pigs did a lot better is the feeling of progression by climbing deeper and deeper into the machine whereas Still Wakes The Deep has you running in circles without a real feeling of progression.I'm still torn wether to recommend this game or not, - if there was a "mixed" option, I'd pick that. It's not a bad game for what it is, but having just recently replayed A Machine For Pigs, Still Wakes The Deep just feels lacking a lot in comparison.

_childDocuments_.review: The Chinese Room, who made an indelible mark in the memory with their first game Dear Esther in 2008, from the then newly emerging walking simulator/WS/ genre, have now served us a survival horror with a cinematic experience ala The ThingStory:*******Cameron McLeary, who is wanted by the Scottish police, is hired as an electrician on an oil rig. When his boss Rennick finds out, he decides to fire him. Before "Caz" leaves the rig, the driller comes into contact with a sea creature whose blood causes mutation of the human organism. The fight for life begins.gameplay:*********It's still WS, albeit much improved. You can run, pick up some things and throw them to distract the mutant crew, jump, or climb, which are not found in normal WS games. But it's still a corridor, so you only go in a certain direction with the impossibility of returning.Also, there is only one save, which is a problem, because if you miss something, only a new game will help you. The playing time is about 8 hours... when you search everything in detail.Graphics and soundtrack:********************The authors used Unreal Engine 5, but just like in their previous game Everybody's Gone to the Rapture, the optimization is not very good here. I have an I9 12900k and a GeForce RTX 3090 and the game went to a maximum of barely 50fps. Maybe you need to adjust the NVIDIA settings again, but I haven't tried that.The soundtrack is great.Achievements:***********You get 100% when you finish the game at least 2x. The only problem is finding the bodies of the crew... although fortunately those you have already found in previous games are counted.Overall evaluation:********************Except for the optimization, this is a quality survival horror. If you liked the movie The Thing, you must not miss this piece. For me, 9/10The Chinese Room,ktorí sa v roku 2008 nezmazateľne zapísali do pamäti svojou prvou hrou Dear Esther,z vtedy novovzniknutého žánru walking simulátor/WS/ nám teraz naservírovali survival horror s filmovým zážitkom ala The ThingPríbeh:*******Cameron McLeary,ktorého hľadá škotska polícia,sa nechá najať ako elektrikár na vrtnej ropnej plošine.Keď na to jeho šef Rennick príde rozhodne sa ho vyhodiť.Skôr ako "Caz" opustí plošinu,vrták sa dostane do kontaktu s morským tvorom,ktorého krv spôsobuje mutáciu ľudského organizmu.Začína sa boj o život.gameplay:*********Stále sa jedná sa o WS aj keď hodne vylepšený.Môžete behať,zbierať nejaké tie veci a hádzať ich aby ste odlákali pozornosť zmutovanej posádky,skákať,poprípade liezť čo sa v bežných WS hrách nenachádzajú.Stále je to ale koridor takže idete len určitým smerom s nemožnosťou sa vrátiť.Tak isto save je len jeden,čo je problém,pretože ak niečo vynecháte tak vám pomôže len nová hra.Herná doba je cca 8 hodín... keď podrobne všetko prehľadávate.Grafika a soundtrack:********************Autori využili Unreal Engine 5 ale tak ako aj v ich minulej hre Everybody's Gone to the Rapture aj tu je optimalizácia nie veľmi dobrá.Mám I9 12900k a GeForce RTX 3090 a hra išla na max sotva 50fps.Možno treba zase poladiť NVIDIA nastavenie ale neskúšal som to.Soundtrack je parádny.Achievementy:***********100% získate keď dohráte hru aspoň 2x.Problémový je len hľadanie tiel posádky...aj keď našťastie sa počítajú tie čo ste už našli v minulých hrách.Celkové zhodnotenie:********************Až na tú optimalizáciu sa jedná o kvalitný survival horror.Ak sa vám páčil film The Thing,tak tento kúsok nesmiete minúť.Za mňa 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This Horror Game Hits DifferentI really liked this. The setting itself is awesome. The oil rig looks (to my untrained eye anyway) very authentic and really adds to the game, it is a truly great setting for a horror game. In fact, even before things go wrong it's a great setting to have a walk around in. Not many of us will ever experience being on a working oil rig. It is super cool to walk around in. The characters and the voice acting are great too and very authentically Scottish. The language on display here might be more horrifying than the actual horror content, these rig workers do not hold back and their authenticity grounds the game and location really well. This helps the plot too as I really did root for some of these people to survive... others not so much, some people are just meant to be food lol.The story is actually one of the very (very) few I've been able to properly follow in a modern game, partly due to the runtime (just over 5 hours for me) and partly to the story not doing anything stupid, it all flows very nicely and everything makes sense, in a horror context anyway.This game is different to other horror games, this has a class and an integrity to it somehow. This is a really nice, very well made piece of gaming right here, well done to the hardworking and talented devs at The Chinese Room.

_childDocuments_.review: A game advertised for a "rich narrative" with "psychological horror" elements, which is in fact nothing more than a glorified walking simulator with quick time events. Gameplay: You walk or run around completing meaningless tasks to buy everyone aboard the ship more time. Occasionally there are scripted monster sequences which you have a path layed out in front of you and must sprint until you reach the next cutscene or scripted event. Yep, there are only a couple of moments where you must figure out how to get past a certain enemy by "playing it smart" (having to throw items across the room a couple of times to reach the next checkpoint). Basically, the encounter design is so shallow that it feels like the original Penumbra was ages ahead of this game, 20 years ago.Controls: Get ready for the most boring and in the beginning unintuitive and confusing control scheme in your life. You have to hold right mouse button to do just about anything, and have quick time events requiring you to react to scripted events. Also don't try running in this game because the player character is slower than a 90 year old man that hasn't run since he stormed the beaches at Normandy.Visuals and environment/level design: Outside areas aren't especially beatiful, they are definitely not bad, but the inside environments have a lot of love and research done to them and it clearly shows. It's a huge shame however none of these areas are ever utilized to their maximum with monsters. Navigating around the oil rig is impressively realistic, or so I would assume as I've not been on one, and I have to give props for this. However, the level design as I said, doesn't make proper use of a lot of areas, and that defeats the purpose so much. It's a shame really.Story: Prepare for a story you have seen everywhere in literally any piece of media. A linear story that starts in media res with the main character  IF YOU CAN'T WRITE A STORY, HIRE SOMEONE THAT CAN. I've seen players here calling it the "best story in a game they've played", but to me that's either a) pretentious or b) clear that these people have never played a videogame in their life. If you want to play a great horror game that has clearly inspired this game, play SOMA. You will see the difference.Horror/atmosphere: Atmosphere is sometimes there, most of the time it isn't, I personally was not really immersed due to the incredible timing of events, scripted sequences and just plain insane amount of "videogame logic" moments that this game has. When the game works, it works, but it quickly fades away sooo easily and you remember you're playing a game. You somehow create a detailed oil rig with humans on it and add cosmic horror, yet you completely manage to destroy the atmosphere. I think that has to be an achievement.Audio: One of the only highlights in the game, sometimes however the audio doesn't allow you to tell where the enemy is because it gets incredibly muffled. Generally good sound design, I don't remember a single track from the music except the credits.Game length: Absolutely inexcuseable to ask for 35 euros for a game will only play once in your life at 4 hours. Absolute disgrace, you should be ashamed of yourself to whoever/whichever team of executives sat down and decided that this price is good.TL;DR This game is a walking simulator, with a story as old as time, but at least it's nice to look and listen to. Super short and super expensive.WHO SHOULD BUY; Casual gamers that are trying to enter the horror genre. It's a super forgiving horror game that holds your hand all the way through.WHO SHOULDN"T BUY; People experienced in horror expecting the next thrill, like Silent Hill 2, SOMA, Amnesia: The Bunker or any other psychological horror game with monsters. You will be disappointed by the shallowness of the game in almost every sector.

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes The Deep takes players into a nightmarish setting aboard a 1970s oil rig in the harsh North Sea. The protagonist and crew members are authentically portrayed as Scots, their accents and dialogue adding to the game's sense of place.It's a linear first-person narrative horror game with light interactive elements.Powered by Unreal Engine, the game excels in its audiovisual presentation, bringing the oil rig to life with striking realism.The developers have crafted a believable, true to life design. Its claustrophobic corridors, creaking metal, and the fleshy biological outbreak create a palpable sense of dread.As the story unfolds, you witness the rig's transformation from a functional workspace into a nightmarish realm. The spreading infestation blocks and changes familiar routes into new unexplored areas.This keeps the scenery fresh but also ratchets up the suspense as you witness the rig's gradual descent into chaos.As you progress through the rig, the game presents a series of carefully crafted scenes and set pieces. The linear design guides you through the story, alternating between tense moments of occasional stealth sections where you avoid monstrous crewmates, exploration and scripted chase sequences. While you are not constantly in danger, these elements combine with the oppressive atmosphere to create a steady sense of unease.To me the game stands out from other recent horror titles. It delivers on its premise, offering a tense narrative. While the ending is sad, it feels fitting for the situation, and the journey to get there is worthwhile.For what the game is, Id give it Very Positive.

_childDocuments_.review: Having just finished the game I feel like i need to write a review. The game came recommended to me by quite a few of my friends so I figured I would give it a shot. However After completing the game i cannot bring myself to recommend it to others.The game has alot of good ideas, and alot of attention to detail in the design of the oil rig ascetically. But I feel that most of the mechanics and many of the major story beats fall short, I wont go into deep detail to avoid spoilers, but one of Roys major story beats just doesn't work like that in reality which took me out of the moment. Overall I found the first hour to two hours of the game to be interesting and enjoyable, but it quickly became a bit of a slog by the end. Most deaths don't feel impactful since only three characters really matter or get any real interaction, I would have preferred a slower burn before the crazy horror stuff started happening. More time to get to know characters, and to build up dread before the release.The enemy AI is quite poorly done, and you can tell when its going to be a chase scene or a cutscene because the monsters will stop doing their normal patrol paths and kind of spaz out until you leave cover so they can 'see' you and spark the instance. Not to mentions there is only really one kind of enemy, and they all move and act exactly the same.The psychological horror also feels tacked on, like it was put in just to tick a box. Its never really explained why your character is hearing the voices, and they dont have any meaningful reactions throughout the game at all, and the sequence after the climax of the story just doesn't really do anything in my opinion.TLDR the game has some good ideas. But it drags out some of them long enough to make them annoying, and the implementation of some of them just fall short of what they could have been or are just not useful in the context of the game.  I would not recommend purchasing this game at full price unless you want to support the devs, buy it on sale if you really love these kinds of games.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I write anything, I just want to say up front, that even though my review is negative overall, I don't do it lightly and it does not mean that this game is a 100% no-no from me. It has plenty of positives and many subjective matters, so please feel free to read more for more details and of course consider opinions of others.I really wanted to love this game, I saw some youtubers praising it, I was all the awards and grades on the steam store page, I love the lovecraftian themes and cosmic horror - this game had all the things going for it to be one of my favorites. I immediately decided to buy and play it. And I was really torn between adoration and confusion.First of all lets take obvious out of the way - the game is gorgeous! Visuals are amazing, the setting is very interesting and not commonly seen (atleast for me), a lot of work and love was put into the environment and a thought out layout of the rig. The atmosphere, the rain droplets on the window, the wind and the shiny oil, it all looks just stunning. The voice acting is second to none. The authentic accents give the game so much character and authenticity, even though I am not a native English speaker and it would be hard for me to understand everything without subtitles, I am glad that it was done that way. Makes it all feel so much more real. The overall development and pacing of the story feels nice, the environment gradually changes, everything that can go wrong does go wrong and the game has some nice surprises. But also this is where one of my main issue with the game begins.While being really well paced the game is also extremely short. I finished my first run at about 7.5 hours, and I was going out of my way to read everything, listen to everything, soak in the atmosphere of every room. Someone who would want to just breeze through the game would do it in less then 5 hours. Short and sweet is not a problem in and of itself, but considering the price of the game, which is 35USD at the time of writing, it is a lot to ask for 5-6 hours experience, which is also worsen by following points.Some of the things from gameplay standpoint feel not very polished and sometimes straight up buggy. While I have not encountered anything gamebraking, I had couple of just annoying and immersion-braking issues. The worst offenders are some of the bosses. Not to spoil anything, their movement and their limbs feel very buggy at times, several times one of them got stuck in some corner giving me and easy pass. Many character animations feel jittery and abrupt, especially when transitioning between jumping and climbing, and some throwable objects just get stuck in tight spaces so I have to restart from the checkpoint. Nothing is too crazy, but considering that the game is that short, it is a shame that it is not more polished from that perspective.Another thing is more a result of a general trope of horror games, but it is still annoying as ever. Many time you will see barricaded doors and passages that are magically opened after a cutscene, many way too convenient accidents, some trivial looking obstacles are impassible and some much more imposing ones are easily completed because they are marked with yellow paint (which to be fair can be disabled). At one moment the game teaches you that you can kick the locked gate open, but it never used in a gameplay ever again. Considering how much effort was put into creating the rig and all the attention to details, such moments feel really strange and videogamy.Being so short does not help the story either, in some cases. There are a lot of characters. A lot. And they all have names and some feelings to them. But the game does not let you get to know them very well. You just briefly get a chance to see some of them during the intro, and after that you mostly hear them on the phone or hear about them from other character. The only problem is that you have no chance to remember who is who and who has what name. It is very confusing that game keeps repeating their names to you but you had no time to attach the face or a character to that name. This is a real missed opportunity. Only couple of characters can be remembered, and only because you interact with them throughout the game constantly.The story is a very subjective matter. What I can say is that it is a very personal story but not very deep or very detailed, a lot of it left to imagination, a lot of it is needed to be read between the lines. Don't expect much explanation to what is going on. It is more about the journey of a character. I will leave it for you to decide if it is a good or a bad.The gameplay is also subjective. I am not a hardcore horror game player and it was ok for me, game does not rely on too many jumpscares, "boss" encounters do not happen too often (considering game's runtime) and they are on the easier side, but it is not a bad thing for me, Many more experienced and hardcore players will probably find the experience lacking, but it was quite nice for me.In conclusion, I want to say that unfortunately I can't recommend this game with clear conscience. It is not a single issue, it is just a lot of small problems and details adding up together to be too much. If it would be a cheaper game I would definitely recommend it, but considering it's price, runtime, and combination of issues I have to do the "thumbs down".

_childDocuments_.review: I love games and stories where the main setting is the setting for the whole game, and the entire environment is utilized for the telling of story.   (i.e, MGS2, Reservoir Dogs, etc.)Good tight environments and definitely scary moments. The mystery of sea is what compelled me to finish the game, however the ending was quite lackluster and it disappoints me a little because the rest of the game was great up to the last hour. I really wanted to at least find out the mystery behind all the weird ♥♥♥♥ happening in the water and the infections, but with this ending focused mainly on the psychology of our main character, I am left wondering if any of that was even real. Other than that, pretty great game and great graphics. Some framerate problems here and there but that's about it for my complaints.Good experience.Oh yeah, and the Scottish voice acting was great.
