_childDocuments_.review: So far, after four hours of playing (with some breaks in between), the game has been really good. It's not quite what I was expecting after seeing some favored YouTubers talking about playing it, but it is still a great game.I do want to point out, the game has a Standard and Story mode option for gameplay. I noticed a lot of Reddit reviews stating the story mode takes out chase scenes and having to sneak or engage with the enemies--it does NOT. It only limits how difficult these encounters are. So if you saw the reviews stating story mode is a walking sim that your grandma can play for the story line without having to rush like I did, they are wrong. This isn't a search and find or collection based game--it is a walking sim in a lot of ways, but there are encounters where you do have to sneak and sometimes run away. I noticed a lot of comments stating there are only three of these events in the entire game for story mode--that is also not true. At three hours in (not knowing how close to the finish I am), I have already had six encounters on story-mode. Not exactly what I wanted for a story mode option as, after reading reviews, I was hoping to be able to relax and not severely panic during chase scenes (IRL personal issues), but it isn't too terrible. I do want to add after finishing the game at 11.7 hours, there were more like 10-15 chase scenes in total. You can try to sneak through many, but several still end in a chase regardless of how well you sneak. There are some jump scares where you have to press whatever button is specified. There are many events where you have to run through obstacles to escape areas, both during chase scenes and areas that are, not timed, but you do have a short period before disaster hits if you're not quick.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Still Wakes the Deep offers solid graphics and level design, with decent mechanics that keep gameplay smooth. The voice acting and characters feel realistic, adding depth to human emotions that play a big role in the narrative. However, the story itself lacks uniqueness, making the overall experience feel average. With a playtime of around 5 hours, it’s a moderately engaging but mediocre game that might not justify its price tag, but I’d still recommend it for those who appreciate character-driven atmospheres and a haunting vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent story with some pretty mediocre gameplay.The whole time it felt like "the Thing" meets "Annihilation".The setting being on an oil rig is very unique and I know nothing about oil rig but it feels like the developers did a LOT of research on how oil rigs operate to make this one feel authentic and use it for very interesting scenarios.All of the dialogue is excellent and really helps make the characters feel like real people.Big recommendation even if it is a little expensive for how long the game is.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: As with all Chinese Room games I've played the story telling is immaculate. Visuals, voice acting and sound are most impressive. Controls are a bit finnicky and could be smoother, especially during swimming sections. At times you had to find the exact spot in which a button prompt would enable and to do that under stress of drowning was true horror, my goodness gracious, I almost quit out. At a point or two I also got caught on seams in the environment and had to jump over them, if you're too fast you may start talking over yourself having triggered 2 voice lines simultaniously, and once I got into an seemingly infinite death loop, but the game sorted that out itself thankfully (well coded, ty, devs). There are also a great deal of accessibility option aside from all other standard options. I am unsure about the FPS cap though.The murky waters here with oil ontop are the true highlight to me, immensely terrifying.I appreciate the realistic details, such as going down on all four to traverse beams, as any sane person would in real life. None of this idiotic balancing on 2 legs when your life depends on it. That you also have to warm up on heaters after being submerged in ice cold water, thank you, you don't survive those temperatures for long. The banter between crew mates was fun too and added much life to the story.It's really really good existential horror. Walking sim, I don't agree. I got turned around some, especially in water, and so you can actually get lost, if only for a short while, even though, yes, the game is linear. There is some platforming, QTEs, stealth sections, chase sequences, all of which you can fail and die to, but no, you cannot defend yourself in hand to hand combat in any other way than to struggle free if the option presents itself. Some people just like to call anything that don't have gunplay walking sims. Like Outlast, or Super Mario.Story is open for some interpretation so if that annoys you more often than it intrigues you and makes you think, maybe stay clear. At the heart of it it's about acceptance I would say. If you like Alien, Lovecraft, John Carpenter and David Cronenberg you may very well enjoy it.*Playing again the sound design is possibly the best I've ever played in my life and def the highlight of the game*
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Although its a unique story and visually appealing, it really isn't a horror game. Its creepy all throughout but its not really interactive to keep throwing cans to make a monster go to a corner of a room multiple times. Just felt like being told a story while hitting a few keys. Not worth the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Should video games get political?  That's a question that has hung over the gaming community for a long time, especially since the mid-2010's and the era of Gamergate.  Some have argued that games should be divorced from politics and should focus solely on escapism.  Others argue that games are inherently political, and removing politics from them is an impossible task.Enter , a game about an oil rig worker trying to survive the aftermath of a disaster and escape a cosmic horror.  But it could also be about a man running away from his issues and only realizing his mistakes when it might be too late to fix them.  Or it could be about the plight of blue collar workers and how they have to face the consequences of an incompetent manager's decisions.In reality it is all of these things and more, because the nature of stories and even art itself is that it carries with it the feelings, beliefs and yes, politics, of its creators and the parts of the world they hail from.  It is impossible for a creative mind to create something out of thin air.  It comes from somewhere, whether it's inspired by the stories they experienced in their youth or the beliefs they developed when they grew up.And if anything,  would feel less inspired without these influences.  Granted, the politics are a small part of the game, but they are there nonetheless.  In terms of gameplay  isn't anything too special: you run, jump, complete quicktime sequences to avoid death, and create distractions to sneak around monsters.  It isn't reinventing the wheel in that sense.  But the story it tells is breathtakingly authentic, thanks to the research that went into making the oil rig feel like a real environment and the use of real Scottish voice actors for the cast.  In fact, my only major gripe is one underwater section that introduced a mechanic the game didn't explain very well, which resulted in looking up what I was supposed to do after dying several times.The elevator pitch for  is that it is  on an oil rig, and that is a very good summary.  But it is also more than that.  And while the debate about whether politics or wokeness or DEI or whatever dumb buzzword they latch onto next will undoubtedly continue, the fact remains that as video games catch more eyes and bring in a more varied audience, they will only become more interesting.And if you're afraid of that well...I guess that's a "you" problem.

_childDocuments_.review: So I've played this for like an hour and I gotta say: Don't buy it. It is literally just a pacifist obstacle course with intense music masquerading as a survival horror. If you don't believe me WATCH all trailers and that is literally about everything in this game so far (minus any fights because I don't think there are any. Really). You'll also notice the player never has any items in his hands... probably because there isn't an inventory system, let alone a combat one This game consists of: 0) Locked doors on an oil rig. -Hope you like finding another way around!  1) Making you 'jump', 'crouch' and 'interact' in a painfully predetermined fashion with little variation or creativity. The controls also feel somehow very appropriate yet poorly mapped in a way you can't really change. You can pick up things in your hands but you can't really do much with them as I recall-No inventory system, health bar, crafting, etc... Just you.-I mean, you'd think a survival horror on an oil rig may involve more creative use of things around you, but nope. Just run through hallways and down stairwells.2) "Narrative" cut-scenes that go from being kinda watchable to quickly feeling like they are strangling you on your couch while you debate whether to skip them or sit there listening for 3 minutes (you can't move during them)NOTE: They all end in you going on a fetch quest because 3) Despite what the trailer says, there actually isn't any fighting (at least not so far, 1 hour in). -No signs of me having an inventory or being able to punch, kick, swing, shoot. So dumb.4) All the scary parts are heavily manufactured as if they are just interactive cut-scenes that are banking on intense graphics and loud music to be fun.Maybe just go buy an identical but much better game like "Alien: Isolation". -That game at least makes you think you can shoot things because it actually gives you a few guns, a clear opponent, simple but immersive survival mechanics and all the fetch quests you could ask for. -It also has an alien!-Asura's Wrath is dope too if you like interactive cut-scenes, fun story and cool game styles.Basically I would maybe pay $10-15 for this. Great graphics (but needs optimization) and awesome voice acting, but nothing really... gameeeee. I wanted a video game, not a $40 story.

_childDocuments_.review: One part Alien Isolation, mixed with the Thing and Deepwater Horizon. This was easily one of the best horror games I've played in the last year. Some people may not be a fan of how linear and simple the gameplay is, but if you're looking for a short, expertly paced horror game, this is it. Definitely worth picking up if you're a horror fan.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: I won't say much besides that this game, from the horror and scares, to the narrative and acting, to the music and visuals, excels in practically all that it tries to do. Don't expect a twelve-hour-long, game-play focused roller-coaster, but that is not what it is attempting to do, and that does not make it any lesser of an experience. It is easily one of the most riveting story and horror games that I've played in recent memory, and I won't spoil the experience by writing more about it. It's inspiration from classics like 'The Thing' is clear, and all else that I can say is to go into this game as blind as you can, and enjoy the ride.

_childDocuments_.review: I have changed my POV for this game many times while the duration of playing it.TL;DR: Would rate about 6/10Pros+ Scottish voicing+ You do not need to curse, the characters will it all the time you want to do it+ Well done animations, arts & details+ You play on an oil rig+ Asssassins Creed on an Oil Rig with scottish ranting. The movement system is kinda even good+ Somewhat of a good story, at least the emotions delivered are good+ You can throw things at monsers (is even an archivement)+ The crew teamship is very well doneCons- It is just pressing some given buttons or run to given points without the need for thinking. It is just an run from A to B game and sometimes press buttons- Many things don't make sense and are very movie-like impossible- No alternative routes, it is just a chain of things you will definetly passInbetweens (I bought the game by accident, so these will be very subjective)~ Permanent anxiety, although after passing the first monster encounter I turned it into a "speedrun", because there is not realy a danger and if you get caught just start 10m behind your death spot.~ Movement is sometimes unneccessary slow~ Not to be able to jump to positions which you should clearly be able to jump to is crazy. While you may feel the price is steep for the 5-7 hours you'll get out of it, I still highly recommend this title, especially if you love  or  minus the action.My biggest praise for this title is the fact that progression felt natural, the flow from scene to scene didn't hold my hand.

_childDocuments_.review: A truly fantastic cinematic horror game, perhaps the best one I've played in a long time. Awesome monster designs, excellent dialogue that can be legitimately funny or heartbreaking at the right times, and great narrative pacing. I'd compare this game more to the likes of Soma, where there is actual gameplay elements like sneaking past or running away from monsters, throwing things to distract them, etc. but the main draw is the atmosphere and story. To me, this game is the perfect culmination of all the narrative games the Chinese Room has made in the past. Heavy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly well designed game, beautiful in both visual and audio design. The voice actors are excellent, and by the end I was feeling so connected to the characters. Reminded me a lot of SOMA (one of my all time favorite games), both in how spooky and thought-provoking the story was. Insane choice of environment, too; I remember when I first saw the trailer I knew the game would be good solely based on the information that it was a horror story set in quite possibly the most remote of settings. Chinese Room really hit this one out of the park!

_childDocuments_.review: I loved playing this Game. The mechanics are simple and easy to get around. The story is fantastic, the voice acting is AAA and UE graphics superb. I usually do not play horror games because of the overuse of jumpscares and complicated game mechanics but this one is simply a gem. pretty linear gameplay, you cant really get stuck since it always goes into one direction. _childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review: 100% recommend this game to anyone who wants an experience. The visuals are stunning, the soundscapes are amazing, the atmosphere is incredible, and the voice acting is beyond a doubt some of the best I've ever heard in a game. Anyone who wants a big bombastic game with lots of combat and exciting action? This probably isn't for you. This is an environment you want to invest yourself into, and all-around a great environment to become immersed in, and if you're playing this expecting a fight-for-your-life monster-killing action game then you're doing yourself and the game an injustice. Love the characters, love the story, love the atmosphere, but don't ask for something it's not advertised as.I do have to mention though, as much as I love the experience I had with this game, it was shockingly hard on my PC to run. Despite having at least the recommended PC requirements, in most cases better, I still had to turn down all the graphical settings to the lowest I could stand, and I was even then getting occasional frame jumps and big lag spikes, all while my poor PCs fans are running like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ airplane the entire time - especially noticeable while entering the deck (perhaps the water graphics?) and ESPECIALLY whenever there were a lot of moving parts or people on screen. I'm incredibly grateful for my noise-cancelling headphones, else the PC trying to take off would've absolutely drowned out the game audio. Despite all this, I did still enjoy my time playing, but it was often distracting to be having to pause and wait for the lag spikes to pass.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

_childDocuments_.review:
STILL WAKES THE DEEP is a first-person narrative horror from The Chinese Room, creator of Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs, Everybody's Gone to the Rapture, and Dear Esther. 

In STILL WAKES THE DEEP, you are an off-shore oil rig worker, fighting for his life through a vicious storm, perilous surroundings, and the dark, freezing North Sea waters. All lines of communication have been severed. All exits are gone. All that remains is to face the unknowable horror that's come aboard. 

Search for your crew and help them survive if you can. Run, climb, and swim through the flooding corridors and storm-lashed outer decks. Face a terrifying, unrelenting foe. And pray that, one day, you get to see your family again.
_childDocuments_.name: Still Wakes the Deep

name: Bramble: The Mountain King
detailed_description: Bramble The Mountain King takes you on a gripping and unsettling journey through stunning environments. Take on the role of Olle, a young boy setting off to rescue his sister, kidnapped by a dreaded troll. Not everything in Bramble is exactly how it seems - in this strange land with creatures big and small, you must be careful when to approach and when to hide. Many hungry and spiteful beasts lurk in these forests and caves. Watch your step.... Call upon the Spark of Courage, an enchanted fragment granting the gifts you need to endure the pitfalls and trials in your path. Defeat the horrid creatures you encounter in different and unique ways. Be warned, courage without kindness can take you down a dark path. Adventure as Olle, a brave boy who sets off to rescue his sister. A beautiful yet dangerous world to explore. Encounter twisted, mythical creatures from Nordic folklore for epic-scale boss battles. Tense, heart-pounding moments with hi-end visuals to match.

_childDocuments_.review: What a gorgeous and well-done game. I hope everyone wondering if it's worth it to definitely give this game a chance. I'm pretty much a wimp when it comes to horror games, but I love learning more about tales and myths of countries around the world so I was too intrigued to let the horror part deter me. I did my first runthrough of this game all in one sitting and it was so much fun to play. I was sufficiently scared by the well-done jumpscares and terrifying scenarios but I loved how after each boss fight, you got the story and lore behind the monster. The ending was extremely well done as well. Highly recommend!!! Great work :)

_childDocuments_.review: 4/10, I sort of recommend this game but not at the current pricetag.I loved the gorgeous atmosphere, which is the game's main selling point, but the game fails to reach farther than that. Somewhat janky platforming, stiff animations and forced camera angles makes for a generally unpleasant experience. The devs seem generally inexperienced rather than lazy which is something I personally can respect. They obviously spent a lot of time on the graphics and sound. I acknowledge the potential of the game and I hope that it has been a good learning opportunity for the devs.I personally don't think that the game is worth 30 usd in its current state but at the same time I would not want to dissuade anyone from purchasing the game if they are really into it.My final thoughts are that it's a worse Little Nightmares but it makes excellent use of nordic folktales and mythology, a theme you'd be hard-pressed to find much of in the gaming community.For anyone who likes the aesthetic of the game I reccomend searching for the name John Bauer, the artist which this game borrows a lot of inspiration from. You can even find some of his paintings within the game and the character Tuva is based on a character from his paintings (Tuvstarr).Shoutout till hen som lade in 1 kilo mjöl postern XD.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly i expected more from this. The high praises and reviews set my expectations really high, but in the end the game was just ok, nothing more. If you're a fan of little nightmares or other 'creepy' games, then pick this up. However if you're looking for a great puzzle platformer for either the puzzling or platforming, then i don't know if this game can satisfy those needs. It's not really a great horror game either because it's more disturbing/disgusting than it is scary. The story then remains as the determining factor for this game and once again i felt that it fell short. This is subjective ofcourse, as many people seemed to have liked the story. The visuals and OST are a real treat though and the game is worth experiencing on that merrit, just not at this pricepoint.The platforming in this game is pretty basic. The character, being just a little kid and all, controls pretty poorly. The walking speed is slow and he doesn't jump very high. This makes sense but doesn't make for particularly engaging platforming. It works well for the stealth sections though, which were the highlight as far as gameplay is concerned. However the stealth is also pretty barebones. There's no distractions you can cause to confuse the enemy, just waiting until they've moved on so you can get a move on. There's also puzzles to do but these were very basic. They were never particularly creative or challenging, just a small obstacle to overcome to move to the next area or avoid detection from the monsters.Speaking of monsters there's a handfull of 'boss fights' in this game. They vary in quality but all of them suffer from the sluggish controls so they're mechanically simple to compensate for that. Thematically they're great though, each boss behaves and looks vastly different. It's just on the actual gameplay front that they fall a bit short. They're also quite creepy for sure, but not scary. In fact there's not a single scary area in the game except for one tiny section in a dark house. This part was tense and the one i'd consider true horror but this part was only a few minutes long. The rest of the game is more unsettling or disturbing than it was dreadfull. I had hoped for more parts akin to what little nightmares does so well.The story was pretty dark, especially that of the background characters and monster backstories. However the main narrative, despite a few dark moments, feels like a lighthearted fairytale in comparison. Without spoiling anything the ending left me dissatisfied, as if the whole game amounted to nothing. The voice over that narrates the whole experience was great though, all of the audio is. The sound effects, voice acting, monster noises and music were all great and the strongpoint of the game in my opinion. The visuals were also very striking but only from a distance. Whenever the camera came closer the game lost it's visual flair. Most of the times though the setpieces and scenery worked, and the game had a consistent artstyle that had some dreamworks accents sprinkled on top.At least the whole experience ran pretty well but for that price it'd better. I had some minor bugs such as the character getting stuck on some geometry but for the most part it's fine. The clunky controls were more of a nuissance though, they made all the gameplay a bit stale and the narrative didn't strike me enough to keep me engaged over this dull gameplay. Had the game played better, had a more memorable story or been much scarier then i'd be satisfied but as it stands i'm not happy with my purchase. Most people seemed to enjoy it though, so chances are pretty high you'd enjoy it too, it just wasn't for me so it gets a thumbs down.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely excellent. I don't think I've ever seen a game with atmosphere done so damn well. And the music, especially during the final boss fight (that was a really nice touch), just wow. Can highly recommend. Even though it is a bit pricey for relatively short playtime (about 4 to 5 hours), the effort that went into this is totally worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Beautiful visuals with lots of details, nice chromatic palette and great atmospheric lighting.- Gorgeous world with many different locations and strong horror/eerie atmosphere. It's something between a dream and a nightmare.- Engaging storytelling and deep lore based on Nordic folklore. Magic blends with emotional moments, peculiar creatures and old legends perfectly.- Great direction and cinematography with nice camera movements, epic sceneries, and awesome cut scenes. It also has good pacing with constant alternations between darker/horror scenes and brighter/calm ones.- Exceptional sound design with convincing environmental sound and tons of creepy, weird ones during the darker regions.- Atmospheric narration with great voice acting performances.- Absolutely amazing score inspired by Nordic folk music too. It gets you immersed and fits perfectly to the rest of the game aesthetics.- Imaginative design of the creatures and enemies. Some of them are really unique.- A lot of splatter moments, corpses, blood and deaths for a game that initially looks like an innocent fairytale. Some scenes are really creepy and you'll die in dozens of different ways.- Decent physics. It's also nice that vegetation and other objects are moving as the characters walks on them. It makes the world feel more realistic.- The books with the fairytales are well illustrated and let you learn more about the lore. A nice addition.The bad- It has some scattered nice ideas, but overall the gameplay is shallow with worn sessions inspired directly by other games (e.g. "Little Nightmares") like avoiding enemies' light, hiding behind obstacles or in tall grass. Stealth mechanics are mediocre, platforming sequences are too simplistic and some QTES here and there are boring. It doesn't offer anything fresh.- Olle's movements are a bit awkward and feel clunky. Some controls are imprecise, especially when jumping and climbing. Other mechanics during boss battles are problematic too. Camera angles can get frustrating from time to time.- Archaic puzzle design. Puzzles are extremely simplistic and uninspiring. It needed something cleverer.- It's nice to be cinematic, but there are many ways to implement it. Especially during the first half there are small cut scene interruptions literally every minute of actual gameplay with a result of ruining the pace you're into and make you feel like not having the full control.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The mountain king takes from games like little nightmares and Inside but instead of the dark backgrounds of little nightmares and the muddy art style of inside, Bramble combines beautiful scenery seamlessly with the more dark and horror themed parts. Seriously this game doesn't miss when it comes to visuals. Every part of the game nails the visual aspect. It's not just the bright jaw dropping parts that stand out, it's the creepy and occasionally brutal moments as well. Usually you can see glimpses of the next boss in the background if you look carefully and it ads to the general uneasiness you feel. The only part i thought felt off is the character models, they look a bit like dolls and so don't really fit in with the realistic graphics. Also the movement can feel a little stiff and animations are a bit jittery however nothing too major. The camera movement and positioning are god tier and really adds to the incredible scenery. Lastly i think there could have been for verity when it come to boss design, the first half of the game it's the same twisted troll looking dudes. One with a lamp, another with a violin and one with a skull mask, this improves after you get to the succubus lady, and i get that the troll dudes are important in Nordic mythology/folklore but still some verity would be nice. Gameplay is simple move forward and occasionally solve a puzzle or fight a boss much like the games it took inspiration from but now you can move in full 3D not just the left and right of inside, but don't get it wrong it's still a linear game with one path to take. Speaking of taking inspiration from inside you know that part where you have to move from cover to cover, avoiding those sonic booms pulses? well this game uses that idea 3 different times, they are all different in some way to keep it interesting but still a little much in my opinion. You get a get a shiny rock in the beginning of the game to use as a light, then later it becomes your weapon to fight bosses. This is a cool way to keep things simple while still having some sort of combat that doesn't need more than one button. Another difference from the others games is that they didn't really have boss fights. Bramble has a more mainstream style to the boss fights, that's not to say it's bad, in fact i thought some of them were pretty cool and interesting but in most cases you just shine light in there eyes a few times then win.The game is really very good and definitely deserves some awards. There is no real big complaints apart from that price. As of time of writing it been out for a few months and i'm sure it will go down in price eventually at full price it's £25 for a full 4 hour game is asking for a lot. It also lacks the replay-ability. Little nightmares had new game + as well as tones of hidden stuff to look for and inside had a few collectables that unlock a secret ending and is a 1/3 the price of Bramble that only has a few wooden statues to get to only see for a few moments before the games ends. But that's up to you, £25 for 4 hours of a great game or wait for a sale? i'll leave that to you.

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a dark fairytale based on Nordic folklore. It's a story about a younger brother in search of his older sister who got kidnapped by a troll. During his search he comes across all kinds of fantasy creatures, some friendly and some dangerous. If you are a fan of games like Little Nightmares you will love this game as well. Great presentation, design, sound, music and atmosphere. It's basically a platformer/puzzle game with some bossbattle mechanics here and there while facing of the evil creatures of the bramble forest. At times this game can get really, and I mean REALLY dark in its themes and does not shy away from gore and gruesome acts. This game doesn't have a M (18+) rating for nothing. Personally I loved the setting and the tone and with it's 4-5 hour runtime it's a nice little fantasy horror game to lose yourself in. Some parts of it are truly beautiful, even more so because of the dark parts. 8.5 out of 10, highly recommended if you like these types of games, just not for the faint of heart or people who do not like children getting hurt.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Very pretty game, but imo the short length doesn't justify the price. 30 bucks for a six hour game? I got it on sale and I still feel cheated. Price aside, I also thought the plot was very hard to follow. For a story focused game, there was not much in the way of exposition or lore to understand who the characters were or why they did what they did. It's basically a gorgeous version of Limbo or Inside.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I have received my copy for free. I have been waiting for this game for several month after playing the demo and the preview. I did not expect receiving a key, so I already planned to buy the game.I am not a controller player pe-se, but I decided to play it with a controller after the first minutes of gameplay. In my opinion it is best to be played with a controller.The story setting is just awesome and so are visuals and sound. I loved every minute of this game and I will play it again. It took me around 6-7 hours to complete the game on stream (chat interaction always eats a lot of time), so it should provide around 3-5 hours of pure gameplay.The game reminded me a lot of Little Nightmares, but it is different in quite some aspects, so just putting it into the same bin feels kind of wrong.The hole game lives from the awesome atmosphere and visuals: It does a constant switch between uplifting and beautiful visuals and then converges into still beautiful but also dark settings.The only thing that might be criticised could be the price point. Would I buy this game for 29,99 €? Yes, I totally would. I expected the game to be released maybe for 20-25 €, so it's a bot above my expected range (leaving the release discount of 10% aside). The Game delivers 3-5 hours of breathtaking gameplay that made me shiver several times. The soundtrack is perfectly aligned with the story. This is mich more I could say about a lot of AAA titles that might deliver 60 hours up of gameplay that grows tedious after a short time.Thank you for this awesome experience! It has been one of the best this year so far. I hope there will be more like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wondered what it's like to be part of a folklore fairy tale? Because this game.. this game will show you.Bramble: The Mountain King has the good and the bad, the funny and the disturbing all rolled into one game. Though the play-through is a bit on the short side, the story, scenery, music and gameplay itself make it well worth your time and money. I felt pulled into the story and like I was actually in that world. The suspense and humor were on point and well-timed. The game was challenging but not so much that it detracted from the story, in fact it added to it.I couldn't have asked for a better experience, and I truly hope to see more games like this from these devs in the future because WOW!

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a horror buff for about 3 decades, and I rarely re-watch movies, much less re-play games. the art and game-play aren't much to turn the nose at, absolutely solid. but the story, and the telling of the story are absolutely, horrifyingly beautiful. I could say so much more about this title, but too much can, in fact, be too much. 9.2 out of 10, will be playing again. Don't sleep on this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Story book walking simulator with beautiful graphics and very cool references to fairy tails.The game includes some limited and not-challenging platforming and repetitive boss encounters that require you to hide behind walls and rocks during regularly timed attacks. Overall, nice story but the gameplay is rather boring and repetitive.  This would be worth getting on sale for about $5 and playing when you need a break from more engaging games.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Branmble is truly like a story book. It's cute, it's imagery is as vivid as it is verdant, and it is deeply dark. It's a short game that won't outstay its welcome. The puzzles are fun, not too hard and sometimes even satisfying. The game ran well, though for some reason the options screen from the main menu was on my second monitor while I played the game. But I only had a couple frame drops in one or two areas while playing this on max settings.The game had a couple shocking gore moments. In many ways it reminded me of Little Nightmares. The attention to folklore was mostly well done. The strongest parts of this game are its aesthetic and score. The horror was effective at points but I feel like all the threats being one shots kind of undermined the building of that tension. That is a small complaint though because this game is still a full package! Very much enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: You get to run around in a magical Scandinavian forest as a miniature human while looking for your missing sister. On your journey you'll encounter various mythological creatures from the Nordic folklore and you get to learn a bit about some of it. Throughout the game you get to enjoy enchanting music and mesmerizing visuals. For better or worse the game is really short, but that makes it an amazing game to just sit back and take your time through it all without the risk of getting bored. The surprising amount of gore might also help with that aspect, it certainly kept me awake. And oh yeah, there's puzzles in the game and each boss fight bring its own unique challenge for the player to overcome. I loved it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is só much darker than I had anticipated, but it is also emotional, beautiful and sometimes even cute (looking at you, baby gnomes!). Also I love John Bauer so it was wonderful to see some of his creations back in the game. :) The music was amazing, with that high old Nordic folk singing and raw fiddle sounds (reminded me of Gåte). Can really recommend this, especially if you like grim nordic folk tales. Although I do advice you to use a controller and not a keyboard. It is doable with keyboard if you're careful but I fell to my death several times because I walked in slightly the wrong direction. :D

_childDocuments_.review: From the first hour I wanted to write a review but I had a hope for some real puzzles and more game play than running and jumping. But again nice graphics and environment. I would recommend it in 12$ price range.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, so this will be my first ever steam game review, and for a good reason.♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this game is a pearl. Went into it, starting to expect a kids game, thinking "what the hell did my buddy recommend me?" - 20 minutes later, I was switching between being in awe, melancholic, and terrified all at the same time. The game plays on norwegian, swedish and finnish folklore, which caused it to affect me deeply as a norwegian. Lots of my childhood fear were now brought to life, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ are they well done and terrifying. On the other side, the game looks and sounds freaking incredible. The songs nearly brought tears to my eyes a few times, and several times I had to stop up and just watch the screen, because of how beautiful it was. Story wise, it captures the player and makes you emotionally invested in it - who doesn't relate to sibling love, and fear of losing someone you love? The controls are the only thing I can criticize at some point, but it didn't nearly ruin my experience with it.TL;DRVisuals: 10/10Sound & Music: 10/10(The Huldra bossfight and final bossfight music is EEEEPIC)Fear, fright & jumpscares: 7/10Story: 7/10Controls & gameplay: 6/10Staying true to norwegian, swedish and finnish folklore: 12/10. This game is truly worth the money. Total playtime around 5-6 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR : Little Nightmares, but on Nordic folklore steroids. I wish they also gave some to the controls.Exploring the captivating world of Nordic folklore myths was an absolute treat, and I loved how they blended in with the narrative. Speaking of the story, while the main plotline didn't leave me in awe, the "side" stories packed a powerful punch. Moments like The game offers a nice take on horror, making it appealing even to those not typically drawn to the genre. The atmosphere is well-crafted, transitioning from eerie to gory to downright disturbing. Special shout-out to The game's aesthetics are nothing short of beautiful, and the level design melds perfectly with the world. You don’t feel like following an obvious, linear path laid out in front of you.The boss battles have some original and cool concepts, cleverly executed and staged for maximum impact. The game has a pretty slow start; the first 30/45 mins are kind of boring but then it gets gradually better pretty quick.While the level design is nice, it can also be tricky. Occasionally, perspectives can lead to unexpected falls, and moments when you think you're safe behind a rock or something, but surprise, you are not.The major downfall, though, lies in the controls. They feel somewhat stiff and, coupled with the level design issues I just mentioned, they led me to several frustrating deaths, briefly pulling me out of the immersive experience.Overall, it was a very good experience. I recommend it and I would give it a strong 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: A linear adventure following a brother and sister who disobeyed their mother and ventured into the forest after dark. At first, the world they've found is full of wonder, but the story gets darker, when the older sister is kidnapped by a troll. The young brother needs to brave the dark corners of the land to save his sister. The gameplay is largely linear, with a few collectables strewn along the levels. The camera is fixed-angle. There's some climbing, a lot of stealth-puzzles (where you need to move from cover to cover, avoiding insta-death line of sight), and even some combat. There some truly memorable enemy encounters, and the many influences of Nordic folklore are very impressive.  I honestly expected the game to be yet another 2d platformer about a small child lost in a dark world, so what this turned out to be truly surprised me. Bramble is steeped in old-school design, but it is a wonderful title nonetheless, with truly memorable encounters, and a wonderful mix of puzzles, combat, stealth and platforming. One of the most under-appreciated titles of the past few years.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique atmospheric game with the best OST. Both beautiful and scary. As a folklore fan I recognized a lot of the fairytales used in the game. The game looks stunning and the story keeps you on your toes for the whole playthrough. The controls for PC are not optimal, then again, it's not a difficult game to play. I might say I got to experience more thanks to miss jumping or falling off thanks to the controls from time to time. Checkpoints are very forgiving so it didn't bother me at all. It's a short game for the price but small studio's need to start somewhere and also have mouths to feed. I definitely recommend.

What few issues I had with the game (mainly a few wonky controls/camera moments) were completely outshone by the rest of this somewhat short, but thoroughly enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is as gorgeous as it is horrifying, with surprises lurking around every corner. The game excels at building tension and suspense while maintaining visual splendor throughout.Phenomenal indie game, every battle feels unique, the Nordic mythology and culture is spilling through the screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble masterfully balances two contrasting atmospheres; one moment, you find yourself in a serene and enchanting world with little creatures and so much light... only to be thrust into a sinister and gory environment the next. This dynamic shift keeps the gameplay immersive and intriguing, as you never quite know what to expect around the corner. However the gameplay could use some improvement, particulary with the camera angles. There are moments when this plus some not so responsive controls can really become frustrating, detracting from the overall experience. Despite those setbacks, the engaging story and the atmospheric design make it a game worth playing. I reccomend giving it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent portrayal of some fae tales! Really into the disturbing yet cutesie feel of this game.It was buggy in that when I would die and auto restart from the most recent checkpoint, certain features like camera movement with my character or interactive items, would not work, so I would have to go to the in game menu to "restart from checkpoint" as a kind of hard reset.The soundtrack is splendid and really pairs well with the scenes. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: ⚠This review can contain spoiler sections. ⚠The views expressed here are all my own. ⚠No experienced player review here because I'm a rookie/casual player.We were promised Nordic folklore with colorful woodlands and ominous locations in the Bramble: The Mountain King trailer. The entire situation, which was driven by a blonde child named Olle and his older sister Lillemor (more the former than the latter), had a Hansel-and-Gretel-like quality to it.I need to say that I was not disappointed.Although I don't have much gaming experience and don't pay much attention to gameplay, I have noticed the following.The controls occasionally seem clanky and give the impression that Olle is either running too slowly or too quickly, even falling from cliffs or buildings. That could occasionally be really aggravating. Can we also talk about how frustrating the camera positioning is? Because you can't always see where you need to go further or properly investigate the lands, that upset me.This game tries to be many things at once: a platformer, a puzzle game, etc. Although it can be confusing at times, I had personally no issues with that.Additionally, some bosses will be more challenging to defeat than others because it is not always immediately obvious how to do it. But almost everything is feasible.Let's not forget the narrator, who adds even more depth to the plot and the universe of Olle. The voice actress did an amazing job !The artwork was fantastic, it was a real enjoyment to read these storybooks in-game.Some players criticized the original soundtrack's dearth of tracks, and while I agree that some more enduring music would have been nice, generally I'm satisfied.The “Witcher 3-inspired music” played during one of the boss battles was both unexpected and satisfying.Even if some game elements were a little grainy in the background, it didn't really matter because generally, the graphics were pretty outstanding.When I first started playing, I assumed it would resemble Little Nightmares, but I quickly discovered that there is nothing similar about this game.The majority of the game was fun for me; certain parts weren't as much fun, but overall, I was really hooked.Although I don't think it's a game you can readily return to, I'll definitely give it another shot one day. 8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Whenever I saw that Steam gave this a 10/10 for horror this year, I bought it instantly. I think this game is unique and as a certain it factor about it that you do not see often in video games. I am super please with everything and think that this was just amazing. I was wowed my the stories and the different elements that were introduced in the game. The art style alone is something that you would want to pick this game up for. The story is there. The trope of saving a sibling is nice and gives Hansel and Gretel vibes. I would say to pick it up and give it a go. It is about 3ish hours long if you are enjoying it and would recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Teaboy's Basic(ish) Reviews....I read a lot of reviews when looking at games on Steam, and it quickly gets tiring – those who write involved, down to the micron scale reviews, although helpful, end up like looking at War & Peace when you’ve only got time for a quick 5 minute dump!  This is middle of the road and to the point – not easy for me as I tend towards sesquipedalian loquaciousness!  Vociferously Verbose?  Alright, verbal diarrhoea.  (Although I hate panning a developer’s work and all the time, effort and love they put into designing these – it is their life after all – this is my honest, personal opinion of my level of enjoyment.  Sorry devs!).  A note on time played:  My Steam clock does not seem to work properly, indeed, it even minuses time on occasion!  Plus, I have a tendency to wander off and leave games running at times, so time played may not be entirely accurate!  Teaboy’s Tonsil Titillators or Toenail Titbits!  (Rating)  Tonsil Tickler (Totally Tops):  The frenchy of which you always dreamt!  To quote a master, “She’s got a tongue like an electric eel and she likes the taste of a Man’s tonsils!”.  An absolute masterpiece and joy to play.  The Tits (Terrific):  Everyone loves playing with these!  Not THE best bit, but such fun on their own you can be lost for hours....mmmm.  What most games you really like score – perfection is so rare after all.   Torso Teaser (Taker of your Time):  It’s a flat stomach....sure it’s nice to look at, run your fingers over, slobber on a bit, sometimes that bellybutton gets your motor running....but it's just basically the corridor between the two ‘gaming rooms’.  The definitive ‘Meh’ - the middle ‘sideways thumb’ option for which everyone on Steam cries.  Todger/Tadger & (scroTum) Taters (Tedious):  Is it an ‘a’ or is it an ‘o’?  Who cares!  The meat can be fun to play with for about 5 minutes of your entire day, the rest it just hangs there and generally gets in the way of doing something else.  The main problem of course, is the two veg sticking to your inside thigh.  This is what this game feels like – the occasional/rare bouts of fun, the rest bobbing like a 19th century British Policeman (now you know why!).  Toenail Tornado (Total Toss):  A playthrough so appalling it’s like being trapped in a Turkish sauna with the ugliest, hairiest, fattest, sweatiest beast of a neolithic hominid who’s trimming his toenails using pliers and the splinters are reminiscent of a scene from the Normandy Landings.  My god how did this get released!?  Teaboy Touts (Score):  Pure scroTum.            Winner of the Dull Award:  Duller than a dullard from Dulwich (a town in England pronounced Dull-Itch, which is exactly how this game feels).The Review:  In a word: Crap.  Totally style over substance.  Looks over personality.  Boobs over brains.  Poontang over simple Human connection and relationship.  If you are awed by good looks and care nothing for anything else, then this is the game for you.  It is a child's gameplay wrapped up in an adult skin with a child's fairy story backdrop.  It is a borderline walking simulator with a mild story driven narrative arc.  For those who say, 'so what?' I bought the game as it claimed it was a platformer and NOT a walking simulator - this is a misinterpretation of these terms At Best.  It..is....so.............sloooooow.  Playing as a small boy whose run speed looks like he's got severe rickets and is barely faster than his trotting jog, it takes forever to travel across the interminably long tracks n trails n corridors n giant caverns....you get the drift.  And for a game that is 100% visual effect you will die often due to an almost indiscernible path you MUST follow.  The game is SO linear it will make gay people straight!  There is ZERO diversion from 'the path', and as mentioned, paths are loooong, movement is so slow and climbing is interminable due to both the slow and long - still getting my drift I hope?  For a 'platformer' there is Extremely little to 'platform'.  The game has a single combat mode which is, you guessed it, slow.  Hold left trigger, targeting reticule appears, right trigger throws a ball of light with auto-targeting that will highlight quite a distance from your actual reticule, but then will not stick, so when you are trying to fire as fast as possible because it is so slow, it misses often against all odds.  And that is it.  Apart from using left trigger to hold the ball of light up when running and right triggering to make it flash when a bramble flower appears, there is simply nothing else to this game.  I was glad when it ended.  I wanted to give it its due and play to the end, but it never got any better.  There are parts where it actually forces you to WALK!  In a game so bloody slow with such long paths and it even forces you to walk....holy smegging y-fronts!  Now this is for you to absorb the ambience, feel the emotion, grasp the existential horror of the moment and the evil of the backstory....but omfg.  Let me be fair, I know this will be right up some people's street and you will know instantly from the above whether it is for you or not.  But for me, it is basically mis-sold.  It is by no means a terrible game which is why it doesn't get my lowest rating, you can see and feel the sheer amount of love the developers put into it, but with all the care and attention to a super realistic world, they forgot the GAMEPLAY!  It honestly felt as if they spent 99% of the development time on visuals and realized right at the end it needed something to DO.  Rowboat near the end, making you repeat the same boss battle THREE TIMES!?  F-off!!  Beautiful visuals, meh story (for an adult - it's a child's nordic fantasy fairytale with adult blood n guts), garbage gameplay.  Sorry.  Not what I was lead to believe.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Everything started good: sun, meadows, flowers, gnomes and games. But then... BUT THEN!Granny is my fav boss XDGreat atmosphere, good music and sound, super cool ending. 10 of 10.UPDThe game shows that you don't have to have hundreds of GBs of textures to make a good game. My respect to devs who made game under 10Gb.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: + Beautiful visuals, interesting theme and story with Nordic folklore, amazing music.- Clumsy camera angles and movement. Not much instructions, unclear how to proceed at times and what controls to use, but I was able to figure things out pretty quickly. Could have been a bit cheaper since it's pretty short, I recommend buying when it's on sale.Other: not as cute as it might seem at first, it gets darker quickly so be aware.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to first say I purchased this game on sale for about $12 USD. At this price, I am pretty satisfied with my purchase, I paid about $2.40 per hour of playtime I got out of this game. It is beautiful, it is fun, and it all goes together very well. It is also extremely dark in every sense of the word. Do not let the trailer fool you, some f***** up s*** happens in this game. The puzzle elements were fun, but not very challenging which was a negative for me. Since puzzles were not hard to figure out, it oftentimes felt more like an exploration (walking simulator) game than a puzzle plat-former. I do not know if I think this game is worth the full asking price or not. There is virtually no replay value besides to snag achievements you missed on your first run, if you missed any at all. I did greatly enjoy the story and all of the Scandinavian folklore that was woven into it and the world in general. I found the final boss battle to be exciting, but it was still not very challenging. This game is interesting, as the story clearly announces this is a game for people who can handle dark mature topics, but the game-play itself is quite simple and will provide little to no challenges to most individuals. All in all, I thought the game was unique and I am glad I played it. If it is on sale, I definitely recommend picking it up if it looks cool to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game for less than 5 hours. It is the same with Little Nightmares in terms of its story. I love how the story flows and ends. You know, we are rooting for happy endings. It is more on action and narration than puzzle. I gave my energy fighting the bosses but luckily I defeated them in less than 10 tries. I really recommend this game. I bet you, you won't get disappointed, so buy now!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble is a great short unique experience.The visuals are beautiful,The sound is excellent and story telling is very very good.The game play can feel a bit clunky but I didn't found it something that interrupts too much.The game makes plunge into this beautifully crafted nightmare that you just want more and more of it.The only downside is that it's a short game... leaving you with a taste for more.Very recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: The last time a story driven game really engaged me emotionally was Hellblade, this is what a story focused game should be, every boss fight, graphics, music and sounds are the game's strongests points, it's not the holy relic of gameplay but it fits all it's other elements quite well because you're no John Wick killalotafaeries
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I always loved short & sweet games and this is one of the better ones. Not much to add. Visually it's among the best thanks to photo-realism provided by UE. The soundtrack is great, my favorite part is in the last boss fight. The story is good, nice little Nordic fairytale. The gameplay is good enough and definitely accessible for beginners, but nothing major I haven't seen before.Technical side is good, but not amazing. The game is under 5 hours long and yet I've ran into 3 bugs where I had to reload my save. The ultrawide support is officially non-existent, because it would mess up the artistic vision, so we get black bars. What art. UUU removes the black bars, but doesn't fix vertical scaling in cutscenes and even some gameplay scenes even when I added a line into the config file to enforce proper scaling. Get with the times, devs. UW is the future, ESPECIALLY for cinematic games like yours.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: The story telling, lore, sound, graphics and atmosphere in this game are amazing. The gameplay is simple but fun. Puzzles, dodging and platforming. The game isn't very long (took me less than 5h and I think I was rather slow). For the price it's easily worth the money. One of my best recent gaming experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a really unique-looking game with incredible art. Game switching between 'light' and 'dark' is something really well made. Story is really interesting, I would say one of the best dark fantasy stories I've played. This is something different, few scenes and boss fights were really dark and scary. And the gameplay is decent, something similar to LIMBO and INSIDE. I would recommend this game on on sale, maybe 30€ is a bit too much for it since I've finished it in 4 hours and I did some exploring.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: The story is so good. So is the horror honestly. It leads you into a false sense of security and strikes you when you've let your guard down. it's sort of like a dream and nightmare repeating itself and the fact that it gives such detailed lore to the universe we're in and the enemies. i really love that. the graphics and gameplay itself is so smooth, all the bosses are more challenging than the last, and you sort of have to get defeated to defeat them. idk. i'm not much of a game reviewer, so i really don't know how to review this, but its so good. you can't not give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really look into it before so I was a little surprised at how much of a horror game this was (I hate horror) but it was still kind of enchanting and unique. Very light on gameplay, more of a playable movie in the vein of Heavy Rain or Life is Strange rather than a platformer or real puzzle game, but stunning visuals, music and story.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely loved this game, the story behind the folklore is super interesting and graphically it's a beautiful game, the only annoying thing that holds it back from being perfect is the physics and the controls can be a bit awkward and jank sometimes, e.g. not grabbing onto walls when its supposed to, falling off ledges easily, getting caught between objects and clipping. but don't let that stop you from playing this gorgeous game, 100% recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember when you were a child and someone read a fairy tale to you? Do you remember experiencing the story you were hearing vividly in your mind's eye? Replicating this feeling is what this game wants to achieve, and it succeeds beautifully at it. There's not much to manage as there are no skills, abilities, perks, etc. All you have to do is experience a story and feel like you're living it. Fair warning: Even though the story is clearly inspired by fairy tales of old, it is not for children. This is Brothers Grimm fire, brimstone, pest and cholera kind of fairy tale, not the Walt Disney kind. There's a fair amount of gore and horror elements in the latter half of the game.In today's sea of samey games, this one convinces by being unique and memorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning relaxing not creepy at all non-horror game 8.5/10The soundtrack and sound design was phenomenal. I could really feel myself being in the environment, listening to every single sound around me. Also, to my surprise, the art and lighting is looking absolutely amazing With the nice play of motion blurs and other effects that are constantly setting up the screen, any given moment could become a wallpaper. The game also handles camera movement really well, giving the player multiple perspectives to play from (not just a regular side scroller/top down)The gameplay delivered, it was well paced, kept me on my toes and knew when to give me a moment to breath. Fighting off each enemy was unique while still letting player react to what they've already learned Some areas gave me literal chills and I was really creeped out. The formating of the story was also well done, as it slowly unravels itself.Cons: At some points while holding the light I had fps drops and stuttering (it ran perfectly smoothly everywhere else). I wouldn't recommend it to someone who doesn't control movement that well, as the constant camera position changes change "which way is forward".
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This reminds me of the Little Nightmares games in a positive way as it takes the best parts of those games. Bramble is a dark Nordic fairytale that is presented as a bedtime story. You have to sneak past various monsters to try and save your sister. The story and the lore was interesting, and rather brutal. It's not a game for kids at all.  The graphics, art and music make the game beautiful and very atmospheric. The puzzles aren't too difficult but also not so easy that it's boring. Just the right amount for this sort of game where the story and the lore are the important things. It's quite short, taking me just over 7 hours to complete, and I'm by no means a speed runner so you might be quicker. So I got it on sale and it was worth it. It's up to you whether that's worth the non sale price or not.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cool to play. Music, image and story is perfect. The game transports you to a magical world in which you have to save yourself from monsters. The game is not so hard to play but sometimes the controls on keyboard are harder to play with. I died so many times, but it keeping me addicted to it. Game is not so scary but have some creepy or gore images.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Very beautiful and atmospheric game. It has strong old tell-tales vibe. Old tales about living near the forest, meeting fairies and running from chtonic forest habitants.Game mechanics are simple, I would say you can control the boy with one hand most of the time. Yet gameplay feels natural and well conducted from developers all around. You can see that developers really worked together to create perfect piece of art.Buy this game - its worth more than the current price (10% off on release)P.S. I was amazed to see the ukrainian language in menu. Thank you, Dimfrost, thousand times thank you
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a hidden gem in the action adventure game genre that shines among the likes of Little Nightmares and Limbo. With a story heavily steeped in Norse folklore, the game does an excellent job with it's visual and narrative storytelling, keeping the player constantly hooked throughout. From the little details in the visuals, the soundtrack, the story - everything just flows so well together and is such a treat to behold! The game is roughly 3 - 5 hours in length, but make no mistake, it still leaves quite the impression when all is said and done. Highly recommend experiencing for yourself!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I had been waiting for this game to come out for awhile now after seeing clips of it online. The game itself doesn't take long to beat, I would say maybe 3 to 4hrs taking my time, and it was well worth it. I loved the feel of the game, the atmosphere, the lore, etc. I especially loved the storybooks you come across explaining the lore behind what either happened to an area you are currently traveling through, or the enemies/boss you have encountered or will encounter. The music and the art was just absolutely beautiful and the song "In the hall of the mountain king" that plays at the final boss I just felt like that tied everything in together, it was epic! I don't know what to say other than please please please support this game and the devs. I hope to see more games like this one in the future and all in all 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A fairy-tale game with good visuals and decent controls, except the fairy-tale is Eastern-European which means you friendly gnomes and sunshine alongside murderous trolls and brutal deaths. Quite an unforgiving game except for fall damage (allowing you to recover eventually) and throwing accuracy. Not difficult though, if you understand where you need to go and what to do. Very much a show-not-tell. Controls are a little finicky on mouse and keyboard but not bad overall. Very nice overall but not fully relaxing game. Play for the story. Get on sale as a playthrough is only ~4 hours long and there is not much to explore beyond the linear gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible from start to finish. I'm a huge fan of mythology and this game did not disappoint! The story is beautifully told, the graphics are great and I thought the overall game has been well thought out. From the mechanics being smooth and in game queues as to where to go etc all flawless. Probably the best game I've played this year. Highly recommend even if it is fairly short (just over 4 hours to complete) the studio have done themselves extremely proud with this.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A really cool horror game, which somehow manages to be extremely brutal and yet adorable and peaceful at times. It got me fascinated with its story and the swedish folklore. My first play-through took me about 7 hours, but I wanted to play it again immediately, to find all hidden secrets. I absolutely fell in love with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Well. I think it's a bit tricky to decide whether I would recommend this or not. I personally bought this solely for the art style and nordic myths, and I got what I wanted. It was delightful to see familiar folklore creatures like Näcken and Skogrået come to life as beautifully designed bosses. You can tell a lot of love went into character design and some of the hauntingly beautiful scenes in between. Couple of scenes in the game made me gasp in awe for how striking they look. Camera angles made it look like a movie, and the narrator really enhanced that "living in a storybook"-kinda feeling. I really enjoyed seeing all this. However, I didn't enjoy playing through it as much. Clunky controls, mediocre at best puzzles, very basic platforming where you only die because of the clunky controls and tricky angles.. It felt like the actual gameplay was an afterthought and main focus was in the visuals. Some things are clearly not thought through: you can insta-drown in a puddle but walk through a waist deep stream. You're taught to throw the light in the beginning, but sometimes it just shines and sometimes it flies when you do exactly the same thing. Basically you never know how your only weapon works and how far it can reach. You can also run, kinda, but not always, and while you can't climb a big rock you can climb up a straight wall apparently because it's rusty.It also felt like the platforming parts were just thrown in there, they didn't feel very connected to the world and lacked meaning. They stood out from the otherwise beautiful and atmospheric world in a negative way, because they were often dull, generic and lacked detail. There's an interesting contrast between gruesome and beautiful in this game, but an annoying one between looks and playability.I would recommend this for the visuals and usage of northern myths, but I can't recommend it overall as a game. I don't regret buying it and I enjoyed it for the parts it was made great and pushed through the rest because I wanted to see more.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, I loved this game, and the story. Swedish folklore didn't scare me at all when I was a kid, (love especially trolls) but bosses and other enemies in this game were freaky scary and hard to fight that you have to struggle a bit ;-), so it's worth lol. It's a short game, depends on your gameplay, for me took 7 hours to beat. There is no support for k+m, only gamepads/hand controller. I have even tried to mapping to keyboard or mouse, but nothing happened.  Well, I was enjoying, and sometimes pissed off lol. So I give a big THUMB UP!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, I was not expecting to like it so much. During the game's journey, I really felt as if I was a child living through a folk tale that my parents would tell me at night to convince me not to misbehave. The music and visuals are also extremely good, being a very cinematic experience, with the camera positioning itself in incredible shots. My only complain, however, has to do with that. Even though it created amazing scenery, sometimes, the camera positioning interfered with gameplay, with me not knowing exactly where to move to. But this was just a very minor inconvenience in the grand scheme of things. I recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: It's not often that I write reviews for games, but this game is phenomenal. It was a joy playing through it and it's some of the best hours I've spent in my life. I really hope we get to see more like this with nordic folklore from this studio.  The music in this game is 10/10, but rendition of "In the Hall of The Mountain King" is out of this world and made me never wanna finish. This game deserves all the hype it's been getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the entire game in one sitting, good pacing and varying gameplay. Music was excellent, graphics was excellent, narration was excellent. The little boss fights were adorable and messed up. Olle was a absolute gigachad, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that kid will need some psychological evaluation when their parents comes back home.
