_childDocuments_.review: This game's asking price is a bit steep for the lack of polish. Trial and error gameplay comes with the territory of the cinematic platformer genre--however, when failures are more the result of finicky controls and readability than the player's own quick reflexes, that challenge becomes frustrating and harms the immersion these games typically strive for.Despite the technical flaws, this game is definitely a breath of fresh air for the genre. Creepy throughout and took me by surprise multiple times. Incredible music, too. There was clear vision in the creative direction, and it's executed really well... except there's not as much literal clear vision in the camera's depth of field; very often nothing is in focus. There's also a bit of recycling in the level design, which for a short game is unfortunate, but thankfully it's not too extreme to be bothersome. I still recommend checking out this game if you have any fondness for the cinematic platformer genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is visually stunning and the story/lore is very engaging. My main gripe with the game is that the odd camera angles can skew your perception too much and often make navigation and platforming difficult. I found certain portions of the platforming especially to be way too finicky and unforgiving, especially due to the aforementioned skewed perspective. What I very much enjoyed about this game though is how it could be whimsical and pleasant in some areas, allowing you to appreciate the gorgeous world around you; yet it could be truly horrific and unsettling in many, many other areas. I did not feel there was a lot of room for exploration in the game as it is geared towards keeping you on a single narrative path. However there are collectibles and other fun achievements to be found and earned in the game, so some exploration is rewarded. It's also a fairly quick game to play. Even though I struggled through it (especially through those finicky platforming sections), it only took me 5 hours to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game really excited. I saw a clip online and it had gotten my attention immediately. It's hard to identify just one problem with the game that made me dislike it but there is a few things I will point out. The gameplay is slow. It's partially due to the fact your character is slow but also that there's a lot of downtime in between the good parts. There's a ton of cutscenes which slow it down even more. From what I played, the controls are iffy at best but there's a lot of platforming. I would die over and over again just trying to make one jump because the controls were so wonky. There's a narrator that talks for a lot of the game as well and while I like her voice and her voice acting, it feels off to me. I think a reason is that the game is supposed to be a cryptid based horror game and the narrator takes me out of it. It struggles with knowing whether or not it wants to be a mysterious storybook themed game and a creepy horror game. The one thing this game fails to do is to bring me into the world. The visuals are amazing and I liked most of what I saw, but the controls weren't fluid and it was frustrating failing at basic platforming because of how the game controls. I tried both keyboard and mouse and controller and neither one worked out.I do plan on eventually going back to the game to finish it, because it does seem like there's a lot of content here and I hoping that maybe there's a patch or two that will help against my complaints. I did edit this review to further explain what I was talking about and fix some typos.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A very atmospheric experience. Thematically, it's occasionally "heavy fare" and should only be enjoyed if you're in a better mood. Unfortunately, the keyboard and mouse controls are sometimes off, so there's a certain potential for frustration. In the end, you get a few very sophisticated hours of puzzle fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to give this a positive review because the art style is great, music is fantastic and they nailed the worldbuilding.However the game is pretty buggy right now. More than once I found myself second-guessing what the next step was because at some places you need to interact with things at exactly the right pixel or you fail. And I had to restart from the last checkpoint a couple of times because the game softlocked.Most creatures are delightful or terrifying and they're all well designed.The voice acting of the gnomes gets frustrating when they keep crying while you're trying to figure out where to go next.The story beats feel off in the second half of the game.One of the bosses that you encounter has all the hallmarks for a final sequence of the game. You walk through a path with music that would suggest that you're nearing the end of the road and then... the game continues for about another hour.Don't get me wrong the actual end of the game is brilliant and it had some of the best music I've heard in a game... but... the game insists on throwing useless gameplay elements at you. It does this throughout the entire game but it gets truly annoying when you have almost reached the end and these elements feel more like filler moments than ever before.Despite this being a negative review all-in all, I would still at least try another game from this studio in the future. However they really need to go through more playtesting on whatever their next game ends up being.

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10 | Visually stunning | Wonderful narration & storytelling | Intriguing. This game is an absolute gem. It's sadly a short game so only expect between 4-6 hours at most for one playthrough but that didn't affect my experience in a negative way. The camera shots & cutscene's were phenomenal for an Indie game. A LOT better than some AAA games these days visual-wise. Some times too basic, generic concept BUT it also fit well into the game and the style of the theme. I also wished the game was a little longer but oh well. Maybe DLC? :)Definitely recommend. _childDocuments_.review: I knew barely anything about this game, but I have been a Little Nightmares fanatic since it's birth. As an appreciator of the dark and whimsical, I knew I had to get it.The music, visuals, horrible enemies and slivers of joy dappled in this game make it a must-play for environmental horror enthusiasts.The true-to-lore designs and stories are to die for, and shed an honest light to Nordic folklore, something we need more of.My only complaint is the lack of more enemy interaction. While I appreciate a good staged boss fight as much as any other, I also love when enemies have more open-world interaction during the chase and the battle. I don't want to draw too many similarities to Little Nightmares, as this game is wildly different, but if we were to receive any more pieces similar to this from Dimfrost in the future, having AI interaction with the enemies like we get in Little Nightmares would be an amazing addition.Definitely play this game, it will take over your mind in the best way possible.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game that dives into Scandinavian folklore. The graphics are beautiful and horrifying (in a good way) causing the horrific scenes to be more intense. It reminds me of Heavy Rain, The Witcher saga, as well as 3D platformers such as It Takes Two (just no multiplayer). The story, environment, and characters are what drive the game the most. While it is only a 9-15 hour game (depending on the player), the game is well worth the price.In summary, if you are not into story-driven, folklore, psychological horror... this game isn't for you. If you are then definitely consider it! I absolutely loved this game and I know I will replay it again.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed a lot of the more intense moments of the game and had a blast playing the more alert sections. The only reason to replay it is doing the Survival achievement that has you play the game without dying or restarting the game. (in theory) as you can fool around with that achievement.Having said that, the controls are iffy at best. I have played with the controller, not the keyboard and mouse and most likely is better made for that, but still, the camera angles, the motion blur, locations that are bigger than they needed to be without serving a purpose and abysmal controls make me rank the game lower than I should have had.You have to fight the camera and controls for some reason, and instead of navigating the tense moments evading the boss, and playing around, the movement is sometimes weird, and you will miss jumps or moves that you would have not missed in any other game.It's a bad blend of 3D where 2D would have worked better.I agree with the comments that the movement is pulling the game down, but storywise, visual presentation and atmosphere is an amazing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent little game that many may have overlooked due to all the blockbusters that have come out in 2023. If you are intrigued by Nordic folklore, folk-tale derived horror or just like games akin to Little Nightmares, I highly recommend this one.The setting of playing as a little boy, searching for his sister in the increasingly horrifying woods in intriguing. Learning about Nordic folktales is interesting and unique. The graphics are alright, but nothing spectacular. However, we need to consider that this has been made by a small, indie team on a tight budget so it is not reasonable to compare it to AAA games or even high-budget AA titles.The asking prices is quite reasonable even without the sale, and for the unique experience this provides, is a bargain when on sale. Do check it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly really loved this game, and it's been a while since I've played something that stood out this much to me. Bramble has its flaws as most games do, I personally found the camera a little wonky and sometimes managed to jump at weird angles to my death with no help from the forest creatures. I also had a couple problems with the game crashing/bugging out initially (I played on steam deck), but after the most recent update it plays great on the deck!If anything I wish I could have roamed around in this fairytale world longer, even with all the monsters out to chomp on me. While not the best graphics I've seen in recent years, everything was beautifully designed, which carries more weight in my opinion. There is a strange harmony between the lovely scenes filled with light and friendly forest creatures and those filled with blood and fear, like a dream that slips into a nightmare. I think these days you can tell when a game is made with heart or just pushed out for the sake of consumption, and Bramble really has a soul of its own.If you want to experience a dark fairytale in a world filled with everything magical and horrifying, check this game out. The story is relatively simple and short, but gives you lots of peeks into something deeper, darker, and even more terribly beautiful.Now excuse me while I go purchase the soundtrack because it is incredible.Side note: skogsrå's magic works on women too, cause I'm smitten
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty great little gem. Definitely recommended if you enjoyed Little Nightmares, Inside, Limbo. Stunning visuals and audio. Interesting puzzles and some pretty intense boss fights. The animation I thought could have used more detail and looked rough in places, maybe for their next game they can invest more resources in it. But all in all a really fun and creepy journey through a twisted little tale. Completed in 5 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, because the things it does well it does VERY well. Incredible art direction, beautiful imagery, and good voice acting. The boss fights are satisfying and the gore is well rendered and adds to the dark tone.But where it succeeds as an experience it fails as a game. The puzzles are extremely easy, to the point of being tedious. They aren't even that long, but just the fact you have to do them at all feels like jumping through hoops because the answer is immediately obvious, every single time. Some puzzles also get repeated, which feels odious when they were already so simple to begin with... The gameplay is basically on rails at all times (barring bossfights), with the direction the camera is moving telling you where you should walk 100% of the time. There is only ever one solution to any obstacle the game throws at you, and almost always only one path to take in any given situation, so the ability to control your character starts to feel redundant after a while.It makes me sad because it cant help but think its a huge a missed opporunity. For example, there are multiple situations where you need to 'find' a key or a handle to get past an obstacle, but instead of hiding it behind a challange or puzzle, it will literally just be a short walk away from the door you need to open or winch you need to pull. You walk over, grab it, bring it back, and get past the obstacle. It just made me wonder why they bothered separating them at all.It's not really a walking simulator, but the interactive elements often feel so secondary to the experience that they might as well not be there. If you just want to watch a movie, you'll probably enjoy this - I was hoping for a more engaging horror/puzzle experience, so I didn't.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble compels you to keep going, challenging enough to give you minor frustrations for a casual gamer, but makes you keep trying. The puzzles are easy to work out enough. Battles are easily grasped and you make it through hoping to see more.Visually, this game is SPECTACULAR, both breathtaking in it's beauty, and with flip side darkness that makes you grimace.The folk tales it is based on are amazing, and you can see from what folklore stemmed many versions recognisable to me, and those that were brand new to me. Music and songs worked wonderfully with the atmosphere. It was both paradise and hell, I commend the artists with the highest praise- we were given quality that even goes beyond most high ranking game companies that sometimes can't get anything right on launch.This game is not for the faint of heart though; please take heed of the warnings they give; they are meant to be harrowing and they are, yet do not be afraid to venture - there are lots of moments of light and hope throughout for a respite for the gamer. Just bear in mind you will see things that may upset you.Story wise it is simple, but the journey is what makes it lovable. I never at one point lost immersion, and this is a game I FULLY recommend to anyone, and a game I will be playing again. I look forward to what they offer next.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Absolutely stunning little game. Highest recommendation to anyone, especially people looking for something fun to get into over a weekend, fans of Nordic folklore, platforming, and games like Limbo/Little Nightmares/Inside.The premise of the game is simple: you're the little brother who needs to find his big sister after you got separated in the forest. On your way, you'll encounter different places and creatures, whose backstories are being told through narrated picture books you'll find along the way. These will also allow you to slowly piece together the background of this world, what happened to it and why.Gameplay wise, this is a linear 3D platformer. None of the platforming was too hard, but the environments were varied and the platforming always engaging. I did have a little difficulty sometimes when they game required fast jumping at some angles, but that's due to me playing with a keyboard and so having to rely on WSAD only for movement. Aside from platforming there are puzzles, which are - again - engaging but easy to understand and follow through. As a result, while these allow you to remain engaged and bring some variety into the game, at no point has it felt like hitting a wall and having to spend any significant amount of time to solve it i.e. think Little Nightmares/Inside, not Myst.Is it scary though? Depends on what you find scary and your threshold. For me, it was definitely creepy at times, and I admit there were 2 parts where I squealed like a.. completely normal adult. Yeah. But at no point did I feel like it's too much, though. Also, I very much appreciated the scary sections/encounters being peppered in sporadically, with many different types of gameplay in between, so that it never felt tiresome or overwhelming. So even a scaredy-cat like myself was able to play through everything and have lots of fun!One place where the controls got a little more demanding were the boss fights. There's several of them marking the end of each section, and while they are not difficult, each has its own skills and you need to get familiar with and counter their skills. But in the end, as with the rest of the game, even this part is geared towards a visual and gameplay spectacle more than it is about telling you to "git gud", so no need to worry about the difficulty!And a'propos the spectacle - this game is an absolute masterpiece as far as the visual experience is concerned. The environments are extremely detailed, aimed at creating an unforgettable atmosphere. While each map is linear, usually with a single path forward, there are secrets and collectables to gather along the way as well. The amazing visual experience is elevated further by the amazing OST. It matches the scenes before you perfectly, enhancing the feelings each place wants to evoke. It also serves very well during boss fights, building up the tension and the mood of the fights. On that note, the voice acting by the Narrator is truly amazing, especially given how none of the characters actually speaks by themselves and we are only told what they said by the Narrator, as if she was reading a book to us.Overall, the game is quite short (it took me 6 hours to finish it, in a day no less!), and oh is it sweet! Even my partner who's not usually interested in this type of games couldn't help but look over my shoulder as I played. If you're looking for something to take your mind off of things, to transport you somewhere and offer a gripping experience - this game is it! Once I started playing I simply could not put the game down and I have absolutely no regrets in spending a large portion of my weekend free time on it!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I would say this game is almost perfection. I love the graphics and the art style, the soundtrack is wonderful, the rendition of the song "den blomstertid nu kommer" with the artist Bjoern is fantastic, I was surprised to hear this song in a game, for swedish people it's very recognizable ,but it absolutely fits the atmosphere and the environment. Also the storytelling is so good. It's impressive how they make all graphics, sound and story work together so well. Besides all this, the gameplay is actually good too. It reminds me a lot of the Little Nightmare-games, and Limbo.The gameplay is simple and I think that most players will get into it easily, the puzzles are mostly easy to solve, but that makes the story move forward too, you will never get bored because you're stuck for too long. It's also pretty directed with camera angles that make you understand where to go next. There are more challenging scenes with some of the bosses, but thanks to the generosity of checkpoints you rarely have to redo a lot of the stages you already passed. I would guess most players will finish the game in 5-8 hours, so don’t expect to have weeks of challenging gameplay. However, the game is totally worth it, it’s more comparable to the feeling when watching a beautiful movie, except that you’re a part of it. But commonly these days many games have so much better stories than most movies from Hollywood. As a swedish person I recognize many of the characters from tales, and creators thought of so many details that it makes me happy. What surprised me is how the first part of the game is so cute and the second part is so violent and dark, it’s a difficult balance but it gives lots of depth to the game that I love. However, I would have liked them to also make a censored version of the game so that I could let my son play it, because I know he would have loved many of the stunning scenes and the puzzles, but some scenes make it difficult to play with a child.9/10*I played the demo first, then I purchased the game at once. I continued to play from where the demo ended. After I finished the game I realized that the demo starts after ⅓ of the game, so I was happy to find out I had ⅓ more to play. :)

It was really interesting (and awesome) to see how the developers used this to create terrifying bosses. Additionally, every boss fight in this game is unique and enjoyable with a fantastic sound track (especially Pesta's boss fight!)So Overall a solid horror game I reccommend playing! 10/10

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, this game does have Little Nightmare vibes, but I personally believe it's even better, It brings Nordic folk lore, a sensational music score, stunning visuals and the most emotional journey of death and discovery, wrapped up in a gritty old burlap sack full of incredible boss fights, timeless story telling, brilliant voice acting and the most compelling game play I have seen to date! This small studio has blown lid off these grim, horror, adventure games, there is nothing really quite like it, I do hope this isn't the only Bramble title they make! Because I'll be following Dimfrost to my grave! Horror games lately are all jump scares and cheap frights, Bramble makes you feel truly creeped out and on edge, with unexpected twists around every rock and thorn, the world is immersive, beautiful, dark and full of exciting puzzles and monsters. A true masterpiece you need in your collection.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a loveletter to Scandinavian folklore.It is bright and joyful, and it is grotesque and cruel. The story is about Olle and Lillemor, two siblings living in medieval Sweden. It starts with a fairytale about Bramble the Mountain king. Their mother warns them that if they go out at night they will be taken by the bramble. So they go out, of course. On their adventure they encounter creatures like gnomes, cloudberry people, trolls and even zombies.The boss fights are very cool and unique, the soundtrack is amazing and the visuals are stunning. The only negative I have to say is that the controls and camera angles felt janky at times, but nothing gamebreaking. Well worth a try, I havent enjoyed a game this much in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Bramble: The Mountain King! The music was definitely one of the highlights. It really added to the immersive experience of the game. The camera angles were also really well done, allowing you to feel like you were really there in the game. And the story was so captivating, it kept you engaged the whole time. It's always great to find a game that captures your attention like this one did.I loved it so much that I went back and completed all the achievements. Highly recommend to any horror game enthusiast!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a neat little cinematic platformer. Collision box issues with its platforms are not too common but noticeable and do detract from the experience if you encounter them. The depth of field effects can be a little obnoxious and it hurts the scenes in which it is most aggressive. Overall, the game is very impressive visually, though. Colours are vibrant and the textures are well detailed. The setting is dark, but whimsical and filled with charming creatures to match the great evils you will face. Some of the game's bosses can be needlessly tedious, it also attempts to make you feel bad for killing a boss in a QTE when the boss will kill you if you fail it. This boss is also shown to have murdered multiple innocent people and used them for strange magic. The soundtrack is an absolute standout; I give it much respect for making appropriate use of Kulning rather than caving to the myth that Scandinavians practiced Tuvan throat singing. The game is short enough that I only began to grow tired of its mechanics towards the very end. A must-buy on sale, and something to consider at full price if this is normally your sort of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Oh this game is fabulous.Suffuse with cultural stories and details, thrilling pace and storytelling, shocking immersion and surprises; this game blew me away! The animation, lighting, and visual effects are really something else. And don't even get me started on the music!!!!! For those who enjoy a good story to sink into over a weekend, this is a MUST-PLAY. Simple mechanics with rewarding and unique challenges! Familiar but refreshing and creative boss fights, with probably the most epic boss fight ever! This game will have you on the edge of your seat, groaning in frustration, and holding your breathe in awe- perhaps even shedding a tear! So spooky, but equally tender... What a wonderfully generous game and a masterful creation any team would be ever so proud to share with the world. Thank you Dimfrost! <3

However, once I used the settings to my liking and got used to the mechanics this game became SO good!The story is nice and the creatures are really interesting. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Solid story and cool atmosphere/monsters. This would be a great animated series or movie. The graphics were good but the constant camera weirdness and overdone depth of field really stopped me from enjoying or appreciating it.The game play is really bad. It's tedious, a walking simulator, and some of the worst "puzzles" I've ever seen. There was one good puzzle at the very end, that is it. Most of the time if I was stuck it was because I overthought a puzzle or couldn't figure out what the game wanted me to do (the latter most often). The last two boss fights are good, the rest are either too easy or tedious and annoying. This game is worth buying at a $15 price, definitely not a $30. I don't feel like I was robbed, just disappointed in what I got. It often tries to be artistic and creative, sometimes succeeds, but I was so bored with the game play that I wasn't impressed with the parts they did well. It felt like getting a bad meal and trying to savor your drink out of pity.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

I can't imagine my view will change when I finish it but if it does I will update my review. Definitely one I'd suggest giving it a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: - Wonderful Visual Design- Great use of Music- Captivating Story Telling and great camera work- Enjoyable boss fights- Emotionally and psychologically impactfulCons: - Very Linear game play- Physics were annoying at times- No real replay-ability. Don't get me wrong, I really like this game and If you enjoy dark fantasy, suspense, and story based game play this is definitely the game for you. I would have preferred a little more free world exploration, off beaten paths, that sort of thing. The developers created a beautiful world and being able to explore it more with easter eggs/secret areas as a reward would have been nice. For the physics: I personally get annoyed when my character has to walk at weird angles and can still fall off the map (looking at you swamp area) or if I have to jump from the right side of the screen to the left, I shouldn't be able to jump behind the object I'm aiming for. Not the biggest of deals, but certainly annoyed me enough to pull me out of the experience a few times. All and all I agree with the general consensus from this community - This is a great game for what it promises to give and I really enjoyed it!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful landscapes contrasting against unsettling sights really set the mood for this game. A wild adventure tugging you between feeling excitement to dread, fearing what you will come upon next and yet not being able to look away. The story is so interesting to me and I love the Scandinavian fables/myths that are apart of this game. The music is at times breathtaking and other times haunting, complimenting the scenes you come upon perfectly. I truly enjoyed this game and was sad once the adventure came to an end.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A game with a pretty epic story, also losts of brutality and sadness. It may look like a game for kids, but it's not. It's very dark and this darkness give it a special entry in my book. Well also it's quality. It's a hardcore adventure with brutal norse mythologies and some more lore in form of mythological story books, that are all very enjoyable and connected to the creatures you find. This game is also ful of cute creatures, but the creatures from the books end up being game bosses. I am usually not a big fan of boss fights, but here they managed to make them pretty interesting. The same can be said with the traversal puzzles. It's a very enjoyable game, it's amazing. Could be my game of the year... absolutely recommended!!

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble is a single player third-person game that is based off of Scandinavian folklore. You play as a small boy named Olle and you travel through the forest looking for your sister. You will encounter many unlikely friends and gruesome enemy's in through your journey. There are also some puzzles and even boss fights around the forest that you will have to get through to find your sister. -"Awe this game is so cute and wholesome! :)"-"WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥♥-"-"I just... I killed it... I am a murderer... Oh god..."This game is pretty complex controls wise, sometimes you fall because you don't actually know what key to click (I died multiple times to this ungodly fate). However, if you want to jump straight into a game with some complicated controls, sometimes frustrating bosses as well as very graphic and horror themes scenes, you will enjoy this game! But if you are super super new to gaming and don't want anything challenging then I would not recommend this game to you until you become more familiar with your controls.The game play is mainly you going through the story you are leaded through the various paths and such. You collect little figurines that have no other purpose then that they are super cute and they are achievements. Most of the game play however comes from the boss fights and various puzzles you will have to solve throughout the game. Which are somewhat simple however if you die a lot you will become super frustrated (like I did).In my personal opinion the graphics are absolutely gorgeous. Its mostly realistic, though sometimes the graphics are a little bit buggy. The music that comes with the scenery and boss fights are also extremely incredible making for the player to become super connected and present with what is happening in the current moment.The community seems nice though I have not interacted with them personally. I have only seen videos and posts that have been posted to steam.You can play however long you like however, realistically it only takes around five hours to complete. I personally do not think it has a lot of replay-ability. In my opinion I really loved this game, the story and soundtrack absolutely are up to par with what I personally enjoy playing. After I get most or all the achievements however, I probably would never play this game again. Doesn't mean that I do not recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth the money. Do know what you are getting into, this game is very dark as true fables are. Tons of gore and violence, but Bramble is so stunning though! One of the most beautiful games I have played, amazing music and shares the stories behind what you are doing, and great foreshadowing. I have even enjoyed replaying the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10A very dark and fun game.Inspired from little nightmares and others.Makes you feel very emotion that is possible (joy, sadness, fear, disgust) The game really makes you think and i love the Swedish folklore aspect, I wish more games do this.The only issue i have is the achievement to not die for the entire run through of the game. it is almost impossible and a lot of the time you die from slipping of a log because the game does not lock you in a 2D direction even though you can only walk 2 ways on the log, This makes you fall and die and restart the game. So they should remove the achievement, fix the controls a bit or make it easier to earn the achievement so that only 0.3% of players earn it.But overall, What a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: good Limbo-like but short. the last few levels are a bit of a slog and they reuse setpieces a few times which is disappointing given the short run time. also the game is not optimized well at all, even if you have a good graphics card your PC is gonna run like a jet engine. buy on sale. i played another Limbo-like released this year, Planet of Lana, and i think Bramble succeeds where that game fumbles by being better-paced and focused on the action and cinematic setpieces instead of on repetitive, tedious, and generally easy puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: A horror experience based on scandinavian folklore.It is a masterpiece.The pacing of the narrative is really well developed, leading us to discover this vast oniric world.There are heartwarming moments followed by terrifying sequences of violence.The sound design is top notch and the levels are fun and creative.I wish all the people involved in this game all the sucess in the world.God Bless you
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: The game has its strengths and its weaknesses. It is beautiful, dark and memorable. The music is fantastic and the game does not shy away from twisted topics. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: the graphics are insanely good. there are a few moments where they wont load fast enough but that is probably just from my own errors. _childDocuments_.review: People who liked Inside, Limbo, Little Nightmares, etc will be very happy with this. What differs are its heavy emphasis on story, some light boss fight sequences, and its use of a more 'dynamic' camera that pans and rotates around set pieces, rather than adhering to strict 2.5-D viewpoint like the others.Good things about Bramble TMK:• Brilliant set pieces, lore, storytelling + environment • Like playing a Grimm's fairy tale• A roiling, brooding, restless soundtrack ranging from exotic to horror film-level scary• Seriously the music is amazing, almost like its own character.Things that are not so great about BTMK:• Pretty awkward controls (intentionally)• Depth perception can be an issue• More trial-and-error than I prefer (it is endemic to the genre but still)• Pretty short but doesn't end too soon.• Boss fights are not that fun imoThe good outweighs the bad by far. Only negative is its length; I think at 6 hours the reg price is a little high but not ridiculous. I got it on sale for ~$9 so I'm happy, it was a very odd and original experience. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly a lot of love has been put into this but I can't recommend it. It has some nice ideas with pretty environments and lovely music, but it's seriously marred by poor character models and animation (the stuff that isn't mocap), imprecise mechanics/platforming and egregious game design. About 70% of this game is dedicated to hard-fail sequences (ie you make a single mistake, you die, you start over eg chase sequences, stealth sequences etc) which wouldn't be so bad if the mechanics and platforming were well-implemented but they aren't, they're just janky as hell. As a result I found it more frustrating than enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely phenomenal game. The cinematics, graphics and art style was just 10/10. I've seen some real beautiful games in my time but this is definitely in my top 5. Music is incredible too! Can't say anything bad about it to be honest. Thoroughly enjoyed playing this through - took me about 5 hours to complete. Definitely recommend this especially if you're stepping your toes into horror.

_childDocuments_.review: This is more of a journey than a game, and its completely worth it.Atmosphere, Visual and effects are an outstanding part of this game.The linear world feels completely alive, it continuously stimulates your eye and does feel as if its completley filled with magic. The world build here does a great job with such an amazing folklore and truly introduces you to how a child might perceive a tale.In contrast to other much darker and scarier games that are similar, most of the areas in this world are very pretty and beautiful almost through the entirety of it.Great music, great narration, a good fairy tail that you would wish to awake from.The only downside to it, its how easy the entire game is (probably the easiest game I have on Steam), there is no challenge, no puzzles (unless you are 8 or less), no need for exploration.An awesome short nightmarish experience!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I found my playthrough of Bramble to be really enjoyable. It took me just under five and a half hours to complete it with 29/30 achievements. That being said, here we go. Positives:-The game's aesthetics are beautiful.-The music perfectly fits the game's atmosphere and mood.-I really enjoyed the lore and the story and as as result I found myself looking forward to each new chapter-The collectible storybooks were a wonderful addition and really added another layer of depth to the world. -The bosses were extremely well designed and detailed. Negatives:-The controls can be a little unresponsive with MnK. There were several times where I tried to pull out Olle's light and flash it and it just wouldn't happen-A bit of a walking sim, which may not be a negative if you really like those!-There was a specific part in the swamp that actually made me little uncomfortable, involving a baby and a puddle. Again, that's just a personal issue subjective to each person. Overall, I give this game a solid 7/10. Would recommend Just exercise caution if you're sensitive to child abuse.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is Little Nightmares if it was based around Scandinavian folklore.And... that's pretty much it. The gameplay features light platforming and puzzling and it looks drop-dead gorgeous.The only gripe I have with it is that the monster designs aren't really that clever, but they make up for it ten-fold with their set-pieces and boss fights. Especially Pesta. Plus, it's folklore. Every monster in folklore looks the same, so it gets a pass.If you're a Little Nightmares fan that wants to play a game with a little more culture behind it, pick up Bramble: The Mountain King and try not to punt the gnomes.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble sits nicely in the very underpopulated type of games such as Little Nightmare I & II and INSIDE. I truly commend these developers for trying to pull off a hand-crafted experience like this, and I will be absolutely following what they do next.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: The price point currently is 29.99, according to google there is between 4-7 hours of game play depending on your skill and willingness to explore. _childDocuments_.review: Lets start with the obvious, this game is absolutely gorgeous, the level of details is simply amazing.The atmosphere is eerie, giving you a feeling of dread and uneasiness at all times (reminding me of the Forest Temple in Ocarina of Time), way to make me feel nostalgic!And i really commend the developers for using Scandinavian folklore as an inspiration, even for things spooky.There's to many games with horror elements, and it's way to often random monsters, or merely amalgamations of things perserved as scary or discomforting, and it's getting tiresome at times.So this is a fresh new take i'm all for!I'm still mesmerized by this game, it certainly lived up hype and praises it got, and i would highly recommend it to just about everyone that feels like they're up for a grand adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: the Mountain King is a fascinating and dark fairy tale bathed in Norwegian folklore. This is a narrative, linear experience that will take you close to 6 hours in your first play through as long as you're not gunning it to the end.  The visuals are spectacular and the gameplay is simple. There are are puzzle, platforming and combat scenarios throughout the game that don’t feel samey.  There are collectables to discover if you take your time exploring the world.I played it twice, back to back.  I thoroughly enjoyed my first play through, but got nothing out of the second.  There is no replayability outside of looking for and collecting the remaining collectables and going for 100%.  I played it through a second time to get more of my money out of it because I knew I would never go back in after that initial 6 hour play-through.Recommend on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't recommend the game.1. There is no real story, no interesting narrative or coherent lore. It's like RPGs in the 80ies: A bad guy (the mountain king) captures your sister and you have to rescue her. Thats the story, it does not go deeper. On the way to the king, you pass through independent episodes in which nothing is really told and in which you don't meet or interact with any interesting NPCs. There are boss battles in some episodes and after a successful fight, at best it is explained who it was and what their back story was.2. Camera work is bad in this game. And because the camera movement also changes the avatar's direction of movement, you have to constantly adapt the direction of movement to the camera movement. This is often unsuccessful and you slip off a plank, fall down or jump off it. The avatar dies unnecessary often because of that, especially if you play with a controller.3. The boss fights are bland and repetitive with a preference for triple repetition.4. The avatar remains colorless. There is no character development. There is just one scene that tells us a little about the protagonist's inner life.5. There is one scene in the game that is very disturbing and really inappropriate for an entertainment medium.6. The avatar is a child and you have to prepare the see the child die often in multiple brutal ways. Don't take the trigger warning lightly. The game mechanics are designed to see the child die often. In principle, the game is a negatively creative way an encyclopedia of various ways in which a child can die or be brutally killed.The violence against children is not even the core problem, the problem is that the game makes nothing out of it. It's just a world in which the most brutal violence is practiced against children. The game does not work discursively with what it depicts, it does not go beyond what it shows graphically, it ultimately does not conduct a meta-discourse about itself, as other games with drastic depictions of violence do (cf. The Last of Us Part II). And that makes it repulsive and boring. Which is a real pity: an interesting meta-discourse would probably have cured the mediocrity in the other areas.In contrast to this game, I can recommend to have a look at two other games that do a lot of the things right that are wrong here. One game is Tunic, which can be described as Zelda meets Dark Souls. This could be for those who like a bit more combat-oriented gameplay. The other is Stray. Less combat-oriented, but with the cat a character you simply have to take to your heart right from the start. A cat exploring the world and doing cat things. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful setting with well great artistic design.  The game was pretty dark at times but it did add to the overall mood and atmosphere.  This game definitely kept my attention and it was a good way to spend a night.  The puzzles were not very challenging but that was fine by me as I was really enjoying moving the story along.  The boss fights were challenging at times but not to the level of outright frustration.  Graphics were excellent as was the sound design and engineering.  The stereo effect was put to good use for developing an awareness of surroundings.  I think a lot of games try that but don't accomplish it very well.  This one does and it was a neat experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy cinematic platformers like Little Nightmares or Inside, there's a good chance you'll enjoy Bramble too. Like those other titles, this is a short but sweet experience that combines light platforming, stealth and chase sequences and very little direct combat. The similarities don't end there; Bramble's dark fairy-tale narrative is often very bleak in tone, though it mixes the lighthearted and the grim to great effect. The are moments of stunning beauty in Bramble but also of visceral gore and horror (this isn't one for the kids!). The environments look great, coming close to photo realism at times and the creatures of Nordic folklore that stalk you are fantastically designed and suitably terrifying.It's important to come into Bramble with the right expectations. This is more an experience than a game. It isn't mechanically interesting or complex, it isn't challenging and it isn't going to take you long to finish. But if you're looking for a straightforward, linear adventure with great visuals, audio and atmosphere, this is well worth a look.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Great story and atmosphere, excellent art and horror elements.I find some of the game design awful, especially the control combined with the arbitrary camera motion. I fell thousand times because of this, the game turned from fun to frustration and made me want to quit. The blur in some scenes made me dizzy, I had to stop and rest several times. @devs Please consider an option to disable the blur.This game is not bad at all! But there are quite many games that won't annoy the player while retain great story and visuals.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: beautiful art and ost, very fun gameplay, not too difficult and i finished the storyline in 4 1/2 hours. camera is a bit strange though, i found that it was hard to gauge depth or figure out where i was supposed to go because it moved so weirdly. wasn't bad enough to make the game too much harder but it definitely made the platforming sections tough.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: First two hours game play: So far the game has been good not great a little slow pace but it seems it's getting better. I feel this game is heavily influenced by Little Nightmares, the game play and mechanic is really similar. Although personally I prefer the Little Nightmare atmosphere over this from horror perspective.Visuals are really good and cool and it's one of the strong aspect of this game, it also has very smooth performance no lag or any stutter so far. Playing highest quality with 3090, 12900K at 1440p.As I said game play is very simple and straight forward, nothing challenging, simple puzzles with interactions like hiding, running and ... Personally I'd prefer to see more challenging puzzles and fights but that's me, you might like this style.Story telling is good but I think it could've been much more than this, I feel I am missing a lot of details about this world and its lore. It could've been told through areas that nothing much is happening, I really wanted to know more about this world but so far it had very limited information. The other negative point that I can mention is that there were lots of walking in this game without anything happening which might be fun to look at the world but the unfortunately you cant control the camera and you are forced in a direction so you cant really look around. Overall I think if you like games like Little Nightmares you probably will like this game too. If you are not fan of that game maybe wait for a discount since it's about 4-5 hours game play I think.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This feels a whole lot like Little Nightmares or Inside where you're moving around (in this case a little bit in 3 dimensions) platforming and solving puzzles. Some of the boss battles were slightly tricky to figure out, but really this isn't a terribly deep thinking puzzler.What really sets this one apart is that you can feel the storytelling and mythology. I swear I know more of these myths than I know of most others, since it feels like I'm living through them.Also like Little Nightmares, this is incredibly dark. I get a fresh rest in the light, and love those moments. Then I transition back into the darkness and am on edge throughout.This is still pretty short. It's tons of fun, but don't go in expecting 20 hours of game play.Easily my favorite parts of the game are stumbling across the books with storytelling and images that related to the area/scenario I'm playing through. Though I say that, I'm not sure I'll forget the rubber ducky anytime soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: --- BRAMBLE: Ivy Climbing Simulator ---In a similar fashion to many other Little Nightmares fans, I went searching for similar experiences.Bramble caught my eye as a potential winner, and I really wanted to like it, but it falls short on several levels.First off, the visuals and soundtrack are excellent, there is no faults there and I commend the work done in that regard with the highest praise.That being said, unfortunately the gameplay is downright boring at best, and tediously infuriating at worst.- Movement is far too sluggish to keep pace with the environments sprawling areas.- Do you like CLIMBING IVY? YOU'RE IN LUCK BECAUSE IT"S OVER HALF OF THE GAME.- There are pointless quicktime-like events and input presses when just letting the player control the character normally would've served the immersion better.- The constant camera angle switching is disorienting and not in a good way for horror. Too often the environment is not readable, the camera is always cutting out important information, and the constant camera switching becomes a nuisance rather than a desired effect.Overall, it feels like they would've been better off at making a movie rather than a game.Side Note: Stopped playing at the 4th chapter due to the really bizarre and lazy insertion of occult/satanic imagery and ritualistic ideals. I understand the games inspirations, but it still feels incredibly dated and absurd to see these things in horror nowadays. It's overdone in horror and it breaks immersion; it's comical at best and spiritually bankrupt at worst. Neither serve game play or world building well.5/10Bramble could've been something special but is drastically held down by the intrusive camera, molasses game play and stereotypical uninspired horror tropes.Bonus Note: The gnomes sound design is literally just a pitched up baby crying and throwing a tantrum and it's pervasive whenever they're around. I don't know what doorknob thought that was a good idea.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. the graphics and audio are breathtaking and really draw you into game-play. The horror is immersive and skin-crawling however defiantly check the trigger warnings. The platforming and parkour isn't too hard or too easy. The enemies gradually use new mechanics as you play and are original except for one enemy which was reused once. The boss battles are challenging but not frustrating and are a good length of fight. you get to ride a hedgehog and idk how they did it but that little guy is adorable. All the character models are amazing looking and the hostile creatures are honestly really intimidating or scary. The voice acting is superb and you really care about the protagonist. now my critiques. The story line is fine but fairly generic and the game halfway through stops being fighting creatures in the woods and throws you into a huge arc which i found to be fairly similar to a lot of other games. Same goes for the ending. I personally would have rather that the game stayed like the first half where you meet fun creatures and battle folklore tales instead of travelling to a mountain to free a king from a curse. That being said I still really enjoyed the story. the baby gnomes are SO ANNOYING when they cry and they don't just cry for a bit and then stop they cry and wail until you save them and it fully makes you not want to save them but you have to.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun, very pretty short game. the music is fantastic and the character designs equally so. My only complaint is with the actual player controls of the game at certain parts, but that aspect may be a better experience if you play with a controller rather than a mouse and keyboard like I played it with. Very immersive, especially if you're about folklore (especially of the Nordic variety). The "boss" fights are all quite unique and don't linger so long that their mechanics become repetitive. 8/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I saw a short portion video on this game and figured I'd try it out..SO glad I did. This game is beautiful. The story line and how they tied in different fables to progress the story, so smooth. I started playing this morning and finished by the evening, so yes it is a short game but damnit...it's so freaking goood. 10/10 recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A very atmospheric game that is sadly ruined by it's controls and game design. I would recommend using a controller over mouse and keyboard but even then the controls are not good. The gameplay itself is extremely linear without any chance to explore the beautiful enviroment. It's very dark at times. And forget about playing it with the recommended gamma settings.Since there is nothing to do but follow the one path that the game allows you to follow I'd rather watch a video of this game then play it myself.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: WOW! This game was truly an experience...a unique one! It had me completely enthralled the entire game! Full range of emotions from joy to disgust and everything in between. The graphics, music, gameplay, storyline, etc were on point. I thought for a moment the wonderful Jonna Jinton was singing one of the songs. Just keep in mind, it does have very dark subjects which can be quite rattling or disturbing and to be honest, I'm not sure how I feel about the ending but still a great gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Try to remember the feelings you got as a child, when your parents read you bedtime stories. The excitement, the fear, the joy, the sense of wonder and your imagination taking you away to an other time and an other world. That's the feelings this game managed to awake in me, even do I now am as old as my parents whas, when they first read those stories for me. It starts of slow and kind of underwhelming, then it sweeps the rug from under your feet and takes you on this wonderful journey. I want to applaud the sounds in this game, especially the ones from the bog level. The creepy laughter and the babycrys, actually sounds like they are coming from the room you are sitting in, or outside it, which makes for an extra creepy experience. This game is a breath of fresh air, after a long time with bad and poor quality games, so I highly recommend it. Thumbs up!👍👍
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: i'd give this 7 out of 10....the art and feel of the game is spot on...it's Little Nightmares written by Brothers Grimmthe controls are garbage. for a game that expects you to walk in a straight line often, it's really hard to walk in a straight line. i'm not sure if this is by design, as the main boy moves like Tin Man with rickets and the game seems to relish/intend on you dying frequently to establish a trial/error system. sometimes i knew what was coming but had to fight the code to stay alive, sometimes failing. i think everyone deserves the privilage to be able to figure out a game on the fly and beat it in one go if they are able. but all that aside it's a unique take on dark fairy tales, worth a play on a good sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Worth every minute and every penny. Phenomenal storytelling, environmental design and soundtrack. Very nostalgic since it had a lot of lore and music reminiscent of my childhood, thanks to growing up in Sweden's beautiful countryside; where the forests and fields are splendid during the day, and quite... unpleasant during the night. If you're fond of Swedish folklore and mythology, this will be a golden gem for you. I was careful to avoid spoilers, so little did I know how perfect it would be to play Bramble: The Mountain King during Midsummer Eve. Wonderful coincidence that really set the mood.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A beautifully crafted game that has found a way to somehow be both enchanting and horrifying. The gameplay is reminiscent of Little Nightmares or INSIDE, and can sometimes be frustrating at times, but it’s a small price to pay to experience the story. You HAVE to play this game, but wait until it goes on sale, only because it’s so short.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely one of the best dark platform games I've completed. The visuals, music and story are beautiful. The only "minus" is that the gameplay could be a bit more extensive - fortunately, we won't get bored with it, because finishing the game takes about 3.5-4 hours. A bloody, dark production, full of references to Nordic folklore. I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Rather annoying gameplay based exclusively on trial / error and repetitions.  The fixed camera is awful, there are many situations when you don't know in which direction to go or jump.  There is not a Depth of Field toggle or slider and the game looks like 7 diopters myopia simulator (fortunately most of it can be disabled in Engine.ini).I had higher expectations about this game because of the nice graphics and the original artistic style but speaking honestly, it sucks.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic. The mix of atmospheric adventure, puzzle platformer and horror with with a story rich folklore topic makes this indie game absolutely fantastic. To be fair, i was quite surprised by the unexpected turns this game took, and yes, it was a roller coaster of emotions, but that is, what I like in a game. With all the unfinished games coming out, Bramble stands for a change. I got more than I asked for and/or expected. I personally struggle with the controls here and there, but that has never been my strong suit. I might see how it goes playing with a controller. Overall, I do recommend this game! Epic Boss Fights, tricky Puzzles, lovingly created characters and bold Horror Elements make this Game must-have.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble is a triumph of sound design and art direction. The world is brilliantly brought to life through Martin Wave and Dan Wakefield's sensational score (namely the arrangement of In the Hall of the Mountain King), and extremely well done camera work.The game does show a few rough edges such as clipping issues and frame dips, but stands tall amongst the linear horror/adventure genre with gameplay that is simple, at times challenging, and constantly innovating on itself. This is an easy recommendation for anyone who wants a tight 4 hour experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This game's a dark one for sure, and real creepy many times. The infused horror elements are really good and I've found myself ill at ease several times. It's got an atmosphere of great melancholy and despair, they've captured this perfectly in all its grimness. While playing this game, as a Swede myself, I often feel and recognize the immense depth and darkness of the Swedish/Northen folk lore and old world fairy tales with all their dark and brutal things that moves and lurks in the Northen mysterious fairy tale nights. It makes me reconnect with my childhood stories with the fascination and dread I felt back then when I heard and read them. I couldn't get enough of them when I was a kid. But, the game's also honey sweet at times with a myriad little curious creatures and personas of the small people of the fay which makes up a fine balance between the darkness and the light, It's a rich game filled to the brim with curious little things, beauty and sweet innocence that is in stark contrast to the heavy darkness that permeates the world. It's a rather unusual a game and I love it. The guys behind it has made a fantastic job of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: For such a short playthrough runtime, it was disappointing to have such clunky feeling and imprecise controls throughout the entire game.  This negatively impacted everything from the already mediocre platforming sections, to making boss fights too long and not enjoyable due to having to repeat multiple times simply due to poor controls. The puzzles were often very simple, yet had poor user conveyance on finding things necessary to solve them.The oft lauded graphics were excellent at times, and rather pedestrian in others, making for an inconsistent visual experience.The story is based on a dark, but narratively flimsy nordic children's fable, and could possibly be a good children's game, but the disturbing visuals, narrative topics and gore make it a decidedly PG-13 affair.It's an average game, but I feel the need to downvote it due to what I feel is quite a bit of overhype.  If you greatly enjoyed playing Limbo, Inside, or Little Nightmares then perhaps buy this on a deep sale ($5-$10 at most) for a one time brief playthrough, as I do not see any replayability in this game and frankly, I do not think this game will stand the test of time.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: What do I like about the game?It hast some ...some...neat mechanics and the boss fights are 10/10and yet my review is nagative.. sooo what do I not like?I do't like how the camera forces you to go in a certain direction and you can not move it freely at all. also the game doesn't allow you to backtrack at all. meaning if you go to far somewhere and then want to check out the other path.. you can't not because the path closed or anything but simply because the game doesn't allow you to go back.It's also quite short... not even 5h, including getting the achievements
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I got drawn in by the beautiful graphics and magical concept, especially as it brings nostalgia and comfort to a swede. But after about an hour I just felt irritation during pretty much the entire game. The constantly shifting angles makes it difficult to follow along with the controls, sometimes you can't even see that it's a new angle you need to follow leading to death. Not to mention that the rules of the game seem to change as you go on, one moment you can't stray of your path if you try and the other the tiniest misstep sends you to your death. It's also confusing what the game wants you to do because the map is too undefined and unclear about the next step. Many levels I've had to retry an annoying amount simply to understand what my goal even is. I strongly considered getting a refund after an hour because of all these reasons but the positive parts made me at least want to finish it. I wish I had just gotten the refund and spared myself the stress.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is an absolutely stunning game. As dark as the story turns out to be, that makes it all the better. I sat down to play it, just to get a feel for the game and told myself I would play a small portion of the game, then play it here and there....I ended up playing it for 5 hours straight. Every time I thought maybe I should take a break the story grew more interesting and sucked me back in. There was a few bugs here and there but over all, its really a stunning and captivating game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic experience. Short story driven game with puzzles and sweet boss battles. A little jank controls sometimes but I will likely play any future games by this developer if they are just as excellent. Down right beautiful visuals, expert tale spinning, and fear inducing musical score. Worth every cent spent and every minute lent. Bravo!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible Nordic fairy tale, complete with the entire scope of lore that is, at all times, beautiful, repulsive and captivating. If you are a fan of stories around frightening trolls that eat children, benevolent forest creatures, whimsical gnomes and malicious kings, you will love this game. It is easy enough for just about anyone to pick up while providing a challenge that doesn't make you want to beat your head into the wall. I strongly recommend playing this with headphones as the sound design is absolute top notch. I do also recommend playing with a controller, as others have mentioned. It feels a lot smoother that way. The content can be very heavy at times but anyone who has read the old school Nordic folklore will tell you that these things were just a part of life and/or myth. The Skogsra in particular was breathtaking - there is a good reason she is their mascot, so to speak. I truly recommend this for anyone who is looking for a quick, narrative driven folk story that makes you just a liiiiittle spooked and leaves you dreaming (or having nightmares) about Scandinavian bedtime stories for days to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: 4.7/5--Music: GreatGraphics: GoodStory: Great (Dark, imo darker than Little Nightmares)--Recommend: yes, to a mature audience, it can get a bit dark so I can see it being uncomfortable to a certain audience--Cons: Got stuck a few times in certain spawn-points so it has it's bugs here and there, but not excessive that it happened to make the game unplayable
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Some things in life you should not experience... this is one of them. Shame cause I love myths, legends and fables of all cultures...But the story was bland and the puzzles just felt like a chore rather than something challenging.The only thing kinda interesting was the music for the final boss battleother than than no idea how its rated overwhelmingly positive.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: It really depends on what you're looking for in this game.Horror? Nah, barely exists and most you get is creepy.Puzzle platforming? Very minimal, and does not test your wits at allAtmospheric interactive movie? Yes, this is probably the best description.It is similar to Inside, but without any of the puzzles.It is similar to Little Nightmare, but without the horror.It is similar to Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons, but without the extra brother to control.It very linear, short, and simple.As mentioned before it is very pretty, atmospheric and sound designs are great.Honestly the visuals are the main reason I bought it. Except I was expecting a bit more... "fun" per say.So if you're looking for a bit more "game" than the visual like me, this is not recommended.Else you'll feel like reading a creepy children's book or a young adult novel like goosebumps.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful The controls are very intuitive It encapsulates the Scandinavian aesthetic perfectly runs flawlessly EDVARD F****NG GRIEG The soundtrack is from out of this world! It's one of the best i've ever heard. The game is extremely short [3-4 hrs] It misnames a few mythical creatures. Despite the run length, some fights are clearly just there to add playtime and add no value to the story. The camera angles can often cause you to fall and makes maneuvering difficult.Ultimately, i'd recommend the game for anyone with an afternoon to kill that enjoys games similar to Inside, Little nightmares and limbo. As the vibe and gameplay style is very similar and clearly draws inspiration from all of the aforementioned titles.The music is phenomenal, and adds real cultural spice to the game to make you really feel enveloped in the culture while playing. Hell, they have Edvard Grieg, you can't beat that.The story is nothing crazy to write home about! Very basic stuff, and it's really more like travelling through many mini-stories with one bigger story that you're actively progressing towards at the same time. If you enjoy Scandinavian culture, or even are Scandinavian, this game is 100% for you! Easily worth the price!Bramble The Mountain king is a fantastic game for any adult and despite a few issues that only some Norse folklore nerds will notice, it's a fantastic game with astounding visuals and an aesthetic that will blow you away!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: It took me about 4.5 hours to complete what is possibly one of the absolute best releases of 2023. Where do I begin to talk about what this game gets right?1. Phenomenal sound track. No matter what you were doing there was very nearly appropriate music or ambient sound to accompany you. The final boss's theme music is definitely my favorite, please make the ost available everywhere. 2. Incredible environments in every chapter. The world felt so genuine, and each environment helped me build a great internal picture of the Bramble world. The vibrancy of one setting contrasted with the melancholy of another didn't feel like a change of pace or deviation, it all flowed naturally together. 3. The Bosses. There was not a single boss fight where I did not have fun. Every boss had their own unique combat style, and very rarely it felt like mechanics were being reused. 4. The story. The overall story was so captivating. A young boy trekking through a harsh and unforgiving world to find a sister that for all he knew was dead, encountering so much that would dissuade anyone who wasn't a protagonist away from adventure and still persevering. The constant conflicts and hardships that young Olle had to endure made for an incredible story of growth and sibling love. 5. The variation in game play. It wasn't all platforming, and it wasn't all combat, and it wasn't all stealth. It blended different game play styles quiet well. My only gripe would be that it was so short for the amount of story building that could have been possible. The Digital Art Book even talks about some scrapped ideas that seemed like they could have been fun. Of course, if scrapping those ideas meant that the game would pace better, that was a good decision to make.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game with good narratives and simple but great gameplay. The only thing I would talk about as negative is the text in certain parts of the game being in the developer's main language and there are no translations for it. This is minimal, but part of my intent on understanding the game completely get's affected. Not even google lens could help me find the meaning of certain parts.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a game developed by Dimfrost Studio and published by Merge GamesThe game offers some nice graphics and a superb aesthetic, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the sameThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game but a fun game nonethelessBramble: The Mountain King overall, however, is an incredibly fun game to play, yet sometimes repetitive and it does get boring if being played for a long time, but is a really good horror adventure game to play in short bursts!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Decently spooky.  Swedes don't ♥♥♥♥ around with their fairy tales.  My major complaint is the controls and movement speed.  Olle sometimes feels like he's going too slow.  Like, you've got monsters trying to kill you, get a little pep in your step.  I wouldn't let that stop you from playing it, though.  Poor kid goes through a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I am writing this review after like a month of not playing it, but managed to have time to type this review so it may not be so accurate. From public opinion this game is by far a great game, but I say otherwise. It's not a horrible game, it's actually a work of art, but there are some major concerns I had while playing this game. To me it seems the original plot of the story kept changing because the creators of the game kept getting more cool ideas and kept squeezing it all together into this small game which ended up making the game's plot very confusing. I started wondering what I am even doing at many parts while playing the game because the story just wasn't it. Aside from all the cool scenes, it's a confusing story game. From trolls to demons like with magic powers to who knows what, the plot wasn't consistent and at times I'm left wondering what is even going on. -- SPOILERSThere is a part of the game which the player climbs what I presume is a light house and at the top is this crystal like thing which you touch and you get this 1900's horror-like clip which I found so irrelevant to the game, whys it even in the game?There were way more annoying/confusing stuff, but I have forgotten since I haven't played it in a while.Aside from that, one of the many things which I found annoying was some of the sound designs. They are either too good for the game, don't fit the game, could be better, or whatever. One example is the little gnome creatures we start helping at the beginning of the game. Why did the creators of the game find it necessary to make them weep, yap, and make noises like little children. It was one of the most annoying things I had to listen to while playing the game.To me this game's story and plot is utter garbage, the only thing keeping people playing this would be the scenery, art, and visuals. I do not recommend unless you are looking for a game with cool effects and such.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: The Scary bits are really tense and can get your heart going. The atmosphere goes from peaceful and joyous to an unrelenting grim without hesitation. A beautiful game with a good fairy tale story. It can be beaten in one sitting, which I really enjoyed. I got the whole experience and I liked it. I was not bored for any of the game play. The voice acting was spot on. The music was also very well done and matched the game perfectly. Give this one a look if you are into some Nordic Lore and fairy tales. However, the content warning at the beginning of the game is no joke and there are some seriously grim moments so take care.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This is a dark Nordic fairytale - and every aspect of the game from the gameplay, to the gorgeous graphics, to the story perfectly captures this. I particularly enjoyed the "boss fights", which I didn't expect from a game like this where you're playing as a vulnerable young boy trying to find his sister. But I enjoyed them a lot, and the boss encounters were fittingly made where you still feel your character is vulnerable, yet you can persist somehow. The atmosphere of the game is amazing, and I was more creeped out by it than most horror games.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: The story was good, the final boss battle was fun. The rest was rather unenjoyable. The gameplay is clunky, hard to play on controller for sure. The perspective often makes it hard for you to judge where your character will land. Most of the boss fights you die because of this or because the game really sucks at telling you what it wants you to do. I am not asking for hand holding but sometimes it really is bad at giving directions.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic little game unlike anything else I've played. Bramble: The Mountain King's probably most similar to Little Nightmares in terms of its gameplay, but it borrows ideas from older cinematic platformers like Another World and Heart of Darkness as well. This isn't to say that the game doesn't bring its own ideas to the table because it certainly does, primarily in the form of its dark fairy tale aesthetic heavily inspired by Scandinavian myths and legends. This is a short and sweet game for sure, lasting only about 4-5 hours, but that feels like the perfect length for the kind of experience it's trying to deliver. If you're a fan of Little Nightmares and cinematic platformers in general, you won't be disappointed. Lovely game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: a fairly short game overall, that's worth playing once.All puzzles are very easy for both new and experienced gamers. Battles can be a bit challenging. You may die a few times. In the end you will find the patterns and do what you have to do. There are no lives in the game or continues (!), meaning that once you sit at your desk/ in front of your PC, you will finish it within 4-5 hours (I left it running and took a 45 min break for lunch and still finished within 5 hours).Is it worth the full price? probably not.
