_childDocuments_.review: Congratulations to Dimfrost on an incredible game!! I was hooked from the first time I saw the trailer a couple years ago and I wishlisted this on Steam and couldn't have been happier. This game exceeded my expectations from the beautiful visuals both gameplay and the interactive beautiful storybook sequences to the incredible audio and story this is one of those very rare experiences that sticks with you for many years to come!  It is a truly memorable experience that is very rare  to get in a game these days. As a huge lover of Norse Mythology and dark Nordic fairytales I couldn't pass this up! If you love Little Nightmares or horror/fantasy games you will love this! I love how Dimfrost never sugarcoated the lore like Disney does all the time. Nordic fables can be both beautiful and very dark and it's nice to see the devs stick to the original source the way these stories were told in the Middle Ages.From the technical side of things the game is very well optimized at Max settings with no shader compillation stutters common to most recent 3D UE4 games. Rock solid performance from start to finish and I haven't encountered any bugs either. This has to be 2023's hidden gem so far! The only thing I wish is that the game was a bit longer because I was so immersed in the game I was sad it ended a bit sooner than expected. Hopefully there will be DLC or a Bramble 2 sequel. _childDocuments_.review: What can I say? I HATE platformers! In fact, I hate all fail-to-perfection games (bye-bye roguelikes and soulslikes, oh, and F1 games). Hence the thumbs down. It's personal. Deeply personal.That said, it's a beautiful game. Of course I fell for it, and suffered through the 3D platforming. I'm Scandinavian after all. It's basically all about three things:First, there is the Swedish and Norwegian folklore and legend of course, the post-viking stuff. Charming. To us at least.Second, less obvious to outsiders perhaps, is the fond and subtle reproduction of the Scandinavian forest. A game like  did a decent job at it, although in a sweeping way because of its genre. But Bramble... such attention to detail! Here's the thing. Up here, In the forest, at dusk, early summer, the painfully brief and precious summer, there is magic in the air. And everything looks  Bramble. Third, even less obvious, but Bramble hit a string in me. Well, the early parts of the game did anyway. I couldn't put words to it at first, but then I realized what it was. It plays just like a childhood dream or nightmare. You would have to go back to one of my all-time favorite games, , to find something similar in that regard.So... I guess what I'm saying is, unless you hate plateformers too, and provided any of the above points appeal to you, then you probably want to put it on the wish list.

_childDocuments_.review: As a Swed I'm a bit biased, but let me tell you this.Bramble: The Mountain King transcends mere gaming and immerses you in a captivating narrative based on Nordic mythology. Reminiscent of the genre exemplified by Little Nightmares, this experience intertwines a compelling story line with breathtaking artwork, accompanied by amazing orchestrated musical scores the game successfully sets and sustains the desired mood. Usually horror games goes the everything is horrible route, but Bramble goes darker and darker and then light again, which gives the gameplay high peaks and low valleys. While it contains fewer unsettling moments than Little Nightmares, Bramble: The Mountain King possesses its own unique charm. It's truly captivates the player from start to finish!Pros* The game is STUNNING both in the 2D & 3D assets used & the environmental design.* The soundtrack is amazing (I've been listening to Blomstertid by Martin Wave & BJORN several times after the play through).* It flawlessly captures the essence of the Scandinavian aesthetic.Cons* At times aggravating checkpoints.* Sometimes misguides the players spacial awareness with the set camera which results in failed jumps.* Short game time.* Many puzzles but few are truly challenging.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this game! As a native Swede it was so refreshing to see some proper Swedish lore and environments. The horror elements are on point, the environments are amazing and the SFX/Soundtrack is damn good! The art is on point (lots of John Bauer inspired stuff), great voice actors and designs. HOWEVER, some of the puzzles was super weird and the auto-lock on system could have had some work before release. I was also bummed out by the weird depth of field, motion blur and grain combined with very very dark areas and it was hard to see what you were doing half of the times. Luckily some amazing individual posted a solution to remove this in a ini file under Windows/Users/(Your user)/AppData/Local/Bramble_TMK/Saved/Config/WindowsNoEditor and then open the Engine.ini file with notepad, and add this text under all the text in that ini file:[SystemSettings]r.MotionBlur.PreferCompute=0r.DepthOfFieldQuality=0r.MotionBlur.Max=0r.MotionBlurQuality=0r.DefaultFeature.MotionBlur=0r.Tonemapper.GrainQuantization=0r.Tonemapper.Quality=0I feel like these graphics settings should be added into the game, and hopefully the devs will in the future. Another thing that other people are complaining about is the price, but I think 30 EUR is more than fair, this world is currently on fire with inflation, we're all trying to get by, especially smaller dev companies. And I'd much rather pay 30 EUR for this game than giving EA or Ubisoft 60, 70, 80, 100(!) bucks for some other half-baked non-ambitious game. 8/10. Strongly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I enjoyed this game and I recommend it to those who played the Little Nightmares games. I wouldn't say this game competes with Little Nightmares in any way, but it's pretty hard to play this game and not acknowledge their similarity (and so I will).Bramble: the Mountain King (BTMK) has upwards of 18 chapters, although it feels more like 14. Each chapter is brief, but they're completely unique and almost each features a "boss fight" of some kind. The game can be beaten in around 5 - 6 hours, and I beat it in 9 hours after getting 100% achievements and writing an achievement guide (check it out!) simultaneously. For this reason, I would say the game is overpriced and more of a $20 game, but I'm not complaining. The art direction is good. The character design and the environment design are great, but the mythology is what makes this game stand out. Each character in BTMK is based off of Nordic fables, and the acts they carry out are dark and demented. Despite encountering the characters only briefly, they are what makes each chapter so memorable. Their tie-in to the main story is fitting, and it's impressive how many meaningful characters you experience in such a short time. Compared to the Little Nightmares games, there isn't really any guessing that has to be done for you to understand what's going on. This is nice, but when you finish the game, there isn't really more for you to do. There's no reason to go look up a lore breakdown or start a discussion why characters behave the way they do because, well, there isn't really any mystery. One thing I really loved about Little Nightmares were the metaphors the designers placed throughout each level, and how they helped foreshadow the story. To put it bluntly, BTMK just lacks that level of depth.From an achievement hunting perspective, this game is very, very accessible although not particularly fun. The majority of achievements are for collecting figurines, so I wouldn't say the achievement hunting experience adds anything to the story of the game. Some are creative, but if you're looking for another "perfect" game to add to your steam profile — this is an easier pick. However, once achievement is to beat the game without dying (which I hate). I personally don't see a replay-ability in this game, so this achievement is a huge chore. All in all, fun game, worth a buy, but consider wishlisting it until there's a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: As anyone with a little interest in fairy tales and legends will gladly tell you, the original stories are dark. Not a little dark, but bleak like the cold dark nights they must have been told in. And I'm surprised to see that Bramble holds on to that darkness and never lets go. Yes, there are cutesy bits with gnomes and hedgehogs - but the gore and horror is full on display here - with a beautiful cinematic art direction and marvelous narration. But you know what has me the most impressed? That aside from all the eyecandy it's not just a tech demo or a walking simulator - there's a proper game too! With several different level designs, challenging puzzles and excellent boss fights. The final boss had me sweaty palms and cursing but I managed, and the feeling of victory was glorious! Haven't had that often before. Anyway, TL;DR: recommended on all levels! Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: I had so much fun playing this game. The setting is beautiful - as is the story, the music and all of the lore. It really draws you into this world of madness and cuteness. I appreciate that the story is somewhat made up for interpretation and that it let's your imagination fill in the "gaps" of the story. Me being a Swede makes me appreciate this even more since it's set in Sweden and with all of the nordic folklore, it was really fun to see. If I should compare it to other games I've experienced it's like a mix of "Inside", "Senua's sacrifice" and "A plauge tale". All really great games, so it gives you an idea of how well made this is. It's not too challenging, and also not too easy. I feel like they balanced the gameplay really well for making both beginners and more advanced players able to enjoy it. The contrast in this game is a big reason that makes it scary and really unsettling. It goes from being adorable to really gory in a second, and it works. I loved to be part of this world, even though I'm really glad I do not have to live in it and don't have to meet those creatures. Or who knows, maybe next time I take a walk in the deep woods I will...

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a rather unique horror adventure game set in a gorgeous atmospheric fantasy world, with a more narrative driven experience, along with it's mixtures of puzzles, boss fights, folklore, and other interesting design decisions. This game, is a very unique experience overall that was captivating from start to finish. I have not played a horror or horror-like game this good in years, and that's really saying something, coming from someone who has tried many different horror and horror-like games over the span of many years. Honestly, my only, tiny, issue is that the ending, although good for what it is, and I understand why the ending is the way that it is, it does feel slightly anti-climatic even though I don't think it's a bad ending by any means. That, and sometimes the overall scale of the world can be a bit confusing at times, but at the same time, that is being done deliberately and to great effect and I also understand why the overall scale of the world is the way that it is. Either way, these issues are rather tiny to such a degree, and I don't even see those issues as real "issues" myself, so this game to me is a 10/10. This game is definitely a must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: As an experience, this game absolutely excels. Yes, there are some .. BS deaths, as some have pointed out, but the checkpoints are veeeeery generous. Don't expect a challenge per se, but do expect an incredible experience. This game is not trying to test your skills at platforming, or anything at all. It's trying to immerse you in an absolutely beautiful narrative experience. And for me, this kind of short but sweet experience is perfect. I often don't finish longer games and keep thinking "I should come back to this some day" and never do. I'm very glad I got to experience this start to finish. Took me just under 5 hours it seems - is that worth the asking price? That's for you to decide. Seeing a movie on the big screen costs more per hour than this, right? I, for one, do not regret my purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed this game. The backgrounds are beautiful, atmospheric, and memorable, featuring gorgeous Scandinavian forest landscapes in all varieties. The character designs look like they're straight out of a John Bauer painting, and the music is highly atmospheric Scandinavian folk music, ending with a great rendition of In The Hall of the Mountain King by Edward Grieg.The story varies from cute and wholesome to horrifically dark. I think maybe they could've cut down on the gore a little, as it felt pretty excessive at times, especially during the troll section early on in the game, though to be fair, the horror of it is pretty accurate to the old and very dark fairytales it borrows from. This is an aspect that I think will turn a few players off the game, though, so keep that in mind if you're considering buying this game. The small boy you play as can also get chopped in half if you're not careful while playing, so it's definitely not a game for the faint of heart.As a Norwegian, I was pleasantly surprised to see that this game doesn't only features Swedish folklore, but also a few creatures that are exclusively Norwegian, such as Pesta and the Mountain King himself. The designs and backstories for Näcken and the Skogsrå are also a nice mix of both the Swedish version and Norwegian version of the creatures, which I quite liked, as it takes the best of both worlds, while still keeping it instantly recognisable to people familiar with either country's folklore. It also isn't afraid to veer a little bit away from the original fairytales, as the main story surrounding the mountain king is a completely original one divorced from the original myths, but it works well.There have been a number of games over the years based around Scandinavian folklore, but no game has done it as well as Bramble, which really nailed the atmosphere and storytelling, and provided fun gameplay to accompany it.

If it wasnt a short game i probably wouldn't have finished.The controls are really janky. i like fixed camera but its done really poorly in this, which makes the platforming kind of unbearable at times, the depth perception sucksThe actual gameplay is barely there, you dont really do much at all and its very samey. the boss fights are all the same thing over and over, with multiple phases which feels like theyre there just for padding because nothing really changesTheres very little sense of threat in this game. The boss fights are pretty simple and short, and all the enemy encounters in general are over in seconds. the majority of this game is walking through e.g. a village with very little to worry about (besides bad platforming lol)Tension is never built. I was getting frustrated by how deeply unscary this game is. I'm a coward who gets scared by the stealth sections in batman games but this just did nothing for me. Because every encounter with a monster was so fleeting there was no time to build any tension. _childDocuments_.review: Bramble is a gem! It's one of the best games I've played. I only wish it could be loger.It's charming, atmospheric, dark, very dark at times. It's quite scary sometimes, but idk if I'd call it a horror game.Most of all it's absolutely beautiful! The scenery, lighting, camera work, sound and music are all stunning.Light, shadow and depth are gorgeous, very well composed in every frame.Visually and in terms of immersion or feeling for me it's a masterpiece.It's not the longest game (finished in ~8hours) but I don't hesitate to recommend it. Money very well spent.The weaker points like some rare, harder boss events, (one in particular) where you need a bit of luck and will probably replay a few times... do not change my overall opinion.Some details that might be important to you:It's mostly about the story, but it's not a walking simulator.It's not a "gamey" game, no combos, no numbers.Parts of the game play  like a 2.5D platformer, others are more freeform 3D, but the camera is always fixed, only rotating or on a fixed trajectory. This is what makes it very cinematographic.It runs great as well, on my 1080 ti it usually stayed over 80fps, always smooth with no hitches.If there's ever a sequel I'll surely check it out.My hope is this is the Witcher 1 of the Bramble series :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is like experiencing one of those surprisingly dark fairy tale stories that are meant to scare children for yourself. In this case, it's heavily based on Scandinavian folklore. In many aspects, the game plays and feels very similar to games like the Little Nightmares series or Limbo/Inside, with the big difference being that you get much more of a concrete narrative here. And I actually quite liked the story of this game, which is rather rare for me. The highlight, of course, is still the atmosphere that really turns this into a captivating experience. We can thank the great looking visuals, music, sound design, and voice narration working together for that.But it wasn't a huge surprise for me that where the game struggles is the gameplay itself. A lot of the game consists of soaking in the atmosphere while solving puzzles that barely can be considered puzzles and doing platforming that can barely be considered platforming because they are so simple and easy. The “boss fights” are mechanically not very complex and often consist of dodging 2-3 different attacks. But I still really enjoyed them for the visual presentation and just for how climatic they feel.I feel like the game could have done more in terms of gameplay, but the atmosphere and narrative really carried it, making this overall a great experience for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely fantastic! I found myself saying "I already love this" without even leaving the first room you spawn in on. What instantly captivated me was the use of fixed camera angles, the atmosphere, and the beautifully talented narrator. At first I found myself thinking the puzzles were too easy, but as the story progressed, I got deeper and deeper into the atmosphere and the world around me so that I didn't care about how easy or difficult it was, I was too busy being captivated. I commend how this game doesn't shy away from blood, gore, and harsher topics. Sometimes games limit themselves by trying to appease everyone. By not doing that, I was able to continuously be surprised by the curve balls the game threw at me. Some small things that I appreciated that this game did was: Not have any cut-scenes or continuation scenes after dying (the game simply fades to black and immediately spawns you back in, no need for excessive waiting or clicking), the fixed camera angles were both unique but also expertly placed so that I wasn't aggravated when trying to maneuver, and I especially appreciated how it locks you in place when walking over single lane objects (like planks and tree limbs) (one of my biggest faults with fixed angle games is how easy it is to fall off small objects but this game eradicates that).I can't recommend this experience of a game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE | WORTHWHILE |  | UNMISSABLEBramble: The Mountain King is an atmospheric horror-adventure game based on Nordic fairytales - think Midsommar meets The Witch, but aged down slightly (children's fables can be kind of messed up, huh?) in game form. The game follows a young boy searching for his sister and navigating a fantastical and often deadly world of gnomes, shapeshifters, trolls, etc. The game is rich in lore and very well-paced. That said, it is quite linear with only one real path to progress. This works well for the game and isn't a negative, in my opinion, but I do think it's worth mentioning. The soundtrack is absolutely beautiful and the environment is lovely too. Having  play during  is nothing short of epic. I think the game struggled at times with allowing for smooth navigation of a 3D world on a 2D screen. This isn't unusual in my experience, but it was frustrating to e.g. jump off something and look like I would be able to land the fall, and then wind up wildly off base and die. That said, the game has chapter select and frequent checkpoints which made it so I didn't have to redo large sections when this happened. Additionally, the game took me about 4.5-5 hours to complete, with my remaining time doing achievement clean-up (~1-1.5 hours). For its listed price, I think it's on the more expensive end for what you get, so while I absolutely recommend this game to those interested, I highly suggest waiting for it to be on a steep discount.In summary, Bramble is a compelling narrative-based adventure game the positive aspects of which are amplified by things such as an incredible soundtrack, creepy atmosphere, and nice artwork. While expensive, it's worth picking up if you're at all interested provided you can get it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: It is easy to recommend Bramble: The Mountain King (which I'll hereafter refer to as simply "Bramble") if you are interested in it for non-gameplay reasons, and that is presumably true if you are reading this review. Judged purely for its game design and gameplay, however, it has some problems.Playing Bramble feels like being part of several dark fairy tales (European fairy tales, specifically Nordic Swedish ones). Some of my favorite moments from the game were terrifying, as I was a young boy trying to escape some scary monster. You should also be aware that some moments are also genuinely horrifying, and the content certainly pulls no punches (despite the playable character being a child this is certainly not a game for children).The environments are beautiful, and sound design and music are also fantastic. The human characters felt uncanny valley-ish to me, but nothing bad enough to ruin the immersiveness of the experience. It was easy for me to get lost in the experience when some of the gameplay elements weren't getting in the way.A large portion of the game's runtime is more of a "walking simulator", where you won't really have any agency besides proceeding on the path that the developers have created. Even the camera and invisible walls prevent exploration in most cases; you definitely are not encouraged to stray from what the developers want you to do (although there are some achievements that require exploring off of the main path, which feels a bit strange when the game design so actively discourages that).There are traditional game elements, however, but I didn't find most of these particularly fun. Most of the game sequences in the first half felt like wastes of time to me (in the sense that the puzzles and action sequences weren't really difficult or rewarding; I would have preferred just keeping things as an interactive story), and most of the game sequences in the second half felt more frustrating to me than fun. Bramble isn't a difficult game, but there were sequences where I actually died an embarrassing number of times, with a large percentage of those times being in ways that felt frustrating.I think that possibly my biggest complaint would be the camera. The aesthetics of camera shots have clearly been given priority over gameplay. I don't actually mind that, and think it was a good choice for this game! But the problem is that gameplay has been created that doesn't take this into account, and then as a player you are asked to do things that are challenging _because of the camera_, with the punishment being swift and severe. (A curious sidenote: It is honestly amazing the number of times that the game expects you the player to walk off some ledge and drop down without having any way to see what is on the other side or how far you are dropping. Early in the game this was just amusing to me, but I just decided to trust the developers. As the game progressed, however, I accumulated more and more deaths that were a result of me walking off ledges or jumping the wrong way because I couldn't judge depth or direction, and then these frequent and intentional drops of faith became more and more stressful.)That's not to say that the gameplay is "bad" (and, to be fair, there were some puzzles and one boss battle that I did enjoy). Instead, it felt like a pretty average indie game, with what I would consider mistakes that I might expect from designers without much experience. I think that the mediocrity of the gameplay was made more frustrating by a few things: 1) Everything else in the experience was so good that the gameplay weaknesses felt jarring, 2) the sequences with frustration and insta-death took away from the tension and atmosphere, and 3) since so much of the game was already a walking simulator it felt superfluous to introduce game mechanics that weren't particularly polished or fun.Bramble reminded me of Little Nightmares in several ways; it felt influenced by it, and had some of the same strengths, but also some of the same weaknesses. Like Little Nightmares, however, I am positive that what I will remember from Bramble when I look back on it in the future are all of the good things, and the frustration will fade. I am definitely glad that I played it.If you look at a trailer or screenshots of the game and think "that looks like something that I would like to play" then I think it's pretty easy to recommend. It absolutely lives up to the promise of getting to experience being part of a dark fairy tale! You may also experience some gameplay frustrations, but the positives easily outweighed the negatives for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble is a great new entry in the cinematic platformer genre, becoming a natural successor to games like Limbo, INSIDE, Unravel, Little Nightmares (etc.) and their fathers ICO and Shadow of the Colossus. This time though, the game takes a step in the 3rd dimension again, making it a full fledged 3D platformer.All of the above mentioned games play a role in being sources of inspiration for Bramble, some more directly than others. Often times you'll think "Hey, I've seen this scene in <insert game from above list>". But the game does also enough of its own things to stand out from the others:- the well executed cinematic tracking shots as you walk through the insanely beautifully designed nature of sweden- a greatly told story referencing nordic myths and fairy tales narrated through voice acting- some of the most detailled gorey nightmare scenes we've yet seenAll of this is embedded in very lighthearted puzzle platforming, very easy and thus not distracting so your eyes can enjoy the many details of this world. The 3D gameplay doesn't involve many unfair jumps, and the checkpoints are very briefly seperated. There are also surprisingly many boss fight, but they are also not very difficult, so the frustration factor is very low. Also the boss phases do have checkpoints.Thus this also comes with a warning: If you seek a challenge in games and get bored easiely with shallow gameplay, Bramble might underwhelm you. For the rest of us, the path of cinematic platformers could not have a better entry today. Bramble foreshadows what's possible with games becoming a playable piece of artwork.I'll gladly return to the world of Bramble often, like the other games in my list above. If you feel the same, this game is definitely for you!(Time after first credit roll: 4.9 hours)

_childDocuments_.review: I tried my best, but its a poor imitation of little nightmares. I find it hard to relate to the story or the character: you play a young boy who attempts to rescue his kidnapped sister from mythological Nordic creatures. But everything you do, see or experience is barely connected. It feels like it is a series of wacky adventures in a dark fantasy world. One time you stumble on a cemetery with zombies, then you find a witch in a swamp, then you just walk through a river out of blood, scary? Not really. It doesn't have to be connected, but it just feels so artificial. It is missing sounds, atmosphere and perspective. Same with the "puzzles" which should belong back to any 90th game: "oh there is a hole in the wall and next to it lies a lever", "oh there is a door with a triangle, circle and cross on it, which ingredients for a spell do I need to combine to open the door?" Those puzzles just bring you back with your thoughts wandering of what you'll have for dinner.

_childDocuments_.review: Full Game Walkthrough Till the End - MUST PLAY GAME !!( I have finished the game and these are my thoughts ) This  Is By Far One of the best Indie Games of 2023 in my opinionAbsurdly good Storytelling and art style especially coming from a small Indie studio that is literally releasing its very first title The world of Bramble is really beautifully portrayed with the right mixture of all things, horror , mystery , atmosphere , music everything is completely spot on fits the overall aesthetic like a glove The game itself is not very long though, you will require around 5 Hours to complete the game maybe even less if you dont die as much as I do The game mechanics for the part is pretty basic until you get to face certain bosses, that is where you see the uniqueness in each of these boss fights, no fight is similar, and there is always something new something surprising waiting for you at the end with a new style of a challenge so the fights dont feel boring at all, the random encounters are full of unique thrill.I had 0 Bugs and Issues throughout the game Rating - 9/10( Would have given it 10/10 only if it was a bit longer cause I thought it could have had at least a couple more lores and bosses )

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is truly a work of art and absolutely worth a play. It takes an incredibly unique and intriguing perspective on horror and plays extremely similarly to Little Nightmares and Inside. While Bramble is great, it certainly isn't perfect. At times it does suffer from clunky controls, minor bugs, and can feel tedious at times. Personally, I felt that it could have been 1-2 chapters shorter. Overall the game doesn't feel scary, as much as it feels tense and disturbing. Despite these things, Bramble overcomes all of its shortcomings with great artistic direction, an awesome final level, lovable characters, and a great soundtrack. I'll definitely be one of the first people in line for Bramble II and have my fingers crossed that a sequel is in the works.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love games like Ico, The Last Guardian, and Little Nightmares, you will fall in love with Bramble: The Mountain King.  If you've never played any of those games, but love Brother's Grimm type stories, horror movies, and puzzles, then you'll love it, too.  This game is beautiful both in scenery, plot, and music.  The bosses are very fun and a good level of challenging.  I wish my computer could have handled the game at it's full potential; I had to play it on the lowest setting, but it was still breathtaking.  The game did a wonderful job of not using unnecessary jump scares to create a feeling of suspense.  The creators did a wonderful job at making it so that, inevitably, even the brightest scenery is no longer safe.  While the game only took me 6 hours, and apparently others 4, I would say it has some replayability... though, mainly for the items you forgot to pick up during your first playthrough.  I bought it on sale ($27) and would say this game is worth it; you can feel all of the amazing effort the creators put into it.  I give it a 9.5/10, mainly because twice I had to restart due to falling into a void... but that's easily fixable.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Although it's short I think it's a must play for anyone that's into horror (or even a good story).I love that (norse) mythology is an essential part of this game and the lore isn't overbearingly deep but still very emotional and if you read all the books you can find out way more about the backstories of the characters. Although it draws inspiration from norse mythology, the designs and lore of the characters are changed for the game and I think it fits well into the universe.It feels like a movie with the amount of (long) cutscenes but they aren't really annoying like other games where you just wait to play again (And tbh sometimes they were a bit of a relief).The combat is rather easy (mostly dodging and a bit of aimed attacks) but it's fine because the focus is on the story (although some hitboxes were a bit ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥). It makes sense that there are no difficulty settings.You get casual and safe introduction to mechanics that you need later on where you're not safe anymore."Level" design and the general pace is fairly simple and often times repetetive but usually not in a disruptive way.The game has beautiful music and it's used very well to create an amazing atmosphere.In general the sound design is excellent (sometimes I couldn't tell if it came from the game or from inside my house) and sets the whole tone of the game.You can feel this especially when there is nothing concerning on the screen but the music becomes more unsettling or disappears and you feel very unsafe even when everything looks normal.The game has beautiful visuals (especially the lighting) and design choices of characters and environment are great.The camera placement is so good - some perspectives are placed like how you are perceived (e.g. the camera is inside a house and you're observing yourself through the window).This makes you feel vulnerable and watched all the time (afraid of what else is lurking around and watching you).You are so small (also literally) and at times you can see the whole background and the vastness of the landscape in contrast to your fragile tiny self.This choice of design is excellent since the camera forces you to watch the background, making you wonder what you're suppose to look at when it centers your view there.It makes you feel like there is something out there and it should be something to look out for feeding into the idea of not being safe at all times.It's unbelievably immersive and in addition to that I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ loved the gnomes & LEMUS! and I genuinely cared for them (RIP little cage gnome and that one gnome that walked into a bear trap).Apart from the beauty of this game it is also genuinly terrifying.Anytime a new "monster" came, it was horrifying like you actually had to run away (it was a genuine threat, not just in game).I was terrified everytime I heard them approaching, I didn't even want to move.They managed to create a perfect balance between the scary parts and the wholesome parts (loved the hide and seek btw, cutest ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing I've ever seen).Everything is in place and has its right to exist in the game (nothing is too much) and I thank the developers for not purposefully stretching the game.There are little details you can easily miss but when you look around (e.g. in the background) and manage to catch it it adds so much to the horror factor and the feeling of unsafety.What's an interesting design choice is that you only get little hints before the bosses come (the wooden figures)and you only get to know the stories (or even names) after defeating them, it makes the first encounters so much better and terrifying because you don't know what they are and everything clicks only after the fight.You begin to feel safe in the cute segments (in the beginning) but you essentially realise that nowhere is safe. I think this game has a "Little nightmares" feeling to it and even some similar mechanics. So if you like that game you will enjoy this one.You can feel that there was so much love put into it.Seriously you could write a whole essay about this game and there are probably a lot of things I've missed but I don't want to go that deep, I already got carried away.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, its on the short side only took about 4.5 hours to beat. Atmosphere and the narrator are 10/10 easily my fav parts of the game is listening to the narrator talk. _childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a very beautiful game but takes a very dark turn about a third into it. _childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a wonderfully made story-driven game. It brings so many unique and new ideas to horror games in general, and folklore-inspired fantasy especially. _childDocuments_.review: I beat it in about 4 and a half hours and i think most the game is amazing there's only 2 sections i didn't like which was the lantern and traps in the water since it forces the flow of game play to really slow down and the part where you can barely see the pathway in the water at one point me and my wife couldn't find where to go besides those personal gripes. _childDocuments_.review: They really put time and effort into this game, I am in love.The graphics are incredible at such a small game size. The amount of compression here is insane while keeping visual appeal, that was the first thing that astounded me. Now to the game play, I went ahead and grabbed the demo, wanting more info before I bought the full game. Let me tell you the "Demo" is not your ordinary run of the mill demo offered. You actually get a whole bunch of content for 100% free and it showcases all of what you need to see to want the full game. Let's just say after beating the demo I instantly bought the game and art book as I fell in love.The music and overall aesthetic of this game is it's true charm, the game developers ability to make you feel small in a massive world is incredible. The POV while running is dynamic while cameras do track and follow, you are not limited to how you wish to play or run around. The mastery in design and art style is a wonder, every page in the art book or in game is drawn with love and attention to detail while holding close that familiar medieval style we all love. Befriending giants and saving children from certain death is always fun too haha, this game makes you happy then instantly sad then happy. It's a whirlwind of emotions and a true masterpiece to play, I will not spoil that for anyone.The monsters and lore of this game is everything I have always wanted in a video game.My rating:Graphics: 8/10 beautiful (Game could be larger to accommodate ray tracing, and added textures etc)Story: 10/10 (Nothing needs to be done here, everything is a joy to play)Movement 8/10 (some jankiness, but hey it's too be expected, jumping mechanics are a tad sticky and not as responsive as I would like, It did not keep me from being able to move fast though, Just takes some learning)Horror!!! Is it scary?: well for me yes, and no. The lore is beautiful paired with amazing gfx and story telling. You will be scared though at certain times, aka jump scares that made me throw my juice at the wall XDOverall this game is worth the price point 100% It is a fair $ for what you receive. (Note to developers)I would be interested in seeing an online game mode or 2-4 coop mode to play with friends. Another game mode could be 5-10 people fighting 2-3 giants in a lake etc. Great game guys! can't wait to see what's next!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game! Absolutely stunning in so many ways. The storytelling throughout was gripping and combined with the visuals, it really made for an awesome game to play. This kind of game is exactly why I love Indie developers. Lots of love, effort, and hard work put into the game to create something amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: What an awesome game, you can tell how much work and love was pour into this. The story is simple - a boy is searching for his lost sister and on the way meets all kinds of creatures from Nordic mythology. it started as an innocent fairy tale, but turned out to be quite brutal and gory. Even as the protagonist is a young boy, this is not a game for children.To sum it up:+graphics are really beautiful, attention to detail can be found everywhere.+soundtrack - well done!+the story - what the protagonist will go through...no spoilers though+cuteness meets brutality, a contrast rarely seen in other games+bosses are quite enjoyable as well-game length is just about right. I finished it in less than 5 hours, but I didn´t explore much and missed many achievements-the protagonist is weak(as can be expected, considering he´s a child) and can die very easilySo do I recommend it? Hell yeah! This is one of the best indie games you will ever have the pleasure to come across.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I so rarely leave reviews on games, but I thought this one warrants one.  This game is absolutely breath taking.  I'm not typically one to fawn over beautiful graphics, however both the graphical fidelity and general art direction of this game is positively stunning. The storyline and horror elements are expertly crafted.  Basically, I am mostly parroting what other reviewers have said previously, though it is certainly all true.On one hand, $30 doesn't seem like a great value proposition for a game that I completed in just over 4 hours.  However, I am going to be thinking about and talking about this game for quite some time I think, so I am going to say that it is absolutely worth it.  If this game goes on sale, it is an absolute no brainer, but if you don't have to worry about spending $30 and are looking for a game that will fully immerse you in a dark fairytale universe and bring you nearly to tears ... please buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: As with many games of this ilk, it is short but sweet, and for me personally its a cut above games like Little nightmares and Inside. The story is well crafted, and you really feel for Olle by the end. I would have liked to see a few more story books, as they were a really fun addition and helped make sense of the situation. Pagan lore is mental. If you have the money and like stories, this will fill a couple of evenings nicely; if you don't have the money, wait for a sale, it is worth a play.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: a beautiful, dark fable of a game. it starts out charming but quickly becomes grim. although the game is short, it evokes strong emotions from start to finish, from delight to disgust, whimsy to horror. took me about 6 hours to complete a play through, though there are a few achievements i missed along the way. i only wish it were longer. i would recommend getting the game on sale since it's so short.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: What should I say, if you are looking for a game that provides a great story, a deep insight into nordic folklore, by times a plattformer, a stealth game, and more than enough adrenaline rushes as well as a chuckle here and there (I'm looking at you, Pesta) this is the perfect game for you.It's been a very long time since I felt that feeling of missing something after finishing a game. The moment the credits roll and there is nothing left but sadness about the end that had to come. Not because of the story but because it had to end at all. Some say the game might be too short but honestly, it's that feeling that tells me that it's just the perfect lenght. It wraps up so nicely and you know it's comming and yet you are not prepared, it feels like nostalgia and you want more.It's a beautiful yet sad and by times gruesome game with so much love for storytelling. Sadly I encountered a bug that, after closing the game, had wiped all my saves. However, the devs were very fast to answer and provide me with a savegame so I could continue where I left off while they figure out how to fix the issue. They are very active in the community hub and answer ASAP which just adds to their love for their creation.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A mix of Little Nightmares and Old folklore stories. Very fun and interesting to play through and meet all the little creatures and monsters. The story gets narrated so it isn't boringly silent all the time and easy to follow. Controls are easy to play with as well. I just had a very fun and chill time playing this game, would definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: great storyline, great music. at first thought the game was a little on the kids-side but once i got through half the gameplay, i can say this is DEFO not for kids, its pretty scary, very intense, bosses were quite hard for someone like me who plays game on easiest setting (there's no difficulty setting here). still enjoyed the game. i also have to mention this game probably has no replayability value, unless you're doing it for the achievements. worth it to get during halloween sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: As far as walking sims go, this is probably one of the better ones, but it's still just very, very little interesting content considering the price tag. Had I not gotten it from a friend, I'm not sure I would've finished it. Most of the game is just walking around with some admittedly pretty cool visuals, it's when the game tries to be more with the few boss battles it features it lost me completely. I admire the effort, but they really just feel like they're wasting your time more than acting as a real roadblock in the way of the main goal. Whole thing could've been condensed down to maybe 90 minutes. There's also some very, very light puzzle elements, but it's mostly just sticking the peg in the right hole, so hardly even worth the footnote I've given it. The story books spread around are pretty interesting though.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Wow... I am speechless... I was expecting a good game, since the reviews were so good... didn't look up anything before playing.... I regret now not buying it the first time I saw it, just to give my immediate support to the dev team. I was absolutely blown away. Everything, from the visual design, sound design, ost, story, mechanics, the pacing (how it goes from a hippie nature trip to brutal gore horror in seconds), even umm, BOSS FIGHTS? Like I know this isn't a type of game to actually have good boss fights... but somehow they are perfectly done. Not to hard, not to easy, great music, great scenes, great backstories, fun to play... I am shocked by this game in the best way possible. If you enjoyed classics like Playdead's Inside, or Tarsier's Little Nightmares, this is a must. If you didn't, first re-evaluate your life choices, and then still get this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly loved this game! Beautifully crafted and the creepy world they built around the characters was very interesting. I was always curious the entire time what new horror awaited me in the next zone.The worst part of the game was finishing it, I wanted to explore more of this world! It is fairly short, and the difficulty is also pretty easy so just relax with a drink and enjoy if you do buy it!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

Aside from that, pretty graphics, beautiful music and a great creepy atmosphere. Really enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A very well made game in regards to audio, graphics and atmosphere and I enjoyed playingit very much!This game is quite linear due to its level design, invisible walls and forced camera perspectivebut this is what I expected from this type of game.Parcour, some riddles, the occasional boss fight and story telling.Can recommend, the mythical athmosphere is a mix of cute creatures and more than a bitof horror sprinkled in. A lot like Grimms' fairy tales but the lore seems to stemfrom scandinavian countries.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I do NOT know anything about the tales this game is inspired and based on but LOVE everything about the world this game puts you in. Everything from the art style to how they tell the story, I found it a very enjoyable experience. You could easily tell that a lot of the gameplay elements were created to add run time (which can say that the games length is the one major negative about it being 3-4 hours long.) but the atmospheres and story telling keep you from overthinking that. If the game was cheaper (I bought on sale for $20) I wouldnt have space to complain about the runtime but I just feel as though possibly this game is better to just watch someone else play. If youre not into that however its definitely a great game to experience BUT again, its short, if you dont want a short game for this price but wanna experience it... just watch someone else play.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I have always loved folklore, and I have always loved horror. Thus it can be assumed that I like folk horror, and this game delivers on all three points. A . It's aesthetically pleasing to the eye, atmospheric, and with a keen sense for details. The soundtrack is a joy to listen to.Only real nitpick I have is that the game is a bit too short, but the experience itself does not overstay its welcome.We need more artistic games like these that do Scandinavian folklore justice. And I do hope that Dimfrost Studios continues in the same track with whatever next project they have in store.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game, some puzzles but mostly driven by the narrative. However there are two gripes I have with the game that prevent my recommending it outright. Firstly the only way to jump off a climbing surface is to jump backwards, which is more often than not directly into an enemy or off the map, resulting in death. The second and much more annoying issue is sprinting. While pressing sprint, more often than not the character doesn't sprint at all, and when he does the pace is barely quicker than the normal jog. If this were fixed in an update, the game would be much less frustrating and more enjoyable. I died many, many times while holding sprint, while watching the boy ignore the instruction completely and just jog carefree while being pursued. Otherwise it's an excellent game and should those two issues be fixed it'd be even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Remarkable, weird, and creepy game. It is a great re-telling of a few folktales that combines many different mechanics and styles in a way that actually really works.At times it feels like:Limbo/Inside (and has some issues of the latter (i.e. you gotta die a few times to figure out a puzzle - it is very hard to not die on your first encounter with many levels)); Plague Tale; Agony; Harry Potter Games (the ones that came out in early 2000s); Witcher 3 (especially Swamp Chapter, but more);Ori;Hellblade;But it never feels derivative - Bramble manages to add an extra spin on each of those "tropes/references" and be a great game in it's own style.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Bramble: The Mountain King is a horror game focusing on themes of Scandinavian/Nordic folklore. And for me, it is a fresh idea mainly because they added a "culture" themed to it. It's not just a "horror" game. It's a retelling of a world yet terrifying portrayal of Nordic folklore and what it means for a kid that had to experience such gruesome tragedies and graphic imagery just to survive. And to look for his sister, means he had to endure harsh environments as well. This game might be short but it was decent. The story writing might be plain and easy to anticipate but they still delivered through scenery,ambient, and musical scoring. The eerie silence, the dreaded environment, and the sound especially when they played "In The Halls of the Mountain King" I just lost it. The thrill is there. All of it, was a nice touch of perfection to me. It really captured the accuracy of every folklore while maintaining a balance of saturation and horror. With that I mean, even if it's a folklore they didn't overdo it. They didn't gave them exaggerated powers. They stayed true to the resource materials. It's a game that are meant not to be feared but it was meant to be educational, to impart a knowledge from another culture. To be able to absorb a material through games is such a wonderful experience to learn new and appreciate things in life. Soooooo, props to DIMFROST for making this wonderful game. I just hope that some other indie devs will follow your creative steps to also commit and do their own version of BRAMBLE. I give this 8.5/10. <3I might platinum the game but not at this moment. I need to prep myself first for a no-death run. HAHAHA
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start by saying that the soundtrack of the game is PHENOMENAL, It perfectly fits into the Nordic/Swedish aesthetic of the game and conveys intense emotions during every scene. The environment is gorgeous, especially in the first two chapters. It's mesmerizing and mystical, with every location and view that could be saved as wallpaper. Though yes, the game can be quite brutal and cruel, the game has a lot of stories to tell about Nordic folklore and I was touched at some moments. With all its beauty, it's still a horror game and it was pretty darn spooky. So if you have the guts and the heart to give it a try, it'll be worth it (especially with headphones).
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this would be a good, creepy game after trying the Demo. After completing it, I did not expect how violent, bloody and dark it got. And it blew me away. It's got that feeling of the old kids/family fantasy films of the 80's... just bloodier.Fantastic game. Short but not too short. Can't recommend highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most atmospheric games I've played, it has a beautifully dark story that pulls you in and keeps you playing. I know some people might think $30 for a 5-7 hour game is "too much" but I rather pay $30 for to watch two movies in the theater, because they most likely won't be as compelling as this. My favorite part is as an American I was very unfamiliar with these stories and the characters and folklore that surrounded it. It made the game all that much more interesting. The only way I can describe this is think of all the grandeur of God of War, but turned into a puzzle/platformer. I don't want to spoil anything, but this game takes you for a ride and the best way to play it is to go in totally blind. Just sit back and enjoy the story!
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful game with a wonderful story; I cannot recommand it enough. I really loved it and I will enjoy playing again. The simplicity of the gameplay allows to fully appreciate the intricate and detailed landscapes. I may be biased because I grew up with swedish stories (Tuva's character reminds me of the nymph in The Sun Egg from Elsa Beskow), but that's not all: the game really goes into the horrific themes of swedish folklore. The deaths are absolutely trashy and the game plays with your BPM and that's one of the things I like the most about it, it dives into the whole "Grimm Brothers" vibe and it does it beautifully.I may also have "In the hall of the mountain king" stuck in my head now.I'm going to sing it. No one around me is safe.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: It was wonderful seeing familiar Nordic creatures and setting in a video game. While there are intense moments and terrifying enemies, the game is only nominally horror-flavored. It could perhaps be compared to a Brothers Grimm story where a seemingly innocent story is laden with disturbing details, not so much heart-pounding anxiety. The environments are absolutely beautiful and the gameplay straightforward enough that the game is easy for casual players to pick up. However, there are some difficulty spikes which may get in the way of the enjoyment of those players who went in expecting a leisurely stroll through an interactive storybook. One of my frustrations with the demo was that it wasn't always clear what you were supposed to do and the same applies to the full game. Aside from a few frustrating bits I enjoyed Bramble a lot. Perfect if you're looking for a game you can finish in a weekend, with many memorable encounters and an immersive atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic addition to the "child in deadly predicaments" sub-genre of platformers, alongside Little Nightmares, Inside and Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons, the latter of which this game shares several similarities.The moment that the classic piece of music that this game takes part of its name from, finally kicked in, made it worth the price of admission for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played for 1 hour but I'm blown away by the fantastic style, setting and premise. When I recommend it to friends I describe it as similar to Limbo, but in a nightmarish nordic folklore setting. Also bought the artbook, haven't gone through it all yet, but just the cover page just blew me away, so magnificant! (if you struggle to find the artbook, it exist as a pdf in the file location for the game)Highly recommend giving the game a try,
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that you play for the storytelling and the atmosphere.The game is simple, not really hard. Graphics are ok, soundtrack is on point!I think it does a great job setting the atmosphere and gets you hook on trying to understand what's going on.It's pretty short and quite easy, the puzzles could have been a bit harder.But overall a great experience and a game to finish in a day or two.gameplay reminds me a bit of little nightmares
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most incredible gaming experiences I've had. The graphics, camera angles, music, story telling...every single bit of this game is truly a masterpiece. Every fable you play through is so thrilling and each chapter doesn't overstay it's welcome or drone on. I ate up every single minute, and the last battle had me squealing with excitement. By the time the credits rolled I was so overwhelmed with how amazing the last chapter was I sat for a while digesting it all. Is it on the shorter side? Maybe, but I did not feel unsatisfied. I could not recommend this game more it really is something special.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review: The game is top-notch story telling, and features amazing art direction and cinematography. Sound design, music... all great. Some of the controls (particularly jumping up onto things) were temperamental in places and took a few times for the game to recognize it as an allowed action. But overall the game play is engaging and rewarding with some clever boss fight mechanics.And Dave, just so you know... there are no spiders.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

_childDocuments_.review:
Bramble The Mountain King takes you on a gripping and unsettling journey through stunning environments. Take on the role of Olle, a young boy setting off to rescue his sister, kidnapped by a dreaded troll. Not everything in Bramble is exactly how it seems - in this strange land with creatures big and small, you must be careful when to approach and when to hide. Many hungry and spiteful beasts lurk in these forests and caves.

Call upon the Spark of Courage, an enchanted fragment granting the gifts you need to endure the pitfalls and trials in your path. Defeat the horrid creatures you encounter in different and unique ways. Be warned, courage without kindness can take you down a dark path.
_childDocuments_.name: Bramble: The Mountain King

name: Storyteller
detailed_description: Storyteller lets you build stories using a visual language. The goal on each level is to make a story that fits the given title by placing settings and characters that react to each other, creating a narrative through their relationships. Storyteller's comic-panel design and charming animations allow for experimentation within the framing of its many stories: just drag and drop characters to see how the story plays out! Play with a library full of characters and themes, heroes and villains, dragons and vampires, infidelity and revenge, love, lies, madness, and more! Use the blank canvas to manipulate secrets and desires, slay monsters or terrorize people with them, betray lovers or bring them together. You know how the stories go — but this time you are the author.
