short_description: Storyteller is an award-winning puzzle game about building stories. Start with a title, settings and characters and create a story that fits the story’s description. Play with stories of love, intrigue, crime, monsters, betrayal, and more!

_childDocuments_.review: Thumb both up and down. Thumb sideways. I do love it, it's extremely fun and clever, but, yes, it is TOO SHORT. Creators deserve to be compensated for their work, but I'm left craving more! If the extra achievements were included (listed) within the game, that would add to the replayability and the sense of getting one's money's worth. So, thumbs up if you're ok with paying the price of a movie with popcorn for about the same length of (very engaging) entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I like almost everything about this game. Things like the gameplay, art, music, narration, the snappiness of the UI, are all great. However, the game is way too easy and finishing it felt like a chore. Only one or two puzzles were slightly challenging and not in a fun way.If you're making a sequel, do everything exactly the same except make the puzzles bigger with more pieces available to the player and allow for more freedom in the solutions.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a cute side scroller type puzzle game, where you have to take a phrase and then turn it into a dramatic scene. You go through a mix of storys and even have some easter eggs in the end. -"Muhahahahaha murder."-"Do I really have the patience for this?"-100%'s the game "Yes... yes I do."This game is definetly fit for any new gamers who are looking into a puzzle game that is more simple. The nice thing about this puzzle game is that you are not in a horror setting or in first person so you can have a super chill experience while also making cute love stories... or murder scenes.The game play itself is pretty simple. You just drag, drop, and rearrange items that the game provides in order to create a scene. Not much else to it.I love the simple 2d style that these graphics offer, its easy on the eyes and its honestly really cute to watch the characters little faces. For being 2d and only really seeing them from the side they are very expressive little guys. The book itself is a little more detailed then the characters, but I overall think it compliments the style of the game and truly makes it feel like you're in a book. This game is single player, however, from what I have seen of the tiktok community and the steam community everyone seems very friendly and willing to help if needed. You can realistically play for as long as you want, however, If you only do one playthrough, with all the content, its only about 3 hours worth. Overall I did really enjoy this game, it made me laugh and had funny little plays that go along with it. I hope they add more, I feel like there wasn't loads in this game and there could be so many chapters to add or even some sort of "sandbox" option where you can use any characters or scenes to create your own story. Also I would say this game is child friendly, so if you want your children to get into puzzle games this could be it. -
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Storyteller is a series of blank comic strips that you fill with backgrounds and characters in order to 'tell' a 'story', (see how they got that title?  Sneaky.) which is provided for each level.Sometimes you are also asked to create the same story again, but with a twist, or in reverse, kind of like a palindrome.  In case you aren't familiar with palindromes, it is a phrase that reads the same in both directions, such as 'racecar', or 'The cat needs room moors de en taceht.'The early levels do a good job of teaching you how to play, with simple plots and few pieces to place, but it does get more tricky later on as you progress toward the higher levels where the complexity increases due to the amount of difficulty going up toward a higher amount than the previous levels had in a sloping manner onward to the final point where you have actually read this entire sentence.  Good for you.Now, there are actually a lot of negative reviews for Storyteller, and thanks to advances in AI writing, I have been able to combine them into one, so that you don't need to bother reading them all.  You're welcome.  Here you go.I get it.  "Furry Sniper Sokoban 12" is only 99 cents.  I have it.  I have all of them.  But unless we want that to be the only thing available, we've got to accept that better things cost more.  Storyteller is a better thing. Duke Otter is on a cliff, and is a .
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Storyteller is a short game, but innovative and cute. It's a combination of logic puzzle and story telling.The game engine and current content are a good start. Given how short the game is, I am hoping the developer will add mod support to open up the whole community to add content. More content from the developer would also be nice, but I could see how coming up with these puzzles would be taxing for a sole developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: It's a brilliantly designed game with great art and humor. It's priced really badly.It is about an hour long, for 20$. It's ridiculously expensive compared to the massive play time and replayability you get in other games that are around the 5-10$ price point. If it was a nice experience all the way through, it might still be worth the bloated price tag. The problem is that, on top of being extremely short, it ends abruptly with no indication. There are levels in the demo that are not present here, the new characters and mechanics apprear once or twice and then are never seen again, the mechanic of the demo of finishing all the levels and then going back to redo all of them from a different perspective is not there, it feels like such a brilliant idea that just didn't get finished. I especially don't understand why some of the characters and mechanics in the demo aren't present here since they were already finished levels in the demo. It feels like an extended demo, not a complete game with a particular design or gameplay experience in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I personally loved this game! I've definitely gotten 120 minutes plus of gameplay, but to be fair, I also streamed it. This is such a great game to stream or play with a group, especially if you are going to get creative with the stories! I like that there are different ways to complete some of the puzzles as well. And...poor Edgar. 😂However, I reject the fact that the prince refuses to kiss the princess when she is cursed because froginism...er...feminism.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game - the concept is interesting, the graphics are cute and well-designed, and some of achievements are pretty cool. For £12.49 though... I just can't. It's a very short game - My partner and I managed to complete this independently on my account twice in just over 2 hours, and that was with us taking time to find what other stories we could make. If there were more freedom in the stories - such as perhaps a freeform one allowing you to add any number of panels, scenes and characters to make a truly unique story, or even just more variation in the scenes available in the chapters, I would change my mind. As it is, this game has a lot of merit and potential, but simply not enough content and variety to make it worth the price! The puzzles become repetitive fast once you get the hang of how the characters interact, and many of the puzzles are essentially reused with maybe one small change.TL;DR a great concept limited by the short duration and relatively narrow gameplay. Absolutely worth playing if it's on sale, but I cannot recommend full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: The game is so short, I thought I was still playing the intro when I realized I had finished the entire game.The concept, the mechanics, the animations, the music, are all excellent. But it leaves you with the feeling that you saw the first episode of a very good series that was canceled after the pilot.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely puzzle game with a wonderful artsyle.The care and craft that has been put into the visuals and all the animated reactions of the characters, as well as the fun and charming gameplay mechanic, made it absolutely worth it, personally. It can (and most likely will) be completed in one go, but it's a game that chose quality over quantity.I would note that there were some levels in the demo that weren't in the final game, which I hope will be added eventually.overalla whimsical little treat
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: It is a really cute and fun game, I had a really good time but it is a bit short (100% in 2h, probably another hour if you want all achievements), I feel like it doesn't add to much from the demo. I hope that there will be other puzzles later but if not, I don't regret buying it cause it was fun and not that expensive !
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game. It was enjoyable, clever and, overall, fun. But, I would only suggest buying it if it less than £5. It doesn't take long to complete (for myself it was around the 2 hour mark) and doesn't have any form of free play (aside from anything extra you could create in each level). If it was longer or had an extra 'create your own stories', it would be an excellent game, but at full price, it's just not worth the money.Edit: With further updates it is becoming better value for money, but would still recommend waiting for a good sale price.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and fun puzzle game, with entertaining vignettes that will melt your heart as you try to figure them out. It's fun not only to figure out the stories and their multiple solutions, but also how the parts and characters interact in fun and funny ways. Like a lot of great stories, it's short but sweet!
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Take on the role of the storyteller in this innovative puzzle storybook game.Storyteller is developed by Daniel Benmergui for Annapurna Interactive.The game opens to a beautifully illustrated storybook, separated into chapters. Each chapter has a number of titles which the player must create the correct sequence of scenes to enact the title. Players create scenes from a limited assortment of images (scenes and people), as in a comic book like setting. Every element of the narrative is fluid, allowing you to change and rearrange scenes and characters at any time. The timeline is also dynamic, so changes made in earlier panels apply to panels after them.Puzzles increase in length and complexity as you progress through the storybook.Definitely recommended for fans of puzzle games.Pros:* Beautifully illustrated* Calming soundtrack* Innovative puzzle gameplay* AchievementsCons:* Price is a little high* No trading cards7/10 (due to being a little overpriced)
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I'd hoped for more freedom.This is simply a puzzle game, and a rather simple one at that.I don't actually recommend the game, unless you've ran out of other puzzle games you wanna play. But I don't dislike the game, so I don't want to hurt the rating, even if it wasn't what I wanted from it.To be clear, I knew it was a puzzle game. But I was expecting one where the point's less to find 'the one and only' solution, and more one where I'm able to come up with funny/creative solutions (yaknow, like Scribblenauts or whatever, but with narratives instead of nouns and adjectives)
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: With a unique art style and a very tongue-in-cheek kind of dark humor, Storyteller from developer Daniel Benmergui and published by the always amazing Annapurrna, asks the question: what if there is more than one way to tell a story?A puzzler with a flair for the macabre, each story invites the player to figure out how the main theme unfolds. Placing characters into situations just to see what happens to them is oddly satisfying. And don’t let it fool you into thinking everything is easy. Some of the pages took repeated tries with entertaining results. The number of times I said “whoops, they’re dead again” was not little.The animation of each character is delightfully wacky, and their expressions are spot on. It’s easy to get lost in Storyteller for a few hours, and still want more.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I was drawn in by the extraordinarily creative demo and immediately bought the game as soon as it came out, only to be let down by the sheer lack of content. The fact that I was able to beat the entire game and still get a refund should tell you something. Especially since out of the 50 or so puzzles, only 2 really managed to be challenging. It really sucks because I feel like there is so much more you could do with this concept and they barely explored any of it.It's really cute, and fun for what it is. But for ten bucks, I recommend you get it when it's on sale, or if/when they add much more content and better puzzles in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles were charming and fun, but this game was entirely too short for how much it costs. It was barely over two hours long, and that seems intentional to prevent refunds. If the game was five hours long then maybe I could recommend it, but I finished it in under two and a half. Spend your money on a different game.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: One of the reasons why I like Indie Games is because they are innovating the industry - AAA games will push forward with hardware and tech but Indie will lead with creativity and originality; whether it hits or miss is another thing.in this case, originality hits successfully and it's refreshing to have something new to play.You get one line of text each page, which tells you the expected outcome and in some cases, a condition(s) getting to that point. And then you add in how you think the story played out.Keep in mind though that this is a puzzle game and not a sandbox story-maker (which would've been interesting to see how that would've panned out), and in most cases, there is one solution, but the game does feel great when you stumble on surprise twists to that criteria.Only 2 issues: price and length - the solution would be that one problem fixes the other, but I'm not sure if there will be more to this than what is there now, so perhaps buy it on sale, but it is still worth a buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: The game tests your wits and makes you think a little and then make you slowly realize you were dumb for only realizing things later when it was plain obvious which panel goes where and which character needs to be placed in that setting. Lastly, unlocking all the secret stamps will really test you unless you find a guide since you really need to be on specific chapters to get most of them. Good luck
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and interesting game! managed to keep the ideas it wanted to put across accessible by experimenting with different characters organically as well as logically. Was a bit confused with the bonus title for the Godot puzzle, possibly a reference i didn't get. Had to look up a walkthrough for the last puzzle once i saw it solved it made much more sense, just missed a few steps. Charming little game, worth its price tag! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I actually really liked Storyteller, but it feels too short to justify the price tag.The concept is great, the core gameplay (experimenting with the interactions between characters in different scenarios) is fun, and the way the game introduces new characters and scenes gradually makes for a nice build-up of depth... and then, right as the puzzles get complex enough to be challenging, the game ends. It's not like it ran out of ways to use its mechanics, either--a lot of the interactions are only used once or twice (the witch being able to transform, for example), so there's clearly plenty of design space left unexplored here.Ultimately, I can't recommend buying the game in its current state--which is a shame, really. The concept clearly has a lot of potential, and the content that's there is good; there just isn't enough content! If the price was lower ($5 or so?) or there were a lot more puzzles, I'd be leaving a much more positive review. As is, though, I don't think Storyteller is worth the price of admission (unless there's a big sale on).
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: This is a poor man's Case of the Golden Idol.  This is in as-of-now pretty limited genre of plot-puzzle games a la Obra Dinn but this is by far the most simplistic example of it.  Goes on sale for ~$10 which is a more accurate asking price for this imo.  To be fair I'm biased against Annapurna but game has all the hallmarks of their style of trying-to-hard-to-be-high-brow overproduction; thinking especially of the unnecessary overwrought voice acting and floaty remixes of well-known classical music pieces.Sort of feel like a No is a little harsh but definitely can't recommend unless you've at least totally exhausted the other two games I've mentioned here.  Also kind of tragic that the store page is a vehicle for selling other Annapurna games, hope the dev's next games are a step up.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun and short, it could be completed in around two hours, which is the perfect length, as you wouldn't want to stretch it out too much. The controls are pretty simple, though some actions, like using right click to quickly remove settings and characters, could have been clarified better. It also allows for the player to think outside of the box.There are some small gripes, mainly switching through different chapters. Revisiting older chapters is a bit of a pain, as you'd have to wait until the animation is complete before you can go another chapter back. Using bookmarks to switch to different chapters could help speed it up just a bit, without completely breaking the immersion. I also have a bit of a concern for UX and maybe accessibility, though I'm not in the position to comment on the latter.What might have been fun, though just an extra, is a sandbox mode in the end, where you're given six or more panels that you can freely fill in to make your own small story.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much. It's super creative, unique and unlike anything I've seen before. But it is SHORT. like, 2 hours worth of playtime kind of short. And for the amount this game costs it just isn't that worth it unless you REALLY want to play this game. Although I still recommend getting the game just be wary that you probably won't be getting your moneys worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointingly short, but what's there is very good.  I hope this game gets some expansions or DLC, as there's a of promise here.  Would like to see more complex permutations of some of the relationships and effects.  I think this is a "buy on sale" recommendation from me at the moment.Edited: Following the recent free update, this game is more than worth it at full price, in my opinion. The new levels are fun and interesting and some of them are pleasantly tricky.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I had various ideas on how this game would unfold.. I feel the best description of this game is, it's very much like playing Clue. You are given a variety of scenes and characters for each page of the story. Different configurations give you different results. Some are straight forward and others you have to jumble around till you get the right ending for the page. Many of the outcomes are comical.I got stuck when I got to the crown; for me it wasn't straight forward on what to do ..fyi you have to move it.Moving the crown will unlock a variety of new stories and achievements to work through.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: The concept is fun, and I like the artstyle. I enjoyed playing it and messing around with different combinations of scenes and pieces. The game is short, however. The puzzles are simple enough that even with optional challenges and achievements, it doesn't take long to get through the whole game. Most of my time was spent playing around after I finished the game to see the different reactions characters would have to different conditions, like how someone reacts different to seeing their dead spouse's grave after being remarried. So yeah, good game, but it'll leave you wishing there was more to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute and short puzzle game. I like all of the different outcomes and everything you can do with the characters. I do wish it was a little bit longer for the price that it is, but the artwork and art style is fantastic so it makes up for the lack of length. I also really liked the small easter egg type of things that there were and that you could get achievements for. Made the game more fun. Cant wait for more releases from them!!
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun, clever, charming, and full of potential -- and also way too short. Why on earth are there so few levels? I breezed through it in 1.5 hours, even through I wasn't trying to rush. Several mechanics are severely underused (family) and some even only used once (vampires). I'm told much of the content of the demo has been cut from the full game, and I can not figure out why.I would be happy if the game was either much cheaper (I've enjoyed just as short games for a few bucks) or it was early access and there was more content on the way, but there isn't. Only buy it if its steeply discounted.Or beat it in <2hrs and get a refund. Whatever, I'm not your dad.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great but it is way too short. I finished it in 4 hours and I was taking my time. The music and visuals are incredible but it definitely could use more levels or content to play though. I was a bit disappointed to see there was no more content to play through. If you really want to play this game, don't buy it for the full price ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets everything right... apart from the length. It is extremely short, and not particularly difficult, which is a shame as the gameplay design is immaculate and left me smiling at the end of almost every puzzle. The music (which mostly consists of gentle remixes of public domain classical music) works wonderfully, and the art-style very charming and perfect for the game.I'm recommending it just on the fact that almost every aspect is done superbly, however do keep in mind that this is an extremely short experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Storyteller is an extraordinary brainteaser of a video game that succeeds in testing the player's capacity to piece together stories using the various prompts provided by each page within its respective chapter. What notably adds to the entertainment value of this product is the incentive of additional "devil" levels that add a more sinister twist to preexisting pages after the player has completed the main storyline. Although this video game is rather brief in its duration and achievements, for $15, it is more than fair in its price and content.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I really feel like i was baited by the demo and let down by a full game. That's a really big shame, because i hoped to have more fun with multiple stories and multiple characters and maybe some variation promised by a jester hat, but what i got is slightly more stories (not enough) and just a crown with no interaction for a reward for completing whole game. i can't reccomend the game for its full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cute game for those who like storytelling, creativity, and chaos. Picked it up on the recommendation of a reader friend who has known me for years, and she was spot on with the game's vibes and my personal interests: promise me cozy murder storytelling via folktales and I am all over it like butter on toast.The game is pretty easy to work your way through. I did the entire base game in about an hour without any assistance. I have to go back in for the final few achievements, but this is probably a 2 to 3 hour game. I'd recommend picking it up on sale if you love committing cozy crime, casual intrigue, monsters, and all other beloved fairy tale components in a twisty narrative (partially of your own making!). Some puzzles are harder than others, and some genuinely had me smiling at the shenanigans alongside the narrators.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I am tentatively recommending this game, because I did enjoy it quite a bit. However, I cannot disagree with its bad reviews either. It is a charming little game, but one that is much too short and much too expensive. My advice? Lower the price or add additional content. Or hey, why not both? _childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Shorter game, but a really really good experience. Don't be turned off by the price tag at all. You'll have a lot of enjoyment with the characters. The art direction is outstanding. Audio effects and music are perfect. All of that with an amazingly novel twist. Just finished 100% the game with my partner, and we hope there will be expansions made.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: For a relatively inexpensive puzzle game, I REALLY ENJOYED IT. I loved playing around with the characters and discovering each of their personalities/motives/desires and seeing the ways they interact with the different objects and scenes. Completing the book was fun, but finding all the ways that the devil/imp could be implemented to twist and turn and change those completed comics was super fun too. Getting 100% completion was a fun challenge and I found it was quite easily accomplished by simply taking the time to mess around and see what could go wrong/happen.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I was very undecided whether to rate the game positively or negatively. _childDocuments_.review: is a great example of delivering on a core gameplay mechanic without padding the playtime with useless fluff. The primary mechanic is innovative, and the added challenges provide a lot of color and creativity.One of the most familiar gameplay loops for puzzles games looks bit like this:It's a design loop that's as older than video games as a whole. At its heart,  is a puzzle game about creating a timeline of events. You get each "scene" with a small list of locations, and characters, and you try to tell the story the narrator gives you. What makes  so unique and mold-breaking is that the game doesn't just tell you that your solution is wrong, it lets you continue to be wrong and plays out the comic strip with your incorrect decisions to its logical conclusion.Are the puzzles the most challenging of all time? No. Are the stories ingenious and inspired? No. But what  does, which I haven't seen many puzzles games do, is explore the space around making mistakes in a puzzle game instead of just chasing what the "correct" solution is. The learning feels a lot more organic, since in real life there's no buzzer and big red X that appears when you fail to do something correctly; you only really learn when you have to see the results of your mistakes.: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: "Storyteller" is an incredibly charming and atmospheric game that swept me off my feet from the very beginning. I fell in love with the artwork immediately, and watching the animated frames change was an absolute delight - they often brought a smile to my face. Kudos to the developers for their clever use of humor, and for infusing the game with a unique touch and tons of personality that I've never seen before. Despite typically not being a fan of puzzle games, I thoroughly enjoyed playing "Storyteller" and was glad to see it finally come to life after all these years. Although it's a relatively short experience, I think it's one that you should savor and not rush through. The amount of love and work put into the game can be felt throughout, which is why I believe it totally deserves its price tag despite being a short game. After completing each level, I couldn't resist having some extra fun by tinkering with the characters and switching up the story's order. It was absolutely entertaining to witness the various outcomes and behaviors of the characters, and I actually found myself playing around with it for quite some time. As someone who typically doesn't leave reviews on Steam, I felt compelled to share my thoughts on this gem after seeing all the negative feedback. It's unfair to judge a game solely based on its length, and I believe "Storyteller" deserves better. I had an absolute blast playing it and am eagerly awaiting more. If you're looking for a charming and entertaining puzzle game that's full of personality, then "Storyteller" is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can not recommend this game.First of all: Graphics, music and the style of this game are very charming and I like it a lot. The idea of an more "open" puzzle-game by solving stories and experiment with the different logical and narrative plot elements are very good and I really wanted to like this game.But the longer you play the game, the more you realize that it has a better idea than execution. First problem is, that you dont have the ability to experiment freely with the narrative elements. Instead of getting more and more narrative elements, characters, props and scenes, you are limited to 1-3 elements of each. Within that scope you can experiment with this elements and its quite fun sometimes to see what happens if you switch the different elements and characters. But especially the later puzzles are frustrating and it seems that your freedom of experimenting gets more LIMITED over time instead of getting more options to solve the puzzles. How cool this game would have been if the developer just said: "Here, you got a bunch of characters, all scenes and props you unlocked so far, now solve the puzzles within the logic of this story". I would LOVE this so much.But instead, you get limited. And some solutions of story puzzles are just there to make it extra hard for you to solve them(maybe so you dont be able to finish the game too fast?) Mostly you just have to think as mean and as cruel as possible to solve the story. So its not that wholesome it could be. Often you need to think "Oh...how bad, cruel and ruthless this character needs to act, so solve this puzzle?" One or two times this would be fun too, but at the later puzzles you have to do this too often and it gets boring very quickly.Another problem is, that the logic of the game is not correct or understandable at some point. In a later puzzle you have to match the exact gender(male instead of the female protagonist) to solve the puzzle, although there was no reason for it, because their roles where totally interchangable.Overall I am not happy with critizing this game. The idea is great, the animations and character designs is adorable and the way how to interact with the panels, characters and such feels so nice and makes a lot of fun. But in the end this game is too limited. Instead of being able to experiment with the story elements, it is just like any other puzzle game: You have to find the correct answer, just the way the developer want you to find. If you want to do it your way, it will fail. Even if the game suggests, its based on real world logic and you can solve the puzzle by using this logic. At the point the illusion of an free puzzle game fades away, the game is a lot less fun and feels very very limited. And it lacks a "free mode" too, where you could make your own story based on the panels. This would be so nice, especially for kids, to experiment with and make their own stories. Maybe even share it in social media and such.The game has so much potetial, but it doesnt use it in the end. So I can only recommend the game for people who want a short puzzle game experience, that is slightly different from other puzzle games. If you hope you find some great innovation in gameplay, you will get disappointed unfortunately. :/

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting, avidly, for this game for 15 years, since it was first announced on the author's blog and won the Nuovo Award for innovative game. I was a huge fan of the flash games  Daniel Benmergui made and Storyteller was the absolute pinnacle of everything he'd done before then. I bought Fidel specifically to support the author in the hope of Storyteller one day being released. I was absolutely overjoyed last year to finally play the Storyteller demo. And that demo was amazing. Absolutely everything I'd hoped for. I was so excited for the game to release. The trouble is, the demo felt better than the full release.  I am so disappointed with how short this game is.  I wandered afk, and also the game crashed, and I still managed to finish the game in well under 2 hours. A lot of the scenarios were ones I'd already played in the demo. I absolutely hate leaving a bad review, especially on release day, but I'm so saddened by this. The core gameplay mechanic is fantastic. The game concept is great. The demo was great.  But what's been released just doesn't feel complete. I'd so many hopes and I'm just sad.I really, really wanted to love this.  I had a lot more fun with the demo.There's less replayability here. It feels less like making an actual story and more like just solving a puzzle with a limited solution. There wasn't the same feeling of having this cool innovative toy to play with that there was with the demo, where you could go back and replay everything, and experiment with the story changing the outcome. It feels like it's lost the essence of everything I loved about the flash games, and the demo, and I'm so sad about that.  I'm really hoping that there'll be extra content released.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself, is pretty fun, however it is a rather quick game with no reason to replay. The reason I'm giving this a thumbs down, is because I got to play the demo while it used to be up. Comparing the demo to the final game, it's become obvious that the end product was heavily rushed. There were a lot of characters and stories completely dropped from the demo. While I understand things change in development, a lot of potential stories were cut out, and it could've made the game play much longer and more interesting. The fact this game is so simple is amazing, but it's such a short game play it shouldn't be worth $15. Getting on sale is recommended if you want a quick game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game about using literal storytelling logic to reach certain outcomes - you arrange the scenes in order, add the characters, and see how changes to the flow of events affect things later in the sequence, like changing variables in an equation. Scenes can change a character's emotional state, affect what they know, equip them with an item, or even kill them - and the characters themselves have different personalities that affect their reactions to events. It's a clever idea and it's executed well; the characters are rendered in a charming storybook style and there's care taken to convey information clearly so you're never confused about things like what a character knows or how they're feeling. The game's only flaw is how short it is--there are a universe of possibilities here, and the puzzles we get only scratch the surface.  I'm hopeful expansions are planned. Until then, this game is like a tiny box of fancy chocolates: exquisite, but over far too soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: "Simple" is the best word that comes to mind to describe this game, The art style is simple. The graphics are simple. The game play is simple. The puzzles are incredibly simple. There is nothing complicated about this game. Which is the problem with the game. Sitting straight through, no distractions, it would be easy to finish this game in an hour or two. Either the puzzles are very obvious, or they are totally random: sometimes it's like throwing a bunch of things at a wall and seeing what sticks.The decision to give this game a positive rating just came down to fun. It was fun for what it was. I am amazed it took so long to come out. I am even more amazed there is just so little content. It feels like a small team production.If you are happy to just have an hour of two of laid back nonsense, then this is a great choice. However, I would wait until the price is pretty darn low - I don't do the refunds for short games thing. And there is no replay value at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Storyteller is a game that I enjoyed a whole bunch. In this game you can put characters and settings in sequence to achieve certain desired scenarios but I think this game truly shines in the way that you can play around with the different characters and settings to get surprising outcomes. This game is not as simple as it appears on the surface and the "devil" and "stamp" levels can be particularly challenging. I think this game is very creative and the developers did a great job with expanding it. The little animations are really cute and I think that the narrator is very talented. I would recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: A short, but delightful experience. I don't like puzzle games, but I like Storyteller. I found myself laughing out loud at some of the solutions, and even when I didn't get the right answers, the characters are so full of personality that I didn't mind experimenting until I got the story right. Most of the puzzles make sense, with excellent iconography for hints. Most of the fun is figuring out how characters will respond to each other within various scenes, and manipulating them until their behavior matches their chapter title.Unfortunately, the menu navigation is awful. Eventually you'll be trying to unlock badges with very specific characters and scenes. With several dozen chapters to scroll through and no listing of their characters and scenes, it gets tedious hunting for the exact combination you'll need. When you've finally achieved 100%, there's no fanfare, no capstone celebration screen--you just go to the menu page and quit.Overall, I love the presentation and humor, but the UI and anticlimactic ending dampened the experience just enough to stop a good game from being great.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: A short puzzle game that requires you to think a lot. I completed this game plus all the achievements with a total of 105 minutes and I loved every minute of it. Though I hope the developers make either a Storyteller 2 or a DLC that allows more stories to be added to this collection of entertaining puzzles. I hope everyone enjoys this funny and morbid game. I give it a 7.5 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really cute game and is 100% worth the money. And some of the puzzles will really leave you stumped for awhile. (side note) if you have a Netflix subscription, at the time of me writing this, you can download the game for free off of Netflix if you are on mobile.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little game with some nice logic ordering puzzles. It is however a pretty easy short puzzle game. 2 hrs and i had completed the main game, there are about 5 achievements i haven't obtained but in terms of new content and puzzles it is done. I was hoping for a sandbox/ extension to the game at the end but alas nothing special on completion. Cute but short.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept, not worth the money at all. Its $20 for less than 2 hours of gameplay content for 100% the game. There is a literally achievement in which you play for 2 hours, so you cannot refund the game at that point. Puzzle are fun but simple, and stamps are a waste of time because they do not tell you their location so the game can pad out run time if you don't lookup a guide. No point in playing this at $20, if this game was worth 5, it would at least be arguable. Just watch a play-through or a twitch streamer play the game not worth at all would have refunded if I could. Summary:- Less than 2 hours of runtime, with unnecessarily hidden content to pad the runtime (game achievement acknowledges this and tricks you into playing more so you can't refund)- Cost too much ($20 for a literally hour of runtime). - Simple and easy puzzles (was interesting though)
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: It's initial game play is short but still very cute. I finished the whole thing it in about four hours. _childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know how to rank this game. I enjoyed it. It's not nearly as open as it seems to tout itself. It's also super short. _childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Storyteller is a creative logic puzzle game, with unique humour and mindful twists. The game requires players to arrange characters and scenarios to fit into a certain narrative. There are 60 normal stages and 10 twists at the end of the game, which can be finished within 2 hours. Many of those stages can be solved in several different ways allowing some degree of player self-expression. Quite a lot of stages also have references in classic literature, discovering them during the play through creates particular memorable experience. However, the game is too simple and too short. It has many good elements and ideas for creating complexity in narratives but ultimately failed in doing so. It throws out many good ideas without further explorations. Overall, I think it is a good game with some minor flaws, which is 7/10 by my standard.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Yes it's a short game, but it's one of the better indie puzzlers I've come across. Its art style is charming and fits well with the game's concept. It's also surprisingly smooth and accommodating considering all sorts of things you can try to fulfill each prompt. The puzzles are quite on the easy side though. I didn't encounter much difficulty except during a couple of levels. One bummer is that the jester levels from the demo are gone, which is a shame. Hopefully they'll add it in as a free DLC. As it currently is, the game might be overpriced for some. If so, wait for a sale. It's well worth it for me so I'm still giving it a solid recommendation. If you'd like a puzzle game similar to this one, but longer and more challenging, try Human Resource Machine and its sequel 7 Billion Humans by Tomorrow Corporation.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful puzzle game. Did it only take me 3 hours to 100% it (with a little help from chat for the last achievment). _childDocuments_.review: An innovative and interactive puzzle game where you are tasked with creating specific scenarios on a storyboard layout with the available scenes and characters. Dynamic timeline allows for a little extra challenge and keeps the plot refreshing as there are multiple solutions available. The levels are fun and often amusing, artwork is adorable and the soundtrack is super cozy and non-repetitive. However £12.50 is too much for a game that you can complete in 1.5 - 2/3 hours imo. Would recommend waiting until it's on sale, at which point it's definitely worth it. Fingers crossed they add more content to this game to round it out.Pros:Beautifully illustratedCalming soundtrackWomen 🤌AchievementsSatisfying clicky noisesCons:Price per content hoursNo point shop items
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: This game is short, but a lot of fun. The point of Storyteller is to place characters in scenes in a certain order based on what the title says the story is supposed to be. The game is split up into fourteen chapters, with the coronation at the end being the end goal for the main portion; afterwards, extra conditions in earlier levels will unlock, including an achievement system for rigging certain scenes in ways the initial story did not intend for. Again, the game is not terribly long -  I got 100% completion in around four hours - and does not have terribly deep game play to go alongside it, but for what it is, I still enjoyed the charm this game does have, with how the characters interact with one another and how certain scenes can affect the relationships to make brand new scenes. If you have some cash to spare, I would say this is definitely worth a playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: It's very cute but there isn't a lot there, watched a few snippets of youtubers play it, and thought I'd give it a shot since it was on sale, but I've gone through almost everything quite quickly and even messed around with some levels to do random goofs, but even then, that only lasted me like an hour and a half. _childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a labor of love. The art style is charming and you really have to get creative in order to solve the puzzles. I know some reviews are upset about the length, but it would be unsustainable for a game like this to be any longer than two hours. Regardless of how long it takes to finish the game, there are over forty different puzzles to solve and some have more than one solution. It's clear that a lot of thought and effort went into making Storyteller so I'm more than happy to pay the asking price for the game. I had a lot of fun playing it and I have no regrets. If you love puzzles and literature then I'd highly recommend this game. (also: one review mentioned a sandbox mechanic though and I think that would really improve the replayability of the game)
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: for someone who wasn't following the game for a decade and haven't seen the demo it was pretty entertaining. the big part of it was understanding how narrative-based rules can be used to create tight logical puzzles. i guess most of the negative reviews come from people who played the demo, so the novelty element wasn't there for them and they just wanted more content, chewing through the game in "under 80 minutes" (allegedly). as i mentioned, it's commendable how the game establishes its rules and then sticks to them. things are logical and make sense. i suppose it can also be considered a "flaw" to some extent, since in a narrative-based game it should be ok to twist the rules in a creative way once in while. but otoh perhaps i wouldn't be saying that if had been hopelessly stuck on one of those "creative twists":)another possible flaw (depending of your political views) is that it's somewhat woke, using same-sex relationships in its solutions quite liberally. i don't think it's particularly appropriate in a fairytale-themed game.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Storyteller is a testament to the power of blending storytelling and game-play into a harmonious whole. Its ability to engage, challenge, and addict players is a commendable feat, making its brevity forgivable in light of the enriching experience it provides. I wholeheartedly recommend Storyteller to anyone seeking a unique fusion of narrative and puzzle-solving. While its addictive nature might lead to a shorter playtime, the memories of untangling intricate stories will undoubtedly linger long after the game is completed.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. It is perfect for when you want something cute and easygoing. _childDocuments_.review: I loved the demo so it is really sad for me to have to give a negative review to the final game. And the puzzles that I liked the most were the ones I remembered from the demo. The new ones felt far less interesting. I feel like something must have happened to the dev team for them to release the game in this state.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to be completely honest, I've been following this game for a while. I'm incredibly upset to give it a thumbs down, but I was severely disappointed to find the lack of content, especially considering the amount of time put into the game. There were only around 50 levels (52 if I'm correct), and the creators had been working on this game for nearly 15 years prior to the release according to gamerant. I also noticed one of my favorite parts of the demo almost completely disappeared. For those who haven't played, at the end of the demo, you unlock a jester hat that gives you a new challenge for each level that changes the story slightly, while providing double the gameplay. In the full release, I've found that only a few levels actually include the extra challenge mechanic, which ends up being unlocked instantaneously.I'm not saying this game is without it's merits, for example the art and puzzles in the game are incredibly fun and beautiful. I love the hand drawn feel and the different characters, and I found it a really fun game. To be completely honest, I think this would be one of my favorite games if they had included more. One way I would've kept this and even given it a better review would be if they had given us a sandbox mode after earning the Storyteller rank. They could've also given us more gameplay with extra levels, or even a character creator or something akin to that. I would love to get this game again later on, if they can provide us with extra mechanics, or extra levels of some sort, like another book or any other ideas I've mentioned. But for now, I'm trying to get a refund sadly.Creators, please add more, I enjoyed the time I had playing your game, but I need more to keep it in my favorites.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: The game was fun and just what I needed for a cozy pick me up. I don't mind paying full price for an Annapurna game, but the length is something to keep in mind if you're someone who would prefer to wait for a sale given how quickly the game can be finished!
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Its a nice puzzle game. It has interesting problem solving challenges involve character interactions. I would recommended it, but the game is short. I beat the game 100% and then hopped off of it, so whatever time my hours played is at is how long it took me to beat. It felt short and that it could of been longer with the learning depth of the characters interaction.Highly recommended if it goes on sales for 35% or more
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! It's a quick 2-3 hours or so of play time. On the challenging prompts, it's really satisfying to come up with a solution and see new little ways that the characters can interact. I did all the achievements and treated them like the bonus puzzles: I gave myself the prompt (the achievement title) and checked a guide to see the location (what chapter and puzzle it could be completed in), just because when I tried without knowing the location I just kept second-guessing whether the prompt was possible where I was, then I'd wind up flipping through the annoying book and trying to remember which puzzles had which characters and which scenes and and and... that just wasn't fun for me, and I feel like doing the achievements the way I did /was/ fun! I don't mind that some people would say I cheated, cause they wouldn't entirely be wrong, but I had fun. All that's not to say I didn't have a few complaints. First was that I felt like the majority of the puzzles were teaching you how certain pieces worked, like what characters' motivations were or what a set piece did. Those ones often felt like a chore once you got past the beginning, because by the middle of the game you don't necessarily need to be taught how it'll work because you understand how the game as a whole works, and if you were going to figure out a particular scene, for example, you could do it in the context of a larger, more challenging puzzle. There were usually just one or maybe two really challenging ones per chapter. Second, it does sometimes fall into the puzzle game trap of 'you've solved the prompt but not in the exact way we had in mind so we're not letting you progress yet.' However, when that happened, usually it was just a little finagling to see what you hadn't fulfilled properly.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: this game is so creative and well made!! the stories are all so different and there are so many aspects that make each one unique. it really challenges you to think outside the box sometimes and that is what makes it so entertaining! i really enjoy this game and can't wait to see how it continues to grow.

_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: A great little game. Including achievements, it is about 90-100 minutes long. It's probably best to let individual consumers decide whether that's long enough for them personally, and reading through the reviews, it's clear that many have decided it's not long enough given the price. (The length/amount of content is effectively the sole source of bad reviews and negative press, very few people dislike the gameplay.) For me at least, I'm not worried spending $15 to support an indie dev making a game they care about, and the 90-100 minutes are very good - a great(if not totally complete) exploration of a very special concept, and substantially better than similar ideas like Framed - so I'd recommend it if you think that's you.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: well.. just finished the game not even 2 hours in, I was expecting more after having this game on my wishlist for nearly 2 years. _childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute little game with a lot of polish to it. It's a short time, about 1-2 hours depending on how fast you're moving, but it made for a very fun night with friends trying to solve the puzzles together. I hear where a lot of the negative reviews complaining that it's overpriced and too short are coming from, but I don't think just because a game costs fifteen bucks it ought to have hours and hours of content; for the same cost as a decent fast food meal or a cheap night out, I think this game is worth the price. It's a cute time!
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: If you're read a couple reviews, you've seen it's a short game. If that's a deal-breaker and you want a game with high replayability, you might want to pass on Storyteller.If you're still reading however, I can recommend it as a pretty novel puzzle game with a charming setting and innovative gameplay. It'd the kind of single sitting experience that gives a breath of fresh game design air, and might leave you thinking about possibilities for future game mechanics along this line.Truth be told, I didn't find it to be _the_ storytelling masterpiece I was hinted at in gamedev circles, and my partner who I played it with got bored midway through (but she's not a big fan of narrative games in the first place). The first chapters of the game are very easy and might not show the full potential of the mechanic. Later chapters get more interesting and provide some interesting challenge.I think I would have liked one or two more scenarios in some chapters to explore the setting further. But I'm also happy with the experience as it is overall.So in short, I had a good evening, it's not my GOTY in the genre (do check out The Case of the Golden Idol if you're itching for more story reconstruction puzzle mechanics), but I'll gladly follow what the devs have in store for future games or DLCs... The credits do say "Book One" ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I can't understand the negative reviews about the game being too expensive for too little content. Sure, the game is one of the shorter games and it is not difficult (apart from a few levels/achievements). But the value of a game does not depend on its length or difficulty. The idea of Storyteller is really unique, the graphics and animations are excellent, and the music fits perfectly! The entire presentation with the book that you page through and close at the end has been realized with a lot of attention to detail. In addition, this is an indie game beein developed over years! I like to support indie developers with such innovative ideas so that they can hopefully continue to realize their own game ideas in the future.So in short: The game is worth every penny! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Cute little different Puzzler with gorgeous Animations. You shouldnt search for a long experience in this game but expect alot of fun and entertainment in this short time. Looking forward to another game of this developer <3
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable experience.Just challenging enough to get the gears grinding but not so much so that any one story or chapter was too difficult to complete.The music fits well and is fun to listen to while you're thinking and trialing a variety of potential solutions, the art style is wonderful and thematic, the little animations and sound effects are a great touch and really bring the stories to life.I only wish there were more stories to solve. Can't wait for updates!
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really great puzzle game but it's just too short for the price tag. It took me just under 2 hours to complete (including the optional puzzles on some of the stories) and that's including the half an hour break I took and left the game on. _childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Despite being short, this game was a fun time! It's a unique puzzle game that isn't too difficult to understand. The concept and art style really stand out to you. With more content coming via a free update in the future, I'd say this game is worth checking out if you want something short and sweet to pass the time!
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: From the get go the concept of Storyteller lured me in along with it's artstyle. It looked so good to play from the little content I watched of it. When I actually played it, the game played really smoothly & felt good to play!The story was not complicated to follow! _childDocuments_.review: For those interested in puzzle games, this is a nice three hour experience, though it might not take quite that long if you're more experienced with that stuff. That was just my time. It gets a little more challenging when trying to break it for those extra couple of achievements, but it's overall a rather easy game.If you're here for the story(pun fully intended), then this is a wonderful little game. As an aspiring storyteller myself this was so much fun to go through in an evening. Brilliant set-up, interesting prompts, lively and distinct characters, and all while giving you full freedom to experiment with the stories you create. My favourite part has to be how each story can play out slightly differently with the same result. Early on there are even plenty of blank panels not necessary for completing the main puzzle allowing you to customise your story a little with an extra panel, as long as it doesn't effect the outcome. This freedom and the extra goals for several levels are ideas I absolutely love.This game captures the heart of storytelling so well. You know what needs to happen, but you have no idea what has to happen for it to get there. Maybe you'll even be left with some space to fill with extra details, just because you like it. Genius concept, small game, brilliant execution. Probably not for the hardcore gamers out there, but if you're considering this game, then that's probably not what you were after in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: Storyteller is a really unique and clever puzzle game, expertly polished with wonderful art, music and sound design. There's a brilliant air of wit and humor about it, and I smiled at many of the story outcomes. If you're looking for a charming puzzler unlike anything else out there, you're going to find that here. If you're looking for a challenge, I also personally felt that the difficulty ramps up nicely. A bunch of the later objectives (especially the bonus and achievement objectives) were genuinely challenging and took me a while to figure out. Only on the very last achievement did I finally cave and look up a hint on the forums, discovering that I'd been trying to get it in the wrong level - which feels fair to admit as being my fault. What I want to express with that anecdote is that I think the game does an absolutely excellent job of communicating with you and subtly nudging you towards the solution, mainly through the wonderfully illustrated reactions of characters in various situations. It never felt like I came across a solution that didn't make sense to me. Considering the complexity of the systems at play, I think that's an impressive feat. I've seen Steam reviews complaining about the length - I got around 4 hours out of the game. Did those players skip the bonus objectives and achievements, or am I just slow? Regardless, the game costs less than an average graphic novel (a comparison I base on the fact the game is basically a set of interactive comic strips), and took me longer to get through. I hardly feel like the length is a genuine reason to not recommend the game, especially if you enjoyed it in general. That said, if there's gonna be DLC with more content, count me in, because I definitely would be excited for more of Storyteller!

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly hate writing bad reviews for indie games - especially ones that have such a great starting concept! But Annapurna published this one, so they will have had a meaningful budget, and big opportunity to do better. Lots of people have said it's too short for the price tag... But that's not the real issue. Short games can be good, and devs work extremely hard even to create short experiences.For me the real issue is the lack of inventiveness. The game forces you to play out the same scenarios again and again, with the same characters - with very little variation. As such, the game gets boring and predictable within 15 minutes. The sad thing is that there are so many easy wins they could have taken to add variety and intrigue. From changing up the character sprites from time to time, to basing each chapter on a different story concept, to adding a sense of meta-progression. Without these basic features, every level feels like you're stuck a time warp. To make matters worse, the system feels very very rigid. Often it seems like there is only one answer, and sometimes those answers don't even feel logical. As a result, the game doesn't offer any opportunities to be creative as a player - which adds to ultimate sense of staleness.

_childDocuments_.review: *Note: I did not write a wall of text. Steam will not allow for any spacing on this one for reasons unknown*With a heavy heart, I give the heavy thumb to Storyteller.The game is easy to pick up, easy on the eyes, and (mostly) easy to finish. So easy, in fact, that I was surprised when I finished the game in an hour and a half. That ninety minute play time included a full thirty minutes stuck on the final level. That's right, it took me a single hour to complete Storyteller's 51 other levels.About 85% of the game feels like a tutorial for some other game that we only glimpse in the final few levels. Several fun concepts like werewolves and vampires and witches, all doing their own supernatural things, are introduced in one level and then completely abandoned for the rest of the game. Only weddings and funerals are ubiquitous.It doesn't matter that the characters are cute, even when they're doing horrid things to one another. It doesn't matter that the animations are clever, even endearing. The game is over before it starts.There aren't even any modding or scripting tools for players to make their own story puzzles to share.Wildermyth, by contrast, includes a robust editor for its comic panels. Though Wildermyth doesn't include any animations for its comics, it does allow for truly involved story telling and is attached to an ACTUAL GAME.Scribblenauts is another game that offers so much more than Storyteller by allowing the players to solve its puzzles in many different ways.Though Storyteller challenges you on some levels to come up with alternate solutions, there isn't any kind of special animation for jumping through these extra hoops, just a box ticked below the story title. A few levels have special Steam Achievements, such as acting out Romeo and Juliet, for instance.To make matter worse, those quick 52 levels feel padded, with one level asking you to depict stasis over 6 panels. That's right, you can finish the level as quickly as you can drag the same characters into the exact same positions. Then, the 'bonus challenge' is to make them leave and come back by simply deleting the pair from one of the middle frames. Maybe that's a spoiler, but only if you're five.Frankly, this feels like an extended $15 tech demo that is meant to be the gateway for DLC packages galore that are made with exclusive in-house tools and cranked out ad nauseum for $5-$10 a pop.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying I enjoyed what I played, just like I did the demo. The visuals are adorable and the animations are pretty smooth. The puzzle aspect was nice. I enjoyed the concept which was why I was so excited for the game.I suppose that's why I was so disappointed when I got an hour and 30 mins in and realised that was it. The whole game. I understand that some games are short and are designed to be and ultimately that is the decision of the creator. My problem was that it felt so jarring, almost leaving me with a feeling that there was no conclusion, that there was no end. In confusion, I watched the credits role, hoping there was something else, only to see them repeat. Again and again. I went back and completed any extra objectives or achievements (making this one of the only games I 100%ed) in the hopes that there was something more - like in the demo - only to be left feeling disappointed. I fully completed this game in under 2 hours and I didn't feel happy, I didn't feel sad it was over. I just felt confusion and then annoyance and then nothing. Except maybe a bit down as I had been looking forwards to this game for ages only to feel like I had played another version of the demo. A more detailed demo from later down the line, but still a demo.If the game were ever expanded, I would probably play it. _childDocuments_.review: As of writing this review the game has a 72% recommend rate, which I think is right on the money for a few reasons:The Good - Wonderfully simple yet effective mechanic of manipulating the order and placement of comic strip scenes and characters in order to create a narrative based on a plot prompt given as the puzzle title. Cute and reactive character models and animations that update in real time as you fool around with scene/character ordering. In general the game has a tight concept executed very well.The Bad - Far too steep a price point for a game I completed in 2.2 hours. Some of the puzzles are unforgivably similar to ones you completed previously in the same chapter. My other major gripe with this game is that I played the demo that came out maybe a year ago, and I do feel that the game has not added much more in the way of content in the intervening months. The armchair developer in me is scratching his head as to what exactly the devs have been doing with the game since the demo launch.Overall: Cute little puzzle game that is far too expensive for an experience you will only play once.

_childDocuments_.review: Storyteller is a creative logic puzzle game, with unique humour and mindful twists.  The game requires players to arrange characters and scenarios to fit into a certain narrative. There are 60 normal stages and 10 twists at the end of the game, which can be finished within 2 hours. Many of those stages can be solved in several different ways allowing some degrees of player self-expression. Quite a lot of stages also have reference in classic literature, discovering them during the play through creates particular memorable experience. However, the game is too simple and too short. It has many good elements and ideas in creating complexity in narratives but ultimately failed in doing so. It throws out many good ideas without further explorations. Overall, I think it is a good game with some minor flaws, which is 7/10 by my standard.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR the game is short but very fun so i personally didn't mind the price.i really enjoyed this game, i've been looking forward to the full release for a while and it was very fun. the art style is cute and overall the game is well-polished. there were a few puzzles which stumped me for a bit, which i consider a good thing! i didn't feel like it was repetitive, you had to achieve different results in each chapter and some are harder than you would initially think.i also liked how there are subtle differences between the characters, for example edgar and lenora are indifferent to the poison without a reason to use it, while isobel shows interest in it. i thought that was a nice way to make them each unique in some aspect.i know a lot of people are upset about the game being short for the price which is why i'm writing a review in the first place. i did feel a bit sad when i got everything completed in only 2 hours, but i think the game was worth the $15 dollars. i had a really fun time playing it, and it's well-made with a solid art style and no bugs. and most important for me, it made me smile and laugh like when i discovered the "frogs kissing" achievement, while still giving me a challenge (that final puzzle got me good). i also think this would be a wonderful game for kids.it might be unlikely but i do hope they release more content for this game because it is such a fun idea and there are so many more stories out there to take inspiration from.

_childDocuments_.review: storyteller is a fun little game that i did enjoy my time with! but depending on how good you are at the puzzles/how much you get stuck, and if you want to get all the achievements or you're fine just beating all the levels once, expect it to take somewhere between 30 min and 2½ hours to fully complete. it's a short, cohesive experience that knows what it's going for and does it well, not outstaying its welcome. this may be a great thing if you're short on time/prefer short games and it does mean that what is here is really polished, but there's only 52 levels and they're mostly pretty short. when i played it, it was just as i was getting into it and really understanding how the puzzles work when it abruptly ended.the first 2 chapters feel like the tutorial, and the last 4 are longer and slightly more difficult, so it's more like 8 tutorial levels, 40 main levels and 4 final challenge levels. there's a handful of levels that have a secondary goal appear after you finished it as a bonus challenge, but if you already did it that way the first time, as i sometimes did, you end up not even getting the extra challenge level to play. and there's already very few of them.the achievements are all easy to get and there aren't many. if that's a pro or a con depends on the player.if this goes on sale for a decent percentage off or they add more levels in the future i would recommend it because i do like the game! but with so little substance i can't say its worth the price tag for everyone. if you're the kind of person that's ok paying more than the average price of a short game to help support small indie developers, then it might be a non-issue for you. but for those with smaller budgets it's a hard sell at full cost. picking it up on sale or if more levels are added on the future is the way to go for those kinds of people in my opinion. this short runtime is going to be especially disappointing for anyone who's been waiting for it for a long time - it's spent a decade in development and while what is here is great, 10 years waiting for a >3 hour game with little replay value at a £12.49 price tag might be a bit of a sting.in short, the game is good! and that's why i wish there was more here.the levels all feel logical. even if you get stuck there's nothing that made me feel that 'how was i supposed to know to do that? it doesn't make any sense' that some puzzle games can fall into. the only one i tripped up on wasn't even a solution to a puzzle, it was getting the martini achievement. but looking at the animation of the relevant character when you see it, i got what they were going for and it made sense. i'm sure depending on the way you think, most people might run in to one or two moments where you just didn't think of something but it makes sense when you know the answer.some levels have multiple solutions, and you're often free to pick from a few characters for the same role so there will be variance but this is a puzzle game and not an interactive storyteller so don't expect to actually tell your own story.music is nice, mostly covers of iconic classical pieces, but that means its not exactly very memorable or exciting. it's the kind of soundtrack that fades into the background and you don't pay attention to. i wouldn't buy the ost myself but it's not bad by any measure. the art of the game is really nice, it knows what it's going for style wise, fitting perfectly with the game and just generally looking really good. there's little animations for every possibility in the stories which does add a lot of charm and help it to feel polished.while i strongly believe that a game shouldn't rely on fan-created content like mods to 'fix' or pad out their game, and the game should be complete and worth the price just for the available official content, having some kind of level editor available so people can create and share levels, either in game or through the steam workshop, would go a long way towards the feeling of it ending too soon. i just kinda think it would be a good idea, regardless of how it's priced or how much is in the game - it just seems like a natural fit for this style of game!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A game with great marred by a lack of content. At the time of this review I have 119 minutes of playtime (Below required steam playtime for refund) 100% completion (except some achievements) and I had more than half an hour AFK. Thankfully there is a custom levels mod, you can find information about it here: Foreword: I had initially intended to write this review on September 27th 2023, one day after the "Devilsh First Update" because I played it start to finish then, but life happened as it often does. All of my comments are from that play period because I really wanted to keep the 119 minutes for the review.Storyteller is a rather unique puzzle game, the gameplay regarding around the panels and the timeline they construct. In each level you try to finish the goal set by the level (And some additional ones that come into play later), creating different stories with the provided actors and stages to meet the goal. The game is rather short, currently featuring about 13 Chapters, all of which can be completed in less than an hour and a half, even with the optional objectives and some levels having a "devil mode" in it adding the devil as a character and changing the level goal.One thing I'll like to mention is that the game has no sandbox mode. I'm not the first one to say that a sandbox mode would fit this game extremely well, and I certainly won't be the last. The thing with the game being that across the 13 Chapters we see a variety of characters and scenarios, but they are all self contained, for the most part with interaction between chapters being very rare. Which is a shame because the potential is there, what would Edgar say to the the magic mirror? What would the witch do if she and Snow White were family? Can a gun kill Dracula? Seeing these interactions play out would be certainly fun but it would also take a lot of development time too. One thing that people may not know about Storyteller is that the game has been in development for a long time, like a LONG TIME. Here is early gameplay footage from a literal decade ago: . So this game has been in development for at least 10 years before release, changing wildly from then to now. So I have to assume that there are technical limitations at play that limit development. So a sandbox mode may be out of the questions but thankfully there is a custom level mod that adds some replayability (The game has close to no replayability right now). You can find more information about it here: I think this game would benefit from any kind of content, if they still exists somewhere the old gameplay versions would be fun extra content, it would allow us to see how the "Story of Storyteller" developed and we can see bonus content. Of course this is a pipe dream but it would help with the lack of content if it did happen. For future updates if we are going to get more expansions like the one for the Garden of Eden that we got in the Devilish update, I'd like to see more interplay between existing chapters, also the "Monsters" chapter desperately needs to be expanded. It adds a lot of cool little features that would be great for future levels, but they each last for 1-3 levels, for example the Dracula level alone adding multiple new mechanics let being a single level is such a waste as there is incredible potential in both that level and the whole chapter.To finish, I believe that Storyteller is a one of a kind game, and I'm sorry that I feel conflicted in recommending it. While I love what it does and believe that it is full of potential, the length of the game with high price tag makes it really hard for me to do so. Yet I ultimately still do, I believe in the potential of the game and in the dev to expand on it further in the future, especially considering that he worked on this game for over a decade. The price tag is a bit too steep to buy out of discount for the content present, but if you have some spare money (or a lot, depending on the region) and want to play a one of a kind puzzle game I would thoroughly recommend it. But be aware of the amount of content, you will likely finish the game in a few short hours (3 at most) so make your purchase accordingly.
