_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to say that this game is too short- that's too reductive. There are several ideas absolutely aching to be explored- the vampirism, seances, the witch and frog- and yet each is over after they've scraped the surface. It demonstrates remarkable detail in terms of putting together 'wrong answers' to get interesting scenarios, which shows that they even already have some of these ideas implemented!I don't quite understand why this was released with so few stories. _childDocuments_.review: Okay, I'm writing this review because there were none when I checked earlier today:If you're looking for a simple and quick game that lets you build a story given the prompt, setting, and characters provided, then you might enjoy Storyteller. Some of the prompts will require you to be creative, while others will be fairly straightforward.PROS: - Cute art style- Fun prompts- Some prompts offer "alternative" storylines (a line appears beneath the prompt).CONS:- About 1 hour of gameplay (maybe 2 if you're really struggling)- Not a lot of freedom in terms of storytelling (you'll usually have to complete prompts a certain type of way)I enjoyed this game, and I hope more prompts are added because Storyteller has the potential to be a lot more expansive.

_childDocuments_.review: My only complaint, is that I ran out of levels XD. A delightful little puzzle game, great for a casual evening, possibly a few depending on how quickly you pickup on the solutions. Puzzles were fun, loved the variety of options, and all the variation in the animations depending on how you laid out the story. Really great! Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun short game that you should wait for a sale on. It's (usually) the kind of puzzle where all the pieces are in front of you, you just have to figure out how to put them all together.That being said, they throw that away with the "secret stamps" part which requires you to guess which level you can do them in. It would've been better if it was more like the devil objectives where it was listed on each level instead of just having to guess, because the stamp titles vary from obvious to vague which level you could assume you had to do them in. I had to resort to a guide to point me at the right levels and even then I needed the guide to do some of the stamps because, for example, the Romeo and Juliet one requires a very specific sequence of events and I didn't understand why it wasn't working with two of them swapped despite being the same story path.Overall this was still a fun time to play with, and it even treats sexuality with some cleverness with some characters being bisexual while others only want to be with men/women.Also you get to shoot God in the face with a gun.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that has been in demo for a long time (1.5+ years from what I gathered), which apparently had a lot more content, I would not recommend buying this.The game is extremely short. For the main game, it's around 1 hour to 1.5 hours max. Achievement hunting afterwards is maybe 0.5 hour to 1 hour. The pricing feels very steep for this amount of gameplay.The game itself is very fun, and uses a very interesting system - But it feels more like a showcase of said system, rather than a full game.

_childDocuments_.review: Changing stuff around and seeing how every change influences every other component in the sequence feels like magic. My brain can't understand how the system came together. _childDocuments_.review: Probably the most unique and well thought-out puzzle game I've ever played! Although it is a bit short for its price, I love the freedom that the levels give you and all the interactions to explore! If I could add one thing to the game, that would be a sandbox mode, unlocked after completing all levels and stamps. You would have access to every character and scene, and there would be no title or goal to follow. So you would just be able to mess around with it and have fun! Overall, great game! I can't wait to see what this game has in store for us next!

_childDocuments_.review: NB: The positive rating is there because I did mostly like the game, but please note the total playtime, so I would consider waiting for a sale.Storyteller is a very simple and relaxing puzzle game, where the one and only puzzle is figuring out how to make a story based on a vague prompt using a small set of "stages" and "characters" (unique for each particular story prompt). Each stage has a limited number of positions for the characters in it, and usually these positions mean something, i.e. placing a character in the bushes while the other two are in the open in the "Affair" stage means that the first character hides and watches the other two kissing (despite the sheer amount of murder and affairs, the game is very innocently cartoonish in its presentation).That's pretty much it. I only had troubles with one level (because it was not obvious that a particular stage with a particular configuration of actors could have a particular effect on a later stage).The newly added Devilish mode, where you need to twist some of the previous stories with the addition of The Devil character, is fun, but rather short. The "stamps" (i.e. hidden achievements) are, unfortunately, somewhat annoying to get, because you need to guess both the story where you can get them at, and the actual prompt, which can be somewhat non-obvious.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: A clever little puzzle game whose only flaw is not living up to its massive potential. A mechanic will be introduced in one level group and then never seen again. I wish there were more advanced levels that mix and match elements from previous levels. Why not vampire Adam and Eve, or spicy detective romance? A sandbox mode would also be welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really fun and engaging puzzle game. Once I started I could hardly stop until I had beaten the whole thing. I would certainly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Not only is it short, it's pretty repetitive too.Lets go over some positives first.Good art and animations. The characters are lively, and have a reaction to almost everything. Very nice. No background colours, which is kind of a shame, but its faded backgrounds work fine.Visual storytelling. Few puzzles involve words being exchanged. Makes stories a lot more dynamic and interesting. And it makes the game work just as well in any language, which is great!The puzzles are fun to solve. Plain and simple. New things are introduced and gradually built upon. A good standard.But the best parts of this game are the side-objectives, which make you play through a level with a twist. These were genuinely great, having you take what you just did and flipping it around until the story is different, but the narrative is the same. But they appear only every few levels. Not for all of them. Which is majorly disappointing.Now... the negatives.Waaaaaaay too short. Overall, the main game + side-objectives took an hour and six minutes to beat. The save file indicates that was 100% of the game. What?! So I went and did the achievements that I hadn't already gotten by accident. Took about 30 minutes. So I have literally seen everything that this $20 game has to offer in an hour and a half.Repetition. The puzzles are all very similar, even from chapter to chapter. The game will build upon a puzzle, giving you all the pieces, then DROP EVERYTHING and on to the next chapter. BUT! You come back to previous themes later on. By that I mean, the themes will just repeat for some chapters, but with a very slightly lengthier solution. The last chapter is fine tho, it's got the longest puzzles with mechanics you are already familiar with. They should add at least 7 more of these chapters.No overarching story. The 'stories' in this game are just each individual level. Chapters don't have a running story, just a theme. The book has no story, just the chapters. Bit of a shame, but I can understand why.The ending. Not much of a spoiler cuz there's barely an ending anyway. Your reward for completing every 'story' in this book? A nicely written "you did it" as the credits roll. No final puzzle, you just did 4 mini final puzzles that didn't even have all the elements, but at least now there's a shadow of a crown in your face.This game, plain and simply, is not worth $20. $10 at the most, tho I'd shoot for $8. This game was meant for iPads. a $3.99 IOS game to get a kid to stay quiet on a two hour car ride.Play FRAMED instead. It's half the price and double the length.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Recommends, but the gameplay is too short and no replayability. Personally, I don't mind the full price, currently felt the content is worth it for the price imo. But no replayability while the game is very short def made the game felt lacking. When I first heard of the game, I thought it was a sandbox type of mode where we could create any story, and I felt the game would be better if it has that kind of mode, merely to increase replayability and fun combination (which could led to more achievement content).Def still recommends in it's current state though.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Storyteller brought to me a fresh and very unique experience to what seems to be lately a very bland genre. Games like storyteller are what is helping revive the genre these past few years. For the price you pay storyteller will have you leaving very satisfied and with it's brand new content update as well it's stamp collecting after end-game/ You will be able to juice out an extra hour or two from this wonderful game. The puzzles themselves can leave you feeling stuck, but never hopeless. The game itself keeps the puzzles fresh and entertaining in a very clever way bringing the player through different periods of time and famous novels. Allowing the player to set up there own story and mess with the characters however the desire. All at the same time giving the player an end goal for each mission in order to move on. The games humor helped elevate each level and the goals really pointed the player in the right direction, but without giving the answer away that easily. Overall storyteller is a game worth your time if puzzles are your thing it certainly did them well and put a fun twist on them too. 6/10Follow my curator page for more critical game reviews!

_childDocuments_.review: Annapurna continues to impress me with the games they publish - always creative, fun and innovative.  Storyteller is a short game with a unique concept.  You have a text prompt of what the "story" should show and various figures or settings to create story panels out of.  The goal is to arrange these in a way that matches the given prompt.  There are also on some of the stages, alternate story prompts to "discover" by playing around with the characters and settings.The entire look and feel of the game is fun and playful, and while I didn't find much of this challenging (I did 100% the game in about 4 hours) I still had a great time and considered an evening well spent.  Also huge props to the people or person in charge of sound - the sound effects were minimal but effective and enjoyable.  The only complaint I have about this game is that not all of the stages have alternate stories to tell.  And they are not marked in any way to indicate that.  So without looking it up, you wouldn't know if playing around with the panels would get you an alternate story or not.  I'd much rather it said on the stage that I'd uncovered 1 of 3 stories or 1 of 1 stories so I didn't waste any time on ones that didn't have that.The long and short of this though is that this game is super fun and creative, and while I don't personally think 14.99 is a good price point for this game, if you can get it on a sale as I did, it sure made for a fun evening.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely charming puzzle game. _childDocuments_.review: So let me get this out of the way, this game feels a bit short. The last batch of puzzles are excellent, but I was somewhat taken aback when I hit the conclusion. However, I'm still recommending this product because length isn't the end-all of a game's execution. Preferably, the creators can add additional puzzles (possibly for free?) in the post-game or deliver new scenarios. However, this is con really is outweighed by the charm and mostly positive execution. I love narrative games and I think this is the type of project that would be perfect for writing classes. There is clearly a good amount of thought put into how a puzzle works in this game because you have to account for motivations, personality changes, and the "why" of a story. At first the puzzles are easy because they are tutorial essentially. However, this title begins to add new wrinkles that made me think about the nature of storytelling itself. Why can't I make this Queen just fall in love with the Bodyguard? How do I make this minor character become more relevant in this scenario? WHY CAN'T I have as MANY PANELS as I WANT? I'm just kidding on that one. Like any good story, brevity and conciseness of the puzzles allows you to hone in on the exact mechanisms rather than deep nuance. Overall, if you want a game that really gets at the core of story construction or is an aspiring writer, this game is a no-brainer even with its short length. However, I can see it not going over well for those that want longer experiences or find these types of puzzles *boring.* For me, i dug it.

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent, short, and well presented, cute puzzle game. Despite the inherently vague mechanics of human emotions and literary plot contrivances we've all come to learn through stories, it manages to stay very logical, only really getting me stuck one time. _childDocuments_.review: I'm torn. Like, genuinely torn. On one hand, this game is an absolute treat; gorgeous graphics, unique vibe, a fun take on puzzling, and a unique way to work in literary references without being "like that". I've been hype for Storyteller since I played it's demo during last year's indie jam and, both stylistically and through it's gameplay, it more than meets my expectations...however...On the other hand...you can knock this game out in an hour. An hour of gameplay...for $15 bucks. Is tough to swallow. The only reason that (as of this review) I have 4.5 in playtime is because after my initial save I did a second pass to 100%, and then after a friend and I did some puzzles together over stream.I am leaving a positive review because it's a beautiful little indie project and I am hoping (HOPING) that there will be future updates with more content. Especially since there were puzzles/narratives in the demo that are NOT in the main game at launch and they could find a way to patch those back in and/or use other classic novels as inspiration for new puzzles! So, yeah, love it, it's an hour of gameplay (maybe an hour and a half if you have a guide up to 100% the achievements first pass), thats a drag, get it when it's cheaper than $15, or not, it's pretty cheap and I'm not your mom. Do what you will with your money.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I thought it's yet another game published by Annapurna that seems to cater to people who like the "indie" in "indie games", but not the "games". The aesthetic of artistic, independent design - but it has to look good so I can show it to my friends! It's not like I'm going to play much of it anyway...Well, no. This is the real deal. It's a puzzle game, asking you to create a specific situation with predefined pieces. It's not a crappy comic book generator, there's actually quite a bit of game in here.The main problem you'll be tackling is the fact that the pieces all have specific rules that they will abide by default. Rules of the world, so to speak. To choose a random example, let's say we take Undyne, Alphys, and Asgore from UNDERTALE. Let's put each of them next to a pile of anime. Alphys would be overjoyed, Asgore would be perplexed, and Undyne would say "what is this dorky crap?" and throw it into the trash. Right?In the context of the game - say you want the Knight to kill the Queen. You have a cliff scene. Simple, right? Make the Knight stand behind the Queen, he will push her, right? But no. The Knight not only is loyal to the Queen, he's also in love with her. You have to create a motive for him to do it; but how? Well, the Knight is also very righteous, and values justice highly... higher than his loyalty to the queen. Maybe he'd change his tune if you were to show him a wicked deed that the Queen committed?Or sometimes the problem is the other way around: there is no visible means for a person to do something. Let's say the cliff isn't there, but the Knight already is convinced that the Queen is wicked. Oh, but there's the execution chamber. The problem is, only someone who's been crowned a monarch can order an execution. So we'd need to have the Knight somehow usurp the throne first...The stories you'll create to achieve these goals are often bizarre, macabre, ridiculous - . That's what this game is. It's just fun. You'll probably chuckle while playing it. "Oh god, I have an idea how to make this happen..." and then you do, and it's a glorious mess. There's even a collection of hidden stamps - little achievements that you get for creating unique interactions and outcomes.My favourite is having Nietzsche shoot God dead, and then have dead God's spirit cower in fear in front of Nietzsche, who's menacingly spinning the gun. "I finally killed you, you bastard! God is dead, and I have killed him!" "Yes bro, you win, now put that away, man!"Do I have complaints, though? Yeah. I wish there was more. I can't believe I'm saying this, I'm always complaining that the games are too long and don't know when to stop, but here everything is so lovely, you can't help but want to keep playing with the little pieces. Especially considering that many pieces are woefully underutilised. Dracula appears... once, I think. So does Nietzsche. Give Vlad VS Fred epic battle for the heart of the Queen from Snow White. _childDocuments_.review: This is a difficult one, because I like the game a lot, and think it has a lot of promise, and would rate my experience with it as very enjoyable. I'd love to recommend this game, but there's a glaring issue that prevents me from doing so. I had completed this game in under two hours, within the refund time window of Steam's policy, and from what I've gathered, so have many other people. It is because of this that I cannot give a positive recommendation to the game, but this isn't necessarily a message for other buyers, but rather for the developers. This may seem like an oxymoron, but I leave a negative review because I enjoyed this game greatly and want to see it succeed further.Now, I'm not a game developer, and I'm not going to get into how much a game should be worth for the work and time put into it by the developers, and how much time a player will have after purchasing and playing, but if there are as many people completing this game within the refund time as I think there are, then there's a problem. I feel like generally, most people are going to want to refund the game after completing it, or near completing it, to get their $20 back and purchase a different game that'll probably give them more hours of game time elsewhere. I am myself still within the refund window, but I'll be keeping a hold of this game out of principle, but I imagine a lot of other people aren't going to do that. That, or they'll look at the average game time and be deterred away from it. Again, I'm not a developer, and don't know what it takes, but I do know that people not purchasing the game based off of hours spent, or refunding the game because of completing it within the refund window is probably bad for business. There are two ways I can see that'll remedy this, and that's either lowering the price to make people less likely to want to return it after completing it so quickly, like I had, or make it more likely for people to want to purchase it in the first place. The second way is by adding more content, though I recognise that it's not that simple. It can be done though, by either adding more chapters in to complete, or more optional challenges for each chapter already existing. I'm sure there are plenty of other ways of tackling this, but I'm worried about it's current price tag with how much play time is available deterring people away from this game, as I think it has a lot of potential. I loved all the puzzles involved and how active the characters where to changes you'd make, even finding little secret interactions that the game didn't readily make obvious until you found it yourself. There's a lot that can be done with this game, but my main criticism so far would be the simplicity of some of the puzzles, coupled with the price of the game for how little time it gives you to play with it, as there's basically no replay-ability whatsoever with the game as it currently stands.TL:DR - Sorry if my post came off as a bit of a ramble. I loved this game and want to see it succeed, but I cannot recommend it as it is due to the price and length of the game. I sincerely hope more is done with this game, as I would love to experience more with it.

_childDocuments_.review: is an enjoyable puzzle game with a unique concept and a solid timeline mechanic. The premise of each level is to build a story using the characters and the settings given to you by mixing and matching them into picture frames, which are then ordered to form a sequence of events. By dragging one or two of the available characters into one of the available environments, you animate them and make them act according to the chosen environment and the story has built so far. Changing something in a previous frame will modify all the subsequent ones to reflect these changes. For example, when a certain character dies, they will appear as a ghost in all frames after the current one, making the other characters interact with them differently than when they were alive.The title of the story will tell you exactly what’s expected of you, and part of the fun is discovering ways to make your characters perform a particular action. Some puzzles are very trivial and can be solved in mere seconds, while others are quite complex and will require you to place the characters in various circumstances so that they end up liking or hating each other, giving them motives to perform the actions suggested by the story’s title. For example, a character placed in a setting containing a gun will pick it up only if they have a motive to do so and will further use that gun to kill another character only if a previous frame made them hate each other.In a way,  is a “find the developer’s solution” kind of game, considering that the levels usually have unique solutions. Some titles are intentionally left vague, though, allowing you to solve a level in two different ways, but even so, the solutions are predetermined and as soon as one of them is reached, the title changes to reflect the flow of the story you chose to create. is a game that will appeal primarily to visual people or those who enjoy from visualizing a story in their minds based on a sequence of pictures, similar to a comic book. While it could look suitable for younger audiences too due to its cute graphics and its unique way of stimulating one’s creativity, I’d say that the logical process required to reach a solution for most of the levels is rather complex, often making one think in terms of intrigue, court affairs, vengeance, jealousy etc.While the gameplay is amusing and entertaining, and the mechanics are well implemented, the game gathers a lot of negativity due to it being overpriced.  can be finished in less than three hours without checking a guide. For that amount of content the asking price of $14.99 is very high, especially since the game doesn’t offer any replayability. Annapurna Interactive is known to deliver quality products (they’re one of my favorite publishers on Steam). Even though  is up to those standards, it’s simply not enough to justify the price, not even at the 50% off discount that the game will likely reach in the next two years.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following Daniel Benmergui's work since I first played I Wish I Were the Moon and Today I Die when I was in middle school. It has been about 16 years since then, and the impact that those 2 games left on me had me hyped to this day for the release of Storyteller. Now that I've played it I can say, I tried to like it, I really did, but at the end the game fell flat in delivering any meaningful experience. Even in a vacuum assuming I hadn't played the two aforementioned games before, Storyteller is at best a mediocre puzzle game. The main mechanic is interesting in concept. The game gives you a storyboard with a predetermined number of panels and it asks you to give each panel a setting and characters. All in order to fulfill a different objective with different panel types and characters per level. Each panel type, each character and even each order of actions creates a different "story"The issue arises with the fact that while the game purports itself to be about telling stories creatively, each level feels as if it can only be solved with a very limited number of configurations. And even worse, many levels wind up feeling like retreads of concepts you saw in previous levels. While game length is not an issue for me personally, I do feel that having a game this short feeling repetitive is fairly troubling.As I said before I had high hopes for this game. But at the end of the day, this is not a thought-provoking project, a vehicle for creativity, nor even a good puzzle game. Storyteller is the logical end result of forcing your way through the sunk-cost-fallacy on a project that only sounded good as a concept, yet clearly didn't work in execution.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely delightful puzzle game where half the fun is determining what your puzzle pieces actually do.  For example, you might have the objective of having one character murder another ... but if you just put them in a room together nothing happens.  So first you might need to give one character a weapon, or even establish a motive.  So you'll need to build a story where this makes sense.  Make one spy on the other having an affair, and then put them in a room where they can pick up a gun, and THEN put them in a room together and see what happens.  But what if the first character doesn't like guns, or doesn't have a romantic interest so won't be bothered by an affair?  Try a different combination, experiment with putting the character in different situations and learn what really motivates them.  The game does an admirable job of helping you up the learning curve with easier cases at first and moving on to more complicated schemes, though nothing is punishingly difficult.  You will feel smart and will likely enjoy helping make these cute (though often dark) stories unfold.

I love how the characters can be put in many different situations, and yet have their own personalities which interact with the the situations. I think there's room for even more exploration of character personality quirks. Some of the puzzles are quite challenging, most are not too hard. I hope they continue adding content to it! Feels a bit short still.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: A clever, pretty puzzle game with enough variety in its different chapters to not feel like you're just solving the same puzzle over and over again. Whilst the beginning is pretty simple, the final chapter gets quite tricky so there is definitely a difficulty curve. For all those saying they refunded this because they finished the whole game "quickly" - shame on you. I'd understand it if it didn't feel like a finished product or it didn't have enough depth, but there has clearly been a lot of effort put into this. If you don't like games that are done within three - four hours, don't buy it. Games should be valued on the enjoyment they give, not how long they last. If your issue is more that you can't afford it for the price, which is perfectly fair, then wait for the sale to experience it at a cheaper price. Don't buy it, finish it, then refund it and mark it down poorly. GoodGood variety of puzzles with some fun solutions to figure outGradual difficulty curveBeautiful art and quirky character animationsBadEnding is pretty anti-climatic
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: great short game to be enjoyed. a lot of creativity to be had, and good for hour or two experience, but overpriced for how little content it has in current time. if in future there is free dlc, or you just happen to find it for very cheap, i implore you explore the fascinating stories you can spin within the pages, but as a whole experience, it leaves still whole lot to ask for
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Cute. Got it on sale for $10 and it was definitely entertaining, but within 3 hours I'd completed the whole game, the free expansion, and gotten all achievements. I hope there are more expansions because it's a genuinely enjoyable piece of entertainment, but it's way too short. I do appreciate that there may be multiple ways to reach a solution - but there are also some solutions the game won't recognize, even though you can see you've met all the criteria (like making sure everyone dies sad - you can break everyone's heart before you kill them, but the game won't acknowledge all versions of this). I wasn't aware of the devil expansion when I bought it and it was a nice surprise, especially because it was more challenging, but it was also incredibly short.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game since the demo was first put up and I am disappointed by the final game. I beat it in the time it would take me to watch a movie. _childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun, but very, very short. I was able to 100% it within 3 hours. If there was some sort of endless mode, or maybe some sort of user-submitted puzzle mode, that would make me like it far more. With as fun as it is, it just feels too short and ultimately unsatisfying - I wanted more, and it's just not there.Feel free to buy it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: It was a fun game, and a few of the puzzles were genuinely tricky to solve... but for the price it was, I thought there would be more chapters, given that once you play through, there isn't a whole lot of replay-ability. There also wasn't as much room for alternate story lines as there was in the demo; many of the scenarios had only one possible "solution." Overall a good game, and the art, animations, and sound effects are great, but maybe wait for a Steam sale to pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I completed the game and all the achievements - without checking any guide - in 2.5 hours according to Steam. I also watched all the credits and read everything the game was throwing at me. It's a great game, great concept, it's fun! It reminds me of Pilgrims, although that one is much cheaper... And that's exactly the issue here. The content doesn't match the price. It gives you roughly one hour of puzzles, and another hour if you want to do all the achievements without checking a guide or asking for help and... once you do that... there's zero replayability. Adding a workshop or more chapters to the book as a free update will definitely change my review though! Buy it during a sale (at least 50% off!)
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: very interesting & fun puzzle game where you create stories with the characters through different scenes. definitely some challenging/thought provoking puzzles in here and you can use your creativity to achieve different outcomes. a little on the short side for the price but i enjoyed the unique experience the game offers!
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun sweet and short puzzle game, for the low asking price there is no reason to skip out on this experience. Definite recommend!PS: After playing for a while, I found it more fun to skip levels when I couldn't solve them and then look at a guide on the way through the game again, as some solutions felt personally unintiutive.Bonus tip: Use keys 1-9 to switch to the chapters so that you don't have to go page by page!
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Such a cute and fun puzzle game! The art is adorable and the stories are actually very interesting. The game is played by going through various 'titles' of stories. It is then up to you to place characters and scenes into various positions to create relationships and various scenarios that prompt the story to play out based on the title. Each of the characters interact differently or have traits that affect how they will behave and you can then further influence their decisions in the panels by creating history with others or establishing events.It's challenging to explain but this game will be loved by people who like to think through puzzles to create a desired outcome. Game overall took about 2 hours to play and 4 hours for all the achievements. Regardless it was totally worth the price and I'd buy it again! Highly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: VERY good and fun game worth the year+ ive been waiting, however it went by way too fast, I feel there needed to be way more content, i only got about an hour of playtime out of it and for $15 bucks an hour just doesnt feel like enough, hopefully there'll be updates with more puzzles because i want more of the game
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I am sad to see so many reviews complaining about length -- this is one of the most genuinely interesting ideas for a game I've ever known. I judged it for IGF *years* ago and had the same response then... I've been eagerly awaiting it all that time. Is it short? Maybe. But it stretches your imagination and concepts of narrative, what a game can be, and creates lovely, playful exploration of story concepts. I cannot shout my praise of this game highly enough. I'd love to see more of it, sure, but that in no way diminishes how great it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting and lovely little puzzle game! If it's on sale, 100% get it. If it's not on sale, it's up to you whether you want to spend the (around) 23 AUD asking price. The animations and lovely and the game charming, but doesn't have much content to bite into.Other than more content, the thing I most want in this game is a freeplay mode. A way to play with all the different characters and setting, and allow us to play with more than 8 panels at a time. I was genuinely surprised to see this wasn't already in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: If you like clever puzzle mechanics, buy this game! It's unique, it's fun(ny), it works great!Like some others, I was reluctant to buy because I had heard the game was only about 2 hours long.My playtime says otherwise, and that's not just because I was acting a little dumb on some levels.After release, the game has so far received some alternate levels and a lot of fun extra story challenges that force you to play with the mechanics in ways you may not have experienced in your regular playthrough.Plus the devs are very active in the community discussions, take on criticism and fix things which is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: This is a brilliant puzzle game. It manages to combine stories and puzzles very intimately and naturally. I've completed all the main puzzles, and can say that each and every one felt fair. There were no obtuse puzzles, even for the stories that ended up with contrived plots.The game still feels a bit short, despite the recent update. I think part of it is because some of the chapters felt a bit too easy, so their 4-5 stories went by in a flash. There were some meaty chapters that needed decent think time, namely the chapters featuring the Queen, but even the "medium" difficulty chapters didn't take too long to figure out. Difficulty varies a bit, some of the late game chapters were much easier than chapters before them.I haven't done much with the recently added stamps, since its kind of annoying to go back and forth between the stamps and the puzzles to figure out what you need to do, and they give off a feel of being optional side content.I strongly recommend the game to anyone who likes puzzle games, with the caveat of the short length of the game. Paid $10 for this during a sale, and although I don't regret it, it does feel steep for the amount of content in the game. It needs a few more difficult chapters.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I really hate choosing no on this game. It has a great artstyle and a neat concept. Some of the puzzles have multiple solutions too.However, it is way too short for the price. I played the demo as well and that felt more satisfying than the game. It really feels like if a game finished just after the tutorial section. If this game is eventually updated with more content I will change my review.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: It took less than 2 hours and there is almost no replay value. If I would have known I would have spent my money elsewhere. If there are free updates and expansions I might consider updating but as it stands now, it's not worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: Due to my only real complaint, which was about content-to-price ratio, having been solved by a free update adding some content (and also, I'm almost certain the pricetag have been lowered since the last time I checked), I have changed this to a positive review.This is one of those times I wish Steam had a more nuanced rating system than just "good" or "bad", because while it may have little content for its price, it has SOUL.It's a cute puzzle game with an interesting timeline mechanic, but it's cruelly short and there's little reason to replay it once you finish it, and therefore little to justify its current price.At the very least, this game would probably benefit from the ability to create and upload custom levels to a workshop, if the devs can't be bothered to make more content for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun with the game and I don't regret getting it, but I can't really recommend it, at least not at it's pricepoint. Within less than 2 hours of playtime, I didn't just beat the game, I 100%ed it(My playtime is only over 2 hours because I was letting the game run in the background while I was setting up my stream). Tbf, I expected it to be short, but not quite that short. Don't get me wrong, I actually don't mind a short game thats high quality, but parts of it even manage to feel repetative, especially in the Duke/Butler section, where so many of the puzzles are basicly the same with only a sligth variation. When you finally do the last one and expect it to unlock something big at the end of the book... there is just nothing. It's over.It's a shame, cus I think this is actually a brilliantly unique concept and I don't mind the more simplistic nature of the puzzles, I just wish there were more.It might just be wishfull thinking but I kinda hope that we are gonna get the tools to make our own puzzles in an update, because if this game actually got moddingsupport and allowed the general playerbase to create new puzzles, it would instantly solve the games biggest issue, which is length. Unless thats the case though, it's up to you if roughly 1,5 hours of gameplay is actually worth the money for you.

Plus, for the time and price, it's basically the same investment as going to the movies, except here you get to make the story yourself, test your thinking skills, and earn some achievements in the process.All in all, I do highly recommend this game. _childDocuments_.review: Cute, but fails to deliver an actually fun experience. Beat the game in just under 3 hours. Puzzle complexity is all over the place, ranging from obnoxiously trivial to arbitrary pedantic. Over half the puzzles were so obvious, they could be completed in under a minute. (Several times, I accidentally solved a puzzle just by switching around frames while trying to do something *else). A couple puzzles literally reuse the material from past puzzles; the solutions are 95% the same. A handful - less than 6 - were both challenging and satisfying to solve. The "harder" puzzles often have one very specific way to solve them; though you may satisfy the conditions for a solution, if it's not *the* solution, you don't get a pass. You're not creating a unique story that fits the description; you're playing a guessing game until you do what the game wants. Puzzles are all themed, which is cute, but they borrow from common tropes and fairy tales. While this helped me familiarize myself with the premise, it also meant the puzzles themselves were not foreign to me; they just rehashed existing dramas from mythical stories. That's not as interesting, IMO. I'd return it, but I took 0.9 extra hours to complete the entire game. Not worth the money/time.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: You should really try to take your time and slow down when playing. Take some breaks too! I only have two real complaints with the game. I wish the UI was a little easier to move around in. Secondly, the game is incredibly short. $15 for a little over two hours of content isn't great. I saw two clips on YouTube, so I had the answer to two chapters, but even cutting out two chapters before the unlockable and achievement content, shouldn't be a two hour affair. If you take it slow and let yourself have more fun, a little less internal drive to keep moving, maybe you can get more bang/dollar.If I could have some more, it would be fun if the narrator was more present, maybe a little aware and talking to me a bit. There were a few times where I was sitting around thinking, and if he dropped a hint for me after 'x' amount of time, would be a fun addition. Probably would have slapped around characters and scenes in a manic rush to get something to happen. then again that's how I beat some of the "New Game +" content.8/10 - Overall

_childDocuments_.review: It's a splendidly charming game with a fun and unique puzzle mechanic. The art and animations are great, and the cozy book aesthetic feels very welcoming. _childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: A cute, and comically morbid puzzle game about recreating and subverting the tropes and trends of old tales. Brief but satisfying.The puzzles ramp up nicely. You learn how frames affect each other before being tasked with orchestrating scenarios that at first examination seem undoable. Fiddling with the scenario to “cheat” the character or scene’s logic to achieve seemingly impossible outcomes hits like manipulating the logic of “Baba is You”, though this game asks, thankfully, much less of me. A recent update added new challenges, including the quite tricky devil remixes which were great fun. I don’t know that I like the bonus stamps, which ask you to create literary references amongst a large pool of possible stories. I’d rather work with the game’s logic than tab out to search old english literature, but achieving some through happenstance was a devious joy. Eat your heart out, Goethe. For me, $15 is a hair much for this game, but I respect what the developers are charging for their excellent work.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Storyteller is a game developed by Daniel Benmergui and published by Annapurna InteractiveThe game offers some nice graphics and a really beautiful aesthetic, it is pleasant all the sameThe game does suffer with it being incredibly short and not offering much in terms of gameplay and more of a short, touching story. For me personally, it didn't bug me at all but if you're expecting a really deep, intricate game with some clever gameplay mechanics and such, Storyteller isn't the game for you.Storyteller overall, however, is a short, beautiful game to play, it is a good interactive adventure game to play in short bursts!

_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: The shop description calls it a puzzle game and that's what it is. Nothing more.It's definitely not about  like the shop description claims and for a game called "Storyteller" that is a massive flaw. You don't come up with stories on your own... All you do is finding the correct pictures to a prefabricated "story" and your options are very limited, especially in the beginning. Later it gets slightly better, but the core problem remains the same: By standards that low you could call the crossword puzzle in a newspaper "Storyteller, the puzzle game".The game's simplistic graphics look nice, though, but that shouldn't be the main selling point of any game. If you want people to enjoy  rather than just looking at it, you have to make sure your  isn't crap. Hence the term...I bought it for 9,23€ and don't think it's worth that much... and it's definitely not worth 13,99€, either.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played a game this fun with so much humor in my lifeStoryteller is a narrative puzzle game. You get a number of frames, some situations, some characters and a general sentence. Your task is to use the characters and the situations in such a way in order to fit to the narrative sentence, in short to tell the story you have to tell. The puzzles won't puzzle you much BUT the game includes specific clauses sometimes that turn the challenge up. While the game is called "Storyteller" the puzzles are all about programming logic in a sense "if that and if that happens or that doesn't happen then there is this outcome". Which is another way to interpret narrative tasks. But the greatest thing and 100% of its charm is the presentation and the humor. The game winks in several literature genres, writers, and cliches by subverting them or by making fun of them. I won't spoil it, but the point that Friedrich Nietzsche makes a cameo appearance had me laughing out loud for a couple of minutes.One of the wittiest and funnest games I have played in my life. Congratulations to the developing team!
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the idea of this game, but ultimately found it more frustrating than fun. (Which is a shame, because a lot of effort was put into it, and it looks and sounds great!)I think a lot of my disappointment stems from how it's repeatedly described as allowing you to 'play with stories', 'experiment', 'you are the author', etc. This paints a picture of a game that lets you get truly creative to solve each prompt, but in reality each puzzle only asks you to shuffle a tiny handful of pieces around until you find the one solution that's allowed.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever loved a game so much and yet can't recommend it. As a puzzler, it is cute. On difficulty, there are a few that you have to tool around with to get right, but nothing is going to drive you nuts.  As many have said, you will beat it in under 2 hours and then you will be done. There's little replayability and there's nothing unlocked.  And yet.. the premise is so strong and the delivery of what it gives you is so well done that you are left wanting so so much more while being so so disappointed at the price you paid. If there was more content coming for already paid customers, if there was Workshop support, if there was a sandbox, if there was anything more I would give it a thumbs up. Since none of that is there, this brilliant niche puzzler will sit with a 'Mostly Negative' because of the amount of content is remarkably short for the price.

_childDocuments_.review: Storyteller is a remarkably creative puzzle game from the mind of Daniel Benmergui. In each page of the storybook, the player is presented with a group of environments and characters. By placing the characters in these locations in a certain order, the stories can be manipulated to have a variety of outcomes. At first you have simple tasks like making two people heartbroken so they can fall in love together, but by the end of the game you'll be setting up murder plots and figuring out how to get certain characters to witness certain events that set up future plot threads. They're all fairly simple, with none of the pages containing more than eight panels, but the endless possibilities in how each page can be rearranged is astounding. Some puzzles even have alternate solutions or special conditions to be met in order to get a bonus mark in your book.Unfortunately, even with all of these possibilities and mechanics, the game rarely fleshes them out. Sure, a few puzzles are tricky, but with the game only taking about an hour to 100%, none of these puzzles really feel like they push the boundary of the game's potential. Just as you're starting to get really into the inner workings of these story elements the game is over, which is a real shame. The artwork is fantastic, the originality of the concept is refreshing, and the gameplay is a lot of fun, but Storyteller ends up feeling like an appetizer without a meal afterward. It's a real shame because if these mechnics were expanded upon I could genuinely see this going down as one of the best puzzle games ever made. If you want a truly unique experience and don't mind things being a little underdeveloped, I can easily recommend Storyteller, but if you're disappointed when a game fails to reach its maximum potential, you might want to wait for the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: It saddens me to see so many negative reviews complaining about the game's length. I do wish it was longer as well, but that doesn't take away from the enjoyment I got out of it.This is a hand-crafted experience. The attention to detail is just mind-boggling, and I was several times surprised by things working exactly as I would have expected them to work when randomly experimenting with characters and locations beyond the explicit game objectives. Making this kind of high-quality content for this game-system certainly took time, thought, and creativity. I repeat that I do wish the game was longer, and I will certainly keep an eye out for any new content that is released. However, refunding the game after completing it and enjoying it is just abusing the system. If you're guilty of that, I recommend you take a good, long look at yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: This game might have been worth the cost if it had a level creation and share function like Mario Maker so you could make your own levels or play levels made by others. As it stands, the game is terribly short, and I do mean absolutely horrendously short. 100% ed in under 2 hours short.The game literally has a grand total of 51 levels. And while that might sound like a big number, for a puzzle game where you can finish each level in under 5 minutes, it really is nothing, and a good 1/4 to 1/2 of these levels are only 3 to 4 panels long. You might think the limited panels would be meant to be a challenge, but no. It's because in every single new "chapter" (as in, every 4 levels) the first 1 or 2 levels are used as a tutorial for the mechanics of that chapter. This means that of the measly 51 levels this game has to offer, a at least a quarter of them are used as short, simple tutorials. There's a reason so many people say this game feels like a tutorial for a bigger, better game it could have been, it's because 1/4 of the time you ARE playing a tutorial.Now, please don't get me wrong, I loved every minute of the game-play. It's genuinely enjoyable, and a neat concept. I think this is a wonderful little game. But it's not worth the price on the label, and don't buy this game if you're looking for enjoyable, long term entertainment.This game just left me feeling disappointed, like so much wasted potential.As it stands, I cannot recommend this game, at least not at full price. Get it when it's something like 90% off, or if you have money to waste I suppose.

_childDocuments_.review: is an excellently cute and charming logic puzzle game where you use a combination of scenes and characters to create a scenario based on a title prompt. Not only is it very clever, but it feels totally intuitive and has endless moments where I feel totally on the same wavelength as the creators, smiling and laughing practically the whole way through. The kind of game you can easily recommend to your parents, or friends who don't even play games that regularly, as all the logic in the puzzles use emotive proxies in signifiers from fables, each with their own intuitive quirks, that resolve much of the inaccessibility in harsh videogame-y logic puzzles. It has easily become a new favourite of mine and will be a go-to recommendation for a casual fun experience.If you liked this game and want more short and sweet charming games filled with love that you can also recommend to similar demographic, I'd recommend , the soothing puzzle home decorating game where you gain insights into your character's life through unpacking their moving boxes.If you liked the storybook style and the aesthetic of the imagery used but want more of a dense story that you can loosely influence in more typical interactive fiction style, I would recommend , the gorgeously illustrated world where you solve murders and scandals in 16th century Europe.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an inventive logic puzzle game, but instead of math or cryptograms, the goal is to use narrative storytelling techniques to solve the puzzles. Plot, character motivation, and continuity are all central to solving the various puzzles, and character archtypes and familiar scenarios make it accessible for anyone who likes a good story. I recommend it to anyone looking for a different sort of logic puzzle game, and especially for anyone who likes playing with narrative techniques.

_childDocuments_.review: You're presented with a number of scenes and characters and have to suss out the correct scenes in the correct order with the correct participants. To beat a level, the title of the level must match the resulting multi-paneled story you created. Coming up with wrong solution can also be funny as each scene and character react according to a set of rules you discover as you play. For example, in the graveyard scene a person observes a tombstone where another person is buried. This changes the second person's status to dead. Also if the first person liked the second person, the first person would be changed to heartbroken. Heartbroken characters can then meet someone new and remarry, or if presented with poison will chug it and die. Dead characters show as a ghost who will frighten most people, unless they were murdered, in which case they tell their tale. There's some replayability, in that levels can have alternate titles to solve, and after you beat all the levels you're presented with more alternate titles involving a new character who is literally the devil. If this sounds interesting to you, you will squeeze out a few fun hours from this game. Not a lot of play time, but I like stuff like this.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT AFTER FIRST UPDATE OCTOBER 2023: My hope in the review below was fulfilled: the developer added a free content patch which added a very significant amount of extra puzzles while also improving on the achievement mechanic! I would definitely double recommend this game now, even at full price. My original review follows below.Here's the short of it: this game is great, beautiful art, high polish, fun puzzles with a unique narrative puzzle mechanic you've never seen before. But the game is also about as short as this two-sentence tl;dr review.At the moment, you should buy it, but if you buy it at full price you should see 50% of that as the cost of the actual game and 50% of that as a donation to support a creative indie developer.The game is NOT over-priced, imho, because you can see and feel where the money went, because artists have to eat. But artists also make unprofitable decisions like spending their time and effort on unique and beautiful puzzle games which, due to the nature of the puzzle genre, have little replayability as opposed to another dime-a-dozen roguelike that has barely half the style and polish of this game but milks the content its got for every minute of playtime it can.As a puzzle game, half the fun here is how beautiful and funny the art is. It's always enjoyable to see the characters' facial expressions and getting to know their personality by that and by how they react to different scenes and scenario's. Who will commit suicide upon a broken heart? Who will commit murder? Narrative suffuses every level of this puzzle game, making it a holistic experience as opposed to just a gimmick.As it stands, not having played the demo will increase your enjoyment, as otherwise you're likely to rush through quite a few of the early puzzles. But even having played the demo quite a bit the full game still threw a few head-scratchers my way that let to great "Ooooo, that's how!" moments.I never was stuck long enough to be frustrated. On the one hand that means that overall most puzzles weren't that hard, on the other hand, getting frustrated isn't that much fun so it's a compliment to the intuitive game design that no puzzle out-stays its welcome.My hope is that in the future, the developer will expand with free content patches and (dare I dream?) a sandbox mode. There were some puzzles in the demo that never made it to the full game, so that's a good sign there's more content in the pipeline! But even if that doesn't happen, I feel this beautiful game is worth sacrificing one or two pizza's or happy meals.There are some games you buy because you'll play them forever, and then there are some games you buy because you'll remember them forever. This is the latter type, and well worth it on that account!10/10 Would get all my characters killed twice again.

I wanted to like this game and have found that a lot of people that originally played the demo liked it more, which is not a good thing in game development. I would have loved if once you were done with the levels you could make your own and post them for other people to try and solve, that one feature would have probably made the repetitive not diverse nature of the book feel more playable and you know that completing the book at least rewards you with more fun game play. _childDocuments_.review: This is my second review of Storyteller. I decided to delete the frist one, after revisting and invastigating the changes. This review was, like this, negative. To summarize it really quick so you get a feeling where I come from before heading down the to the newer points of critism i have.My initial run contained 1.6h and managed to beat everything the had to offer at the time and got rewared with 100% Achievements. With how much the games cost time became my biggest complained. I acknowledge the games qualities and noted that there is an update announced to add more content to the game. I remaind hopefull things would turn better and the game growing to an acceptable size of content. The update came and I missed the opportunity to play it. Timed passed and a friend of mine reminded me after purchasing the game herself that I wanted to revisit it. The Update itself brought a set of new levels and little mischiefivious touch to already played once. The old achievements have been removed and replaced by new ones. Although they still do exist within the game just not as a reward here on steam. Like the main game the new content is fun again. Sadly I managed to beat all new stuff within 30 minutes. Therefore bringing the game up to a little over 2h of playtime. With this my main complain remains. I understand that developing a game has its price. And I am willed to pay the price. But this game feels nothing like a teaser for more. After 2h I felt like playing prolog and now the real game starts with complex and long scenes making my brain go up in flames. But thats not the case. So feeling robbed this game is nothing more than wasted potential. There are two things here I wanna clarify or talk about that I noticed. Both matters are of the same type. Refunds. Steam has a refund policy. Allowing you to refund a game with 14 Days of aa purchase and with no more than 2h of playtime. Storyteller for the price they ask I wouldnt wonder that perhaps some refunded the game. Here comes my clarification. I would never. Although I am not satisfied with the game I finished it. I feel a refund applies to games that are unfinsished or unbeatable in terms of not entertaining enough by me. Like watching a movie in cinema. You cant just refund the movie ticket just because you didnt like the movie. Here comes the thing i noticed. They added an achievement to tackle this misbehaviour of others. There is an achievement that requires you to play the game for 2h. In case you want 100% Achievements in ledig way you need to keep the game. As willing I am not to refund and as much as I understand the devs wanna keep the money. I kinda have the feeling this is a little to much. It gives of the vibe that the devs rather than adding more content to one day justifying the price they choose a non consumer friendly way. Always a bad sign. Nonetheless I d like to point out again that the game itself is not terrible. In fact its good. Sadly it plays below its own potential. I wished for more and the perhaps final update didnt deliver. Only hope remaining is a sequel having more content to offer. I am willing to give Storyteller 2 a chance if its ever happen to be. Until then I wish all of you a good day.

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely fresh concept for a puzzle game. I could try to explain this game but its quite hard to do with text. Its best just to watch the first level on youtube to get the concept. If I had to explain: its a game where you get a prompt and you have to use your assets to recreate the prompt.That being said there is a lot going on trying to make those prompts. You can follow the prompts or make completely different story lines if you want to, those weird situations that you yourself create are incredibly interesting and fun. And beating some of the harder levels is also extremely satisfying. Its a really original and interesting concept and that alone would make me recommend this game. All of this is backed up with a fantastic art style and extremely clear UI design. Animations flow freely and its clear what is going on even if you make a couple of big changes to your story lineup. All in all its incredible.There are 2 problems however. The prompts aren't always extremely clear, there were a couple of times where I genuinely didn't understand what the game was asking of me. A big majority of the prompts are clear and interesting, but those like 3 or so confusing levels are quite frustrating. The reason they are so frustrating is because of the 2nd problem. The games length, all in all you can finish it in around 1 to 2 hours (Maybe 3 with achievements) without any real replay value or bonus challenges. In that length of time everything basically has to be perfect so those couple of bad levels really pop out when the game is this short. A workshop mode where players can create levels for the community would have been really appreciated, or even reusing the same levels and making more interesting prompts like they did for the achievements would also have been fantastic.If you can handle a games shortness then this is a really fun experience, if its worth 13 bucks is up to you. For me it was more then worth it. I enjoyed this more then I enjoyed some games that are 10 + hours long. The older I get the more I appreciate these kinds of original and quick fire games. If you go into it knowing that its short then I guarantee you will have a really enjoyable experience. Now to hope they release DLC or some free updates to expand even more on this incredible concept.

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about Storyteller but am going to fall on the "recommended" side for its creativity, unique puzzling experience, cute medieval-style art, and references to Sherlock Holmes, Edgar Allan Poe, Shakespeare, Game of Thrones and fairy tales. I got it on sale. As others have said, it's a short game. I found most puzzles incredibly easy, and a few that didn't make any sense to me at all. Very few puzzles were in the middle between those two extremes, but it was in the middle - with increased difficulty but clear objectives - that the sweet spot of enjoyment seemed to lie. I wanted more from this game. Not just more puzzles, but more variety. More characters, more scenes, more possible combinations, maybe some more comedy and less tragedy. It's a great idea for a game and they haven't gone anywhere near its full potential.After playing the whole game and only getting two achievements, I found out the remaining achievements really have nothing at all to do with anything that happens in the course of the game. The only way to actually get all of the achievements is to either find them accidentally, spend hours trying an infinite number of combinations, or to make a list of them and then go and play them as if they were new puzzles. That seems weird to me. In most games, achievements come during the course of gameplay - completing chapters, finding alternate solutions - not from random, unrelated things.UPDATE: Since writing this review, they've changed the achievements and added some new content. It's great stuff! I hope there's a Storyteller 2 someday.

_childDocuments_.review: is a short puzzle game with an emphasis on the player to craft stories, some romantic, some complex but overall charming. This is a game where you piece together puzzle elements to create the story. The game takes the form of a book in which you create the story panel by panel, much like a comic book. For each puzzle you're given a set of characters and are supposed to arrange them to fit a story of the title you're given. So there is no one story in this game but a variety of mini stories to tell divided up into chapters. The joy of this game is to play around with the characters by placing them in various panels to see what happens. Trial and error can be rewarding and entertaining. Some of the tales will be familiar to many. Love, betrayal and jealousy fuel many of the stories. Some are your classic fairy tales to stories of a Shakespearean nature such as Romeo & Juliet. The settings in this game are pretty straight forward and basic. You have audio level, language, fullscreen or windowed, quality and the ability to turn the narrator on or off. The pages of the book are yellowed and look washed out in contrast to the characters (who look like decals or stickers) and have more colouring to them. Once you drop the characters into a scene they will play an animation and those animations will vary depending on their placement in the story. The soundtrack sounds like something you would hear in a story about royalty and the narrator's voice is so well done. I kept the narrator on as I personally enjoyed his humour. * After completing the main levels go back through the chapters to play the Devil levels (the chapter level marked with a pentagram)* There are 31 bonus stamps to collect (for where to find these I suggest looking at one of many great community guides)* I played the whole game with a mouse but the game does support a controller. * To get the achievement for playing over two hours close the game and re-open it after the two hour mark for it to activate. I enjoyed this game. It is quite short so I suggest getting it on sale. But the animations and stories can be pretty funny and entertaining. It is a really different type of game and really can not compare it to anything else I have played. So the uniqueness was very refreshing. There are not a lot of achievements but they are obtainable without too much stress. The only one I don’t like is having to play for over two hours. It is obvious to me why that one is thrown in there for such a short game. Still it did take me close to two hours to actually finish the game (maybe a tad shy). So take that for what it is. Overall a fun game that brings something different to the table. 📖

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game for about 10 years. It is fun, but frankly I'm a bit disappointed. Some of this comes from features that were in previous publicly shown versions of the game which is a bit unfair, but it mostly comes from the size of the game. You can finish the entire game in well under two hours, and besides a few achievements, which you have to slowly navigate to a level they're even possible in, that's it.That, paired with a very slow to navigate UI for selecting levels which saps my desire to go back to them (Something like a "Table of contents" that lists chapters is needed so players can jump to the one they want without clicking through them sequentially), is the reasoning behind this review.I'll probably go back and play though the entire game again in some time, because it is a lot of fun and it's interesting to fiddle with it, but I can't recommend it for someone else to spend their money on.Update 1: Original review had 80 minuets at time of review as reference for the opinions stated above.I was going to change my review to positive after the devil update, I believe it added enough to the game with an enjoyable twist that kept things interesting for it to be a worth-while purchase (and re-added previous content as I complained about in my original review.) The other complaints I had at time of review still stand; I find the user experience very poor. Adding more achievements that are now in-game is nice (the reward is mainly seeing unique animations/screens), but does not change how annoying it is to navigate to where those achievements can be earned. The addition of the "Worth it" achievement is what stopped me from ever changing this review. The achievement is only for playing the game for 2 hours, the steam no-questions refund cutoff. This achievement both directly mocks the sentiment I stated in my original review (that the game lacked too much content and was too short to be "worth it", i.e. recommending others to pay money for), and is poorly implemented. At time of writing, I have over 2 hours of playtime but lack the achievement. Forcing any user who did enjoy and complete the game (and the update for some time after its release) to idle for two hours is poor by any metric. If the developer wants his game to be seen as worth buying and keeping by consumers, he must craft it into a state where they see it that way. Obviously some people will game the system, and I'm not endorsing that, but responding this way is not building goodwill.

But even then... there just isn't enough for the asking price. I got it on sale but for £10 it only gave me about an hour of content. Only one puzzle really stumped me. _childDocuments_.review: First review, cause this game feels very special. I finished the actual game in about 2 hours, with an additional hour to get the stamps, using a guide for which levels to use. The short time might be a turn-off for some, but I don't regret the purchase at all. The art style is distinct and charming, and it's a really unique puzzler. It was enjoyable to learn the pre-existing relationships between characters, their personalities, and how they interact with scenes, using all of this information to build the steps towards the goal.My only complaint stems from the UI, specifically navigating between chapters. There are tabs on the book to go between the chapters and the menus at the end; I was surprised that chapter tabs were not added as well. This isn't an issue going through the puzzles in order, but when you're paging through the chapters looking for the characters you need for a stamp, waiting for the page flip animation going through each of the ~15 chapters feels very slow. This is ultimately why I ended up using a guide to find which chapters could be used for which stamps. Another potential improvement would be an index at the end of the book, allowing you to quickly navigate to a story that contains a specific character or scene.That complaint aside, I really enjoyed this, and if a sequel or expansion were added, I would certainly buy it. Like any good puzzler, it leaves you craving more of the problems it was asking you to solve.
_childDocuments_.name: Storyteller

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, let me say this: This game is great, BUT I would like to put some criticism into it as well.Let me start with the pros:- The puzzles are challenging yet not too much to make it impossible.- The art style is neat, liked both the character and background designs- The BGM is a good assortment of recreated classical songs.- Essentially each level has some extra replay-ability (Do some random things with the characters like making a certain character drink wine to the point of addiction or something.Here's some cons though:- The price for this game is too high for its own good, I mean, I paid 20 bucks to get about 2 hours of game play (Some of that was because I was thinking for a solution for a puzzle.) If it was less than 10 dollars, then I wouldn't mind as much.- The game was too darn short. I mean I will admit, I am a fast gamer and puzzle solver, but before I knew it was getting difficult, it was over.- The lack of the jester hat challenges (From the demo) was kinda a missed opportunity, and yes, I know that some levels had bonus conditions, but it didn't feel the same. They weren't as bizarre or strange as the ones in the demo.- The puzzles themselves were too linear when it came to solutions, unlike the demo where you could find about 2 or more solutions for a single puzzle.- The end itself was anti-climatic, I don't want to spoil it, so let me tell you don't expect much after you get the crown in the  conclusion, this game gets 3/5 stars for me. 2 for being good while it lasted, and 1 for the concept.Maybe if this gets an update, or some DLC, I'll change my mind.My advice for getting this game? Wait until it's half off or close. It's fun. Just too short and too expensive for its size.Edit: They added an achievement for playing more than 2 hours. Wow.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game, it was a quirky little game that has definitely been through a lot in terms of development- I think 10-15 years of development is what I've heard and to my knowledge, it's hand-drawn. But regardless of that, I feel there isn't enough replay value and the game is pretty short.I can appreciate the artistry, but for $22.49 AUD, it doesn't really deliver. _childDocuments_.review: Storyteller is a charming, witty, but oft frustrating game that ends just as it's getting good. Even with the recent (Sept. 2023) update it's still just too short for the price of the game--even on sale.Pros: The art style and narration is perfect and was clearly made with a lot of though and care. I love how the character models change in response to the scene, such as old Edgar or sleeping Lenora. The game controls work well and are very responsive. It feels great when a puzzle is a literary references and you already know the solution. The extra challenges on some level are what I found most fun and I would have enjoyed more of these.Cons: Game length is huge issue. If it hadn't been for my completionist tendencies and the fact that the stamps don't seem to activate until you get the Crown, I probably could have 100% this game within the Steam return window.The devil content update I think would have been better as it's own chapter with more introduction to the content that one lone tutorial level. Backtracking to find the stages was irritating especially as I jumped around revisiting levels and I was stumped because I didn't fully understand the devil mechanics. I think just a little more structure could have really helped both these issues. I'm not sure if this was a bug or as intended, but Stamps didn't activate for me until after I got the Crown, which meant a lot of backtracking to find levels where I KNOW I completed certain challenges, which would activate as soon as I opened the level. This is especially frustrating since the game doesn't tell you what level can solve each stamp, requiring you to go back through every level manually and guess if I can complete the stamp.Some additional feedback, I think a Hint function could go a long way, even one with limited uses powered by how many levels you've completed. There were often times I needed a small nudge or had one wrong scene and would turn to a third-party guide out of frustration. Implementing a Hint function would allow players who want/need the help to get it without hindering players who are fine without.Ultimately, I feel that Storyteller is 70% of the way to the finish-line of making a really good game. I think that in a year's time, after additional content updates it will feel like a complete experience. But in it's current state I don't recommend unless HEAVILY on sale.

name: The Plucky Squire
detailed_description: The Plucky Squire follows the magical adventures of Jot and his friends - storybook characters who discover a three-dimensional world outside the pages of their book. When the malevolent Humgrump realizes he's the villain of the book - destined to lose his battle against the forces of good for all eternity - he kicks the heroic Jot out of its pages and changes the story forever. Jot must face challenges, unlike anything he's ever seen if he is to save his friends from Humgrump's dark forces and restore the book's happy ending. Jump between 2D and 3D worlds in this charming action-adventure - solving puzzles, boxing badgers, flying with a jetpack, and enjoying many more delightful and surprising mini-challenges as you become the hero of a living storybook.
