_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely charming!Everything in this adventure feels so well thought out, from the intuitive puzzle design, to the unique boss encounters, to the seamless transitions between 2D and 3D gameplay. The story are characters are wonderful, and the art style and storybook-like presentation carry everything so well. The length of the game feels very satisfying, with no extra padding trying to artificially extend it.As an adult, I totally love this game, and had I played it as a kid, I know I would've been absolutely obsessed.Ran into a couple minor glitches, but the autosaves are frequent, so never lost more than a minute of progress.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: A celebration of art in all of it's forms, The Plucky Squire is as much a homage to picture books and video games as it is to painting, writting, sculpting, it's ultimately a story about creativity.It is, however, a very, very casual adventure, filled with minigames and perspective changes at every turn to keep things interesting,  many of them homages to other games in the medium, all brought a smile to my face, but this means as a pond it is both incredibly wide and incredibly shallow, anyone expecting any depth in it will be disappointed, but I have to say I do not share the opinions of most reviews saying the puzzle were too easy and handholdy, I was stuck for a while in quite a few of them, not an hour or so, but definitely a reasonable amount to get the noggin joggin.If there is one thing I disliked though, it was the combat, namely how Jot has all kinds of different abilities he can purchase at the shop, but all of them deal less damage than just mashing the attack button, with enemies dropping health every second kill, mashing you way through combat is much more effective than actually trying to engage with the secondary skills. Combat can be easy and still engaging, see the decades of 3D Zeldas out there, but there is a structure to it, and this ain't it.The Plucky Squire won't set the world on fire with new ideas, but as a celebration of everything that came before and hope of what has yet to come, it is a good reminder of how fun videogames, and art in general, can be.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: Great game to introduce to someone who hasn't played a video game before under the age of 12. Children will definitely love this game, as for adults I feel like the difficulty could be said a bit higher, the many beards should have an option of appearing or not on first playthrough. Currently with the price, I feel like it should definitely have been set for $20 instead of 30.I would still recommend this game but wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty nice art style and story telling game kinda unique in it's own way with how you are progressing trough the book as you play the game. Gameplay and puzzles are pretty simple yet different every chapter you go. There is a hint option if you are stuck on a puzzle so you won't have to worry about looking up a guide just to progress. Few of collectibles are pretty well hidden and you will probably have to replay few chapters if you want to get everything 100%. The whole game took me around 9 hours to beat and the rest was finishing the rest of the achievements I had left. Pretty solid game for a fair price.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to love the game it is just a very slim experience. Beautiful art style but that's all the game is. I'm more than halfway through and feels like I've barely done anything. It has barely utilized the storybook to 3D world mechanic in any interesting way. When we've seen Zelda and Mario use this same technique in a much more innovative way it is disappointing that a game that is all about that mechanic to barely use it. The platforming is extremely simple, puzzles are more annoying to complete since they're so simple while the game hand holds you, and combat is barely there.This feels like just the demo of a game but instead is the full release.Also I've encountered several glitches that has forced me to reload from the nearest checkpoint which then can involve whole cutscenes or puzzles again.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to the plucky squire for a very long time and I would say that my expectations were definitely met. The game is creative, fun, and very surprising with tons of different types of mini games and fun mechanics to explore. The art style is super precious and the music really immerses you in the fantasy world of Jot. My only frustrations with this game would be that there are occasional bugs that you will come across. Some bugs that just require a restart, and some bugs that will soft lock you and stop your progression into the story (which i'm currently experiencing). Typically this would make me stop playing the game, but to find out what happens to Jot and his friends, I'd say it's worth the wait.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: The core of this game, clear to anyone who's seen a trailer, is of course a playable picturebook, with the amount of narrative and dialog you'd expect from that kind of medium. When it becomes interactive, the environments are contained within two pages, which lead to the next pages, so don't expect branching paths or an open world.The twist is that you can leave the book and explore the outside, 3 dimensional, world. The desk on which the book is lying is only slightly more open but mostly a space to obtain tools to manipulate the book from the outside, allowing for some innovative gameplay. Puzzles aren't terribly deep but feel fresh thanks to the varied gameplay both in and out of the book. As opposed to what you might have read elsewhere (Kotaku, cough), the dialog doesn't spoil any puzzles. But there are optional hints from a character named Minibeard.You don't travel alone and each character has their own unique gameplay. And depending on the occasion, the main character may adopt different playstyles as well. On the surface, it's a classic Zelda like but there are also rhythm, stealth, arcade puzzle, boxing and shooting elements to it so it's a mix of genres and a love letter to gaming calling back to its roots, and drawing innovation from the meta gameplay that contains all those varied elements.The execution of what the devs set out to do, with its whimsical art and writing, tight controls and polished gameplay, would be flawless if it weren't for some technical issues. Framerate is not as stable as one would hope and especially towards the end the rate at which you might encounter progress breaking bugs increases (hopefully this will be ironed out with patches). But the auto saves are pretty frequent so you can just quit and start again, without losing much progress. In the rare cases where you have to do stuff again, it will be much faster once you already know what to do.Being a UE4 game, this works with praydog's UEVR mod. I recommend to not set the decoupled pitch option (which usually is the first thing you want to do) so you don't have to look down at the book which is an awful strain to the neck. Both the frame rate (I reduced the quality setting from the default epic to low and render resolution to 80%) and some of the camera perspectives will test your VR legs so I don't recommend this as your first VR game. But if you can play it, the game's little big world really shines in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game thoroughly but the fact that it didn't let you do your own thinking and instead took your hand guiding you to everything was a bit underwhelming. Also I missed some scrolls and for some I have to replay the whole game with a new save, not good. It would be a good addition to indicate on which chapters you're missing a glitchbird because I really don't know where are the missing ones I've got left.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: I was hyped as ♥♥♥♥ for this game in the lead up (so much that I decided to drop the $30 on it day 1), but sadly that hype was too much and now I'm a little disappointed. Idk, it's charming and not bad, but it feels like a lot of other Indie games where it seems dope as hell but it's kind of just *shrugs*. Plucky Squire is mainly a Zelda-like (I guess?) that has 2D gameplay, and some 3D gameplay. It's all very serviceable and the main neat stuff this game does is the puzzles that revolve around "meta" stuff of books. You can swap *certain* words around to change a gate from "closed" to "open" (etc.). Or there are puzzles revolved around turning the pages or gravity affecting stuff in the book from tilting the pages. There are also quite a lot of gameplay changes from an early Punch-Out boss, to Super Bust-a-Move, to side scroll jetpack shooting, and a rhythm game too. These are fine and work, just feels like it spreads itself with all this.FINAL BOSS SPOILERS:The final boss reuses 3 of those minigames I mentioned and ♥♥♥♥ man I don't want to play Bust-a-Move or Punch Out! You didn't give me enough time to learn how to play Punch Out or Bust-a-Move! Don't make it the final boss! Thank god you can skip minigames and those count because I hated that ♥♥♥♥.FINAL BOSS SPOILERS OVER/Overall, this game is charming, has a beautiful 2D artstyle, and serviceable gameplay, but it is not really what I am left slightly disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: The Plucky Squire is such a breathe of fresh air, and with such an imaginative adventure that easily blends 2D and 3D gameplay. This game is a true standout to why you should invest more time in playing indie titles, because these developers have created an amazing game with such passion.The game's unique art style is very well done, both in 2D and 3D presence. The narrator does a nice job explaining the story of the hero of and his challenging journey with friends to take on many foes ahead.The gameplay is a perfect balance of challenging and rewarding. The puzzles don't overstay their welcome and offer a nice break between chapters. The pacing of the game overall is smooth as well, transitioning seamlessly through chapters of a book.The game runs very well, I haven't experienced any issues on my end, and the soundtrack compliments the vibrant world in a lovely way. Overall, this game is a clear love letter from the developers who have been working on this project for a long time. Be sure to support them as The Plucky Squire is an absolute gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: This is the perfect casual gaming experience that anyone will like. The story does not overstay it's welcome as the game is only 10 chapters. You do have two story options with 'adventure' and 'story' mode. Story mode is a very casual experience, adventure is a tad harder. Graphics are incredible and the transition between 2D and 3D is flawless and integrated in the game perfectly with the puzzles and collectibles. Puzzles are pretty simple, maybe a couple head scratches for a few minutes here and there. Collectibles are simple with artwork (50 to collect) and 'glitchbirds' (10 to collect). Some can be pretty hard to find, but it's fun. You do have a chapter replay once a chapter is beaten if you miss anything.Combat is super super simple. You have a few upgrades to have new combat moves and more damage, but it isn't anything too crazy. The bosses are where the game shines more and when the game evolves more into just your standard 'attack with a sword' game it's really fun.One of my favorite games of the year and can see myself playing it every once and awhile after initial completion.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I'm playing this on Steam Deck LCD. It runs smoothly. Love the artistic style and narrative story presentation of this game. My kids and wife enjoyed it also.I just wish it was a bit longer as I didn't want for it to end already. Also the boss mini games were you need to hit the things that the boss is throwing at you is a little bit lame, wish they added more mechanics into it, it gets old after a few fails.At first I was bit hesitant on buying it full price, was thinking of waiting for a sale. After watching a bunch of reviews online, decided to buy it already. It was worth every penny.  Overall, I highly recommend The Plucky Squire.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: This could have been a great game.  It is a very cool concept marred by poor design and bugs beyond belief.  It’s hard grasping the fact that a game this buggy passed Beta testing and quality control before its release.  The gameplay is overly simplistic and lacks any sort of challenge.  You are given two difficulty options - Adventure and Story modes.  Adventure mode is supposed to offer a challenge, but there is pretty much no challenge.  The auto hint system that is built into the game can’t be turned off, so you are pretty much guided by the hand throughout the game.  Instead of introducing new abilities or weapons and letting you figure out how to use them, the game tells you exactly what you need to use a weapon or ability on in order to progress.Next, the glitches and bugs are so bad that they, several times throughout the game, cause the game to freeze completely or slow down so much that you have to reboot your game system and restart from your last save.  This is utterly maddening.While not a $60 AAA title, this game is not worth its $30 price tag.  At best, it’s a bargain $10 game designed for five year olds.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this, I really did, but found out rather quickly after you are able to leave and re-enter the book that I'm just not having fun. Might be for some folks, but it's just not for me.The art direction is phenomenal, the game sounds amazing, the concept is unique and very inspired... but it's just not fun. Feels very slow and the start takes quite awhile to get through, combat is bland and doesn't offer much, and overall while the whole mechanic of being able to leave the book and manipulate the pages is really a great idea, the game fails to capitalize on this concept in a meaningful way beyond leave book -> move to different part of book -> enter book again. On top of this the game feels the need to stop you in your tracks to toss dialogue at you almost constantly grinding the flow to a total standstill.Wish it brought more to the table but what is here just isn't fun enough for me to want to keep going.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: Aesthetic and concept are cool. But, that concept isn't explored at all beyond the story book and kid's desk. All other usages boil down to minigames that are uninspired at best, and mostly tedious. The combat has nothing to it. The only useful upgrade is the sword throw, which trivializes most fights. The puzzles could be interesting, if the game didn't have extreme railroading and spoil area solutions upon entry. Hell, I started looking away from the screen during dialog in hopes of getting some small sense of discovery. There are some mechanics with the book that could be interesting, but they're never really explored or combined beyond their initial introduction. Confusingly, the final boss uses none of these mechanics and is just a boring collection of reused mini-games. The game is extremely linear with very little exploration. Even within that linearity, the flow of the game is constant interrupted due to unimportant/uninteresting dialogue.I also have to mention that I experienced a few bugs. Nothing that really ruined the experience, but there were 3-4 times where I had to reload the game and lose progress due to being soft-locked. I finished it because the art team clearly put a lot of love into this game and I hoped it would get better. But, I'm walking away with a bad taste in my mouth and I regret spending $30 on it. That being said, I expected a cozy Zelda-like with unique art style. I now realize that this game may be intended solely for kids. If that's true, then I'm not the target audience. But I still can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: The Plucky Squire is a charming, fun indie game that brings a fresh twist to platformers with its seamless blend of 2D and 3D gameplay! It's like a playful mix of classic Mario mechanics with some extra flair, and the transitions between perspectives keep things exciting. The visuals are adorable, and the level design is creative, making it easy to get lost in its cute, vibrant world.That said, while the story is sweet, it doesn’t dig too deep—it’s more about the adventure and gameplay here. If you're a fan of indie gems that offer unique twists on familiar mechanics, this one’s a must-play. We need more games like The Plucky Squire.

_childDocuments_.review: In spite of the stellar art direction I cannot recommend the games:- it takes controls away from the player all the time - it is very restrictive, even disabling tools for no reason half of the time- it has a lot of softlock glitches. I wanted to finish the game but after 4 softlocks that forced me to reload a chapter I don't care anymore.This is my first negative evaluation on steam. _childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely stunning, a real technical achievement in blending 2D and 3D so seamlessly. The trailer captivated me, and I was genuinely excited to dive in.The gameplay itself is decent—nothing groundbreaking, but that's not necessarily a flaw. There's a good variety of modes that kept things interesting and fun when I was actually allowed to play.  Unfortunately, the game seems determined to pull control away every 1-2 minutes, forcing you to sit through cutscenes or dialogue that feel endless. I don’t mind a good cutscene, but when they’re this frequent, and the characters or story lack depth, it becomes tedious. I play games for the interactivity, not to sit through endless exposition.The game doesn’t trust the player to figure things out, constantly hand-holding through every new mechanic. This kills the joy of discovery, leaving little room for the player to explore or uncover secrets on their own. A bit more freedom and faith in the player’s ability would’ve made this a far more enjoyable experience.It’s disappointing to say, but I can’t recommend this beautiful game despite its immense potential.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: This game felt like it was made for eight years old children. I don't know if it was intentional or accidental.The non stop narrator comments with drawing mini cutscenes butcher the entire dynamic and flow and you just start to yawn.The first boss fight felt very boring and repetitive, you do the same actions for too long, no cliffhangers or unexpected mechanic changes.Audio design felt weak, the music is too cute and childish while sound effects constantly missed opportunities to make funny gags.It felt like those generic TV cartoons which little children watch all day.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: The Plucky Squire is a charming action-adventure game with a lot of potential, though it falls short in a few areas. The 2D sections are beautifully designed with clean, vibrant graphics, making them an absolute delight. However, the 3D segments feel somewhat generic, resembling a typical platformer. The game is highly linear, with only one solution to each puzzle, and often feels too hand-holdy as NPCs and camera cues frequently provide hints unprompted.While the puzzles, such as those involving words to alter the story, are creative, they are quite simple and designed for a younger audience. The game features various minigames and cool ideas that don’t overstay their welcome, but the low difficulty level means that combat can often be solved by simply swinging your weapon, making the upgrades feel largely unnecessary. Upgrades feel underwhelming, mostly offering two special attacks and basic damage boosts, which don't add much variety.In terms of accessibility, The Plucky Squire shines with options like jump assists and invincibility, and even lets you skip some minigames if they are too hard. The story largely feels predictable and underwhelming... up untill the like last third of the game. Then finally it gets more interesting and even gameplay gets somewheat challenging. However, The Plucky Squire has no dialogue or scene skip, making replaying for collectibles a chore.Ultimately, The Plucky Squire is filled with style but lacks the substance to fully deliver on its ambitious ideas. It’s a fun, family-friendly experience, but might leave some older players wanting more complexity. Worth playing, but perhaps at a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: Visually the game is stunning, no complaints there, but the game play is very lacking. Puzzles are incredibly easy and combat might as well be non-existent, you can spam attack and are almost always guaranteed a health drop. I was hoping for there to be more minigames to pad out the game play, but they are few and far between.Overall, i liked what i saw on screen, it just bored me by the second hour. I'd definitely recommend this game to those with small kids.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: Frustratingly mediocre and less than the sum of its parts. I had been hoping for something halfway between Supraland and Evoland; playing with the physicality of the storybook and the desk with a few cute motifs of other games and genres for variety. The Plucky Squire hits those notes occasionally, but most of the time it's extremely trite puzzles that are both fiddly and simple, and with a variety of NPCs that shout out the answer before you get the opportunity to even look at the puzzle. The presentation and structure speaks to a lack of confidence in the game, as barely a moment goes by without a reference to another piece of media to distract from the token combat and platforming. The game is also incredibly short, only a few hours long but still feeling padded with repeated puzzles and slowly dragging carried objects from area to area.This game had a lot of potential but every mechanical gimmick and every story beat was already done better in Chicory, and the base gameplay was perfected 30 years ago in A Link to the Past. There's nothing here that you haven't seen before, and the gestalt feels cheap rather than celebratory.Edit: I somehow forgot to mention the incessant softlocks and glitches. Catching on geometry, puzzles not uniformly acknowledging completion, unclear objectives, and seams between map tiles causing ugly pixel gaps.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: Was pretty hyped for this game overall but with the amount of softlocks I experienced and had to troubleshoot I’d say wait until it’s updated and fixed or on sale. Overall ok story, pretty creative and I love the art style but the amount of softlocks and bugs I had to deal with completely killed any momentum it had going for it while playing.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute and charming game clearly made with a lot of heart and passion. I absolutely loved the mixed media look, how styles wouldn't match but the game would blend them, it was so fun! It's definitely a game intended to be easy for kids to play, there's next to no challenge here and minigames are skippable if you want to. If you're looking for a visual treat and about 10 hours of enjoyable story, or if you have young children who want something cute to play, definitely pick it up (maybe on sale)
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review: The Plucky Squire is one of the best indie games of 2024.I followed the game's development since its reveal and having played through the game, it is exactly what I expected - a wonderful and joyful adventure that took me back to a much simpler time.The art style was something that I was immediately drawn to. I was concerned that the game would be all style but no substance but that turned out to be not the case at all. The gameplay variety is something that can easily last for another playthrough - there is plenty of combat, puzzles, minigames and collectibles to keep you busy. The presentation, again, is fantastic to look at and a joy to experience. Jumping between the painted storybook and the 3D world is not only creative but pretty memorable.The game launched with a few frustrating technical issues and bugs but some of them have already been addressed. I just wished though that we wouldn't have to fiddle with some outside software to cap the framerate - because of this, screen tearing was an issue that affected the game's presentation but overall, I didn't mind it too much.Nevertheless, the Plucky Squire easily earns my wholehearted recommendation even at full price!
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

_childDocuments_.review:
The Plucky Squire follows the magical adventures of Jot and his friends - storybook characters who discover a three-dimensional world outside the pages of their book.

When the malevolent Humgrump realises he's the villain of the book - destined to lose his battle against the forces of good for all eternity - he kicks the heroic Jot out of its pages and changes the story forever.

Jot must face challenges unlike anything he's ever seen if he is to save his friends from Humgrump's dark forces and restore the book's happy ending.

Jump between 2D and 3D worlds in this charming action adventure - solving puzzles, boxing badgers, flying with a jetpack, and enjoying many more delightful and surprising mini challenges as you become the hero of a living storybook.
_childDocuments_.name: The Plucky Squire

name: Lies of P
detailed_description: You are a puppet created by Geppetto who’s caught in a web of lies with unimaginable monsters and untrustworthy figures standing between you and the events that have befallen the world of Lies of P. You are awakened by a mysterious voice that guides you through the plagued city of Krat - a once lively place that has been poisoned by madness and bloodlust. In our soulslike, you must adapt yourself and your weapons to face untold horrors, untangle the unfathomable secrets of the city's elites and choose whether to confront predicaments with the truth or weave lies to overcome them on the journey to find yourself. ・ A DARKLY ELEGANT AND CRUEL WORLD Unearth the secrets of the city of Krat – a place soaked in the style of the Belle Epoque era which once thrived due to its puppet industry and now sees its streets covered in blood. ・BATTLE WITH TWISTED INSTRUMENTS Develop a unique combat style to counter vicious enemies and terrain by weaving together dynamic weapon combinations, utilizing the Legion Arms, and activating new abilities. ・WHAT’S IN A LIE? There will be times when you will be confronted with choices where you can give comfort to others in sorrow or despair by lying…or you can choose to tell the truth. Carve your own path. ・A CLASSIC REIMAGINED Experience the beloved fairy tale of Pinocchio reinterpreted as a dark, grim narrative that allows players to discover the secrets and symbols hidden within the world of Lies of P.

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is definitely not a game for everyone. You will repeatedly die, that's to be expected and intended so I don't fault the game for being difficult. That's by design.(-) Negatives- The flow to combat doesn't feel completely engaging and fun to me. It feels too much like it wants to be the same and yet differentiate itself from its inspiration simultaneously. Overall for myself the combat didn't have the best flow and I felt as though there was never an actual satisfaction when toppling a challenge. It's peculiar to put it this way, but the combat felt sloppy and generally inconvenient. Since the combat is arguably suppose to be the most engaging thing, it missed the mark immensely. Again though, this is just my opinion. Even after finishing the game I was happier to close the book on this game as oppose to playing again. I'm not the biggest fan of the mid combo delayed attacks. You get used to them but the rhythm felt awkward on my end. I would say this game has delayed attacks in excess, so if you aren't able to wrap your head around that you may have a particularly difficult time. Just don't smash the guard button. Actually take the time to figure out timing as frustrating as that can be at times.- One of the biggest issues you will see online and I wholeheartedly agree is that the game is way too linear for it's own good. You will pretty much always be on the path to progression which some people may like, but it's incredibly on rails the whole way start to finish.(People screech about this opinion, but if you want to play a "parry game" then play Sekiro. I would argue the world traversal and combat are so well crafted that it was overall satisfying and a joy to play multiple times. Yes, that game is marginally easier. That could be because the parry/combat flow feel so smooth for myself).(+) Positives- Genuinely found this world to be intriguing and I was interested in the lore and story as I progress. This was arguably the one thing that motivated me to actually make it to the end. I was satisfied and I'm curious as to how they intend to continue with what unfold in the true ending. - Graphically the game is phenomenal and it runs flawlessly on my end (My setup is pretty strong so there lies my bias)-Each area looked amazing and were presented spectacularly.- Enemy design was fairly good. Some could have easily been improved upon, but expect the bosses to have had the most attention to detail. Normal mobs will have slight variances.

_childDocuments_.review: So first of all, the premise is interesting. This incarnation of Pinocchio is unironically very fitting for a souls-like. The setting with puppets, humans and monsters has everything you need. There is even room to explore Pinocchio and all the side npcs as characters. The level of quality on display was a surprise at first, but very soon I realised how truly great this game is. The reason it was a surprise is because my first thoughts were  “baby’s first sekiro and bloodborne”. Which isn’t technically wrong, but the way they used the formula, their own ideas and this semi-original setting elevated it to the level of some of the best souls-likes ever made. If the Nioh games didn’t exist, Lies of P would’ve taken a spot on my list of top 3, next to DS1 and Sekiro. It’s just that good. Having a clever idea is one thing, but high level of execution is what matters the most. The weapon assembling system is genius. Not only is it a perfect fit for the puppet theme, it’s one of the best weapon systems I’ve ever encountered so far. Matching different tops and handles is interesting. They get different moves and ranges, but you don’t lose resources. This system encourages experimentation, because disassembling and reassembling weapons costs you nothing. Only upgrading the top changes the raw damage output. Altering the handle lets you change how from which stats it starts scaling. Incredibly versatile. You receive plenty of resources to try as many builds and approaches as you like.I love it when a game uses the setting and theme creatively. It makes a lot of sense that Pinocchio, a puppet, would be able to fight all these huge robots and monsters. It also explains why he can withstand all the horrific stuff that happens to him. The narrative of a puppet becoming human is handled pretty well thanks to the out-of-combat mechanics. The lying/telling the truth system is simple, but gets the job done and there’s enough good storytelling and dialogue to make up for it. Sharpening your weapon with your mechanical arm? Really damn cool. It’s seems like a minor thing, but it really adds to the puppet theme. The problem is that it replenishes durability instead of sharpness, which a whetstone wouldn’t do technically, but it’s a minor nitpick. The music is great. Even just listening to the Phonograph/gramophone in the Hotel feels novel. Partially because of the atmosphere and partially because of the music choice. The records you play there are usually linked to specific characters you meet, so there’s an additional layer of story and immersion. It’s not without flaws of course. Two that spring to mind are the Door Guardian boss and the seemingly random boss difficulty. The boss difficulty one is puzzling, because the game is very linear. You go from A to B to C, so the randomness is strange. I’ve killed at least 4 bosses on my first try while being 100% sure that the boss was about to go into phase 2. Then suddenly the achievement for killing it pops up and it’s over. They were still fun fights, but some bosses are just far easier than others. Walker, Green Monster and Victor all happen after King of Puppets, but KoP was trickier than all 3 of those by far. The lightning lady seems way harder than the last two bosses.Only one boss is just plain bad and that’s the Door Guardian. He’s just a stupid gimmick boss that dies in seconds when you figure out what the trick is, but the trick is dumb. He’s not even original design-wise, he’s a reused Victor model with a crystal hand. I have enough reason to believe that this game is actually great and not just another souls-like clone. But most importantly, you can wear a mask of a german shepherd dog, which I thought was very amusing. Who cares about being a real boy, when you can be the goodest boy?

_childDocuments_.review: A very good souls-like! It's clear the developers put a lot of heart and hard work into this.Perfect Guard (a.k.a. perfect parry) system constantly had me saying "I think I could play Sekiro now!" followed soon after by "No way I'm ready for Sekiro!". Loop and repeat.Also, if you want to get through the game for the story but are stuck on a boss and wanting to solo it, here is my suggestion. Learn how to save a copy of the game files in a folder, and do this before facing every boss. That way you can use a specter to help and continue the story, but if you really think you have what it takes to solo it, reload the save at your leisure at a later date and you'll have the exact same stats as when you first attempted it. This also is a good way to keep a backup of your files if something goes horribly wrong with your save.

_childDocuments_.review: The masterpiece of souls genre. Better than any of ds1-3 in most aspects.Pros:-Great bossfigts. Well balanced stat-wise. All attacks are well telegraphed. You have both parry(or just block) and dodge roll as your defense mechanics and even simply walking and all of them work and the game encourages you to pick particular answer to emeny's move but doesn't force you, it is just easier to catch the timing with parry or dodge depending on the move or just positioning yourself properly to avoid being hit with a combo. There are tools to cheese through hard sections if you want to, especially on NG+. No bs attack animations like in elden ring - it is easy to understand when the attack is going to hit you.-Actual story, not a pile of random lore-No attrition runs. The game doesn't throw multiple elite enemies at you until the very final chapter. There is only one annoying platfroming stage in the entire game.-More fluid combat than in souls series as in less recovery frames from dodges and attacks.Cons:-Not much exploration. Levels are not just straight tunnels but rather linear. Though this turns into advantage on NG+ when you just want to hit the bosses.-Rather short, probably shorter than any game of souls franchise. But part of that due to rather easy levels.-Can't really recommend as entry point to souls games. It is quite hard to get overleveled and tone down difficulty by exploring. And some of the bosses are really hard (but fair so you may just get good).

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic in every way. Best Soulsborne I've played, mechanically, outside of an actual FromSoft title. Story wise, Lies of P is a beautiful mix of Bloodborne and Mega Man X. _childDocuments_.review: Overall, I would only recommend it if you really really like souls-like games.The graphics and the art direction are great. The characters are likeable and the story is intriguing, but the combat system can be frustrating at times.I still like this game and might even try out NG+, but I also want to rant about some of the decisions they made for the combat system lol. - The stagger system: I don't understand why they make you do a heavy attack for the enemy to enter a staggered state. To reach the stagger-able phase, you need to do a bunch of perfect block and heavy attacks already. Naturally, the reward is to be able to deal that critical hit, but no, you have to then perform a heavy attack in a short time window to get that reward. The enemy keeps on attacking during that stagger-able phase as well, so even if you do everything perfectly, there's still a good chance that you just cannot get that critical hit. It's very unsatisfying to say the least.- The camera: The Archbishop fight alone makes me want to list this. When the boss is huge, sometimes you can't see anything if you are near a wall or too close to the boss. The Archbishop fight is especially bad b/c he has attacks that can force you into those situations.- Level up: Just let me do it at the stargazers please...- Overall:The game has very good level design and art direction. I don't think anything is super unreasonable. However some of the mechanics just takes away a lot of the excitement and fun you get from this types of games. I would recommend it if you love souls like game.Edit:Finished the game and I'm half way through NG+. I have to say it's more fun in NG+ especially when I got that twin dragon sword. Parrying boss with that sword's charged attack is so satisfying. I do find the late game story to fall flat mainly because I cannot understand the villain's motivation at all.The last three boss have very cool designs. The camera angle is still an issue, but I got used to it so it felt less painful than the Archbishop. The last three fights require a lot of concentration. I was so focused on parrying and attacking at the right opening, I didn't even notice that I beat them by the end...It felt like they should still have half of their heath bar lol. It's hard to say if that was a good experience or not....I enjoyed learning the moves but didn't feel much when I beat them which is wired.

_childDocuments_.review: In a shocking turn of events, with this purchase I paid money for a game, and I got a game. Crazy, I know. Full game, no micro transactions, no DLC, no day one patches, no micro stutters, no bugs to polish, no unfinished gameplay elements...a full game. What a crazy concept!Even on my now very aged computer (RTX2060/6700k/16gb ram) it runs absolutely flawlessly. Not a single frame drop, maxed out graphics at 1440P, not even DLSS needed, locked 60 FPS. It looks amazing, has a fantastic atmosphere and is great fun.Apart from the worldbuilding, there's not much new here. If you've played Sekiro and Bloodborne, you know exactly what you're going to get. This is perfect to me, but might not be for you. Personally I find the game a bit too easy, but some people find it very hard - again, your mileage may vary. Consider I've finished Sekiro / Bloodborne / DS1&3 up to max scaling NG7+ solo without any summoning, so lots of experience. There's a big emphasis on perfect parries. I mean big. You will not get through with blocks and dodges. If you're used to DS / Elden Ring type gameplay you might have to readjust quite a bit.The only minus I can give to this game is occasional texture pop-in. Otherwise this is the best release of this year for me. Needless to say, I highly recommend it, especially if you enjoyed Sekiro.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good gameplay (it better be, considering they took Sekiro, Bloodborne, and Elden Ring and mashed them into one). Boss fights that range in quality from pretty good to incredible. Solid level design, reasonable difficulty, enjoyable world/lore/characters. Surprisingly enjoyable story (you also don't have to watch a Vaati video to understand it). Soundtrack is good as well. I'd say the game is highly replayable, but mileage may vary. Everything "new" this game does it does well (that being said, it doesn't innovate too much). The game is linear, and a lot of enemies have really nasty delay attacks, so if you hate either of those things you probably won't like this game. It also has slight variations in damage when you attack (you can roll -10% - +10%) for God only knows what reason. It's not really noticeable except for when a trash mob sometimes takes one more hit. The voice acting is also questionable at times (never down-right awful, but it's definitely noticeable). I also don't care about voice acting in games, but it is worth mentioning (only played in English). There are also a few instances in both text and voice-acting where I'm not really sure if things were translated to English as well as they could have been. The final area of the game could also be cut in half and it'd probably be more enjoyable. It's clear actual effort and possibly love went into this game, and it's not just some slop trying to cash-in on the recent "soulslike" trend.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 gameGreat combat, runs super smoothly, gorgeous graphics and pretty great voice acting too. Good not be glazing more for this game. Only issues are some corpse runs here and there, and a few difficulty jumps. If you're new to soulslike games, learn to parry as early in the game as you can. This games bosses have a great mix of mechanical and organic designs that actually makes them more interesting as you continue to play. Favorite boss is the third boss and then the second to last. Hope you have fun playing if you decide to pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want an idea of what this game is, yes it's a souls-like. There's no dodging the inspiration here because the devs wear it on their sleeves, but do not be mistaken and lump this in with the many mediocre titles emulating Fromsoft's designs. This is an absolutely stunning experience front to back, packed with an engaging gameplay loop and story (It's not *just* Pinocchio). There are some difficulty spikes, but where many games make you feel like you're just not doing enough, Lies of P really emphasizes the parry. This is a much more linear experience than Dark Souls or Elden Ring, and feels more like a cross between Sekiro and Bloodborne, and who could ask for more.This game is lacking in a little more creative level design, not that the art direction isn't gushing with creativity. I just wish alternative paths felt a little more deep and rewarding than a chest at the end of an optional hallway. Besides that the music, weapons, bosses, and characters were all killer. Don't miss out on this gem.

_childDocuments_.review: As a total newcomer to the entire genre of Souls games, I was a little intimidated by the idea of this game being too difficult for me to beat given the reputation of the genre. I decided to stick through it anyway because the setting seemed intriguing, and was blown away by the highly polished atmosphere, story, and gameplay.The combat is tight, but after some patience and practise I got the hang of the perfect parry mechanic and the back-and-forth dance of combat and flew through the game. Some bosses took me longer than others, but I didn't feel that any were unfair, and even as a newcomer I managed to beat the majority of them within what I felt was a reasonable amount of tries--with no use of spectres/throwables for my run.For the first time in my life I actually want to do a NG+ (and maybe a NG++) run to see all the endings and try out new weapons and builds, and I'm super excited to see what the DLC will bring as well. The devs seem to be really passionate and listen to their community well and I'm looking forward to seeing what other games they put out in the future.Aside from Lies of P, my only other experience in the genre is a dip into Elden Ring, which I didn't finish... but I plan to go back to complete it and try out FromSoft's other titles with the newfound confidence beating Lies of P has given me.Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: So, I originally wrote a review after giving up at 30 hours in. As can be seen I have put in a few more hours, and I want to be fair in my review... I stand by that I do not recommend this game, but that does not mean it's a bad game.It's a good game. It's a very good game. It is solid. Nothing about it feels sloppy or rushed. Great care was taken to design this game. It's actually mind boggling in some sense how good it is. It's a fun concept. It's got great graphics. It has solid gameplay. It has way more variety in terms of weapons and skills. It's easily one of the best games ever made.However, I still stand by what I originally said: A lot of Soulslike type games, including Dark Souls 3 and Elden Ring have the attitude of "Hard is what gamers want, so let's punish them", but there comes a point when some of these games just get too hard. Dark Souls 3 was borderline too hard, but a lot of the "too hard" bosses in that game were optional, and Elden Ring at least had easy mode options available through summoning. Lies of P is simply just "too hard".To put things  in perspective, I started  out this game thinking, "I'm going to try to do this game on my own. I'm not going to use summoning." Then I got to what I think was the fourth boss, and I spent an hour memorizing every move in both phases until I finally got it, and that's when I was done with the game. I was not interested in spending an hour to  learn the next boss so I tried once or twice then used the summon. It got to the point where if a summon was available on a boss I used it without even one try. I suppose that was my downfall because eventually I got to the point where I had no skills and the summon wasn't good enough to help on it's own, and at that point I said screw it, "I hate this game, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone," and then I wrote this review. (By the way, every boss is hard, there are never any pushover bosses like Pinwheel to add some pacing to the game.) Realistically most people that play this are going to spend about half an hour exploring a cool map, having fun, then an hour or more trying to get through the area's boss fight. Or they will summon. If that seems fun to you then you might enjoy it.What bugs me is... The game has cool level design that is fun to explore, and it has a cool premise, but it is ruined by these ridiculously difficult boss fights, and to be clear they are all ridiculous. No one ever beat any boss in this game on the first try, and if they said they did they either watched a bunch of videos on how to do it first, or they are lying. Certainly no one playing this game blindly, as I did, got them. (Or they summoned. I got one boss on the first try because I summoned on the first try.)In conclusion, it's sad, but the game is just too hard, even with the supposed easy mode of summoning, so I can't recommend it. At least if you are interested in completing it. If you don't actually complete games you play you might enjoy it until it gets too hard, at which point you can move on.I should mention that this game also has the Dark Souls problem that you can't really experiment with weapons because once you pick  a weapon to upgrade you are pretty much stuck with  it because upgrade materials are rare.I made it 30 hours without looking anything up, but I'm at my wits end so I'm absolutely going to look up what to do from here on out, and what type of build to use, and maybe I'll change my tune on  not recommending this, but I doubt it.Thus ends my original review. I wrote that before defeating Laxasia. So there were basically three more bosses to go after that. Believe me, I summoned. I made it as easy as possible for myself and it still wasn't "easy."Then came... The Nameless Puppet. And I was thinking, I stand by my review.  Well I watched a bunch of supposed "cheese" methods to defeating it. All of those "cheese" methods were lies. Lies about Lies of P. There is no cheese to defeat the Nameless Puppet. None whatsoever. The answer is the old cliche of "Git Gud". That's it. I have to admit that to defeat the nameless puppet, I didn't really "Git Gud" but I "Got Okay". I flippin' learned to do perfect guards on that thing. A skill I had spent the whole game avoiding. I spent 6 hours on that thing just to practice perfect guarding. That kind of helped, but then I had to watch another video of how to defeat that  puppet and then another 3 hours later I defeated that thing. I honestly feel like a lot of it was luck. Just lucky that it did moves that I was better at perfect guarding or dodging. I'm pretty sure if I tried to defeat it again it would be another 2-3 hours to get lucky enough. Who knows though.I don't think I'll be playing New Game Plus. The idea of the game being harder than it already was is something I'm not interested in dealing with. Sure I'd like to go through and do all the things I missed the first time around, but I don't think it's worth the frustration.So, yeah, if you like self torture, play the game. If not, don't. Also I suppose if you are "gud" then you might do okay with the game as well. But if you are like me and games make you throw temper tantrums, do not play this game. (Speaking of which, throwing temper trantrums didn't help. That's one thing I stopped doing to defeat the Nameless Puppet, it's a bad habit that you can develop in the game that is going to seriously hold you back.)

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually write reviews, but I enjoyed myself so much playing this game that ultimately it would be a disservice if I didn't express my feelings about it. Lies of P is, arguably, the best non-FromSoft Soulslike game you can play right now. It takes many of the aspects that make the Souls series great and utilizes them in a way that not only feels original and fresh, but is also immensely fun. The combat is sufficiently different from both Dark Souls and Bloodborne to be its own thing, but it's refined in such a way that longtime fans will feel right at home once they get used to the gameplay loop.Similar to Bloodborne, the game has a roster of consistently great weapons with unique movesets and special abilities each, and while I didn't really experiment with it, the player is free to switch the different parts to alter both the weapon scaling and moveset. Most of the boss fights require you to try and parry the boss attacks to throw them off balance and hopefully break their weapons so their overall damage is reduced. While this was perfectly fine for me, it should be noted that you'll need to learn at least the basics of parrying for the more difficult (or outright impossible) to dodge attacks.The game looks amazing, and something rare in our modern gaming era, it also  amazing. With all graphic settings on high, I don't think the game ever went below 100 fps which is incredible considering just how good it looks. As for the story, some will be pleased to know you won't need to read 100 item descriptions and watch 4 hours of lore videos to decipher it, but rather it's perfectly understandable even in a single playthrough; while it's no masterpiece, it's serviceable enough to keep the player interested through the 30 or so hours they'll take to beat the game.Overall, Lies of P is not only a big love letter to the Souls series but also an amazing original product that is able to stand on its own, and I strongly recommend it to anyone who likes Action RPGs and challenging games.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the hardest souls like game that I have ever played, including all of the souls series. I would highly recommend. This game is a total love letter to the whole soulsborne series and it shows. I thoroughly enjoyed my experience with this game.Pros-Boss fights are fun and memorable (except for probably two of them) -Great combat system and very stylish as well as engaging-Story and atmosphere are on point-Level design is on par with the rest of the souls series.-Music is killer-Has a lot of quality of life things that should be standard in all upcoming souls games-The overall pacing is fantastic-Performance is great! Nice to see a modern PC release not have BS performance issue (All of Jedi Survivor, Dead Space Remake cut scenes and stuttering, and the entirety of The Callisto Protocol)Cons-The way the belt system works is awful. The lack of any hold to go to first slot function is absolutely unforgivable(The souls series wasn't best but I would argue after DS3 and Elden RIng there is not excuse.)-Weapon Durability - This might be controversial, but I am not sure. Besides applying buffs to your weapon, the entire durability mechanic was either negligible or downright aggravating, I absolutely despise having to repair my weapons in the middle of the fight. I know that there are rings and items to help, but if you have jump through so many hoops to mitigate or complete remove it than why even have it. Completely useless mechanic in my opinion. * Cries whilst having DS2 durability bug PTSDOverall I would recommend this to any souls veteran whether they be casual or super hardcore into the series. It's really nice to finally see a true souls like experience that is on par with its influences and in some ways better. I would not recommend to new players who have no experience in any of the games, Obviously I'd recommend new players playing one or two the souls series games, especially Bloodborne.Congratulations on the team that made this game possible. Can't wait to see what they put out next.My super biased and subjective rating if it was worth anything, would be 9 Ergos out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent! At first I merely liked the game, but the longer I went, the more deep, interesting, and emotionally charged it revealed itself to be.Lies of P takes a lot of cues from Bloodborne and some from Sekiro, and it's a great addition to its genre. Apparently some people say it's harder than Elden Ring, but I didn't find that to be the case. By building a character with strong health and armor for my first playthrough, I gave myself enough room for mistakes that I actually overcame many of its challenges in about 1 to 3 tries. But I don't consider that a bad thing; it felt intense in the moment all the same! In the few spots where I did need more tries than that, I was late enough in the game that I had lots of different weapons and other tools to try new approaches with.It's true what you may have heard about the English translation being imperfect, but it's a minor thing, more on the level of "that's not quite the right tone and diction for a history book" than actually being difficult to understand. The voiced lines tend to sound more sensible than the written text, and the performances are solid!The smallness of my nitpicks with Lies of P are a testament to how good it is. One is that the enemy variety and environmental detail are a little bit sparse compared to From Software's works, and I do mean only a little. Another is that the enemy attack animations are harder to read than I'm used to in Elden Ring and Sekiro, so it can be tricky to get perfect parries until you study the enemies for a while. Even so, I suspect it's intentional that perfectly blocking everything the first time you see it is hard, and I probably wasn't much better at it my first time through Sekiro.The lore and story leave some things unsaid but aren't as shrouded in mystery as, say, Dark Souls. For me, it's just right!Anyway, if you're a fan of the Souls-like genre, this one's definitely worth a try!(It says a controller is recommended, but if you grew up on mouse and keyboard like me, don't worry, mouse and keyboard are perfectly fine.)

_childDocuments_.review: A different take on Pinocchio, where you play as P. Its a 3rd person action game(Classified as soulslike).Compared to other soulslike and fromsoft games, this game has its own unique identity.Unique FeaturesYou can mix and match weapon movesets and blades, with the fact you only need to upgrade the "blade" it makes it easy to test other handle and movesets.Guarding enemy attacks causes chip damage that can be recovered by attacking(like bloodborne). Perfect blocking causes stagger damage.A "upgrade" tree in addition to your stats, allowing you to modify your playstyle.(Such as dodge orientated or block focused), as well as the legion arm equipment, allowing for unique moves(Like a exploding shield or grabbing arm)While the game is linear, the map itself uses clever shortcuts such that your starting position never change, bvut by unlocking doors you can take shortcuts. The maps on the other hand is disjointed, which I guess is to be expected when you need long corridors.Enemys are tough but fair, with recent balance patches balancing things out.

The setting is really well done the city of Krat is beautiful and feels like its from the early 1900's with a bit of a fantasy feel.As for issues I had with the game the were all incredibly minor as far as problems go no real big bugs or issues encountered so you're good on that side.If our thinking about getting the game and are experienced in souls likes, and usually play a more melee oriented play-style lies of p is a fantastic and I can;'t recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: If I had to describe  with one word - it would definitely be . Every decision the devs made leads to a remarkably unpleasant experience. In all honesty, I can  recommend this game either to the fans of soulslike genre or to the newcomers. If you want a game with deflects just play Sekiro, it's much better.Here's a more comprehensive list of issues (and some good parts) about this game: The game looks quite good and can stand toe to toe with other 2023 releases in terms of graphical fidelity. Sure, it may not have pathtracing or some other bells and whistles of the recent titles, but that doesn't really take away from the style and atmosphere this game presents. For how good this looks, the game performs very well and i've never had a CTD or a drop beyond 144 fps. Can't say how the performance scales on lower end machines, tho. You get what you've been promised. A re-imagined story of Pinocchio with a wicked twist on the familiar characters. While it's not my cup of tea, it's definitely inventive and deserves praise in terms of setting and atmosphere.  Every boss fills like a part of the world and like they are exactly where they need to be. Also design-wise, each boss is varied and somehow looks like one of the best From Soft's bosses. Bossed don't attack you just because you disengage and heal. That's good.  You can regain one healing item if you run out by attacking enemies. That's also a great idea and helps in a pinch without affecting the tension of running low on heals. I personally couldn't care less about Pinocchio's story and the game haven't convinced me to care. The more traditional and 'in your face' style of storytelling didn't help either. I do recognize that some people crave a more digestible story in a soulslike and that game provides it, i guess. But i found the story quite boring and uninspiring.  Cool idea of mixing and matching blades and handles. On paper. In the actual game you quickly find the one thing that you like and play with it for the rest of the game. Also the coolest weapons (boss weapons with cool and unique movesets) are exempt from the system and can't be mixed and matched. That only raises the chances of you not engaging with the system much. It's okay. Lying is fun sometimes, but it doesn't affect the game nearly enough for me to care. I also hate that you have to listen to the entire songs you find to get more humanity. I don't like the songs and I don't want to listen to them, period. Once again, cool idea on paper but severely underutilized. Enemies don't change their attacks or behaviour, you don't get some material\weapon reward for it. You just make an enemy a tiny little bit easier. The game tries to be both Bloodborne and Sekiro and turns out to be the worst of both worlds. Let's start with the parries. Just like everyone else has already mentioned, the parry window is too tight. Especially for how erratically most enemies attack. ESPECIALLY for puppets. Their wind up animations are ludicrous and timing a perfect parry is extremely hard. Great choice for the first enemies in the game, the enemies on which players will be learning how to parry. Puppet bosses suffer from the same thing. Oh you want to parry? Let me delay my attack just enough so you'll get hit. You also can't fan the parry button like in Sekiro, so you either commit to a block or go for the perfect parry. With an extremely tight perfect parry window this results in you eating the attack most of the time and dying. Rallying mechanic (regaining health by attacking) is locked behind a block. Why? Instead of being able to regen any lost health, you can only regain chip damage you got while blocking. This creates a bigger gap between committing to a block or going for the parry. Because IF you get hit you won't get a chance to heal from attacking. Dodging is just pathetic. Very little distance and very few i-frames. Oh, and remember the red unblockable attacks bosses and mini bosses do? They ignore dodge i-frames and still hit you, have fun! So what we get is a play style that's not aggressive and relies on rote memorization of attacks to counter them. You never really set the pace for the fight, you just react to what the boss does (and hopefully you react perfectly, otherwise you either lose health or boss regains it) and you whittle the boss down in small windows they give for attacks. You have no poise and can be hit out of basically everything. That makes some of the enemies and bosses extremely hard to stagger to deal a big attack. It's much worse with heavy weapons and handles on which heavy attacks do multiple hits. Since stagger only applies on the last hit. This leads to the situation where the boss is staggerable, and you find a window to fully charge a heavy attack, AND you hit them, but you only manage to hit them twice out of the 3 attacks you have in the animation - and the boss hits you out of it. No stagger for you and some lost health as a gift. While boss art design is great, boss game design is awful. First issue has already been mentioned a million times: 2 phase bosses. They are not fun, especially when it's a completely different boss in the second phase. Sure, one or two surprise appearances spice up the game, but when basically every boss after the 3rd one is some variation of a 2 phase boss - it's just annoying. Bosses are too tanky. You never feel like you damage the boss, rather you just chip away at the giant health pool they have. Add to that the health regeneration and you get extremely annoying boss encounters. And you usually do it twice :) Why do they exist in a post Elden Ring world? Why do I have to run to the bosses door each time I die? Just why? Your souls spawn outside the door, you basically get no punishment for dying besides spending your consumables. The only punishment is you have to slog through half a level holding the B button to fight the boss again. Sure, they are mostly not long, but they shouldn't be there at all. No one likes boss runbacks.  General level design is boring and too easy. This creates a giant difficulty spike between levels you play and bosses you defeat on those levels. The developers seem to think that everyone likes poison swamp, rolling boulders and status effects in soulslike. So you get a lot of extremely annoying places where you'll be poisoned and trapped. Again, this kind of thing can spice up a level or two, IF you don't expect it. In Lies of P basically every other item pick up or bridge is a trap, you become accustomed to it and just get annoyed when the fifth bridge in a row breaks under you. I also hope you like dealing with status effects, since there are a ton. And a ton of levels where status effect dealing enemies and props are a big obstacle. Annoying. That's it. Too many status effects and too tanky. Why do I have to buy items that would literally be abundant trash in other soulslike? You even have to buy pebbles (cogs in this case) to throw and get the enemy attention.  Shut up already, I don't want exposition thrown at me and listening to his snarky comments makes me sick.  I don't care that I can remove this with the P-organ mods, this shouldn't have been in the game. This game doesn't encourage aggressive play and this mechanic showcases this problem.

Great game and can't wait for a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: satisfying soulslike combat, incredibly good boss designs and enemy variety, art and animation quality occasionally surpasses fromsoft. The P organ upgrade tree is cool and actually gives interesting gameplay perks. The weapon mixing system is cool even though I didn't really use it much. The game is also really long, almost excessively so. Enemy and boss variety keeps it fresh to the end, and there are only a couple boss rematches.Cons: weird writing and confused story and themes. A lot of the dialog feels very amateurish. The comic relief does not hit. The story is a tired "search for immortality creates a zombie disease," but with puppets mixed in. I know some people like that it tells more of a real story than most souls games, but it just did not do it for me. Some hitboxes and parry windows are a little questionable but most are ok.The naming conventions for all the different resources and consumables are dumb. Even 40 hours in I was still mixing up Legion and Fable.Still overall a great dark souls clone! Easy recommend if you like soulsbornering games.

_childDocuments_.review: Very nicely polished game with great combat mechanics and thoughtful bosses and weapon designs, the story is great however it's much more linear than the traditional soul games. Overall speaking, the positives in the game definitely overwhelms its negatives, making this game one of the only soul-like that provides a similar level of experience compared to the ones created by from software.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game overall! The world and visuals are stunning and the gritty retelling of a classic fairy-tale just WORKS. The combat is challenging for sure, as expected, but there were only a couple boss fights that truly gave me headaches. This truly feels like a love letter to Bloodborne and FromSoft in general. With that said,  Regardless of their individual difficulties, some of the best boss fights truly feel like a dance; careful battles of attacking quick openings that punishes any sort of hesitancy or misstep. The weapon system is very creative and allows for lots of unique combinations that fit many different styles. I did not have much issue with needing to farm or feeling too weak for any specific area throughout the game. The areas, while fairly linear, provide lots of small detours to explore and collect goodies. I never felt like I was rushing through the game at all, and each area presented a new challenge that kept the game fresh.The character writing & voice acting is VERY well done.  Each character holds much more depth than expected, and being able to watch Pinocchio evolve over time was a great addition to the story.Simply put, I can't recommend this game enough, regardless if you are a Souls vet or brand new to the genre. It's a creative retelling of a classic story that will give you a new appreciation for the original, with combat that's fast and exciting. The devs knocked it out of the park.

_childDocuments_.review: Title: A Masterpiece of Dark Fantasy - Lies of PReview:Lies of P is an extraordinary adventure that masterfully blends the haunting atmosphere of dark fantasy with the timeless tale of Pinocchio, resulting in a game that is nothing short of a masterpiece. From the moment you step into its beautifully crafted world, you are drawn into a narrative that is both familiar and intriguingly unique.Visuals and Art Design:The game's visuals are a stunning testament to the power of artistic vision and technical prowess. Every environment, from the eerie, shadowed streets to the grand, decaying structures, is meticulously detailed and dripping with atmosphere. The character designs are equally impressive, bringing to life a cast of characters that are as memorable as they are unsettling.Storytelling and Atmosphere:Lies of P excels in storytelling, weaving a dark and captivating narrative that keeps you hooked from beginning to end. The reimagining of the classic Pinocchio story is both clever and profound, exploring themes of identity, humanity, and deception with a maturity and depth that is rare in the gaming world. The atmosphere is thick with tension and mystery, perfectly complemented by a hauntingly beautiful soundtrack that lingers long after you've put down the controller.Gameplay and Mechanics:The gameplay mechanics are finely tuned, offering a challenging yet rewarding experience that will appeal to both newcomers and seasoned veterans of the genre. Combat is fluid and satisfying, with a variety of weapons and abilities that allow for a deeply personalized playstyle. The difficulty is well-balanced, providing a sense of accomplishment with each hard-fought victory.Innovative Features:One of the standout features of Lies of P is its innovative approach to choice and consequence. Your decisions have a tangible impact on the world and characters around you, leading to multiple endings that ensure a high replay value. The game constantly challenges you to question your morality and the nature of truth, making every choice feel significant and impactful.Conclusion:Lies of P is a breathtaking journey that sets a new standard for dark fantasy games. It combines a compelling narrative, stunning visuals, and engaging gameplay to create an experience that is both unforgettable and profound. Whether you are a fan of the original Pinocchio story or simply a lover of immersive, narrative-driven games, Lies of P is an absolute must-play. Prepare to be enchanted, challenged, and utterly captivated by this incredible adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: In memory of a great writer Carlo CollodiThat is the lyrics this game meets a player and I have to agree with that one, because devs sure did a good job on the game and story they worked on!Now about my experience with the game and ups and downs of this game.On the plus side:- Very interesting story with some twists, very cool bosses, weapons and level design- A memorizable characters and interesting story telling of Pinnocio- Very friendly ergo system. You dont lose it all if you die second time like in Soulsborne series and most of the Soulslikes, you just lost a part of it and with a certain upgrades of P-Organ you can make it so you lose even less- Interesting system of the P-Organ upgrades that makes you have locked abilitys and more heals, etc- Hard to miss anything story wise unlike Miyazaki and FromSoftware gamesFor the minus sides:- Very weird curve difficulty, I personally gave up on beating bosses alone and started to summon a Specters around chapter 8- Delayed hits. Yes, Elden Ring also had such issues, but not to such a scale.- Unblockable (red) attacks that autoaims at the main character. That is such a pain in the back that got myself burned a few times- Some of the abilities that should be in base game are blocked in P-Organ, such as a good dodge. That should not be a thing- Perfect parry. I am not really a fan of the idea since I need to get that 0.5 second of a perfect block. _childDocuments_.review: Good game, but has at points incredibly frustrating enemy mechanics and attack patters. Every single boss has multi hit combos, delay attacks, some sort of charge and grab. We don't have that many tools to counter that except of course the parry. That being said you can just focus on upgrading healing cells and basically play this as any other souls game. Faster weapons seems to beat slower weapons by huge margin as outside of special attacks we don't have almost any poise, any attack from any enemy can interrupt your attack only it's literally the moment it hits. Bigger weapons as they should eat more stamina and are slower but when there is no poise during the attack you will just get smacked. There are exceptions with some special attacks that give you poise, but well you can still use those with faster weapons for great effect. So if you don't want to scream at your screen too much just use some faster handle. Generally they game is very polished, runs well. There is a strong theme and it get's very souls like towards the end when you get more lore. So outside of devs making sure that you are NOT having too much fun at times it's pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: All this game does is show that the FromSoft formula is near perfection. The game itself is good, but not worth the hype. It's a 7/10 at best. I really don't like the parry mechanic being the main point. I hated Sekiro as well because of the "perfect parry" mechanic. I think it really takes away from what makes these games good. It wants you to be aggressive like Bloodborne, but then also play slow and just parry until you get a stagger off. It doesn't really work well in my opinion. My personal build is Motivity, so my attacks are very slow. I will parry and barely get 1 attack in after the enemy's chain of attacks. The heavy charge attacks are also so slow, that it makes it really hard to get it off before getting hit. The world is linear, which isn't a bad thing, but the areas feel really small and have no real substance besides enemies. I think the areas with "zombie" like creatures in the woods is also pretty random.Lastly, I feel like the enemies are either too easy or too hard. Minibosses are everywhere and even sometimes right before a checkpoint. I will choose to run to the checkpoint door and open it before fighting them, which I never felt I had to do in other souls games. Bosses are extremely hard, as it's all just about parrying all the attacks. Bringing in a summon almost hinders you in certain fights, because it makes it harder to get a stagger off when they take the aggro.All in all, it's an okay game with many similarities to FromSoft games. I just think the world, story, fighting, and enemies could use work.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game with a lot of new tweaks to ideas or just new ones entirely, though sadly a lot of those could have been implemented better along with some really irksome pet peeve issues for me. Still would highly recommend for just the fact that it was able to competently make a souls game while trying a lot of new things which I do appreciate. While it is challenging, with specters and throw items, you can make the game a lot less challenging to suit your taste. Personally, summoned a phantom once to try it out and rarely used consumables cause I was enjoying the parry system. But that's just me, play a game for your enjoyment; and I definitely think there is plenty of enjoyment to be had in this game (first run is probably around 30-40 hours, mines more cause I really enjoyed the hotel music records). : Speaking from a first run through mindset after doing just about everything (I'll do NG+ when the DLC drops) some pros would definitely be the guard hp rally and parry system. They elicit a more aggressive play-style which I found fun (wish I could have played Bloodborne). And while I'm not good on parrying, I'll say the timing issues are largely down to just me not fully meshing with it for awhile, and still having skill issues even now. However, I do think the guard animation your forced into after a perfect block is far to long leading to some frustration when I just want to get my attack in (I'm a strength or well, motivity build, so I need some actual time to swing). In fact a lot of animations feel like they could have been sped up a bit. But I'd only call those mild frustrations. A pet peeve would be the weapons bouncing off walls, that has never and will never feel good. The world itself with interesting with minor side tracks that give you a good but more linear experience, granted that's what I was looking for so that was a plus to me. The voice acting as well was so good I actually feel like mentioning, far from just serviceable, it was honestly a stand out : A minor one first, the jump feels terrible, just plain and simple. The telegraphs on some of the attacks is a bit, well, just feels spiteful. Manus was a pain because his resting animation and a attack animation were similar, the slow down to bait out parries is darn near criminal sometimes, and those last ditch attacks after a stagger on the bosses (while I get what they were going for) is all just a bit much. The rope arm specifically I pray it got some hyper armor, came out faster, or had tighter hitboxes. Cause seeing a opening and hitting the rope the second it was safe to do so but still having the enemy get a hit out before you (especially when its like a horizontal swipe that isn't even close to you) and knocking you out of the animation was just depressing. They could have leaned a bit more into the rule of cool for rope arm, the fact it's just slightly to short to grab a enemy across a gap or the fact you move back a little so you cannot use it to yank a enemy into the abyss while on a beam were disheartening. On that note, kind of wish fables were a bit weaker but charged quicker so I could weave them into combat more though that issue is reduced in the later game and NG+s.
