_childDocuments_.review: Fairly solid game and I'd give it an 8.5/10. Incredible attempt at a Soulslike from a studio that isn't From Software and easily one of the better ones of those.If you're itching for a new Souls game after Elden Ring, this will hit the spot.It's actually got a great deal of the makings of a good Souls game down and you can see they paid an amazing attention to detail with the mechanics and feel every place you look. The feel of the game is somewhere between Dark Souls 3 and Bloodborne with some of their own refinement. I went through on a lightweight build and was able to hop around like in Bloodborne itself, but I've been told the game gives a lot of Sekiro vibes with the parrying and block system, which the weightier dodges make you rely on a lot more.There were a few points where I felt like your companion character, Gemini, got too exposition dumpy, but for the most part I enjoyed the presentation, even if there were maybe a few too many texts to pick up. But the texts you pick up are akin to what you'd find in Resident Evil where you have neat little tales about what's going on in the world. Past that, the story is presented like Sekiro where there are a decent few characters of importance in the world who you converse with. The weapon system is actually pretty neat and allows you to mix and match the head and handle of everything but the boss weapons, basically. The handle controls the moveset and scaling you get (though you can alter this slightly) while the head determines the speed and damage type. Alongside that, instead of a gun like in Bloodborne, you get what amounts to a Sekiro Prosethetic arm in function, though these have a lot more direct damage often.There were a few places where the hitboxes felt a bit off (a boss midway through the game was able to punch forward with me behind it and pull me into a grab attack) and where bosses seemed like they tracked and pivoted more than they maybe should, but this was the exception and not the norm. The later game humanoid bosses were especially satisfying to fight actually. Overall boss difficulty is a bit on the harder end vs From Soft's fare, but it's a good time. As far as normal enemies, the typical big boys you fight once and then banish for that playthrough always give something worthwhile with the respawning bigger enemies always able to drop the item, and frequently, that you need to summon an NPC at major bosses.All in all, I had a great time with the game. I look forward to seeing what Round 8 Studios cooks up in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the best and/or most faithful imitation of the From Software formula up to this point. It has some great boss fights, music, visuals, and even a decent story. You can tell the devs put a ton of effort into this, even if it is kinda derivative. While some in-between areas of the game are linear and somewhat repetitive, the main areas usually have some fun level designs. These areas scratch that dungeon-crawling itch and have plenty of shortcuts and other stuff to discover. There are plenty of weapons and accompanying builds to choose from, and you can even mix and match weapon parts to create something new. I didn't use this feature much and mostly stuck with a motivity-based boss weapon in my playthrough, but it's cool to have. The combat itself is good, and there is an emphasis on perfectly timing your blocks. This can lead to staggering your opponent or breaking their weapons in most cases. Different enemy types are weak to certain elements like any other souls-like game. Using that to your advantage can make some of the boss fights pretty trivial. On the topic of bosses themselves, I only really struggled with one of them for a bit. Most of the fights are pretty straightforward if you've played any other souls game. You'll find much more of a challenge in Sekiro or Bloodborne for sure. Overall I enjoyed my 19 hours, but don't have a strong desire to replay it. You could easily double or triple that play time to 100% the game if that's what you're into. I would recommend for like $30 or less to any bored souls fans. It's a good game but it won't blow your mind. For those that want to play this in place of Bloodborne because they don't have a PS4, keep holding on to hope for a port because this does not replace that game.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so scared that this game would disappoint me despite because of all the hype I had built up around its announcement and demo: thankfully I came away from Lies of P overwhelmingly impressed. AND it has some insanely good PC optimization, I never dropped a single frame throughout the whole experience. I've played so many souls likes and every FromSoft souls like game, and if I this game was dropped on to my lap with no forewarning I'd say that FromSoft made this game themselves. It is just a great combination of Bloodborne and Sekiro.I can't say it's for everyone, there are some difficulty curves that can't be overcome with some of the cheesier ways that the Souls games or Elden Ring allows: you HAVE to learn the mechanics and integrate them into your play. But in short, if you love souls games and souls-likes this is probably the pinnacle of taking what makes those games great and transforming them into a new experience. I'd highly recommend it, and I can't wait to get through NG+ and see some other endings.*Maybe light spoiler below this*Also, if their sequel or DLC bait is true - please let this company succeed enough to do it. _childDocuments_.review: So, I love this game; “Lies of P” is marked as my favorite game of all time. Not to brag, but I have recently gotten all the achievements in the game and have played for almost 50 hours. I will continue playing and try different challenge runs because I LOVE this game so much. I love the combat; it's responsive, fun, never a dull moment, and most of all, it actually feels like I can fight how I want, either being balls-to-the-wall crazy or playing safe. Not only that, but I enjoyed all the Souls games (especially Bloodborne), and one thing I love the most is the weapon choices. I love to perfect guard any chance I get I may ♥♥♥♥ up here and there, but its the learning the timing and understand why I screwed up that makes it fun. Lies of P has unique and interesting choices in every chapter, offering so many ways to play with different weapons. I beat the game with a motivity build, a technique build, and advance build ALL of them are viable (including a run with no P organ motivity build. lowest vigor technique build).Of course, I will address the fact that the weapon assembly is considered not needed; this is something I would like to say crafting in elden ring was not needed but was there for your liking. Same thing for Lies of P: you have the OPTION to use the assembly to change the ways your weapons work. I added this to note that I have heard a lot of people argue about this, but I enjoyed the option to use it. The mobs in the game, hands down, have some of the best-looking enemies in the genre. I mean, there were some mobs that were haunting, with their looks reminiscing the horror genre. Everything looks amazing from a horror aesthetic standpoint and from a gameplay standpoint, mini bosses, some of which I would even consider as hard as regular bosses. Speaking of bosses, every one of them is great. I will say Lies of P has a lot of phase 2 bosses, but personally, I enjoy all of them. Bosses kept getting harder and harder at a consistent rate. Never did I say, “OMG, I can't do this.” I always felt that I could do it because it's a step up from the last one, making me feel like I have gotten better each kill.The side quests and characters are awesome. I loved every single person's story; they all had merit and/or good reasoning, and most importantly, I actually gave a ♥♥♥♥ about them. Never in souls like when I worried about what's going to happen to someone until this game. They all have great character development throughout the game, making sure you can follow along fairly easily with what's going on. Speaking of character development, the story I enjoyed completely. Out of all the souls like I played, its best story is that nothing is hidden, and there is no secret lore dropped into the main story of the game.  Most of the main story is explained pretty simply to the player. The only thing that the player has to do is just talk to the NPCs around the game, and everything is clearly explained to you about any topic about which you might be curious about. The music is something to enjoy every day, no question about it. I would sit there and listen to the amazing music playing. If I could, I would buy all the bosses soundtracks (I WANT TO DO THAT). I love picking up the records from the NPCS because I know I am getting rewarded for getting them and listening to them for story reasons. I think this game deserves a 9 out of 10, but I am biased as all hell, so I say a 10, because that's my personal opinion on it. I see people saying there is a flaw here and there, but I personally enjoyed this game a HELL OF A LOT. This game is rated really highly for a reason: it is a great game that should be enjoyed by everybody. I would add I am more than willing to help someone out if they need help founding out or knowing a strat with the game and no I wont give the git gud I want everybody to succeed in this game that I think is a masterpiece. P.S this is my very first review on anything on steam it just so happen to be my favorite game lol.

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is an incredible game that takes the classic Pinocchio story and gives it a dark, intriguing twist. The RPG elements, including weapon upgrades and character customization, add depth and replayability, allowing players to tailor their experience. Overall, Lies of P is a must-play for fans of Souls-likes' and anyone looking for a captivating and immersive gaming experience.

_childDocuments_.review: VERY GOOD game just short of Great. Every category is very good, but there is just something that keeps it from being 10/10.  Combat is fluid and can feel very satisfying when you perform your plan perfectly. I do mean your plan too. Being compared to Seikero the worst of the souls games I think is a disservice to Lies of P. As it has literally dozens more options for how you take on fights. Parry and single sword is only one option. Dodge isn't worthless and with the upgrades feels good. Not all Red attacks are you must parry there are dodges and positioning with reach and speed in your attacks having lots of variety depending on the weapon you pick. What keeps it from great for me is the enemy variety. You fight everything from colour swaps to bosses now trash mobs. You will be super familiar with the few dozen enemy types by the end and it can feel a bit long in the tooth because of it. Difficulty is a bit odd curved as the hardest boss at least for me was Chap 5 not even half way, but no other boss even came close to the effort. Note boss was patched after so probably just awesome fun now. Bosses are mostly fantastic. I think I found one I felt was a boring with the rest being fun to overcome. The ball was dropped a bit with some mostly from a lore perspective on the dud. Third boss to the end was just pointless? They did nothing the whole game just show up get more cutscene time than most of the cast and die. I point to the most egregious example but several feel like they just show up and it leaves things feeling slightly disjointed. As a matter of fact no less than 3 times was I convinced I was at the final boss. Customization is great on paper and good in practice. When first seeing the mixing handles and blades along with the P-organ options it really gives this feel that this char will be yours and unique to your style, build, personality. However, I'm fairly sure 90% of my P-organ is exactly the same as everyone elses. 4rth Organ tree I had 2 from as they tend to buff items, but given you can't buy unlimited it really ended up feeling as if that tree required you to get the skill and then grind just to make them worth the investment. Vs the previous tree's where each upgrade felt impactful. Thus, in the end i'm sure my quartz ended up like everyone's with the ones that didn't require grind to make useful.  Handles/blades sound great, but there are 5 and a half advance style weapons in the game and most scale well with their start. I swapped for fun, but legit couldn't outdo the sparky stick stock style. Overall you are getting a LONG game. 50 hours till the end and while a little long you will recognise all the souls staples. Fluid enough that it won't give you that off feeling when controlling such as with lords of the fallen or ninja souls. You will slip right in like slipping on your favourite pair of cozy jammy jams. I have zero issue's giving this a thumbs up recommendation and even saying it very well might be the best non from soft souls game out there and even above a few of there lesser outings!

_childDocuments_.review: I love the part in which P said "it's time to lie" and then lied all over place and, somehow, that is the requisite for the best ending.Absolutely stellar level design. The developer understood that a souls game is made or broken by its encounters above anything else. The reason why dark souls 2 is considered the weakest of the series while having excellent mechanics and levels is simply that the encounters sucked, which shows that even from software sometimes fumbles. Apart from a couple of areas (and like I said, it's not like the originals were flawless), Lies of P manages to maintain every encounter fun to figure out.The only bad thing I want to mention is how there are no major secret areas and bosses. During a normal playthrough, you will most likely explore everything. It's a linear, streamlined experience, which is not necessarily bad but makes me wonder why this aspect in the original souls games is often glossed over. In Bloodborne, a small part of an otherwise late game area can be accessed by getting killed by one particular enemy. There are several optional bosses, all of them of high quality. None of this is present in lies of p. Save from one final choice, every boss you kill in your first playthrough is also every boss in the game.That said, this game is extremely replay able and I'm on my second playthrough with a completely different build.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed this, for about 90% of the playthrough. Will give you the highs and lows quickly.Fantastic and why Lies of P was more enjoyable than Elden Ring:- NO INPUT READING. Dark Souls and Elden Ring essentially cheat by reading your keypresses and responding instantaneously. Frankly, its garbage, and an idiotic mechanic that should never have been implemented. You're basically fighting yourself, or finding ways to 'cheese' the boss, which takes away all the fun and skill of the fight because the AI is straight up cheating. LoP doesn't input read therefore each fight feels organic and rewarding. - IT LETS *YOU* STAGGER THE ENEMY! God, how many times in Elden Ring did I take entirely unncessary damage because of basic hits staggering me. Then you'd fall down, get hit more on standing up or at the end of a roll. Meanwhile, yes you can guard counter, but you can't stagger and you can't hit them when they're down (but they can hit you!). LoP gives this power back to you, and puts you on equal footing with the AI. They can stagger but so can you. Its actually fair and I can't believe I even had to type that.Pros:- Beautiful, stunning game on the Unreal Engine. Looks fantastic, ran at constant 120 capped on a 3070 super on ultra. A++- The characters are all voiced well, interesting, and their individual stories intermingle and flow together. I, for the most part, found them quite interesting, notably the King of Riddles.- Combat is challenging, but not busted. There are one or two fights in the game you will likely struggle hard with, but for the most part this is far more palatable than ER or DS. And for that, I'm appreciative. I enjoy 'hard' games, I don't enjoy overly punishing and brutal boss fights that require dozen upon dozens or more attempts or even full character ability/build respecs just to get past. - The overall story, while somewhat confusing, was a very cool spin on the classic Pinnochio tale. The devs really did their homework and wove in some very unique color that you might not even know about. For example, one of the groups in the game are the 'Alchemists'. A weapon you can find later in the game is called the 'Uroboros Wheel'. The 'Oroboros' is, in fact, the sigil of the actual Alchemist guild from about 400 CE and represents the duality of man (ring any bells?). Cons:- Like seemingly every Korean game, some of the translations and phrasings feel weird in English. I can't quit put my finger on it but it just feels off. Many people are quick to point out that Pinnochio's heart and the skill tree in the game is called 'P Organ'. Im as juvenile as the next guy but this just feels too obvious...- This game, like seemingly every other soulsborne on the planet, suffers what I consider to be the cardinal sin of boss fights in gaming. They give you an incredibly challenging boss with limited resources that, once dead, you guessed it....turns into something else and surprise...phase 2. Now you have no health, you've burned your resources and hes even harder than phase 1. Can we collectively agree to stop doing this in video games? Im so !@#$ing done with it. Just give me the boss and let me move on. Phase 1, phase 2, phase 3, 'bonus boss' is just straight cancer.- Lastly, I gotta echo what others have said and say that the final chapter of the game dragged on WAY past what was enjoyable. It was a brutal, painful, monotonous slog. On top of this, I clocked in at about 25 hours to complete this. I would say that act 10 alone was about 6 or 7 of those hours. They basically wrap up the story, ship you off to boss island, build you up for the 'Ok this is it!' moment. And that moment doesnt come until about 7 hours later, and that was playing quickly. And JUST WHEN YOU THINK ITS OVER...SURPRISE...IT ISNT. (I did enjoy the story element of this but I did not appreciate being dragged along for this seemingly endless ending). Its like that movie thats 3 hours long but could easily have been 90 minutes and you just get exhausted and want to leave the theater half way through. The game, up until this point, was fantastic, gorgeous and flowed beautifully across the different zones. Then it all came to an abrupt halt that absolutely sucked my energy out to keep going, it truly was a marathon I did not want to finish (but did).Looking forward to our, ahem, red-heeled heroine next, Neowiz. Nice job.

_childDocuments_.review: This was my first Souls game, so this review is less so through the lens of "if you like Bloodborne, you will/will not like this game" etc, as I think this can convolute much of the game's intricate value. Lies of P throws you into a phenomenally crafted world for you to become engulfed. It is set in a Belle-Époque-style era, a period in French history distinguished by the wealthy’s attempts to fall back into an artificially carefree, fairy-tale existence, while the dreadfulness of reality takes place just outside of their lavish ballrooms and red-carpeted opera houses. As a result, this class of people and the world around them were not prepared for the grim products of their own negligence. This is just at the surface of happenings you discover while going through Lies of P—The Puppet Frenzy, the Petrification Disease, and more complicated dynamics between puppets, alchemists, and those who seek power have their roots in places you would not expect. Seeing the effects of these ongoing tragedies and why they are happening in different parts of the world is very intriguing. The player learns things at the same rate as the protagonist Pinocchio, who has only recently awoken from a long state of dormancy during the climax of these events. In other words, the story never gets ahead of your thinking because you start off naturally oblivious, and rely rightfully on the world-building, from both the environment and a diverse set of characters, many of them deceptive, as the mysteries are received in pieces to a bigger puzzle. Additionally, unlike other puppets, you have the ability to lie, which makes for often difficult decisions in a world in which you ideally want to pave a pathway to betterment. With Lies of P having amazing art direction, collecting and linking these revelations in your head becomes an exciting motive while going through the story.Finally, this makes the gameplay itself fun and rewarding because it simply makes sense for various types of enemies to be located in their respective environments as you go through the story – something I find inconsistent in a lot of other RPGs. The game definitely has great replayability for the first few times as it has different skills, weapon combinations, legion arms, and thus playstyles. My biggest complaint is that although the weapons are very cool, I think it is unfair to say that there are “over 100 weapon combinations” since many of them are just unviable or silly to craft. Also, I think the game is definitely on the harder side, more specifically because it has one of the tightest parry windows in any video game I’ve seen. At this point, however, a lot of this is simply preference, and I, being a non-seasoned Souls player, adapted just fine. Generally, the bosses are great and it feels intensely satisfying once I beat any of them. Lies of P is an inspired project taking from other great games and a popular fairy tale, yet it still manages to be beautifully unique on its own and that is something I really appreciate, especially during a time when gaming and other media has been lingering in sequel hell for quite some time. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: One of the easier souls-likes for sure. Some bosses share the same attack animations and the move-sets for weapons are rather limited. That said, it's overall a tight experience with a responsive combat system and visually varied locations.  The game is entirely linear, but the level design is tight and the limited exploration within each level is generally rewarded. Story is low on my list of important things for games to have, but this has a passable story for a souls-like game despite not really being my cup of tea story-beat-wise. I'm sure some will really enjoy the story, but it's hardly the reason why you would play a game like this anyway.The parry is the most useful and powerful defensive tool you have in your arsenal. You can beat the game without it, but it's gonna make things that much harder. Just get used to the parry early on and practice with it. It allows you to avoid damage from essentially everything if done right and serves as an offensive tool as well as it breaks down enemy posture. The timing is more generous than people let on; it comes out fast and you can use it in a very reactionary manner rather than having to memorize specific parry timings for each enemy attack animation. Perhaps most importantly, Lies of P manages to forge its own identity even while borrowing heavily from Bloodbourne and the souls-series. Both visually and mechanically, it manages to make something uniquely its own even with the obvious soulsbourne inspiration.

_childDocuments_.review: I unironically enjoy this game more than Elden Ring. It's so nice I bought it twice, with my first time through being on PS5. It's a tough but fair souls-like that can be a bit punishing, but is hugely rewarding to master the nuances of it's systems and combat. Within the Souls-like genre, Lies of P has easily my favorite world and story so far. While most of it is based on the original Pinocchio fable, there are a wide range of other works that are liberally cribbed from as well. Throughout the lore you'll find references to the works of Isaac Asimov, Mary Shelly's Frankenstein, and even Batman. I also really like the central theme of the story, as to whether P is merely a puppet, or a living being whose existence deserves respect. Circumstances force you to kill numerous humans over the course of the game, and it's tragic almost every time, as P's uncertain humanity makes it very ambiguous as to if he has any right to defend himself against these desperate people.On a technical level this game is a triumph. During my entire playtime I didn't experience a single crash, let alone even a single glitch. The game is also insanely well optimized, looking fantastic while running silky smooth even without any DLSS or AMD upscaling. While the visual assets that make up the world aren't especially elaborate or detailed, everything is well designed and utilized to create a really effectively foreboding atmosphere. If I had any complaints, it would probably be that the character lip flaps don't match their dialogue at all. It might just be an issue with the animation not matching the English track, but I swear most of the time it looks like they're just going "rarrrr rarrr rarrrr rarrrr rarrrr". It's a little distracting, but no biggie. The core gameplay here is more punishing than most games in the genre, while also being a lot more fair, well, most of time anyway. This is another parry heavy system similar to Sekiro, where you have to time your blocks perfectly with the enemies attacks. The timing isn't as tricky as Dark Souls or Elden Ring, but it's still fairly demanding. Blocking an attack without parrying will only mitigate a percentage of the damage, with the rest being partially deducted from your health bar. Similar to Bloodborne, you can recover that lost health if you quickly counterattack the enemy, but if you take another hit it's gone forever. Attacking and parrying both require stamina, so you need to carefully balance your offence and defense. A system like this could be a miserable experience, but fortunately the game cuts you a fair amount of slack in terms of the enemy design. The overwhelming majority of enemies are extremely fair in their attack patterns and tells, allowing you to learn and master the timing of their attacks without much difficulty. The bosses really kick it up a notch though, and while some of them definitely gave me a hard time, I always felt like i had the tool kit necessary to pull through. That's really the highest praise I can give a game like this, where even if you're struggling, it always feels like there's another trick you haven't tried yet, or some tool you may be neglecting. Just persevere, learn the attack pattern, and inevitably you'll make it through. While I'm not going to shame anyone for utilizing all the game's features, I would highly recommend abstaining from summoning the AI helper during boss fights. This isn't an Elden Ring situation, these bosses were designed to be fought solo and you're really cheating yourself by not savoring these encounters. Except the Black Rabbit Brotherhood. F those dirty gankers. Lies of P is easily a genre masterpiece and an absolute recommend for anyone even remotely interested in Souls-likes. It's fairly regularly on sale for a very reasonable price and it's easily worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game today and, while i like it A LOT, i have some complaints, and i will start this little review with those:1) This is my main problem, to the point that overall i liked the Lords of the Fallen reboot quite a bit more because of it:while LOTF's world is far from being anywhere near as good as any of Fromsoftware's games, it is at least very compelling well designed and intriguing to explore...and exploration + finding secrets and examining the world/lore is by far my favorite aspect of these games.Unfortunately Lies of P has, by far and beyond, the most boring world of any soulslike i've ever played (maybe tied with Thymesia).. the linearity of it is staggering, and that one time every now and then that you find a pseudo secret, 90% of the time it turns out to give you some very basic consumable...the least exciting thing ever.I was not expecting the intricacies and complexity of Dark Souls 1's world design...but i hoped to at least find something like Dark Souls 2, or even a hub-based structure like Demon's Souls...anything that would make me not pay as much attention to the linearity of the whole game.My favorite thing in these games, on subsequent playthroughs, is to do stuff in a completely different order...Take Dark Souls 1 for example: right from the start you can go to Undead Burg, Petite Londo, take the master key and go directly to Blighttown or pass through the wyvern canyon and get to darkroot basin, and each one of these choices then splits into multiple subchoices, and by the end of it your successive playthroughs will have a completely different rythm compared to the first one.In Dark Souls 2 you can choose between going to Heide first, or the Fallen giants forest..Dark Souls 3 gives you some options in what to explore first once you get past the undead settlement, and there are a lot of completely optional areas and bosses.Each game, from Demon's Souls to Sekiro (not to mention Elden Ring) captivated me thanks to this aspect... Lies of P has none of it...you'll always go from A, to B, to C..period.2) i really dislike the fact that, most of the time, enemies are meant to be memorized rather than reacted to; animations are often way too clunky, mechanical and sudden for you to react to most of them on your first go (some said "of course they are clunky, they are puppets". First of, i dont think that makes it good regardless and also, this problem is present with monster and human enemies too)it was one thing if only me, the average Souls player, had this problem..but i've seen some of the people that make a living out of speedrunning-playing these games have the same exact criticism (Squilla..Afro..Oroboro..Sabaku..Cowboy etc etc)3) the skill tree locks away from you stuff that in my opinion should be avaiable by default: (two very important ones being chaining dodges together without a cooldown inbetween & being able to dodge once you get knocked down)the developers also seem to think this, because they started fixing this issue.4) many people say that this game is "Bloodborne on PC", focusing especially on the thematics and atmosphere ... and i just don't get that...Don't get me wrong: the atmosphere it creates is very unique and fascinating, and has a lot to say... but it's incredibly different compared to Bloodborne, and they have 2 very different approaches when it comes to telling their stories.The "Lovecraftian/Eldritch" aspect of this game is also extremely secondary if not completely ignorable, while Bloodborne made it it's complete focus, to the point that to this day i think it's the only action game that has ever managed to portray Lovecraft's themes perfectly, and that is because it understands that "scale", when it comes to Lovecraft, matters, and creating a world where you feel like there are seemingly infinite horrors lurking around is important.Hence why in Bloodborne, even after you manage to slay simil-god entities, the illusion that you are powerless doesn't get shattered, because (spoiler) you're still left with both the uncertainty that you were a pawn from the start, or that you simply fought against very weak exemplars of the horrors the cosmo hides, and you're left wondering if you even understood a fraction of what is out there.It's why for years people said that Lovecraft couldn't be accurately represented in an action game, and why most of the succesful attempts were non-combat games (The Last Door or Amnesia for example)..that's because entities like Cthulhu-Yog sothot etc are not meant to even be comprehended by any other living being, let alone be fought against.To make it short: other than a couple mechanics like rally-regain .. i just don't see the similarities with Bloodborne (they also have two massively different representations of a simil-victorian era)As a last note for people that are still unsure wether to buy Lies of P or LOTF: this game definitely focuses A LOT more on the bosses than the areas-world..which is interestingly the exact opposite of Lords of the Fallen. Keep that in mind and, in my opinion, use it as your main pivot point when deciding which of the two you want to play first

_childDocuments_.review: I finished my first playthrough after roughly 23 hours. This included collecting most of the loot, secret items, and some NPC questlines that the game has to offer. What makes this game really hit home is it's beautifully crafted story and the immediate familiarity one gets when it comes to mechanics, level design, and overall gameplay of the souls series. For context I've played all of the From Software games except for Dark Souls 2 and lies of p is way up there as one of my faves. The narrative is simple and straightforward but the world building and environments you explore really do a good job at setting the tone for the whole game. NPCs add a bit of complexity with the various interactions you have with them. The game does a good job at connecting their storylines and giving you a few options as to how you would want to respond to a conversation. The whole puppet and human thing.I've had no issue with enemy variety. In fact, I found it very interesting every time I would encounter a new foe in a new area and that it would completely make sense as to why these enemies look and act a certain way. It doesn't feel generic and every single area has something to keep you on your toesCombat is challenging and satisfying. The dodging, parrying, and stagger system feel just right. Everytime I die, I understood why and didn't completely feel like random BS (Except for one boss). Also, I don't know who thought of the whole separate blades and handles system but it is genius. I would find myself spending a lot of time experimenting with builds just to see how a specific weapon handle would work with a new blade I found.

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of p, what a game it was, For whoever dreamt of Bloodborne on PC, this is as close as you can get, the art, the graphics, the Aesthetics, the story,  the music, enemy designs and boss's, all of these are checked in this game. Now for the mechanics, as it looks and feels, it is a souls like game and very good one at that, taken a little bit from each souls borne sekiro, it is a bit punishing during boss fights especially  when you parry/deflect attacks it has to be at a very precises moments, but when you get the hang of it, it can be very satisfying, ( and the i frames are a bit iffy but its fine)and of course you can't have a souls like game without having the camera being against you when they push you to the edge of the arena XD, and sometimes the recovery mechanics are not friendly at all especially when you get knocked down to the ground, but as they always say ( git gud) Weapons assembly was a really nice idea and trying to mix and match certain weapons with each other made different kinds of play style. the things i hated about it was ( in my play-through and experience) how the boss' changed their attack patterns each time i enter the arena and some times how some of them keep an attack chain while having their stagger bar on and you can't even get close to them, but it was nice and fun even though i did not like it XD. Also when the Legion arm is empty and you use it makes idle and not able to move or dodge, free hits for the boss, hope this can be changed in their future DLC.9/10 Highly recommend it

_childDocuments_.review: So, Lies of P? Next best thing to Bloodborne on PC? The Soul-clone to eat all other Soul-clones? An overrated piece of crap with bad design? No, its none of these things. What it is is a super solid refinement of elements you most likely have already seen, mixed together in a pretty and interesting setting, with good voice acting, solid story and suburb presentation. This game is the manifestation of the idea of refining the wheel, and it does this super well. One notable standout is the focus on parrying in combat, and how it  can make almost any fight a hell of a lot more easy. While not as necessary in my experience as it is in Sekiro, its still a linchpin in most viable strategies, and it does shape many boss encounters, and that has its perks and drawbacks. This I think is will the biggest watershed if players will enjoy the game or not. For my part, I did, and I kept enjoying learning patterns of the many interesting bosses you fight in this game. Now for some critique, even if its minor: While this game refines many of the good features of other souls-titles, it suffers from similar problems: The camera can, and will screw you over against faster and bigger enemies, random death traps that get you ones are dotted around the game, adding nothing expect a sigh from you as you have to run and fetch your Ergo again and the armor system is very, very basic, with mostly just basic stat improvements at the expense of weight. For many players coming from DS3 or Elden Ring, they will also find the game much slower then those two, with longer regeneration on stamina and more limited dodge spamming. At the end of the day, I full and utterly recommend this game to people who love Souls-games, and are looking for another fix in this gene, and do not mind similar elements being refined and implemented in interesting ways. For those completely new to this kind of game, I would recommend Elden Ring first, as a solid introduction, but if the aesthetics, theme or weapon-system in this game seems more interesting, then this can serve as a solid introduction to this genre of gaming. Capital work from the Studio.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr if you're a die hard souls fan, you'll have a blast. anything short of that, stay awayThis game is the last stop before souls-games head into full ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ territory. Souls games have a problem with players being too good at them, so in order to make a game that souls fans still have fun with they need to make things willfully ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. This game has some significant steps into proper ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. The parry window is just a bit before the attack hits, so screw your muscle memory, screw what makes sense, and just shortens the window between your indication of an attack and when you'd have to parry it. Bosses will slide 30 feet during a stationary animation to hit you. The timing of attacks is completely nonsensical, whether it is 6 hit combos with wildly varying attack timing, or a boss doing a pile driver and hanging in the air like wylie coyote before slamming down faster than things fall. Or the entirety of that terrible swamp boss. All of that said, some much great in this game too. The story is awesome, characters are neat, the options are fun, the weapon system is awesome, in general the bosses are great, the arm and quartz stuff is great and unique, everything is pretty. The optimization is pretty terrible, but that's just kind of how things are in the "RaY tRaCIng" era.So there is a ton of great stuff in this game. It also highlights how souls games really need to have a "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" mode for the die hard souls fans that want to no-life every souls like and still have things be challenging, so that the game isnt ruined for everyone else who would like perfectly normal things to want like: attack timings that make sense, parry timings that make sense, and bosses being stationary when their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ feet aren't moving. All of those things completely destroy the flow of combat.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for something truly special, then Lies of P is for you. Not only that, Lies of P is the closest thing to a true souls-like you'll ever experience and I'll gladly tell you why while singing the praises of this fantastic masterpiece. Let's go!This game had me engaged the entire time from the mysterious beginning, to the alluring middle, and finally the end (depending on which ending you choose.) I absolutely loved how different this game was from even FROMSOFTWARE games. *Gameplay- The gameplay is as if Sekiro and Bloodborne and a baby. It's fast paced but forces you to chill out and be careful or you're gonna get an ass slappin. The way your character moves feels great and responsive to how you choose to control him. *Parry System- Do you like feeling like a badass? Sekiro birthed a new generation of badass gamers by testing their reflexes and skills, creating the feeling of moving like a shinobi. While Bloodborne taught us that your trusty weapons along with your skills will get you through any dark night good hunter. If Bloodborne had a parry system.... Dayum right? Lies of P's parry system is fast and punchy. It encourages you to be patient with your parry and confident with your attacks. Your parry is sharp and fast. When you do it correctly enough can knock the attacker back like "Damn what just happened to me?" Also you get rewarded for it. When you you parry you have the opportunity to break the enemy's weapon with a shower of sparks to follow. This game has a lot of sparks, its actually really neat. The sound for the parry is superb as well. Eventually, you'll see the enemy's health turn white. Hit em with a charged attack and you're golden my friend. You'll get yourself into some wild parry battles, just make sure you practice up. *Weapons- The weapons are so awesome! You get two types: special and normal. But don't be discouraged by "normal" because with each of them, you can break them apart and mix and match them to create a fighting style that fits you best. There were so many weapon combos I tried out that were funny but extremely useful in their application. Others were as if you were meant to break the weapon and handle apart to find their real partner. So not only are their cool weapons and combos, they all also come with special abilities and can be combined. There are some craaaaaaaazy awesome moves you can perform not only with special weapons but also normal as well. Gah I'm excited for you! Did you like the shinobi tool in Sekiro? Well you're in luck my friend because your character gets one too and you can have a bunch of fun with it. You can set your arm to specific builds and play styles to your liking. *Story- The story is basically based off Pinocchio but listen, it's not that simple by any means. Just when you think it's about one thing, you'll be pleasantly surprised to find out that there is a lot more going on. This story is dark and you must find the light. The secrets of the cause for it all. What you are. I wish I could discuss the story in depth but I don't want to spoil it. I'll just tell you that this story has so much heart. The NPCs feel, your character feels, and the tale itself is an invitation to experience it with them. When you hear the music, interact, and LIE you will come to understand more and more. *Atmosphere- This game is beautiful turn them graphics on MAX! While you're playing tis game you'll come to realize that you aren't just playing a game. This biz looks real and like you've been here before. Based in the Belle Epoque era, you get to look back on an early France with a steampunk garnish. One of the many things that makes FROMSOFTWARE games so special is taking a moment to just look around. Lies of P captures this concept. I'll spoil one area, the Opera House is magnificent and gorgeous my god. Just the birds eye view of the city will blow you away. So take a moment and smell the flowers yo, you just might like whatcha see. *CONCLUSION- I hope I could convince some of you to give this game a chance. If you already have, then I'm sure you read this and nodded your head. Lies of P is truly special and I think every gamer should give this a try, especially if you love souls like games. Make my words. NEOWIZ and Round8 Studio understand what it means to create a souls like, set the bar, and usher in a new future for this genre. I know those are some big claims but until you play it, you'll just have to trust me and other reviews.

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is a fascinating case of a game being inspired (in this case by Soulsborne) and not only meeting but in some ways even exceeding its point of origin. I'm an avid Soulsborne vet and this game has absolutely swept me off my feet as a "Souls-like" that for all intents and purposes very nearly feels as if it is an actual Miyazaki-helmed Soulsborne entry fresh off of From Software's presses. You play as "P", a puppet that strangely possesses free will that is awakened in the midst of a crisis in the steampunk city of Krat. It is a world where puppets have revolted against the people and overtaken the city while a mysterious disease infests what people have survived the frenzy. In a tale that is a dark, steampunk twist on the classic text "The Adventures of Pinocchio" by Carlo Collodi you must find your father Gepetto, take back the city of Krat from the rogue puppets, and perhaps discover the true nature of the Petrification Disease that is sweeping the city. But what kind of boy will you be on your journey? Will you be a good boy for father and always tell the truth? Or will you exercise your free will and lie to the people, lie to your friends during quests or at your safe haven of Hotel Krat? Right to the faces of your enemies? Maybe you'll fall somewhere in between. But unique to you, that is ultimately your choice.This game is a Soulsborne game through and through. Soulsborne veterans will feel right at home, new players to the genre won't have a tough time picking it up as the game does a great job of building you up in the very early sections. That being said the game is challenging in true Souls fashion. The highest compliment I can pay Neowiz is say that they made this game with love. The most accurate expression I can detail for this game is that it feels like mish mosh of some of my favorite Soulsborne titles. It has the pace of Dark Souls 3, the presence of rewarding offense like Bloodborne (complete with regaining life on hit after taking damage), yet notably an INCREDIBLE and appreciated focus on developing precise and skillful defense as in Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice (parrying in this game is as rewarded and important as Sekiro's deflect mechanic with consideration to stagger and critical attacks). It's a fusion all of these best parts yet it comes together to offer a truly unique experience in and of itself. My only possible nitpick is that the level design while close to the mark at times feels noticeably linear although in a lot of ways I think that works for this game. Also the English voice acting can feel a little campy at times.The game is very well optimized and super smooth for PC. The combat is excellent with challenging bosses. There are amazing layers of taking apart and combining equipment to jury rig your own highly unique weapon via mix and match. The story is quite feasibly rather good and easier to follow than your typical Soulsborne. Telling the truth or lying dictating how quests and encounters play out is a really ambitious mechanic. And the game has one of THE most beautiful soundtracks I've heard in a video game. There's a lot to love about Lies of P as a love letter to Soulsborne but also as an imaginative reinterpretation of The Adventures of Pinocchio. If you love Soulsborne, if you love action games with polished combat, are a fan of steampunk, or are just looking for a game that will challenge your precision and skill this is an easy "buy this game and don't look back". There's a metric ton that feels very special and different about the vision present in this game.But am I lying to you or am I telling you the truth? There's only one way to be sure. Book your trip to the City of Krat and play Lies of P!

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Soulsborne games ever made by a studio that isn't FromSoftware. If you loved Bloodborne or have wanted to try it, this game will scratch that itch and then some.Visually and stylistically the game gives you that Bloodborne feeling with its own setting taking place in a dystopian version of Pinocchio.Gameplay wise, Lies of P feels like a mashup of Dark Souls, Sekiro, and Bloodborne with its mechanics with some unique aspects thrown in as well. It has the interconnected areas of Dark Souls, the parrying emphasis and prosthetic arm of Sekiro, and the health regain system of Bloodborne. For its own twist, Lies of P introduces weapon creation where you can swap the blades and handles of your weapons to alter their moveset and skills.The game is challenging and you will want to learn the mechanics well, but it feels very rewarding when you do. However, it is also doable to get through the entire game without parrying at all if you struggle with it. Blocking is a viable strategy because you can regain health lost if you counterattack before you're hit directly. The game feels smaller in scale than Bloodborne and the Souls series, but what's within those areas works well and doesn't feel bloated.I was actually very invested in the mystery of the puppet frenzy within this alternate world of Pinocchio, and I very much enjoyed how they went about it.Overall, this is probably my favourite game purchase of the year. I would 100% recommend this to Souls fans and I'm excited to see the sequel from this studio.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is Amazing, if you are looking for a souls like with atmosphere, solemn music, relatively versatile combat, and a pretty clear story line, but is still different from your typical from soft game, this is the way to go. I can't explain how excited I was for this game to come out because of having perfect blocks, and all the other different mechanics it introduced into the combat system that allowed you to adapt to enemies. Even from the demo, there was never a time where I felt that the bosses were repetitive so there was almost no one combat style fits all for the whole game. While it does borrow mechanics from Blood borne in terms of propagating a more aggressive play style, you will slowly but surely learn that not all bosses can be approached in the same manner, and it will take some time to learn their attack patterns, so at least for me when reaching end game patience was KEY, meanwhile in the beginning it wasn't as much of a worry. Overall a damn amazing game that kept me enthralled throughout my verging on 60 hours of game play, and definitely something that any souls like fan who isn't afraid to fail should try. Can't wait to see more amazing games from this studio.

They dance around the battlefield seemingly weightless, even though they are larger then you. Oh don't worry you can just perfect block, except, perfect block is the least intuitive system Ive seen in a while. The blocking doesnt line up with the animation leading you to guess when blocking is needed and reacting within a moment because enemies can attack 10 times before you can attack once.I know ill try a heavy attack, surely that will stagger him. Well guess what you don't have hyperarmour, even for a second, so any heavy attack that isnt perfectly timed ends up in failure.I can appreciate what this game is trying to do and i actually like it in some areas, its just so unforgiving that it becomes unfun to run back to the same miniboss 15 times.I still can not recommend this game until the core problem of the game is fixed and that is the parry window and attack animations which added together make it incredibly frustrating for all but the try hardiest of try hards.

_childDocuments_.review: it's sekiro meets bloodborne meets twink pinocchio and it's absolutely sick as hell. if that's enough of a pitch to get you excited then i fully encourage you to go for itif you're not a Hardcore Fromsoft Veteran (or even if you are) my biggest caveat is that the bosses in this game are hard. really hard. even once you've figured out how to engage with the game on its own terms, you will die a lot learning each boss' moves and timings. if you're gonna dive in, you will need patience, willingness to fail and learn, and know when to take breaks. i'm a complete sicko for these games and i still had maddening fights that took dozens of attempts, and fights where i had to take a break til the next day to wind down and let knowledge and muscle memory have a chance to sink in. there are a number of bosses i'd place on par with some of the hardest fromsoft fights, like ludwig or orphan of kos or isshin. the flipside of that coin though is that most of those same fights were also just as cool and immensely rewarding to surpass. if you can accept that at times you may run into walls that you have to keep throwing yourself at over and over again, i think the satisfaction when you pull through is absolutely worth it...but everyone and their grandma has already talked to death about the difficulty, and i don't want the only takeaway people have to be "oh it's a hard soulslike." lies of P is clearly a massive labor of love, and it really shines with the amount of effort and care that went into it. the core mechanics and controls are very unapologetically Soulsian, but it adds in enough of its own mechanics and systems and ideas and style to carve out its own distinct identity. the game's art and visuals are gorgeous, with tons of lovingly-made scene-setting details scattered about. they manage to make a setting and time period and Vibe that i usually don't care for at all and get me totally into it. and i am no lover of Uncanny 19th Century Steampunk Androids, but all the attention placed into the enemy designs and animations and sound design come together to make Evil Puppets so unsettling and believable and wonderfully creepy that i can't help but admire it. if you can put a robot on my screen meant to look like a clownish parade master or a cartoon-ass 1800s cop and make me go "oh ♥♥♥♥ this is sick actually" you have really worked a miraclethere's plenty more i could go on about, like the excellent setting-immersing soundtrack, or the fantastic thoughtful level design, or the tricks and traps and pranks that would make hidetaka miyazaki himself shed a tear of joy, but sufficed to say it is good. really really good. the level of polish on every facet is enough that you'd be forgiven for thinking it was fromsoft-developedthe one really noticable scuff in that polish though is the translation. the voiced main story lines can sometimes feel a bit strange or stilted, the miscellaneous optional Lore Documents sometimes border on nonsensical, and there are a number of ambiguities and outright errors in descriptions for some mechanical things like perks/upgrades. it's one major weakness that can interfere with taking the story seriously, and cause frustration when things aren't properly explainedbut... for me at least, the game manages to overcome that anyway. i don't mind doing a little tinkering or research to try to decipher a vague perk description, and despite the awkwardness of the translation the story still managed to get me really invested. the ideas and plot and writing are all so unabashedly earnest and ambitious that the feeling behind it all still shines through clear as day. "what if a fairy tale was F*CKED up!!" is story archetype that's usually drenched in tedious irony and cynicism, but lies of P avoids that completely. it is about "what if pinnochio was in a MESSED UP MURDER ROBOT WORLD and LYING WAS GOOD* ACTUALLY" but it takes it all completely seriously, thoughtfully looking at themes from this old-ass fairy tale and turning them on their head. it finds creative, playful ways to incorporate and reinterpret elements of the original story - i'm sure way more of the things in the game are homages to OG pinocchio than i even realize, given i'm not sure i've ever really experienced anything other than the disney version. and ultimately it picks up an ages-old preachy, puritanical fable to get kids to obey their parents and not lie; and turns it into a dark, atmospheric, gripping rumination on how lies can sometimes be one of the things that make us most human. by being so genuine, and unafraid to cram in every big wacky ambitious idea they wanted to, i feel like lies of P kind of... singlehandedly destroys the concept of "cringe". you can see how much love the people who made this game wholeheartedly put into making it, that for you to jeer and call it awkward or uncool would indisputably make *you* the weird onethe voice actors play an important part in selling it all too. some of the VA quality is... mixed, but the majority of them put in good and even great performances. an unusual word choice or ill-fitting line in a script is jarring, but if an actor manages to deliver that weird line well enough to convey the emotion intended behind it, that can go a long way to patching up the friction and confusion and help you stay immersed in the story. and their success rate at that is high enough to keep the story and key characters engaging and intriguing. also a special shoutout to the VA for Arlecchino, who had the second most fun recording his lines that any human has ever had in a game studio recording booth (first place of course being Takenobu Mitsuyoshi recording the daytona soundtrack)Lies of P really surprised me. it kind of came out of nowhere like "check it out: twink pinocchio soulslike" and then turned out to be one of my favorite gaming experiences of this year, in a year where i have had a lot of new favorite gaming experiences. it's exciting to see a couple of previously pretty unknown studios coming together to bring some fresh ideas to the well-trodden genre of the soulslike, and have an execution that knocks it out of the park so roundly. i'm definitely looking forward to seeing what more this team comes out with in the future. but even more than that, i hope everyone working at neowiz and round8 are getting some much-deserved rest and paid vacation time... even though the conditions of the game industry make that sadly unlikely (major spoilers for a deep endgame boss) (only click this if youve beaten the game)

_childDocuments_.review: What a masterpiece. Completely blew me out of the water, all my expectations were shattered. The weapon combinations are so fun, my personal favorite weapon was the scythe, so fun to use. Runs incredibly, looks incredible, game play is incredible. _childDocuments_.review: I really think this is the best soulslike. Having similar combat and trial-and-error stuff as Fromsoft's game is one thing, but the devs really understood what makes people love Fromsoft's games the most. The art direction was great, the bosses were fun, the soundtrack was beautiful, and they made some really likable characters. Really good progression system and gameplay mechanics, they gave a lot of ways to tackle stuff, although I don't think I ever used the wish cubes much besides the regen one a few times early on. Legion arms were great, and being able to use 2 of them in endgame was really nice. Of course I don't think the game is perfect. Heavy weapons definitely feel a little harder to work with when it came to charge attacks. With the game relying heavily on using a charge attack to stagger an enemy, its definitely hard to even get one off in some bosses. I mitigated this problem using the saw blade blade + booster glaive handle for most of the game - having the gap closer with the handle and the blade's long reach didn't make this as much of an issue. I think the parry system was fine, I complained about it at first being used to Sekiro and all, but it definitely did click. But the final boss (of the true ending) second phase did get me complaining again.Optimization was really damn good too, I run with a 2070 Super and a Ryzen 5 3600 and I never crashed once. Stutters every now and then, but otherwise was running at a very stable 120FPS. Very welcome, considering other AAA releases these days.Overall a really really good game, I had a lot of fun. Definitely worth the full price tag, and I look forward to the sequel the studio has foreshadowed in the ending I got.

_childDocuments_.review: Best non-Fromsoft 3D Soulslike but a comfortable margin (yes, including the new LOTF in my opinion).Great looking, polished & bug free, satisfying combat, great world and story. The story unravels in that slightly hidden way that souls games usually do, but actually is a lot more coherent and followable, which I personally appreciate.Combat is similar to Sekiro, with a bit of Bloodborne thrown in. Some Souls fans that hated Sekiro might not like this style on that much but it really clicked with me. There is also a weapon system which involves switching the blades and handles of weapons around and it's absolutely inspired and creates fantastic variety and allows a lot of creativity in how you play (a major shortcoming of Sekiro).The game has a few minor flaws, much of which has been addressed already by the makers, even if not implemented yet. It's clear a lot of care has gone into this game. The few negative points that aren't fixed, or about to be, are:The game is quite linear so if you love the exploration element of souls games it's perhaps a bit lacking versus others but I almost prefer that and it didn't bother me at all. I can see it bothering some though.I feel like the rage attacks aren't fleshed out in the way they are in Sekiro. Similarly to Sekiro you can't dodge the rage attacks but in Sekiro there is always another counter, either mikiri counter a thrust (which is the most satisfying game mechanic ever) or jump over a sweep, both resulting in big punishes. The only way to counter a rage attack in Lies of P is to parry the ability perfectly, which in itself made the timing hard to learn. The punishes you get for parrying the rage attacks are relatively minor and I found surviving the rage attacks was often the key to winning the fight, meaning the best way to avoid the attacks was often to run away, which isn't great.Lastly, some of the bosses were a bit frustrating. They were hard and you had to learn them properly, which I loved. However, there are far too many bosses that had 2nd phases that were entirely different bosses, meaning you had to fight your way through an entire difficult boss, just get destroyed immediately and learn a tiny element of phase 2 over and over. Also, few too many multi target fights for my liking but they were largely well done to be fair.Those are pretty minor gripes all in all and it's one of my favourite games that have come out in a long while. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is almost a perfect souls style action game! I Wish STEAM would include a MIXED option for Recommendations.  The story, lore, atmosphere, art style, graphics and sound all are excellent. The character leveling and attributes are kind of weird in my opinion and somewhat confusing but... whatever, not a deal breaker.The combat in this game is fun against the standard run-through enemies.. but it's the Boss fights where this game falls apart. The boss fights and mini boss fights are HORRIBLE. I didn't find any of them to be fun and honestly the rewards didn't seem to be all that great. The player character reaction time is too slow, blocking and dodging is very difficult and you can't roll out of the way. I also found my character getting pinned between an enemy and the level objects (furniture, wall, ect.) Your character constantly gets staggered and knocked out of the attack animations.  Boss/ MiNI Boss fights just feel so bad, unfair and pissed me off. Then to add even more insult to injury.. Almost every boss is a dual stage,  which I personally hate. Sometimes it's ok because it adds the element of surprise... but in this game it's just way over done. Many of  the powerful enemies also have delayed attacks which make it very difficult to time the dodge, then combine that with very tiny dodge window... just makes a lot of the encounters not fun and aggravating.Recommendations for combat.. Dodging or rolls should cancel your attacks while potentially costing some FP or stamina. Give the ability to avoid attacks without being limited to Perry system. Once you have started an attack, you are committed to attack, then boss/larger enemy begins their attack, which is faster then your attacks, knocks you out of your attack, cancels your attack, you take damage and can't get out of the way because you started an attack. and the cycle continues all throughout the game.As of patch 1.2 I would give this a 7/10. If some of the issues I already mentioned were to be addressed then I would probably give this game an 8 or a 9.

Once you learn enemy attacks, it becomes manageable, but it'll still throw you off frequently. _childDocuments_.review: I really would have loved to have played this game on release day, i want to imagine this review would been different. I've heard so many good things about Lies of P, from it being "better than any other from software game" or even people saying it's "Sekiro 2" I must say we've played different games if you think that. I came with very high expectations to be honest, the game is not bad, I even agree with the first statement, there are certain design decisions in this game that I hope From Soft will copy for the next installments of Sekiro and Dark Souls, but there are so many other decisions that I find pitiful and ruined my experience. To begin with I don't understand why people call this Sekiro, there is literally no point of comparison between the two, in Sekiro the fights are a constant dance between you and your enemy where you do parry's to break the enemy's stance, every attack is telegraphed to the millimeter, every move designed to work with the Wolf's way of fighting, I came to Lies of P with this mentality of making parrys to the enemies but unlike the 2 last final bosses is relatively unnecessary I would even say that it is not even the way this game is intended to be played. In Sekiro you're always looking to have control over the combat and always be in a "safe" position if that makes any sense. Lies of P turns this system upside down and gives you a Risk-Reward type of system, instead of looking to be safe you are always looking to give that "last hit" to the enemy to either recover extra health or to charge up your estus vial. I certainly found counterproductive to parry enemies and bosses when it's easier to dodge, get behind the enemy and attack.The boss design is bad, not very memorable and half of them are monsters or giant puppets that have the same attack pattern, three strong attacks and a jump, some of them change having an elemental pasive but beyond that, only the last boss and Laxasia are the most relevant of the game and tbh they're not that challenging, and here is a thing that i HATE about the bosses in this game its the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ second phases, every single ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boss have a second phase, i wouldnt hate this if phases where consistent between them, but no, the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ big puppet boss evolves in to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ small femboy with really fast attacks. Level desing is very linear and most of it is just the developers copying everything good that from soft do on their games, its shameless how Dark souls this game feels, everything from opening doors to how the camera tilts in cinematics, its just from software, the only thing that this game do diferent its that you kill puppets and to be honest i love the puppets desing and kark or however the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ city is called, but the second part of the game is just resident evil 4 fighting zombies and out of nowhere some "alchemists cult" join the game? i was expecting that everything in the game would be robots and the steampunk atmosphere but that just tilt in to monsters of flesh, quite weird but ok. To end my review this games make 2 really good things different from the from soft games, the risk-reward system of fighting and the quarts upgrades that are just the sekiro system of leveling up, other than that its a mid souls game with really bad boss desings. (i dont even mention story on my review because i just skipped every single dialogue since in souls game the way npc's talk are just so obnoxious its not even fun trying to follow any kind of story, they should have tried to do it differently, but nah)

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely souls-like, perhaps one that does not spend effort in innovating as much as it does refining and distilling the beloved elements of the genre. The player is equipped with the hugely powerful perfect block mechanic from Sekiro, reasonable i-frames on a step-dodge, and a balanced blocking system that rewards confidence and tempered aggression. The story is engaging and, thank god, not hidden behind item descriptions, loading screens, or (needlessly) missable npc engagements. The game is a blessing for the FOMO player in all of us, with reminders and visual indicators for optional npc questlines. The bossfights have short respawn approaches and fair health bars. I found the movesets of many enemies to be less fluid and intuitive than Sekiro; the first experiences with most enemies that couldn't be stunned lock resulted in needless damage taken or death. I do consider this a flaw, but not an insurmountable one. It is only as much a flaw as you are unenthusiastic to die and try again. In my experience, the game is fun and tight enough that a handful of deaths in the process of improvement didn't bother me any.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game! Having finished it just moments ago, I must state with absolute certainty that Lies of P is everything and more that a fan of the soulslike formula would thoroughly enjoy. Everything from art direction to musical score is a tantalizing treat for the player. If you are a fan of games like Sekiro, look no further than Lies of P.From start to finish, Lies of P masterfully envelopes the player in a dark fantasy retelling of the classic tale of Pinocchio from which it draws its inspiration, with unique twists and turns of its own. Embark in the city of Krat that has been utterly ravaged by the onslaught of an event known as the puppet frenzy as you fight your way through the mechanized terrors that lurk around every streetcorner. What madness could have caused such death and destruction? And what other secrets could such a once prosperous city truly hold? Only you can find out should you endeavor to take up arms and fight your way to the truth.

_childDocuments_.review: I was buying this game to get a discount Fromsoft game, but what I found instead was truly special in ways I did not expect.Lies of P wears its inspirations on its sleeve, so it is easy to assume that many people who think about buying the game (and reading this review as a result) want to play something like Bloodborne and are contemplating if they should buy this one.This review is for people like that. I have 100%ed every FromSoft game including Bloodborne, so the described experience might be completely different for a new player to the genre.Let's cut to the chase - I think Lies of P is a much better game than Bloodborne. Before you leave a clown award on this review, please give me a moment to explain.Before we start, it is important to note that I absolutely love Bloodborne. But, in my opinion, people really tend to overhype it for what it is. The main game Bloodborne has 2 or 3 good bosses with literally every other boss being "strafe right hit R1". Bosses like Paarl died without me even understanding what just happened. Lies of P avoids this issue completely, and nearly every single boss (with a single exception, looking at you Chapter 10 gang) feels amazing to fight.It scratches the same itch as good Sekiro bosses do. You get into this flow state where you can parry attack after attack and it just feels incredible. Bosses in Lies of P rarely die on a first attempt. Game really demands you to learn the attack pattern of each boss and perform well throughout the whole fight.If you are a newer player I think Bloodborne will be a much better starting point. Lies of P is rough. I would even go as far as to say that this is the hardest souls-like game I’ve ever played. But as usual, you have your options. Summoning NPCs to draw boss aggro away, using absolutely busted throwables, or a shield-hand will make the experience a ton easier if you are looking to tone down difficulty a notch.While the level design in Bloodborne might be less linear, it kinda feels homogenized to me. The entirety of Yahrnam just feels the same, I can't name any non-DLC area that isn't a city or a forest. At the same time each area in Lies of P feels distinct to me. It might be more linear, but level design is equally as great. A bunch of nooks and crannies to explore, secrets to find and shortcuts to open.One of the biggest issues I have with Bloodborne that this game avoids is the lack of gameplay variety. Sure, trick weapons are cool and all, but not being able to change your build to try out new weapons funnels you into using just a couple of weapons during your entire playthrough. You don't get enough upgrade materials to upgrade some random weapon on a whim and play with it for a while.Both of these issues combined resulted in me playing the entirety of Bloodborne start to finish with a cane-whip thing because it felt like the most effective weapon at nearly all times. Sure, I might’ve found something better along the way, but I couldn’t risk spending precious upgrade materials to check out the weapon at its full potential. Lies of P is extremely generous with weapon upgrade materials but strikes a perfect balance where you wouldn’t be able to upgrade everything under the sun immediately either.While might not seem important, it’s the little things that add up during the playtime that decide your overall enjoyment of the game. For example, the fast travel system in Bloodborne is horrible, zones are split into different fast-travel objects with no images attached to names of locations, and sometimes it's infuriating to try and remember which place was which. I don’t even have to mention the fact that healing items not replenishing on rest.Lies of P, on top of improving everything I just mentioned also goes the extra mile by having a bunch of QoL stuff, like training dummies in the hub to check your weapon damage and movesets, tells you when a certain NPC wants to talk to you, and reminds you where you picked up that quest you just completed so you don't have to teleport around the entire game trying to remember who wanted this bottle of wine you just found.Both games have great stories, but I liked the story for Lies of P more. This point is completely subjective though, more so than everything else. Characters in Lies of P were interesting enough for me to come back to Hotel Krat to listen to what they had to say each time a new dialogue became available. There’s just something so magical about the Hotel, the music, the ambiance, I just can’t get enough of it.At this point it might sound like I just hate Bloodborne, but no, not at all. I think it was a brilliant game, but isn't a gift from gaming Gods that many people make it out to be.Is Lies of P without faults? Of course no. Some of the boss attacks aren't clearly telegraphed, the difficulty balancing can use more work. The endgame is rough with chapter 10's gank boss absolutely sucking and climbing the tower in the end being rather tedious. However, these issues don't stop the game from being absolutely fantastic in my opinion.Overall, I don't think most people would ever agree that this game is better than Bloodborne simply because of how iconic Bloodborne has become over the years. But for me Lies of P is so much more. Such a beautiful game, really didn't expect it to be this great when I was buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is definitely the best souls-like in a while. It has a LOT of mechanics, but it is not too overwhelming to get the hang of. In fact, I think every mechanic this game adds to the genre is very good and well executed. The story is pretty good, it's a very fun Pinocchio story with a steampunk Victorian backdrop. The characters are fairly engaging and have some good voice work, I really enjoyed talking to them and finding out their secrets. If a game can get me to stop skipping dialogue then it has done well in my eyes.The bosses are hard but not overly punishing in most cases. Some of the late game bosses, one in particular, have extra long attack combos that can feel very cheesy. I don't necessarily think this is a bad thing, as it forces you to watch out for these attacks and prepare yourself. Overall I loved this game, and as an avid fan of the Souls-like genre, I can say that this is my absolute favorite souls-like to date.
