_childDocuments_.review: This game is great. I've played a LOT of Soulslikes, and this is the first one that's gotten the actual feel of playing the character *right*. Most of these games, even the ones I like, don't have the right weight to the characters, it's either too floaty, or too heavy. Playing Lies of P feels perfect. The world design is excellent, the story is way better than I expected, and and actually makes the idea of Pinocchio Souls work unironically. Overall, this is the first Soulslike that actually carries its weight in conversation with FromSoftware's games.I've seen a lot of complaints about the difficulty, and it is hard, but like most good Soulslikes, that difficulty can usually be gotten around by changing up your build, using consumables, or upgrading your weapons. Personally, I found it about on the level of Bloodborne in difficulty, but your mileage may vary.A few nitpicks:- The ability to respec your character is hidden *very* late into the game. It's open immediately during NG+, but for NG, it's completely blocked off for ~70% of the game.- The true final boss is definitely overtuned. Specifically its second phase has way too much health. The devs have been going through and adjusting boss health, so I fully expect it will get nerfed at some point.- The game doesn't explain its weapon crafting system very well. You can combine the blade (damage type) and handle (moveset) of any normal weapons in the game, but each blade is only good at either slashing, or stabbing damage, and you'll dramatically lower your damage output if you combine a slashing blade on a stabbing handle, or vice-versa. This is fine in itself, but it's very easy to miss, or not understand the marker that tells you this.- The game is completely linear. There are no optional areas. That's disappointing, the sense of exploration, and finding cool hidden secrets is very important in games, and having optional areas to go explore when you're stuck on a main boss is important.Overall, this game is 100% worth your time. I'm looking forward to the follow-up teased at the very end of the game, and any other projects out of this studio.

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly solid game that looks, runs and plays beautifully, there is some strong albeit linear level design (which in and of itself isn't a bad thing per-say), the encounters within the levels are enjoyable and ask of the player to make meaningful moment to moment decisions. Really cool boss fights, weapons and locales, fun little secrets when you explore around and the story is a very interesting spin on the Pinocchio novel.The gameplay itself is very familiar if you've played these kinds of games before, however it has a strong sense of identity and brings great ideas to the table to genre conventions like visceral/critical/fatal attacks, weapon durability, weapon crafting in the form of handle and blade switching with very interesting movesets and specials in the form of fable arts, and a very satisfying parrying mechanic, just to name a few.All in all, a quality title, this is the best Soulslike game I've played not made by Fromsoftware, alongside Nioh. Congrats to Round 8 Studio and Neowiz on such a strong title.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I have played in last few years, and a brilliant achievement of its creators.I honestly had more fun with Lies of P than I had with Elden Ring, which is wild considering, that I considered Lies of P to be a gimmicky souls clone at first - but it very quickly has proven that it not only has its own identity, but that it even has a soul, as much as any video game can have one. + Visuals are great+ Music is great+ Enemy designs are memorable+ Boss fights are very challenging but (mostly) fair+ Worldbuilding is interesting+ Atmosphere is amazing+ Weapons are different enough from each other for me to want to experiment with many of themHonestly, the only major flaw that I can think of is that it is pretty obvious that developers had not enough time and / or money to fully polish last quarter of the game, as second to last chapter is the shortest in the game, and the last chapter is overly long, but it has the most boring visual design that can be found in this title, turning the last 2 hours of the game into a slog (outside of the amazing boss fights). I am really impressed with Lies of P - when its gets a DLC, I will buy this DLC, and when it gets a sequel, I will buy this sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is a fantastic soulslike, but you have to be willing to meet the game on it's terms and be willing to learn what it wants from you.The presentation in both the visual and audio department is great. The different environments you go to are unique, and fit the overall tone/atmosphere the game is going for. The music only ever positively adds to the experience; it is never annoying or out of place. The sound effects clearly communicate the games mechanics without being grating. I never experienced any issues with performance or crashes, but my pc is top of the line. There isn't a single complaint I can think of in this department.The story is interesting. It is much more direct in it's conveyance of character, world, and general plot than anything Fromsoftware has recently done. It isn't anything overly moving or outstanding, but it works well and serves it's purpose. It's side characters add somewhat to the plot but aren't anything major. Overall it doesn't stand out, but there's nothing wrong with it, and when compared to many other modern releases I much prefer this simple way of storytelling over something obnoxious, preachy, or outright meaningless.Now on to what I feel and have seen to be the greatest point of contention when it comes to this game. The gameplay. I have seen and heard many mentions of things such as "the dodge doesn't work" or "the perfect guard timing is too tight", and I couldn't disagree more. The intent for these defensive mechanics is pretty clear to me, and that is that the game is specifically designed around NOT having a one size fits all solution to it's defense. Moment after moment with this game I was rewarded for adapting my approach to defending against different enemies' offense and punished for trying to brute force with only one of the tools presented to me. Making use of the perfect blocks when attack sequences you are ready for come, dodging through attacks you are less prepared for, running and repositioning to bait out or strafe an attack, or deciding to take the recoverable damage on your block are all key parts of this game's defensive systems. The unique mechanics of legion arms and fable arts add some nice flair to the offense built around the use of light and heavy attacks to deal damage and build an enemy's stun. The bosses range from alright to masterworks. (Laxasia being my favorite, and the standard stalker battles being the weakest in my opinion)Overall Lies of P is an excellent game for fans of the genre still willing to learn, and looking for a unique challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: In the year 2023, amidst the release of many high-profile games, Game Director Choi Ji-Won, in collaboration with Neowiz and Round8 Studio, managed to deliver what, at first glance, appeared to be just another souls-like game. However, it turned out to be an incredible fantasy experience with just the right blend of detail and difficulty. Unlike other souls-like games, where the details can often be blurry, in this world, you can dive deeper into the story and understand the intricate strings being pulled behind the scenes. Below, I will rate various aspects of the game to provide a perspective.Gameplay: 8/10While I did enjoy the gameplay and found it quite engaging, the difficulty progression seemed slightly off. There were times when I faced tougher challenges earlier in the game rather than in the later stages. Additionally, I encountered an unusual occurrence that may have been a bug. In one of the later stages, an NPC asked me to check on another NPC's well-being. However, upon reloading the stage, the worried NPC appeared lifeless near the troubled NPC, while back at their initial location, they behaved oddly, lacking the usual human-like talking animations. I'm not sure if this was intentional or a bug.Graphics and Visuals: 10/10In my honest opinion, the world is beautifully crafted and exceeded my visual expectations.Story and Narrative: 8/10Inspired by Carlo Collodi's 'The Adventures of Pinocchio,' the game gracefully adapts this source material into a souls-like design. However, from a gameplay perspective, some actions can lock you out of necessary collectibles for achievements. While not immersion-breaking, it can be somewhat irksome.Audio and Sound: 10/10The audio and sound design went above and beyond my expectations. I'm disappointed that the original soundtrack isn't available on any music platforms, despite my efforts to find it.Level Design and Environments: 7/10I appreciated the visual aesthetics and pathways; however, some designs felt overly defensive, as if the game wanted to prove its toughness. While I enjoy a challenge, and I understand it's a souls-like game, there's no reason for one boss fight arena to be smaller than most of the areas I explored before it.Controls and User Interface: 10/10If there's one key takeaway for other souls-like games from this IP, it's the excellent transparency between quests and the main storyline. I never felt lost during a side quest, and I didn't need to consult a guide to complete them.From this point on, I will refrain from assigning numerical scores, as I believe these aspects shouldn't be rated.Replayability:For me, there isn't much incentive to replay the game after completing everything it has to offer. However, there might be potential for unique multiplayer or DLC in the future, which could change this aspect. For now, enjoy the story and conquer the bosses in your own way.Difficulty and Learning Curve:As with any souls-like game, there's a learning curve, and it may take some time to get used to it. The parry window is smaller than in other titles, and there isn't a gauge to predict enemy stagger. My advice is to always be ready to roll away, and when the enemy starts glowing, hit them with a Shot Put from a safe distance. Later in the game, there's also a vendor who sells any desired amount.Game Length and Content:It took me 76 hours to complete the game and experience everything it had to offer. However, for those of you who are solely interested in the story and gameplay, I would estimate a happy medium of 40-50 hours. I eagerly anticipate additional content such as DLCs, or perhaps even another sequel (fingers crossed).That's a wrap on my two cents. I hope you consider giving this game a shot!

_childDocuments_.review: ---note my review is bias due to my experience with dark souls games/franchise.---Put very simple: Awesome story, Extremely soul-like and I mean that in a good way. I'm a big fan of the dark and twisted spin they put on the well known story of pinocchio. The new story really adds to the experience as it let's you enjoy the soul-like gameplay in a refreshing new way. So in a sense, you get to enjoy 2 things at the same time that is old already known, (the story of pinocchio and soul-like gameplay), and experience them as brand new. Therefor, I would rate the story and gameplay as following:Story: 8,5/10    Gameplay: 9/10 The story and Gameplay gets a -1 due to some aspects of the game design which leaves me a bit wanting. The story also gets a -0,5 from me since, while it was great it was not perfect. Simply put without spoilers I wanted a bit more details/story telling than what we got. The ending was really good but a bit more elaboration further onto the climax/plot twist would have been very nice.Game design: 7/10-1: If you are a hardened soul-franchise player like me, this game is rather easy. Only the optional final boss was a bit of a challenge. Also, the game is too forgiving with checkpoints. Meaning, in dark souls you usually have to fight your way through a range of enemies to reach a boss, and then fight the boss with what ressources you have left from your last checkpoint. However, in this game you will almost always recieve a checkpoint right at the entrance to the boss.-1: You can only customize your appearance cosmeticly, meaning you don't get varies sets of armor to choose from and select in slots like head, body, arms and legs. You do though get many different and cool full body costumes to choose from with 2 slots beside the full body, hat/mask and face(glasses and such).-1: There is pretty much no way to fight ranged. There is no archery or magic in this game, which means you can only fight as a melee class. There are different melee fighting styles though, but all in all I miss a bit more variety to choose from.Summary:All in all, I really enjoyed this game and I can't wait for the DLC and sequel. Very excited for what comes next.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very very hard, even for souls veterans. You may not finish this game even if you have played a lot of Fromsoft titles.I've played every Fromsoft title since demons' souls and, aside from Sekiro, they always give you a way to "adjust" the difficulty based on what kind of experience you want. Even Armored Core 6 does it.This game does not do that. This game is closer to Sekiro in that it is pretty brutal and you will not be able to cheese anything. You have to learn the boss, you have to bring the right tools, and you have to learn the mechanics. Bloodborne and Sekiro had a baby and that baby is a pissed off eldritch horror ninja about to throw you out the window with its little baby arms.The parry window is very tight (closer to souls than Sekiro) and multiple parries in a row are required on bosses. Many. Think 5-12 on some bosses (with varied rapid timing or even needing to look for different strings of attacks that start the same).Some mechanics you might need (such as dodging off the ground after getting flattened) are locked behind an upgrade system. You also can't respec your character until you finish chapter 7, which could be pretty hard to do if you made a terrible character.Upgrade materials are pretty reasonable. You can buy an unlimited number of them up to certain stopgaps. This means you can experiment with different handles/blades as you see fit and not worry about not having enough materials (unlike elden ring, where you get most of the bells really late in the game).Weapon damage type and element type matter. Therefore, it's a good idea to learn more than one weapon so you can handle different enemy and boss types. You could also just use a single weapon the entire time, but you may have some fights that are absolutely brutal as a result. Make sure your weapon's blade works with your hilts attack type. If you're stabbing with a hammer, it's going to do very little damage.Take it easy. This game could be "too hard" for your patience level and that's okay. No one cares if you beat it or whatever and you aren't lesser if you can't finish something.Some point form about some non combat stuff:- Story has been good, if not a little predictable. But being told the obvious stuff after you already figured it out is annoying. I'd prefer if the exposition was just left out of dialogue entirely but hey, different strokes for different folks.- The world is pretty awesome. A lot of the environments are great to look at, especially some of the indoor ones. Lots of variety as well.- Levels are quite linear with some side paths and the usual shortcut love. I honestly enjoy that type of level design and am over the "open world and 40 paths that all have items down them" design that is in a lot of games lately.- Player expression seems good, other than needing to choose between guard (if using big weapons) and parry (all weapons will need to do this at least sometimes). The dodge is actually better than its given credit for, but parry is super important for getting the boss off your back. Everything else about how you fight is pretty fluid.- Weapon selection is very good because there are a good chunk of them and then handle/blade swapping just increases that number by a ton. Although, the items that change scaling could be a little more aggressive to complement handle/blade combinations better. It's hard to use a Motivity handle with a light blade and try to scale it off of Technique or Advance, for example. Advance has this problem more than the other two stats because the blade also needs to have an element on it to scale off of the handle's Advance stat. I'd recommend a balance build (even Motivity and Technique) or an advance build (change element/damage type based on what you're fighting) for a first playthrough because those will give you the best options for when you run into a wall.- Music is great. Some of the "record" songs are just beautiful selections. My personal favourite was the song that was in the demo: "Feel".- Has a little too much of the "you go for one guy and there's a guy hidden on the side" gag that you see in souls games.- It feels good to control your character. They feel nimble and powerful.- Costumes are fun. They also don't affect your stats so you can look however you like. That's always great.- I can hold a stable 120 FPS in a souls-like, which is a very pleasant feeling after playing Elden Ring, where I was struggling to keep a consistent framerate.- The game doesn't feel unfinished, like a lot of games these days. It feels pretty dang polished. I've had zero crashes or bugs. The worst thing I've seen is a ragdolled enemy clipping in the wall and freaking out a bit, which it then stopped doing after a second.Give it a go if you like hard games. Watch someone else play it if you don't. Buy the game if you want to support or play it. Either way you're voting with your wallet about the types of games that are being made.

_childDocuments_.review: My time with Lies of P was exactly the intense and gratifying experience I hoped for. As one who holds Bloodborne in the highest regard as one of From Software’s finest achievements, I was absolutely enamored with Round 8 Studio’s unique, clever take on the formula. While the game broadly functions similarly to the best the souls-like genre has to offer, Lies of P‘s tweaks and refinements are so masterfully planned out and implemented that they make every moment of gameplay a pleasure. From the dopamine hits provided by exploring the labyrinthine level layouts, to the extreme delight of finally besting a challenging boss, there’s nary a moment of Lies of P‘s meaty campaign that feels wasted or unsatisfactory. With a post-credits teaser hinting at a second incredible twist on another literary classic lying in wait, the future looks bright for this new addition to the genre.Lies of P, welcome to the top!

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone here like Bloodborne?Jokes aside, Lies of P has been shaping up to be a very interesting and challenging game. If you're into Souls-likes and whatnot, you know what you're here for. It's pretty tough at certain points, but finally making it out of the other side of a boss fight with the W still feels awesome and cathartic. I think my only real complaints so far are that character respecs take like 20 hours to get to, so I hope you're down for whatever you bumbled your build into, and that the chip damage you take when blocking feels way way too punishing if you ask me. Beyond that, the game has been incredibly solid. The aesthetic and themes are fun, the game actually runs pretty amazingly well, and it fixes some of the longstanding issues involving quests that From Software's Souls games have always had in terms of their obtuseness. This game even manages to make a group boss fight be pretty good.---Beat the game today. It's great! Advance stat builds are a little short on options, but I guess that's the price you pay for exploiting weaknesses and stuff. Lots of fun-ass weapons and gear land in your hands throughout the game that make New Game+ an enticing option.

_childDocuments_.review: Update 2: Heavy weapons are still the hard mode in this game. But for a first entry into soulslike games from this developer, the game is excellent.Lies of Pie is a competent souls-like. The setting is unique, the atmosphere is great and graphics are good. The story seems to be your run-of-the-mill robot (puppet) uprising and is told via some NPCs and lore notes you can pick up on the way.The levels are kind of linear with few shortcuts to be unlocked. Enemy variety is okay.Character progression is your standard souls game. There are weapons, talismans and equipment (armor) slots. Your character can also equip different costumes only changing your appearance.The combat is obviously the main focus for the standard souls player. It's stamina based. You have your weapon with strong/charged and light attacks in your right hand and a variety of arms with unique attacks or tools in your left. There are combat comsumables too. You either block, dodge or parry. Blocking damage will depending on your weapon negate a percentage of the damage you receive. Health can be reclaimed by instantly attacking in a small time frame after getting damaged. Dodging will obvioulsy completely negate damage but uses Stamina.The game is pushing you into parrying enemies. If you perfect parry your enemy you might break its weapon and you might get them into a vulnerable state, where it is susceptible to poise break, enabling you to land a critical hit. This system would be fine, but the parry has a weird timing to it. There seems to be a small delay to it. You might think, you parried fine and still get damaged. Combine this with the choppy movement of most early enemies and this can get frustrating. Minor gripe: I really don't like, how you need to use a charged attack to make use of the enemies vulnerable state. If you are facing an aggressive opponent you might have perfect parried them but won't be able to stagger them because you won't get a charged attack in. Kind of negates you the reward for getting those parries in.There is no stealth but you can get backstabs if the enemy hasn't noticed you. Backstabs sometimes work during a fight but there is no real consistency on when you can or cannot backstab.All in all Lies of P is a decent game. If you are looking for a new souls game you won't be disappointed. If you hate Denuvo you obviously skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game, please do not listen to the people spouting the terrible opinions about it. I give it a solid 9/10 and deem it "must play" for anyone that enjoys these types of games. I urge the developers to beware of trying to appease the people complaining about certain difficulty aspects of the game. Don't lose your identity by chasing a larger audience. Just continuing improving on your game and the sale will continue to come. Some feed back from me personally: some weapon types could stand to see some improvements, particularly the more nimble weapons especially during boss fights. The issue I encountered frequently was they simply cant compete with the larger heavier hitting weapons in terms of effectiveness due to the additional chip damage you take when blocking attacks and the fact that you are frequently pushed out of range when blocking to get any significant punishes off even when perfect guarding efficiently. On top of that, the lower attack rating makes it require more perfect guards to break poise of the the attacker. All these factors combined just means you have to perfect guard more often, are punished far more heavily when you miss it due to additional chip damage and when you're counter attacking you do less damage. I would like to see additional benefits bestowed on these weapons to close the gap between them and the large weapons for a better variety of viable options to choose from during these excellent boss fights. A great start is making the parry fable arts for the weapons more instantaneous (far less wind up) but in exchange it should cost fable arts meter weather you land it or not, and perhaps make it cost more fable arts meter so builds that focus on this play style also have to use quarts more heavily on fable arts meter upgrades rather than increasing their cell charges putting emphasis on on precision but offering big pay offs if you master it. Like if you made the fable arts for these weapons more powerful and made most of them reliable gap closer combo starters options that can be used during combat rather than a heavy handed stagger punish that takes a aot of time to complete (which most are) this would give this weapon class a different identity from the slow methodical play of block and punishing that the larger weapons offer and accelerate at.

_childDocuments_.review: To sum up my thoughts… Lies of P is the best game I have played in the last couple of years. The only experiences I can think that rival the time I have had with this game are playing Outer Wilds for the first time, and that legendary first play through of Elden Ring. That isn’t saying Lies of P is without fault, but if you are a fan of soulslike games - or just games with fair difficulty, an interesting and engaging world, and a beautiful soundtrack - it is hard not to recommend Lies of P. I will now go in-depth on several different aspects of the game including Story, Combat/Gameplay, MISC, and the Completion Experience. There will be minor spoilers for what the game contains, but I will not go into any specifics that would ruin your experience. Soulslikes are often known for having confusing stories that are often up for your own interpretation – this game is not quite like that. There is a fairly straightforward plot to follow, and while it is not spoonfeed down your mouth, I did not find myself rushing to YouTube to watch a lore summary after beating the game. Speaking of the story itself, this game is a twisted interpretation of the Pinocchio tale. If you’re a fan of the story then there are a lot of fun easter eggs to pick up on, but for the most part you don’t need any knowledge coming in. The characters and plot are fairly interesting, but this isn’t quite on the same level as something like God of War or Red Dead Redemption. It did keep me engaged enough though to want to read any of the little lore notes scattered throughout the game, as those provide some additional context to what is going on in Krat. Overall, I was happy with the story Lies of P provided. Some of the character questlines nearly made me tear up and I am excited to see what is in store for this world.Lies of P is a hard game. It requires precision to parry correctly, it demands an understanding of each enemy and bosses moveset, and most importantly you need to stay determined. These are staples of the genre and Lies of P is no different. What separates this game from a lot of the other soulslikes though, is that this game is polished and refined to another level. Every encounter is balanced and the animation work makes it easy to tell what a boss is doing. Even fromsoftware struggles with this sometimes, but Lies of P nails it. There is only one boss in this game that is in my opinion “bad”. It is a gank fight where you can suddenly get pulled across the arena. Thankfully, the fight is not too hard and the rest of the boss roster ranges from good to f*****g amazing. Seriously, I am surprised by how solid this boss roster is.Your character also has access to many different forms of customization and progression. There is a skill tree, a leveling system, a weapon crafting system, a customizable flask, amulets, a sort of armor system, and even  a customizable prosthetic arm. These are all introduced at a reasonable pace, so I did not find myself getting overwhelmed by all the things I could tweak. The way your character controls is also solid, and each weapon feels good to use. These elements, combined with the great bosses, make Lies of P a challenging, but fair and rewarding experience.The only part of the gameplay I would say is weak is the level design. Don’t get me wrong, the levels look great! This game is linear though, with pretty much 0 optional areas. The levels themselves are designed fairly decently, with shortcuts that loop back on one another and plenty to discover within, but don’t expect to find entirely secret levels just by jumping into a painting of anything.The only thing I want to touch on here is the music. It goes hard. I don’t want to go into too much detail to avoid spoilers, but this game has a way of providing some beautiful tracks at certain moments that really helped me get immersed into the world. It’s something special.It took me around 50 hours to 100% this game. It does require at least 3 playthroughs to get all the different endings and collectibles. All of the collectibles items are fairly straight forward though. I will say that a decent amount are locked behind NPC quests, but this game does have a way of telling you when to talk to certain NPCs to progress their story. The quest lines themselves also are not too complicated and I was able to complete them all without a guide. My recommendation would be to play the game however you want on your first run, then look up a guide on anything you missed. It should be a fairly straightforward and fun experience, with the hardest part being just getting good enough to beat the game.Lies of P is my favorite game I have played this year. If upon watching the trailers you think this looks kind of fun and like something you might enjoy, I highly encourage you to check it out. Best of luck!P.S Feel free to friend request me on Steam if you want to keep up on my completionist journey!

_childDocuments_.review: So i finished my first playthrough of this game in 49 hours, but if you will play it, it will be probably something around 30-ish hours.Is the game worth it? ♥♥♥♥ yeah it is. It is easly one of the best souls-like games i've played (especially since this is a non-fromsoftware game), and i absolutely love it... and becouse of that i will tell you what i hate about it, but first i'll throw in that the story of the game is suprisingly good as well as the OSTs cause GOD are they beautiful.Now to what i hate about it the most (i thought there will be more, but i can only think of this one) are the bosses. Don't get me wrong, the bosses are pretty cool. They have mostly good design and good music. The issue here is how these bosses work. See, in Lies of P around 60-70% of big guys you'll have to face have the same pattern:Start the fight --> get to know the pattern of the boss you're fighting --> you killed him good job! now, ♥♥♥♥ you here is a second hp bar --> the boss is twice as fast now --> die and suffer through having to beat the same phase everytime which sometimes takes actually a long time.Some people say Gemini is annoying, i don't agree with it at all but then again it's subjective. The last thing i guess i can kind of say is something i dont like, or more a thing that is kind of a bummer, are the outfits. _childDocuments_.review: This game is way better than I initially thought it would be. It borrows most heavily gameplay wise from a mix of Bloodborne and Sekiro, and heavily rewards mastering either good dodge timing or parrying (not Dark Souls parry, Sekiro parry). The game runs really well, honestly better than most Soulsborne games do on release, I don't think I have EVER seen the framerate dip below 60 if I locked it to 60, or dip below 105fps if I locked it to 120. That alone is pretty impressive.Storywise, it's actually quite a bit more than "Pinocchio-Souls". Some say it has similarities to the original non-Disney fable, but I'm not up on that myself. The story has similar beats here and there to classic Souls territory (world's going to hell in a handbasket, you gain souls (Ergo) from killing things, big boss Ergo gives you boss weapons, level up lady (which I could do without), NPCs being either cryptic or giving you background lore). I actually found learning about the world quite enjoyable, and love some NPCs, like Venigni.Without spoiling, the story takes a few interesting turns, and makes some interesting references throughout, including a Sherlock Holmes reference and Oscar Wilde reference, fitting for a Baroque period game. The Baroque environments look gorgeous and the music is magnificent. It hits every point a From Software fan would want to see in a "Souls-like", while still doing its own thing story wise. If this game was not competing against some heavy hitters already, I'd genuinely consider it a contender for GOTY. At the very least if you like Souls-games, you should give it a try. I love every Soulsborne including Sekiro so I find this game to be an utter joy to play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does such a brilliant job of integrating the sekiro deflect mechanics with traditional souls combat; something promised in Elden Ring but not fully delivered beyond a generic stance break ability.Out of any souls game, this one allows me to approach fights absolutely however I'm most comfortable with. The entire game is playable with dodge rolling for example, although certain bosses will encourage certain combat styles, making it especially rewarding to master each system and recognise when to apply it. Better multi enemy fights than other Souls games, with good use of audio cues to help you understand what is going on off screen. Some super derivative bosses and movesets, but the aforementioned combat improvements make this less noticeable.Lots of world building is delivered in order to flesh out the world; and ensure the endings have impact. Throughout the game it is clear that your choices are going to make a difference at the end, although the ambiguity creates a lot of tension. I ended up not liking my ending very much but that was because my choices had backed me into a corner decision wise.The game feels very familiar, although progression is somewhat dated in comparison to combat - playing out more like DS2 with linear areas that don't necessarily transition smoothly, although lots of shortcuts and looping back in on yourself to enjoy. This isn't really a problem for me as the souls market is a little starved for linear level design at the moment. Areas are still for the most part memorable and distinct, although I would have liked the boss designs to be more representative of their arenas and the local enemies you fight before them., although I am still missing one boss. Planning to complete the achievements for this as I'm loving the experience.Now I have collected all the achievements for this game I'd like to slightly append my review.I got to experience the rise of P ending for one of them, which requires lots of thought surrounding the humanity system. I think this was a great choice and gets the player to interact with things they otherwise might not, like the piano. My final run took me just short of 5 hours which is a great tell of the quality of a souls game. Once you master all of the mechanics and routes this game can be ran very fast which I think is excellent.The story of this game is quite deep and am looking forward to it being expanded in the future. Certainly overall has to be a top 3 souls game for me, really just engaging mechanics used throughout that I will deeply miss when Elden Ring DLC finally releases. The parry, legion arm, fable art meter, health recovery system are all elements that just elevate the gameplay in this game well beyond almost every other game in the genre. It is of course beautiful and very thematic, while also being a solid length with a quality standalone story.

_childDocuments_.review: As an amateur player of Souls-like games, I find "Lies of P" to be a story-rich and authentic game, definitely catchy with a combat system forgiving for beginners. Same for those who prefer dodging or attacking from a distance with a big sword - you folks can too defeat bosses and progress through the storyline. My point is that this game is a good fit for both types of players and is highly recommended for those who enjoy interesting story plots."Lies of P" is among the top three best games of my 2023, and trust me, it will be a valuable addition to your Steam library.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game if you have appetite for a souls-like game. The level design is great and the side quests are also well designed. Other than that, it is your typical souls-game with all the frustrating elements, like you've got suicide dogs which alight itself on fire and explode in you vicinity, dogs with slashing tails and cone heads to pierce you, so have fun with that ♥♥♥♥. You can clearly see, right from the beginning, that this game takes a lot of inspiration from sekiro, bloodborne and dark souls. I do have some gripes about parrying and guarding. _childDocuments_.review: An 8/10 that COULD be a 10/10 with a single patch. Let me start with all the good: The atmosphere is GORGEOUS, the combat is SMOOTH and SATISFYING, the voice acting ranges from decent to amazing, the story and lore is deep and interesting, the NPCs are lovable, hatable, complex, and never boring (except for one NPC that kind of does nothing).And now for the big gripe I have with the game. The bosses seriously need another animation pass. The telegraphed attacks are downright abysmal in SOME cases. It's odd because there are some bosses that are perfect top to bottom. Telegraph their attacks juuust enough for you to survive. And then there are others that will hold an attack for whole seconds then you have approximately 4 frames to see when the attack is coming out. Oh you don't have 50ms reaction time? Nobody on this planet does. These poorly telegraphed attacks mean that instead of relying on reaction time and skill you are instead forced to do homework and memorize attack patterns (which still doesn't work because some attacks have 0 windup). Which is normally a fine thing to mastering a boss, but should not be a minimum requirement. I'm looking at you Fu, EB, KofP, and [Final Boss] (abbreviated for spoilers). Give us more bosses like Victor, GM, and Lax you knocked it OUT OF THE PARK with those three specifically.Also eat my puppet posterior if you say "skill issue" my favorite bosses were some of the hardest in the game. I love a hard boss, in fact I wish some of the bosses were harder, GM kicks ass but I beat it in one attempt. Same with TWL.Gripes aside, it's not an issue with the core game. This is something that could be patched in a few weeks. Just a few more frames of animation just before the attack comes out so these epic fights don't turn into frustrating slogs. Love this game, will probably do NG+ some time in the future, and I can't WAIT for the next game. You guys have real talent.

_childDocuments_.review: Who doesn't love a dark cynical Pinocchio Soul-Like? You'll rethink your life wondering if you too are just a mere puppet. But put those strings of worry aside Brother, for you shall break the commandments instilled in all puppets. You will lie. You will kill. You will die.When you find weapons you can break them into two pieces, blade and handle, and reassemble most into your own creations to make fun builds that cater to your style. _childDocuments_.review: Man, what an amazing game Lies of P is. Without a doubt, it’s the best non FromSoft Souls-like out there. The story is very good, the voice acting is excellent, level design is very carefully done and works very well, combat is very satisfying and breaking the enemies’ weapons never gets old. The visuals are also amazing, but I think one of the strongest points of this game is the music, which is simply amazing and breathtaking.My only two observations for this game are:1. It’s a linear game, and although there is some exploring to do and secrets to find, it is not very open. I personally don’t mind this very much, not every game has to be open world or have big areas to be good, I very much enjoyed the amount of exploration this game has to offer, but some people might find it a bit too linear. 2. The runback to some of the bosses’ arena. Luckily you can very easily ignore the enemies on the path, but you’re still going to waste some time going from the Stargazer to the arena, which can get boring. Not all bosses have this problem, but it is present enough that I feel the need to mention it.All in all, an amazing game that I can’t recommend enough! Neowiz made a fantastic game and I can’t wait to see what they come up with next time!

_childDocuments_.review: 8.7/10 - Fantastic-It's a shame that it's a set character, I always prefer to see a character creator. -Unfortunately the game comes together best in NG+ but NG is still quite good. Mostly owed to late-game rewards, such as final boss weapons and certain cosmetics making the game overall more enjoyable. This can also be considered a very fortunate thing as it means the reward structure pays out, and it gives you reasons to replay the game. -Combat is great, but I would have liked more fluidity for things such as swapping weapons and legion arms. As it stands the animation is slow and feels very clunky if you're not literally doing nothing else at the time, making it very difficult to effectively change tactics while in combat.-Puppet String is love, Puppet String is life. That thing will stop any mook enemy dead in their tracks and enable powerful jumping attacks with the potential to stagger even the burliest enemy types. The other Legion Arms are also pretty good for what they do, just not AS good.-A very small parry window makes it difficult, if not just annoying, to attempt to parry enemies with jittery and delayed attacks. Of which there are many, making the risk not quite equal to the reward in many cases. It can still be very effective and satisfying for bosses with more rhythmic attack patterns however.-Mostly solid to really good boss design. A lot of 2-phase bosses makes for encounters with a lot of meat on them. Most crucially it ends on a high note, with the final boss being the decidedly best in the game, something I can't recall happening since I played Sekiro.-A select few enemies are incredibly dumb and I hate every fiber of their stupid being(non-bosses). -Level design is competent, but there is a slight over-reliance on enemies sitting around in obscure corners waiting to ambush you and nigh-indistinguishable weak floorboards that constantly break away under your feet until you grow paranoid that every bridge or wooden path you see will self-destruct once you step on it.-Side-content such as character stories and treasure hunts are a good diversion from main progression and have satisfying rewards. There is a good amount of hidden treasure in each level to keep you curious and alert to anomalies in your surroundings. A much better motivator than aforementioned ambushes and floorboards.-Waifu is cute. Wholesome. Must protecc.-Side-kick Gemini is a stand-up guy and mildly amusing, managing not to be overbearing or plain annoying.-Setting and aesthetic is neat, though the choice of puppet enemies can make combat frustrating at times. And though it's a small part of the overall plot "World Expo Gone Wrong" is a cool hook. -There was never any reason why the "drop your exp/currency" mechanic should have out-lived the Demon's/Dark Souls series, but I guess it's what everyone does nowadays... so, that's okay I guess?

_childDocuments_.review: What better place to start then by saying this is without a doubt the best game you can currently find within the souls-like genre. After almost 100 hours and after almost finishing my second playthrough, it still blows my mind how perfectly Neowiz seemed to have studied what made Souls games so captivating and rewarding for thousands of players. If you are a fan of this genre, this should be an absolute must-play and is well worth the price. However, if you are simply looking for an action game with a good story and some RPG elements, you might be turned off by this game. Not because this game doesn't have a a great and nuanced story with detailed worldbuilding and a polished combat system that encourages diversity (which it absolutely delivers); but because the difficulty curve is one of the highest I have experienced so far in games. Although this game does offer some opportunities to lower the difficulty of bosses and area traversal (e.g. overpowered throwing items, NPC summons for bosses, low levelling cost), Neowiz takes the same approach of player perseverance that linear games like Sekiro adopt. Particularly in the early-game, this can be frustrating and off-putting for players, as many enemy attacks are quite punishing. I admit that I was put off by the game's oddly small window for successful parries and a seemingly disproportionate level of risk for the amount of reward you get for these individual actions when I had played the demo. You could absolutely interpret this as a fault of the developers and I would be hard-pressed to defend these developmental choices, but nonetheless I still purchased the full game and persevered throughout the rest of the game. And you know what? It was genuinely really fricking fun! That's it, that's the end of the review lol. Though I could delve into more detail, it wouldn't really add to the overall message I'm trying to get across with this review.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Bosses are cool but become tedious really quickly. At first it was hard, and then a learning curve, and then "Okay parry these 6 attacks in a row before I can land 1 hit." It felt good for a while. I've played all the Souls games and Sekiro, so I know the drill. I'm using a greatsword for fun and for better block if I whiff a parry, for reference. I feel like parrying has yielded better results for downing bosses, but it still feels unsatisfying as a gameplay loop. (Sekiro did involve parrying a lot as well, and I don't intend to compare them. With that said, it did feel satisfying to parry a combo in Sekiro, and just doesn't in this game)Now when I see a boss gate, I don't think "Oh cool, a new boss! This'll be sick!! :)!" I think "God, I'm going to have to memorize the parry timings for another 3-hit combo, three 2-hit combos, and a 5-7-hit combo plus red attacks before I have a chance." I genuinely don't feel like finishing the game, it seems like chores or eating vegetables instead of a fun time. The combat is fun, and the zones I have played through have been fun. It's a cool world to explore with neat little side-quests. I may still continue after writing this, but as of now it's not even frustrating, the bosses just got boring due to how over engineered they feel. When I do beat the boss after taking the time to memorize everything, I feel good, but the next time I see a boss gate I lose my appetite to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid. 8/10. Can't compete with From Software though. Too many bosses have status affects like shock, decay, etc. There are also many more instances where there will be a cheeky enemy placed around a corner to knock you off of a ledge or something. Enemies have a TON of poise, which makes the game feel less responsive to your attacks. Getting the white bar to stagger an enemy always felt inconsistent. LOTS of the same enemy throughout the game, would've loved to see more variety. Killed about 2000 robot butlers with a candelabra or a robot cop with a bully-club. Don't like the timer when deciding to lie or tell the truth. Since there are so many achievements attached to your answers, it would be nice to be able to pause the conversation and look up which answer you need to choose. Loved the P-Organ, loved that the game shows you when an NPC wants to speak, loved that large enemies would often drop something worth it like quartz or a new item. The story was better than expected. Overall, it is definitely worth playing, but only after you've played demon souls, dark souls 1-3, sekiro, bloodborne, and elden ring. _childDocuments_.review: I took my time with this game, to complete almost all of the things it has to offer. I cannot recommend this game in the current state. Although I have reached the end, this game is way too hard in a bad way. The parry mechanics are not great and the parry window is too tight. Weight management in game is atrocious, having to dump stat points into capacity when leveling up is an awful design. Mini bosses are sometimes harder than bosses, which is not an issue when there is one, but multiple swarming you and stunlocking to death is just lame.Game also insists on bosses having two phases where phase two is ten times harder than phase one. I get that it is cool, but overdoing it isn't. Elden ring had a perfect sweetspot.Game insists on parry mechanics, dodging will mostly harm you. For a game that does that, it is very strange that when parrying, weapon durability drastically decreases. To increase it mid fight (when fights are longer, two phase) takes time, time enough to be stunlocked to death. That is just a quality of life thing which would help.The game started good, but went downhill very fast, right around the cathedral boss (not to spoil, people playing it will know).All in all, it has potential, hopefully developers listen to the majority of the feedback around parrying and overdoing the boss fights.

_childDocuments_.review: I try to avoid spoiling anything as much as possible and vaguely touch on a few outside of a location name drop.  I had some free time and really enjoyed this game so I decided to write a review which I'm not really the greatest at.  If you just want the somewhat insightful bits then you can probably skip the first section and skim the others because I don't think I can extract a detailed tl;dr - though I have one at the bottom if you really want to skip the review just look at the thumbs up.•A word of cautionThis is a game I'd probably recommend a stranger to the genre not touch (unless you are very patient and are willing to throw yourself at the wall of difficulty until you get better). My reasoning is it is very punishing to fail to dodge or miss a block - especially a perfect block - and that the game does not really provide non-frustrating opportunities to learn how to do so.  Puppets are harder to read telegraphs from and some of the later 'elite mobs' are a test of your ability to whittle them down.  There are a few wake up calls where you will be suddenly forced to improve your skill.  But don't let me stop you from trying.•Comparison(s) to other games in the same genre.If I had to pick two games to directly compare them to it'd be Sekiro (perfect blocking and the arm gadget) and Bloodborne (fast paced, health recovery revenge system) but that doesn't accurately respect Lies of P as it has its own perfect mix of mechanics inspired from both titles.  It is worth giving this game an open mind in regards to learning mechanics.  Which is odd considering I think the skills you would learn from Sekiro and Bloodborne will help you in the long run but would also probably interfere with your ability to initially interact with the special mix that Lies of P implemented.  Very few enemies are really "unfair" in how they attack you but the ones that are can still be beaten.•My experience (Generalizing my build and my thoughts on it).I went through the game as an advance (elemental) damage build, but my main stat was actually capacity due to how your defense stats are set up in the form of puppet parts and every new find is heavier and heavier, and that the more weight percentage you have the slower you actually move and recover stamina. Fair warning you get the short end of the stick in return for easy access to elemental damage statuses which there is one for each type of enemy in the game.  The amount of weapon handles that actually have advance scaling on them is far and few between and if you put a weapon head on an advance scaling handle that does not have elemental damage on it then you get screwed - and vice versa (elemental blade on standard scaling handles).  There is one exception in the form of an electric weapon with a mechanic tied to the blade itself where it powers up the electric portion of your damage by landing hits up to four times for a short duration if you don't land another hit.  In my opinion there is a clear winner among the handles because it has a very fast thrust combo that has decent range as well as high advance scaling.  I preferred faster weapons with a medium reach overall.  I legit couldn't beat one boss because of the length of my weapon at one point and when I changed handles I did it in one fresh go.  Did not really try motivity (strength) and slower swinging weapons (Yoinked the blade off any I did try, love the disassemble system btw).  I did a quick experiment with elemental buff items and came to the conclusion that they are not influenced by your stats or weapon handle scaling tier.•Can you change your build / NG+?Yes, there is a respec but it is relatively late into the game.  The room is near the end of the Grand Exhibition.  It has individual options for your Level, Legion arm(s) and P-organ.  This costs gold coins that you can passively farm off a tree you get early-mid game so I recommend keeping at eye on harvesting these.  After completing the game I respecced out of Advance (elemental) and went into Technique (Dex) for a change of pace.  NG+ offers you an early unlock of the respec area and you get to keep your access to the coin tree.  I haven't done much of my NG+ run but the game so far has scaled roughly to my available stats.•Misc comments.The collectible vinyls for the gramophone (music) in the hotel are kind of insane in quality.  All but one that I have personally found have all be pleasant to listen to.The AI boss helper is honestly kind of dumb and will likely get rocked by the boss before it does anything meaningful unless you go out of your way to keep it alive or somehow stagger the boss and create a period of time where you both go all out.  However this dumb little helper has actually made the difference in a few fights where I'd otherwise have to learn how to properly counter certain moves.Some of the writing for the important parts of the story I experienced rubbed me the wrong way but didn't outright ruin anything expect for one, which I cannot go into specific detail due to how spoiler-y it is.  I thought the choice I made could've had been handled differently instead of how it actually happened just because of how another NPC implied that maybe there was something but it was actually nothing.  I walked in, made a choice, then walked out the way to go and that was literally it.  Maybe I should've thought a little harder about the weight of my choice but I really did not like the commentary from the NPC sort of playing with my expectations.Some legion arms don't really shine unless you invest into them so you may have to experiment with upgrading and respeccing.•The Tl;dr without any of the actual useful bits if you care about my personal opinion.The game exceeded my expectations and is very solid overall.  It's in my top 3 non-Fromsoft action-rpgs and I'm looking forward to hopefully the next title given that my initial thought was "Pinocchio souls?  That sounds really stupid but the demo gameplay was promising so I will play it for the gameplay".  This game is honestly a real boy.

_childDocuments_.review: 8.5/10Lies of P is the closest souls like to fromsoftwares line up of games that follows the spirit of the games near perfectly and brings its own formula. It feels like a true Bloodborne successor in a way while we wait for a port to pc one day come. (or until the ShadPS4 Emulator gets the kinks figured out). The story even is a good spin on Pinocchio that definitely has me intrigued more on where they plan on taking the story. However, the game starts to slowly fall apart at Chapter 9 and only goes down hill from there leaning into artificial difficulty, gimmick bosses, and bad enemy placement that would make Dark Souls 2 blush with envy. It got so bad with me that the game started to drag and I just wanted it to end so much so that I chose the possible bad ending to avoid the boss fight at the end.  It feels like the game play and level design wise needed to be touched up more or was rushed to the end due to time constraints. Dark Souls 1 was similar to this but I never felt it or knew about it on my first play through while this one I did heavily.  - Is a Fromsoftware game through and through-Soundtrack is great- Story is well done -A true Bloodborne successor-Weapon variety is great with the handle system-After chapter 9 it goes down hill- Gimmick bosses that feel like they are trying to create difficulty for no reason. -Enemies regenerate health. Not an issue on its own with small enemies, but the big ones drag out a fight longer than need be. Some even just start regenerating it slowly without attack you first.-Enemy placement starts to really get annoying similar to some of Dark Souls 3 enemy placements in some levels.-Level Design in Chapter 11 really feels like they want to take Sens Fortress from Darks Souls 1 and times it be 3 to again add more difficulty. - I wish there was more costumes and more varied. Feels like they just were touching the tip of the ice berg with costumes but never went fully forward. Maybe the dlc can help add more. My best advice I can give without spoilers is before chapter 9, stock up on throw able and resources to be ready for a temporary lock out in an area. Usually I get on the band wagon of wanting to replay a souls game after I beat it, but this one I'm going to wait for either the dlc or give it a few months before replaying it. That third act genuinely pissed me off and makes me not want to replay it again.

_childDocuments_.review: My overall experience with the game has been fantastic. I like the artstyle, the characters, the soundtrack and most importantly Combat coupled with the artstyle is the most important part of souls-like games. When combat is executed perfectly it feels like you are a well-oiled terminator killing machine. From perfect parrying, dodging, charging and then delivering a fatal attack on an enemy feels good, if you actually can. The perfect parry window is  small and coupled with almost every enemy delaying and in some cases even holding their attacks until they are close enough to hit you can make you feel frustrated. I wish the perfect parry window was longer or while you are parrying you can let go and parry again to hopefully get that perfect parry. Currently you can't because you are semi-locked into regular parrying unless you roll away.You have no poise, the enemy however does have poise and this creates situations where you are charging a heavy attack but some regular attack by an enemy interrupts it. Can you imagine using a 3 bar fable art and right before it connects with an enemy it gets interrupted by a regular attack. Goodbye 3 fable art bars, it was nice knowing you. This also creates situations where if an enemy attacks fast enough (and they do) and they have an attack combo of 5-10 you can be stunlocked into death.This makes me wish some animations for the player were shorter than they are. The unnecessary loss of control during the buildup of an attack or after an attack has already landed. I've already hit the enemy why is my guy trying to twirl his damn weapon or holding his weapon out just move please. This also makes me wish the player attack animations had a slightly longer reach. The amount of times i thought my attack would connect with an enemy with some weapons that should have longer range and then they didn't was ridiculous. This paired with the fact that almost every enemy has a longer or far longer reach than you soured some fights and made me cheese them with the wrench fable art.The weight system could solve these animation gripes IF weight actually mattered. There is almost no difference in playing light weight, medium weight or heavy weight. The only things that change are your stamina refill rate and your rolling speed. You should be able to run faster or swing your weapon faster at lighter weight but no.Some P-Organ upgrades like the extra dodge and dodge from the ground should be available by default instead of locked behind upgrades but what do i know.It also doesn't help that the saintess statue that allows you to respec your levels, P-Organ and Legion upgrades unlocks roughly in the middle of the game. Weapon upgrade materials are also kind of rare, expecially for special weapons. Want to try out a new weapon? Oh you didn't save your upgrade materials? Too bad, you're punished.The difficulty is here and there. Some encounters with mini-bosses or elite enemies are harder than most of the bosses. Examples are: The mad clown before the opera and the electric version in the swamp, The crazy clown in the arcade cellar and abbey. both the mad clowns and the crazy clown in the abbey can be bypassed by running past them if you so choose to. The crazy clown in the arcade cellar however cannot be passed until you defeat it. I had more trouble with the crazy clown than ANY of the bosses or mini-bosses/elites before it. Let's also not forget the other elite that you encounter in the arcade cellar and malum district that does that very quick spinning attack.I've been hearing people say that  is difficult and it is, because it is the first boss that has 2 phases. Some attacks are very fast and painful but there are plenty of opportunities for counterattacks.I've been hearing people say that the king of puppets is difficult and it is. Phase 1 is fine, Phase 2 is also fine until the half point where the boss launches a multi-hit combo attack at you while chasing you down. This can be frustrating because being stunlocked and watching your character die because you cannot do anything is not great. Despite this there are plenty of opportunities for counterattacking.I've been hearing people say that the swamp monster is difficult and it absolutely is. It was the most frustrating fight in the entire game until then and continued to be the most difficult fight right until the second last boss. Phase 1 was fine, Phase 2 however significantly reduces the amount of counterattacking opportunities not only because the boss is very fast but because the boss has extra delayed attacks and will quickly launch into another combo of attacks. it is also a very quick and mobile boss.If you thought these bosses were difficult then  will make them seem like warmups. If you thought the previous bosses were fast, this boss is quite literally lightning-fast. If you thought the previous bosses hit hard, this boss will murder you. If you thought the previous bosses had stingy counterattack opportunities, this boss will fly halfway across the arena away from you into the air and attack you. it is doable but damn if it wasn't the most difficult fight in the entire game.And finally the final boss is more annoying than difficult due to long-range sweeping attacks and AoE zones that appear in the middle of the map and where the boss is at set intervals.The one encounter that i personally feel like was absolutely spot on was  because not once did i feel like the boss had ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ range, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ speed or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ combo attacks. If i got hit it was because i made a mistake. Despite all this i however had a great time playing through it the first time and will be doing a NG+ playthrough.

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is a thrilling Souls-Like Game, that lets you dive into a lovely detailed world full of puppets.I am writing this review after having played the game for two hours and to make a long story short, for those of you, who do not want to read the entire review:  Thumbs up.UPDATE AFTER HAVIN PLAYED:  8 hrs: Still great. The story really hooks me up. The wapons you can craft to fit your playing style, the characters, the setting itself :DSo let's start with the technical aspects of the game: I clearly want to state, that I'm playing on a high-end machine including: RTX 4090, I7 13700K, 32 GB RAM, and RAID 0 NVMes so I can not talk about the performance of low to mid-range PCs. But so far I can tell, that the game works perfectly fine! Some Details are listed below: With that said, I would give from a technical point of view a clear 10 / 10. And I want to remind people here: Although I have such a good machine, this does not imply that the performance is always really smooth. I played games at the release date, where I had: frame drops, bugs, bad collision detection, glitches, and so forth. A game that runs that smoothly already PRE-Release is not released that often.You will really like this game, if you like Dark Souls, Sekiro, or any other Souls-like game. Like in Dark Souls, you have StarGazer (Bonfire) which will save your game, refill life and "potions", but revive all the enemies. There is a small detail I would like to share with you which I really enjoyed:The puppet (main character) you are playing can level up in the hotel when talking to Sophia. But before you come to the Hotel, you already have a Boss fight which is not that easy to beat (it took me something like 5 tries, but my skill level is mäah :D), so in the first levels, you can level up by interacting with the StarGazer. As I wanted to somehow compensate for my skill issue, I simply killed the small enemies a dozen times to get enough resources to level up enough to make the fight easier. This works for some levels, but after you reach a certain level, you can not level up anymore until you reach the hotel --> On a certain point the game wants you to learn the mechanics of the enemy and to develop some skills. I like the balance here very much because the fight is not too easy (although leveled up) but not too hard that you want to quit the game. It feels kind of rewarding for me. I really like such small details.What I also would like to add at this point: This game is not blindly a Dark Souls copy (which the first hour on some points felt a bit like that), it brings different mechanics and tries to give the player a unique touch, charm, and gameplay style. What do I mean precisely here:A lot is of course also similar to Dark Souls, like the already mentioned StarGazers, enemies that become alive again after using them, a more linear way of gameplay, the difficulty, and the atmosphere, but it's not simply another skin on top of that. It is a very good game on its own.I don't know too much so I can not really spoil you here, so don't worry, but I really like the Pinocchio vibes here. It made me laugh sometimes and reminds me a bit of my childhood. I really like the theme: A bit of IRobot (a movie with Will Smith), but with puppets that slay humans. From Lore's point of view, the puppets are built like that they can not Lie, but YOU can. Because YOU are a special puppet, searching for your "crafter", Geppetto :D Holy Moly, I'm already entirely hooked by that :DShut up and take my money!

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is a remarkable game that excels on multiple fronts. The storytelling is gripping, weaving a tale filled with mystery and intrigue that kept me engrossed throughout. The characters are nuanced, adding depth to an already compelling narrative.The combat mechanics are top-notch, offering a seamless blend of strategy and action. Each battle feels dynamic and requires both skill and thoughtful decision-making, making every encounter immensely satisfying.One of the game's strengths lies in its well-placed secrets and subtle hints. Exploring the world uncovers hidden gems, rewarding curiosity and adding an extra layer of immersion to an already richly detailed environment.Lies of P is a standout experience, seamlessly integrating a captivating story, engaging combat, and a world teeming with secrets. It's a must-play for anyone seeking a deeply immersive and satisfying gaming adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't buy this game if you dislike games such as: Bioshock, Bloodborne, Dark Souls, Demons Souls, Dishonored, Elden Ring, Resident Evil, and Sekiro. Don't buy this game if you don't like South Korea or their aesthetic tendencies. This game made me want to play Elden Ring again. I was craving more of an open world. It rewards aggressive combat. It runs better than Elden Ring in terms of FPS.The level design and aesthetic are pleasing. The BGM and records you can obtain for playback are nice as well. The voice acting leaves something to be desired imo. The story is slow and really starts to pick up towards the end of the game into your second playthrough. Getting all of the achievements in this game is very easy. I never get this much completion in most of the games I play.I'm writing this review just before starting my third playthrough for the last four achievements i'm missing. I don't think there's much in the way of story content or new items to be had in NG+2 onwards. Overall, I would give it 8/10. This is based on the things I care about in a game: story, aesthetic, level design, combat, music, and voice acting. I don't know what it is, but I feel like there's something missing... maybe it was too short or maybe they didn't blend enough elements from other games into Lies of P but that's the vibe i'm getting.I was significantly disappointed with the story until I was approaching the end of the game. I felt like they had a lot of material to pull from based on what they made this game about. The story really started making more sense as I was playing the game a second time. I found myself noticing elements from other games everywhere and thinking, "yeah, I probably would have added or done the same thing here."I hope they release DLC for this game, and continue to make games like this, based on stories like this.

_childDocuments_.review: With Sekiro-esque combat, and Bloodborne aesthetics, Lies of P is easily one of the best souls-like games to come out, and is my personal game of the year. The music, amazing optimization, aesthetics, characters, and story are all phenomenal, and the combat feels rewarding when you really learn to get those perfect guards down. My biggest gripe with the game, would be the boss health. I don't mind having boss fights that have a second health bar, but there are SO many in this game, some right after the other. It can quickly become exhausting for the player, and I feel that some of the bosses would have benefited from just having a phase 2 halfway through the one bar. That's honestly my only gripe though. Other than that, the game is phenomenal and has so many intricacies and details that tie into the choices you make and the story of Pinocchio. Easily 9.5/10 and one of my favorite games of all time now. Highly recommend for a lover of soulsborne type games.

_childDocuments_.review: The game started off promising. Although it is extremely derivative of Fromsoft games (to a comical degree), I was having fun for the first few acts. The story is completely nonsensical but the aesthetic is cool and the first few bosses were great. I like how you can customize your weapon by mix-and-matching parts. As I progressed further into the game I started noticing some glaring problems that eventually led me to quit before finishing it.1. Boss health pools are absurdly large. Every mid-late game fight felt like soloing an MMO Raid Boss with 2 phases. I had a fully upgraded weapon and even if I used a summon to tank and just wailed on the boss freely I was doing pathetically low damage.2. The perfect parry mechanic is horrendously designed. The window for a successful parry is extremely small compared to Sekiro, but at the same time the reward is much lower. Executing a successful chain of parries usually just means you get to hit them with 1 or 2 attacks after, dealing 1/500th of their HP. There is a posture system, but breaking their posture just puts them into a "vulnerable" state, where you are given a very brief window to land a fully charged attack, which is frequently impossible due to the enemy running away or beginning an attack you must dodge. If you manage to do all that your reward is 1 backstab. Amazing. Despite all this, the bosses are designed so you are required to parry them many times to win.3. Big slow weapons are completely unviable. Your character has no poise and a slight breeze will interrupt his animations. Enemies also attack quickly and in rapid succession so finding a window to swing is close to impossible.4. Pointless time waste. All the upgrade vendors are like a 45 second walk away from each other for some reason. You have to return to the hub town to level rather than being able to do it at the bonfire. Excessive runbacks to bosses. There is a time-gated currency in the game that you only get 1 of every 10 minutes and the timer does not work while the game is closed.5. All the prosthetic arms felt pretty much useless. The shield one for example does an explosion when you block with it. It has a pretty hefty cooldown and was doing about 1/4 the damage of my light attack. 6. Obnoxious level designs reminiscent of Dark Souls 2. Stuff like walking on rafters while ranged enemies shoot at you and if you get hit once you fall off and die.

_childDocuments_.review: Disgustingly good. Here's a few ups and a few downs:The many good things:- Outstanding realisation of the souls-like genre/formula. If you enjoy these games, you'll most likely enjoy this one. Think Bloodborne aesthetics, Sekiro combat, and general Dark Souls mechanics.- Great story. That good mix of utterly obscure, deeply unsettling, and completely fascinating.- Hub area is "Hotel Krat" and it's very charming. You slowly populate it with the survivors you find as you play, including your dad. He's totally OK and Definitely Not Crazy™.- There's an in-game cat you can pet. If you can win its trust.- The graphics aren't just beautiful, they're well optimised. You can enjoy this game's splendour without fretting too much about your framerate. There's also some technical hints and clues that suggest ray tracing will probably be added eventually.Some downs:- The combat is varied enough to be interesting but can be seen as rather "one-note" as it mostly revolves around mastering the /incredibly/ tight parry windows. No matter what build or playstyle you're rocking, you must eventually become Parry The Platypus if you want to finish the game.- As with all RPGs and especially souls-likes, grinding will make the game easier. Too little and you'll be overwhelmed by simple enemies, too much and you'll breeze right through. - Ray tracing is not here yet, and we are all the poorer for it since this game has fantastic potential for it with already-excellent lighting, scenery, and visual direction.I don't do numbers. No stars or ?/10s from me. It's a simple question of "Is it good or not good?" and this game is good. Very good. If you like the Souls-like genre then this is worthy of your time and money. That's all there is to it.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the best games I have ever played. 120hrs, max level 561 at NG+7, because I didn't want to farm for Ergo so I just decided to play through it 7 times. The game definitely has more pros and cons in my opinion.The one thing I enjoyed most about this game is the direct approach to the story. There in no confusion to where you need to go, you are guided throughout the story. Side quests aren't as direct but they are side quests for a reason. Also, main NPCs in Krat Hotel also have character side stories as well. Lastly, there are 3 total endings in the game, so while you don't have to do all 3, to get the most out of the game I would recommend getting the endings, especially the True Ending. All in all, it's a beautiful game. It is quite challenging but for those that have played Sekiro, you may find the guard system to be very familiar and the overall difficulty to be similar in comparison as well.I would highly recommend the game. Enjoy the story, be patient and yeah, enjoy!
