_childDocuments_.review: Describing my experience with Lies of P as simply another 'souls-like ARPG' would be entirely reductive to the amount of passion & attention-to-detail presented by the teams at Neowiz and Round8 Studio. Lies of P sees you lead as Gepetto's puppet in a twisted, gloomy take on the folktale of Pinocchio. Waking up in an eerie train station, you soon make your way outside to the city of Krat, where a sudden trigger in the puppets causes a haunting massacre that sets the tone for the rest of the game.     On that note, atmosphere is the name. Hotel Krat is your central hub, and it quickly evolved from being a brief trip to level up my weapons into a safe retreat where I could listen to a vibrant soundtrack in the background as I spoke with the many charismatic faces that made up this iconic location. It's not just the hub area - everything from oil-lined streets to infested cathedrals, the immense amount of detail present within the level design itself across most of the chapters is incredibly impressive. Whether it was my first playthrough or my sixth, I could not help but immerse myself in all of the intricately placed bodies & texts around the city that truly cements this game as an all-time example of how to do proper environmental storytelling within linear experiences. Neowiz and Round8 really wear the inspiration on their sleeves with the worldbuilding here and it's very well executed. (Note: it runs flawlessly for me on an upper-end rig, but even on my steam deck it is the best performing game I own. It's also very nicely balanced and well-paced. I would say I preferred the difficulty around launch, as it really heightened my enjoyment of this game in a unique way because of how challenging it was. But it's still a decent challenge and NG+ definitely brought that difficulty back.)      Combat is really where Lies of P hits all of its strides for me. As a fan of FromSoftware's 'soulsborne' entries for the better part of a decade, I believe Lies of P implements so many positive spins on their formula that I would recommend this over the traditional souls games to any player, regardless of experience (well... maybe play Sekiro.) For example, one of my favorite mechanics is pulse recharge, which allows you to gain one more charge to your healing consumable if you are at zero. This feature would change the entire dynamic of so many of my fights in an instant. Maybe I'm playing defensively, I've got two more heals and 60% of the boss's health left; in scenarios like this, every single time I reached zero heals, my brain would switch to aggression immediately in the hopes of regaining a charge and feel more 'comfortable.' I cannot speak to everyone's experience, but this mechanic made me a better player over time as I was PUSHED into being more active in my gameplay and subsequently rewarded with the most satisfying sound effect I've heard since the Halo CE shield recharge as a single pulse cell materializes right back into your upper belt.      Another great feature to the combat sandbox is the ability to assemble weapons. This is the single-most innovative design choice that Lies of P offers. Every weapon comes in two distinct parts, the blade tip and the handle. Each part has their respective stats; however, you can alter the handle to scale off of different stats than the ones it drops with. This opens up a lot of customization and encourages player experimentation, because at no extra-cost, your entire moveset and ability options can change in a matter of seconds. I myself am a Guts sword girl through and through, but even I felt compelled to experiment and eventually beat the game with my own ridiculous combinations. (Note: For me, this self-expression was VERY important in my enjoyment of the game, and I think it's a great innovation to the souls combat formula to allow your players to test out ANY weapon handle's moveset with... every other weapon's blade. Admittedly boss weapons are restricted from being customized and the scaling of both parts' stab/slash stat means that your options for good damage are inherently limited, but it offers so much freedom regardless that I would not mind seeing it return in the sequel.)      Story is the point I want to end this off on. For as long as I have cherished Bloodborne's lore, the original trilogy's lore, etc. I have never actually felt connected to the events of the stories presented in souls-like games. There's always been a strange disconnect for me being able to enjoy the challenge of the gameplay rather than caring about the story. I can say Lies of P genuinely moved me in a way no other games in this subgenre have. I believe the most obvious explanation for this is the greater emphasis on dialogue and player onboarding that Lies of P engages in. There is a real sense here with the amount of dialogue you'll receive from a character off-screen during gameplay or in the middle of a boss fight that Neowiz really wanted to make players feel INVOLVED in the big character moments as they are happening, rather than reading about them from a lore description (which is also a method of storytelling present with a lot to read up on that is engaging.) To be clear, I have no issue with this, but I really prefer the focus on character engaging with me, the truths/lies you decide to tell them, and the almost-immediate consequences those decisions can have as they relay their reactions back to you. You can ignore or fight multiple bosses by making a simple decision. I like that. The narrative throughline that is happening above all of the character stories is decently executed, but the character quests is really where Lies of P shines (shoutout to Arlecchino.) Everyone is voice acted phenomenally, and this could not be a Lies of P review without making mention of how pivotal this game's original soundtrack is to the overall experience. The music feels tied to the characters' stories, as many records you can play back at Hotel Krat are received from quest completions. This makes even something as seemingly trivial as playing a record on a record player feel rewarding in itself, as you learn more about an NPC's journey through this world or simply enjoy a great tune in the background.      This has become my comfort game, and affectionately so. That doesn't mean it is devoid of things I disliked, as the final area of the game, Arche Abbey, has got to be the single-most tedious level I have played in recent memory. Running through this moody grey wasteland to a grey tower with grey floors and repeated enemies from throughout the entire game got tiring incredibly fast, and it's a shame that the area with this game's pinnacle challenges is also so uninspired in its design. Additionally, I do not think the armor system, dubbed "Defense parts," is particularly exciting. I think this could be fleshed out a little more, but finding more parts throughout the game is almost never exciting because they are always going to be better than your previous find, and they do not change any part of your puppet's appearance. I do like the cosmetics available here, but I definitely prefer the more free-form style of armor expression in other souls-likes. The legion arm system is probably the most disappointing aspect for me, delivering options to customize your limb similar to the prosthetic tools in Sekiro. I do not like the implementation in this game because it feels stiff to me. This is not something I have the knowledge to explain away, but it feels very restricted and with the low amount of legion I always have, it just left a lot to be desired for me because I mainly relied on parrying and counterattacking.      Despite my negatives, I adore this game. At the time of writing I have unlocked everything pre-DLC and waiting in anticipation for it as well as the recently announced sequel. If you've ever got a weekend to knockout a surprisingly compelling souls-like, this is absolutely the one for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you like Dark Souls or Elden Ring? Do you like Sekiro even more? Then this game is probably for you."Git gud" — people often say this ironically, yet it perfectly encapsulates the thrill of the Souls-like genre. In a different game, you'd win or lose based on luck (looking at you, Darkest Dungeon), or by simply outleveling the challenge (hello, The Witcher 3). Here, you triumph by  and . That's why it's so satisfying to finally beat the boss that kicked your ass previously — because you know that you genuinely earned the victory, that you are now better than you used to be. This realization, even on a subconscious level, brings incredible satisfaction, as the human psyche is hardwired to reward self-improvement. It's the reason why people fell in love with Dark Souls, even if only some of them can articulate it in precise terms. It's also the reason why so many get the wrong idea about the difficulty: it's not that the game is hard, it's that you haven't learned it yet. Of course, not everyone is equally fit — some people have slower reflexes, quickly lose composure in stressful situations, have shorter attention spans, are bad at recognizing patterns, or simply don't have enough free time. However, this game does not demand feats of inhuman prowess from you — it's a commercial product, designed to be played by an average person. Therefore, even if I can't 100% guarantee that you have what it takes to beat Lies of P, it's statistically likely that you do. The rest is up to you: keep an open mind, persist, and learn. Everything is impossible until you figure out how to do it, then it's just a matter of execution. Have fun!On top of phenomenal gameplay, this game also has beautiful visuals, extremely satisfying sound effects, and a truly marvelous soundtrack. Unfortunately, game's narrative is falls short, largely because of how the values of the original Pinocchio story are subverted. I was also dissatisfied with how Italian culture is treated here. Aside from a few Italian names and one character, who is a walking caricature, there is  Italian about the setting. In fact, the few Italian features that are present here feel out of place against the backdrop of the architecture and French language in the diegetic songs.It's one thing to question the nature of human beings, what it means to be one, and how lying plays into it. It's a completely different thing to also insist on definitive answers to those questions, especially if the answers are not particularly intelligent. On the surface, the narrative presents you with the dilemma of choosing between sweet lies and horrible truths — but if you do more than one playthrough, you'll realize that lying was meant to be the objectively correct option in  case, unless you want to get a horribly unsatisfying ending (the third option, available regardless of lying, is a horribly morbid and nonsensical ending). I don't know what kind of world the developers of this game live in, but in my world, being lied to usually means being taken advantage of, and that has never been a good thing in my experience. Perhaps I'll have a different perspective on the game's narrative or its philosophical ideas once I've familiarized myself with the many lore videos on YouTube, but for now, this is my honest opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: Review updated after completing the game. Based on Launch version, before the difficulty nerfs in patch 1.2.0.0.Hands down the best souls-like i've ever played not made by Fromsoft themselves, and i've played most of them and love the "genre" to death. It is a must play for any fans of Dark Souls and Bloodborne, and while nothing might ever beat Dark Souls 1's interconnected world design, and Bloodborne's atmosphere and combat, this game to me is one that does not come far behind in what it tries to accomplish. It carries most of the core mechanics from the Souls series that will be familiar to veterans, yet also have some new innovations of their own, like the Legion arm and Weapon assembly system amongst others.Positives: + The world. The atmosphere. A dark spin of Pinocchio.+ The P-organ system (skill system).+ Weapon disassembly.+ Progression systems in general are great.+ Boss fights (without NPC summons) are good. A certain mid-game boss was insane and so much fun, the feeling of beating it after hours with a sliver of health left truly felt so good. (This was before they nerfed him, now its probably not as challenging and thus not as rewarding).+ More parry-focused combat (like Sekiro) with a stagger system rather than roll-spam (like DS3), which is great imo.+ Animations and models are stunning. (Some exceptions, see negatives below)+ No armor stats, true fashion-souls! Stat improvements comes from elsewhere (Defense parts), so you can use whatever costume you like.+ Well optimized, at least for me. High stable FPS on max settings, not a single crash. This deserves a mention considering how rare an optimized game on launch has become these days.+ No major bugs for me. (See negatives)+ HDR is stunning in this game!+ King of Riddles voice is awesome!Negatives:- Too linear. Some shortcuts per area, but there are no divergent paths like Dark Souls where you can wander into higher level areas early and so on. This game barely have sidetracks in the same area, you do sometimes get items/chests around corners etc but thats about it, rest is following the set path. I never got lost, which might be a good thing for some.- The character animation when sprinting and turning feels like he's on ice.- I sometimes get stuck into enemies when trying to dodge from an attack, its hard to explain, I wasnt able to move until the boss typically made another attack that "unstuck" us.- NPC animations when talking looks really wierd and out of sync.- Apprently there are some gamebreaking bugs reported, and the devs have acknowledged this so it likely will be fixed in patch, as stated above I did not encounter any real bugs myself outside of a few texture issues in the world and getting dodge-stuck as mentioned.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe a goofy, dark, edgy retelling of a 19th century children's novel has become one of my favourite videogames. Lies of P is absolutely incredible. It combines the gameplay of Fromsoftware's two best games (Sekiro and Bloodborne) and condenses it into a nearly perfect 20-30 hour package. It has the best roster of boss fights in any "soulslike" game I've played. One boss near the end of the game rivals Sword Saint Isshin and Slave Knight Gael in terms of quality. The combat is fun and engaging. The tight parry window takes awhile to get used to, but once it clicks it feels great.If you are a Dark Souls fan, you should play this game. It runs well on PC. No bugs or significant frame rate drops. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: In July of this year, I decided to take a deep dive into the Souls-like genre by finally dusting off my copy of Dark Souls III and completing it for the first time. After enjoying my time with the game, I completed Sekiro (a masterpiece) and about half of Elden Ring (a game which I did not have a good time with and probably deserves its own review at some point down the road). Before moving on to Dark Souls, Dark Souls II, or a Dark Souls III replay, I decided to move off the beaten path and check out Lies of P. I am happy to say that Lies of P offers some of the best that a Souls-like has offered thus far.Lies of P uses a combat system that employs a mix of other Souls-like games, taking the dodging and rolling from Dark Souls and combining it with the "perfect parrying" system of Sekiro. This blend of combat keeps fights feeling urgent while also leaving a lot of choice up to the player as to how they beat certain bosses. Getting a feel for a boss's attacks? Perfect parry them until you break their weapon, negating most of the damage they give out. Finding it hard to learn timing for said attacks? Dodge around them to get behind the boss and sneak attacks in. Even if not every boss is amazing, the combat system feels great and keeps you engaged throughout.Aesthetically, Lies of P is also a huge success. Using the Pinocchio fairy tale as a barebones framework, the devs construct a world that blends steampunk influence with corruption, zombie-like creature design. The overlap between these two, especially in the latter half of the game, is striking. These gorgeous visuals combine with a lush soundtrack in a really masterful way.My major gripes with Lies of P are mostly found in the third act of the game, and largely have to do with an overreliance on status effect encounters. Balancing in a Souls-like context is tough, and oftentimes devs have to ride a very fine line between satisfying challenge and frustrating challenge. Unfortunately, the amount of enemies (both bosses and normal enemies) in the final third of the game that inflict obnoxious status effects on you is staggering. These status effects range from decaying your weapon faster to just killing you immediately. They are easily the worst the game has to offer, which may be a positive thing in a game full of stuff to love.The boss quality in Lies of P is great overall. Although the game has its fair share of your average beast-like Souls bosses, there are some pretty stellar fights scattered throughout that feel like fast duels which really force you to learn there moves. One in particular, Laxasia the Complete, is perhaps one of the best fights in a Souls game period. The feeling of slowly learning her attacks and chipping away at her until you finally best her calls to mind many of the best encounters in Sekiro, which is some of the highest praise I could offer a game of this caliber.All in all, Lies of P is a very good Souls-like that makes improvements not yet incorporated even by Fromsoft. I look forward to the DLC for Lies of P, as well as the other games they make down the road. If you are at all interested in Souls-likes, you would do well to check out Lies of P..

_childDocuments_.review: In my humble opinion, this is the best souls-like game I've played (Bloodborne, Elden Ring, and this one). It has all of the best parts of those games, while adding many quality of life features like the subtle quest tracking. The combat feels incredibly satisfying, and the enemies/bosses have lots of variety. This game might very well have the best souls bosses. My only complaint here is that sometimes the health bars can be a bit much and it can feel like it's more tedium than difficulty. But that's pretty minor, and I had many more moments of enjoyment and genuine difficulty than moments where I felt my time was being wasted.The environments are beautiful and the level design is immaculate. When I finally found the gold coin tree and realized I was back at the hotel, my mind was blown. Some of this is probably open world fatigue, since Elden Ring is the last single player game I played before this one, but I simply loved the linear level design here. I never felt too stuck or lost, there's always a pretty clear path forward, but each nook and cranny still has something to discover to make exploring them feel worth it. It's not an easy game, but it's excellently crafted and your hard work always feels rewarded. If you can accept getting ♥♥♥♥ on as you learn enemy patterns and get better at the game, you would be doing yourself a disservice by skipping this game. If you're super easily frustrated, probably pass on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat has major issues but is for the most part serviceable if you need to play another souls like. The main story is boring and badly delivered but again serviceable. Where things majorly fall apart is when it comes to world building and level design. Bland uninteresting environments and linear pathways so basic it's almost impossible to miss items or feel a true sense of exploration. You constantly hit dead ends that make no sense within the world. There is zero sense that the places you visit might've once been used for anything other than a combat arena. The few times in the game you enter a new area with distinct decor your companion will kill any tension, immersion, and enjoyment of the experience by monologuing with obnoxious voice acting about the things you are seeing with your own eyes demonstrating a fundamental misunderstanding of world building. The major crisis of enemy variety also contributes to this lack of reality especially when it comes to the blue zombie and all its variants which feel extremely lazy. Bosses suffer from this lack of creativity design wise too with most introduced with minimal narrative weight and killed leaving zero impact. The final area in the lead up to the last boss is an egregious example of all the issues in the game with it being a massive slog of linear paths, repeating enemies, and boring bosses. The final boss is seriously uninspired. Only buy on sale and play all fromsoft games first.

_childDocuments_.review: A cynic might look at Lies of P from the outside as being another in a long line of feeble soulslikes, treading the ground paved by Bloodborne with a thin veneer of Pinocchio. I'm not a negative person, but even I was skeptical when I first heard about it. However, I'm so incredibly glad I gave this a try, and those cynics are missing out, because Lies of P is an incredibly high-quality and enjoyable game that's I'd say is the first to reach (or even surpass) some of the Souls games.From almost every standpoint, the game shines. It performs and looks better than Elden Ring did, both in terms of fidelity and the art style / aesthetic of the game's location, the city of Krat. It's got very good level design that incorporates the Souls tradition of making the most of its areas with clever interconnections, double-backs, and shortcuts. Its weapon system, which allows you to mix and match the handles and blades of weapons to create unique combinations, is an interesting and intuitive one that allows for a lot of variety. I really enjoyed a circular saw attached to a shovel handle for instance, and a forked spear on a piston driver. However, it also offers unique boss weapons that are cool enough to make the choice of what to use even harder. The normal music is fine, but the music on the records is great. The overall story is pretty interesting, more straightforward than the typical Souls. You can really get invested in some of the other characters, and I like the crux being P's own grappling with humanity and his own ego.The combat is the focal point of the game, and it is satisfyingly difficult. The tight parry timing (which I generally suck at) and the low i-frames for dodging mean you have to be on point, and paired with enemy Fury attacks that can only be parried plus lots of delays, tracking, and other such elements make Lies of P one of the tougher games that I've ever played. I only one-shot a handful of bosses (including one chapter boss), with fights varying between 3-5 and 5-10 attempts for the most part, and two standout chapter bosses that took me ~1.5 hours and ~1.75 hours repeatedly. However, it's never really unfair. I felt myself getting better as I played. You just have to keep at it and improving. If I could beat this game, so can you.In terms of flaws, there's almost none. The game is extremely linear, which I don't mind sometimes, but if you want a globe-trotting adventure this isn't it. Some of the VAs are a little weak (but not nearly all of them). The slash-stab system limits weapon customization a little, and if you want character customization, this doesn't have that (though P does get a lot of costumes). Overall, Lies of P is phenomenal. I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a challenge and a great time!

_childDocuments_.review: No poise.Annoying runback.Dex, Int, Str stats are all the same.Unnecessary status effects.Long Flurry attacksMovement/mobility locked via skill tree.Probably one of the best in the souls-like genre.It's a good game, but I don't think I can recommend it to a total beginner.Updated:Ng+ done. The NG+ experience is much more enjoyable, primarily because I've already unlocked mobility. I focused more on the story and achieved my desired ending.I would also add some things that really stood out1.The hitboxes of big bosses can be problematic as they inflict damage on your character.2.The "Gotcha bit**h"/ambush-type enemies is excessive. While it adds variety occasionally, it becomes quite annoying when encountered in every section.3.The return to platformer sections is notably frustrating due to the reliance on a single button for dodging, running, and jumping.4.The emphasis on capacity stats is overwhelming.Despite these issues, I must reiterate that this game stands out as one of the best in the souls-like genre. Players familiar with FromSoftware games or any souls-like titles should definitely give this one a chance.Additionally, there seems to be a hint of DLC in the final cutscene, and I'm eagerly looking forward to it.

_childDocuments_.review: update & final note after Ng4 - Climbing the NG+ ladder, it shows more and more how utterly garbage the combat system in this game is and how worthless 70% of weapons and 90% of abilities in this game are The animation canceling, the absurd input indiciation. Very unfortunate a game with these stunning visuals, soundtrack and amazing atmosphere gets ruined by the biggest turdpile of a combat system i have ever seen in any soulsborne clone. If you hired some playtesters they would have told you that the broad majority of weapons and abilities is legit not usable in most of the fights just once without getting punished by the awful awful design of the input indication. Its honestly so bad it makes me cringe. If you want to design bosses like Nioh does, you should design the combat around it similar to how Nioh does. It took me 3 playthrougsh alone to get the Great Lie weapon because it glitched out twice. If obtaining a weapon demands an entire playthrough dedicated to it, you probably dont wanna mess that up as well. Dont mind me tho, you already won thanks to the absurd positive review bombing by people with barely 5 hours played or maybe even some bots how many devs do nowadays - congratulations ! --A great game that knows how to frustrate with mechanics that their Idol Dark Souls abandoned for a good reason.The obvious: graphics, sound and visuals are amazing. The entire atmosphere is absolutely great.Howsoever, imo the gameplay suffers from several issues:-absurd inbalance among weapons -imbalance isnt just caused by dps difference but mainly because this game absolutely does not allow long-going-combos or big long swings-dodge requires upgrading to be close as good as perfect-blocks (which is likely intended to be the "optimal gameplay")-the input indication (dice roll what the enemy does whenever you press a button) is absurdly aggressive in this game. it often causes animation cancels in order for the boss/enemy to react to the player. i am aware that we moved away from "enemy has a mechanic and if you learn it you mastered that sort of enemy" - but in this game every enemy is a dragonslayer armour boss fightfrom dks3.-dodge and perfect block windows are incredibly tight. Sekiro (perfect block only) and bloodborne (dodge only) did these kind of systems very fair and satisfying while still being difficult. i wonder why Lies of P tries to be "extra" hardcore. Its not hardcore its again, frustratingFurther annoyances:-enemy positioning between stargazers(bonfires) is very weird and frustrating. as an example:you kill 15 normal enemies, you encounter a new miniboss, kill it, you kill another 10-15 little enemies, you encounter another miniboss that you havent seen before so you will die-deathtraps often do not give you a hint, this is especially annoying when they are placed before a stargazer-minibosses have absurd amounts of hp at times and im afraid thats cause they kept them at their same stat values throughout the entire games (minibosses from early in the game will reappaer and be way less challenging)-some enemies like puppets, crawling puppets etc. get hyperarmor (stunimmunity) whenever they feel like it-in addition to what i already said regarding input indication - a lot of bosses almost become passive, walking around - waiting to react to whatever you do-a lot of weapons have a very inconvenient moveset. for example - stab > swing > stab > swing. the stab pushes the enemy out of the swing range which makes me not wanting to use them.-Since there is rewards for completing the both entirely lying or speaking the truth, there is a severe lack of indicator what actually is a lie or the truth at the moment.I sincerely hope the devs keep balancing and fixing issues - everything but the gameplay in this game is topnotch and easily is on the same level as a fromsoft game. So for now i would only recommend this game during a sale, unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately I can't recommend this game. The problem is not the difficulty but a rather boring gameplay design that relies way to much on one mechanic with extremely small margin for error.The story of Lies of P is somewhat intriguing as it loosely uses the classical tale of Pinocchio as its premise but twists it around in various ways. If you know the children's story then you can recognize the various characters from it that you're encountering and just like in Pinocchio itself lies play an important part in the early parts of the story.Visually the game is serviceable. It's not exactly impressive by current standards but also not ugly.In terms of gameplay it borrows heavily from Dark Souls in the principles but also makes a lot of the same mistakes with inventory management for example which is just as much of a pain here as it is in games like Dark Souls and Elden Ring. Everything must be prepared before a fight because you can't just pause the game and change something. Everything must be done live during the fight which always carries a lot of potential for frustration.The thing that actually breaks the game for me though is the gameplay during combat itself as it is centered entirely around blocking (or rather parrying as you're doing the blocking with a weapon and not with a shield). When you "block" and attack your character takes reduced damage and you can recover the lost health at least partially by attacking the enemy. In addition you can do perfect blocks by timing the blocking perfectly to damage or destroy an enemies weapon and/or stagger them more quickly for a heavy damage attack. Dodging is possible but severely limited in effectiveness. So if you cannot block attacks perfectly in terms of timing then you have to rely on static blocking and slow movement with occasional dodges to then deal out heavy attacks in the small time frames you have available. In addition without perfect blocks you cannot damage or destroy an enemy weapon from what I've see so far.The gameplay therefore (when you cannot block perfectly) comes down to:1. Walk to an enemy2. Hold block until weapon combo is done3. Strike enemy 1-3 times4. Hold block until enemy combo is done5. Strike enemyRinse and repeat. There is a secondary weapon in the left arm of the character but outside of the grappler and flamethrower type weapon arms which can be used to affect enemies at a range (pull them in or put them on fire) I haven't seen any use for the off-hand. I have tried that once or twice but the energy management is annoying and the usability is limited. In any way if you have good timing with the blocking ability you could get fun out of this game. If however you are like me failing 9 out of 10 times when you try to do a perfect block and have to stick to more basic strategies this game may become very tedious, frustrating and boring.It's unfortunate as with more options in making blocking and the perfect blocks more easily usable and dodging a more viable alternative the game could be more fun even if the enemies and bosses were overall tought to defeat.

_childDocuments_.review: This game just pisses me off. Every design decision was specifically made to trip-up souls players. Attack timings are always unintuitive and way too many attack animations are hidden, or instant. Red attacks need to be parried perfectly, but if you don't have the timing down, good luck dodging them with the useless i-frames on the dodge. Can't run away from 90% of them either. There's literally no other counter play than just practising getting the timing down.Sekiro is my favourite FromSoft game, but something about this game borrowing the parry mechanic doesn't sit right with me. It's clearly the intended way to play the game, but the combat lacks the dance-like flow of that game so it ends up being a guessing simulator with how often delayed, infrequent and random the attacks are.And the atmosphere/aesthetics borrow a lot from Bloodborne. That and Demon Souls are the only two I haven't played, but I'm not really impressed with it. Every environment is almost exactly the same, or at least feels the same. Not fun to traverse after the second area.It's good, up to a point, because of its novelty and remixing of Souls-like mechanics. Then it just gets annoying. Going around every area expecting the same boring formula:Here's an item specifically placed as a trap or an ambush.Here's a solo enemy also placed as an ambush.Here's a large enemy surrounded by four smaller enemies that will, you guessed it, ambush you.This enemy will NOT be staggered by your heavy attacks because of constant hyper-armor on infinitely delayed attacks.And finally here's a boss at the end. It has a red attack that will chase you to the end of the arena, delayed significantly so you specifically can't parry it, and will also have a larger hitbox so you can't out-space or dodge it. It also has a 3-hit combo that actually is a 4-hit delayed combo that is ACTUALLY a 5-hit combo. Lastly it has an insanely fast, unreactable attack that it does randomly whenever you are in the middle of an attack.Just this, over and over again.

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P (PC, 100%, 58 hours and 3 runs)This has become my favorite souls game to date.The story, atmosphere, rpg depth, weapons, combat, and especially the music, have rocketed this to my number one spot. I love Fromsoft games, which has given me the appropriate mindset to play this game at all, but it's amazing what an actual narrative with meaning and characters I care about will do for my enjoyment.Best description for gameplay and vibes would be Bloodborne and Sekiro got together and had a baby haha. They were clearly heavily influenced by their muses, in all of the best ways. It's tough as nails, you better be prepared to parry because rolling won't save you. Parry combat is much more enjoyable for me than is i-frame rolling tag because it feels visceral and epic.Story is haunting and made me think of what it means to be a human, with truth and lies serving as the moral center - it's serendipitous that I've been reading a book about lying concurrently haha. It spins the tale of Pinnochio into a horror survival game, which works surprisingly well. Paired with an absolutely banging soundtrack, it delivers the tale hauntingly. I've saved over 10 of the different tracks because they keep replaying in my head haha, they really popped off with the score.Weapons are awesome. Not as outlandishly cool and varied as Bloodborne, but they introduce a cool weapon assembly feature that lets you mix and match hilts and blades/hammers/etc. I made sure to try a different weapon for every boss, to satisfying effects. One mindset the Elden Ring DLC finally got me into was experimenting with different weapons, and I think it does a lot for my appreciation of the depth these games have. You have a mechanical Legion Arm that lets you have abilities like flamethrowers and land mines and heavy ammunition, which adds even more variety.[10:00 AM]Not a perfect game - some mechanics like having to level up my carrying capacity instead of health or attack is annoying, but not game breaking. Difficulty isn't consistent, as some bosses are pushovers and then suddenly you must become a parry god for others haha, but it also didn't ruin things for me. Love a good challenge, and this game will do that.For being Neowiz's and Round8's first major game (they formerly did mostly mobile gacha stuff), this is an incredibly impressive first outing. I'm stoked for the DLC and the sequel. I don't really do NG+/Revenge tours, but I did two after my first playthrough because I wanted 100% and to have fun with breaking the game with wild builds. So good.Big recommend if you're a souls fan looking for a satisfying gauntlet paired with a memorable world and incredible music.

_childDocuments_.review: Lis of P took me around 31 hours to beat, and its a *very* good souls game, combat feels nice, the main mechanics of assembling your own weapons and legion arms is both unique and can make some pretty powerful combos, the area's look amazing, no one area is a cluttered maze like in other games, and the bossfights are (for the most part) superb.The only two main gripes i have are the parry window for some enemies *sweeping* attacks can feel rather awkward to attempt to parry, and the roll, though ti gets you out of most instances of danger, can feel trashy at times. The roll is like that of the Nioh games, thinking of 2 specifically, where you have the ability to roll twice, but instead of the second roll extending your first quick step type roll, it feels like a roll, a pause where you can get hit, and then a second roll. It felt better to just spam the quick step in a given direction. Though this is a skill you don't *have* to grab, I'd be nice it the double roll felt a tad better, but that's just my opinion, definitely recommend grabbing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful feeling, to actually play a really good game, without actually encountering any issues at all. No bugs, no glitches, no disconnects, no errors, absolutely nothing! What a brilliant work the devs have done! Kudos to everyone involved in this project! Story wise? I really enjoy it a lot, can't wait to see where it leads (Still progressing). Difficulty wise I think is harder than Elden Ring, maybe somewhat near to Bloodborne.Combat/Mechanics wise, the game is really well put together, and everything makes sense. The Talent Tree/skills/weapon upgrades adds real progression to the game, you feel every single upgrade you actually add to either of the mentioned options.The graphics are also very well designed, and as stated previously, it runs flawlessly. Not one single issue the entire time I was playing the game. Also watching streamers, none of them ever encountered any issues with the game.Overall, I think this is how a game should be released, which is really really rare these days, so from my point of view, this game is a must for everyone that loves the soulslike genre. The content should easily offer around 50-60 hours of content, if you never fail and just burst through everything, which is not really doable, since the game (from my point of view) is not really that easy. But it has loads of things to experience with, and try new builds, new weapons combinations etc.Easy 10/10 from my point of view!

_childDocuments_.review: I have not had much fun with this game from start to finish.There is a huge discrepancy with having a frame perfect block mechanic and enemies having  erratic attack patterns I've seen yet. There is no rhythm to enemies' attack patterns and you need to memorise their exact timings without having to rely on visual cues. Their combos last up to ten attacks or more, during which you cannot retaliate because if you do you will be, more often than not, stuck in their combo until your HP depletes.You will frequently be caught out by a sudden follow-up attack after you think a combo is finished. Not a single fight felt like they were designed for enjoyment. The enemies have some of the most aggressive tracking I've ever seen in a a souls-like Action RPG: even if you try to roll underneath a jumping enemy, they will spin around 180°—in mid-air—to hit you. Some unblockable attacks will literally move the boss right next to you within a space of one or two frames.The developers are  adamant you must perfectly master their Perfect Guard mechanic, while the only incentive to perfect block is to not take damage: which doesn't feel rewarding enough. The developers claim the boss weapons will break, but it takes way too long time until that happens, and their damage penalty is negligible at best even when it happens.This is extra problematic when every enemy moves faster than you do, no matter your current weight limit. Your dodge rolls have such a pathetically short travel distance that enemies will keep catching up to you mid-combo until you run out of stamina. You are also prone to fighting groups of enemies often, even during some boss fights.All in all, the core gameplay loop of fighting enemies feels uncontrollable and haphazard at best when compared to other games in the same genre.

_childDocuments_.review: Right up there with FromSoft's games, but not as good as a FromSoft game.- Combat in general feels amazing- Enemy variety is high (visually and their movesets)- Bosses are awesome (visually and their movesets) and there are like 15 of them- Story is mysterious and intriguing and the broad strokes of it are pretty interesting- Runs perfectly (this one makes it way better than From games outside of Elden Ring)- Upgrades are very meaningful (especially via the Quartz system). You get upgrades like "can now dodge from grounded state".- Builds aren't really that diverse. Motivity, Technique and Advance determine which weapon handles you can use. And weapon handles determine movesets. But there are very few movesets that are entirely unique to one of those stats. Maybe 1 or 2.- Characters aren't very well developed. Pretty bad voice work. Pretty inconsequential dialogue that usually goes on for too long. Gemini talks way too much and usually says stuff that doesn't quite follow the events that took place prior.- "The Truth" in this game pales by contrast with The Truths revealed in Bloodborne, Dark Souls and Elden Ring. Actually sort of amounts to a schlocky SyFy/horror plot, once you learn what's going on.- Level design is very linear, and shortcuts aren't very impressive outside of one great one. They're just basic checkpoints.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic Souls-like game. In a way, almost harder than souls if you play like I do (preferring to dodge rather than block or parry). The I-frames and parry timing is EXTREMELY unforgiving. As many other people have mentioned, it feels very Bloodborne., both the feel of the graphics and the feel of the gameplay. It tends to reward being aggressive rather than defensive (more akin to Bloodborne or Sekiro in my opinion). Also, the locations of shortcuts and save points feels VERY similar to any Fromsoft game, to the point of turning a corner and expecting to find said save point... and it being there. But why fix what isn't broken? It's nice pacing and didn't ever feel too far or too near. I think my only complaint is how the enemies attack. The timings on their hits can be judged after a LONG time of observing them, but starting out, the attacks are unpredictable and difficult to read. The mobs also track the player far too well, making it near impossible to dodge or get out of the way, unless you time it correctly. Even as the attack is happening, the enemy will sometimes continue to rotate and track the player. Not a bad feature in and of itself, but it can be frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: They should have made telegraphy better like Sekiro, so you can actually guard. This game has some instant hits, so you have no way of predicting unless you memorize the move-sets perfectly. It's also not helpful that some moves have the same windup, so you can't all the time predict how much you wait before you guard because you don't know what follows. So guarding is only sometimes good.Dodging is also partly useful because it's not feasible in some situation. The game actually wants you to combine dodging with guarding, but they haven't balanced that very well. It's the worst of both worlds, like parrying from Elden Ring with dodging from Sekiro.

_childDocuments_.review: Dodging is criminally underpowered, and even if it weren't a lot of enemies have overpowered wide angle attacks that orient towards you mid-animation to ensure they hit you. An attack that seems to be specifically designed to hit you no matter what you do is, to put it kindly... an interesting design choice.Parry is an absolute joke, and needs to be completely re-worked. It's not responsive enough, and unreliable - especially against multiple attacks in succession. You are punished for spamming parry, but parry timing is so unforgiving it's controller-throwing levels of frustrating.Most basic skills and abilities are locked to the P Organ system. Which is a garbage design choice. At least some of these should be available much earlier in the game. The damage you take out paces your ability to heal roughly a half hour into the game and heaven forbid you make a mistake - there goes all the charges of your pulse cell.Visually, this game is absolutely gorgeous, so credit where it is earned. But the game is also needlessly difficult and sometimes just seems like plain BS. Any hesitation or even one small mistake punishes you with death, often before you can really learn anything about the encounter.  We all make mistakes, and when we;re honest with ourselves we can admit the exact stupid choice that caused our death. But we learn from it, adjust and move on. But when you start feeling like it's not your fault for dying, a game is doing something wrong.I suppose at this point the question is whether I regret purchasing this game? At the moment, I do not. But without some at least minor gameplay tweaks (hopefully around parry timing) I imagine that I might be inclined to say yes once I get further into the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is an extremely polished and fully fleshed out game. I'd level only one serious criticism against it: You have to work a little to find the fun...See, the game has this perfect parry mechanic. If you block an attack at just the right instant you deal posture damage to your attacker. Some weapons also have enhanced parries that are harder to land but deal massive damage.The issue is not with the parry itself, I think it's tuned appropriately, but rather how the parry makes you approach the game. You can parry damn near every attack in the game, and you'll usually be rewarded for it. Because parrying is hard but not impossible, it's easy to fall into this trap where your overcome bosses and enemies by parrying everything. I beat a few bosses by bashing into them over and over again until I could win by standing completely still and just parrying every single attack. Parrying was a universal hammer so everything became a nail.This is an extremely boring and hard way to play the game. It really boils all the flavor off of what are surprisingly deep and intricate boss fights. I know maybe I sound like a moron but I fell for the juicy parry sounds and massive damage numbers. I thought I was playing optimally, but eventually I got really bored and frustrated. The thing is, some attacks are not worth parrying. The game tries to subtly make this clear to you by throwing attacks that will knock you away from your target if you parry them, but will leave the enemy wide open for counterattack if you dodge them. More importantly, the game is just friendlier and a lot more fun if you dodge, block, and out-space attacks from time to time. You'll find yourself moving more, improvising more, and having tenser, more dynamic fights. And you'll beat the bosses in fewer attempts because you don't need to memorize EVERY parry timing for EVERY attack.I do think the game could do a little more to force players out of the "always parry" comfort zone/trap. But it might just be a product my own egotistical desire to beat everything in the "most highly skilled" way possible.You have been warned dear gamer. Also make sure to level your HP, this game's not supposed to be excruciating. And yeah, this is a negative review because I actually want people to read it. To hell with your collectivism I'm a special snowflake. ME ME ME ME ME.

_childDocuments_.review: As of now I am on the second day of the early release, and I started at around 6 pm on the first. The game's main combat system felt a little light at first and you are given only around 6 attributes to level up to make your own build. I spent the first hour or so trying different swords and combos of attack and honestly it felt simple. It is now 4 am on the second day and I have not stopped playing. With a small break in the middle to eat I spent ten hours on this game. All I can say without spoiling much is that the game only really opens its massive puppet jaws to swallow you whole is when you are given the ability to change your weapon's handles and blades. This seemingly small ability changes the way you play the game with each handle changing the MOVE-SET of the weapon and each piece of the weapon having a special ability. _childDocuments_.review: I don't know how they did it, but a studio other than Fromsoft actually managed to make a good souls like. Let me start off with the obvious: the developers' localization team was not great and it shows. Lore notes are phrased strangely and voice acting can range from passable to terrible. However, the story is not what makes this game great. The combat system takes the classic mechanics from the main souls series and tweaks aggression all the way up. You are rewarded with heals by attacking, and leaving enemies alone lets them recover HP. This combines to reward you for getting up close and personal. Hell, if you are aggressive enough, you get rewarded with staggers and further damage. The animations are brutal and the controls feel tight. The only weak points gameplay-wise are some absurdly short telegraphs on attacks late game. Level design also becomes somewhat repetitive as you notice patterns of the same tricks, enemy layouts, and shortcut placements. However, the changing enemies and scenery make up for it. The weapon system is also quite innovate, although I didn't mess around with it enough to have an opinion. Overall, if you're looking for another souls game to play while we wait on Elden Ring 2 in 20 years, this is it.

The first half was perfect pacing, though maybe after BB it was on the easier side, but I really enjoyed my time and was looking forward to new bosses. However, after the midpoint, the pacing REALLY faltered - it got unexpectedly harder, the bosses seemed to have more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mechanics than I was used to and I just stopped having fun. Luckily, near the very end, the game got better again and the bosses were challenging, but not unfair. So I finished the game on a great note and I look forward to the DLC (if it ever comes) - just wanted to give a heads up that for some people the pacing may feel odd at one point in the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is one of the best soulslike games that I have played. The story is very serviceable and a bit more cinematic than most soulslike games but there are many collectibles and items that fill you in on the world and how it has gotten into this apocalyptic state. The combat is very good and encourages the player learning how to perfect guard/parry instead of strictly relying on dodging. The weapon parts being interchangeable and not requiring the player have a specific amount of strength/dexterity is a very nice change. My major gripe is the lack of poise. Enemies sometimes being unfazed by your attacks especially the heavy attacks can get annoying at times. Another gripe I have is the bosses and enemies having way too many delayed attacks instead of more unique combos of attacks. I would definitely recommend this game to any souls fans as well as others that like a challenge.

_childDocuments_.review: Version:- 1.1.2.0Positives:- The game is well-optimized and I did not experience performance issues or frame-time problems during my 25-odd hours.- Shader pre-compilation on game launch.- Short loading times between warps.- The game's setting is intruiging and there are several sidequests with recurring characters worth doing.- Interesting and unique story.- Exploration and being inquisitive is usually being rewarded, thus making even dead ends worthwile.- Various small quality of life features like stamina automatically refilling when passing through a fog gate or quest indicators on the quick-travel list are highly appreciated.- Decent amount of map variety with enough unique locales to keep the game fresh throughout.- Main hub vendors inventories can be expanded.- The game is beautifully scored, the music heightens every moment.- The changing weather is a really nice visual touch.- Interesting roster of bosses, including (but not limited to): Beast-like robots, gank squads, Mr. X, cut content from Nier Automata, Nightmare on Sesame Street, Konrad the Traitor, and much more!- Mr. Venigni's dialogue is awesome from beginning to end.Negatives:- The story is being pushed onto you with the subtlety of a sledgehammer.- No option to switch between Xbox and Playstation button prompts for us Steam Input users.- The roll feels bad and off, because it is artifically gimped for the game's skill tree. Until you pump skill points into the respective perks, you are effectively being punished Dark Souls II-style just for the audacity of playing the game.- Enemy chain attacks - even when blocked [normally] - chip off a considerable amount of health.- There is no telegraph as to how many of these chain attacks are being chained together, it is random. Fuoco spinning five times in a row isn't challenging - it is just annoying.- The timing of certain enemy attacks feels "off", making it incredibly hard to judge when to time blocks. Not sure if this is an animation issue or whatnot.- The player has no poise, while enemies seemingly do. This makes trying to use heavy attacks for staggering enemies or trying to seize the stagger state a complete chore because you will be interrupted during these precious few seconds.- Player movement speed feels anemic compared to the enemies.- Enemies attack faster than the player can recover. Again, this is something that can partially be mitigated through the skill tree later on, but why is this an issue to begin with?- Perfect guard is just a split second, the window to execute is way too small.- Backstabbing is unreliable (does not work despite prompt or does work despite having no prompt) and seemingly vanishes completely in the later half of the game.- Game suffers from having Bleak Faith's long ladder fetish.Final thoughts:If only Neowiz hadn't tried to innovate on Bloodborne's combat system by introducing some of Sekiro's ideas into the game, we would've ended up with a good Soulsborne game. What we are being left with instead is an overtuned game that was made artifically harder by gimping the player and favouring the enemies to force the use of blocks over dodges and strongarms you into its own flavour of combat flow. Unfortunately, this isn't what I wanted from the game and therefore it is not enjoyable for me.So note: If you want Bloodborne-like combat, this ain't it - despite appearances suggesting otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've ever played. As my first souls(like) game it wasn't too difficult that I couldn't beat it (took me 40 hours in total). As any other in the genre, it had some frustrating moments, but nothing too ragequit-inducing.The story and setting create a great atmosphere that I would best describe as decaying steampunk, that of an almost deserted, once blooming, Victorian city, now turned depressing through its decay caused by the puppet frenzy.This is compensated by the feeling that the game gave off (at least to me) of a hope always existing somewhere far away, but nevertheless reachable, and it really creates a nice contrast. Speaking about contrast, game looks good without being too taxing, you don't need the latest specs at all to run it smoothly, and even the low graphic settings look solid.I don't know how well I can comment on the gameplay since, again, this is the only soulslike game I've played until the moment of this review, but the aesthetic and feeling it gives off while you play reaches artistic levels rarely seen in new games.Each hotel (your base) NPC has their own story which you can complete through the right choices. Paired with the lore dropped off in loading screens and collectible item descriptions and, of course, the main storyline dialogue and cutscenes, you feel as if you are slowly and subtly unraveling the secret behind everything related to Krat, while some mysteries may never become fully solved, leaving the truth to speculation.All in all, this experience is about becoming human and exploring a world that you feel was once your home, although, at the same time, you could've been a complete stranger to before.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a great deal here to love. The soundtrack is absolutely stunning, the atmosphere is both intriguing and curiously dark. The cast and crew are wonderful, and quite honestly the length of the game surprised me - it's not long, just more than I anticipated. Even the weapons, the variety, the design and ability to modify are really unique. Then there's the problems. The areas at first are really cool and quite intricate, but this begins to wane around the halfway mark as you begin to be dropped into relatively bland areas with some fairly painstaking bosses to overcome. "Tough but fair" for me applied for most of the encounters but there are some truly awful fights that did exceptionally well to highlight shortfalls that are present.It feels like things are butting heads. Parrying window is pretty tight and feels weird kinda often, and guard regain was of absolutely no value to my experience. (Though it certainly helps some of the bosses you aren't able to stay near) Delayed attacks are present effectively everywhere and in some cases quite extreme. Hit boxes are both great, and really bad, tracking in general could use improvement. Crouching through swings feels cool, but getting hit by a sword combo that ended five feet away from you is super not and an experience I frequently had. Aside from that, heavy attacks to complete poise breaks is tedious and often enemies seemed to become more aggressive/evasive in this state making it difficult to complete heavy attacks, especially those at the end of long strings due to weapon handles. This feels deeply counter intuitive and unrewarding.Difficulty is a contentious subject, so I will say that for me the pacing was very appropriate for the first half. It genuinely felt great in fact, many of the early bosses were fun to get to know despite the annoying delays. But the late game just sorta unravels. Bosses become hyper aggressive, but you can't really be hyper aggressive, and the systems fail to support what feels like an adequate response. The easiest way I can think to describe it is just like the fun turns into work. The last few fights, especially the last in particular, are what will stop me from coming back for a second run. If you are not familiar with the souls-like genre, this is probably a bad idea.If you are, there's some fun here but cherish that early ride cause the end is a straight up let down

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a pleasant surprise. I first realized Lies of P would be something special when I took a step outside of the tutorial building. The scenery with the rain was so peaceful, but also sad. It gave me a similar feeling to leaving the cave for the first time in dark souls 2. The kind of thing that makes you stop the game for a second to just take it all in.Beyond the incredible graphics and scenery, Lies of P has a fantastic combat system. I think the parry mechanic should be mandatory in all soulslikes. I can't get over how satisfying it is in this game. You also get a couple other tools to use like the legion arms and weapon abilities.I also loved the enemy robots how each one felt unique and dangerous. In a lot of ways Lies of P felt like a boss rush which is good. One criticism I have of darksouls is that sometimes the lulls between big bosses and normal enemies have too much variance. The bosses are basically maximum fun and progressing through the world is usually kind of boring. You basically do whatever you have to do to make it to the next boss. Lies of P is not like this. I found it very entertaining throughout. A lot of  the enemies felt perfectly balanced for me where I wasn't getting frustrated, but also felt really challenged. You get rewarded a lot for parrying so the system encourages risky gameplay. Because of this dying wasn't so bad because it my personal choice to parry the whole game.Strongly recommend Lies of P even at full price. If you are addicted to souls-likes this is a must play game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best "souls-like" game I have ever played which is not a FromSoft title. In fact, I would say that Lies of P is better than many FromSoft titles as well. From a story perspective, it beats ALL FromSoft titles, as there is rarely any understandable story in FromSoft titles (you often have to read up online about the lore behind FromSoft titles to understand what is going on). And the soundtrack to lies of P is spectacular. I bought it for $9.99 here on Steam and listen to it almost every day. This is a 9/10 game. If you like souls-like games, get it and play it. The ONLY reason I don't give it a 10 is because there is no co-op feature in the game. I really wanted to summon my friends and play with them in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: THE GOODThere are a lot of good things like the visuals and music, but they're all stolen.THE BADPLAGIARISMI have played many Soulslikes. I have played many games that took some of From Softs elements and mechanics and made it work.I played good and bad versions of those. I played Mortal Shell, I played Lords of the Fallen, I played Nioh, I played the Surge.Never have I seen a game that steals literally everything, down to the fonts.This game is not a Soulslike. This game is blatant plagiarism.First, I was enamored with the game. "Hey this reminds me of Bloodborne". "Hey this is also like Bloodborne, but worse".And all of those "Hey this is just like Bloodborne, but worse" quickly started adding up.The game is "very heavily" inspired by Bloodborne. You have a poorly implemented Rally mechanic,you have status buildups that work exactly like in bloodborne, the atmosphere and aesthetic played a "heavy influence", the dark symphonic music, the dark victorian theme, some assets are direct copies, the story is a direct copy of Bloodborne ("puppets gave gone mad, except you" vs. "hunters have gone mad, except you").Then there are giant rolling balls you have to avoid, the gestures (the shrug animation is literally identical), the quest NPCs behind windows, the cube being basically the Elden Ring teardrop flask, the entire Ergo system being literally Souls, the corpse run to pick back up your Souls, boss Ergo being boss Souls you trade for a choice between a weapon and an accessory, moonstones are titanite shards, the healing pulse (Estus) replenishing after killing a bunch of enemies existed in DS3, the prosthetic arm is from Sekiro.Hell, even the bad camera when fighting large monsters and EVEN THE FONTS are copied from Bloodborne.Even the basic mobs are a 1-1 copy of bloodborne's torch huntsman. Every time I fought one I expected it shout "Away! Away!"COMBAT- The game is basically Bloodborne but clunkier- No animation canceling- Input action delay- Action queue / animation stacking- Slow MC animations, especially in comparison to the opponent, meaning you get stunlocked- excessive amount of delayed attacks ruin the cadence and rhythm of the combat for me- basic movement abilities are locked behind the P Guard, like rolling twice with reduced delay (and even then the delay is still there)- The rally system, directly copies from Bloodborne. It worked in Bloodborne, because you were discouraged from blocking,there was not even a functional shield to find, you were encouraged to be aggressive and to attack, you could staggerby being hyperaggressive. In Lies of P, the enemies will be much more aggressive, start long combos you will have toperfect parry 8-10 times or dodge, meaning you can not really make use of this mechanic that is supposedly there toencourage you to attack to regain HP. It's just copied without understanding why it worked in BB.- Stagger is technically a good system, rewarding you for being aggressive. However, in order to actually staggeronce the bar is full, you have to use a (slow) charged R2, meaning you're most likely to eat an attack or possibly an entire chain of attacks. The enemies are hyper aggressive, so you are not very likely to find a window to do so.And once you stagger, the window to position yourself on the red circle and do a visceral attack is tiny, and you willoften miss it if you use heavier weapons. This combined makes this yet another useless mechanic that was copied fromSoulsborne without understanding why it worked in Soulsborne.Something odd I also found:- The stargazers are copies of the DS bonfires where you can level up, the first stargazer lets you level there, yet from then on, you can not level up at stargazers anymore and have to go to the hubCONCLUSIONMany games keep copying and layering Soulsborne mechanics on top of each other without understanding what made them work, and often those mechanics just clash with each other.This is another one of those. However, this is the most excessive, blatant, shameless, soulless and cynical example of it I've ever seen. At the same time, they managed to make the combat much, much worse.The combat is slow, unresponsive and clunky, your animations are slow, your animations are queued, there is no animation cancel, and you will get stunlocked. Not even the story has any signs of originality, being a direct retelling of Pinocchio.It's a shameless ripoff. If I want to play Bloodborne, I'll go play Bloodborne, instead of bad plagiarism of it.This game is what you get if you tell ChatGPT to make Bloodborne with a Pinocchio story.There is 0 originality and creativity in this game.The story is not their own, their graphics, mechanics, artwork, music is not their own, so how am I even supposed to rate it?I hope From Soft sues for plagiarism.no rating/10

_childDocuments_.review: Having completed Rise of P and taking into account all the ups and down. I am left with a mixed sense of appreciation, and apprehension for the title.  As a world building experience it takes its time to push you into the lore of your surroundings, which captivates and intrigues, as it seems to be a dark world of the fable Pinocchio that we know. While the world captivates, the characters in which you interact with are sorely lacking, leaving little room for dynamic character interactions and leans more into a senseless forced confrontation with little rewards. The environments do hold their own charm, each one lovely and holds a level of eerie the keeps you on your toes for a hidden enemy, or environmental hazard. The next part, i will warn of spoilers for some information centralizes enemies and combat mechanics. While you are confronted with various sets of enemies their main dynamic is the following. Puppets, Corpses, and Humans. While each one fights in a different manner they are relatively all easy to manage, sadly with little variation outside of the brute class which can be troublesome when you are unprepared. One way to combat these foes is the Legion Arm, While it comes is several forms many are actually unnecessary and could be removed from the game without it having any negative effect as a whole. Weapons are a controversial point as there seems to be an issue of movement, when attacking there is always a delay from when you press the button, to when the actual attack happens, this creates an unpleasant and more often then not unbalanced, frustrating experience. The delay is actually carries through all weapons regardless of weight, but the heavier the item, the greater the delay, even consumables take about 1.5-2 seconds before taking full effect. My major concern however. is the boss fights. While unique there is too large a struggle when all bosses have a more intense movement then what you, as the player, should have. This would not be a problem if the game itself did not try to force you to use blocking as a PRIMARY mechanic, which again, translates after a delay that only serves to sour the experience. Delays can be managed but if the formula that constructed the play style does not work then the formula needs to be changed. If the structure of a mechanic is flawed, then the mechanic must be fined tuned, removing any unneeded material that bares no genuine weight or benefit for the game. Does this mean this game isn't worth playing? It's hard for me to say for everybody that enjoys soul-borne style games. And this is the closest we will get to a bloodborne for PC for who knows how long. With rumors of a second game in development I would hope they fine tune the problems from this game, and improve upon them in the second. I do recommend giving this game a try however if you enjoy dark story telling, but please approach it with a grain of salt as it can be frustrating when the gameplay and controls do not mesh appropriately.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Soulslike games not made by FromSoft. If you wanted something to scratch the Bloodborne itch, this is it. Cons:  - Durability is a thing, but it can be restored with a infinite use grindstone in your inventory - When you have "Souls" to recover after death they are drained away as you take damage, but can be recovered if you kill the enemy that damaged you. - Dodging is basically worthless until you unlock the ability to chain them together and to dodge from a downed position, and even then Enemy Fury Attacks don't allow for Dodge I-Frames anyway. - If you exchange one of the "Boss Souls" for an Amulet instead of a Weapon you get locked out of a Cryptic Vessel Solution. (Frozen Feast)Pros: + Weapon Handles and Blades can be mixed and matched to your liking, as scaling and swing style is determined by the handle, and damage and damage type is determined by the blade. + "Souls" are dropped outside of boss arenas so you aren't committed to finishing the boss fight. + Parrying is very fun and works like Sekiro in a lot of ways. You can break enemy weapons by parrying enough times. + Stagger attacks can be triggered by parrying or damage, and it shows you where to stand to start it. + The level design is fantastic and they provide plenty of unlockable shortcuts in each area making traversal a breeze. + The graphics are beautiful and really scratch the "Victorian Gothic" itch. + Runs great on my machine. No crashes, and only 1 notable bug that only happened once and was fixed with a reboot. (I died to a grab and the game did not send me back to the "Bonfire.")Overall fantastic game, even most of the cons are nitpicks. Buy this game when you can!

_childDocuments_.review: Soulslikes not made by from fall into basically three categories:Good - Nioh, Jedi Fallen Order/SurvivorOk - Lords of the Fallen 2014, The SurgeReally Bad - Mortal Shell, Code Vein, Wo LongWhen they get things bad, they get things REALLY bad. And when they get things good, they are fun but missing a little bit of the magic that FromSoft is able to do.UNTIL NOW BAYBEEEEEELies of P is the most perfect From clone of all time and in doing their best imitation job they didn't try really anything that drastic to subvert your expectations. If I fell into a coma in 2015 shortly after completing Bloodborne and then woke up last week and you told me this was a spiritual successor I'd believe it completely. Combat is both punishing AND fun. The areas, even the annoyingly designed ones aren't long enough to have you dreading them even on a second or third playthrough. The bosses are tough enough that you will hardly beat any of them in a single try (I only did two) but fair enough that you won't spend nearly as much time as you did on Malenia or Isshin. The story isn't much here, but it is enjoyable and unlike Dark Souls you don't have to read 1200 item descriptions and watch 6 hours of Vaati on YouTube to piece together 30% of it. A must for fans of the genre, and the first Soulslike to firmly be in the GREAT category.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Masochistic Memory-Based Quick Time Event (Soulslike / MMBQTE) games on the market today. A solid 5/10.As a post- Soulslike, the game utilizes the same QTE-based gameplay of , which was evolved from that used in .The optimal strategy is to limit movement, position yourself so the camera isn't stuck in a wall, and hit one button to perfect guard. You'll be doing a lot of waiting for the right moment to hit the QTE parry.Where  and  displayed button prompts or a symbol on screen, indicating the need to press a different button to pass special QTEs,  turns the boss red but still requires the single guard button to be used.Animations are core to the Soulslike experience and where most fall short. Having smooth animations results in a game that's probably too easy for the Self-Flagellents of the Cult of Souls, so developers are using new techniques. uses fast windup animations with severely delayed swing animations to trick players, while  showers the screen with particle effects to obscure both windups and swings. simply chooses a random direction for your dodge, regardless of which buttons you are pressing at the time. takes the approach of divorcing windups and swings entirely, focusing on brute force memorization of timings. It's not hard, but until you learn the timings, the developers intend for you to spend a lot of time in "You Died" loading screens, core to the Soulslike experience.The color palette of the game is an award-winning relentless gray-brown. Light sources are exclusively orange-brown.Every location is littered with dead bodies (= Soulslike).It has Victorian-era architecture, which is almost as Soulslike as castles full of dead bodies. It's also used in , , , and .This is a good Soulslike / MMBQTE, one of the best available.For $60, though, there are better QTE-based memory games. It's flashier than the Concentration card game, but not as dynamic.I might finish the game eventually, but coming off of beating  twice in a row recently, I need a break from Masochistic Memory-Based QTEs for a while.
