_childDocuments_.review: I want to summarise this review first, and I might change it later. I think the game is OK, but has a lot of major (and minor) design issues. I think unless you love standing still and learning the block timings for every attack, you will not find this game as fun as other Soulslike games.- General animation jank and core combat isn't super smooth compared to other modern Souls offerings.- Lots of convenience features that should be in the game but aren't- Lots of confusing mechanics or oddities that are poorly explained (e.g. leveling)- Weapon animations are very lack lustre.- Enemies reading your controller inputs to do frame perfect dodges. Some even do Dark Souls style parry+ripostes on you from controller reads.- Seemingly no super armor at all, even if you dump all your Fable into 1 attack. This isn't in and of itself a huge issue because the game can be designed around it. But this game isn't!- Because dodging is completely useless (which is something I will address in major issues) the choice of equipment heaviness is meaningless. You might as well just pile on the equipment because dodging is practically worthless.- Also -- weight of items just seems to solely go up. I've encounter no 'pretty good for a light armor' options, and all my amulets (Elden Ring Trinkets) just get more and more weight as they get more useful. This means you're really forced to level capacity, and just choose the heaviest equipment. No creativity.- Net effect of the above two is that so far, about 14 hours in, there are no real equipment building options other than which weapons you use.- The stages are jokes, barring a 'mini boss' or two in the dungeons. It's only the Bosses that are any challenge. Unlike other Souls games, the stages themselves are basically 0 threat. The monsters are basically complete fodder.Sekiro, Wo Long, and other Souls games all have the choice of blocking, parrying, dodging, or just running out of the way. Each works well for different attacks and is a valid choice for particular reasons.But in Lies of P the only thing that matters is Perfect Block. Positioning and movement have almost no effect on boss fights, other than not getting stuck on a wall. So it never feels particularly fun to fight bosses.You literally just stand still, watch their weapon, and perfect block spam. In 90% of circumstances dodging is *strictly worse*, not a valid option with different advantages and disadvantages, just worse. So you stand still and block, that's the gameplay.In Souls, you fight a boss and you die to hits overhead attack. You recognise the telegraph and you either block, parry, dodge, or run out of the way. If you fail, you get 1 hit (mostly). If you die, you know why.You eventually figure out what strat works for that attack... and for all the other attacks! And then you beat the boss and you feel great!!But in Lies of P? There is only ONE answer to how to deal with the fight: block.Run #1. Perfect block 80% of the attacks, not enough, you run out of pots and die.#2. 81% of the attacks, not enough...#3. 82%...#10: Finally, p.block 90%, which is enough to beat the fight.It doesn't feel like 'understanding the fight' and defeating it. When you die it doesn't feel like you've done anything fatally wrong. Each attempt feels like you doing the same thing. Then you just win. There is no creativity of 'figuring out the strat', just: block better bozo. I don't know why they thought this was a good idea. Babies know better than to design games with mechanics like this. There is nothing extra I need to say about this. It doesn't add meaningful choices like in Monster Hunter. It doesn't fit the gameplay. It is just TERRIBLE and UNFUN.When you perfect block you are rewarded with no damage taken, but also a large amount of damage caused to the enemy's stagger bar (hidden, which sucks -- dumb design choice), similar to Sekiro/Wo Long. However, to confirm the stagger you need to do a SLOW heavy charge attack and land it.If the boss jumps back, or you're just not in a decent position, then you will miss the timing to confirm the stagger, and you will lose all the reward of being a badass perfect-blocker. If the boss starts an attack, since we have no super armor (see moderate issues) even on our Fable attacks, you'll just get interrupted. 🤡From a game design point of view, perfect block -> eventually stagger -> execution attack, is crazy fun (as demonstrated in Sekiro/Wo Long) and it's a great way of rewarding the player for good play. One of my favourite mechanics of all time!But Lies of P basically spits in your face w/ a randomiser. If the boss jumps away, does a combo, or is just generally fast? Good luck landing the charge attack! You can make all the best choices as a player and still get screwed. 🤡There are SO MANY things in this game that feel like "Wow... this is literally just Dark Souls" or "Wow they literally just took this from Bloodborne". But unlike other Soulsborne games which try to make significant fundamental changes to the formula, Lies of P tries to play it straight... keyword TRIES.Lies of P will have the NPCs speaking in cryptic and mystical ways, and they have items with lore descriptions in them! Just like Dark Souls! BUT... it also has NPCs narrating at you for minutes at a time, characters that won't stop lore dropping you in the middle of a fight to explain stuff, and also about 50% of the treasures you'll find on the ground are journals for you to read to learn about the lore, rather than useful items. If wouldn't be a big deal if the game was clearly aiming at a story-strong Soulslike (like, say, Code Vein or Nioh, which have a lot of cutscenes) but they're clearly trying to do a Souls-lore thing... and so it just doesn't work!The writing overall is also poor, and the English dialogue, while not machine translation level, is very odd at times and clearly not intentional. From Soft did god tier level work to get the English dialogue to be as good as it is, and this team just doesn't have it yet. It's genuinely a pain to listen to half the characters, and it feels like an amateur trying to replicate Souls style dialogue and failing at it. Other Souls-like didn't have this problem, because they did their own thing and weren't trying to be the closest thing to Dark Souls.There are also more minor things like... They want you to level up at the Maiden character... Just like Dark Souls!! except they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ it up by having you level up at Bonfires initially, then they change it after the first boss fight without much explanation. I went all the way through the next boss questioning why the bonfire wasn't work!They also literally put the Physick flask in the game... except it sucks ass. It takes forever to activate, only gives you one minor effect. And it *doesn't regen with rests* you have to go find a specific character off in the middle of nowhere to get your flask charge back. It's completely useless.They even do the Quest NPCs you can talk to through the windows thing that Bloodborne does, except it's very hamhanded and token. It feels like a cheap way to not need to make an NPC model, rather than something that adds a lot of interesting lore and surviving life to the dying city.There is more to complain about but I literally can't fit in this post.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is like an amalgamation of SEKIRO and BLOODBORNE but in a slower pace than the both of them, the game is the closest to a different company creating fromsoftware game i have seen so far!1. The story itself combines certain aspects of: Lovecraft, Stephen king, Bram Stoker and combined it with apparel from the rennaisance and 17th to early 19th century architecture (kinda). It becomes an incredible story in many aspects as well as the game itself giving out small little points of references towards: Great litterature works from different times such as Berserker and Pinocchio, hidden as well as visible points of references towards Fromsoftware (this in turn can create fanfiction which can tie the worlds together in terms of storytelling which is a great litterary science technique! Props to the creator from me here!).2. The combat system is fluid, a bit slower than bloodborne/sekiro but not as slow as Dark souls 2! There are as well numerous combat/game mechanics which both rewards the player for learning them and utilizing them but there are also mechanics which PUNISH the player if they are ignored or not improved upon (which is a very good balance and follows in the footsteps of Miyazakis most beloved Fromsoftware games).Enemies themselves are not that difficult (there are ofc exceptions such as "elite enemies" and certain enviromental combinations which makes the game much harder) and the bosses are very well made in terms of combat and visual/sounding/enviromental aspects! The BOSSES themselves act as difficulty spikes which give an immense sense of achievement when beaten but they also give the player the KNOWLEDGE of what needs to be improved upon in order to progress the game further. This difficulty spike system, according to me, is a very well thought up system that makes the player feel good about fighting them and eventually defeating them!3. Audio and Video is very well done in so many ways that both new fans to Soul-like games can enjoy but also veteran soul-like players can appreciate and truly love. Voice actors from different Fromsoftware games have been included, such as Anthony Howell who voiced Margit The Fell in ELDEN RING.The localization of the game may seem odd but it is very VERY similar to Bloodborne, this may both a minus or a plus depending on your own subjective view on it!Video in itself (cinematics) are well created and give off a certain auro/vibe to it depending on your location, an example is *NOT A SPOILER* when certain bosses would enter the boss arena in tune with a certain enviromental setting and allegorical reference towards litterature, the sound itself that the player hears and the music that amplifies it just makes the experience better (and ofc the graphics of the game is really well made, had to put that in somewhere!).All in all it isnt as high on a pedestal for me as lets say Bloodborne and Elden ring BUT this game has truly won a place in my heart, not only because of the actual game but also because of the many aspects of kindness and respect towards other creators AND players.Highly Recc this game!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Lies of P is a Souls-like masterpiece. The gameplay itself defied my expectations, with a parrying system akin to Sekiro and a rally system much like Bloodborne -- but while still being a game with its own identity. The story itself made it worth playing as well; some Souls fans may not prefer the more straightforward nature of story delivery, but to me, a story worth telling is one worth telling in plain view. Looking forward to what comes next from this studio.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never played a souls-like before, but this is a lot of fun! I had to work really hard for the first boss, but I felt so accomplished once I got him! Graphics are gorgeous, and the soundtrack and voice acting is great. Some of the controls took some getting used to, but I swapped the interact and the jump, and now it's pretty sweet! (xbox controller) 9/10, I recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: I guess most people like the game. As much as I tried to love it... I just can't.The look and sound is great. Also, I like the general idea of the game. But the amount of bugs and glitches I experienced are just ruining it. Enemies that are stuck in walls, attacks that go through any collider and teleporting/jumping enemies to call a few.On top of that, the combat system is a bad joke. As a fighting game player, it is extremely annoying me how badly this was implemented. So many moves that should actually hit are not registered properly. Then moves that should never hit... well they do hit. Inputs often feel delayed and imprecise. Turning every fight into random ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Not even to mention how stupidly the enemies behave. It couldn't be cheaper. And to finalize the rant about the combat system... It gets sooo boring. You are staring on a monitor for minutes just to see the same moves and animations over and over again. Almost as exciting as staring onto a blank wall.So what can I say... I tried to love it but the mission failed. I still think that this game could actually be good. But not in its current state.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: The best non from-soft soulslike I have played. The only real issue is the world generally being a single complex corridor. Having no alternate paths to take through the world generally kills it's replay value. Outside of that combat is excellent, world and enemy designs are great and the game runs well. An easy recommendation to anyone who enjoys soulslikes or newcomers who are OK with a challenging game. Super impressive for a first attempt at the genre so many people get wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best action-RPGs of all time. Its customizable weapons and bevvy of universal spell-like actions encourage players to engage in problem solving deeper than "git gud". Despite how strong the RPG elements are, this game's  in the best way—the action hits hard and fast, and you've gotta use every tool in your toolbox to survive and thrive. I've replayed this game (including NG+ cycles) about 4 times now and still finding ways to improve, more weird ways to approach encounters.Played it on GamePass and loved it so much I bought it here and transferred my saves over (which is a hassle).

_childDocuments_.review: When i first saw the concept trailer ages back for Lies of P i was intrigued by the premise and love old fairy tales but i had my doubts about a newer studio handling a souls type game. I played a few clones this year that did not quite cut it but Lies of P is quite the masterpiece.Fantastic gothic setting and a grim fairy tale story which is incredibly well told through NPCs and the odd cutscene. The mystery of Alidoro was particularly interesting as was the overall concept of telling lies and how it impacted each character.Fighting mechanics which for me is the most important factor of a souls like are spot on with every hit feeling solid and a balanced counter system that never felt unfair. I used two weapons for my first play through that i maxxed out but there are loads of weapons for you here to play with and customise along with the usual boss weapons and P's arm which has a multitude of uses.Graphics were truly beautiful as was the score, i have not unlocked all the albums yet, but the ones i found were great original pieces.Are some bosses annoying? of course. But this is a souls like baby, so expect to get your ass handed to you a few times, nothing too taxing though once you learn their move sets.I don't like to throw the term goty around often, but unless Lords of the fallen blows this out of the water. Lies of P is my game of the year so far and im excited to see what the studio puts out next.

The springs and cogs that made up his body sparked with life, as the Tinman succumbs to gaslit truths...Deep within, he knew he cannot die, arriving at a hotel, he chooses to lie...By following whispers the Tinman found his secret, inside held the key, to knowing his youth...The heart of a puppet beats loudly, for the fairy begs forgiveness...The clock strikes, for the strings began to wither, Geppetto's Puppet became ever darer...The arm binds what was thought lost, a father's sacrifice, he gives us...The Tinman grows angry, ending this error, but there was still something he had to give her...Finally he rests a sorrow head, for the fairy thanks this Tinman...Ruby slippers tap 3 times, we as the viewer, know there is something bigger...Thank you for reading, Wolv-REX. -Lies of P-

_childDocuments_.review: Common enemies are too easy and then bosses are ridiculously hard. Numeros combo attack chains leaving little opportunity to attack. Also, the game is extremely linear. You can only follow one path and that's it. There isn't any concrete way to upgrade defenses and even weapons all seem to be the same when it comes to dealing damage. There's very little you can do as a player because even upgrading status isn't game changing, so the only way to beat bosses is to memorize their punishing attack combos. it's not fun that way.Also, most bosses start to have second phases and if you die on the second phase, you need to start from scratch. Again, IT'S NOT FUN. I am not recommending this game until they fix this.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: Wether you decide that this is inspired by or simply a rip-off of Bloodborne, either way you still have to admit that there was passion in its creation.It may be cliche and done to death by now but I absolutely adore this grim and gritty rendition of a classic fairy tale and I feel it fits right in amongst the soulsborne genre.The pacing and flow of the game feels quite natural in terms of events and exploration; whilst there's a lot to see and discover, you never get too lost or too constricted.Combat takes some getting used to yet after a time feels familiar and intuitive. A nice feature of being able to mix and match different blades to handles means you can form the perfect weapons with the right damage types and move-sets for your play style, and there are a great many weapons to find and unlock (with this game having possibly one of the greatest and just straight up fun DEX weapon movesets in all soulsbornes, and I say that as a STR player at heart).In regards to design, I feel that everything fits quite well.Don't even get me started on the music. I thoroughly enjoyed all the tracks in this game, especially the records, just an absolute delight.Visually, characters and locations are both beautiful and mysterious, enemies are equal parts cool and horrifying, I very much adore the old, Victorian AND eldritch horror style.Attack timings can seem a little weird at first but they're nothing the average gamer can't get used to, just like with all games of this type you simply, observe, adapt, and overcome, or in other words, git gud.One thing I could complain about is that when you talk to someone they lose their dynamic audio and sound like they're coming from the centre of the screen, even if they might be way off, at the same time you can't move your camera at all during dialogue so after certain cutscenes you're staring directly at the back of P's head and can't see the person you're talking to. It's not a great, big problem but it is a little annoying at times when I'm just out here trying to appreciate the visuals and the scenarios of the game.But that's all I can think of at the moment.A phenomenal experience of a game and just a lot of fun in general.I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review: "Lies of P," developed by Round 8 Studio and published by Neowiz, is a game that not only redefines the Soulslike genre but also reimagines a classic tale with a dark twist. This game is a harmonious blend of challenging gameplay, captivating music, and a unique narrative inspired by the story of Pinocchio.The gameplay in "Lies of P" is a delightful mix of familiar Soulslike mechanics and new, innovative elements. The weapon diversity is particularly noteworthy. Each weapon brings its own flavor to the combat, allowing players to tailor their playstyle to their liking. The Legion Arms stand out as a highlight, offering a variety of unique abilities and playstyles. During my first playthrough, the Aegis Shield became my go-to weapon, providing a perfect balance of offense and defense.However, the game's side quests leave something to be desired. While the main narrative is rich and engaging, many of the side quests boil down to simple fetch quests, lacking depth and narrative intrigue. Despite this, there are a few gems among them. The side quest involving Alidoro, and the fox with her brother cat, are particularly memorable. Alidoro emerges as one of the most interesting NPCs in the game, with a backstory that adds a layer of depth to the world of "Lies of P."When it comes to boss battles, "Lies of P" does not disappoint. Each boss is a masterpiece of design and gameplay, but three stand out: the Nameless Puppet, Laxasia and Romeo. The Nameless Puppet presents a haunting challenge, its mysterious aura adding to the intensity of the fight. On the other hand, Laxasia is not only visually stunning but also boast an impressive moveset that makes the battle both challenging and exhilarating.In conclusion, "Lies of P" is a remarkable addition to the Soulslike genre. Its unique setting, inspired by the tale of Pinocchio, sets it apart from its contemporaries. The game's music is a hauntingly beautiful accompaniment to the dark world of Krat. While the side quests could use more depth, the main narrative and the boss battles more than make up for this shortcoming. The weapon diversity, especially the Legion Arms, adds an extra layer of enjoyment to the gameplay. "Lies of P" is a game that not only Soulslike fans but also lovers of innovative storytelling should experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Lies of P

_childDocuments_.review:
You wake up at an abandoned train station in Krat, a city overwhelmed by madness and bloodlust. In front of you lies a single note that reads:

"Find Mr. Geppetto. He's here in the city."

Play as Pinocchio, a puppet mechanoid, and fight through everything in your path to find this mystery person. But don't expect any help along the way and don't make the mistake of trusting anyone.

You must always lie to others if you hope to become human.

Inspired by the familiar story of Pinocchio, Lies of P is an action souls-like game set in a cruel, dark Belle Epoque world.

name: A Little to the Left
detailed_description: Sort, stack, and organize household objects into just the right spot in A Little to the Left, a tidy puzzle game with a mischievous cat who likes to shake things up! Puzzles hidden among household objects Multiple solutions make for intuitive and satisfying puzzle design A puzzle unique for you every day with The Daily Tidy Delivery Perfect for casual puzzle game fans and those who get a jolt of satisfaction from a well organized space Feel free to skip levels with the 'Let It Be' option, and choose when you want to tackle certain messes Need a hint? A little or a lot? With a unique hint system, you control how much of the solution is revealed in each level. Which way should the clock hands point? How to arrange the eggs? Who put so many stickers on this fruit?!? Come enjoy a calming world in an observational puzzle game with surprises around every corner. Featuring charming illustrations and surprising scenarios, A Little to the Left is satisfying and curious with over 100 delightful puzzles to discover. Keep your eye out for a mischievous cat who has an inclination for chaos! In the Daily Tidy mode, you’ll get a puzzle delivered EVERY DAY with variations on our favorite puzzles that’s unique to you. Find all the solutions each day to earn fun badges! If only tidying in real life was this rewarding. Want that festive joy in July? Feeling like a fright in May? A Little to the Left now features a puzzle Archive, granting permanent access to the formerly limited-time seasonal levels. Now enjoy messes based around Xmas, Easter, Halloween, and more, no matter the month. FEATURES: Over 100 unique logical puzzles Quick-to-solve puzzles make for satisfying gameplay Intuitive drag and drop controls A puzzle unique to you delivered each day with The Daily Tidy Delivery Multiple solutions Charming illustration Atmospheric sound design A mischievous (but very cute) cat Funny and playful, great for all ages!

_childDocuments_.review: An entertaining and charming short and simple game that unfortunately frequently flirts between relaxing cathartic organization and frustrating OCD-esque nitpicking very quickly.I would not recommend based on:Several instances of interactable elements randomly stopping responding, forcing a restart of the puzzle.Many puzzles in certain chapters become trial and error; Chapter 5 is most egregious for thisAn optional onscreen menu button would be appreciated for accessibility, ESC is the only key used on the keyboardHints are typically just flat out answers for 1 completion method, and kill immersion by requiring several steps to view and return to the puzzle: ESC>Hints>Manually erase scribbles on notepad>Onscreen 'X'>Resume) each step with a ~1-2 second animation that has to playGetting 100% of the achievements requires both   and   days of completing a Daily Challenge level

The actual games are also not nearly as detailed as the handful of levels you see on social media, they are mostly sorting rocks, or leaves, or jars of sand. _childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a very casual and fun organizing game. I really enjoy the levels where you put items in specific slots, but I like the variety in puzzles. The achievements are fun, and I think that having more than one way to complete some levels adds a challenge, but still keeps the casual flow of the game. The daily tidy seems to be a nice add-on, allowing for a "new" daily puzzle to scratch that organization itch.If you enjoy puzzle games, then this one is totally worth it. I did get it on sale, but I think I enjoyed myself enough to say it's worth the price for those who truly enjoy putting things exactly where they belong.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredibly satisfying. The sound and visual design are excellent, and the puzzles are the right amount of challenging. Lots of fun and so far I've found that it has a good amount of replayability with DLCs, achievement challenges, daily tidies, and other tidbits. I can also see myself picking this up again in a few years for a full play-through and not remembering the answers to puzzles. This a wonderful cozy game, I love it!

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for A Little to the Left to come to iPad since the game first came out. Decided to wait no longer and am playing on my PC and laptop. _childDocuments_.review: [EDIT] Just so you know, the last DLC is riddled with bug, and instead of making an announce so you know that X level is currently bugged, they do so in a discussion so they don't tarnish their release with "warning it's bugged". This will honestly affect my review of the game as a whole, it's an unacceptable behavior to hide what is happening and leave you searching for half an hour just to avoid to have an announcement which would let you know that this and that thing aren't fixed.I have some difficulties to judge this game, even though I bought it at release and played along the dailies and specials. Dailies are actually my problem and what is making me want to give this advice : Buy this game on sale.A Little To The Left is a cozy puzzle games which will allow you to relax and even scratches that itch of "I want everything to be ranged in this specific order" as it's the point of it. The whole game in itself is satisfying, as I said, it scratches that itch and does it properly all along its numerous levels.HOWEVER, if you're expecting the same for the dailies, prepare to be disappointed. The dailies are no others than a little selection of those puzzles you already solved with random items coming from other puzzles, but it's only a few of those puzzles on repeat over and over again, which means that this itch that brought you to that game is now tainted by the fact you already did those 10 puzzles in repeat (I honestly think it's more around 7 identical puzzles all week long) but there is no novelty beside that today you'll be sorting pasta instead of leaves. I do appreciate the addition of specials for Christmas and Easter, but I would love even more than instead of those 10 puzzles, every single one of them would be added little by little so you don't feel like you're doing the same thing every day for the sake of getting your achievement, because at some point, it becomes more that than scratching an itch. You already know the limited set of dailies and it's "one more thing do do" rather than being surprised by this one puzzle you didn't have since a while.So this is my plea to the dev : You promised dailies, dailies there are but doing the same set 100 times is honestly not a pleasure. Your puzzles are already made, so add them little by little to the dailies instead of serving the same annoying set of sands to sort by range of colors and then by shape which I seem to get 3 times a week and got me away from the game for quite some time. The material is there, pretty please, make the dailies fun and not a pain.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really fun puzzle game.Not for someone who needs high levels of stimulation, this game is very relaxed and chilled out. Literally, you organise stuff on every level. The final level is a fun mix of the puzzle skills you've learned. It is fun to try and discover the different patterns and that some levels have multiple solves. I also love that when you play there is no time limit, no stress, just you and the puzzle, you also don't have to find all the solves when they have multi-solve levels which is a nice way to keep on moving through the game if you get stuck. The way clues are done is also very helpful, you rub out the page to show the solve meaning you decide just how much of a hint you get, a perfect mechanic for me when at times I just needed a little guidance and didn't want to spoil the fun of actually understanding the pattern.I'm especially grateful that the game is not traditional puzzle based, I get so stressed out by traditional puzzles, this is more about pattern recognition, something I adore!!

Currently playing the DLC, 4 levels in and quality is still top notch.Edit 2 hrs later:Im about halfway in to the DLC and I am disappointed that at least 3 of the levels have been "petting cat". I can see by the icons of future levels that there is more cat petting. They shouldnt have been levels, but merely cut scenes. Also, I hate cats. I they were dogs I would be less disappointed, but still, calling it a level to click on a cat's face once is cheap af.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice concept, but far too many puzzles just don't explain themselves well at all.  For example there's a pegboard where you hang tools, but it's entirely unclear what the points on the tools are that will  interact with the pegs, sometimes going so far as communicating with the player incorrectly that some parts CANNOT be used to hang the tools because they don't grip.. until you find the one place that they can.The game is at its best when the puzzles are extremely simple and obvious and just pleasant to advance through.  The trickier ones are just poorly tuned.  Puzzle design is hard, but if you choose to make a puzzle game that's the stuff you have to get right.The game includes hints, which is a good idea.  However, most of them are really not hints at all, just showing you the solution state instead of giving you a hint as to how to get there.  As a result, for some puzzles, the "hint" leaves nothing for you to consider at all, just copy the layout.  For others, it gives you no help at all, as you still have no idea how to achieve that layout, even if you might have already been trying to achieve it. As above, hinting for puzzles requires laborious play-testing, but it's simply part of delivering quality puzzle experiences.---I will add that the DLC gets a lot right that the base game did not.  It would probably be more worth it to buy the DLC without the base game if that was an option, but it's not.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Idk if it's my autism messing things up for me or what, but my (mis?)understanding of A Little to the Left going in was that this would be a super chill puzzle game. No stress, multiple solutions, cute albeit pesky cat that pops in and doots stuff around with his paws just to mess with you antagonist-style. What I got was...not really that. And I was not only disappointed, I was actually pretty angry. I got this game on sale and I still think I paid too much.The puzzles start off fun. They scratch that particular "everything in its place" itch, as so many others have said. But the game quickly devolves into, "Wait, what the hell am I supposed to be doing?" So many of the puzzles have just a single solution, and SO many of those solutions are so utterly convoluted and/or arbitrary that it became incredibly frustrating. And by the time I've clicked around enough to finally figure it out, the puzzle gets ripped away from me before I can properly observe/glean satisfaction from what I did. Worst of all was the Polaroid puzzle. An online walkthrough I looked at literally said, "This is the solution. I don't know why." What kind of game design is that? And what's more, THE CAT IS BARELY THERE. Do not promise an autistic lady a cat and then cheap out! >:(I also agree with another user who commented that the end sequence went on for an absurd amount of time. Like...absurd absurd.Just get Unpacking.

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left advertises itself as an "tidying simulator" and that is true for some of the puzzles. I enjoy the way all of the objects feel and sound when moved and how they all snap into place; it's very cathartic. However, I think a game like that comprises of only that would get old quickly and luckily the creators of this game seem to agree. You quickly learn that many of the levels can be solved in multiple ways, and that's where the secret genius of A Little to the Left is unlocked.The game, especially over the course of its expansions, morphs into a puzzle game about recognizing logical and visual patterns. Since the game never gives written instructions on anything, you're really forced to sit there and scan for the little details in items. I was frequently blown away by comically tiny details such as the lines on a mug because you realize how intricately every item in the game was sculpted to make these patterns line up. Not all of the puzzles are amazing at this, but when A Little to the Left is at its best there's not many other puzzles games quite like it. Don't boil this title down to a "wholesome cleaning game"; it's a lot smarter than it lets on.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A charming puzzle game based around organizing various things. There are quite a few different styles of puzzle to organize, and many have multiple solutions to them. Most of the solutions are pretty intuitive, and although one or two of them seemed daunting at the beginning none of the puzzles were frustrating and almost all felt satisfying to solve. Overall would recommend for anyone looking for a laid back puzzle game, or looking to scratch an organizing itch.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this was supposed to be a relaxed game but boy was I in for a treat hahaha not only is it relaxing and soothing but it also has some challenges that once you solved them you feel good about your in-game organizing skills. It scratched a party of my brain I didn't know needed to be scratched.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Not only are many of the puzzle solutions entirely too specific/fidgety (to the point that even with a walkthrough I had to on multiple occasions play "hunt for the exact correct rotation/placement down to the pixel"), but many of the puzzle solutions require a color gradient as the solution.  As someone with mere color deficiency (not even color blindness) I found these almost impossible to solve without a walkthrough (and some even with).  The developers even noted this on their "list of things to address" with another review ages ago, yet it still is not implemented despite the game being on its first DLC.What was billed as a relaxing and satisfying organization game became an experience in frustration and anger the further in to the game I got.  Can not recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: You know how in life you want everything in order and then everything is perfect? Well, nothing in life is like that! I have developed a love/hate relationship with this game. It's way more fun than first appears but be careful because it's way more difficult! If you are a casual gamer who doesn't care if you get every achievement  you will be happily content with this game! If you are like me who isn't satisfied with partial completion of anything then be prepared because some of the achievements will take you over 100 days to get and you will have to play this more than once. I am in love with this game though. I want the cat for my own and I just love a little challenge in what I do. Have fun everyone and understand it is ok to get help with a level if you need it. Besides if you do get help then that person will buy the game for themselves and you'll have more things to talk about. Just be careful when you go shopping. Your brain will see everything in the store and you will find yourself creating ways to fix the messes of the world!  Zen out everyone and I'll see you on the Tidy side!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game in a bundle and I would technically say I got my money's worth out of it. However, there is some glitches I've encountered, such as finishing the level right and it still not saying it's complete, which seems to be a reoccurring issue for me. It's a shame because I can tell this is a good and satisfying game when things run well.... I'm holding out hope that the glitches will be tidied up eventually.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: In the vein of Unpacking, "A Little to the Left" is one of these cozy games with no pressure, puzzles are cute and accessible, very satisfying (a lot of them revolve around organizing), the theme is very comfy and the art is lovely as well. It took me a few hours to finish, and I still have a few things to do (you can complete some puzzles different ways and I want to explore them more!). Strongly recommend :)Bonus points: cats <3
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This DLC for the game is super cute but there are a handful of levels that you just simply pet the cat and thats it and theres a bunch of levels that are pretty quick and seem like not a lot of thought was put into saying that, there are a bunch of really good well thought out tough levels that were really fun and interesting to solve.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely sweet cozy game! Really enjoyed the playthrough. I definitely recommend not watching a lot of gameplay ahead of time because you can get spoiled very quickly. The only minor thing I disliked was that on some of the organization levels you could get small things overlapping with the handles to open and close drawers and then because the drawer was in the way you couldn't get the small thing back out, effectively softlocking the level. Visual & sound design was excellent & I will happily buy more DLC!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I'm becoming way too addicted to this, I always love organisation games like Unpacking and stuff like this, so this is a treat for me. I personally turned off the music as I wanted to hear the chimes if I did something right, but when I had the music on it was lovely. It's a great game, and the cat is a menace, so the puzzles where it shows up are always a...albeit frustrating, treat :D  (reminds me of mine!)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Satisfying and simple game about organizing. Rarely, some levels can glitch out and not give you a completion star despite matching the hint exactly, but even if that does happen, there is a "let it be" option for skipping levels, and you can come back later and finish it when it starts working. Sadly, very little replayability and can be beaten quickly once you understand what the game expects from you to complete each level.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: very chill game. a couple levels had me stumped a little bit, so the hint option was really helpful! The cat you see every so often was really cute, and it was nice that you could see it try and mess with a couple levels. The ending was very cool when you turned into the cat and could mess with the previous levels! _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Overall very cute game, creative puzzles. HOWEVER, two maybe drawbacks on the game (for me):1.) The Seeing Stars DLC was infuriating, I felt the strong majority of those puzzles were not intuitive, or had multiple logical solutions that didn't count as solves.2.) As someone who enjoys 100%-ing games, the achievements in this are absurd. With some examples being "play 30 days in a row" and "complete 100 'daily tidies'". Forcing your player base to do daily check-ins (when the entire game is otherwise completed) takes this from a puzzle game to a chore very quickly.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: i loved playing through this game and figuring out all the puzzles, especially the ones that make you think for a little while. finally understanding the objective on a level and seeing it organized in an appealing way make for a very satisfying experience. i just wish there were more levels. it took me about 3 hours to complete one star on all the levels, so i'm hoping some new content gets released in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left has some interesting concepts for puzzles, and playing through it is entertaining enough, but I think the puzzles could be explored and made better. The game has a bad flow, with slow switches between puzzle, menu and so on. Additionally the cutscenes are boring and un-skipable. I like the idea of the star system they use for multiple solutions, but immo more puzzles should have multiple solutions. I don't really like the hints for the levels. First of all, they don't help with multiple solutions (as far as I'm aware), and secondly, they don't explain why you are doing it. Showing a picture of what you are supposed to do is kinda boring, but I guess it's cool that you have to reveal it yourself.Lastly the daily puzzles suck. Very repetetive, a bug/bad setup here or there, and just kinda boring. Also very easy to just work around the "daily" part of doing them. Just an unnecessary padding of extra content, to make the game seem bigger.In the end it's not that bad tho. If you want an organising-game it's worth a play, if you are looking for a puzzle game, I'd say there are better picks.

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy, relaxing, and overall delightful. The puzzles are fun and varied, and each one typically has multiple ways that it can be solved which allows the game to be replayed at least a couple of times. The art style is charming, the music is a great accompaniment, and there's a cat. Enjoyable and worth a play through if you're a fan of cozy, relaxed puzzle games.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing cozy game. Perfect for procrastinating actually tidying up or just continuing if you already did so. It is obvious this was a labor of love game for the dev team.The art style is minimalistic, the colors are pleasant to the eye and the music is relaxing. Perfect for a little breather from real life responsibilities.The puzzles themselves aren't that hard to figure out, altho the alternative solutions aren't always the most obvious (the third solution for leaves took a while for me). The pacing they created with puzzles is amazing to me since I didn't know that was possible to do. I Love what they did at the end or rather with the puzzles at the end, it gave me a great feel good high.While I do recommend this game for those who like puzzles and get a kick out of making things tidy, I must say I expected more content out of it. Its a solid 4 hour game (i did all the puzzles including the multiple solutions in this time frame) and for the price it's at i feel like it should have been more content to it, so i recommend getting it on sale if you are used to getting more than 4h of gameplay inside of this price range. That said it does have daily puzzles that are different everyday and work up to achievements that give it more replay value, since base puzzles stay the same.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I hoped this would be another zen game like Unpacking. I was sadly mistaken.I want to like this game very badly, but I just can't in good conscience recommend it to anyone. The idea of having little guidance is fine in theory, but more than a handful of puzzles are so abstract in what they expect out of you as to be baffling. And I say this as someone on the spectrum, when even I struggle to see the pattern they want, you might have messed up.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game and in theory it was perfect, but it has so many issues that make it unenjoyable. For starters, I personally find the music and sound effects to have a lot of sudden high tones which are not relaxing in the slightest. But that's easily solved, just kind of defeats the purpose a little bit.The controls are god awful. My resolution is set correctly yet it makes me play with a giant cursor and some of the puzzles were resulting in my mouse going off screen and my movement snapped back to what it was before. I tried playing with a controller and it was the most frustrating experience ever, there are too many things to move around from and it's too clunky.The puzzles were cute and I liked the idea, but in a game where some of them have multiple solutions, why not ask us if we want to try again for the other solutions? That just didn't make any sense to me and the menus feel so clunky that going back to do that is a pain. Also some of the solutions are just weird depending on how your brain works. There's one set with some books and they're SUPPOSED to start with ONE big one, the smallest going in the middle, and back up to a big one. I personally did it in decreasing size order because that's how I'd personally want to organize something like that. And playing on a controller and having to move all those books around? No. I personally feel like a game about moving things to organize them should give you a little bit more freedom, or I guess have more solutions stored. Everyone arranges things differently and being stuck in a box with this makes it quite annoying. Even Unpacking has a mode that you can freely place things and while that wouldn't translate exactly here, I think having one solution for most of those puzzles is a mistake and makes it less appealing to people who obsess over organization.Let's not beat around the bush, this game specifically appeals to people with various mental illnesses and the way they set it up doesn't work well with those mental illnesses. I'm sure for some people this is great but if you have issues letting go of control or need things to be a certain way? Pass on this.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a delightful, stress-free experience perfect for those who find joy in tidying up and organizing, all within a beautifully crafted and relaxing world.Offering a soothing, orderly escape from the chaos of everyday life, the game invites players to sort and organize household items, turning mundane tasks into satisfying challenges. The simplicity of arranging books, kitchenware, and office supplies based on size, color, or shape becomes surprisingly addictive, especially when a mischievous cat adds playful disruptions.With over 75 puzzles, the game gradually increases in complexity, requiring more thoughtful solutions as you progress. While the early levels are straightforward, later puzzles introduce more abstract thinking, making each new challenge feel fresh and engaging. The game’s warm pastel visuals and soothing soundtrack create a calming atmosphere, encouraging players to take their time and enjoy the process.Despite a few puzzles that might feel a bit obtuse, the game’s hint system provides gentle guidance without giving away all possible solutions. The inclusion of a “Daily Tidy” feature adds replayability, offering new puzzles every day.Overall, A Little to the Left is a tranquil escape, perfect for those who find peace in putting things in order. With its gentle challenges, relaxing visuals, and calming soundtrack - it offers a stress-free escape into a beautifully crafted world where the simple act of creating order brings satisfaction and peace.It's asking price is pretty fair, but I'd personally get it when it is on sale. It regularly goes on sale for under $10 and is totally worth it at that price point.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Charming and enjoyable! I can feel the love put into the game from every ounce of content, my only real gripe would be that there is, very minimal replay value. I do understand however that that is simply the nature of this kind of game. The achievements for the long term daily check ins do honestly feel odd when aware of the fact that you would likely only open the game to do the daily puzzle. Aside from that I do honestly recommend the game for anyone who enjoys virtual organization and relaxing puzzle solving.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: As an artist who loves puzzles, i found this game quite enjoyable. Its art style is so welcoming and warm (like a home) and just playing through it you can see just how much effort has gone into the design, story, music, sounds and overall variety of puzzles. Some are simple, some have multiple answers and some are just satisfying. I found it gratifying when i was able to figure out the harder multiple answers, although i haven't figured out all yet ;). Its a simple concept which is why i feel this game has gone above and beyond in its relaxing and cute game play. I was excited to play this game and was not disappointed. I really do love the art style too
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Any and all satisfaction from arranging things was lost due to the irritating UI: - Having to watch the animation of my completed levels play in its entirety before being able to select a level to go to. - Spending more time trying to get the item to fall into the EXACT place in order to complete a level, when visually it was already correct. Spent more time on some levels spamming left click to try and find the exact pixel it needs to line up to despite already finding the solution- For some reason, despite releasing an item, sometimes it would continue to move out of the position I'd placed it in, resulting in having to once again find the EXACT location- Solutions are vague and arbitrary, which became more annoying the longer the game was played
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A very relaxing, but sometimes tricky puzzle game. But be aware that you won't have 50 hours of gameplay. I think the price is okay because the game looks pretty and you can see the love the game has received. If necessary, get it on sale.The levels don't always have just one solution, which I really appreciate. But I'll be honest, I wouldn't have come up with some of the solutions myself. I had a lot of fun solving the puzzles and can only recommend the game!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: The soundtrack and art are very pleasant and nice, the levels are short yet numerous enough to feel like a full game, and the levels themselves are satisfying in a way that their generally low difficulties are not drawbacks. The option to skip a level and come back later is monumental for preventing the occasional hard level from breaking your momentum. You can bet I'll be replaying this and scampering all over it for all of those achievements). Also, the developers truly understand cats on a deep level.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say I’m glad I bought this on sale. The art direction and the idea behind the game are great. The execution was lacking for me. I found myself to be increasingly frustrated because more often than not the goal of a puzzle was not clear to me and even if you’ve understood the goal there’s little to no indicator if something quite literally needs to be placed just a little further to the left or right to be considered correct. This caused me to rearrange whole puzzles even though my initial solution was correct but the game didn’t recognise it as such. After a while it also became quite repetitive. I wish there was a neutral button but I can not in good faith give a thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, but rather short.  I enjoyed most of it, but there were some issues that bothered me, and maybe worth considering by those wanting to buy it.  The biggest problem I had was that the puzzles don't have any introduction as to what you have to do to solve them.  On many puzzles, this is the biggest challenge.  Once you figure it out, the solution is trivial.  I am not fond of this genre.  I like a challenging puzzle where the rules are given to you and you spend your time applying them to solve the puzzle.  Anyway, there is a hint system, which can unstick you and there is also a "let it be" button to skip. I used both.  In a few cases, as far as I could tell, the puzzle was solved , but it wouldn't move on, so I used the latter button. Despite my annoyance with some aspects, I still recommend it heartily.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I sincerely think it's not fair that you've added demanded daily play achievements for 100% completion. Can't recommend it for that reason alone, even if the game itself is short and sweet.EDIT: It appears that a developer has responded to this review. Please do understand that while I did enjoy my time with this game, I cannot support daily grind achievements. While there ARE many people who enjoy daily tidies, there are people who DON'T at the same time. By adding these, you're locking several players out of 100% completion.What if somebody isn't able to get to their computer one day? A 30 day grind achievement is REQUIRED for 100% completion, and if somebody misses a single day? Boom. Done.I'm sorry, but I still do not think these should be in the game. By rewarding fans of the tidies, you have accidentally created a situation where you've locked several people out of a complete experience. My genuine suggestion is to at least remove the DAILY ones. The 7, 14, 30 ones. These lock a HUGE majority of individuals out of the achievements at hand.Please do keep in mind, I am a fan of what is here, and I would legitimately love to give this game a positive review for the gentle puzzles and serene atmosphere. But I'm sorry, I just do not think it's justifiable or correct to have these achievements on hand.
