_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a text-free zen puzzle experience, with a surprising amount of depth and challenge to it.  If you're expecting narrative with mindless puzzles thrown in, that is not what you're going to get...  be prepared to get stumped again and again!Even more involved are getting all in-game stars and all Steam achievements.  I'm very impressed by this game; much moreso than I was expecting to be!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I really really wanted to like this game. The graphics and art are super cute and nice. Though I found the puzzles to be very unintuitive and boring. i found that most of the puzzles barely made sense even after checking the hints and the ones that did make sense were very unsatisfying and anticlimactic. And fwiw im typically someone who avoids hints and guides up until the very last moment when i am really 100% stumped, i enjoy working out even the toughest puzzles on my own. I kept waiting for the puzzles to get better or for there to be some sort of story along with it but sadly neither happened. The puzzles were too boring or illogical for there to be no story, it needed serious compensation. The puzzles that didn't make sense even after the hints really felt like the devs just chose random placements for things and then stuck with it. if you didnt get the exact pattern right, the puzzle wouldnt be solved, even if there was no rhyme or reason to the "pattern". I found myself just copying the hints like i was copying someones science homework without actually studying it myself lol. it sucked. honestly, if you want a good satisfying puzzle/organizing game, just play Unpacking or Assembled With Care. I was really disappointed, Ive been waiting for this game for sooo long!!! I expected more. The cat was cute though, but not enough to make up for the lack of good content. :((
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Super chill game, was worth the wait! The DLC also is a great add-on. Some of the solutions are things that would have never crossed my mind, and some achievements are a little glitchy and have poor descriptions, but a very enjoyable game to complete. Still have some of the Daily Tidy -achievements to gain, so I'll try to keep on top of that.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderfully calming game about organizing a home. "A Little to the Left" provides a beautiful gaming experience that encourages players to slow down and enjoy the space they're in, working through simple puzzles while enjoying the beautifully simple artwork. If you rush through it, this game can be finished in a few hours, or you can take your time and stretch out the gameplay. Daily tidies and small secrets throughout encourage the player to continue to return to the game in order to discover every solution.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Puzzles are very fun and engaging, with a lot of clever details hidden in the puzzles. Whilst the puzzles can be relatively challenging, some are quite easy, and most puzzles can be completed in under 10 minutes. It also features a nice looking art style and overall is well designed, The game is a bit pricey for the amount of content, at a bit over $20 AUD, and finished the base game in a bit under 5 hours. They do upload daily puzzles, but most of the ones I've seen are just repeats of puzzles from the base game, and aren't as engaging as you already know how to solve them. Overall still a good game, I thoroughly enjoyed playing it and recommend it to anyone looking for a puzzle game, especially those new to the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A little to the Left is beautifully illustrated puzzle game that will get the gears turning in your head. With that being said I feel it is a little pricey of a game.  I would definitely wait and pick it up on sale.Pros:- thought provoking puzzle- Select puzzles have multiple solutions- Visually stunning- There are daily puzzles, but keep in mind they will be similar to puzzles you have already completedCons:- Price point is a little to high
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: With all my love... get this when it is on sale. It's a fun time waster. Need to kill time before another game releases, this is perfect.This will not fill that puzzle game itch.Think more -Unpacking- which this game should just be bundled with.!!! If you can't distinguish colors in the thumbnails then this will be unplayable for you sadly!!!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: One of my favourite cozy games. the levels keep you on your toes and have lots of hidden little achievments in them. As a completionist freak you can definitely spend some hours here and not get tired at all. Fun to solve with friends as well. For me the DLC's are totally worth it. It's hard to find a game as well done and PURRRRFECT as this one:)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a nice, relaxed puzzle game. There's no pressure from a timer or any other reason to rush, and that's good. Because honestly some of the puzzles are downright un-intuitive.I found I either needed to use a hint, or mess with stuff for a good while on a level before something "clicked" and I suddenly got what I needed to do.The game has a good number of Steam achievements, providing decent replay value. But added replay value comes from the Tidy of the Day, which is a nice way to not have to engage the story, but still take on a quick puzzle.I recommend A Little to the Left, as a relaxed but challenging puzzle game with a cute story and relatable premise.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is the kind of game where I really wish there an option for a middle choice between "I recommend" and "I don't recommend." Basically my experience with this from puzzle to puzzle was all over the place. I'd say between 1/3 and 1/2 of the puzzles left me deeply frustrated for reasons I can't give other than "that's not how my brain works." I would run into puzzles where I flatly could not figure out what it wanted from me, and others where I did something that made total sense to me wasn't an acceptable solution (that second thing wouldn't bug me except for when I found out some puzzles have multiple accepted solutions and somehow what made 100% sense to me still wasn't among the solutions). When it frustrated me, it REALLY frustrated me. But the hint system got me through, and some of the puzzles were deeply satisfying to figure out on my own. So... I just slogged through the frustrations for the hit of joy when one fully clicked with me. So call it a tepid recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really nice and calming game to play. There is a DLC that I have yet to play, but its just really fun to play with the music in the background after a long day of school or work. I highly reccommend this to people looking for a chill puzzle game (especially if you like organizing and/or cats)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I truly adore "A Little to the Left", it's fun, can be challenging and it's like a good scratch for that certain part of my brain that likes to sort and group things.I'm really into completing all of the achievements, so I'm definitely going back almost everyday to do my dailies.However, I also can understand frustration that the game is kinda short and if you're done with it once, there's almost no fun in replaying. If you're not an achievement hunter like I am then it's completely understandable. Maybe devs can bless us with some DLC in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Although this seems like a game that will go by quick it's very fun and the daily puzzles keep it interesting! I was very happy when they released both DLCs and I hope they keep making more content. Once everything is played through it is fund finding out how to solve the remaining achievements. This game is perfect for those cozy gamers like me and won't hurt you if you have motion sickness!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing! The DLC's always are just as high quality as the base game, and it's all worth the money. DO NOT SEARCH UP SOLUTIONS TO THE LEVELS. I did, and I regret it because I would have enjoyed spending more time on the game trying to figure it out myself. Left me with a comfortingly sad feeling while playing, though I don't think it was intended.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: That was a very fun game. Main Graphics are cute and cozy, music relaxing. I enjoyed multiple ways to do certain levels. Some little details were annoying to check and change when I thought I did everything right.Main levels were awesome, had a bit of a theme to them. Seasonal levels were a fun addition. I didn't really enjoy the daily levels - they were fun for few days, but got boring/repetitive pretty fast. As for playability - it is possible to play levels again after finishing the game for the first time. But, knowing solutions it wont be as fun. The game has few hours of content + extra seasonal/daily levels. It can be worth it but on at least 50% sale.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a little more thinky and puzzle-like than I expected, especially after playing Unpacked, but it still feels Zen and is relaxing because there's no pressure to complete the puzzles. They have a quite good Hint feature that helps you with how the puzzle could be solved without just showing you the solution. You can even choose an option to just let it be and move on to the next puzzle if you don't want to finish one. It's a great game for me for winding down.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly as satisfying as you think it will be! The puzzles are grouped into various themed "chapters" and many of them come with a variety of possible solutions for you to try out. So, once you finish with one solution, you're encouraged to go back and try to discover more before you move on to the next puzzle. It's very relaxing and lasted a lot longer than I thought it would....took me about 5hrs to get through. 7/10
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable and cozy puzzle game with a mischievous cat for fans of Unpacking. Most puzzles are incredibly intuitive, especially once you take the time to explore a bit without hints. Would just recommend purchasing when on sale because playthrough is very quick, which makes its higher price point feel a bit inflated unless you plan to take the time to 100% everything.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left feels like is was made for me. As someone who habitually sorts their effects with purposeful direction, I found myself kicking my feet with glee upon sorting so many of the solutions in this puzzle game. It's hard to put into words, but this particular style of puzzle just makes my brain happy.Fortunately, puzzles are not constrained to orthodox or practical sorting solutions. Instead, you frequently must perceive overarching patterns in minute details. For example, a series of objects may form a continuous pattern when arranged properly. When properly arranged, the solutions are so satisfying I had trouble tearing myself away from the game.The puzzles strike a great balance of genuine headscratchers, and simpler yet still gratifying arrangements. A Little to the Left trusts you as a player, offering no tutorials or explanations for its puzzles. Inevitably, there will be the occasional alternate solution which leaves you stumped, and though rare, some of these are not altogether intuitive.The game wraps up in a surprisingly sweet and arresting ending, and its feline "antagonist" is such a cute little fella. Then the DLC presents more involved puzzles which utilize the recurring patterns seen in the base game in larger spaces, often utilizing multiple patterns for different series of objects.I adore A Little to the Left. No puzzle game has quite scratched the itch like this one, and I was joyous as I played through it. While its specific style is personally appealing, I also just think it's a tremendously charming puzzler all its own, and I encourage you to give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game while housesitting and I pretty much completed the entire game. I have not tried the DLC's yet, but I really liked the base game, especially all the achievements you can earn. Very nice to decompress and zone out to.Update: I have played the entirety of Cupboards & Drawers and I really liked it! Definitely recommend it if you are looking to expand the base game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo awhile back and instantly was in love. I'm very happy to see this game out now. I've played a lot of different puzzle games and this one is unique. Really scratches that itch to straighten and sort things. Some of the puzzles are head-scratchers, but it's good to stretch the mind. They balance out the soothing, easy puzzles. The music and art style is great too. For those wondering if the price is too steep, remember it's made by just two people who spent a lot of time working on something fresh for the puzzle realm.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, However once you're finished, you're finished. You can buy the DLCs sure, but then after you finish those, there's nothing to do. The daily challenges are repetitive and some of the levels you just pet a cat. I paid five dollars just to pet a virtual cat. The game is fun, satisfying, and makes you think really hard sometimes about the solutions, but I wish it could just expand without needing your money. I get it's an indie game, but it's a little annoying. My advice is to probably just clean up your in real life room. Remember to support your local small business.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking forward to this game for a looooong time. Just bought it and I'm loving it. I got through half of it in my first sitting and I can't wait to keep going! Bravo to the devs.Update after completing all the puzzles: This game is grrrreat! The final chapter has some very wacky and clever puzzles. Overall, I completed all the puzzles in 3.6 hours. Great game!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking for a relaxing but satisfying game after Unboxing, and this looked very similar. You basically just click and drag objects until they are in some kind of "satisfying" order, like arranging books in height order.The first few levels were easy, but satisfying. Then the game quickly devolved into really confusing levels where it's not clear at all what you're supposed to be doing. For example, there's a level with a calendar and a pack of stickers with flowers, dots, squiggles, etc. Some stickers have already been placed on the calendar, so you need to figure out which days you should put the rest of them on. After a while of not being able to figure it out, I went to the forum, and someone said that you just have to put a sticker every 9 days. Why? I don't understand. What appointment does anyone have that is every 9 days?? How is the player meant to figure that out???After a few of these puzzles I was becoming genuinely irritated. I don't mind paying a lot for a niche indie experience but I'm probably just going to refund this one.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Over 3 hours of bliss, took my absolute time with this game and it was really what I needed. Very calming and a bit cheeky with the cat, loved the ending and interaction during the credits. Makes me think of games like Gorogora, Unpacking, and Windosill. It's very user friendly with hints if you get stuck on the puzzles, and there's the option to skip a level altogether, and no timers involved! Beautiful art style and very appealing colouring, nothing too overwhelming at all! 10/10!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It's really expensive for the amount of puzzles you get and the playtime, it took me about 2-3 hours to finish the entire thing with 100% completion I would only recommend getting it if you really really like puzzles, and waiting till it's on sale to get it. Also there is a daily puzzle which is pretty neat, and probably how I've racked up so much playtime
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A delicate blend of: cute, elegance, challenge, elegant design, and cat memes. The game is woefully short, but it makes up for it with a delicate charm. I found most of the puzzles to be "easy", in that it was clear what the game wanted you to do and how to do it. About 5% of the levels and additional solves required a bit of savvy but not in a way that would be frustrating for the user. This game was oddly calming for me while I've heard others say that the game feels frustrating. There is no time pressure here; take your time and find new ways to look at things. On a final note, I found the game's music to be mesmerizing, even luring. Any puzzle fan should have this game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: There's really not a lot here to justify purchasing this at full price. The levels are pretty repetitive, with mechanics running old after awhile. The daily tidy's are really misused, and you'll find yourself doing the same levels over and over, meaning the one thing pulling you back goes stale quick. Also Whenever I open the game the DLC for it appears in my shopping cart, so I don't like that.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. It was sold to me as a really satisfying and zen game about organising things. A part of it is, and those parts are fantastic. The art is simple and cute. It has all the right parts to make it a great game. But it isn't. To much of the game is increasingly difficult and obscure solutions to, what should be, simple puzzles. Do the developers expect me to sit on those leaf levels (especially the second one) and trial and error the solution? Without giving to much away for people that do what to try this game. This "puzzle" involves selecting the right items out of everything or it resets. Normal games have visual indicators or patters to assist this. This game said no to that. Why are those blank screen and random item "puzzles" like that? I thought it might just be like a timed thing where you can move on after playing with the items for a certain amount of time, or that there was some sort of picture to build. No. There is a picture to build...a hyper specific picture...with no reference to it...and everything has to be specifically placed or you won't get the level. Honestly, I never thought a game about organising would need a walk-through, but this game does. It is also super sad to see the walk-through's with explanations for the solutions to the "puzzles" being "I have no idea why this is the solution, it just is." I think that is the problem. The "puzzles"exist to stump you and be different. Not to scratch the itch that organising brings. The game does have hints though....and by hints....I mean they give you the answer. I'm assuming because even they know that some solutions are too stupid and complex for anyone to spend time figuring out. To be honest, I wouldn't recommend this game to anyone that wants to have a relaxing time. There are better games out there.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game and it's right up my alley in terms of puzzles. This is not a simple cleanup/sorting game so it can leave you frustrated at times but I found the puzzles pretty rewarding to complete. I will admit I blazed through it pretty quickly, so I'd love to see more added to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I 100000% recommend this game. A Little to the Left is just so cozy and relaxing. And I believe it has a high replay-ably I replay it ALL the time. It does not get boring in my opinion. I would love more levels, I wish it was like Candy Crush with like 1000's of levels cause I would every SINGLE one. They even have the Daily Tidies, which is like a daily remastered version of the levels not in the DLC pack (but don't quote me on that not too sure if they used any from the DLC but I don't think so). You get one daily tidy a day and they are different everyday. I absolutely love this game, thank you Max Inferno and Secret Mode for this game!! :)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It definitely didn't pass the dollars to hour requirement. Some games pad their score by simply having such a memorable experience that a short time is enjoyable.This ain't it.The puzzles were mostly just too easy, but were held back by the fiddly method of executing the solution. I'd often be right, but I hadn't nudged the object into the correct pixel, which eventually led me to check hints to verify if I was the moron, or if the game was the moron (it was the game).
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I really love the concept and I had it wishlisted for a year or longer and played the demo. The only thing that really bugged me is how finicky some of the puzzles are..like I'm looking at the hint doing exactly what it says to do and it won't clear the puzzle. Overall it's fun if you like casual games and love to organize but it fell a little short for me personally. I think I just had higher expectations after waiting for it to release for so long. I thought the game would be like a relaxing multiple solution puzzle game but it's not. It's pretty much JUST a puzzle game and not relaxing at all. The longer I played the more frustrated I got. Also for just 4 hours to complete everything it's a little overpriced. I just expected more and am pretty disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: while some of the puzzles are fun, they really require you to think like the developers and not think logically. the price is also a bit absurd considering the length of the game and simplicity of the puzzles, which are usually "arrange from tallest to shortest," "arrange symmetrically," "put in boxes," and occasionally something so obtuse that the hint actually makes you angry. If it were under 5 dollars it'd be okay, but for the price its kinda disappointing
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I love this little puzzle game, just bought the DLC. It's a great break from other games if you play multiplayer or competitive like me. It will pick your brain sometimes, but it's very satisfying. I hope they continue making more content like this. Highly recommend especially if you just need something to relax and focus on.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and relaxing game. If you love puzzle pattern games then this one is for you. It only took me about 4 hours to finish the main game plus the DLC, and by finish I mean get every star on every puzzle. Was a little disappointed that 4 of the DLC puzzles (so 4 of the total 29) were just petting a cat. If anything I think those cute tidbits should be added on at the end or beginning of a puzzle. That's pretty much my only complaint. I love that there's daily puzzles you can do and the more you finish the more badges you get, it keeps me coming back to the game. The music is also absolutely gorgeous! Love love love this game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: For a game that's supposed to be relaxing, the poor detection makes it anything but. It seems like almost every level even after solving the puzzle I then have to spend five minutes inanely nudging it a pixel at a time before the game realizes I solved it. Several puzzles I would use the hint just because the game wasn't recognizing my answer, and the hint would depict the exact solution I had performed that wasn't being accepted. No thank you, my blood pressure doesn't need this.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This has to be one of my favorite puzzle games ever. Art is really cute, love all the colors, music is good and even sound effects are satisfying. I love this game so much that at this point I've played most of the puzzles multiple times. Now I just remember a lot of the solutions so well that I can't really play the game anymore hahah. Was super excited when I saw the news about a DLC and got it almost immediately. The DLC had some of my favorite puzzles and I loved it! Absolutely loved playing Little To The Left so I hope they'll add more content (or make more DLCs). It's a short game so it's easy to finish in a few days.I love that there's a lot of different types of puzzles. A lot of them are easy and chill, some of them were honestly so difficult that clues became very handy. It's just too bad that when the puzzles has alternative solutions, you don't get any clues for them.  It's easy to get stuck in some of the puzzles but I guess it's also a good thing that there's some real challenge too. The game really forces you to slow down and be creative.If I had to say something negative about the game, it would be those daily puzzles. They keep repeating the same ones and when you're trying to get the achievements for completing a ton of them, it gets really boring and tiring. I get that making a different puzzle daily is probably impossible, but I do wish there was more variety. I mostly gave up and will just finish one here and there if I feel like it now. They do add seasonal puzzles which is really nice.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A really cute puzzle game! It can be very satisfying to sort things but it can also be frustrating. Sometimes a solution is exactly what you think and sometimes the way you would actually want to sort the items isn't a solution at all. It is nice that many levels have multiple options though. Overall, I recommend if you like sorting and organising!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I played unpacking while I was pregnant because I was trying very hard to avoid stress at all costs. This game has been recommended to me since but I have ignored it as it didn't look like my kind of game. But I gave it a shot and it has been a lot of fun and sooooo cozy! If you don't like spending time figuring out puzzles this one is not for you. I encourage you to take your time because if you use hints and rush through you will complete the base game really quickly. I look forward to playing the DLCs. :3
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the most amazing things I've ever downloaded. I watched the Game Grumps video on it, and immediately loved how calming it looked. It has this soft and complementary color scheme and flow to it that's extremely relaxing. Each puzzle is different, and you get to stop thinking for a second and just try to figure it out. I like that some of the puzzles have several different ways to solve them, and I finished the whole game in one night. If you like organization or have issues with calming down, it's a great game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I beat this game a little while ago after getting it in a humble bundle, and I thought that I'd leave I review! It's fun, relaxing, and very low-stakes, including a hint button in the pause menu that can be very helpful if you're beginning to feel stumped. Many of the puzzle solutions are clever, but not so much so that you don't have an idea for where to start. I decided against getting the DLC, but only because I enjoyed the more mundane object sorting levels over the cupboard and drawer levels, which the DLC is themed around.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It's like their demo had the best level taken out of each section of the game. Not having guidance in an organization game is fine, but this one gets so abstract that you don't know what you're doing. they give you *some* indication by making things click in place, which doesn't really feel satisfying and it feels even worse when a cat knocks over all of your work. It feels like if I don't know what the puzzle solution is i can just wave my mouse all over the place until something clicks. The worst puzzle so far is the one with the . I still don't understand it. There should be a better hint system. they are NOT hints, they are quite literally just the solution for the puzzle. I thought and hoped that this game was going to be a satisfying calming organizing game but it's a puzzle game, which wasn't what was displayed with the puzzles shown in the demo which we're more focused on easy calm organization. One might question, maybe I'm just bad at puzzles? Let me show you the  puzzle or quite a few in this game and see if you can solve them with no hints or context on what is supposed to be done.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game. Some levels are not easy though, and some levels are also repetitive. I love organizational games though, so I do enjoy it for the most part. Be prepared to be amazed at what some of the solutions look like because some are absolutely tough. There are some where even with the hints, I still don't get /why/ it's the correct solution.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, "A Little to the Left" is a very enjoyable and satisfying experience - even if a few of the puzzles are not quiet as intuitive as probably intended (the hint mechanic will save you in those rare occasions). Lovely art style and animations, wonderful soundtrack, lots of achievements. Perhaps a bit pricy? Nevertheless, I do recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: The art is really charming and I like the puzzle design. I get tired after doing a puzzle or two and so I only play for a few minutes a day at most, but I feel like that's how this game is best played. It made me sad to see so many people complain about the price; I feel like it's well worth full price for an entirely hand drawn indie game that's very unique and whimsical. The creators did an amazing job.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I have been wanting to play this game for a long time after seeing other people playing it and finally I get my hands on this game. It is relaxing yet needs some brainstorming to understand how to solve certain puzzles. There are also a few ways to complete several puzzles. Nevertheless, it was fun. By the way, there is an achievement if you do not scratch any of the hints and there is also another achievement for using the hints several times. Obviously, I needed to use some of the hints when I got stuck. LOL
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I'd recommend this game to someone who doesn't like how open ended things like Unpacking or House Flipper etc are. If you want a ton of short low-key Warioware-ish puzzles with specific answers to find you'll have a great time with this. Unfortunately for me I think I prefer something more open-ended. Sometimes I didn't like the organization methods chosen, or the categorization felt really strange or counter-intuitive to me, and there's no allowance for that in the solutions so it started to just get frustrating. I tried to go back to it again more recently and had the same issues, so I think this one's just not for me.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I went from finding this game incredibly frustrating to appreciating the game for what it is. I'm a person who has a hard time seeing other's perspective.. And that's why I had a hard time with this game. I had such a hard time seeing other people's solutions so I had to look up how to do certain puzzles. But I have to say after 13 hours in the game that the more I play the better it got, I started thinking outside the box. I have now replayed the game 3 times and bought their dlc.  My next goal is to 100% in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I paid $15 for this game. For that price, I would have expected hundreds of levels, and that isn't the case. The puzzles are fun, I enjoy the atmosphere, and the art is lovely, but I am a bit disappointed at this price point. I understand a 2D, animated puzzle game takes more effort than a 3D one. However, I would call this a $7-$8 game. There is a 'daily tidy,' but- if the first day is anything to go off of- they may just be rehashes of the levels themselves. I would definitely like to see this game be updated with more levels.Wait for it to go on sale. The only reason I have 8 hours on it is because I let it sit up on my computer for a while; I could have realistically finished this in 1.5-2hrs. And, admittedly, some sequences feel a little bit  drawn out, even for a slow, relaxing game like this. Credit sequence was very cute.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for an unpacking game this is not it. I saw some videos that made it seem like it was but there are very few levels that give that vibe.  This is a puzzle game. I love puzzle games though however, some of these puzzle seem impossible to figure out with out looking at a guide. One specific level that comes to mind is the one with sea shells where you have to put them in a pattern and maybe I must missed something but you could have sat there for hours trying to figure it out and still got the pattern right. If you like brain teasers, really hard ones, from time to time this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Im going to be completely honest, I saw this game on TikTok as well as from various streamers. It seemed like a pretty chill game. I went onto steam and noticed how it was like $15 and thought that was an okay price for such a chill and stress relieving game. I literally finished both the original game and the DLC in around an hour. I spent al most $20 on a game that can only be played once to enjoy. I am so disappointed in how short this game is. Yes, Im aware of the "daily sorts" but they are usually so short and are quite literally copies of other sorting levels. I cannot believe I spent $20 on this game let alone paid any money for it at all. This is a game that could be purchased on the app store for like $2 if not for free. I do not recommend this game. Save your money and literally just watch someone play the 20 levels this game provides.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Unique puzzle game about putting stuff where it may or may not belong. They have daily puzzles and some extra DLC. Some of the placements don't really register unless you try and click them into place multiple times, mostly on any level that requires pattern creation. Overall, a decent puzzle experience. Despite a few tiny annoyances, it's a solid game. Anyone who is a fan of cozy/puzzle genres would enjoy a second playthrough after the first completion.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty boring, pointless 'daily tasks' connected to alot of achievements to just drag out the game (if you like getting achievements anyway) Would be 10x better if you could at least place objects wherever to find a solution but almost everything has a set place so doesn't allow for any creative funny/dumb solutions.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this. Okay, some of the levels might seem a little unclear to start with, but there's a hint available. For the most part it's soothing and very playable. Being neurodiverse, this one lands in all the right places, it's so calming and pleasing to create order out of chaos, and recognise patterns. Not sure why tidying up a cutlery drawer or toolbox is so much more pleasing to do in a game than in real life, but there you are. Many medications have been no help in dealing with my panic and while therapy does help it is a slow process through small wins. This game has helped me calm down many times during those long nights, when I had originally thought there was no end for the panic in sight. _childDocuments_.review: A Little To The Left is a series of puzzles that center around ordering items after certain criteria and figuring out what the ideal way to stack, sort or align certain household items is. These can be either very simple, like correctly rotating a picture frame so that it hangs straight, or can get quite complex, like having to sort in an entire toolbox. The game is incredibly visually appealing and has very well-selected color schemes, great background music and a beautiful variety of items that you have to sort into very statisfying arrangements. Gameplay-wise I found it a lot of fun to figure out the "twists" of how to sort items, as the game keeps their levels and setups quite creative, and the levels are short enough that it's hard to stop playing. Even the type of items to sort and the environments to sort them into are very varied. My one annoyance with the game was that sometimes it's not very well-communicated if an item is actually "locked in" to the spot, or if the game doesnt fully recognize it as being located correctly, and when you just sorted 35-or-so items and *something* is not correct, that can be quite frustrating. Sometimes it's a bit hard to really understand what the game wants you to do exactly, and I had a few levels where I had to brute-force the start a bit to understand where I am even supposed to place things. And there were 2 or 3 puzzles that I found a bit too much "out there", where it was a bit hard to really understand what the level actually wanted me to do. (and if you suck at jigsaw puzzles there will be one level that will drive you absolutely up the wall) Overall, I think the game wasn't fully what I expected, but I don't really mean this in a bad way - I expected it to be more of a Zen-like "order these items however you want" type of game, but I found the puzzles to be very engaging and the game really did a lot of creative stuff with this basic premise, and quite positively surprised me. Some levels were a tad bit frustrating, but they're usually balanced out with a lot of fun and creative levels in-between. This is definetly not among the most memorable, impactful or innovative games I've ever played, but it makes for a fun evening or two playing through it and is quite beautiful to look at and fun to interact with.

It is indeed a short game but I found it very enjoyable, but I can see how it wouldn't be for everyone. I love puzzles and I LOVE sorting and organizing things. The nature of the puzzles, the music, and the art were very soothing for me. I've been having kind of a rough time with life lately and this game was a very comforting way to "problem solve" and sort of zen-out. Like some other reviews have said, the control/cursor can be a little annoying sometimes. I only struggled with a handful of the puzzles, in terms of being completely stumped at what angle to solve it from, and usually if I step away and come back to the game later or another day, with fresh eyes, I was able to solve it. A couple times I resorted to using hints.overall, if you like puzzles and sorting, and you like chill music and cute pastel art, i'd recommend this. I hope they release more games like this or a follow up, because I could happily keep enjoying this for a long time.

He is an adorable fluffy villain (but only of other and organisation). And honourable mention for all the beautiful furry and featherly babies at the credits - love them too!This is just such a love project and it shows. If you enjoyed games like Unpacking and want to add some puzzly challenge to the mix, you SHOULD get this game!

The sound and visual designs are wonderfully cozy, and I love the kitty who seems determined to mess up the perfect organization! I imagine some might find it annoying, but as someone who's had cats for almost my entire life it is a very cute - and accurate - inclusion. _childDocuments_.review: -  A Little to the Left is a gorgeous game dripping with mid-century Realism. Many of the levels and their contents look like they were ripped directly for a 1950s home ec textbook-  The use of color is also nice. I liked how most levels used a restricted palette, giving each a screen print sort of feel-  While the soundtrack wasn't bad, it did feel a little out of tune with the visual style. Given the artwork that harkens back some 70-80 years, I would have expected the genre of the backing tracks to follow suit. While they are a pleasant mix of dreamy synth, ethereal piano, nicely varied percussion, and playful back-and-forths of plucked and bowed strings, the style feels contemporary and out of place-  I rarely feel motivated to mention sound design, but A Little to the Left does a great job in this regard. The various clinks, whooshes, clatters, and scrapes you'd expect to hear while shuffling various objects around are faithful and instantly identifiable. It really does capture the auditory experience of rummaging around in a messy drawer for a book of matches- I don't wander into the "cozy organization puzzle game" world very often, but unlike the last one of these I played (Unpacking), there's not really any attempt at storytelling. Just clean, organize, and watch out for - Although the vibes are indeed mostly cozy, I bumped into some frustration when trying to figure out some of the alternate solutions to certain levels. Those wound up crashing the party enough that I wound up using a guide when I circled back to 100% the game. Some of the solutions are fairly insipid, and I don't know if I would have gotten there naturally (looking at you, pen level)- Your enjoyment of the game is wholly dependent on how much you enjoy this style of gameplay, and perhaps the tasks of tidying and organizing as a whole. Do you find it meditative and satisfying? Then you're probably going to enjoy this experience, especially with its pretty visuals. Do you find it boring and frustrating? Then don't even bother considering- The gameplay can be almost wholly described as "click and drag object to correct spot". Beyond that, you occasionally stave of incursions from your luxurious Persian cat- I don't have any compulsive need to organize, so I'm probably not gonna revisit this one- I'm still undecided on how I feel about this sort of game (not that I've played many of them). All I really have to compare it to is Unpacking. While I liked the unspoken narrative of that title, I kinda hated the "puzzles". With so few restrictions, I found myself mostly piling up garbage into technically correct positions and moving on to the next level. A Little to the Left, on the other hand, gives you the satisfaction of feeling like you're actually solving a puzzle by adding set solutions, but the lack of any motivating pretense means that the whole experience feels a bit pointless. It made me wonder why I was bothering to tidy up my virtual cutlery drawer when my real one is a jumbled mess. Oh well. At least it motivated me to finally reorganize a few of my actual kitchen's messy cabinets- I feel like I write this on a lot of point-and-click games that I wind up playing on Steam Deck, but the same thought applies: the trackpads are sufficient, but M/K would have been smoother- . A passably satisfying experience with some pretty visuals and slick foley work, but little more. I mildly enjoyed the organization gameplay, but if you don't, you're going to have a much worse time

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game. The art style is beautiful, the pace is pleasingly slow and the puzzles that work are brilliant. The puzzles that are the best in this game - the ones that require you to observe the screen carefully and apply a bit of logic - slowly disappear from rotation. This leaves a collection of puzzles with no place to start and no way to know you're going in the right direction without using the hints.The hint system is very good, with the option to uncover the solution as much or as little as you like. I also appreciate the "Let it be" option, which lets you skip a level and come back to it later.The satisfaction of solving a puzzle is quickly squashed by frustration when presented with objects or a puzzle layout that doesn't make sense no matter which angle you look at it from. It detracts from the clever mechanics of the puzzles that work. Perhaps worth picking  up on sale, but overall this is a disappointing puzzle game.

_childDocuments_.review: Let me start with why I wouldn't recommend this game: Even on sale, there are simply not enough unique, challenging puzzles to justify the price tag.This game has a ton of strengths: the art style and sound design are phenomenal, the cat is adorable, and there are certainly some very clever and satisfying puzzles. The issue lies in the fact that a majority of the puzzles are so straightforward, repeat an idea that's already been seen multiple times without new mechanics, or aren't even puzzles (petting the cat was cute once, but realizing that multiple of the levels being advertised were clicking on the cat took me aback). I really enjoyed it for the first half, but when I realized the game wasn't actually progressing in difficulty at all, I became more annoyed.All of the promotions and advertisements that led me to purchase this game were puzzles relating to sorting drawers, cabinets, etc. From reading the reviews, it seems that was a common motivator- the satisfying puzzles where a pair of scissors fits in a perfect spot and whatnot. I loved these levels, and actually disagree with a lot of the reviews saying they were too nuanced or nonsensical. I felt that these levels perfectly built on the simple skills taught in the basic puzzles and combined them, so you found yourself wondering "does this need to be in color order? Are there indents indicating a numerical order?" These were the moments that felt like the price was justified and even if the game was 50% these levels, I would recommend it. However, it's not. The majority of the puzzles take less than a minute, some even less than 30 seconds, and often repeat the exact same principle over and over again. Shockingly, they get even simpler and more repetitive in the final chapters of the game, which caught me super off guard. This game has the perfect opportunity to build on concepts and combine them, increasing in difficult as it proceeds, and actually demonstrates that it's capable of it in the drawer levels. Instead, the ending feels like a tunnel of doing the same 3 puzzles over and over until the credits roll, and I hardly felt accomplished by the ending of the base game or DLC.Perhaps the most overwhelming feeling I got from this game: If you removed the puzzles that repeated or were so straightforward you had to pause and reflect on how much money you spent on it, this game feels like a truly excellent mobile/tablet game that you would pay a few dollars for or get with a subscription and have a great time playing. I completed a single star on every level in the base game and DLC in under 4 hours (removing time spent with the game open while I stepped away, etc.), which is one of the poorer ratios cost to content I've seen from similar titles. The DLC has about the ratio of challenging to basic puzzles I would expect from the entire game.I can't emphasize enough that this game oozes the love that was put into it- there was clearly so much passion and thought put into so many elements, and I really wanted to love it. Based on the DLC, it seems to be heading in the right direction, but I don't think I could justify spending any more money on additional levels.

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is an uncomfortable puzzle game. The premise is light and arty and fun: you are tidying up and also there is a cat that sometimes messes up your tidying, so figure out the organization logic of each level and earn a bit of satisfaction from imposing order upon chaos. It's fairly polished little package of riddles, but it really depends on your opinions on cats and on the real life activity that this is a video game version of.Basically, I think it suffers from too many issues to be all that fun. The basic interaction loop, of dragging a thing around and seeing what happens to it, behaves quite oddly sometimes, for instance refusing to grab a particular object or dragging it an inconsistent rate. The systems that detect when an element is close enough to solved to adjust it into place, are a little too eager to interfere. The riddles oscillate between too simple and irritatingly large but have a lot of trouble hitting the sweet spot. There's a theme of like, celebrating cats, I guess, that didn't really land for me. It kinda felt like cleaning up someone else's house while they talked about their cat, which might be your bag but it ain't mine.I find this to be a disappointing game overall. Not because it didn't try its best, but because it demonstrated that its premise is just undeliverable. There's too much bespoke logic and assets and creativity that needs to go into each level of this game, for how quickly the player can breeze through it and how attentive the designer needs to be to possible player solutions. Both failure modes of the level design---the player finding an arrangement the designer didn't recognize as a solution, and the player accidentally falling into a solution that they didn't even notice---feel more bad than a success feels good, I think. And the daily puzzle mode serves campaign puzzles with some of the elements randomized, which for me is too similar to the campaign; the prospect of playing that every day for a hundred days, in order to get a little badge and a cheevo, is kind of insulting.

_childDocuments_.review: The puzzles are equally cute and frustrating. Half the challenge for the puzzles seem to be making very minute changes to pieces until the game finally deems the answer correct. The puzzles shouldn't need to be pixel perfect for aligning things. Towards the end of the game, there are "puzzles" where there is no logical solution. The puzzle is simply "make this look aesthetically pleasing, as arbitrarily determined by the game devs". Even if you use symmetry and make it look nice, if it's not in the exact layout that the devs, arbiters of aesthetics, deem correct, you won't get credit for it. These are less puzzles and more a mind reading activities. There's no real problem solving.The other frustration is the controls. The control scheme only allows you to drag items, so no rotation or anything like that. The game then decides whether an object should be oriented differently or not. Many times, you're left hunting to see where the game wants you to start a puzzle (waiting for the object to "snap" in place). I've also had issues where an object will reorient itself, leading me to believe it was correctly placed. When I picked up the piece again, it would revert to its original orientation and not switch back. I don't know if collision from other objects caused this, but it lead me to believe a piece was placed correctly when it wasn't even facing the correct way.Another small, but bizarre design choice is the main menu. You click the "play" button, expecting the game to take you to your current/last puzzle, like virtually every other video game created in the last two decades. However, for this game, "play" apparently means "new game" because it starts you from the very first puzzle. You actually want to click "levels" and then scroll through tens/hundreds of puzzles until you get to where you were last. I wanted to like this game, but it needs some polish.

_childDocuments_.review: “A little to the left” is both a phrase that I hear way too often when helping my mom change furniture around in her house, which she does at least once every couple of months, and the name of an I know I joked about the whole furniture thing, but honestly, I’m pretty sure that precise scenario is where the developer got the name of the game from. You see,  with the very first level being all about fixing a picture that needs to be tilted just a little to the left. I see what you did there, devs! Honestly, I love the name of the game. It fits.But what DOES it fit into, exactly? What is the full package? Well,  You have a level select screen with over 75 quick levels that give you a variety of objects that you need to organize within whatever frame the level provides you with. If you get a bunch of books side by side, for example, you’ll know you’ll probably have to shift the books around to organize them in a way that makes sense, be it by size, cover design, whatever. On another level, you’re given stickers to apply to a calendar, or stamps to apply to letters. Whatever the case,  The worst were the ones that just gave me an empty space and a bunch of objects. In those, you’re supposed to arrange the objects in the right way, except as far as I can tell, there’s only one way to find out the correct arrangement, and that’s via trial and error.  The game does try to alleviate this by having a kind of a snap effect to an object when you put it in the right place, along with a DING sound that plays, but for me, that was simply too inconsistent to rely on. Well, I say hint because that’s the name in the game, but the truth is the hint is actually the entire answer of the puzzle, but it’s displayed in a way that can be a hint. It’s quite brilliant, really. Let me explain. The answer is basically written in a notebook, but scribbled over. You can get an eraser and erase all the scribbles, which reveal the puzzle’s answer. However, if you only want a hint, you can choose to erase just part of the scribbles, and reveal just a bit of the answer. This way, the player has full control over how much help they want, and I find that to be pretty cool. Basically, you complete a puzzle and you get a star. However, if you complete a puzzle and you see there are two or more stars to get, that means there is another solution to your level. Just like with the puzzles, the solutions can also be unintuitive sometimes. However, in this case, not even the hint will help you, as the hint only shows you the answer to one of the solutions. The rest is on you.  In a game as simple as this, in which you play by clicking and dragging your mouse, that’s mostly okay, but this fact can generate some confusion in some areas, such as the stars. I’ve seen players for example who thought these stars were ratings, and that they were being too slow/doing something wrong. If you finish all the content of this game and want more, fret not:  so at least once a day you can hop back in and do that. In this vein, the game is very relaxing.  The game is very good at making you feel like your worries are melting away… if you don’t get frustrated at some of the puzzles. For me, the puzzles varied wildly in quality, with the best ones being very intuitive and a nice challenge in figuring out how to accomplish your objective, and the worst ones being the ones in which you have no idea nor clue what you’re even meant to do, or, even worse, the empty space ones in which you know what you have to do but have no way to tell which object goes where in the game’s preferred organization. Thankfully, I found more intuitive puzzles than I found the other type, but there were still many more of the latter than I think should have been.If you think you’re okay with this caveat I mentioned, then you’ll probably find this game very relaxing, much in the vein of Unpacking, if you played that. But if you tend to get frustrated when a game wants a different solution than your perfectly valid one, or upon feeling that a puzzle might be unfair… then it might be best for you to steer clear of this title. For me, I had a good time, even with the frustration. Certainly commendable work, especially for a 2 person team. If you do pick up the game, I do hope you enjoy it. And if you want to talk about the game, I’m always down to chat! You can find me just a little to your left. … I’m so sorry. I’m actually probably thousands of kilometers away but I really wanted to make the joke.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate to give this game a negative review--this is another case where I wish Steam had a "meh" button in addition to thumbs up/down.When I heard about this game, I was very excited to play it. I've always been obsessive about organizing stuff, so it sounded perfect for me. But somehow...this just isn't quite it.My number one issue with the game is actually the setting. It seems to take place in some Martha Stewart dreamscape: nothing but houseplants, seashells, pretty rocks, and household objects. Weirdly enough, there is basically zero overlap between the things I actually like to organize in real life and the things I get to organize in this game. There's no level where you re-indent all your code, or where you get to redo the cable management behind the TV, or where you have to guess what screw goes in what hole as you put a smartphone back together. So I really couldn't relate to the overall scenario that much.Another issue is how boring most of the puzzles are. The solution to half the puzzles is just to sort by color. And if not that, then just sort by size, or make the shapes fit with each other. There are only a few really tricky puzzles that call for any lateral thinking at all. A handful of the levels don't even have a single, correct solution; you just have to . It's more of an color-acuity test than real puzzler.I was also let down by the level of interactivity. You can click and drag to rearrange stuff on the screen--and that's it. You can't attach parts together, break things, fold things, turn parts over, etc. So most of the mechanical, kinesthetic joy that comes from disassembling or fixing stuff is lost. It especially stings in the tool-themed chapter; you get a screen full of bolts, nuts, and wrenches, but can you put the nuts on the bolts, maybe using the wrenches? Nope. They get organized in some sort of cafeteria tray, same as the seashells and paperclips from before.I was also unimpressed with the audio. The music is very repetitive and not very good. There is one track with this one arpeggiated piano chord, and it just goes up the scale, down the scale, up the scale, down the scale...I had to put the game on mute when I came back to replay the levels for 100% completion. The sound effects for picking up and moving objects around are also much too loud; the effect is often pretty jarring. If you move stuff around too fast, it turns into some kind of extreme ASMR.And there are some other careless details besides all that. For instance, many levels have more than one solution. After finding one solution, I always wanted to try to get the others (sometimes they are painfully obvious). But the game automatically boots you off to the next level, so you have to exit to the level select and pick out the level the hard way. Another example is the daily puzzles; I think they are automatically generated from maybe 5 or 10 possible templates. The solutions are the same every time, so after a couple repetitions you can solve them on sight. Not sure how this is supposed to retain my interest.Still, there are a few things I liked about the game. The narrative with the cat is a cute way to tie the different chapters together, and there are a couple of memorable puzzles in the mix. The art style is consistent and fits with the rest of the game, and it's a nice, focused experience. I can't deny that it held my attention for long enough to finish the game and do some achievement-hunting (the devs promise that the broken ones will be fixed in the next update). I'm sure some people will like this game much more than I did.

You can only unlock one daily per day (they don't 'store up' the unlocks) and 100% achievement completion is locked behind doing at least 100 of these things, with an achievement requiring a 30 day streak as well. All of the dailies are reiterations of the same puzzle types you play in the main game. Making you log in repeatedly for over a month really soured my impression of this game, not going to bother 100%ing it. Wouldn't recommend paying full price for this game considering over half of the 'content' is time gated.
