_childDocuments_.review: Overall, it was an okay game; I wouldn't recommend it or not recommend it in particular. I thought it was more of an organization game as advertised, though it ended up being more of a puzzle game, which wasn't really what I was expecting. It had a few organizing levels, which were nice, though there were less than 5 in the entire game. The art style and music were really nice and relaxing, unlike some of the actual gameplay.The first chapter or so is really nice, and I actually said how nice and relaxing the game was several times. Puzzle games are some of my favorites; however, this one seemed needlessly difficult at times (I'm talking to you level 51). It almost seemed like a game that you should just play with an online walkthrough pulled up since you'll probably need it several times. (If you were able to get through this with no hints on your own, props to you because I certainly didn't.). I would give it a 6/10. The credits near the end were a nice touch though, as you got to destroy a bunch of things, unlike the vuage disappointment I felt when that cat's paw came across the screen and undid all my hard work. (Admittedly, though the cat did make some of the levels funnier.).One other small thing is that this might not be a game for perfectionists in terms of steam achievements. I didn't realize it before buying the game (for about $10; wish it had been less), but some of the achievements require the DLC to get. This means that without spending another $15 or so, you'll never get all the achievements, something that I personally hate when games do.Thank you for taking the time to read through my review. <3
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I have had my eyes on this game for quite a while, I think I first saw it on a wholesome direct and it felt like someone had made a game specifically for my weird enjoyment of menial virtual tasks. I thought it would just be a nice little organisation game, something satisfying. But it's also a fantastic puzzle game! I don't think it's super hard but I've had to take time to think and I absolutely love that for some levels there are a number of different ways to solve them and you can go back to get the other methods. While I think you could probably work your way through the game pretty fast there seem to be daily challenges coming out, at least a year is planned for this it seems so there's a lot of content. So if you want a chill and not too tricky puzzle game (at least what it seems like from the early levels) I really think this game is worth your money.Also the art is super charming, the music is chill and my silly little reptile brain gets pleased by ordering things nicely.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Just like the "Unpacking" game, this one allows anyone with an organizational mind to relax and solve puzzle after puzzle at their leisure. This one is a little more puzzle based with correct answers to every puzzle while Unpacked allowed you almost free reign to how you organized each room. I still thoroughly love this game and get on it every day for the "Daily Tidy". The devs are constantly updating the game and keeping an eye on bugs that need fixed, especially ones concerning the achievements. I can also appreciate that they removed a couple achievements that would take years to get based on the requirement that it must be done during a holiday event. Overall this game was definitely worth the price and is a fun game for people who can relax while also putting their mind to work.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A very unique & well made game. I went in expecting an organisation game but it turned to be more of an IQ test! I enjoy it nevertheless. The puzzles are intelligently and creatively designed. I am also heavily biased because I love cats. I love calm games like these where you can just think about how to solve a problem, and bonus points for it being so aesthetically pleasing.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Fun fun fun! This game is soooo cute! I love the vibe of the game. You're not only solving puzzles but you're tidying up the home and you're seeing how the simple story progresses with the kitty. Super cozy puzzle game. I love the DLC and I LOVE the daily tidies! It keeps me playing the game every day just for the achievements :)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: If you need to unwind after a long day, this is the game for you. This game is satisfying to play not only because of the stunning visuals, but also thanks to the great sound design that makes placing objects and finishing levels feel *so accomplishing*. The puzzles are also done wonderfully, where even repeating mechanics don't feel boring but instead new and refreshing. Looking forward to new content <33
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: If OCD and modern art had an illegitimate love child, this game would be it.I give it 5 stars out of 5. Neatly aligned stars... Stars that are ordered largest to smallest. With a logical colour sequence... And angled correctly so the edges align....can you hear that purring?......Its getting louder.Oh god, ITS A PAW!MY NEATLY ORGANISED STARS... NOOooooOOoooo....
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. The puzzles are uniquely entertaining, the solutions to so many of them are perfectly complex, but you always have the option to get a hint or 'let it be' if something is a little bit too frustrating. The daily tidy keeps you coming back, and the new archive levels are a blast. Their player support is incredible, they get back to you so quickly and seem glad to help out to ensure that their players are enjoying the game. If you're looking for something to help you let go of the stress of the day, this game is absolutely the way to go. Thank y'all for making such a great game!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A game by OCD's, for OCD'sPros:* Excellent escalation of puzzle difficulty, with some humor tossed in to break up tension.  Puzzles are generally that of organizing objects and/or clutter, but usually the underlying pattern to follow is not immediately obvious.* Great music and effects.Cons:* Since the whole point of the game is to discern the underlying pattern of each level, and some levels (not most) can be a little twitchy on recognizing your success, I went a little mad trying to fine-tune what I thought was a valid pattern... only to rage-quit, look up the solution, and find I was waaaaaaaaay off.TL;DR: 9/10 if you like puzzles - else, avoid.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta give it up to the marketing team, because I was so excited for this game. And then after buying it on release day, I was like "Oh wait, this is like a million other puzzle games."Put the leaves color order. Make the spoons go smallest to largest. Turn the clock until a shadow in the background matches.I've played that game. I've played that game a hundred times. Any game under "puzzle, casual, relaxing, cute" is going to be this exact game. The marketing made it seem like it reinvented the genre. It didn't. It's a "puzzle, casual, relaxing, cute" game. You hear those tags, you know exactly what the game is. ... And you don't really expect it to be $15 (and no discount on release day). Also, needing to get things pixel perfect is annoying. A lot of puzzle games will say "Ah, you're 92% of the way, we'll just jiggle everything a little for you to get it perfect, you obviously know the answer." It genuinely felt like it was every a good fourth of the puzzles in this game I would get the right answer, not proceed, look at the hint, see the hint was the answer I did, and have to jiggle everything around for a solid minute trying to get it *exactly* where they needed to be. Genuinely, my playtime is as long as it is for this exact issue. Specifically from the postcard puzzle, where I had the correct answer for 30 minutes and it just wasn't "clicking" into place. It was Unpacking in spirit, but not execution. I wanted to put things in a drawer the way I wanted to.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Some puzzles are fun... most are too easy or boring, or don't make any sense. I breezed through it in 2 hours and when I had discovered it was over I was kinda disappointed. The majority of the levels are Not organization base, instead just visual puzzles that don't really make sense.not worth it. And I was refused a refund cause I took too long playing it...
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If logic puzzles are your cup of tea, give A Little to the Left a shot. Just make sure you read lots of reviews or watch a let's play or two so you get a good sense of the game's difficulty before buying.  If you're looking for a more dollhouse-like experience similar to Unpacking, skip this one.Many of the puzzles are fun and give you a sense of accomplishment when solved. Others are IMPOSSIBLE to figure out without hints (thank goodness for the 'ding' and items snapping to the grid as self-corrects), making the game more frustrating than fun. I stumbled my way to more than one solution before I even knew there were actual hints available in the pause menu. Even then, I didn't always understand what I did to get the puzzle right. I suspect many of you are smarter and far more patient than I am, so your mileage may vary.As other players wrote, the demo doesn't set the right expectations for the the difficulty of the full game. The art style and music are lovely, and the levels that allow you to sort, order and organize just so are a blast. Less enjoyable are the rage-quit worthy-logic puzzles scattered throughout an otherwise chill game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I don't see many nuanced reviews on this game, which I don't quite get. I played the main game some time ago and just now got the DLC.Let's start with the positives:-It is an incredibly aesthetically pleasing game! Cute graphics, a nice art style, and a color palette that is very soothing on the eye without having that incredibly monotone beige thing going on or only being pastel. All in all: very pretty!-The puzzles, overall, are quite nice. I love the cupboard Idea, I like the range in difficulty for the most part and as a casual, sometimes nicely tricky, puzzle game it is very nice. There are several levels where I went: "Oh that's a neat Idea!" after figuring it out-I really like the puzzles with 3 or more answers, those were always funNow the negatives:-For the price, especially the new DLC price, it is not enough gameplay by far. The DLC cost 6 euros and I almost felt robbed by the lack of content, there's only so much you can do with the concept, but we'll get to that-Some Levels feel rushed or made with very little love. Levels like that Seashell ordering one don't have that sorting feeling that makes so much sense, where it might be tricky in parts, but generally intuitive. It felt like its simply the prettiest way of arranging the shells according to the makers. It just feels illogical... And I really hate that. Yes tricky, even very tricky is fine. But it has to be solvable, not through trial and error, but logic.-please stop with the cat levels. It's a cute gimmick, but there were 3 or 4 (maybe more) so-called "levels" in the DLC that were simply clicking on the kitty to "pet" it. It felt like the makers were just trying to increase the level count in the DLC without more work.-some levels with only one answer also feel like they were made for a 3rd grader. Cute, but not what I'd expect for that price-very repetitive in parts, again I like the drawer-type sorting idea a lot, but not for it to be every level. Some ideas are just overdone without adding any new spin most of the timeAll in all: I enjoyed this a lot while playing and was very excited about the DLC which immensely disappointed me in the end. It's cute, but thinking about it now it is very overpriced and it's just that: kinda cute, very pretty but nothing groundbreaking. Get it or don't get it, you're probably really gonna like it, but there is also a lot to improve and change and you're gonna have to live with that.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: i thoroughly enjoyed this game! it's extremely satisfying (for the most part) and is a fun game to play to pass the time and just enjoy some cute graphics and sounds. i would recommend this game to everyone, especially if you enjoy some brain games, puzzles, and sorting. i enjoyed this game so much i completed it in 4 days! i hope everyone enjoys this game as much as i did :)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing. I had such high hopes for this game.The best parts of the game feel like a more structured version of "Unpacking", with lots of cute little scenes to organize in an intuitive or a logical way. It's relaxing and scratches a very particular itch.Then there's the rest of the game. A good number of the puzzle completely lacks the "intuitive" and "logical" parts of the above statement. The problem is that these puzzles insist on a "right" answer, even when there is no discernible reason for that right answer. For example: arrange a bunch of random seashells in a *very* specific way, with no way of knowing what the right way is. These puzzles are frustrating and demoralizing, and they kill the relaxing vibe of the game.Hints might have softened the blow, but the "hint" system in the game just immediately tells you the "right" answer, removing any sense of accomplishment as soon as its used.In closing: it's half of a very good little game. If you're the kind of person who isn't too bothered by just following directions in a puzzle game, or you're not bothered by skipping levels (at least there's a skip button!), then I can recommend giving this a look. Otherwise, maybe stay away.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, this in NOT the game about organising things - it's more about finding patterns. At least sometimes.I was expecting relaxing puzzle game, with emphasis on "puzzle".Is it relaxing? Maybe, sort of, in some cases. But when it's not relaxing, it can be frustrating (or boring, which is even worse).How about puzzle aspect? Not much of a challenge, there are some interesting levels, but mostly they just eat up your time. And the best example (which means the worst levels) are "Daily Tidy" - small, easy variations of main levels. I finished 3 and I don't believe they got any better than that. I'm discouraged to check those every day...On top of that, two times I made everything as it suppose to be, but game didn't recognized it - I even compared with correct solution. When I was sure it's correct, I had to reset level and then it worked, but I lost couple of minutes checking what could be wrong. I know, couple of minutes doesn't sound bad, but still, it is frustrating.On the bright side, visuals are very nice, and some ideas are really good.And the cat? Or rather, THE CAT? I'm more of a dog person, so it didn't stole my heart, just like game itself.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a little misleading. It's more of a puzzle game than a relaxing organizing game. Some levels area little more difficult for the sole reason that there is nothing to instruct you on what you need to do except for a hint button on the pause screen. (I wish that was on the main screen, but oh well). However, this is somewhat counter-acted by the fact that most levels have multiple ways to complete them. So far the game is a really nice aesthetic, but don't go in with the idea that it's just an OCD simulator.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun and satisfying game. The Cupboards and Drawers DLC is even better than the main game so make sure to buy them both. The one thing I dislike is the Daily Tidies. They are immensly repetitive especially when you want to get to a 30-day streak. It feels like they cycle between four or five puzzles for these.Also a colourblind mode would be very helpful, some puzzles were impossible to complete without help from someone else.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I've decided to give this game a positive review, with caveats.  Very cute game with great graphics.  Some of the levels I absolutely loved doing, others were annoying and a couple, it took me a while to understand how to do.  I think which types of puzzles you enjoy will just come down to personal preference.I enjoy doing the "Daily Tidy" as a quick mind puzzle every day.  I plan to buy the Cupboard & Drawers DLC but plan to skip the Seeing Stars, based on their reviews.It is short and most of them are very easy so I would wait for a sale.Edit 10/20/24:  I just finished the Cupboards & Drawers DLC and I was very pleasantly surprised.  I enjoyed all of the "puzzles" and some of them were surprisingly challenging.  It is short so wait for a sale (or you can get a discount based on owning the base game) but I would definitely recommend this DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be so good, but it falls short. Some levels are intuitive enough that they make sense, but somewhere between "half" and "most" of the puzzles don't give any indication at all of what you're supposed to do. For example, one level gives you a handful of pencils of varying lengths. The natural assumption is that you are supposed to arrange them in order based on their length, which is true, but what the game gives you NO indication of AT ALL is that you're supposed to . Another example is a level where it gives you a bunch of envelopes with some stamps. Again, with NO indication of what you're supposed to do, you have to just click around the guess, Turns out, you . Another level has you stack papers on top of each other, but then a very similar appearing level wants you arrange them on (invisible) hot spots around the background. There's nothing distinguishing those mechanics.So this game is basically just "click around randomly until you find the invisible hot spots." It seems like they are supposed to be puzzles for you to figure out, but forgot to include the actual puzzle.The "hint" system gives you the full answer (at least on the levels I used it on), which is definitely not a reasonable thing for a game like this that gives no indication of what you're supposed to do.I don't generally bash on games where it's obvious I'm not the target audience, because I don't think that's really fair. In this case though, I *am* the target audience, as far as I can tell, and enjoyed the few levels that made sense.  2/10, A for effort. If the UI were fixed to provide indicators for where the invisible hot spots are, or even indicators about what each puzzle is supposed to be, maybe a riddle or something, the game could be so much better.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Endearing puzzle game. A few levels were not intuitive in the slightest, but the rest were on point. Good mix of fairly simple to complex levels.Completed main game and DLC in 8 hours, and was taking my time so it isn't the longest game out there but personally it was worth it.Looking at the locked achievements, they expect people to do more playthroughs than I probably will. Might go through it a second time to try new ways to solve some puzzles but that's about it.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: There were a few levels in A Little to the Left that I really enjoyed. But I was hoping for more organization gameplay, like Unpacking, instead of just another basic puzzle game. Most of the level have nothing to do with organizing or fixing anything. You just fumble around until you figure out what the puzzle wants you to do. I'm not a fan of these types of games and feel they never really hit the balance between providing a challenge but also giving you enough information to go on.If you like an average puzzle game where you have to figure out what the game is actually asking you to do before you can even attempt to know the answer, this is probably for you. But even still, it's definitely overpriced. This would be better around the 4.99usd mark.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game was super fun. I finished it in just a couple days because I couldn't stop playing it. It's a great game if you want a relaxing puzzle themed game with calming music and colors. The artwork is beautiful, and the cats are adorable. The most satisfying part of this game is that every single item you interact with has a space where it fits like a glove, whether it's a physical space, or a pattern/design that you need to match up. There are a lot of levels to "tidy up" and even some levels have multiple ways to tidy them. Truly a neat, unique, fun game. Worth every penny and every minute of my time.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: What a great little game!Finished the main game in about 4 hours, mainly because I was so relaxed and focused playing that I didn't realise it was 4am already.The music is great, the puzzles are easy enough that they don't overwhelm you, but difficult enough you have to actually think how to solve things. This might be controversial but I wasn't a full-on fan of the cat messing up my solutions, and I disagree with the key that is supposed to "look like a 6" (it doesn't!!). However it is an excellent puzzle and I'm looking forward to playing the DLC. Highly recommend if you like puzzles without instructions, tidying up, bento boxes, 5S-style organisation, cosy music, plants and cats (or skip if you're not into the above).
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not saying this is a bad game, and I'm not saying I loathed every second playing it, but it just was not for me. I found the hints sometimes completely useless and for a game highly recommended based off of my history I can't comprehend why I didn't enjoy it that much. My favourite part was probably the last stage. Though I did quite enjoy how some stages had multiple solutions (wish we also had hints for each solution) and some solutions came easier (struggling to count in some levels so that one is probably on me). I did overall enjoy it enough to finish it, just not enough that I'm considering strongly finishing all achievements (I probably still will tbh, I like finishing things). All in all, not as easy as first assumed and so I didn't enjoy it as much as other 'similar' games.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: "Try a little to the left. Please, just give it a chance." We say."No, no, no, no." They say. They shake their heads and go; "We don't like a little to the left.""Please", we beg. "Just try it. Can't you see how many people like it?""We refuse to go a little to the left. It's too difficult. We don't want to solve these silly puzzles.""But... It's so peaceful here. So cozy. So nice."They don't get it. And I can't force cups in my utensil drawer. I won't solve a puzzle by forcing pieces into places they don't fit. I dont expect to go all the way to the left. Just a little. *mic drop*
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely little puzzle game that has good balance between a genuine challenge and just putting things in places. There were a couple of levels I struggled with for a good while, and unfortunately I couldn't complete the Clock level in Chapter 5 of the base game because it drops my frames. That's mostly just the fault of my crappy computer, though.I especially enjoy how there are no penalties for needing help, and you can skip levels and come back to them whenever you want to, without being required to finish any to progress through the rest of the game.I absolutely adore this game overall, though, and even the credits were fun!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely game for everyone who enjoys a cozy and relaxing game or someone in need of a palette cleanser in between bigger titles.I really enjoyed the sounddesign, artstyle and the way the hintsystem worked (you have the option to only reveal the section you need help with therefore not spoiling the rest for you).The DLC is almost better than the main game imo. That being said if you add the price of both it is a steep price tag for the amount of playtime you will get out of this. But if you enjoy achievement hunting then you will probably get your money's worth. I still recommend to get this game on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could leave a neutral review, but I can’t. So I’ve decided to pick a negative review. I just don’t feel the game is worth the price. There’s not a lot of gameplay for what you pay. When the game ended, I was like “That’s it?” I think this was meant for a more novice puzzle game player who won’t speed through the levels like I did. For now, I’ll try to solve some of the puzzles again and hope the DLC might provide more gameplay.Edit: It would appear as though the daily tidy rotates from a very small selection of puzzles from the main game. I don't understand why the selection is so small given how many puzzles are in the game. One of them has already repeated since I began playing the game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who fell in love with the original game and the cupboards and drawers DLC, i was so excited for this but once i started playing i honestly felt like i was forcing myself to finish each level at some points. I appreciate the notion of having more solutions but there's is no point in adding them when they aren't going to make any sense. Alot of the levels had what felt like pointless, unintuitive solutions that, without a hint, you were never going to figure out or think of, which forced me to, for many levels use hints which ruin the satisfaction and point of the game. Frustrating, tedious and sometimes outright impossible to figure out on your own. Not to mention the new implementation of interact into solutions which often times meant you had everything right but ended up having to use a hint because you hadn't clicked that one thing just right and now it's moved everything else around it out of place. Art style was amazing as usual, i loved the increased amount of content but here it happens to be quantity over quality (with some level exceptions) given that it's more expensive than the original DLC i would definetly stick with Cupboards and Drawers and the original game this DLC is not as enjoyable and honestly frustrating and dissapointing.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't think this game is worth the price. It took me three hours to beat and I am stupid. You can either replay levels that you already remember how to solve (giving them no purpose) or do one puzzle a day that are often repeats from the main story. I try and do the daily puzzles to give them a chance but they are often the most memorable or tedious puzzles from the game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend the Seeing Stars DLC to anyone who likes A Little to the Left and is prepared for more of a challenge. Overall I enjoyed these puzzles very much. Many of them have 3-5 possible solutions, requiring a lot of creative thinking and pattern recognition. There were a few that were frustratingly ambiguous - such as the pizza level that could've had 15 or more reasonable solutions, but somehow we had to read the devs' minds and only pick four. As others have mentioned, I had a few issues fiddling with items that wouldn't click into place but this is the same problem I had in the main game and I know how to deal with it by now. It didn't stop me from getting all 100/100 stars (with a few hints and a lot of trial/error). But if you're not looking to strain your brain, maybe stick with the Daily Tidies and steer clear of this DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Very satisfying organization game. Some of the levels are a little finicky, but they're really well done. The art style is aesthetically pleasing, and the music is SO relaxing--I love to play this game before bed to get sleepy. I also loved the gimmick in the credits (I won't spoil, but it's very fun). Plus this game features cute cats that purr when you pet them <3
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A very cute and relaxing puzzle game. The music is really calming, I could listen to it on repeat completely independent of the game. The puzzles themselves are very visually appealing, and present enough of a challenge without being TOO MUCH of a challenge, you know? I also love that there are multiple ways to do several of the puzzles instead of it being one and done, there's so much creativity put into the solutions. At first I was a bit disappointed that the Daily Tidies are repeats of puzzles you have done, I thought they would be new puzzles introduced daily but tbh I understand how unrealistic that was. I still enjoy doing them for the achievements, and it's definitely helping me to get in the practice for the perfection achievement hehe.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: it has been fun playing. I've completed all the puzzles from archive, the game itself, and the cupboards dlc. i need the stars dlc. every puzzle was absolutely feasible. some were a little challenging to get all of the solutions for a level or getting every piece--but it was not at the cost of being too tedious. I think the devs balanced it well. also, there were a few interactions I enjoyed that they implemented--particularly with the kitty and how to get certain achievements.overall, id recommend--especially if on sale :) it was quite relaxing and enjoyable.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting concept for game, many instances where I was left scratching my head as I had absolutely no idea what the level was asking of me. Thankfully there was a function to skip the level & get a hint. The inclusion of the cat was a nice touch, as someone who owns a feline companion I know only too well how mischievous they can be when tidying :)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I've played through this multiple times because the sense of zen it gives me is beyond compare. I was delighted when they released the DLC. I just wish it was longer. There's no major challenge to it, but if you're playing it to be challenged than play a different game. This is for scratching your brain only.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I decided to play this game because I was feeling really down, and after playing through it, I felt much better and more calm. This game really felt nice for my OCD and it was a relaxing experience to play through it all, getting achievements I didn't know I could get was the best part though. This is a somewhat challenging but simple game and l would recommend it to other players.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun little puzzle game. The daily tidy is what makes the price tag worth it, because otherwise I was ale to get through most of the puzzles within two hours. The only other thing I wasn't a fan of was the music; it started to get on my nerves after a while, but I just turned the sound off and still enjoyed puzzling out the levels (you do need the sound for a few of the levels).
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I love the art style for this game, it is beautifully illustrated, the main reason I purchased this game. The sound design is also lovely.As far as the gameplay goes, some of the levels I find extremely frustrating & difficult to understand. Some of the ways that things are "organized" don't make any sense to my brain. I am also someone who thrives off of instruction/knowledge & the lack of direction provided for the more abstract levels can leave me looking online for answers. I know I can use the provided hints option (& sometimes I do), but I just don't love how that feels as a gameplay experience personally.I totally understand & respect the direction that the developers took with this game, I acknowledge that the things I critiqued above are things that I personally don't like about the game but many others do love. My purpose for leaving this review is simply to help out anyone else who might have the same mindset as me.I do still like the game & will continue to play it through to the end, but overall I am a little disappointed that I don't like it as much as I originally thought I would when I bought it.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: After a little over four hours of gameplay, I can say that while I have played more exciting or technically impressive games, I have rarely played one as charming as this.The game is exceptionally lovingly designed, and everything is coherent and fits well together. The music is also just right for a puzzle game, neither too intrusive nor too dull.A bit about the gameplay: You move from puzzle to puzzle, with most puzzles taking place on a single screen. Sometimes you need to arrange objects in a specific order, other times you have to recognize hidden patterns. With a bit of thought, you can always find the solution, and some puzzles even have multiple solutions! I find it particularly enjoyable to discover which alternative solutions the game demands. The graphic style is reminiscent of hand-drawn artworks and is not only very atmospheric overall with a beautiful color scheme, but it also allows for fatigue-free puzzle solving, as the screen never feels overloaded or 'loud.'Overall, you can tell in every corner and almost every puzzle that this game wasn't made just to make a quick buck but that a lot of heart and care went into 'A Little to the Left.'If I had to criticize anything, it would probably be that the controls are sometimes a bit finicky, but so far, that hasn't detracted from my enjoyment of the game.In some puzzles, a cat decides it wants to join in and cause some mischief. And just like with a real cat, you can't be mad at the virtual pet because it's too cute (cat owners will know what I mean!), even though you usually only see its paw :)All in all, it's a very fun and at the same time very relaxing cozy game, full of clever puzzles whose difficulty gently increases as the game progresses, and imaginative ideas.If you like puzzle games (and cats),  supporting the charming developers and giving the game a chance is a no brainer for me!(If you don't like cats, by the way, that's okay too ;) )
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this a "meh" rating because if this is your thing, it's a good game. Overall I'd say get it on sale. I liked the style and the music, but it felt more like a mobile game than a computer game, especially with the daily challenges and achievements for daily tidies - I personally don't know many people who load up a game on Steam for a short daily puzzle, but I do know loads of people who do it a daily sudoku, solitaire or suchlike on their phone on the way to work. I also feel that there could be more of a plot - I know it's a puzzle game, but I bought this game because I loved other tidying games like Unpacking and Handle With Care, which has puzzles but it does also have an overarching story that makes you want to keep playing and doing those puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game. Got hooked and couldn't stop playing until I completed the main game and both DLCs. It's very clear that a lot of love and thought went into making this game. The addition of the cat(s) really sold the it for me and set the mood of the game. Many a time when I'd be organizing my mischievious lil' kippers would come out of nowhere to deliberately mess everything up, often times even run into my carefully crafted projects at full speed.The puzzles are fun and exciting to figure out, they're not too hard and I only needed hints for a few puzzles. The DLCs increase the difficulty of the puzzles but only slightly, which I appreciate. There's something very satisfying with how well the devs have managed to balance the puzzles difficulty, with some puzzles being very easy to figure out like putting a jigsaw puzzle together with others being slightly more complicated such as figuring out the exact way to organize a small subset of puzzle pieces to unlock the full puzzle. It's very well done.There are some very well-designed puzzles that make me think that someone had to sacrifice their soul just to come up with. It's really insane how well thought out and pretty the puzzles are.There's some very small details about this game that I really enjoy, one thing is that there's a golden pen cap in the main game but missing its pen. Then in the DLC you finally get to see the full pen and put the cap on it then organize the pen itself. It's a very satisfying through line.I would be completely open to any new DLCs made for this game. So happy that the devs have made the effort to give us more content up until now and I absolutely adore the Daily Tidys. They're fun and make me excited to recheck the game and redo some of my favorite puzzles. Highly recommend this game! Go buy it and support the people who made this game! So much love and thought went into making this game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute and relaxing. Some make you think outside the box to get the extra stars but worth it in the end, especially if you have OCD. The achievements are pretty easy to get as well if you go back and redo some levels to get them. Kinda struggled on how to get the last two achievements that require a clean play through but figured out I had reset my progress enable to get them.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I thoughtfully enjoy this game. I'm on 56 daily tidies and they still don't feel like awful copy and paste.Honestly a fun organisational game where you also get to hunt for patterns for secret solutions. Both the DLC's are of a good length in comparison to the main game. Definitely grab it if its on offer.There are a few puzzles I didn't enjoy but I feel like that's common with puzzle games anyway (I don't enjoy the constellation ones or the calendar ones.). But even if you struggle, the hint system makes it fun to work through the tricky parts and figure out the solution.Overall a very good game and worth grabbing if you like similar games
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game to play if you want something casual and relaxing. Doesn't demand too much time all in one go and it's quite satisfying. The puzzles are fun but get repetitive, especially in the fourth and fifth sections and the daily tidies (I'm sure I've done the matching clock hands to shadows puzzle like 5 times now). Probably not worth $15 but worth a few hours for sure
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is neat, although it's a bit too full of itself for my own liking. A lot of the puzzles are fun to solve and figure out the rules, while others feel cheap. The fact that some puzzles have multiple solutions is really neat, but it feels like a punch in the gut that those extra solutions don't have any hints. And also that the hint for every puzzle is just… revealing the solution, rather than being an actual hint.It also has the *worst* toggle-hold setting of any game I've ever played, where it seems to be the least-effort implementation. There are lots of points where your hold can be "dropped" while moving objects in certain ways, and for the ordinary hold setting this is fine since you need to let go and re-click to grab again, but the toggle-hold requires you to click twice. Or, in some cases, something that only requires a simple tap requires clicking twice. It made this game unnecessarily frustrating at times.The game definitely overdoes achievements by giving achievements for using hints, for not using hints, for skipping levels, for not skipping levels. And some weird obscure achievements that just feel like filler. I know a lot of people don't really care for achievements, but I like using them as a form of completion, and this game really spits in the face of that.And finally… the daily tidy is a neat feature until you realise that it's just randomly reskinned versions of existing levels. It would be fun if the daily tidy only used levels you've already completed, or if you could complete levels via the daily tidy, but that's not how it works. It would have been nice to see parity for this, but since it's just an extra feature, I won't hold it against the game. I've had *some* fun with it.Overall… I would give this game an extremely positive review and a solid recommend if it weren't for the stuff I mentioned. Since steam forces a positive or negative review, I'll skew toward positive, but it's not nearly what I hoped for.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Aiming for all achievements currently, but it is an extremely fun game. Makes you think and see things from a different perspective. I'll admit it was super challenging, and hints were used quite often, especially for the DLC's. Nonetheless, beautiful game; love the colors; love the animations; super cute. It has cats!! My favorite, I own like 5 of them, so as a cat lady, this was adorable for me to play; I really enjoyed it. I hope for more DLC's in the future (probably not going to happen, but I can dream), I love a great challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I did. And I tried. I  puzzle games, and this was pitched to me as a ""relaxing"" puzzle/organisational game. It's not relaxing. It's really, really not relaxing. In fact, it's frustrating. So frustrating in fact that I could feel my brain splitting in half as I desperately tried to figure out what the game wanted me to do on some stages. So, perhaps I went into it with the wrong expectations, thus ruining it for myself forever. Maybe it won't be the same for you.However, I feel like even if I had been told, "hey, this is a puzzle game," I'd still feel a bit irked. The cursor feels janky/rigid no matter how I change the settings (and no other games are giving me this trouble). The cat in this game, somehow, is the first cat in a video game that  It's not enjoyable seeing hard work get destroyed by its malicious l'il paws.Things came to a crashing end for me at the Box level. I don't know what happened to me. It was like my brain was actually getting tortured. Neurons were screaming at me that they didn't get it. Click, Grab, Click, Grab, Shuffle, Click, Grab, , Click, Grab, Click, Grab, Shuffle— This game is going to be satisfying for some people. I know it will be. But, there is a small chance, a tiny chance, that maybe your brain is like mine and that this game is serotonin  that you just paid $22.95AUD to make your brain scream at you.A Little Less to the Left, please.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game but... I don't think I do.I think there should be more than one 'answer' for most if not all of the puzzles and went in thinking it would be a lot more freeform than it is. It falls short on being relaxing or challenging and is somewhere in the middle around 'mildly annoying/boring.' It feels like there no real 'reward' or satisfying 'ah ha!' moment when figuring out what the level wants you to do and rarely does the puzzle feel fun to do. Its a lot of 'push stuff around until the game tells me I did it right' and then move on to the next. I am up to chapter three right now and I do like it more than the previous levels, (it feels like I'm actually using my brain a little bit on these ones!) but at this point I'm hesitant to recommend the game. Maybe wait for a sale if you're really keen.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on sale after watching SimplyNotLogical play a few levels on her YouTube stream. Some of the levels are very easy, while others are quite difficult. Each level allows you to see a hint of the finished puzzle, but some levels have multiple solutions. It was frustrating trying to solve for some of the less obvious puzzle solutions, but felt rewarding when I was able to unlock all stars for a level with multiple solutions. I would definitely recommend this game if you enjoy puzzles, however if you are a master puzzle solver you may take less play through's then I did and may not feel you got you money's worth. I finished the main game in four days spread over a few weeks, with about an hour devoted to playing in the afternoon when I had time. I'm still hunting for some of the achievements from this game, which I enjoy the replay and that they give a new puzzle every day to complete towards some of those achievements. The cat theme to this game is subtle, and the cat itself only appears in a few levels, though is more so in the final chapter.If you're not sure if you'd enjoy this game there are plenty of play through's online to watch, I personally love the art style and soft music, it's a fuzzy cozy no pressure game of puzzles, simple tidying and symmetry.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is easily one of the best puzzle games I've ever played. The puzzles aren't the most challenging at the beginning, and I would never describe them as overwhelmingly hard, but they're so very fun. You might be questioning whether or not it's worth it for fifteen dollars, but you can stop questioning now. It's so full of personality, and if you buy the bundle with the DLC, it will be one of the best purchases you've made.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the OCD nature of this game at the beginning and the feeling of figuring out how to solve things in multiple ways. But that feeling quickly drops off a cliff not far into the game. Many of the puzzles have only a single solution that isn't very fun or is just excessively tedious to complete. I found myself just getting frustrated with some of the puzzles rather than enjoying a relaxing game of organizing things in different ways. I bought this after watching some streamers play through only the first chapter because it looked like a lot of fun. But after playing almost through chapter four, I can see that I only ever enjoyed the first chapter. The rest is a grind to get through and I don't know if I'll ever go back and finish it - it's killed my motivation to continue.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely game that's exactly as advertised. You organize stuff, some levels have multiple solutions and other puzzles I was lost on, but they're mostly relatively simple. There's also hints if you ever get lost. I heard there will be some more puzzles and I'm very excited for that, however I do wish there was more variety in the daily tidies as you're supposed to do 100 for the achievements (possibly more if you miss the consecutive for a month). I really liked the easter egg event having different puzzles, like putting the glass back to match the patterns, I really loved those puzzles. Otherwise, calm cute game and you get to see a little menace kitty and who doesn't love that?
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite nice and relaxing most of the times, achievements are not hard to obtain (tho be warned you need a playthru without using hints for one of them, I had to replay the whole game after making the mistake of using a hint).I personally recommend the game as it is fun tho frustrating at certain points.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad puzzle game. But the emphasis should be on PUZZLE. Due to the marketing I was expecting a more zen experience like unboxing. So much of the game offers itself as "organizing, with multiple solutions for puzzles, and sometimes a cute cat to fuss with". My experience was more "increasingly obtuse puzzles meant to stump you on purpose, and a cat that appears largely once you've beaten your head against a puzzle and solved it just to mess it up on purpose". It's a cute game, I don't entirely regret getting it. But it was NOT remotely what I had wanted going into it. Which is a shame, since the first few puzzles hit that satisfying spot. But it soon turned to 'there is one RIGHT way to do this' solutions, and I found myself struggling to interpret what the creator thought was a "satisfying" solution versus what I thought looked appealing. By the last chapter, all the stages are metaphysical challenges (spoilers : one has you moving a mirror to arrange items specifically how they appear in the reflection, in order to match) with hard "there is One Right Way to solve this" answers. I hadn't bought this looking for a game that was "oops all adventure room point and click game puzzles". I wanted something more like Unpacking that perhaps had solutions but freeform and relaxing enough to not feel like I was fighting the game just to finish it.Also, that tupperware end scene went on for WAY too long.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Fun but you will 100% complete this and the DLC in 5.5 hours tops. Not really hard but satisfying. Tho there are plenty of way's to order stuff that is not part of the options.But for 11€ it is a bit steep. I have a rule. 1€ per hour played. And as you complete it in, let's say 6. The full pack is 21€ So it would need 15 more hours of playtime to be perfect.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect if you're looking for a calm little game with no stress and no expectations except making things tidy. There were a couple I had to look up solutions for, I will admit, because the lack of instructions made it a little frustrating to figure out on my own, but the ability to skip levels and come back later is a wonderful solution to that challenge. Highly recommend for a chill, short game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely delightful little game. The puzzles are satisfying and imaginative (and sometimes have more than one answer!) I appreciated the hint/let it be options, which ensured that the few levels I got really stuck on didn't stop me from progressing or detract from the enjoyability of the game. The illustrations are bright and cheerful, and the music is cute as well. The daily tidy is a nice way to get a little fun out of the game every day, too. If you like to sort and tidy up, this one's for you!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and charming puzzle game. The style and polish of the game is very relaxing and I highly recommend it!There was only one puzzle that I couldn't figure it out, the one with the skull in a box, which I don't think I would've ever understood. Otherwise I found most puzzles satisfying!I love that the dev team is actively paying attention to feedback on the community page which lead to changes like reworking of the achievements. I had given up on 100% when I originally played because the daily tidy achievements were kinda insane. But 100 is very doable with some patience :) Or by changing the clock, but it was a nice routine to pop onto the game for a minute or two and do a daily tidy.Looking forward to the DLC!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I've had my eye on this game for a long time since I first saw it in a Wholesome Direct, and I only spontaneously bought it + the DLC the other day. I have since finished every single puzzle, including the ones in the DLC and the ones from the Daily Tidy archive. I enjoyed this game a lot more than I thought I would!! This game has no explanations for the puzzles which can be frustrating, especially if you're someone who needs clear requirements/rules. But!! I find that the charm point of this game is being able to experiment with different possible solutions. The music and the sound effects also rock :-) I look forward to future Daily Tidies and DLCs (maybe??) because I loved all the puzzles in the Cupboards & Drawers DLC a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I thought this would be a super simple, easy organization game, but puzzles are harder than I thought they'd be... in a good way! I enjoy that there are often multiple ways to solve a puzzle and the answers aren't always obvious. I have about an hour playtime and am enjoying myself so far. I usually play a few puzzles when I feel especially anxious, and it helps calm my thoughts down and clear my head.I think this game balances easy and calming gameplay with actual brainteasers well; some puzzles are quick solves, others require you to sit and think about what you're looking at a little more. It's probably not what you're looking for if you just want something mindless to unwind with after a taxing day, but if you find logic puzzles and organization a nice way to chill out, you might like this. The only downside IMO is that some puzzle ideas repeat, and while they do seem to all have different answers, that can feel a little redundant.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so satisfying when you get to organize the little trinkets. The cupboards and drawers DLC is by far  my favorite, and I really enjoyed seeing all the cats throughout. I will say it did get a little frustrating on certain levels, and some I was just downright baffled. But overall, I think this is definitely worth the play, and a great game to hop onto at the end of a day.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game provided me with one of the most incredibly profound experiences I've ever had when playing a game. It is like I could physically feel the love and soul poured into this game from the developers and artists and it just overwhelmed me at the end once I finished all the levels. The way the cat character's narrative developed through the progression of the game was so beautifully subtle, and if you have a pet you love I feel the impact of this narrative wont be lost on you. Even in the designs of the levels, some of the items you are tidying up feel like they belong to someone, and the act of sorting out their items feels like an intimate connection with someone very unique and special. The game is very short and I would recommend playing through the whole thing in one sitting to get the whole experience. This game has mountain loads of creativity with such a simple and effective concept coupled with beautiful art, music and sound design, I can't see how you could regret picking up this game. And thank you Max Inferno for an experience I wont forget.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Was quite satisfying at first, though some levels weren't obvious what needed to be done and the methods didn't make much sense. The last level made absolutely no sense and felt more like a drug-trip as I was forced to watch a cat in varying poses whilst being bombarded by coloured circles. Weird choice. Unskippable.At least the stacking portion of that level was somewhat nice, shame there wasn't more of it.The snowflake and calendar game I wouldn't consider satisfying. Having to endlessly scroll through a bright page to find shapes, that are often overlapping, wasn't really fun and was mainly just tediously boring. The calendar required me to count- which whilst I don't have trouble with, it's not something I like to do when I just want to unwind and relax.The daily tidy is a nice feature (when the above levels aren't involved), but for game completion enthusiasts, I can't recommend this game.The games involving the pencil organisation, either by length or symbols or colour, were .Trying to get them into position- they'd line up and 'snap' when you dragged them to the space- then suddenly and without reason, snap OUT of position and go crooked. What? Why is this such a horrible placement issue?One achievement requires 100 days played- to complete the Daily Tidy 100 times. It seems a little ridiculous since once you have completed the game in its entirety, (which took me around 4 hours- mostly as I was distracted by watching a film on the other monitor), 100 days is a rather silly goal to reach in a game that can be completed in less than half a day.10 Days would be a better goal, even 50 but that too would be a stretch, especially as one of the 'daily tidy' was a single tidy of pulling 6 leaves off a plant to make it symmetrical. That was it.It's a complete farce- thankfully it can be nullified by simply changing the System time (still a farce to do 100 times)There is also no V-Sync or option to cap framerate. I get it, it's not an intensive game, but implementing this option is still important so PC's aren't ramping to go to the highest possible FPS when it simply isn't needed and the resources can be used elsewhere.Furthermore, to acquire 100% of Achievements, you are required to buy and complete the DLC- which is a pretty bad practice for developers to implement in an attempt to encourage people to buy their additional content.Separating the DLC into its own game with its own achievements would be a better choice- or simply have the DLC not have achievements- or simply offer it free-of-charge if they really want it to have achievements. If people really do enjoy the game, they'd buy the DLC regardless of achievements or not, as it is currently it seems like an attempt to goad players into buying it.("Want 100%? Buy our DLC and you can have it!")Whilst that may not have been the intention, it's still poor practice.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I wish Steam offered middle-ground reviews, this is a maybe. I RECOMMEND the game if you really think you'll like it and if it's on sale. I DON'T RECOMMEND the game however, because there simply isn't enough content for the price, some solutions are repeated multiple times and some puzzles are super finicky. It's cute though and the idea was good!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Review from someone with ADHD:the positives: it looks cute. the negatives: I played 5 min of this the refunded. Why would this game ever be $14.99? It's like if they took House Flipper, cut all of the graphics out of it, and then just gave up puzzle variation. This should be an app game for $5.00 bucks, that would make sense. But $14.99 for what, 75+ puzzles of just organizing things? What in the hell is that? I'm sure this was truly relaxing for some people but oh my god to me it was just anxiety producing seeing these mismatched items and then putting them in ways that felt, clunky and bad. If I wanted to clean things, I'd pay 2.50 for a ticket back on the train and clean my room, why is this a game? At least in House Flipper you have like, a house to complete, so you can see how it's changing over time, and you get excited about the next power washer section, stuff like that. You know what this made me feel like? It made me feel like I was drinking boba with the tapioca at the bottom, and you have to get all the tapioca balls in the straw or you feel anxious. At least I do. But in this case you solve it, and then you just jump to getting more of a mess! There's no "look at all these fixed things you did" it's just, hey you are anxious about this messed up area, you put things either next to or onto things, then you get a star and then go to the next mess. Don't play this game. Please. And if you have ADHD, man I hope you can enjoy this, but this game at this price just made me reallly annoyed. If this was $5.00 this review would not have been as harsh.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I sure do love my animals. This game made me realize how even though my animals frustrate me sometimes, especially while trying to keep a tidy home, I love them unconditionally - - all the way to the moon and back. This is a fantastic game for anyone who likes to fixate on things and maybe thinks they're a weirdo. The daily cleaning mini-games will become a ritual for me before going to work or doing homework. Exercises like this get my brain in the right mood and focused. It's also amusing to play while sharing your screen with a friend, so you can share how weird you are about how you organize or solve puzzles. The art style and music are phenomenal. There are a couple of levels where some of the noises of the puzzles are a bit grating, but other than that; I had a fantastic time playing through it.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10I absolutely love the style of this game and it genuinely helped me calm myself through some tough spots this past year. It genuinely is one of my top 10 currently <3I'd say my only gripe is the bit where you have to form a symmetrical pattern out of nature stuff. The hint it gave wasn't quite clear enough so I had to look up the solution. But once I knew what to do it was easy and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game has great aesthetics and starts off with reasonable progression in concepts and difficulties. I found it absurdly charming to begin with, though the music got really repetitive really quickly. Unfortunately, as with many logical puzzle games, the logic behind some of the solutions was difficult for me to follow. I got to a point of frustration where I had to walk away, and when I returned, the frustration levels didn't really go down. So this isn't a game for me, but if people like puzzles that don't do a lot of hand-holding and works with items found in most houses in fun ways, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I'm the most virgo virgo you'll ever meet; cleaning and organizing is my hobby, to the point where it's a curse. I thought that A Little to the Left would give me a similar enjoyment to Unpacking, but while the art style and color palette are fun, the gameplay itself is disappointing. My main complaint is that puzzles have very specific answers, even when there are multiple solutions, so completing a puzzle doesn't give me much satisfaction. Real tidiers know that each tidier has their own system. Solving some of these puzzles actually gave me an ick because they are so far from what I would consider organized.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little game about sorting objects based on certain criteria. This is a more casual puzzle game as opposed to something like The Witness or Baba is You, but it has it's own unique charm and I had fun figuring out the levels.THat being said, it is a short for $15 so I would recommend waiting for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: If, like me, you've got a bit of OCD then this game is for you. A little too quirky in places and often a bit frustrating but I loved every minute of it. It's basically putting stuff in order but it's cleverly done and I shall await the next DLC with eager anticipation. Nicely priced too as I felt I'd got my monies worth on both the original game and the DLC which I bought the moment I'd finished the game. Looking forward to more of the same from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who absolutely loves games that revolve around organization, puzzles and just wholesome content, a little to the left had everything. I expected for it to be a quick play, as most games like this are, but the levels just kept coming and I couldn't have been happier. I'm sad that its over but can see myself playing it again, if you enjoy games like unpacked or assemble with care...this is probably right up your alley.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, A little to the left is a wonderful puzzle game, flawed only by a few things:Many of the puzzles require too much precision. You will have everything correct but one battery is a pixel out of place. Thre should be more allowance for this to cut down on frustration. There's also some levels where it's difficult to figure out where to start and all the pieces of the puzzle are in a pile. In actual puzzle building you can see all your pieces but not in this game which makes starting very difficult in places.The other flaw is that the best levels in the game (drawer organizing) are few and far between. Considering I bought the game for those levels, I would do anything for a level pack of 20 or so of just drawer organizing. Overall I'd still recommend this game jsut go in knowing that the drawer levels are not that common and someof the puzzles you will solve but because there's a pixel off, you can't get the puzzle to ding and give you the star. You can skip the level but it's still frustrating. More drawer levels please!!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game- very relaxing and fun enough to where you're challenged but not stressed (other than that one box challenge lol I was holding it off til the literal end.) _childDocuments_.review: Cute Game with great creative Puzzles. Also notable is the awesome score, which really makes the game relaxing and calming. AAnd especially notable are all the developer animals shown in the Credits. So overall a perfect Game.I personally have 3 Problems, but those are completionist related. 1. The no Hint Achievement is placed further below the use a hint achievement. So because of this i used a hint on purpose to get the achievement and later deeply regret because i will need to wait some time till i can go through the game again without getting bored. I would just leave the: let it be achievement and use a hint achievement away, then a clean walkthrough would also be more interesting to achieve.2. Having Achievements for the DLC is cool, but that they are placed in the main game again means: i have to buy the dlc to get 100%.3. Having Dailys in a short puzzle Game is a big no go for me. I only Accept those in games where progress is basically optional like in Fortnite. If i dont care about the Battle Pass, i dont need to come back daily. At the same time those games are designed to be played forever, while this game is linear and when youre done youre done. Just as a completionist you have to come back daily to do those. Not a good decision imo.Thats a lot of Text for critism but to be clear, it is an fantastic game, just small points kinda annoying me.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly pretty game with each level having a lot of visually striking and unique objects to try to organize.The main issue is that the puzzles start becoming absurdly esoteric after a bit with my personal experience being seeking out a guide or activating a hint before reaching my own solution or repetitively dropping everything randomly until an audio cue played or the object snapped into place which never felt satisfying.I honestly wouldn't be too perturbed by how backed into a corner some solutions are if the game gave more levels multiple stars to collect as SOME progress is being made, but very few actually have multiple solutions and require finding 'THE' way.At least there's no punishment or downsides for hints and you can always skip a level, but with how short the game is it feels like a waste, and as someone who likes 100%ing as I go along it reached a point where it got annoying.The price is also rather a lot more than what I'd expect with all this in mind and would honestly see it working more as a visually striking paid mobile game.If you're looking for a cute yet complicated puzzler then feel free to try it out, but the advertising of it being satisfying begins fading the further you go which drags down the art when worked into a full product.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Good Game, wait for a sale tho- If you are really debating on buying the game and want to know if its worth it- its not worth 15 bucks, I will be honest. The game has nothing necessarily bad going for it, but don't let the 75+ levels fool you like it fooled me. In total, there are 80 actual levels you can do, and some have different solutions to them. Though I would say that some of the levels are wayyyy too easy, and some are way too hard. It goes from organizing 5 colored pencils in the order of a rainbow in 5 seconds, to hanging up different tools on a wall based on where the nails are which took me like 15 minutes to figure out. Its about 2-3 hours of gameplay. With little repeatability. The game can genuinely be more picky on how to organize things than you would think. I personally think it would be way better if you reorganized everything in the way you wanted, and then said you were finished with the level, and continue to the next. Then at the end it could show you all the before and afters, and you get that feeling of having cleaned or fixed the mess to your liking, and not having to do it the way the game wanted you to. Maybe like an alternate game mode like that, idk. The art style and sound are really really nice though, I am personally a huge fan of all the little noises it plays when you interact with all the different items on all the levels. I like the sound of satisfying noises so if you are the same then this game definitely is nice in that field. Also the daily tidy thing is nice, but it just chooses a random level for you to do, so you are just repeating a level you've already done if you beat the game. So they take like 5 seconds to do. I would say this game is much more like a 5/10 dollar game as is, but I do think the devs plan to add more levels in the future, which is cool. Game itself is fun though, and a good 75-80% of the levels are satisfying to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is a comfort food of a game. It's good at teaching the player how to play it and building difficulty in a fairly steady ramp. It has enough variety too. it's hint system is well thought out and the ability to skip a level is a relief. It has depth with the ability to find different solution, the DCL and the daily puzzle. Both the graphics and music are charming. It knows how to surprise. And, in the end, it's a bit of a love story.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I feel bad not enjoying this one. I love these kinds of relaxing puzzle games. However, I found a few aspects tedious that were growing a little more obvious over time.Some puzzles have more than one solution, but the hints are rigid. At least, I think so anyway, I did not see a way to get a hint for an alternative solution. So if you solve a more challenging puzzle but can't figure out the second or third solution, you're left either flailing or giving up. There were a few puzzles as well where I could see a potential solution, but it wasn't a solution that the devs had considered so it doesn't work.But these were relatively small issues. The one that made me stop and put the game back was the soup can labels. The solution was obvious, yet it wasn't working. I finally gave up and checked the hint, and...I was right. I had been a pixel off of the exact positioning. It had multiple solutions, and I realized then that I probably would not be able to 100% this game. No hints for the alternative solution, and armed with the knowledge that it would have to be pixel-perfect I switched to the next puzzle. Solved it easily, but then found that some of the alternatives that I was coming up with weren't working.It's not a good fit for me. Only some of the puzzles have a clever "aha" moment, and the game has a few intentional moments of making a mess. It might be a good fit for you, so I'd say give it a try and if it doesn't click after an hour, it isn't for you either.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I would probably give this game a 9/10 for people with neurodivergencies, a 7/10 for people who like cozy gaming, and a 6/10 for everyone else. Overall it's just extremely satisfying to arrange everything so tediously. I think sometimes it can become a bit picky with how EXACT it sometimes requires you to be (especially the Drawers DLC) but it's something you can relax into and use your brain for.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. Its a very calm and chill game that challenges you without adding stress. _childDocuments_.review: 5/5 As someone who loves organization and sorting things, this is such a fun and cozy game to de-stress and spend some time alone, with a podcast or some music and just solve a few puzzles. Due to this, something that should be a relaxing, satisfying puzzle game ends up being frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get it twisted, I  this game. The art is fantastic, the music is relaxing, and the controls are great. The price is a little much for how much content there is in the game. There is a daily play mode, where a new puzzle is unlocked each day, but after finishing the game in two sittings, I'm not sure I'm going to bother coming back to play a level that will only take 3 to 5 minutes to complete.I'm not saying that the price is exorbitant or anything, but for what the game is, and how finicky some of the levels can be with precise placements, the price is a touch high.If you are willing to spend $15 to fill a single afternoon playing an organizational puzzle game, then do it. It has the same vibe as Unpacking, but it's all about the puzzle of how things fit together. Plus you get to pet the cat in the last level.

_childDocuments_.review: 10h+ 4/10 1 (if you don't use the hint system) Yes, I would highly recommend  No Yes, achievements like "not using the hint system during the whole campaign" and "Using the hint system on every level"  Yes, doing 265 daily puzzles (And one achievement for doing 300 on consecutive days Yes Yes Yes, for a few achievements you have to solve the daily puzzles on consecutive days with the highest one being 300 days in a row No Yes, you have achievements for using the hint system all the time and for never using it NoI have such a hard time writing this review. On one hand, I adored the game, I had such a lovely time playing it. It was wholesome, fun and with moments frustrating because some of the puzzles with multiple solutions and not being able to figure out the other solutions. The game has a great hint system, but that will only show the main solution, not the others solutions.  So for people who love organizing/cleaning in games, this is a lovely one and I would highly recommend it. For achievement hunters, it is a totally different story. With the promise of this game kinda expected a relaxing achievement list. The ones where you have to do something special at a specific level and completing all the levels with all solutions would be the type of achievements I totally would expect and was ready for. Sadly it has so many frustrating achievements as the one to use no hints during the whole campaign as well as to use the hint on every level, but the worse are the 365 dailies and the 300 consecutive dailies, especially that last one. I believe it is possible to "cheat" a little bit on this by changing your computer time, but I'm not up for those types of challenges. Especially when you can get totally stuck and start over when one day you aren't able to solve the puzzle of that day. The developers have responded to  about how crazy the achievements are and that they will think about maybe redoing some of them, so that gives a bit of hope. For now, if you enjoy puzzle games, especially when there is some sort of organizing involved, I would highly recommend this game as it is a lot of fun! As an achievement hunter, I would for now wait and see what the developers will decide to do with those very tedious achievements.
