_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing cozy game that has puzzles which vary from easy to perplexing. While the more complex puzzles had me vexed for minutes on end, I did manage to solve them all without hints. But for those of you who find a puzzle too difficult, then the hint system is a great way to move past a puzzle and not forfeit on an otherwise chill game. I enjoy the puzzles that have multiple solutions, as that allows for some replayability.I'm sure some of you will enjoy your interactions with the cat. I found the ones where the cat appears after you solve the puzzle to be amusing. The ones "while" you are working on a puzzle, less so. Maybe I'm just not a cat person? Or maybe I just don't like the cat making a mess out of my neatly organized work. No idea.There are a lot of Steam achievements, but I take affront to the ones that are awarded because you used a hint or skipped puzzles. It's like the game is forcefully telling me: "Do you want to get those achievements, so you can work towards 100%? If so, then JUST DO IT." I don't think anyone WANTS to display an achievement that shows they needed a hint or skipped a puzzle altogether. But hey, that's just me. On the other hand, when playing "Above Snakes" I did kill myself on purpose to snakes, bees... and falling trees... just to unlock those three achievements.Overall? A great game if you're searching for a cozy, relaxing, chill game that require careful thought and very little twitch reflexes. I plan to purchase the two DLCs now that I have finished all five chapters of the original game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, and I think it has a lot of merit. The game's style is really cute and very well crafted. It is visually very strong and what drew me into the game to begin with.However, I just can't say the same about the puzzle design. I understand it is first and foremost, a puzzle game where you have to find the "catch". But it advertises itself as a relaxing organisational experience and it's not really that. Some puzzles only have one set answer even if you can craft many different ways to organise the scene.I found myself frustrated as I can't figure out why my answer wasn't correct, after a few times of feeling this way I just couldn't keep playing. The real answers are too abstract and sometimes feel arbitrary. Sometimes I would just stumble upon these "real answers" randomly because of the items snapping into place and playing an audio cue.I think a way that could make this game feel better to play is allow more and looser answers to all puzzles. Let the players experiment and find all the possible solutions. When I'm done with a level, instead of moving me forward, let me retry and fiddle around and see what different and abstract answers I can make up.The "let it be" option is a good design choice but feels unsatisfying to click when I've made my own answer.I feel like the whole time I'm cleaning someone else's house with their rules instead of my own spaces which makes the game feel tedious unintentionally. It's a cute game if you like abstract puzzles that look pretty, not really for those looking for a zen and carefree experience.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: "A great little game to relax with." At least that's what I thought until I saw the repetitive daily tasks and positioning puzzles (clover and leaves from trees) that can't be solved with logic. So the game is too boring for me. If these "puzzles" had been at the beginning, I would have refunded the game immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game fairly close to its release date as I and a friend were highly anticipating it after seeing it advertised to us several times. Unfortunately, we found the advertisements to be fairly misleading. We were anticipating a mostly sorting-based game, only to find it to be a relatively small portion of the game (like the drawer levels). We each finished the game, mutually agreed "well, that wasn't what I'd really wanted or was expecting" and never played it again. Gave it the fairest shot I could. And then some time later they release a DLC for more levels like what they were advertising in the first place... lol.This game is relaxing and the art style is pleasing. I did enjoy the puzzles that were like what was being advertised. If this game were entirely about putting pens and screws into their right spots, I would have ten times the playtime. The later levels in particular I found to be progressively less enjoyable, although there are uninteresting puzzles throughout. I can't find it in me to recommend others spend like $20 CAD on a relatively short-life puzzle game with hit-or-miss puzzles.

It helped me relax after long and stressful days, I just wish it was longer!

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because I was looking for something like unpacking. But I honestly found the whole thing so asinine that I was just really disappointed when I realized that the whole game is just really menial children's puzzles. I played for 2 hours to see if I was missing something. I'm not. It's just mind-numbingly boring. Not really a story or through-line, no big picture or satisfying before and after. The game is cute and well-designed, it just absolutely doesn't capture my attention.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Good puzzle game. Took about 3 hours to complete -- which IS short, but I feel very fair for the sale price I nabbed it at. Great aesthetic all the way through. Puzzles had a very satisfying range of difficulties, with more than one way to complete most and some pretty novel solutions. Some stumped me a while, some were quite obvious. All were fun.Really enjoyed this, all the way through the adorable credits.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: amazing game the art was amazing and the colours are super nice with the way everything just fits so well together i wish my house looked like that. i highly recommend you get this game and play it for yourself and in the end credits it was amazing to see all of those animals and rip Elliot, im so glad i took the time to play this game
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully designed organisation game that doesn't stray too far into the obscure. I've played point-and-clicks before, and I don't tend to get along with them, often finding the puzzle solutions too obscure. You're expected to read the developers mind - this isn't the case with A Little to the Left, because I know it was made by people whose brains work the same way as mine. It took a little getting used to, learning what is and isn't an acceptable approach to organisation within the game's world, but once you've learned it, you'll probably be able to power through the game and return to the puzzles that didn't click on another day (thank you for the 'let it be' feature)! I only needed to look up the solutions to the most obscure puzzles, but probably could have sussed them if I'd given myself enough time. The daily tidy is also neat, though quickly becomes repetitive.As an aside, the art and sound design are brilliant. Well worth the purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute and fun game! I love that they have mixed in easy, medium, and hard puzzles throughout, rather than just getting harder and harder. There are multiple solutions to most puzzles as well, making it even sweeter because you can do a puzzle 2-3 times, looking for a different way to solve it each time. Last, but certainly not least, the kitty! It makes this game extra cute and its cheeky behaviour makes this game unique.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I want to like this game, I just can't. Some of the puzzles just have some hyper-specific answer it expects you to just know. I have had a good number of times something feels like it should've been a solution, but it was the game just misguiding you with design. While this might be seen as a feature to make it harder, it honestly just feels like a slap to the face because I paid attention to the wrong detail, and the only way you can tell it's the wrong trail is by following it.And other times, you're supposed to put objects in certain places they will just snap to, but you don't know that's what you're supposed to do until you try putting the objects all across the screen. Some kind of indicator would've been nice. And I had an issue when I "solved" a level correctly, it didn't complete. I had to restart the level and try the same exact solution again to complete it, which will make you feel like you're going insane if you didn't take a hint. Overall, the game is pretty and has a relaxing feel to it but poor UI choices, hyper specific solutions, and false solutions have just ruined the experience for me.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Such a lovely and cute game. I've wanted to play it for a while now, so my expectations were really high, but it did live up to them. The puzzles are fun, although some can be a little tiring (I'm looking at you, mailboxes puzzle). The music is perfect, it sets the mood and guides the player without them noticing much. The sound design overall is great. Visually, well, this game is known for its aesthetic after all. It's so pretty!!!!!The DLC gets a little too annoying for me sometimes… You know, drawers and stuff. It's too much “open this, close that, now open that again” for me. But besides that, it's nice!! And also a good follow-up to the main game. Although maybe a little pricy by itself.I did go back and forth in the main game several times to get closer to 100%, but it was nice. Even when I already knew the answers to every puzzle, I was enjoying the game. So yeah, between that and daily puzzles —something I did not expect at all—, this game is worth replaying. Something not usual with short games.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: The base game and the DLC were pretty fun and had lots of variety to them. However - to unlock all achievements, you have to solve 75 days worth of boring, uninspired, and buggy cycle of 8 repeating puzzles. Which makes me change my recommendation to "not recommended" since one has to deal with this slog for about 73 more days than they had to interact with the more fun part of the original game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to love this game. Having enjoyed Unpacking and Assemble with Care, I thought this would run in a similar vein. Unfortunately A Little to the Left - while it looks great - quickly becomes annoying and frustrating. What the game wants from you as a solution is often obscure and you have to rely on the hint (which gives you the solution right away. A gradual hint system would have been much better). Not to mention how finicky placement can be. On a particular level involving tools, the game would not accept my solution because one item was a pixel or two out of alignment, despite being where the damn thing needed to be.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: idk how i feel about it really, some of the puzzles consist of 'scribles' which is basiclly trial and error to solve it rather then a thought evoking puzzle. I also think the game is over priced, even on sale for 9$ Im not convinced, I was hoping to get some puzzles with many solutions that you didn't see at first, but every one has been I can see all of them right away and really it just takes time to put them together, and of course the level has to restart for each solution... for some reason. like when you walked in a portal 2 map you don't even know where the exit is and of course not the solution either and even when you think you do you might not. im jumping the gun a little, i've only played like 40 min of it but 85% of my time is spend moving stuff to the solution I already know rather then actually puzzle solving..   it is a feel good game but I also FEEL like that is a cop out as that should be supplemental and not the focus.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: it was cute but i wish it would have been more organization i was under the impression that this would be a more relaxing experience where you can organize stuff without one correct solution but i found myself getting frustrated and confused at these puzzles and a good handful of them it wouldnt say it was correct when it was i even looked up the solution to be sure and it still wouldnt say i completed it no matter what i did
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: it's good to play through, but i'm sick to death of the daily puzzles. I don't want to have to wait for the puzzle to come in, I want to sit and mindlessly organise the objects. The fact that I have to wait to do more is extremely annoying and has turned me away from an otherwise good game.Like I recommend it, but if you're someone who wants to 100% the game, then I can't say you should buy it because it demands that you play every day so you can quickly do the dailies and get the last of the achievements. I think it's stupid to expect players to open the game for a single puzzle, then come back tomorrow and do the same thing.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game, HOWEVER, I have one big struggle with it: There are NO true instructions/help page that I can find. When you jump in you just get thrown a puzzle, but there's never any explanation or words. Not at the beginning, not on the main menu, I couldn't find a help menu, etc. There is a "HINT" option, but I don't feel the hints are clear at all. I tried the hint twice, only when really needed, and it almost made it more confusing.I'm neurodivergent and really struggle when instructions/tasks aren't clearly explained...I ended up getting really overwhelmed after some levels. The first some puzzles I was able to work my way through, but once I hit a pattern I couldn't figure out even the hint felt not enough. It was so frustrating. I ended up more stressed and not relaxed.I know this may seem stupid to many, but I'm leaving this comment for the one person who may also feel this and need more clear instructions.The game is adorable, but I feel disappointed. It's just not for me I guess. :(
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Relaxing and fun organization game. Has a variety of difficult and easy puzzles as well as many different types of puzzles to complete. Both DLC packs are just as fun as the original game, full of charm and interesting puzzles. Some puzzles are a little picky about specific about the order of things, whether something is organized from left to right vs right to left, but otherwise a wonderful experience!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art, delightful sound effects, and a good variety of puzzles and interesting perspectives. I never got frustrated because I could skip levels and return to them. Plus even if I had a hard time finishing a level the hint format is really nice (both erasing to reveal and giving just enough info for an "ah-ha!" moment) so I never got bummed out by it. I liked the achievements for asking for hints too, it felt very non-judgmental and contributed to the whole chill vibe. Sometimes I would just mess around on a level because it was fun to move stuff around With the puzzle aspect I don't feel like it was repetitive, and I see myself replaying this again and coming back to it to unwind because of how entertaining it is to solve even if I know the answer. Overall 100/10 probably my favorite pc game to date! Best money I've spent on steam. Definitely going to buy the DLC later too, hoping that's just as good.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Does not worth the price. I don't really understand the star rating criteria, the few first chapters feel somewhat comforting, but then when a "destroyer" appear during my cleaning process, I literally swear. No thanks. I love the destroyer, in real life, but back tf away when I'm cleaning. I appreciate the daily puzzle, but as someone who cannot play games everyday, not really my thing.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. It is very intuitive to control but as you play the puzzles get increasingly more challenging. Some reviewers seem frustrated that they don't see what the pattern is to some levels. If you like puzzle games in any way, this is a very good game. However if you find yourself getting frustrated with a level, you have to try to think outside the box.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It's OK. Don't expect "puzzle-puzzles"; it's mostly symmetry, counting and pattern finding. Color blind people might have difficulty with some levels. Too much UX is sacrificed for flavor; there should be a replay button for doing alternative solutions immediately during first play, and the animations and sluggish controls get old quick. I've lost count how many times I've had to nudge items to make them count. A bit expensive for the value, not much replayability (the daily puzzles seems like rehashes so far).
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite puzzle games ever. The art style first of all, is incredibly amazing, it was probably chosen with the puzzles in mind because they work so well together. I do love the premise because it really gives a familiar feeling, its all just normal stuff yk? The puzzle logic is also one of my favorites and in my opinion the game does a good job letting you know how everything works right off the bat. I like the game and both of the DLCs
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I do love the idea, and was drawn to this game because of my frustration with the short length of Unpacking and how there were so many "wrong" ways to organize things. However, I wasn't expecting to encounter the idea that there are a bunch of wrong ways to organize things in this game as well. When there's a stack of books of the same height, I thought color and size was an appropriate way to organize. Apparently, you have to make the colors link in a way it wants as well. This carried on, and various other little things.Frustratingly, there's no words or anything that would tell you how the game works. Nothing that says "sometimes there is more than one way to organize this one" or "this one only has ONE correct way, despite how many ways you can think of."Maybe if you aren't going to be bothered by every organization idea you try being wrong, then this would work for you. For me, some of them are quite the stretch and the lack of information + possible time limit affecting my star score? It's confusing, if nothing else. I don't personally find it comforting to race and try as organize as fast as possible.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A really unique, wholesome game about putting things in order. Some of the larger tray based levels with lots of little nuts and bolts were really enjoyable and I wish there were more of them. I didn't like some of the more abstract levels, like the symmetry or constellations ones.All in all, I think the game is worth the asking price and then some.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game was really frustrating. I liked the concept, but i find that the game doesn't offer enough freedom. For each level there's 1-3 very specific solutions, and for most levels i found more ways of sorting the objects that just weren't a valid solution to the level.Also a lot of the solutions weren't very satisfying- for example a level where you need to purposefully tilt the photo frames so none of them are straight ?? I was also personally not a fan of the sound effects. I can see the appeal but it's definitely not for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cute and pretty, I genuinely love it so much. I also love the implementation of the cat, it makes the game feel so much more like home. We get to see into the daily lives of the creators which I think is super cool, and the puzzles are the perfect difficulty. Plus, having the Daily Tidy menu allows me to do a quick puzzle everyday, even if I'm on a time crunch, allowing me to keep my smarts. Such a wonderful game, if you're skeptical then just download it anyways because I can assure you it's amazing <3
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I am somewhere in chapter 3 (out of 5) and the more I play, the less I enjoy the puzzles. Some puzzles have multiple solutions, but others only have one and if you deviate from it, it doesn't count, even though you organized it well. I also couldn't make any sense to some of the answers, like there was no logic involved and it was just random, it could just be because I am stupid though... Another issue I had a couple times is that one of the items was 1 pixel from the "correct" position, so it didn't count as a win :/The artstyle and music are chill, I just expected it to give you more freedom, so this isn't for me. I would rate it middle if I could, but I chose negative because I am leaning a bit more towards that.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game was very cute, cozy, and relaxing. I loved the simple puzzles and appreciated that some puzzles can be solved multiple ways (and need to be completed EVERY possible way to complete chapters). The game took me around 5 hours to complete, but I haven't played the DLC nor completed every achievement yet. I'll likely come back to the game in a few months when I've forgotten the answers to do a new playthrough. Even though I really enjoyed this game, for only 5 hours of game time, you may want to purchase it during a sale :)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I did not read up on this game prior to playing, and was just going based off of some out of context videos I saw online. I originally thought this was going to be a cozy, organizing game where you decide how you'd like to organize things, but it is not like that at all. This is a cozy Puzzle Solving game! the music is super relaxing, and it has a "hint" feature if you ever get stuck solving the puzzles. I did have to google a number of solutions to 100% the game as quite a handful of puzzles had multiple solutions. Great game for unwinding after a stressful day, and definitely helped get my mind off of personal things. Plus I loooove cats, and there are TONS of adorable cat moments. 10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is wonderful, the music is so soothing, and the puzzles are plenty fun. They range from simple to slightly tricky, complicated enough to still feel like you're being challenged but not too complicated that you'll lose your marbles. I love that you can even solve certain puzzles in many different ways. A Little to the Left was such a satisfying experience. Would play again.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I cried on the first levelTo put it simply, a Little to the Left is a puzzle game about tidying up, with the interference of a cat that i took to naming "Milo"It's the simplicity of the game, that left me in tears as i played the first few levelsI was diagnosed with ADHD and Autism early on in my life, so i've never had what one would call a tidy lifeBut this game made me enjoy cleaning, the way things fell into the place, the soundtrack albeit simplistic, gave the game an extra oomphThe way the game guides you feels like a warm hug, even the hints, unlike other games where you would get a penalty for using hints, A Little to the Left rewards you for itPlease buy this game if you feel like you aren't yourself lately, and thank yourself later
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I have ADD and have never in my adult life had the ability to have a clean and non-messy home.I don't reallt know how, but this game somehow teached me to not get overwhealmed when cleaning.My apartment now looks all clean, mess-free AND I can now let people in my home without having to clean 7 hours before their arrival.THX! I've dreamt about having this ability for years...I'm so thankfull!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game and wish there were more like it. The puzzles are the perfect difficulty for someone who just wants to unwind with a cute and comfortable game. I'm currently going for 100% completion, and if any completionists are out there this is a fair one to go for! The sound design is fantastic, the music is so so so relaxing, and it's very clear to me that the devs wanted to make a puzzle game for people who might be new to puzzle games but don't want to be handheld through a game.It's super beginner friendly too, with the hint system giving you the option to see how much of a hint you want, as well as hints to the multiple solutions a level might have. You can even skip levels if they're just too difficult for you, and the only penalty you get is just not getting the star (a few levels are locked behind stars, so it makes sense that being unable to solve puzzles would make it hard to unlock the harder puzzles).My only downside with the game is the lack of variety in the daily tidies. I know they pull from levels in the game, but the pool of levels feels so small for the daily that I'm in and out in minutes. But that really doesn't detract from my overall enjoyment of the game, and would only really matter to a completionist.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: The game is overall fun and enjoyable. I feel that some of the achievements are bit annoying, especially the ones that require you to have a daily tidy streak Of thirty days in a row. Other than that, the game is enjoyable and the puzzles are fun. Just don't expect really intense puzzles in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the experience and blasted through it, some of these really got me thinking haha Especially when there are several solutions :DGreat cozy game, I totally recommend if you like organizing puzzles and are looking for a game you can play in small sessions when you've got a few minutes to spare. Though, be careful it can be addictive...
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Whilst branded as an organising game, it's more of a puzzle game which wouldn't be a problem if it wasn't for the fact that the puzzles are often nonsensical. The solutions do not always align with how an individual may organise things, and since that is a subjective matter the fact there is only ever one solution to a level leads to frustration when attempting to play.A cute concept, but not all that well executed - for the asking price I would've expected a much more cohesive experience that allowed for different expressions when choosing how to solve each level.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I'm about halfway through the game (I think), and enjoying it so much. It's very fun and satisfying. There are so many different levels that I think it's worth the price. Some of the levels feel more like organization, while others feel like I'm solving a puzzle, and are even a bit challenging to figure out how to complete the level. But so far there's a good enough hints system that I haven't gotten stuck anywhere.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is a relaxing little organization game that is great if you love chilling out and cleaning up. I played this game on call with some friends and it was a great experience just organizing and chitchatting for a few hours. Some of this game's hints are kind of unclear though, or they hint at a solution that you have already solved. If I could change anything about this game, I would add a hint for every solution to every level, as most of them have multiple correct answers. Other than that, the game was fun, the art style is cute, and the cat owns my whole heart. The cat was my favorite. But the rest of the game was still five stars.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: When I first was introduced to this game through the demo, I thought it would be mostly a satisfying, light puzzler similar to Unpacking, with the focus primarily on tidying things up instead of solving semi-difficult puzzles. The end result is more 50/50 - some of the puzzles and their multiple solutions come very naturally, and feel comfy like organizing a drawer.  That's where the game shines. But others were too abstract and necessitated guesswork or the hint button. This is frustrating because sometimes the "hint" is just a depiction of the solution. Based on the reviews, I was expecting the game to be maximum 2 hours, so I was pleasantly surprised when I was still finishing puzzles after twice that runtime. If you enjoyed the demo, I think it is worth paying full price for this version. My only strong negative about this game is the second to last puzzle which goes on for way WAAAYYY too long and nearly made me ragequit. It didn't help that it was the least fun puzzle in the game to boot. But overall, 7/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great if you love puzzle games. Some of the puzzles are harder to figure out than others, of course, and the game offers a hint system. There are daily puzzles, the Daily Tidy's. The art style is really cute. It's a very relaxed and relaxing game even when a cat starts swiping at your neatly placed items. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I am sad to leave a poor review of this game.  Conceptually, it's very cute, and I greatly enjoyed the majority of it.  I have two grievances.One is that it felt like there was a tangible decline in the puzzle quality as the game went on.  There was an acceptable amount of redundancy, I would say - although you can only straighten photos or sort junk drawers so many times before the novelty wears off - but some of the puzzles were genuinely frustrating.  A few of them made no sense to me and required hints and I have no idea how anyone would have ever figured them out without them; there were also a few instances where I just clicked around randomly to find interactions with items that were not at all obvious and I don't feel like that's good design.  The frustrations I started to feel in the second half of the game took a lot away from the enjoyment I got out of the first half.My second issue - the larger one - was playtime/content.  Even with the struggles I had, I completed the base game in 3 hours.  I am glad I bought this on sale, but still don't feel it was particularly good value for the money.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Would I recommend this game? Yes I would. It's a gorgeous game from head to toe and extremely fun and satisfying to play, makes me want to find every drawer in my house and put everything together shape perfect. However if you're someone who plays a lot of puzzle games this is incredibly short, got it completed in a little over 5 hours, minus a couple of stars (that includes the DLC). I love the design and puzzle style and I want more!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Makes my neurodivergent brain go brrrr. This game had a few really clever moments that surprised me.My literal only complaint is that a 30 day streak for daily puzzles is rough, especially since there's only about 15 hours of content if you include the DLC and archived puzzles, so the achievement become about remembering to do it once you finished the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Just a cutesy time-passer with strong 'just one more puzzle' energy.- The cursor design and click detection are quite poor, especially when playing on a laptop track pad or the steam deck. I found myself getting a little frustrated with this.- There is a point in the game where you are unable to skip a 'cutscene' in order to continue on. It isn't long, but this would have been a nice feature. I wasn't a fan of the time it took to move from one puzzle to the next.- Many of the puzzles feel like pure 'filler' and are not challenging, nor interesting. For example there are countless 'symmetry' puzzles, where you're given some amount of shapes and need to create symmetry along a central Y axis.  This disappointed me, because there were many puzzles that felt quite cheeky/clever otherwise. At ~5 casual hours in length the game serves its purpose well, but I wouldn't classify it as  or a 'must buy' puzzler. I appreciate the trance the game put me in, and there's a lot of love put into this. So worth the $15, and even better if you can get it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A game great for people who like organisation or tidiness. Its relaxing and some levels have some difficulty in figuring out the order to organise especially those levels with the different options to organise. Overall, its a game that is worth your time and perhaps money (if it is on sale, it's definitely worth it)! :)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I got this for my partner and I cuz it looked cute, fun and would scratch the 'tism itch. The first few puzzles were fun and enjoyable but as the game went on we both became increasingly disappointed and frustrated. The devs say the puzzles become more "abstract" as the game goes on but they only seem to become less logical and solved in a way only an insane person would think of.The constellation puzzle was so defeating because it... literally shows you how to solve it? It takes no brain power or thought. The clock though, THE CLOCK. ARE YOU KIDDING ME??!Most puzzles seems to work on colour, shape and size. After a while it gets very old. I thought this could be a good recommendation for children but ehhh... I can't even recommend it for kids.Extremely disappointed. It's cute, has some good ideas but ultimately I wouldn't recommend it. If you're trying to get all the achievements for Daily Tidy, I wish you all the best - your brain will be melted by the end of it.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a super comfy puzzle game that often presents you with a rather simple but disorganised scene which needs arranging in a certain way. These puzzles range from sorting items into compartments, arranging stacks of boxes or finding hidden patterns in everyday objects.The puzzles are of a very nice difficulty, never going too far off of the deep end, although I would argue that a few can be a bit unclear as to what the end goal ultimately is. Still, a handful of the puzzles you encounter have multiple solutions, which it encourages you to explore and find all of. I personally found this to be quite enjoyable as often I would find one solution, and come back later to explore it with a different mind and find the other solutions.The game also has some sort of daily new puzzle system which appears to make variants of existing puzzles in the game, leading to a nice treat should you wish to check in each day for a few minutes of thinking.I'd recommend this for anyone looking for a very light and relaxing puzzle game. Bonus recommend if you're a cat lover as you'll often find your progress charmfully impeded by a feline friend.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: for $15, you get 3 hours of quality game play. Puzzles are in NO particular difficulty.  Artsy game that feels like it was made by a team of cat ladies. I softflocked myself on breadcrumbs by putting them too close to the edge of the screen. I wish the game was just a little bit shorter or i was a little more sober so i could get a refund by finishing under 2 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Purchased this game for my girlfriend. It kept her quiet and out of my hair. 10/10 would recommend. Serious review: was a very well put together relaxing game to play. The artwork is beautiful and simple concept of the game means there's no stress when playing. Would highly recommend this to anyone that wants a chill game to play.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not the best at writing game reviews, but, I just have to say this was one of my favourite games of the year, such a simple concept but so well made and thought out; it also helped relieve my gaming fatigue so much by making the levels challenging yet doable. The constant rush of achievement is brilliant and being able to finish it in five hours left me feeling very happy from beginning to end, I think there should be a lot more games such as this one; quick, cute, funny. Just the perfect package :) p.s don't play if you are likely to want to buy a cat, you will give in
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game primarily to play on my steam deck and I have been thoroughly enjoying it since purchasing it. A quick note to those who want to go after the achievements quickly, it is going to take a full year to get them all playing daily, so if that is something you don’t want to do then pass this over. But the point of this game is for players to pass the time in a nice relaxing manner with no rush to solve them in a timely manner and no penalty for failure either. In fact you can go through the whole game without solving everything and still get to the credits. And each level has hints where you could slowly expose what is needed to figure out if you’re on the right track or not. The “campaign” is about 3 hours long and every day you get a new puzzle which is just a different variation of the “campaign” puzzles. The only thing I would probably change is maybe the pricing, maybe down to $10 USD, but that’s just me. Regardless, I’m looking forward to whatever the next game this small studio will come out with next, and be kind to the developers. This seems to be their first game that they’ve made.

_childDocuments_.review: "A Little to the Left" caters to those who find joy in organizing items by patterns, but the experience isn't as straightforward as it seems.- The game's multiple solutions for puzzles are intriguing, but finding the specific "correct" solution can be elusive. This becomes frustrating when a solution that visually appeals to you is not recognized as valid.- Puzzle solutions involve various elements like object height, size, color, and symmetry. However, the object snap mechanism, crucial for determining correct placements, feels weak. Objects often need extra adjustments even when they are correctly placed, leading to confusion.- The game's music was a letdown for me. It's repetitive and simplistic, with some tracks featuring high-pitched tones that were uncomfortable for my tinnitus.- The narrative is minimal and underdeveloped, especially when compared to "Unpacking," which skillfully tells a story through item progression without any dialogue. A similar storytelling approach in "A Little to the Left" could have enhanced the gaming experience.- I appreciated the flexible solution approach in "Unpacking," where the main rules are item placement in specific rooms and avoidance of clutter on the floor. Implementing a similar flexibility in "A Little to the Left" could reduce player frustration.- In conclusion, while the game aims to provide a calming and satisfying experience, it often leads to frustration due to its strict solution criteria and missed opportunities in narrative and gameplay mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so satisfying! I played the demo a while back and was looking forward to the full release. So glad it's finally here. Most are pretty intuitive to solve without a hint, or by just uncovering one tiny portion of the hint screen to give you a place to start. I also like how there are visual and auditory clues when you get something right or wrong. Things snap into place and a tiny chime sounds when you get it right, for many puzzles. (Things can also snap or settle into the wrong place, but it doesn't chime in this case.) If something is in the wrong spot, it will often skew off-kilter so you  know it doesn't go there. Overall, I find this puzzle game to be calming and very enjoyable and I look forward to continuing. I am about to finish chapter 3 after just shy of 4 hours, and have unlocked 10/51 achievements. I am not specifically seeking achievements yet, but likely will go back for any I missed. I noticed you can go back and replay previous puzzles which I was grateful for because I accidentally skipped one I was having a tough time with, when I was trying to figure out if I had to save. (Note: the game seems to auto-save your progress.) Daily puzzles are a total mystery to me. Have not been able to solve one.*edited to correct the time played*Second edit: About 8.5 hours to get all solutions to all puzzles. Thank you to the reviewer who mentioned the "stars" as I hadn't even noticed them. I thought it was pretty fun to go back and think of another way to solve the same puzzle besides the first way that occurred to me. Overall I enjoyed this game a lot, and I'll probably go back to do the Daily Tidy occasionally as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very sweet, cute little puzzle game, easy to play and finish in one day. If you love organising things to be "just so," this is the game for you. No bad guys (other than a cat that'll sometimes bat things away) and no pressure. The only negative thing is the "daily tidies" can get a little tedious, especially if you're trying to do the achievements for them. It just cycles through the same few puzzles over and over. The worst one is the cat made of stars, because it's just the same few images repeated often. Over-all though, this game is pretty good and I'm looking forward to the drawers and cupboards DLC, because those levels were my favourites.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is definitely a niche game, as although it is a puzzle game, it does involve organizing drawers or rearranging cabinets to complete the puzzles.  I find all these puzzles to be fun, scratch that itch of solving a casual but sometimes detailed puzzle, and all around an awesome game.  Some of the puzzles even have multiple solutions to stretch the players problem solving skills.  The fact that there is a daily puzzle is also awesome, as I can start my day with a cup of coffee and a nice puzzle.  There was no doubt when the DLC dropped that I would get it, and it is worth every penny.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This game looked cute and simple like the Unpacking game I LOVE. I must be too slow or something because the puzzles can be incredibly difficult. There are no instructions so you have to guess or use hints to figure out what the puzzle actually is. It's like when someone says "Do it" with no other information. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I was interested in the game after playing the demo, and I like the game, but if you're looking for a similar experience to Unpacking this might not be it. The first chapters hit that vibe for me, but the later chapters have more "there is only one solution" puzzles, and some of them are just kind of confusing. Though I don't think any of the puzzles have any completely out of nowhere solutions, sometimes it does feel like you just have to do what the game wants despite finding another satisfying way (and there's still one puzzle solution I cannot figure out the logic behind, but only that one) I was hoping for more multiple solution puzzles, but they only make up about a fourth of the campaign puzzles. Also the ending was weird and I think it went on for a bit too long, but it was very pretty.I recommend the game still, it's a very relaxing and pretty puzzle game. The majority of the puzzles are good, and there's a cute cat.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game is really cute, and well made. And the fact there are multiple achievements to log in and do the Daily. But the daily is a level that'll take you 10 seconds at most.It's going to take me 2-3 months to get 100% achievements on this game and that's frankly ridiculous.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: Cute graphics. Nice music. But not all the puzzles are intuitive, and when you go to look at the hint, there doesn't seem to be a logical way to get to it.They want it one way and one way only on puzzles that don't seem to be that way. Then on other parts there's not a specific way though there seems that there should be one.Was not what I was expecting. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favourite games. It is SO fun to play. It's the kind of game I wish I could get a lifetime supply of, but at the same time it is good that I don't because I would just play it non-stop. I would forget to feed myself. I would not sleep. _childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite puzzle game, it's extremely relaxing while offering unique challenges. Visually, the art is consistently cute. The music is relaxing and cheery. _childDocuments_.review: Makes my brain happy to arrange various items in satisfying ways. It was mostly pretty easy imo but I am really into that stuff so... Love the cat so much! Only downside is that I completely finished after less than 4 hrs so maybe a lil pricy for the playtime. Wish there were even more levels. Still a great game, I enjoyed it for sure!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a solid little puzzle game with a gorgeous art style and clearly lots of love was put forth in developing it.I do have some minor complaints. _childDocuments_.review: Thought I would love this game from the demo but honestly it did not live up to my expectations. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: For the people that like when everything has its own place. This review comes after full "story" completion, and most solution variation completed for those interested in time to complete!I can't say how much I appreciate that the game had little nudges towards the "correct" answer for the puzzles, and that there are *multiple* ways to complete the puzzles. Most of the levels are variations on a theme, and after completing simple versions early on, the later puzzles become less cryptic for what needs to be accomplished.The aesthetics of the game were super satisfying to work within, and the hints work well within this little world the developers created. You can reveal only as much as you need while still needing to do a little leg work to determine what the hint is referring to.I played bits of this on controller and keyboard, and both work great. The controller has lock on for certain puzzles where things get kinda small to grab. Things that require precision placement are also nudged into place where necessary, and certain objects will reorient themselves to give you a tiny hint of where they might need to be placed.Overall, a quick little game to pick up that's peaceful with bits of humor! There's also "daily tidies" that you can come back to for little puzzles every day.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: A Little to the Left is a comfy little puzzle game that provides a nice and novel experience that hits close to home.  It is easy to pick up and hard to put down, and by the end of it, you’ll be taking pride in the spaces you’ve cleaned.  The premise is simple: every puzzle consists of a mess that needs to be cleaned.  The game does not explicitly describe how that must be accomplished, so the player must inductively determine what “clean” means.  However, I think you’ll find that most of the puzzles click quite easily, as everything is grounded in the cleaning of everyday things.  The patterns are intuitive and rewarding, and even if you don’t see it, the game allows you to obtain hints and/or skip any level.  It really is an accessible game that anyone and everyone can appreciate.The one thing I wish was that the game was longer.  I want more, and the new DLC will rectify this problem, but it really does leave a mark on you.  The game does provide “Daily Tidies,” a randomly generated daily level, but it isn’t sufficient.  They are just randomizations of the levels in the main campaign, so they can become boring quickly.Some believe that the game is too short for its price, but I would disagree.  Overall, even at full price, I wholeheartedly believe it is worth every dollar.  It may be short, but the experience, the challenge, it’s all unforgettable.  I would highly recommend this game, and I can’t wait for the DLC!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It is frustrating but in a good way. I enjoyed getting mad and trying to figure out what they wanted me to do. Some levels were defiantly super hard but thats what made it more fun! I brought it out with people at work and it was funny to also watch them struggle with the levels and me knowing what the actual rule is!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I would probably not recommend it unless you want something short. It's very cute, the art style works really well. While there's a theme to the puzzles, there isn't really a story - which is where Unpacking does it better. The combo of Daily Tidy and achievements based on them feels like the devs try to coerce you into playing more long after the game is done (Complete 30 Consecutive Daily Tidy's)
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what I can say that hasn't already been said by other people much better than I could ever say it. What a wonderful game. It's so sweet, the puzzles are such a delightful range of easy to understand and difficult to complete, and I absolutely adored the sound design. Their foley team deserves a raise.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: I love organizing and tidying and puzzles. Other reviews expressed my experience accurately- this is not zen or what feel like real puzzles at all. I wanted to call this an OCD simulator and say it feels like hell, but another review mentioned that if you do have OCD this game is triggering and confirmed the game is hell. I am not sure who finds this relaxing, but I don't think I was the target audience.Edit: I finished the game (mostly out of spite). Most of the puzzles are more tedious than challenging. _childDocuments_.review: This game was an extremely chill experience and a fun puzzle game. I will admit it wasn't always the most intuitive and I once had the game bug out on me and refuse to mark give me the screen that told me I'd gotten the puzzle correct but these were tiny hiccups in the experience. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a very intuitive game. Unless the game has sound cues, which I wouldn't use as I play my games on mute so as to not disturb others. Essentially, as far as I'm aware, the game gives you a jumbled mess and you figure out how to organize it. But only in the way the game wants and it doesn't give you any hints on what it needs, so you spend a bunch of time clicking and dragging and hoping by chance the thing you're holding snaps into place. _childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: After playing A Little to the Left for 100 days straight, I can honestly say that it's a really peaceful way to do daily brain puzzles (often with more than one way to organize or solve a puzzle) with a subtle puzzle storyline that incorporates the messy chaos of living with a cat. It's a gorgeous game of puzzle and organization that anyone who likes games similar to Assemble with Care and Unpacking will love. 6/10Cupboards and Drawers DLC: The new DLC adds 25 new levels with some interesting new mechanics of how to organize and is a great expansion for anyone who enjoyed the base game. It's another cute addition with little breaks for reprieve about ever 5 levels or so that involve petting the cat (which makes it more than worth my money). 5.5/10Snack Pack, Something Eggstra, and Good Tidyings: This archive collection brings a lot of seasonal joy to the game. Hopefully they add back in the achievements related to these tasks to encourage more people to explore cleaning this clutter. 5.5/10Seeing Stars DLC: While this DLC didn't quite stick on theme as much as I would've liked or as much as the Cupboards and Drawers DLC, I actually enjoyed the puzzles and organization more. This was one of the more interactive sets of puzzles I've seen from this game. Plus more cute cat friends! 6/10
_childDocuments_.name: A Little to the Left

_childDocuments_.review: This is the cutest, most wholesome game I've ever played. The art is beautiful, the music is beautiful, and the message I gleaned from it is beautiful. Life is messy. No matter how much you try to organize or make things perfect, there is no perfect. And that's okay. <3 The process is the fun part, especially if you have the love of special critter friends to share it with. Thank you for making this game.

_childDocuments_.review: During the cold months my partner and I play video games together, but she finds many games frustrating. Most popular games pair keyboard and mouse controls with time-sensitive actions, which can be difficult for people who aren't chronically engaged in the hobby (like me :P).A Little to the Left presents satisfying short terms goals to be achieved with intuitive, at-your-own-pace controls. The low skill floor makes this accessible for most people, and the inherently satisfying challenges keep more familiar gamers happy and engaged!

The 'daily tidy' is often reused levels. It ranges from making something look like a mirror of itself with plants to burning candles from long to short. _childDocuments_.review: I bought the game as well as the Drawers and Cupboards DLC. I think it's a fun game of solving puzzles, some of which have multiple ways to solve. My only complaint is with some levels in the DLC. There are some glitches (specifically one that doesn't recognize when I do everything needed for the "A Balanced Meal" achievement), and -in my opinion- too many levels where there is no puzzle, just petting the cat. _childDocuments_.review: There are so many things I enjoyed about this game.  The art style, the amount of levels, the music, the environmental storytelling.... It was so fantastic to play.  I thoroughly enjoyed this game so much.One of  my favourite features of this game was the "Let It Be" feature.  The way it was worded and the fact that I could.... let a puzzle be as it was and move on was so nice.  I really enjoy puzzle games, but sometimes I really struggle solving them and with the frustration I would stop playing.  This feature allowed me to continue without feeling bad for continuing to another level.I thought, for me, the difficulty levels were pretty well balanced for me.  I am very much a novice puzzle enjoyer, so I found some puzzles challenging enough, and some more easy and I enjoy that a lot.This game was such a joy to play, and I am honestly so excited to go back and play through the whole thing again!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing! If you like organizing and tidying this is absolutely the game for you. The puzzles range from simple to very challenging and there is a lot of content with the daily tidy. I keep playing my favorite levels over again because it is so calming. 10/10 all the way!DLC: I loved the idea of the idea of the Cupboards and Drawers being the main focus of the DLC, Those were some of my favorite levels as well. My favorite level in the DLC was the jewelry box, hands down. I loved the idea of secret compartments that only opened a certain way! Taking cover and retreating is not an option for Grave, he only ever goes full steam ahead, preferably right through his enemies. Style on your foes with gun-tastic stylish combat Stylish third-person shooting meets close-range martial arts, creating seamlessly flowing action as you crush your enemies in a gory ballet of bullets. Utilise your unlimited ammo Cerberus pistols and your transformable EVO-coffin to unleash devastating combos in pursuit of maximum damage and style. Let there be Vengeance Strap in for a wild ride, an epic & emotional story of vengeance, love and loyalty, with more than 12 hours of gameplay in the story mode, for Gungrave fans and newcomers alike. Enjoy the Scenery Go on an epic adventure across South-East Asia, based on real-life locations with a dark, futuristic twist.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a pretty big fan of Gungrave Overdose back in the day. I loved the Nightow-styled visuals, the ridiculous characters, the way everything would be torn apart and riddled with bullets after a firefight. The first four levels of Gungrave GORE are alright. Grave can now pull enemies to him with a hook to use as meat shields and can throw them. There are finishers now too. Otherwise, Grave plays just as he did in Overdose. But it's been 18 years and Overdose was kind of clunky for 2004. And while Overdose was 9 stages long with three different characters, GORE has 31 stages. There are two other characters, but you play as them for a single level each. Grave's basic gameplay never changes.The game is extremely repetitive and is stretched insanely thin by the time the credits roll. As far as improvements, the camera isn't glued to Grave's back and you can aim with your mouse. But pretty much everything else is worse. The game's art style is hideous, with awful character designs in generic levels. The visuals are no longer manga-style and the game just looks like it could be anything. The story is a nonsensical mess that doesn't have entertaining dialogue exchanges like Overdose did. Instead, the two characters with the worst designs have long conversations about SEED. The levels are long corridors where you do nothing but shoot things most of the time. However, there's some platforming too, which is some of the worst platforming I've ever seen. If you're like me, you'll have an okay time for most of the first five levels until you find yourself on top of the train in level 5. Here, you have to dodge and jump over signs that kill you in a couple of hits. Think back to PS2-era Gungrave and remember how rigid the movement was now imagine platforming with those controls. Platforming rears its ugly head multiple times and falling can lead to dying instantly. There are a handful of sections where you have to do something other than shoot things and they're always nothing short of atrocious. But the worst thing is the enemy placement. Enemies feel thrown into the levels without any attention paid to balance. You walk through a door and get assaulted by a ton of rockets, sniper shots, flames, and a hail of bullets from enemies positioned behind foes with shields and ones with swords that deflect bullets. The enemy rockets are much like the ones in Ninja Gaiden 2. You'll be trying to fight only to have to deal with rocket after rocket slamming into you. And the stunlocking is nuts. So many enemy attacks stun you, so forget about standing in place and using Grave's awesome shoot-out mode. You'll just get stunlocked and have to either grab someone to use as a shield or spam demolition attacks to refill your health gauge. Grave feels as brittle as glass, but he also feels weak. The hit detection on his Grave Hauler is also poor and it barely feels like it even hits enemies. Oh, and you need currency to upgrade Grave, but it stays the same in every level. You'll need more and more to upgrade Grave's parameters but the amount you get for later levels doesn't increase.The gameplay is putrid. The basic shooting is still kind of fun, but this game lasts over 10 hours and you'll practically only be using Grave's pistols. You also can't unlock the other 2 characters for play after beating the game. You play as them in their individual levels and that's it. This game was delayed for three entire years and it's amazing that this is the best Iggymob could do. I wish we had a good new Gungrave game, but this one is just an insult to the franchise. That anyone expects you to play $50 for it is madness.
_childDocuments_.name: Gungrave G.O.R.E

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game at launch via game pass. I'm a huge Gungrave fan so I couldn't miss it, but despite me beating it at launch, I had a miserable time for most of my playthrough. However, Iggymob has been on point with listening to criticisms, because nearly every gameplay complaint I had at launch has been fixed in patches. I would now go so far as to say Gungrave GORE is a good game. It's still imperfect in many ways, and the game's budget was half a bag of Doritos and a dream (and it shows), but damn if they didn't turn an awful product into a good one, which is no small feat. And it's a miracle we even got a new Gungrave to begin with (the VR games don't count, trust me). If you're into aggressively 6-7/10 PS2-era action game schlock, Gungrave GORE is well worth it on a decent sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Gungrave G.O.R.E

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for the next triple A Devil May Cry style character action game, this isn't it. If you are looking for a simpler 3rd person shooter about a dead guy carrying around a coffin shooting crackheads, you'll get some enjoyment out of this. I once heard that the original Gungrave for the PS2 was designed around the idea that a drunk salary man, after getting home from a hard day of work, could play a game without having to focus and just have a good time. In this regard I feel like Gungrave G.O.R.E stays true to that formula. It's a simple and stylish game. That's the essence of the franchise and it doesn't have to be much else to be worthwhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Gungrave G.O.R.E

_childDocuments_.review: "Kusoge", "So bad its good" and etc, are just lame excuses that represent the insecurities of many. If something is GOOD, then it is GOOD. You don't have to fit in with the rest of the hivemind that you feel inclined to justify your lack of self-thought by feeble means. What kind of statement is even "Best 7/10 game!", like why does everything have to be with scores? Why do we even measure our enjoyment? Everyone is quick to make assumptions and judgments, for this very reason we have games like Gungrave G.O.R.E totally overshadowed by such shallow remarks. G.O.R.E is not your typical action game, many commercialize it as such, but its highly different than the likes of Devil May Cry or Bayonetta. What you have here is pure, unfiltered Arcade Shoot Em' Up that has a heavy emphasis on scoring and utilizing your tools for effective Clears. If this doesn't seem like your cup of tea, that's no biggie. Gungrave series is definitely an acquired taste and if you want to see what you're getting yourself into, at least try playing the first game on the PS2 to have a clear idea. If you liked it, then congratulations on being part of the outcasts who think this series has just as much depth as the beloved "10/10" classics.Gungrave G.O.R.E is such a breath of fresh air in the Gaming industry whilst also being archaic in its values. Everything has to be modernized to appeal to the Status Quo for the Big Men in suits, even Nostalgia-baiting people with the "Olde" by remaking classics, and totally butchering them with microtransactions. Of course, the very same hivemind does not really mind this and is ready to have you impaled on a cross if you claim the "Resident Evil 4 Remake is a massive downgrade" but that's an entire issue of its own. P.S. I've played this game from start to finish on Hard on my first run, just git gud if you're crying about the Train stage. It really is not even an issue.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the strangest recommendation I've ever made.Gungrave G.O.R.E, which I will not be properly writing out again, feels exactly like playing a weirdo small-name game in the PS2 era. There were dozens of underrated gems back then, things that by and large slipped under the radar, and many of them never got to see the light of day again. Shinobi is dead forever, I might be the only person alive who loved Onimusha: Dawn of Dreams.Gungrave was a game I never managed to track down, and then one day I woke up to see that there was a sequel. Coming to Steam, of all things! I knew I had to give it a go once I had the chance.Well.Do I recommend this game to everyone? Yes, but only because it's been ages since I saw a game with this much heart and soul poured into it. I don't think the majority of players will enjoy this game - there are clunky controls (which I find tolerable because it's just like on the PS2), some lingering jank (which gives it charm), and the sound design in particular is constantly failing the visuals. The voice acting is PS2-era bad (which I love!), the gameplay is relatively simple (I enjoy it for it, it feels extremely arcadey) but the game just oozes heart.I've never heard of this studio before, but what I can tell you with absolute certainty is that they put their hearts and souls into making this game, and it's a really solid niche title for what it is. It's jank, it's fun, it's loud, it's flashy, it's completely ridiculous. This game would also legitimately gain 2 points on a 10 point scale if it had proper sound design, like, there has to be a sound library that's within budget they could use that contains sounds for 'chainsaw' and 'big laser powering up', right?unironically the only reason I don't record a bunch of foley myself and send it to the devs with full free license to use it is that I don't have access to the equipment I used to work with anymore :(And the fact I'd be willing to put in that work otherwise should tell you everything you need to know about this game and how I feel about it. This game is great fun. I recommend it. Statistically speaking you'll probably hate it. Buy it anyway. It's delightful 2000s edge.**UPDATE AUGUST 8 2023:**Whoa, I got a response from the developers! I never expected THAT!I kind of wrote this because I wanted to recommend this to my friends so I wrote it up as an easy way to share that, I never expected the devs would see it.I want to clarify a few things in light of that.1: I really genuinely do love this game, and I do recommend at least trying it to everyone who sees this. If you think you MIGHT like this game, you almost certainly will.2: I understand game development is super hard and I don't want you to think I was ragging overly much on the sound designer - it's difficult work, I've done stuff in that field before and people underestimate how challenging it can be. I just really think it's worth the effort, because the visuals are SO GOOD by and large that the underwhelming sound accompanying it undercuts them. This game could easily thrive off being loud and stylish with some more oomph to things like the railgun sniper shot at the end, the enemy attacks, etc.Grave's guns and Bunji's guns both sound fantastic, by the way. Very well done! And I find the voice acting fun and charming, this really does bring back nostalgia for the PS2 era in the best way.I genuinely look forward to any future work you guys put out!

_childDocuments_.review: Played the hell out of this on PS4.  A truly phenomenal action game that rewards tactical engagement with the level design with an awesome chaining system, and flashy combat feats with Art Score.  If you're just playing for completion, to "experience" the game, you're going to miss the point.  It flashes the scoring and ranking systems in your face for a reason, you're supposed to play it like an arcade game.  To actually engage with the game's mechanics and be rewarded for improving as a player, rather than just have its world and story presented to you.  You know?  To have fun playing a game?  Remember that?The PC port suffers from some of the usual UE4 gremlins, which do improve after first boot, but the game looks great on PC and has a good options menu.  Not played beyond the first level but can't imagine it gets any worse (or indeed better). Frame rate is good (even with RT and no FSR on a 6900 XT), which is the important thing.  Just remember to disable the Steam overlay, which causes massive hitches whenever it pops up.  You need to focus on the game anyway :) Oh, and the game crashes on startup if it doesn't have access to the audio stream, so you can't listen to bit-perfect CD quality music while playing, which is a mild shame for all 3 of us who give a ♥♥♥♥.  The sound design is great anyway so it's worth playing with all the sliders up.If you like playing games, buy the hell out of this, especially for £9.  If you like talking about/critiquing games, and their "immersive worlds", and call anything that constitutes actual game design or mechanics "dated", I hear there's a new Assassin's Creed out.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever played the other games, you would know that the stories and voice acting weren't the best thing in the entire world. Gungrave 2002 was incredibly bare bones plot wise and Overdose's story, while better by a long shot from its predecessor, was mediocre at best. GORE is, unfortunately, no different. Its story is, at points, difficult to follow and built shallow compared to other games. These new villains feel empty and a bit boring and they aren't as interesting or memorable compared to the first and second game. The voice acting is... atrocious and hard to listen to. Playing with the radio off is basically mandatory. But despite all of these negatives, I still would implore anyone with at least an interest in the franchise to try the game. Hell, try Overdose too, or at least watch the first two games if you can't play them. These games are made with love, care and attention and I can tell the people who work on these games LOVE what they do and what they work on. ESPECIALLY on GORE. I've listened and read a lot of the director's interviews and just listening to him speak about it, I can tell this game was a stressful labor of love that went through in the end.The developers, by the way, are amazing. It seems each month they actually listen to the fanbase and their critiques and make the game better with updates that make life so much easier. It feels rare nowadays to get developers who care and listen.I fell in love with the gameplay, which is just a fun mindless shoot-em-up that took a lot of inspiration from its predecessors. This game feels like it's stuck in the 2000s but has modern upgrades, which is a big relief since departing from the basic gameplay format would betray what these games have been built upon. It's flashy and spunky and fun to keep playing over and over again. The set dressing is also really nice to see too. The details you can stumble upon, such as a shooting range during the Vietnam stages, are small but lend to a sense of life in the stages that might be empty otherwise. If you like games with a sense of charm, nostalgia and a 2000s feel, try this game because you won't regret it. If you end up liking the characters, I'd recommend you to watch the anime. Actually, no watch the anime first, the games, and THEN play GORE because this game feels like a big love letter.

_childDocuments_.review: Gungrave G.O.R.E is frustrating. Not because I didn't enjoy the game, quite the contrary, I think its the most fun game I've played all year. It is frustrating because of how much I fundamentally disagree with the common consensus while simultaneously understanding where those frustrations are coming from.I think this game is a painfully misunderstood gem that highlights an era and style of game design that we never see a lot of these days, now that every game is polished to a mirror sheen and asks so little of its players. It is precisely because of how much Gungrave G.O.R.E asks of its players that I feel the game is misunderstood. Because the game has a steep difficulty and an even steeper learning curve. But at the same time, it is the mastery of that learning curve and skill that makes the game so satisfying.Not only that, but it is a lost art to see a game that is designed solely in favor of a satisfying gameplay loop and takes a scorched earth approach to any of the bells and whistles we've all come to expect from modern action games. Gungrave G.O.R.E has no dazzling cinematic sequences or environmental storytelling. What you see is what you get, which is a solidly designed hybrid between a shooter and a character action game. And for what its worth, the designers of the game have gone through a lot of effort, both during development and after through patches, to ensure that the basic gameplay loop of shooting and maintaining high scores is as satisfying as it can be. Contrary to popular belief, the level design, enemy design and combat design is built to make those moment to moment gameplay decisions challenging and satisfying. Experienced players that can master the game's mechanics will find a rewarding experience in ways that many recent games have not been able to quite match up to. But despite my praise to the game's core design and skillfully implemented core mechanics, I cannot deny that there is a massive lack of consistency in the quality of the level-to-level, moment-to-moment design of the game. Some parts are amazing at testing your skill while simultaneously giving you a good time. Some parts just feel like they weren't play-tested in any capacity. Still, with recent patches, I see that Iggymob has done the best job they can to smooth out the rough edges of development and ensure that the player experience is as rewarding as could be. Knowing the development history of this game, I can't help but root for Iggymob at the end of the day. They made one of the most unique games released in the past year and a true love letter to this genre and era of game design, all the while struggling to set up shop in a place where its even more difficult to secure funding while at the same time working with a very niche IP. The fact that the game is as polished as it is compared to more expensive AAA releases really says something about their passion.And despite all the parts that weren't fun to play, I've still played Gungrave G.O.R.E many times over because the good of what they gave us I think far outshines the few moments where it perhaps took me more time than I'd like to in order to adapt to the more difficult and downright unfair sections.But that does come with the territory. At the end of the day, I'd rather have a game that's this satisfying on a sheer mechanical level that has a handful of frustrating levels or portions, than a game that is polished to a mirror sheen and has nothing unique to say or offer.So I leave my review with this. If everything you hear and see about Gungrave G.O.R.E sounds appalling, if you would be instantly turned off by a game with a simple and repetitive gameplay loop because it doesn't have enough variety to satisfy you, if the game's lack of budget for cinematic sequences makes you bored, and if a game with intense difficulty frustrates you; then yeah, Gungrave G.O.R.E is probably not for you. You should probably not buy the game.If you like a game full of soul however and you have a strong interest in this genre, then go ahead and give it a try. I promise that it will be quite rewarding.

_childDocuments_.review: Critiquing the critique.Saying that the game is something from a bygone era or PS2-like title is just lazy and uninspired. It's not a cinematic game filled with hubs & open world. It doesn't have any extra bloat like RPG elements or collectibles sprinkled around. You don't walk around aimlessly or explore. The whole framework of the gameplay and stages rely and are based on one thing, density. Gameplay density.It's an arcade game. You play for score, not for a story. You don't get a "break from the gameplay" during the stages, you fight tooth and nail all the way through. Just like in a SHMUP. Try playing the game like a SHMUP and it will click. Engage with the beat system, chain & link your combos, move around and utilize the space, don't hide behind corners or parry, you don't need to. The game will punish you for slugging around.Move, dodge, jump, shoot, keep that flame alive and most importantly, kick their ass.
