_childDocuments_.review: Gungrave G.O.R.E. is a exceptional traditional over the top arcade video action game, that captures the glory from the old days really well, yet remains very accessible to newcomers alike. It also comes with a massive soundtrack, that continuously delivers badass pumping beats. This game can be very stress releaving on a light difficulty mode.Its a triple A B game.(Eventhough i am not familiar with the roots of Gungrave, nor the previous games, nor the anime, this review is purely based on my experience with this installment.)A good thing to realise first, is that Gungrave G.O.R.E. is a traditional arcade video game, and traditional arcade games, can be very repetitive. And, well, so is this one.But nevertheless, it comes with the territory, yet to me, the repetitiveness is very well compensated by the great variety in level theme, and scenery design, the great use of the color palette, the badass soundtrack, the classic video game vibe, corny humor, and over the top badass special weapons / abillity's, with my personal favorite being the"Doom's Rain" ability :) This game really brings back that old school arcade cabinet atmosphere feeling, just like, when you would walk into a video arcade, back in the 80's / 90's. I personally just really love these games.This game can be a breath of fresh air, when you pick it up now and then, and can be very stress releaving. I found myself smiling on more then one occasion, while playing this game. I mean, don't you just wonder sometimes, how Grave can put all this mad, badass weaponry, into his coffin ? XDAlso, when you progress through the game, eventualy, there is also a bit of Max Payne flavour mixed into Gungrave. * Once you unlock Bunji ** But only a little bit of flavour though. ** Those who played the Max Payne series will recognise. *It might have some technical down sides for some, yes, there was some stuttering for me too in the beginning, when i first started playing this game, but they mostly fixed it eventually in my play through down the lane. And yes, the low res explosion animations, really can make you feel, like you where back in the 90's again. Yet i do believe, that people from back in the day, but also newcommers alike, yet also people with high and low end systems, might also be able to appreciate this game. (If you like the genre that is) Because, it will bring fun to the table. For me personally, this experience was a reminder about the days, when it was all about fun and gameplay, and games didn't took themselves all that seriously.It's a real good stress releaving classic arcade action video game, in an evolved form, with over the top madness, for oldschoolers and newcomers alike. So set your mind free, crank up the speakers, and enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Gungrave G.O.R.E. I love this game. I played Gungrave G.O.R.E for about 13 hours and I would like to speak about what I loved & what needs to be improved. Action games have been improving as generations passed by. Improving means actions games became better but at the same time more complicated and harder. In that sense, Gungrave G.O.R.E kept the fun that was there in the past. Less complicated and simple yet has this weird-ish attractiveness. I’d say I still comeback to it even though I am complaining at times.  So here goes my review.Pros:At first, I was like “What the F-!”. However, I found myself getting more and more immersed into the game. The game looked a janky but as I was beating the stages and equipped new skills, it got me thinking “What is this game? And I got to a point where I think the game is actually fun to play:” Here are my pros. #1. Nothing is stopping me. Nothing gets on my way and it destroys everything. It delivers that I am something special in-game very clearly. Maybe because we are fighting against drug cartel, there is no guilt trip by killing them all. Dual pistols don’t need to be reloaded. Bullet rain is the word. When I see the high numbers of enemies, I go “there are simply too many!” but I see myself getting rid of them all in no time. #2.Simple. You don’t have to think too much. Kill all if you see them. You can destroy objects as well and you are onto the next stage. Someone like me who doesn’t like when things are complicated, such a pleasure experience. #3. Cool looking character. Grave and Bunji are still cool. Silent Grave. Never seen a protagonist who doesn’t speak in modern games. I was expecting him to say something cool but nothing was there. However, Grave looks very unique and the design is cool so just looking at him shoot made Grave look cool #4.Playing time. Not too long, not too short. Maybe that is one of the reasons why I was so into the game. When a lot of enemies come out or when you face someone strong, you are so focused to a point you don’t even care about what’s around you. #5.Shield system really makes my palm sweaty.Very old yet classic method. You fight until the shield goes all the way down and when you destroy them all, you get excited by looking at the shield regenerating. That must be one of the attractiveness yet makes you complain at the same time? Cons:Studio said they inherited the pros of previous game but I can feel that cons were also inherited. I will write about the cons now. #1.Too loud. Too too loud. Shooting, exploding sound, and enemies’ sound effect are all mixed and very loud. I highly advise that you adjust the volume.  #2.Visuals were not so satisfactory. Comparing with likes of Call of Duty and God of War, they don’t look good at all. I mean we don’t even have to go there and compare since the visual quality isn’t really top notch anyway. Gungrave’s original version was not recognized by the visuals anyway so it is somewhat acceptable. #3. Crazy difficulty of some stages. The game is easy once you upgrade them but without upgrading your character, it will make you down. #4. Please add auto fire! Please!!I won’t explain further, you will know what I mean when you play the game. This game also pros and cons just like the other games but I find the game entertaining so I recommend playing this game. I am looking forward to the studio to patch the game to make the game better. I would like to see what studio Iggymob can do with their next move since they revived a title that was dead for a long time. It is hard to say this game is a good game for everyone but for those who don’t like overly complicated games or making you farm, this is a good game for action gamers who are like me.

_childDocuments_.review: Gungrave G.O.R.E is a game that doesn't pretend to be anything other than what it is...no side missions, pointless collectables, or secrets to be found here to pad out the content. You have but one simple objective, and that is to kill all the things. Its a relatively short experience, having clocked in just over 8 hours on my first playthrough, where 75% of the game was done in normal difficulty and the rest on easy because it becomes entirely too ret*rded in terms of difficulty to a point where you'd probably have to go back and grind previous levels just to keep up with wtf is happening, and I just cannot be bothered to do that. Aimbotting NPCs, one shot shield busting attacks, constantly getting f*cking fire and poison gas dropped on you, weak special abilities and entirely too expensive upgrades that even getting an A rank on most missions can't afford. You don't get any more or less of a reward for playing other difficulties either so you just make the game harder for no reason other than to make it hard, to which most of it is just artificial difficulty...I really so no way of been able to out skill all the bullsh*t that comes at you half the time.Its an insanely repetitive game, and that fact sinks in quite quickly after the initial buzz of "oh this is awesome!" just annihilating bad guys in waves. Forgettable and annoying cast of characters, recycled voice lines spammed constantly as you move between rooms, a really convoluted story that I guess you'd have to have played the PS games and/or watched the anime to know wtf they're all flapping on about most of the time.Eh...a good concept of a game that I initially thought would be like Devil May Cry, but ultimately very poorly executed and just a bit boring unfortunately.

_childDocuments_.review: Here's the thing. This is a game targeted at a very specific niche audience; that is, those that played Gungrave and Gungrave O.D.I was not one of those people until recently. I can't in good conscience recommend anyone ever pay $50 for this thing, but it goes on sale every now and then. I got it for $10, but honestly think I would be willing to pay about $20, and that's as someone with an appreciation for its goofy edginess. It's REALLY niche; it feels like the PS2 games, and it looks like a PS3 game. Do yourself a favor and turn on the cel-shading option. It's more tolerable that way.I heard it was quite buggy at release: I'm happy to say that I have encountered no show-stoppers so far. Worst issues so far are lame cutscenes, nonsense story, and dear LORD please hire a native English speaker to proofread your English text. It's giving me conniptions, I'd do it for free but I can't be bothered to try and mod another UE4 game.Also, they got an entire Japanese dub but they didn't dub the mobsters in anything other than Korean and (poor) English. They speak like five generic lines, was it really that difficult?Here's some suggestions if you decide to play:1. TURN OFF THE RADIO VOICE. She's horrible, no matter the language. You're welcome. Unfortunately nothing can be done about the obnoxious holographic objective markers. The game is one long hallway, why are these even a thing?2. Upgrade your bullet damage. Hard is going to be a nightmare without it. Honestly, maybe don't play Hard until you've already upgraded your stats... it's tedious and unfun as hell if you don't.3. Just for fun, take a shot every time the game loads a cutscene and it's just Grave walking silently. It's hilarious. On second thought, don't do that, you'll get cirrhosis.

_childDocuments_.review: disclaimer : my review is based on the game post patches, which is how i experienced it for the first time, i am well aware of the issues it had at launch but i do not plan to keep it included since they were not part of the experience i hadthat being said, WHAT A GAME ! it fixes a lot from Overdose and adds new quality to life to the series that just made the experience flow much better.mouse aiming meaning you can quick turn and better focus on more dangerous targets, being able to play the entire game as bunji, the game taking into consideration parts of the anime and the other games into account, there are many praises i can give to this game, but there are indeed issues still present.while the game is a improvement, the team is relativelly new with the series so there was some ground to be set, for example, they focused too much on their new OC quartz and my girl mika barely got much screen time, the cutscenes range from being some of the best in the market to amateurish dolls moving, i believe there was some budget thing going, as in they didn't had enough for all cutscenes so they only focused on the really HYPE ones.there were enough bugs here and there that bothered me forcing me to restart checkpoint and i can see those being a bigger problem on gore difficulty, because there are no checkpoints on gore difficulty.the game also isn't as tightly packed as the first game but i can't blame it much as i blame overdose, there is no way for gore to be as well paced as the original, the original is simple in its mechanics and it can be finished in 3 to 4 hours, meaning you finish the game before being tired of the mechanics, it would be unfair to expect the same from gore, since gore implements much more features and mechanics, that being said i still wish it had less stages, 31 is too much.still its much better than overdose, because overdose increases its lenght without changing much about the original, so its just long and really bad.i'm hopeful for what the team has to offer, because they proved capable of making a very good formula for the series and they seem to have just as much love for bunji as i do, tho they got so much hate since launch that they added a free dlc that is switch exclusive out of spite lol.

The core of the game is fun with honing in on the most dangerous targets, racking up combos and strategically deploying special skills. It is a shame then that the scoring system could use some tweaking. First of all it is difficult to tell if the amount of a measured metric tallied up at the end of the level you acquired enough of. Combo is one the components which is irritating to get right, to keep it going you have to be shooting either enemies or object in the environment. It takes a second of not shoot a correct object to lose it, losing it past the half way mark of the level means possibly losing out on a high score at the end of the level. This is annoying because the level design works not in your favour, levels are not always clear were to go next, the guidance from the game helps, but you have to be keeping a combo going at all times. Not all object are destructible which hinders your planning and routing thru the level, why couldn'tthe game geometry as bare bones as it is already be simplified in vein of God Hand to help with this?. A way to keep your combo going while being in a vunerable state as a trade-off would help a lot in this game.Overall there are other nitpicks, it is a fresh game in this gaming market, nowhere else you will find it, majority of it is janky, but you will enjoy it. A minus is the lackluster use of Gungrave IP which seems very bland in comparison to the manga, anime adaptation or even the 2002 game.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to say this game is pretty dumb, but you know what? It's fun. It's hard to die, with constantly recharging shields if you can avoid damage and super moves that give you back health equal to the meter spent PLUS initializing an uninterruptable shield regen PLUS executions for some guys. But when you stick it on hard mode, the constant hail of bullets and little choices like "Now I'm going to melee these dudes, now I'm going to kite this group to do a giant rocket launcher volley" feels good. You COULD let your shield regen between gaps in encounters, but that would break your chain, which means your max chain rank suffers at end of level. You COULD just rapid fire everything, but that affects your style rank because you don't get style points for standard shot kills... you need to burn rage meter to do that. And how do you move from encounter to encounter without breaking chain? You shoot scenery. You should be moving into the middle of a room, looking for the big glowing "Go here next" arrow in the middle of the gunfight, and slaughtering your way towards that so you don't have to let your numbers go down. So, it's simple and addictive because of the simplicity. Kinda like Burnout games, it's a whole lot of flash and style, mostly just playing to beat your score. For the 10 bucks I got it for in late September 2023, perfect. Would NOT buy at 50, but it sounds like the devs are listening to issues and correcting them, so that might be worth supporting them for more dollarbucks. I'll probably pick up the cosmetic DLCs just to throw another couple bucks at em, something I don't usually do. Issues: - Sometimes the hit detection is real spotty when manual aim comes into play. The laser beam is this crazy thin hurtbox and you'll spend more time trying to get it to adjust to clip something than it doing real damage. Hits like a truck if you sweep it across minions, but worthless for bosses. - Buttons have a weird feel to them sometimes. You tap RB to pull an enemy to you, including for executions, and hold it to dash and execute, but if they're on a ledge and you see the execution prompt, do the chain pull, it'll pull you to them instead... and if there's a bottomless pit, you just died. It's weird. - Other button weirdness. There's a lag to confirm in the menus, so if you try to exit, for example, there's this awkward moment where you're not sure if the button registered. Minor, not really a thing that comes up much until you're bailing on the game, but it's strange that it happens. - Character models are like old women in mocap suits. Can't really see it until you watch cutscenes, but it's kinda like upscaled Dreamcast fidelity, back when they were still figuring out basic gestures.

_childDocuments_.review: Played this on Game Pass and I pretty much stopped when I bought Bunji in the shop towards, like, the middle of the game. I couldn't get the DLC at the time since they were preorder bonuses but now they're available for purchase. Which is great! Because the Death Ronin and Overdose Grave skins are SO COOL. Anyway, the game is equally as good as it is flawed. Shooting feels really good and the Demolition attacks are EASILY the best part about the combat. However, there really isn't much of a story which is a bummer but given how this is meant to emulate the mindless arcade shooters of yore, I can learn to live with it. I can live with the voice acting as well. I actually think it weirdly enhances the experience to some degree,When I played the game last year, there were quite a few gameplay issues that have largely been fixed. However, I still think that while the level design is okay at the beginning, it takes a HUGE hit in quality further in the game. Enemies also had a habit of REALLY crowding around you later on in the game where the only means of escape is to throw out the most crowd control-y move you have, which I found jarring even a game like Gungrave. Enemies can get pretty frustrating overall but they have gotten balance changes since the launch build, which is great. Also, the grind for DNA can get very time consuming. Upgrades and characters can get pretty expensive and as a result, I ended up having to grind for a considerably long time. I will give credit where credit is due. Iggymob has certainly been listening to complaints and have been releasing patches, regardless of the state of this game.And on a related note! Bunji. Thank you, Iggymob, for letting us play as Bunji. :) But I have one thing to say about it. Bunji feels very limited compared to the LARGE amount of tools in Grave's moveset. Granted, Bunji doesn't necessarily have to be as expansive with his loadout as Grave but I was always confused as to why he had 3 demolition moves instead of 4. That's probably my only complaint and I love playing as him regardless. This game has come a long way since its rough launch and I'm glad that Iggymob is willing to fix the game. Especially since the announcement for this game is how I got into Gungrave in the first place. The game is very easy to jump into without any knowledge of the game but I wanted to play the older games anyway because I thought they looked cool. Do I recommend this one though? Yes, but with caution. If you want to pretend like its 2008 again and experience this game for its strengths and weaknesses, be my guest. Up to you if you want to wait for a sale or not, it's your money. But, if you want a game with more depth than "shoot-everything-in-your-wake-with-little-regard-for-your-health-bar,' then this is definitely not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell in raising Brandon from the dead for one more genocide, Iggymob did it with love. Even if they got some things horribly wrong.I would criticize the game's art style, but to even call it an art style would be way too generous. They haphazardly dumped a big bucket of unreal engine onto their game without a shred of artistic vision. It's clean, bright, colorful, and utterly flavorless. It's all such a far cry from the slick and gritty anime style of the first 2 games, design that was exaggerated yet meaningful, characters and locations that could stick in your mind. This game, conversely, slaps a bunch of color on the screen without actually trying to paint a picture. It's downright criminal.The sterilized gruel Gore puts in your face almost invalidates the game for me, but beneath the plastic veneer, the soul of the franchise can still be felt.The man is very much the same tank you piloted back on the Ps2, but he's never been more responsive or had so many dance moves. Melee is far less rigid, with new situational combo enders. You can only bring four demolition shots on each stage, but you can whip them out at the drop of a hat without navigating a menu. In action, Grave is the best he has ever been, even if he does look like a goony doll now.While Gore is kind enough to put extra shootables in between arenas so you can keep your beat count high, level design is largely a miss compared to the older games. There are occasional hints of thought and structure to enemy placement in Gore, but it all typically devolves into a mess of random technicolor idiots marching directly toward you. Thankfully, lining them up and ripping through them all with a single massive bullet is always a pleasure.Bunji is an unlockable character, and he's functionally a quicker but simpler Grave. The other playable character, Quartz, you get for just one level. She has such a melee-centric approach that I guess the devs just couldn't figure out how to implement her in the main campaign where enemies start shooting and they just never stop shooting. It's a shame they couldn't manage to deliver a wildly new style to tackle each stage in a brand new way.I feel the places Gore falls short isn't for lack of passion, but money and/or talent. In animating his crazy demolition shots, in trying to cap off each stage with a cool cutscene finish, in putting in so many different enemy types and factions and surprisingly decent music, there were definitely people involved in this revival who really wanted to be there even if the budget was tight. Though the cover definitely looks rough, I think their effort still shows in a charming way.Nowadays, it's refreshing to have a game that plays straight with stupid edgy fun without having to submerge it in irony.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a die-hard fan of the Gungrave series since it came out on Playstation 2, then absolutely.However, when it was initially released, there were some levels that were insanely difficult, even whenon easy. the hardest parts were the Train level, the last Vietnam level in which you played Quartz;a new female character in this game, and the final part of Turonty's HQ which requires you to re-enactthe laser corridor from Resident Evil 4, plus the third to last level of the game itself.Fortunately, since the 1.0 patch, Quartz's level was made easier, and even Grave has a toggle for his gunsso now he can fire in full-auto mode. However, to just to inform you all in advance, G.O.R.E difficulty isso hard that it has no checkpoint save function on each level...however, if you somehow manage to completethe game on G.O.R.E mode, you will be rewarded with the most OP skin for Grave with its own unique skillset in its arsenal...this skin, is Brandon Heat himself. when playing as Brandon, your normal shots breakenemy shields easily and his demolition shot set are so unique to him...it's as if you're reliving Brandon'sfight scenes from the Gungrave anime.Now, would I recommend it to gamers who are new to the Gungrave series? Honestly, I dunno.Unless you're a glutton to the amount of punishment Gungrave G.O.R.E deals, then be my guest.Update: If any of you are still playing Gungrave G.O.R.E, then have I got good news for you.Seems like some of the Switch-exclusive content such as Grave's street gear, as well as 2 new characters;RocketBilly Redcadillac & Harry McDowell have made it to Steam & other consoles. if that's the case,we'll most like get Quartz as a fully-playable character throughout the game as well Yensen the Boostmaster,just like in the Nintendo Switch version. _childDocuments_.review: Gungrave G.O.R.E lives up to its name, especially the G.O.R.E part. It's fun, challenging and a lot more complex than your average hack-and-slash action RPG.Do I ram into the enemy, focus fire on them, grab someone to use as meat shield or dodge and kite like crazy? Do I use rage mode to mow down the enemy or a demolition shot to recover HP? The game feels challenging right from the start. Your character, Beyond the Grave, can feel clunky, but that's his character, and he makes up for it with his diverse and powerful kit. Two stages so far have felt like a DPS check that required me to either save up demolition shots in advance or straight up lower the difficulty, but I've been loving this game so far.The graphics are ok, then lighting is great, the rendering is pretty intense and it's even got ray tracing - a much welcomed addition after the game got delayed since before real time ray tracing was a thing - but the environment has a low and noticeable polygon count and it's stuttered like 1-2 times every 1-2 stages, which is a lot less common than haters say. Disabling v-sync might have helped some.I'm writing this review early to offset some of the hate the game's received. Gungrave G.O.R.E is not a marvel of engineering, but it still stands out as one of the most fun and challenging games of its genre. As someone who didn't get to play the PS2 original and having watched the masterpiece anime adaptation, I'm enjoying this game, and love the style.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been a fan of the first two games and the anime. I have played multiple play through on those games as they have quite good re-playable value. I only play up to the train part and I really want to finish the game before writing the review but I want to do a preliminary review of what I feel thus far.Gameplay: it feels somewhat subpar, I really want to love it but it is not good for 2022 game. Combat system should be more fluid especially the way they throw in enemies at you. Melee is underwhelm but in the previous game it wasn't too bad as most of enemies use gun and it was GUNgrave afterall. While GORE has expand much more on the melee combat for Grave, it's not polish. The fluid between shooting and meleeing is not there at all. There's too many animation lag between swinging coffin and back to shooting. See that you can unlock more combos later but it strikes me a question that the animation lag decreases as the skill is increased in lvl. Demolition point feels cap out when you have max point and the gauge stops. The gauge should keeps filling like the old game and the extra point can use for something else like regen the shield or health. With how much enemies they throw at you, why can't Grave use Death Hauler as a shield? There are so many cool combos and transform of the Death Hauler into bunches of weapon but it can't block attacks?The train level is really annoying and it's hardly being called challenging. There's no balance in term of challenge, it's like the dev making it nearly impossible to beat and call challenge. It's like they tried to be Ninja Gaiden, Seikiro, and DMC hard but their combat and movement system is not great. Why trying to do platform and time sensitive challenge when the player can't even do combos and jump accurately. At least give the player an option to destroy the sign ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ through like what Grave would have done usually. He's not nimble and pretty much solve everything through destruction. Don't try to make him into Dante.I wish they would bring back the cinematic finish with cool music like the previous game. If I recalled, GGOD didn't do it neither but it was cool in the first game.Character design: I understand that this was done by Korean developer and you can tell by the art style. I don't really have problem with that but it feels like they have took out all the Nightow style from Gungrave. The "History" option to see the back story was nice but it was done so terribly where why bother? Like, it's better to just get the cutscene from the game and make it into little movies. It was already done in anime style and it was great! Though I like the costume design especially for Grave, it's throwback of the old one and mix with the new. I like it. I haven't seen all other character design but hopefully, I'll go back and get past that damn train and see all the other characters especially Bunji. Unfortunately, Juji and RB aren't in this game. It would be cool if they can be unlocked later or something.Music: In the previous game and anime, the music was done by Imahori Tsuneo. The style of the music was great and it was part of what makes it Gungrave. Gunlock Overdrive was used in the first two opening theme so why was it not in this one? I wish they would be a cinematic opening similar to the first two. Not having Tsuneo music feels let down as a fan.At beginning, I was going to leave positive review and not recommend to the non-GG fan. However, with everything I experience thus far, I feel that it might even make the fan feel let down like how I feel.PS: Where's my bloody pre-order bonus?!! I wanted to do a playthrough with OD outfit damnit.EDIT: I love how fast the patch and improvement is made and how the developer listen to community feedback. I changed the recommendation but leaving the original feedback.While I would love to have Tsuneo for music, the current music is great as well. I'm a fan of Monster Hunter and love music for that game too. I'm just biased toward original soundtrack from the old games.

_childDocuments_.review: In the first version of the game Gungrave G.O.R.E cemented itself as a worthy sequel to Overdose with level and boss design made to torture, infuriate and otherwise bring your patience to its edge with combat mechanics that, while they are distinct from its predecessors, brought a satisfying and fresh take on a formula that is not replicated in any of its contemporaries à la Devil May Cry, Bayonetta, etc. and this changed soon after with a couple of patches, in its current state I struggle to recommend this game anymore as they've removed essential components to its difficulty through rebalances of mechanics, area design and bosses that devalue the need of the mechanics they've iterated upon from Overdose and while patch 1.00 was the beginning of this feeling with a movement speed buff that allows you to outrun enemy bullets while shooting and the redesign of a few stages like the caves platforming section which now serves as an awkwardly paced intermediary section between kill rooms I still thought a lot of changes while ruining my own fun for the game were still a polished change to the experience that would allow it to be enjoyed by more people, but now we are on patch 1.01 where I truly feel they have killed the experience through a buff to Demolition Shot guage gain that makes it near impossible to die even on G.O.R.E difficulty, they also seemingly removed the generic enemies in condorbraves boss fight which I truly cannot fathom the need to do so as its the only thing that makes dodging his shots difficult I would've never first tried him on the previous patch and certainly not the first version of the game but now these and several other changes are making stages on the hardest difficulty barely something I have to pay attention to. I struggle to understand a lot of the other changes made as well such as 3 hit melee strings parrying rockets making death tornado a borderline useless attack and making the easier parry timing in this game feel completely unecessary, shield enemies having their shield health severely nerfed making them barely a consideration when fighting because you're likely to just break their shields regardless and even changes unrelated to balance like the weird camera angle change made during the executioners blood Demolition Shot.Overall they've stripped various aspects of the difficulty that felt carefully considered and well crafted to compensate for people that can't accept any form of jank in their video games, unfortunately the game is by nature janky so this is still in the game but without any of the difficulty that brings things together and you're left with a lack of challenge that makes many of the abilities in the game necessary and you're left with no depth to the games mechanics that while stylish in combination with the extensive length of the game I feel do not justify the purchase of G.O.R.E on their own.
_childDocuments_.name: Gungrave G.O.R.E

_childDocuments_.review:
In Gungrave G.O.R.E, play the gun-wielding badass anti-hero of your dreams as you mow down tons of enemies in a gory ballet of bullets and experience a story of vengeance, love and loyalty, all in a beautiful third-person action shooter, combining the best that Eastern and Western game design have to offer.

As the titular Gunslinger of Resurrection, you become the badass anti-hero of your dreams, an ultimate killing machine, brutalising your foes without mercy. Taking cover and retreating is not an option for Grave, he only ever goes full steam ahead, preferably right through his enemies.

Stylish third-person shooting meets close-range martial arts, creating seamlessly flowing action as you crush your enemies in a gory ballet of bullets. Utilise your unlimited ammo Cerberus pistols and your transformable EVO-coffin to unleash devastating combos in pursuit of maximum damage and style.

name: Centipede: Recharged
detailed_description: The original bug-blasting arcade game is back! Centipede: Recharged has been reimagined for modern gameplay, with vibrant visuals designed for modern screens, a 16:9 field of play, and an original soundtrack from award-winning video game composer Megan McDuffee. Aim for a high score in the old school arcade mode and earn bragging rights with your name at the top of the leaderboard. Or test your skills and rank on the boards in one of 30 intensely creative challenges, which twist the gameplay in new and exciting ways. A dozen new power-ups can give you an edge by introducing abilities like screen-clearing explosions, rail guns, and even slowing down time. Every mode and level is playable in local co-op mode with a friend. Key Features: Old Meets New: Classic Centipede gameplay updated for smooth control, and visuals for modern PCs and consoles Powered Up: A dozen power-ups are yours for the taking - scare enemies away, catch them off guard with a side-shot, drop a row of bombs, and more Challenge: Compete in a series of 30 challenges designed to put even the most seasoned players to the test Compete: Reach the top of country global leaderboards for arcade and individual challenge modes Bring a Friend: Play local co-op with a friend in every mode .. blast bugs and chase scores together Get in the Groove: Get into the rhythm of a good run to the original score by Megan McDuffee

Key Features: Old Meets New: Classic Centipede gameplay updated for smooth control, and visuals for modern PCs and consoles Powered Up: A dozen power-ups are yours for the taking - scare enemies away, catch them off guard with a side-shot, drop a row of bombs, and more Challenge: Compete in a series of 30 challenges designed to put even the most seasoned players to the test Compete: Reach the top of country global leaderboards for arcade and individual challenge modes Bring a Friend: Play local co-op with a friend in every mode .. blast bugs and chase scores together Get in the Groove: Get into the rhythm of a good run to the original score by Megan McDuffee

_childDocuments_.review: Let me preface this by saying that I love Centipede. I've been playing it for most of my life, and I've played it on a variety of platforms, both through emulations and ports. I've even played the original arcade game with the trackball (with a Millipede exterior, funnily enough). Needless to say, I know what I'm talking about when I say that Centipede: Recharged is a bit of a letdown.Now the most obvious thing you'll notice is the visuals, which have been altered from the original's raster graphics to look like vector graphics along the lines of other Atari arcade classics like Asteroids and Tempest, and while it looks stylish, the overall design looks better on paper than in actual gameplay. The game has been altered to take up the whole screen, which probably looks neater for a modern gamer raised on 16:9 games, but it means that the creatures have a lot more distance to travel, which hurts the speed and energy that make the original game so fun. Furthermore, a big part of the strategy is keeping an eye on the surroundings, and a larger playing field just makes it more of a pain, which isn't helped by the unnecessary (though thankfully optional, and not even default) option to zoom the screen onto the player.The redone sound also does more harm than good to the experience. In the original, Atari's proprietary POKEY sound chip, the same one used in their 8-bit computers and the infamous Atari 5200, is used to give the iconic sounds. Each of the enemies has a distinct sound, giving the player a cue to plan a strategy to deal with them. Recharged gives them more realistic sounds, which again, sound better in theory than in practice. The sounds are so subtle that I often barely notice when new enemies pop up. Making things worse is the generic, forgettable wavetable music, which often threaten to drown the sounds out.One thing I didn't mention in the original version of this review was that the shooting feels a bit slower than the original. Maybe it's just because of the larger playing field, but the Bug Blaster seems to fire more slowly than in the original, making it somewhat harder to time your moves unless you have a power-up.On that note, the addition of power-ups is a mixed bag. They can and do make the game a little more playable, but I consider them to be a bit of a gimmick; the original was fun without them. It's not like Arkanoid, where the power-ups added a genuinely enjoyable new layer to the gameplay. If anything, they wouldn't have been necessary if it weren't for the game's other flaws. It also doesn't help that the first time I shoot a spider in a given playthrough, the game momentarily freezes, though honestly that may just be down to my less-than-optimal computer setup.Another issue I have that I didn't previously mention was the removal of levels in the main arcade mode. The changing levels helped make the original more fun, as you had a sense of progression. In Recharged, I don't get that; for as long as I've played, everything seems to be the same difficulty.When I first wrote this review, the game was missing mouse control, which was a huge oversight in my opinion. Like I said at the beginning, the original arcade version used a trackball to control the Bug Blaster, and the resulting precise controls are a major part of what makes it so addicting. Admittedly, a lot of earlier ports had to port the game over without the ability to use a trackball, and the results, while usually still fun, do feel a bit more floaty than the original as a result, but in my experience, a mouse works just as well, if not better (then again, the vast majority of my experience with the game has been with a mouse, so I may be biased). Playing with a keyboard just doesn't cut it, and while an analog stick is more precise, it's just not the same. But the worst part is that playing with an Xbox or Xinput controller doesn't even work in my experience. I've gotten it to work perfectly literally once in my time playing, and every other time something goes wrong. When I turn on the game after turning off my computer, the game stops responding to the controller, even though it works with everything else. Unplugging and plugging it back in fixes the issue for the menus, but in the actual game, only the control stick works. The button that's supposed to fire does absolutely nothing, and I have to use the keyboard for firing. Of course, I did all of this before the addition of mouse support, so I imagine this has been fixed too, but honestly, I just don't have the motivation to test it out again, considering I can now play it using my preferred method.Back when I first reviewed this game, I was a lot more upset with the game due to the controls, but now they've been fixed, my opinion has definitely improved. At least now the game actually feels a bit more like the original. Still, considering the dull audio, questionable changes, and the poor intial launch, I'd be lying if I said I fully recommend it, not for $10 at least. Maybe it's my nostalgia and purist nature, but if given the choice between the original arcade classic and Recharged, I'd take the original in a heartbeat.I'm not familiar with the developer, Adamvision, but I've heard they've done great work elsewhere, and I do strongly commend them for their ability to address the more pressing complaints, especially regarding the controls. I'm certainly open to playing more of their product. It's just too bad that this game in particular didn't live up to my expectations. Still, at least now I can say it's playable, even if I do completely prefer the original, which is definitely a testament to the devs' dedication.

_childDocuments_.review: Centipede is my all-time favorite arcade game. I built my own arcade cabinet with a classic trackball just to play it. So once I found out about this game, I had to try it. I will admit, I was put off by the large amount of negative reviews, but the game is at a fair price, so I figured I would try it out, and I'm happy I did. First off, just to be clear, this game is NOT the classic Centipede from 1981 and the game clearly doesn't try to be. I think the problem the reviewers are having with this game is they are expecting the classic game, but doesn't make a lot of sense to me because the promotional images and footage make that clear. If you want the classic arcade, go play it, there are multiple avenues to do so. This game is not going to give you the same classic experience.What this game does do is take the original idea of the classic arcade and gives it a modern twist. This game is not at all meant to replace the 1981 classic, instead it tries something new, which is what fans of other popular franchises often beg for. So, I don't understand why people are punishing this game for trying something new. The new ideas this game presents gives the original classic a fresh twist for players to try to master, and I applaud them for doing that.It took me a while to get used to the game, to be honest. I didn't know how I felt about it a first, but once I understand the true premise of the game, I started to get hooked. I was a little unwelcoming of the power-ups, but with so much going on at once on the larger playing field, you'll come to find that the power-ups are pretty essential. The other strategies used in the classic still work here but just on a larger scale, such as trying to keep your playing area clean, trying to manipulate the centipede for quick points, and reducing the poisonous mushrooms when you have an opportunity.The co-op mode is probably the best this game has to offer. This mode had us playing over and over again, and saying “one more” many more times than we should.The only issue I have with the game is the distracting visuals. That is certainly unnecessary and the only complaint I have. Sometimes I died because I couldn’t even tell there was something about to run into me. I wish I could turn them off. This becomes even more annoying when you are shooting down the centipede from the head up. You can’t tell if you are about it collide with it because the explosion animation completely covers what you're hitting.  Overall, an awesome experience and if you're willing to try out a new take of an old classic arcade, this might be worth a shot. No quarters necessary.

_childDocuments_.review: REVIEW #55Centipede: Recharged----------This was my first taste of Atari's recent "Recharged" series, and I'm pretty impressed by what's offered here. Atari has had a bad reputation in the past when it comes to remakes of their most popular classics, and Centipede has been among of the victims of Atari's remake meat grinder once or twice. However, Adamvision and Sneaky Box did a really good job at updating it in a way that feels new but still maintains the structure of the classic gameplay, resulting in a game that feels like a unique yet fun experience.For those unfamiliar with the classic, Centipede is a top-down shooter with the player being able to move around a large portion of the playfield's bottom half. At the top, various bugs and insects will begin to invade the play area while spiders will approach from the sides. Being a classic arcade game, the goal is simply to get the highest score that you can.Centipede: Recharged updates this formula in a couple of different ways, one of which is the addition of weapon power-ups. While this could easily end up being a gimmicky trope, the power-ups offered here are well-balanced and satisfying to use. There's 3 different variations of game play, each with its own unique leaderboard. Challenge stages and local co-op are also available, rounding out this rather robust package of a classic game remake.There really isn't anything bad to say about this title. Graphics and sound are great, music is pleasant and appropriate, controls are well-designed, and I've yet to encounter a technical issue. I will say that action can build up and get so frantic that it's easy to lose track of adversaries getting close to your position, resulting in a sudden "Game Over". However, I blame that more on my attention span than the game.NOTE: Co-op was not evaluated for this review.

Classic, while probably the weakest of the bunch, (I'll get to why later) still gives you a relatively pure Centipede experience. Recharged Classic is just recharged with 3 lives which makes it  a longer experience, perfect for when you're just looking to see a high number when you die. Challenge mode is for when you get bored of the other three modes and you want to try out masochism. Now it's time for me to complain about Classic Mode. I like it, but I wish that it lived up to its name better. It's not level based like the original, so it feels more overwhelming, which I'm not opposed to, but with the name Classic, I kind of expected just the original Centipede but with upgraded graphics, but no. I do think the Classic mode that we have has value, but I kind of wish that we also had the original with updated graphics, or heck, even just an emulation of the original arcade version. _childDocuments_.review: So some mobile devs saw  and said, hey, we've seen that "vaporwave" art the kids love, and Atari doesn't care what happens to their IPs nowadays, so let's churn out a knockoff! Whereas  &  iterated on and blew up the original's gameplay in supremely satisfying ways, though,  didn't really care about that "gameplay" thing and as such broke the original in several ways.  Namely: a) The playfield is way larger than the original, yet your shots have been slowed and take too long to travel the playfield to control the increased enemy hordes.  b) Aiming is  persnickety, and shots have to be pinpoint accurate to hit  -  good luck with that, given that one of the few ways this game is faithful to the original is the trackball mechanics and the attendant slipslidy movement (analog stick only here; sorry, no d-pad).  c) The mushrooms take more hits to kill and are  to get rid of given the slower shot speed and tiny hitboxes, leading to numerous scenarios where I am unloading and unloading into a centipede that's  of my face and not hitting it, because the first segment I hit turned into the Masada of mushrooms, the Krak des Chevaliers of mushrooms.  d) The playfield never clears out the garbage that accumulates, and the devs like to spawn scorpions every five seconds that spawn adamantium poison mushrooms that you're not able to hit reliably over the super-wide playfield.  Hey, everyone's favorite part of  is when all the enemies are bunched up on the bottom third of the screen, right?  That's what everyone loves.You do get power-ups  -  you pretty much  to be running a power-up constantly to survive  -  but they're not as fun or satisfying as, say, the screen-sweeping laser beams or giant ghost-squashing Pac-Men of .  By far the most useful are the explosive bullets, since their AoE nullifies the aiming/tiny hitbox problems and will help get rid of the 256,000 poison mushrooms littering your screen 60 seconds in.  Ditto the spread gun, though the smaller 3-shot variant still tends to miss a lot.  The railgun is useless.  Side cannons have potential but can't hit due to the aiming.  Rapid fire actually should have been default shot speed  -  see, that's the thing with these "'70s arcade games reimagined" projects: you have to go bigger & bolder, on both the enemy side  the player's.  You can't leave the player less equipped to deal with things than they were in the original. Also: the fun sound effects and changing palettes of the original are completely absent.  WTF?I used "mobile" at the top as shorthand for "cheap and thoughtless," but  really is designed for mobile sensibilities  -  given the length of the average game and content available, you're really not expected to be spending more than an hour & change on this.  I'll probably continue to screw around with , because I love  and will continue trying futilely to get mileage out of this broke-ass version and am fundamentally stupid.  Those smarter should just get  and hit up the rock-solid originals instead. Yeah, came to my senses and asked for a refund.  Every death is cheap.  This game just really frustrates attempts to have fun with it.

Baseball? sure. Games with a ball that you control? absolutely.but not for centipede. I always liked it more on Regular Atari.I digress. A few distinctions to be made, here.1 - this IS NOT OG centipede2 -the game is not gona reward you for letting the scorpions freeze the shrooms...bc it's not OG centipede.3- Fleas are a plague of the gods, sent upon you to kill your smile4 - powerups are fun, but eventually.. you start to rely on them, and you will find yourself watchign for ants ( or are they spiders? ) every chance you get. It's a neccesary addiction; however, as you cannot keep up with a 16:9 fiels using the regualr gun.suggesiton - the regualr gun mechanic deosnt work here, bc we are playing on 3 boards ( size-wise ) at once. This does not work for the OG gun.You have taken elements from this OG, and then changed them in a good way - but left weird bits in that are counter-intuitive to thenewer gameplay.you move TOO fast, but shoot VERY slow - even if you dont miss, that long board means you arent gettign to shoot another bullet for longer than you expect.( centipede makes you shoot one bullet at a time, until it hits somehting, as soon as it hits somehting - you can immedittely fire again. this means when close, you can hold fire, and have a rapid shot )I do enjoy this, so far. it's just frustrating that the game is almost unwinnable after you hit50k points ( it gets hairy at 30k, and the double flea swarm at 40 is nigh unbearable) pray to the RNGesus that you get a solid powerup, make sure to wall in the bottom half, so you have room to breathe - and always- ALWAYS - remove clutter on your side of the board any chance you get.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Centipede: Recharged is a genuine remake/remaster of the original arcade shooter, Centipede.  The graphics got a minor update, switching to neon style 2D vector art instead of the old pixelcrap (in fairness, pixels were the best the computers at the time were capable of, but no excuses today).  The big plus here is mouse control, giving you a way smoother and more responsive capability.  So another reason indie devs who fail to take advantage of PC hardware have no excuses. Anyway this is still a very shallow arcade game by today's standards (we've got games like Baldur's Gate 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 to compare this to), and the pricing is just an insult to fans of arcade games and modern PC gamers alike. On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.The poor quality of this game is reflected by how many people spent time with it.  At the time of this review, SteamDB shows the all-time peak player number was only 7 players.  This is a remarkably low number, and now, the only player activity occurs once or twice a month, presumably someone loading it up to see what it is then quickly uninstalling it.  Considering there's over 120 million gamers on Steam and well over 50,000 games for gamers to choose from, the overwhelming lack of interest in this low quality game is to be expected.Centipede: Recharged has the utterly unrealistic price of around $9 USD, it's not worth it given you can play Centipede and it's many clones for free on the web, especially considering the sheer number of completely free, much higher quality games on Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Fun!  I remember pumping quarters into the original Centipede game in the arcade as a kid, so this takes me back.  I like how the game gives you the option of playing the "classic" or "recharged" version of the game.  I like the various power-ups that the spiders drop.  This game is a really fun time-waster.  Totally worth purchasing.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: "Centipede: Recharged" is a neon-infused nostalgia trip that takes the classic bug-squishing action and cranks it up to eleven. Armed with a laser cannon, you blast through waves of centipedes and other creepy-crawlies in a dazzling, chaotic rave of color and sound.The gameplay is addictive and frantic, with power-ups dropping like candy from a piñata. Whether you're slowing down time or unleashing a spread shot, each power-up makes you feel like an insect-squashing demigod. The pulsating 80s synthwave soundtrack keeps your adrenaline pumping, and the zaps and booms of your laser are music to your ears.While the action can get overwhelmingly hectic, leading to moments of bewildered frustration, it's all part of the fun. "Centipede: Recharged" is a delightful, high-energy romp that will keep you glued to your screen and questioning your sanity. Happy hunting!Note:Overall my experience playing the game was good... but I did have some issues playing it on my SteamDeck.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game. addictive and classic yet updated.My only problem is that controllers don't work. I even have the Atari VCS Wireless Classic Joystick and it doesn't work. Not sure if i'm doing anything wrong but Missile Command was plug & play and works fine. sucks because I specifically got that controller for the recharged games.Other than that, the game is very fun. it could just be an issue for me and my computer. I have Windows 11 so maybe that's what it is? If anyone has run into this issue and got it working, please let me know. I can't seem to find anything on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I'd say this game is good, love the missions mode, all the huge amount of power ups, and this game has the best soundtrack of all the Recharged games I think the soundtrack is a highlight of this game, my biggest issue by far is the sound design, to me the reason why Centipede was such a classic was the iconic sounds the Spiders, Centipedes, your bullets, and the sound you make when you earn another life, another big flaw in this game is it doesn't feel as frantic as the arcade classic, my last issue which I don't consider but I wish the game had an artstyle more like Gravitar Recharged because the original had a pastel look which would have greatly benefited this particular title.A nice bonus would be if we had the gun autofire or at least the option for it, other than that this is a good title if you can snatch it for like 5 dollars
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Very good Centipede game, includes Original, Original Recharged, Recharged (MODES)   + SOLO or Co-Op shared screen.All are in the new graphics style though, so 1 life only in the Recharged (MAIN) game, same as all the new Atari releases around this time.New variants have modifiers drop when you kill those spiders that appear in your space, and then they have a timer bar at the bottom, too good to let you have always.Yes, it has audio controls and full screen and not.Rig of 5600X/RX6800 stays at 144FPS at 1440p for me in actual gameplay.Works great with mouse that was all I cared about!In summary:Recharged means, new graphics, enhanced game mechanics, and 1 life to live!Original is new graphics, original 3 lives old shool arcade game rules, no enhancements.Original Recharged is just Recharged above with 3 lives instead of 1.Leaderboards exist, world/friends only/local.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of retro games especially arcade game, so I thought a first it was going to be boring, but this I discover it a very fun game for any type of gamers and what got me interest is there's challenge mode and it had co-op, but local only there's no online co-op which they should have added to the game, but to be honest I like it and I recommend getting this game, but I also suggest you wait until it goes on sale because it can be a bit pricey.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: I liked Centipede back in the day, but it's been about a decade since I've played it and I decided not to play the original first before playing this because I didn't want it to sway my opinion. This game should be able to stand on its own and shouldn't necessarily be judged on how perfectly it recreates the old game.So anyway, I liked it. It has the same addictive gameplay as the original with updated visuals and sounds, which I think is the big thing holding back a lot of retro games from being loved by modern players--they're addictive to play, but look and sound too primitive.Some things I didn't like about it:You can switch between keyboard controls and mouse controls. I found the mouse controls to be better, but I wanted to use the arrow keys to move (not WASD) and it didn't appear as though I could map them myself. The 16x9 screen is an obvious choice for a game coming out in 2021, but it also slows down the pacing of the game because the centipedes have more space to get through. Maybe they should have sped them up or kept the thinner aspect ratio and filled the screen with other stuff.Those were minor annoyances though. I really just started playing and I'm excited to jump back in!
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like it.  Despite mouse and trackball support being added according to the DEVS the mouse doesn't work. No matter what settings I tweek I can't get the mouse to work except in the main menu area.I'm stuck playing with W, A, S, D and space bar.  I want my money back, lol.UPDATE:  The Dev recently hit me up and asked me to have another look at the game.   I did and they've fixed the mouse controls completely. I work from home and need a distraction that's quick and easy to play or put down. This is it.  Thanks Adamvision!
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Great sounds, crisp visuals, and addictive play. Exactly what you want out of a remake. You have all the feeling of an arcade cabinet (for us olds that used them) while having a fully modern SHMUP experience. The power-ups keep it interesting as it leads to different and more complex strategies. I am very addicted to the challenges as they really stretch your comfort with the game play and keep it fresh when you have a rough arcade run. It has probably been a decade since a not-RPG got me to rack up this many hours in a game so quickly. The added mouse support works really well and I appreciate the varied input options in general since it allows more people to play. Excited to see what else we will get out of the Atari Recharged series if this is our first taste.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, this was my favorite game in arcades and on my Atari growing up, so I am STOKED that it has been remade.  This version takes what is an amazing retro game and puts a "modern" feel to it, and I love it.  The mechanics are great and I love the different challenge modes it has too.  The music is also quite enjoyable to listen to, which is an amazing addition.  I have been putting timers up every time I play so that I don't just play it endlessly.  I can't wait for more games from this same group to be released.  I also love that you can reach out to the developer (Adamvision Studios) when you have issues and they get resolved quickly and without push-back.  It's always nice to have a developer that is so devoted to making sure their game(s) is working properly. 10/10 DO recommend for anyone that loves score chasing games.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: a Fun and Challenging throwback to the arcade days of Centipede in Pizza shops, arcades, skating rinks and bowling alleys.  the new challenges and powerups add a lot more to the game and the randomized powerup drops definitely can make the game more fun (or frustrating) the leaderboards also provide a good method of competing with your friends and random players worldwide.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: I find it so hard to understand why this game has so many negative reviews. I personally am loving it, I like the Modernised gameplay with the brutal push as far as you can go. I did originally experience issues with the controller, as described by other reviews, but then I remembered that this is steam and tried it in big picture mode (it was fine).
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more like Pac-Man DX Championship Edition with the retro neon look and gameplay changes that rewards completing challanges than playing long for a high score, so be warned if you're expecting this to be like the arcade original (it's not).It's decent to play but not as great as Tempest 4000, but for $10 I won't complain.  You only get one life so you must master the powerups obtained from the spider, especially when you quickly get swarmed by poisoned centipedes.If you like challanges and getting achivements then get this version, any purists who wants the original arcade gameplay would be better off playing the arcade version off Atari Vault which plays way faster.BTW... They finally added mouse support, but you have to enable it in the Settings menu AND unplug your gamepad.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Another fun game. I think I enjoyed the Recharged version of Missile Command just a little bit more, but this is still good. There's the expected arcade mode, and also a challenge mode with various tasks to complete (get X points, destroy X mushrooms, etc.). It also has local co-op.Overall, I enjoyed this and am looking forward to Black Widow: Recharged. I would love to see VR versions of this line of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

_childDocuments_.review: Initiate insect extermination in this widescreen glow-up of one of the greatest arcade games of all time. The rules are the same as 1981: shoot the centipedes as they descend the playing field, and contend around the shot-blocking and path-altering mushrooms they leave behind. New to Centipede: Recharged are power-ups dropped by the spiders, such as explosive bullets, spread shots, and a devastating railgun. Fight for high scores in Arcade mode either solo or with a new simultaneous couch co-op feature. Tackle more than two dozen challenges that test bug-shooting prowess and introduce clever uses for the new powerups, with additional challenges exclusive to the Atari VCS. Take it to the next level with global leaderboards for the best records in the world, and earn more than 15 achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Centipede: Recharged

Explore the abyss!

Earth, 3024.

Natural resources are scarce and the survival of the human race is in danger. Desperate to find new energy resources, the ASAN creates a biomechanical robot called Nep2no that is capable of withstanding extreme depths in the hope of finding new energy sources. After many years of exploration, a new energy source is found, code named "Gaia".

Your mission will be to find the "Gaia" energy stones by exploring the depths. To do so, you must control Nep2no by counteracting gravity and the surrounding darkness with the aid of a Light that will go out little by little.

name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery
detailed_description: Feature List • Paint, sketch, and retouch your artwork to complete your masterpiece and your memories • Dive into and explore beautiful panoramic, hand-animated worlds inspired by Miyazaki/Studio Ghibli visuals • Experience an evocative story, through the eyes of a passionate artist • Step into a new painter’s artistic adventure - awaiting those who complete the main story About the Game Behind the Frame is a vivid, interactive fiction about an aspiring artist on the cusp of finishing the final piece of her gallery submission. A relaxing, eloquent experience that can be played at any pace. Become immersed in a panoramic world filled with resplendent colors, beautiful hand-animated visuals, and a smooth, easy-listening soundtrack. As a passionate artist, seek the missing colors that will bring your paintings to life - all while remembering to take the occasional coffee and breakfast breaks that keep you going. There is more than what meets the eye, for every painting has a story to tell.
