The puzzles are just challenging enough to keep it interesting, but never so hard that you feel stuck. The music and pacing of the story are very 'cozy' and I would recommend taking in the beautiful art and atmosphere rather than rushing to the end. That being said, there's about 1 hour of content, so you'll definitely finish in one sitting.Ultimately, I recommend the game if you're looking for something cozy to unwind AND if you can find it on sale. I do regret buying this at full prize, because it's simply quite short and I don't think I will run it again anytime soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This fun game is about helping an artist complete her masterpiece. You start your day by making breakfast, having coffee, and listening to music. The game's title, "Behind the Frame," made me think about hidden things in life and art, which turned out to be true as the game unfolded and showed a personal story about memories and lost love.I enjoyed playing this game by myself and with my daughter; she loves it too. It even inspired her to ask for the same breakfast as in the game – eggs and bread!I hope there's a sequel with more puzzles and a longer story, maybe with the option to change the music. This game is great for the whole family because it's lovely, easy to play, and appeals to everyone.The only downsides are that it's a bit short, and you can only do painting in the game. It would be nice to have more things to do and the option to change the music while you play.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very cute game, although bittersweet in a way. Its kinda of a point and click, but the artwork is so pretty that honestly, I played it a second time just because of that. Couldnt get all the acheivements tho... which is kinda frustrating but it is what it is. I would recommend this if you're just feeling for a little game that plays well in one sitting.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really emotional, touching sort of game. It felt like a short movie of sorts, interactive but mostly focused on depicting a story. However in this format the story is told by you interacting with the setting and characters. I think it works very well, and while the experience itself is very short, I enjoyed myself.I knew going in the sort of experience I'd be getting, and while I normally prefer games that give a bit more quantity in playtime...the game looked great, and I'd say it was made up for by quality. The storytelling is phenomenal, the scenes and animations look, as many others have said, very much like a Studio Ghibli quality; extremely high, detailed, and evoking emotions with their minute details.I loved this game, and would highly recommend going in as blind as possible to the details of the story for the best experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: An interesting take on an artistic storyline. Very unique, but very short as well. However it was beautiful. Nice looking ghibli animations. _childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: As a lover of immersive storytelling and captivating visuals, I recently had the pleasure of experiencing "Behind the Frame," and let me just say, it's an absolute gem in the world of indie gaming.From the moment I delved into the enchanting world crafted by the talented team at Silver Lining Studio, I was spellbound. The game effortlessly weaves together a touching narrative with stunning hand-painted visuals, creating an experience that feels like stepping into a living, breathing work of art.At its core, "Behind the Frame" is a story about creativity, passion, and the beauty of human connection. Through the eyes of a budding artist, players embark on a journey of self-discovery as they navigate the complexities of life, love, and art. Along the way, they'll encounter charming characters, each with their own unique stories to share, adding depth and richness to the world.What truly sets "Behind the Frame" apart is its innovative gameplay mechanics. The clever use of perspective puzzles adds an extra layer of immersion, allowing players to interact with the environment in creative ways that feel both intuitive and satisfying. Whether it's rearranging objects in a cluttered studio or piecing together a forgotten memory, every puzzle feels like a natural extension of the narrative, seamlessly blending gameplay and storytelling into a cohesive whole.Of course, none of this would be possible without the game's breathtaking visuals and enchanting soundtrack. From the vibrant streets of the city to the tranquil solitude of the artist's studio, every scene is rendered with meticulous attention to detail, inviting players to lose themselves in a world of color and imagination. And the hauntingly beautiful score, composed by the talented team at Triodust, serves as the perfect accompaniment to the journey, evoking a wide range of emotions from joy to melancholy.In the end, "Behind the Frame" isn't just a game – it's an experience. It's a reminder that sometimes, the most profound moments in life can be found in the simplest of pleasures: a brushstroke on a canvas, a shared laugh with a friend, or a fleeting moment of inspiration. So if you're looking for a game that will touch your heart, stimulate your mind, and leave you with a newfound appreciation for the beauty of the world around you, look no further than "Behind the Frame." It's a true work of art in every sense of the word.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: The game lasts only two hours, but how much this intense playing time remains in the heart. A touching story about drawing pictures, feelings, the importance of the moment and the importance of a cat. Perhaps due to its compact duration, or maybe due to the skill of the scriptwriters, the game does not out of tune in any of its notes, concentrating on pure emotion. It turns out that for a beautiful ending, you don't need someone to die from an incurable disease, you don't need fanfare and applause, just a quiet look at the paintings and brushes with the name is enough. The gameplay includes interacting with the paintings and solving puzzles (even if there are not so many of them as we would like) with wonderful unforgettable music.The work of the designers is phenomenal, the visual in the game is so juicy that you want to bite off a piece of it, that's it. so smoothly and in detail, it is pleasant to look at what is happening. This is the case when quality is much more important than quantity, and the fantastic journey that this game gives you will be remembered for a very long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I can tell, the game has a nice atmosphere, even if it felt a bit off pretty quickly, with puzzles just being there. If you're still interested, perhaps try out the demo and see if you encounter the same problem.TL;DR: Seems like a nice game, doesn't work due to technical bugs. _childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a calm, relaxing game with lovely music, this is it. _childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Big disappointment :(    (spoilers ahead /!\)I was so excited to play this game due to super positive reviews and the fact that I love indie games of this kind; however the game didn't live up to my expectations. If it was a bad game without any "soul" or talent behind, I would'nt have written this comment. The animation and the drawings are amazing, and it shows that the team was really into this project, and that's why I am upset. They missed an incredible opportunity of creating a short film; there's not really a gameplay and the puzzles are too easy, even a young child can do it. I know, the point is to feel and discover the story, but the clues (to the story not the puzzles) are given so easely I knew what happend since the begining of chapter 2. My point is that it doesn't really feel like a game, more like (as I said) a short film, and the gameplay could have been more interesting with harder puzzlesSpoilers for the story here !!:The saddest thing here is the story: it hint since the begining that the 2 characters knew each other and had some kind of a relationship (confirmed at the end or just in the whole game) and Amber (the protagonist) doesn't remember any of it; the supposed husband is an old man that ignores or doesn't seem to see Amber. All of it can make us come to the conclusion that Amber is dead and her ghost couldn't move past that (or something like that). Furthermore, in the 5th chapter, it looks like the reality around Amber begin to shift and she appears to be in a sort a purgatory to confront what happend with her past/husband/New york exhibition and her (logicaly) death. But no, it just confirms that yeah, her husband is/was/will be (????) the neighbor and she sees her old self in front of her husband exhibition and the credits are rolling. So many questions unanswered : why can't the dude see her? why is she seeing her past/future/present (I don't even know) and hallucinate paintings? Why doesn't she remember anything ?? I know some stories need/can let some things in the vague, and let people think about it, but not the main plot that the game wants us to know ?? I really don't know the story of the game, not because I didn't discovered some secret info, but because the game teased us a story that doesn't really have an end. If I missed some critical notes (it doesn't seem like the case) my bad but the key point of a video game story shouldn't be in a missable note !!! But I will give credit when credit is due: as I said, the drawings are amazing; it seems straight up from a ghibli movie, the colors are vibrant, the environnement is breathtaking and the musique is just so immersive. I loved the passage in the 5th chapter where you go into the frame and stand in the painting; for exemple in the purple field. And that's why I am so disappointed: there is SO MUCH wasted potential; so many good ideas that were not developped, a story that isn't well explained (and sometime it's to much explained as the main character insist on "oh I wonder who put that here" or "oh who is in that painting ?" whereas it's litteraly her) and certain cool gameplay mecanics that appears in the first chapter then dip in the others. In my opinion, this is a problem of platform: this story wasn't really made for a video game; it would have work perfectly in a short animation film, it really would have been a masterpiece. If you wanna buy this game, or you bought it and loved it, there is absolutly no problem, it's just my personnal opinion. Another thing : 1 hour of """""gameplay""""" for 9$ with a story that could have been explained in 5minutes isn't really something that I like. The team did an incredible job (no hate for them of course), just some mistakes that ruined the experience for me; I still liked the game, just think it was really disappointing for every price awarded and the reviews saying this is the most incredible indie game ever made. I hope this review helped in someways !notes => sorry if there is some mistakes, I am not a native english speaker

_childDocuments_.review: First time EVER when I cry while playing a game.It literally torn me inside - there ware maybe worse things happening in real live that would make any grown man cry - but for me this game was more heartbreaking than anything, I was crying so bad that the wife came to ask me what happened.Maybe it made me feel this way because I never felt/lost true love like Jack felt? _childDocuments_.review: It looks good and it's evocative, However, it's also short (less than an hour) and pretentious. _childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenary is a visual novel about two people who bond over sharing a love of art. You play as the painter Amber, though there is also a section where you get to play as Jack, and you learn their story of how they met, their friendship and what led them to part ways. You collect colors along the way that you use to complete each painting. While doing so, you are rewarded with more clues as to what happened between the relationship of Amber and Jack. The soundtrack will make you feel very relaxed too and everything is lyrical and poetic about the tone of the game. There will be many puzzles involved where you can take everything at your own pace to figure out where you need to go next. It doesn't feel frustrating because the music that is playing is always calm and will accompany you with a relaxing puzzle-solving experience.The visuals are breathtaking and beautiful and if you are someone who is into that, character narrative and interpersonal relationships between characters and you are also a fan of arts, then this game is definitely one for you ^^

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to put a thumb up for the art, but seeing as this "game" only has overwhelming positive reviews, I feel compelled to put it down. This is not a game. This is a "ghibli styled", slice of life anime story where you are asked to participate, in a very pointless way, to have the tape advance. Yes the art is beautiful... make animes then, if this is what you're good at, but presenting this as a game is just wrong!- The puzzling is extremely basic and repetitive.- The gameplay with the brush a catastrophe unless you play with touchpad (don't know if it is made for it). - The complete dual storyline took me 1.7h to finish.- Repetitive actions to symbolize the routine (in a less than 2h game lengh, excuse me??? You actually dare to ask people to repeate the same thing 4 times?) - lazy writing- Yet another life/love/death story without any fantasy nor imagination- An absolute mental jerk-off from a taiwanese (not japanese this time) studio, who think that they are just sooooo romantic!! NOT...This left a really bitter taste in my mouth, despite really trying to focus on the good here.- Now things are not all terrible. As said, the art is spot on. Guys, please just make animes!! Please please please.- The main story conclusion is a nice twist- Got my eyes watery- Very, very cute slice of lifeThat's it.Now, you know why after reading "Best overall game", "Best mobile game", "Best game direction"... blabla bluhhhhh I just CANNOT put a thumb up! Thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: As an artist and graphics design student myself, this game calls to me in so many ways. We play as a girl who is trying to get to New York and share her graphic skills. She also tries hard to get in touch with her neighbor, who is also an artist. We spend the entirety of the game creating very lovely art pieces and sketching what we see. The story and the art are very reminiscent of Studio Ghibli (and I would personally love to see it turned into an animated film). The music is simply fantastic. Some of the puzzles confused the heck out of me, but I think I was mostly just getting ahead of myself. I would love to see more from this dev,

_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game. The art throughout is incredible and an absolute joy to look at. The story was also quite intriguing. It is revealed over the course of a few short chapters. In each chapter, we step into the role of the young artist and after completing some simple tasks, solving matching puzzles, and finishing paintings, a nostalgic episode plays out that connects the artwork from the chapter to the character's life. I'm not sure I understood all the parts of the story, but even though the details are left a little fuzzy, the emotions are really well conveyed. Overall, I enjoyed playing the game and spending some time its little world.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I love the art and animation!!It gives off a Studio Ghibli movie vibes like "Only Yesterday". _childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Like the game said, "There is more than what meets the eye, for every painting has a story to tell." And I didn't expect the story would be that wonderful and touched my heart. This game is an absolute must-play. The art, puzzles, interactions, and story are all truly amazing and detailed. Painting isn't just about art, but there is story/meaning behind it.The main story is divided into chapters and once player finished it, a bonus story unlocked. _childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Aww. This was lovely. Solid animation, comforting music, fluid gameplay, and puzzles that aren't much more than "match the colors." The story is simple, heartwarming, and a bit sad. The "mystery" is pretty obvious, but the whole story didn't click until the very end, which was nice. _childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: Really beautiful and aesthetic game, my only gripe is that the game is kinda short. _childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: “Behind the Frame” is a cute and very relaxing art game. You dabble a lot with painting pictures, have to solve some easy puzzles and follow the story of two talented painters with their unfulfilled love-story. This is a good-natured game that left me with an overall feeling of pleasant warmth. The weaker points of “Behind the Frame” are some repetitive game elements in the first chapters (you have to prepare breakfast and coffee three times in exactly the same way) and I feel the price is a bit steep for a game that I could finish twice and get all the achievements within 4,6 hours. So if it is on sale and you like this type of game you should go for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: When i picked this game for the fact that it looked chill to play, i was not expecting the amount of quality that was put into this. The game is a simple point and click game, not alot of difficult puzzles since it felt like it just flowed easily into place for the most part. The story tells a tale of a up and coming painter whos looking to get known in the world, painting masterpieces, all the while keeping an eye on her neighbor who has his own story mixed in that the painter will soon come to realise. The animations in the game was breathtaking, i was not expecting it to be so incredible, it was like a mix of anime but also at the same time, one of them old silent film movies where if a person spoke, the screen would go black with the persons message, and i like that as it makes it really unique. The soundtrack was calm and soothing to listen to, and at one point a lil mysterious. While i did only one casual playthough from start to end, i did not earn every achievement *because i'm not into such things, i'm more into stories*, however there are alot of hidden achievements that'll be tricky to find. My only complaint would be its not a long game, but that itself is alright, not all stories needs to be hours upon hours long, sometimes the best stories, like this one, can be short but sweet.While the game can be short, the amazing work that has gone into this game is well worth full price in my opinion, that and with the quality of the animations, i would love to see it be turned into a anime or a movie, i think it has soo much potential. I've played many games this year, but i would have to say that this game, even if it was short but sweet, would have to be my game of the year~
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: One of the cutest and most heartwarming games I've ever played. The storyline and art style are so beautiful, the game is a masterpiece. The soundtrack is also so wonderful and calming, I had such a great time playing.It's short, and can be completed quickly. I highly recommend buying this game and the DLC.
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: For artists, visually or musically. Will always have a story behind its piece. You always wonder what goes through an artists mind when you find a particular illustration or song that resonates with you. At times, you find yourself listening to a song or looking at a picture, and all of a sudden, you instantly receive a flashback of a particular time in your life. Whatever emotion that memory holds, it will always be a memory you're fond of. Be it a memory of a past relationship with someone dear, or simpler days where the expectations of the world didn't weigh upon you as much. Though I believe that's the best part, it's cemented for the rest of your life. It may be a famous piece that people will one day browse at an art museum, or a song that many others will listen to online or on the radio. Then, there's always those that will never see the recognition it  truly deserves. Though the game was short, it did bring a tear to my eye. The art style is definitely inspired by works from Studio Ghibli. The puzzles weren't too difficult and weren't that straight forward. Those with photographic memory will prosper aha. I hope to see more completed titles from Silver Lining studio in the future. What would the world be without Art?
_childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: During my play through, another game came to mind. The Graveyard, a game where you play as an old lady walking around a graveyard. It truly was a revolting game, I don't know how you make a game that simple run so badly.So why am I bringing up  a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and kind of pretentious game? Well, because it advertised itself as an "explorable painting rather than a game". And that's kinda what Behind the Frame is.  It's an explorable painting with so many tiny details and artistic value put into it.Let us forget the Graveyard and never think about it again. Behind the Frame is a very good game. It's a point and click game where you paint. It's easy, fast, and responsive. I found great joy when my barrage of scribbles just suddenly transformed a very well drawn umbrella. Which I suppose is a plus, you don't really need to draw anything as the game knows what you're doing. The only time it was an issue was near the end of the game where you needed to write some letters. No matter how much I tried it would not register and then I just drew a a black square and the game was like  "ah yes, this is the letter A".There's a lot of puzzles(duh), it's how you advance the story, and I mean, they're kinda easy but maybe that's just me though, since I have a galaxy level gigabrain. It's certainly not a detriment against game, a lot of these puzzles are cleverly laid out, and they're chill. The whole game is chill.So basically, the animation. It's very good. Really good, paired with the cute art style and beautiful background art. II won't speak about the story since it's better to see it first hand, but it was sweet. I'm sure someone will cry because of it. Not me since I'm a manly man who eats bricks. But even a brick eater like me can realize what a heartful tale this is.Behind the Frame: The Finest Landscape, which, by the way,  why the colon. Both titles work fine on their own. My guess is the devs just couldn't decide which one to use. Anyway, it's very good. Short and memorable, and it was worth my money and time.

_childDocuments_.review: We as humans tend to dwell on death and what lies beyond. It's only natural as we simply don't know. Behind the Frame explores this concept with an emotional tug-of-war of a story, but you really need to pay attention, and a lot of the story is more between the lines and not what's really being shown in front of you. There's a lot of assumption that you know what's happening when the main character looks shockingly off in the distance based on the previous scene. It's done fairly well too.Most of Behind the Frame is puzzle solving. It takes a dark twist halfway through and it surprised me. Your goal is to acquire all five missing colors on your paint palette to finish your painting. To do this each color is locked away behind a chapter puzzle. These got rather complex towards the end, but nothing you can't figure out without exploring and finding that key item that gives you that "AHA!" moment. Some puzzles are as simple as matching colors on a painting to memorization. Nothing is overly complex and it does eventually come together. The painting itself is a matter of scribbling enough in the empty space and it will auto-fill. Nothing extraordinary there. There are some other small tasks like making food which is as simple and dragging items around.There isn't a lot of context on the main character's life itself through any reading of notes or anything. It's pretty much learning about her past and her connection with her neighbor. The game has gorgeous anime-Ghibli-inspired art with a few small cut scenes thrown in. I never got tired of looking at the game, but it is confined to mostly her apartment. Every so often you "dive" into a painting, but it's usually just for story context. There were a few panoramic scenes that were breathtaking. I actually felt like I stepped into a painting myself a few times.In the end, the game is over in about 90 minutes or less depending on how long it takes you to solve the more complex puzzles in the final chapters. Without having to solve these this game is over in an hour. The story does unfold quite a bit towards the end and without voice acting it gets a lot of emotions across and I have to give the developers credit for that. Most of these short indie games don't have any meaning behind them. They have some clever gameplay ideas or neat visuals and nothing beyond that. Behind the Frame actually tugged at my heart strings a bit and got me thinking at the end which is more than I can say for 60-hour-long AAA titles. If you want a puzzle-filled emotional evening with great visuals and fun gameplay mechanics then look no further.

_childDocuments_.review: "Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery" is a mobile app that's been dumped on Steam as if it was a real PC game (it's not)... it's a cash grab from greedy mobile devs.It's a point and click adventure mobile app interspersed with Taiwanese animation (in the Japanese anime style, I guess imitation is the highest form of flattery) and tells a whimsical story about an aspiring artist, her hopes and dreams, in a pleasant slice-of-life style that is a mainstay for a lot of professional animation.Before we get into the defects, which are few but enough to disqualify this as a PC game, it's worth mentioning that the story is good, the animation is top notch... and uh, we can get all of that from watching a YouTube playthrough of the game, so it's not going to factor heavily into the review, especially when gameplay is incredibly shallow and just exists to step you through to the next bit of story.   My gaming rig is not primarily intended for me to watch YouTube on.   YouTube, by the way, is free to watch... this free mobile app, however, will cost you money on PC.  Even though it's free on mobile. From a technical perspective, as a mobile app, this doesn't meet basic minimum requirements that most PC gamers expect as standard.There's no option to change the resolution and no useful graphics tweaks.  There's no way to ensure this is running at the native resolution of your display.  There's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.The controls can't be customised because the game has such a dumbed down, simplified interface that it's just iPhone screen tapping stuff.  The fact that the interface is this dumbed down might be seen as a problem in itself, however... this is a fairly shallow experience if you're the kind of gamer that likes to play games with deep, rich control schemes and interaction.  You'll get none of that here.Because this is a mobile app, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the iPhones that the mobile app was designed for.  These are unfortunate handicaps and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was an afterthought for the iPhone developers who are to blame for this.  The mobile app is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for mobile phones forces upon a game.  Once more, mobile devs have made gaming worse for everyone.  I didn't spend thousands on building a gaming rig just so I could pretend it's an iPhone.These technical defects push this mobile app below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.Once more we see greedy mobile devs trying to scam PC gamers. On Steam, this is $13 USD, on app stores, it's free. Mobile devs must learn PC gamers are not here to be gouged, and can't be expected to pay a premium for a free mobile app just because it's been lazily dumped on Steam.  This is unacceptable disrespect for PC gamers.For comparison, the $13 asking price for this mobile app on PC could get you games like "Project Zomboid", "Dead by Daylight" or "Rust".  That's right... if you want this game, you can go buy Dead By Daylight, .See why I must recommend against paying money for free mobile apps on Steam??Because this can be played free elsewhere, and because of the other defects, it's impossible to recommend.Who do they think we are?

_childDocuments_.review: First I want to say that the idea behind and the artistic style of this game are both very good. So, why cannot I recommend this game? Because in my option this shouldn't have become a game at all. Would the company have created  a 20 minute animated short film out of the story, chances are I would have liked it a lot!However they chose to make this a ~2 hour game, 30 minutes of which I spent trying to figure out why the game repeatedly hangs in the between-chapter cutszenes (see forum entries), which already spoiled most of the pleasure. Then there's about 10 minutes of cutscenes (which are just fine) and the rest is some crude painting and some "EXIT ROOM" style mini games, just so easy and with so many hints there's not a chance you can do them wrong. And no, baking toast and making coffee in a computer game is not exactly "fun" either, and it's mandatory.Besides this I must admit that I had to read some forum thread in order to  understand the story ... and usually I don't have that much trouble understanding short films.The music was very fitting and one of the good aspects of this art piece.Short game short: If you like interactive, twisted stories, like to look at paintings and don't mind waiting and prefer relaxing games over mind-boggingly ones, this can be a good choice. But if you are looking for a challenging fun game, there are many better ones out there, even with equally good story and art style.P.S. I'll never understand why some game makers require you to press a button or click somewhere just to make the main menu appear. As if the start screen is sooo much nicer with a text like "Press here to start" than with the menu itself.P.P.S. If you like paintings and interesting stories, you might want want to have a look at "Eastshade". I very much enjoyed that game and in "Eastshade" you can at least choose yourself (most of the time) what to paint. Also it's much longer and a feast for the eyes as well.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- It's gorgeous visually. Amazing hand drawn graphics, great lighting and chromatic palette.- Awesome animations during the cut scenes. They are as smooth and pleasant as an anime movie.- Strong, weird atmosphere. It mixes nicely reality with imagination and manages to gets you immersed.- Cool, calm music that enhances the atmosphere even more.- The story is pretty simplistic, but in the way it's revealed it gets interesting and emotional.- Good rhythm. The monotonous, repetitive beginning strengthens what comes next. - It's pretty relaxing.The bad- Control mechanics needed a lot more thought and work in order to resemble better the action of painting and get you more immersed. Other interactions with things around you are pretty simplistic too.- Puzzles are just easy, repetitive, well worn pattern match ones. No creativity, no challenge. You just solve them mechanically.- Dialogues and text are too shallow. Like it's made for children or tries too hard to be cute.- The protagonists needed some more depth and backstories in order to make you care more about them. It could be so much stronger emotionally that way.  - Sound design is pretty empty with almost no environmental sounds. Girl's sound effects are pretty annoying and feel unnatural.

_childDocuments_.review: Behind the Frame is a story-driven point-and-click game with light puzzle elements.The narration is done through texts, stunning visuals, and paintings.You may consider this more of an interactive story that can be completed in one sitting (around 2 hours).The art style and animation are top-notch. It's worth playing for that.The story is quite emotional. The timeline seemed messed up. And it's possible that you may not understand what's going on in the first place since there is no explanation given. So, it relies on the player's imagination and ingenuity.The story reminded me of the movie "La La Land." It felt like the theme was inspired by it (intentionally or not, I don't know). But I expected a different ending (a bit let down by it).The music tracks catch the various moods perfectly. The sound design is also on point.So many of the achievements don't make that much sense. So, you may need a guide to get them. But it's easy to get them through "the chapter select" after completing the game.Also, there is a short DLC that can be played after finishing the game. Nice addition, and quite important to understand the story.I'll recommend getting it at a discounted price if you are looking for an interactive story-like game (Duration: 1 to 2 hours).My verdict: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Sound, images, words. This is a game that has been carefully, lovingly crafted in every nook and cranny, so that everything works together to immerse you in the cosy, cluttered apartment of a young artist whose world you inhabit. She stares at a large canvass which you must help her finish, over the course of the days to come. You are quickly enlisted into her daily routine; find a cassette and put on some music; fry an egg for breakfast; make the morning coffee; get a bit further with completing her resume and application for the art exhibition. Then the day’s painting must commence. The way the routine repeats each day until it becomes a familiar ritual creates a peaceful, calming backdrop which, for me, evoked something of the experience of lockdown; the artist, alone in her flat with her daily routine and work to immerse herself in; glimpses through her window of the sad, solitary man who lives in the apartment opposite and who also seems to paint; the sleepy presence of a cat who acts as a bridge between the two in the absence of any spoken contact or communication.Each day you paint a little more, but then the direction of travel starts to veer off in unexpected, mysterious directions. The comfortable routine which has been so carefully established to the point that the player is expertly racing through each item (eggs, check; coffee, check; morning sketches, check) starts to be subverted as fragments of a totally different narrative start to emerge. It is like the process by which layers of paint are painstakingly scraped away from a canvass to reveal a different, startling image, related to the first but representative of the artist’s original intentions. The true image which starts to emerge is one of love, loss, and the recovery of memory. Plenty of space is left for the player to interpret exactly what everything means, but clues and suggestions are littered around both the apartment and the wider scenes and spaces from the past which we start to visit. As you piece together the mystery and reassemble the full picture of events, the puzzles are unlikely to impede you for long; frustration rarely builds, and the pervading atmosphere of cosy calm never really departs. Part game, part interactive narrative-audio story experience, Behind the Frame is a magical and peaceful world to immerse yourself in for the several hours it will take to complete.

_childDocuments_.review: Played a game that felt exactly like watching an anime? Meet Behind the Frame, a wonderfully drawn, animated, and sound tracked game with a very beautiful story. In Behind the Frame, you play a painting student going through the normal routine of every day life, until an event/encounter causes you to discover that not everything is at it seems. It's a journey of happiness, discovery, pain, and nostalgia, rolled into a few hours of gameplay.The game is a puzzle click-through where you have to complete certain tasks in order to unlock and move onto the next scene. Some tasks involve simply clicking things in the right order, others require you to find hidden objects and connect them to certain pieces, some involve a little artistry (you do play a painter!); all of it as a means of going through the story. Behind the Frame has a really beautiful soundtrack to accompany the scenes, done to match the emotions and flow of the story. The artwork is also breathtaking because it is reminiscent of something from Studio Ghibli in some parts, but then shifts to a watercolor-like or painting scenario the next. You can see that a lot of effort was put into each scene and each act in the game, and they put a lot of detail into even the littlest of things.It's hard not to appreciate or love a game that one can feel they can relate to, even if the game can be played in about 1-2 hours only.Pros: Great artwork, story, and soundtrack. Cons: The game is short. Right as you feel you start to feel emotionally invested, it ends. Also, certain parts of the game aren't clear about how to move on or what the next step is. Some click-guessing may be involved. I had to close and restart the game because the game hanged.Still, a great game to try. But best to purchase this on sale since it doesn't take long to complete.

_childDocuments_.review: The visuals are nice and reminiscent of the animation works of Studio Ghibli and are definitely the highlight of the game, the background music is very chill and soothing, the atmosphere is neat. The gameplay was....meh. It was okay for a two hour indie game and i liked that there were more puzzles than i anticipated, but it was nothing too memorable and engaging.However, there were a few things that made me dislike the game.First, it isnt a very long game. So there definitely was room for voice acting. I understand that when a game is very long or has a load of text, you dont want to invest in a voice actor. BUT interestingly, there IS some voice acting. Everytime something happens or you interact with objects, your character will say "Oh", "Aah", "Hmm", "Wow", "Weeell". And it was....so....effing....annoying. It actually made me put down my headphones after ten minutes and play the game without sound. I know i could have disabled the "voice acting" in the options, but it infuriated me enough to just simply dont play with any of it. Like seriously, instead of those redundant interjections the voice actress could have been used to speak meaningful lines.Second, there were lots of text bugs, where not even sometimes, but very often the text just wouldnt disappear. That perse be isnt a major problem, unless of course as long as there is text on the screen the game disallows you from interacting with objects. So you just sit there a whole minute or two, waiting for the text to disappear. Thank god i had a cup of tea to sip on. This nuisance actively discourages you from interacting with the game world.Third, and this is completely nitpicking a design choice and just for the achievement hunters out there. Some of the achievements are just....stupid. Click this painting ten times, walk up those stairs four times. Like, wtf? Ironically i did fulfill some of those requirements, where i would just randomly click on things a few times. But "OH NO!!, you only clicked that specific thing 100 times, not 101 times! Jokes on you!". What was the train of thought behind some of those decisions?Fourth, when you look around your apartment you technically dont stand in a rendered environment, but in a drawn frame. Which is consistent with the rest of the games art style. But it also means the objects and perspectives are all set, which isnt how we humans experience reality. Even the slightest tilt of your head will change how objects are oriented towards your eyes and each other relative to you. This resulted in me feeling some dizziness when looking around the appartment too fast, especially when searching for something on the floor or looking higher up towards the ceiling. However, i didnt see anyone else complain about this in the reviews, so i might be a 1% exception to this.Fifth, the story might be heartfelt and fundamentally a good take on the compromisses of life. And it is in fact executed pretty nicely! But, to my personal taste, it was way too depressing for me. After closing the game i felt some sort of relief that i could go back to my real life problems and not having to think about those fictional characters again, and that is usually not a good sign for the enjoyment of a game, or any story at that. But maybe i am too cynical in that regard.So all in all, Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery is an okay indie game with all its heart in its art design and a nice concept for a story and gameplay loop. But some of the design choices and the execution of some technical realizations are done really poorly. There were way too many things that resulted in me abhorring this experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Introduction:"Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery" is a beautifully crafted indie game that delves into the world of artistry, offering a unique blend of puzzle-solving and emotional storytelling. Developed by a talented team, this game invites players to step into the shoes of an aspiring artist and embark on a journey filled with creativity, mystery, and personal growth.Gameplay:At its core, "Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery" is a puzzle-adventure game where players guide the brush strokes of the protagonist while helping her navigate through various challenges. As you explore the artist's cozy apartment, you'll encounter a brusque neighbor and his mischievous cat, adding an element of intrigue and subtle humor to the experience.The gameplay primarily revolves around solving puzzles that range from simple logic challenges to more intricate tasks related to painting and artistic expression. These puzzles seamlessly integrate with the narrative, offering a sense of purpose and immersion. The controls are intuitive and responsive, making it easy to manipulate the artist's tools and interact with the environment.Artistic Expression and Narrative:What sets "Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery" apart is its emphasis on artistic expression and storytelling. As you progress through the game, the artist's painting gradually takes shape, representing her personal journey and emotions. This visual metaphor beautifully intertwines with the narrative, which unveils an emotional tale of chance encounters and hidden connections between unrelated yet familiar moments.The storytelling is poignant, evoking a range of emotions from joy and curiosity to introspection and empathy. The dialogue is well-written and engaging, effectively capturing the personalities of the characters and their evolving relationships. The game also cleverly uses environmental details and subtle visual cues to enhance the narrative, immersing players in the artist's world.Visuals and Sound Design:Visually, "Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery" is a treat for the eyes. The hand-painted art style exudes charm and elegance, reminiscent of traditional watercolor illustrations. The attention to detail in each scene is remarkable, creating a cozy atmosphere that draws players into the artist's surroundings. From the vibrant colors to the delicate brushwork, the game's visuals are a true work of art.Complementing the stunning visuals is a soothing soundtrack that captures the essence of the game's tranquil setting. The music gracefully accompanies the gameplay, immersing players in a serene and contemplative ambiance. Additionally, the sound effects and voice acting are of high quality, further enhancing the overall immersion.Conclusion:"Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery" is a captivating and introspective journey that seamlessly blends art, puzzles, and storytelling. Through its unique gameplay mechanics, players are invited to explore the world of an aspiring artist, unraveling a heartfelt narrative filled with emotion and personal growth. With its stunning visuals, engaging puzzles, and evocative soundtrack, this indie gem offers an experience that will leave a lasting impression on both art enthusiasts and gamers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: Roughly 2h to 100%, it's a beautifully short game. Obviously the references to Ghibli are pretty strong and mentioned quite often in other reviews, but it really does fall in line with that style. This game is very reminiscent of Hiromasa Yonebayashi's works and I absolutely love it for that.The gameplay is quite simple, point and click areas around the rooms and a painting minigame are the majority of what you need to do alongside a few simple puzzles. A few easy to miss achievements but not a hassle at all to replay for. For being such a short tale it still gives that punch-to-the-gut "who's cutting onions?" feeling, again akin to Maro's film work in the vein as Omoide no Marnie/When Marnie Was There - a highly impressive feat for this studio. I really hope this development studio creates more projects in the future as the storytelling and animation is absolutely beautiful. My only complaints is I wish it were so much longer; I am so sad that it's already over. Behind the Frame is an absolutely lovely game.

_childDocuments_.review: During a few scenes I was afraid I'm going to cringe at the conclusion of the game, expecting it to get a bit too cliche, but the overall payoff was great. It's a very short, cute experience that starts cosy, then turns a bit surreal and dark, then once again wholesome. A tiny adventure.It's fascinating to observe the developers' decisions on how to use their limited budget and time. Some moments are meant to hit the hardest and have detailed highly stylized illustrations, properly timed ambient and music, fancy character animations, and a sense of style, while others are trying to just get things done as cheaply as they can without getting jarring. If the studio were to get a huge pile of money, I have no doubt they would turn it into a Visual Novel classic. That's why I really hope that the community actually keeps the game on their accounts instead of refunding it. Let's reward the artists for their effort.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was so serene and ghibli-esque and an overall joy to play. Centred around painting, the player discover the story line as the heroine does through various paintings. This one has a little bit of a butterfly effect with the game jumping through the past and present frequently; although it does not become confusing. The puzzles were simplistic and all colour/painting centred as it is the focal point of the game. I particularly enjoyed the references to artists throughout the game, mainly in the achievements. The art style is very reminiscent to that of Studio Ghibli and emulates the vibes perfectly. Many of the backdrops throughout the game could be interchangeable with Ghibli movies. The hues were vibrant and warm-toned to match many of the naturescapes. The actual plot of this game is so cute and well done for such a short game. Using paintings as plot devices was a very clever and fitting way of storytelling. The story itself is straight out of a ghibli movie with the ending being the best part of the game. The ending was perfectly done and encapsulates what many girls want. This is a perfect game for anyone who loves ghibli movies with the game itself sharing similarities to The Wind Rises (the good parts) and Howl's Moving Castle. The DLC was also great since you didn't have to pay extra for it haha! Also, there's a cute cat!

_childDocuments_.review: Damn. This was such a hard call but I really don’t think I can recommend this as a “game”.There are so many good things about this. The story is beautiful, the art and animation is absolutely stunning and the music is gorgeous. It’s a great story that definitely made me cry and I think if this was just a short animation film… I would’ve appreciated this so much more.The issue is that this is not a game. At best it’s an interactive film, and for the price and the amount of “gameplay” there is, it really isn’t worth it, especially because you can complete the whole story in less than 2 hours (maybe this was intentional so that people could instantly refund on steam as soon as they finished the story, jk pls don’t do this). The gameplay also consists of repetitive motions that are more mindless actions as opposed to actual gameplay, they are so tedious and personally, any “gameplay” I did ruined the flow of the story for me. I’d be invested in the story and trying to figure out what was going to happen next when bam, they threw in a random “puzzle”, if it can even be called that? The “puzzles” are so basic and easy even my dumba** with one brain cell was able to figure it out at 3am. They’re just more tedious tasks I need to finish in order to unlock more story and animations. The thing that honestly confirmed I couldn’t recommend this game was yet again another gameplay issue. SPOILER ALERT WARNING (not heavy, I’m just describing the “gameplay” and what frustrated me to no end):At one point in the game where  and I’m not even joking or exaggerating when I say that it legit took me 15 minutes to complete this “puzzle” because the margin for error was so low… I had to look up a walkthrough of the game just so I could find the correct placement and how exactly they wanted me to draw in order to get past this stupid part. This was at a super emotional point in the story as well and this just absolutely ruined any immersion I had in the story because I was frustrated and annoyed for 15 minutes with this stupid task that I couldn’t get past for the life of me. So, TLDR: If this was a short film I would have rated it an 11/10. As a game though, it’s like a 4/10 due to the horrendous “gameplay” and tedious tasks that brought no joy to my poor heart that just wanted to witness a beautiful story ;-;

_childDocuments_.review: This game is currently in the Humble Choice for May 2023, this is part of my coverage of the bundle. If you are interested in the game and it's before June 6th, 2022, consider picking up the game as part of the current monthly bundle.A beautifully told hour-long story.Behind the Frame is gorgeous, there are beautiful animated scenes that will play along with a solid point-and-click puzzle game that’s pretty reasonable in difficulty.  There are a ton of a-ha moments.  There’s also an interesting narrative being told here, where… honestly, I’m not sure exactly what the story is. I’ve heard three different interpretations from what I took away, and I’m quite glad that the game doesn’t give a firm answer, but is left open to the player to understand. That being said, I’m already done with Behind the Frame and finished in that first hour.  That’s short, reminding me of games like Gorogoa, but also like Gorogoa, this is a beautiful experience, and it’s touching to the point where I’d consider replaying it, especially with the story that may need a second playthrough to consider. Pick this up if you want a beautiful art-filled game.  This is unique in several ways, and the puzzles are solid.  While the game is short, this is a title I’ll probably think about for some time.  In that way, it reminds me of Her Story, a game that I love, but also will just sit around considering the story.  Behind the Frame is short but memorable.If you enjoyed this review or want to know what I think of other games in the bundle, check out the full review on or subscribe to my Youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: On first play, this seems like a very easy game.  Then you realize that what you're being asked to do makes little sense.  There are too many strange coincidences and mysteries.  What story can possibly explain the oddness that creeps into an ordinary day of painting, cute kitty invasion, and the mixture of your creations with those of your neighbor?  You need to read the changing environment to progress through the puzzles, but while you are collecting pieces of sketchbook and tubes of colored paint, to complete the picture that will launch your career, you are literally connecting the dots about the truth of your situation.  That's when the game becomes truly interesting.  Puzzles advance in difficulty but are mostly logical and well integrated into the narrative.  The main character, with all her sighs and murmers, and her love of sudden splotches of bright color, is incredibly appealing,   If you like Borges, cute but mischievous cats, and sudden memory paradoxes, this game is definitely worth buying. SPOILERS!!!!!:

My trouble was that the characters are pretty detailed, but live in a world I don't, so it just never connected with me.The plot is simple, boy looses cat, starts canvassing neighbourhood; girl helps find cat. Boy then accidentally bumps into girl sometimes at coffee shop. It goes on from there quite a way, but I'm not going to spoil it for you. because it has a plot and trajectory, but it just never hit for me. I mean there are things for you to work out, and you build a picture of the timeline as you go, but I hope they release a DLC that fills in more of the timeline.I did find the game a relaxing play, but I would never pay the full price for it, it's too short, even with the JACK DLC. Mainly I liked it for the art style and the visuals which are great, but they are backed by a tired plot-line that does not hold it together. It's even fun to play the game a second time, just for the visuals. I am a bit partial so some paintbrush work myself, and found that although it's pretty easy to use a mouse to colour-by-numbers and paint inside the boxes. so anyone can play this game/story. But because it did not feel like it was hard enough to complete the "paint-by-numbers" style puzzles, each portrait lacked it's own sense of achievement. Perhaps if the images were "rendered" a bit cleaner and with more detail, it might have felt like something. No artistic skill required at all. Unpacking was a recent play that left me warm inside, but Behind the Frame is a beautiful, eloquent, well-crafted story that both makes you smile and makes you cry at the same time. I won't talk further on the plot because I feel it necessary anyone and everyone should play this as it will resonate with each individual separately. _childDocuments_.review: Behind the Frame is a beautiful interactive story about an aspiring artist. As you progress you start recognising familiarity between certain objects and unlock an even deeper story.I thoroughly enjoyed this game. Perfect for relaxing, having a hot drink and being guided through the life of an artist. Art style and visuals were absolutely beautiful, the music- soothing and a well-written story which has you focused and constantly wondering what you will find next.The game is split into chapters, each with its own focus on a pinnacle part of the story. No dialogue (apart from letters), no voice acting - just a well written and well executed masterpiece. Game does not feel rushed, nor extended - with just about 2 hours of gameplay.Behind the Frame has you reflecting on your own personal life by the end of the game, ultimately hitting your emotions. Honestly, I enjoyed it so much - after completing the game, you unlock a new chapter in which the story is shown from a different perspective. This hit even harder.Overall, beautifully written and executed and would honestly recommend anyone try it out.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those "get it on sale" recommendations.The game is absolutely stunning and the story and gameplay hits that artsy whimsical spot for me.Yeah, let me paint, but also make coffee beforehand and scetch the neighbors cat by the window!The only downside is the length. I got through it in just over an hour, and that is REALLY short.Though I can't fully blame the game for it, because it's such a handcrafted experience, of course it's shorter if there is so much work put into tiny details, I suppose?I could have used more puzzles for padding, I guess.I had some slight "bugs" that padded the playtime too, sometimes you have to wait for dialogue to disappear on its own and it takes quite a while to do so and if  you're an impatient clicker like myself you run the risk of clicking the same prompt again, having to wait again... so yeah, it actually probably hit the sub one hour mark just because of those scenes.Still, it's a very beautiful and enjoyable little experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game if you like interactive visual novels but it isn't worth the asking price, I bought it in a bundle and you should do the same or wait for a deep sale.The game is ok if you are in the mood for a relaxing visual novel with some lite puzzles mixed in. _childDocuments_.name: Behind the Frame: The Finest Scenery

_childDocuments_.review: This is such beautiful game. From its vibrant atmosphere to the endearing gameplay, I enjoyed every moment of it. Without spoiling much of the story, Behind The Frame covers a story of a young female artist preparing her application for her New York exhibit. But as the story progresses it covers the story of two distant creatives that yearn for one another and the story behind how they influenced one another with their presence. I love how the game focuses on an implied love but leaves you to decide how their relationship lies.The game’s art style is heavily inspired by Studio Ghibli’s films and the cutscenes although short, always captured my attention. I found the visuals along with the wonderful soundtrack orchestrated such a wonderful and evocative story that pulled at my heart.The music across all six chapters brought about feelings of nostalgia and calm that contrasts with life in the big city. The story hooked me and the simple yet intricate detail that sits behind every puzzle provide a seamless and enjoyable experience. This is a laid-back visual novel that I found to be quite enrapturing. The title pf this game was something I never understood but as I completed the game it touched me. Paintings and photos are meant to hold a moment in time. It's beautiful how something as simple as an image can convey something really meaningful. This game truly shows with every work of art that there's a story... \

_childDocuments_.review:
Guide brush strokes and solve a variety of puzzles to help an aspiring artist complete her masterpiece amid her brusque neighbor's gaze and his pesky cat. As her painting starts to take shape, uncover an emotional tale of chance and artistry revealed behind unrelated yet familiar moments. 

Behind the Frame is a vivid, interactive fiction about an aspiring artist on the cusp of finishing the final piece of her gallery submission.

A relaxing, eloquent experience that can be played at any pace. Become immersed in a panoramic world filled with resplendent colors, beautiful hand-animated visuals, and a smooth, easy-listening soundtrack.

As a passionate artist, seek the missing colors that will bring your paintings to life - all while remembering to take the occasional coffee and breakfast breaks that keep you going. There is more than what meets the eye, for every painting has a story to tell.

name: Minishoot' Adventures
detailed_description: THE UNCHOSEN HAS RETURNED... His minions have emerged from the underworld, your village has been destroyed, and all your friends are now trapped in corrupted crystal... Embark on a journey to save the world in this bullet-filled adventure, born from our desire to mix the joy of open-ended exploration with a top-down shooter's juicy game feel. ENGAGE WITH TIGHT COMBAT Take control of a swift and responsive spaceship, and shoot your way through handcrafted encounters supported by a crystal clear esthetic and crispy game feel. Overcome bosses in intense Bullet Hell battles, with difficulty options for both newcomers and veterans. VENTURE ON YOUR OWN Plunge into an entirely handcrafted world built with many interconnections to explore on your own. Lush caverns, ancient temples and sunken cities await you with their unique treasures, challenges and secrets. RECLAIM THE STOLEN POWERS Finding the Primordial Powers will improve your combat and exploration abilities while also opening up the map bit by bit as you unlock new paths and reveal shortcuts. IMPROVE YOUR SHIP Upgrade your ship by leveling up, finding various items and buying equipment. Don't forget to rescue your adorable friends; each of them will help you in their own way! A GAME MADE FOR YOU Whether you like chill exploration or hardcore Bullet Hell, we got you covered with 3 difficulty modes, aiming assistance, auto fire and more accessibility options.

_childDocuments_.review: Here to just echo the description of old-school Zelda / Metroid / bullet hell mashup. I had a great time playing this on the Steam Deck.Pros-Progression is able to be customized at any time (upgrade aspects of your ship, or downgrade and swap points around) and you're always getting experience as you explore the world (or while you run back to where you last met your end)-Upgrades to provide you clear indications of where you are missing upgrades/unlocks, so you eventually won't have to go re-exploring every nook and cranny.-Bullet patterns weren't entirely unreasonable (beat the game in Advanced mode), but some of those later patterns will have you sweating and keeping a memory of how to dodge each onslaught.Cons-Getting back to where you were if you die in the main overworld can be a bit frustrating, as there is no fast-travel or waypoints. While the world is small enough to return in short order, may be slightly annoying if you keep throwing yourself at a particular challenge-There is an arena area where there is an additional goal to complete other than just beating each stage. but having no immediate retry option was annoying when I was aiming to complete the extra goal.Definitely had a great time with this game, love mashups of different genres that really pull it off well.

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot' Adventures is a top-down bullet-hell Zelda-like metroidvania. I know this game counts as a metroidvania on a very loose term, but it has a connected world, lots of ability-gated areas, loads of hidden items, rewarding exploration, and everything else you can see in that genre. It is also one of the best metroidvania I've played. The game is consistent with its level design. The art style is clean and memorable. It really hard to not recommend this game.→: One thing I especially love about this game is how seamless you can travel from areas to areas. You can go anywhere on the open world map encountering no loading screen (well of course underground areas and dungeons still need loading). This design creates a sense of freedom which is common in other games feature open world design. Yet in Minishoot' Adventures, exploration and a pair of keen eyes are always rewarding. And as a metroidvania, it is always exciting to see how far you can go without acquiring the first ability.→: Because of the game's perspective, this metroidvania has some gating abilities unusual to other games in the same genre. Thus, double jump, air dash, etc are out of the equation. Instead we have abilities that benefit you with the bullet hell gameplay like explosion which can damage enemies and destroy projectiles and slowing down time for easier maneuver amidst the sea of bullets. Definitely something to look forward to if you're tired of the 2D side-scrolling design the metroidvanias are known for.→: Recently a lot of metroidvania just assume players will hit every wall they run into and try to get away with as little hints as possible for the items hidden across the world. This is a foul practice in my book, and I am glad Minishoot' Adventures does things right. Secret passages covered by unusually dense foliage, small cracks on the otherwise smooth walls, projectiles coming from seemingly out-of-bound places, button under a big lily-pad, just to name a few.→: I usually condemn too much arena-style fights as a lazy tactic to stall as much as time as possible, but the gameplay of Minishoot' Adventures makes me want to have more of this fights. Thanks to the bullet-hell, every arena fight feels hand-crafted and follows a specific pattern. It requires players to focus on dodging, repositioning, and shooting back so often time the fights feel more engaging.→Clean art style.→It's cute to see the little planes spinning around to express their emotion.→The little racing games with the spirits are fun.→You can see the lifespan of the projectiles indicated by the inner circle shrinking.→Breaking things are quite rewarding in this game.→More guns with different firing patterns Raiden-style to unlock would be lovely.→The order of recharging active abilities feels weird.中文小簡評→這款嚴格說起來不太算Metroidvania，但是他有太多這類型遊戲應有的特色，所以我說算就算！→做對了許多同期同類型遊戲欠缺的設計。→乾淨簡單的畫風。→無縫接軌大地圖，到哪裡幾乎不需要讀取。→跟其他Metroidvania不一樣的解鎖技能，玩膩2D橫向卷軸的可以試試這款。→隱藏道具的提示，給足線索讓玩家自己發現，而不是直接認定玩家會敲每一到牆。→難得有一款遊戲會讓我喜歡競技場行戰鬥，可能是因為子彈地獄的關係，打起來特別有感。→小飛機透過轉圈圈表達心情特別可愛。→與精靈賽跑很有趣。→敵人射的每發子彈都可以看的出何時會消失。→如果能像雷電那樣有多點射擊模式就好了。→技能充能的順序很奇怪。

_childDocuments_.review: "Zelda meets Galaga… and we get a beautiful little gem. It's a simple and straightforward game, with some secrets and a lot of exploration. The game's strength, in my opinion, is the exploration. The bosses aren't difficult, even on hard mode, but they became tedious for me. It felt like the fights would never end; on hard mode, the bosses are much faster and have much more health, so mistakes, especially early on, are heavily punished. However, the game is still not very demanding—you don’t lose anything if you die; you just have to redo the boss and return to the point where you died to resume exploring.Once you get enough upgrades, the game becomes much easier and, again, the most enjoyable part is the exploration: discovering secret areas and figuring out how to reach the items we see on the map.I only encountered one small bug, which was fixed by entering and exiting the game… several times. For some reason, a vendor wouldn't give me the option to buy the last item, even though I had what it was needed; but in the end, I was able to.Overall, a good game. I hope to see more from the developers ♥

The whole presentation is very lighthearted but charmful, but the tight controls and various missions make this game a throughout enjoyable game.Highly recommended little gem that draws from nostalgic elements but are accessible and lovable to everyone!

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10. Absolutely recommended.The demo did a good job hyping this game up - and the full release delivered. I had an absolute blast for the 10h playthrough I just finished. 👍 The Good:- 🖥️ Cute, clean visuals- 🔊 Pleasant Soundscape- ♿ Accessibility options ON TOP of normal difficulty options- ⬆️ Satisfying upgrade system  - ♻️ Respec anytime - even in combat!- 🚿 Good bullet-hell gameplay (even though I'm not the biggest fan of that generally)- 🪙 Great implementation of secrets and collectibles in the game- 🕹️ Movement feels responsive- 📈 Upgrade pacing is well done - lots of games give you the cool stuff right before the end of the game, this game actually lets you play with the fun stuff from quite early.- 🕳️ Falling down a crevasse or into (deep) water doesn't cost health, so "platforming" sections are quite forgiving.🤏 The Neutral:- 🏎️ I kinda hate races. There are 8 races. Those are not mandatory for finishing the main story. You will need to complete them though for the true ending. Luckily I could just respec into move/boost and turn game speed down to 50% (Accessibility options), so they were ok.- ☠️ Dying in the overworld is kind of harsh since it respawns you at "town". It's located in the center (and there will be tons of shortcuts) so it's not too bad, but still annoying. Didn't happen often though.- ⏳ Strangely you can't pause the game at all (neither ESC or uprade menu) while the level-up animation plays; the game still runs normally (moving/shooting etc), you just can't pause it. 🤷👎 The Bad:- ⁉️ Sometimes progression through the map is not very clear. I got "stuck" twice in the game (separate occasions) and had to re-check quite a bit of the map to find where I needed to go

_childDocuments_.review: Minishoot' Adventures is a small team indie game that punches above its weight class due to its incredible attention to getting the core formula right: the result is a game where combat feels as intense as Enter the Gungeon (while being easier), and exploration is as intoxicating as the 2D Zelda / Metroidvania games you played as a child. Fresh and heartwarming ~10 hours fling :)(+)  is great at giving you hints to hidden secrets / new paths to explore after grabbing a new ability. This results in a game that's difficult to put down because you're constantly high on the urge to explore, looking for friends to save, shortcuts to unlock, heart pieces and powers to collect.(+)  that conveys all information you need without overloading the screen and giving you a lot of text explanations. Best examples are the character's wings showing Boost recharge status, the sound trigger when it fills up, the white dot in enemy projectiles which lets you know when they're about to fade. The color coding sky blue / red / black and reddish is clean. (+)  that are precise and responsive. (+) The arena / pantheon challenge was my favorite part of the game. The end game fully challenged my ability to play with advanced powers and it was pure joy.(+) There's flexibility in shooting and aiming modes that I enjoyed.(-) Infuriating one-shot bullets that are by far my least favorite feature of the platformer / puzzle sequences.(-) After falling into a pit, there's no indication of where you'll respawn, and no invincibility frames to protect you from damage. (-) Epilogue feels anticlimactic(-) Quite difficult to have smooth, high FPS despite having a good GPU. I was stuck at 40ish during exploration and often < 30 during combat. I'm not sure what causes this and there don't seem to be options to turn off to improve performance. (-) "Dodge roll" dash arrives quite late in the game: I would have preferred to have it earlier, and have combats requiring you to use it.
_childDocuments_.name: Minishoot' Adventures

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic twin-stick shooter that's fun to explore and a joy to play.(++) Even better on Steam Deck(++) Great movement, great combat, great flow(++) Various types of enemies requiring different approaches(+) No skill gate-keeping: Offers different difficulties and adjustable auto-aim setting on top of it(+) Basic save-the-world story but it's delivered in a charming and fitting manner (and it's not much in the way)(+) Upgrading your abilities matters and you can feel the difference from the get-go(-) The art style is not the worst but the flash-like aspect where no two graphical elements blend together (due to strong outlines, odd color choices, round angles everywhere and flat lighting) makes the game look way too cheap(-) The whole environment (its every element) is placed on a grid and to no benefit whatsoever(-) Some mechanics can be tiresome: The metroidvania design is too strict and too much on the nose; some passages and bosses more frustrating than fun; the interconnected caves are just annoying and pain to navigate around

_childDocuments_.review: (Обзор на русском )Twin-stick-bullet-hell-top-down-shooter-metroidvania (and it's not joke!)• Balanced metroidvania, where our activities are distributed between world exploring, arena fights with enemies and bosses, and races.• Left stick is used for movement, right one for shooting. You can configure aiming help or even enable auto-shooting.+ The world is full of secrets. You can start exploring many nearby biomes even with few starting abilities (like dash).+ Many types of enemies, their large elite versions and dangerous corrupted ones.+ Killing enemies gives experience that spend to increasing damage, fire rate, distance, crit. chance and speed. You can freely change abilities according to situations.+ Bosses. Each has several phases with few attack patterns. You can beat them now — or get more experience and fight later.+ Races. Another activity where you should quickly finish a track.+ Optional charged abilities that help in battles and relics with passive buffs.+ Shortcut ways between biomes.+ Map indicators that help find all collectables.+ End-game challenges.+ Simple but cute graphics. Some places look amazing.+ 100%🌻 achievements that don't require being super-human.= You can be highly overpowered.= Background music just does its work: no hit, no annoyance.= There are availability settings for game speed and infinite health.– I'm sad that charged abilities are not using for world secrets.– Few times I want to use a custom marker for the map, but there's no such option.– The story is simple cliché.Cool genre fusion for anybody who looks for interesting metroidvanias. Great 10 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun twin stick shooter - there are a ton of options to customise gameplay as well - three basic difficulty levels, a few different shooting styles to pick from - manual, semi and fully auto - as well as accessibility options like infinite energy etc for when you need it.As for gameplay its an interesting mashup of top down Zelda adventuring/Metroidvania style ability gating and a fairly chill bullet hell, in that you'll have to put some thought into how you tackle rooms full of enemies shooting in patterns, BUT you wont be feeling like one wrong move and you're dead.You have to pick up or get given map fragments, you can buy things like completion indicators and an item that returns you to the main village at will.The demo gives you a basic idea of what the gameplay is like, I loved it and bought the game based on it so if in doubt give it a go.Plays like a dream on deck as well.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game. It's Zelda meets Asteroids or Super Stardust, and it's exactly what you would want from that combo.It's a twin-stick shooter with a vast overworld to explore, abilities to acquire, skills to level-up, etc. There are secret areas to find, extra challenges to overcome, bosses to destroy, and new allies to save.It has charming graphics and music, and enough varied difficulty options that most players should be able to tune it for the exact right amount of challenge. Bullet-hell pros might not find themselves pushed to the limit, but it will have everyone else on the edge of their seats.I was so excited when I first heard about this game that I bought it and played it right away. I love it so much that after 15ish hours, 100%ing the game, and getting all but one achievement, I immediately restarted it on the highest difficulty.If Zelda + Asteroids sounds at all appealing to you, you owe it to yourself to give this little gem a try. _childDocuments_.review: Minishoot' Adventures is an excellent combination of twin-stick shooter gameplay and the "unlock upgrades to let you explore earlier areas in greater depth" design of so-called Metroidvania games. You have to find parts of the overland map as pickups, and since the game gives you no guidance as to where they are, you can often explore most of an area before getting the map for it, and on top of that there's no maps at all for dungeons and other indoor areas, with several of them being maze-like enough that they kind of deserve it, especially the sewers under the desert.However, that only detracts slightly from a really good game. Highly recommended!
